units.la: AB ea tempestate, quâ animum meum ad graviora quædam disciplinarum studia adieci, imprimis illud mihi propositum fuit, ut in evolvendis omnis ævi scriptoribus nihil æquè sectarer quam documenta earum rerum, quæ ad sacrarum literarum intelligentiam pertinerent. Existimabam enim id quod res est, Sacri codicis lectionem, non Theologis modò, sed omnibus bonis viris & præsertim eruditis debêre esse iucundissimam, nec nobis qui in literario otio vivimus aliud magis serió agendum, quàm ut quàm optimè cognitus intellectusque sit is sermo quo olim usus ipse Deus est. Hinc quantum temporis alii otii oblectamentis tribuerunt, tantum egomet mihi ad linguam Sanctam excolendam sumpsi, cuius fructus in hunc finem videbatur utilissimus. Et illius sane operae nunquam hactenus me poenituit. Vix enim dicere possum, quantopere animum meum delectaverit Hebraismus, cum Biblica volumina, Rabbinorum Commentarios, & ea quae in Talmudis pandectis à Iudaeis erudite scripta sunt, evolverem. Vbicunque enim loca salebrosa & difficilia (quibus haec literatura alios deterret,) gradum meum morabantur, amor mitigabat laborem, & utilitatis fructus ulterius amorem incitabat, nec unquam ab illis studiis nisi serena fronte recessi. Et quamvis deinde me Providentia Divina לגרום גרם אחר os aliud rodere iusserit, & cogitationes meae ad philosophicas disciplinas applicandae fuerint, priscas tamen nostras musas literulis Hebraicis & Græcis subnixas, ita relinquere non potui, quin semper aliquid de subscisivo tempore illis tribuerem. Ex quo quoque hæ qualescunque animadversiones, quas in subsidium memoriæ adnotavi, ne fugitiva oblivio eas mihi subduceret, & quæ nunc in publicum egrediuntur suum ortum habent. Nec profecto ullum fore credo, qui ad talia transcendere illicitum putet mihi aut aliis, quos suus ordo locusque in aliis muniis detinet. Homo Musarum sacris initiatus, non est (ut ait Cæcilius) unius operis remex & baiulus, generosa mens ad unius res miscellam scientiam non adstringitur, neque alligatur: semper sese versat illa, concutitque, quicquid pulchrum & scitu dignum videt, id omne scit esse suum. Divinæ virgines musæ adstant ubique, & omnes ad se invitant, neminem illæ aversantur qui bonam spem non curavit. Iubent omnes exsurgere, animos sumere, & se quoque honestis conatibus dignos fingere. Satis prosecto aliàs frigent hæc studia, quamvis nemo ab ipsorum limine arceatur. Dicendum enim aperte est, admodum ofcitanter & supinè vivimus. Anglorum, Gallorum & vicinarum gentium verba & voces discimus, tam ingeniosi cùm simus, unam illam non intelligimus linguam, quam sanè unam didicisse operæ esset pretium. Magna pars palàm illam contemnit, ut plurimùm humi repentia ingenia, & à quibus ne hilum in solida literatura exspectabis. Alii verò animum suum quidem ad hoc pulcherrimum studium applicant, sed plerumque ita perfunctoriè, ut quidem ad fores Hebraismi accedant, quod facillimum, interiora autem sacraria, Syriasmum atque Rabbinismum ne voto quidem penetrent: Cùm tamen ad diiudicandum quanti sint in Hebraismo thesauri, meo animo pergendum ultra sit, & dispiciendum, quid Iudæi vernaculi Bibliorum interpretes pretes recte aut secus dixerint, & tunc demum nobis ius fasque erit, de iis rebus liberè dissertare, quarum notitia non aliunde erui nisi ex sacro codice potest. Possem hic meam sententiam adductis exemplis probare, & ostendere quot errores apud omnis generis scriptores ex ignorantiæ huius literaturæ pullularint, si hoc tempore illud agere animus esset, & si mihi de Hebraismi patrocinio ullo modo laborandum; habet enim ille quibus & auctoribus & rationibus causam suam pulchrè tueatur, ut potiùs malignitatis nomine suspecti esse debeant, qui eius contemptum præ se ferunt; quàm assentationis, qui de eo honorificè sentiunt & loquuntur. In posteriorum gratiam adornatum est quicquid hac vice circa Talmudica scrinii nostri repagula perrumpere potuit: quæ oppidò pauca sunt respectu illorum quæ aliàs se obtulissent. Sed rebus nostris consultum non censebamus omnia quæ parata habebamus unâ vice fortunæ committere; Et cùm & optimarum rerum si minus satietas, certè sit modus quidam, etiam in collectione materiarû videbatur modus adhibendus. Quòd si tamen hæc à Doctis aliquo favore excipiantur, ita ut aliquando ad secundam editionem deveniendum sit, illam duplo auctiorem promittimus. Quid vero nunc præstiterimus, melius legendo animadvertet lector, ne domestico præconio vanitatem prodamus, & iudicii eius libertatem impediamus; hoc tamen absque iactantia credere volumus, nos multa adduxisse, quæ Theologis ad sacrarum litterarum intelligentiam inservire possunt, & quæ oblectabunt alios qui Hebraismum amant. Quæ vero prætermisimus, qualia sunt Philologicæ quæstiones circa textum sacrum, & recentiorum Iudæorum ritus, ea studiosus lector elegantèr tractata apud Cl. Hottingerum in Thes. & apud Leusdenium in Philog. & Synag. Buxtorfii reperiet. Libuit enim nobis hac vice præcipuè illarum rerum fastigia pervadere, quæ propiùs priscos Hebræos & cultum posterioris templi spectarent, utpote quæ magnum pondus in explicatione Novi Test. afferre possent, & quæ in lectione Talmudicorum inprimis exstarent. Poterunt tamen & illa, si ita eruditis visum, huic operi ad maiorem eius commendationem suo tempore adiungi. Quod autem has nostras curas sub forma Lexici edere voluerimus, plurimæ nobis adfuerunt causæ & rationes: Præterquàm quòd videbamus præsens opus hoc modo aliorum & nostris inventis semper locupletari posse, insuper non contemnenda utilitas ex illo ordine affulgebat, quòd Hebraismo initiatus, instructus solo Lexico Talm.Celeb. Buxtorfi, ad enucleandas vocum significationes, facili labore in Misnæ & aliorum Talmudicorum tractatuum sensus pervenire possit, modò antea in nostro Lexico materiam circa quam occupatur, legerit & ruminaverit, ad quam facilè reperiendam alphabetica dispositio non inutilis erit. Addidimus enim hunc in finem loco supplementi singularem indicem in Maslictot Misnæ, ut studiosum eò magis adiuvaremus. Hoc enim dicere possumus, nihil nobis, dum illa scripta excutiebamus, maiorem difficultatem creasse quàm quòd nullum præceptorem habuerimus, qui nobis materialia præslibaret: quamvis enim Lexica Aruch & Buxtorsianum vocum significationes suppeditent, ut plurimùm tamen stylus Talmudicus tam varium sensum præ se fert, ut sæpè anxius & dubius hæreas quinam sit amplectendus; Ex qua difficultate tamen facilè te extricabis, si iam aliquâ ratione mente perceperis quid in genere de hoc vel illo Iudæi sentiant. Sed præcipua huius nostri propositi ratio, & quæ primo loco dicenda fuisset, est consilium Clariss. Viri D.Leigt-
units.tr: From the time when I devoted myself to the more serious studies of learning, my chief aim has been that, in reading through the writers of every age, I should pursue nothing more eagerly than the teachings that bear on the understanding of the sacred letters. For I have judged, as is indeed the case, that the reading of the sacred volume ought to be the most delightful thing not only for theologians but for all good men, and especially for the learned. Nor should we who live in literary leisure have any more earnest task than to know as thoroughly as possible, and to understand, the language in which God himself once spoke. So, whatever time others have given to the pleasures of leisure, I have devoted to cultivating the holy tongue, whose fruit seemed most useful to this end. Indeed I have never regretted that labour. I can hardly say how greatly Hebraism has delighted my mind, whenever I have worked through the biblical books, the commentaries of the rabbis, and the things learnedly written by the Jews in the compendia of the Talmud. Wherever rough and difficult passages, which deter others from this literature, have slowed my progress, love of the subject has eased the toil, and the fruit of the usefulness has further kindled that love; nor have I ever left those studies except with a cheerful brow. And although divine Providence afterwards bade me gnaw another's bone, and my thoughts had to be turned to philosophical disciplines, I could not bring myself to abandon our old Muses, which rest on the small letters of Hebrew and Greek, without always giving them something from my spare time. From this, too, these observations, whatever their worth, which I noted down as an aid to memory, so that fleeting forgetfulness might not steal them from me, have their origin, and they now come out into the public. Nor do I believe there will be anyone who thinks it improper for me, or for others whom their proper office and place keep busy elsewhere, to step across into such matters. A man initiated into the rites of the Muses is not, as Caecilius says, a rower and carrier of a single task; a noble mind is not bound or tied to the knowledge of one thing only. It is always moving about and stirring things up, and whatever it sees that is beautiful and worth knowing, it counts all of it as its own. The divine maidens, the Muses, stand present everywhere and invite all to themselves; they reject no one who has not neglected good hope. They bid everyone to rise, take heart, and make themselves worthy of honest endeavours too. Surely these studies are otherwise rather cold, although no one is shut out from their threshold. For it must be said plainly that we live in a very sluggish and careless way. We learn the words and speech of the English, the French and the neighbouring peoples, and although we are so clever, we do not understand that one language, which it would surely be worth the effort to have learned thoroughly. A great part openly despises it, as do minds for the most part creeping on the ground, from whom you will expect not the least thing in solid learning. Others indeed apply their minds to this most beautiful study, but for the most part so superficially that they approach the doorway of Hebraism, which is easiest, but do not even in wish penetrate the inner sanctuaries, Syriasm and Rabbinism. Yet in order to judge how great the treasures are in Hebraism, my mind must go further, and it must be examined what the Jewish interpreters of the Bible in the vernacular have said rightly or otherwise; and only then will it be lawful and right for us to discourse freely on those things whose knowledge can be drawn from no source except the sacred volume. I could here prove my view by adducing examples, and show how many errors have sprung up among writers of every kind from ignorance of this literature, if I had the mind to do that at this time, and if I had to labour in any way for the defence of Hebraism. For it has grounds and authorities by which it can fittingly defend its cause, so that those who show contempt for it ought rather to be suspected of malice than those who think and speak of it with honour are suspected of flattery. For the benefit of posterity I have prepared whatever could in this instance break through the barriers of our chest of Talmudic material; these are indeed very few compared with those that would otherwise have presented themselves. But I did not think it wise to entrust to the chance of fortune all that we had ready at one time; and since, if not satiety of good things, there is at least a certain measure, it seemed that a measure ought to be applied even in gathering the material. But if these labours are received by the learned with some favour, so that at some time a second edition has to be made, we promise it will be twice as large. What we have now achieved, the reader will perceive better by reading, lest we betray vanity by a domestic boast and hamper the freedom of his judgment. Nevertheless we wish to believe, without boasting, that we have brought forward many things that can serve theologians for understanding the sacred letters, and that will delight others who love Hebraism. As for the things we have passed over, such as the philological questions concerning the sacred text, and the customs of the more recent Jews, the studious reader will find them elegantly treated by the distinguished Hottinger in his Thesaurus, and in Leusden's Philologus Hebraeo-Mixtus and Philologus Synagogicus in the works of Buxtorf. For on this occasion we chose chiefly to go through those summits of matters which bear more closely on the ancient Hebrews and the worship of the later temple, since these could carry great weight in the explanation of the New Testament, and which above all lie in the reading of the Talmudic writings. Yet those things too may, if learned men think fit, be added to this work at a suitable time, for its greater recommendation. As to why we wished to publish these our labours in the form of a lexicon, there were many causes and reasons for us: besides the fact that we saw this present work could in this way be enriched continually by the discoveries of others and our own, there also shone forth a not contemptible advantage from that arrangement, that one who has been initiated into Hebrew and is equipped with only the Lexicon Talmudicum of the celebrated Buxtorf can, with easy labour, arrive at the meanings of the words for explaining the sense of the Mishnah and of the other Talmudic treatises, provided he has first read and pondered in our Lexicon the material with which he is occupied; for finding it easily, the alphabetical arrangement will not be useless. For to this end we have added, in place of a supplement, a special index to the Masekhot of the Mishnah, so as to help the student the more. For this we can say: while we were searching through those writings, nothing created greater difficulty for us than that we had no teacher to taste the material beforehand for us. For although the lexicons of Aruch and Buxtorf supply the meanings of the words, nevertheless the Talmudic style for the most part carries so varied a sense that you often stand anxious and doubtful as to which one is to be adopted. Yet you will easily extricate yourself from this difficulty if you have already grasped in your mind, in some way, what the Jews in general think about this or that. But the principal reason for this undertaking of ours, and which should have been stated first, is the counsel of the most distinguished man, Mr. Leigh,

Is, cùm Oxonii hærerem, humanissimis suis literis mihi petenti, quid præcipuè in Hebraismo utiliter & cum fructu tentari posset, respondit : Se nihil scire quo magis studium Hebraicum adiuvari posset, quàm si quis Talmud utrumque, præcipuè Hierosolymitanum legeret, & in codicillos ordine Alphabetico conjiceret, quicquid aut ad historiam aut ritus veterum Hebræorum explanandos faceret ; Vnumquemque deinde ea quæ in suum usum facient, indè expromere posse: Omnia vertere esse nimis tædiosum, imitandas esse apes, quæ mel undiquaque ex infinitis flosculis congerunt & colligunt, quamvis omnes fibrillas texturæ plantarum non excutiant. Et sanè ita est, viris ingenuis & doctis hæc quam sequuti sumus methodus sufficiet, לחסרי לב Indoctis & incuriosis vero nec alia proderit. Ita iudicarunt Viri Magni Dn. Peaucokius Orientalium literarum Columen & Prof. Oxon D. Henricus Iu-stellus, omnis elegantioris literaturæ promotor, quos difficillimum est laudare, quia ut merito laudantur, ita satis laudari non possunt. Hi ambo egregiè nos consiliis & operâ adiuvarunt; præcipuè D. Iustellus, cuius petitionum protela tandem verecundiam nostram expugnarunt, ita ut etiam in publica Scena apparere, & depositum hunc partum tolli sustinuerimus. Si culpa temeritatis deprecanda est, cum ipso omnem partiar invidiam, ipsius culpa erit quod flagitare non desierit, mea quod studio eius sim obsequutus. Honoris causa etiam his adiungere debemus Celeberrimos Viros verè λεύφανον χρυσᾶ ψυχῆς, qui in Gallia & Anglia nos amarunt, ad omnia honesta calcar addiderunt , reducem φίλην εἰς παιδίᾳ χαίαν [?] D. Nicolaum Toinardum Aurelianensem , qui natura doctrinaque informatus est ad omnem virtutis gloriam , uti sufficienter orbi literario probavit in nova sua Chronologia & harmonia , item in observationibus illis physicis quas Parisiis apud Hubinum in vico St. Martini edidit. Et ostendet porro in illa quaestione , An Christus die mortem eius praecedente Pascha celebraverit ? Stat enim pro negativa , nec ut credo absque magno pondere argumentorum , usquedum antem ea nobis produxerit, retinebimus affirmativam sententiam , quam pag. 455; huius operis innuimus. Sequitur par amicorum ex Anglia ; D.
units.tr: Mr. Leigh, most learned in Hebrew, and one of not many, whose authority I have always held in high regard, and from whom I gratefully acknowledge that I learned very many things. When I was staying at Oxford, he answered my humane letters asking what in Hebraism could usefully and fruitfully be attempted above all, as follows: that he knew nothing by which the study of Hebrew could be helped more than if someone read both Talmuds, especially the Jerusalem one, and put into alphabetically ordered notebooks whatever served to explain either the history or the customs of the ancient Hebrews; each person could then draw from there whatever would serve his own use. To translate everything, he said, was too tedious; we should imitate the bees, which gather and collect honey from countless little flowers on every side, though they do not shake out every fibre of the texture of the plants. And indeed it is so: for learned and honourable men this method which we have followed will suffice, but for the unlearned and careless it will benefit nothing else. So have judged the great men, Dr. Pococke, the pillar of Oriental letters, and Professor Henry Justel of Oxford, promoter of all more elegant learning, whom it is very hard to praise, because, though they are deservedly praised, they cannot be praised enough. These two helped us excellently with their counsel and labour; especially Dr. Justel, whose repeated requests at last overcame our modesty, so that we allowed ourselves to appear on the public stage and to let this deposited offspring be lifted up. If blame for rashness must be deprecated, I shall share all the odium with him: it will be his fault that he did not cease to demand, and mine that I yielded to his zeal. For the sake of honour we ought also to add to these the most celebrated men, truly a golden-souled glory [λεύφανον χρυσᾶ ψυχῆς], who loved us in France and England and added spurs to every honourable undertaking: Dr. Stephen Gaussen, professor of theology in the Academy of Saumur, a man furnished with every resource of talent and learning, at whose urging I once translated into Latin the objections of Abarbanel on chapter 53 of Isaiah; Dr. Nicolas Toinard of Orléans, who by nature and learning was formed for every glory of virtue, as he has sufficiently proved to the literary world in his new Chronology and Harmony, and likewise in those physical observations which he published at Paris at the shop of Hubin in the Rue St. Martin. And he will further show, in that question, Did Christ celebrate the Passover before his death? For he takes the negative side, and not, I believe, without great weight of arguments; but until he has brought that forward for us, we shall retain the affirmative opinion, which we have indicated on page 455 of this work. units.tr: Bernhard, fellow of St. John's College, Oxford, and Professor of Mathematics in the University, and Dr. William Gise, fellow of Oriel College: men of astonishing learning, in whom all Oriental literature dwells elegantly, and in Dr. Gise almost to a miracle. Indeed there is scarcely any language in the whole world, of which monuments are preserved for the perpetuity of letters, that he has not investigated with unremitting labour, though he is not yet twenty-four years of age. Their judgment has always seemed to me like a very great theatre, and I am heartily glad that my efforts have pleased them. But, most courteous reader, when you have read through these my remarks, I beg you to remember to judge everything with clemency rather than strict justice [χῷ τὴν ἑπιπινειαν ἐν ἐξ ἀχειβοδικιᾷς]. Many things will perhaps be not so well said or placed, and in these you will give the more generous construction [χεῖερ πείζονι]. We are not of such overbearing arrogance as to

units.la: In tanta communis naturæ imbecillitate, solos nos superesse existimemus, quibus interdum venia opus non fit. In omnibus ἀπαντῆς ἐομψῳ ἀβίἀλεσι, hallucinamur omnes, nec quisquam est, qui tam bene animum suum disciplinis obfirmavit, ut nihil fugere eum possit aut fallere. Parati profecto sumus simulac monuerit quis meliora, sententiam mutare. Pertinaciam enim pro opinione induere non est nostrum. Ipsi nos si quando errores nostros odorati fuerimus, sponte hanc gratiam à nobis inibimus, & primi eos indicabimus, ne quis forte studio nostri deceptus, hallucinationes nostras cæcis oculis prætereat. Tandem ut mihi mea, sic sua Typographo imputabis menda. Omnibus enim absens occurrere non potui; Norunt alii, qualia sint illorum librorum fata, qui procul authoribus typis describuntur. Verùm ut ipse inter legendum observare poteris , pauca ac leviora illa sunt quæ evitari non potuerunt ob preli festina-tionem; Graviora vero , si quæ sint, ex Indice erratorum facilè corriges;
units.tr: In such great frailty of our common nature, we do not suppose that we alone are left, we who sometimes do not need pardon. In all things all men [ἀπαντῆς ἐομψῳ ἀβίἀλεσι] go astray, and there is no one who has so firmly fortified his mind by learning that he can escape or be deceived by nothing. We are certainly ready, as soon as anyone shows us something better, to change our opinion. For it is not our way to cling stubbornly to an opinion. If ever we have sniffed out our own errors, we will of our own accord take this favour upon ourselves and be the first to point them out, lest anyone, deceived by his zeal for us, pass over our mistakes with blind eyes. Finally, just as you will charge my errors to me, so you will charge the mistakes to the printer. For I could not be present to correct everything from afar. Others know what fate awaits books that are printed far from their authors. But, as you yourself will be able to observe while reading, the few and lighter errors are those which could not be avoided because of the haste of the press; the more serious ones, if there are any, you will easily correct from the Index of Errata;

units.tr: Scarcely before was it permitted to penetrate these unknown recesses; now that task will require little labour. Does greater usefulness recommend the book? Or can the subject itself be worthier of its own champion? Let others follow; the learned nation will cherish the offspring, and the author will be a great glory to Lausanne.

units.tr: (1) On how many kinds of Adar there are, i.e. the month of February, see page 8 of this work. (2) "Proclaim" (משמיעין) means the same as "announce" (מכריזין): to publish and promulgate by a public herald, so that everyone knows and hears that the half-shekel must be paid at the appointed time. (3) On the shekels, see page 600. (4) Maimonides, in Kilaim chapter 2, near the end, reports what they proclaimed concerning heterogeneous plants: that each man should go into his garden (לגינתו) and his field (ורשדהו) and root out the heterogeneous plants. On heterogeneous plants in general, see page 241. (5) On the biblical readings, see page 320. (6) On what the scroll (מגילת) is, see pages 320 and 321, where certain circumstances are noted that were observed in the reading of the book of Esther, which they here understand by the scroll. (7) On the distinction between a city (כרך), a town (עיר), and a village (כפר), see pages 117 and 118. (8) They repair the roads for two reasons. First, so that those coming from the provinces to the Passover feast may be able to take the road and measure it quickly. This repair was to be carried out so diligently that it could even have been a reason for intercalation; see page 277. Second, so that those who had killed someone by accident would not meet any obstacle on their flight. The text is chiefly to be understood of this repair, as may be seen from Maimonides, Hilchot Rozeach chapter 8: On the fifteenth day of Adar in every year the court sends out agents to repair the roads, and they take care to mend every place that has collapsed or fallen into disrepair. And if ever the Sanhedrin neglected this business, it would be judged as though it had itself shed blood, if perhaps the slayer had been killed by the avenger for an unexpected murder. We have spoken of this repair of the roads on page 53. (9) In the pools of water called mikvaot (מקוואות), the unclean purified themselves by washing before the feast and the offering of sacrifices; on what a mikveh (מקוה) is, see page 337. (10) "They mark" (מצייצין), in the language of Ziyyun and Siggun, "they paint, that is, they mark with a sign or some figure," says the Gloss; so that those who wish to remain clean may be able to avoid those sepulchral places. See Sepulchrum, page 599. (11) The Sanhedrin sends deputies on the fifteenth day of February, who go around (פסכנין לבדוק) to see whether people have obeyed and complied with the edict of the Sanhedrin of 10 February concerning the eradication of heterogeneous plants. To this effect Maimonides, in Kilaim chapter 2, near the end. (12) In the time of our Lord Jesus Christ especially, transgressors (עוברי עבור) multiplied, and the Jewish people openly fell into all kinds of vices; see pages 372 and 373. (13) If anyone does not obey the admonition of the deputies, who begin their inspection on 15 February, and does not root out the heterogeneous plants from his land before the feast of Passover, the deputies (בחולו של מועד, that is, on some day within the first and last days of the feast) go out again and make such a field common property (Germ. geben ihme Preiß) as a penalty for the disobedient man, if in it there is still one of the twenty-four kinds of heterogeneous plants. (4) Ab eo tempore quò mensæ collocatæ sunt in provinciis, neminem ad solvendum hemysiclum cogunt, sed illum à solventibus recipiunt, & ab aliis petunt בנחת placidè. At si quis siclum non solverit usque ad diem 25. Feb. & mensæ iam collocatæ sint in Sanctuario, nemini amplius parcunt, & ab illis quæ nummis carent pignora sumunt, etiam ipsis invitis, imò usque ad vestimenta ipsorum. Sic Maymon. in Schekalim cap.1. (5) De Levitis vid. pag.325. (6) De Proselytis vid. pag.402. & 491. (7) De Servis vid. p. 596. (8) Quot mulieres habeant privilegia; vid. p. 190. (9) Quando pubertas in masculis & fœmellis incipiat, & quis sit קשנה & קשנה vid.pag.493. & pag. 8.9.
units.tr: (1) When מקדש and מנחה are set against each other, מקדש means the Temple at Jerusalem together with the whole city, and מנחה means the other cities in the land of Israel. So Maym. in Taanith ch. 4, at the beginning. (2) In the provinces and at Jerusalem, public tables were set up for collecting the shekel. Commissioners and money-changers sat at them, exchanging money; these are properly called שולחנים (p. 212). (3) For the many names the Temple has, see p. 637. (4) From the time the tables were set up in the provinces, they do not compel anyone to pay the half-shekel but accept it from those who pay and ask others quietly (בנחת). But if anyone has not paid the shekel by the 25th of February, and the tables have now been set up in the Sanctuary, they spare no one any longer. They take pledges from those who lack coins, even against their will, indeed even down to their clothes. So Maimonides in Shekalim ch. 1. (5) On the Levites, see p. 325. (6) On proselytes, see pp. 402 and 491. (7) On slaves, see p. 596. (8) On which women have privileges, see p. 190. (9) On when puberty begins in males and females, and who is a קטן and a קטנה, see pp. 493 and 8, 9.

units.la: 8.9. (10) Sensus est, Minorennem qui semel pro patre pecunias attulit, semper deinde illas singulis annis iterum afferre debere & posse, donec maior natu pro se ipso siclum solvat. Vid. Maym. Schekal. cap.1. (11) פני דרך שלום significat aliquando pacis & concordiae causâ, aliquando honoris & civilitatis causâ, ut hic indecorum enim fuisset tam rigide cum venerandis illis Viris agere; Notat tamen Maymon l. m. c. quamvis pignora à Sacerdotibus non sumserint, ipsos tamen non cessasse ab ipsis petere donec solvissent. (12) De titulo Rabbi vid.pag 498. (13) Quis fuerit Rabbi Ichuda vid.pag.255. (14) Quis Ben Bucri fuerit videre poteris ex Iuchasin. (15) De urbe Iafne vid. p.250. (16) De Rabban Iochanan Ben Saccai vid. p.284. (17) Occurrit obiectioni, quam Sacerdotes pro sua exemptione ex Lev. vi. facere possent; se scil. nihil debere, quia oblatio ipsorum debeat manere integra: cum tamen pecunia siclorum ad varios usus adhibeatur. (18) De עומר vid. p.572. & 485. (19) De panibus propositionis vid.pag. 437. & 572. (21) Omnia tamen cedebant Sacerdotibus, vid. pag.576.
units.tr: 8, 9. (10) The meaning is this: a minor who has once brought money on behalf of his father must and may bring it again every year, until he comes of age and pays the shekel for himself. See Maimonides, Shekalim ch. 1. (11) פני דרך שלום means sometimes for the sake of peace and harmony, and sometimes for the sake of honour and courtesy, as here; for it would have been unseemly to deal so harshly with those venerable men. Maimonides, in the same chapter, notes, however, that although the priests did not take pledges, they did not stop asking them for the money until they had paid. (12) On the title Rabbi, see p. 498. (13) On who Rabbi Ichuda was, see p. 255. (14) On who Ben Bucri was, you may learn from Juchasin. (15) On the city of Jabneh, see p. 250. (16) On Rabban Johanan ben Zakkai, see p. 284. (17) He meets an objection which the priests might raise from Leviticus 6 for their own exemption: namely, that they owe nothing, because their offering ought to remain whole, although the shekel money is applied to various uses. (18) On the עומר, see pp. 572 and 485. (19) On the showbread, see pp. 437 and 572. (21) All these things, however, belonged to the priests; see p. 576.

units.la: V. Etiamsi autem dicant, mulieres ser- vos & parvulos non oppignorari, si tamen [siclum] dare volunt, ab ipsis accipiunt.
units.tr: V. Even if they say that women, slaves and small children are not distrained, yet if they wish to give the [shekel], they receive it from them.

units.la: Si autem (1) Idololatra aliquis aut (2) Cuthaeus [siclum]
units.tr: But if any idolater or (2) Cuthaean wished to pay the [shekel], they would not take it from him.

units.la: וקיני יולדות זחטאות ואשמות אבל נדרי ונדבות מקבלין מידן זה הכלל כל שניד ונירב מקבלין מידן וכל שאין נידר ולא נידב אין מקבלין מידן: ובן הוא מפורש על ידי עזרא שנאמ' לא לכם ולנו לבנות בית לאלוהינו :
units.tr: Votive offerings and freewill offerings they accept from them. The rule is this: whatever is vowed or freely offered they accept from them, but whatever is neither vowed nor freely offered they do not accept from them. This is made clear by Ezra, who says: "It is not for you and for us to build a house to our God."

units.la: pendere vellet, ab illis non reciperent. Neque etiam ab illis recipiunt (3) nidos profluvio laborantium, nec nidos (4) puerperarum, nec sacrificia pro (5) peccatis aut (6 reatu : Accipiunt tamen (7) votiva & voluntaria munera ab ipsis. In summa, à [gentili] qui vovet & sponte offert accipiunt; ab illo vero qui non vovet nec sponte offert non accipiunt. Hoc innuit Esras dicens (cap.4.3.) Non vestrum & nostrum est aedificare domum Dei nostri.
units.tr: Nor do they accept from them the nests of those suffering from a flux, nor the nests of women in childbed, nor sacrifices for sin or for guilt. They do, however, accept votive and voluntary gifts from them. In sum, from a [gentile] who vows and offers of his own accord they accept; from one who neither vows nor offers of his own accord they do not accept. Ezra hints at this when he says (ch. 4.3): It is not yours and ours to build the house of our God.

units.la: ו ואלו שחייבין בקלבון לוים וישראלים וגרים ועבדים משוחררים אבל לא כהנים נשים ועבדים וקטנים השוקל על ידי כהן על ידי אשר על ידי עבד על ידי
units.tr: These are the ones who are obliged to pay the collybus: Levites, Israelites, proselytes and freed slaves. But priests, women, slaves and minors are exempt. If someone weighs out the shekel through a priest, a woman, a slave or a minor, he is exempt.

units.la: VI. Hi autem sunt qui tenentur dare(8) Collybum, Levitæ, Israelitæ, Proselyti, servi manumissi: at Sacerdotes, mulieres, exempti sunt. Si quis per Sacerdotem, mulierem, servum,
units.tr: VI. These are the ones who are bound to give the collybus: Levites, Israelites, proselytes, freed slaves; but priests, women, slaves and minors are exempt. If someone makes the exchange through a priest, a woman, a slave or a minor, he is free of the collybus; but if he makes it himself, or through his partner, he must give one collybus.

units.la: קטן פטור ואם שקל על ידו ועל יד חבירו חייב בקלבון אחד רבי מאיר אומר ב׳ קולבנות הנותן סלע ונוטל שקל חייב שתי קלבנות׃
units.tr: If someone pays through a minor, he is exempt. If he weighs it out through himself and through his partner, he is liable for one collybus. R. Meir says two collybi. He who gives a sela and takes a shekel is liable for two collybi.

units.tr: ...bos. He who brings a shekel in two half-shekels is bound to give [a collybus].

units.la: ז השוקל על ידי עני ועל ידי שכנו ועל יד בן עידו פטור ואם הלוום חייב האחין השותפין שחייבין בקלבון פטורין במעשר בהמה ומחייבין במעשר בהמה פטורין מן הקלבון וכמה הוא קלבון מעה כסף דברי רבי מאיר וחכמים אומרים חצי׃ vum , minorennem permutaverit, (à solutione Collybi) liber est, si verò ipse permutauerit, aut per socium suum, tenetur dare Collybum unum. R. (9) Meir dixerat duos Collybos, & accipit sinre duos collybos.
units.tr: He who weighs out the shekel through a poor man, or through his neighbour, or through his fellow citizen, is exempt. If he lent it to them, he is liable. Brothers who are partners, and who are liable for the collybus, are exempt from the tithe of cattle; and those liable for the tithe of cattle are exempt from the collybus. And how much is the collybus? A maah of silver, according to R. Meir; but the sages say half. ...mutation by a minor, (from the payment of the collybus) he is free; but if he himself made the exchange, or through his partner, he must give one collybus. R. Meir had said two collybi, and [the Mishnah] takes it without two collybi.

units.la: VII. Qui solven- do ficlum [permutat] per (10) pauperem, per vicinum suum, per (11) concivem suum (à Collybo) liber est. Si verò ipsis mu- tuò dedit, tenetur.
units.tr: VII. He who, in paying the shekel, exchanges through a poor man (10), through his neighbour (11), or through his fellow citizen, is free from the collybus. But if he has lent them money, he is liable.

units.la: Fratres illi qui societatem inter se inierunt, si tenentur ad Collybum liberi sunt à solutione, (12) decimarum animalium; & si non liberi sunt à decimis beftiarum, liberi funt à Collybo. Quantus autem eft Collybus ? Secundùm R. Meir, eft (13) obolus argenteus ; fecundùm Sapientes verò eft dimidia pars eius.
units.tr: Those brothers who have entered into partnership with one another: if they are liable for the collybus, they are free from paying the tithe of animals; and if they are not free from the tithe of beasts, they are free from the collybus. How much is the collybus? According to R. Meir it is one silver obol (12); according to the Sages it is half of that (13).

Quandoquidem unufquifque opus habeat hemificlo, ille qui illum folvere cogitat, adit Trapezitam השולחני, & permutat שקל בשני חצאין Unum Siclum in duos dimidios, ויתן לו התוספת על השקל & dat ipfi aliquid fuperabundans fuper ficlum, [i.e. pro labore permutationis, aliquid ficlo exhibito fuperaddit,] ואותה התוספת נקראת קלבון Et illud fuperabundans (vel fuperadditum) vocatur קלבון Collybus. units.tr: (1) The abbreviation is resolved as עובד כוכבים ומזלות [worshipping stars and constellations], a circumlocution by which all Gentiles are denoted without distinction. (2) The Cuthaeans are the Samaritans, on whom see p. 581. (3) On what nests are, see p. 570; on those with a flux, see p. 489. (4) See pp. 570–571. (5) On sin offerings, see p. 558. (6) On trespass offerings, see p. 562. (7) See p. 566, where mention is also made of those sacrifices that were accepted from a Gentile. (8) What the collybus is you will learn from Maimonides in Shekalim, chapter 3, at the beginning. Since each person needs a half-shekel, the one who intends to pay it goes to the money-changer, השולחני [the money-changer], and exchanges one shekel for two halves, שקל בשני חצאין [one shekel into two halves], and gives him something over the shekel, [that is, for the labour of the exchange he adds something to the shekel handed over], ואותה התוספת נקראת קלבון [and that surplus is called collybus]. See also under Siclus, p. 602. (9) On who Rabbi Meir was, see p. 366. (10) On the poor, see p. 457. (11) On how much time is required for someone to become a citizen of a city, see p. 117. (12) On the tithe of cattle, see p. 151. (13) On what מעשר [tithe] is, see p. 379.

Si accidit ut aliqua urbs ficlos suos miserit, & illi furto surripiantur, aut perdantur, si [pecunia] iam (3) oblata fuerit, iurant legati (4) quæstoribus si vero nulla [ adhuc oblatio facta ] iurant concivibus suis: & urbs illa loco horum [ siclorum] alios mittit. Si pecunia illa iterum reperitur, aut hæc & illa summa transit anno sequenti.
units.tr: I. They combine the shekels for the travelling expenses, on account of the burden of the road. Just as there were chests in the Sanctuary, so too there were chests in the provinces. If it happens that a town has sent its shekels and they are stolen or lost, then if the money has already been offered, the envoys swear to the treasurers; but if no offering has yet been made, they swear to their fellow citizens. That town then sends other shekels in place of these. If the money is found again, or this and that sum passes over to the following year.

units.la: (1) Ex difficili distinctione lit. ב. & כ. fit ut quidam legant דרבונות Darbonot, alii דרכמנות vel דרכונות Darcmanot, vel Darconot; quae posterior lectio nobis magis arridet, ut hoc vocabulum suum originem ducat à דרך via, & דרכונות Germanicè sonent Reiß-Gelt; moneta itineraria. Quid autem fuerint vid.pag 379. (2) שופרות quid fuerint, & qualem usum habuerint, vid.pag.226. (3) Id est; si pecunia iam in summam collecta & à civibus illius urbis in hunc finem destinata fuerit, ut mittatur Hierosolymas in thesaurum templi. (4) De quaestoribus templi vid. apud אזרכליך pag 3ꝛ. Notat autem circa hoc legatorum iuramentum Maymon in Schekal. c. 3. illud non admitti, nisi הלסטים Latrones vi siclos ipsis abripuerint, & tunc iuramento quæstores acquiescere ; שהתורם תורם עשר הגבוי וע העתיר : לגבורת וכרשות דקדש הן quia ille qui oblationem disposuit, & summam collegit, computationem facit pro numero nummorum iam solutorum, & qui adhuc solvi debuerunt; illaque iam sanêta æstimabatur, & erat. (5) Prævaricatur idcirco, quia partim defraudat intentionem siclum sibi committentis, partim verò & præcipuè, quia siclus ille iam computationem eius qui oblationem colligit intravit, & ita iam sanctus est. (6)Ita in hunc sensum Maymonides Schekalim c. 3. sub sin. (7) Si hemisiclum ex illis pecuniis decimarum solverit. (8) De decimis secundis vid.pag.129. & 159. debebant illæ Hierosolymis comedi, & forsan aliquis ipsas vendidit, ut siclum solveret. (9) De anno septimo vid.pag.56. & 294. & seq.pag.296. dicitur non licere fructus anni septimi vendere: præsupponit Ergò Misna, aliquem fructus illos vendidisse & siclum ex nummis illis solvisse. (10) Edet loco illorum quæ vendidit alia, si decimæ secundæ fuerint, facere id debuit Hierosolymis; Si fructus anni septimi, præstet id in celebratione anni septimi. Confer Maymon. in 3. cap. Schekalim.
units.tr: (1) Because the letters ב and כ are hard to tell apart, some read דרבונות (Darbonot), others דרכמנות or דרכונות (Darcmanot or Darconot). I prefer the latter reading, since this word derives from דרך [derek, way], and דרכונות would sound in German like Reiß-Gelt, that is, travelling money. On what these coins were, see p. 379. (2) On what the שופרות [shofrot] were and what use they served, see p. 226. (3) That is: if money has already been collected in a sum and set aside for this purpose by the citizens of that town, to be sent to Jerusalem for the temple treasury. (4) On the temple treasurers, see the note on p. 3 in the work of אזרכליך. Maimonides, in Schekalim chapter 3, observes that the oath of the envoys is not admitted unless robbers (הלסטים) have seized six shekels from them, and then the treasurers accept the oath. The Mishnah reads: "because the one who sets aside the offering and gathers the sum makes the reckoning according to the number of coins already paid and those still owed; and that sum is already regarded as holy." (5) He acts wrongly, because he partly defrauds the intention of the one who entrusted him with the shekel, and partly, and chiefly, because that shekel has already entered into the reckoning of the one who collects the offering and so is already holy. (6) Maimonides, in Schekalim chapter 3 near the end, is to this effect. (7) If he pays a half-shekel from those coins of tithe money. (8) On the second tithes see pp. 129 and 159: those were to be eaten in Jerusalem, and perhaps someone sold them in order to pay the shekel. (9) On the seventh year see pp. 56, 294 and following, and p. 296: it is said that it is not lawful to sell the produce of the seventh year. The Mishnah therefore presupposes that someone sold that produce and paid the shekel from the proceeds. (10) He shall make good, in place of what he sold, something else; if they were second tithes he ought to have done this in Jerusalem; if the produce of the seventh year, he must make restitution in the observance of the seventh year. Compare Maimonides on chapter 3 of Schekalim.

units.la: אומרים מותרן נדבה pro ficlo meo : (2) Schámæani dicunt, ובית הלל אומרים illos quos nondum מותרן חולין שאביא immisit [posse] ad כהן לשקלי שוין spontaneam oblatioשהמותר חולין אלו nem [adhiberi.] (3) לחטאת שהמותר Hilleliani verò diנדברה שאביא מהן cunt, illos quos non- חטאת שוין שמותרן dum immisit, profaחולין: nos esse. Confentiunt verò utrinque, quod si ex [nummis] aliquos immitterem ad ficlum meum pendendum, residuum ipsorum (4) profanum esse. Item (si dicerem) illud (quod residuum est) sit pro peccato meo, etiam confentiunt, residuum ad spontaneam oblationem [adhiberi posse.] Confentiunt etiam, si aliquid immitterem pro peccato, residuum profanum esse.
units.tr: The school of Shammai says: they are a free-will offering (nedavah) for my shekel; the school of Hillel says: they are profane (ḥullin) for my shekel, and the coins I put in are fit for the shekel and are equal. The Shammaites say that the excess of the ordinary coins which I shall put in [may be applied] to the free-will offering; the Hillelites say that the excess which I shall put in is profane. Both agree that if I put some of the coins in to pay my shekel, the residue of those coins is profane. Likewise, if I said that the residue is for my sin-offering, they also agree that the residue may be applied to a free-will offering. They agree too that if I put something in as a sin-offering, the residue is profane.

units.la: IV. Dixit Rabbi
units.tr: IV. Rabbi said

units.la: ד אמר רבי שמעון IV. Dixit Rabbi (5) Simeon, Quænam מה בין שקלים לחטאת eft differentia inter שלשקלים יש להן [nummos] qui ad fi- קיצבה ולחטאת אין clum pendendum לה קיצבה רבי [immittuntur,] & in- ter nummos qui pro pecca-
units.tr: Rabbi Simeon said: What is the difference between the coins that are put in for the shekel, which have a fixed amount, and the coins for the sin-offering, which have no fixed amount? Rabbi Judah replied: Indeed, there is no fixed determination for shekels either. For when the Israelites came up from captivity, they paid darconot, and then again [selaim]; afterwards they paid half a shekel, indeed they paid only denarii.

Nam cùm Israelitæ ex captivitate ascendebant , solvebant Darconor, & deinde iterum (6) Selaim: postea solvebant dimidium siclum, imò (7) denarios solvere volummodò. Respondit R. Simeon, Etiamsi res ita se habet, tamen semper idem omnes [pro sisicli erunt;] At pro peccato unus solvit dimidium, alter duos, tertius tres.
units.tr: Rabbi Simeon replied: Even if the matter stands so, yet all should always be the same, [a fixed sum]. For the shekel is a certain fixed sum, but for the sin-money no fixed sum has been set; Rabbi Judah replied: indeed there is no fixed determination for shekels. For when the Israelites came up from captivity, they paid darconot, then selaim; afterwards they paid half a shekel, or indeed merely denarii. Rabbi Simeon replied: even if the matter stands so, yet for all it will always be the same sum; but for the sin-offering, one pays a half, another two, a third three.

units.tr: The nests of those with a flux, of women in childbirth, and their sin-offerings and the remainders of these, as well as the (offerings) for sin and guilt, can be applied to a free-will offering. In sum, the residues of all things offered under the name of sin or guilt become free-will offerings. The residue of money consecrated for a burnt offering must be spent on a burnt offering. The residue of a meal offering goes to a meal offering; the residue of peace offerings to peace offerings; the residue of the Passover to a peace offering. The residue of Nazirites goes to Nazirites; the residue of a Nazirite's offering is to be spent on a free-will offering. The residue of the poor goes to the poor; the residue of a poor man goes to that same poor man. The residue of captives is spent on captives; the residue of a captive goes to that same captive. The residue of the dead goes to the dead; the residue of a dead man comes to his heirs. Rabbi Meir says: the residue of the dead is to be left until Elijah comes. Rabbi Nathan says: from the residue of the dead they build a monument over his sepulchre.

units.tr: In three seasons of the year they set apart the chamber: before Passover, before Pentecost, and before the Feast of Tabernacles; and these are also the times for tithing cattle. So say Rabbi Akiba. Ben Azzai says: on the twenty-ninth of Adar, the first of Sivan, and the twenty-ninth of Av. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Simeon say: on the first of Nisan, the first of Sivan, and the twenty-ninth of Elul. They did not name the first of Tishri because it is a festival day, and one may not tithe on a festival; therefore they moved it to the twenty-ninth of Elul.

units.la: I. {T}Er in anno curant de (1) conclavi, in spatio semestri ante Pascha, in spatio semestri ante (2) pentecosten, & in spatio semestri ante (3) scenopegiam. In quibus temporibus etiam decimæ bestiarum colliguntur. Verba sunt (4) R. Akibæ. Ben Asai verò dicit id fieri, vicesimo nono Februarii, & die primo Maij, ut & vicesimo nono Iulij. R. (5) Eliezer & R. Simeon dicunt, primo die Martij, & primo Maij, & vicesimo nono Augusti. Quare autem dicunt die vicesimo nono Augusti, gusti, ] & non primo die Septembris. Quia ille dies primus Septembris est dies festus; at in die festo decimare non licet, & proinde id rejecerunt in diem 29. Augusti.
units.tr: I. In the year they take care of the chamber: in the half-year before Passover, in the half-year before Pentecost, and in the half-year before the Feast of Tabernacles. At these times the tithes of cattle are also gathered. These are the words of Rabbi Akiba. Ben Azzai, however, says it is done on the twenty-ninth of February and the first of May, and also on the twenty-ninth of July. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Simeon say on the first of March, the first of May, and the twenty-ninth of August. Why do they say the twenty-ninth of August and not the first of September? Because that first day of September is a festival day, and on a festival day it is not lawful to tithe; therefore they put it off to the twenty-ninth of August.

The one who sets apart the chamber does not enter with a folded garment, nor with shoes, nor with sandals, nor with phylacteries, nor with amulets; lest perhaps he become poor and they say, because of the iniquity he committed in the chamber he has become poor; or lest perhaps he become rich and they say, he has grown rich from the tithe of the chamber, because a man

units.tr: II. They emptied the chamber into three chests, each of which held three seahs. On these was written א Aleph, ב Beth, ג Gimel. Rabbi Ishmael says the inscription was Greek: Alpha, Beta, Gamla. The one who is to empty the chamber in this way does not go in with a folded garment, nor with shoes, nor with sandals, nor with phylacteries, nor with amulets; lest, if he should become poor, they say that it was because of the wrong he committed

units.tr: The Gimel box of the house of Rabban Gamaliel used to enter, and he would take the coin between his fingers and throw it before the one setting apart; and the one setting apart intends it and pushes it into the box. The one setting apart does not set apart until they say to him, "Set apart," and they say to him "Set apart, set apart, set apart," three times.

units.la: misit in conclavi, pauperascit. Aut si ditesceret, dicerent, ex pecunia conclavis dives factus est. Nam homini necessarium est æquè coram hominibus peccati suspicione carere, ac coram Deo debet innocens esse, sicuti dicitur Numer.32.22. Et sitis puri coram Iehova & Israele. Et Proverb. 3.4. Et inveni gratiam & intellectum boni coram Deo & hominibus.
units.tr: he committed in the chamber, and he has become poor; or if he has grown rich, they say that he has grown rich from the money of the chamber. For a man must be as blameless before men as he ought to be innocent before God, as it is said in Numbers 32:22: "And you shall be clear before the LORD and before Israel"; and in Proverbs 3:4: "And you shall find grace and good understanding in the sight of God and of men."

units.la: III. (Traditio) Familiæ Rabban (9) Gamalielis ; (Ille qui conclave evacuaturus erat) ingrediebatur, & ficlos eius manibus imponebant, & coram illo spargebant ; ille verò ad id attendebat, & pecunias arculae immittebat. Insuper ille qui evacuabat non evacuabat, ufquedum ad (10) ipfos dixiffet, eva-cuabo, & illi refpondiffent (11) ter, evacua, evacua, evacua.
units.tr: III. (Tradition) of the household of Rabban Gamaliel: (He who was about to empty the chamber) would enter, and they would place the shekels in his hands and scatter them before him; he would attend to this and put the money into the chest. Moreover, the one who was emptying did not empty until he had said to them, "I will empty," and they had answered him three times, "Empty, empty, empty."

units.la: ד תרם את הראשונה ומחפה בקטבלאוי שנייה ומחפה בקטבלאו שלישית לא הירה מחפה שמא ישכח ויתרום מן הדבר התרום תרם את הראשונה לשם ארץ והשנייה לשם כרכים המוקפין לה והשלישי לשם בבל ולשם מדי מרינורת ולשם הרחוקים:
units.tr: He sets apart the first and covers it with a cloth; the second, and covers it with a cloth; the third he does not cover, lest he forget and wish to set apart again what has already been set apart. He set apart the first in the name of the land of Israel; the second in the name of the walled cities around it; and the third in the name of Babylon, and of Media, and of the distant provinces.

units.la: IV. (12) Replet ciftam א, & illam cooperit linteo suo. Ciftam deinde ב, & illam quoque tegit operculo suo. Ciftam ג vero non cooperit, ne oblivifcatur, & velit implere quod iam impletum est. Replet ciftam א in nomine (13) terræ Ifrael; ciftam ב in nomine civitatum [terræ Israel] adiacentium. Ciftam ג in nomine (14) Babel, Mediæ, & provinciarum difsitarum.
units.tr: IV. He fills the first chest, א, and covers it with his linen cloth. Then he fills the second chest, ב, and covers it with its lid too. But the third chest, ג, he does not cover, lest he forget and wish to fill what has already been filled. He fills the first chest in the name of the land of Israel; the second in the name of the cities of Israel that lie around it; the third in the name of Babylon, Media, and the distant provinces.

units.tr: (1) We have already said that the shekels collected in the provinces are sent by envoys to the treasury of the Temple. That treasure is deposited "in one chamber from among the chambers in the sanctuary" [בלשכה אתה מן הלשכות בכקדש], which is called the chamber [לשכת]. See p. 227. Of this chamber, [Maimonides says in Shekalim,] "they locked all its doors with keys and sealed them with seals" [סגרו כה וחותמין דלתותיהם, עליה חותמות]. (2) On Pentecost see p. 203. (3) On the Feast of Tabernacles see p. 196. (4) On Rabbi Akiba see pp. 22–23. (5) On R. Eliezer see p. 169. (6) On shoes and sandals see p. 587. (7) See Tephillin, p. 656. (8) On amulets see p. 33. (9) On Rabban Gamaliel see p. 224. (10) For "the guards" [השומרין], Maimonides explains: "those who stood outside the chamber" [עומדי כחוץ]. (11) They also used this threefold repetition in other ceremonies, as in the reaping of the sheaf of firstfruits; see p. 485. (12) For the understanding of this verse, see the words of the Gloss quoted on p. 228. (13) On the land of Israel, see p. 267. (14) On Babylonia, see p. 62.

units.tr: Mishnah 4:2. The red cow, the scapegoat, and the crimson thread come from the contribution of the chamber. The lamb for the cow, the lamb for the scapegoat, the crimson thread between its horns, the water channels, the city wall and towers, and in short all the city's needs come from the surplus of the chamber [ב פרה ושעיר המשתלה ולשון של זהורית באין מתרומת הלשכה כבש פרה וכבש שעיר המשתלה ולשון שבין קרניו ואמת המים וחומרת העיר ומגדלותיה וכל צרכי העיר באין משירי הלשכה]. The guardians of the Church and of the plants in the seventh year have their wages from this chamber money. R. Ioshua says: if anyone offered himself voluntarily, he could be a guardian for nothing. They replied: unless it is at the Church's expense.

units.tr: II. The red cow and the he-goat for release, and the crimson thread, are bought with this chamber money. The steps of the red cow, the he-goat for release, and the thread between its horns, the water channels, and the wall and towers of the city, all that the city needs in short, come from the remaining chamber money.

(7) De lingua coccinea vid. pag. 185. quid illa fuerit docet Glossa; לשון של זהוריה צמר צבוע כשני תולעת; Lefchon Sehorit est lana murice coccineoque colore tincta. (8) vid. Kedron pag. 314. (9) Tum canales quibus aqua in templum devehebatur, tum ille qui in ipsa urbe. (10) Postquàm ille qui conclave ingressus tres cistas plenas implevit, sicli qui in cistis vocantur תרומת Truma conclavis. וה שישאר שם יותר על מה שיש בקופות הוא הנקרא שירי הלשכה; Illi verò qui praterea adhuc in conclavi sunt excepti illis qui sunt in cistis, vocantur residuum conclavis. Maymon Schekal. cap. 2.
units.tr: (1) On the continual sacrifice, see p. 556. (2) On what the aftergrowth [ספיחין] is, see p. 295. (3) In the jubilee year, or the seventh year, all the fruits were common, hefker [הפקר]; yet the omer and the two loaves had to be offered from the new crops. Therefore the Sanhedrin appointed some guards, who received their wages from the chamber, to keep a certain portion of the crops, from which the omer and the two loaves could then be offered. So Maimonides, Shekalim ch. 4. (4) The word מתנדב may have another sense, and is often understood as a spontaneous offering, but we have followed Maimonides. (5) On the red cow, see p. (6) On the he-goat for release, see p. 185 f. (7) On the crimson thread, see p. 185. What it was the Gloss explains: "the thread of crimson is wool dyed with the murex and the scarlet colour" [לשון של זהוריה צמר צבוע כשני תולעת; Lefchon Sehorit est lana murice coccineoque colore tincta]. (8) See Kedron p. 314. (9) Both the channels by which water was conveyed into the Temple, and the one within the city itself. (10) After the one who entered the chamber had filled three full chests, the shekels which are called in the chests the contribution of the chamber [תרומת הלשכה]; those which remain there beyond what is in the chests are called the remainder of the chamber. Maimonides, Shekalim ch. 2.

units.la: III. Quid
units.tr: III. What

units.la: ג מותר שירי הלשכה מה היו עושין בהן לוקחין בהן יינורת[?] שמנים וסלתות והשכר להקדש דברי רבי ישמעאל ר' עקיבא אומר אין משתברין משל הקדש ולא משל ענגיים :
units.tr: 3. What did they do with the surplus of the chamber? They bought with it wine, oil and flour, and the remainder went to the sacred treasury. So says R. Ishmael. R. Akiba says: it is not to be spent from what belongs to the sanctuary, nor from what belongs to the ענגיים [angiyim].

units.la: ד מותר תרומה מרה היו עושין בה ריקועי זהב ציפוי לבתי קרשי הקדשים רבי ישמעאל אומר מותר הפירורין לקיץ המזבח ומותר התרומה לכלי שרת רבי עקיבא אומר מותר התרומה לקיץ המזבח ומותר נסכים לכלי
units.tr: The surplus of the myrrh contribution they used to make into beaten gold plating for the boards of the Holy of Holies. Rabbi Ishmael says: the surplus of the crumbs goes to the plaster [קיץ] of the altar, and the surplus of the contribution goes to the sacred vessels. Rabbi Akiba says: the surplus of the contribution goes to the plaster of the altar, and the surplus of the libations goes to the vessels.

units.la: III. Quid cum illis nummis faciunt, quæ ex (1) Residuis pecuniis conclavis superstunt. Emunt ex illis (2) vina, (3) olea, (4)similas, & lucrum cedit sancto. Verba sunt R. Ismael. R. Akiba dicit ; non lucrantur cum re sancta, neque cum re pauperum. IV. Quid autem faciunt, cum residua ciftarum pecunia ? Illa conficiunt laminas aureas (5) ad sanctum Sanctorum obducendum. R. Ismael dicit reliquum fructuum impenditur ad (6) æstivandum altare. Residuum vero pecuniæ ciftarum ad (7) vasa cultus comparanda. R. Akiba dicit, Red שרת רבי חנניה סגן הכהנים אומר מותר נסכים לקיץ המזבח ומותר התרומה לכלי שרת זה וזה לא היו מודים בפירות:
units.tr: III. What do they do with those coins, which remain over from the residue of the money of the chamber? They buy from them wines, oils, fine flours, and the profit goes to the sanctuary. These are the words of R. Ishmael. R. Akiba says: they do not profit from the holy thing, nor from the thing of the poor. IV. What, then, do they do when the residue of the chests' money remains? They make golden plates to cover the Holy of Holies. R. Ishmael says the residue of the fruits is spent on the summer altar, and the residue of the contribution on the vessels of service. R. Akiba says: the residue of the contribution to the summer altar, and the residue of the libations to the vessels. R. Chananiah, deputy of the priests, says: the residue of the libations to the summer altar, and the residue of the contribution to the vessels of service. Neither of these agreed about the fruits. [שרת רבי חנניה סגן הכהנים אומר מותר נסכים לקיץ המזבח ומותר התרומה לכלי שרת זה וזה לא היו מודים בפירות]

units.la: fiduum pecuniæ starum ad æstivan-dum altare, & resi-duum libaminum ad vafa cultus. R. Chanina Sacerdotum (†) vicarius dicit; residua libaminum ad æstivandum altare, & residuum cistarum pecuniæ ad vafa cultus. Hic autem & ille respectu fructuum non confentiunt. ה מותר הקטורת מה היו עושין בה מפרישין ממנה שבר האומנים ומחללין אותה על שבר האומני (נ"א מעורת) ונותנין אותה לאומני בשכרן וחוזרין ולוקחין אותה מתרומה חדשה ואם בא חדש בזמנן לוקחין אותה
units.tr: ...the surplus of the chests for the summer repair of the altar, and the surplus of the drink offerings for the vessels of service. R. Chanina, deputy of the priests, says: the surplus of the drink offerings for the summer repair of the altar, and the surplus of the chest money for the vessels of service. Here and there they do not agree about the fruits. Mishnah 4:5. What do they do with the surplus of the incense? They set aside from it the wages of the craftsmen, and they make it profane for the craftsmen's wages, and give it to the craftsmen as their pay; and then they take it again from the new contribution. And if the new shekels arrive in their season, they take it from the new, not from the old [ה מותר הקטורת מה היו עושין בה מפרישין ממנה שבר האומנים ומחללין אותה על שבר האומנים (נ"א מעורת) ונותנין אותה לאומנים בשכרן וחוזרין ולוקחין אותה מתרומה חדשה ואם בא חדש בזמנן לוקחין אותה מתרומה חדשה ולא מן הישנה].

units.la: V. Quid fit cum refiduo (8) suffitus? Separant ab ipso mercedem (9) operariorum. Aut illud refiduum plane profanum faciunt propter mercedem operariorum & dant illud Operariis in mercedem ipsorum. Et deinde ex (10) novis siclis novum suffitum parant. מתרומה חדשה ואם rant. Et si noui fi-לא מן הישנה cli nondum exhibiti fuerint, & non numerati tempore consueto, sumptum [pro sufsitu] ex siclis veteribus [anni precedentis] faciunt.
units.tr: V. What is done with the surplus of the incense? They set aside from it the craftsmen's wages. Either they make that surplus wholly profane because of the craftsmen's wages and give it to the workmen as their pay. And then they make new incense from new shekels. And if the new shekels have not yet been brought in, and not counted at the usual time, they make the incense from the old shekels of the preceding year.

units.la: (1) Quæstio non est de quibusvis residuis num-mis, sed de illis quæ שירי הלשכה vocantur, & de qui-bus in notis præced. (2) De vino vid. f. loc. Vino utebantur in cultu quotidiano ad libamen faciendum. Vid. pag. 143. & 577. (3) De oleo vid. pag. 427. de eius usu in cultu templi vid. pag 574. & 575. (4) Vid. de סולת pag. 573. quænam fuerit optima simila vid. 270. (5) De Sancto Sanctorum vid. pag. (6) Glossa. לקיץ המובח פירות למוכר כשאין נדרים ונדבות והסובח כטל מביאין עולות כמו שרוך בני אדם להביא פירות אחר הסעודה Ad æstivandum altare; id est, ad comparandos fructus altari; si enim nemo ex voto aliquid attulerit, & ita alta e quieseret, comparant ex illa pecunia holocausta; sicuti mos est filiis hominum fructus & bellaria adferre convivio peracto. Hoc sensu holocausta vocantur fructus. (7) Quot illa vasa sint & unde petantur vid. pag. 138. (†) Vid. de Sagan. pag. 547. & 548. (8) De suffitu vid. pag. 140. (9) Operarii illi intelliguntur qui semper vacabant לברק הבית reparationi templi. (10) Ex siclis illo anno Hierosolymam allatis & in thesaurum repositis.
units.tr: (1) The question concerns not just any leftover coins, but those called שירי הלשכה [shire ha-lishkah], about which see the preceding notes. (2) On wine, see f. loc. Wine was used in the daily worship for the drink offering. See pp. 143 and 577. (3) On oil, see p. 427; on its use in the temple worship, see pp. 574 and 575. (4) On סולת [solet, fine flour], see p. 573; on what the best fine flour was, see p. 270. (5) On the Holy of Holies, see p. (6) Gloss: לקיץ המובח פירות למוכר כשאין נדרים ונדבות והסובח כטל מביאין עולות כמו שרוך בני אדם להביא פירות אחר הסעודה To provide for the altar, that is, to buy fruits for the altar. For if no one brought anything by vow or freewill offering, and the altar thus lay idle, they bought burnt offerings with that money, just as it is the custom of men to bring fruits and dainties to a feast once the meal is over. In this sense the burnt offerings are called fruits. (7) On how many those vessels are and whence they are taken, see p. 138. (†) On the Sagan, see pp. 547 and 548. (8) On the incense offering, see p. 140. (9) Those workmen are understood to be the ones who were always employed לברק הבית [le-barek ha-bayit] for the repair of the temple. (10) From the shekels brought to Jerusalem in that year and deposited in the treasury.

units.la: ראוין לקרבנות הצבור ינתנו לאומנין בשכרן דברי ר' עקיבא אמר לו בן עזאי אינה היא המדה אלא מפרישין מהן שכר האומנין ומחללין אותן על מעורת האומנין ונותנין אותן לאומנין בשכרן וחוזרין ולוקחין אותן מתרומה חדשה : & loco horum nummorum alios sumunt ex recentiori truma.
units.tr: The animals fit for the public sacrifices are given to the craftsmen as their wages. These are the words of R. Akiba. Ben Azzai said to him: this is not the rule. Rather, they set aside from them the craftsmen's wages, and the consecrated things are made profane over the craftsmen's wages and given to the craftsmen as their pay, and then they take those same things back from new heave-offering. [Instead of these coins they take others from the newer heave-offering.]

units.la: ז המקדיש נכסיו והיתה בהם המה ראייה לגבי המזבח זכרים ונקבות ר' אליעזר אומר זכרים ימכרו לצורכי עולות ונקיבות ימכרו לצרכי
units.tr: (Hebrew) If a man consecrates his property, and in it there are animals fit for the altar, male and female, R. Eliezer says: the males shall be sold for burnt offerings, and the females shall be sold for peace offerings.

units.la: ctificat , & in illis quædam digna sunt ad oblationes Ecclesiæ, dantur illa operariis in mercedem ipsorum. Verba sunt R. Akibæ. Dixit ipsi Ben Asai, non sic proceditur : sed ex illis separant pro mercede operariorum, & profana redduntur separata, ut cedant in pecunias operariis,illaque deinde dant operariis in mercedem ipsorum;
units.tr: ...are consecrated, and among them some are fit for the offerings of the Church: these are given to the workmen as their wages. These are the words of R. Akiba. Ben Azzai said to him: this is not how the procedure goes. Rather, they set aside from them the workmen's wages, and the things so set aside are made profane so that their value may go to the workmen in money, and then they give those same things to the workmen as their wages.

units.la: VII. Si in alicuius facultatibus sanctificatis, sunt aliqua iumenta, quæ ad altare apta sunt, tum masculini, tum fœminini generis, secundùm R. Eliesèrem masculi vendi debent;
units.tr: VII. If among the sanctified possessions of anyone there are some beasts of burden that are fit for the altar, both male and female, then according to R. Eliezer the males ought to be sold.

units.la: Elicfer æquat guit. R. Papia debent; illis qui holocaustis (2) opus habent: fœmellæ verò in ufum facrificiorum pacificorum, & pecunia ex illis acquisita, cum reliquis facultatibus impenditur ad templi (3) ufum. Secundùm R. Iehofuam autem, debent mascult offerri in holocaustum, & fœmellæ debent divendi illis, qui facrificiis pacificis opus habent. Ex pretio autem ipsarum debent holocausta fieri, reliquæ facultates verò, adhiberi possunt ad templi usum. R.Akiba inquit, magis placent ea quæ R. Eliefer dixit, quam quæ R. Iehonegotium, R.Iehofua s inquit, audivi [dari casus] secundum sententiam utriusque, scilicet, quod illius facultates quae restricte sanctificatae sunt, impendi possint ex sententia R. Eliezeris; illius vero qui absolute eas sanctificavit, ex sententia R. Iehosuae.
units.tr: R. Eliezer holds the same view as the others. R. Papia says: the males are to be offered for burnt offerings, and the females are for the use of the peace offerings, and the money obtained from them is spent together with the rest of the property on the use of the Temple. But according to R. Jehoshua, the males ought to be offered as burnt offerings, and the females ought to be sold to those who need peace offerings. From the price of the females the burnt offerings are to be made, and the rest of the property may be applied to the use of the Temple. R. Akiba says: those things which R. Eliezer said please me more than those which R. Jehoshua said. I heard the case [it was given] according to the opinion of each: namely, that the property of the one who consecrated it in a restricted way may be spent according to the opinion of R. Eliezer, but the property of the one who consecrated it absolutely may be spent according to the opinion of R. Jehoshua.

units.la: ח המקדיש נכסיו והיו בהן דברים ראויין על גבי המזבח ינות שמנים ועופות רבי אליעזר אומר ימכרו לצרכי אותו המץ ויביא בדמיהם עילות ושאר נכסים יפלו לבדק הבית:
units.tr: (Hebrew) If a man consecrates his property, and in it there are things fit for the altar, such as oils and birds, R. Eliezer says: they shall be sold for the needs of the altar, and with their price he shall bring burnt offerings, and the rest of the property shall fall to the repair of the house.

units.la: VIII. Si aliquis facultates suas sanctificaverit, & in illis sint res aptæ ad altare, ut vina olea, aves, secundum R. Eliefezerem illa divendi debent, illis qui talibus [ad offerendum] opus habent, pretium deinde ipsorum ad holocausta impenditur; reliquæ vero facultates ad templi necessitates applicantur.
units.tr: VIII. If anyone consecrates his property, and in it there are things fit for the altar, such as wines, oils, and birds: according to R. Eliezer, these are to be sold to those who have need of such things for offering, and their price is then spent on burnt offerings; but the rest of the property is applied to the needs of the Temple.

units.la: ט אוהד לשלשים יום משערין את הלשכה כל המקבל עליו לספק סלתות מארבע עמדו משלשה יספק מארבע משלש
units.tr: (Hebrew) Every thirty days they assess the chamber's prices. Whoever undertakes to supply fine flour, from four measures he supplies, from three... he supplies four, from three...

units.la: IX. Semel in mense (4) pretia conclavis determinant: Si aliquis in se recepit respectu Similæ prospicere, mensura quadruplici; Et accidit ut [pro eodem בeodem pretio] ad triplicem veniat, tamen qnadruplicem mensuram dare tenetur. Si verò tres mensuras promiserit, & deinde [pretium] ad quatuor mensuras ascendebat, quatuor etiam mensuras exhibere tenetur. Quia manus rei sanctæ (5) superior est. Si similia vermibus corrumpetur, corrumpitur ipsi, si vinum acesceret, acescit ipsi. Neque pecuniæ ipsi traduntur, donec altare (6) ornaverit.
units.tr: IX. Once a month they fix the prices of the chamber. If anyone undertakes to provide fine flour, he must give a fourfold measure; and if it happens that at the same price the price rises to a triple measure, he is still bound to give the fourfold measure. If he promised three measures, and afterwards the price rose to four measures, he is also bound to supply four measures, because the hand [of the holy thing] is higher. If it is corrupted by worms, it is corrupted for him; if the wine turns sour, it turns sour for him. Nor is the money handed over to him until he has adorned the altar.

units.la: NOTÆ.
units.tr: NOTES.

units.la: (1) Sanctificat, i. e. testamento suo sacris usibus legat. (2) Qui ad quæstores templi accedunt, & sacrificaturi animal, quali ad rite sacrificandum opus habent, de illis emere volunt. Vid. cap. seq. v. 3. 4. (3) proprie ad reparationem templi. (4) i. e. semel in mense [vel ut textus] intrà triginta dies determinant, statuunt, quid & quantum numerari debeat illis, qui oleum, vinum, similam, & alia in usum templi necessaria, suppeditabant. (5) i. e. ærarium templi damnum non patitur, obtinet immutabiliter qualecunque pactum sit, quicquid promiserint, & quæstores stipulati sunt. (6) Donec iam ad altare attulerit necessaria, & re ipsa quod promisit præstiterit.
units.tr: (1) He sanctifies, that is, bequeaths it by his will to sacred uses. (2) Those who come to the treasurers of the temple, and who are about to sacrifice an animal, wish to buy from them the things they need for offering the sacrifice properly. See the following chapter, verses 3 and 4. (3) Properly, for the repair of the temple. (4) That is, once a month [or as the text has it], within thirty days, they determine and fix what and how much must be paid to those who supplied oil, wine, fine flour, and other things needed for the use of the temple. (5) That is, the treasury of the temple suffers no loss: whatever agreement was made, it holds unchanged, whatever they promised and the treasurers stipulated. (6) That is, until he has already brought the necessary things to the altar and actually done what he promised.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: המונין שהיו במקדש יוחנן בן פינחס על ההותמורת אחידה על הנסכים מתיא בן שמואל על הפייסות פתחיא על הקינין פתחיא זה מרדכי למה נקרא שמו פתחיא שהיה פותח ברבריים והורשן וידע שבעים לשון בן אחיה על חולי מעיים נחוניא חופר שיחין גביני כרוז בן גבר על נעילת שערים בן בבי על הפקיע בן ארזה על הצלצל
units.tr: The overseers who were in the Temple: Johanan ben Pinchas over the seals; Achiah over the libations; Mattiah ben Shmuel over the lots; Petachiah over the birds' nests. This Petachiah is Mordecai. Why was he called Petachiah? Because he opened (poteach) matters and explained them, and he knew seventy languages. Ben Achiah over those with bowel diseases; Nechuniah the digger of ditches; Gabini the herald; Ben Gever over the closing of the gates; Ben Bevai over the flogging; Ben Arza over the cymbal; Hogros ben Levi over the singing; the house of Garmu over the baking of the showbread; the house of Abtinas over the making of the incense; Eleazar over the veil; and Pinchas over the vestments.

units.la: {1}I (1) præfe- H I fuerunt in Sanctuario. Iohannes fil. Pinchas figillorum fuit [custos.] Achias, (2) libamininum. Mathias fil. Samuelis, fortium. Petachias turturum. Petachias ille est Mardochai, quare autem vocatur Petachias: Quia ille res aperiebat, & ipsas explicabat, 70. deinde (3) linguarum callens erat. Ben Achia [præfectus] fuit super (4) ægrotos. units.tr: {1}I (1) They were overseers in the Sanctuary. John son of Pinchas was keeper of the seals. Achias, of the libations. Mathias son of Samuel, of the lots. Petachias, of the turtledoves. This Petachias is Mordecai; why is he called Petachias? Because he opened those matters and explained them, and he was skilled in seventy languages. Ben Achia was [in charge] of the sick. Nechonias had charge of the fountains and canals. Gebhina was the herald. Ben Gebher was appointed to the (7) gates to be closed.

units.la: (1) præfecti fuerunt in Sanctuario.
units.tr: (1) They were overseers in the Sanctuary.

units.tr: Hagros ben Levi over the song; the house of Garmo over the making of the showbread; the house of Abtinas over the making of the incense; Eleazar over the veil; and Pinchas over the vestments.

units.tr: II. They appoint no fewer than three treasurers and no fewer than three chamberlains. They do not commit the oversight of the Church's money to fewer than two, except Ben Achiah, who looks after the sick, and Eleazar, who presides over the veils, whom the Church appointed.

The poor man's sin-offering and the rich man's: the calf goes with the libations of oxen, large and small, male and female, except those of rams; the male goes with the libations of rams only; the sin-offering goes with the libations of the three animals of lepers.

units.tr: IV. Whoever wishes to obtain libations goes to Johanan, the prefect of the seals, and pays him the money that is required, and receives from him a seal.

units.la: חותם בא לו אצל אחיה שהוא ממונה על הנכסים ונותן לו חותם ומקבל ממנו נכסים ולערב באין זה אצל זה ואחיה מוציא את החותמות ומקבל כנגדן מעות ואם הותירו הותירו להקדש ואם פחתו היה משלם יוחנן מניתו שיד הקדש על העליונה:
units.tr: He then goes to Achiah, who is in charge of the libations; he gives him the seal and receives libations from him. In the evening they settle accounts with each other: Achiah takes back the seals and receives money in exchange for them. If there is a surplus, it goes to the sacred funds; if there is a shortfall, Johanan makes it good from his own treasury, since the hand of the sanctuary is uppermost.

units.la: ה מי שאבד ממנו הותמו ממתיגין לו עד הערב אם מצאו לו כדי חותמו נותנין לו ואם לאו לא היו נותנין לו ושם merat, sumit deinde ab ipso sigillum, & illud fert ad Achiam præfectum libaminum, porrigit ipsi sigillum, & ab ipso libamina sumit. sub vesperam conveniunt hi [duo prefecti.] Achias profert sua sigilla, & loco ipsorum pecuniam sumit. Si aliquid in illis redundat, confertur id ad Sancta, Si vero deficit id restituit Iohannes ex domo sua, quia manus Sancti superior est.
units.tr: 5. If someone has lost his seal, they wait for him until evening; if they find enough to match his seal, they give it to him; if not, they do not give it to him. And there [he] takes the seal from him, and carries it to Achiah, the overseer of the libations, hands him the seal, and receives libations from him. Toward evening [the two overseers] meet. Achiah produces his seals and takes money in their place. If there is any surplus in them, it is added to the sacred funds; if there is a deficit, Johanan restores it from his own house, since the hand of the sanctuary is uppermost.

units.la: V. Si aliquis sigillum suum perdit, exspectant usque ad vesperam, si aliquid reperiunt, quod est ut sigilum eius, dant ipsi [quod opus habet.]
units.tr: V. If anyone loses his seal, they wait until evening; if they find something that is like his seal, they give him what he needs.

units.tr: There were two chambers in the Temple: one the chamber of the secret (gifts), and one the chamber of vessels. Into the chamber of the secret the God-fearing put gifts in secret, and the poor of good family were supported from it in secret. Into the chamber of vessels whoever volunteered a vessel threw it in; after thirty days the treasurers opened it, and any vessel found in it that needed repair they set aside, and the rest... If nothing was found, they gave nothing either. The name is written, because of... [ו שתי לשכות היו במקדש אחת לשכת חשאים ואחת לשכת הכלים לשכת חשאים ירא חטא נותנים לתוכה בחשאי ועניים בני טובים מתפרנסין מתוכה בחשאי לשכת הכלים כל מי שהוא מתנדב כלי זורקו לתוכה ואחר לשלשים יום גזברין פותחין אותה וכל כלי שמצאו בו צריך לברק הבירת מניחין איתו והשאר]

units.la: VI. Duo (1) Con- clavia erant in tem- plo, unum vocaba- tur conclave (2) oc- cultorum, alterum vero (3) conclave vasium.
units.tr: VI. There were two chambers in the Temple. One was called the chamber (1) of the secret ones, and the other (2) the chamber of vessels.

units.la: Conclave occultorum erat, in quod homines pii occultè aliquid projiciebant, ex quo deinde pauperes filii bonorum occultè alebantur. Conclave vasium verò est, in quod aliquis projicit, quod ex vasibus sponte offerre vult. Semel autem in 30. diebus, Thesaurarii illud aperiunt, & omnia vasa
units.tr: The chamber of the secret ones was the one into which pious men secretly put something, from which the poor sons of good families were then secretly supported. The chamber of vessels is the one into which anyone casts whatever he wishes to offer voluntarily from among the vessels. Once every 30 days the treasurers open it, and they keep all the vessels they judge necessary for the Temple,

units.la: נמכרין ודמיהן נופלין quæ cogitant necef-לשכת בדק הבית : faria esse templo re-

units.tr: while the proceeds of those that are sold go into the (4) chamber of the Temple's necessities.

And although these storerooms are said to be "in the sanctuary" [במקדש], they are not to be placed in the holier part but only "in the court" [בעזרת], as we indicated on p. 229. For under the name "sanctuary" [מקדש] we must understand the whole "Mount of the House" [הר הבית], the Temple Mount, as appears from Maimonides in Beth Habech. (4) In the great chamber.

He came and said to his fellow, "He did not manage to finish the matter before his soul departed." And they knew for certain [בייחוד] that the ark had been hidden there [ששם הארון נגנז].
