units.tr: 3 And where did they bow down: four on the north, four on the south, three on the east and two on the west, facing the thirteen gates [שערים], the places of adoration. Where then was the other? Opposite the chamber of wood (for tradition holds it), the ark was hidden there.

units.la: II. Historia de Sacerdote quodam, qui operi intentus vidit stratum diversum à reliquo [pavimento.] Abit ad id socio suo indican- dum, sed vix rem to- tam enarraverat cùm animam efflavit. Et tunc clarè sciverunt, arcam ibi esse Abs- conditam. III. Quomodo adorabant? Quatuor [adorabant] versus septentrionem: qua- tuor versus meri- diem. Tres versus Orientem: & duo
units.tr: II. Story of a priest who, busy at work, saw a pavement different from the rest. He went to tell his companion, but had barely finished relating the whole matter when he breathed his last; and then they clearly knew that the ark was hidden there. III. How did they prostrate? Four toward the north, four toward the south, three toward the east, and two toward the west, corresponding to the thirteen gates.

Portæ meridionales versus (6) latus occidentale flectentes erant (7) porta superior, porta (8) Hiddelek ; porta (9) primogenitorum, porta aquæ. Quare autem vocatur porta aquæ, quia per eam afferunt phyalam aquæ (10) libationis in festo tabernaculorum ; R. Eliefer fil. Iacob dicit, quia in illa aquæ mutabuntur egressuræ sub limine ædis. E regione istarum [portarum] in septentrione adhærent occidenti , (11) Porta Ieconiæ, porta oblationis, porta mulierum , porta cantici. At quare nuncu-
units.tr: The southern gates adjoin the west: the Upper Gate, the Hiddelek Gate, the Gate of the Firstborn, and the Water Gate. Why is it called the Water Gate? Because through it they brought in the flask of water for the libation at the Feast of Tabernacles. Rabbi Eliezer son of Jacob says: because through it the waters that are to flow out from under the threshold of the house will be diverted. Opposite these gates, on the north, adjoining the west, are the Gate of Jeconiah, the Gate of the Offering, the Gate of the Women, and the Gate of Song. Why is it called the Gate of Jeconiah? Because Jeconiah went out through it into his exile. [דרומיים סמיכין למערב שער העליון שער הדלק שער הבכורות שער המים למה נקרא שמו שער המים שבו מכניסין צלוחית של מים של נסוך בחג רבי אליעזר בן יעקב אומר בי המים מפכים העתידין להיות יוצאין מתחת מפתן הבית לעומתן בצפון סמוכין למערב שער יכניה שער קרבן שער נשים שער השיר למה נקרא שמו שער יכניה שבו יצא יכניה בגלותו במזרח שער ניקנור ושני פשפשים] And the two gates in the west were not named.

units.la: (1) Glossa. שופרו תנורת צורות מלמעלה כשופר Schopharot sunt cistulæ oblongæ sensim in minorem modum desinentes, ut cornua. De illis vid. pag. 226. (2) Illas recenset v. seq. vid. etiam pag. 556. ubi de tabulis marmoreis. & pag. 643. (3) De illis adorationibus loquitur Codex Atiddot cap. 2. v 3. Ab interiori parte [atrii gentium] erat סורג Cancellata sepes, altitudine decem palmorum, cui inerant פרצורים effractæ Eluvæ tredecim, quas effregerant Reges Græciæ : Sed eas denuò Iudæi obsepserant, sive restaurarant, & constituerant iis respondentes tredecim adorationes. Nomen יון Græcia non satis convenienter historiæ apponitur, nam illæ effracturæ Asiæ & Syriæ regibus potius quam Græciæ ascribi debent ; Iudæi ita sæpius confundunt authores calamitatum quæ ipsis contigerunt. Adoratio autem quam restaurationis occasione obseruarunt, non uno loco peracta fuit, sed prout quis accederet ad hanc vel illam ruinam, בשתחוה וכורת על אבן מלכות יון Adorabat & confitebatur gratiæ agens pro interitu regni Gracia. (4) Conclaue transftuli quia דיר העציים nihil aliud est quam Thesaurus ligni. De hoc conclavi vid.pag.125. (5) De illo loco arcæ vid.pag.28. (6) Aliter hæc ita exprimi possunt. Quarum (portarum) australes vicinæ occidenti. (7) De porta superiori in priori templo, quam ædificavit Iotham vid. 2. (Chronic. 27. 3. Et quamvis illa hic ad Austrum collocetur, negant tamen alii Rabbini illam hunc locum occupaffe, rationem sumunt ex Ezech. 9. 2. ubi Propheta, antequàm templum novum & spirituale defcripfiffer, difertis verbis affirmat, portam superiorem respicere Aquilonem. (8) Latinè potest vocari porta Ardoris, quæ alium habuit usum, quàm ut illac vulgus promifcuè ingrederetur, fcil. ut per eam liga, quibus ignis in altari ex lege Levit.6.12. perpetuò ardebat, inferrentur. Hoc expressit Glossa, שער הדלק לשכת העציים שרוליקים על המובח Porta Hiddelek est porta conclavis lignorum, quæ in altari consumebantur. (9) Hæc porta quæ fecunda erat in latere auftrali, & quæ priori orientem versus succedebat, ex eo habet nomen, שש מכניסי quod illâ primogenita inferrent, הבכורות ששחישתן גדרום qua ad austrum maftabantur. Obadia de Bartenora Comment. in Middot cap. i. v. 4. (10) De hoc libamine vid. pag.200. (11) Aliter illæ portæ vocantur, vid.pag.473. Et videtur Rabbinum cuius traditio hic recensetur aliquas nomenclationes non ita usitatas adhibuisse: Sanè Iofephus refert, occiduam partem atrii portam non habuiffe, sed ibi perpetuum exstructum fuisse murum: cùm tamen hic sub finem huius versus dua porta in Occidente ponantur. (11) De Porta Nikanoris vid. pag. 473.
units.tr: (1) Gloss. Shofaroth [שופרו]: boxes shaped like the top of a horn, narrowing gradually to a smaller size, Shofaroth are oblong little boxes gradually tapering to a smaller size, like horns. On these see p. 226. (2) He lists them in the next verse; see also p. 556, where he speaks of the marble tables, and p. 643. (3) The Codex Atiddot speaks of these adorations in chapter 2, verse 3: On the inner side [of the court of the Gentiles] there was a lattice fence [סורג], ten palms high, in which were breaches [פרצורים], thirteen breached gaps, which the kings of Greece had broken through. But the Jews had fenced them in again, or repaired them, and set up thirteen adorations corresponding to them. The name Greece [יון] is not very fittingly attached to the history, for those breaches should be ascribed to the kings of Asia and Syria rather than to Greece; the Jews often confuse in this way the authors of the calamities that befell them. The adoration, moreover, which they observed on the occasion of the repair, was not performed in one place, but wherever one came to this or that breach: [בשתחוה וכורת על אבן מלכות יון] he adored and confessed, giving thanks for grace over the fall of the kingdom of Greece. (4) I have translated conclave because [דיר העציים] is nothing other than the treasury of wood. On this room see p. 125. (5) On that place of the ark see p. 28. (6) These words can be expressed otherwise, thus: of which (gates) the southern ones are near the west. (7) On the upper gate in the former temple, which Jotham built (2 Chron. 27.3), see there. And although it is placed here on the south, other rabbis deny that it occupied this place, taking their reason from Ezek. 9.2, where the prophet, before he had described the new and spiritual temple, states in plain words that the upper gate faces north. (8) In Latin the gate can be called the Gate of Burning, which had a use other than that the common people should enter through it, namely that through it the wood by which the fire on the altar burned continually, according to the law in Lev. 6.12, might be carried in. The gloss expresses this: [שער הדלק לשכת העציים שרוליקים על המובח] The Hiddelek gate is the gate of the room of the wood which was consumed on the altar. (9) This gate, which was the second on the south side, and which succeeded the first looking east, has its name from this, [שש מכניסי] that they brought in the firstborn through it, [הבכורות ששחישתן גדרום] which were slaughtered on the south. Obadiah of Bertinoro, Commentary on Middot ch. 1 v. 4. (10) On this libation see p. 200. (11) Those gates are called otherwise; see p. 473. And it seems that the rabbi whose tradition is recounted here used some nomenclature not so common; indeed Josephus reports that the western part of the court had no gate, but that a perpetual wall was built there, although here at the end of this verse two gates are placed in the west. (11) On the Gate of Nicanor see p. 473.

units.la: ד שלשה עשר שולחנות היו במקדש שמונה של שיש בבית המטבחים שעליהן מדיחין את הקרבים ושנים במערב הכבש א׳ של שיש וא׳ של כסף על של שיש היו נותנים את האיברי׳ על של כסף כלי שרת ושנים באולם מכפנים על פתח הבית אחד של זהב על ואהד[?] של שיש נותנים לחם הפנים בבניסתו ועל של זהב ביציאתו שמעלין בקדש ולא מורידין
units.tr: Thirteen tables were in the Temple: eight of marble in the slaughterhouse, on which they washed the entrails; and two on the west of the ramp, one of marble and one of silver: on the marble they placed the pieces, and on the silver the vessels of service; and two in the hall within the door of the house, one of gold and one of marble: on the marble they put the showbread when it came in, and on the gold when it went out; they go up in holiness and do not go down. [שלשה עשר שולחנות היו במקדש שמונה של שיש בבית המטבחים שעליהן מדיחין את הקרבים ושנים במערב הכבש א׳ של שיש וא׳ של כסף על של שיש היו נותנים את האיברים על של כסף כלי שרת ושנים באולם מבפנים על פתח הבית אחד של זהב ואחד של שיש נותנים לחם הפנים בביאתו ועל של זהב ביציאתו שמעלין בקודש ולא מורידין]

Duæ deinde erant versus Occasum (2) Ascensus [altaris] quarum una erat marmorea, altera vero argentea: Marmoreæ imponebant membra, argenteæ vero vasa cultûs. units.tr: IV. There were thirteen tables in the Sanctuary: eight of marble in the (1) slaughterhouse, on which they rinsed the entrails. Then there were two toward the west of the (2) ascent [of the altar], one of marble and the other of silver: the marble ones held the limbs, the silver ones the vessels of service. There were also two tables in the (3) portico outside the gate of the Sanctuary: one was of marble, the other of gold. On the marble they placed the showbread when they brought it into the [Sanctuary], and on the gold they placed it when they took it out from the

units.la: ואחד של זהב מכפנים שעליו לחם הפנים תמיד:
units.tr: ואחד של זהב מכפנים שעליו לחם הפנים תמיד: [And one of gold was on the inside, upon which the showbread was always placed.]

units.la: Sanctuario efferebant. Nam in rebus sanctis semper ascendunt, non descendunt. Una denique tabula aurea erat ab intra, & suprà ipsam perpetuò expositi erant panes propositionis.
units.tr: Once they had carried it out of the Sanctuary. For in holy things they always ascend, not descend. And finally, one golden table was within, and above it the showbread was continually displayed.

[Thirteen chests were in the Temple, and on them was written: New shekels; old shekels; nests; young pigeons for burnt offering; wood; frankincense; gold for atonement. Six were for voluntary offerings.]

units.la: V. Tredecim Ci-stæ erant in Sanctuario, & illis inscriptum erat: Sicli novi. Sicli veteres, Nidi. Pulli pro holocausto. Ligna. Thus: Aurum pro expia-tione. Sex reliquæ autem sunt pro spontanea oblatione. Sicli novi sunt, qui eo ipso anno quo debentur offe-runtur. Veteres verò sunt illi, qui eo anno quo debebantur, non fuerunt so-luti, sed solùm anno sequenti afferuntur. Nidi
units.tr: V. There were thirteen chests in the Sanctuary, and on them was inscribed: New shekels; old shekels; nests; young birds for burnt offering; wood; frankincense; gold for atonement. The remaining six are for voluntary offering. New shekels are those which are offered in the very year in which they are due. Old ones are those which, in the year in which they were due, were not paid, but are brought only in the following year. Nests

units.la: רבי יהודה וחכמי אומרים קינן אחד חטאת ואחד עולה וגוזל, עולה כולן : עולות
units.tr: R. Judah and the sages say: a nest, whether for a sin offering or a burnt offering, and the robber's [gozel] offering, are all burnt offerings [olot].

units.la: ו האומר הרי עלי עצם לא יפחות משני גיזרין לבונה לא יפחות מקומץ זהב לא יפחות מדינר זהב ששה לנדבה נדבה מה היו עושין בה לוקחין בה עולות הבשר לשם והעורות לכהנים זה מדרש דרש יהוידע כהן
units.tr: If someone says, "Upon me is a [bone]," he must not give less than two pieces of wood. For frankincense he must not give less than a handful; for gold, not less than a golden denar; six for a freewill offering. For a freewill offering, what did they do with it? They bought burnt offerings with it, the flesh for the Name and the hides for the priests. This is the exposition that Jehoiada the priest gave.

units.la: Nidi sunt Turtures. Pulli holocausti sunt pulli columbarum, quorum scil. pecuniâ holocausta fieri debent. Sic sentit R. Iehuda : Sapientes vero dicunt, [nummos] turturum [impendi] partim ad [Sacrificium] pro peccato, partim vero pro holocausto. Columbarum vero in universum ad holocaustum.
units.tr: Nests are turtledoves. Young birds for the burnt offering are young pigeons, for which, namely, burnt offerings ought to be made with money. So R. Judah thinks. But the sages say that the money of turtledoves is spent partly on the sacrifice for sin, partly on the burnt offering. Pigeons, however, in general go to the burnt offering.

units.la: VI. Qui dicit, mihi [voto] incumbit, ligna [offerre.] Pauciora quam duo segmenta non offerat. [Qui dicit] ego thus debeo: non minus pugillo det. Aurum [debeo] minus quàm denarium aureum dare non debet. Sex [cistulæ] sunt, pro spontanea oblatione. Quid autem illâ faciunt? Emunt illâ holocausta quorum
units.tr: VI. Whoever says, "I am bound by a vow to offer wood," shall not offer fewer than two segments. Whoever says, "I owe frankincense," shall give not less than a handful. "I owe gold," he shall give not less than a golden denarius. Six chests are for voluntary offerings. What, then, do they do with them? They buy with them burnt offerings, the

units.la: גדול אשם הוא אשום (5) carnes Dei sunt, (6) pelles vero Sacerdotum. Quæ est expositio Iehoiadæ summi Sacerdotis, quando explicat illud, (7) quod אשם sit quod Deo offertur pro reatu. Hæc est generalis regula; omnis pecunia, quæ propter peccatum aut reatum offertur impenditur ad holocausta; caro cedit Deo & pelles Sacerdotibus; quia duo sunt loca scripturæ, quæ Deo & Sacerdotibus reatum solvendum esse docent; & deinde dicitur 2.Reg.12.17. Pecunia pro delicto, & pecunia pro peccato, non inferebatur in domum Iehovæ: Sacerdotibus cedebant.
units.tr: גדול אשם הוא אשם [The greater guilt offering is a guilt offering.] The flesh belongs to God, but the skins to the priests. This is the explanation of Jehoiada the high priest, when he expounds that the guilt offering is what is offered to God for guilt. This is the general rule: all money that is offered on account of sin or guilt is spent on burnt offerings; the flesh goes to God and the skins to the priests, because there are two passages of Scripture which teach that the guilt must be paid to God and to the priests. Then it is said, 2 Kings 12.17: The money for trespass and the money for sin was not brought into the house of Jehovah; it went to the priests.

units.la: (1) Iudæis sacrificia quædam supt קדשי קדשים alia vero קדשים קלים vid. pag.549. Pro priori autem victimarum genere annuli parati erant ad Septen-triotrionem Altaris, ut ibi animalia mactarentur, ex lege Lev.1.11. Mactabit eum ad latus altaris aquilonare. In eodem altaris latere, [ut patet ex Middot 3.5.] iis qui victimas pelle nudabant, caeteraque peragebant, locum paraverant, in quo octo erant Columnae lapideae, & humiles, columnis vero erantimpositae quadratae trabes uncis instructae, in quibus animalia ad excoriandum suspendebant; [vid.pag.553.] Suspensa ita animalia [inquit R. Schemaja] מפשיטין ומנתחים ומביאין הקרבניים ע־ שולחנות ש־ שיש שלמטה בין העמודי Excoriabant & dissecabant, atq; intestina extrahebant in mensas marmoreas, quae inferius inter columnas sita erant. Extracta Intestina deinde מריחים פעם ראשונה בלשכת מריחים כצינעת Abluunt prima vice in conclavi lavantium, in occulto, quia valde sordida sunt à stercore: Deinde iterum intestina, stomacho excepto, in illis mensis, de quibus Misna loquitur, abluebant. Hoc observavit Tosaphta in cap.5. Middot. Hae mensae autem ex Marmore confectae erant, שהשיש סקר ומצנן ושומר הנשר שלא יסריח Quia marmor rigidam & frigidam reddit carnem, conservatq; eandem ne foeteat. Bartenora in Mtddot 3.5.
units.tr: (1) Among the Jews some sacrifices are of the "most holy things" [קדשי קדשים] and others of the "lesser holy things" [קדשים קלים]; see p. 549. For the former kind of victim, rings were prepared on the north side of the altar, so that the animals might be slaughtered there, according to the law: Lev. 1:11, "He shall kill it on the north side of the altar." On the same side of the altar, as is clear from Middot 3.5, they had prepared a place for those who stripped the victims of their skins and carried out the other work. There were eight stone columns there, low ones, and on the columns were laid square beams fitted with hooks, from which the animals were hung for skinning; [see p. 553.] Thus hung, the animals were, as R. Schemaja says, [מפשיטין ומנתחים ומביאין הקרבניים ע־ שולחנות ש־ שיש שלמטה בין העמודי] skinned and cut up, and the sacrificial parts were brought to the marble tables that stood below between the columns. The entrails were then [מריחים פעם ראשונה בלשכת מריחים כצינעת] washed for the first time in the chamber of the washers, in a private place, because they are very foul with dung. Then the entrails were washed again, except the stomach, on those tables of which the Mishnah speaks. The Tosefta on chapter 5 of Middot noted this. These tables were made of marble, [שהשיש סקר ומצנן ושומר הנשר שלא יסריח] because marble makes the flesh stiff and cold and keeps it from going bad. Bartenora on Middot 3.5.

(6) Vid. pag.554 (7) Cum hic etiam alius sensus esse possit, adeat Lector, Glossatores, & videat quis subistitui queat: Mihi videtur hic etiam novam periodum incipere posse, & sicuti in lineis praecedentibus textus retulit, quorsum Oblatio הנרבה faciat, & ad quid adhibeatur, ita nunc sermo flectatur ad sacrificium pro reatu, hoc modo: Sacrificium pro reatu vero Deo in {expiationem} expiationem reatus cedit. Quod hic monuisse sufficit; non enim nunc omnes commentationes excutere vacat.
units.tr: (1) On the ascent of the altar see p. 16. (3) On the porch see p. 642. (4) See p. 643. (5) That is, those offerings of which no portion goes either to the priests or to the offerers, but which are wholly consumed by fire. (6) See p. 554. (7) Since another sense may be possible here, let the reader consult the commentators and see what might be substituted. It seems to me that here too a new sentence may begin: just as in the preceding lines the text told why the offering [הנרבה] is made and what it is used for, so now the discussion turns to the sacrifice for guilt, in this way: "But the sacrifice for guilt goes to God for the expiation of guilt." This is enough to have noted here, for I do not now have the leisure to examine all the commentaries.

units.tr: to lighten: half and half, they go to the burnt offering [להקל מחצה למחצה]. Moreover,

units.tr: the second tithe are assigned to the second tithe. If they are equally distant from this and that, they too go to the second tithe. This is the general rule: (1) they go to the nearer one to make things easier, but those in the middle are assigned to make things stricter.

units.la: ב מעות שנמצאו [Hebrew] I I. Nummi qui
units.tr: II. Coins which [מעות שנמצאו]

units.tr: Coins found in the mount of the Temple are tithe money; those found elsewhere in the year are common.

units.tr: for the burnt offering: tithe, on the mount [לעולה מעשר בהר]; of the cattle

units.la: הבית חולין בירושלם [Hebrew] bus, semper decimæ
units.tr: of the Temple [הבית] are common in Jerusalem [חולין בירושלם];

units.la: sunt; qui reperiun-
units.tr: dealers, they are always tithe. Those found

units.tr: on the Temple Mount

units.la: בשער הרגל מעשר ובשאר בל ימות השנה חולין : cōmunes sunt. Qui Hierosolymis [repe-riuntur] tempore fe-storum , decimæ sunt, in aliis vero anni diebus communes.
units.tr: At the festival gate, tithe [מעשר]; and on all other days of the year, common [חולין]: they are common. Those found in Jerusalem at the time of the festivals are tithes; on the other days of the year they are common.

units.la: ג בשר שנמצא בעורה איברין עולות ותיכורת חטאות בירושלם זבחי שלמים זה וזה תעובר צורתו ויצא לבית השריפה נמצא בגבולין איברין נבילות חתיכות מותרות ובשעת הרגל שהנשך מרובה אף איברין מותרין :
units.tr: Meat found in the court: if they are limbs of burnt offerings or sin offerings in Jerusalem, they are peace offerings. If both have changed their form, they go out to the place of burning. Meat found in the provinces: if they are limbs, they are treated as carcasses [נבילות]; if they are pieces, they are permitted. At the festival, when the slaughter is great, even limbs are permitted.

units.la: III. Caro quæ in atrio reperitur , si membra sunt ad ho-locaustum [cedit] sa-crificio pro pecca-to. [Carnes quæ re-periuntur] Hierosfo-lymis, sunt Sacrificia pacifica. Si vero hæ & illæ (2) figuram suam permutarunt ? ad (3) conclave com-bustionis abeunt. [Carnes quæ reperi-riuntur] in limitibus, si membra sunt, ut cadauera [æstimantur] si vero frusta sunt, licita sunt. Tempore festorum autem, in quo magna copia carnium est, etiam membra licita sunt.
units.tr: Meat found in the court: if they are limbs, they go to the burnt offering or the sin offering. Meat found in Jerusalem consists of peace offerings. But if these and those have changed their form, they go to the place of burning. Meat found in the provinces: if they are limbs, they are judged like carcasses; if they are pieces, they are permitted. At the time of the festivals, however, when there is a great abundance of meat, even limbs are permitted.

units.la: ד בהמה שנמצארת מירושלם ועד מגדל
units.tr: IV. Of the cattle found from Jerusalem as far as the Migdal Eder,

units.tr: IV. Of the cattle found within Jerusalem

units.tr: males: burnt offerings; females: sacrifices of peace offerings

units.tr: are peace offerings. R. Judah says that if among them there is one fit for the Passover, it is a Passover (offering)

units.la: רבי יהודה אומר mundi plagas repe-
units.tr: for the Passover, [it is a Passover] if it is found thirty days before the festival.

units.tr: [Hebrew] Passover [פסחים]

units.tr: [Hebrew] before the festival (רגל) thirty days [שלשים יום]

units.la: יום : quit, si inter illos
units.tr: [Hebrew] R. Judah says [רבי יהודה אומר]

units.la: [masculos] reperiatur aliquis, qui aptus sit ad Pascha, Pascha fit, [modo reperiatur] triginta diebus ante Festum.
units.tr: If among the males any one is found that is fit for the Passover, it becomes a Passover (offering), provided it is found thirty days before the festival.

units.la: ה בראשונה היו ממשכנין את מוצאיה עד שהוא מביא נסכיה חזרו להיות מניחין אותה ובורחין התקינו בית דין שיהו נסכיה באין משל ציבור : V. Ab initio op-pignorabant eum, qui pecus reperierat, donec afferret libamina eius. Sed inceperunt homines illa pecora relinquere, & fugere, constituit itaque Synedrium ut libamina [sumptus] Ecclesiæ fierent.
units.tr: V. Formerly they would hold in pledge the owner of the animal until he brought its libations. But people began to leave the animals and flee, so the Synedrium decreed that its libations should come from the public funds of the Church. [ה בראשונה היו ממשכנין את מוצאיה עד שהוא מביא נסכיה חזרו להיות מניחין אותה ובורחין התקינו בית דין שיהו נסכיה באין משל ציבור]

units.la: ו אמר רבי שמעון שבעה דברי התקינו בית דין וזה אחד VI. Dixit R. Si-meon, septem de-creta fecit Synedrium; & hoc unum
units.tr: And R. Simeon said: The court of judgment ordained seven decrees, and this is one of them.

units.la: מהן עב[?]ום ששלח עולתו ממרינת ושלח עמה נסכים קריבין משלו ואם לאו קריבין משל ציבור וכן גר שמת והניח זבחים אם יש לו נסכים קריבין משלו ואם לאו קריבין משל צבור ותנאי בית דין הואא על כהן גדול שמת שתהא מנחתו קריבה משל צבור רבי יהודה אומר משל יורשין ושלימה היתה קריבה:
units.tr: Of these: if a Gentile [עכו"ם] sent his burnt offering from overseas and sent with it libations, the libations are offered from his own funds; if not, they are offered from public funds. Likewise a proselyte who died and left sacrifices: if he has libations, they are offered from his own; if not, they are offered from public funds. The ruling of the court concerned a high priest who died, that his meal offering should be offered from public funds. R. Judah says: from the heirs' funds; and it was offered in full.

units.la: fiæ fiat. R.Iehuda inquit dum sumptu, ut oblatio
units.tr: ...let it be done. R. Judah says: at the expense, so that the offering may be made.

units.la: ז על המלח ועל העצים שיהו הכהנים eft ex ipfis. Reliqua funt, quòd fi Idololatra aliquis ex provincia maritima mitteret holocaustum unà cum libamine, illud quoque offerri debere, fi verò nullum miferit, addi debere [fumptu] Ecclefiæ. Similiter fi aliquis peregrinus moriens reliquerit sacrificia, si habet libamina, ex illis offerunt: sin minus sumptu Ecclesiæ addunt. Extendit Synedrium hoc quoque ad Summum Sacerdotem defunctum, ut oblatio eius [Sumptu] Eccle[offerri] debet, hæreintegra sit.
units.tr: VII. Concerning the salt and the wood, that the priests should (have them)... The rest is that if some idolater from the maritime province were to send a burnt offering together with a libation, it too should be offered; but if he sent none, it should be added from the public funds of the Church. Similarly, if some stranger dying leaves sacrifices, if he has libations, they offer from those; if not, they add from the public funds. The Synedrium extended this also to the deceased High Priest, so that his offering should be offered from the public funds of the Church, and his heritage should remain whole. [על המלח ועל העצים שיהו הכהנים]

units.la: VII. [Conftituit deinde] Circa sal & lignum,
units.tr: VII. He next lays down concerning salt and wood,

units.la: נאותים בהן ועל lignum, ut Sacerdo- חפרה שלא יהו tes ex illis aliquam מועלין באפרה ועל utilitatem recipiant: הקינין הפסולות שיהו Item circa vaccæ באורת משל ציבור ר rufæ cineres, ne illæ יוסי אומר המספק in usum eorum ce- את הקינין מספק את dant. Item ut loco הפסולורת : turturum illegitimaEcclesiæ parentur: rum, aliæ sumptu R. Iose dicit, quod
units.tr: Concerning salt and wood, so that the priests may not gain some benefit from them, [נאותים בהן על העצים שלא יהו הכהנים מועלין באפרה ועל הקינין הפסולות שיהו באות משל ציבור]. Likewise concerning the ashes of the red heifer, that they not be put to their own use. Likewise, so that in place of the unfit turtledoves others are provided at public expense. R. Jose says [רבי יוסי אומר], that whoever supplies the turtledoves should also supply the unfit ones [המספק את הקינין מספק את הפסולות].

units.la: ille qui de turturibus prospicit, etiam locò illegitimarum prospiciat.
units.tr: He who provides for the turtledoves should also provide in place of the unfit ones.

units.la: NOTÆ.
units.tr: NOTES.

units.la: (1) Referunt pecunias repertas ad illud quod propius est, ut ita facilitati studeant, & simul significent illud minus æstimandum esse; illud vero quod in medio reperitur, relegant ad illud quod magis æstimatur. Ita consueta apud Magistros est formula argumentandi מק׳ ודומר à minori ad majus. (2) תעובר צורתו מעגירין אותן מלגניהם עד שיפסלו בנותר : Quæ permutarunt figuram suam &c. id est, quæ tamdiu manibus hominum tritæ fuerunt, ut quasi aridæ, iam illegitimæ sint. Gloss. (3) Erat focus in templo in quo reliquia ossa holocaustorum & alia frusta sacrificiorum in cineres redigebantur; In illum etiam relegebant carnes de quibus sermo in Mišna. (4) De MigdalEder vid. pag.355.
units.tr: (1) They refer money found to the nearer thing, so that they may favour ease, and at the same time signify that the lesser thing is to be valued less; but what is found in the middle they refer to what is valued more. Thus the customary formula among the Masters for arguing [מק׳ ודומר] is from the less to the greater (a minori ad majus). (2) [תעובר צורתו מעגירין אותן מלגניהם עד שיפסלו בנותר] Those which have changed their form, etc., that is, those which have been rubbed so long in human hands that, as if dry, they are now unfit. Gloss. (3) There was a hearth in the temple in which the remains of bones of the burnt offerings and other scraps of sacrifices were reduced to ashes; into it they also used to refer the flesh of which the Mishnah speaks. (4) On Migdal Eder see p. 355.

units.la: א כל הרוקין הנמצאים בירושלם טהורין חוץ משל שוק העליון דברי רבי מאיר רבי יוסי אומר בשאר ימות השנה שבאמצע טמאין ושבצדדין טהורים ובשעה הרגל שבאמצע טהורים ושבצדדים טמאין שמפני שהן מועטין מסתלקין לצדדין׃ impura. Quoniam enim latera deflectunt.
units.tr: (1) All the pools found in Jerusalem are clean, except that of the upper market, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yose says: in the other days of the year those in the middle are unclean and those at the sides are clean, but at the time of the festival those in the middle are clean and those at the sides are unclean, because, since they are few, they withdraw to the sides. Impure. For they deflect to the sides.

units.la: ב כל הכלים הנמצאים בירושלם דרך ירידה לבית הטבילה טמאין דרך עליה טהודין שלא
units.tr: (2) All the vessels found in Jerusalem, those going down to the bath of immersion are unclean; those going up are clean, [דרך ירידה לבית הטבילה טמאין דרך עליה טהודין שלא] so that ...

units.la: CAPUT VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: 1. Omnis (1) Saliva quæ Hierosolymis reperitur, æstimatur munda, exceptâ salivâ vici superioris. Sic sentit R. Meir. R. Iosé verò dicit, illa quæ in reliquis diebus anni in media [via] reperitur, impura est, quæ verò in lateribus pura. Tempore Festi verò illa quæ in medio [reperitur] pura est, & quæ in parietibus illi (2) pauci sunt, ad
units.tr: 1. All spittle found in Jerusalem is considered clean, except the spittle of the upper market. So R. Meir holds. R. Jose, however, says that spittle found in the middle of the way on the other days of the year is unclean, but that found at the sides is clean. At the time of the Feast, however, that which is found in the middle is clean, and that on the walls, [where] there are few [people]... to

units.la: I I. Omnia vasa quæ reperiuntur Hierosolymis, in via descensus ad lavatorium, immunda sunt; quæ verò in via ascensus [reperiuntur] munda
units.tr: II. All vessels found in Jerusalem, on the way down to the bath, are unclean; those found on the way up are clean.

units.la: כדהך ירידתן עליתן דברי רבי מאיר רבי יוסי אומר כולן טהורין הוץ מן הסל והמגריפה והמריצה המיהדין לקברות:
units.tr: As their descent, so their ascent: these are the words of R. Meir. R. Jose says: all are clean except the basket, the shovel and the bier, which are for graves. [כדהך ירידתן עליתן דברי רבי מאיר רבי יוסי אומר כולן טהורין הוץ מן הסל והמגריפה והמריצה המיהדין לקברות]

units.la: quæ instrumenta propria
units.tr: which are the proper instruments

units.la: ג סכין שנמצאת ב״ד שוחט בר מיד בשלשה עשר שונה ומטביל וקופיץ בין בזה ובין בזה שונה ומטביל חל ארבע עשר להיוב בשבת שוחט בה מיד בט׳ו שוחט בה מיד נמצאת קשורה לסכין הרי זו כסכין:
units.tr: 3. A knife found in the hand of a slaughterer, who used it at once on the thirteenth, is changed and immersed. A sickle or scythe is treated the same way. If the fourteenth falls on the Sabbath, one slaughters with it at once on the fifteenth. If it is found tied to a knife, it is like a knife.

units.la: decimum quintum, ifto test. Si reperiatur alliga tur ut cultra. munda sunt ; quoniani descensus eorum , non est ut ascensus eorum. Sic sentit Rabbi Meir, sed R. Iose inquit, omnia pura sunt, excepto Canistro, (3) palâ, & (4) malleo : a sunt sepulturæ.
units.tr: Fifteenth, the text: If it is found tied like a knife, it is clean, since its descent is not like its ascent. So Rabbi Meir thinks. But R. Jose says all are clean except the basket, the spade and the mattock, which are for graves.

units.la: III. (5) Cultrum quod repertum est die decimo quarto, statim eo mactare licet. Si verò repertum est die decimo tertio, ablui debet. Securis verò sive hoc, sive illo [die reperiatur,] ablui debet. Si accidit ut dies decimus quartus incidat in Sabbathum, statim cultro mactare licet. Si in statim mactare portum cultris, æstima-
units.tr: III. A knife found on the fourteenth day may be used at once for slaughter. If it is found on the thirteenth day, it must be immersed. An axe, whether it is found on this day or that, must be immersed. If it happens that the fourteenth day falls on the Sabbath, one may slaughter with the knife at once. If on the fourteenth day one may slaughter at once with the knives, let it be judged (the sentence breaks off in the source).

units.la: ד פרוכת שנטמאת בולד הטומאה מטבילין אותה בפנים ומכניסין אותהּ מיד ואת שנטמאת באב הטומאה מטבלין אותה בחוץ ושוטחין אותה בחיל מפני שצריכה הערב שמש ואם היתה חדשה שוטחין אותה על גג האצטבא בדי שיראו זן שהיא נאר׃
units.tr: 4. A curtain that has become unclean through a child of uncleanness is immersed inside and brought in again at once. But one made unclean through a father of uncleanness is immersed outside and spread out in the court, because it needs the sun to set. If it is new, they spread it on the roof of the portico so that people may see how fine its weaving is.

units.la: ה רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר משום רבי שמעון בן הסגן פרוכת עביר טפח IV. Si velum immundum redditum est, per (6) filium immunditiei, ipsum intra abluunt, & statim iterum inferunt; si vero immundum est per patrem immunditiei, ipsum extra lavant, & deinde expandunt in (7) antemurali. Si novum est ipsum expandunt in tecto porticus, ut populus videat texturam eius, quàm pulchra sit.
units.tr: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben HaSegan: a curtain requires a handbreadth. IV. If a veil has become unclean through a child of uncleanness, they wash it inside and bring it in again at once; but if it is unclean through a father of uncleanness, they wash it outside and then spread it out in the forecourt. If it is new, they spread it on the roof of the portico, so that the people may see its weaving, how beautiful it is.

units.la: העם את מלאכו
units.tr: that the people see its work

units.la: V. R. Simeon fil. Vicarii Sacerdotum. Veli crassitudo est palmus, & contextus est ex 72. filiis, quorum unumquodque habet 24. filamenta. In longitudine habet 40. cubitos,
units.tr: V. R. Simeon, son of the Vicar of the Priests. The thickness of the veil is a palm, and it is woven of seventy-two threads, each of which has twenty-four strands. In length it is forty cubits,

units.la: ועל שבעים ושנים נימין נארגת ועל כל נימא ונימא ב׳ד
units.tr: and it is woven of seventy-two threads, and on each thread twenty-four [strands]. [ועל שבעים ושנים נימין נארגת ועל כל נימא ונימא ב׳ד]

units.la: חותין ארכה ארבעים אמה ורחבה עשרים אמה ומשמונים ושתי רבוע נעשית ושתים עושין בכל שנה ושלש מאות כהנים מטבילין אותה׃
units.tr: its length is forty cubits and its breadth twenty cubits, and it is made into a square of eighty-two; two are made each year, and three hundred priests immerse it. [חותין ארכה ארבעים אמה ורחבה עשרים אמה ומשמונים ושתי רבוע נעשית ושתים עושין בכל שנה ושלש מאות כהנים מטבילין אותה]

units.la: ו בשר קדשי הקדשים שנטמא בין באב הטומאה בין בולד הטומאה בין בפנים בין בחוץ בית שמאי אומרים הכל ישרף בפנים חוץ משנטמא באב הטומאה בחוץ ובית הלל אומרים הכל ישרף בחוץ חוץ ממי שנטמא בולד הטומאה בפנים׃ bitos, in latitudine vero decem : Et ex 82. myriadibus confectus est. Duo singulis annis conficiuntur. Trecenti Sacerdotes ipsum lavant.
units.tr: 6. The flesh of the Most Holy things that became unclean, whether through a father of uncleanness or a child of uncleanness, whether inside or outside: the School of Shammai say everything is burned inside, except what became unclean through a father of uncleanness outside; the School of Hillel say everything is burned outside, except what became unclean through a child of uncleanness inside. [בשר קדשי הקדשים שנטמא בין באב הטומאה בין בולד הטומאה בין בפנים בין בחוץ בית שמאי אומרים הכל ישרף בפנים חוץ משנטמא באב הטומאה בחוץ ובית הלל אומרים הכל ישרף בחוץ חוץ ממי שנטמא בולד הטומאה בפנים׃]

units.la: V I. De carne (§) Sancti Sanctorum, quæ immunda est si- ve per patrem im- munditiei, sive per filium, sive intrà, sive extrà, Schammæani sentiunt, omnia in- trà comburenda es- se, excepto eo quod immundum est, per patrem immunditiei ab extrà.
units.tr: VI. Concerning the flesh of the Holy of Holies, which is unclean, whether through a father of uncleanness or through a child, whether inside or outside: the Shammaites hold that everything is to be burned inside, except what is unclean through a father of uncleanness from outside.

units.la: Hilleliani verò dicunt, omnia extrà comburi debere, exceptô illo quod impurum est à filio immunditiei ab intrà.
units.tr: The Hillelites, however, say everything must be burned outside, except what is unclean through a child of uncleanness from inside.

units.la: f
units.tr: f

units.la: ז רבי אליעזי אומר אר שנטמא באב הטומאה בין בפנים בין בחוץ ישרף בחוץ ואת שנטמא בולד הטומאה בין בפנים בין בחוץ ישרף בפנים רבי עקיבא אומר מקום טומאתו שם שריפתו׃
units.tr: 7. R. Eliezer says: whatever is unclean through a father of uncleanness, whether inside or outside, must be burned outside; but whatever is unclean through a child of uncleanness, whether outside or inside, must be burned inside. Rabbi Akiba says: the place of its uncleanness is the place of its burning.

units.la: ח אברי התמיד ניתנין מחצה כבש ולמטה במערב (ס"א במזרח) ושל מוספין ניתנין מחצה כבש ולמטה במזרח (ס"א במערב) ושל ראשי חדשים ניתנין על כרכוב המזבח מלמעלה (ס"א מתחת
units.tr: 8. The limbs of the daily offering are placed from the half of the ramp and below on the west (another reading: east), and those of the additional offerings are placed from the half of the ramp and below on the east (another reading: west), and those of the new moons are placed on the cornice of the altar from above (another reading: from beneath).

units.la: VII. R. Eliefer inquit illud quod immundum est per patrem Immunditiei, sive extrà, sive intrà, comburi debet extrà; illud verò quod immundum est per filium immunditici, sive extra sive intra, intra comburi debet. Rabbi Akiba inquit ubi est immundum ibi comburatur.
units.tr: VII. R. Eliezer says: whatever became unclean through a father of uncleanness, whether outside or inside, must be burned outside; but whatever became unclean through a child of uncleanness, whether outside or inside, must be burned inside. Rabbi Akiba says: where it is unclean, there let it be burned.

units.la: VIII. Membra sacrificii iugis, ponuntur in dimidia parte (9) graduum & infrà occidentem versus [aliud exempl. orientem versus.] (Membra verò) sacrificiorum additicium, ponuntur in mediis gradibus & infrà, orientem versus, [ex. al. occidentem versus.] Sacrificia
units.tr: VIII. The limbs of the continual sacrifice are placed in the half of the ramp and below, toward the west [another copy: toward the east]. The limbs of the additional sacrifices are placed in the middle of the steps and below, toward the east [another copy: toward the west]. The sacrifices of the new moons are placed below the cornice of the altar, in its upper part [another copy: in its lower part].

units.la: כרכוב המזבח מלמטה השקלים והביכורי' א נוהגין אלא בפו הבית אבל מעש דגן ומעשר בהמר והבכורות נוהגין ב' בפני הבית בין שלא בפני הבית המקדיש שקלים וביכורים הר ה קדש רבי שמעו אומר האומר ביכוריכ קדש אינן קדש :
units.tr: The shekels and first-fruits are in force only while the Temple stands, but the tithe of grain and of cattle and the firstborn are in force both before and after the Temple stands. Whoever consecrates shekels and first-fruits, they are holy. R. Shimon says: one who says "my first-fruits are holy," they are not holy. [כרכוב המזבח מלמטה השקלים והביכורי' א נוהגין אלא בפו הבית אבל מעש דגן ומעשר בהמר והבכורות נוהגין ב' בפני הבית בין שלא בפני הבית המקדיש שקלים וביכורים הר ה קדש רבי שמעו אומר האומר ביכוריכ קדש אינן קדש :]

units.la: cia autem (io) noviluniorum ponuntur infrà ambitum in parte superiore. [al. ex. in parte inferiore.] Sicli & primitiæ non folvuntur ante templum & risi stante templo. Decimæ frumenti vero & pecoris, primogenituræque solvuntur ante templum & post templum. Si quis sanctificet siclos & primitias, illa sancta sunt. R. Simeon licit, primitiæ quæ sancto usui devoventur indæ non sunt.
units.tr: The shekels and first-fruits are not paid before the Temple, and not when the Temple is standing; the tithes of grain and of cattle and the firstborn are paid both before and after the Temple. If anyone consecrates shekels and first-fruits, they are holy. R. Simeon says: first-fruits that are devoted to sacred use are not holy.

units.la: (1) Vid.pag.610. הרוקן verò Sputum vel Salivam sic docet Glossa quando infit, הרוקן מה שמשלי האדם מפיו שאליוא כלעו Harokin est illud quod homo x ore suo ejicit, & in vernacula vocatur Salive. (2) n anni diebus profestis, Pharisæi & munditici stuentes deflectebant ad latera, occursum populi & rofanæ plebis fugientes, & tunc saliva in parietibus aunda erat, in medio viæ verò immunda. In festo crò in quo unusquisque munditiei operam dare debet, in medio viæ etiam Pharisæi ibant, immund[?] vero & alienigenæ quorum minor numerus ad lat[?]
units.tr: (1) See p. 610. The Gloss defines הרוקן [harokin], the spittle or saliva, thus: "Harokin is that which a man ejects from his mouth; in the vernacular it is called salive" [הרוקן]. (2) On ordinary days the Pharisees and the ritually scrupulous kept to the sides, shrinking from the crowd and the profane common people, and so the saliva was on the walls, while in the middle of the road it was unclean. But on the feast, when everyone ought to take pains over cleanness, the Pharisees also went in the middle of the road, while the unclean and foreigners, of whom there were fewer, [went to the side].

units.la: (3) מגריפה כלי שגורפין בו העצמות Magrepha, instrumentum quo colligunt & accumulant offa.
units.tr: (3) מגריפה [magrepha], an instrument with which they scrape together and heap up bones.

units.tr: (4) An instrument with which they crush and break bones [כלי שמרצצין ומשברין בו העצמות].

Blessed is he who gives strength and power to the weary, and multiplies might to those who have no power [בסייעתא רחמנא האלוהים נשלמה מסכת שקלים ה"ן ר"ק זה או"תי עשה לבושי וכסותי ברוך נותן ליעף כוח ועצמה וליתמא ואין אונים ירבה גבורה].

units.la: IN QVO ORDINE ALPHABETICO notantur & referuntur praecipua; qua circa veterum Hebraeorum Dogmata, ritus, & statuta, in utroque Talmude, Maymonidis & aliorum scriptis, occurrunt:
units.tr: IN WHICH, IN ALPHABETICAL ORDER, ARE NOTED AND REFERRED TO THE CHIEF MATTERS THAT OCCUR IN BOTH TALMUDS AND IN THE WRITINGS OF MAIMONIDES AND OTHERS, CONCERNING THE DOGMAS, RITES AND ORDINANCES OF THE ANCIENT HEBREWS.

units.la: A.
units.tr: A.

units.la: אב Ab, Mensis quintus incipiens à novilunio Iulii nostri. Illius mensis die nono quinque calamitosa contigerunt. 1. eo die decretum est populum non ingressurum in terram promissam. 2. eo die devastatum est templum primum. 3. ille dies etiam excidium attulit templo secundo. 4. illo die excisa est civitas ביתר Bethar, (de qua vid. s. l.) 5. aratro versa est civitas Hierosolymitana. Taanit c. 4. §. 6. Hinc משנכנס אב ממעטין בשמחה Postquam Mensis אב initium suum capit, diminuunt latitias, ibid. Non quòd hæc omnia illo die accidisse crederent, sed (ut notat Gemara) quod faustum ad diem aliquem faustum reducere in usu haberent, infaustum ad nefastum. Hoc nota ad cap. 1. Math. ubi in v. 17. compu atio 14. g neraiionum etiam non est accurata, ex usu vulgari.
units.tr: Ab [אב], the fifth month, beginning from the new moon of our July. Five calamities befell on the ninth day of this month. (1) On that day it was decreed that the people would not enter the promised land. (2) On that day the first temple was laid waste. (3) That same day also brought the destruction of the second temple. (4) On that day the city of Bethar was destroyed (on which see under its own letter). (5) The city of Jerusalem was ploughed over. Taanit ch. 4, §6. Hence: "When the month Ab begins, they diminish joy" [משנכנס אב ממעטין בשמחה], ibid. They did not believe that all these things happened on that day, but (as the Gemara notes) it was their custom to refer what was fortunate to a fortunate day and what was unfortunate to an unlucky one. Note this on Matt. ch. 1, where the count of the generations in v. 17 is also not exact, following common usage.

units.la: אבא & אבי Abba & Abi, Necesse est ut distinguas harum vocum sensum, quarum una sonat idioma Hebraicum, altera Chaldaicum. Nam vox אבי patrem quidem naturalem denotat, at simul patrem etiam civilem, seniorem, Dominum, Doctorem, Magistratum; at vox אבא solùmodò denotat patrem naturalem aut adoptantem; & insuper non solùm significat patrem, sed patrem meum. Hanc distinctionem discimus ex Targumistis, qui ubicunque fit mentio de patre naturali adhibuerunt vocem אבא ut Gen.xxxii. 7. Gen.xxvii.34. Gen.xlviii.18. Iud.xi.36. Esai.viii.4. Vbi verò de patre civili, aliam apposuerunt vocem: Exempla sunt Gen.iv. 20. 21.1.Sam.x.12. 2.Reg.ii.12. 2.Reg. v.13. 2.Reg. vi. 21. ubi אבי fermè semper Targum reddit per רב & כר quæ promiscuè Dominum significant. Confer hic Marc. xiv. 36. ubi Christus angoribus circumseptus ipsum Deum tamen sensu suavissimo invenit אבא patrem suum. vide etiam Rom.viii.15. Quòd autem אבא etiam significet pater meus, patet ex Bab. Sanhed. sol.37.1. Ne quisquam dicat vicino suo אבא גדול באביך pater meus est major patre tuo: item ex Bav. Batra sol. 10. 2. Salomon dixit, obser-
units.tr: Abba and Abi [אבא ואבי]. You must distinguish the sense of these words: one is a Hebrew idiom, the other Chaldee. The word אבי denotes a natural father, but at the same time also a civil father, an elder, a lord, a teacher, a magistrate. The word אבא, however, denotes only a natural or adoptive father, and moreover signifies not merely father but my father. We learn this distinction from the Targumists, who wherever they speak of a natural father used the word אבא, as at Gen. 32:7, Gen. 27:34, Gen. 48:18, Judg. 11:36, Isa. 8:4. Where they speak of a civil father, however, they used another word. Examples are Gen. 4:20-21, 1 Sam. 10:12, 2 Kings 2:12, 2 Kings 5:13, 2 Kings 6:21, where the Targum almost always renders אבי by רב and כר, which indiscriminately signify lord. Compare here Mark 14:36, where Christ, surrounded by anguish, nevertheless finds God himself with the most sweet sense as אבא, his Father. See also Rom. 8:15. That אבא also means my father is clear from Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 37.1: "Let no one say to his neighbour, אבא גדול באביך, my father is greater than your father"; likewise from Bava Batra fol. 10.2: "Solomon said, observe" [observate] מה פירש אבא, What does my father say? See also Aruch under אבא.

units.la: observate מה פירש אבא Quid dicat pater meus? vid. etiam Aruch in אבא.
units.tr: Observe, What does my father say? [מה פירש אבא].

units.la: זקני בית אב vel אנשי כית אב zikne beth ab vel anfche beth ab vocantur in Middot. cap. 1. & alibi seniores illius sacerdotum ordinis, qui illo die ministrabat; fuerunt enim custodes septimanarum in sex ordines vel familias divisi, singulis diebus ministrabat una, die vero septimo simul omnes ministrabant, qui per illam septimanam excubias & alia officia subierant. vid. Maymon. Hal. K. Hamikd. c. 4. in med.
units.tr: The zikne beth ab or anshe beth ab [זקני בית אב / אנשי בית אב] are called, in Middot ch. 1 and elsewhere, the elders of that order of priests which was serving on that day. For the priestly courses were divided into six orders or families who kept guard in weekly turns: on each day one order served, while on the seventh day all served together, those who had undertaken the watches and other duties during that week. See Maimonides, Hilchot Klei Hamikdash, ch. 4, in the middle.

units.la: ABRAHAMVS in Cananitida advenienſ à Bereschit Rabba sect. 39. introducitur primùm in partem eius borealem; Textus sic se habet: Dixit Deus Abrahamo לך לך abi tibi; vocibus duplicatis, ob duplex iter; unum ab Aram Naharaim, aliud ab Aram Nachor. Dum versabatur Abrahamus in Aram Naharaim, & Aram Nachor, vidit homines edentes bibentes, & ludentes; Dixit ergo ne sit portio mea in ista terra. At postquam venit צור לסולמה של Ad scalam Tyriorum vidit homines operam dantes pastinationi, agricultura, vindemiationi, & tum dixit sit portio mea in hac terra. §. Qui vocat Abrahamum אברם peccat contra praeceptum affirmativum, Hierof. Berac. p. 3. c. 4. sic nec Sara Sarai & Israel Iacob sunt vocandi ibid. §. Quomodo Abraham Idololatriae restitit vide Stellas &c. §. Quòd Iudaei semen Abrahae sint admodum gloriantur; Bava Metzia sol. 83,1. Historia est de R. Iochanan Ben Matthia, qui dixit filio suo, Ito & conduc nobis operarios; ivit ille, & paflus est cum iis pro vitâ; cum verò ad patrem veniret dixit ei pater. Mi fili quamvis pares iis convivia patria conviviis Salomonis, non tamen satis officiò tuo fungeris, quoniam illi sunt fi. i Abrahami, Isaaci, & Iacobi: &c. Hinc etia n Ioh.viii.33. clamitant Σπέρμα Αβραάμ ἐσμεν. Quibus tamen reponi potest quod in ipsismet pandectis exstat Schabbat sol. 53.1. תשה וכות אבות (Cessavit meritum Patrum, Abrahami, Isaaci & Iacobi, à diebus Hosea Prophetæ &c. quare nihil vobis est quod amplius jactetis. §. Abrahamum dolore circumcisionis ægrotantem visitavit Deus, & quæsivit quomodo se haberet. Rafchi ad Gen. 18. 1. Vt & Berefchit Ketanna in locum. §. Diabolus Abrahamum coram Deo accusavit, sicuti Iobum criminatus est, ut autem Deus integritatem eius ostenderet, ipsum de filio immolando tentare voluit. Sanhed. Sect. אלו הן הנחנקין §. Abraham non coluit Sabbathum. Berefchit Ketanna ad Gen.2. v.3. Abraham erat Astrologus. vid. Astrologus.
units.tr: ABRAHAM, on entering Canaan, is first introduced into its northern part, according to Bereshit Rabba sect. 39. The text reads as follows: "God said to Abraham, לך לך, go yourself; the words are doubled because of the double journey, one from Aram Naharaim and the other from Aram Nahor. While Abraham was in Aram Naharaim and Aram Nahor, he saw men eating, drinking and making merry, and he said: let my portion not be in this land. But after he came to the Tyrians' ladder [צור לסולמה של], he saw men busy with planting, tilling and vintage, and then he said: let my portion be in this land." §. He who calls Abraham Abram sins against an affirmative precept, Jerusalem Berakhot p. 3, ch. 4. Nor are Sarai and Sarah, or Jacob and Israel, to be so named (ibid.). §. On how Abraham resisted idolatry, see Stars, etc. §. That the Jews are the seed of Abraham they boast greatly: Bava Metzia fol. 83.1. There is a story about R. Yochanan ben Matthia, who said to his son, "Go and hire labourers for us." He went and bargained with them for their living; when he came back to his father, the father said to him: "My son, although your banquets are equal to the banquets of Solomon, you do not yet perform your duty well enough, since they are the sons of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob," etc. Hence also in John 8:33 they cry out, We are the seed of Abraham. To this, however, it may be replied that in the very pandects there stands (Shabbat fol. 53.1): "The merit of the fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, ceased from the days of the prophet Hosea," etc. So you have nothing more to boast of. §. God visited Abraham, sick with the pain of circumcision, and asked how he was. Rashi on Gen. 18:1, and Bereshit Katanna in the place. §. The devil accused Abraham before God, just as he accused Job; but in order to show his integrity God wished to test him by the sacrifice of his son. Sanhedrin, sect. "These are the strangled." §. Abraham did not keep the Sabbath. Bereshit Katanna on Gen. 2:3. Abraham was an astrologer. See Astrologer.

units.la: ACON יבין est Ptolomais Iosephi. de bello lib.2. c.17. Vsque ad Aconem extendebatur terra Israelitica secundum illud in Hierof. Schevii sol.35.3. R. Iose Ben Chanania exosculatus est fornicem Aconis, & dixit; Hucusque est terra Israelitica. §. R. Simeon bibit vinum Acone, quod fecit ut dubitatum fuerit an sit intra terram nec ne. H.Challah f.60.2. vid. Iuchasin sol.71.1. §. Balneum Veneris erat Acone Avoda Sarah c.3.§.4. Miratus est R. Iehuda quòd viderit incolas Acone in immunditie maßas suas pinsere, cùm tamen æstimabantur esse in terra Israelitica, ( & proindè ad munditiem obseruandam obstricturi) Bab. Sanhed. f. 5. 2.
units.tr: ACCO [עכו], which is Ptolemais of Josephus, On the War bk. 2, ch. 17. The land of Israel extended as far as Acco, according to what is said in Jerusalem Sheviit fol. 35.3: "R. Jose ben Chanania kissed the vault of Acco and said: thus far is the land of Israel." §. R. Simeon drank wine at Acco, which made people doubt whether it was within the land or not. Jerusalem Challah f. 60.2. See Yuchasin fol. 71.1. §. The bath of Venus was at Acco. Avodah Zarah ch. 3, §4. R. Yehudah was astonished that he saw the inhabitants of Acco kneading their dough in uncleanness, although they were reckoned to be in the land of Israel (and therefore bound to observe cleanness). Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 5.2.

units.la: ACCVMBENDI ritus dum cibum capiebant, ex his elici poterit. Gloss. in Beracot sol. 46. 2. Soliti sunt comedere discumbentes, & reclinati in latus sinistrum, & pedibus ad terram, singuli per lectos singulos; At cùm forent שתי משת duo lectuli (inquit Gemara) ille qui primus erat sedit summus, & secundus ab eo לבעלה היםנו sedit supra eum, ita (sicuti Gloss addit) ut lectus secundi fuerit juxta cervical primi. (Cùm tres forent, dignissimus discubuit in medio, secundus ab eo supra eum, & tertius infra, siue ut Gloss. discubuit juxta pedes primi. Additur denique loc. cit. in Gloss. quod si dignissimus velit loqui cùm secundo ab eo, necesse est ut erigat se ab accubitu suo & erectus sedeat, nam quamdiu manet reclinatus non poterit colloqui cum eo, quia secundus est post occiput primi. Hac ratione discumbentibus Christo & discipulis Ioh. xiii. Petrus accubuit à tergo Christi, & Iohannes à sinu. Iohannes in sinu Christi, & Christus in sinu Petri. Hic etiam notare potes mensam ordinariam Pharisæi vel discipuli sapientum parvæ admodum magnitudinis fuisse, ita ut plures quàm tres illi vix assidere potuerint, secundùm illius descriptionem quam habemus in Bava Bathra sol. 57. 2. Qualis est mensa discipuli sapientum? שני שלש
units.tr: Of the custom of reclining while they took their food, something may be gathered from these passages. Gloss on Berakhot, fol. 46. 2. They used to eat reclining, leaning on the left side, with their feet towards the ground, each man on a separate couch. But when there were two couches (says the Gemara), the one who was first sat highest, and the second sat above him [לבעלה], so that (as the Gloss adds) the couch of the second was next to the pillow of the first. (When there were three, the most honoured reclined in the middle, the second above him, and the third below, or, as the Gloss has it, reclined beside the feet of the first. The Gloss adds, in the same place, that if the most honoured wished to speak with the second, he had to raise himself from his couch and sit upright, for as long as he remained reclining he could not converse with him, since the second was behind the head of the first. By this arrangement Peter reclined behind Christ, and John on his breast, when Christ and the disciples reclined at table (John xiii). John was in Christ's bosom, and Christ in Peter's bosom. Here you may also note that the ordinary table of a Pharisee or a disciple of the wise was very small, so that scarcely more than three could sit beside it, according to the description we have in Bava Bathra, fol. 57. 2. What is the table of a disciple of the wise? [שני שלש]

units.la: Due partes de tribus strata sunt mappa, & tertia pars nuda est, & super istam partem dispositæ sunt scutellæ & olera, ושבעתו מבחוץ annulus autem mensa erat ab extra. Admodum parvæ debuerunt esse illæ mensæ si annulis illas suspendere voluerunt, prout docet Glossa hunc usum annulos habuisse, ne scilicet mensæ tàm facilè immunditiem contraherent. Ad extraordinarios verò usus, ut in paschatis convivio laxiores adhibuerunt mensas, quas ita suspendere non licuit. Accubitus in cibo capiendo securitatem denotavit, Beracot f.42.1. quòd accubitus factus fuerit ad latus sinistrum etiam confirmatur à Maymon. in Chametz Vmatza c. 7. Cl. Buxtorf. viii. differtat. 306.
units.tr: Two parts of the three are covered with a cloth, and the third part is bare, and upon that part are set the dishes and the vegetables; [ושבעתו מבחוץ] but the ring was on the outside of the table. Those tables must have been very small if they meant to hang them up by rings, as the Gloss teaches, that rings were used so that the tables would not so easily contract uncleanness. For more unusual occasions, as at the Passover feast, they used larger tables, which could not be hung up in this way. That reclining while taking food denoted security is shown by Beracot, fol. 42. 1. That the reclining was done on the left side is also confirmed by Maimonides, Chametz Umatza, ch. 7. See Buxtorf, Dissertation 8, 306.

units.la: אכסניא Acsania, Prout observavi aliquando sumitur, pro regis Iudæorum exercitu qui ad expeditionem progreditur, aut per hunc vel illum locum transit; in Demai cap. 3. dicitur licëre exercitum alere τα Demai, (vid. f. 1.) si alimentum intranseundum efflagitet,vid.Bartenoram in loc.
units.tr: Acsania: as I have sometimes observed, this word is used of the army of the kings of Judah when it advances on an expedition or passes through this or that place. In Demai ch. 3 it is said that it is lawful to feed the army from the Demai produce (see f. 1) if the army demands provisions for passing through. See Bartenora on the passage.

units.la: אין אנו אחראין לרמאי in Demai cap.3.§.5. significat nullam habemus cautionem de futuro damno respectu illorum qui fraudibus utuntur. Wir haben keine Versprechung für Schaden / in ansehen der jenigen die betriegen wollen.
units.tr: "We are not responsible for a deceiver" [אין אנו אחראין לרמאי] in Demai ch. 3 §5 means that we have no guarantee against future loss with respect to those who use fraud. (German: "We give no promise of compensation for loss, with regard to those who want to cheat.")

units.la: Adam creatus fuit in ipso loco in quo deinde ædificatum fuit altare, ut idem esset ipsi locus expiationis quàm creationis. Maymon.
units.tr: Adam was created in the very place where the altar was afterwards built, so that the place of atonement was the same as the place of his creation. Maimonides.

units.la: in Beth Habechc. 2. Iuchafin fol. 9. 1. Midrafch Tillim fol. 41. 2. §. Eft qui opinatur veftimenta ifta Adami, quæ vocantur כתנות יור fuiffe é pilis camelorum. Berefchit Rab. §. 20. In lege R. Meir invenerunt scriptum (annotatum in margine) אור כתנות veftes lucis, (pro כתנות עור veftibus pelliceis:) R. Ifaac dicit, quod fuerint ficuti tenuia ifta linea veftimenta, quæ à Beihfchean afferuntur. R. Samuel Bar Nachman dicit, erant מצער גבליים de pilis camelorum, & leporum. §. Fabulantur Vajikfa Rabba fect. 14. Adamum primò androgynum creatum fuiffe, deindè Deum illum diffecuiffe, & ex una parte mafculum ex altera vero fæminam confecifle. §. Adam primus à fine mundi ufque ad alterum finem creatus fuit, poftquam autem in peccatum lapfus eft, minoravit eum Deus; Sanhed.fect. אחר דיני מכוכות Talibus hyperbolicis loquutionibus, denotant excellentem naturam Adami ante lapfum; vid. Gloff. ad cap. 11. Sanhed. §. Adamus fuit creatus facie verfus orientem difpofita, ut folem afpiceret orientem. Bechai in Deut. 3. 23. §. Per centum & triginta annos quibus Adam feparatus fuit ab Eva genuit impuros fpiritus. Erubbin cap. 2. Hi funt plagæ hominum quatenus tanquam filii eius prodierunt מצר לילית רבתא ולילית זעירתא ex Lilit maiore & Lilit minore. Tzeror Hammor in Lev. fect. אישה כיתורע §. De Adami peccati in pofteros derivatione vid. Peccatum originale &c. §. Adam omnia perdidit לאותו מיתה וגורם צרויק & illi justo fuit causa mortis. Midrasch C. helet ad Ecclesiast. 7. v.14. vid. Cl. Buxt. in אדם. De Eva vid.5.1. De Creatione Adami vid. Creationem. De Adamo sequentia habet Baal Hatturim Comment. in Gen. אדם vocatur quia Deus ipsum creavit ex terra, quæ vocatur אדמה. Adam per Notaricon est אפר Cinis, דם Sanguis, מרה Fel; quia omnes homines ex his constant. Alii Kabbalistæ insulsè dicunt, tres literas in אדם significare אדם דויד משיח Adam, David, Messias, quasi hinc concludi posset, Adami Spiritum in Davidem, Davidis in Messiam migrasse.
units.tr: In Beth Habechirah ch. 2, Iuchasin fol. 9.1, Midrash Tillim fol. 41.2 §: some hold that those garments of Adam, which are called כתנות אור [coats of skin], were made of camels' hair. Bereshit Rabba §20: In the lore of R. Meir they found it written (noted in the margin) אור כתנות, garments of light (instead of כתנות עור, garments of skin). R. Isaac says that they were like those fine linen garments which are brought from Beth-she'an. R. Samuel bar Nachman says they were of camel's and hare's hair. §: Vayikra Rabba sect. 14 invents fables: that Adam was first created androgynous, and then God split him apart and made a male from one side and a female from the other. §: Adam was the first to be created from one end of the world to the other; but after he fell into sin, God diminished him. Sanhedrin sect. אחר דיני מכוכות. By such hyperbolical expressions they denote the excellent nature of Adam before the fall; see Gloss on Sanhedrin ch. 11. §: Adam was created with his face turned toward the east, so that he might look upon the rising sun. Bachai on Deut. 3.23. §: During the hundred and thirty years in which Adam was separated from Eve, he begot unclean spirits. Erubin ch. 2. These are the plagues of men, insofar as they came forth as his sons, מצר לילית רבתא ולילית זעירתא, from Lilith the greater and Lilith the lesser. Tzeror Hammor on Lev. sect. אישה כיתורע. On the derivation of Adam's sin to his posterity, see Original Sin, etc. §: Adam lost everything, לאותו מיתה וגורם, and was the cause of death to that righteous man. Midrash Qoheleth on Eccles. 7.14. See Cl. Buxtorf under Adam. On Eve see 5.1. On the creation of Adam see Creation. Concerning Adam the following is found in Baal Hatturim, Commentary on Genesis: Adam is so called because God created him from the earth, which is called אדמה. By notarikon, Adam is אפר, ashes; דם, blood; מרה, gall, because all men consist of these. Other Kabbalists foolishly say that the three letters of Adam signify Adam, David, Messiah, as if it could be concluded from this that the spirit of Adam passed into David, and the spirit of David into the Messiah.

units.la: ADAR mensis,quarto quoque anno duplex est, primus vocatur אדר ראשון Adar primus, vel aliquandò simpliciter אדר, secundus verò ואדר Masseçet Megillah in pluribus locis præcipuè c.1.4. §. Si novilunium mensis אדר inciderit in Sabbatum, legunt sectionem de siclis (Exod.30. 11.) si inciderit in medium Sabbathi expectant donec Sabbathum transierit. In Sabbatho secundo huius mensis, legunt sect. זכור (Deut.24.17.) In Sabbatho tertio sect. de vacca rufa. Quarto sect. quæ incipit à cap. 10. Exod. Quinto iterum redeunt ad legendas השנים Haphtaroth. Megillah c.3.4.
units.tr: The month ADAR, in every fourth year, is double. The first is called Adar Rishon, first Adar, or sometimes simply Adar; the second is Ve-Adar. Tractate Megillah in many places, especially ch. 1.4 §. If the new moon of the month Adar falls on the Sabbath, they read the section about the shekels (Exod. 30.11); if it falls in the middle of the Sabbath, they wait until the Sabbath is over. On the second Sabbath of this month they read the section Zachor (Deut. 24.17). On the third Sabbath, the section about the red heifer. On the fourth, the section beginning at ch. 10 of Exodus. On the fifth they again return to reading the Haphtaroth. Megillah ch. 3.4.

units.la: ADEPS intestinorum, ad esum àDeo prohibitus est, quia nimium saturat, concoctionem impedit, sanguinemque frigidum & crassum generat. More Nevoch. iii.48.
units.tr: The fat of the entrails was forbidden by God as food, because it satiates too much, hinders digestion, and generates cold and thick blood. Guide of the Perplexed iii.48.

units.la: ADOLESCENTVLA, Græcè νεανίσκος, ita vocatur quandò duodecim annos complevit.
units.tr: ADOLESCENTULA, in Greek neaniskos: she is so called when she has completed twelve years.

units.la: Maymon in Ifchut.cap.2. Filia à die nativitatis fuæ usquedum compleat duodecim annos vocatur תינוקת או קטנה parvula aut puellula. At cum expievit duodecim annos & diem unum נקראת נערה vocatur adolescentula. vid. etiam Pubertas. Hoc etiam Evangelista obfervavit Marc. v. poftquam enim Iairi filiam adolefcentulam fuiffe dixiffet v. 23. verfu deinde 42. addit illam fuiffe ἐτῶν ἀωδϑκα. §. Quanquam Iudæi fatis fint indulgentes in externis amoris fignis, Pater tamen fecundùm ipforum canones filiam amplexationibus & ofculis liberius excipere non debet poftquàm ætatis annum nonû prætergreffa eft, nec mater filium poftquam duodecennis factus eft. Neque adeò muliere inde à tertio ætatis anno ad ullum minifterium, qualia funt exhibendi cibi & potus, manuum lavandarum & fimilium uti licet, five fit adolefcentula five adultior שלא יבוא לידי הרהור ne in perverfas cogitationes incidat. vid. Maym. ad v. 4. cap.vii.Sanhed. item Kiddufchin cap.4.
units.tr: Maimonides in Ishut ch. 2: A girl from the day of her birth until she completes twelve years is called תינוקת או קטנה, a little child or a little girl. But when she has completed twelve years and one day, she is called נערה, an adolescent girl. See also Puberty. The Evangelist also observed this in Mark 5. For after he had said in v. 23 that Jairus' daughter was an adolescent girl, then in v. 42 he adds that she was ἐτῶν δώδεκα, twelve years old. §: Although the Jews are fairly indulgent in outward signs of affection, a father according to their canons ought not to embrace and kiss his daughter too freely once she has passed the ninth year of her age, nor a mother her son once he has become twelve. Nor is it lawful for a woman, from the third year of a child's age onward, to perform any service such as serving food and drink, or washing hands, and the like, whether she is an adolescent or older, שלא יבוא לידי הרהור, lest she fall into lewd thoughts. See Maimonides on v. 4, ch. 7, Sanhedrin; likewise Kiddushin ch. 4.

units.la: DE ADVLTERIO, inceftu, fornicatione, prolixè Maymon. ad cap.vii. Sanhed. v.4. Summa eft, in inceftu nihil interesse five mixtio fiat prout folet, five aliter. Idem etiam obfervari in illo qui cum mafculo aut beftia rem habet. In actibus illis diftinguendum effe inter משמש qui eft האכר כל המכנים & inter מערה qui eft העשרה כל המכנים. Ad fupplicium alicui irrogandum non requiritur feminis effufio הוצאת שכבת זרע, fed tantùm הכנסת האכר. §. Sunt מנאפי ביד ודגל qui per-
units.tr: ON ADULTERY, incest, and fornication, at length in Maimonides on Sanhedrin ch. 7, v. 4. The sum is this: in incest it makes no difference whether intercourse takes place in the usual way or otherwise. The same is observed for one who has relations with a male or with a beast. In these acts one must distinguish between משמש, which is the contact of the organ, and מערה, which is the insertion of the organ. For inflicting punishment on someone, the emission of seed, הוצאת שכבת זרע, is not required, but only the הכנסת האבר, the insertion of the member. §: There are those who commit adultery מנאפי ביד ודגל, with hand and finger, who

units.la: sonam interdictam violant contrectatione lascivia, nutuque impudico: Qui etiam flagris caeduntur. §. Praecepto Lev.18.6. etiam omnia irritamenta libidinis prohibentur, ut ne formam quidem personae interdictae intueri liceat cum animo voluptatem suam explendi: (Confer Matth. 5. 28.) Ideoque Rabbini verbum dici putant, quasi ex forma faciei voluptatem cepit: (vel ut Plautus, oculis epulis dedit.) §. Qui constuprat innuptam flagellandus est. §. Quidam Rabbi quoties ex oratorio domum rediret, chirothecis aut etiam manibus sororis suae osculum figebat. Is destitit tandem, postquam vidit id nullo respectu licitum esse. §. Mulier adultera interdicta est viro, nisi si vi compressa sit, &c. §. Christus Iudaicam gentem vocat Math. xii. 39. quod bene de illa natione secundum literam potest intelligi, nam tunc temporis ita multiplicati fuerunt adulteri, ut Rabban Iochanan Ben Saccai (de quo vid. f. 1.) qui post excidium templi & urbis adhuc vixit, coactus fuerit decreto Synedrii aquas amaras ad probationem suspectarum ob adulterium institutas, abrogare; quia plurimi erant adulterii palam. vid. Sotah. sol.47. 1. Maym. in Sotah cap.3. illum autem processum quem in suspecta muliere potanda habuerunt, ex ipsamet Rubrica inferius apud aquas amaras referemus. §. Punit Deus adulterium morte Le.xx.10. At dicunt magistri omnis mors cuius est mentio in lege simpliciter (absque definitione generis mortis) strangulatio est, verum excipiunt נשואה בת ישראל כחנק Si filia Israelita nupta est & adultera fit, strangulanda est, ארוסה בסקרלה si vero desponsata tantum est lapidanda. Filia Sacerdotis nupta si adultera lapidanda, cum desponsata tantum comburenda. Sanhed. sol. 51. 2. Quaeri hic potest an adultera illa quae Ioh. viii. ad Christum deducta fuit, nupta vel desponsata fuerit? ‏‎ ‎. Accusatores eius v. 5. dicunt Moysen praecepisse ut tales lapidarentur, ex modo dictis itaque arguo, illam fuisse vel Israelitisam nondum junctam viro, sed tantum desponsatam; vel Sacerdotissam nuptam: quoniam in illas exercebatur supplicium lapidationis. De Fornicatione vid. f. 1.
units.tr: violate a forbidden person by lascivious touching and shameless nodding; these too are beaten with rods. §: By the precept of Leviticus 18.6, all incitements to lust are also forbidden, so that it is not even permitted to look upon the form of a forbidden person with the intention of satisfying one's pleasure (compare Matt. 5.28). Therefore the rabbis think the verb is used as if he took pleasure from the form of the face (or, as Plautus has it, he fed his eyes with a feast). §: One who ravishes an unmarried woman is to be flogged. §: A certain Rabbi, whenever he returned home from the house of prayer, would press a kiss upon his sister's gloves or even her hands; he finally stopped, after he saw that this was not permitted in any respect. §: An adulterous woman is forbidden to her husband, unless she was forced to submit, etc. §: Christ calls the Jewish nation an adulterous generation (Matt. 12.39), which can well be understood of that nation in the literal sense, for at that time adulteries had so multiplied that Rabban Johanan ben Zakkai (on whom see f. 1), who lived on after the destruction of the temple and city, was compelled by a decree of the Sanhedrin to abolish the bitter waters instituted for testing wives suspected of adultery, because there were very many cases of open adultery. See Sotah fol. 47.1; Maimonides on Sotah ch. 3. We shall give the procedure they followed in making a suspected woman drink, from the rubric itself below under bitter waters. §: God punishes adultery with death, Lev. 20.10. But the masters say that every death mentioned in the law without specification is strangulation; yet they except: נשואה בת ישראל כחנק, if an Israelite daughter is married and commits adultery, she is to be strangled; ארוסה בסקילה, but if she is only betrothed, she is to be stoned. If a priest's daughter is married and commits adultery, she is to be stoned; but if only betrothed, she is to be burned. Sanhedrin fol. 51.2. Here one may ask whether that adulterous woman who was brought to Christ in John 8 was married or betrothed. Her accusers, v. 5, say that Moses commanded that such women be stoned. From what has been said I therefore argue that she was either an Israelite woman not yet joined to a husband but only betrothed, or a married priest's daughter, since the punishment of stoning was practiced on those. On Fornication see f. 1.

units.la: ÆGROTVM in Sabbatho ungere permisit R. Meir. למזוג יין ושמן miscendo oleum cum vino, cum vero ipse decumbere, ut idem ipsi fieret non permisit. H. Beracot c.1. p.2. vid. etiam Maym. Hal. Milah c.2.7. Quod erat dispensatio satis laxa de accurata illa abstinentia medendi in ipso Sabbatho: nam alias videmus Christum non parum invidiae apud Iudaeos sibi conflasse, quod in Sabbatho aliquos sanare non horruerit. De his habes plura in Sabbatho &c. §. Post applicata aegrotis remedia in usu habuerunt dicere Surge à morbo tuo; sic ad profluviosam Bab. Schabb. f.110. in fine omnium remediorum dixerunt קום מזיב surge à profluvio tuo: quod idem est ac si dixissent, opto ut surgas à profluvio tuo. Christus etiam dixit ad puellulam Marc. v. 41. טליתא קומי Ταλιθα κουμι, idiomate quidem vulgari sed non sensu, ex illis enim verbis non aliquod votum sed imperans vigor & authoritas emicuit. §. Ille ægrotus apud Iudæos iam magnam valetudinis partem acquisivisse, & in tuto esse existimabatur, qui cibum sumpsit; ita Hierof. Beracot sol. 9. 4. concludunt discipuli à R. Chanania missi, filium R. Gamalielis qui decumbebat, convaluisse, Quia illa hora requisiuit cibum. Si nobis hariolari licet, hæc fuit ratio, cur restituta puellâ Marc. v. Christus deinde v. 43. iusserit ut cibus ipsi porrigeretur: ne scilicet adstantes de persecta puellæ valetudine dubitarent.§. Quando preces pro ægrotantibus fundebat R. Chanina Ben Dufa, dicere solitus est; Hic victurus est, Hic vero moriturus, quærentibus unde hoc dignosceret, respondit אם שגורה תפלתי בפי Si oratio mihi expedita est in ore cognosco eum esse acceptum, sin minus, scio moriturum. Mass. Beracot. c. 5. 5.
units.tr: R. Meir permitted anointing a sick man on the Sabbath, by mixing oil with wine [למזוג יין ושמן], but he did not permit it to be done to himself when he lay sick. H. Beracot c.1 p.2; see also Maym. Hal. Milah c.2.7. This was a fairly lax dispensation from the strict abstinence from healing on the Sabbath itself. Otherwise we see that Christ stirred up no small hatred against himself among the Jews, because he did not shrink from healing some people on the Sabbath. You will find more on this in Sabbatho &c., §. After applying remedies to the sick, they were accustomed to say Rise from your sickness. So in the case of the woman with a flux, Bab. Schabb. f.110, at the end of all the remedies they said קום מזיב [qum mizib], rise from your flux, which is the same as if they had said I wish that you may rise from your flux. Christ also said to the little girl, Mark 5:41, טליתא קומי [talitha qumi; Ταλιθα κουμι], in a vernacular idiom but not in its sense. For those words did not express some wish, but a commanding power and authority shone forth from them. §. Among the Jews, a sick man who had taken food was thought to have already regained a great part of his health and to be out of danger. So the disciples sent from R. Chanania in Hierof. Beracot sol. 9.4 conclude that the son of R. Gamaliel, who lay sick, had recovered, because at that hour he asked for food. If we may conjecture, this was the reason why Christ, after the girl had been restored (Mark 5), then ordered (v. 43) that food be given to her: namely, so that those standing by should not doubt the girl's perfect health. §. When R. Chanina Ben Dufa prayed for the sick, he used to say: This one is going to live; this one is going to die. When people asked how he knew this, he replied: אם שגורה תפלתי בפי [im shegurah tefillati befi], If my prayer comes readily to my mouth, I know that he is accepted; if not, I know that he will die. Mass. Beracot c.5.5.

units.la: ÆMVLARVM fœminarum filii (1. Sam. 1. 6.) fuerunt בית עמובי familia Annubæa è Beth Zeboim, & בית נקיפי familia Nekiphæa è Beth Koschefch, & tamen Sacerdotium magnum obtinuerunt nepotes ipsorum. Hierof. Ievamot sol. 3. 1. §. de æmulatione mariti erga uxorem vid. aquas amaras.
units.tr: The sons of the rival wife (1 Sam. 1:6) belonged to the family of the Annubites [בית עמובי], familia Annubæa, from Beth Zeboim, and to the family of the Nekiphites [בית נקיפי] from Beth Koschefch; and yet their grandsons obtained the great priesthood. Hierof. Ievamot sol. 3.1. On the jealousy of a husband toward his wife, see aquas amaras.

units.la: ÆGYPTIOS coluisse signum arietis docet nos lex divina (secundùm expositionem Onkeli,) ac propterea non solùm prohibitum
units.tr: The divine law teaches us that the Egyptians worshipped the sign of the ram (according to the exposition of Onkelos), and therefore it was not only forbidden among them

units.la: fuisse inter ipsos mactare oves, sed & ovium pastores in summo contemptu & abominatione fuisse. In Ægypto noluit ossa sua relinqui Iosephus secundum Iudæos propter has rationes, est quia ipsi admodum grave fuisset, subterranea & molesta illa גלגול revolutione, in terram Canaan ad resurrectionem deferri, nam extra terram sanctam aliquam resurrectionem fore Iudæi negant. vid. Kethubot sol. iii. 1. rationem reddit Maym. in Hal. Melachim. כל השוכן בארץ ישראל עונותיו מחולין שנא' ובל יאטר חליתי Omnium qui terram Israël inhabitant iniquitates condonatas esse, 5. quod dicitur Iesai. 33. 24. Neque dicet habitator agrotus sum: populus habitans in ea levatus erit iniquitate. Ex quo deinde secundùm Maymon. concludunt. Quod ille qui modò ad mensuram quatuor cubitorum ingreditur terram Israelis, jam dignus fiat vita æterna. Qui verò in illa sepelitur, illius peccata expiantur, & locus sepultura ipsi sit loco altaris expiationis: Deut.xxxii.43. ac terram suam populumque expiat. Præstare quidem quando quis adhuc vivus in terram sanctam se conferat, si tamen id fieri non posset, ab ipsis Patriarchis nos exemplum habere, id etiam post mortem utile esse. Maymonidis commentator ex Talmude Hierof. insuper aliquid affert quod ad maiorem huius rei dilucidationem facit. Bar Kria, inquit, cum R. Eleasaro deambulavit באיסטרין in publicis stratis, & viderunt arculas advectas ex locis peregrinis. Dixit R. Kria Eleasaro: Quid prodest ipsis (tantis sumptibus huc perlati) Quin ego contra tales illud Ierem.2.7. usurpo, haereditatem meam posuistis; dum vivebatis in abominationem, nunc venitis, & contaminatis terram postquam mortui estis. Respondit Eleasar, quamprimum ad hanc regionem pertinent נושלין גוש עפר ומניחין על ארונו Sumunt glebam friabilem & ponunt eam in feretrum, freti dicto Deut.xxxii.43. propitius erit terra sua. Nisi plane siniistre auguramur, fuerunt feretra illa allata ex Ægypto, nec aliter R. Kria illum locum Ieremiae bene applicare potuit; qui enim illuc iverant להשתקע stabilem sedem fingendi causa, secundum Maymonidem idem fecerunt; ac si terram Canaam contemptui & abominationi habuissent, quia incolarum Ægypti opera erant מקולקלות יותר מכל ארצות depravata & conspurcata pro operibus omnium reliquarum gentium; partim vero quia sanctam gentem miseris modis prophana afflictaverat natio: Hinc ille Canon מותר לשכון בכל הארץ חוץ : מארץ מצרים licitum est habitare in universo mundo excepta Ægypto. Quae perpendens R. Vrian, hanc obiectionem ad marginem apposuit, in Hal. Melach. c.5. יש תימה על קהילות שוכנים שם ועל רבינו המחבר שהלך לגור : שם Mirari ergo subit de totu Ecclesias ibi degentibus, item de scriptore nostro (Maymonide) qui ibi peregrinatus est. Quod quidem verum est, nam fuit Maymonides per plurimos annos in aula Ægyptiaca, & quidem regius medicus; ut ex propriis literis quas ad Samuelem Abben Tybbon dedit videre est. Sed Doctor Vrian debuisset etiam observare, nullam esse tam generalem regulam quæ non suas exceptiones admittat; Itaque respondemus huius canonis vim aliquo modo cessasse, postquàm Iudæi laribus pulsi, & sanctuarium devastatum fuit. 2.
