Chanania erat און איש Civis urbis Ono. Iuch sin ubi anteà. Existimant Talmud. hanc urbem iam à diebus Iofuæ muris cinctam fuisse,at flammis absumptam in bello Gibeithico. vid. l. c.
units.tr: Ono, a city that lay three miles from Lydda. "Rabbi Jacob said: Lydda and Ono are three miles apart," etc. "Rabbi Simai and Rabbi Zadok professed in the meantime: the year is intercalated in Lydda, and they kept the Sabbath in [זמן]," etc. Chullin fol. 39.2; Bab. Ketubot f. 3.2; Chullin fol. 56.2; Megillah, Hierosolymitan, fol. 70.1. Rabbi Chanania was a man of Ono, a citizen of the city of Ono. Iuchasin, where cited above. The Talmudists think this city was already walled in the days of Joshua, but was burnt with fire in the war of Gibeah. See ibid.

units.la: Aquæ ineptæ ad aspersionem immundorum quænam? vid. Immundorum &c.
units.tr: What waters were unsuitable for sprinkling the unclean? See Unclean, etc.

units.la: Aquæ amaræ potatio, in probatione mulieris ob adulterium suspectæ prolixè in Sotah à Maymonide describitur; Nos hic integram fermè de hac ceremonia rubricam ex Mischna afferemus. Qui zelo prosequitur uxorem suam Num. 5. 14. R. Eliefer dicit, si zelum suum ipsi ostendit coram duobus, ipsam ex ore unius potare potest, aut ex semet ipso. At R. Iehosua vult, ut si ipsam zeletur coram duobus, ipsam quoque ex duorum ore potet.
units.tr: The drinking of the bitter water, in the proving of a woman suspected of adultery, is described at length in Sotah by Maimonides. Here we shall give almost the whole rubric of this ceremony from the Mishnah. "If a spirit of jealousy comes upon a man" (Num. 5:14). Rabbi Eliezer says: if he shows his jealousy before two witnesses, she may drink from the mouth of one of them, or from his own. But Rabbi Joshua holds that if he is jealous of her before two, she shall also drink from the mouth of the two.

units.la: §. לוה כיצד בקנאי Quando (maritus) Zelotypus dicitur? Si uxori coram duobus dicit, ne colloquere cum N. & tamen cum ipso colloquitur. Hucusque tamen licita est domui suæ, & ad esum oblationis admittitur; Sed si cum illo aliquod latibulum ingreditur, & cum eo in illo loco tantùm moratur, ut possit immunda fieri, אסורה לביתה domui suæ illicita est (non ampliùs marito nisi accedente potu aquæ amaræ licita est,) nec ad oblationis esum admittitur. tur, & si moritur eius maritus, calceum extrahit, nec à defuncti fratre ducitur. (tempus verò ad illam immundam reddendam sufficit, si tantundem duraverit, ac requiritur ad ovum coquendum & absorbendum, inquit Maym.)
units.tr: §. "When is a husband called jealous?" If he says to his wife before two witnesses, "Do not speak with N.," and yet she speaks with him, she is still permitted to her house and admitted to eat of the offering. But if she goes into some hiding place with him and stays there with him only long enough for her to become unclean, she is forbidden to her house (she is no longer permitted to her husband unless the bitter water is drunk), and she is not admitted to eat of the offering. ... And if her husband dies, she removes her shoe and is not taken in marriage by the dead man's brother. (The time sufficient to render her unclean is, if it lasted as long as is needed to boil and swallow an egg, says Maimonides.)

units.la: §. Hæ illicitæ sunt ad oblationem comedendam; quæ dicit marito, ego tibi immunda sum. Et quæ dicit ego poculum amaritudinis non bibam; Item illa quam maritus potare non vult; Item cum qua maritus concumbit dum in via sunt ad Senatum petendum, qui in illo tractu est. Hinc discipuli duo Sapientum illos comitari debent, ne forte cum illa congrediatur.
units.tr: §. These are forbidden to eat of the offering: she who says to her husband, "I am unclean to you"; she who says, "I will not drink the cup of bitterness"; likewise she whom the husband does not wish to give to drink; and she with whom the husband lies while they are on the way to seek the Sanhedrin, which sits in that district. Hence two disciples of the sages ought to accompany them, lest perhaps she meet with him.

units.la: §. Postquàm ad Senatum magnum, qui Hierosolymis sedet adducta est, ipsi eadem ratione terrorem incutiunt, ac faciunt in negotio testium qui de crimine capitali testantur, ipsique dicunt בתי הרבה יין עושה שחוק עושה הרבה ילדות עושה הרבה שכנים רעים עושים עשי לשמו הגדול Filia mea, quod (Maritus Zelotypiâ te prosequitur) multum vini (quo te ingurgitare solebas) effecit, immoderatus risus, facundi partus, improborum vicinorum multitudo in causa sunt, Ede itaque confessionem nomini Dei maximi, sicuti à talibus mulieribus lex id postulat, ne per aquas deleantur. Dicunt denique ipsi plurima alia, ad quæ audienda nec ipsa nec familia eius paterna sufficiunt; (Vt illam ad confessionem adigere & à potu si rea esset deterrêre possint.)
units.tr: §. After she has been brought before the Great Sanhedrin, which sits at Jerusalem, they strike terror into her in the same way as they do in the matter of witnesses who testify to a capital crime, and they say to her: "My daughter, because much wine (which you used to guzzle) produces mirth, and much wine produces childishness, and many evil neighbours are the cause, make confession to the name of the great God, as the law requires of such women, lest you be destroyed by the waters." They also say many other things, to hear which neither she nor her paternal family is equal, so that they might compel her to confession and deter her from drinking, if she were guilty.

units.la: §. Si ad hæc Senatus verba dicit immunda sum, instrumentum dotis eius disrumpitur, & à marito dimittitur. Si verò asseverat se mundam esse, illam ducunt ad portam templi orientalem, quæ est ad ostium portæ Nicanoris. (Maymonides hic notat, illos mulierem à Senatu non statim & recta via ad hunc locum deduxisse, sed aliquo circuitu ut sos esse, si forte inter eundum sententiam mutare vellet.) Duxerunt autem illam ad portam Nicanoris, ut in frequentiori populi corona potaretur, nam secundum effatum R. Schemajæ הוא משמש כל כניסה ויציאה של עזרה Hac porta omnes ingrediebantur & egrediebantur atrium magnum. Ibi itaque omnium oculis expositia tegitur vestimentis nigris. Si ornata est aureis ornamentis, catellis, monilibus, annulis, ea omnia ipsi detrahunt, ad ipsam turpem reddendam, (animum eius humiliandum.) Deinde Sacerdos profert הכל מצרי funem vimineum, illoque supra vestimenta eam cingit. Quivis qui eam videre desiderat ipsam tunc videre potest, exceptis servis & ancillis eius מפני שלבה גם בתן quia animum respectu eorum efferre possset. Omnes etiam mulieres ad eam conspiciendam admittuntur, ut in hoc exemplo erudiantur.
units.tr: §. If at these words of the Senate she says I am unclean, the deed of her dowry is torn up and she is dismissed by her husband. But if she insists that she is clean, they lead her to the east gate of the Temple, which is at the door of the gate of Nicanor. (Maimonides notes here that they did not take the woman from the Senate straight to this place by the shortest route, but by some roundabout way, so that she might change her mind if she wished while on the way.) They led her to the gate of Nicanor so that she might drink before a fuller crowd of people, for according to the saying of R. Schemaja [הוא משמש כל כניסה ויציאה], By this gate all went in and out of the great court. There, displayed before everyone's eyes, she is covered with black garments. If she is adorned with golden ornaments, necklaces, chains and rings, they strip all of these from her, to make her shameful (and to humble her spirit). Then the priest brings out a rope of wicker [הכל מצרי] and girds her with it over her garments. Anyone who wishes to see her may then see her, except her male and female servants, [מפני שלבה גם בתן] because she might lift up her heart in their presence. All women are also admitted to look at her, so that they may be instructed by this example.

units.la: §. במרה שאדם מודד בה מודרין לו Quâ ratione homo mensurat ea quoque ipsi mensuratur: illa anteà se ornaverat ad transgressionem: Deus autem nunc illam sædam reddit. Illa se detexit, Deus nunc illam quoque detegit.
units.tr: §. [במרה שאדם מודד בה מודרין לו] By the measure with which a man measures, it is measured to him again. She had previously adorned herself for transgression; now God makes her foul. She uncovered herself; now God uncovers her too.

units.la: Femur eius transgressionis principium fecit, illud sequutus est venter: ita in potatione aquæ amaræ femur eius primò consumetur, & deinde etiam eius venter, usquedum planè nihil de corpore eius superfit. Sotah. cap. 1.
units.tr: Her thigh was the beginning of her transgression, and the belly followed it; so in the drinking of the bitter water her thigh is consumed first, and then her belly too, until nothing at all of her body remains. Sotah, chapter 1.

units.la: §. Deinde affert Sacerdos בנחתה בתוך מנחת כפיפה מצרית munus eius in corbe vimineo, ipsumque manibus eius imponit, ad ipsam defatigandam, (forsan enim fatigata ad se redit & resipiscere potest.) Omnes oblationes in principio & fine ponuntur in כלי שרת vasa ministerii (vasa ad cultum ordinarium confecta:) Mulieris verò potandæ munus principio reponitur in canistro vimineo, & non nisi in fine in vase ministerii. Omnium מנחות oblationum materia est oleum & thus, omnes מנחות fiunt ex tritico, sed hæc tantùm ex hordeo. Mincha Omer etiamsi ex hordeo fiat, fit tamen ex extruso, cùm hæc ex farina præparetur. Rabban Gamaliel dicit, sicuti opus eius fuit מעשה בהמה opus bestiarum, ita quoque oblationem eius esse cibum bestialem.
units.tr: §. Then the priest presents her offering [בנחתה בתוך מנחת כפיפה מצרית] in a wicker basket and places it in her hands, so that she may be wearied out (for perhaps, being wearied, she will come to herself and be able to repent). All offerings are placed at the beginning and end in the vessels of ministry (vessels made for the ordinary worship). But the offering of the woman to be made to drink is placed at the beginning in a wicker basket, and only at the end in a vessel of ministry. The material of all the offerings is oil and incense; all meal-offerings are made of wheat, but this one only of barley. Even the omer-offering, though it is made of barley, is made of parched grain, whereas this one is prepared from flour. Rabban Gamaliel says that, just as her deed was the deed of beasts, so her offering is beastly food.

units.la: §. Producit etiam Sacerdos scutellam testaceam novam, & ipsi infundit sextarium aquæ מן הכיור ex labro; R. Iuda dicit, sufficit infundere quartarium. Hoc facto ingreditur Sacerdos templum, & ad latus dextrum pergit, ad locum quendam qui habebat אמה על אמה cubitum ad cubitum (locus erat quadraturam habens,) qui tabulâ operiebatur cui infixus erat annulus, apprehendens itaque annulum,tabulam elevat,& super ipsam pulverem sumit; de qua tantum aquæ inspergit, quantum requiritur ut in superficie aquæ observari possit.
units.tr: §. The priest also brings out a new earthen bowl and pours into it a sixth of a measure of water [מן הכיור] from the laver; R. Judah says it is enough to pour in a quarter. This done, the priest enters the Temple and goes to the right side, to a place which had [אמה על אמה] a cubit by a cubit (the place was square), which was covered with a board to which a ring was fixed. Taking hold of the ring, he lifts the board and takes dust from upon it; from this he sprinkles as much water as is needed so that it can be seen on the surface of the water.

units.la: §. Posteà Sacerdos se accingit ad scribendum את מגילה librum eius, loca quæ scribit desumit ex Num. v.19. 20. 21. 22. Illis autem non addit & Respondebit mulier Amen, Amen. Sacerdos non debet scribere super tabulam, aut chartam pergamenam, aut tabulam manualem את הספר על sed super volumen quia dicitur l. c. v. 23. in libro &c. Literas autem exprimit non cum gummi neque vitriolo, neque ullâ aliâ re quæ notat, sed scribet cum atramento, q. d. & delebit, debet scribere ut deleri possit.
units.tr: §. Afterwards the priest sets himself to write [את מגילה] her scroll, taking the words he writes from Num. 5:19, 20, 21, 22. He does not, however, add The woman will answer, Amen, Amen. The priest ought not to write on a tablet, or on parchment, or on a wax tablet [את הספר על] but upon a scroll, because it is said in the same chapter, verse 23, in the book, etc. He does not write the letters with gum, nor with vitriol, nor with any other substance that leaves a mark, but writes with ink, that is, and he shall blot it out; he must write so that it can be blotted out.

units.la: §. Mulier debet Amen dicere ad maledictionem, quando dicit Sacerdos det te Iehova. in maledictionem; debet Amen dicere ad adiurationem Amen ad ex illo viro. Amen ad ex viro alio, Amen quòd non declinavi, neque desponsata neque ducta. Amen quòd me non commaculaverim, sin immunda facta sim, veniant super me omnes illæ maledictiones.
units.tr: §. The woman must say Amen to the curse when the priest says The LORD make you a curse; she must say Amen to the adjuration, Amen to that man, Amen to another man, Amen to I have not turned aside, neither betrothed nor married. Amen to I have not defiled myself; but if I have become unclean, let all those curses come upon me.

units.la: §. In eo consentiunt nullum munus adferri ab illa muliere, quæ vitii accusatur ante desponsationem, aut postquàm expulsa est. Neque ab illa quæ post potationem iterum in Zelotypiam viri incurrit, & denuò ad potationem adducitur. Sotah c. 2.
units.tr: §. They agree that no offering is brought by a woman who is accused of a fault before betrothal, or after she has been dismissed; nor by one who, after drinking, again falls into her husband's jealousy and is again brought to the drinking. Sotah, chapter 2.

units.la: §. Sumit posteà Sacerdos munus eius ex corbe vimineo, & vasi ministerii imponit, deinde coniunctim ea in mulieris manus dat: quò facto manus suas inferius ad illud suffinendum applicat,& deinde illud agitat. (nam non permissum erat ut mulier oblationem propriis viribus agitaret vid. תנופה.) Agitat ita Sacerdos & offert, pugillat & adolet, residuum verò à Sacerdotibus comeditur. Parum refert five camprimò potet, & deinde oblationem eius osserat, sive vice versa.
units.tr: §. Then the priest takes her offering from the wicker basket and places it in the vessel of ministry, and then gives both together into the woman's hands; having done this, he places his own hands beneath to support it, and then waves it. (For a woman was not permitted to wave the offering by her own strength; see [תנופה].) So the priest waves and offers it, takes a handful and burns it on the altar, and the rest is eaten by the priests. It matters little whether she first drinks and then her offering is presented, or the reverse.

units.la: §. Si mulier cùm nondum abrasus est libelluseius, dicit,non bibam, libellus eius absconditur,& munus eius dispergitur super cinerem, nec libello eius possunt aliam mulierem declınantem (ob adulterium suspectam) potare. Si cùm iam abrasus est libellus eius dicit, Ego Immunda sum, aquæ effunduntur, & munus eius dispergitur super cinerem. Si dicit mulier postquàm abrasus est libellus eius, non bibam מערים אותה ומשקין אותה בעל ברחה ipsam ad potum excitant, & nolentem volentem potant.
units.tr: §. If, when her little scroll has not yet been blotted out, she says, I will not drink, her little scroll is hidden and her offering is scattered upon the ashes, and her scroll can no longer be used to make another woman who turns aside (suspected of adultery) drink. If, when her scroll has already been blotted out, she says, I am unclean, the waters are poured out and her offering is scattered upon the ashes. If the woman says, after her scroll has been blotted out, I will not drink, [מערים אותה ומשקין אותה בעל ברחה] they force her and make her drink, whether she is willing or unwilling.

units.la: §. אינה מסכת לשתות (si rea est) vix potum absolvit, cùm statim facies eius pallescit, oculi eius protuberant, tota deinde nervis oppletur, (hoc ita explicant, sicuti aliquando fabri lignarii asseribus florum & aliarum rerum figuram insculpunt, ita etiam inflati & tumescentes nervi faciei mulieris potatæ referunt quandam ramorum & bacillorum speciem. Hoc autem fit si maritus nunquâ coiverit coitu illicito, nam aquæ non explorant si unquâ illius criminis fe reum fecit Maym. Sotah. c.3.) Quòd si accidit, statim illam educere præcipiunt, ne atrium inquinetur. Si ipsi est Iustitia illa ipsi aderit; si iusta est (potatio illa) proderit ipsi per annum unum, per annos duos, per tres annos. ( notant enim retributionem quam mulieres honestæ ex illa potatione sperare potuerunt, non semper potationem statim infequuutam esse. Imò etiam impuris quasdam potationes non subitò nocuisse, qualis autem gradus peccati esse debuerit, ut id acciderèt Magistri non definiunt. )
units.tr: §. [אינה מסכת לשתות] (if she is guilty) she hardly finishes drinking when at once her face turns pale, her eyes bulge, and then her whole body is filled with swelling. They explain this as follows: just as carpenters sometimes carve the figure of flowers and other things into boards, so the swollen and distended veins of the face of the woman who has drunk show a kind of pattern of branches and twigs. This happens, however, only if the husband has never had intercourse with her in an unlawful way, for the waters do not test a woman if she was ever guilty of that crime. (Maimonides, Sotah, chapter 3.) But if it happens, they order that she be led out at once, so that the court is not defiled. If she is guilty, the punishment will come upon her; if she is innocent, that drinking will benefit her for one year, for two years, for three years. (For they note that the reward which honourable women could hope for from that drinking did not always follow immediately upon it; indeed, some drinkings did not at once harm the impure. What degree of sin must have been present for this to happen, the teachers do not define.)

units.la: §. Munus Mulieris potandæ immundum est donec in vasi sanctificetur, & tunc est ut omnes reliquæ oblationes, & redimi potest, & comburi. Hæ sunt quarum oblationes comburuntur, quæ dicit, Immunda sum tibi, & quæ id testibus probare potest. Item quæ dicit non bibam, & maritus eius illam potare non vult. Filiæ Israeliticæ, quæ Sacerdoti nupsit, munus comburitur; filiæ Sacerdotis quæ Israelitæ nupsit munus comeditur. Sotah. cap. 3.
units.tr: §. The offering of the woman who is to drink is unclean until it is sanctified in the vessel, and then it is like all other offerings, and it may be redeemed, and it may be burned. Those whose offerings are burned are: the one who says, I am unclean to you, and who can prove it by witnesses; likewise the one who says she will not drink, and whose husband does not wish her to drink. The offering of an Israelite woman who has married a priest is burned; the offering of a priest's daughter who has married an Israelite is eaten. Sotah, chapter 3.

units.la: §. Hæ sunt quæ non potantur neque cum dote dimittuntur. Desponsata & quæ Leviro nubere debet, vidua summi Sacerdotis, repudiata Sacerdotis vulgaris; uxor alicuius Israelitæ, quæ spuria & Nethinæa est, Item uxor spurii & Nethinæi quæ Israelitis est. Si accidebat ut aliquis viduam novissimè defuncti duceret, quæ à priori marito concepisset, aut fœtum in lucem editum lactaret, illam maritus potare non poterat, ( quia talis nuptias citius celebravit quam permissum erat : decreverunt enim magistri, ut per trimestre expectet. Maym. Gerusalem cap. 11. Ita respectu lactantis per duos annos moras nectere debuit יניקתו ימן זמן שכך quia hoc est tempus lactationis.) Sterilis & anus non potantur nec dotem sumunt, omnes autem reliquæ mulieres, aut poculum bibere debent, aut nullam dotem habebunt.
units.tr: §. These are the ones who are not made to drink, nor are they dismissed with their dowry: a betrothed woman, and one who ought to marry a levir; the widow of the high priest; the divorced woman of an ordinary priest; the wife of any Israelite who is a bastard or a Nethinite; likewise the wife of a bastard or a Nethinite who is married to an Israelite. If it happened that someone married a widow of a man who had just died, who had conceived by her former husband, or who was suckling a child born of that marriage, her husband could not make her drink (because he had celebrated such a marriage sooner than was permitted: for the teachers decreed that he should wait for three months. Maimonides, Jerusalem, chapter 11). Likewise, with regard to a nursing woman, he ought to delay for two years, [יניקתו ימן זמן שכך] because this is the time of nursing. A barren woman and an old woman are not made to drink, nor do they take a dowry; but all other women must either drink the cup or else will have no dowry.

units.la: §. Vxor Sacerdotis potari potest, deindeque ipsi iterum licita est. Vxor Eunuchi etiam potatur.
units.tr: A priest's wife may be made to drink, and afterwards she is again lawful to him. A eunuch's wife may also be made to drink.

units.la: §. Hæ sunt quas Senatus (loco maritorum) zelat,uxor cuius maritus surdus aut fatuus est, Item cuius maritus est in carcere, non ea intentione ut eam potet, sed ut illam illegitimam reddat ad dotem sumendam. Sotah. c.4. כשם שהמים בודקין אותה כך המים בודקין אותו, Sicuti aqua (mulierem suspectam) probant, ita quoque probant ipsum: (id est eandem pœnam sentiet ille qui cum ea rem habuit, si illa moritur, idem quoque ipsi accidit, prout in pari reatu sunt, ita etiam æqualiter puniuntur.) Sicuti illicita est marito, ita quoque omni cum ea concumbenti. Sotah.cap.5.
units.tr: These are the cases in which the Sanhedrin takes the husband's place and acts zealously: a wife whose husband is deaf or insane; likewise a wife whose husband is in prison, not with the intention that she should drink, but so that she is rendered unfit to receive her dowry. Sotah. c.4. [כשם שהמים בודקין אותה כך המים בודקין אותו] Just as the water tests her, so it tests him (that is, the man who had relations with her suffers the same penalty: if she dies, the same thing happens to him, and since they share the same guilt, they are equally punished). Just as she is forbidden to her husband, so she is forbidden to anyone who lies with her. Sotah. cap.5.

units.la: §. Seƈtio de Muliere declinante in omni lingua legi potest. Sotah. c.7.
units.tr: The section on the woman who goes astray can be read in every language. Sotah c.7.

units.la: §. A quo tempore multiplicati sunt Adulteri cessarunt aquæ amaræ, R. Iochanan Ben Saccai abrogavit ipsas fretus dicto Hosea 4.14. Sotah. cap. 9.
units.tr: From the time when adulteries multiplied, the bitter waters ceased. Rabbi Johanan ben Zakkai abolished them, relying on the saying in Hosea 4.14. Sotah cap. 9.

units.la: §. Pro Coronide fit hæc historia. Bab. Berac. sol. 19. 1. Schemaja & Abtalion aderunt Carchemit ancillam libertinam ut potaret aquas amaras. Ardens fuit Zelolypiâ mariti erga hanc suam uxorem, nam quoniam non deprehensa erat in adulterio detecto, potuisset eam dimittere lege traditionali, quæ repudiá permisit extra causam adulterii, aut potuisset eam ad examen aquæ amaræ non adducere, sed nullum argumentum duritiem cordis eius delinire poterat; uxor potum fumere debuit.
units.tr: This story serves as a finale. Bab. Berac. fol. 19.1: Shemaiah and Abtalion came to Carchemith, a freedwoman, to make her drink the bitter waters. The husband burned with jealousy towards this wife of his. Since she had not been caught in adultery, he could have divorced her under the traditional law, which allowed divorce apart from a cause of adultery, or he could have refrained from bringing her to the test of the bitter water. But no argument could soften the hardness of his heart, and the wife had to drink.

units.la: §. Hic ritus plurimas mulieres in officiò continuit, quæ aliàs genio indulsissent; Repudia autem genti Iudaicæ concessa effecerunt ut raro hæc ceremonia peracta fuerit, fi enim animum à muliere aversum habuerunt, facilè causam aliquam separationis repererunt.
units.tr: This rite kept many women within their duty who would otherwise have indulged their desires. But the divorces granted to the Jewish people meant that this ceremony was rarely performed: if husbands had turned against their wives, they easily found some reason for separation.

units.la: §. Ex his autem huius ceremoniæ particularibus dilucidare potes loc. Ioh. viii. de Adultera ad Christum ducta : Accusatores illam deduxerunt in templum ubi Christus populum docebat; potatio mulieris ob adulterium suspectæ etiam in atrio templi fieri debuit. Canones supera recitati, ut & Bammidbar Rabba sol. 235. dicunt, quòd fi maritus qui uxorem suam accusat aliquando fuerit paris criminis reus, & illicito concubitu fe aliquando commaculavisset, uxorem quamvis adulterii rea fit ab aquis tamen intactam fore. Christus in hoc processu etiam ipsos interrogat accufantes, an à pari reatu insontes effent ? quando dicit, Qui vestrûm fine peccato est &c. Ad uxorem suspectam explorandam Sacerdos fe inclinare debuit ad pulverem fumendum : Debuit in libro adiurationis & maledictionis scribere. Christus etiam κα῾λω κν῾φας τῆ῾ς ∫αχλι῾χω ἐ῾γραφεν ἐ῾ις τὴν γῆν tanquam in libro, Sagax denique interpres plura alia in suum usum hic odorari poterit.
units.tr: From these particulars of the ceremony you can clarify John 8, concerning the adulteress brought to Christ. The accusers led her into the temple, where Christ was teaching the people; the drinking of a woman suspected of adultery also had to take place in the court of the temple. The canons recited above, as Bamidbar Rabba fol. 235 also says, state that if a husband who accuses his wife was himself at some time guilty of the same crime, and had at some time defiled himself by illicit intercourse, then his wife, though accused of adultery, will nevertheless be unharmed by the waters. In this proceeding Christ also asks the accusers whether they themselves were free of the same guilt, when he says, "He among you who is without sin, etc." To test the suspected wife, the priest had to stoop to take up the dust; he had to write in the book of adjuration and cursing. Christ too [κάτω κύψας τῷ δακτύλῳ ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν] stooped down and wrote with his finger on the ground, as if in a book. Finally, a shrewd interpreter may sniff out many other things here for his own use.

units.la: Aquæ libatio in Festo Tabernaculorum vid. Festum Tabern.
units.tr: The pouring out of water at the Feast of Tabernacles: see "Festum Tabern."

units.la: Aquilonaris ventus flat singulis mediis noctibus. Ievam. 72. 2.
units.tr: The north wind blows every midnight. Ievam. 72.2.

units.la: §. Qui vult dives fieri adeat aquilonem B. Batra 25. 2.
units.tr: Whoever wishes to become rich, let him face the north. B. Batra 25.2.

units.la: §. Arca, Mensa (typus bonorum corporalium) versus aquilonem posita fuit Cosri 104.
units.tr: The ark and the table (a type of bodily goods) were placed facing the north. Cosri 104.

units.la: §. Aquilonem versus collocandus est thalamus nuptialis, secundum illud Ptal. 17. 14. Berac.52. de הכסא בית idem observant ibid. sol. 62. 1.
units.tr: The bridal chamber is to be placed towards the north, according to the saying in Psalm 17.14. Berac. 52. On the "house of the seat" [בית הכסא] they observe the same thing, ibid. fol. 62.1.

units.la: §. In plurimis locis Iudæi clamitant, omne malum venire à Septentrione צפון, quia maxima mala quæ ipsis contigerunt ab aquilonaribus populis ipsis illata fuerunt.
units.tr: In many places the Jews cry out that all evil comes from the North [צפון], because the greatest misfortunes that befell them were inflicted on them by northern peoples.

units.la: §. Causa cur in deserto circuncisio intermissa fuit, est venti aquilonaris defectus, hoc enim spirante valde salubris est sanguinis missio, in quacunque parte corporis fiat. Aquilonaris ventus vero non spiravit in deserto per quadraginta annos, ne columna nubis quæ illos interdiu ducebat dissiparetur; huius enim venti particulare est quod disjiciat vapores: vid. Ievam. cap.8. sol.72. 1. Kimchi in Iosuam cap. 5. 2.
units.tr: The reason circumcision was omitted in the wilderness was the lack of the north wind. When this wind blows, bloodletting is very beneficial, wherever on the body it is done. But the north wind did not blow in the wilderness for forty years, lest the pillar of cloud that led them by day should be scattered; for it is a property of this wind to disperse vapours. See Ievam. cap.8 fol.72.1; Kimchi on Joshua 5.2. ## ON THE ARK

units.la: DE ARCA loco vid. Maym.Beth Habech. c.4. & supra quædam cit. apud Altare.
units.tr: For the place, see Maimonides, Beth Habechirah c.4, and the passages cited above under Altar.

units.la: ARGENTUM sacrum, triplex ponitur. עובר ספר Semiciclus quem persolvebat quotannis omnis transiens per recensitos h. e. numeratos Exod.30. (vid. de Siclis.) משנה ספר Quod quilibet pro redemptione anima solvebat. Et קסד quod quis sponte offerebat 1 Reg.20.5. Argentum cuius in lege mentio fit est argentum Tyrium (ponderis & bonitatis ut in urbe Tyri, ubi nummi omnes erant argentei, nulli aerei) sed per Rabbinorum argentum, intelligitur argentum provinciale: id autem absolute dictum sumitur pro nummo octonario, minimo nummo Tyri argenteo: de Siclo intelligitur octonarius Sicli Tyri: de Denario intelligitur octonarius denarii Tyri. R.Sal.Iarchi in Kidduchin c.11.1. vid. Inf. in Moneta.
units.tr: Sacred silver is of three kinds. (1) [עובר ספר] The half-shekel which every passer-by among those counted paid each year, that is, those numbered, Exod. 30 (see on the shekels). (2) [משנה ספר] What each person paid for the redemption of his soul. (3) [קסד] What someone offered of his own free will, 1 Kings 20.5. The silver mentioned in the Law is Tyrian silver (of the weight and quality used in the city of Tyre, where all coins were silver and none bronze). But by the rabbis "silver" is understood as provincial silver. The term, taken absolutely, is used for the octonary coin, the smallest silver coin of Tyre: the shekel is understood as the octonary of the Tyrian shekel, and the denarius as the octonary of the Tyrian denarius. R. Sal. Iarchi on Kiddushin c.11.1. See below under Money.

units.la: Arbal erat vallis Hierof.Taanith f. 69. 2. erat illa inter Zipporim & Tiberiada Iuchasin f.65. 1. Inde erat Nittai qui praefecturam gessit cum Iosua f.Perachiae Avot. c.1. v.6. Mentio fit סאה Modii Arbelitani Hierof. Peah f. 20. 2. de Simeone & Rabba iter faciendi per vallem Arbel vid. Hierof. Berac. p.1. col.3. sub m.
units.tr: Arbal was a valley: Hierof. Taanith f. 69.2. It lay between Zippori and Tiberias: Iuchasin f. 65.1. From there came Nittai, who was prefect together with Joshua: f. Perachiah, Avot c.1 v.6. Mention is made of the seah of Arbel measure: Hierof. Peah f. 20.2. Concerning Simeon and Rabba and their journey through the valley of Arbel, see Hierof. Berac. p.1 col.3 sub m.

units.la: Arbor vitae sic dictus est ab effectu & arbor scientiae ab eventu; More Nevoch.1.2. Quaenam arbor haec fuerit an vitis vel ficus vid. Sanhed. sol.70.1. Schertzer Trif.Orient.98.
units.tr: The tree of life is so called from its effect, and the tree of knowledge from its outcome: More Nevoch 1.2. As to what this tree was, whether a vine or a fig, see Sanhed. fol.70.1; Schertzer Trif. Orient. 98.

units.la: Arborem quae fructus suos excutit immaturos notant בסיקרא colore rubro, & lapidibus onerant. Hierof.Scheviit f.35.c.3. Quasi hoc stigmate ipsas ad pudorem adigere voluissent. In anno Iubilaei illas etiam ita notare licet: Maym.H. Schemita c.1.
units.tr: A tree that sheds its fruit before it is ripe they mark with [בסיקרא] with red colour and load with stones. Hierof. Scheviit f. 35 c.3. It is as if they wished by this brand to drive them to shame. In the Jubilee year one may also mark them in this way: Maym. H. Schemita c.1.

units.la: Arisout est idem ac שותפות societas Peah.5.5.
units.tr: Arisout is the same as [שותפות] partnership: Peah 5.5.

units.la: Arcubot Peah. 7. 4. sunt כרוכות כופרות בוֹמְרוֹת ligaturæ vel convolutiones palmitum vitis : has significationes non observ. Lex.
units.tr: Arcubot Peah 7.4 are [כרוכות כופרות בוֹמְרוֹת], bindings or twinings of vine shoots. The Lexicon has not noted these meanings.

units.la: ARTIFICIUM vide Opificium.
units.tr: ARTIFICIUM: see Opificium.

units.la: Asiæ nomen si augu-ari licet, venit à memoria stirpis Gigantæa in medio ferè Asiæ degentis, & præ omnibus Asiaticis monstrosæ & stupendæ. Hos certè quos Hebraicè רפאים gigantes vocamus Syriacè & Chaldaicè loquentes, præcipuè autem Samaritani Asaos vocarunt. vid. Samaritanum Gen.xv. Deut.11.20.
units.tr: If the name of Asia may be derived by a guess, it comes from the memory of the Giant race, who lived roughly in the middle of Asia and were monstrous and astonishing beyond all other Asiatics. Those whom we call in Hebrew gigantes [רפאים], speaking Syriac and Chaldee, and especially the Samaritans, called Asaos. See the Samaritan text at Gen. 15 and Deut. 11.20.

units.la: Asinus & pullus eius à Talmudicis in Hierof. Bava Metzia sol.11.1. חמור וגיידור קשון vocantur; quibus respondent ἐνον ἡ πῶλον Math.21.2. Mirum est quod Christus loco cit. iubeat absque pactis & conditionibus asinam abducere; cum tamen Iudæorum canones circa conductionem asini tam accurati fuerint, ut ille in Metzia sol.78. vocetur גול raptor, qui asinum ad alia adhibuerit, quam intendit eius possessor.
units.tr: The donkey and its foal are called by the Talmudists, in the Jerusalem Talmud, Bava Metzia fol. 11.1, [חמור וגיידור קשון]. To these corresponds the Greek [ἐπ᾽ ὄνον ἢ πῶλον] at Matt. 21.2. It is remarkable that Christ, in the passage cited, orders the ass to be led away without agreements or conditions, when the canons of the Jews concerning the hiring of an ass were so exact that in Bava Metzia fol. 78 the man who used an ass for some purpose other than its owner intended is called a [גול], a robber.

units.la: Bab. Sanhed. sol. 98.1. quæstio incidit quomodo locus Danielis VII.13. quòd Messias venturus sit in nubibus cœli, & Zacharia 9.v.9. quòd venturus sit insidens asino; conciliari possint, & respondetur, Si boni sunt Israelitæ, tunc veniet in nubibus cœli; si vero non boni, tunc inequitans asino. Contrarium dicere debuissent, Messias veniet in nubibus, ut vindex & ultor, quia Iudæi erga eum pessimi; at venit insidens asino, non quia Iudæi boni, sed quia ille bonus
units.tr: In Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 98.1 the question arises how the passage in Daniel 7.13, that the Messiah will come in the clouds of heaven, and Zechariah 9.9, that he will come riding on an ass, can be reconciled. The answer given is: If the Israelites are good, then he will come in the clouds of heaven; but if they are not good, then riding on an ass. They ought to have said the contrary: the Messiah will come in the clouds as avenger and punisher, since the Jews are most wicked towards him; but he comes riding on an ass, not because the Jews are good, but because he himself is good.

units.la: De Mesia asino inequitante porrò ibidem ita pergunt. שבור מלכא Sapores Rex dixit Samuele, Dicitis vos Messiam vestrum venturum super Asinum, ergo mittam ei equum nobilem. Respondit ei, non est tibi equus centimaculus, qualis est eius Asinus. Ad quae verba ita commentatur Cl. Leigtfootus. Iudei in Summa Messiae humilitate fastum sominant, etiam in ipsius asino.
units.tr: Further, in the same place they continue about the Messiah riding on an ass as follows: [שבור מלכא]. King Sapores said to Samuel: You say that your Messiah will come upon an ass; therefore I will send him a noble horse. He replied to him: You have no horse with a hundred spots such as his ass is. On these words the learned Lightfoot comments: The Jews, in the humility of their Messiah, dream up pomp, even in his ass.

units.la: ASKALON Interpreti Samaritano idem est cum Gerar Gen. xx.1.
units.tr: ASKALON: to the Samaritan interpreter it is the same as Gerar, Gen. 20.1.

units.la: §. Diftabat Afcalon ab Hierofolymis lxv.m. paffuum Iosephi de bello l.3. c.1. Quod de veteriori intelligendum, Beniamin enim in itinerario p.80. duplicem Afcalonem memorat; antiquam & novam.
units.tr: Ashkelon was sixty-five miles distant from Jerusalem, Josephus, Of the War book 3, ch. 1. This must be understood of the older city, for Benjamin, in his Itinerary p. 80, mentions two Ashkelons, the old and the new.

units.la: § Ab Afcalone ad Auftrum eft Regio Ethnica, atque Afca'on ipfa pro regione Ethnica reputatur, (Exceptis quibufdam pomariis & hortis & locis proxime adiacentibus,qui intra terram reputabantur.) R.Nissin in Gittin c.1.
units.tr: From Ashkelon southward lies the Gentile region, and Ashkelon itself is reckoned as Gentile territory (except certain orchards and gardens and places lying close by, which were reckoned within the land). R. Nissim in Gittin ch. 1.

units.la: §. Inter fana famofiora etiam recenfetur fanum Zeriphae Afcalone. Bab. Avodah Sarah fol. ii. 2.
units.tr: Among the more famous shrines is also counted the shrine of Zeriphae at Ashkelon. Bab. Avodah Zarah fol. ii. 2.

units.la: §. Ob uredinem vifam in frugibus Afcalone,indiGum eft univerfale Ieiunium. Maff.Taanith c.3.6.
units.tr: Because of mildew seen in the crops at Ashkelon, a general fast was decreed. Mas. Taanith ch. 3.6.

units.la: §. Simeon Ben Schetach Afcalone uno eodemque die fufpendit 80. faeminas veneficas: Hieros.Sanhed. fol.23.3. de quo proceffu, quid tenendum fit, vid. Simeon Ben Schetach.
units.tr: Simeon ben Shetach at Ashkelon hanged eighty sorceresses on one and the same day. Jerusalem Sanhedrin fol. 23.3. As to what is to be held concerning this proceeding, see Simeon Ben Schetach.

units.la: ASTRONOMI, Aftrologi. In eis lex non invenitur.Sepher Hammufar c.10. fol.98.1. Dixit quidam, Ergo ex Aftronomia mea vidi me non fore idoneum ad generandum filium; Responderunt ipsi relinque hanc tuam Aftronomiam שאין מזל לישראל Non est enim astrum Israeli. Israeli. Bab. Schabbat sol. 156. 1.
units.tr: ASTRONOMERS, astrologers. The law does not mention them. Sepher Hammufar ch. 10, fol. 98.1: a certain man said, "From my astronomy I have seen that I am not fit to beget a son." They answered him: "Leave this astronomy of yours, for there is no [שאין מזל לישראל], no constellation for Israel." Bab. Shabbat fol. 156.1.

units.la: §. Abraham erat excellens כוכבי חווה Astrologus Bava Bathra sol. 16. 2. Notat R. Salomoh ad Ioma sol. 26. 2. Reges Occidentis & Orientis convenisse Abrahamum ad discendam Astronomiam. vid. etiam Planeta.
units.tr: Abraham was an outstanding astrologer [כוכבי חווה]. Bava Bathra fol. 16.2. R. Solomon, on Yoma fol. 26.2, notes that the kings of the West and East came to Abraham to learn astronomy. See also Planeta.

units.la: Asyli civitates tres separavit Moses trans Iordanem, & ex oppolito tres separavit Iosua in terra Canaan. Iuxta se positæ erant, eo modo quo duo vitium ordines in vinea. Hebron in Iudæa, ex oppolito Bezer in Eremo. Schechem in monte Ephraim, ex oppolito Ramot in Gilead. Cadefch in monte Nephtali ex oppolito Golan in Basan. Bab. Maccot. f. 9. 2.
units.tr: Moses separated three cities of refuge beyond the Jordan, and opposite them Joshua separated three in the land of Canaan. They were set next to one another, in the way two rows of vines stand in a vineyard: Hebron in Judah, opposite Bezer in the wilderness; Shechem in Mount Ephraim, opposite Ramoth in Gilead; Kedesh in Mount Naphtali, opposite Golan in Bashan. Bab. Makkot fol. 9.2.

units.la: §. Vias ad Asylum ducentes, dilatavit & purgavit Synedrium ab omni offendiculo, fluvios pontibus stravit, & in omni bivio posuit signum in quo erat scriptum מקלט מקלט ne à via fugientes errarent. Maymon. Hal. Rozeach cap. 8.
units.tr: The roads leading to the refuge were widened and cleared of every obstacle by the Sanhedrin; the rivers were bridged, and at every crossroads a sign was set up on which was written [מקלט מקלט], so that fugitives should not go astray from the road. Maimonides, Hilchot Rozeach, ch. 8.

units.la: §. Qui ex accidenti summum Pontificem interfecerit, fugere potest ad civitatem refugii, sed illinc nunquam redire. Bab. Sanhed. f. 18. 2.
units.tr: Whoever by accident kills the high priest may flee to the city of refuge, but he may never return from there. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 18.2.

units.la: §. Hi in urbe Asyli exulare debent. Ille qui aliquem imprudens interfecerit, ut si aliquis cylindrum impulerit, dolium demiserit, & illud fracto fune aliquem interfecerit. In his & omnibus reliquis casibus, hæc regula observatur; quod per descensum factum est, ob id exulat; quod non per descensum ob id non exulat. Si quis lapidem in publicum projiciens, quempiam interfecerit exulat. Si quis proiecerit lapidem in atrium suum, cædemque fecerit, si læso eo intrandi ius est, exulat, sin minùs, non exulat. Pater causa filii, filius causa patris exulat. Inquilinus non exulat, nisi Inquilini causa; (nam si Israelitam occiderit capite plectitur.) Maym.Hal.Rozeach. cap. 5.
units.tr: These must go into exile in the city of refuge: one who kills someone unintentionally, as when someone pushes a cylinder, drops a cask, and with the rope broken kills a person. In these and all other cases the following rule is observed: what happened by a fall, for that he goes into exile; what did not happen by a fall, for that he does not go into exile. If someone throws a stone into a public place and kills a person, he goes into exile. If someone throws a stone into his own courtyard and causes a death, he goes into exile if the injured man had a right to enter; if not, he does not. A father is exiled for the cause of his son, a son for the cause of his father. A sojourner is not exiled, unless it is for a sojourner's cause; for if he kills an Israelite, he is punished with death. Maimonides, Hilchot Rozeach, ch. 5.

units.la: §. Vrbes asyli delectæ ultra Iordanem non recipiebant ad illas fugientes, nisi postquàm & illæ in terra Canaan delectæ erant. Fugienti ad asylum in usu habuerunt duos discipulos sapientum adiungere, ne forte in via ipsum occideret vindex. Olim sive quis volens sive imprudens cædem fecisset, ad urbem refugii se recipiebat, & Senatus misisis ministris illum inde trahebat: si reus erat condemnabatur, si vero innocens liber dimittebatur; qui exilium merebatur in locum pristinum deportabatur.
units.tr: The cities of refuge chosen beyond the Jordan did not receive those fleeing to them until those in the land of Canaan had also been chosen. It was the custom to attach two disciples of the wise to one fleeing to the refuge, lest perhaps the avenger kill him on the way. In former times, whether someone had killed intentionally or unintentionally, he would betake himself to the city of refuge, and the Senate sent officers who dragged him out from there: if he was guilty he was condemned, but if innocent he was released; one who deserved exile was taken back to his former place.

units.la: §. Ex exilio quod homicidæ in urbibus afyli patiebantur, ipsos restituere & revocare poterat, mors Sacerdotis summi sive ille simpliciter oleo unctionis, aut vestitu initiatus fuerit, (v.Sacerdotes.) Etiam mors Sacerdotis unẜi ad bellum homicidas exules restituere poteft, inquit Akiba. Propterea etiam matres horum Sacerdotum, exulibus amictum & victum præbebant, ne filiorum suorum mortem precibus accelerarent.
units.tr: From the exile which manslayers suffered in the cities of refuge, they could be restored and recalled by the death of the high priest, whether he had been initiated simply by anointing oil or by vestments (see Priests). Also the death of the high priest anointed for war can restore exiled manslayers, says Akiba. Therefore the mothers of these priests also provided clothing and food for the exiles, lest they hasten their sons' death by their prayers.

units.la: §. Qui in Interregno damnatus est, aut Sacerdotem summum interfecit, aut si ipse Sacerdos summus cædem patraverit, ille nunquam urbem Asyli egredi poterit.
units.tr: Whoever was condemned during the interregnum, or who killed the high priest, or if the high priest himself committed a killing, can never leave the city of refuge.

units.la: §. Sicut urbs ita quoque territorium eius recirecipit homicidas (postquàm urbis Asyli territorium ingressus es in tanta securitate esse debes ac si inter ipsos civitatis muros te recepisses.)
units.tr: As the city, so also its territory receives manslayers. (Once you have entered the territory of the city of refuge, you ought to be in as much safety as if you had been received within the very walls of the city.)

units.la: §. Si incolæ illius civitatis homicidam honore volunt afficere, dicet illi homicida, ego sum,si illi nihilominus insistunt,honorem accipere potest. Hal. Rozeach c.8.
units.tr: If the inhabitants of that city wish to honour the manslayer, the manslayer shall say to them, "I am the manslayer." If they nevertheless insist, he may accept the honour. Hilchot Rozeach ch. 8.

units.la: definitionem habes apud Maymon. in Hal.Beth Habech.c.1.l.19. Quatuor in templo erant atria,atrium gentium,atrium mulierum, & atrium Israelis, & atrium Sacerdotum. Nos singula consideràbimus separatim, & quæ de illis nunc occurrunt breviter recensebimus.
units.tr: You have the definition in Maimonides, Hilchot Beth ha-Bechirah, ch. 1, l. 19. There were four courts in the Temple: the court of the Gentiles, the court of the women, the court of Israel, and the court of the priests. We shall consider each separately, and briefly recount what is now found about them.

units.la: Atrium gentium duplici nomine vocatur à Rabbinis, aliquando vocatur הר הבית mons templi, aliquando verò חול profanum vel commune. Hinc Author Tosaphtot in Perah c.2. Exeunt per portam ducentem ex Atrio mulierum לחול in atrium commune &c. Ratio huius appellationis est 1. quia illuc accedere poterant Ethnici, ut videtur ex illo dicto quod exstat Hierof. Auoda Sarah sol. 40.1. R. Gamaliel ambulans בהר הבית in atrio gentium, vidit fœminam Ethnicam ac de ea benedixit. &c. 2. quia excommunicati & lugentes illuc veniebant, ut apparet ex Middot cap.2.2. ibi enim docetur qualem viam fecerint in atrio gentium lugentes aut excommunicati, (v. s.1.) Etiam ille qui hircum emissarium educebat, quamvis pollutus atrium gentium ingredi potuit, Bab.Ioma sol.66.2.
units.tr: The court of the Gentiles is called by the Rabbis by a double name: sometimes it is called "the mountain of the house" [הר הבית], and sometimes "profane" or "common" [חול]. Hence the author of the Tosaphot on Perah, ch. 2: They go out through the gate leading from the court of the women to the common court [לחול], etc. The reason for this name is, first, that Gentiles could go there, as appears from the saying in Jerusalem Avodah Zarah fol. 40.1: R. Gamaliel, walking in the mountain of the house [בהר הבית], that is in the court of the Gentiles, saw a Gentile woman and blessed her, etc. Second, because excommunicated persons and mourners came there, as appears from Middot ch. 2.2, for there it is taught what way the mourners or the excommunicated made in the court of the Gentiles (see above, s. 1). Also he who led out the scapegoat, though polluted, could enter the court of the Gentiles. Bab. Yoma fol. 66.2.

units.la: §. Maximum spatium atrii gentium erat ab austro, proximum ei ab Oriente, tertium ab Aquilóne; minimum vero ab Occidente. Eo loco ubi maius erat spatium, maior erat eius usus. Middot. c.2.2.
units.tr: The largest space of the court of the Gentiles was on the south, the next on the east, the third on the north; the smallest on the west. In the place where the space was greater, its use was greater. Middot ch. 2.2.

units.la: §. E aat in muro spatium hoc ambiente, quinque portæ, (vid. de illis infra Portas.) intusque muro contiguæ erant porticus, vel basilicæ duplicatæ, quæ & ambulachra præbuerunt periucunda, & simul à pluviis protegebant. Middot. c.1.3.
units.tr: Moreover, in the wall that encloses this space there were five gates (see on them below under Portas). Right against the inner side of the wall ran colonnades, or double basilicas, which provided pleasant walkways and at the same time gave protection from the rain. Middot. c.1.3.

units.la: §. De muro quem hoc atrium circumivit vid. in חיל lit. C. vocatur ille antemurale & ab eo ascendebatur in atrium mulierum gradibus duodecim. Middot. c. 2.3.
units.tr: On the wall that surrounded this court, see under חיל [chel], letter C. It is called the antemural, and from it one ascended into the Court of the Women by twelve steps. Middot. c.2.3.

units.la: §. Atrium mulierum שערות נשים tantùm unam portam habuit ab Oriente, quæ Act. iii.2. vocatur & apud Iofeph. de bello l. 5. c.14. Corinthiaca. Ab Aquilone & Austro etiam tantùm una erat. Muro ab interiori parte etiam Basilicæ contiguæ erant sed non duplicatæ ut in atrio exteriori. Ante illas positæ erant tredecim cistæ, in quas infundebantur nummi oblati. (vid. Gazophylacium.)
units.tr: The Court of the Women [שערות נשים, Shaarot Nashim] had only one gate, on the east, which is called in Acts 3:2, and by Josephus in De bello book 5, chapter 14, the Corinthian gate. On the north and south it likewise had only one gate each. On the inner side of the wall there were also basilicas, but these were not doubled as in the outer court. In front of them were placed thirteen chests into which the offered coins were poured (see Gazophylacium).

units.la: §. Arii mulierum longitudo erat 135. cubitorum, & latitudo 135. cubitorum, quatuorque conclavia erant in quatuor eius angulis: (vid. Conclavia.)
units.tr: The Court of the Women was 135 cubits long and 135 cubits wide, and there were four chambers at its four corners (see Conclavia).

units.la: §. In summis lateribus læve ac planum erat atrium mulierum: sed id circumscripserunt interno podio, ut mulieres superne prospicerent, viri autem inferne ne miscerentur. vid. Middot. Cl.l'Empereur c.2.5.
units.tr: Along its sides the Court of the Women was level and flat. But it was enclosed by an inner balcony, so that the women could look down from above while the men below were kept from mingling with them. See Middot, Cl. L'Empereur, c.2.5.

units.la: §. In hoc atrio mulierum cebebratum est tripudium in festo Tabernaculorum. (v.f.l.)
units.tr: In this Court of the Women the dancing was held at the Feast of Tabernacles (v.f.l.).

units.la: §. Sacratius erat atrium mulierum quàm חיל antemurale, nam in atrium mulierum nemo ingredi debuit qui erat יום טבול i. e. qui immunditiem contraxerat eadem die abluendam. Maymon in Beth Habeh. c.7.
units.tr: The Court of the Women was holier than the חיל [chel], the antemural, for no one who was יום טבול [yom tevul], that is, who had contracted an uncleanness that had to be washed away the same day, was to enter the Court of the Women. Maimonides, in Beth ha-Behirah, c.7.

units.la: §. In Atrium Israelis (quod apud scriptores Hebraeos κατ' ἐξοχὴν atrium vocatur, non excludendo atrium Sacerdotum, à quo quidem distinctum erat, sed non divisum ut atrium mulierum:) ex atrio mulierum ascensum est gradibus quindecim Ioseph. de bello l. 5. c.14. In festo tabernaculorum Levitae steterunt super hos quindecim gradus, cùm Lyris, Cytharis, & Cymbalis. Succah. c.5.14.
units.tr: Into the Court of Israel (which the Hebrew writers call by eminence the court [κατ' ἐξοχὴν ἀτρίον], not excluding the Court of the Priests, from which it was indeed distinct but not divided as the Court of the Women was), one ascended from the Court of the Women by fifteen steps. Josephus, De bello book 5, chapter 14. At the Feast of Tabernacles the Levites stood on these fifteen steps, with lyres, harps, and cymbals. Succah c.5.14.

units.la: §. Porta orientalis huius atrii vocabatur Porta Nicanoris Middot. c.2.3. (v.f.l.) Ad huius atrii latus meridionale erat conclave ligni, conclave scaturiginis, & conclave Gazit. (v.f.l.) Middot. c.5 3. A latere septentrionali habebat Portam & Cameram Nitsots, Middot. c.1.5. Sequebatur conclave lavantium & conclaveHapparvae. Item Porta oblationis, conclave falis (Middot. c.5.2.) Et porta Beth Hammoked.
units.tr: The east gate of this court was called the Gate of Nicanor. Middot c.2.3 (v.f.l.). On the south side of this court were the wood chamber, the chamber of the spring, and the chamber of Gazit (v.f.l.); Middot c.5.3. On the north side was the gate and chamber of Nitsotz; Middot c.1.5. Next came the chamber of the washers and the chamber of Happarvah. Likewise the Gate of the Offering, the chamber of salt (Middot c.5.2), and the Gate of Beth Hammoked.

units.la: §. Atrium Israelis erat longitudine 135. cubitorum, latitudine undecim. Middot.c.2.6. Per totum hoc atrium ambulatū est in plano, atque inde ascensum est in atrium Sacerdotum gradu uno, altitudine cubitali, cui impositum erat pulpitum pro Levitis psallentibus, atque in eo erant tres gradus, singuli scilicet cubiti dimidii. Reperitur ergo atrium Sacerdotum duobus cubitis cum dimidio altius atrio Israelis.
units.tr: The Court of Israel was 135 cubits long and eleven cubits wide. Middot c.2.6. One walked across this whole court on level ground, and from there one ascended into the Court of the Priests by one step, a cubit high, on which was set a platform for the Levites who sang psalms; on this platform there were three steps, each half a cubit high. So the Court of the Priests stood two and a half cubits higher than the Court of Israel.

units.la: §. Atrium Sacerdotum erat longitudine 150. cubitorum, latitudine undecim: capita trabium dividebant inter atrium Israelis & Sacerdotum. Per Atrium Sacerdotum perrectum est in plano, itemque per spatium iuxta Altare,perque spatium inter altare & Pronaon. Illuc ascensum est duodecim gradibus singulis semicubitalibus. Consule Cl. Leigtfoot (Cent. Chorog. p. 66.
units.tr: The Court of the Priests was 150 cubits long and eleven cubits wide; the heads of the beams divided the Court of Israel from the Court of the Priests. Through the Court of the Priests one walked on level ground, likewise through the space beside the altar, and through the space between the altar and the porch. Thither one ascended by twelve steps, each half a cubit high. Consult Cl. Lightfoot, Centuria Chorographica, p. 66.

units.la: §. Cur Atrium עזרה vocatum fuerit rationem reddit Kimchi כי כל הבא להתפלל שם בלב שלום נעוד כיי אלוהיו : quia quisquis eo accederet precatum sincero animo עזר opitulabalur ei Dom.Deus. Vid. pl. ap.Cl. L'Empereur Midd. p.15. de atriorum differenti Sanctitate vid. Sanctum.
units.tr: Why the court was called עזרה [azarah] Kimchi gives the reason: כי כל הבא להתפלל שם בלב שלום נעזר כו׳ אלהיו [ki kol haba lehitpallel sham belev shalem na'ezar ke'o' Elohav], that is, because whoever came there to pray with a sincere heart was helped by the Lord his God. See more in Cl. L'Empereur, Middot p. 15. On the differing holiness of the courts see under Sanctum.

units.la: §. Quando postfesta atrium purificare voluunt, lavant vasa quae in eo sunt, & dicunt plebeiis, cavete ne tangatis mensam, Candelabrum, illaque polluatis. Quaecunque vasa in Sanctuario sunt, habent sua שניים & שלשי secunda & tertia,ut si primum pollutum sit, alterum vice eius succedat. Omnia vasa quae in Sanctuario sunt ad lotionem tenentur, praeter altare aureum & aeneum, שרן כקרקע quia infiar foli sunt, id est non sunt capacia ut recipiant pollutionem.Chagiga c.3.
units.tr: When after the festivals they wish to purify the court, they wash the vessels that are in it, and they tell the common people: beware of touching the table or the candlestick and so defiling them. Every vessel in the sanctuary has its secunda and tertia (שניים [sheni] and שלישי [shelishi]), so that if the first becomes defiled, the second takes its place. All the vessels that are in the sanctuary must be washed, except the golden and bronze altars, which are שרן כקרקע [sheran kekarka], because they are like the floor, that is, they cannot receive defilement. Chagigah c.3.

units.la: §. In atrio Israelis nemo sedere potuit praeter reges ex familia Davidis, Maym. Beth Habech. cap. 7. Quando itaque legimus in N. Test. Christum sedisse in templo,
units.tr: No one could sit in the Court of Israel except the kings of the house of David. Maimonides, Beth ha-Behirah cap. 7. Therefore, when we read in the New Testament that Christ sat in the temple,

units.la: non dicendum ipsum in atrio Israelis sedisse, sed vel in atrio mulierum vel Gentium. Legimus Ioh. viii. 59. Iudæos lapides sustulisse ad Christum lapidandum; sive illud in atrio mulierum sive gentium factum fit, an probabile est lapides ibi reperiri potuisse, cùm tanta Sacerdotum multitudo, & accurata diligentia templum semper nitidissimè purgatum fuisse arguant? Imò à Gemaristis ad cap. 2. 2. Sotah determinatur, quod si Sacerdos nullum pulverem in fundo templi reperiret, ut ab extra pulverem in templi solum depellere liceret. Si itaque accidere potuit, ut ibi nullus fuerit pulvis notabilis, quanto minus lapides. Hæc difficultas iam Schabbat sol.115.1. ex occasione R. Gamalielis præcipientis ut defoderetur quidam liber Iobi Targumizatus sub acervo luti, mota & agitata fuit; quidam enim ibi quærit וכי טיט בהר הבית At num est lutum in monte templi? Huic sciolo à Glossa responsum est, fuisse ibi cæmentum quo ædificabant. Nos eadem ratione respondemus, fuisse ibi lapides quibus ædificabant. Nam primò R. ille Gamaliel præsidiatum tenuit solùm ultimis Christi annis. (v. f. 1.) & tamen tunc adhuc ædificabant. Deinde Iosephus Antiq. lib. 20. cap. 8. refert, populum Agrippam ursisse ut porticum Orientalem restauraret, quia videbat otium esse operariis, qui erant plures quam xviii. millia tam multi enim opifices semper occupationem petebant. Secundùm computum deniq; quadraginta sex annorum in quibus templum ædificatum fuit, cum annis Herodis saltem hoc constabit,templum tunc vel nondum fuisse absolutum, v.1 non ita pridem, ita ut plenè nondum purgari potuerit.
units.tr: we must not say that he sat in the Court of Israel, but either in the Court of the Women or in the Court of the Gentiles. We read in John 8:59 that the Jews took up stones to stone Christ. Whether this happened in the Court of the Women or in the Court of the Gentiles, is it probable that stones could be found there, when the great number of priests and the careful diligence show that the temple was always kept most scrupulously clean? Indeed, the Gemarists, on Sotah 2.2, determine that if a priest found no dust at the bottom of the temple, it was lawful to brush dust onto the temple floor from outside. If it could happen that there was no noticeable dust there, how much less stones? This difficulty was already raised in Shabbat fol. 115.1, on the occasion of Rabban Gamaliel's command that a certain book of Job, translated into Aramaic, be buried under a heap of mud; some asked: וכי טיט בהר הבית [ukhi tiṭ bahar haBayit], And is there mud on the mount of the temple? The Gloss answered this simpleton that there was cement there with which they built. We answer on the same principle: there were stones there with which they built. For, first, that Gamaliel held the presidency only in the last years of Christ (v.f.l.), and yet they were still building then. Next, Josephus, Antiquities book 20, chapter 8, reports that the people urged Agrippa to restore the eastern portico, because he saw that the workmen, who were more than 18,000, were idle, for so many craftsmen always sought work. Finally, by the reckoning of the forty-six years in which the temple was built, it will be established, at least with the years of Herod, that the temple was then either not yet finished or not long finished, so that it could not yet have been fully cleansed.

units.la: Atrium magnum erat Hierosolymis פסץ בית dictum, quò congregati sunt illi qui de novilunio testari volebant, atque ibi à Synedrio examinabantur, aliquando etiam convivio excipiebantur ut eò libentius accederent. Rosch Haschana c.2. v.5.
units.tr: The great Atrium at Jerusalem was called פסץ בית [Beth Pasz], where those gathered who wished to testify about the new moon, and there they were examined by the Sanhedrin; sometimes they were also entertained with a feast, so that they would come more willingly. Rosh Hashanah c.2 v.5.

units.la: §. Erant deinde Hierosolymis quædam atria, ædificata super petram, sub quibus erat חלחexcavatio, ne ibi possent sepulchra fieri; in illa atria ducebant quasdam mulieres ut ibi parerent, & infantes educarent, ut cum ibi securum sit à contactu sepulchri, mundi pueri, & proinde apti essent, ad aspergendum pollutos à morticinio aquâ purificationis: debebant autè ibi pueri secundum R. Salomonem usque ad annum septimum, secundum Tosiphta verò usque ad duodecimum manere. Deinde cùm alicuius aspersio peragenda erat, ad locum ubi id præstandum, bobus inequitantes vehebantur, qui crassitudine ventris ipsos à periculo pollutionis à sepulchro tutos faciebant. Parah. c.3.2. Comment.
units.tr: Furthermore, there were certain courts at Jerusalem, built over rock, beneath which was an excavation <bl>חלח</bl> [chalach], so that graves could not be made there. Into these courts they brought certain women to give birth there and raise their infants, so that, since they were safe there from contact with a grave, the boys would be clean and therefore fit to sprinkle with the water of purification those defiled by a corpse. According to R. Solomon the boys were to remain there until the age of seven, but according to the Tosefta until the age of twelve. Then, when someone was to be sprinkled, they were carried to the place where this was to be done, riding on oxen, whose bulk of belly kept them safe from the danger of contamination from a grave. Parah c.3.2, commentary.

units.la: §. Per Atriorum Commixtionem חצרות עידובי de qua tanta sunt in tractatu עירובין quem latinè dedit Sebast. Schmid, rem breviter sic habeto. Habitarunt plures familiæ iuxta unum commune atrium. Cum itaque non liceret Sabbatho quicquam exportare מרשות לרשות à loco qui erat unius iuris, vel conditionis, in locum qui alterius, (ut docetur in Schabbat & inf. cit. ap. Sabbathum,) ideoque non licuerit cuivis ex iltis familiis aliquid efferre è domo sua in atrium ostio suo adiacens, & è contra; communionem & commixtionem iuris inierunt omnes, idque per comestionem unâ,cibi ab omnibus simul collati, & tunc fuit licitum. Et hæc est illa commixtio Atriorum. Ad talem confuetudinem forsan alluditur ab Apostolo 1.Cor. x. 16. quando de communione loquitur.
units.tr: On the Commixture of Courts [חצרות עירובי, chatzerot eruvei], about which there is so much in the tractate Eruvin, which Sebastian Schmid has given in Latin, here is the matter briefly. Several families lived beside one common court. Since it was not lawful on the Sabbath to carry anything out מרשות לרשות [mireshut lireshut], from a place under one jurisdiction or status into a place under another (as is taught in Shabbat and below under Sabbath), it was therefore not lawful for any of those families to carry anything out of his own house into the court adjoining his door, or the reverse. So they all entered into a communion and commixture of right, by eating together a meal of food brought together by all at once, and then it was permitted. This is that commixture of courts. Perhaps the Apostle alludes to such a custom at 1 Corinthians 10:16, when he speaks of communion.

units.la: Aurora. Egressio [illegible, ~3 letters] ad lucem aurora, est corpori sicut chalybs ferro. Somnus cum radiis aurorae est senibus sicut chalybs ferro. Bab.Beracot. sol. 62.2. Ab aurora ufquedum totus oriens lucidus est homo 4. milliarium iter conficere potest, Ex eo quod illucescit oriens usque ad solis ortum totidem. Israelis redemptio est aurorae similis. Hierof.Beracot p.1. col.3. vid. Israel.
units.tr: Dawn. Going out to the light of dawn is to the body what steel is to iron. Sleep with the rays of dawn is to the old what steel is to iron. Bab. Berachot fol. 62.2. From dawn until sunrise, a man can walk four miles: from the time the east begins to brighten until the sun rises, the same distance. Israel's redemption is like the dawn. Jerusalem Berachot p. 1, col. 3. See Israel.

units.la: Aves iussit Deus offerre, ut consuleretur illorum paupertati, in quorum facultate non erat boves offerre. Quare etiam ex avium speciebus communiores & frequentiores in terra Israelitica designavit, quales sunt puelli columbarum & turtures. More Nev. iii. 46. de ave Phaenice v. Lexicon Talmud. p.720.
units.tr: God commanded that birds be offered, so that the poverty of those who could not afford to offer oxen might be relieved. For this reason He also designated, from among the kinds of birds, the more common and frequent ones in the land of Israel, such as young pigeons and turtledoves. More Nevochim iii. 46, on the bird Phoenix; see Lexicon Talmudicum p. 720.

units.la: Auris. Quare auris tota dura est, auricula autem mollis? nempe quod fi audiat homo minus honestum [illegible, ~5 letters] Auriculam incurvet in eam, opplendo scilicet aurem, ne audiat. Ketubhot. sol.5.2. v. Digitos.
units.tr: Ear. Why is the whole ear hard, but the little ear soft? Namely, because if a man hears something less decent, he should bend the little ear into it, plugging the ear so that he does not hear. Ketubot fol. 5.2. See Fingers.

units.la: Austrum & Australis vid. Iudaea.
units.tr: The south wind and the southern region: see Judaea.

units.la: BABA Ben Butah.
units.tr: Baba Ben Butah.

units.la: De eo sic Iuchasin sol. 52. 2. Ben Butah fuit Schammæi discipulus doctus valde & senex. Rex Herodes ipsius oculos stibio fucavit, i. e. ipsum cæcum reddidit, (forsan ipsa hac materia adhibita,) cùm in initio regni sui sapientes interficeret. Ille etiam est qui Herodi dedit consilium sanctuarium reædificandi, ut scilicet in expiationem, quod lucem mundi i. e. Sapientes depresserat alteram lucem mundi, id est, templum restauraret. Erat enim Herodes servus familiæ Asmoneæ, ut refertur in Bab. Batra f.3.2. & propter oraculum tẽ Bat Kol, quod aliquando dixerat, quicunque servus nunc rebellaverit, prosperè rem geret, contrà Dominos suos insurrexit, & omnes interfecit, ut & etiam illos Rabbinos qui ex Dicto Deut.xvii.15. invasioni eius restituerunt; relicto solum Baba Ben Butahe filiis Bethiræ, Hillele, Menachemo, quorum quidam fugâ salutem quæsiverunt, alii verò non recto & adverso tramite, regimini Herodis resistendo.
units.tr: Concerning him, thus Jochasin, fol. 52.2. Ben Butah was a very learned and old disciple of Shammai. King Herod stained his eyes with antimony, that is, made him blind (perhaps using that very substance), when at the beginning of his reign he was killing the wise. He is also the one who advised Herod to rebuild the sanctuary, so that, as an atonement for having brought down the light of the world, that is, the Sages, he might restore another light of the world, that is, the temple. For Herod was a slave of the Asmonean family, as is related in Bab. Baba Batra fol. 3.2, and because of the oracle of the Bat Kol, which had once declared that whatever slave now rebelled would prosper, he rose up against his masters and killed them all, and also those rabbis who, on the basis of the saying in Deut. 17:15, had supported his rule. Only Baba Ben Butah and the sons of Bethira, Hillel and Menachem, were left; some of them sought safety in flight, others, not by a straight and honest path, resisted Herod's rule.

units.la: BABYLONIOS ita odio habuerunt incolæ terræ Israeliticæ, ut unumquemque iudecorè se gerentem, Babylonium, & ita ipsorum nomine vocaverint. Gloss.in Bab.Ioma f.66. Ex eodem loco discimus Babylonios illos qui dicuntur in Mishna hircum emissarium ad egrediendum impulisse, non fuisse natione Babylonios sed Alexandrinos, à populo adstante tamen propter intempestivam impulsionem ita vocatos. Non est violentiæ ius in Babylonia, nemo alium poteşt cogere, aut per vim aliquid à debitore rapere. Bab.Gittin. sol.58. 2. §. E Babel ascenderunt יוחסין עשרה decem stirpes. 1. Sacerdotes. 2. Levitæ. 3. Israelitæ. 4. חלולי profani quo ad Sacerdotium. 5. Proselyti. 6. Servi manumissi. 7. Nothi. 8. Nethinæi. 9. שתוקי spurii, certæ matris at incerti patris. 10. אסופ Collectitii è plateis, matre patreque incertis. Kiddushchin c. 4. 1. Gens certè maculosa, & ideo in hac colluvie è Babylone educta, ne totum semen Iudaicum illic adhuc commorans, ab ea commaculaaretur. Non enim ascendit Esra è Babylone usquedum eam puram reddidisset in star farina. (inquit Gem.Bab.) A Synedrio verò Hierosolymitano, deinde abundè provideri potuit, ne legitimi cum illegitimis copulantur, & ita Genealogiæ conturbarentur. Quas ut integras conservarent in tanta Colluvie magnâ curâ opus fuit.
units.tr: The inhabitants of the land of Israel so hated the Babylonians that they called anyone who behaved badly a Babylonian, using their name in this way. Gloss. on Bab. Yoma fol. 66. From the same passage we learn that those Babylonians who are said in the Mishnah to have pushed the scapegoat over the cliff were not Babylonians by nation but Alexandrians, though the bystanders called them Babylonians because of their untimely push. There is no right of violence in Babylonia: no one can compel another, or seize anything from a debtor by force. Bab. Gittin fol. 58.2. §. Ten lineages (יוחסין עשרה) ascended from Babylon: (1) priests; (2) Levites; (3) Israelites; (4) the profane (חלולי) as regards the priesthood; (5) proselytes; (6) freed slaves; (7) bastards; (8) Nethinim; (9) foundlings (שתוקי), of a known mother but unknown father; (10) gatherings (אסופ) from the streets, with both mother and father unknown. Kiddushin ch. 4.1. This was certainly a stained people, and therefore they were brought up from Babylon out of this mixed mass, lest the whole Jewish seed, still living there, be defiled by it. For Ezra did not come up from Babylon until he had made it pure as fine flour, as the Gemara of Babylon says. The Sanhedrin of Jerusalem could then provide thoroughly, so that the legitimate were not joined with the illegitimate and the genealogies thrown into confusion. To keep these intact amid such a mixed multitude required great care.

units.la: §. Post reditum ex Babylonia, cùm facies uxorum Israelitarum נתפחמו adeo denigratæ essent, ut maritis non amplius placerent, ipsas mariti deseruerunt, & duxerunt uxores alienigenas. Berefchit. Rabba f. 18.
units.tr: §. After the return from Babylon, when the faces of the Israelite wives had become so blackened (נתפחמו) that they were darkened, and no longer pleased their husbands, the husbands deserted them and took foreign wives. Bereshit Rabba fol. 18.

units.la: §. Dispersio Iudæorum duplex fuit, erat Διασπορά Ἑλλήνων qui Græco Idiomate utebantur, & de quibus loquuntur sacræ literæ Ioh. VII.35. Et Διασπορὰ Βαβυλωνίων καὶ πρῶτον qui usi sunt lingua Hebræa vel Trans-Euphratensi. Dispersio Babylonica à Iudæis Palæstinis semper habita est, nobilior, dignior, sanctior dispersione Græca. Nam terra Babylonica eodem gradu puritatis venit ac Israelitica. R. Salomo in Gittin, folio 2. 1. Et progenies Iudæorum in Babylonia clariot quàm inter Græcos, & purior quam in ipsa Iudæa ut ex supradictis ex Kiddušchin sol. 69. 2. patet.
units.tr: §. The dispersion of the Jews was twofold: there was the Dispersion of the Greeks (Διασπορά Ἑλλήνων), who used the Greek language, and of whom the sacred letters speak in John 7:35; and the Dispersion of the Babylonians (Διασπορὰ Βαβυλωνίων), who used the Hebrew or Trans-Euphratean tongue, and who came first. The Babylonian dispersion was always regarded by the Jews of Palestine as nobler, worthier, and holier than the Greek dispersion, for the land of Babylon attained the same degree of purity as the land of Israel. R. Solomon on Gittin fol. 2.1. And the progeny of the Jews in Babylonia was more illustrious than among the Greeks, and purer than in Judaea itself, as appears from the above-cited Kiddushin fol. 69.2.

units.la: De Baculum gestandi ritu vid. peram.
units.tr: On the custom of carrying a staff, see wallet.

units.la: הבדלה Habhdala significat separationem Sabbathi, cum insequenti die, quæ fit cum candela, quam נר התבדל vocant, & benedictione quæ incipit בורא פרי העץ Berac. 52. Cl. Buxtorf.Syn. Iud. p.247. & L. Talm. p.262.
units.tr: Habdalah (הבדלה) means the separation of the Sabbath from the following day, which is performed with a candle, called the candle of separation (נר התבדל), and with the blessing that begins "Blessed be the Creator of the fruit of the tree" (בורא פרי העץ). Berachot 52. See Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica p. 247, and Lexicon Talmudicum p. 262.

units.la: Balneum Veneris erat Acone &c. vid. Venus. Balnea etiam in Sabbatho adibant, sed in se abstergendo hoc observarunt, ut lintea illa quibus se absterserant balneatoribus non reddèrent, sed in fenestram proximam deponerent, quia Balneatores suspecti sunt de expressione aquæ, quod in Sabbatho esset peccatum. (Erant autem fenestræ variæ ante balneum, intrantes vestes suas deponebant. vid. Taharot cap. 7.) Possunt balneatores etiam mulierum vestimenta sc. lintea in Sabbatho in balneum ferre. Schabbat sol.147.2. De nummis qui dantur Ministro balnei vid. Hierof. Maaser Scheni cap.1.Gloss. Non ingredietur homo balneum, neque in officinam Coriariorum tempore Minchæ sive precationis Schabbat cap. 1. Balneator non poterat Rex fieri, quia opificium eius contemptibile est. Kiddušchin sol.92.1.
units.tr: The bath of Venus was at Acre, etc.; see Venus. People also went to the baths on the Sabbath, but in washing themselves they observed this rule: they did not return the linen cloths with which they had dried themselves to the bath attendants, but laid them down on a nearby window, because bath attendants were suspected of wringing out water, which was a sin on the Sabbath. (There were various window-niches before the bath, where those entering put down their clothes; see Taharot ch. 7.) Bath attendants may even carry women's garments, that is, linen cloths, into the bath on the Sabbath. Shabbat fol. 147.2. On the coins given to the bath attendant, see Jerusalem Maaser Sheni ch. 1, and the Gloss. A man shall not enter the bath, nor the workshop of the tanners, at the time of Minchah, that is, the prayer. Shabbat ch. 1. A bath attendant could not become king, because his trade is contemptible. Kiddushin fol. 92.1.

units.la: Qui Barbæ Angulum corrumpit פאת הזקן ואין qui angulos capitis sui circumtondet, calviticm in capite suo facit, se secat unâ cæsurâ ob defunctum, vapulat. Maccot.c.3 §.5.
units.tr: One who spoils the corner of his beard (פאת הזקן) and (ואין) trims around the corners of his head, making a bald spot on his head, or cuts himself with a single incision for the dead, is flogged. Makkot ch. 3 §. 5.

units.la: Baruch, quamvis diligenter sequutus sit, Prophetam Ieremiam, qui etiam sæpius eum instituit & exercuit, adeò ut ipse speraret, se aliquando prophetaturum, tamen prohibitus fuit, secundùm illud Ierem.45.3.5. Quæ ita exponi possunt, Prophetiam pro captu Baruchi nimis fuisse arduam. Id est vel ipsum non satis exercitum fuisse in studiis, vel propter captivitatem in qua erat, nimis tristis, quàm ut prophetaret. More Nevoch.II.31.
units.tr: Baruch, although he diligently followed the prophet Jeremiah, who also often trained and exercised him, so that he himself hoped at some time to prophesy, was nevertheless forbidden to do so, according to Jeremiah 45:3, 5. These things can be explained thus: prophecy was too difficult for Baruch's capacity; that is, either he was not sufficiently trained in his studies, or, because of the captivity he was in, he was too sad to prophesy. More Nevochim II.31.

units.la: BAPTISMUS, est vel טבילת גרות Baptismus ad Proselytismum, vel טבילת נדה Bap ismus hominis impuri, aut mulieris menstruatæ. G'ossa Bab. Ievamot sol.45.2. Primus qui Proselyticum baptismum induxit fuit Iacob, cum Sichemitidas fœminas & alios in Ecclesiam & familiam suam adoptabat, secundùm Gen.xxxv.2. Vbi Aben Esra interpretatur והטהרו Et mundamini, per הגוף שירחצו quòd corpus abluerint. Sic per circuncisionem (quæ facta est in Ægypto) Baptismum (qui factus est in deserto, secundùm dictum sanctificabis eos hodie) & Sacrificium, missus est Israel in fœdus. Maymon Issure biah c.13. Idem observatum est respectu Proselytarum illorum qui tempore Davidis & Salomonis Iudaica Sacra amplexi sunt. Ibid. Hinc tritum illud axioma אין גר עד שימול ויטבול Non est Proselyta, usquedum baptizetur & circuncidatur. vid. differentes de hoc Gemaristas in Ievamot sol.46.2. Videtur tamen hoc effatum non fuisse tam universale, quin aliquando exceptiones factæ, & ad proselytum faciendum solus Baptismus sufficerit. Ita legimus Pesachin c.8. Quòd Proselytus Pascha co-
units.tr: BAPTISM is either the baptism of proselytism (טבילת גרות), or the baptism of a man who is unclean, or of a menstruating woman (טבילת נדה). Gloss on Bab. Yevamot fol. 45.2. The first to introduce proselyte baptism was Jacob, when he adopted the Shechemite women and others into his Church and household, according to Genesis 35:2. There Aben Ezra explains "and be clean" (והטהרו) as that they washed the body. Thus through circumcision (which was performed in Egypt), baptism (which was performed in the wilderness, according to the saying "you shall sanctify them today"), and sacrifice, Israel was brought into the covenant. Maimonides, Issure Bi'ah ch. 13. The same was observed with regard to those proselytes who embraced the Jewish sacred rites in the time of David and Solomon. Ibid. Hence the well-worn axiom: "There is no proselyte until he is baptized and circumcised" (אין גר עד שימול ויטבול), Non est proselytus, donec baptizetur et circumcidatur. See the Gemarists, who differ on this point, in Yevamot fol. 46.2. Yet this saying does not seem to have been so universal that there were never exceptions, and that baptism alone was not sufficient to make a proselyte. Thus we read in Pesachim ch. 8 that a proselyte may eat the Passover in the evening, provided only that he is baptized.

units.la: E medere poffit in vefpere modo Baptizetur. Et Hierof. Pesachin fol.36.2. fuiffe סטרטיוין Milites Hierofolymis, qui fe baptizarunt & comederunt Pafchata fua vefpere. Vides hos Profelytos effe abfque praeeunte circuncifione.
units.tr: And Jerusalem Pesachim fol. 36.2 says that the soldiers at Jerusalem (στρατιῶται) who baptized themselves and ate their Passover in the evening were such. You see that these proselytes were without preceding circumcision.

units.la: §. Parvuli & infantes, ut plurimùm baptizabantur cum parentibus; fi verò puerulus patre orbatus fit, & mater eum ad baptifmum adducat, iuffu Synedrii praefentibus tribus baptizatur. Bab. (hetubbot fol. 11. 1. vid. Gloff. & Gemaram poft.
units.tr: §. Little children and infants were for the most part baptized along with their parents; but if a little boy has been bereaved of his father, and his mother brings him to baptism, he is baptized by order of the Sanhedrin in the presence of three. Bab. Ketubot fol. 11.1; see the Gloss and the Gemara below.

units.la: §. Si mulier gravida profelytiffa fiat, filius eius deinde non opus habet baptifmo, nam imputatur ei baptifmus matris.Bab.Ievam.f.76.1.
units.tr: §. If a pregnant woman becomes a proselyte, her son has no need of baptism afterwards, for the baptism of the mother is imputed to him. Bab. Yevamot f.76.1.

units.la: §. Si Ifraelita prehendat infantem aut parvulum gentilem, eumque baptizet in nomine profelyti, Ecce ille eft profelytus. Maymon in עברי c. 8. Obferva hic Phrafeologias,Baptizare aliquem in nomine profelyti, item Circuncidere aliquem in nomine liberi, (quae pofterior Phrafeolog. extat Hierof. Ievamot f.8.4.
