In his verbis, Ecce invenit quis Infantem eiectum ac baptizat eum in nomine fervi, circuncide & tu eum in nomine fervi; in nomine liberi, circuncide & tu eum in nomine liberi.) quae nihil aliud fignificant quam Aliquem profelytum aut liberum facere, five talem declarare: ficuti Bab. Ievamot fol.45.2. baptizari לשם אנתה in nomine foeminae nihil aliud eft quàm baptizari נדה שבילת ablutione polluta.
units.tr: §. If an Israelite takes hold of an infant or small gentile child and baptizes him in the name of a proselyte, behold, he is a proselyte. Maimonides in עברי c.8. Observe the phraseology here: to baptize someone in the name of a proselyte, and likewise to circumcise someone in the name of a freeman. The latter phrase occurs in Jerusalem Yevamot f.8.4: "Behold, someone finds an infant cast out and baptizes him in the name of a slave; circumcise him too in the name of a slave; in the name of a freeman, circumcise him in the name of a freeman." These expressions signify nothing other than making someone a proselyte or a freeman, or declaring him to be such. So too in Bab. Yevamot fol.45.2, to be baptized לשם אנתה, "in the name of a woman," means nothing other than to be baptized in the polluted ablution of a menstruating woman.

units.la: §. Non baptizabant profelytum noctu Ievamot fol.46.2.
units.tr: §. They did not baptize a proselyte by night. Yevamot fol.46.2.

units.la: §. Non baptizabant noviter circuncifum nisi post sanatum vulnus, eo quòd aquæ vulneri essent noxiæ Ievamot sol.45. 2.
units.tr: §. They did not baptize a newly circumcised man until the wound had healed, because water would harm the wound. Yevamot fol.45.2.

units.la: §. Nec quidem lavabantur immundi quàm interdiu Megillah sol. 20.1.
units.tr: §. Nor were the unclean washed except by day. Megillah fol.20.1.

units.la: §. Proselytum non baptizabant Sabbatho aut die festo. Maymon. Iffure biah c. 13.
units.tr: §. They did not baptize a proselyte on the Sabbath or on a festival day. Maimonides, Issurei Biah c.13.

units.la: §. In illo Baptismo præsentes esse debent tres discipuli sapientum, qui rem rite præstandam caveant, & Catechumenum paucis instruant; toti negotio tanquam testes adsint. Ievamot f. 46.2. Nos in nostro baptismo tres testes in cæhabemus, Patrem, Filium, & Spiritum Sanctum.
units.tr: §. At that baptism three disciples of the wise must be present, who take care that the matter is rightly done, briefly instruct the catechumen, and stand by as witnesses to the whole transaction. Yevamot f.46.2. In our baptism we have three witnesses: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: §. [illegible, ~12 letters] Noxii sunt proselyti Israeli sicut scabies Ievamot sol. 47. 2: plurimi enim pristinorum morum tenaces, legis Israeliticæ imperiti, dogmata & bonos mores corruperunt.
units.tr: §. [illegible] Proselytes are harmful to Israel like a scab. Yevamot fol.47.2: for most of them, tenacious of their former customs and unskilled in the law of Israel, have corrupted the doctrines and good morals.

units.la: §.Baptizandus erat proselytus in tali מקוה aquarũ congregatione, quæ aliàs idonea erat abluedæ menstruosæ. (de qua vid. Lavabatur homo.)
units.tr: §. The proselyte had to be baptized in such a gathering of waters (a mikveh) as was otherwise suitable for washing the menstruant. (On this see Lavabatur homo.)

units.la: §. Alii אותו טבילין ipsum baptizabant, vel הוא שובל ille ipse se immergebat merstone unâ; & tali ut & apex digiti capillique perfectè mergerentur. Nam si quis se totum abluerit, excepto minimi digiti apice, adhuc immundus censebatur. Maymon. Hal. מקואות c. 1.&.4.
units.tr: §. Others had him immerse himself, or he himself dipped in one immersion, and in such a way that even the tip of a finger and a hair were wholly submerged. For if someone washed his whole body except the tip of the little finger, he was still considered unclean. Maimonides, Hilchot Mikvaot c.1 and 4.

units.la: §. In diebus R. Iosuæ Ben Levi conati sunt quidam extirpare hanc immersionem, fœminarum Galilæarum gratiâ, eo quòd illæ præ frigore sterilescerent.Hierof.Berac.sol.6.3.
units.tr: §. In the days of R. Joshua ben Levi some tried to abolish this immersion for the sake of the Galilean women, because they became barren from the cold. Jerusalem Berakhot fol.6.3.

units.la: §. Postquam aliquis convaluerit à vulnere circuncisionis, adducunt eum ad baptismum; collocatumque in aqua rursus edocent de gravioribus & levioribus quibusdam, quibus auditis immergit se, & ascendit, & ecce tunc est ut Israelita quoad omnia. Foeminam prolectiffam foeminæ sistunt in aquis, collo tenus: duoq; discipuli sapientum ab extra stantes, edocent eam de quibusdam levioribus præceptis, quibusdam-que gravioribus, tum ea interea stat in aquis, & immergit se ipsam: atque illi aversâ facie exeunt, dum ea ascendit ex aqua. Ievam. & Maymon ubi supra. De lotione ab impuritate v. f. 1.
units.tr: §. Once someone has recovered from the wound of circumcision, they bring him to baptism. Placed in the water, he is again instructed about certain weightier and lighter matters; when he has heard these, he immerses himself and comes up, and then, behold, he is in all respects as an Israelite. They set a female proselyte in the water up to her neck, in the presence of a woman. Two disciples of the wise, standing outside, instruct her about certain lighter precepts and certain weightier ones. Meanwhile she stands in the water and immerses herself, and they go out with their faces turned away while she comes up from the water. Yevamot and Maimonides, as above. On washing away impurity see f.1.

units.la: Bath Kol בת קול usum habuit inter Iudæos, postquàm Spiritus Sanctus ab Israele recessit Bab. Sanhed sol. 11. 1. vid. Cl. Buxt. lex. Talm. in בת p. 340.
units.tr: §. Bath Kol [בת קול] was in use among the Jews after the Holy Spirit had departed from Israel. Bab. Sanhedrin fol.11.1; see Buxtorf, Lex. Talm. under בת, p.340.

units.la: §. Propter oraculum à Bath Kol prolatum rebellavit Herodes. vid. supra Baba Ben Butah. An autem Bath Kol vox Spiritus Sancti fuerit debilior ut quidam volunt, an verò Diaboli opus iudicare omnibus in promptu est. Cessaverant enim iam tum, secundùm Iudæorum propria testimonia, Prophetæ cum omnibus reliquis oraculis. Nec hoc quod Herodes audivit, oraculum, aut ullum aliud spiritus sancti naturam sapit: exceptâ forsan voce Migremus hinc, quam auditam fuisse Iosephus memorat, cùm portæ Templi à se ipsis aperiebantur; Quod uti non negamus, ita & affirmare non dubitamus, omnes reliquas τῆς Bath Kol narrationes, meras præstigias & lusus Diaboli fuisse; quibus usus est ad homines seducendos, & veritatem Christianæ doctrinæ diminuendam; quasi illa oracula & voces, quæ Pater cœleftis edidit, quibusque filium suum alloquutus est, & in quibus Christiana religio non parùm fundamenti habet, nihil extraordinarii haberent, & etiam circa alios homines factæ effent, quem palpum eò melius illi generationi obtrudere poterat, quia præter modum omnibus magicis artibus & nequitiis dedita erat. ( vid. Magicas artes.) Sanè Spiritus Sanctus non ad rebellandum adhortatur, si- cuti Bath Kol, respectu Herodis fecisse dicitur, neque ita indifferenter verba Dei commendat, ut hoc vel illud relinquere possimus & supersedere, uti factum in illis verbis quæ in Hierof. Beracot sol. 3. 2. leguntur, quibus Bath Kol dixit, Schammai quidem & Hillelis sententias verba Dei esse : Sed Hillelis verba tamen in controversia, etiam sub pœna mortis sequenda esse. Credibile deinde admodum est, illas declarationes, quas secundùm Hierof. Avoda Sarah sol. 4. 2. & Bab. Sanhed. sol. 11. Bath Kol in gratiam Hillelis & Samuelis Parvi Hierichunte in camera Ben Gadiæ, & in עליית דיבנה Camera Iabbnensi præsentibus senioribus & discipulorum coronâ fecit, illos videlicet idoneos esse recipiendo Spiritum Sanctum : aliquo artificio editas esse, ut his doctoribus eò maior fama & authoritas conciliaretur. Potest etiam esse ut maxima pars harum auditionum τῆς Bath Kol mera imaginatio fuerit, postquàm opinio animis ipsorum insederat, & communis fama obtinuerat tales voces aliquando de cœlo audiri. Nam sicut Bath Kol definitur in Pirke Tofaphot ad Sanhedrin cap. 1: 29. nihil aliud erat, quàm vox (sive Echo) quæ egredicbatur ex voce tonitru. Quìam facilè autem aliquis simplici & credulo ingenio, persuasus in tonitru Bath Kol aeri, sibi imaginari potuit, hæc aut illa verba tonitru nunc protulisse; planè ac aliquando pueri campanis & nolis voces & verba attribuunt. Sed quod adhuc magis est, non solùm tonitru pro רש Bath Kol genitores habuerunt, sed si semel sibi proposuerant Bath Kol audire, quicquid oppidò sensus ipsorum afficiebat, aut in aures illabebatur, statim pro רש Bath Kol voce sumpserunt: exempla adsunt ad manus. Hierof. Schabbat sol.8.3. dicitur, R "Simeon Ben Lachisch, & R. Iochanan defiderarunt videre faciem Samuelis [qui erat Doctor Babylonicus;] sequamur inquiunt, "Bath Kol. Iuxta Scholam ergò itinerantes "audiverunt vocem pueri iflud legentis (in "1.Sam.15.1.) ושמואל מת Et Samuel mortuus est; "Hoc obfervarunt, & sic evenit, nam mortuus "est Samuel Babylonicus, sic cùm R. Iona & R. "Iofe profecti essent visitatum R.Acha ægrotan"tem, etiam sibi proposuerunt vocem BathKol "sequi, in via audiverunt vocem fæminæ, cu"iusdam, vicinæ suæ dicentis, Extinguitur "lucerna, cui illa. Ne extinguatur Lucerna "Israelis. Quæ verba statim tanquam רש Bath Kol in omen morbi interpretati sunt.
units.tr: §. Herod rebelled on account of an oracle delivered by a Bath Kol; see above under Baba ben Buta. Whether the Bath Kol was a voice of the Holy Spirit of lesser power, as some wish, or the work of the Devil, is for everyone to judge at once. For the prophets, together with all the other oracles, had already ceased by then, according to the Jews' own testimonies. Nor does the oracle that Herod heard, or any other, savour of the nature of the Holy Spirit, except perhaps the voice Let us depart hence, which Josephus records was heard when the doors of the Temple opened of their own accord. As we do not deny this, so we do not hesitate to affirm that all the other narratives of the Bath Kol were mere illusions and tricks of the Devil, by which he sought to seduce men and to diminish the truth of Christian doctrine, as if those oracles and voices which the heavenly Father uttered, by which he addressed his Son, and on which the Christian religion has no small foundation, were nothing extraordinary and had also been made to other men. The Devil could the more easily foist these upon that generation, since it was given beyond measure to all magical arts and wickedness. (See Magicas artes.) Surely the Holy Spirit does not urge rebellion, as the Bath Kol is said to have done with regard to Herod, nor does he commend the words of God so indifferently that we may take up this or that and set the rest aside, as happened in those words read in Jerusalem Berakhot fol.3.2, in which the Bath Kol said: "The opinions of Shammai and Hillel are indeed the words of God, but the words of Hillel are to be followed in controversy, even under pain of death." It is also quite credible that those declarations which the Bath Kol made, according to Jerusalem Avodah Zarah fol.4.2 and Bab. Sanhedrin fol.11, in favour of Hillel and Samuel the Younger at Jericho, in the upper room of Ben Gadia, and in the upper room of Yavneh, in the presence of the elders and a crowd of disciples, namely that these men were fit to receive the Holy Spirit, were produced by some contrivance, so that greater fame and authority might be won for these teachers. It may also be that the greater part of these hearings of the Bath Kol was mere imagination, once the opinion had settled in their minds and common report had prevailed that such voices were sometimes heard from heaven. For as the Bath Kol is defined in Pirke Tosafot on Sanhedrin cap.1, 29, it was nothing other than "a voice (or echo) which issued from a clap of thunder." How easily, then, someone of simple and credulous mind, persuaded that the Bath Kol lies in the thunder of the air, could imagine that this or that word had now been uttered by the thunder, just as children sometimes attribute voices and words to bells and cowbells. What is still more, the Jews not only took the thunder for their Bath Kol: if they had once resolved to hear a Bath Kol, whatever sound struck their senses or slipped into their ears they straightway took for a Bath Kol voice. Examples are at hand. In Jerusalem Shabbat fol.8.3 it is said: R. Simeon ben Lakish and R. Johanan wished to see the face of Samuel [who was a Babylonian teacher]. "Let us follow the Bath Kol," they say. Travelling in accordance with the school, they heard the voice of a boy reading (in 1 Sam. 15.1) "And Samuel is dead." They noted this, and so it came about, for the Babylonian Samuel died. Likewise, when R. Jonah and R. Jose had set out to visit the sick R. Acha, they too resolved to follow a Bath Kol. On the way they heard the voice of a certain woman, her neighbour, saying, "The lamp is going out," to which the other replied, "Let not the lamp of Israel be extinguished." These words they at once interpreted, as a Bath Kol, as an omen of the illness.

units.la: §. Cùm R. Eliefer filius Hyrcani inter disputandum, argumentis suis nihil efficere pofset, ut ipsi assensus adhiberetur, exivit Bath Kol & dixit. Quid vobis cum R. Eleafare? secundùm dum quem traditio semper est explicanda. Bava Metzia sol.59.2. Sed nota quomodo Doctor Ieremias respondit: postquàm vocem Bathkol audivit, exclamavit. Quoniam nobis data est lex e monte Sinai, nos non curamus Bath Kol. Idem regerendum Iudaeis, si nobis multitudine illa suarum Bathkol aliquid probare vellent.
units.tr: §. When R. Eliezer ben Hyrcanus, in disputation, could achieve nothing with his arguments so that assent was given to him, a Bath Kol came forth and said: "What have you to do with R. Eliezer? The law is always to be explained according to him." Bava Metzia fol.59.2. But note how the teacher Jeremiah answered: after he had heard the Bath Kol, he exclaimed, "Since the law was given to us from Mount Sinai, we do not heed a Bath Kol." The same should be returned to the Jews, if they wished to prove anything to us by that multitude of their Bath Kols.

units.la: בדיקה Bedika De qua in Sanhed. c.5.2. & alibi, denotat rimationem in Iudiciis, & est secundùm Maymon. דברים שאינם מורים de rebus ad causam essentiam non pertinentibus. v. g. quali veste indutus fuerit creditor &c. De illis verò quae ad causae essentiam pertinent, v. g. quam summam creditor mutuam dedit? vocant חקירה & דרישה quasi diceres ἀνάκρισιν & ἐξέτασιν. Quaeritur loco modo citato, quid interest inter בדיקות & חקירות. Si alter testium ignorantiam suam profiteatur, in חקירות testimonium ipsorum non recipitur. In בדיקה verò, etiamsi uterque urget, sibi constare, testimonium tamen ipsorum non labefactatur. Si verò unus alteri contradicat, tunc testimonium ipsorum nec in חקירה nec in בדיקה recipitur. vid. Maymon. in Sanhed. c. 4.
units.tr: Bedika [בדיקה]: of which Sanhedrin 5.2 and elsewhere speak, denotes a probing in judicial proceedings. According to Maimonides, it concerns matters that do not pertain to the essence of the case (דברים שאינם מורים), e.g. in what sort of clothing the creditor was dressed, and so on. Questions about what pertains to the essence of the case, e.g. what sum the creditor lent, they call chakirah [חקירה] and derishah [דרישה], as if you said ἀνάκρισις and ἐξέτασις. In the passage cited, it is asked what the difference is between bedikot [בדיקות] and chakirot [חקירות]. If one of the witnesses confesses his ignorance, their testimony is not accepted in the chakirot. In the bedika, however, even if each insists that he is consistent, their testimony is not overturned. If one witness contradicts the other, then their testimony is accepted neither in the chakirah nor in the bedika. See Maimonides on Sanhedrin, ch. 4.

units.la: BEELZEBUL Pronuntiarunt Pharisaei Math.12.24. non Beelzebub, ut plurimi pronuntiant, nam Idololatriam probrosò nomine vocarunt זבוב stercus, (vid. Idololat.) Et Daemona inter omnia Daemonia pessimum illum duxerunt qui dominatus est Idolis, & quem proinde בעל זבוב Dominum Idololatriae nominarunt. Princeps spirituum verò est Asmodaeus, sic Aruch ex
units.tr: BEELZEBUL: The Pharisees pronounced it, Matt. 12:24, not Beelzebub, as most people pronounce it. For they called idolatry by the contemptuous name זבוב, dung (see Idololatria). They also regarded as the worst of all demons the one who ruled over the idols, and therefore named him בעל זבוב, Lord of the Idolatry. The prince of the spirits, however, is Asmodeus, so Aruch says

units.la: DeBello varia. §. Rex nulla gerit bella בתחילה primò (& postquàm ad regnum pervenit) אלא ציזוה מלחם nisi bellum præcepti. Quale fuit bellū quod contraVII.populos & Amalekum gellum fuit, aut quale esse potest, quod rex su cipit ad Israelem ab hoste imminente liberandum. Si nullum tale bellum ipsi faciendum incumbit, licet ipsi aggredi 'רשו הרשת מלחמת bellum poteftatis ( vel arbitrarium ) quod est bellum quod (nullo præcepto ad illud obligante) cum reliquis gentibus mundi aggreditur ad fines imperii multiplicandos, ושמעו ולהרבות גדולתו & ad maiestatem famamque suam augendam.
units.tr: On war, various points. §. A king wages no wars בתחילה [at first] (and not until he has come to the kingdom), אלא ציוו מלחמה [but only the war he is commanded], only a war of command. Such was the war against the seven peoples and against Amalek, or such as may be undertaken to deliver Israel from an imminent enemy. If no such war is incumbent on him, he may engage in a war of power (or of choice), which is a war he undertakes (with no command obliging him to it) against the other nations of the world, in order to enlarge the boundaries of his realm, and to increase his greatness and to augment his majesty and fame.

units.la: §. Si aggreditur bellum præc pti non opus habet potestatem à Synedrio magno petere, sed quando lubet egreditur, populumque ad exeundum cogit. At fi bellum potestatis gerere vult, populum absque consensu Synedrii magni educere non debet.
units.tr: §. If he undertakes a war of command, he need not ask the great Sanhedrin for power; he goes out whenever he pleases and compels the people to go out with him. But if he wishes to wage a war of power, he must not lead the people out without the consent of the great Sanhedrin.

units.la: §: Quando verò Rex bellum gerit, extra viam ordinariam erumpere potest, ad viam sibi faciendam, & nemo ipsum impedire poteft ודרך המלך אין לה שיעור nam via regia non est mensura constituta, sed dilatatur pro neceffitate. Quapropter Rex non coarctat vias propter vineam huius, aut agrum illius, sed recta progreditur.
units.tr: §. When the king wages war, he may break out beyond the ordinary road to make a way for himself, and no one may hinder him. דרך המלך אין לה שיעור [the king's road has no fixed measure], for the royal road has no set width, but is widened as necessity requires. Therefore the king does not narrow the roads on account of this man's vineyard or that man's field, but goes straight on.

units.la: §. Præcepto affirmativo Deut.20.17.obligamur ad vii. gentes excindendas, quare fi quis ex ipsis in manus tuas veniat, & tu ipsum non interficis, peccas contra præceptum לא תעשה negativum; hinc etiam videmus omnem iam ipsorum periisse memoriam.
units.tr: §. By the affirmative precept, Deut. 20:17, we are obliged to destroy the seven nations; so if any of them comes into your hands and you do not kill him, you sin against the negative precept, לא תעשה [you shall not]. Hence we also see that the memory of all of them has perished.

units.la: §. Præcepto etiam affirmativo Deut.25. 19. obligamur ad memoriam Amaleki delendam, neque unquam seponere debemus odium & inimicitiam nostram.
units.tr: §. By the affirmative precept, Deut. 25:19, we are obliged to blot out the memory of Amalek, and we must never lay aside our hatred and enmity toward him.

units.la: §. Omnes regiones quas rex ita cum consensu Synedrii subiugaverit sunt רבים כנוש subiugatio multorum ( considerantur ut legitime subactæ ) & similes sunt terræ Israel quam Iehofua vicit. Maymon Hal. Melach.c.v.
units.tr: §. All regions which the king has thus subdued with the consent of the Sanhedrin are רבים כנוש [a subjection of many], a subjection of many (they are regarded as lawfully conquered), and they are like the land of Israel which Joshua conquered. Maimonides, Hilchot Melachim, ch. 5.

units.la: §. Nemini inferunt bellum עד שקוראין שלום לו nisi prius ipsi pacem obtulerint, five fit bellum potestatis, five præcepti. Si pacem acceperint, & septem præcepta filiorum Noæ susceperint, neminem exillis interficiunt, sed fiunt solum tributarii; Si recipere volunt tributum, non vero servitutem, aut fi recipere volunt servitutem non autem tributum, illos non audiunt;recipere debent utrumque.Servitus העבד autem in eo consistit, ut nullis ossiciis in Israële præficiantur, ut humiles sint erga Israelem. Tributum vero ut parati sint infervire regi tam corporibus quàm facultatibus.
units.tr: §. They make war on no one עד שקוראין שלום לו [until they have offered him peace], unless they have first offered him peace, whether it is a war of power or of command. If they accept peace and take upon themselves the seven precepts of the sons of Noah, none of them is killed, but they become merely tributaries. If they are willing to accept tribute but not servitude, or servitude but not tribute, they are not heard; they must accept both. Servitude (העבד) consists in this: that they are placed in no office over Israel, that they are humble toward Israel. Tribute consists in this: that they are ready to serve the king with both their bodies and their goods.

units.la: §. Potest Rex talibus conditionibus cum ipsis transigere, ut accipiat dimidiam partem pecuniæ eorum, aut bonorum immobilium, & relinquat ipsis omnia mobilia, aut omnia immobilia, prout cum ipsis pangere velit. Nefas autem est pactum fallere, postquàm de pace transactum est, & receperunt septem præcepta Noachi.
units.tr: §. The king may make an agreement with them on such terms that he takes half of their money or of their immovable goods, and leaves them all their movable goods, or all their immovable goods, as he wishes to arrange with them. It is unlawful, however, to break a covenant once peace has been agreed and they have accepted the seven precepts of Noah.

units.la: §. Si vero pacem recipere renuunt, bellum cum ipsis gerendum est,licetq; omnes qui arma gerere possunt interficere, facultates diripere; infantes vero & mulieres interficere non licet, nisi in bello praecepti contra Amalekitas aut septem populos Cananiticos: nam ex illis nemo vivus relinquendus est, postquam semel pacem accipere renuerunt.
units.tr: §. If they refuse to accept peace, war must be waged against them, and it is lawful to kill all who can bear arms and to plunder their property. But it is not lawful to kill infants and women, except in the war of command against the Amalekites or the seven Canaanite peoples; for none of these may be left alive, since they have once refused to accept peace.

units.la: §. Antequam terram Canaan ingredere-tur Iosua שלש כתבים tria diplomata scripsit, in primo perscriptum erat; fugiat qui vult; in secundo ישלים להשלים מי שרוצה accipiat pacem qui vult, in tertio מי שרוצה לעשות מלחמה יעשה Qui bellum gerere vult, gerat. Si res ita se habet quare incolae Gibeon astu usi sunt? ℟. quia primitus in genere solum ad pacem invitati erant, illam tamen non acceperunt, ignorantes hunc modum procedendi Israelitas habere, & se serio ad pacem invitari.
units.tr: §. Before Joshua entered the land of Canaan, he wrote three documents (שלש כתבים). In the first it was written: Let him who wishes flee; in the second: Let him who wishes accept peace (ישלים להשלים מי שרוצה); in the third: Let him who wishes to make war, make it (מי שרוצה לעשות מלחמה יעשה). If this is so, why did the inhabitants of Gibeon act with cunning? Answer: because at first they were invited to peace only in general terms, and they did not accept it, not knowing that the Israelites had this manner of proceeding, and that they were seriously invited to peace.

units.la: §. Quando se accingunt ad aliquam urbem oppugnandam, illam non obsident omnibus quatuor angulis vel plagis, sed tantum à tribus, ut relinquant spatium ad fugiendum unicuique qui voluerit eripere vitam suam. Non truncant arbores fructiferas quae sunt extra urbem, nec prohibent ab illis אסת המים canales & irrigationes, ut exarescant. Quicunque arborem truncaverit vapulat, truncant autem steriles quantum voluerint.
units.tr: §. When they set out to attack a city, they do not besiege it on all four sides or quarters, but only on three, so that there remains room for flight for anyone who wishes to save his life. They do not cut down fruit trees outside the city, nor do they cut off from them the אסת המים [water channels and irrigation], channels and irrigation, so that they wither. Whoever cuts down a fruit tree is flogged, but they may cut down barren trees as much as they wish.

units.la: §. Obsident urbes gentium Sabbatho, & praeliantur cum illis Sabbatho, sec. dict. Deut. 20. ult. ubi perinde est, sive bellum fit praecepti sive potestatis.
units.tr: §. They besiege the cities of the nations on the Sabbath, and they fight with them on the Sabbath, according to the last words of Deut. 20, where it makes no difference whether the war is of command or of power.

units.la: §. כשחונין חונין בכל בקום Si Caftrametantur, ubique castra ponere possunt.
units.tr: §. כשחונין חונין בכל מקום [When they encamp, they may encamp anywhere]. If they pitch camp, they may pitch camp anywhere.

units.la: §. Qui in bello interficitur, sepelitur eo loco in quo cecidit.
units.tr: §. He who is killed in battle is buried in the place where he fell.

units.la: §. Quatuor privilegia habent in Castris, 1. possunt comedere (v.Demai.) 2. possunt cibum fumere illotis manibus. 3. possunt advehere ligna ex omnibus locis, 4. sunt liberi (v. Atria & traƈt. עירובין.) nam omnes res in Sabbatho, ex tentorio in tentorium, ex tugurio in tugurium removere possunt.
units.tr: §. They have four privileges in the camp: (1) they may eat (see Demai); (2) they may take food with unwashed hands; (3) they may carry wood from any place; (4) they are free (see Atria and the tractate Eruvin), for on the Sabbath they may remove all things from tent to tent and from hut to hut.

units.la: §. Omnia Castra cingunt macerie altitudine decem palmorum.
units.tr: §. All camps are surrounded by a wall ten handbreadths high.

units.la: §. Prohibitum est evacuare corpus intra fines castrorum, aut in confpeƈtu campi patentis : sed iubet lex ordinare viam peculiarem ad fe ibi evacuandum Deut. xxiii. 12. Similiter praeceptum est ut quilibet paxillum habeat suspensum unâ cum armis suis, & egrediatur in illam viam, & effodiat ibi scrobem quò tegat egestum. Sive arca fœderis in castris fit, five non, semper hoc observandum. Maymon. Hal. Melachim c.6.
units.tr: §. It is forbidden to relieve the body within the bounds of the camp, or in sight of the open field; but the law commands that a special road be arranged for relieving oneself there, Deut. 23:12. Likewise it is commanded that each man have a peg hung up along with his weapons, and that he go out on that road and dig a pit there to cover his dung. Whether or not the ark of the covenant is in the camp, this must always be observed. Maimonides, Hilchot Melachim, ch. 6.

units.la: §. Cùm ad bellum praecepti, tum ad bellum potestatis ordinant Sacerdotem, qui populum alloquatur tempore belli: quem deinde ungunt oleo unctionis (vid. Vnctio,) & ille est qui vulgò vocatur Vnctus belli. Hic Sacerdos duabus vicibus ad populum verba facit, primâ vice quando milites leguntur, ex Deut. xx. 5. Secunda quando iam in acie stant & ad pugnam parati sunt. Tunc enim omnes acies in conspectu habens, ex loco editiori in lingua sancta populum sic alloquitur. Audi Israel, vos proceditis hodie in prelium contra hostes vestros, ne mollescat cor vestrum, ne timete neque trepidate, nec expavescite metu eorum. Nam Iehova Deus vester ambulat vobiscum, praliando pro vobis, ad servandum vos. Et quoniam fieri non potest, ut omnes ipsum Sacerdotem sic loquentem intelligere possint, quod ille dixit per substitutos Sacerdotes, per totum exercitum promulgatur. Deinde Vnctus belli de novo loquitur, Quicunque novam edificavit domum, aut vineam plantavit, aut uxorem duxit, revertatur domum. Hoc per præfectos & elatâ voce divulgatur. (nota illos nón reverti si bellum sit præcepti, quia tunc omnes in bellum ire debent.) Tandem præfecti etiam ita exclamant, Quicunque timent & habent cor molle revertantur. Purgatis ita cohortibus ab omnibus illis qui militia liberi sunt, aciem ordinant, in capita & principia præficiunt capitaneos, à tergo autem constituunt præsectos (fergeans) fortes & validos וכשולין של ברזל בידיהן claves ferreas in manibus tenentes, illisque dant potestatem ossa comminuendi illorum qui à pugna secedere vellent.
units.tr: §. Both for a war of command and for a war of power they appoint a priest, who addresses the people at the time of battle; he is then anointed with the anointing oil (see Unctio), and he is the one commonly called the anointed for war. This priest speaks to the people twice: the first time when the soldiers are enrolled, from Deut. 20:5; the second when they already stand in battle array and are ready to fight. For then, having all the lines in view, he addresses the people from a higher place in the holy tongue in this way: Hear, O Israel, you go out today to battle against your enemies; let not your heart be faint, do not fear or tremble, nor be terrified by them. For the LORD your God goes with you, fighting for you, to save you. And since it cannot happen that all can understand the priest speaking thus, what he has said is proclaimed through the whole army by appointed priests. Then the anointed for war speaks again: Whoever has built a new house, or planted a vineyard, or taken a wife, let him return home. This is proclaimed through the officers and in a loud voice. (Note that these do not return if the war is of command, because then all must go to war.) Finally the officers also cry out: Whoever is afraid and has a faint heart, let him return. When the cohorts have thus been cleared of all who are free from military service, they arrange the battle line, they appoint captains at the head and at the front, and at the rear they station strong and vigorous officers (fergeans) holding iron clubs in their hands, and they give them power to break the bones of those who would withdraw from the battle.

units.la: §. Illi verò qui audită Sacerdotis unćti voce ita ex acie excedunt, alimenta deinde subministrant exercitui, & vias disponunt.
units.tr: §. Those, however, who on hearing the voice of the anointed Priest leave the battle line then supply food to the army and prepare the roads.

units.la: §. Nullus qui prole caret & sterilis est in
units.tr: §. No one who is without offspring and is barren is

units.la: bellum ire cogitur, talem enim אין מטריחין בשום דבר non obligant ad ullum officium subeundum. Maymon. Hal. Melach. cap. 7.
units.tr: compelled to go to war, for they do not obligate anyone to undertake any office [אין מטריחין בשום דבר]. Maymon. Hal. Melach. cap. 7.

units.la: Bileam de quo usurpant hoc dictum; Camelus abiens quaesitum cornua, aures abscindebant ipsi. Sanhed. folio 106. 1. Ielammedenu folio 83. 2. Postquàm enim mercede conductus erat, ut prophetaret adversus populum Dei, amisit donum prophetiæ quo praeditus erat.
units.tr: Balaam, of whom they use this saying: A camel going away sought horns; they themselves cut off its ears. Sanhed. fol. 106.1. Ielammedenu fol. 83.2. For after he was hired to prophesy against the people of God, he lost the gift of prophecy with which he had been endowed.

units.la: Tres sunt Reges & quatuor Idiotæ, quibus nulla est pars in seculo venturo: Tres Reges sunt Ieroboam, Achab & Manasses: Quatuor idiotæ sunt, Bileam, Doeg, Achitophel & Gehasi; Sanhed. folio 90. 1. Bileam habuit duos filios יוחנא ומברא Iannes καὶ Iambres de quibus Apostolus 2. ad Timoth. 3. 8. vid. Cl. Buxtorf. Lex. Talmud. p. 945.
units.tr: There are three kings and four idiots who have no portion in the age to come. The three kings are Jeroboam, Ahab and Manasseh. The four idiots are Balaam, Doeg, Ahithophel and Gehazi. Sanhed. fol. 90.1. Balaam had two sons, Iannes and Iambres [יוחנא ומברא; Ἰάννης καὶ Ἴαμβρης], of whom the Apostle speaks in 2 Tim. 3.8. See Cl. Buxtorf, Lex. Talm. p. 945.

units.la: Ben Nezer apud Iudaeos famosus fuit latro. Chetubbot folio 51. 2. Hic (in Palæstina) Ben Nezer vocatur Rex. Hic verò (in Babylonia) vocatur latro קרי ליסטיס Glossa. Ben Nezer latro fuit, & cepit urbes, & regnavit in iis, & factus est Dux latronum.
units.tr: Ben Nezer was a famous robber among the Jews. Chetubbot fol. 51.2. Here (in Palestine) Ben Nezer is called King, but there (in Babylonia) he is called robber [קרי ליסטיס]. Gloss: Ben Nezer was a robber, and he took cities and reigned in them, and became leader of the robbers.

units.la: §. De Ben Nezer etiam legimus in Beresch. Rabba Sect. 76. Intuitus sum cornua, & ecce cornu aliud parvum ascendit inter ea (Dan. VII. 8.) זה בן נצר Hic est Ben Nezer. Admodum fallor si aculeato hoc stylo Christum, qui vocatur Ναζωραῖος, non petant, nam solent ita obtegere malam suam mentem obscura aliqua expressione; suspicionem auget, quod Aruch in voce קרן locum illum Danielis exponat per מלכות הכותים regnum Cuthaeorum, qua formula loquendi ut plurimum Christianorum imperium significare solent.vid.Cl.Buxt.Lex.Talm.p.1383.
units.tr: §. We read of Ben Nezer also in Bereshit Rabba, sect. 76: I looked at the horns, and behold, another little horn came up among them (Dan. 7.8): [זה בן נצר] This is Ben Nezer. I am much mistaken if with this barbed pen they are not aiming at Christ, who is called the Nazarene [Ναζωραῖος], for they are accustomed to cover their evil mind in this way with some obscure expression. Suspicion is increased by the fact that the Aruch, under the word קרן, explains that passage of Daniel as [מלכות הכותים] the kingdom of the Cuthaeans, a form of speech by which they usually mean the empire of the Christians. See Cl. Buxtorf, Lex. Talm. p. 1383.

units.la: בן דינאי Ben Dinai Etiam fuit latro apud Talmudicos celeberrimus,nam postquam flagitiosus esse incepit ita multiplicatus fuit homicidarum numerus, ut Synedrium coactum fuerit Ceremoniam decapitationis vaccae (de qua vid. Iuvenca decollatio.) abrogare. vid. Sotah sol.47.1.
units.tr: [בן דינאי] Ben Dinai was also a most celebrated robber among the Talmudists. After he began to be wicked, the number of murderers increased so much that the Sanhedrin was compelled to abolish the ceremony of beheading the heifer (on which see Iuvenca decollatio). See Sotah fol. 47.1.

units.la: §. Huius Ben Dinai enormia crimina secerunt, ut ipsi nomen mutatum fuerit; antea enim vocabatur Techina Ben Perifcha, sed deinde ipsum vocarunt בן הרצחן Filium homicidam.
units.tr: §. The heinous crimes of this Ben Dinai brought it about that his name was changed. For previously he was called Techina Ben Perischa, but afterwards they called him [בן הרצחן] son of the murderer.

units.la: §. De Ben Dinai etiam mentio fit Chetubbot sol. 27.1. ubi scribitur בן דונאי Ben Donai. vide etiam Kelim sol.12.2.
units.tr: §. Ben Dinai is also mentioned in Chetubbot fol. 27.1, where it is written [בן דונאי] Ben Donai. See also Kelim fol. 12.2.

units.la: בן סטדא Ben Sadta exportavit magias ex Ægypto per caesuras quas fecerat in carne sua (ne scilicet a magis Ægyptiacis deprehenderetur, noluerunt enim illi suas artes vulgares fieri.) Bab.Schabbat sol.104 2. vid. Cl. Buxt. Lex. Talm.p.1460. In Ægyptum autem migravit cum Iehosua fil. Perachiae, Sanhed. sol.107.2. vid. etiam supra Ægyptus.
units.tr: [בן סטדא] Ben Sadta brought magic out of Egypt through the cuts he had made in his flesh (so that he would not be detected by the Egyptian magicians, for they did not want their arts to become common). Bab. Schabbat fol. 104.2. See Cl. Buxtorf, Lex. Talm. p. 1460. He migrated to Egypt with Iehosua son of Perachia, Sanhed. fol. 107.2. See also above under Ægyptus.

units.la: §. Cur mater eius ita vocetur rationem reddit Gemara in Schabb. l.c. משת רא מבעלה declinavit ea a Marito.
units.tr: §. The reason why his mother is so called is given by the Gemara on Schabbat, l.c.: [משת רא מבעלה] she turned away from her husband.

units.la: §. In loco citato Sanhed. dicunt ישו כשף Iesus magicam exercuit, & decepit, atque ad idololatriam adegit Israelem. Item sol. 43. 1. eiusdem tractatus haec leguntur. Vespere pafchatis suspenderunt Iesum, & mortem eius praecessit praco per quadriginta dies sic dicens, Egreditur ille lapidandus, eo quod praestigiis usus est, & decepit, atque ad idololatriam adegit Israelem.
units.tr: §. In the place cited, Sanhed., they say [ישו כשף] Jesus practised magic and deceived, and led Israel into idolatry. Likewise in fol. 43.1 of the same tractate these words are read: On the evening of Passover they hanged Jesus, and for forty days a herald went before his death, saying thus: "He goes forth to be stoned, because he practised sorcery and deceived and led Israel into idolatry."

units.la: §. Matrem Ben Sadtae dicunt fuisse מרים מגדלא (fubolfacio Μαρίαν Μαγδαλήνην.) Bab. Sanhed. sol. 67. 1. Lapidarunt Ben Sadta in Lydda, & suspenderunt eum in vespera Pafchatis. Hic autem filius Sadta, fuit filius Pandira. Dixit quidem Rabh Chafda Maritus (matris eius) fuit Sadta, maritus Pandira, maritus Papus fil. Iuda. Sed tamen dico matrem eius fuisse Sadtam נשיא מגדלא מרים Mariam videlicet, plicatricem capillorum mulierum. Vid. Schabbat sol. 104. 2. Chagiga sol. 4. 2. & Gloss. In Gittin sol. 90. 1. dicitur Papus Ben Iuda fuit maritus נשים מגדלא מרים orta est inter ipsos discordia, & illa se in adulteria praecipitavit.
units.tr: §. They say that the mother of Ben Sadta was [מרים מגדלא] (Mary of Magdala, Μαρίαν Μαγδαλήνην). Bab. Sanhed. fol. 67.1: They stoned Ben Sadta in Lydda and hanged him on the evening of Passover. This Ben Sadta was son of Pandira. Rav Chisda indeed said: the husband (of his mother) was Sadta, the husband Pandira, the husband Papus son of Judah. But still I say his mother was Sadta, [נשיא מגדלא מרים] Mary, that is, the dresser of women's hair. See Schabbat fol. 104.2, Chagiga fol. 4.2 and the Gloss. In Gittin fol. 90.1 it is said: Papus ben Judah was the husband of [נשים מגדלא מרים] and discord arose between them, and she threw herself into adultery.

units.la: §. An per Ben Sadta Iudaei latus Domini nostri fodiant in utramque partem disputant viri docti. Negat R. Tam ad locum Schabbat sol. 104. 2. Iesum Nazarenum intelligi. Affirmant alii, ipsos Iudaeos ex professo aliquas historiae circumstantias corrupisse, ne Christiani virus percipere possint. Pro hac sententia multum ponderis addit sententia Iuchafin p. 17. 1. quâ R. Abraham existimat R. Perachiam cum quo dicunt Iesum in Ægyptum fugisse,
units.tr: §. Learned men dispute on both sides whether the Jews, by means of Ben Sadta, pierce the side of our Lord. R. Tam, on the passage in Schabbat fol. 104.2, denies that Jesus the Nazarene is meant. Others affirm that the Jews themselves had deliberately corrupted certain circumstances of the history, so that Christians might not perceive the poison. The opinion of Juchasin p. 17.1 adds much weight to this view, in which R. Abraham thinks that R. Perachia, with whom they say Jesus fled into Egypt,

units.la: fuisse etiam Domini nostri præceptorem; quomodo autem hac ratione Chronologiam corrumpant, ostendimus in Hist. Doct. Misnic. quam Oxonii in lucem emisimus.
units.tr: was also the teacher of our Lord. How they corrupt chronology in this way we have shown in the Hist. Doct. Misnic., which we published at Oxford.

units.la: בן כוזבא Ben Cosba impostor, cuius causâ facta est ab Adriano obsidio Betharana. Cur interfectus fuerit rationem habemus in Bab. Sanhed. sol. 93.2. Dixit Rabba Messias odorabit & iudicabit (sciet ὑσμήσεις hominum, sicuti Christus se hanc notam habere commonstravit Matth.12.25.) Non per confpectum oculorum iudicabit &c. Ben Cosba regnavit annos duos & dimidium; dixitque Rabbinis; Ego sum Messias: dixerunt ei, de Messia scribitur quod odorabit, & iudicabit; (Gloss. subolebit ei de homine,) videamus nos num odorare tu possis & iudicare כיון דחויה דלא בריח ודאין קטילוה Cumque viderent non posse eum odorare & iudicare, interfecerunt ipsum.
units.tr: [בן כוזבא] Ben Cosba, an impostor, on whose account Hadrian laid siege to Bethar. We have the reason for his death in Bab. Sanhed. fol. 93.2: Rabba said: The Messiah will smell out and judge (he will perceive the odours of men, just as Christ showed that he had this mark, Matt. 12.25) not by the sight of his eyes will he judge, etc. Ben Cosba reigned two and a half years, and said to the rabbis: I am the Messiah. They said to him: Of the Messiah it is written that he will smell out and judge (Gloss: he will perceive a man by smell) let us see whether you can smell out and judge. [כיון דחויה דלא בריח ודאין קטילוה] When they saw that he could not smell out and judge, they killed him.

units.la: §. In aliis locis verò dicitur ipsum בר כוכב five Cosba in clade expugnationis urbis cecidisse, non autem à propriis hominibus cecidisse. Vid. plura inferiùs in ביתר vid. Sanhed.97.
units.tr: §. In other places, however, it is said that Ben Cosba, or Bar Kokhba [בר כוכב], fell in the disaster of the capture of the city, and not that he fell at the hands of his own people. See more below under [ביתר]. See Sanhed. 97.

units.la: 2. Gittin 57.1. Zemach David 41. Taanit.68.2.
units.tr: 2. Gittin 57.1. Zemach David 41. Taanit 68.2.

units.la: בני בתירא Bene Bethira fuerunt in Sodalitio Schemajæ & Abtalionis, & cùm Hillel veniret ex Babel, ut post ipsos principatum ambiret, ipsimet Hillelem principem constituerunt, semet ipsos ex humilitate principatu abdicantes. Historia extat in Hierof. Pesachim sol. 33. 1. Traditio aliquando excidit filiis Bethira, nam inciderat dies decimus quartus, (quo Pascha celebrari debebat) in Sabbatum thum, & illi ignorabant an pafcha Sabbathum pelleret nec ne. Hunc fcrupulum ipfis exemit Hillel, & propterea ipfum ad præfecturam promoverunt.
units.tr: [בני בתירא] The Bene Bethira were in the fellowship of Shemaiah and Abtalion. When Hillel came from Babylon to seek the leadership after them, they themselves appointed Hillel prince, renouncing the leadership out of humility. The story is in Hierof. Pesachim fol. 33.1: The tradition once slipped from the sons of Bethira, for the fourteenth day (on which the Passover was to be celebrated) fell on the Sabbath, and they did not know whether the Passover overrode the Sabbath or not. Hillel removed this scruple from them, and for that reason they promoted him to the presidency.

units.la: §. Nomina horum fratrum ; fuerunt Iehuda& Iehofua, quorum prior diutiffimè vixit, & fub fenectutem fuam fe in Babel contulit, à quo loco Hierofolymas nunquam reverfus eft; ne quidem in feftis folennibus, quia ætate & annis, & apparitione publica, excufatus erat. Vid. Iuchafin fol.18, 2. 19.1.
units.tr: §. The names of these brothers: they were Jehuda and Iehosua. The former lived a very long time, and in his old age he withdrew to Babylon, from which place he never returned to Jerusalem, not even at the solemn feasts, since he was excused on account of his age, his years and his public standing. See Juchasin fol. 18.2, 19.1.

units.la: רועי בהמה דקה Rogne behema dakka, vid. Pastores.
units.tr: [רועי בהמה דקה] Rogne behema dakka; see Ministers.

units.la: Benedictiones varias nobis tractatus Beracot describit.
units.tr: The tractate Berachot describes for us various blessings.

units.la: §. Quales benedictiones dicere debeat qui Sacerdotes in templo congregatos videt recenfetur Hierof. Berac.p.2.c.3. fub med.
units.tr: §. What blessings one ought to say who sees the priests gathered in the temple is recounted in Hierof. Berac. p. 2, c. 3, under the middle.

units.la: §. Ex benedictionibus aliquis dignosci poteft, an difcipulus fapientis vel idiota fit.Ibid.
units.tr: §. From the blessings one can tell whether someone is a disciple of a wise man or an ignorant man. Ibid.

units.la: §. Benedictio pro arboribus eft בורא פרי העץ וכו' Pro vino בורא פרי הגפן וכו' Pro pane המוציא לחם מן הארץ וכו' Benedictio pro illo quod de terra non nafcitur, pro aceto, pro fructibus deciduis, pro הגובאי locuftis (quales cibus Ioh. Bapt. fuerunt) eft illa quæ incipit שהכל five per cuius verbum fiunt omnia Berac. c.6.3.
units.tr: §. The blessing for trees is [בורא פרי העץ וכו'] who creates the fruit of the tree, etc. For wine it is [בורא פרי הגפן וכו'] who creates the fruit of the vine, etc. For bread it is [המוציא לחם מן הארץ וכו'] who brings forth bread from the earth, etc. The blessing for that which does not grow from the earth, for vinegar, for fallen fruits, and for locusts [הגובאי] (such as John the Baptist's food was) is that which begins [שהכל], by whose word all things come to be. Berachot c. 6.3.

units.la: §. Non benedicendum pro eo quod fpecies maledictionis eft. Benedicit unufquifque feorfim fi ad comedendum confederint; fiverò accubuerint, unus benedicit omnium nomine. Benedicendi regula generalis eft, quod ubicunque fit principale cum accessorio v.g. salsamentum & panis, sufficiat si <bl>העקר</bl> principale (quale in exemplo adducto est salsamentum) benedicatur. Berac. c.6.7.8
units.tr: §. It is not to be blessed over what is a kind of curse. Each person blesses separately if they gather to eat; but if they recline together, one blesses on behalf of all. The general rule for blessings is that where there is a principal item with an accessory, e.g. salted relish and bread, it suffices to bless the principal, which in the example given is the salted relish [העקר]. Berac. c.6.7.8

units.la: §. Non benedicunt pro cibo nisi quantitatem ovi, aut ad minimum olivæ habeat. Benedictionem ita instituunt ut præsentibus tribus dicat נברך benedicamus; præsentibus decem dicat נברך אלוהינו Benedicamus Deo nostro. Prout ille benedixerit vicissim præsentes post eum ea repetendo benedicunt. Berac. c. 7. 3. Non benedicunt pro vino priusquàm ei aqua sit affusa. Non benedicunt pro candela aut aromatibus gentium, neque pro lucerna aut aromatibus mortuorum Berac.8.
units.tr: §. They do not bless over food unless it amounts to at least the size of an egg, or at the least an olive. They institute the blessing thus: if three are present, the one who leads says let us bless [נברך]; if ten are present, he says let us bless our God [נברך אלוהינו]. As he has blessed, those present afterwards repeat the words and bless in turn. Berac. c.7.3. They do not bless over wine until water has been poured into it. They do not bless over a candle or over the spices of the Gentiles, nor over a lamp or the spices of the dead. Berac.8.

units.la: §. Cùm quis locum videt, in quo edita sunt Israeli miracula, ita benedicet ברוך שעשה נסים לאבותינו Benedictus sit ille qui fecit signa Patrum nostrùm. Si verò conspicit locum ex quo idololatria extirpata, tunc ita benedicit ברוך שעיקר עבור זרה
units.tr: §. When someone sees a place where miracles were done for Israel, he blesses thus: [ברוך שעשה נסים לאבותינו] Blessed be he who wrought signs for our fathers. But if he sees a place from which idolatry was uprooted, then he blesses thus: [ברוך שעיקר עבודה זרה].

units.la: §· Benedictio quam ob cometas dicunt, aut fulgura, tonitrua, ventos hæc est <bl>ברוך שכוחו וגבורתו מלא עולם</bl>
units.tr: §. The blessing they say on account of comets, or lightnings, thunders and winds, is: [ברוך שכוחו וגבורתו מלא עולם] Blessed be he whose strength and might fill the world.

units.la: §. Etiam benedicunt ob montes, colles, maria, imbres, nuntia bona & nuntia mala, pro bono quidem מעין הרעה respectu mali, pro malo הטובה מעין respectu boni.
units.tr: §. They also bless over mountains, hills, seas, rains, and over good news and bad news: for good news, [מעין הרעה] in respect of evil; for bad news, [הטובה מעין] in respect of good.

units.la: §. Ab Esra & Synedrio constitutum est, ut omnibus benedictionibus in Sanctuario adderetur clausula מן העולם ועד עולם à sæculo in sæculum; ut animis Ecclesiæ antitodum aliquod contra pravam de futuro seculo Sadducæorum fum opinionem inftillaretur. Beracot.c.9.
units.tr: §. Ezra and the Sanhedrin ordained that the clause [מן העולם ועד עולם] from age to age be added to all the blessings in the Sanctuary, so that some antidote against the Sadducees' perverse opinion about the future age might be instilled into the minds of the Church. Beracot c.9.

units.la: §. Sacerdotum benedicendi ratio in בתי כנסיות Synagogis hæc erat, ftabant ut poffent vertere facies fuas verfus populum; Minifter verò Ecclefiæ erat è regione Sacerdotum, & verbotim recitabat tres benedictiones, hac ratione, Benedicat te &c. Refponderunt Sacerdotes Benedicat te, & fic in cæteris : ufquedum in ultima benedictione totus populus dicat Amen. Vid. Maymon in Berac.c.5.4.Pluta vid.ap. Preces, Orationes.
units.tr: §. The manner in which the priests blessed in the synagogues [בתי כנסיות] was this: they stood so that they could turn their faces toward the people; the minister of the congregation stood opposite the priests and recited the three blessings word for word, in this way: May he bless you, etc. The priests answered May he bless you, and so on through the rest, until at the last blessing the whole people said Amen. See Maimonides on Berakhot c.5.4. More is found under Prayers, Orations.

units.la: Bethoron eft Iofepho Βαιθωρὼ de bello lib. 1. c.10. & diftitit fucundùm eum C. circiter ftadia ab Hierofolymis. Antiq.lib.20.c.4.
units.tr: Bethoron is Βαιθωρὼ in Josephus, On the War book 1 c.10, and according to him it was about a hundred stadia from Jerusalem. Antiquities book 20 c.4.

units.la: §. In Bethoron periit exercitus magnus Cananiticus Iof. x. fecundùm Iudæos non fimplici grandine fed lapidibus ad hoc ævum ufque durantibus obrutus. Hinc illud Bab.Beracot fol. 54. 1. Quicunque viderit locum ubi Ifraelita tranfierunt mare, ubi tranfierunt Iordanem, ubi fluvius Arnon, aut אבני אלגביש lapides illos grandes in defcenfu Bethhoronis, benedicere tenetur.
units.tr: §. At Bethoron a great Canaanite army perished (Josh. 10), according to the Jews overwhelmed not by ordinary hail but by stones that last down to this day. Hence that passage in the Babylonian Berakhot fol. 54.1: "Whoever sees the place where the Israelites crossed the sea, where they crossed the Jordan, the river Arnon, or the great hailstones [אבני אלגביש] on the descent of Bethoron, is bound to bless."

units.la: §. Credunt eodem loci cecidiffe exercitum Sancheribi. vid.Gloff. in verba prædicta.
units.tr: §. They believe that the army of Sennacherib fell in the same place. See the Gloss on the words above.

units.la: §. Afcenfus Bethoronis erat admodum angustus, nec erat, quò declinares ad dextram aut finiftram Bab. Sanhed. fol.32 2. in Gloff. In his angustiis cladem passus est Ceftius apud Iofeph.de bello lib.2. c.4.
units.tr: §. The ascent to Bethoron was very narrow, and there was no room to turn aside to the right or the left. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 32.2, in the Gloss. In these narrows Cestius suffered defeat, as Josephus relates in On the War book 2 c.4.

units.la: Bethel erat olim Luza de qua vide nugantes Rabbinos in Iud. 1.23.
units.tr: Bethel was formerly Luza, on which see the trifling Rabbis on Judges 1.23.

units.la: §. Bethel aliquando vocatur Beth-aven
units.tr: §. Bethel is sometimes called Beth-aven.

units.la: Hierof. Schab. fol. 11. 4. Avod. Sarah fol. 43. 3. Oppidum illud quod aliquando vocatum eft Bethel, postea vocatum eft Bethaven, (propter idololatriam hoc nomen ipsi impofuerunt.) vid. etiam Chaldæum ad Hof. iv. 15.
units.tr: Jerusalem Shabbat fol. 11.4. Avodah Zarah fol. 43.3: "The town that was once called Bethel was afterwards called Bethaven" (they gave it this name on account of idolatry). See also the Chaldee on Hosea 4.15.

units.la: §. Sita erat Bethel in montano Iof. 16. 1.
units.tr: §. Bethel lay in the mountain country, Josh. 16.1.

units.la: BETHANIA & Beth-amara idem sunt, ficuti apud Talmudicos בית עמרא significat locum lana, & בית עניא locum ovium. Vel si בית הניא legendum erit, quasi Domus doctrinæ, non mirum est si Βηθανία aliquando apud Ev. Ioh. ponatur per Βηθσαβαρα, nam בית הבדה etiam domum explicationis doctrinæ significat. Non itaque mirandum si idem locus apud sacros authores multiplici nomine aliquando in diversis exemplaribus exprimatur.
units.tr: Bethania and Beth-amara are the same; so among the Talmudists [בית עמרא] means place of wool, and [בית עניא] place of sheep. Or if [בית הניא] is to be read, as house of teaching, it is no wonder that in the Gospel of John Βηθανία is sometimes given as Βηθσαβαρα, for [בית הבדה] also means house of the explanation of doctrine. It is therefore no wonder that the same place is in sacred authors sometimes expressed under various names in different copies.

units.la: §. Bethania in qua Christus sæpius diversatus est, forsan ille ipse locus est quem Talmudici חניות בני חנן Taberna filiorum (Chanan, Hierof. Berac. fol. 16. 1. & חניות של בית הניו Tabernas τῆς Beth heno, Bab. Metzia fol. 88. 1. vocant. Nam primò בית הניו Beth Heno, & בית הניו Bethene sive Bethania idem sunt. Deinde certum est Bethaniam fuisse in aliquo tractu montis oliveti, at Hierof. Taanit fol. 69. 2. expressa Tabernarum in monte oliveto fit mentio, in his verbis. Duæ Cedri erant in monte oliveto, sub una earum erant quatuor Taberna, ubi vendebantur omnia ad purificationes necessaria &c.
units.tr: §. Bethany, where Christ often lodged, is perhaps the very place which the Talmudists call the booths of the sons of Hanan [חניות בני חנן] (Jerusalem Berakhot fol. 16.1) and the booths of Beth Heno [חניות של בית הניו] (Bab. Metzia fol. 88.1). For, first, Beth Heno and Bethene or Bethania are the same. Then it is certain that Bethany lay in some part of the Mount of Olives; and Jerusalem Taanit fol. 69.2 expressly mentions booths on the Mount of Olives, in these words: There were two cedars on the Mount of Olives; under one of them were four booths where everything necessary for purifications was sold, etc.

units.la: §. In Bethania fuit lavatorium מרחץ, ut apparet ex historiola Gemaristarum in Bab. Cholin. fol. 53. 1. Dilaceravit vulpes ovem במרחץ בית הניו ad lavatorium Bethanienfe, ad- ducta ducta est causa coram sapientibus, ut diiudicarent an ovis esset דריסה vel טריפה ? (vid. Lex. Buxt.) Probabile est in hac collectione aquarum se lavasse qui immundi erant, & deinde coemptis ex illis tabernis quas in Bethania fuisse diximus, quae ad oblationes pro purificationibus requirebantur, recta Hierosolymam tendisse.
units.tr: §. In Bethany there was a bath [מרחץ], as appears from the little story of the Gemarists in Bab. Chullin fol. 53.1: A fox tore a sheep at the bath of Bethany; the case was brought before the sages to decide whether the sheep was trampled [דריסה] or torn [טריפה]? (see Buxtorf's lexicon). It is probable that in this gathering of waters those who were unclean washed themselves, and then, having bought what was required for the offerings of purification from those booths which we said were in Bethany, went straight to Jerusalem.

units.la: בית גוברין Beth Gubbrin, huius loci situs latet; fuit quaedam גברה Gabbara supra Caesaream Philippi, sed incertum est an Beth Gubhrin fuerit nec ne. Beth Gubhrin aliquam famam obtinuit propter R. Iochanan de quo Hierof. Megillah sol. 71. 2.
units.tr: [בית גוברין] Beth Gubbrin: the site of this place is obscure. There was a certain Gabbara above Caesarea Philippi, but it is uncertain whether Beth Gubrin was that place or not. Beth Gubrin gained some fame on account of R. Iochanan, concerning whom see Jerusalem Megillah fol. 71.2.

units.la: בית המוקד Beth hammoked, Locus focarius. In templo duo loca fuerunt sic vocata, unus focus magnus, alter focus parvus; in magno foco vel culina erat semper ignis ad calefaciendum pedes Sacerdotum custodum templi, qui nudis pedibus semper incedebant. In parva culina erat ignis, de quo petebatur ignis ad sacrificia, quando ignis iste erat pluviis extinctus. Tamid. c. 1.
units.tr: [בית המוקד] Beth hammoked, the place of the hearth. In the Temple there were two places so called: one the great hearth, the other the small hearth. In the great hearth or kitchen there was always a fire to warm the feet of the priests who kept guard in the Temple and who always walked with bare feet. In the small kitchen there was a fire from which fire was taken for the sacrifices when that fire had been put out by the rains. Tamid c.1.

units.la: §. Tribus locis Sacerdotes excubias agunt, in Beth Abtines, in Nitsots, & loco focario, Middot c. 1.
units.tr: §. The priests keep watch in three places: in Beth Abtines, in Nitsots, and at the hearth. Middot c.1.

units.la: §. בית המוקד כיפה ובית גדול היה מוקף רובדים אבן של locus focarius erat fornix ac domus magna cincta intrinsecus stratis lapideis. Tamid. c.1. vid. Bartenoram Comment.
units.tr: §. [בית המוקד כיפה ובית גדול היה מוקף רובדים אבן] The place of the hearth was a vaulted chamber, and the great house was surrounded inside by stone pavements. Tamid c.1. See Bartenora's commentary.

units.la: §. Quatuor conclavia erant in loco focario (magno,) quorum duo erant in loco sancto, duo vero in profano, habebat etiam duas portas, una aperta erat verfus fpatium intermurale, altera vero atrium refpiciebat. Middot. c. 1. 6. 7. vid. etiam Maymon. Hal. Beth Habeth.c.5. circa med.
units.tr: §. There were four chambers in the (great) hearth place: two were in the holy place and two in the profane. It also had two gates: one opened toward the intermural space, the other looked toward the court. Middot c.1, 6, 7. See also Maimonides, Hilchot Beth Habechirah c.5, about the middle.

units.la: Beth Chadudo eft locus ubi erenium incepit,diftans ab Hierofolyma tribus milliaribus,in regione Bethoronis; illa via ducebatur hircus Azazel. Ioma fol.68. 2.
units.tr: [בית חדודו] Beth Chadudo is the place where the desert began, three miles from Jerusalem, in the region of Bethoron; by that road the goat for Azazel was led. Yoma fol. 68.2.

units.la: Beth Cherem eft vallis, ex qua lapides ad altare exftruendum adduƈti fuerunt. Middot c.3. 4. terra huius vallis aquam ita coloravit, ut illa non diffimilis fuerit fanguinis profluviosæ, hinc illa formula loquendi in Nidda cap.2.v.ult. בימי אדמה מבקעת בית כרם Ut aqua terra è convalle Beth (erem.
units.tr: [בית כרם] Beth Cherem is a valley from which stones were brought to build the altar. Middot c.3, 4. The earth of this valley coloured water so that it was not unlike the blood of one suffering a flux; hence that expression in Niddah c.2, last verse: as water with earth from the valley of Beth-cherem.

units.la: Beth Maron, de hoc loco fit mentio in Schemot Rabba fe&t. 5. Historia est de fratre & forore, frater habitabat in גוש חלב Gufch Chalab, foror vero in בית מרון Beth Maron. Ortum est incendium in Gufch Chalab, & venit foror complexaque fratrem est. Fuerunt itaque hæc loca vicina, at Gufch Chalab fuit in Aferitide, ut patet ex historia de oleo pretiofissimo coempto in Gufch Chalab. Menachot fol.85. 2.
units.tr: [בית מרון] Beth Maron: this place is mentioned in Shemot Rabba section 5. The story concerns a brother and sister: the brother lived in Gush Chalav [גוש חלב], the sister in Beth Maron. A fire broke out in Gush Chalav, and the sister came and embraced her brother. These places were therefore neighbouring; and Gush Chalav was in Aferitis, as is clear from the story of very precious oil bought in Gush Chalav. Menachot fol. 85.2.

units.la: §. De Maronita vel Maronenfi exstant historiæ in Hierof. Kiddufchin fol. 6. 3. & Bava Bathra fol. 17. 1.
units.tr: On the Maronite, or Maronensian, there are accounts in Hierof. Kiddufchin fol. 6.3 and Bava Bathra fol. 17.1.

units.la: §. In tractatu Rofch hafchana folio 16. 1. hic locus mihi non parum difficultatis creavit, cum illum tract. recenfebam. In initio anni כל באי עולם עוברין למניו כנגי מרון Omnes venientes in mundum transeunt coram Deo sicut filii Maron. Quidam מרון בני כבני interpretantur, ut oves, quo fundamento nescio; In Gemara Resch Lakisch interpretatur כמעולות בני מרון Sicut asceníus Beth Maron, qui secundum Glossam, erat via admodum angusta, ut duo non potuerint simul illic incedere, unus a latere alterius, nam erat profunda vallis ab utroque via latere. Ita ut sensus loci sit, homines tunc cum annum incipit a Deo quasi recenseri, & in lustratione unum post alterum dijudicari, eadem ratione ac per ascensum Maronitanum unus post alterum procedit, & in conspectum venit.
units.tr: In tractate Rosch hafchana folio 16.1 this passage gave me no small difficulty when I was reviewing that tractate. At the beginning of the year it reads: All who come into the world pass before God like the sons of Maron [כל באי עולם עוברין למניו כנגי מרון]. Some interpret "sons of Maron" as "like sheep", on a basis I do not know. In the Gemara, Resch Lakisch interprets it as like the ascent of Beth Maron [כמעולות בני מרון], which, according to the Gloss, was a very narrow road, so that two could not walk there side by side, since there was a deep valley on either side of the road. The sense of the passage, then, is that at the start of the year people are, as it were, reviewed by God, and in the judgement are examined one after another, just as on the Maronite ascent they go up one after another and come into view.

units.la: ביתר Biter vel Bether a quibusdam pronuntiatur, sed melius ביתר Betar, quasi בי תר domus inquisitoris. Devastata fuit haec urbs per Adrianum imperatorem; causas excidii dant varias. Primaria est Rebellio Ben Cosbae in Romanos, alia est, quia accenderunt lucernas in Bethar post excidium templi, malis quibusdam consiliis ad id adducti. Hierof. Taanith folio 68. 4. 69. 1. Aliam adhuc rationem afferunt in Bab. Gittin folio 57. 1. אשקא דרספק חריב ביתר ob crus carpenti vastata est Bethara. Nam ut filia Casaris currum reparare possent, excidemunt cedrum, (de cuius cedri usu vid. cum nascebatur infans.) Hoc agre tulerunt Iudai, & eos qui cedrum amputaverant interfecerunt. Relatum est Casari rebellare Iudaeos, qui in ira profectus excidit totum cornu Israelis.
units.tr: Some pronounce ביתר as Biter or Bether, but more correctly it is בית ר Betar, as if the house of the inquisitor [בי תר]. This city was laid waste by the emperor Hadrian, and writers give various causes of its destruction. The chief is the rebellion of Ben Cosba against the Romans. Another is that they lit lamps in Bethar after the destruction of the temple, having been led to do so by certain wicked counsels. Hierosolymitan Taanith, folio 68.4 and 69.1. They offer yet another reason in Babylonian Gittin folio 57.1: אשקא דרספק חריב ביתר [the wagon's axle], Bethar was laid waste on account of the leg of a wagon. For, so that the emperor's daughter could repair her chariot, they cut down a cedar (on the use of this cedar see when an infant was born). The Jews took this badly and killed those who had cut down the cedar. It was reported to Caesar that the Jews were rebelling, and in anger he set out and cut down the whole horn of Israel.

units.la: §. Adrianus obsidionem Betharis continuavit per tres annos & dimidium. Hierof. Taanith sol.68.4.Cum eam caperent,intersecrunt mares & fæminas & parvulos, ita ut sanguis eorum flueret in mare magnum &c. Bab. Gittin ubi supra. vid. etiam Echa Rabbeti c. 2. ubi dicitur Bethare 50. fuisse scholas, quarum unaquæque non minus quàm 300. discipulos continebat : postquàm vicerant hostes באו השונאים וכרכו כל אחד ואחד בספרו ושרפו אותם venerunt & unumquemque suo volumini involventes omnes combusserunt. R. Iochanan dicit tantam vim sanguinis ibi fusam esse, ut equus immergeretur sanguini usque ad frenum, & sanguinis fluxus volveret lapides של מאה ארבעים סאה quadragenarios &c.
units.tr: §. Hadrian continued the siege of Bethar for three years and a half. Jerusalem Talmud, Taanith fol. 68.4: When they took it, they killed the men, the women and the little children, so that their blood flowed into the Great Sea, etc. Babylonian Talmud, Gittin, as above. See also Echa Rabbeti ch. 2, where it is said that there were fifty schools at Bethar, each of which held no fewer than 300 pupils. After the enemies had conquered, [ba'u hasonim vekharekhu kol ehad ve'ehad bisifro vesarefu otam] they came and wrapped each one in his own book, and burned them all. R. Johanan says that so much blood was poured out there that a horse was submerged in blood up to its bridle, and the flow of blood rolled stones [shel me'ah arba'im se'ah] forty seahs in weight, etc.

units.la: בית המדרש Beth Hammidrasch, vid. Synago- gam.
units.tr: Beth Hammidrasch [בית המדרש], see Synagogue.

units.la: בית פגי Bethphage erat intra Hierosolymam, sicut videtur ex Bab. Sanhed. sol. 14. 2. Vbi glossa ad hæc verba מצאן אבית פגי וה יסר' עלהן וכו Si invenerint Synedrium considens in Bethphage & notat בית פגי םקום לפניים מן חומת העיר וגידון כירושלם לכל דבריו Bethphage fuit locus intra muros urbis, & reputata est sicut ipsa Hierosolyma quoad omnia. Idem etiam elici potest ex Pesachim sol. 63. 2. Qui sacrificium gratiarum actionis maclat intra murum, & panis eius est extra murum; panis non sanctus est. Quid est extra murum? R. Iochanan dicit extra murum Bethphage. Glossa, Bethphage est locus extimus Hierosolymarum, & quicunque est extra mœnia Bethphage, est extra Hierosolymas, extra quas sacra comedi non possunt. Vide Pascha.Panes. Vide
units.tr: Bethphage [בית פגי] was within Jerusalem, as appears from the Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin fol. 14.2, where the gloss on these words, [matsa'an be-beit pagi, vehe yoshev 'alehen vekhu'] If they find the Sanhedrin sitting in Bethphage, notes: Bethphage was a place within the walls of the city, and it was reckoned as Jerusalem itself in all respects. The same can also be drawn from Pesachim fol. 63.2: He who slaughters a thank-offering inside the wall, and whose bread is outside the wall, has bread that is not holy. What is "outside the wall"? R. Johanan says: outside the wall, at Bethphage. The gloss: Bethphage is the outermost place of Jerusalem, and whoever is outside the walls of Bethphage is outside Jerusalem, outside which sacred things may not be eaten. See Pascha, Panes. See.

units.la: etiam Bava Metzia folio 90. 1.
units.tr: See also Bava Metzia folio 90.1.

units.la: §. Significatur deinde nomine בית פגי infima pars montis Oliveti, quæ ad urbem excurrit, propter פגי Grossos ficuum qui erant in hoc tractu frequentes, vel quia illam partem Hierosolymarum tangebat & respiciebat, quæ Bethphage vocatur. Qui urbeculam vel villam huius nominis extra Hierosolymas constituunt, nihil habent quo se sustineant præter Monachorum fabellas, qui peregrinantibus superstitiósis canunt quod volunt. Cùm Marcus cap.xi.1. dicit Quum appropinquarent Hierosolymæ ad Bethphage & Bethaniam: solùm indicavit locum illum, ubi se mutuò contingebant duo tractus montis oliveti, Bethphage & Bethania dicti, non autem villas sic nominatas; nam ex Ioh. xii. patet Dominum nostrum in Bethania vico Lazari pernoctasse, & post aliquam profectionem, mane solum ad hunc locum pervenisse. Cùm Christus ad cœlum ascendit discipulos suos eduxit Εως εἰς Βηθανίαν Luc.xxiv.50. Certè ibi non Bethania Lazari intelligenda, sed tractus ille oliveti, qui ab Hierosolymis ultra iter Sabbaticum non distabat, ut videtur ex Act.i. 12. & ad quem aliter vix venire poterant nisi eundo per tractum Bethphage vocatum. Sed aliquis objicere possset, Christus Discipulis cùm perventum erat ad Bethphage & Bethaniam monstrasse villam quæ erat κατέναντι ἀντῆς Marc. ii.1. quænam autem villa fuisset si non Bethphage? Bethania Lazari villa longiùs distabat, & ex illa venerant. ℞. villa quam commonstravit Christus
units.tr: §. The name [beit pagi] also denotes the lowest part of the Mount of Olives, which runs down toward the city, because of the pagi [green figs], which were common in this tract, or because it touched and faced that part of Jerusalem which is called Bethphage. Those who set up a little town or village of this name outside Jerusalem have nothing to support them except the fables of the monks, who sing whatever they like to superstitious pilgrims. When Mark 11:1 says, When they drew near to Jerusalem, unto Bethphage and Bethany, he indicated only that place where the two tracts of the Mount of Olives, called Bethphage and Bethany, touched each other, and not villages so named; for from John 12 it is clear that our Lord spent the night in Bethany, the village of Lazarus, and only came to this place the next morning after a certain journey. When Christ ascended into heaven he led his disciples out [heos eis Bethanian] as far as Bethany (Luke 24:50). Certainly here we must not understand the village of Lazarus, but that tract of the Mount of Olives, which, as appears from Acts 1:12, was not more than a Sabbath day's journey from Jerusalem, and which they could scarcely have reached otherwise than by passing through the tract called Bethphage. But someone might object: when they had come to Bethphage and Bethany, Christ showed the disciples a village which was [katenanti autes] over against them (Mark 11:2); but what village would it have been if not Bethphage? Bethany of Lazarus was farther away, and they had come from there. Answer: the village which Christ showed to the disciples was those booths [beit hini] (on which see Bethany), erected there in considerable numbers, and presenting the appearance of a fine village.

units.la: Discipulis,fuerunt tabernæ illæ בית היני(de quibus vid.Bethania) magno satis numero ibi erectæ, & speciem villæ speciosæ præ se ferentes. Certè ut ex aliquo loco singulis menfibus 40. feæ columbarum pro fœminarum purificationibus produci potuerint,ut diciturHierof.Taanit fol.69.2. & denique ibi plurima alia proftarent,requiritur , ut villa satis laxa fuerit.
units.tr: For it is certain that from one place forty pairs of doves could be supplied every month for the purification of women, as is said in Jerusalem Talmud, Taanith fol. 69.2, and finally, since many other things were sold there, the village must have been fairly spacious.

units.la: בית שאן Bethfchean Scytopolis, una ex urbibus Decapolitanis.
units.tr: Beth-shean, Scythopolis, one of the Decapolitan cities.

units.la: §. R. Ichuda folvit Bethfcheanem à Demai decimatione rerum dubiarum. Hierof.Demai fol.22.3. Permiffio illa partim propter R. Meir facta fuit qui comederat folia olerum non decimatorum in Bethfchean, Cholinfol. 6. 2. partim verò quia exiftimabatur effe extra terram Ifraeliticam. Iarchi in loc. huius rei ratio verò fuit, quia afcendentes è Babylone illam nonfubiugarunt.Iarchi inDemai.c.1.v.3.habitabatur itaq; adhuc ab Ethnicis,quibus Iudæi mixti erant,ab accurata traditionum obfervatione liberi. Hos etiam invifere voluit Chriftus, Marc.vii.31.
units.tr: §. R. Ichuda released Beth-shean from the tithing of doubtful produce (demai). Jerusalem Talmud, Demai fol. 22.3. The exemption was granted partly because of R. Meir, who had eaten leaves of vegetables that had not been tithed in Beth-shean (Chullin fol. 6.2), and partly because it was thought to lie outside the land of Israel. Rashi on that passage gives the reason: "because those who came up from Babylon did not subdue it." Rashi on Demai c.1 v.3. It was therefore still inhabited by Gentiles, among whom Jews lived mixed in, and so was free from the strict observance of the traditions. Christ also wished to visit these people, Mark 7:31.

units.la: בית נמר Beth Nemar vid. in N.
units.tr: Beth Nemar, see under N.

units.la: ביעור Biour defcribitur in Maafer Scheni c.5.6. In vefpera primi diei fefti pafchatis, anni quarti & anni feptimi eft ביעור. Quomodo autem illam fecerunt? נותנין תרומה ותרומה מעשר לבעליה ומעשר ראשון לבעליו ומעשר עני לבעליו ומעשר שני והככורים מתבערים בכל מקום: Præbent decimas, & decimarum decimas, decimas primas, decimas pauperum illis quibus debentur, primitias autem& decimas fecundas plane abolent.
units.tr: Biur is described in Maaser Sheni c.5 m.6. On the evening of the first day of the Passover festival, in the fourth and seventh years, there is biur. But how did they carry it out? "They set aside terumah, and terumah of the tithe, for its owner, and first tithe for its owner, and the tithe for the poor for its owner; and second tithe and first fruits are wholly burned up everywhere." [נותנין תרומה ותרומה מעשר לבעליה ומעשר ראשון לבעליו ומעשר עני לבעליו ומעשר שני והככורים מתבערים בכל מקום]

units.la: §. Quid ביעור fit difces à gloffatoribus in ScheScheuiit c.9.2. In compendio rem sic habeto; Anno septimo fructus in apothecas repositos comedere licuit, quamdiu penderent istius generis fructus in arbore, in ista regione: cum vero ulterius in arboribus eos invenire non dabatur istos quos collegerant, aut quos domi repoluerant, ejicere oportuit, & non de iis comedere ita ut antea. De hac ביעור in anno septimo accuratè ut omnia tractat Maymonides noster in Hal. Schemita. c.7. de abolitione fermentati in Pascha vid.f.1.
units.tr: §. What biur is you may learn from the glossators on Sheviit c.9 m.2. In short, the position is this. In the seventh year it was permitted to eat fruit stored in storehouses for as long as fruit of that kind was still hanging on the trees in that region. When such fruit could no longer be found on the trees, the produce they had gathered or stored at home had to be removed, and could not be eaten as before. Our Maimonides treats this biur of the seventh year accurately and in full, as he does all matters, in Hilchot Shemitta c.7. On the removal of leaven at Passover see f.1.

units.la: בִּיכּוּרִים Bicchourim, de Primitiis vid. suo loco.
units.tr: Bikkurim, first fruits: see in its place.

units.la: בִּיתּוּר Bithur in Callah cap. 4. 10. non est Bethar; sed secundùm glossam urbs quaedam extra terram.
units.tr: Bithur in Kallah c.4 m.10 is not Bethar; according to the gloss it is a certain city outside the land.

units.la: Blasphemus non reus fit lapidationis, nisi expresserit, nomen (proprium Dei,) dicit R. I.F. Corchæ, toto die examinantur בכינוי adhibito tetro nomine v.g percutiat Iofe Iofen. Consummatio Iudicio morte non afficiunt ob solum כינוי tetrum nomen, sed omnibus foras exactis, testium natu maximum interrogant, dicendo, edissere, quodcunq; nomen audivisti expresse. Tum ille hoc refert. Iudices autem stant erecti, vestesque discerpunt, non resarciendas: (concinnà nempe futurâ, sed crassâ licet, quam consuendi rationem vocant מכלב & שלל) Sanhed. cap. 7.5. Vide Gemaram Babylonicam, quae copiosè ad hunc locum edisserit, quare iudices in pedes exsurgant, quare vestimenta scindant, quare ea non liceat resuere.
units.tr: A blasphemer is not liable to stoning unless he has pronounced the name, the proper name of God, says R. I. F. Corcha. All day they are examined, with the euphemism used for the tetragrammaton, for example, "may Jose strike Jose." In conclusion, they do not condemn to death merely on account of a euphemism for the tetragrammaton. But when everyone has been led out, they question the eldest of the witnesses, saying, "Tell us, whatever name you heard expressly." Then he reports it. The judges stand up and tear their garments, which may not be mended again (that is, neatly sewn, though with a coarse stitch, which they call makhlav and shalal). Sanhedrin c.7 m.5. See the Babylonian Gemara, which at length explains this passage: why the judges rise to their feet, why they tear their garments, and why it is not permitted to sew them up again.

units.la: §. Qui Deum blasphemaverit ורה עבודה בשם nomine aliquo Idololatriæ, Zelotypi הקנאים in ipsum incurrunt & ipsum interficiunt. Si verò ad Synedrium adducitur, non lapidatur, nisi blasphemaverit nomine aliquo proprio Dei.
units.tr: §. One who blasphemes God by naming some idolatrous rite is set upon by the zealots (haqqana'im) and killed. But if he is brought before the Sanhedrin, he is not stoned unless he has blasphemed by some proper name of God.

units.la: §. In genere omnes qui audiunt blasphemiam vestimenta dilacerare debent, etiam si blasphemia solummodò effet בכיוי, si scilicet blasphemans Israelita fuerit, alias non lacerant pro pter Idolatras gentiles. Vnum idemque est si quis blasphemiam ex alterius qui audivit ore percipit, sive ex ipso blasphemantis ore.
units.tr: §. In general, all who hear blasphemy ought to tear their garments, even if the blasphemy was only a euphemism, that is, if the blasphemer was an Israelite. Otherwise they do not tear them on account of Gentile idolaters. It is one and the same whether someone takes in the blasphemy from the mouth of the one who heard it or from the mouth of the blasphemer himself.

units.la: §. כל העדים והדיינים סומכין את ידיהן אחד ואחר על ראש המגדף וכו' Testes & Iudices, manus suas unus post alteram capiti blasphemantis imponunt & dicunt דמך בראשך Sanguis sit super caput tuum &c. hoc in nullo qui a Synedrio capitali supplicio afficitur, observatur, excepto in blasphemo. &c. Maymon Avoda Sarah c. 2. sub sin. In iudicio Christi observarunt lacerationem vestium, cùm secundùm hypothesin ipsorum protulisset blasphemiam os sanctissimum. De impositione manuum in caput eius nihil legimus, nisi forte conspuendo & verberando faciem eius ad hunc ritum alludere voluerint.
units.tr: §. "All the witnesses and judges lay their hands, one after another, on the head of the blasphemer, etc., and say, 'Your blood be upon your head,' etc." This is observed in no case of a person sentenced to capital punishment by the Sanhedrin except that of the blasphemer. Maimonides, Avodah Zarah c.2, at the end. In Christ's trial they observed the tearing of garments, since on their hypothesis that most holy mouth had uttered blasphemy. Of the laying of hands upon his head we read nothing, unless perhaps they meant to allude to this rite by spitting upon and beating his face.

units.la: C. I. n.
units.tr: Chapter I, n.

units.la: CAbi loquacitatis 10. descenderunt in mundum, novem abstulerunt mulieres. 10. Sapientia, 9. abstulit terra sancta. Decem divitiarum, 9. abstulit Roma. Decem pulchitudinis, nis, 9. abstulit Ierusalem. Decem paupertatis, 9. abstulit Babel. Decem superbia, 9. Elam. Decem fortitudinis, 9. abstulerunt Persæ. Decem pediculorum, 9. abstulit Media. Decem incantationum, 9. sumpserunt Ægyptii. Decem plagarum, 9. abstulerunt porci. Decem scortationis, 9. Arabia. Decem impudentiæ, 9. Mischan. 10. Nigredinis, novem Æthiopes. Decem somni, 9. Servi sibi attribuerunt. Kidduschin sol.49.2.
units.tr: When the ten measures of talkativeness came down into the world, women took nine. Of wisdom, the Holy Land took nine. Of riches, Rome took nine. Of beauty, Jerusalem took nine. Of poverty, Babylon took nine. Of pride, Elam took nine. Of strength, the Persians took nine. Of lice, Media took nine. Of incantations, the Egyptians took nine. Of plagues, the swine took nine. Of fornication, Arabia took nine. Of impudence, Mischan took nine. Of blackness, the Ethiopians took nine. Of sleep, the servants took nine for themselves. Kiddushin fol. 49.2.

units.la: כבול Chabbul 1. Reg. ix. 12. 13. lxx. interpretati sunt ὀρίου, ex qua ratione, non ita apparet. Hierosolymitani Chabbul sic definiät in Schabbat sol. 7. כבול ארץ שאינה עושה פירות Chabul terram significat quæ non fert fructus. In Bab. Schabb. sol. 54. aliter Etymologiam rimantur.
