Quid sibi vult terra Chabul? Rabb Houna dicit, quia incolæ eius מכובלין בככף ובוהב erant involuti argento & auro. Objicit Abba, si res ita se haberent, quare ergo illæ civitates terræ Chabul Hiramo displicuerunt, si tam divites fuerunt? R. idcirco displicuerunt, quia propter affluentiam opum delicati & teneri erant, proindeque inepti ad opera Regis.
units.tr: Chabbul, 1 Kings 9:12-13. The Seventy translated it [ὀρίου]; for what reason, does not clearly appear. The Jerusalem sages define Chabbul thus in Shabbat fol. 7: "Chabul means a land that does not bear fruit." In the Babylonian Shabbat fol. 54 they seek another etymology. "What does the land of Chabul mean? Rav Huna says, because its inhabitants were wrapped in silver and gold." Abba objects: if things were so, why did those cities in the land of Chabul displease Hiram, if they were so rich? The answer is that they displeased him because, through the abundance of their wealth, they were delicate and soft, and therefore unfit for the king's works.

units.la: §. Aliam nomenclationem reperiit R. Nachman Bar Isaak loc.cit. terra Chabul חיתה חיכשון erat falsa & fissuris hians, & vocata est (habul quia mergitur in ea crus usque ad periscelides.
units.tr: §. R. Nachman bar Isaac, in the same place, finds another explanation. The land of Chabul was "a false land, gaping with fissures," and it was called Chabul because a foot sinks into it up to the ankle-bands.

units.la: §. Glossator ad locum Bab. Schab. 54. dicit urbes illas quas Salomo dedit Hiramo & quas ille כבול vocavit, fuisse numero 22. cum in fonte sacro solum 20. fuisse dicatur.
units.tr: §. The gloss on the passage in Bab. Shabbat 54 says that the cities which Solomon gave to Hiram, and which he called Chabul, were twenty-two in number, though Scripture says only twenty.

units.la: Cadesch Barnea & קדש simpliciter ab omnibus Orientalium Interpretibus redditur קדש. Cadesch Barnea est Oakelofo ארץ גאיא קדש Ionathani ארץ גיעה קדש Targum. Hierosolym. רגיית קדש. Gemaristis גועה קדש.
units.tr: Kadesh Barnea, and simply Kadesh, is rendered by all the Eastern interpreters as Kadesh. Kadesh Barnea is in Onkelos "the land of Gaya Kadesh"; in Jonathan "the land of Giah Kadesh"; in the Jerusalem Targum "Regiyat Kadesh"; among the Gemarists "Gu'ah Kadesh."

units.la: §. Rekam erat terrae Israeliticae limes, ita tamen ut quasi extra terram esse aestimaretur. Hinc ista. Omnes macula quae veniunt à קדש munda. (Gloss. non enim determinarunt de maculis alienigenarum.) Gittin c. 1. 1. Ievamot. sol. 16. 1.
units.tr: §. Rekam was the boundary of the land of Israel, but in such a way that it was reckoned as if it were outside the land. Hence the saying: "All stains that come from Kadesh are clean" (the gloss adds, for they did not determine concerning the stains of foreigners). Gittin c.1 m.1; Yevamot fol. 16.1.

units.la: §. Duo loca nomine קדש insignita erant; in terrae limitibus, unum erat Cadesch à parte Australi, alterum verò Cadesch à parte Orientali, de qua loquitur R. Niffim in Gittin. cap. 1. ad ea verba מרקם למורח דרקם כמורח Quando dicit, Rekam ipsa pro oriente mundi (pro terra Ethnica) reputatur, non pro terra Israelitica.
units.tr: §. Two places were marked by the name Kadesh within the boundaries of the land: one was Kadesh on the south side, the other Kadesh on the east side. R. Nissim speaks of the latter in Gittin c.1, on the words "Rekam to the east, Rekam as the east" (מרקם למורח דרקם כמורח). When he says, "Rekam itself is reckoned to the east of the world" (that is, to the Gentile land), "and not to the land of Israel."

units.la: Caeremoniales leges ad quinque categorias referri possunt. 1. ad personas Sacras vid. Sacerdos summus. Sacerdotes vulgares. Levita. 2. ad Actiones Sacras. vid. Sacrificia, Circuncisio, Pascha. 3. ad Res Sacras. vid. primitia decima. 4. ad loca Sacra vid. Templum. 5. ad tempora Sacra, vid. Novilunia, Pascha, Pentecoste, festum Tabernaculorum, annus Sabbaticus, Iubilaeum.
units.tr: The ceremonial laws can be referred to five categories. (1) To sacred persons: the high priest, the ordinary priests, the Levites. (2) To sacred actions: sacrifices, circumcision, the Passover. (3) To sacred things: first fruits, tithes. (4) To sacred places: the Temple. (5) To sacred times: new moons, the Passover, Pentecost, the feast of Tabernacles, the sabbatical year, the jubilee.

units.la: Caesarea, Iosuae xi. 1. Arabs Interpres, dicit fuisse Hatzor; fieri tamen potest ut ille non Caesaream Stratonis de qua nunc loquimur, sed Caesaream Philippi intellexerit. Iudaei vocant Ekron Bab. Megillah sol. 6. 1.
units.tr: Caesarea, Joshua 11:1. The Arabic interpreter says it was Hatzor. It may be, however, that he understood not Caesarea of Straton, which we are now discussing, but Caesarea Philippi. The Jews call it Ekron, Bab. Megillah fol. 6.1.

units.la: §. Ab Asmonaeis vocata est אחירת מגדל צור InchaIuchafin folio 74. 1.
units.tr: §. The Hasmoneans called it Achirat Migdal Tzor. Juchasin fol. 74.1.

units.la: §. Habitabatur Cæsarea à Iudæis, Samaritanis, & Ethnicis ; hinc quædam loca Iudæis immunda erant, & specialiter locus in quem per arcum ingrediendum. Hierof. Nazir sol. 56. 1.
units.tr: §. Caesarea was inhabited by Jews, Samaritans and Gentiles; hence some places were unclean for Jews, and especially the place which had to be entered through an arch. Jerusalem Talmud, Nazir fol. 56.1.

units.la: §. Portus Cæsareæ in tribunali Hierosolymitano non æstimatus fuit eiusdem puritatis ut civitas, (sine dubio enim propter colluviem populi, in portu maior immundities & plures profani erant.) vid. historiam de libello repudii allato à portu Cæsareæ in Hierof. Gittin sol. 43. 2.
units.tr: §. The harbour of Caesarea was not regarded as having the same purity as the city in the Jerusalem court. Doubtless this was because of the crowd of people: in the harbour there was greater uncleanness and more profane persons. See the account of the bill of divorce brought from the harbour of Caesarea, Jerusalem Talmud, Gittin fol. 43.2.

units.la: §. Præclara Cæsareæ fuit Academia, in qua floruerunt R. Hofchaja Ruba Hierof. Terumot folio 47.1. item R. Abhu, Iuchafin sol. 74.1. R. Zerikan, Hierof. Pesachin sol.28.1.
units.tr: §. The academy of Caesarea was famous, and in it flourished R. Hofchaja Ruba, Hierof. Terumot folio 47.1; likewise R. Abhu, Iuchafin sol. 74.1; and R. Zerikan, Hierof. Pesachin sol. 28.1.

units.la: §. Celebratur Hierof. Nazir, & Hierof. Berachot כנישתא מרדתה דקיסרי Synagoga Maradta Cæsarea.
units.tr: §. Hierof. Nazir and Hierof. Berachot are cited, with the synagogue of Maradta at Caesarea [כנישתא מרדתה דקיסרי], Synagogue Maradta Caesarea.

units.la: §. Cæsarea Philippi est apud Talmudicos eiusdem classis cum Bethsheane, ut inter Decapolitanas numeretur, argumentum afferri potest ex Ptolomæo, qui eam numerat inter urbes Phænicia mediterranea, & ex Iosepho qui in vita sua innuit Syros eius incolas fuisse.
units.tr: §. Among the Talmudists, Caesarea Philippi belongs to the same class as Bethsheane, so that it is counted among the Decapolitan cities. An argument for this can be drawn from Ptolemy, who counts it among the cities of Mediterranean Phoenicia, and from Josephus, who in his Life hints that its inhabitants were Syrians.

units.la: In CÆNACULUM ascendere usitatum erat apud Iudæos quando de lege aut religione disceptabatur. Schabb. cap. 1. 7. Ha sunt traditiones quas docuerunt בעליה in cænaculo Chanania Ben Chezekia &c. Hierof. Sanhed. folio 24. 3. ascenderunt Seniores לעליה in caenaculum in Hierichunte. Ascenderunt etiam in cænaculum in Iabbne. Iuchasin sol.23.2. Rabh Iochanan & disciputi eius ascenderunt ῑεις ὑπερῷον, & legerunt & exposuerunt.
units.tr: To go up into an UPPER ROOM was customary among the Jews when a matter of law or religion was being debated. Schabb. ch. 1, 7: These are the traditions which those in the upper room of Chanania ben Chezekia taught, etc. Hierof. Sanhed. folio 24.3: the elders went up to the upper room in Hierichunte. They also went up to the upper room in Iabbne. Iuchasin sol. 23.2: Rabh Iochanan and his disciples went up into the upper room [εἰς ὑπερῷον], and read and expounded.

units.la: §. De talibus עליות cænaculis intelligenda sunt loca Marci xiv.15. Act.1.13. Ex hoc etiam dilucidari potest, locus Marci 11.4. ἀπελθοντες τὴν εἰςηγησιν. Christus enim cum Pharisæis & legum doctoribus non fuit in inferioribus domus partibus, sed sedit, in cænaculo ad differendum ordinato, in conclavi altiori vel supremo, ad quod perfosso tecto statim venire licuit. Si autem ponatur Christum in inferiori aliqua Camera fuisse, quæ non parietum & contignationum strata perrumpenda fuissent? De חגיגה Chagiga, vid. Pascha.
units.tr: §. The places in Mark 14.15 and Acts 1.13 are to be understood of such upper rooms (עליות). This may also make clear the passage in Mark 11.4, ἀπελθόντες τὴν εἰσηγησιν [going away, the ... ]. For Christ, with the Pharisees and the teachers of the law, was not in the lower parts of the house but sat in an upper room set aside for debate, in a higher or topmost chamber, to which access was gained at once by breaking through the roof. For if one supposes that Christ was in some lower chamber, through what walls and floors would they have had to break? On the Chagiga, see under Pascha.

units.la: CAINUM & Abel unico partu ab Eva in lucem editos fuisse sentit R.Iose apud R.Elieferem in Pirke cap. 21. deceptus verbis ותוסף ללרת & perrexit parere: quasi illa denotarent continuum pariendi actum, cum sola mens Mosis fuerit compendiose loqui.
units.tr: CAIN and Abel were, according to R. Jose, brought into the light by Eve at a single birth, as reported by R. Eliezer in Pirke ch. 21. He was misled by the words ותוסף ללדת [vatosef laledet], and she went on to bear, as though they denoted a continuous act of bearing, when Moses' mind was only speaking in a summary way.

units.la: Alii fingunt cum Caino & Habele, genitas esse Gemellas, ut Saidus Patricides Patriarcha Alexandrinus Annal. p.15. Congressus est ergo, inquit, Adam cum Eva, quæ cum concepisset, peperit puerum & puellam, puerum appellavit Cain, puellam אצרון; Rursus concepit & puerum itidem ac puellam peperit, quorum hanc אוין Avvina, illum Habel nominavit. Item R.Sal.Iarchi שלש אתים רבוי הם מלמד שתאומה גולדה עם קין ועם הבל Tres את Eth multiplicati docent, gemellam fuisse natam cum Caino & Habele. Sed hac ratione concludere licèret non duas sed tres gemellas fuisse, cum quinquies particula חא in duobus versibus legatur.
units.tr: Others invent that Cain and Abel were born as twins, as Saidus Patricides, patriarch of Alexandria, does in his Annals p. 15: Adam therefore, he says, had intercourse with Eve, who, when she had conceived, bore a boy and a girl; the boy she called Cain, and the girl she called [Azurun, אצרון]. Again she conceived, and likewise bore a boy and a girl; of these she called the girl [Avvina, אוין] Avvina, and the boy Abel. Likewise R. Sal. Iarchi: The three multiplied [את] eth teach that a twin girl was born with Cain and Abel. But by this reasoning one could conclude that there were not two but three twin girls, since the particle eth [את] is read five times in two verses.

units.la: Circa Sacrificium Caini notandum, illum & fratrem eius ritum significandi didicisse ab Adamo, cui Deus illum monstravit tempore illo quo post promissionem pelliceas vestes protoplastis parabat, ut enim pellis haberi posset, animal occidi debuit, mactatum & excoriatum confirmandæ promissionis ergo, statim Deus in victimam comburi curavit. Hanc coniecturam amplexus est Iarchius ad verba Psalm. LXIX. 32. Quæ melior videbitur Iehovæ bove &c. הוא שור שהקריב אדם ראשון Eos hic est, quem obtulit Adam primus, quiqué creatus fuit integræ statura &c. Idem Onkelos.
units.tr: Concerning Cain's sacrifice it should be noted that he and his brother learned the rite of signifying from Adam, to whom God showed it at the time when, after the promise, he was preparing skin garments for the first parents. For a skin to be had, an animal had to be killed; having been slain and flayed, it was at once, to confirm the promise, offered by God to be burned as a victim. Iarchi embraces this conjecture on the words of Psalm 69.32, which shall please the Lord better than an ox, etc. הוא שור שהקריב אדם ראשון [this is the ox that the first Adam offered], who was created in full stature, etc. Onkelos says the same.

units.la: Cain Sacrificium suum adduxit ad certum & pro Sacrificiis destinatum locum, sed non placet sententia illorum qui dicunt כי הזנחו הבאה אל אביו Quod adduxerit Sacrificium ad patrem suum. Aben Esra.
units.tr: Cain brought his sacrifice to a definite place appointed for sacrifices, but the view of those who say כי הזנחו הבאה אל אביו [that he brought the offering to his father] does not please me, that he brought the sacrifice to his father. Aben Ezra.

units.la: Quod materiam oblationis attinet, negat Aben Esra illam fuisse primitias frugum. In Tanchuma sol. 3. statuitur tanquam ex communi Sententia Magistrorum, oblationem Caini sumptam fuisse מזרע משתן Ex Semine lini.
units.tr: As to the matter of the offering, Aben Ezra denies that it was the firstfruits of the crops. In Tanchuma sol. 3 it is laid down, as the common opinion of the masters, that Cain's offering was taken from the seed of flax [מזרע פשתן].

units.la: Quid Cain loquutus sit cum Habele secundum Genef. 4. 8. expressit Targum Hierosolymitanum. Et dixit Cain ad Habel fratrem: veni & egrediamur foras. Et accidit, cum egressi essent ambo in agrum, respondit Cain: Non est Iudicium, nec iudex, nec seculum aliud, nec merces bona pro iustis, nec pœna pro impiis. Nec Dei misericordiâ creatus est mundus, nec Dei miseri-cordiâ regitur,eo quòd suscepta est oblatio tua cum beneplacito. Respondit Habel : est Iudicium; est Iudex : est Seculum aliud&c. Sed quia opera mea sunt meliora tuis, suscepta est oblato mea cum beneplacito : tua autem non est suscepta. Ex hac altercatione, deinde credunt eadem infequutam. Aben Efra existimat etiam, Cainum hoc in loco Habeli recitasse תוכחת כל Omnem illam disputationem, quæ Deo cum ipso intercesserat. Veteres autem Cabbalistæ sentiunt æmulationem fratrum ortam esse ex eo, quòd Adamus Habeli desponderit coniugem formosiorem, Hinc apud R. Elieserum cap.21. R. Zadok illud בשדה in agro qui erat locus in quo Cain cædis occasionem captavit, explicat, Cum uxore quæsimilis est agro, sicut dicitur: Homo enim arbor agri. Hanc traditionem retinuerunt Orientales ut videtur ex Eutychio Alexandrino Apud Cl. Heideggerum de Vit. Pat. Exerc.V.p.192.
units.tr: What Cain said to Abel, according to Gen. 4.8, the Jerusalem Targum sets forth: And Cain said to Abel his brother: Come, let us go out. And it came about, when they had both gone out into the field, that Cain answered: There is no judgement, nor judge, nor another world, nor good reward for the righteous, nor punishment for the wicked. Nor was the world created by the mercy of God, nor is it governed by the mercy of God, because your offering was accepted with favour. Abel answered: There is judgement, there is a judge, there is another world, etc. But because my works are better than yours, my offering was accepted with favour, and yours was not accepted. From this altercation they then believe the same thing followed. Aben Ezra also thinks that Cain in this place recited to Abel all that disputation which had passed between him and God. But the older Cabbalists hold that the rivalry of the brothers arose from the fact that Adam betrothed to Abel a wife more beautiful. Hence in R. Eliezer ch. 21, R. Zadok explains the word בשדה [in the field], which was the place where Cain seized the occasion for murder, as meaning with a wife who is like a field, as it is said: For man is a tree of the field. It seems the Orientals retained this tradition, as is clear from Eutychius of Alexandria, cited by the distinguished Heidegger in De Vita Patriarcharum Exercitationes V, p. 192.

units.la: Circa Signum quod Deus Caino impressit, variè ab Hebreis luditur. R. Salomoh Iarchi Impressit fronti eius literam ex nomine suo. Tanchuma sol.4. vult signum illud fuisse שבת, & Deum illud primitus dedisse Adamo in remissionis signum, & deinde etiam Caino. R. Eliefer contendit in Pirke cap.21. fuisse signum istud literam unam ex Alphabeto Hebraico, brachio Caini impressam. Alii putant ubicunque locorum fuerit Cain, partem aliquam circunstantis terræ tremuisse.
units.tr: Concerning the sign that God put on Cain, the Hebrews play in various ways. R. Solomon Iarchi: He impressed on his forehead the letter from his own name. Tanchuma sol. 4 holds that the sign was שבת [Sabbath], and that God first gave it to Adam as a sign of remission, and afterwards also to Cain. R. Eliezer maintains in Pirke ch. 21 that the sign was one letter of the Hebrew alphabet, impressed on Cain's arm. Others think that wherever Cain was, some part of the surrounding land trembled.

units.la: De
units.tr: On

units.la: CAlcei extractio ita fit. Glos fe confert ad illum locum ubi Levir habitat, iudicesque convenit. Qui ante omnia illi & Leviro illud confulunt, quod ipsos maximè decet, si juvencula est & ille iuvenis, ut eam ducat. Si verò illa Iuvencula & ille senex, aut vice versa, ut calceum extrahat. Deinde iudices locum definire debent, ut ibi coràm illis sedentibus extractio fieri possit, ipsamque expedite legere docent אבא לא לא Non vult &c. (textum sc. illum qui ita incipit.) ita ut illa verba uno anhelitu dicere possit.
units.tr: The extraction of the shoe is carried out as follows. The Glos comes to the place where the levir lives, and the judges assemble. They first advise him and the levir (which chiefly suits them) whether he should take her as his wife, if she is a young woman and he a young man. If, however, she is a young woman and he an old man, or the reverse, they advise that the shoe be drawn off. Then the judges must fix a place where the extraction can be done before them as they sit, and they teach him to read clearly Abba lo lo, that is, "He does not wish," etc. (namely the passage that begins so), so that he can say those words in one breath.

units.la: §. Noctu nemini calceus extrahitur; nec extrahitur aliis, nisi qui patrem & matrem Israelitas habuerunt.
units.tr: Section. No shoe is drawn off at night, nor is it drawn off for anyone except those whose father and mother were Israelites.

units.la: §. Fratria calceum allatum, qui soleam habet sed lino non confutus est, pedi dextro Leviri induit, ligat, & deinde cum ipso coràm iudicibus assurgit.
units.tr: Section. The brother-in-law brings a shoe which has a sole but is not sewn with thread. He puts it on the levir's right foot, ties it, and then rises with him before the judges.

units.la: §. Quo facto glos legit in lingua Sancta illa verba, Renuit Leviri jus mihi præstare &c. Levir verò illa verba, Nolo ducere ipsam: simulque pedem suum in terram figit; Glos autem sedens calcei ligamenta solvit, calceumque exuit, illum in terram dejicit, & tunc statim ac calceus proiectus est, aliis nubendi facultatem acquirit.
units.tr: Section. When this is done, the Glos reads in the holy tongue the words, He refuses to perform the duty of a levir for me, etc. The levir says the words, I do not wish to take her, and at the same time plants his foot on the ground. The Glos, sitting, loosens the straps of the shoe, takes it off and throws it to the ground, and as soon as the shoe has been thrown off, the woman acquires the freedom to marry another.

units.la: §. Posteà surgit & coram Leviro sputum eiaculat, & legit, Ita fiet viro qui non ædificabit.&c. Iudices accurate observant quomodo expuerit, & deinde cum omnibus præsentibus ter clamant, ad finem lectionis fratriæ חלוץ
units.tr: Section. Afterwards she rises, spits before the levir, and reads, So shall it be done to the man who does not build, etc. The judges watch carefully how she spat, and then, with all those present, they cry out three times, at the end of the reading, chalutz [חלוץ].

units.la: הנעל Extraßus est Calceus.
units.tr: Hannaal [הנעל]: The shoe has been drawn off.

units.la: §. Si Levir cæcus est, aut pes eius dexter abscissus fit, ipsi calceus extrahi nequit, debet enim sputum videre, & pedi eius dextro calceus indui.
units.tr: Section. If the levir is blind, or his right foot has been cut off, the shoe cannot be drawn off from him, for he must be able to see the spitting, and the shoe must be put on his right foot.

units.la: §. Si calceus nimis magnus fuerit aut nimis parvus, ita ut eo incedere non possit, aut confutus ex lino, aut contextus simpliciter ex crinibus, aut factus ex ligno, subere, musco, extractio huius calcei illegitima est.
units.tr: Section. If the shoe is too large or too small, so that he cannot walk in it, or if it is sewn with thread, or simply woven from hair, or made of wood, cork or moss, the extraction of such a shoe is invalid.

units.la: §. Si per artificium multum sputi collegerit aut ex ore eius profluat sanguis, aut si ventus sputum dissipaverit, antequàm e regione faciei eius veniret, extractio irrita est; debet enim sputum naturale esse, & omnia reliqua accuratè observari. Maymonides in Hal. Iebhom Vachalitza. c. 4.
units.tr: Section. If by some trick she has gathered up much spittle, or blood flows from her mouth, or if the wind scatters the spittle before it reaches the level of his face, the extraction is void; for the spittle must be natural, and all the other things must be observed carefully. Maimonides, Hilchot Yevamot ve-chalitza, chapter 4.

units.la: §. De Calceis & Sandaliis vid. Sandalia.
units.tr: Section. On shoes and sandals see Sandalia.

units.la: §. Calcei solutione servus tanquam arrhabone emebatur. vid. Servus Canan.
units.tr: Section. A slave was bought by the loosening of a shoe, as if by an earnest. See Servus Canan.

units.la: CALCEUS Psal. 60. 10. legimus super Edomaum projiciam calceum meum &c. ibi secundùm R. Imman. significat etiam Chirothecam. Quia mos erat regum urbem fortem obsidentium, ut Rex Chirothecam projiceret intra urbem; q. d. nunquam se ab urbe recessurum nisi urbe captâ. vid. Chaldaum in Ruth. 4.7.8. Succah sol. 52. 2. Elia in Thisbi in פעמ & Lex. Pagn. in red.
units.tr: SHOE In Psalm 60:10 we read, Over Edom will I cast out my shoe, etc. There, according to R. Immanuel, it also means a glove. For it was the custom of kings besieging a strong city to throw a glove into the city, as if to say that they would never withdraw from the city until it was taken. See the Chaldee at Ruth 4:7–8; Succah fol. 52.2; Elijah of Tishbi, under pa'am; and Pagnin's lexicon, under red.

units.la: CAMELORUM τρίχας vocant Talmudici צמר בגליים Menachot sol. 39. 2. Vestis non est ei prater lanam לרבות צמר גמלי וצמר ארנבי Ad addendum lanam vel pilos Camelorum & lanam leporinam. §. Com-
units.tr: CAMELS The Talmudists call the hairs (of camels) tricha, that is, tzemer begalim [צמר בגליים], Menachot fol. 39.2. "He has no garment except wool," to be added to, letarbot tzemer gemali ve-tzemer arnabi [לרבות צמר גמלי וצמר ארנבי], "wool or hairs of camels and rabbit's wool."

units.la: §. Commiscere lanam ovium cum pilis camelorum non fuit licitum, quia in vestimentis omnia prohibentur heterogenea vid. Orach Chajim lib.2.309.
units.tr: Section. It was not permitted to mix sheep's wool with camel's hair, because in garments all heterogeneous things are forbidden. See Orach Chayim, book 2, 309.

units.la: §. In Berefchit Rabba. §. 20. exiftimat R. Samuel Bar Nachman, veftimentum quod fecit Deus Adamo, fuiffe מצמר גמלים de pilis Camelorum,& pilis leporum.
units.tr: Section. In Bereshit Rabba §20, R. Samuel bar Nachman thinks that the garment God made for Adam was mi-tzemer gemalim [מצמר גמלים], of camel's hair and hares' hair.

units.la: Cana in qua Chriftus nuptiis interfuit, forfan eft illud כנה de quo legimus apud Iuchafin fol. 57. In fine capitis feptimi Bava Metzia eft traditio. Abba Chalaphta de Cephar Chanania dicit nomine R. Meir &c. ובל כי כפר חנגיה היא כפר Et videtur mihi, quod Cephar Chanania fit Cephar f.pagus (canna: ficut probabile eft ex capite nono tractatus Scheviit, nam ibi erat initium Galilaea inferioris.
units.tr: The Cana at which Christ was present at the wedding is perhaps that Kenah which we read of in Yuchasin fol. 57. At the end of the seventh chapter of Bava Metzia there is a tradition: Abba Chalafta, from Kefar Chananiah, says in the name of R. Meir, etc.; and ve-chol ki Kefar Chananyah hi kefar [ובל כי כפר חנגיה היא כפר]. And it seems to me that Kefar Chananiah is a village (kefar, Cana), as is probable from the ninth chapter of the tractate Shevi'it, for there was the beginning of Lower Galilee.

units.la: §. קנה cum litera initiali Koph eft civitas in tribu Afer, Iof.xix. 28. ubi Græca quædam habent Καρσαν alia vero Καρα.
units.tr: Section. Kanah [קנה], with the initial letter Qoph, is a city in the tribe of Asher, Joshua 19:28, where some Greek copies have Karsan, others Kara.

units.la: §. Memoratur etiam apud Talmudicos קיני Keni, ut in Obalot c.18. v.ult. רבי ובית דינו נסנו על קיני Rabbi & confeffus eius numeratis fuffragiis de Keni eam puram pronuntiarunt.
units.tr: Section. Keni is also mentioned among the Talmudists, as in Oholot chapter 18, last verse: "Rabbi and his court, the votes having been counted, pronounced Keni clean."

units.la: §. Bis occurrit mentio pagi Καρα apud Iosephum Antiq. lib.13 23. Et in vita eius.
units.tr: Section. The village Kara is mentioned twice in Josephus, Antiquities, book 13, chapter 23, and in his Life.

units.la: Cananæ populi. In catalogo excidendarum gentium etiam Perizæos habes; at Gen. x. inter filios Cananis Perizæus non numeratur; hinc etiam quidam supponunt illos populos Perizaos dictos esse, quasi diceres paganos, eò quod in villis & pagis degerent non munitis.
units.tr: Canaanite peoples. In the list of nations to be destroyed you also find the Perizzites; yet in Genesis 10 the Perizzite is not counted among the sons of Canaan. Hence some suppose that these peoples were called Perizzites, as if you would say pagans, because they lived in villages and unwalled hamlets.

units.la: Probabile eft quafdam familias Cananiticæ ftirpis,denominatas fuiffe non ab ipfiffimo immediato filio Cananis,à quo originem deduxerunt, fed àfamofo ac memorabili aliquo homine iftius ftirpis. Vide Cl. Leigtfootum in Chorog.Marci p.86. Huius claffis etiam erant Kenazi, Kenmizai, & Kadmonai: Quas nationes nondum Iudai fubiugarunt, fed ia fiet tempore Meffiæ,& ex illarum civitatibus adhuc tres aliæ civitates refugii ordinabuntur. Maymon in רוצח cap.8.Berefchit Rabba fol.28.2. Quales illæ nationes fint, diffentiunt Magiftri: Hierofolymitani in Kiddufchin fol.61.4.dicunt effe Salmæos, Sabæos, Nabatheos. Vel Afiam,Carthagenam, & Turkiam. Babylonici vero in Bab. Bathra fol.56. 1. Effe Napthuchæos, Arabes, & Salmæos; Secundùm R. Iehudam sunt illæ gentes, Mons Seir, Amon & Moab. Secundùm R. Simeonem עורפסיים Afiam & Hiffpaniam.
units.tr: It is probable that certain families of the Canaanite stock were named not after the immediate son of Canaan from whom they descended, but after some famous and memorable man of that stock. See the learned Lightfoot on Mark, p. 86. Of this class also were the Kenizzites, Kenmizzites and Kadmonites. These nations the Jews have not yet subdued, but this will be done in the time of the Messiah, and from their cities three other cities of refuge will be appointed. Maimonides, Hilchot Rotze'ach, chapter 8; Bereshit Rabba fol. 28.2. The teachers disagree about what these nations are. The Jerusalem Talmud, Kiddushin fol. 61.4, says they are the Salmaeans, Sabaeans and Nabataeans, or Asia, Carthage and Turkey. The Babylonian teachers, in Bava Batra fol. 56.1, say they are the Naphtuchaeans, Arabs and Salmaeans. According to R. Yehudah, these nations are Mount Seir, Ammon and Moab. According to R. Simeon, Orpsiim [עורפסיים] are Asia and Spain.

units.la: §. Bellum quod contra feptem gentes gefferunt Ifraelitæ erat מלחמת מצוה bellum præcepti, à quo nemo excipiebatur nec ipfe fponfus in thalamo. Maym. Hal. Melach. c.7. Quomodo Girgefæi præfente Alexandro magno cum Ifraelitis de repetundis expoftularunt. vid. Alexander.
units.tr: Section. The war which the Israelites waged against the seven nations was milchemet mitzvah [מלחמת מצוה], a war of command, from which no one was exempt, not even the bridegroom in his bridal chamber. Maimonides, Hilchot Melachim, chapter 7. How the Girgashites, in the presence of Alexander the Great, complained to him with the Israelites about extortion, see under Alexander.

units.la: CAPERNAUM inter Tiberiada & Tarichæas fita fuit, & probabile eft illam urbem nomen fumpfiffe à πηγὴ πολιμωζτη Καπερναὺμ fonte dulciffimo, Capernaum vocato, quia fecundùm Iofephum de bello lib. 3. c. 35. regionem Gennefar irrigavit.
units.tr: CAPERNAUM lay between Tiberias and Tarichaea, and it is probable that the city took its name from a very sweet spring, called Capernaum [πηγὴ γλυκυτάτη Καπερναούμ], because, according to Josephus, On the War, book 3, chapter 35, it watered the region of Gennesaret.

units.la: §. Guil. Tyrius lib. 10. cap. 16. nobis aliquam Capernaum ad littus maris mediterranei describit, prout illa cuius mentionem facit facer codex, ad littus maris Gennesareticי fuit.
units.tr: Section. William of Tyre, book 10, chapter 16, describes for us a certain Capernaum on the shore of the Mediterranean sea, but the one mentioned by the holy codex was on the shore of the Sea of Gennesaret.

units.la: §. De נחום כפר Capernaum legitur in Midrasch Cohelet folio 85. 2. Chanina filius, fratris R. Iosua profeßus est כפרנחום, & fecerunt in eum מינאי haretici aliquid incantationis, &c.
units.tr: Concerning Kefar Nachum [נחום כפר], Capernaum, we read in Midrash Kohelet, folio 85.2: "Chanina the son of the brother of R. Joshua professed (the faith) of Capernaum, and the heretics (minim) performed some incantation over him," etc.

units.la: כפר צמח Caphar tzemach urbs vel pagus Decapolitanus. Rabbi solvit eam à decimatione rerum dubiarum vid. Hierof. Demai fol. 22. 3. R. Salomo hunc locum vocat כפר סמי per extraordinariam n x transmutationem.
units.tr: Kefar Tzemach [כפר צמח], a city or village of the Decapolis. Rabbi released it from the tithing of doubtful produce; see the Jerusalem Talmud, Demai fol. 22.3. R. Solomon calls this place Kefar Simi [כפר סמי], through an extraordinary transposition of letters.

units.la: §. Dicitur eius nihil licet pronuntiare nisi illa in ab Hierosolymitanis numerari inter Vrbes prohibitas in limite. עיירות אסורות בתחום
units.tr: Section. It is said that nothing of it may be pronounced unless it is numbered by the Jerusalemites among the cities forbidden within the boundary [עיירות אסורות בתחום].

units.la: כפר קרניים Caphar Carnain. De hoc pago sic loquuntur Hierosolymitani loco modo cit. Caphar Carnaim est eiusdem conditionis cum Beth Scheane. Id est, est Iuris Ethnici.
units.tr: Kefar Karnayim [כפר קרניים], Caphar Carnaim. Of this village the Jerusalemites speak thus in the passage just cited: "Caphar Carnaim is of the same condition as Beth Shean," that is, it is subject to the law of the Gentiles.

units.la: כפר עמ"ק Caphar sive pagus Imki, eius memoria fit in Taanith fol. 21. 1. Civitas in qua sunt quingenti pedites ut Caphar Imki.
units.tr: Kefar Imki [כפר עמ"ק], the village or pagus Imki; its memory is preserved in Ta'anit fol. 21.1: "A city in which there are five hundred foot-soldiers, like Kefar Imki."

units.la: §. In textu Talmudico scribitur עפ"י, sed Aruch & R. Salomo עבקי ponunt.
units.tr: Section. In the Talmudic text it is written Ayin-Pe [עפ"י], but the Aruch and R. Solomon give Ayin-Bet-Qof-Yod [עבקי].

units.la: §. Sandalia quaedam ab hoc loco famosa fuerunt, & עבקי סנדלי calcei Imkiensis vocantur, Kelim c. 9.
units.tr: Section. Certain sandals were famous from this place, and they are called sandals of Imki [עבקי סנדלי], calcei Imkiensis, Kelim chapter 9.

units.la: כפר ביש Oppidum malum sonat, quod ita nominatum fuit דלא יהבי ביתא לאו שפיוא quod non praberet, domum hospitalem.
units.tr: Bad town is what the name means, because it was so called since it did not provide a hospitable house (Aramaic: dela yehavei bayta la shafyo) [דלא יהבי ביתא לאו שפיוא].

units.la: §. כפר שחלי Oppidum à quadam herba sic dictum, quod ilta he. ba nutrirentur. Bab. Gittin sol.57.1. Vbi etiam fit mentio כפר דכריא Oppidi masculorum, idco dictum quòd uxores ipsorum primo parerent mares, & deinde fœmellas, & sic desinerent, vel sicuti dicitur HierofTaanith sol 69 i quod nisi indè aliquo discederent fœminæ, non pœtuerunt non mares parere.
units.tr: Kafar Sechali: a town named from a certain herb, because children were nourished on it. Bab. Gittin fol. 57.1. There is also mention there of Kafar Dekaria, town of males, so called because the wives there first bore males and then females, and so it ended. Or, as is said in Hierosolymitanum Taanith fol. 69.1, unless the women had left there, they could not stop bearing males.

units.la: (hanania oppidum, Hierof. Avoda Zaaah sol. 43. 2. etiam כפר הנניה כפר חן Oppidum Cana vocatur.
units.tr: (Hananiah, a town. Jerusalem Avodah Zarah fol. 43.2.) Kafar Hananiah is also called Kafar Chan, town of Cana.

units.la: §. Caphar Chananiæ erat medium Galileæ; Schevit cap.9. v. 2. distabat à כפר עיתני Oppido Vtbni 30.milliaria.Gloff.ad Bab.Berac sol.43.2.
units.tr: Kafar Chananiah lay in the middle of Galilee. Shevit ch. 9, v. 2, places it 30 miles from Kafar Itni, town of Utbni. Gloss on Bab. Berachot fol. 43.2.

units.la: §. Familia Mamal, & familia Gorionis tempore famis ficus atque uvas aridas pauperibus ex כפר שיחין & כפר הנניה distribuerunt. Bab. E ubbin sol. 51. 1.
units.tr: In a famine the family of Mamal and the family of Gorion distributed dried figs and grapes to the poor from Kafar Sichin and Kafar Hananiah. Bab. Eruvin fol. 51.1.

units.la: CARNIS
units.tr: FLESH

units.la: Esum ante diluvium illicitum fuisse plurimi referunt Rabbini.
units.tr: Many rabbis report that eating flesh was forbidden before the flood.

units.la: Aben Esra in Genes. 1. 29. 30. הני נתתי לכם Ecce dedi vobis: Permisit his verbis, inquit, filiis Adam & omni animam vivam habenti comedere. Omnis quidem barba & omnis frutlus arboris concessus est Homini. At om is herba viridis data est bestiis & omni reptili, ועב כה לא התיר הבשר Et hactenus non concessit Deus carnem nisi post diluvium.
units.tr: Aben Ezra on Genesis 1:29-30. "Behold, I have given you" [הני נתתי לכם]. He says that with these words God permitted the sons of Adam and every living soul to eat. Indeed every herb and every fruit of tree was granted to man, but every green herb was given to the beasts and to every creeping thing. "And up to this point God did not permit flesh" [ועד כה לא התיר הבשר], except after the flood.

units.la: Iarchius in eund. locum. Permissum non erat Adamo & mulieri eius occidere ullam creaturam, & carnem comedere; Postquam verò venevenerunt filii Noë, בשר ותיר להים Permisit eis Deus earnem, sicut scriptum est, Omne reptile quod vivit &c. Similia reperies in Bereschit Rabba sect.34. apud Iosephum Albo lib. פרק parte III. c.14 15. Mehajje Bea Israel in Conciliat. q.10. in Genes. Quae omnia originem trahunt à sententia R. Ienanan is in Gem Sanhed. cap.7.
units.tr: Jarchi on the same passage. It was not permitted to Adam and his wife to kill any creature and eat flesh. But after the sons of Noah came, God permitted them flesh [בשר ותיר להים], as it is written, "Every creeping thing that lives," etc. Similar things you will find in Bereshit Rabba sect. 34; in Joseph Albo, book 3, chapters 14 and 15; in Mehajje Bea Israel in Conciliator q. 10 on Genesis. All of these derive from the opinion of R. Yannai in Gemara Sanhedrin ch. 7.

units.la: Carmel. Mons ille non longè distat à mari mediterraneo; quod ex eo apparet, quòd ille qui a vertice eius sub occasum solis descendit, & se in mari lavat, adhuc æstimetur טבול יום interdiu lotus, & quasi pleno die se lavasset, ex H erof. Beracot sol.2 2. col.
units.tr: Mount Carmel is not far from the Mediterranean Sea. This is clear from the fact that one who comes down from its summit toward sunset and washes himself in the sea is still reckoned as one who has bathed by day [טבול יום], as if he had washed in full daylight. Jerusalem Berachot fol. 2.2, col.

units.la: Si Casus nocturnus Sacerdoti excubias agenti in templo, contigisset, per cochleam descendebat in cryptam porticus & ibi se lavabat. Middot c.1. v.ult.
units.tr: If a nocturnal emission happened to a priest keeping watch in the temple, he went down by a spiral stair into the crypt of the portico and washed himself there. Middot ch. 1, last verse.

units.la: Castigationes temporales, sunt quasi fax accensa in manu hominis, ut cognoscatur כה טיבו עם נורא Qualis sit status eius cum creatore suo. Baal Akeda. Pulchra est Iudæorum castigatio, sicut lorum rubrum לסוסיא חיורא, equo albo Rc. Chagig. sol.9.2.
units.tr: Temporal chastisements are like a torch lit in a man's hand, so that he may know what his state is with his Creator. Baal Akeda. The Jewish comparison is fine: like a red strap on a white horse. Chagigah fol. 9.2.

units.la: §. Castigationes מכר קין abrodunt, vel finiunt omnes iniquitates hominis: quasi sanguinem hominis exhauriunt, & vires consumunt, ut iniquè agere desinat. Berac. sol.5 1. Shabbat sol. 33. 1. de duplici castig. vid. Buxt. L x. Talm.p 965.
units.tr: Chastisements wipe out, or put an end to, all of a man's iniquities. They drain away his blood, as it were, and use up his strength, so that he ceases to act wickedly. Berachot fol. 5.1; Shabbat fol. 33.1. On the twofold chastisement see Buxtorf, Lex. Talm. p. 965.

units.la: Caupones. Veritas omnis hominis invenitur in mundo, præter cauponum. R.D. Kimchi L. R. סנו. Ita Horat Satyr. Perfidus hic caupo.
units.tr: Innkeepers. Every man's honesty is found in the world except that of innkeepers. R. D. Kimchi, Lexicon Radicum, root סנו. So Horace, Satires: "This treacherous innkeeper" [Perfidus hic caupo].

units.la: §. Cauponi non vendendum Demai aut fructus qui non decimati sunt antea, non sunt enim credendi. Demai c.3 5 6.
units.tr: Demai, or fruit that has not previously been tithed, must not be sold to innkeepers, for they are not to be trusted. Demai ch. 3, §§ 5-6.

units.la: Causæ pecuniariæ à tribus diiudicantur, partium quæque unum deligit sibi, & pariter adscisciunt tertium. Pars quæque Iudicem ab adversario delectum repudiandi ius habet, si illum ob propinquitatem aut aliam causam ad hoc ineptum esse demonstrare poterit. Qui dixerit, Ego causam meam patri meo vel etiam tuo detulero fidens, imò etiam על שלושי רועי בקר tribus bubulcis, secundùm R. Meir retractare poterit, sed non secundùm sapientes. Sanhed. cap.3.1.2. de causis capitalibus vid. Iudicia.
units.tr: Monetary cases are decided by three judges. Each party chooses one for himself, and together they take a third. Each party has the right to reject a judge chosen by its opponent, if it can show that he is unfit because of kinship or some other cause. Someone who says, "I will confidently commit my case to my father, or even to yours," or even "to three herdsmen" [על שלושי רועי בקר], may retract this according to R. Meir, but not according to the sages. Sanhedrin ch. 3, §§ 1-2. On capital cases see Judicia.

units.la: חבריכם Chaverim, Ita vocantur תלמידי חכמים discipuli sapientum, quia illorum societas quâ inter se invicem conglutinati sunt, est חברת נאמנה societas vera, quaque ad שם חברת שמים Dei communionem ducit. Qui autem pro חבר haberi vult, cum plebeis se miscere non debet, nec aridos nec humidos fructus ipsis divendere, aut ab illis emere. Non debet apud plebeios hospitari, non debet educare בהמה דקה parvum pecus, nec lascivire in votis vovendis, nec se ob mortuum immundum reddere. Demai cap.2.3. §. Qui vult חבר esse debet suam חברות suscipere coram tribus aliis חברים religiosis, qui ipsum quoque per triginta dies probant, & deinde demum à discipulo sapientum fit נאמן ille de quo omnes debent persuasi esse, illum omnem munditiem sectari, & quaerere. Maymon. ad loc. Ex his multis locis Talmudicis elegantem lucem aspergere poteris, præcipuè iis quæ de נאמן occurrunt in Demai.
units.tr: Chaverim [חבריכם]. This is what disciples of the wise [תלמידי חכמים] are called, because the fellowship by which they are bound together is a faithful fellowship [חברת נאמנה], which leads to the communion of God [שם חברת שמים]. Whoever wishes to be regarded as a chaver must not mix with common people, nor sell them dry or moist fruits, nor buy from them. He must not lodge among the common people, must not keep small cattle, must not be frivolous in making vows, and must not make himself unclean for a dead unclean person. Demai ch. 2-3. Whoever wishes to be a chaver must take up his fellowship before three other religious chaverim, who test him for thirty days. Then at last he becomes a faithful man [נאמן], of whom all must be persuaded that he pursues and seeks all purity. Maimonides on the passage. From the many Talmudic passages you may shed an elegant light, especially those about the faithful man [נאמן] that occur in Demai.

units.la: §. Num חברים ad statuendam Neomeniam ingrediantur quæruntᵣ in Hierof.Sanhed. sol.18. 3. dixit R.Hoschaia,cûm ego חבר essem, induxit me R. Samuel Ben Isaac ad statuendam Neomeniam, ego autem ignoravi num è numero essem nec ne.
units.tr: Whether the chaverim may enter to fix the New Moon is asked in Jerusalem Sanhedrin fol. 18.3. R. Hoshaya said: "When I was a chaver, R. Samuel ben Isaac brought me in to fix the New Moon, but I did not know whether I was among their number or not."

units.la: §. Cum Rabban Gamaliel annum emboliʒare vellet,convocavit ad septem seniores; ingressi autem sunt octo; dixit Rabban Gamaliel, quis huc ingressus est absq; venia? Ego respondit Samuel Parvus, (qui ex numero חברים erat.) Hîc & aliis locis חבר simpliciter studiosum & hominem doctrinâ imbutum significat: Sed aliquando ut supra aliquo modo innuimus latiùs sumitur, pro omnibus illis qui vitam devotiorem quàm vulgus profitentur,sive doƈti sint sive indoƈti; hinc mentio fit חבר כותי Religiosi Samaritani Bab. Beracot sol. 44.2. נחתום חבר Pistoris religiosi Ioma sol.8.2. חבריא זעירא וחבריא רברבי Religiosorum maiorum & minorum B. Batra sol. 17.1. חברי מדכן בגלילא Religiosi Galilei purificant i.e. secund. Gloss. mundant vinum suum & oleum in libationem, si forte in diebus ipsorum ædificetur templum.
units.tr: When Rabban Gamaliel wished to intercalate the year, he summoned seven elders, but eight came in. Rabban Gamaliel said, "Who came in without permission?" Samuel the Small answered, "I did" (he was one of the number of the chaverim). Here and elsewhere chaver simply means a student and a man steeped in learning. But sometimes, as we hinted above, it is taken more broadly, for all who profess a more devout life than the common people, whether learned or unlearned. Hence mention is made of a chaver Kutei, religious Samaritan (Bab. Berachot fol. 44.2); a chaver nachtum, religious baker (Yoma fol. 8.2); the chaverei ze'ira and chaverei rabrabei, religious of the lesser and greater (B. Batra fol. 17.1); and the chaverei medakhan bigelila, religious of Galilee who purify, that is, according to the Gloss, they cleanse their wine and oil for libation, in case the temple should perhaps be built in their days.

units.la: גד יון Gad Iavan est locus in templo,eius mentio fit in tract. יבין c.1.5.Videt unam multiplicatam instar trium כמן גד יון לשולוח quæ sunt à Gad Iavan ad Siloam. Giossatores & Aruch quid Gad Iavan sic explicant. יון גד est Phraseologia deducta à verbis istis העורכים לגד שלחן Esai.lxv. 11. Et est locus ubi reges Graci erexerunt idolum: Sicut dicitur in Cod. Avoda Zarah, in angulo ortum astivum spectante Asmonai abdiderunt lapides altaris, quod profanaverant Graeci idolisfuu. De loco illo in quo lapides altaris profanati à familia Asmonæa positi fuerunt vid. Middot cap.1.6.
units.tr: Gad Javan [גד יון] is a place in the temple. It is mentioned in the tractate Middot, ch. 1, §5, where one stone is seen multiplied like three, which lie "from Gad Javan to Siloam." The glossators and the Aruch explain Gad Javan in this way. "Gad Javan" is a phrase derived from the words "who prepare a table for Gad" (Isaiah 65:11). It is the place where the Greek kings set up an idol. As it is said in the Gemara of Avodah Zarah: in the corner facing the summer sunrise, the Hasmoneans hid the stones of the altar, which the Greeks had profaned with idols. On the place where the stones of the altar, profaned, were laid by the Hasmonean family, see Middot ch. 1, §6.

units.la: Christi discipuli quinque numerantur Bab. Sanhed.sol.43.1. Tradunt Rabbini quinque fuerunt discipuli Iesu. מתאי נקאי נצר ובוני ותודה Matthai (Matthaeus) Nakai, Nezer, Boni, & Thodah (Iudas.) de Salvatore nostro vid.Cl.Butx.Lex. Talm. p.991.1184.
units.tr: The disciples of Christ are numbered as five. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 43.1: The rabbis hand down that there were five disciples of Jesus: Mattai, Nakai, Netzer, Buni, and Todah [מתאי נקאי נצר ובוני ותודה], that is Matthew, Nakai, Netzer, Buni, and Thodah (Judas). On our Saviour see Cl. Buxtorf, Lex. Talm. pp. 991, 1184.

units.la: §. De Christi profectione in Ægyptum vid. Ægyptus.
units.tr: On Christ's journey into Egypt see Egypt.

units.la: §. An Iudæi per Ben Sadta Christum intelligant vide Ben Sadta.
units.tr: On whether the Jews understand Christ by Ben Sadta, see Ben Sadta.

units.la: §. De Messia plurima, Vide suo loco.
units.tr: On the Messiah there is very much; see in its place.

units.la: §. Quod toties nomini Christi in Novo Testamento, superaddatur nomen Iesu contra Iudæorum perfidiam fit, qui Messiam & Christum quidem profitentur, sed Iesum Nazarenum eum esse strenuò negant.
units.tr: That the name of Jesus is added so often to the name of Christ in the New Testament is directed against the perfidy of the Jews, who indeed profess that the Messiah and Christ is, but who strenuously deny that Jesus of Nazareth is he.

units.la: §. Evangelistæ, Christi genealogiam, non ad Mariam sed Iosephum maritum Mariæ, aut ad Eli Mariæ patrem deducunt, propter illam rationem quæ Iuchasin folio 55. 2. proponitur משפחה משפחת אם אין קרוה Familia materna non vocanda est familia.
units.tr: §. The Evangelists trace Christ's genealogy either to Joseph, the husband of Mary, or to Eli, Mary's father, rather than to Mary herself, on the principle stated in Iuchasin, folio 55, column 2: מִשְׁפַּחַת אֵם אֵין קוֹרִין לָהּ מִשְׁפָּחָה [The maternal family is not to be called a family.]

units.la: §. Christus baptizatus fuit cùm vigesimum nonum annum iam compleverat,& tricesimum iam recens inchoarat: hoc sonant verba Lucæ, ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα ὤν, secundùm illud Iudæorum axioma in Rosch Haschana sol.
units.tr: §. Christ was baptized when he had already completed his twenty-ninth year and had only just begun his thirtieth. Luke's words, ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα ὤν [beginning about thirty years old], suggest this, according to the Jewish axiom in Rosh Hashanah.

units.la: 2.2. יום אחר בשנה חשוב שנה Dies primus anni reputatur pro ipso anno.
units.tr: 2.2. יוֹם אַחַר בַּשָּׁנָה חָשׁוּב שָׁנָה [The first day of the year is reckoned as the year itself.]

units.la: §. Christus in oppido Capernaum civis fuit, & ut civis didrachma solvit Matth.17. 24. Non autem difficile fuit ius civitatis acquirere nam in Bava Bathra c.1. dicitur, sufficere ut aliquis ibi per duodecim menses habitaverit. Cur autem Nazaretham deseruerit post transfactos illic 26. aut 27.annos patet ex Luc.iv.28.
units.tr: §. Christ was a citizen of the town of Capernaum, and as a citizen he paid the didrachma (Matt. 17:24). It was not difficult to acquire the rights of citizenship, for in Bava Bathra, chapter 1, it is said that it is enough for someone to have lived there for twelve months. Why he left Nazareth after spending twenty-six or twenty-seven years there is clear from Luke 4:28.

units.la: §. Christus loquutus est ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων Matth. 7.29. quia ille verborum suorum authoritatem non stabilivit solo aliquo תנו רבנן tradiderunt Magistri aut אומרים חכמי dixerunt sapientes, sicuti fecerunt Scribae & Pharisaei, nisi enim illi oraculum aliquod traditionale adduxissent מסנו קבלו לא eorum doctrinam non receperunt. Sic filii Bethirae noluerunt fidem adhibere Hilleli, nisi postquam dixisset, Sic audivi a Schemaja atque Abtalione. Hierof. Pesachin folio 33.1.
units.tr: §. Christ spoke ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων [as one having authority] (Matt. 7:29), because he did not establish the authority of his words by citing some tradition, as the Scribes and Pharisees did, with phrases such as תָּנוּ רַבָּנָן [the Masters have taught] or אוֹמְרִים חֲכָמִים [the sages have said]. For unless they had produced some traditional saying, מְסֹרֶת קִבְּלוּ לֹא [they did not receive his teaching]. So the sons of Bethira would not give credit to Hillel unless he had said, Thus I heard from Shemaiah and Avtalion (Jerusalem Talmud, Pesachim, folio 33, column 1).

units.la: §. Christus duodecim elegit discipulos, pro numero tribuum Israeliticarum, hi vocantur Hebraicè שלוחי Apostoli, quo titulo etiam insigniti sunt Moses & Aaron à Chaldaeo Paraphraste Hierem.11.1. haec vox שלוח hanc emphasin habet, ut non nude nuntium sonet, sed nuntium vices mittentis gerentem. Nam שלוחו של אדם כמותו Apostolus cuiusvis est sicut ipse a quo deputatur. Bab Berac. sol.34.2.
units.tr: §. Christ chose twelve disciples, corresponding to the number of the tribes of Israel. In Hebrew they are called שְׁלוּחֵי [apostles], a title by which Moses and Aaron were also honoured by the Chaldee paraphrast (Jeremiah 11:1). The word שָׁלוּחַ has this emphasis: it signifies not merely a messenger but one who acts in the place of the sender. For שְׁלוּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּמוֹתוֹ [a man's apostle is as himself, by whom he is appointed] (Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot, folio 34, column 2).

units.la: §. Christus verè dici potest fuisse in sepulchro per tres יונה ἡμέρας τρεῖς, quamvis dè fuerit maxima pars diei primi, atque nox omninò ac longè maxima pars diei tertii, nam
units.tr: §. Christ may truly be said to have been in the tomb for three days, יוֹנָה [three days; τρεῖς ἡμέρας], although the greater part of the first day was over and the night, together with the greater part of the third day, was entirely and far the larger portion.

units.la: Hierof. Schabb. fol. 12. 1. dicitur עונה ולילה יום dies & nox constituunt עונה, & pars עונה est sicut totum. Si itaque pars זמן עונה concludit totum, sequitur hoc idiomate etiam partem illam minutulam diei tertii quo Christus resurrexit, pro toto die & noête eum sequente esse numerandam. Vide quæ computant de immunditie fœminæ in triduum Gemarista ad Schabb. c.9.3. De Christi condemnatione à Synedrio vid. Iudicia.
units.tr: For the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, folio 12, column 1, says that עוֹנָה וְלַיְלָה יוֹם [a day and a night make up an onah], and that a part of an onah is as the whole. If, then, a part of an onah counts for the whole, it follows by this idiom that even that tiny part of the third day on which Christ rose must be counted as the whole day and the night following it. Compare what the Gemarist reckons about the uncleanness of a woman for three days, in Shabbat, chapter 9, column 3. On Christ's condemnation by the Sanhedrin, see Judgments.

units.la: Christiani vid.gentes: In Christianorum laudem nihil dicere debes, v. g. quàm pulcher est ifte נ"ו Christianus. R. Salomoh ad Deut.7.2. & Bechai ad illum locum fol. 196. 4. Te non polluere debes rebus mulierum (christianarum. Aben Esra. Deut.7.5. Quomodo Christianorum scholas vocent. vid. Scholæ.
units.tr: Christians, or Gentiles. You must say nothing in praise of Christians, for example: how beautiful is that נוֹצְרִי [Christian]! R. Solomon on Deuteronomy 7:2, and Bechai on that place, folio 196, column 4: You must not defile yourself with the things of women (Christian women). Aben Ezra on Deuteronomy 7:5. On how they call the Christian schools, see Schools.

units.la: Chammat Gadaræ גדר חמתא urbecula fic diēta propter Thermas Tiberiadis: à qua tantillum distabat, ut quoad iter Sabbathicum Tiberienses & Chammatenses constituerent civitatem unam. Fit etiam mentio apud Talmudicos חמת רפאל (chammat Pellæ sive Callirrhoe. de Chammat vide Megillah fol.6.1. Hierof.Erubbin fol.23.4. Hierof.Kiddufchin fol.46.
units.tr: Chammat Gadara (גַּדְרָא חַמְתָּא), a small town so called because of the hot baths of Tiberias, from which it was so near that, as regards the Sabbath journey, the people of Tiberias and of Chammat were treated as one city. Mention is also made among the Talmudists of חַמַּת רָפָאֵל [Chammat Pella, or Callirrhoe]. On Chammat see Megillah, folio 6, column 1; Jerusalem Erubin, folio 23, column 4; Jerusalem Kiddushin, folio 46.

units.la: 3. Hierof.Scheviit fol.36.3.
units.tr: 3. Jerusalem Sheviit, folio 36, column 3.

units.la: Cherubini ab utraque extremitate arcæ præsignarunt aliquo modo duos illos angulos in sepulchro Christi Ioh.xx.12.
units.tr: The cherubim at either end of the ark in some way foreshadowed those two angles in Christ's tomb (John 20:12).

units.la: §. De Cherubinis hæc leguntur in Bava Batra fol. 99.1. Onkelos profelytus dicit כרובים מעשה צעצועים Cherubini erant instar puerorum recedentium à magistro. Id est facie partim erga magistrum versâ, partim erga viam quâ illi perrecturi. Nam ut Gemaristæ, Cum praestaret Israel voluntatem Dei, aliter in alierius faciem respexerunt Cherubini, at vero cum non, tum respexerunt parietes.
units.tr: §. The following is read about the cherubim in Bava Batra, folio 99, column 1. Onkelos the proselyte says: כְּרוּבִים מַעֲשֵׂה צַעֲצוּעִים [the cherubim were like children walking away from their teacher]. That is, with their faces partly turned towards the teacher and partly towards the road on which they were about to go. For, as the Gemarists say: When Israel did the will of God, the cherubim looked at one another's faces; but when it did not, they looked at the walls.

units.la: §. Chagiga sol.13.2. quæritur, quid est כרוב ? Respond. כרביא שכן ככל קורין ליניקא Idem quod כרביא sicut puer. Nam in Babylonia puerum vocant רביא.
units.tr: §. Chagigah, folio 13, column 2, asks: what is כְּרוּב [cherub]? The answer: כְּרַבְיָא [a little child], the same as רַבְיָא, like a child, for in Babylonia they call a child רַבְיָא.

units.la: חכחשה HaCchascha est בעדות עצאז contradictio illa quæ illi fit circa ipsum testimonium, ut si unum par testium dicat, rem factam alter neget. הומה autem est עצאם בעדים Circa testes; cùm probatur ipsos nescire an res ita se habeat nec ne. Hæc nisi præsentibus prioribus testibus non fit; illa est absentibus &c. Maymon. Hal. Edusl. cap. 18.
units.tr: חֲכָחֲשָׁה [Hakhachasha] is the contradiction that arises concerning the testimony itself, as when one pair of witnesses says a thing was done and another denies it. הוֹמָה, however, is concerning the witnesses, when it is shown that they do not know whether the matter is so or not. The former does not arise unless the first witnesses are present; the latter arises when they are absent, etc. Maimonides, Hilchot Edut, chapter 18.

units.la: החיצונים Ha Chitsonim ὁι ἐξω (quæ Phraseologia etiam occurrit Marc. iv. 11.) Iudæis erant Ethnici; nam quicquid regionis extra terram Israeliticam erat, illud solummodò vocarunt חוצה לארץ Extra terram, huius nominationis clarum exemplum habes in Bava Batra sol. 27.2. Arbor cuius pars dimidia nascitur intra terram Israeliticam, & dimidia pars extra terram &c.
units.tr: הַחִיצוֹנִים [Hachitsonim], οἱ ἔξω [those outside] (a phrase also found in Mark 4:11), were Gentiles to the Jews. For whatever lay outside the land of Israel they called simply חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ [outside the land]. A clear example of this usage is in Bava Batra, folio 27, column 2: A tree half of which grows within the land of Israel, and half outside the land, etc.

units.la: §. ספרים חיצונים libri ὶ ἐξω extranei, sunt aliquando simpliciter libri Ethnicorum, aliquando verò חכמת יונית של sapientia Græcorum. Aruch in voce מרום.
units.tr: §. ספרים חיצונים [outside books; βιβλία ἔξω, external books] are sometimes simply the books of the Gentiles, and sometimes the wisdom of the Greeks. Aruch, under the word מרום.

units.la: §. Vox חיצונים etiam aliquando nonnullos de gente Iudaica denotat. Megillah sol.24.2.
units.tr: §. The word חיצונים also sometimes denotes certain people of the Jewish nation. Megillah, folio 24, column 2.

units.la: Qui dat phylacteria sua infronte sua, aut inpalma sua חרי זה דרך הקראי Ecce morem sequitur Karaitarum. Et qui unum ex iis anro obducit, daiqve super vestem quae est ad manum דרי ו דרך החיצונים Ecce is morem sequi ur τῶν ἐξω. Gloss. חיצונים sunt homines qui proprium arbitrium sequuntur, & non sententiam sapientum.
units.tr: He who puts his phylacteries on his forehead or on his palm, הרי זה דרך הקראים [behold, this follows the custom of the Karaites]. Behold, he follows the custom of the Karaites. And he who covers one of them with gold, and puts it on the garment that is at hand, וְהֵרִי וְהוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַחִיצוֹנִים [behold, this is the custom of the outsiders]. Behold, he follows the custom of οἱ ἔξω [those outside]. Gloss: outsiders are men who follow their own judgment and not the opinion of the sages.

units.la: חיל Chel vid. Atrium.
units.tr: חֵיל [Chel], see Court.

units.la: CIRCUNCISIO. Præceptum circumcidendi omnes mascules. Qui non circuncisus est, in pœnam כרת excidii incurrit.
units.tr: CIRCUMCISION. The precept to circumcise all males. He who is not circumcised incurs the penalty of excision [karet, כרת].

units.la: §. Pater, Dominus servi, tum in familia nati, cùm pecuniâ acquisiti, filium & servos circuncidere debent, si id non faciunt peccant in præceptum affirmativum, & in ta i negligentia Synedrium illos circumcidi curat, etiam invitis patribus aut dominis, non enim patitur ut incircuncisus fit in Israele. Si autem acciderit ut talis infans aut servus à Synedrio circumcidi non possit, statim ac ætatem habet, ipse se circumcidere debet.
units.tr: A father, or a master of a slave, whether the slave was born in the household or acquired for money, must circumcise his son and his slaves. If they fail to do so, they sin against the affirmative precept. If, through such negligence, the Sanhedrin arranges for them to be circumcised, it does so even against the will of the fathers or masters, for it does not allow anyone to remain uncircumcised in Israel. If it happens that such an infant or slave cannot be circumcised by the Sanhedrin, he must circumcise himself as soon as he comes of age.

units.la: §. Eadem est ratio servi qui natus est inter Israelitas, & illius quem à gentibus acquisiverunt, nisi quòd illum qui in familia natus est circuncidant die octavo, pecuniâ verò acquisitum primo die emptionis. Si tamen accidit, ut quis servum senem ex gentilibus comparet, & ille se circumcidere renuat, expectare poterit cum ipso duodecim menses, quibus effluxis non diutiùs reincendus est, sed gentilibus iterum divendi debet, nisi in pacto coram domino gentili ipsi promiserit, se ipsum non ad circuncisionem adacturum, & servus septem Noachidarum præcepta in fe susceperit, alias tollendus & dimittendus est.
units.tr: The rule for a slave born among the Israelites is the same as for one acquired from the Gentiles, except that the one born in the household is circumcised on the eighth day, while the one bought is circumcised on the first day after the purchase. If, however, it happens that someone buys an elderly slave from the Gentiles, and the slave refuses to be circumcised, the master may wait with him for twelve months. When these have passed, he may no longer keep him, but must sell him again to the Gentiles, unless he has promised in a contract, before the Gentile master, that he will not compel him to circumcision, and the slave has taken upon himself the seven precepts of the sons of Noah. Otherwise he must be removed and dismissed.

units.la: §. Si quis ex gentilibus defiderat proselyta fieri, ante omnia fe circuncidere debet; fi verò iam circuncifus fuerit, cùm adhuc gentilis erat, nihilominus die octava ad sanguinem fœderis ex loco circuncifo stillandum tenetur. Ad idem obligatur qui circuncifus nascitur.
units.tr: If any Gentile wishes to become a proselyte, he must first of all circumcise himself. If, however, he was already circumcised while still a Gentile, he is nevertheless bound to let blood flow from the circumcised place on the eighth day, for the blood of the covenant. The same obligation falls on one who is born circumcised.

units.la: §. Androgynus, & ille qui duo præputia habet, item qui ex ventre matris exciditur: debent etiam die octavâ circuncidi.
units.tr: A hermaphrodite, and one who has two foreskins, likewise one who is cut out of his mother's womb, must also be circumcised on the eighth day.

units.la: §. Circuncisio fit de die non autem de nocte, sive sit tempore ordinario, quod est dies octavus, sive extraordinario, quod est à die nono & ultra. Illa quæ tempore ordinario fit pellit Sabbathum (i.e. in Sabbatho fieri potest:) Extraordinaria verò non pellit Sabbathum, neque ullum alium diem festum. Extraordinaria tamen & ordinaria fieri debet quamvis papula albicans lepræ in mentula appareat, quia præceptum affirmativum pellit negativum. Circuncisio Androgyni, illius qui ex ventre excisus, illius qui duo præputia habet, si incidit in Sabbathum, illud non pellit, sed debet fieri באתד בשבת ἐν μίᾳ σαββάτων die scilicet nono à generatione ipsorum.
units.tr: Circumcision is performed by day and not by night, whether it takes place at the regular time, which is the eighth day, or at the irregular time, which is from the ninth day onwards. The circumcision performed at the regular time overrides the Sabbath (that is, it may be done on the Sabbath). The irregular circumcision, however, does not override the Sabbath or any other festival day. Both the irregular and the regular circumcision must be performed even if a white spot of leprosy appears on the member, because an affirmative precept overrides a negative one. The circumcision of a hermaphrodite, of one cut from the womb, and of one who has two foreskins, if it falls on the Sabbath, is not overridden by it, but must be done on the first day of the week [באתד בשבת] [ἐν μιᾷ σαββάτων], namely on the ninth day from their birth.

units.la: §. Ægrotum non circuncidunt, sed expectant donec convaluerit. Similiter si infans die octavo viridis aut ruber appareat, expectant donec sanguis eius communem infantum colorem acquisiverit.
units.tr: §. The sick child is not circumcised, but they wait until he has recovered. Similarly, if on the eighth day an infant appears green or red, they wait until his blood has taken on the common colour of infants.

units.la: §. Si contigerit ut mulier primogenitum &
units.tr: §. If it happens that a woman has circumcised her firstborn and, on the eighth day, her second son as well,

units.la: H secundum suum filium die octava circumciderit, & ambo mortui sint, tertium die octava circumcidere non debet, sed expectabit usquedum vires sufficientes acquisiverit, ad dolores perferendos. In summa, in his caute agendum, & nihil est, à quo periculum mortis non dispensat. Maymon. Hal. Milah. cap. 1.
units.tr: and both have died, she must not circumcise a third on the eighth day, but shall wait until he has acquired sufficient strength to endure the pain. In short, caution must be exercised in these matters, and there is nothing from which danger of death does not excuse. Maimonides, Hilchot Milah, chap. 1.

units.la: §. Vnusquisque circumcidere potest, præputiatus, servus, mulier, parvulus, mulier, in eo loco ubi virum commodè habere non possunt; excepto gentili; si tamen ille circuncidisset, circuncisionem non reiterant.
units.tr: Anyone may circumcise: one who is uncircumcised, a slave, a woman, a child, a woman, in a place where men cannot conveniently be had; except a Gentile. If, however, a Gentile has circumcised, they do not repeat the circumcision.

units.la: §. Instrumenta circuncisionis esse possunt cultri lapidei, vitrei, novacula, & alia ex ferro confecta, sed non fustum Cannæ, quia admodum periculosum est.
units.tr: The instruments of circumcision may be knives of stone, of glass, a razor, and others made of iron, but not a stick of reed, because that is very dangerous.

units.la: §. Circuncisio ita fit, circuncisor imponit mentulæ bacillum, & præputium quantum potest super illum extendit, deinde forcipe partem eius prehendit, & novacula præcidit. Deinde duobus pollicis unguibus præputium arripit & devolvit, donec glans tota denudatur; quo facto sanguinem exsugit, donec advenerit sanguis è remotioribus corporis partibus, vulnerique emplastrum imponit. Qui simpliciter præputium præcidit, non vero etiam devolvit, est quasi non circuncidisset.
units.tr: Circumcision is done thus: the circumciser places a little stick on the member and stretches the foreskin over it as far as he can. Then with forceps he grasps part of it and cuts it off with a razor. Then, with the nails of his two thumbs, he seizes the foreskin and rolls it back until the whole glans is uncovered. When this is done, he sucks out the blood until blood comes from the more distant parts of the body, and he applies a plaster to the wound. One who merely cuts off the foreskin without also rolling it back is as if he had not circumcised at all.

units.la: §. Iteranda est circuncisio secundum sapientes, si præputium alicuius ita concreverit, & magnum factum fuerit, ut non dignosci possit, an circuncisus sit nec ne.
units.tr: According to the wise men, circumcision must be repeated if the foreskin of someone has grown together and has become so large that it cannot be determined whether he is circumcised or not.

units.la: §. Si ea quæ ipsis opus sunt ad circumcisionem nondum præparaverint ante Sabbathum, ipsis quidem ea præparare non licet, sed gentili alicui mandare possunt, ut illa adferat. Maymon.cit.tratt.c.2.
units.tr: If before the Sabbath they have not prepared the things needed for the circumcision, they are not permitted to prepare them themselves, but they may instruct some Gentile to bring them. Maimonides, loc. cit., tract. ch. 2.

units.la: §. De benedictionibus quas circumcisor, sive sit pater sive alius dicere debet, vid. Maymon in cap.3. Milah. Cl. Buxtorf. in Synagoga.
units.tr: Concerning the blessings which the circumciser, whether he is the father or another person, must recite, see Maimonides on ch. 3 of Milah. Cl. Buxtorf, in Synagoga.

units.la: §. Non benedicitur cum stillare faciunt sanguinem proselyto iam ante circuncisio, & puero qui circuncisus nascitur, nec cum Androgynus circunciditur, quia ille perfectus masculus non est.
units.tr: No blessing is said when they draw blood from a proselyte who was already circumcised beforehand, nor for a boy who was born circumcised, nor when a hermaphrodite is circumcised, because such a one is not a perfect male.

units.la: §. Si quis gentilis circuncidi peteret à Iudæo, ad id adactus propter ulcus aut vulnus aliquod quod in præputio eius est, ipsum circuncidere non debet, nisi vera intentione circuncidendi accesserit. Maymon.l.m.c.
units.tr: If a Gentile should ask a Jew to circumcise him, having been driven to it on account of some ulcer or wound on his foreskin, the Jew must not circumcise him unless he has approached with a genuine intention of being circumcised. Maimonides, loc. cit.

units.la: §. Circuncisio instituta est tùm ut hominum libido diminuatur, & membrum hoc quantum fieri potest ad illum actum debilitetur; cùm ut illi qui eiusdem fidei participes sunt, habeant aliquod signum, quod illos coniungat, & ab aliis discernat. Nam quoniam hoc est durissimum quid, non quivis illud suscipiet.
units.tr: Circumcision was instituted both so that human lust might be diminished and this member weakened as far as possible for that act, and so that those who share the same faith might have some sign which joins them together and distinguishes them from others. For since this is a very hard thing, not everyone would undertake it.

units.la: §. Circuncisio debet fieri in infantia ob tres rationes, 1. est, quia fi exspectaretur donec infans adolesceret, tùm id forte non amplius faceret. 2. quia non sentit tam magnum dolorem sicut adultus, tùm ob cutis suæ teneritatem, cùm propter imaginationis debilitatem.
units.tr: Circumcision ought to be performed in infancy, for three reasons. (1) If one waited until the infant grew up, perhaps he would then no longer do it. (2) Because he does not feel so great a pain as an adult, both on account of the tenderness of his skin and because of the weakness of his imagination.

units.la: 3. quia parentes admodum exiguam rationem habent infantis recenter nati. Die octavo vero circuncisio fieri debuit, quia vix ante illum diem infantes propter nimiam debilitatem, & humiditatem illos dolores ferre possent. Maymon More Nevoch.iii. 49.
units.tr: (3) Because parents have very little regard for an infant recently born. The circumcision ought indeed to be performed on the eighth day, because scarcely before that day can infants, on account of their excessive weakness and moistness, endure such pains. Maimonides, More Nevochim, iii. 49.

units.la: §. Perfequutione durante cum in בורני Burni & aliis locis non auderent circuncisionem infantum proclamare, statuerunt ut signum circuncisionis sonus molarum (quibus aromata praeparabant)essct. Ita in ברור חיל Beror Chel lumine candelae interdiu, aut plurium noête signum exhibuerunt, ac si quis publico praeconio edixisset, convivium circuncisionis (aut etiam nuptiarum, quod ipsis etiam prohibitum erat, vid. Aruch in אור) esse ibi. Gloss.ad Bab.Sanhed. sol.31.2. Quamvis deinde cessaret perfequutio, non tamen cessavit ista consuetudo.Chetubh. sol.25.3.
units.tr: While persecution was ongoing, and in Burni and other places they did not dare to announce the circumcision of infants, they agreed that the sign of a circumcision should be the sound of millstones (with which they prepared spices). Thus in Beror Chel, they showed a sign by a candle's light by day, or by several lights by night, as if someone had announced by public proclamation that there was a feast of circumcision (or even of a wedding, which was also forbidden to them; see Aruch under or) there. Gloss on Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin, fol. 31.2. Although the persecution afterwards ceased, this custom nevertheless did not cease. Chetubot, fol. 25.3.

units.la: §. Servus alicuius proselyti circuncidendus est etiam invitus, at filius alicuius non circuncidendus est invitus. Hieros. Ievamot folio 8.4.
units.tr: A slave of any proselyte must be circumcised even against his will, but the son of anyone must not be circumcised against his will. Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot, fol. 8.4.

units.la: §. Dicunt Rabbini nostri, quod omnis Israel reeecerat circuncisionem in Ægypto. At tandem sunt circuncisi הנלה בדם הפסח ונתערב דם המילה & commiftus est sanguis pafchatis, cum sanguine circuncisionis. Accepitque Deus unumquemque eorum, atque eum exosculatus est. Schemot Rabba Sect. 19.
units.tr: §. Our rabbis say that all Israel had neglected circumcision in Egypt. But at last they were circumcised, and the blood of the Passover was mingled with the blood of circumcision, and God took each one of them and kissed him. Shemot Rabba, sect. 19.

units.la: §. Maymon. Iffure Biah c.13. Per tria introducti sunt Israelitae in foedus; per circuncisionem, baptismum & oblationem sacrificii. His tribus etiam opus habet Ethnicus,si vult in foedus admitti.
units.tr: Maimonides, Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah, ch. 13. Israelites were brought into the covenant through three things: through circumcision, baptism, and the offering of a sacrifice. A Gentile also needs these three things, if he wishes to be admitted into the covenant.

units.la: CIVIS. Qui duodecim menses in civitate aliqua commoratus est, civis fit, קנה כה בית דירה הרי Si vero domum commorationis sibi comparaverit ille statim quoque ius civium sibi acquirit. Bava Batra c.1.5. vid. etiam Bab. Sanhed. sol.112.1. Hoc Gemara Hierof. sic explicat. Si quis commoretur in urbe triginta dies, fit sicut unus e civibus,quoad cistam eleemofynariam; si 6. menses, quoad vestitum; Si 12. menses quoad tributa & vectigalia. Gem. Babyl. addit, si 9. menses, quoad sepulturam.
units.tr: CITIZEN. One who has lived for twelve months in some city becomes a citizen. But if he has acquired a house of residence for himself, he at once also acquires the rights of citizens. Bava Batra, ch. 1, 5; see also Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin, fol. 112.1. The Jerusalem Gemara explains this as follows: if someone lives in a city for thirty days, he becomes like one of the citizens as regards the alms box; if for six months, as regards clothing; if for twelve months, as regards taxes and tolls. The Babylonian Gemara adds that if for nine months, as regards burial.

units.la: כלה ערב Ita vocatur illud ferrum quod tecto templi impositum erat, ne aves considendo murum conspurcarent. Maymonides in Hal. Beth Habech. cap. 4. med. illud ita describit גובה המעקה שלש אמות וטו של ביזל כמי סייף גובהו אמה על גבי המעקה סביב כדי שלא ינוחו עליו העופות: Altitudo Peribolii erat trium cubitorum, & lamina ferrea acuta ut gladius altitudine cubiti erat extremitati & circunferentia eius imposita, ne aves ibi quiescerent. Vid.L.Tal.Buxtorf.p.1038.
units.tr: Kela arev [כלה ערב] is the name given to that iron which was placed on the roof of the Temple, so that birds could not perch on the wall and foul it. Maimonides, in Hilchot Beth ha-Behirah, ch. 4, near the middle, describes it thus: "The height of the parapet was three cubits, and a sharp iron plate, like a sword, a cubit high, was set on top of the parapet all round, so that birds would not rest on it" [גובה המעקה שלש אמות וטו של ביזל כמי סייף גובהו אמה על גבי המעקה סביב כדי שלא ינוחו עליו העופות]. See Buxtorf's Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 1038.

units.la: CIVITATES,urbes oppidaq; triplici etiam nomine designant כרכים & כפרים & עיירות, quibus apud Evangelistas respondent πόλεις & κώμαι & κωμοπόλεις. כרכים redduntur per πόλεις & עיירות per κωμοπόλεις ex sensu eorum quae leguntur Bab. Chetub. sol.110. Vir non potest uxorem cogere, ut eum sequatur habitatum לא מעיר לכרך ולא מכרך לעיר non ex oppido in civitatem, nec ex civitate in urbem. Cuius rei ratio est respectu כרך civitatis, quia in civitate reperienda & habenda sunt quælibet, אלא בעיר Ast in oppido non habenda sunt quælibet, nam secundum Gloss. כרך maior est עיר oppido, & in כרך civitate locus est platearum quo conveniunt omnes cirumhabitantes ad forum ibique habenda sunt quælibet. Cur vero maritus non cogere potuerit uxorem relinquendi העיר oppidum, & ipsum sequendi in כרך civitatem, hanc rationem reddunt Gloss. quia Habitatio in Kerachin est peior, quia omnes illic habitant, & domus sunt compressa, & contigua, ita ut non sit ibi aura libera. At vero בעיר in oppido sunt horti & paradisi iuxta domos & aura salubrior.
units.tr: Cities, towns and villages are designated by three terms: kerakhin [כרכים], kefarim [כפרים] and ayarot [עיירות]. In the Evangelists these correspond to poleis [πόλεις], kōmai [κῶμαι] and kōmopoleis [κωμοπόλεις]. Kerakhin is rendered poleis and ayarot kōmopoleis, according to the sense of the passage in the Babylonian Talmud, Ketubot, p. 110: "A man cannot compel his wife to follow him when he removes from a town [ayir] to a city [kerakh], nor from a city to a town." The reason for this, with respect to a kerakh (city), is that in a city everything must be found and obtained, ela be-ir [אלא בעיר]; but in a town not everything need be obtained. For, according to the Gloss, a kerakh is larger than an ir (town), and in a kerakh, a city, there is a place of squares where all the surrounding inhabitants come together to the market, and there everything must be obtained. Why, however, the husband could not compel his wife to leave the ir (town) and follow him into the kerakh (city), the Gloss gives this reason: because living in kerakhin is worse, since everyone lives there, the houses are crowded and joined together, so that there is no free air. But in the ir, the town, there are gardens and orchards beside the houses, and the air is more wholesome.

units.la: §. Rem in Compendio sic habeto. Vrbes terræ Ifraeliticæ distinguuntur in כרכים oppida mœnibus cincta a diebus Iosua & עירות urbes, sive munitæ sint nec ne, sive vocentur גדולות magnæ vel קטנות parvæ, modo (ut notat Pirke Tosaphot art.2.) ibi sint decem homines otii orantes & legentes legem. At loca שאין כהן בטלין in quibus non sunt decem otiosi indicantur esse villa. Megillah c.1.1.
units.tr: By way of summary, take the following. The cities of the Land of Israel are divided into kerakhin, walled towns from the days of Joshua, and ayarot, cities, whether they are fortified or not, and whether they are called gedolot (great) or ketanot (small), provided that (as the Tosafot of Pirqe note, art. 2) there are ten men there, at leisure, praying and reading the Law. But places in which there are not ten men at leisure are called villages. Megillah, ch. 1, sec. 1.

units.la: §. Respectu urbium hæ observabantur cautiones. 1. Intra quinquaginta cubitos ab urbe nullum columbarium ædificari debuit, (ne columbæ hortos & semina perderent. 2. non permiserunt arborem intra 25. cubitos ab urbe decoris causa. 3. non permiserunt cadavera aut sepulchra, aut officinam coriariam, nisi intra 50. cubitos ab urbe Bava Batra c.2.5.
units.tr: With respect to cities the following precautions were observed. (1) No dovecote was to be built within fifty cubits of a city, lest the doves destroy the gardens and seed. (2) They did not permit a tree within twenty-five cubits of a city, for the sake of decency. (3) They did not permit corpses or graves, or a tannery, except at a distance of fifty cubits from the city. Bava Batra, ch. 2, sec. 5.

units.la: Creatio est actio להוציא יש מאין producendi entis ex nihilo. Abenefra ad Genes.1.
units.tr: Creation is the act lehotsi yesh me-ayin [להוציא יש מאין], that is, of bringing a being forth out of nothing. Ibn Ezra on Genesis 1.

units.la: Beth in Bereschit 1. denotare potest ברכה Benedictionem, quasi Deus dixisset, incipiam cum Benedictione. בוך significat benedixit & maledixit, quia Biblia & benedictionem & maledictionem annuntiant. 2. Denotare potest שני עולמי duplicem mundum, hunc & futurum, de illis enim ubique sonat Sacra pagina. 3. forsan illâ literâ ב Deus alludit ad duplicem legem, scriptam & oralem, aut ad bina templa, templum primum & secundum. Sic ludit Baal Haturim Genes. 1.
units.tr: The letter beth in Bereshit (Gen. 1) may denote berakhah, blessing, as if God had said: I will begin with a blessing. Bara [בוך] signifies both "he blessed" and "he cursed", because Scripture proclaims both blessing and curse. (2) It may denote shnei olamim, the two worlds, this one and the future one, for it is of these that Holy Scripture speaks everywhere. (3) Perhaps by this letter beth God alludes to the twofold law, written and oral, or to the two temples, the first and the second. So the Baal ha-Turim plays on Genesis 1.

units.la: בראשית notat, Deum dum mundum conderet, animo iam concepisse exstructionem templi. Kimchi & Rabboth sest.1. Ex illa voce enim exsculpi potest ראש בית Domus prima.
units.tr: Bereshit [בראשית] signifies that God, while he was founding the world, had already conceived in his mind the building of the Temple. Kimchi and Rabbot, sect. 1. For from that word can be carved out rosh bayit, the first house.
