units.la: Malè Christiani Iudæorum Cabbalam sequentes ex ברא elicere volunt Trinitatem, quasi א insigniret אב Patrem, בן ב filium, רוח ר Spiritum S. Dant enim hoc modo hæreticis & infidelibus ansam augustissimum hoc mysterium cavillandi, sicuti fecit Enjedinus, addito Sarcasmo, א denotare ארה, & ר designare ראשית, ב verò esse initium vocis בליעל.
units.tr: Christians who follow the Cabbala of the Jews wrongly wish to draw the Trinity from bara [ברא], as if the aleph signified Father ('av), the beth the Son (ben), and the resh the Holy Spirit (ruach). In this way they give heretics and unbelievers an occasion to mock this most august mystery, as Enjedinus did, adding a sarcasm: that aleph denotes arah, the curse, and resh designates reshit, the beginning, while beth is indeed the beginning of the word beliya'al [בליעל].

units.la: Deus hominem Creaturus inquit נעשה ארם Faciamus hominem; circa quem locum & prisci & veteres Iudæi ex iusta Dei excæcatione varie errarunt.
units.tr: When God was about to create man, he said: Na'aseh adam [נעשה ארם], "Let us make man." Concerning this passage both the ancient and the old Jews, through the just blindness of God, have erred in various ways.

units.la: 1. Philo de Opificio Mundi pag. 15. Mysterii S.S. Trinitatis ignarus, quomodo intelligeret verba Dei ita ambiguus hæsit, ut in hæc verba erumperet, Verissimam causam locutionis illius (in numero plurali) Necesse est Deum solum scire.
units.tr: (1) Philo, in De opificio mundi, p. 15, ignorant of the mystery of the Most Holy Trinity, hesitated so uncertainly over how to understand God's words that he burst out in these words: "The truest cause of that manner of speaking (in the plural number) must be known to God alone."

units.la: 2. Quidam faciunt נעשה praeteritum passivum tertiae personae, non futurum activum primae, ac insuper fingunt בצלמו esse verbum Mosis, hoc sensu: Creatus est homo ad imaginem nostram, nempe humanam. Quam detorsionem merito Aben Esra לב חסר פירוש Explicationem hominis fatui vocat.
units.tr: (2) Some make na'aseh a passive past tense of the third person, not an active future of the first person, and moreover they invent that betsalmo is a word of Moses, in this sense: "Man was created in our image", namely the human image. Ibn Ezra calls this distortion, rightly, lev chaser perush [לב חסר פירוש], an explanation of a foolish man.

units.la: 3. Saadias facit Deum loquentem על מנהג מלכים Iuxta consuetudinem regum. Cuius expositionem mendacii arguit Aben Esra.
units.tr: (3) Saadia makes God speak al minhag melakhim, according to the custom of kings. Ibn Ezra proves this explanation to be false.

units.la: 4. Ioseph Kimchi, teste Abrabanele, verbum faciamus retulit tum ad Deum, qui insudit animam rationalem, tum ad terram à qua est corpus, & corporeae eius facultates. Haec Sententia etiam est acutissimi Maymonidis.
units.tr: (4) Joseph Kimchi, according to Abarbanel's report, referred the words "Let us make" both to God, who infused the rational soul, and to the earth from which the body is, and its bodily faculties. This opinion is also that of the most acute Maimonides.

units.la: 5. R. Iochanan in Gemar. Sanhed. cap.4.f.11. existimat Deum hic nihil fecisse אלא אם נטיל בסוד של מעלה Nisi habito consilio cum familia superna. Id est, interprete Maymonide, nisi inspexerit mundum intelligentiarum.
units.tr: (5) R. Yochanan, in the Gemara of Sanhedrin, ch. 4, f. 11, thinks that God did nothing here ela im natal be-sod shel ma'alah [אלא אם נטיל בסוד של מעלה], except having taken counsel with the heavenly family. That is, as Maimonides explains, except that he looked at the world of intelligences.

units.la: 6. Aben Esrae sententia est, Deum haec verba ad Angelos dixisse, & eos in societatem operis fuisse accitos. Quasi Deus dicere voluisset, venite faciamus hominem, terra & aqua quae occupata sunt ad germina producenda, non hominem facient, sed nos in eo producendo occupabimur.
units.tr: (6) The opinion of Ibn Ezra is that God spoke these words to the angels, and that they were summoned to share in the work. As if God wished to say: "Come, let us make man; the earth and water, which are busy producing seeds, will not make man, but we shall be occupied in producing him."

units.la: Fecit Deus hominem התחתוני מן ex Inferioribus, והעליוני מן & Superioribus, corpus ex inserioribus, animam ex superioribus. Iarchius, Genef.n.7. Quoad Imaginem, secundum quam Deus hominem creavit, Iarchius & Lipmannus in Nizachon, illam interpretantur Ideam, quam de homine expresserat Deus; verba Iarchii sunt כצלמו ברפוס שלן Ad imaginem nostram, id est, ad typum qui est in nobis. Sic autem Deus de homine non plus dixisset, quàm dici potuit de qualibet creatura: nihil enim Deus fecit quod non ad ideam in intellectu suo existentem expressit. Maym.in More Nev.lib.i.c.i.censet hominem ad imaginem & similitudinem Dei conditum מפני השכל אלהי המכורך בו Propter intellectum divinum qui ipsi inest. Sed hac ratione etiam impii imaginem Dei gestarent, cùm etiam sint praediti intelligendi facultate. Ex Midrasch Tillim & Vaijkra Rabba citat quosdam Raymundus Martinus in pug.fid. p.3. Dist.2.c.2. quorum sententia fuit animam hominis esse imaginem Dei, Quia implet corpus ut Deus mundum, nec edit, quia unica est in corpore sicuti Deus in mundo &c. Videt & non videtur, non dormit, nec locum eius quisquam novit.
units.tr: God made man: the lower part mi-ha-tachtonim [מן התחתוני] from the inferiors, and the upper part mi-ha-elyonim [והעליוני מן] from the superiors: the body from the inferiors, the soul from the superiors. Yarchi, on Genesis, n. 7. As to the image, according to which God created man, Yarchi and Lipmann in the Nizzachon interpret it as the idea which God had formed of man; Yarchi's words are ke-tsalmo [כצלמו] "according to our image", i.e. "according to the type which is in us". But in that case God would have said no more of man than could be said of any creature, for God made nothing that he did not form according to an idea existing in his intellect. Maimonides, in More Nevukhim, bk. 1, ch. 1, holds that man was made in the image and likeness of God mi-pnei ha-sekhel ha-elohi ha-mekhurakh bo [מפני השכל אלהי המכורך בו], because of the divine intellect that is joined to him. But by this reasoning the impious too would bear the image of God, since they also are endowed with the faculty of understanding. Raymundus Martinus, in Pugio fidei, p. 3, dist. 2, ch. 2, cites from the Midrash Tillim and Vayikra Rabba certain writers whose opinion was that the soul of man is the image of God, "because it fills the body as God fills the world, and does not eat, because it is one in the body as God is in the world, etc. It sees and is not seen, it does not sleep, and no one knows its place."

units.la: CREDITUM omne dubium est: forte venit, forte non venit (eius solutio) & si venit solutio pecuniae malae sunt; (i.e. malis pecuniis solvitur) Pesach sol. 113. 1. Sunt qui non solvunt quod debent nisi Danista ipsis dentes confringat. Bemid.Rab. sol.228.1.
units.tr: Every loan is doubtful: perhaps it will come back, perhaps it will not (its solution). And if it comes back, the solution is with bad money (that is, it is paid with bad money). Pesachim, p. 113, sec. 1. There are those who do not pay what they owe unless the creditor breaks their teeth. Bemidbar Rabba, p. 228, sec. 1.

units.la: כרת Karath Exterminium. Exscindetur anima eius, in Sacra Scriptura designat secundum R. Salomonem, morietur Solitarius sine liberis, ante sexagesimum vita annum. Qui infra moritur, ex hac poena est, ob specialia peccata; qui supra, ex benedictione id habet, proinde qui illum attigerunt annum, solebant convivium Eucharisticum instituere, quod non sunt ante tempus excisi. Schabbat 57.1. Tosapht. Moed Katon 28.1. R.D. Kimchi Esai.38.10. Reus המיתה mortem simplicem solus patitur; הכרת Exterminium vero ipse & semen eius. Fagius Exod.12.n.15. Amama Antibarb.954. Cl.Peaukoky Porta Mosis.n.158. De כרת vid. Aben Ffram ad Exod. xii.15. Ephodæus ad More Nebhocim p.3. c.41. Abarbenel ad Num.xv.22. Maymon Hal. התשובה c.8 qui credit כרת totius hominis, secundum corpus & animam, extinctionem denotare. §. Denotat itaque כרת non excisionem à coetu publico per censuram Ecclesiasticam, sed excisionem per vindictam divinam; aliquando tamen quando reum ad excisionem adiudicant, ipsum iudicio Dei tradunt coniunctâ censurâ & poenâ à Synedrio, aliquando non. De mera traditione ad iudicium Dei, absque ulla poena à Synedrio inflicta, loquuntur illa in Hierof.Bava Kama sol. 5.2. פשור כדיני ארם רחייב גדיני שמים Absolutus est Iudicio hominum at reus Iudicio cœli (Dei.) De Iudicio vero Dei & Synedrii coniunctis sonant hæc ibid. Si tenetur ad restitutionem rei factus à Synedrio, non ignoscit ei cœlum (Deus) usquedum solverit. At in Bab.Megillah sol.7. 2. qui poenam à Synedrio indictam passus est, exsolvitur ab excisione: quando dicunt; Omnes excisionis rei, cum vapulaverint, absolvuntur ab excisione sua: sicut dicitur, Et vilis sit frater tuus in conspectu tuo Cum vapulaverit,Ec. e est frater tuus.
units.tr: Karet [כרת], extermination: "that soul shall be cut off" (exscindetur anima eius) in Holy Scripture, according to R. Solomon, designates "he shall die childless and solitary, before the sixtieth year of life". He who dies before that age suffers this punishment because of special sins; he who dies after it has it as a blessing, and therefore those who had reached that year used to hold a Eucharistic feast, because they had not been cut off before their time. Shabbat 57, sec. 1; Tosefta, Moed Qatan 28, sec. 1; R. D. Kimchi on Isaiah 38:10. The guilty man alone suffers simple death (mitah), but karet, extermination, falls on himself and his seed. Fagius on Exodus 12, n. 15; Amama, Antibarbarus, p. 954; the Most Illustrious Peaukoky, Porta Mosis, n. 158. On karet see Ibn Ezra on Exodus 12:15; Efodaeus on the More Nebukhim, p. 3, ch. 41; Abarbanel on Numbers 15:22; Maimonides, Hilchot Teshuvah, ch. 8, who believes that karet denotes the extinction of the whole man, body and soul. §. Therefore karet denotes not exclusion from the public assembly by ecclesiastical censure, but exclusion by divine vengeance; sometimes, however, when they adjudge the guilty man to karet, they hand him over to the judgment of God, together with censure and punishment from the Sanhedrin, and sometimes not. The passage in the Jerusalem Talmud, Bava Qamma, p. 5, sec. 2, speaks of a mere handing over to the judgment of God, without any punishment inflicted by the Sanhedrin: "He is absolved by the judgment of men, but the guilty man is held by the judgment of heaven" (of God). But concerning the joint judgment of God and the Sanhedrin the following is said in the same place: "If he who was made by the Sanhedrin liable to restitution does not pay, heaven (God) does not forgive him until he has paid." But in the Babylonian Megillah, p. 7, sec. 2: he who has suffered the punishment inflicted by the Sanhedrin is freed from karet, for they say: "All who are liable to karet, when they have been beaten, are absolved from their karet, as it is said: 'And your brother be vile in your sight' (Deut. 25:3); when he has been beaten, your brother is in your sight."

units.la: Crucis signum vocant שתי וערב tegmen & subflamen. Illo Christianos characterizant & distinguunt. Vid Beehai in lib. כד הקמה sol.xo.i. Ibi enim locum Iscf.66.17. Christianos denotare dicit. ירמוז לשתי וערב של ארום שהם מתקדשי'נו, Indicat CrucemChriftianorum quasanctificant se &c.
units.tr: They call the sign of the cross שתי וערב [shti varev] woof and warp. By this they mark and distinguish Christians. See Beehai in the book כד הקמה [Kad ha-Kemach], sol. xo.i. For there he says that the place Isa. 66.17 denotes Christians: it points to the woof and warp of Edom, which are those who sanctify themselves [ירמוז לשתי וערב של ארום שהם מתקדשים], that is, it indicates the cross of the Christians, by which they sanctify themselves, etc.

units.la: COMBUSTIONIS supplicium vid. de Vrendis. vid. etiam supplicia.
units.tr: The punishment of BURNING: see Burning. See also punishments.

units.la: COLLYBISTÆ vid. in Templo erat Emporium.
units.tr: COLLYBISTAE: see In the Temple there was a marketplace.

units.la: COMA. Permiserunt Abuteli radere Comam, quia vicinus erat regno; id est, quia vivebat circa tempora regni Græcorum, qui crines capitis anterioris rescindunt usque ad aures, è regione frontis totius, & sinebant capillos superiores versus cervicem sparsos & fluxos. Cl. Castell ex Aruch in קומי.
units.tr: COMA. The Abutelites were permitted to shave the hair, because they were neighbours of the kingdom; that is, because they lived around the time of the Greek kingdom, who cut the front hair of the head up to the ears, across the whole brow, and let the upper hair fall loose and spread over the neck. Cl. Castell from Aruch, under קומי.

units.la: §. Qui calvitiem in capite suo facit, capitis sui Angulos tondet, secat se unâ cæsurâ ob defunctum, vapulat. Si secuerit se unâ cæsurâ ob quinos demortuos, aut quinis cæsuris ob unum, ob quamlibet tenetur. Maccot. c. 3.§.5.
units.tr: §. He who makes a bald place on his head, shaves the corners of his head, or cuts himself with one incision for a dead person, is flogged. If he cuts himself with one incision for five dead persons, or with five incisions for one, he is liable for each. Makkoth, ch. 3, §5.

units.la: COMPARERE in festo omnes debent, excepto surdo, stulto, parvulo שומטום genitalibus obturato, Androgyno, mulieribus, servis nondum manumissis, claudo, cæco, ægroto, sene, & qui non potest pedibus ascendere. Qui comparet secundùm Schammæum debet afferre שתי כסף duos nummos argenteos, בחגיגה in festivitate vero unum. Hilleliani contrarium sentiunt. (hagiga c. 1.
units.tr: Everyone must appear at the festival, except the deaf, the fool, the minor, one whose genitals are stopped up, the hermaphrodite, women, slaves not yet freed, the lame, the blind, the sick, the old, and whoever cannot climb on foot. He who appears, according to Shammai, must bring two silver coins, but on the festival itself one. The Hillelites think the opposite. (Hagigah, ch. 1.)

units.la: §. Hanc comparitionem in festo vocant ראית & ipsam festi celebrationem חגיגה. Iudæi nullum habuerunt Calendarium scriptum, sed novilunia & primus dies mensis vel ignibus sublevatis vel missis nuntiis ex Synedrii ordinatione ipsis innotescebat ; Postquam aute[?] familiis dies festi significatus erat, lege ob[?] gabantur omnes tempore statuto Hierosol[?] mas petere, ad festum celebrandum. Comp[?] ritio autem ipsorum facta est in atrio tem[?] die primo festi, & offerebant Sacrificium co[?] paritionis ; afferebant etiam oblationes p[?] Chagiga & oblationes pro gaudio, quas מ[?] שמחה vocarunt. Miraculo certè simile e[?] quòd omnia in laribus domesticis ita reli[?] quere, & quod Hierosolyma pro ta[?] ta multitudine & commeatum & comm[?] da hospitia suppeditare potuerit. Et tam[?] id factum esse refert Abbot R. Nathan cap. 3[?] Decem miracula facta sunt patribus nostris in Sanctuario. Nulla unquam mulier abortum pa[?] est ex nidore carnium Sacrificiorum ; Nullus u[?] quam impegit in Hierosolyma; Nullus unquar[?] lapsus est Hierosolyma; Nullus unquam erat ab[?] tus Hierosolymis; Nullus unquam dixit adsocia[?] suum non inveni ignem ad affandum meum P[?] scha ; Aut quod nullum lectum repereri[?] aut quod ipsius hospitium ipsi nimis ang[?] stum sit.
units.tr: This appearance at the festival they call re'iyah, and the celebration of the festival itself hagigah. The Jews had no written calendar; but the new moons and the first day of the month were made known to them, either by raised fires or by messengers sent by the decree of the Sanhedrin. After the day of the festival had been signified to the families, all were obliged by law to seek Jerusalem at the appointed time to celebrate the feast. Their appearance was made in the court of the Temple on the first day of the feast, and they offered the sacrifice of appearance; they also brought the offerings for the Hagigah and the offerings for joy, which they called chagigat simchah. Surely a miracle much like this took place, that they could leave everything thus in their household shrines, and that Jerusalem could supply lodging, provisions and accommodation for so great a multitude. And R. Nathan, in his Abot, ch. 3, reports that this happened: Ten miracles were done for our fathers in the Sanctuary. No woman ever miscarried from the smell of the flesh of the sacrifices; no fly was ever seen in Jerusalem; no one ever suffered a discharge in Jerusalem; no one ever had to say that his lodging was too cramped; no one ever said to his neighbour that he could not find room to lodge in Jerusalem. Or that no bed was found wanting, or that his lodging was too narrow for him.

units.la: חומש הפקודים Chumasch happekudim c[?]
units.tr: The Book of Numbers (Chumash happekudim)

units.la: currit in Ioma c. 7. & S[?] tah cap. 7. Quid proprie significaret diu a[?] xius haesi ; tandem reperi illud denotare brum Numerorum, & in locis citatis sumi p[?] illa benedictione quam faciebat Summus S[?] cerdos Hebraicè in die expiationis ; inc[?] pit autem illa lectio Numero. 29. 7. & Lev[?] tic.16. Apud Maymon. in Tamid cap. 8.sum[?] t tur etiam pro Levitico.
units.tr: It occurs in Yoma, ch. 7, and Sotah, ch. 7. I long hesitated over what this properly signified; at last I found that it denotes the Book of Numbers, and that in the passages cited it is taken for that blessing which the High Priest pronounced in Hebrew on the Day of Atonement; that reading begins at Num. 29.7 and Lev. 16. In Maimonides, in Tamid, ch. 8, it is also taken for Leviticus.

units.la: CONCLAVIA quatuor habebat atrium mulierum, in quatuor suis angulis posita. Ad ortum B. umalem erat atrium Naziræorum, in quo Naziræi Eucharistias suas coquebant, & se tondebant. Ad ortum æstivum erat לשכת בית עצים conclave lignorum, ubi Sacerdotes immundi ligna scrutabantur, an immunia essent à vermibus. Ad occasum æstivum erat conclave leprosorum; Ad occasum Brumalem Conclave vini atque olei. Middot. cap.2. §.5. Maym. B. Habech. c.5.
units.tr: CHAMBERS. The court of the women had four, placed at its four corners. On the north side was the court of the Nazirites, in which the Nazirites cooked their peace offerings and shaved themselves. On the east-summer side was the chamber of the wood-house (לשכת בית עצים), where the priests who were unclean inspected the wood, to see whether it was free from worms. On the west-summer side was the chamber of the lepers; on the west-winter side the chamber of wine and oil. Middoth, ch. 2, §5. Maimonides, Beth ha-Behirah, ch. 5.

units.la: §. Sex conclavia erant in atrio Israelis, à parte Australi Conclave ligni, (in quo ligna iam à vermibus perscrutata recondebantur) Conclave Scaturiginis, Conclave Gazit. In parte Aquilonari Conclave Salis, Conclav: הפרוה, Et Conclave lavantium. Middot c.5. §.3.
units.tr: §. There were six chambers in the court of Israel: on the south side the chamber of wood (in which the wood already inspected for worms was stored), the chamber of the spring, and the chamber of Gazith. On the north side the chamber of salt, the chamber of the hafruah (הפרוה), and the chamber of the washers. Middoth, ch. 5, §3.

units.la: §. Conclave Gazit לשכת הגזית erat כמין בסיליקי גדולה Instar Basilicæ magna, dimidia pars eius erat in loco Sancto, & altera dimidia in prophano; duoque habuit ostia, quorum unum versus Sanctum, alterum versus profanum aperiebatur, unum nempe in atrio, alterum in antemurali. Sedit Synedrium non in atrii parte; (nam in atrio non nisi Regibus ex familia Davidis sedere licuit,) sed in ea parte conclavis Gazit, quæ in חיל antemurali erat. Ioma folio vigesimo quinto. 1. In hoc conclavi sedebat Synedrii præses à parte occidentali. Ibid. Abh Beth Din (vide Synedrium). à dextra eius, atque utrinque in hemicyclo seniores. Maymon. in Sanhed. c.1. In hoc conclavi synedrium etiam de Sacerdotibus, qui propter aliquam labem accusati erant, iudicabat. Ioma sol. 19. 1. Existimavit olim V. C. Conft. l'Empereur in notis ad Middot p. 119. Iudam Iscarioten nummos proditionis, postquam ipsum sceleris poenituisset, & Patres Conscripti illos resumere renuerant in huius conclavis solum proiecisse; Sed an Synedrium tunc temporis in Gazith sederit, decidimus apud Synedrium.
units.tr: §. The chamber of Gazith (לשכת הגזית) was like a great basilica; half of it was in the holy place and the other half in the profane; it had two doors, one opening towards the holy, the other towards the profane, namely one into the court and the other into the forecourt. The Sanhedrin did not sit in the part of the court (for in the court it was lawful for none but kings of the house of David to sit), but in that part of the chamber of Gazith which was in the forecourt (חיל). Yoma, folio 25.1. In this chamber the president of the Sanhedrin sat on the west side. Ibid. The Av Beth Din (see Sanhedrin) sat on his right, and on either side in the semicircle the elders. Maimonides, in Sanhedrin, ch. 1. In this chamber the Sanhedrin also judged priests who had been accused of some stain. Yoma, fol. 19.1. The learned Constantin l'Empereur, in his notes on Middoth, p. 119, once thought that Judas Iscariot had cast down the money of betrayal in this chamber alone, after he repented of his crime, and the conscript fathers refused to take it back. But whether the Sanhedrin then sat in Gazith, we settle under Sanhedrin.

units.la: §. Conclave הגולה scaturiginis proximum fuit תש Conclavi Gazit ab Oriente; in eo autem erat puteus & trochlæa, unde aquas suppeditabant toti atrio Middot c.5. Iom. sol.19.
units.tr: §. The chamber of the spring (לשכת הגולה) lay next to the chamber of Gazith on the east; in it was a well and a pulley, from which they supplied water to the whole court. Middoth, ch. 5; Yoma, fol. 19.

units.la: §. In Conclavi lavantium lavabant victimarum intestina, in Conclavi הפרוה condiebant victimarum pelles. Huius nomenclationis rationem vid. Bab. Ioma sol 35.1. In tecto eius erat Balneum pro Sacerdote Magno in die expiationis. Middot c.5.2.
units.tr: §. In the chamber of the washers they washed the entrails of the victims; in the chamber of the hafruah they salted the skins of the victims. For the reason for this name see Babylonian Talmud, Yoma, fol. 35.1. On its roof was a bath for the High Priest on the Day of Atonement. Middoth, ch. 5, §2.

units.la: §. Conclave פרהדרין erat supra conclave lignorum in atrio Israelis, alias etiam vocatur לשכת בולוטי Camera Consiliariorum; quia in ea Sacerdotes de negotiis Templi consultabant. Summus Sacerdos etiam in illa degebat septem diebus ante diem expiationis. Ioma c.1. Middot c.5. de hoc conclavi haec legimus in Bab. Ioma sol.8.2. Num fuit conclave פרהדרין προβουλιον? Nonne conclave בולוטי Βουλευτῶν? Primo vocabatur לשכת בולוטי (conclave Βουλευτῶν, At cum Pontificatus emeretur pecuniâ, annuatimque mutamutaretur הללו כפרהדרין Sicut annuatim mutantur πρόεδροι Regis, exinde vocabatur לשכת פרהדרין Conclave προέδριον. Gloss. dicit בולוטי לשון שרים βασιλεῖς denotat principes. Aruch verò in ea sententia est, בולוטי esse יון לשון vocem Graecam, & consiliarium denotare. Et certè ibi collocamus בית דין של כוהני Consilium Sacerdotum, cui praesidebat Summus Sacerdos Chetubb.cap.1. Nota hic ἐνγμένα βασιλεῖ apud Marcum xv. 43. membrum forsan huius Senatus fuisse, nam cur alias ita vocatus fuisset, vix ulla apparet ratio.
units.tr: §. The chamber of the Parhedrin was above the chamber of wood in the court of Israel. It was also called the chamber of the Bulutin (לשכת בולוטי), the council chamber, because in it the priests consulted about the affairs of the Temple. The High Priest also lived in it for seven days before the Day of Atonement. Yoma, ch. 1; Middoth, ch. 5. We read of this chamber in the Babylonian Talmud, Yoma, fol. 8.2. Was the chamber of Parhedrin the proedrion? Was not the chamber of Bulutin the boulewtwn? At first it was called the chamber of Bulutin (the chamber of the council), but since the priesthood was bought with money and changed each year, as the presidents of the king are changed each year, it was then called the chamber of Parhedrin, the proedrion chamber. The Gloss says that Bulutin in the language of the princes (βασιλεῖς) denotes princes. Aruch, however, holds that Bulutin is a Greek word and denotes a counsellor. And certainly there we place the council of the priests, over which the High Priest presided. Ketubot, ch. 1. Note here that the one who was joined to the king in Mark 15.43 was perhaps a member of this senate, for there is hardly any reason why he would otherwise have been so called.

units.la: §. Camera sive Conclave ניצוץ est locus ubi Levitae excubias agunt Middot c. 1 §. 3. De Beth Mokad vid. suo 1. in B. In Conclavi Beth Mokad erant quatuor conclavia. 1. Conclave agnorum לשכת טלאים ubi illi ad usum altaris reservabantur. 2. Conclave panum propositionis. 3. Conclave ubi repositi sunt lapides altaris ab Asmonaeis, cum Reges Graeciae altare prophanarant. 4. Conclave quo in Balneum descendebatur. Maym.Bet.Habech.c.5.
units.tr: §. The chamber or hall of the nitzotz (ניצוץ) is the place where the Levites keep watch. Middoth, ch. 1, §3. On Beth Mokad see my note under B. In the chamber of Beth Mokad there were four chambers: 1. The chamber of the lambs (לשכת טלאים), where those set aside for the use of the altar were kept. 2. The chamber of the showbread. 3. The chamber where the stones of the altar were stored, which the Hasmoneans had removed when the kings of Greece had profaned the altar. 4. The chamber by which one went down to the bath. Maimonides, Beth ha-Behirah, ch. 5.

units.la: §. Conclavia erant infra atrium Israelitarum, quae aperta erant versus atrium mulierum, in quae Levitae citharas & nablia collocabant, cum reliquis instrumentis Musicis. Middot c. 2.6.
units.tr: §. There were chambers beneath the court of the Israelites, which were open towards the court of the women, in which the Levites placed their harps and psalteries, with the other musical instruments. Middoth, ch. 2, §6.

units.la: CONCUPISCENTIA יצר הרע similis est in principio, filo aranea, in fine ubi assenseris, similis est denso funi plaustri. Succah sol. 52. 1. Alius dixit, à principio venit ut viator, deinde הוא נעשה בעל הבית fit herus domesticus. Vid. Berefch.Rabba sect.22. vid. peccatum orig. Quis est fortis ? הכובש את יצרו qui subigit concupiscentiam suam. Avot. c.4. De ער יצר הרע vid. Cl. Buxt. L.Tal.p.973.
units.tr: Concupiscence [יצר הרע] is at first like a spider's thread, but at the end, once you have yielded to it, it is like the thick cable of a wagon. Sukkah fol. 52.1. Another said: at first it comes like a passing traveller, and then "it becomes the master of the house." See Bereshit Rabba sect. 22; see original sin. Who is strong? "He who subdues his concupiscence" [הכובש את יצרו]. Avot c. 4. On the evil inclination see Cl. Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 973.

units.la: CONCUBINÆ. פלגשים quas veteres Iudæi habuerunt, erant uxores servæ absque scripto dotali, aut sponsalibus ducta, quarum liberi legatis tantùm non autem hæreditate fruebantur; Sanhed 21.1: פלגש dicitur; quasi אשה ופלג, uxor divisa, dimidiata.
units.tr: CONCUBINES. The concubines [פלגשים] whom the ancient Jews had were servant-wives, taken without a written dowry contract or betrothal. Their children enjoyed only bequests, not inheritance. Sanhedrin 21.1: the word פלגש is said to be as if from אשה ופלג, a wife divided, half a wife.

units.la: §. R. Moses Nachmanides in suo Commentario in leg. Gen.25.6. absolutè concubinis neque desponsationem, neque literas dotis permittit, & citata à nobis 7ũ Sanhedrin verba aliter explicat, sed Abarbanel in cap.19. Iudicum Nachmanidem prolixè refellit, & tandem concludit hanc Talmudis veram esse lectionem. אשה בקרושין וכתובה Vxor ducitur cum desponsatione, & instrumento dotali פלגש בקרושין ובלא כתובה Concubina cum desponsatione absq; instrumento dotali. Nam, inquit, quomodo potuisent Sapientes nostri credere, Davidem habuisse concubinas non desponsatas, & quæ nullam rationem uxorum habuerint? Si concubinæ non desponsatæ fuissent, Israelitis non solùm fuissent illicitæ, sed omnes liberi illarum fuissent spurii. Nota tamen hic quod Maymonides dicit cap. 4. Halac. Melach. Licet Regi ducere uxores & concubinas absque instrumento dotali & sponsalibus, אלא ביחוד כלבד קנה אותן, ונותרת וכותרת nam coniunctione sola illas acquirit & sibi licitas facit. אבל ההדיוט אסור בפילגש אלא באמה העבריה בלבד אחר ייעוד Homo privatus autem primò non potest concubinam sumere nisi sit ancilla Hebraa, & deinde semper desponsationem adhibere debet.
units.tr: R. Moses Nachmanides, in his commentary on Genesis 25.6, absolutely permits concubines neither betrothal nor a dowry document, and he explains differently the words of the Sanhedrin tractate that we have cited. But Abarbanel, on Judges ch. 19, refutes Nachmanides at length and finally concludes that this is the true reading of the Talmud: "A wife is taken with betrothal and a dowry document; a concubine with betrothal but without a dowry document." For, he says, how could our Sages believe that David had concubines who were not betrothed and who had no standing as wives? If the concubines had not been betrothed, they would not only have been forbidden to Israelites, but all their children would have been bastards. Note here, however, that Maimonides says in ch. 4 of Hilchot Melachim: "A king may take wives and concubines without a dowry document and betrothal, for by intercourse alone he acquires them and makes them lawful to himself. But a private man may take a concubine only if she is a Hebrew maidservant, and he must always add betrothal."

units.la: §. Licet etiam Regi omnes suas concubinas ad officia necessaria in Palatio suo cogere, & ex una facere coquam, ex altera aromatricem &c. Maym. l.m.c.
units.tr: The king may also compel all his concubines to necessary services in his palace, making one a cook, another a perfumer, and so on. Maimonides, loc. cit.

units.la: Confessio decimarum מעשר נידוי poterat fieri in omni lingua. Sotah c. 7. 1. Hac dici possunt בכל לשון in omnia lingua, Sectio Sota Confessio decima,lectio Schemaa &c.
units.tr: The confession of tithes [מעשר נידוי] could be made in every language. Sotah c. 7.1. These things can be said in any language: the section of Sotah, the confession of tithe, the reading of the Shema, and so on.

units.la: §. Exstat confessio decimarum Deut. xxvi. 13. Tunc dices coram Iehova Deo tuo, sustuli quod sanctum est in domo mea. Debebat Israelita, ut indigetat Glossa, confessionem illam edere, si duo anni effluxerant, à quibus decimas Hierosolymas non advexit. Talis decimatio deinde vocatur מעשר שני בעשר Decima secunda, quasi מעשר של שתי שנים decima duorum annorum. Quid autem proprie מעשר שני fit vid. Decima.
units.tr: The confession of tithes is found in Deuteronomy 26.13: "Then you shall say before the LORD your God, I have brought away what is holy out of my house." An Israelite, as the Gloss points out, had to make that confession if two years had passed since he had last brought tithes up to Jerusalem. Such a tithe is then called the second tithe [מעשר שני], as if it were the tithe of two years. For what the second tithe is exactly, see Decima.

units.la: ne Confidas tibi usque ad diem mortis tuae. Pirke avot c. 2. אל תאמן עצמך בשלוה גופך Ne confidas in incolumitate corporis tui. Quot enim contulerunt se in lectum, qui non surrexerunt? quot cubitum iverunt sani, & surrexerunt agri? Orchot chayim.
units.tr: "Do not trust yourself until the day of your death." Pirke Avot c. 2: "Do not trust yourself in the soundness of your body" [אל תאמן עצמך בשלוה גופך]. For how many have lain down in bed and not risen again? How many have gone to sleep in health and risen sick? Orchot Chayim.

units.la: Convivium in quo non est sal, non est convivium. Beracot sol.441.1. Ad convivia divites invitant pauperes, & viatores. Ibid. sol.43.1. Nullum convivium est sine moleitia. Schabbat sol.153.1. Qui recte servit tria epula in Sabbatho, liberatur à tribus poenis; à doloribus Messiae, à judicio Gehenna, à bello Gog &
units.tr: A feast at which there is no salt is not a feast. Berachot fol. 44.1. At feasts the rich invite the poor and travellers. Ibid. fol. 43.1. No feast is without some trouble. Shabbat fol. 153.1. Whoever duly eats three meals on the Sabbath is freed from three punishments: from the pangs of the Messiah, from the judgement of Gehenna, and from the war of Gog and

units.la: Magog. Ibid. sol.118.1. Machsos Hispan. 11. 137. De Convivio multa habet Maymon in Hal.Beracot c.7. Summa hæc est.Postquam locum convivii ingressi sunt, honoratior ex illis manus omnium primus lavat, & deinde etiam primo loco accumbit ( de ritu hoc vide Accumbendi ritus.) Pater familias super cibum benedicit, יצא בוצע ואח"כ & deinde dissindit. Non debet scissionem (panis) incipere, nisi postquam sal allatum fuerit cum uniuscuiusq; edulio. Frusta non debet nimis parva facere, ne appareat כצר עין quasi avarus esset, nec nimis magna, פני שנראה כרעבתן ne videatur ipsos pro helluonibus sumere.
units.tr: Magog. Ibid. fol. 118.1. Machsor Hispan. 11. 137. Maimonides has much on feasting in Hilchot Berachot ch. 7. The sum is this. After they have entered the place of the feast, the most honoured of them first washes the hands of all, and then also reclines first at table (on this custom see the entry on the ritual of reclining). The head of the household blesses over the food, then breaks the bread [יצא בוצע ואח"כ], and only then distributes it. He must not begin breaking the bread until salt has been brought with each dish. He must not make the pieces too small, lest he appear stingy [כצר עין], nor too large, lest he seem to be taken for a glutton [כרעבתן].

units.la: Sabbatho vero licet magnum fructum abscindere : ואינו בוצע אלא ממקום שכשל יפה non autem abscindere debet nisi quod elegantèr coltum est. Qui scindit panem, extendit manum suam primus in patinam. (vid. Gittin sol. 59. 2. Beracot sol.47.1.) nec licet gustare accumbentibus, nisi post illum qui benedixit. Si scissor vult honoris causâ permittere ut alius ante se manum cibo admoveat, id facere poterit. שנים מתתיין זה לוה בקערה שלשה אין מתתיין Duo se invicem in patina exspectant, sed non tres. Non confabulantur inter edendum שלא יבואו לידי סכנת ne in periculum (obstructionis asperæ arteriæ) incidant : Quare etiam si vinum ipsis inter edendum propinatur, unusquisq; apud semetipsum benedicit, ne loquendo in periculum incidat. Edentem autem non aspiciunt intentè, quasi ipsius bolas supputarent, ne ipsum pudore afficiant. Qui accumbentibus inservit, non debet cum ipsis comedere, ודך רחמנות ליתן לתוך פיו מכל תבשיל ותבשיל כדי לישב דעתו benevolentia tamen est ipsi ex omni edulio aliquid ingerere, ad sedandum appetitum eius. Licet bibere vinum per fistulas; moris etiam est in diebus æstivis herbas, fructusque convivis apponere, non autem in diebus pluviosis, מפני שבמאסין quia tunc hoc tædiosum esset. Hospitibus non licet quicquam puerulis aut aliis de cibis appositis dare שמא יתב יויש בעל הסעוד ne Dominus convivii pudore afficiatur: forsan enim non paravit, ut semper alia suppeditare posset. In summa, כל המביאין לידי בושה לבעל הסעודה אסורין omnia illicita sunt quæ Dominum convivii aliquo modo pudore afficere possent. In conviviis usu habuerunt, psalmos & rythmos secundùm literas Alphabeti scriptos, ad exhilarandos hospites recitare & cantare. Medrasch Ruth cap. 1.13. Convivio peracto Deo gratias agunt, & removent mensam, manusque lavant: nullis cæremoniis observatis, שאין מכבדין כידי מווהמו nam manibus inquinatis non cæremoniatur. (venia verbo Barbaro.) Ita etiam nullas complimentorum ambages faciunt in pontibus, aut stratis, sed solùm in introitu coram porta cui מווה affigi potest. Lotione manuum peracta infertur המוגבר thuribulum, & qui super cibos benedixit etiam super thuribulum benedicit, Omnibus respondentibus Amen. Tandem repletur poculum, quartale continens, & quod vocant כוס הברכה poculum benedictionis, & asseruntur aromata, benedictioneque facta super unumquodque, poculum exhauritur, & ita convivium claudโitur. Plura vid. Maffec.Berac. c.8.1. & in toto hoc Maymon. tract.
units.tr: On the Sabbath, however, one may cut off a large piece, but he may break only from the part that has been nicely baked. He who breaks the bread stretches out his hand first over the dish (see Gittin fol. 59.2; Berachot fol. 47.1). Nor may those reclining taste anything until after the one who blessed. If the one breaking wishes, out of respect, to allow another to put his hand to the food before himself, he may do so. "Two may wait for each other over the dish, but not three." They do not talk while eating, so that they do not fall into danger (of obstruction of the windpipe); therefore even if wine is handed round during the meal, each one blesses for himself, lest by speaking he fall into danger. They do not look intently at the one eating, as if counting his mouthfuls, so as not to shame him. One who serves those reclining must not eat with them, but out of kindness it is fitting to put a little of every dish into his mouth, to calm his appetite. It is allowed to drink wine through tubes. It is also customary in summer to set herbs and fruits before the guests, but not on rainy days, because then it would be tedious. Guests may not give anything from the dishes set out to small children or others, lest the host of the feast be shamed: perhaps he has not prepared enough to be able to supply more. In sum, everything that might in any way bring shame upon the host of the feast is forbidden. At feasts they were accustomed to recite and sing psalms and verses composed according to the letters of the alphabet, to cheer the guests. Midrash Ruth ch. 1.13. When the feast is over, they give thanks to God, remove the table, and wash their hands; no ceremonies are observed, for one does not perform ceremonies with unclean hands (pardon the barbarous word). Likewise they make no long compliments on bridges or couches, but only at the entrance, before the door, where the mezuzah may be fixed. When the washing of hands is done, the censer [המוגבר] is brought in, and he who blessed over the food also blesses over the censer, all answering Amen. Finally the cup, holding a quart, which they call "the cup of blessing" [כוס הברכה], is filled, and spices are brought in; a blessing is said over each, the cup is drained, and so the feast is closed. For more, see Maffec. Berac. c. 8.1 and Maimonides throughout that tractate.

units.la: Consessus nobiliores fuerunt in Lydda sub R. Eleasare; sub Rabban Iochanan Ben Saccai in לבוד חיל. In פיעין sub R. Iofua. In Iabhne sub R. Gamaliele; in Bene Barak sub R. Akiba. Romæ, præfide R. Mathia. In Sicni Rectore R. Chananía Ben Teradion. In Zipporin Rectore R. Iofe. In Nisibin, Rectore Iudah Ben Bethira. In Pompeditha RectoreR. Iosua; in Beth Schaarim, Rectore Rabbi. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 32. 2. Quæ omnia quidem בית דין vocantur, sed in quibusdam ex illis locis simplices Scholæ fuerunt, non autem tales Senatus qualis Majestuosus ille in conclavi Gazit, qui ut præstantissimus his appenditur coronidis loco. vid. Synedria.
units.tr: The more noble assemblies were at Lydda under R. Eleazar; under Rabban Johanan ben Zakkai at Lebud Chayil [לבוד חיל]; at Pe'in under R. Joshua; at Jabneh under R. Gamaliel; at Bene Berak under R. Akiba. At Rome, presided over by R. Mathia. At Sicni, the rector was R. Hananiah ben Teradion. At Zippori, the rector was R. Jose. At Nisibis, the rector was Judah ben Bethira. At Pumbedita, the rector was R. Joshua; at Beth Shearim, the rector was Rabbi. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 32.2. All of these are indeed called "house of judgement" [בית דין], but in some of those places they were simply schools, not such a Senate as that majestic one in the chamber Gazit, which is set down as the most excellent of all and, as it were, the crown of the rest. See Synedria.

units.la: Contractuum instrumentis inscribebatur à iudicibus ad eorum confirmationem, שטרות &c. Contractus prodiit in confpectum nostrum testificantibus N. & N. de subsignatione manuum suarum; unde confirmamus & stabilimus eum. Metzia 7. 2. vid. Cl. Castellum in pp.
units.tr: Contracts: the judges wrote out the documents of contract to confirm them: "shetarot" [שטרות], etc. "The contract has come before us, with N. and N. testifying to the signing of their hands; therefore we confirm and establish it." Metzia 7.2. See the distinguished Castellus in pp.

units.la: Coriarius. Talis fuit Iudas Ifcariot; vid. f. 1. Væ illi cuius opificium coriarium est. Kiddufchin fol.82.2. Et proinde ex Coriariis nullus poterat Rex fieri; Maymon. Hal. Melachim c.1. & Kiddufchin 1. m. c. Cadavera, sepulchra, officinas coriariorum, quinquaginta cubitos ab urbe removent, neque illam collocant nisi versus orientem urbis. Bava Batra Batra sol.23.1. in Mifchna. Coriariorum ossicinam nemo ingredi debuit tempore precum. Schabbat cap.1. in Mifchna.
units.tr: Tanner. Judas Iscariot was of this kind; see f. 1. Woe to him whose trade is tanning. Kiddufchin fol. 82.2. For this reason no tanner could be made king: Maymon. Hal. Melachim c.1, and Kiddufchin 1 m. c. "They remove corpses, graves and tanners' workshops fifty cubits from the city, and they place them only towards the east of the city." Bava Batra Batra fol. 23.1, in the Mifchna. No one ought to enter a tanner's workshop at the time of prayer. Schabbat cap. 1, in the Mifchna.

units.la: de CORONA triplici sibi data gloriantur Rabbini; Altaris, Mensæ, & Arcæ. Altaris id est Sacerdotii, quam obtinuit Aharon : Mensæ id est regni, quam consecutus est David; nam Reges solent in mensa divitias & maiestatem suam ostentare. Arcæ id est legis divinæ, quæ reposita fuit in arca, ut peterent eam omnes. Ex legis autem cognitione oritur sapientia, & corona sapientiæ maior est coronâ regni. Secundùm illud Proverb. 8. 15. Per me (sapientiam) reges regnant. Bab.Ioma sol.72.2. Maym. Hal.Talmud thorah cap.3.
units.tr: The Rabbis boast of a threefold crown given to them: of the altar, of the table and of the ark. The crown of the altar is that of the priesthood, which Aaron obtained; the crown of the table is that of the kingdom, which David attained, for kings are accustomed to display their riches and majesty at the table; the crown of the ark is that of the divine law, which was placed in the ark so that all might seek it. Wisdom arises from knowledge of the law, and the crown of wisdom is greater than the crown of kingdom. According to Proverb. 8.15, By me (wisdom) kings reign. Bab.Ioma fol. 72.2. Maym. Hal.Talmud thorah cap. 3.

units.la: de CORREPTIONE fratris peccantis. Vid. Offensio.
units.tr: On the REBUKE of a sinning brother. See Offensio.

units.la: מכזיב vel כזיב Macfith vel Chefith est ille locus, qui terræ Ifraeliticæ limen fac t & quem ultimò occuparunt Iudæi ex captivitate Babylonica redeuntes. Hoc nomine etiam exprimitur ille locus, quem ultimò occuparunt Israelitæ ex Ægypto ascendentes. Maymon dicit illa loca libera esse à Demai, quia quasi extra terram Israeliticam existere exiftimantur. In Demai c.1.3. vide Scheviit 6.1. Hierof. Avoda Zarah 40.1.
units.tr: מכזיב or כזיב [Machsiv or Kezib], Macfith or Chefith, is the place which forms the threshold of the Israelite land, and which the Jews returning from the Babylonian captivity occupied last. By this name is also designated the place which the Israelites occupied last when they came up out of Egypt. Maymon says these places are free from Demai, because they are considered to lie outside the Israelite land. On Demai c. 1.3 see Scheviit 6.1. Hierof. Avoda Zarah 40.1.

units.la: CUCURBITARUM varia genera habuerunt in terra Israelitica, ut videre est ex versu secundo Kilaim cap.1. Una species erat דלעת הרמוצה cucurbita tessellata : de cuius gustu Maymonides refert, illum ita amarum & ingratum suisse, ut comedi non potuerit, nisi prius cucurbita obtecta fuerit cinere calenti, à quo cü aliquæ eius partes urebantur, illa deinde רמוצה vocabatur. Ein geflekelter Kürbiß.
units.tr: There were various kinds of gourds in the land of Israel, as can be seen from the second verse of Kilaim cap. 1. One kind was דלעת הרמוצה [delaat harmutzah], the checkered gourd. Maimonides reports that its taste was so bitter and unpleasant that it could not be eaten unless first covered with hot ashes, by which some of its parts were burned; it was then called רמוצה [remutzah]. Ein geflekelter Kürbiß.

units.la: CULTUS quotidianus templi. Sacerdotes ex excubias egerant in Beth Mokad (vid. f. cum אנשי בית אב (v.f.l.) Summo mane se labant & vestimenta ad cultum requisita induebant ; nam quod lotionem attinet, hunc habuerunt Canonem ין אדם נכנם לעזרה לעבודה אפילו טהור עד שישבול Ne quis ingressus atrium ad cultum peragendum, quamvis pure ingrediatur, nisi postquam se laverit. Ioma Postquam autem semel lotionem peregerunt, iteratione lotionis per totum diem non opus habent, nisi postquam naturæ satisfecerint, tunc enim pedes & manus lavant. (Confer loc.Ioma 3.10.) Omnibus ita paratis exspectarunt Pfidem cultus הממונה, qui pulsans ad fores in mittebatur : nullum tempus fixum Præses habebat, aliquando accedebat מקריאת הגבר cantum galli, aut circiter hoc tempus, aliquando citius aut tardius. Tamid.c.i.
units.tr: The daily service of the temple. The priests kept watch in Beth Mokad (see f.; with the men of the house of the father, v.f.l.). Early in the morning they washed and put on the garments required for the service; for as regards washing they had this rule: "No one who enters the court to perform the service, even if he is clean, may do so until he has washed." Ioma. Once they had performed the washing, they did not need to repeat it throughout the day, except after relieving nature; then they washed hands and feet. (Compare the passage in Ioma 3.10.) With everything thus prepared they waited for the officer in charge, הממונה [hamemunneh], who went round knocking at the doors. The president had no fixed time: sometimes he came at cantum galli, the crowing of the cock, or about that time, and sometimes earlier or later. Tamid c.1.

units.la: §. Deinde sumptis clavibus aperiebant הפשפש valvulam & è Beth Mokad ingrediebantur in Atrium, manibus tenentes אבוקות של אור duas faces aureas, seque in duas catervas dividebant, una petiit portam cum atrii orientalem, altera occidentalem, inter eundum in omnia inquirebant, & seper ulterius pergebant, donec sibi invicem occurrerent apud בית עושי חביתי Conclave lorum qui placentas coquebant, in quo occurrentes se invicem interrogarunt, an omnia bene se habeant. beant ? Eadem opera etiam excitarunt Placentarios, ut sartagines præpararent ad Summi Sacerdotis oblationem. Talmid c.1.
units.tr: Then, the keys having been taken, they opened the valvulam (הפשפש [hapashpash], the little door) and went from Beth Mokad into the court, holding in their hands duas faces aureas (אבוקות של אור [avukot shel or], two golden torches). They divided into two companies: one went towards the east gate of the court, the other towards the west. As they went they inquired into everything, and always went further until they met at בית עושי חביתי [beit osei chavitti], the Conclave lorum qui placentas coquebant, the chamber of those who baked the cakes. Meeting there, they asked one another an omnia bene se habeant, whether all was well. At the same time they also roused the Placentarios, the cake-makers, to prepare the pans for the oblation of the High Priest. Talmid c.1.

units.la: §. Postquam ita hæc visitatio peracta est, Præses eos convocat ad sortem faciendam. De quo ritu v. Sors.
units.tr: When this inspection had been completed, the president called them together to make the lot. On this rite see Sors.

units.la: §. Cui sors contigit purgandi altare holocaustorum, ( quod officium sorte omnium primum dist ibuebatur. ) Socios suos relinquit in conclavi Gazit, & lotis pedibus manibusque opus suum aggreditur. Maymon. Tamid c.1. Super altare semper triplicem ignem nutriebant, (Maym.Tamid. c.2.) unus & quidem maior destinatus erat ad sacrificia consumenda; ex altero desumebant prunas ad thymiama in loco sancto adolendum; Tertius nullum alium usum habuit, nisi ut ignis in altari continuò conservaretur. Altare itaque purgaturus sumit כפף מחתת patinam argenteam, & ad summitatem altaris ascendit, carbones huc atque illuc congregat, & patinam suam replet illis qui consumpti sunt, quam deinde descendendo ad pavimentum defert, & in parte orientali altaris evacuat. Tamid c.1. 4.
units.tr: He to whom the lot fell to cleanse the altar of burnt offerings (which office was the first to be assigned by lot) leaves his companions in the chamber Gazit, and, having washed his feet and hands, sets to his work. Maymon. Tamid c.1. On the altar they always kept three fires burning (Maym. Tamid c.2). One, the larger, was destined for consuming the sacrifices; from another they took coals for burning incense in the holy place; the third had no other use than that the fire on the altar be continually kept up. The priest who is to cleanse the altar takes a כף מחתה [kaf machtah], a patinam argenteam, a silver pan, and goes up to the top of the altar, gathers the coals here and there, and fills his pan with those that have been consumed. Then, descending to the pavement, he carries it and empties it on the east side of the altar. Tamid c.1.4.

units.la: §. Statim ac Sacerdotes socii eius vident, ipsum descendisse וצו currunt, ובאו & abeunt, ורמהרו & festinant sanctificare & lavare manus suas מכיור הכיור ex labro; ( v.f.1.) deinde arripiunt הסגריות והצינרו forcipes & furcas suas, & altare ascendentes removent ad latus altaris, si aliqua frusta de sacrificio præcedentis diei remansissent; omnes cineres aggregant ad unum cumulum in medio altaris, & ex illis
units.tr: As soon as his fellow priests see that he has come down, they currunt (וצו [vatzu], run) and abeunt (ובאו [uva'u], and come) and festinant (ורמהרו [veramaharu], and hurry) to sanctify and wash their hands from the כיור [kiyor], the labro, the laver. Then they seize the forcipes & furcas suas, their tongs and forks (הסגריות והצינרו), and going up the altar they remove to the side of the altar any pieces that remained from the sacrifice of the previous day. They gather all the ashes into one heap in the middle of the altar, and from these

units.la: tantum desumunt quantum requiritur ad vas מסכתר nominatum ( & quod continebat dimidiam partem Chomer) replendum, secumque deferunt. Semper tamen supra altare mediocrem cumu um cinerum, quem חצאן nominant relinquentes. Delatos hos cineres alii Sacerdotes extra civitatem deferunt, illosque in locum aliquem à procellis venti tutum seponunt, ut ibi, nullos ad usus adhibendi, conquiescant. Vid. Tamid. c. 2.
units.tr: they take only as much as is needed to fill the vessel called מסכתר [maskhoret], which held half a chomer, and carry it away. Yet they always leave on the altar a moderate heap of ashes, which they call חצאן [chatzan]. The ashes that have been carried off are taken outside the city by other priests and set aside in some place safe from the winds, so that they may rest there and be used for no purpose. See Tamid. c.2.

units.la: §. Hanc Altaris purgationem ut plurimum incipiebant cum diluculo, sed in 3. magnis festis citius, & in die expiationis, illam iam media nocte peragebant. (v. f. 1.) Remotis autem modo quo diximus cineribus, ignem adaptant; & ante omnia excitant ignem magnum מערכה גדולה struis magna ad partem orientalem altaris; ad hunc ignem omnis generis ligna adhiberi poterant exceptis lignis olivarum & vitium. (quomodo autem ligna antea purgarint vid. Conclave ligni.) Deinde instruunt struem secundam ad cornu altaris meridionale, ut in loco descensui aptissimo, & ad prunas deferendas commodissimo: ad hunc ignem præcipuè ligna ficuum adhibebant. Indifferens erat quocunque in loco tertius ignis excitabatur. Præter hæc ligna duas taleolas singulares igni imponebant, & deinde frusta sacrificii diei præcedentis nondum consumptæ lignis & strui superaddebant. His peractis conculerunt se Sacerdotes iterum in conclave Gazith ad aliam sortem proiiciendam.
units.tr: They usually began this cleansing of the altar at dawn, but on the three great feasts earlier, and on the Day of Atonement they performed it already at midnight. (v. f. 1.) Having removed the ashes in the way we have described, they kindle the fire. Above all they light a great fire, מערכה גדולה [maarakhah gedolah], struis magna, a great pile, on the east side of the altar. For this fire any kind of wood could be used except olive and vine wood. (On how they formerly prepared the wood, see Conclave ligni.) Then they lay a second pile at the south horn of the altar, as being the most suitable place for descending and the most convenient for bringing down the coals; for this fire they especially used fig wood. It did not matter in what place the third fire was kindled. Besides this wood they placed two single little sticks on the fire, and then added to the wood and pile the pieces of the previous day's sacrifice that were not yet consumed. When these things were done, the priests gathered again in the chamber Gazit to cast another lot.

units.la: §. Sorte secunda decernebatur 1. quis sacrificium iuge mactare deberet. 2. Quis sanguinem spargeret. 3. Quis mundaret Altare incensus sive suffitus. 4. Quis adaptaret Candelabra & lampades. 5. Quis caput & crura ad gradus altaris deferret. 6. Quis humeros eius portaret. 7. Quis caudam & pedes. 8. Quis pectus & gulam. 9. Quis lumbos. 10. Quis intestina. 11. Quis הסולם Similam. 12. Quis Placentas summi Sacerdotis. 13. Quis vinum libaret. In quibus nota, nolummodo primum forte iacta fuisse electum, reliqua munia vero Sacerdotes obiisse pro ratione ordinis quo ipsum sequebantur, ita ut secundus ab ipso officium secundum, tertius tertium, & consequenter obtinuerit. vid. Comment. ad Tamid. c.3. v.1.
units.tr: By the second lot it was decided: (1) who should slaughter the continual sacrifice; (2) who should sprinkle the blood; (3) who should cleanse the altar of incense, or burn incense on it; (4) who should arrange the candlesticks and lamps; (5) who should carry the head and legs to the steps of the altar; (6) who should carry its shoulders; (7) who should carry the tail and feet; (8) who should carry the breast and gullet; (9) who should carry the loins; (10) who should carry the entrails; (11) who should carry the הסולם [hasolet], Similam, the fine flour; (12) who should carry the cakes of the High Priest; (13) who should pour the wine libation. In these matters note that only the first was chosen by lot, while the remaining duties the priests discharged according to the order in which they followed him, so that the second after him obtained the second duty, the third the third, and so on in succession. See Comment. ad Tamid. c.3. v.1.

units.la: §. Duae aliae sortes adhuc in usu erant, scilicet quis frusta illa sacrificii ab ascensu altaris in eius summitatem ferre deberet; Quis suffitum in altari thymiamatis adoleret. Sed illae sortes paulo tardius iactae fuerunt, quam hae de quibus hactenus loquuti sumus.
units.tr: §. Two other lots were still in use: one to decide who should carry the pieces of the sacrifice from the foot of the altar up to its top, and one to decide who should burn the incense of the fragrant offering on the altar. But these lots were cast a little later than those of which we have spoken so far.

units.la: §. Sacerdotes illi qui neque sorte neq; alio modo ad officia electi fuerunt, exuerunt vestimenta sua Sacerdotalia, & se applicabant ad minora officia templi, qualia fuerunt afferre vasa, auferre cineres altaris &c.
units.tr: §. Those priests who had been chosen neither by lot nor in any other way laid aside their priestly garments and turned to the lesser duties of the temple, such as carrying in the vessels, carrying out the ashes from the altar, and so on.

units.la: §. His omnibus summo mane peractis, Praefectus cultus iubet, ut observent, an tempus offerendi sacrificium iuge adsit. Statim unus aut alter in summitatem templi ascendit, (vid. rubricam diei expiationis,) & si videt iam diem illuxisse clamat ברקא (Clarus iam dies est. Praefectus tunc ut plurimum ab ipso petit האיר
units.tr: §. When all these things had been done early in the morning, the Prefect of the service orders them to watch whether the time for offering the continual sacrifice has come. Straightway one or another climbs to the top of the temple (see the rubric of the day of atonement), and if he sees that day has already dawned, he cries out ברקא (Already the day is bright. Then the prefect for the most part asks him האיר [hāʾir, "Has it grown light?"]

units.la: פני כל המזרח עד שהוא באחרון An totum cœlum usque ad Hebron lucidum est; Si respondet ita, iubet praefectus afferri agnum ex conclavi agnorum. Qui etiam statim affertur, & etiamsi agni iam antequam illuc deducerentur visitati fuerint an omni maculâ carerent, nihilominus inquisitio ope candelæ repetitur.
units.tr: פני כל המזרח עד שהוא באחרון [Has the whole eastern sky, as far as Hebron, become bright?] Is the whole heaven as far as Hebron bright? If he answers yes, the prefect orders a lamb to be brought from the chamber of the lambs. It is brought at once; and even if the lambs had been examined for blemishes before they were led there, the inspection is nevertheless repeated by the light of a candle.

units.la: §. Ille qui forte electus fuit ad agnum mactandum, illum adducit לבית המטבחי ad illum locum in quo solebat mactari; omnes illi qui destinati sunt ad sanguinem spargendum & membra ferenda ipsum sequuntur; alii vero petunt לשכת הכליים conclave vasium, & ex illo afferunt 93. vasa quæ omnia ad cultum illo die adhibere solent; in uno ex illis vasibus agno potum præbent, ut eò facilius excoriari possit.
units.tr: §. The one who has happened to be chosen to slaughter the lamb leads it to the place in which it was accustomed to be slaughtered, לבית המטבחי [to the slaughter-house]. All those assigned to sprinkle the blood and carry the pieces follow him; others go to the chamber of the vessels, לשכת הכלים [lishkat ha-kelim], and from there bring the ninety-three vessels which were customarily used in the service on that day. From one of these vessels they give the lamb a drink, so that it may be flayed more easily.

units.la: §. Seniores quibus commissæ erant claves atrii (vid. אנשי מעמד & Amarcalin.) ordinario tempore curabant aperiri portas atrii. Cùm portæ ultimæ duorum atriorum aperiebantur tubis clangebant, & ita Levitis omnibus qui illo die cultui adesse debebant, signum dabant sua munia obeundi. Vltimo etiam aperiebatur שער הגדול porta templi maxima, ad intromittendos illos duos qui debebant præparare altare aureum, & adornare lampades: Qui etiam in hunc finem quatuor instrumenta vel vasa secum tulerunt, duo erant aurea & vocabantur שני & כו; (vid. Tamid. c. 3. 6.) duo reliqua erant מפתחות.
units.tr: §. The elders to whom the keys of the court had been entrusted (see אנשי מעמד [men of the station] and Amarcalin) took care, at the usual time, to have the gates of the court opened. When the last gates of the two courts were opened, they sounded the trumpets, and so gave the Levites, all of whom had to be present at the service that day, the signal to perform their duties. Last of all the שער הגדול [great gate] was opened, the greatest gate of the temple, to admit the two men who were to prepare the golden altar and trim the lamps. For this purpose they also carried four instruments or vessels with them: two were of gold and were called שני [shin] and כו [kaf] (see Tamid c. 3, 6); the two remaining were the מפתחות [keys].

units.la: §. Statim ac ille qui mactaturus erat agnum audiebat strepitum portæ magnæ, agnum iugulabat; ille qui purgare debebat altare fuhitus, ipsum mundabat cùm agnus mactabatur. Ille qui lampades mundare & adornare debebat aliquas ex illis mundabat cùm sanguis spargebatur. Altare incensus ita purgabatur; Sacerdos purgaturus sumpsit patinam vel vas שנ illudque coram altari ponebat, deinde volâ manus capiebat carbones & cineres, & illos in Teni immittebat, reliqua verò in illud verrebat; vasque ibi relinquens egrediebatur. Lampades verò hunc in modum adornabant. אכן היה לפני המנורה Lapis erat coram candelabro, cui tres gradus incisi erant; illis insistebat Sacerdos, & illas lampades quæ extinctæ erant novo oleo & lychnucho instruebat, & iterum incendebat illis lampadibus, quæ vigorem suum retinuerant. Hoc tamen non observarunt כנר מערבי in lampade occidentali, (quæ non illa erat quæ maximè occidentem versus posita, sed quæ in medio omnium posita erat.) nam si illa extincta erat, non potuerat nisi igne altaris refici. Lampades verò illas quas adhuc incensas reperiebat, purgabat, illisque novum oleum suppeditabat. Hoc tempore Sacerdos ille solùm 5. lampades, non autem omnes 7. adornat. Quibus omnibus paratis egreditur; Idem faciunt reliqui qui spargebant sanguinem, excoriabant sacrificium iuge, & illud in partes dividebant; nam postquam frusta eius ad gradus altaris fuerunt allata, & sale conspersa, omnes iterum petunt conclave Gazit, & se ad preces componunt. vid. Tamid c.3. Iomæ c.3. Maym. Tamid c.6.
units.tr: §. As soon as the man who was about to slaughter the lamb heard the noise of the great gate, he cut the lamb's throat; the man who was to clean the altar of the fire ritually cleansed it while the lamb was being slaughtered. The man who was to trim and tend the lamps cleaned some of them while the blood was being sprinkled. The altar of incense was cleansed in this way: the priest who was to cleanse it took the dish or vessel שנ [shin] and set it down before the altar; then with his hand he took coals and ashes, and put them into the Teni [tēnî], and swept the rest into it; leaving the vessel there, he went out. The lamps were trimmed in this way: אכן היה לפני המנורה [there was a stone before the lampstand], a stone was before the candelabrum, in which three steps were cut; the priest stood upon these and provided fresh oil and wicks for the lamps that had gone out, and again lit from the fire those lamps which had kept their strength. They did not, however, observe this with the כנר מערבי [western lamp], the lamp on the west side, which was not the one placed furthest toward the west but the one placed in the middle of them all; for if that one had gone out, it could be relit only from the fire of the altar. But the lamps which he found still burning he cleaned and supplied with fresh oil. At this time that priest trims only five lamps, not all seven. When all these things are prepared, he goes out. The others who sprinkled the blood, flayed the continual sacrifice and divided it into pieces do the same; for after its pieces had been brought to the steps of the altar and sprinkled with salt, they all again seek the chamber Gazit and betake themselves to prayer. See Tamid c. 3, Yoma c. 3, Maimonides, Tamid c. 6.

units.la: §. Preces quas omnium primò dicunt ita sonant ; Amajli nos ô Deus Domine noster amore æterno; tu magna misericordia nos prosequutus es ô Pater & Rex noster! Propter patres nostros, qui confidentiam suam in te posuerunt, & quibus dedisti statuta vita. Etiam nobis sis gratiosus, ô Pater, miserere nostri Pater summè misericors. Et cordibus nostris instilla, ut possimus intelligere, cognoscere, docere, observare omnia verba statutorum tuorum in charitate; illumina oculos nostros lege tua, da cordibus nostris retinere præcepta tua, & timere nomen tuum &c. vid. Maymon Tamid. cap.6. & Sepher tephilot.
units.tr: §. The prayers which they say first of all sound thus: Amajli, we beseech thee, O Lord our God, with eternal love; with great mercy hast thou cherished us, O our Father and King! For the sake of our fathers, who placed their confidence in thee, and to whom thou gavest statutes of life, be gracious to us also, O Father, have mercy upon us, Father most merciful. And instil into our hearts that we may understand, know, teach, and observe all the words of thy statutes in love; enlighten our eyes by thy law, grant that our hearts may hold fast thy precepts, and fear thy name, etc. See Maimonides, Tamid c. 6, and Sepher Tephilot.

units.la: Deinde sequitur recitatio decem præceptorum Dei, & Phylacteriorum, (de quibus vid. f.1.)
units.tr: Then follows the recital of the ten commandments of God, and of the phylacteries (on which see f. 1).

units.la: §. Quod tempus adolendi suffitum attinet, de eo hunc habent Canonem in Ioma c.3. קטורת של שחר היתה קריבה בין דם לאיברים של בין הערביים בין איברים לנסכים Suffitus matutinus offertur inter aspersionem sanguinis & collocationem membrorum ad gradus altaris,& suffitus vespertinus inter collocationè membrorum, & oblationè libaminis vini. Quis debeat hoc officio fungi iterum sorte decretum, & simul,quis ad superficiem altaris frusta sacrificii deferret. Ille qui sorte ad adolendum electus fuit, sumebat patinam argenteam, in qua erat thuribulum suffitu plenum ; & comitatus aliquo Sacerdote qui gerit prunas ab igne altaris desumptas templum ingreditur. Cùm ita procedunt,sonant מגריפה instrumentum quod admodum sonorum erat, triplicem in finem, (Tamid cap. 5.)
units.tr: §. As for the time for burning incense, they have this rule in Yoma c. 3: קטורת של שחר היתה קריבה בין דם לאיברים של בין הערביים בין איברים לנסכים [The morning incense was offered between the sprinkling of the blood and the laying of the pieces on the altar, and the evening incense between the laying of the pieces and the pouring of the drink offering of wine]. The morning incense is offered between the sprinkling of the blood and the placing of the members on the steps of the altar, and the evening incense between the placing of the members and the offering of the libation of wine. By lot it was again decided who should discharge this office, and at the same time who should carry the pieces of the sacrifice to the top of the altar. He who had been chosen by lot to burn the incense took the silver dish, in which was the censer full of incense; and accompanied by another priest who carried coals taken from the altar fire, he entered the sanctuary. As they proceed, they sound the מגריפה [magrepah], an instrument of very loud sound, for a threefold purpose (Tamid c. 5):

units.la: 1. Ut unusquisque Sacerdos sciret Sacerdotes fratres suos iam ad cultum paratos esse, & ita se etiam ad officium accingeret.
units.tr: 1. So that every priest might know that his fellow priests were now ready for the service, and might thus also gird himself for his office.

units.la: 2. Ut quivis Levita signum hoc audiens se ad canendum praepararet.
units.tr: 2. So that every Levite, hearing the signal, might prepare himself to sing.

units.la: 3. Vt ראש המעמד Praeses stationis illos sacerdotes qui nondum tunc mundi & parati, ad portam Orientalem (Nicanoris) deduceret, ad eos ibi reprehendendos. Illi duo qui altare suffitus & lampades purgaverant, hos duos praecedunt, unus sumit suum שין quod posuisse coram altari diximus, & incurvando se egreditur; alter etiam suum vas כו (quod apud lapidem Candelabri reliquerat) sumendo egreditur. Ille qui prunas attulit, illas super altare disponit, & alterum solum relinquendo reverentia facta egreditur. Caeterum לא היה המקטיר מקטיר עד שהממונה אומר לו הקטר ille qui adolere debet non adolet donec praefectus ipsi dicat ( elatâ voce) suffumiga: Imò ipse summus Sacerdos non adolet, nisi postquam Praefectus ipsi dixit אישי כ"ג הקטר Domine summe Sacerdos, fumiga. Signo autem adolendi dato omnes qui in atrio sunt se ad reliquas preces accingunt. Vid. Maym. l.c. & Tamid c. 6.
units.tr: 3. That the ראש המעמד [head of the station], the prefect of the station, might lead those priests who were not yet then clean and ready to the Eastern Gate (of Nicanor), to rebuke them there. The two who had cleansed the altar of incense and the lamps go before these two: one takes his שין [shin], which we said he had set down before the altar, and goes out bowing; the other also goes out, taking his vessel כו [kaf], which he had left by the stone of the candelabrum. He who had brought the coals arranges them upon the altar, and leaving only the other behind, goes out after making reverence. Moreover, the one who is to burn incense does not burn it until the prefect says to him, in a raised voice, burn incense. Indeed the high priest himself does not burn it until the prefect has said to him, אישי כ"ג הקטר [ishi kohen gadol, haqter], Lord high priest, burn incense. When the signal for burning has been given, all who are in the court betake themselves to the remaining prayers. See Maimonides, l.c., and Tamid c. 6.

units.la: §. Illae preces praecipuè sequentes fuerunt. 1. Oratio vocatur אמת ויציב quia illa his verbis incipiebat; & quoniam illae orationes in Tamid cap. 5. non plenè adducuntur, hic integras eas referre lubet. Oratio itaque prima ita sonat. Verum & stabile, firmum & certum, integrum & fidele, amabile & delectabile, pulchrum, terribile, & gloriosum, ordinatum acceptabile, bonum & elegans est hoc verbum pro nobis perpetuo. Verum aeterni Dei Regis nostri, rupis Iacobi, scutum salutis nostra in perpetuum; Ille est certus, & nomen eius est certum, thronus eius firmus. Regnum & veritas stabilita in aeternum, &c. 2. Oratio vocatur in Tamid c. 5. עכודע & apud Maymon. in Temid. c.6. רצה. Tenor eius hic est. Gratus sit tibi, o Deus, populus Israel, precesque eius. Restaura cultum domus tuae, & aspice holocaustum Israelis eiusque preces in favore, in complacentia, sitque tibi semper acceptus cultus Israelis. Laudamus te qui es Deus Dominus noster, & Deus patrum nostrorum, Deus omnium Creaturarum, gloria & laus sit tibi, quod nos conservasti &c. 3. Oratio sic incipiebat דא שלום Da pacem, bonitatem, felicitatem, gratiam, misericordiam, pro omni tuo populo Israel, &c. 4. Oratio sive benedictio erat solum in usu in Sabbatho, cum illi qui praecedenti septimana inservierant, domum petunt; illa ita sonat. Qui habitare fecit nomen suum in hac domo, faciat ut apud vos habitet, charitas, fraternitas, pax, & amicitia. Ita etiam clausit Epist. 2. ad Corinthios Paulus, ὁ Θεὸς τῆς ἀγάπης καὶ εἰρήνης ἔσται μετ' ὑμῶν. Plura de precibus vid. f. 1. vid. Comment. ad Tamid. l.c. §. Peractis & ad finem perductis precibus, ille, cui forte contigit ponere frusta agni in ignem, se ad hoc agendum accingit, & primo illa incondite in ignem conjicit, deinde de verò in ordinem disponit.
units.tr: §. The prayers that follow were chiefly these. 1. The prayer called אמת ויציב [Emet ve-yatsiv, "True and firm"], because it begins with these words; and since in Tamid c. 5 those prayers are not quoted in full, I am glad to give them here entire. The first prayer, then, runs thus: True and stable, firm and certain, whole and faithful, lovely and delightful, beautiful, terrible and glorious, ordered, acceptable, good and graceful is this word for us forever. True is the eternal God, our King, the rock of Jacob, the shield of our salvation for ever. He is certain, and his name is certain, his throne is firm. The kingdom and truth are established for ever, etc. 2. The prayer called in Tamid c. 5 עכודע [ʿavodah] and in Maimonides, Tamid c. 6, רצה [ratseh]. Its tenor is this: Be pleased with us, O God, with thy people Israel and their prayers. Restore the service of thy house, and regard the burnt offering of Israel and its prayers with favour and good will, and may the service of Israel always be acceptable to thee. We praise thee, who art God, our Lord, and the God of our fathers, God of all creatures; glory and praise be to thee, that thou hast preserved us, etc. 3. The prayer began thus, דא שלום [Grant peace]: Grant peace, goodness, blessing, grace, mercy, for all thy people Israel, etc. 4. The fourth prayer, or blessing, was in use only on the Sabbath, when those who had served in the previous week went home; it runs thus: He who has caused his name to dwell in this house, may he cause charity, brotherhood, peace and friendship to dwell among you. So also Paul closed the second epistle to the Corinthians: ὁ Θεὸς τῆς ἀγάπης καὶ εἰρήνης ἔσται μετ' ὑμῶν [The God of love and peace shall be with you]. For more on the prayers see f. 1; see the commentary on Tamid l.c., §. Peractis. And when the prayers have been completed and brought to an end, he to whom it has chanced to fall to place the pieces of the lamb upon the fire sets about this task; and first he casts them into the fire in disorder, then afterwards arranges them in order.

units.la: §. Deinde Sacerdotes, præcipuè autem illi qui cultui in loco sancto interfuerunt, stantes super gradus qui in propylæum ducebant, elevabant manus suas & benedicebant populo. Manus elevabant supra capita, sparsis digitis, & unus ex ipsis recitabat Numer.6.24.25.26. quos versus reliqui repetebant, benedictione una, in Synagogis verò faciebant ex his verbis tres benedictiones. Populus autem respondebat.Benedictus sit Deus Israelis בן עולם עד עולם à seculo in seculum. De hac benedictione Sacerdotum vide Taanith c. 4. Maymon. in Tephill. & Bircat HaCohan. c.14.& 15.
units.tr: §. Then the priests, especially those who had taken part in the service in the holy place, standing on the steps that led up to the propylaeum, raised their hands and blessed the people. They raised their hands above their heads with the fingers spread, and one of them recited Numbers 6:24-26, which the others repeated, making one blessing; in the synagogues, however, they made three blessings from these words. The people answered: May the God of Israel be blessed [בן עולם עד עולם] from age to age. On this blessing of the priests see Taanith ch. 4, Maimonides in Tephillah, and Birkat HaKohen ch. 14 and 15.

units.la: §. Deinde offerebatur הסולת & postea החביתין placenta Summi Sacerdotis; libamenque vini. Hæc excipiebat Musica, tandemque populus incurvatione facta dimittebatur.
units.tr: §. Next was offered the fine flour [הסולת], and afterwards the baked cakes [החביתין], the cake of the high priest, and a drink offering of wine. Music followed these, and at last the people were dismissed after a bow.

units.la: §. Cultus Vespertinus à matutino quem nunc describimus non differt, nisi in accidentariis quibusdam. Sortes non projiciebantur vesperi nisi pro illo qui debebat adolere, reliqua munia peragebantur ab illis qui mane in officiis fuerunt. Suffitus vesperi paululùm tardius offerebatur, quàm mane. Sacerdotes etiam non semper benedicebant vesperi, quamvis tamen ut plurimum id fiebat vid. c.
units.tr: The evening service does not differ from the morning service which we now describe, except in certain incidental matters. Lots were not cast in the evening except for the one who was to offer incense; the other duties were carried out by those who had served in the morning. The evening incense was offered a little later than the morning incense. Nor did the priests always pronounce the blessing in the evening, although it was usually done, see Taanit. c. 4.

units.la: 4. Taanit.
units.tr: Taanit.

units.la: §. Iam referemus quædam quæ in personis requirebantur, si cultum suum in templo rite peragere voluerunt. 1. לא יכנס אדם להר הבית : במקלו Nemo debuit montem templi baculo ascendere. Beracot. c.9. Zavim. c.1. Gemara. Maymon in Beth Habech. c. 7. Non enim in locum pacis arma percussoria afferenda, aut templum quasi fatigare existimandum. Exc pe tamen ab hac regula praefectum custodiarum, qui baculo instructus erat, ad percutiendos dormientes Levitas. Christus non baculo idcirco usus est sed flagellis, cum mercatores ex templo expelleret. 11. Nemo debuit ad templum accedere במנעל שברבליו calceis in pedibus suis. Poterant tamen sandalia pedibus induere, at Levitæ & Sacerdotes quando munia sua obibant, debebant nec calceis nec sandaliis instructi sed nudipedes esse, Erach. c.2. in Gemara. III. Nemo debet ad templum accedere באפונדתו או בוצק שעלרגליו aut pedibus pulvere conspurcatis. IV. Nemo debet accedere כסעות הצרורין לו בסרונו pecuniis ligatis in crumena sua. Nam alias cum de Deo cogitandum ad nummos nostros animam deflectimus. Licuit tamen in manu afferre, quod vel pro sacrificiis vel eleemosynis destinatum.
units.tr: §. We will now set out certain things required of persons, if they wished to perform their worship in the temple duly. (1) לא יכנס אדם להר הבית במקלו [No one shall enter the mountain of the house with a staff]. No one ought to ascend the mountain of the temple with a staff. Berachot c. 9. Zavim c. 1. Gemara. Maimonides in Beth Habechirah c. 7. For weapons for striking must not be brought into a place of peace, nor should the temple be thought of as something to be wearied. Yet from this rule the prefect of the guards was excepted, who carried a staff for striking the sleeping Levites. Christ did not use a staff for this purpose but a whip, when he drove the merchants out of the temple. (2) No one ought to come to the temple במנעל שברגליו [with shoes on his feet]. With sandals on his feet. Yet they could put sandals on their feet; but the Levites and priests, when they performed their duties, ought to be neither in shoes nor sandals but barefoot. Erachin c. 2, in the Gemara. (3) No one ought to come to the temple באפונדתו או בוצק שעל רגליו [with dust on his feet or with his feet soiled with mud]. (4) No one ought to come כסעות הצרורין לו בכיסו [with money tied up in his purse]. For otherwise, while we ought to be thinking of God, we turn our minds to our coins. Yet it was permitted to carry in the hand what was set aside for sacrifices or alms.

units.la: §. Postquam ad montem templi perventum, unusquisque haec quatuor observare debet. I. אסור לרוק בכל הר הבית Prohibitum est in monte templi sputum eiaculari, si vero exspuere cogitur, sputum debet ejicere in aliquam partem vestimenti sui. Maymon.Beth Habech. c.7. 2. ראשו כנגד שער מודחי Debet ab omni indecoro gestu abstinere, praecipuè è regione portæ Nikanoris: Id est nemo ridere aut cachinnari, alium irridere, multò minùs inhonestius quid committere debuit. 3. לא יעשה הר הבית קפנדריא Nemo debuit templum compendium via facere. Id est, per illud ire si forte loco quo tendis propior esses: nam ad templum nemo venire debet nisi religionis causâ. Vid. Maymon in Tephillah cap. i. 4. Qui ingressus est atrium יהוד בנחת debet cum gravitate & modestia procedere usque ad locum in quem tendit.
units.tr: §. After one has come to the mountain of the temple, each person ought to observe these four things. (1) אסור לרוק בכל הר הבית [It is forbidden to spit anywhere on the mountain of the temple]. It is forbidden to eject spittle on the mountain of the temple; but if one is compelled to spit, he should throw the spittle onto some part of his garment. Maimonides, Beth Habechirah c. 7. (2) ראשו כנגד שער ניקנור [His head against the gate of Nicanor]. He ought to abstain from every indecorous gesture, especially opposite the Gate of Nicanor. That is, no one ought to laugh or guffaw, mock another, much less commit anything more unseemly. (3) לא יעשה הר הבית קפנדריא [No one shall make the mountain of the temple a shortcut]. That is, one should not pass through it in case it happens to be nearer to the place to which you are heading; for no one ought to come to the temple except for reasons of religion. See Maimonides in Tephillah ch. 1. (4) One who has entered the court יהוד בנחת [should proceed with gravity and modesty] until he reaches the place to which he is heading.

units.la: §. אין מתפלל אלא בעומד Ad preces se stando componere debent, Maym. Hal. Tephil. c. 5. de hoc gestu vid. preces.
