units.tr: §. אין מתפלל אלא בעומד [One does not pray except standing]. They ought to compose themselves to prayer by standing, Maimonides, Hilchot Tephillah c. 5. On this posture see prayers.

units.la: §. אין ישיבה בעזרה אלא למלכים בית דוד Nemo in Atrio Israelis sedere poterat, nisi Rex ex familia Davidis. Maym. Beth Habech. c.7. Vid. Kimchi in 1. Sam 1. & Lev Gersom, qui credunt id aliquando etiam summo Pontifici licere.
units.tr: §. [לא יעמוד בראש מגולה] No one ought to pour out his prayers or stand with his head uncovered; indeed the wise never prayed except veiled. Maimonides, Tephillah ch. 5. So too in R. Nathan on Avot ch. 6. Nicodemus composes himself for prayer [מתעטף], veiled.

units.la: §. לא יעמוד בראש מגולה Nemo preces suas fundere aut stare debet detecto capite, imo sapientes nunquam nisi velati orarunt. Maymon. Tephillah c.5. Sic apud R. Nathan in Abbot c.6. Nicodemus ad orationem se componit מתעטף velatus.
units.tr: §. The bodily postures they used in their worship were threefold: (1) [כריעה] genuflexion; (2) [קדה] bowing of the head; (3) [השתחויה] prostration of the body, which ought not to be used except by those who knew themselves to be blameless and upright, like Joshua. Maimonides, Hilchot Tephillah ch. 5. On these see prayer.

units.la: §. Gestus corporis, quo in cultu suo usi sunt, triplex erat; 1. erat כריעה genuflexio. 2. קדה Capitis incurvatio. 3. השתחויה Corporis prostratio, quae non debebant adhiberi nisi ab illis, qui se ipsos integros & iustos sciebant ut Iosua. Maymon. Hal. Tephilla cap. 5. vid. de his preces.
units.tr: When the service was finished, while they were intending to return home, they were not to turn their backs on the altar (Maimonides, Hilchot Beth HaBechirah ch. 7); therefore they also went out of the court walking backwards. The last thing to be observed was that they should not leave by the gate through which they had entered. Middot, Maaseh, ch. 2.

units.la: Cultu peracto, dum domum redire intenduntnon debebant terga altari vertere,(Maymon: Hal. Beth Habech c. 7.) quare etiam retrorsum eundo ex atrio egrediebantur; Vltimum verò quod observandum, erat, ne egrederentur per illam portam quâ ingressi sunt. Maff. Middot. cap. 2.
units.tr: When the worship was finished, and they intended to return home, they ought not to turn their backs on the altar (Maimonides, Hilchot Beth Habechirah c. 7); therefore they also went out of the court walking backwards. The last thing to be observed was that they should not leave by the gate through which they had entered. Middot ch. 2.

units.la: CURSORES habuerunt Reges Orientales; eximii cursoris exemplum habes in Hierof. Taanit sol. 68. col. 3. ibi enim recensetur, quòd בלרות Cursor egressus fit Hierosolyma, primo die Augusti, & spatio unius diei & noctis pervenerit Tyrum. De Tabellariis vel cursoribus Ahafveri vid. MedrafchEfther cap.1.8. De memorabilibus aliarum gentium cursoribus vid. Lipfii Cent. 3. Epift. 59. ad Nicolaum Micaultium.
units.tr: Eastern kings had couriers; an outstanding example of a swift courier you have in Jerusalem Taanit fol. 68, col. 3. For there it is recorded that a courier (בלרות) left Jerusalem on the first day of August and in the space of one day and one night reached Tyre. On the postal messengers or couriers of Ahasuerus see Midrash Esther ch. 1, 8. On the notable couriers of other nations see Lipsius, Cent. 3, Ep. 59, to Nicolas Micault.

units.la: de CUSTODIA templi vid. excubias. vid. Levitas.
units.tr: On the GUARD of the temple see watches. See Levites.

units.la: D. ד
units.tr: D. ד

units.la: DÆMONES meridiani sunt periculosissimi. R. Saadia & AbenEsra Iob. 3.5. Eò maior esse debet cura de oratione meridiana Alcoran. Sura 11. 237.
units.tr: Demons at midday are the most dangerous. R. Saadia and Aben Ezra on Job 3:5. For this reason greater care ought to be taken over the midday prayer. Alcoran, Sura 11. 237.

units.la: §. In novo testamento multa legimus de Dæmoniacis & lunaticis; ad ipsorum dilucidationem considera quæ Talmudici de שושו dicunt. In Hierof. Trumot sol. 40. 2. hæc legimus. Hæc sunt signa τὲ שושו, Exit nocte & pernoctat inter sepulchra, & vestes suas lacerat, & quodcunque ei datur pessundat, (confer Math. 8.28.) Dicit Rabb Houna, At num ille solum, in quibus hæc omnia? Ego dico quod non. Qui exit nocte קניסריקום Chondriacus est. Qui pernoctat inter sepulchreta מקשר לשרים fumigat Diabolis. Qui vestes suas lacerat est כוליקום Melancholi-cus. cus. Et qui pessundat quodcunque ei datur קורדיקוס Cardiacus. Et paulò inferius פעמים Aliquando furit, aliquando est sanus; dum furit habendus est pro sano ... est ad omnia.
units.tr: §. In the New Testament we read much about the demoniacs and the lunatics. To understand them better, consider what the Talmudists say about שושו [shushu]. In Hierosolymitan Trumot, sol. 40.2, we read these words: "These are the signs of the shushu: he goes out at night and spends the night among the tombs, tears his garments, and destroys whatever is given to him" (compare Matt. 8:28). "Rabbi Huna says: But is it only in those who have all these things? I say no. He who goes out at night is a chondriac [קניסריקום]. He who spends the night among the tombs fumigates the devils [מקשר לשרים]. He who tears his garments is a melancholic [כוליקום]. And he who destroys whatever is given to him is a cardiac [קורדיקוס]." And a little further on: "Sometimes he rages, sometimes he is sane; while he rages he is to be held as sane... he is fit for everything."

units.la: §. De חרש ושוטה Surdo muto & Lunatico plurima in Mishna habemus loca; Terumah c.1. 1. ad Trumam non admittuntur. Cholin c.1.1. Excluduntur à mactatione bestiarum.
units.tr: §. There are very many passages in the Mishnah about the deaf-mute [חרש] and the lunatic [שוטה]. Terumah c. 1.1: they are not admitted to the terumah. Chullin c. 1.1: they are excluded from the slaughter of beasts.

units.la: §. Iudæis usitatum erat morbos graviores, eos præsertim quibus vel distortum est corpus, vel mens turbata, malis spiritibus attribuere. Maymon in Girufchin c.2. מי שהיה רוח רעה מבעתת אותו ואסר כשהתחיל בו החולי Si quis vexatus spiritu malo dixerit, cum illum primo invaserit ipse morbus, conscribite libellum repudii uxori meæ &c. Maff. Gittin cap.7.1. מי שאחז קורדיקוס ואמר כתבו גט לאשתי לא אמר כלום Si quis quem invaserit Cordicus, dicat, conscribite libellum repudii uxori meæ, nihil plane dixit, (ipsi non est obediendum.) Glossatores dicunt Cordiacum esse Dæmonem qui dominatur in nimium vini novi bibentibus. Maymonides vero in loc.cit. dicit, קורדיקוס est morbus generatus à repletione vasorum cerebri, à quo confunditur intellectus: Estque morbus è genere morborum comitialium. Ecce hic habes eundem Dæmona & morbum.
units.tr: §. It was customary among the Jews to attribute the more serious diseases, especially those by which the body is distorted or the mind disturbed, to evil spirits. Maimonides on Gerushin c. 2: "If someone vexed by an evil spirit, when the illness first seized him, said: 'Write a bill of divorce for my wife,' etc." Mishnah Gittin cap. 7.1: "If someone whom the cordicus has seized says, 'Write a bill of divorce for my wife,' he has said nothing at all" (he is not to be obeyed). The glossators say that the cordiacus is a demon who rules over those who drink too much new wine. Maimonides, however, in the same place, says that the cordiacus is a disease generated from the overfilling of the vessels of the brain, by which the understanding is confused; and it is a disease of the kind of epileptic illnesses. Behold, here you have the same demon and disease.

units.la: §. Aruch in rad. שכתא refert dari quendam Dæmonem nomine Schibta qui præhendens cervices infantum nervos eorum exsiccet & contrahat.
units.tr: §. Aruch, in the root שכתא, reports that there is a certain demon named Schibta, who seizes the necks of infants and dries up and contracts their sinews.

units.la: §. Bab, Berac. sol.51. 2. dicitur; qui pocula duplicata ebibit שרים על ידי גיוק plectitur per Diabolum.
units.tr: §. Bab. Berachot sol. 51.2 says: whoever drinks double cups is struck by the Devil (שרים על ידי גיוק).

units.la: §. Sæpius etiam in Talmudicis mentio fit רוחות טומאת spiritum impurorum τῶν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων, Exemplum afferemus ex Sanhed. sol.65.2. דורש אל המתים Necromantes ille est, qui inedia se macerat, atque it & pernoctat inter sepulchreta, eo fine ut habitet super eum רוח טומאה Spiritus immundi. (Gloss. ut dæmon sepulchreti eum amet, atque adiuvet in incantationibus suis.) Cum versiculum istum R.Akibha legeret, flevit, & dixit; si ieiunanti eum in finem ut super ipsum veniat spiritus immundus, spiritus etiam superveniat; multò magis ieiunanti ut Spiritus Sanctus superveniat, ille superveniret. At quid ego faciam, cùm peccata nostra nos separaverint à Deo &c. De Principe Dæmoniorum vide Belzebul &c. in B. Quidam Iudæus Ramæ Dæmonem eiecit. Gloss.Bab.Ioma sol.57.1.
units.tr: §. Frequently too the Talmudic writings mention "unclean spirits" [רוחות טומאה; τῶν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων]. We shall give an example from Sanhedrin sol. 65.2: "A necromancer [דורש אל המתים] is one who wastes himself with fasting, goes out and spends the night among the tombs, so that an unclean spirit may dwell upon him." (Gloss: so that the demon of the tomb may love him and help him in his incantations.) When R. Akiba read this verse, he wept and said: if, when a man fasts so that an unclean spirit may come upon him, a spirit does come upon him, how much more would the Holy Spirit come upon one who fasts that the Holy Spirit may come upon him? But what am I to do, since our sins have separated us from God, etc. On the prince of demons see Beelzebul, etc., in B. A certain Jew at Rome cast out a demon. Gloss. Bab. Yoma sol. 57.1.

units.la: DACTYLUS stomacho ieiuno est acerbus. Metzia sol.113.2. Dactyli טוביגא Tufianei i.e. qui Tubhianæ crescunt admodum parvi æstimabantur, quia in illo loco vix ad maturitatem perveniebant. Cholin sol.46.2. de Palmorum usu in Festo Tabernaculorum vid. in F.festum tabern. Ab ipsis Iericho תמרי עיר vocata Deut. 34. Dactyli laxant, calefaciunt, satiant, sed non oblectant, i.e. dulcedine nocent. Gittin. folio 70.1.
units.tr: DATES are harsh to an empty stomach. Metzia sol. 113.2. The dates Tufianei [טוביגא], that is, those which grow at Tubhia, were held in very low esteem, because in that place they scarcely reached maturity. Chullin sol. 46.2. On the use of palms at the Feast of Tabernacles see under the feast of Tabernacles. Jericho itself is called the city of palms [תמרי עיר] in Deut. 34. Dates loosen the bowels, warm, and satisfy, but do not delight, that is, they harm by their sweetness. Gittin folio 70.1.

units.la: DAVID. Nisi fuisset David, non fecisset Ioab bellum, & nisi fuisset Ioab, non dedisset David opcoperam legi Sanhed. sol. 49. de Corona Davidis, quomodo eam gestarit cûm pondus eius fuerit talentum auri v.L.T.Cl.Buxt. p.6.18.
units.tr: DAVID. Had there been no David, Joab would not have waged war; and had there been no Joab, David would not have... as I read in Sanhedrin sol. 49, concerning the crown of David: how he bore it, since its weight was a talent of gold. v. L. T. Cl. Buxt. p. 6.18.

units.la: DALMANUTHA Marci viii. 10. potest derivari quasi dicetur בית דאלמנות Domum viduitatis; habebant enim in usu, viduis domunculas iuxta domus patrum suorum ædificare, sicuti patet ex Bava Batra sol.98.2. Quàm facilè autem ab aliqua splendidiore viduitatis domo hic locus denominari potuit.
units.tr: DALMANUTHA (Mark 8:10) can be derived as if it were said בית דאלמנות, the house of widowhood. For they had the custom of building little houses for widows beside the houses of their fathers, as appears from Bava Batra sol. 98.2. How easily, however, this place could have been named after some more splendid house of widowhood.

units.la: §. Potest etiam hoc nomen deductum esse à voce צלמון Zalmon de quo fit mentio Iudic.ix. 48. v in ו mutato secundùm consuetum. Syris & Arabibus Idioma. Apud Talmudicos mentio fit זז Zalmon Ievamot sol. 122 1. Historia est de homine quodam in Zalmon &c. Item Kilaim c. 4. v. 9. Bava Bathra sol.82.2. Sed in illis locis non videtur intelligi illud Zalmon Sichemiticum de quo Iud. ix. mentio fit, præcipuè in Kilaim, nam ibi dicitur בא מעשה לפני חכמים illud quod in Zalmon contigerat, adductum fuisse & diiudicandum traditum Sapientibus. Quid enim Samaritæ cum Sapientibus Iudæorum? nihil autem incommodi erit, si intelligamus hunc locum propinquum fuisse Tiberiadi, & causam huius incolæ Zalmon ad ipsos adductam fuisse Sapientes Tiberiade Academiam constituentes.
units.tr: §. This name can also be derived from the word צלמון, Zalmon, mentioned in Judg. 9:48, with ו put for ו according to the usual practice (an idiom of the Syrians and Arabs). Among the Talmudists mention is made of Zalmon: Yevamot sol. 122.1, "There is a story about a certain man in Zalmon", etc. Likewise Kilaim c. 4 v. 9, and Bava Batra sol. 82.2. But in those places it does not seem that the Zalmon of Shechem mentioned in Judges 9 is meant, especially in Kilaim, for there it is said: "The case that happened in Zalmon was brought before the wise men and handed over to the Sages for judgment." For what have the Samaritans to do with the Sages of the Jews? Nothing inconvenient, however, follows if we understand this place to have been near Tiberias, and the case of an inhabitant of Zalmon to have been brought before the Sages who established their academy at Tiberias.

units.la: DILUCULI distinctio apud Rabbinos hæc est i. erat אויל דשחרא Cerva aurora. Prima lucis apparitio: Hierof. Berac. sol.2.3. R. Chaia & R. Simeon itinerantes simul mane quodam in valle Arbel, viderunt Cervam aurora, quod lux eius
units.tr: DAWN (diluculum). The distinction among the Rabbis is this: i. there is the hind of dawn [אילה דשחרא], Cerva aurora, the first appearance of light. Hierosolymitan Berachot sol. 2.3: "R. Chiya and R. Simeon, travelling together one morning in the valley of Arbel, saw the hind of dawn, how its light

units.la: diffunderet æthera. Dixit R. Chaia, Talis futura est redemptio Israelis. Primò gradatim & minutim procedit, at quò magis procedet eò magis augebitur. ii. משיביר בין תכלת ללבן (cum distinguere quis poterit inter colorem Hyacinthinum & album. iii. Cum lucescit oriens משיאור המורח. iv. בנץ החמה Oriente sole. Ita enim disting. Hierof. Berac. sol. 13. A quo tempore recitant Phylacteria mane? Ab eo tempore quo distinguere quis poterit inter colorem hyacinthinum & album &c. Item sol. 2. 3. A prodeunte (erva aurora usquedum lucescat oriens, Et à quo lucescit oriens, usquedum oriatur Sol. &c. Ad hos quatuor temporis articulos non inconcinnè adoptat Phraseologias Evangelistarum V. Cl. D. Leigtfootus. Ad primum refert τὴ ἐπιφανείαν Math. c. 28. 1. Ad secundum πρὸς σύστασιν ἐπὶ ἱσῆς Iohannis 20. 1. Ad tertium ὀψὲ βαθέως Luca 24. 1. Ad quartum λίαν πρωΐ & tamen ἀνατέλλαντος τὸ ἥλιος Marci 16. 2. Quâ re animadversâ facillima eorum est reconciliatio.
units.tr: spread through the sky. R. Chiya said: Such will be the redemption of Israel. At first it proceeds gradually and little by little, but the further it goes, the more it will increase." ii. "When one can distinguish between the hyacinth colour and white" [משיביר בין תכלת ללבן]. iii. "When the east begins to lighten" [משיאור המורח]. iv. "At sunrise" [בנץ החמה]. For thus distinguish Hierosolymitan Berachot sol. 13: "From what time do they recite the phylacteries in the morning? From the time when one can distinguish between the hyacinth and the white," etc. Also sol. 2.3: "From the coming forth of the hind of dawn until the east begins to lighten, and from when the east lightens until the sun rises," etc. The most learned Mr. Lightfoot not inelegantly fits these four moments of time to the phrases of the Evangelists. To the first he refers the appearing [ἐπιφανείαν], Matt. 28:1; to the second the dawn at the first light [πρὸς σύστασιν ἐπὶ ἱσῆς], John 20:1; to the third the very deep dawn [ὀψὲ βαθέως], Luke 24:1; to the fourth very early [λίαν πρωΐ], and yet when the sun had risen [ἀνατέλλαντος τὸ ἥλιος], Mark 16:2. Once this is noted, their reconciliation is very easy.

units.la: çùm Debitor apud Iudæos solvendo non erat, dabat Iudex creditori litteras, quibus persequi poterat debitoris bona, quocunque tempore & loco ea reperiret, eaque post 90. dies liberè occupare, idque proclamari curabat iudex per præconem. Metzia f. 35. 2. & 108. 2.
units.tr: When a debtor among the Jews was not able to pay, the judge gave the creditor a letter by which he could pursue the debtor's goods, at whatever time and place he found them, and seize them freely after 90 days; and the judge saw to it that this was proclaimed by a herald. Metzia f. 35.2 and 108.2.

units.la: cùm Decem præcepta promulgabantur, populus quidem sonum audivit, sed distinctè verba non percepit, sicuti Moses. More Nevoch. ii. 32.
units.tr: When the Ten Commandments were proclaimed, the people indeed heard a sound, but did not perceive the words distinctly, as Moses did. More Nevochim ii. 32.

units.la: §. Decem in Synagoga esse debent, aliàs plurimas actiones omittunt. vid. Synagog. & Megillah c. 4. v. 3.
units.tr: Ten must be present in the synagogue, otherwise they omit very many actions. See Synagogue and Megillah c. 4 v. 3.

units.la: Decimæ. De illis varia in Massectot Maaser. Peah, & alibi curiosus lector reperiet; Nos hic de magno cumulo paucula libabimus.
units.tr: Tithes. There is much about these in the tractate Maaser, Peah, and elsewhere, which the curious reader will find; here we shall take only a few small sips from the great heap.

units.la: §. De decimis hæc est generalis regula כל שהוא אוכל ונשמר וגדולין מן הארץ הייב במעשרות Quodcunque cedit in cibum, quodque custoditur (i.e. quod non est communis iuris) quodque e terra nascitur, decimari debet. Maaserot cap.i. v.i.
units.tr: On tithes the general rule is this: "Whatever is taken as food, and is kept (that is, is not of common law), and grows from the earth, must be tithed." Maaserot ch. 1 v. 1.

units.la: §. Ex lege, decimatio erat pecorum, frugum & fructuum : cuius modus & mensura secundùm Scribas hæc erat. E frugibus triturandis & ventilabro purgatis. 1. Excipitur quinta pars pro Sacerdote : hæc vocatur תרומה גדולה oblatio magna. 2. Decima pars residui Levitæ cedit : vocabatur hæc מעשר ראשון decima prima. 3. Decima pars iterum è residuo tollenda, & comedenda Hierosolymis, aut redimenda : vocabatur hæc מעשר שני Decima secunda. 4. Levita Decimas dat è suo Sacerdoti, vocantur hæ מעשר המעשר Decima Decimarum. Hæc ex Peah & Demai paululum diducemus inferiùs.
units.tr: §. By the law, tithes were paid on livestock, grain and fruit. According to the Scribes, the manner and measure of this were as follows. From grain that has been threshed and cleaned with the winnowing fan: (1) a fifth part is taken for the priest; this is called [תרומה גדולה], the great offering. (2) The tenth part of what remains falls to the Levites; this was called [מעשר ראשון], the first tithe. (3) A tenth part is again taken from what remains, and is to be eaten at Jerusalem or redeemed; this was called [מעשר שני], the second tithe. (4) The Levite gives tithes from his own portion to the priest; these are called [מעשר המעשר], the tithe of tithes. We shall explain these matters from Peah and Demai a little further below.

units.la: §. Olerum decimatio est à Rabbinis מעשר ירק דרבנן Bab. Ioma sol 83 2. Non erat illa institutionis divinæ, sed humanæ; inter illa olera etiam numerantur הדגרונות quæ herba secundùm Scheviit c. 1. 1. etiam legibus anni septimi obnoxia est: ab Aruch illa vocatur מנטה & definitur esse herbam suavis odoris, quam in Synagogis spargunt. Item שבת de quo sic loquitur Gloss. in Bab. Avoda Zarah sol.7.2. שבת lingua Romana est Anethum & decimatur sive colligatur viride, sive maturum.
units.tr: §. The tithing of herbs is a rabbinical institution [מעשר ירק דרבנן]. Bab. Ioma fol. 83.2. It was not of divine institution but of human. Among those herbs are also counted the [הדגרונות], which, according to Sheviit ch. 1 mishnah 1, is also subject to the laws of the seventh year. The Aruch calls it [מנטה] and defines it as an herb of pleasant smell, which they scatter in the synagogues. Likewise [שבת], of which the Gloss speaks thus in Bab. Avoda Zarah fol. 7.2: [שבת] in the Roman language is dill, and it is tithed whether green or ripe.

units.la: Item τὸ κύμινον ןמכ qui fructus etiam inter decimanda numeratur Demai c. 2. 1. Confer Matth.23.23.
units.tr: Likewise [ןמכ] cumin, a fruit which is also counted among the things to be tithed, Demai ch. 2 mishnah 1. Compare Matt. 23.23.

units.la: §. Decimæ quæ dantur pauperibus, vocantur עשר יפ. Extra terram Israeliticam decimas non solvunt. Bava Batra sol.27.2.
units.tr: §. The tithes which are given to the poor are called [עשר יפ]. Outside the land of Israel they do not pay tithes. Bava Batra fol. 27.2.

units.la: §. Decimæ Sacerdotibus & Levitis, (de quorum decimis etiam locus modò citatus loquitur.) dabantur, ut tota Levitica trib9 Deo consecrata, semper cultu ei9 vacare posset, nec aratione aut satione detineretur. Decimas secundas præcepit lex tantùm in victualibus Hierosolymam asportare, eò quòd hoc necessario cogat eleemosynas inde facere, cùm non nisi in cibo & potu erogari potuerint. Maymon. More Nevoch III.39.
units.tr: §. Tithes were given to the priests and Levites (of whose tithes the passage just cited also speaks), so that the whole tribe of Levi, consecrated to God, might always be free for his worship and not be held back by ploughing or sowing. The law prescribed that second tithes be carried up to Jerusalem only in the form of victuals, because this necessarily compels one to make alms from them, since they could be spent only on food and drink. Maimonides, More Nevochim III.39.

units.la: §. Motanum Iudæ quidam à decimatione eximere studuerunt Hierof. Demai sol. 24. 4. cuius conaminis alia vix est ratio, quàm quòd regio illa iam nimis Ethnicissaret, & non exigerentur Decimæ ab Ethnicis. Idumæi enim qui ibi habitabant, Iudaicos quidem ritus amplexi erant, at cæterùm nec amici Iudæorum nec religionis.
units.tr: §. Some have tried to exempt the district of Motanum of Judah from tithing (Hierosolymitan Demai fol. 24.4). The only reason for this attempt is that the region had already become too heathen, and tithes were not exacted from Gentiles. For the Idumaeans who lived there had indeed embraced Jewish rites, but were neither friends of the Jews nor of their religion.

units.la: §. A Decimis liber est, qui agrum communem factum ןפאם occupavit, donec ventilaverit. Qui rem ad sacros usus devotam redimit, ad decimas tenetur donec quæstor templi ventilaverit. Peah c.1.5. A decimis liber est, qui fructus suos cum spicilegio pauperis commutaverit, accepti scilicet spicilegii respectu; si verò cum paupere commutat, quod aliàs pauperi debebatur decimas dare debet. Peah c.5.5.
units.tr: §. One is free from tithes who has occupied a field made common [ופאם] until he has winnowed. One who redeems a thing devoted to sacred uses is bound to tithes until the treasurer of the temple has winnowed. Peah ch. 1 mishnah 5. One is free from tithes who has exchanged his produce for a poor man's gleaning, namely with respect to the gleaning received. But if he exchanges with a poor man what was otherwise owed to the poor, he must give tithes. Peah ch. 5 mishnah 5.

units.la: § עשר
units.tr: § Tithe [עשר].

units.la: §. מעשר שבולת decimae spicae sunt quando p ter familias ex acervo, cui quaedam spicilegii spicae immixtae fuerunt, protert duas spicas, & unā acceptā dicit לקט שבולת זאת תהיה אם ודם ואם אינה שבולת הלקט יהיו המעשרות המחויבות לה בזאת השבולת האחרת Si hae spica pertinet ad spicilegium, bene est; si vero non, sint ipsi debita decima in hac altera spica; tradit deinde primam spicam pauperi, alteram vero Sacerdoti: Maymonides ad Peah cap. 5. 2.
units.tr: §. The tithe of an ear of grain [מעשר שבולת] arises when the householder, from a heap in which some ears of gleaning have been mixed, brings out two ears and, taking one, says: "Let this ear be gleaning. If it is an ear of gleaning, well and good; if not, let the tithes owed on it be owed on this other ear" [לקט שבולת זאת תהיה אם ודם ואם אינה שבולת הלקט יהיו המעשרות המחויבות לה בזאת השבולת האחרת]. Then he gives the first ear to the poor and the other to the priest. "If this ear belongs to the gleaning, well; if not, let the tithes owed on it be owed on this other ear" [Si hae spica pertinet ad spicilegium, bene est; si vero non, sint ipsi debita decima in hac altera spica]. Maimonides on Peah ch. 5 mishnah 2.

units.la: §. Qui vult avellere folia oleris sive herbarum, ad sublevandum onus, non debet avulsa seponere nisi postquam decimas ab iis sumpserit. Si quis olera emerit, & ea venditori reddere vult, ea reddere non potest, nisi antea decimas ex illis separaverit, & earum pecuniam venditori dederit: Si vero olera nondum suis manibus acceperit, à decimis liber est. Sic qui in via fructus reperit, & eos edere aut abscondere vult, debet decimas separare; at ab illis liber est, si illos vult abscondere aut seponere ne ab Ethnicis aut aliis diripiantur. Demai. cap. 2. 3. Qui cauponae farinam aut fructus dat, debet illos decimare, quia tales existimantur non omnia accurate observare, sed facile cum aliis rebus miscere. Idem observare debet qui aliquid dat socrui suae (solent enim illae mulierculae avaritiae deditae esse.) Demai. 3. 5. 6.
units.tr: §. One who wishes to pull off the leaves of vegetables or herbs, to lighten the load, must not set aside what is pulled off until he has first taken tithes from it. If someone has bought vegetables and wishes to return them to the seller, he cannot return them unless he has first separated tithes from them and given their price to the seller; but if he has not yet received the vegetables into his own hands, he is free from tithes. So too one who finds fruit on the road and wishes to eat or hide it must separate tithes; but he is free from them if he wishes to hide or set it aside so that it is not seized by Gentiles or others. Demai ch. 2 mishnah 3. One who gives flour or fruit to an innkeeper ought to tithe it, because such people are thought not to observe everything accurately, but easily to mix things with others. The same should be observed by one who gives anything to his mother-in-law, for such little women are wont to be given to avarice. Demai 3.5.6.

units.la: §. Qui promisit socio suo, se cum ipso cibum sumpturum, sed deinde ipsi ob decimas suspeătus fit, cum illo edere potest primo die septimanæ,aut primo nuptiarum die, sed non ultra. Ingressus in urbem si quis aliquem interrogat, quis est hic ‎נאמן‎ in decimis (i.e. quis est cui fidere possim in frugibus, illas esse decimatas.) & ille ipsi monstret N. Ille quem monstravit æstimatur pro ‎נאמן‎. Demai c.4. in Maym. ‎נאמן‎ idem est ac ἀληθινὸς & ut plurimùm denotat eum cuius verbum & testimonium in re quavis acceptandum : Et quid propriè ‎נאמן‎ respectu frugum fit, percipies ex Chagigah sol.24.2.
units.tr: §. One who has promised his companion that he would eat food with him, but afterwards became suspicious of him concerning tithes, may eat with him on the first day of the week or on the first day of the wedding, but not beyond. If someone entering a city asks, "Who here is [נאמן] trustworthy in tithes?" (that is, who is one I can trust regarding produce, that it has been tithed), and the man points out N., he who was pointed out is esteemed as [נאמן]. Demai ch. 4 in Maimonides. [נאמן] is the same as [ἀληθινὸς], and it usually denotes one whose word and testimony is to be accepted in any matter. What [נאמן] properly means with respect to produce you will perceive from Chagigah fol. 24.2.

units.la: Hominibus Iudæa ‎נאמנים‎ fides habenda de puritate vini & olei. Id est, hominibus nomine & facie non notis Sacerdotibus, tamen cùm offerrent vinum & oleum,fides habebatur de eius puritate,ob ipsum locum habitationis.
units.tr: Men in Judea are to be believed concerning the purity of wine and oil [נאמנים]. That is, to priests who did not know the men by name or face, yet when they offered wine and oil, credence was given to its purity, on account of the place of their dwelling itself.

units.la: §. Qui panem àpistore aut à ‎פלוני‎ proxeneta panis sumit, debet ab illo separare ‎תרומה‎ ‎מעשר‎ oblationem decimarum, dicendo unum ex centum, quod est in hoc latere, sit oblatio decimarum. Demai. c.5.1.4.
units.tr: §. One who takes bread from a baker, or from [פלוני], a bread-seller, must separate from it the [תרומה מעשר], the offering of tithes, saying that one in a hundred of what is in this loaf is to be the offering of tithes. Demai ch. 5 mishnah 1, 4.

units.la: §. A decimis liber est,qui agrum suum pauperibus communem fecerit.Peah 6.1.inMaym. Cùm decimas pauperum porrigunt, unicuique non minùs quàm dimidium Cabum dant. Pauperi verò qui de loco in locum Eleemosynas exigit, non minus dant ‎מככר בפונדיון‎ pane qui dimidiatum in Sufeum valet. Peah.8.5.7.
units.tr: §. One is free from tithes who has made his field common to the poor. Peah 6.1 in Maimonides. When they give the tithes to the poor, they give to each not less than half a cab. But to a poor man who begs alms from place to place, they give not less than a loaf [מככר בפונדיון] which is worth half a sufeum. Peah 8.5.7.

units.la: §. Ex frugibus Israelitarum decimæ solvi possunt pro gentili, & ex frugibus gentilis pro Israelita &c. Demai. c.5.9.Trumam debebant omnia illa quæ in ‎צץ נקוב‎ vase concavo & terra repleto crescebant, non autem illa quæ in
units.tr: §. Tithes from the produce of Israelites may be paid on behalf of a Gentile, and from the produce of a Gentile on behalf of an Israelite, and so on. Demai ch. 5 mishnah 9. They owed terumah for all those things which grew in a hollow [צץ נקוב] vessel filled with earth, but not those which grew in a

units.la: vase plano proveniebant ibid. Qui ab alienigena conduxit agrum certâ summâ pecuniæ, debet, antequam Domino agri satisfaciat, decimas persolvere; si agrum conduxit à Sacerdote aut Levita, decimæ sunt Domini agri. Demai cap.6. Prohibitum est solvere decimas in Sabbatho aut die festo. Maymon ad v.1.c.7. Demai.
units.tr: flat vessel, ibid. One who has leased a field from a foreigner for a fixed sum of money must pay the tithes before he satisfies the Lord of the field; if he leased the field from a priest or Levite, the tithes belong to the lord of the field. Demai ch. 6. It is forbidden to pay tithes on the Sabbath or a festival day. Maimonides on v. 1 ch. 7. Demai.

units.la: §. Decimas pecoris qui separat, colligit omnes agnos in stabulum, cui facit ostium parvum, ut non possint egredi duo simul; constituuntur matres illorum foris, quæ balant, audi- entes autem vocem ipsarum agni egrediuntur unus post alterum. Tum incipit numerare virgâ, unus, duo, tres: & decimum egredientem percutit virgâ rubricatâ, dicens ista est decima. Maymon. Hal.Becorot. c.7.1. de decimis vid.plura apud Demai.
units.tr: §. One who separates the tithe of livestock gathers all the lambs into a fold, which has a small door so that no two can go out together. Their mothers are placed outside, bleating, and the lambs, hearing their voices, come out one after another. Then he begins to count with a rod, "one, two, three," and strikes the tenth one as it comes out with a red-dyed rod, saying, "This is the tithe." Maimonides, Hilchot Behorot ch. 7.1. For more on tithes see Demai.

units.la: §. De Decimarum confessione vid. Confessio.
units.tr: §. On the confession of tithes see Confessio.

units.la: DEFRAUDATIO.
units.tr: DEFRAUDATION.

units.la: semper sit homo cautus de fraude uxoris suæ, quando enim lachrymæ eius prodeunt, tunc fraus eius proxima est.
units.tr: A man should always be cautious about the deceit of his wife, for when her tears appear, her deceit is near at hand.

units.la: §. Tria sunt ante quæ non clauditur cortina i.e. non celari possunt coram Deo; Defraudatio, Rapina & Idololatria; Ad ea nunquam connivet Deus, sed perpetuus ipsorum ultor existit. Rabh Chasda dixit; Omnes portæ claudi possunt coram Deo חוץ משער אונאית excepta porta defraudationis. Bab.Beva Metzia f.59.1.
units.tr: There are three things before which the curtain is not closed, that is, which cannot be hidden from God: defrauding, robbery and idolatry. God never overlooks these, but always remains their avenger. Rabh Chasda said: all gates can be closed before God except the gate of defrauding [חוץ משער אונאות]. Bab. Beva Metzia f. 59.1.

units.la: דכא Demai, definitur הפסף שלא נורע אם הוציאו מסנו מתנות הק"בה illud de quo dubitatur, an decima & dona quæ Deo debentur ex illo data fuerint. Hi autem sunt הקלין illa quæ ctus fit, cum illo edere potest primo die septimanæ,aut primo nuptiarum die, sed non ultra. Ingressus in urbem si quis aliquem interrogat, quis est hic ‎נאמן in decimis (i. e. quis est cui fidere possim in frugibus, illas esse decimatas.) & ille ipsi monstret N. Ille quem monstravit æstimatur pro ‎נאמן. Demai c.4. in Maym. ‎נאמן idem est ac ἀληθινὸς & ut plurimùm denotat eum cuius verbum & testimonium in re quavis acceptandum : Et quid propriè ‎נאמן respectu frugum fit, percipies ex Chagigah sol.24.2.
units.tr: Demai, defined as that about which it is doubted whether tithes and the gifts due to God were given from it. These are the things that are not bound to tithing, which one may eat with him on the first day of the week, or on the first day of his wedding, but not beyond that. If someone entering a city asks, "Who is this faithful one in tithes?" (that is, who is someone I may trust concerning the produce, that it has been tithed), and he points out N., the one he pointed out is regarded as faithful. Demai c.4. in Maimonides. "Faithful" is the same as truthful, and usually denotes one whose word and testimony are to be accepted in any matter. What "faithful" properly means with respect to produce you will learn from Chagigah 24.2.

units.la: Hominibus Iudaa ‎נאמנין fides habenda de puritate vini & olei. Id est, hominibus nomine & facie non notis Sacerdotibus, tamen cùm offerrent vinum & oleum,fides habebatur de eius puritate,ob ipsum locum habitationis.
units.tr: To the men of Judea, the faithful: trust is to be placed in the purity of wine and oil. That is, to priests whose name and face were not known, yet when they offered wine and oil, trust was given to its purity, on account of the place where they lived.

units.la: §. Qui panem à pistore aut à ‎פלטר proxeneta panis sumit, debet ab illo separare ‎תרומת מעשר oblationem decimarum, dicendo unum ex centum, quod est in hoc latere, sit oblatio decimarum. Demai. c.5.1.4.
units.tr: Whoever takes bread from a baker, or from a palter (proxeneta panis, a bread-broker), must separate from it the tithe offering [תרומת מעשר], saying: let one in a hundred, which is in this loaf, be the tithe offering. Demai c.5.1.4.

units.la: §. A decimis liber est,qui agrum suum pauperibus communem fecerit.Peah 6.1.inMaym. Cùm decimas pauperum porrigunt, unicuique non minùs quàm dimidium Cabum dant. Pauperi verò qui de loco in locum Eleemosynas exigit, non minus dant ‎מככר בפונדיון pane qui dimidiatum ‎וו Sufaum valet. Peah.8.5.7.
units.tr: One who has made his field common to the poor is free from tithes. Peah 6.1, in Maym. When they give the tithes to the poor, they give each not less than half a cab. To a poor man who goes from place to place begging alms, they give not less than a loaf worth a half-pundion Sufaum [the value of a loaf of bread]. Peah 8.5.7.

units.la: §. Ex frugibus Israelitarum decimæ solvi possunt pro gentili, & ex frugibus gentilis pro Israelita &c. Demai. c.5.9.Trumam debebant omnia illa quæ in ‎קוב עציץ vase concavo & terra repleto crescebant, non autem illa quæ in vase plano proveniebant ibid. Qui ab alienigena conduxit agrum certâ summâ pecuniæ, debet, antequam Domino agri satisfaciat, decimas persolvere; si agrum conduxit à Sacerdote aut Levita, decimæ sunt Domini agri. Demai cap.6. Prohibitum est solvere decimas in Sabbatho aut die festo. Maymon ad v.1.c.7. Demai.
units.tr: From the produce of Israelites tithes may be paid on behalf of a Gentile, and from the produce of a Gentile on behalf of an Israelite, and so on. Demai c.5.9. The heave offering was owed on all that grew in a hollow vessel filled with earth, but not on what grew in a flat vessel. Ibid. One who rents a field from a foreigner for a fixed sum of money must pay the tithes before he satisfies the owner of the field; if he rented it from a priest or a Levite, the tithes belong to the owner of the field. Demai c.6. It is forbidden to pay tithes on the Sabbath or on a festival day. Maimonides on v.1, c.7. Demai.

units.la: §. Decimas pecoris qui separat, colligit omnes agnos in stabulum, cui facit ostium parvum, ut non possint egredi duo simul; constituuntur matres illorum foris, quæ balant, audientes autem vocem ipsarum agni egrediuntur unus post alterum. Tum incipit numerare virgâ, unus, duo, tres: & decimum egredientem percutit virgâ rubricatâ, dicens ista est decima. Maymon. Hal. Becorot. c.7.1. de decimis vid.plura apud Demai.
units.tr: One who separates the tithe of livestock gathers all the lambs into a fold that has a small door, so that no two can go out together. Their mothers are stationed outside, bleating; hearing their voices, the lambs come out one after another. Then he begins to count with a rod, one, two, three, and the tenth one as it comes out he strikes with a rod dipped in red, saying: this is the tithe. Maimonides, Hal. Becorot c.7.1. More on tithes may be found in Demai.

units.la: §. De Decimarum confessione vid. Confessio.
units.tr: On the confession of tithes see Confessio.

units.la: DEFRAUDATIO.
units.tr: DEFRAUDATION.

units.la: semper fit homo cautus de fraude uxoris suæ, quando enim lachrymæ eius prodeunt, tunc fraus eius proxima est.
units.tr: A man should always be cautious about the deceit of his wife, for when her tears appear, her deceit is near at hand.

units.la: §. Tria sunt ante quæ non clauditur cortina i.e. non celari possunt coram Deo; Defraudatio, Rapina & Idololatria; Ad ea nunquam connivet Deus, sed perpetuus ipsorum ultor existit. Rabh Chasda dixit; Omnes portæ claudi possunt coram Deo חוץ משער אונאות excepta porta defraudationis. Bab.Beva Metzia f.59.1.
units.tr: There are three things before which the curtain is not closed, that is, which cannot be hidden from God: defrauding, robbery and idolatry. God never overlooks these, but always remains their avenger. Rabh Chasda said: all gates can be closed before God except the gate of defrauding [חוץ משער אונאות]. Bab. Beva Metzia f. 59.1.

units.la: דכאי Demai, definitur הספק שלא נודע אם הוציאו ממנו מתנות הק"בת illud de quo dubitatur, an decima & dona quæ Deo debentur ex illo data fuerint. Hi autem sunt הקליץ illa quæ non ad Demai tenentur הִשִּׁתִין ficuum sylvestrium genus, פּוּלְצַארְקִי quod Arucho est forsan malogranata. יִוִּירִי Sorbus arbor. בנות שוח (vid.ficus) בנות שקמה (vid.Lex.Buxt.) Dactyli a palma decidui. גופני Species oleris sive herbae anetho similis. חנצפו Capparis (quod est ex Arabico קאפר) אוג Arbutsti cuiusdam fructus specialis terrae Israeliticae. Acetum terrae Israeliticae quod non fiebat ex vino sed Dactylis : Et Coriandrum Demai c.1.1.
units.tr: Demai, defined as that about which it is doubted whether tithes and the gifts due to God were given from it. These are the things not subject to Demai: the wild fig, a kind of sylvan fig [השתין]; pulzarqi, which Aruch thinks is perhaps the pomegranate; yivri, the sorb tree; the dates of the sycamore (see the fig; see Buxtorf's Lexicon); dates fallen from the palm; gufni, a kind of herb like dill; hancafu, caper (from the Arabic qapar); ug, a particular fruit of the land of Israel; the vinegar of the land of Israel, which was made not from wine but from dates; and coriander. Demai c.1.1.

units.la: §. Demai hoc privilegium habet, ut liberum fit à כיעור excussione in fine anni 3. & 7. possit comedi à lugente, afferri Hierosolymas & iterum efferri,plebeiis ad esum dari; quae aliàs circa decimas secundas fieri non poterant. Demai. c.1.2.
units.tr: Demai has this privilege: it is freed from the shaking out at the end of the third and seventh years; it may be eaten by a mourner, brought to Jerusalem and carried out again, and given to commoners to eat, which otherwise could not be done with second tithes. Demai c.1.2.

units.la: §. A Demai liber est, qui fructus emit ad ferendum, aut ad cibanda pecora, mucorem vini ad coria praeparanda, oleum pro lucerna, aut ad ungenda vasa. Item locus מכויב (v.f. 1.) ibid.v.3.
units.tr: One is free from Demai who buys produce for feeding animals or for carrying, wine lees for preparing hides, oil for a lamp or for anointing vessels. Likewise a place [מכויב]. Ibid. v.3.

units.la: §. Illa quae in omni loco ob Demai decimanda veniunt haec sunt: Palathae ficuum, Dactyli, ryza, Cuminum. Tabernariis vt Demai vendere non licet, nisi במה גסה יהיו משעיין magnâ utantur mensurâ, ut faciunt המיסונורית magni mercatores frumenti; Mensura autem גסה definitur, esse in aridis tres cabos, in liquoribus vero quantum pro denario divenditur.
units.tr: Those things which are subject to tithing in every place are these: dried figs, dates, rice, cumin. Shopkeepers may not sell as Demai unless they use a large measure [במה גסה], as the great grain merchants do. A large measure is defined as three cabs for dry goods, and for liquids as much as is sold for a denarius.

units.la: Demai cap.2. vt Demai dari potest pauperibus in cibum, ut & hospitibus, quales sunt milites regis transeuntes. Triticum illud quod molitori peregrino, Cutheo aut uni ex הארץ עם plebeio molcndum traditur, Demai est, praesumitur enim illos decimas non bene observare. A τῳ Demai non separantur pauperum decimę anno secundo, neque locum ubi esse debet designant. Demai c.3.4. Qui plura desiderat ipsum tract. Demai consulat.
units.tr: Demai c.2. What is Demai may be given to the poor for food, as also to guests, such as the king's soldiers passing through. Wheat that is handed over to a foreign miller, or to a Cuthean, or to one of the common people [עם הארץ] to be ground, is Demai, for it is presumed that they do not observe the tithes properly. From what is Demai the tithes of the poor are not separated in the second year, nor do they designate the place where they ought to be. Demai c.3.4. Whoever desires more should consult the tractate Demai.

units.la: DENARIUS דינר & זוז Zuz Rabbinis idem valent. Aruch in זוו. Quarta ars sicli argentei est זוז חד דנסף Zuz unus argenti Gloss. in Bav. Batra sol. 166.1. Denarios vocant lingua Gemarist̄ica Sufim.
units.tr: Denarius [דינר] and zuz [זוז] are equal in value among the rabbis. Aruch on zuz. A quarter of a silver shekel is zuz one silver piece. Gloss on Bava Batra fol. 166.1. In the Gemara language they call denarii sufim.

units.la: §. In Talmudicis Ducenti Sufæi vel Denarii erant summa admodum celebris, & frequentissimæ mentionis. Chetubh. c.1.3. Si quis grandavior coeat cum minorenni, aut quis minorennis cum grandaeviori, aut sauciata, Dos earum est מאתים Ducentorum fusaorum. Ita v. 2. Virginis dos est ducentorum fusaorum.
units.tr: In the Talmud the two hundred sufaei, or denarii, are a very famous sum and mentioned very often. Ketubot c.1.3. If an older man has intercourse with a minor, or a minor with an older man, or a woman who has been injured, their dowry is two hundred sufaei [מאתים]. So also v.2: the dowry of a virgin is two hundred sufaei.

units.la: §. Bava Kama c.8.6. Si quis impingat alteri colaphum in maxillam זוו מאתי לו נותן Det ei ducentos fusaos. Chetubh. sol. 17.1. Fœmina iam vidua facta, aut divortio dimissa, quae virgo nupta erat, habeat pro dote ducentos fusaos.
units.tr: Bava Kama c.8.6. If anyone strikes another on the cheek, he shall give him two hundred sufaei [זוז מאתים]. Ketubot fol. 17.1. A woman who has become a widow, or who has been divorced, having been a married virgin, shall have two hundred sufaei as her dowry.

units.la: Haec celebratissima summa etiam est in ore discipulorum Marci. vi.37.
units.tr: This very well-known sum is also on the lips of the disciples of Mark 6.37.

units.la: §. Denarius ille qui Christo allatus fuit Marci.xii.16. fuit Denarius Cæsareanus דינרא קיסרנא id est fuit alius formæ & inscriptionis, quàm communes זוזים Sufei erant. De tali Denario mentio fit Bab. Avoda Zarah folio 6.2. התנא מינאות דשרה לירח דינרא
units.tr: The denarius that was brought to Christ, Mark 12.16, was a Caesarean denarius [דינרא קיסרנא], that is, it was of a different form and inscription from the common zuzim [זוזים] of the Sufaei. Mention of such a denarius is made in Bab. Avoda Zarah folio 6.2: the Tanna [...] of the denarius [...].

units.la: [Hebrew and Greek words above are transcribed as far as legible; the last line is partly uncertain.]
units.tr: [The Hebrew and Greek words above are transcribed as far as they are legible; the last line is partly uncertain.]

units.la: Ethnicus quidam misit R.Iehuda principi Denarium Cæsareanum &c. Probabile etiam est, Denarium illum fuisse argenteum, secundum illum Canonem, qui legitur in Bava Bathra sol.166.1. דינרין סתם משם של כסף Denarii absolutè positi, intelligendi sunt denarii argentei.
units.tr: A certain heathen sent to R. Jehudah the prince a Caesarean denarius, etc. It is also probable that that denarius was of silver, according to that canon which is read in Bava Bathra fol. 166.1: denarii absolutely put are to be understood as silver denarii.

units.la: §. Denarius aureus valebat viginti quinque denarios argenteos. Gloss. ad Cheritut. c.1.v.7. vid. Moneta.
units.tr: The gold denarius was worth twenty-five silver denarii. Gloss on Cheritut ch. 1 v. 7. See Moneta.

units.la: DESPONSATIO.
units.tr: Betrothal

units.la: In illa uxor sibi quasdam facultates reservabat in proprium usum, extra dotem in contractu matrimoniali descriptam, illæ deinde vocabantur נכסי מלוג facultates usuariæ. B.Kama p.90.1.
units.tr: In that arrangement the wife kept for her own use certain property beyond the dowry described in the marriage contract. This was then called נכסי מלוג [nechasei milug], usufructuary property. B. Kama p. 90.1.

units.la: §. Triplici modo desponsatur fœmina, pecuniâ scilicet, aut scripto aut coitu; & sic desponsata, tametsi adhuc non maritata, nec in domum viri introducta, illius tamen est uxor; si quis cum ea rem habuerit, à Synedrio morte plectendus est. Maym. Hal. אישות cap.1. vid. Nuptiæ.
units.tr: A woman is betrothed in three ways: by money, by writing, or by intercourse. A woman so betrothed, although not yet married nor brought into her husband's house, is nevertheless his wife; if anyone has relations with her, he is to be put to death by the Sanhedrin. Maimonides, Hilchot Ishut ch. 1. See Nuptiae.

units.la: DEUS tria singulis diebus מכרן promulgando quasi admiratur, cœlibem qui habitat in urbe & non peccat; pauperem, rem amissam restituentem; divitem fructus suos verecundè decimantem. Pesachim f.113 1.
units.tr: God, as it were, marvels every day at three things, which are proclaimed: a celibate man who lives in a city and does not sin; a poor man who restores lost property; and a rich man who modestly tithes his produce. Pesachim f. 113.1.

units.la: §. In Dei operibus si quid pravi videatur esse, ignorantiæ animæ tribuendum; hæc ignorantia aperte fatenda. Cosri 376 380.
units.tr: If anything in God's works seems amiss, it is to be attributed to the ignorance of the soul, and this ignorance must be openly confessed. Cosri 376-380.

units.la: §. Actiones Dei omnes bonæ sunt, quia Deus nihil facit præter existentiam; existentia autem omnis bona est; mala verò sunt privationes, à quibus actio non dependet. More Nevoch. iii.10.
units.tr: All God's actions are good, because God does nothing except existence, and all existence is good; evils are privations, on which action does not depend. More Nevochim iii. 10.

units.la: §. An Deus voluntate absoluta בחפץ משוט quempiam puniat, sine iusta & nota causa, vid. Abarbanel in Iesai. xxxviii.
units.tr: Whether God by absolute will, בחפץ משוט [bechefetz mashut], punishes anyone without a just and known cause, see Abarbanel on Isaiah 38.

units.la: §. Multa loquuntur Iudæi de Dei sigillo חותמו קבה של ה"א Hierof. Sanhed sol. 18. מה חותמו קבה"ש Quodnam est sigillum Sancti benedicti. R. Bibai dicit אמת veritas. מהו אמת At quid est veritas? R. Bon dicit אלהים חיים ומלך עולם Deus vivens & Rex æternus. Resh Lakisch dicit א est prima litera Alphabeti, מ media, & ת ultima; quasi diceret ego Iehova sum primus, nec quicquam accepi à quopiam, & prater me non est Deus &c. Bab. Sanhedrin sol. 64.1. & Ioma sol. 69.2. historia est de Synagoga magna eiulante נפל להו מיתקא מרקיעא דהוא כתוב בה אמת Cecidit tandem iis schedula de firmamento, in qua scriptum erat אמת veritas. R Chanina dicit. Inde disce, quòd sigillum Dei est veritas. Christus est Character Patris, Veritas Patris, τύπον ὁ πατὴρ ἱστορήσει Ioh. vi. 27. & Ioh. xiv. 6. vid. infra Veritas.
units.tr: The Jews say much about the seal of God, חותמו של הקב"ה [chotamo shel hakadosh baruch hu]. Hierosolymitan Sanhedrin fol. 18: "What is the seal of the Holy One, blessed be he? R. Bibai says: truth," אמת [emet]; "But what is truth? R. Bon says: the living God and eternal King," אלהים חיים ומלך עולם [Elohim chayim umelech olam]. "Resh Lakish says: Aleph is the first letter of the alphabet, mem the middle, and tav the last; as if to say, I, Jehovah, am first, and have received nothing from anyone, and beside me there is no God," etc. Babylonian Sanhedrin fol. 64.1 and Yoma fol. 69.2. The story is about the Great Synagogue lamenting: "A schedule fell to them from the firmament, on which was written אמת [emet], truth." R. Chanina says: "From this learn that the seal of God is truth." Christ is the character of the Father, the truth of the Father: τύπον ὁ πατὴρ [typon ho patēr], John 6:27 and John 14:6. See below, Veritas.

units.la: Deus Benedictus non facit ut homines carnales, qui primò ponunt suum nomen, deinde honoris titulum, veluti N. Augustus. N. Imperator Leresch.Rabba sect.1. Dei nomina vid. in N.
units.tr: Blessed God does not act as carnal men do, who first put their own name and then an honorific title, as "N. Augustus, N. Imperator." Bereshit Rabba sect. 1. For the names of God see under N.

units.la: Deus Benedictus non sumit ultionem ab aliquo populo, nisi donec legerit אורוגלוגין שלה obligationem eius, quantum debeat. Beresch. R. S. 28.
units.tr: Blessed God does not take vengeance on any people until he has read their obligation, אורוגלוגין שלה [orugeloghin shelah], and how much they owe. Bereshit Rabba 28.

units.la: Deus inter homines excelsus respicit excelsum, neque excellens respicit humilem; sed Deus longè aliter, ipse est excelsus & respicit humiles. Sotah. sol. 5. 1. Quando Deus recordatur filiorum suorum cum dolore habitantium inter gentes, duas ingentes emittit lachrymas in mare magnum, quarum sonus auditur ab una extremitate Mundi ad alteram, & ille est tertiæ tremor. Beracot sol.59.1.
units.tr: Among men the high regards the high, and the excellent does not regard the lowly; but God is quite otherwise: he is high and regards the humble. Sotah fol. 5.1. When God remembers his sons dwelling among the nations with grief, he sends forth two great tears into the great sea, whose sound is heard from one end of the world to the other; and that is the trembling of the third. Berachot fol. 59.1.

units.la: §. Quando Deus Misericors venit ad liberandum Israelem ex Ægypto, non misit legatum vel angelum, sed Deus Bened. ipsemet venit. Hierof. Horaiot cap.3. ab init. לא חלי ולא מרגיש גברא דמריא סייעית Nulla agritudine afficitur, nec quicquam curat is, quem Dominus adiuvat. Bab.Ioma sol.22.2.
units.tr: When the merciful God came to free Israel from Egypt, he sent no envoy or angel, but blessed God himself came. Jerusalem Talmud, Horayot ch. 3, beginning. "He is not afflicted by any distress, nor does he care for the man whom the Lord helps," לא חלי ולא מרגיש גברא דמריא סייעית [la chali velo margish gavra demarya sayiit]. Babylonian Yoma fol. 22.2.

units.la: §. Decem nomina Rabbini Deo attribuerunt. vid.Leusdenium in notis ad Pirke Avoth. Buxtorf. in Lex. Talm. pag.90. & in radicibus מקום, שמים, שכינה, גבורה, יתכרך. Vocant ipsum in libro Cosri semper אלקים vel אלהים, ne promiscuo usu ptophanent nomen אלוהים.
units.tr: The rabbis attributed ten names to God. See Leusden in his notes on Pirke Avot; Buxtorf in Lex. Talm. p. 90, and under the roots מקום [makom], שמים [shamayim], שכינה [shekhinah], גבורה [gevurah], יתברך [yitbarakh]. In the book Cosri they always call him אלקים [Elokim] or אלהים [Elohim], so that they do not profane the name אלוהים [Eloah] by promiscuous use.

units.la: DICERE אמר in historia Creationis intelligitur de voluntate Dei. More Nevoch.1.68.
units.tr: "To say," אמר [amar], in the account of creation is understood of God's will. More Nevochim 1.68.

units.la: DIES. Quomodo Iudæi diem supputent vid. Christus.
units.tr: DAYS. How the Jews reckon the day; see Christ.

units.la: §. Totus dies idoneus est ad lectionem Megillæ, item hymni quem vocant הלל, ad clangorem tubæ, ad gestationem palmarum לתפלת המוספין ad orationem supererogatoriam, ad confessionem super iuvencos, confessionem decimarum, confessionem diei expiationum, ad manus impositionem, mactationem, תנופה agitationem, חגשה &c. ad potandam Sotah, ad decollandum vitulum, ad leprosi purificationem. Tota nox idonea est ad manipuli demessionem, suffumigationem adipum & membrorum. Megillah c.2. v.5.6. Noctu iudicandum non est, sed interdiu, fi tractantur iudicia capitalia; fi vero tractatur Iudi-ium Pecuniarium, potuit illud interdiu inceptum noctu termi.nari. Sanhed. c.4.v 1. Peffimi homines in iudicio Christi facientes opus tenebrarum, hunc Canonem non obferyarunt.
units.tr: §. The whole day is suitable for reading the Megillah, likewise for the hymn called Hallel, for the sounding of the trumpet, for carrying palms for the additional prayer (musaphin), for supererogatory prayer, for the confession over the heifer, the confession of tithes, the confession of the Day of Atonement, for the laying on of hands, for slaughter, for waving (tenufah), for lifting up (hagashah), etc., for giving the Sotah to drink, for beheading the calf, and for the purification of a leper. The whole night is suitable for reaping the sheaf and for burning the fat and the limbs. Megillah c.2 v.5, 6. Judgment is not to be given by night but by day, if capital cases are being handled. If a monetary case is being handled, a trial begun by day may be concluded by night. Sanhed. c.4 v.1. Wicked men, doing the works of darkness at the judgment of Christ, did not observe this canon.

units.la: §. De dilucidi distinctionibus vid. suo loco de Hebdomadis supputatione v.f.1. in H.
units.tr: §. On the distinctions of the day, see in its place on the reckoning of the weeks, v.f.1. in H.

units.la: DIGITIS micando & fortem projiciendo in templo munia diuidebant Ioma c. 2. 1. Ab initio omnium ille, qui voluit purgare altare a cineribus, illud peragere poterat; Si plurimi erant qui hoc facere intendebant, cursu certarunt, & ille qui alios quatuor cubitos in gradibus altaris anteverterat, illud opus perficere potuit. Si duo erant aequales, rafectus cultus dicebat Micare digitus; cum autem aliquando accidisset, ut unus alterum de gradibus deturbasset, & ille crus fregisset, Synedrium ordinavit, ut in posterum forte rem decideret. In micatione digitorum In micatione digitorum produxerunt vel elevarunt digitum unum, aut duos, sed non elevarunt pollicem in Sanctuario, id est, ad micationem non licuit pollice uti. Vide Commentarium Maymon. ad locum Ioma c.2.1.
units.tr: By flicking their fingers and casting lots in the Temple, they distributed the duties. Joma c.2 §1. From the beginning of all, whoever wished to clear the altar of ashes could do so. If many intended to do this, they competed in a race, and whoever had outstripped the others by four cubits on the steps of the altar could complete the task. If there were two equal, they decided by flicking a finger. But when it once happened that one pushed the other off the steps and broke his leg, the Sanhedrin ordered that in future the matter be settled by lot. In the flicking of fingers they extended or raised one finger or two, but they did not raise the thumb in the Sanctuary; that is, in flicking it was not permitted to use the thumb. See the commentary of Maimonides on the passage Joma c.2 §1.

units.la: §. Quare acuti sunt digiti? quia si audiat homo verbum inhonestum, infigat digitos in aures ne audiat. Keturbhot. f.5.2.
units.tr: §. Why are the fingers pointed? Because if a man hears a dishonourable word, he thrusts his fingers into his ears so as not to hear it. Keturbhot f.5.2.

units.la: DIOCLETIANUS Imperator: eius saepius mentio fit in Talmude Hierof ut in Beracot sol.61. Cum Tiberiada accederet Rex Diocletianus viderunt R.(bajam, fundentium sepulcrorum
units.tr: DIOCLETIAN, the Emperor: his name is mentioned often in the Jerusalem Talmud, as in Berachot fol. 61: When King Diocletian was approaching Tiberias, they saw R. Bajam pouring out the graves

units.la: L ut ipsum videret. Vid. Hierof. Nasir sol. 56.1.
units.tr: so that he might see him. See Jerusalem Nazir fol. 56.1.

units.la: §. דיקליטינוס Dicletinus congregavit fluvios & confecit mare Apamia. Idem recitatur in Chetubbot sol.35.2. atque ibi vocatur Docletianus דוקליטינוס.
units.tr: §. Diclinus (Diocletian) gathered the rivers and made the sea of Apamea. The same is recited in Ketubot fol. 35.2, where he is called Docletianus.

units.la: §. Pueri R. Iehudæ iótibus contuderunt דיקלוט Diclot porcarium; Evasit ille tandem Rex, & propter hoc factum expostulavit cum Rabbinis; responderunt illi: Diclot חזירא porcarium contempsimus דיקליטיאנוס מלכא Diocletianum regem non contemnimus. Hierof. Trumot sol. 46.2.3.
units.tr: §. The boys of R. Judah struck Diclot, a swineherd, with blows. He escaped at last and became king, and on account of this deed he complained to the rabbis. They answered him: We despised Diclot the swineherd; we do not despise King Diocletian. Jerusalem Trumot fol. 46.2, 3.

units.la: §. Curavit Diocletianus inscriptionem poni in foro Zur sive Tyri, in æternum amoris & beneficii erga cives monumentum. Exstat illa Hier.Avod.Zarah. sol. 39.4. אנא דיקלטיאנוס מלכא שבנית אהן ידידת דצור לגדיית דארקליס אחי תמניא יומין Ego Diocletianus Rex hoc forum Tyri condidi fortunæ fratris mei (Maximiani) Herculii, spatio octoginta dierum. De Diocletiano etiam vide loca Hierof. Ioma sol.41.4. Schevuot sol.34.4. Scheviit sol.38.4.
units.tr: §. Diocletian had an inscription placed in the forum of Zur, or Tyre, as a lasting monument of his love and benefaction towards the citizens. It is extant in Jerusalem Avodah Zarah fol. 39.4: I, Diocletian the king, built this forum of Tyre for the fortune of my brother Herculius (Maximian), within the space of eighty days. On Diocletian see also the passages of the Jerusalem Talmud, Joma fol. 41.4, Shevuot fol. 34.4, Shevi'it fol. 38.4.

units.la: Discipuli Sapientum תלמידי חכמים non solum dicuntur illi, qui sapientiæ studiosi, sed qui & ipsi sapientes erant, & tamen modestiæ causâ libentius sapientum discipuli, quàm σοφοί Sapientes audire malebant;
units.tr: The disciples of the wise (talmide chachamim) are called not only those who are eager for wisdom, but also those who were themselves wise. Yet out of modesty they preferred to be called disciples of the sages rather than to hear themselves called sophoi (wise men).

units.la: §. In urbe, in qua capita sunt תלמידי חכמים Discipuli sapientum, ne habites, quia non est ibi metus Domini. Pesachim sol.113.1. Schabbat folio 11.1.
units.tr: §. In a city in which there are the heads, the disciples of the wise, do not live there, for there is no fear of the Lord. Pesachim fol. 113.1; Shabbat fol. 11.1.

units.la: §. Discipuli sapientum erant in Synedrio magno in tribus ordinibus collocati, in quolibet ordine 23. ex illis cooptabantur Iudices in Sanhedrin, & si quid haberent quod dicerent in defensionem accusati, admittebantur in loco iudicii. Maymon. Hal. Sanh. drin c.1. 7. & c.10.8.
units.tr: §. The disciples of the wise were placed in the Great Sanhedrin in three ranks, twenty-three in each rank. From among them judges were chosen for the Sanhedrin, and if they had anything to say in defence of the accused, they were admitted into the place of judgment. Maimonides, Hilchot Sanhedrin c.1 §7 and c.10 §8.

units.la: §. De honore & immunitatibus discipulorum sapientum vid. יורה דיעה H. ה'ת.vid.etiam חכרים in C. & promotionem. Discipulos ad pedes praeceptorum sedisse apparet ex Pirke Avot. c. 1. פתאכ Pulverisa te in pulvere pedum sapientum,&c. vid.Lex Talm. Buxt. p.1146.
units.tr: §. On the honour and immunities of the disciples of the wise, see Yoreh De'ah, H. HT; see also the passages on chachamim in C. and on promotion. That the disciples sat at the feet of their teachers appears from Pirke Avot c.1: Cover yourself with the dust of the feet of the sages, etc. See Buxtorf's Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 1146.

units.la: Δῶρον est vox etiam nota & usitata Talmudicis. Zevachin sol.7.2. אמר רבא עולה דורון היא Dicit Rabba Holocaustum est δῶρον. Vbi glossa. Holocaustum non offertur ad expiandum pro facto aliquo: Sed postquam poenitentia expiavit peccatum, venit holocaustum להקביל פנים ut cum favore homo recipiatur &c.
units.tr: Doron (gift) is also a word known and in common use among the Talmudists. Zevachim fol. 7.2: Rabba says a burnt offering is a doron. Where the gloss says: A burnt offering is not offered to expiate some deed; but after repentance has expiated the sin, the burnt offering comes, so that the man may be received with favour (lehaqbil panim), etc.

units.la: §. Pesachin sol.118.2. Ægyptus afferet דורון למשיח δῶρον מ Messiae.
units.tr: §. Pesachim fol. 118.2: Egypt will bring a gift (doron) to the Messiah.

units.la: דרך ארץ Derech ereths, Proprie sonat via terra, sed hic modus loquendi varia apud Rabbinos denotat. 1. mortem. 2. civilitatem sive urbanitatem. 3. actum Venereum; 4. studium & laborem quaerendi victum. Hac significatione dicitur in Abhot c.2. יפה תלמוד תורה עם דרך ארץ שיגיעת שניהם משכחת עון: Pulchra est doctrina legis cum artificio aliquo adjuncto, nam labor utriusque oblivisci facit peccati.
units.tr: Derech eretz, properly meaning "the way of the land," but in the rabbis this phrase denotes various things: 1. death; 2. civility or courtesy; 3. the sexual act; 4. zeal and labour in seeking a living. In this sense it is said in Avot c.2: Fine is the study of the Law joined with some worldly occupation, for the labour of both makes sin forgotten.

units.la: E.
units.tr: E.

units.la: ELEEMOSYNÆ sunt מלח ממון sal divitiarum, cuius denegatio Idololatria dicitur, Adag.
units.tr: ALMSGIVING is מלח ממון, salt of riches, and to refuse it is called idolatry, Adag.

units.la: §. Eleemosynam nomine צִדְקָה insigniverunt Rabbini, quia plurimum ad iustificationem conferre putabant. Hinc dicitur, Si quis quadrantem unum pauperi dederit in Eleemosynam, particeps fit beatifica visionis. Bab. Batra sol.10.1. Midrasch Tillin in Psal.xvii.15.
units.tr: The rabbis named almsgiving צְדָקָה, because they thought it contributed greatly to justification. Hence the saying: If anyone gives a quadrant to the poor as alms, he becomes a partaker of the beatific vision. Bab. Batra sol. 10.1. Midrash Tillim on Ps. 17.15.

units.la: §. Cùm quidam Eleemosynam daret dixit. Hunc tibi nummum do, ea propter, ut vivant filii mei, atque ut ipse acquiram mundum futurum. Bab. Kofch Hafchana sol.4.1.
units.tr: When someone was giving alms, he said: I give you this coin so that my sons may live, and so that I myself may gain the world to come. Bab. Kofch Hafchana sol. 4.1.

units.la: §. Si Eleemosynas prastiteris è crumena tua, custodiet te Deus ab omni damno & nocumento. Hieros. Peah sol.15.2. vid. etiam Bab.Beracot sol.55.1.
units.tr: If you give alms from your purse, God will keep you from every loss and harm. Hieros. Peah sol. 15.2. See also Bab. Berachot sol. 55.1.

units.la: §. Rex Monobazes cùm à Cognatis propter magnas eleemosynas in pauperes erogatas audiret, se sua & maiorum bona atterere, cùm illi ea auxissent, respondit: Opes suas reposuerunt patres mei in terra, ego meas in cœlo. Historia extat in Hieros. Peah. sol. 15. 2. Bab. Bava Batra sol.11.1.
units.tr: When Monobazus the king heard from his relatives that he was squandering his own and his ancestors' goods on great alms to the poor, though they had increased those goods, he replied: My fathers stored up their riches on earth; I store up mine in heaven. The story is found in Hieros. Peah sol. 15.2 and Bab. Bava Batra sol. 11.1.

units.la: §. Rex Iaunai vidit quendam, nummum pauperi dantem palàm, cui dixit, præstat non dedisse, quàm sic dedisse. Chagiga sol.5.1.
units.tr: King Jannai saw someone giving a coin openly to a poor man, and said to him: It is better not to have given than to have given in this way. Chagiga sol. 5.1.

units.la: §. Eleemosynam ordinariam tripartiuntur Magistri. Prima erat לתמחוי Sportula vel canif-tro publico. תמחוי enim secundùm Aruch, erat vas quoddam, in quo colligebantur panis & sculenta לעניי עולם pro pauperibus mundi, i.e. pro mendicis quibusvis ostiatim petentibus, etiam Ethnicis: secundùm illud Hieros.Peah sol.21.1. תמחוי לכל אדם Scutella Eleemosynaria fuit pro quolibet homine. Hæc Eleemosyna se-cuncundùm Aruch גנבית ככל יום ב"ג ומתחלקת בשלשה exigebatur quotidie per tres viros, & distribuebatur per tres. Exigebatur ab oppidanis per collectores intra fores eorū,quod patet per cautionem istam Bava Batra sol.8.2. צבאי צרקה אין רשאין לפרוש זה כזה אבל פורש זה לשער וזה חנירת Non licet colleCtoribus Eleemosynæ ab invicem se separare, nisi quod hic secedere posset ad portam, ille ad tabernam. Id est semper se debebant in conspectu habere, nec ipsis licuit, divisim & separatim Eleemosynas colligere, ne oriretur suspicio, ipsos data in proprium usum contulisse.
units.tr: The masters divided the ordinary alms into three kinds. The first was the לתמחוי, the public dish or soup kitchen. According to the Aruch, the תמחוי was a certain vessel into which bread and food were collected לעניי עולם, for the poor of the world, that is, for beggars of any kind who asked from door to door, even Gentiles; according to that saying in Hieros. Peah sol. 21.1: תמחוי לכל אדם, the alms dish was for every man. This alms, according to the Aruch, גנבית ככל יום ב"ג ומתחלקת בשלשה, was collected daily by three men and distributed by three. It was collected from the townspeople by collectors at their doors, as is clear from that rule in Bava Batra sol. 8.2: צבאי צרקה אין רשאין לפרוש זה כזה אבל פורש זה לשער וזה חנירת, Collectors of alms may not separate from one another, except that one may go off to the gate and the other to the shop. That is, they had always to keep one another in view, nor were they allowed to collect alms separately and apart, lest suspicion arise that they had diverted the gifts to their own use.

units.la: Secunda Eleemosyna dabatur לקופה in arcam pauperum publicam, distribuenda solùm pauperibus illiùs urbis. Colligebatur illa per שני גבאי צרק duos Collectores, & distribuebatur per tres, qui in genere פרנסין vocantur: Rationem numeri reddunt in Peah c.8.7. & in Gem. Cista eleemosynaria exigitur per duos,& distribuitur per tres. Exigitur per duos שאין עושים שררות על ציבור פחות משנים Nam non faciunt ꝏ:aɛiav in Synagoga minorem quàm duorum; & distribuitur per tres, sicuti iudicia pecuniaria transiguntur per tres. vid. Maymon. Sanhed.c.1. Colligebatur hæc Eleemosyna in Synagoga Sabbatho,& distribuebatur pauperibus vespere Sabbathi, hinc illud קופה מערב שבת לערב Cista Eleemosynaria à vespere Sabbathi ad v-sperum Sabbathi; scutella Eleemosynaria unoquoque die. vid. Bartenoram ad Peah l. 2.
units.tr: The second alms was given לקופה, into the public chest of the poor, to be distributed only to the poor of that city. It was collected by שני גבאי צרק, two collectors, and distributed by three, who are called in general פרנסין. They give an account of the numbers in Peah c. 8.7 and in the Gemara. The alms chest is collected by two and distributed by three. It is collected by two, שאין עושים שררות על ציבור פחות משנים, for they do not exercise authority over the community with fewer than two; and it is distributed by three, just as monetary judgments are conducted by three. See Maimonides, Sanhedrin c. 1. This alms was collected in the synagogue on the Sabbath and distributed to the poor on the evening of the Sabbath; hence the saying קופה מערב שבת לערב, the alms chest from the evening of the Sabbath to the evening of the Sabbath; the alms dish every day. See Bartenora on Peah l. 2.

units.la: Tertiam Eleemosynam dederunt ex agro, camque præcipuè quadruplicem. 1. Angulum agri non demessum. (v.s.l. ) 2. manipulos in agro relictos, vel ex oblivione vel voluntarie. (v. שכחה ) 3. Reliquias vindemiationis (vid. לקט ) 4. Decimas pauperum עני מעשר quæ ter in die distribuebantur. (vid. angulus agri.) In his omnibus Eleemosynis non legitur ipsos tubas admibuisse, ita ut locus Matth.vi. 2. de extraordinariis quibusdam Eleemosynis intelligendus sit.
units.tr: The third alms they took from the field, and this in particular was fourfold: 1. the corner of the field not reaped (see angulus agri); 2. the sheaves left in the field, either by forgetfulness or deliberately (see שכחה); 3. the gleanings of the vintage (see לקט); 4. the tithes for the poor, עני מעשר, which were distributed three times a day (see angulus agri). In none of these alms is it read that they sounded trumpets, so the passage Matth. 6.2 must be understood of certain extraordinary alms.

units.la: §. Iam supra notavimus quòd plurimi inter Iudæos ostentando Eleemosynas dederint, & quod mercedem ex illis, quasi ex opere operato, ex pectarint; exemplum adhuc adducamus ex Hieros.sol.21.2. R. Lazar fuit Eleemosynarius Synagoga. Ingressus aliquando domum suam, dixit, Quid novi? Responderunt: Venerunt huc quidam, & comederunt ac biberunt, & pro te preces fuderunt. Tunc (inquit ille,) non est merces bona. Cum verò aliquando alii accessissent, & post concessum ipsis cibum & potum ipsi convitiati essent, dixit: Iam erit merces bona. Quicquid autem de ostentatione ipsorum in Eleemosynis referatur, certum tamen est, quòd plurimi summè approbarint Eleemosynas secreto erogatas; hinc etiam in templo instituerunt לשכת חשאי conclave silentium, quod erat Gazophylacium aliquod, in quod Eleemosynas suas contulerunt. Viri religiosissimi silenter & clanculum, ut inde nutrirentur pueri pauperes virorum bonorum. Vid. Aruch in שח & Mass.Schekalim c.s.6. Hoc etiam apud ipsos fuit adagium גדול העושה צדקה בסתר יותר מכשה ὁ ποιῶν ἐλεημοσύνην ἐν κρυπτῷ (ut hunc loc. vertit tit Cl.Leigtf.)maior est ipso Mose Mag. nostro. Bab.BavaBatra sol.9.2.
units.tr: Above we have already noted that many among the Jews gave alms for show and gained a reward from them, as if by the work done; let us add another example from Hieros. sol. 21.2: R. Lazar was the almoner of the synagogue. Once he came into his house and said, "What is new?" They replied: "Some men came here, and ate and drank, and poured out prayers for you." Then (he said) there is no good reward. But when others later came, and after they had been given food and drink they reviled him, he said: "Now there will be a good reward." Whatever is reported of their ostentation in alms, it is certain, however, that very many highly approved of alms given in secret. Hence in the temple they also established the לשכת חשאי, the silent chamber, which was a treasury into which they put their alms. The most devout men gave silently and secretly, so that poor children of good men might be fed from it. See Aruch in שח and Mas. Shekalim c. 5.6. Among them there was also this saying: גדול העושה צדקה בסתר יותר מכשה ὁ ποιῶν ἐλεημοσύνην ἐν κρυπτῷ (as Cl. Leigh renders this passage), he who gives alms in secret is greater than Moses our teacher [gadol ha'oseh tsedaqah be-seter yoter mi-kulam; ho poiōn eleēmosynēn en kryptō]. Bab. Bava Batra sol. 9.2.

units.la: Elias. De exspectato adventu Eliæ in Talmudicis quam plurima reperiuntur. Kimchi in Malach iv. 23. Restituit Deus (inquit) animam Eliæ, quæ ascendit olim in cœlum, in corpus creatum instar corporis eius prioris כי גופו הראשון שב ואין Nam corpus eius primum ad terram rediit cum ille ascenderet in cœlum, unumquodque elementum in elementum suum. Cum autem eum vivificaverit Deus in corpore,mittet eum ad Israelem ante diem iudicii, & admonebit singulos, ut ad Deum convertantur &c.
units.tr: Elijah. Very many things about the expected coming of Elijah are found in the Talmudic writings. Kimchi on Malachi 4.23 says: God (he says) restores the soul of Elijah, which once ascended into heaven, into a created body like his former body, כי גופו הראשון שב ואין [ki gufo ha-rishon shav ve-ein], for his first body returned to the earth when he ascended into heaven, each element to its own element. But when God has made him alive again in the body, he will send him to Israel before the day of judgment, and he will admonish each one to turn to God, etc.

units.la: §. Aben Esra, in eundem locum sic cōmentatur. Comperimus Eliam vixisse in diebus Ahaziæ filii Achab; Et etiam reperimus, ipsum post mortem Iehoschaphati ad filium eius Ahaziam scripsisse epistolam, sicut dicitur: Et venit epistola ad eum ab Elia Propheta. ואין ספק כי בימי הכמינו הקרושים נראח Et absque controversia est, eum visum fuisse in diebus Sapientum Sanctorum nostrorum. Acceleret Deus ex misericordia sua prophetiam suam, atque terminum adventus eius.
units.tr: §. Abraham ibn Ezra comments on the same passage thus: We find that Elijah lived in the days of Ahaziah son of Ahab. And we also find that after the death of Jehoshaphat he wrote a letter to his son Ahaziah, as it is said: "And a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet." והאין ספק כי בימי הכמינו הקרושים נראח, And there is no doubt that he was seen in the days of our holy sages [ve-ein safeq ki be-yemei ḥakhameinu ha-qedoshim nir'ah]. May God in his mercy hasten his prophecy and the time of his coming.

units.la: Vides hic Aben Esram apparitionum Eliæ mentionem facere, & certè in pluribus aliis locis mentio fit, quòd Elias apparuerit; quòd sine dubio præstigiis Diaboli, ut Bath kol effectum fuit.
units.tr: You see here that Ibn Ezra mentions appearances of Elijah, and certainly in many other places there is mention that Elijah appeared; which without doubt was done by the deceits of the devil, as the bat kol was.

units.la: §. Eliam Sabbatizantem in monte Carmel supponunt Talmudici in Hieros. Pejachin sol. 30.2. Ne comburatur Trumah, de qua dubitatur, an munda sit, an immunda, ne Elias sabbatizans in monte Carmelo adveniat, & testetur
units.tr: §. The Talmudists suppose that Elijah was keeping the Sabbath on Mount Carmel, in Hieros. Pesachim sol. 30.2: Let the Terumah, about which there is doubt whether it is clean or unclean, be burned, lest Elijah, keeping the Sabbath on Mount Carmel, arrive and bear witness

units.la: de ea Sabbatho, quòd sit munda.
units.tr: concerning it on the Sabbath, that it is clean.

units.la: § E.as scrupulos & diligens omnia enucleaturus est. Invenit quis apud se sibi edulam contractuum, & non novit quid sibi velit, יהוה fiponat eam usquedum אליהו adve: erit Elias Rava Meizia c.1.v.ult. Si quis aliquid ⁠ordinem repererit, & publico praeconio facto possessores eius noncognoverit, apud se reponat usquedum advenerit Elias. Maymon in G'zelah cap.13. Periochen Ezech.xlv.18.19. עתיד אליהו לפרש Elias explicaturus est. Menachot sol. 45.1.
units.tr: §. He will explain every scruple and difficulty. If someone finds a sweet dish set aside for him, and does not know what it means, יהוה [YHWH] let him keep it until אליהו [Elijah] comes: Elijah will come. Rava Meizia c. 1, last verse. If someone finds an object, and after public proclamation does not know its owners, let him keep it by him until Elijah comes. Maimonides, Gezelah c. 13. Ezekiel 45.18–19 is cited: Elijah is going to explain. עתיד אליהו לפרש [atid Eliyahu lefarosh]. Elijah will explain. Menachot sol. 45.1.

units.la: §. Bab. rubbin, sol. 43.2. disputatur quonam die Hebdomadae venturus Messias, & quonam Elias: inter alia haec occurrunt לא אתא אליהו מאתמול Elias non venit heri: id est, eodem die quo venit, prodibit in publicum, & non latebit veniens heri in hodiernum. Certi sunt Israelitae Eliam nec vesperi diem festorum, מפני טורח propter laborem. Item לא אתי אליהו בשבת Elias non veniet in Sabbatho. (vid. Hieros. Pesach.sol.30.2.) G.Off. propter laborem; id est propter praeparationem in Sabbathum, ne scilicet necessaria Sabbatho non perfecta relinquantur, ut obviam ei eant; aut propter laborem in conviviis, ne scilicet omittant comestiones Sabbathicas. Ex glossatoribus in paginam Latam haec tria observare poteris. 1. לפני Ante adventum filii Davidis advenit Elias, ad Evangelizandum de eo. 2. לא אתי משיח בחר בשבת Non veniet Messias primo die Sabbathum insequente, quia Elias, qui ipsum praecedere debet, non veniet in in Sabbatho. 3. הלא כשיח בן יוסף יש לו
units.tr: §. In the Bab. Rabbin sol. 43.2 it is disputed on which day of the week the Messiah will come, and on which day Elijah will come. Among other things these occur: לא אתא אליהו מאתמול, Elijah did not come yesterday [lo ata Eliyahu me-atmol]: that is, on the day on which he comes he will come out into public, and he will not be hidden, coming yesterday into today. The Israelites are sure that Elijah does not come on the evening of a feast day, פני טורח, on account of the labour. Likewise לא אתי אליהו בשבת, Elijah does not come on the Sabbath [lo ati Eliyahu be-shabbat]. (See Hieros. Pesachim sol. 30.2.) The gloss says: on account of the labour; that is, on account of the preparation for the Sabbath, so that things needed for the Sabbath should not be left unfinished when they go out to meet him; or on account of the labour at feasts, so that they do not omit the Sabbath meals. From the glossators on the Latin page you may note these three points. 1. לפני, before the coming of the son of David Elijah comes, to announce the good news of him [lifnei]. 2. לא אתי משיח בחר בשבת, the Messiah will not come on the first day of the following Sabbath, because Elijah, who must go before him, will not come on the Sabbath. 3. הלא כשיח בן יוסף יש לו [ha-lo ki-shiaḥ ben Yosef yesh lo].

units.la: §. Plurima fingunt Iudæi, quæ restaurarus fi E s B b.Kiduschin.sol.71.1. יטהר הכהורים purificabit nobis, eosque resticuet congregationi. vid etiam Kimchi Zach. ix. 6. Israeli reddet urnam Mannæ, phialam sacri olei, phialam aquæ, & sunt qui dicunt, virgam Aaronis. Tanchum in Exod. 1.
units.tr: The Jews invent many things, which [Elijah] will restore. The Talmud, Kiddushin fol. 71.1, says he "will purify the priests for us" and restore them to the congregation. See also Kimchi on Zech. 9:6. They say he will give back to Israel the urn of manna, the flask of holy oil, and the flask of water; and some say the rod of Aaron. Tanchuma on Exodus, 1.

units.la: §. Scrupulum movent Iudæi, an corvi panem & carnem attulerint Eliæ, an homines qui vocantur עורבים, sic Kimchi in locum. In eundem sensum hoc legimus in Berefch. Rabba sect 33 R. Iehuda dicit עורבים attulerunt panem & carnem mane & vespere ad Eliam, עיר היא כתחום בית שאן ושטה עירבו Urbs ista erat in limitibus Beth Shean, & vocabatur Orbo.
units.tr: The Jews raise a doubt whether ravens brought bread and meat to Elijah, or whether it was men called orevim [עורבים], so Kimchi on the passage.
