To the same effect we read in Bereshit Rabbah, sect. 33, R. Jehudah says that the orevim [עורבים] brought bread and meat to Elijah morning and evening. "That city was within the bounds of Beth Shean and was called Orbo" [עירבו].

units.la: Eliezer. Inter illos qui hoc nomine occurrunt, duo præcipuè famosi fuerunt. Eliefer Ben Harsum, & Eliefer fil. Hircani. Eliefer Ben Harfum fuit coætanus Antigoni, & talibus divitiis affluens, ut possederit mille urbes in arida, & mille urbes in mari: id est ditissimus & magnus Dominus in Palæstina fuit. Hoc enim vult hyperbole. E quamvis opulentissimus fuerit, magna fortuna tamen abusus non est, sed perpetuo studiis incubuit. Iuchaf. p.15.2. Semel cum studiorum gratia, utrem farinæ in dorso ferens, esset in via ad aliquam scholam, incurrerunt in ipsum servi eius & voluerunt ipsum facere אנגריא (v. f. 1.) Hi enim servi Dominum suum studiis incumbentem, & qui splendidam hæreditatem per alios administrabat, nunquam viderant.
units.tr: Among those who bear this name, two were especially famous: Eliezer ben Harsum and Eliezer son of Hyrcanus. Eliezer ben Harsum was a contemporary of Antigonus and so abounded in wealth that he owned a thousand cities on land and a thousand on the sea; that is, he was a very rich and great lord in Palestine. For this is what the hyperbole means. Although he was very wealthy, he did not misuse his great fortune but devoted himself constantly to study. Juchasin, p. 15.2. Once, when he was on his way to a school for the sake of study, carrying a bag of flour on his back, his servants met him and wanted to make him an angaria (v. f. 1). For these servants had never seen their master devoted to study, since he had entrusted the management of his splendid estate to others.

units.la: §. R.Eliefer, fil.Hyrcani magni, æstimatur, ita ut ipsum aliquando הגדול magnum nominent; In Mischna intelligitur, quoties םתנ absolute R. Eliefer ponitur. Halic. Olam p.1. c.3. Composuit ille quædam capitula, quæ V.C. Guil.Vorstius latinitate donavit. Ad præsidiatum pervenire non potuit, quamvis doctrinâ & canitie venerabilis erat: caussas vide in Iuchasin. Cùm pro præsidiatu disputaret, argumenta sua præter rationum pondera, etiam signis stabilire conatus est. Bava Metzia sol.59.2. Akiba ipsum ingenti amore prosequutus est, & mortem eius acerbè deploravit. vid. Bab. Sanhed. f.68. De aliis Elieferis poteris consulere Iuchasin in יוחסין.
units.tr: R. Eliezer, son of Hyrcanus the Great, is highly esteemed; so much so that they sometimes call him "the Great." In the Mishnah he is meant whenever R. Eliezer is mentioned without qualification. Halicoth Olam, p. 1, c. 3. He composed certain chapters, which the venerable Guilielmus Vorstius translated into Latin. He could not attain the presidency, although he was venerable for his learning and white hair; for the reasons see Juchasin. When he argued for the presidency, he tried to establish his arguments not only by the weight of his reasons but also by signs. Bava Metzia, fol. 59.2. Akiba cherished him with great love and mourned his death bitterly. See Bab. Sanhedrin, fol. 68. About the other Eliezers you may consult Juchasin under Yuchasin.

units.la: EMAUS. Mishna illum locum designat per עימאוס Hierof. verò in Scheviit sol.38.4. per אמאוס denotantes locum חמת thermas Tiberienses, sive propè Tiberiadem.
units.tr: EMMAUS. The Mishnah designates that place as Imaus. But the Jerusalem Talmud, in Shevi'it, fol. 38.4, gives Amaus, meaning the place of Hamat, the hot baths of Tiberias, or near Tiberias.

units.la: §. A Bethhorone ad Emmaunta erat montanum. Hierof.Scheviit l.c. Distabat illa Hierosolymis stadiis sexaginta Luc.xxiv. 13.
units.tr: From Beth-horon to Emmaus there was a mountain. Jerusalem Talmud, Shevi'it, l.c. It was sixty furlongs from Jerusalem. Luke 24:13.

units.la: §. In Erachin c.2.4. fit mentio בית משפחות Familiarum Beth Pegarim & Beth Zeparia ex Emaunte: Glossaque dicit Incolas Emmauntis fuisse Israelitas generosos, sacerdotesque filias ipsorum duxisse in uxores.
units.tr: In Erachin, c. 2.4, mention is made of the families of Beth Pegarim and Beth Zeparia from Emmaus. The gloss says that the inhabitants of Emmaus were noble Israelites, and they took the daughters of priests as wives.

units.la: EMMAUS. Midrasch Cohelet c.7.6. R. Iochanan Ben Saccai 50. habuit Discipulos, quamdiu vivebat, semper sedebant coram eo, cum verò moreretur, profecti sunt Iabhnen; R. Eliefer autem, filius Erech,ivit ad uxorem eius לאמאוס Emmaum tem מקום מים יפים locum aquarum amœnarum, & habitationis iucunda.
units.tr: EMMAUS. Midrash Kohelet, c. 7.6. R. Johanan ben Zakkai had fifty disciples. As long as he lived they always sat before him; but when he died they went away to Jabneh. R. Eliezer, son of Arach, however, went to his widow, to Emmaum, a place of beautiful waters and a pleasant dwelling.

units.la: ESTER de illa vide Cl.Buxt.L.T.178.
units.tr: ESTHER: see Cl. Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 178 about her.

units.la: ENOCH Hæb. חנוך quod μεταμέρισθη consecratum denotat, à Talmudicis vocatur משטרון ut à Paraph. Ionath. ad Genef v. 24. Idem citatur ex Medrasch Ruth in Zohar sol. 81. vid. Buxt. in Lex. Talm. In Iuchasin sol.134. vocatur אדריס Adra.
units.tr: ENOCH. The Hebrew חנוך, which denotes consecrated (the Greek μετατέθειται, "was translated"), is called by the Talmudists מששטרון, as in the Paraphrast Jonathan on Gen. 5:24. The same is quoted from Midrash Ruth in the Zohar, fol. 81. See Buxtorf in Lexicon Talmudicum. In Juchasin, fol. 134, he is called אדריס, Adra.

units.la: De Enochi pietate non bene sentiunt Iudæi; Iarchius verba Genes. v.24. Et ambulavit Enoch cum Deo ita ... ; Ambulavit cum Deo, id est iustus fuit, sed levis tamen & inconstans, solitus cito ad malum deflectere, לפיכך מהר הק בה וסיולקו וחסיתו קודם ומנו Ideo festinavit Deus benedictus, & transtulit eum, & ante tempus mori fecit. Et hoc est, quod annus eius quo mortuus est, descriptus est scribendo: & non erat nempe in hoc seculo, ad implendos annos suos. Ita in Berefchit Rabba dicunt in loc. fuisse Enochum Hypocritam, nunc iustum nunc improbum. Ideo Deum tempore iustitiæ ipsius, quo cum Deo ambulabat, eum sustulisse subito, ne rursum deficeret.
units.tr: The Jews do not think well of the piety of Enoch. Jarchi, on the words of Gen. 5:24, "And Enoch walked with God," says: "Walked with God, that is, he was righteous, but light and inconstant, accustomed to turn quickly to evil. Therefore God, blessed be he, hastened and took him, and made him die before his time. And this is why the year of his death is written down: and he was not, namely in this world, to complete his years." Likewise in Bereshit Rabbah, in loc., they say that Enoch was a hypocrite, now righteous, now wicked. Therefore God, in the time of his righteousness, when he walked with God, suddenly took him away, lest he fall away again.

units.la: Quoad Raptum Enochi, Aben Esra putat, mortuum esse, & deinde post mortem a Deo assumptum: idem sentiunt Abarbenel & R. Salomon; at contrarium habent Targum Onkelosi & Ionathanis.
units.tr: As to the rapture of Enoch, Aben Ezra thinks that he died and was afterwards taken up by God after death. Abarbanel and R. Solomon hold the same view; but the Targum of Onkelos and of Jonathan have the opposite.

units.la: Locus in quem raptus Enochus secundum Kimchium in lib.ii. Reg.ii.1. est Paradisus terrestris; & statum, in quo erant nostri Protoplasti, etiam conditionem Enochi suisse, ipsius est sententia.
units.tr: According to Kimchi, on 2 Kings 2:1, the place into which Enoch was caught up is the earthly paradise; and his own opinion is that Enoch's condition was the same as that in which our first parents were.

units.la: Ephraim de quo II. Paralypom. 13. 19. est oppidum in terra Israelis frugibus fertilissimum. Præstantissima quoque simila ex illo proferebatur; indè factum est proverbium: Num tu stramen inducis in Ephraim. Bab. Menachot folio 55. 1. & usurpatur ut illud Græcorum ... Vide Aruch in יחני.
units.tr: Ephraim, of which 2 Chron. 13:19 speaks, is a town in the land of Israel very fertile in crops. Its very excellent fine flour was also exported from there, and from this arose the proverb: "Do you bring straw into Ephraim?" Babylonian Talmud, Menachot, fol. 55.1. It is used like that Greek saying... See Aruch under Yochani.

units.la: Epicureum triplicem facit Maymon in Hal. Teschubba cap. 3. 14. Qui ait nullam prorsus prophetiam esse: Nec scientiam quæ pertingat ad cor hominis; & qui abnegat prophetiam Mosis magistri nostri; quique ait, Creatorem nescire actiones hominum. Item in Hal. v"y cap. 2. 8. Epicurei sunt, qui consoluunt cognitiones animi sui, ignari earum, quas diximus verum, donec transgressi posissima legis capita offendant per contumaciam. De Epicureo vid. L.T.B. pag. 194 195.
units.tr: Maimonides, in Hilchot Teshuvah, c. 3.14, makes three kinds of Epicurean: one who says there is no prophecy at all, nor any knowledge that reaches the heart of man; one who denies the prophecy of Moses our teacher; and one who says that the Creator does not know the actions of men. Likewise in Hilchot Yesodei, c. 2.8: Epicureans are those who scorn the knowledge of their own minds, ignorant of those things which we have called true, until they stumble upon the most important heads of the law through obstinacy. On the Epicurean see L.T.B., pp. 194–195.

units.la: In Eremo esse vel degere sermè semper significat vitam ruri non in urbe transigere, opponitur enim Eremus urbi. Menachot c. 7 1. Quinque Seah ירושלמית Hierosolymitana, valent sex seahs מדבריות Eremiticas. i. e. Rusticas. Bab. Erubbin sol 83 1. Seah Hierosolymitana excedit Seam Eremi sexta parte.
units.tr: To be or to dwell in the wilderness usually means to pass life in the country rather than in the city, for eremus is opposed to urbs. Menachot, c. 7.1: Five seahs of Jerusalem measure are worth six seahs of the wilderness, that is, of the country. Babylonian Talmud, Eruvin, fol. 83.1: A seah of Jerusalem exceeds a seah of the wilderness by a sixth part.

units.la: §. אילנות מדבריות sunt (Maymon. ad cap. 1. Demai) arbores quæ sunt communis iuris, & non unius Domini in communibus saltibus scilicet & pascuis. Ita etiam pecora מדבריות Ere-
units.tr: "Trees of the wilderness" (Maimonides on chapter 1 of Demai) are trees which are of common right and not of a single owner, namely in common pastures and grazing lands. So also the cattle of the wilderness

units.la: mi vocantur illa, quæ foris & in agris nutriuntur, aut in montibus, ut in montosis regionibus in usu est, oppositè ad illa quæ in urbe aluntur. Hanc differentiam facit Canon Hierof. Schabbat sol.45.2. & Beza sol.40.1. ופ ושוחטין משקין אין Non potant & mactant pecora Eremi, sed potant הביתות domestica : (ut scilicet melius excoriari possint.)
units.tr: are called those which are fed outside, in the fields, or in the mountains, as is customary in mountainous regions, as opposed to those which are reared in the city. The Canon of the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, fol. 45.2, and Beitzah, fol. 40.1, makes this distinction: "They do not give to drink nor slaughter the cattle of the wilderness, but they give to drink domestic ones" (so that, of course, they may be skinned more easily).

units.la: §. Hinc apparet, quàm malè argumententur pro vita Monastica ex Matth.iii.1. Secundùm communem & vulgarem sententiam educatus erat Iohannes in monte regali; at secundùm Hierof.Tanith sol.69.1. Mons regalis myriademurbiù habuit, Quomodo ergò ibi desertù?
units.tr: Hence it is clear how badly they argue for monastic life from Matt. 3:1. According to the common and popular opinion John was brought up in the royal mountain; but according to the Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit, fol. 69.1, the royal mountain had ten thousand towns. How then was it a desert there?

units.la: Esaias. Gemaristæ in Iebhamot sol. 49 2. referunt hunc Prophetam interfectum fuisse à Rege Manasse, præcipuè ideo, quòd accusaverat Israelem ob impuritatem labiorum. Verba historiæ hæc sunt. Dixit Esaias; Novi quòd (Rex Manasses) non auscultaturus sit, quicquid ipsi dixero; si quid protulero ad conciliationem Scriptura, (cuius quasdam apparentes contradictiones rex ipsi obiecerat, ut ex antecedentibus patet:) ille fastuosè aget. Dixit ergò, ארולע איבלי Concludam me intra hanc cedrum. Adduxerunt cedrum, & serrâ diffecuerunt eam. כימשת להרי פומה נח נפשיה (umque serra os eius attingeret, expiravit. Idque ideo quòd dixerat, Ego habito inter populum impurum.
units.tr: Isaiah. The Gemarists in Yevamot, fol. 49.2, report that this prophet was killed by King Manasseh, chiefly because he had accused Israel of uncleanness of lips. The words of the story are these: Isaiah said: "I know that (King Manasseh) will not listen to whatever I say; if I bring forward anything to reconcile Scripture (whose apparent contradictions the king had objected to him, as is clear from what precedes), he will act arrogantly." So he said, ארולע איבלי [Ar'ola ibli]: "I will hide myself within this cedar." They brought the cedar and cut it through with a saw. When the saw reached his mouth [כימשת להרי פומה נח נפשיה] he expired. And this was because he had said, "I dwell among an unclean people."

units.la: Esavus noluit permittere Iosepho, ut patrem sepeliret. Cl Buxt.L.T.p.41.
units.tr: Esau refused to allow Joseph to bury his father. Cl. Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 41.

units.la: Esras floruit anno Mundi 3413. Erat præses כנסת חגרולת Synagoga magna, & omnium Doctorum Misnicorum Pater. Religione & manfuetudine ipfum Mofen æquabat. Iuchafin pag.13. Elias in præfat. Mafor. & Zacuthus Efram cum Zerubabele & Malachia confundunt. Pater Efræ fuit Saarias fil.Afarixæ, vid. Zemach David.
units.tr: Ezra flourished in the year of the world 3413. He was president of the Great Synagogue [כנסת הגדולה] and father of all the Mishnaic teachers. He matched Moses himself in piety and gentleness. Iuchafin p. 13. Elias in Preface to the Masorah and Zacuthus confuse Ezra with Zerubbabel and Malachi. Ezra's father was Seraiah, son of Azariah; see Zemach David.

units.la: §. Cum Efras è Babel Hierofolymas afcenderet, fecum abduxit omnes illegitimè natos, & quorum genealogia ignota erat, ut populus, quem in Babel relinquebat,essetּ נקי כסולח Purim inflar farinæ. Quod prolixè videre potes in Kiddufchin c.4.1. Gem. Efra cum reliquis senatoribus (quorum aliquos recenset Abarban. in præf. ad Nachalat Avot.) fecit Maforam, punctationem & accentus super tota Biblia. Elias præf.3. Mafor.
units.tr: When Ezra went up from Babylon to Jerusalem, he took with him all who had been born illegitimately and whose genealogy was unknown, so that the people he left behind in Babylon would be pure as flour [נקי כסולח]. You can see this at length in Kiddushin c. 4, (1), Gem. Ezra, together with the other senators (some of whom are listed by Abarbanel in the preface to Nachalat Avot), made the Masorah, the pointing and the accents over the whole Bible. Elias, Preface 3, Masorah.

units.la: §. Vt Ecclesia ab Efra recenter purgata & instituta, iusto & decenti regimine dirigeretur, Efras plurimas fancivit constitutiones, principaliores sunt decem illæ, quæ in Baba Kama fol.75.1.recensentur. 1. ut institueretur publica legis lectio diebus septimanæ secundo & quinto. 2. ut in Sabbatho ad Mincham legeretur. 3.fancivit ablutionem gonorrhaicis. 4. sessionem iudicum in civitatibus diebus hebdomadæ secundo & quinto. 5. Permisit Aromatariis ut circumire possent per urbes, ad Israelitarum decus. 6. Præcepit ut lavarent (vestimenta)die quinto septimanæ, propter gloriam Sabbathi. 7. ut pinserent & coquerent panem vesperi, qui Sabbathum antecedit, ut ספרוס fructum dari posset pauperibus in Sabbatho. 8. Indulsit allii esum nocte Sabbathum præcedente, quia gignit amorem & tollit cupiditates. 9. ut mulier accincta esset בסינר Succinctlorio posteriori & anteriori; (ad scandalum evitandum.) 10. Constitutum est, unamquamque mulierem tribus diebus ante suam purificationem se pectere & mundare debere,&c.
units.tr: So that the Church, freshly purged and established by Ezra, might be guided by a just and fitting order, Ezra laid down many constitutions. The chief ones are the ten listed in Baba Kama fol. 75.1: (1) a public reading of the law was to be instituted on the second and fifth days of the week; (2) it was to be read at the Minchah on the Sabbath; (3) he ordained ablution for those with gonorrhoea; (4) judges were to sit in the cities on the second and fifth days of the week; (5) he permitted perfumers to travel through the towns, for the honour of Israel; (6) he commanded that garments be washed on the fifth day of the week, for the glory of the Sabbath; (7) bread was to be kneaded and baked in the evening before the Sabbath, so that a portion [ספרוס] could be given to the poor on the Sabbath; (8) he allowed the eating of garlic on the night before the Sabbath, because it kindles love and removes lust; (9) a woman was to be girded with a succinctorium behind and in front (to avoid scandal); (10) it was decided that each woman must comb and cleanse herself three days before her purification, etc.

units.la: §. Esras magnoperè restitit Sadducæorum hæresi in diebus suis pullulascenti,& ut aliquod symbolum poneretur, quo Orthodoxi à pravè sentientibus distinguerentur, visum est ipsi decernere,ut ad coronidem omnium orationum, quæ in templo fundebantur diceretur מן העולם עד עולם A seculo in seculum. Bab. Beracot. sol.54. Assueverat populus in captivitate Babylonica Chaldeæ linguæ, ita ut Hæbraicam non nisi cum difficultate intelligeret: huic incommodo ut consuleretur, instituit Esra התורגמן Synagoga interpretem, qui adstans legenti in lege, verficulatim ea vernaculè redderet, quæ lecta fuerant è fonte Hebræo, ut ex Hierof. Megillah sol.7.4. elicere est.
units.tr: Ezra strongly opposed the heresy of the Sadducees, which was sprouting up in his days. So that some creed might be set down by which the orthodox could be distinguished from those who thought wrongly, he decided that at the close of all the prayers poured out in the temple the words From age to age [מן העולם עד עולם] should be said. Bab. Berachot fol. 54. The people in the Babylonian captivity had grown accustomed to the Chaldean language, so that they understood Hebrew only with difficulty. To remedy this inconvenience Ezra instituted the targumist [התורגמן], the interpreter of the synagogue, who stood beside the one reading in the law and rendered into the vernacular, verse by verse, what had been read from the Hebrew source, as can be gathered from Jerusalem Megillah fol. 7.4.

units.la: §. Præcepit Esras,ut Iubilæum post captivitatem iterum inciperent ab anno septimo restaurationis templi. Maymon. Hal. Iobel cap.10. Cæterùm dignus erat Esra, ut data fuisset lex per manus eius Israeli, si non præcessisset ipsum Moses.Bab. Sanhed. c.2.f.21.
units.tr: Ezra ordered that the Jubilee be begun again after the captivity, counting from the seventh year of the restoration of the temple. Maimonides, Hilchot Yobel c. 10. Moreover, Ezra would have been worthy to have the law given to Israel through his hands, had Moses not come before him. Bab. Sanhedrin c. 2, f. 21.

units.la: §. Vixit Esras, secundùm Chronica Iudæorum, usque ad annum,quo Alexander Magnus Hierosolymas venit, & deinde die decimo mensis Tebhet sive Decembris suo fato functus est; quo anno ut memorant, etiam sublati fuerunt Haggeus, Zacharias, Malachias, unâ cum Prophetis,
units.tr: According to the Jewish chronicles, Ezra lived until the year in which Alexander the Great came to Jerusalem, and then on the tenth day of the month Tebhet, that is December, he died. In that year, as they report, Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi were also taken away, together with the prophets,

units.la: È EVANGELIUM quomodo Iudæi vocitent vid. Cl.Buxt.L.T.p.8.& 42.
units.tr: EVA: how the Jews name her. See Cl. Buxtorf, L.T., pp. 8 and 42.

units.la: Eva post auditam promissionem, quæ protophlastos crexit ad spem salutis, vocata est חוה non tam quia facta erat mater omnis viventium corporaliter Genef.iii.12. quàm quòd crediderit promissioni divinæ, & ita prima spiritualiter revixerit.
units.tr: After the promise was heard, which raised the first man to hope of salvation, Eve was called Havah [חוה]. She was given this name not so much because she was made the mother of all living bodily (Genef. iii. 12), but because she believed the divine promise, and so the first woman was spiritually revived.

units.la: Rupertus Tuitiensis, Adamo admodum absurdam sententiam attribuit, cùm referit, Adamum ex animi superbia divinam mortis sententiam adversus se prolatam contemnentem, appellasse uxorem suam חוה matrem viventium, ut qui mortem non extimesceret, & æquè se vitæ compotem crederet, ac si nunquam peccasset. Non minùs est absurdus Baal Haturim, qui חוה derivat à חוה garrire, loqui, è cœlo enim fingunt decem cabos garritus vel colloquiorum descendisse, & novem ex illis cessisse mulieribus. vid. (abi.
units.tr: Rupertus Tuitiensis attributes a quite absurd opinion to Adam. He reports that Adam, scorning the divine sentence of death pronounced against him, out of pride of spirit, called his wife Havah [חוה], the mother of the living, as one who did not fear death and believed herself to be as much mistress of life as if she had never sinned. Baal Haturim is no less absurd, for he derives Havah [חוה] from the verb [חוה] meaning to chatter, to speak. For they imagine that ten kinds of chatter, or conversations, came down from heaven, and that nine of them passed to women. See (abi.

units.la: Apud vocem Adam retulimus, Hebræorum sententiam esse, ipsius corpus non fuisse ודי אנחנו uniforme, sed biforme; qua ratione Adamus fuit à fronte, & Eva à tergo, & utrumque corpus ad scapulas quasi pice agglutinatum. Hæc est mens in Berefchit Rabba R. Samuelis Bar Nachman, Menasse Ben Israel Conciliat. in Genef. viii. ubi etiam inter suffragia numerat Iarchium, Aben Efram, Rabbenu Babye, R. Eliefer, & Isaacum Karsu. His adjè Maym.More Nevoch. p.2. c.30.
units.tr: As we noted under the word Adam, the opinion of the Hebrews is that his body was not uniform but biform. By this reasoning Adam was in front and Eve at the back, and the two bodies were stuck together at the shoulder-blades, as if with pitch. This is the view in Berefchit Rabba of R. Samuel Bar Nachman. Menasse Ben Israel, in his Conciliat. on Genef. viii., also counts among its supporters Iarchius, Aben Efram, Rabbenu Babye, R. Eliefer, and Isaac Karsu. To these add Maym. More Nevoch. p. 2, c. 30.

units.la: Circa lapsum Eva sequentia observamus.
units.tr: Concerning the fall we observe the following.

units.la: Diabolum tentasse satentur Rabb. Eliefer. fer Pirke. cap.13. & Maymon in More Nebhoch. lib.II.c.30. Cuius verba sunt. Oportet te scire, quomodo illud explicent in Midrafch, videlicet Serpentem fuisse equitatum, qui magnitudine camelum superaret; Seforem autem eum fuisse, qui deceperat Evam, Samaelem nempe, quam nomenclaturam absolute Sathana tribuunt.
units.tr: Rabbi Eliezer in Pirke, cap. 13, and Maimonides in More Nebhoch, lib. II, c. 30, confess that the devil tempted her. Maimonides' words are: You must know how they explain it in the Midrash, namely that the serpent was a beast that rode, and surpassed a camel in size; but the seducer was he who deceived Eve, namely Samael, a name which they attribute absolutely to Satan.

units.la: Occasionem tentationis sumpsisse Diabolum refert Iarchius, quia eos vidcrat nudos, & occupatos בתשמיש, quam felicitatem ipsis invidebat.
units.tr: Iarchius reports that the devil took the occasion of the temptation because he had seen them naked and occupied with sexual intercourse [בתשמיש], a happiness which he envied.

units.la: Serpens, quando dixit Novit Deus, cavillabatur invidiâ Dei, reformidantis societatem & similitudinem aliorum. Hoc exprimit Iarchius, כל אומן שוכא את בני אומנותו Quilibet nutritius edit filios quos nutrit, vel magis secundùm sensum Iarchii, omnis opifex edit alios & similes opifices. Si enim de arbore comederitis, (inquit Diabolus) scit Deus, vos ipsi similes futuros, vos fore יוצרי העולם Creatores mundi, ut ipse est; quare ex invidia vobis esum illius fructus prohibuit.
units.tr: When the serpent said God knows, he was mocking, out of envy of God, who feared the fellowship and likeness of others. Iarchius expresses this: Every nurse rears the children she nurses, or, more in keeping with Iarchius' sense, every craftsman produces other craftsmen like himself [כל אומן שוכא את בני אומנותו]. For, said the devil, if you eat of the tree, God knows that you yourselves will be like him, that you will be creators of the world [יוצרי העולם], as he is. Therefore, out of envy, he forbade you to eat its fruit.

units.la: Abarbenelis sententia est, neque serpentem alloquutum Evam, neque deinde Deum serpentem, cùm ipsi suam annuntiavit poenam, sed serpentem arborem scandisse, fructum decerpisse, atque sic exemplo Evam fefellisse; Dei verò verba intelligit de decreto, quod de ipso decrevit.
units.tr: Abarbanel's view is that the serpent did not address Eve, nor did God then address the serpent when he announced its punishment to it. Rather, the serpent climbed the tree, plucked the fruit, and so deceived Eve by example. He understands God's words as referring to the decree that God had made concerning the serpent.

units.la: Ad Quæstionem, an Serpens pedibus instructus fuerit antequam puniretur, Respond. affirmando Chaldæus Paraphrastes, R. Eliezer, Moses Bar Cepha, Salom. Iarchi cuius hæc sunt verba, היו לו רגלים ונקצצו Habebat Serpens pedes, sed ipsi praecisi sunt.
units.tr: To the question whether the serpent was furnished with feet before it was punished, the answer is affirmative, as given by the Chaldee Paraphrast, R. Eliezer, Moses Bar Cepha, Salomon Iarchi, whose words are: [היו לו רגלים ונקצצו]. It had feet, but they were cut off.

units.la: Referunt Iarchius ad Genef. iv. 1. & Moses Haddarfchan in Berefchit Rabba, Adamum operam liberis dedisse, & uxorem suam cognovisse iam in Paradiso: cum tamen contextus narrationis Mosaicae manifeste ostendat,id demum post eius expulsionem factum.
units.tr: Iarchius on Genef. iv. 1, and Moses Haddarshan on Berefchit Rabba, relate that Adam had begotten children and already knew his wife in Paradise. Yet the context of the Mosaic narrative clearly shows that this happened only after his expulsion.

units.la: Eunuchus duplex est, vel מכטן האדם à nativitate talis, & qui ab utero illam imperfectionem habet, vel סריס האדם Eunuchus ab homine talis factus, cum vi vel voluntarie castratus fuit. Zabbin c.2.1. Ievamot 79.2. Maymon. Hal. אישות c.2.Hic Hebraeis invisus fuit,Deut.xxiii.
units.tr: A eunuch is of two kinds: either one who is such from birth [מכטן האדם], who has that defect from the womb; or one made a eunuch by man [סריס האדם], who was castrated either by force or voluntarily. See Zabbin c. 2, 1; Ievamot 79. 2; Maymon. Hal. Ishut c. 2. This kind was hated by the Hebrews, Deut. xxiii.

units.la: 1. Romanis maxime: ad Sacerdotium & Synedrii consiliariatum pertingere non potuit, (quia illi,ut carentes liberis,ut plurimum crudeles esse solent.) Sanhed. fol.30.2.
units.tr: 1. Chiefly among the Romans. Such a man could not attain to the priesthood or to a seat as counsellor in the Sanhedrin, because eunuchs, as lacking children, are usually cruel. Sanhed. fol. 30. 2.

units.la: §. Fit etiam mentio apud Maymon. 1. c. סריס חמה Eunuchi Solis, qui fermè cum Eunucho ארם coincidit, & definitur, ille qui mox vigesimum annum implevit ולא הביא שתי שערות למשה ולא בוקן Nec tamen infra, nec in barba duos pilos produxit, insuperque omnia Eunuchi signa habet, quae sunt: שאין לו זקן ושערו לקוי ובשרו מחליק ואין מימי רגליו מעלין רתיחה וכשמטיר מים אינו עושה כיפה ושככר זרעו דיהה ואין מימי רגליו מחמיצין ורוחף כיפות הגשמים ואינו מעלה בשרו הבל וקולו לקוי ואין ניבר בין איש לאישרו: Quae sicuti curiosis adduxi, ita ipsimet exponant, si lubuerit.
units.tr: §. Maimonides, l.c., also mentions the eunuch of the sun [סריס חמה], which almost coincides with the eunuch of the other kind. He is defined as one who has completed his twentieth year and has not produced two hairs, neither on the pubes nor in the beard, and who moreover has all the signs of a eunuch. These are: he has no beard, his hair is sparse, his flesh is smooth, the water of his feet does not foam or bubble, when it rains he makes no bubble, his seed is pale, the water of his feet does not ferment, his skin does not give off vapour, his voice is thin, and he cannot be distinguished between man and woman. I have adduced these for the curious, to expound as they themselves see fit.

units.la: EXCINDETUR anima eius vid.כרת.
units.tr: HIS SOUL SHALL BE CUT OFF [כרת].

units.la: de Excommunicatione usitata apud Hebraeos vid. Seldenum de Synedrio. Cl. Buxtorf. in נרוי & הרם Levissima species erat נרוי Separatio à cætu Ecclesiæ, & erat solummodo amolitio vel amandatio, quando Sacerdotes aliquem immundum & detestandum aversabantur; erat autem illa separatio ad quatuor cubitos, durans triginta dies, si resipiscat: sin minùs duplicatur ad sexaginta, aut triplicatur ad 90. dies. Si nec tum resipuerit secundâ specie punitur, quæ vocatur הרם: Primâ Excommunicationis specie punitus vocatur מנודה, Secundâ מוחרם. הנגודה fit propter 24. causas, quas recenset Maymon in Hal.Talmud thora c.6. & Cl. Buxtorf. in Lex. Talm. p.1304.
units.tr: On the excommunication used among the Hebrews, see Selden, de Synedrio, and Cl. Buxtorf under [נידוי] and [חרם]. The mildest kind was [נידוי], separation from the assembly of the Church. It was merely a removal or expulsion, when the priests shunned someone unclean and detestable. This separation extended to four cubits and lasted thirty days, if he repented. If not, it was doubled to sixty days or tripled to ninety. If he still did not repent, he was punished with the second kind, which is called [חרם]. Punishment by the first kind of excommunication is called [מנודה], by the second [מוחרם]. [נידוי] is imposed for twenty-four causes, which Maimonides lists in Hal. Talmud Torah c. 6, and Buxtorf in Lex. Talm. p. 1304.

units.la: §. הנגודה Excommunicatus primâ specie non debet se tondere aut lavare instar lugentis, quamdiu excommunicatus est. Si triginta dies in festo aliquo finiantur, & excommunicatus absolvatur, potest in festo se tondere. Maymon. ubi supra c.7. & Megillah c.3. Non admittitur in consessum ordinarium decem personarum, non sedent iuxta eum ad quatuor ulnas. Docere tamen potest & discere cum aliis separatim. Conducit & conducitur. Propter debita pecuniaria neminem excommunicant, nisi iudicii nomine priùs ter moneatur. Si quis moriatur in excommunicatione ista, iudices feretro eius lapidem imponi curant, indicantes quòd fuerit dignus, ut lapidari fuisset, quòd pœnitentiam non egerit, & separatus fuerit à cœtu Ecclesiæ. Maymon. Hal.Talm. thora cap.7. Exemplum in excommunicatione mortui habes Berach. f.19.1. ubi Elieseris cuiusdam mortui feretrum lapidatum fuisse dicitur.
units.tr: §. One excommunicated in the first kind [נידוי] must not shave or wash like a mourner, as long as he is under excommunication. If the thirty days end on some festival and he is absolved, he may shave on the festival. See Maimonides, ibid., c. 7, and Megillah c. 3. He is not admitted to the ordinary assembly of ten persons, and they do not sit within four ells of him. He may, however, teach and learn separately with others. He may hire and be hired. For debts of money they excommunicate no one unless he has first been warned three times in the name of the court. If anyone dies under this excommunication, the judges have a stone placed on his bier, indicating that he deserved to be stoned, because he did not repent and was separated from the assembly of the Church. See Maimonides, Hal. Talm. Torah c. 7. An example of excommunication after death is in Berach. f. 19. 1, where the bier of a certain dead man named Eliezer is said to have been stoned.

units.la: §. Excommunicatio נידוי faciebat vel כפניו in facie excommunicati, coràm, vel לא בפניו non coràm. Si coram excommunicatio fit alicui denuntiata, etiam coram solvenda est. Si non coram, poterat vel coràm vel non coram solvi. Si quis absens excommunicandus erat, ipsi excommunicatio significabatur per alium aliquem, (talis annuntiationis exemplum exstat Hierof. Moed Katon cap.3.) vel per schedam à Scriba publico scriptam, quæ dicebatur כתב של נידוי vid. Maymon. l.m.c. &Schulchan Aruch in Chosen hamishpat num.11.sect.4.
units.tr: §. Excommunication [נידוי] was either [כפניו], in the face of the excommunicated person, that is, in his presence, or [לא בפניו], not in his presence. If the excommunication was pronounced in someone's presence, it must also be lifted in his presence. If it was pronounced in his absence, it could be lifted either in his presence or not. If someone who was to be excommunicated was absent, the sentence was made known to him through another person (an example of such an announcement is in Hierosol. Moed Katon c. 3), or by a writing set down by a public scribe, which was called [כתב של נידוי]. See Maimonides, l.m. c., and Shulchan Aruch in Chosen hamishpat num. 11, sect. 4.

units.la: §. Viros doctos & præstantes propter nulla delicta excommunicant בפרהסיא publicè, nisi propter delictum Ieroboami & Sociorum eius: In reliquis verò culpis ipsos plagis cædunt בצנעא in secreto, & extra publicum conspectum. Maymon. ibid.
units.tr: §. They do not excommunicate learned and eminent men publicly [בפרהסיא] for any offences, except the offence of Jeroboam and his associates. For other faults they beat them in secret [בצנעא], out of public view. See Maimonides, ibid.

units.la: §. Excommunicabant olim Cuthæos per שם המפורש Nomen Iehova. Capit. R.Eliezeris c.38. Tanchuma sect. וישב.
units.tr: §. They once excommunicated the Cuthaeans by the Ineffable Name [שם המפורש], the name Jehovah. See Capit. R. Eliezeris c. 38, and Tanchuma, sect. [וישב].

units.la: §. De septem illis qui sunt לשמים כנודין Cœlitus excommunicati, vid. Pesachin sol.113.2.
units.tr: §. On the seven who are [לשמים כנודין], excommunicated by heaven, see Pesachin fol. 113. 2.

units.la: §. המוחרם אינו שונה לאחרים ואין שונין לו Excommunicatione חרם percussus, neque docet nec discit cum aliis, solus autem potest studere, ne doctrinæ suæ oblivisca tur. Non conducit neque conducitur: nullum commercium, nulla consuetudo cum ipso habenda, duntaxat ipsi licet victualia emere. Maymon. Hal.Talm. torah.cap.7.
units.tr: §. One smitten with [חרם] excommunication does not teach others, nor are others taught by him; he may study alone, so that he does not forget his learning. He neither hires nor is hired. No commerce or fellowship is to be had with him; only it is lawful to buy food from him. See Maimonides, Hal. Talm. Torah, c. 7.

units.la: §. Cum tali excommunicato non licet edere nec bibere. Iore Dea num.334. parag.5. (Confer 1.Cor.5.11.
units.tr: §. With such an excommunicated person it is not lawful to eat or drink. See Iore Dea num. 334, parag. 5. (Compare 1 Cor. 5. 11.)

units.la: §. חרם non potest fieri nisi in coetu & à coetu decem virorum Pirke R.Eliefer cap. 38. Potest autem solvi à tribus etiam הדיוטות vulgaribus, vel ab uno gravi viro המופחה. Maymon ubi supra.
units.tr: Herem cannot be made except in an assembly and by an assembly of ten men (Pirke R. Eliezer ch. 38). It may, however, be loosed by three ordinary men, or by one grave man [המופחה]. Maimonides, as above.

units.la: §. Formam Anathematis Iudaici refert Cl. Buxtorf. in חרם.
units.tr: The form of the Jewish anathema is given by the famous Buxtorf, under חרם.

units.la: §. Tertia excommunicationis species & omnium gravissima vocatur שמתא, per quam homo post omnia humana media totaliter & finaliter soli divino iudicio destinabatur: Probabile est, illud nomen esse compositum ex שו Deus & אתא venit, ut ita idem sit quod Apostoli אתא מרן Maranatha: Dominus venit. Alii vero uti in Moed Katon sol.17.1. dicunt שמתא idem esse ac מיתה שם ibi est mors, vel שממה desolatio: quia ut notat Gloss. est consumptus & perditus.
units.tr: The third kind of excommunication, and the most severe of all, is called שמתא [shammata]. By it a man, after all human means had failed, was wholly and finally left to the divine judgment alone. It is probable that this name is compounded of שו (God) and אתא (comes), so that it means the same as the Apostle's Maranatha, "the Lord comes." Others, however, as in Moed Katan fol. 17.1, say that שמתא is the same as מיתה שם, "there is death," or שממה, "desolation," because, as the Gloss notes, the man is consumed and destroyed.

units.la: §. Schammata gravius esse excommunicationis genus, patet ex Glossa R.Salomonis in Pesach sol.52.1. Ibi enim rationem dat, quare Sapiens non excommunicetur, משום דשמתא חמורה Quia Schammata res gravissima est, habebant autem rationem legis divinae. In hunc sensum etiam scribit R.Ascher in Tosaphot Pesach sol.130.col.2. אין משמתינן אלא על דבר חמור Excommunicatione שמתא non utimur nisi propter rem gravissimam.
units.tr: That shammata is a more severe kind of excommunication is clear from the gloss of R. Solomon on Pesachim fol. 52.1. There he gives the reason why a sage is not excommunicated: "because shammata is a most grave matter, and they had regard to the divine law." To the same effect R. Asher writes in the Tosafot on Pesachim fol. 130, col. 2: "We do not excommunicate with shammata except for a most grave matter."

units.la: §. Aliquando נדוי & שמתא confunduntur, ut ex Lex.Talm. p.2467. videre est: ubi etiam aliis exemplis probat שמתא non semper sensu illo rigido fumi, ut plane omnem solutionem excludat. Ibi etiam plura de Schammata reperies.
units.tr: Sometimes נדוי [niddui] and שמתא are confused, as may be seen from Lex. Talm. p. 2467. There, by other examples too, he shows that שמתא is not always taken in that rigid sense, so as to exclude every possibility of absolution. There you will also find more about shammata.

units.la: §. Salomo in templo duas constituit portas, per unam sponsi, per alteram vero excommunicati soli ingrediebantur; lugentes obvelabant ora, sed non excommunicati; quando ita templum ingrediebantur per illas portas, ab omnibus egredientibus salutabantur; lugenti dicebant Ille qui hanc domum inhabitat, consoletur te השובן בית יתנחם. Excommunicato vero, Qui inhabitat hanc domum יתיב בלבך indat animo tuo, ut obtempere√s verbis sapientum tuorum, & reflituant te. Nota hic, communem ingrediendi viam in templum fuisse ad dextram, egrediendi vero ad sinistram; At excommunicati, lugentes, soli illi erant, qui sinistra via & extraordinario ut ita dicam, itinere usi sunt. Ex his portis poterant ita omnes egredi, sed praeter hos nemo ingredi. vid. Middot. c. 2. Pirke Eliezer c. 17.
units.tr: Solomon set up two gates in the temple: through one the bridegrooms entered, through the other only the excommunicated. Mourners covered their faces, but not the excommunicated. When people entered the temple through these gates, they were greeted by everyone going out. To the mourner they said, "May he who dwells in this house comfort you" [השובן בית יתנחם]. To the excommunicated they said, "May he who dwells in this house" [יתיב בלבך] "put it into your heart to obey the words of your sages, and so they may restore you." Note here that the common way of entering the temple was on the right, and of leaving on the left; but the excommunicated and the mourners alone used the left way, and, as I may say, an extraordinary route. Through these gates everyone could go out, but no one could go in except these. See Middot ch. 2, Pirke Eliezer ch. 17.

units.la: §. In solenni excommunicatione tubis ad clangendum usi sunt. Bab. Sanhed. sol. 107.2. Produxit Iosua fil. Perachia quadringentas tubas, & (Iesum) Anathematizavit. vid. eiusdem Tract. sol. 7.2. ubi Gloss. cum agitur de כלי ניינ exprese dicit, tubis iudices ut sos furifie ad excommunicationem. De praeconio publico contra obstinatos in vitiis edito vid. offensio.
units.tr: In a solemn excommunication they used trumpets for sounding. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 107.2: "Joshua son of Perachiah brought out four hundred trumpets and anathematized (Jesus)." See the same tractate, fol. 7.2, where the Gloss, when treating of the כלי [keli], expressly says that "judges sound trumpets for excommunication." For the public proclamation against those obstinate in vices, see offensio.

units.la: Expiationis festum celebrabatur die decimo mensis Tisri: Septem dies ante festum Sacerdos summus e domo sua sese confert ad conclave (Hebrew), ut se exerceat circa ritus diei expiationis adventantis, & ad othcium illius diei se promptum paratumq; reddat. Postquam eò se contulit, ei alium Sacerdotem substituunt, si quod vitium forte ipsi contingeret: Secundum R.Iehudam ipsi etiam alia uxor substituitur, si forte uxor eius moreretur; nam in illo die uxorem habere debet, quia preces ipsi pro integra domo familiaque eius fundendæ sunt. Ioma c.1.
units.tr: The feast of atonement was celebrated on the tenth day of the month Tishri. Seven days before the feast, the high priest withdrew from his house to a chamber (Hebrew), to practise the rites of the approaching Day of Atonement and to make himself ready and prepared for the duties of that day. Once he had gone there, another priest was appointed in his place, in case some defect should befall him. According to R. Judah, another wife was also appointed for him, in case his wife should die; for on that day he ought to have a wife, since prayers are to be poured out for his whole house and family. Yoma ch. 1.

units.la: §. Cum ibi erat Summus Sacerdos, quinquies in die se lavabat, & decies manus & pedes sanctificabat; atque hæc omnia in loco sancto peragebat, eâ solâ lotione exceptâ, quæ fiebat in loco prophano,supra portas aquarum. Gemara ad Ioma. Omnibus istis septem diebus ipse sanguinem spargebat, suffitum a olebat,lucernas aptabat, pedem & caput sacrificii iugis offerebat; Synedrium etiam ad ipsum mittebat aliquos ex senioribus, qui coram ipso legebant ritus peragendos in die expiationis,& ipsi dicebant,Domine Sacerdos magne, lege ipsemet, forsan oblitus es, aut forsan non didicisti. (sub templo secundo enim sæpius ad Sacerdotium pervenerunt homines indocti, solâ Regum gratiâ, aut suis artibus ad hoc munus erecti: Maymon.)
units.tr: While the high priest was there, he washed himself five times a day and sanctified his hands and feet ten times; all of this he did in the holy place, except for one washing, which was done in a profane place above the water gates. Gemara on Yoma. On all those seven days he himself sprinkled blood, offered incense, trimmed the lamps, and offered the foot and head of the continual sacrifice. The Sanhedrin also sent some of the elders to him, who read to him the rites to be performed on the Day of Atonement, and they said to him, "Great priest, read it yourself; perhaps you have forgotten, or perhaps you never learned it." (For under the second temple, unlearned men were often raised to the priesthood, by the sole favour of kings or by their own arts: Maimonides.)

units.la: §. Vespera diem expiationis præcedente adducebant summo Sacerdoti iuvencos, aritetes,ut eos mactando expeditus fieret ad ministerium: vesperâ quoque hac non permittebant ei multùm edere, quia cibus somnium inducit. Deinde Seniores Synedrii cum Senioribus Sacerdotum, cum in conclave Abtines ducebant, & discedentes ipsum sic adiurabant אישי כהן גדול אנו שלוחי בית דין ואתה שלוחינו ושליח בית דין משכיעין אנו עליך בכי ששיכן את שמו בנית הוה שלא תשנה דבר מכל מה שאמרנו לך :
units.tr: On the evening before the Day of Atonement they brought young bullocks and rams to the high priest, so that by slaughtering them he might be free for the ministry. On this evening too they did not allow him to eat much, because food induces sleep. Then the elders of the Sanhedrin, together with the elders of the priests, led him into the chamber of Abtines, and as they departed they adjured him thus: "Priest of the great priest, we are the messengers of the court, and you are our messenger and the messenger of the court; we adjure you by him whose name dwells in this house that you change nothing of all that we have told you" [אישי כהן גדול אנו שלוחי בית דין ואתה שלוחינו ושליח בית דין משכיעין אנו עליך בכי ששיכן את שמו בנית הזה שלא תשנה דבר מכל מה שאמרנו לך].

units.la: Domine Sacerdos magne, nos legati fumus Synedrii magni, & tu legatus noster & Synedrii, adiuramus te per eum cuius nomen habitat in boc templo, ne mutes quicquam ex omnibus istis, quae tibi diximus. Deinde hic & illi flentes discesserunt; luramentum autem hoc introductum fuit, quia Sacerdotes quidam, extra velum adolere, & alia mutare conati sunt.
units.tr: "Great priest, we are the envoys of the great Sanhedrin, and you are our envoy and that of the Sanhedrin; we adjure you by him whose name dwells in this temple that you change none of all those things which we have told you." Then they withdrew, both these and those weeping. This oath was introduced because some priests had tried to burn incense outside the veil and to change other things.

units.la: §. Dimissis Synedrii legatis, fummus Sacerdos, fi doctus erat, legebat & exponebat; sin minus, discipuli sapientum legebant & exponebant; lectionem vero sumebant ex Esra, Zacharia, Chron.Daniele, &c.
units.tr: When the envoys of the Sanhedrin had been dismissed, the high priest, if he was learned, read and expounded; if not, the disciples of the sages read and expounded. They took the reading from Ezra, Zechariah, Chronicles, Daniel, and so on.

units.la: Si dormire gestiebat, iuniores Sacerdotes percutiebant coram eo digito indice (i.e. sonum ipsorum illisione fecerunt, vel tibiis luserunt, quod magis arridet,) & ipsi dicebant, Domine Sacerdos, remitte semel super pavimentum, (i.e. pedibus consiste aliquantulum) ipsumque ita occupatum tenebant, donec mactationis tempus instaret.
units.tr: If he was eager to sleep, the younger priests struck with the index finger in front of him (that is, they made a sound by striking, or they played on pipes, which pleases him more), and they said, "Priest, stand up once on the pavement" (that is, stand on your feet for a little while). They kept him thus occupied until the time of the sacrifice drew near.

units.la: §. Singulis diebus expurgabant altare sub gallicinium, in die expiationis vero à media nocte, & in tribus festis magnis à vigilia prima, quia in illis festis ad gallicinium atrium Israelitis iam repletum erat.
units.tr: Each day they cleaned the altar at cockcrow; on the Day of Atonement, from midnight; and on the three great feasts, from the first watch, because on those feasts the court was already full of Israelites by cockcrow.

units.la: Si instabat tempus mactationis, clamabat speculator ברקאי Coruscationes, vel illuminatum est cœlum usque ad Hebron. Quo audito, deducebatur summus Sacerdos ad lavatorium, (in cultu enim omnis ille qui naturæ satisfe‐ cerat, manus & pedes lavare debebat.) extendebant autem inter ipsum & populum velum byssinum, ne, dum lavabat, in eius conspecu esset.
units.tr: When the time of the sacrifice drew near, the watchman called out "Barqai" (Lightnings), or "the sky is lit up as far as Hebron." On hearing this, the high priest was led to the laver (for in worship everyone who had satisfied a natural need had to wash hands and feet). A linen veil was stretched between him and the people, so that while he washed he would not be in their sight.

units.la: §. Hoc facto induebatur vestibus aureis, & mactabat iuge sacrificium, sanguinem accipiebat, spargebat, intrabat ad adolendum, aptabat lucernas, caput membra, frixa, & vina offerebat.
units.tr: Having done this, he was clothed in golden vestments, slaughtered the continual sacrifice, received and sprinkled the blood, went in to offer incense, trimmed the lamps, and offered the head, limbs, fat, and wine.

units.la: Manè Summus Sacerdos induebatur vestibus quæ octodecim, vesperi vero vestibus quæ duodecim minas valebant, quæ pecunia ex Ecclesiæ nummis erogabatur.
units.tr: In the morning the high priest was clothed in vestments worth eighteen minas, and in the evening in vestments worth twelve minas; this money was paid out of the Church's funds.

units.la: §. Quando Iuvencum pro se & domo sua mactabat Summus Sacerdos, stabat in Oriente, facie in Occidentem versa, manibusque impositis confitebatur, dicens; Obsecro, Domine, deliqui ego & domus mea, remitte nunc delicta, iuxta quod scriptum est in lege, Quoniam in die hac expiabit &c.
units.tr: When the high priest slaughtered the bullock for himself and his house, he stood on the east side, facing west, and with his hands laid on he made confession, saying: "I beseech you, Lord, I and my house have sinned; now forgive the sins, according as it is written in the law, 'For on this day he shall make atonement'," and so on.

units.la: Deinde ibat ad orientem altaris, Vicarius eius erat ipsi à dexteris, præfectus custodiæ à sinistris.
units.tr: Then he went to the east side of the altar; his deputy stood on his right, and the prefect of the guard on his left.

units.la: Ibi erant duo hirci, cum forte in urna. Sorte proiectâ quis debeat offerri & quis emitti, sortes hircis imponebat dicendo לה׳ יהוה.
units.tr: There were two goats, and the lots were in an urn. When the lot had been cast as to which should be offered and which sent away, he placed the lots on the goats, saying "For the LORD" [לה׳ יהוה].

units.la: Deinde ad caput hirci emissarii alligabat linguam coccineam, & sistebat eum ad locū, unde erat emittend°, alteram vero linguam alligabat ad cervicem hirci mactandi; postea secundâ vice ibat ad iuvencum, quem pro se & familia sua offerebat, repetens eadem verba, quæ antea. Precibus peractis mactabat ipsum, sanguinem in patera excipiebat, dabat miscenti, & cum prunis in thuribulo ab altari desumptis progrediebatur versus Sanctum Sanctorum; inter procedendum pugillabat suffitum, & vela transeundo pergebat; donec perveniret ad arcam, inter cuius duos vectes deinde collocabat thuribulum, suffimentum super prunas congerebat, ita ut tota domus repleretur fumo; exibat retrorsum, brevem orationem in domo exteriore recitabat, nec diu orationi insistebat, ne Israeli metum incuteret; (si enim diu moratus fuisset, populus facile suspicari potuisset, illum mortuum esse, nam Maymon. dicit plurimos qui non debito modo adoleverant, morte punitos fuisse.)
units.tr: Then he tied a scarlet thread to the head of the scapegoat and set it at the place from which it was to be sent away; the other thread he tied to the neck of the goat to be slaughtered. Afterwards, a second time, he went to the bullock which he offered for himself and his family, repeating the same words as before. When the prayers were finished, he slaughtered it, received the blood in a dish, and gave it to the one who stirred it. Then, with coals taken from the altar in a censer, he went forward towards the Holy of Holies; as he went he took up incense in handfuls and passed through the veils, until he reached the ark, between whose two poles he set down the censer and heaped the incense upon the coals, so that the whole house was filled with smoke. He came out backwards, recited a brief prayer in the outer house, and did not linger over it, lest he strike fear into Israel. (For if he had delayed long, the people could easily have suspected that he was dead; Maimonides says that many who had not burned incense in the proper manner were punished with death.)

units.la: §. A quo tempore sublata fuit arca, thuribulum collocabat super lapidem illum cui arca impósita erat; thuribulo dispósito sanguinem à miscente sumebat, intrabat iterum in Sanctuarium, & stabat inter vectes arcæ, & ex illo spargebat semel sursum, & septies deorsum, non intuebatur ad spargendum sursum aut deorsum, (i. e. non intuebatur propitiatorium, multò minùs illud sanguine aspergebat ex intentione, quod observ.) Postquam autem Sanctum Sanctorum debito ritu expiavit, sanguinem Iuvenci & hirci denuò sumpsit, ad tabernaculum conventus expiandum. Post factam expiationem quicquid sanguinis supererat, effundebatur ad basin altaris exterioris, ex quo loco per fistulam in torrentem Kedron manabat, vendebaturque olitoribus ad ftercorandos hortos. Si accideret, ut Summus Sacerdos aliquod ministerium, ex illis quæ hoc die peragenda sunt anteverteret, ita ut non legitimum ordinem observaret, omnia frustra sunt.
units.tr: §. From the time the ark was removed, he placed the censer on the stone on which the ark had rested. With the censer set down, he took the blood from the one who was mixing it, went back into the Sanctuary, stood between the poles of the ark, and sprinkled from it once upward and seven times downward. He did not look up or down while sprinkling (that is, he did not look at the mercy seat, much less sprinkle it deliberately with the blood, which should be noted). Once he had made atonement for the Holy of Holies in the proper manner, he took the blood of the bullock and of the goat again, to make atonement for the tent of meeting. After the atonement was made, whatever blood was left was poured out at the base of the outer altar. From there it ran through a conduit into the Kidron brook, and was sold to gardeners to fertilise their gardens. If it happened that the High Priest performed some part of the rites to be carried out on this day out of its order, so that he did not keep the lawful sequence, everything was in vain.

units.la: §. Hirci diei expiationis debent esse pares aspectu, statura & pretio, simul etiam à grege sumpti. Si unus ex illis forte iactâ moritur, alius in eius locum adduci debet, & fi compar non reperitur, par novum hircorum adduci debet. [illegible, ~3 letters]bat Sum. Sacerd. ad hircum emissarium, duasque manus ei imponebat, & confitebatur, Obsecro Domine, deliquit & rebellis fuit Domus Israel, remitte nunc delicta, sicut scriptum est, quia in die hoc expiabit super vos, ad mundandum vos coram Iehova &c. Sacerdotes verò & populus, qui in atrio stabat, cùm nomen Iehova ex ore eius egrediebatur, fe incurvabant, & in facies procumbentes dicebant, fit nomen gloriosum regni eius in secula seculorum.
units.tr: §. The goats of the Day of Atonement must be alike in appearance, size and price, and both taken from the same flock. If one of them happens to die before the lot is cast, another must be brought in its place; and if no like one is found, a new pair of goats must be brought. The High Priest stood by the scapegoat and laid both hands upon it and confessed: I beseech you, O Lord, your people the house of Israel has sinned and rebelled; forgive their sins now, as it is written, for on this day he shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you before Jehovah, etc. The priests and the people who stood in the court, when the name Jehovah went out from his mouth, bowed themselves and, falling on their faces, said: Blessed be the name of the glory of his kingdom for ever and ever.

units.la: §. Deinde hircus traadebatur ei, qui eum in desertum ducturus erat; Quivis ad ducendum legitimus erat, non tamen permittebant, ut Israelita eum duceret, quamvis nec hoc semper observatum fuerit. Egrediebatur hircus super tabulatum (Gall. Efchaffaut,) propter Babylonios, qui crines ei vellicabant, & ad egrediendum utgebant. (v.Babyl.) Tribus milliaribus, (alii dicunt duodecim) distabat Hierosolyma & locus pix quo deportandus erat hircus, & nonaginta nobiles Hierofolymitani comitabantur hirci ductorem usque ad Tabernaculum primum, quorum erant decem(ulterius non poterant, propter terminum Sabbathi, )alii deinde ipsum ad secundum Tabernaculum comitabantur, & sic deinceps, excepto ultimo, ex quo non progrediebantur ad locum Zuk, sed stabant e longinquo, & observabant, quid ductor acturus esset. Ille verò cum ibi appulit, dividebat linguam coccineam, unam partem alligabat rupi, alteram inter cornua hirci, postea hircum depellebat deorsum, qui vix ad medium precipitii perveniens iam in frusta diminutus erat. Ductor verò hirci ibat ad ultimum Tabernaculum, & in illo sedebat, donec advesperasceret.
units.tr: §. Then the goat was handed over to the man who was to lead it into the wilderness. Anyone was lawful to lead it, though they did not permit an Israelite to do so, although even this was not always observed. The goat went out upon a platform (Fr. echafaud) because of the Babylonians, who used to pluck its hair and urge it to go out. The place to which the goat was to be taken was three miles (others say twelve) from Jerusalem, and ninety noble Jerusalemites accompanied the leader of the goat as far as the first booth; of these, ten (they could not go further because of the Sabbath limit) accompanied him to the second booth, and so on, except for the last, beyond which they did not go on to the place of Zuk, but stood at a distance and watched what the leader would do. When he arrived there, he divided a scarlet thread, tied one part to the rock and the other between the goat's horns, and then pushed the goat down, and by the time it reached the middle of the precipice it was already torn into pieces. The leader of the goat then went to the last booth and sat in it until evening came.

units.la: §. Hirco Asafel dimisso summus Sacerdos iuvencum & hircum, qui comburi debebant, findebat, & eorum viscera educebat, deinde extra urbem in illum locum ubi cineres altaris deferri solebant, portari & comburi curabat. Hircum emissarium in desertum venisse Sacerdoti summo significabatur ex speculis, in quibus agitatione sudarii signum dabant.
units.tr: §. After the scapegoat had been sent away to Azazel, the High Priest cut up the bullock and the goat that were to be burned, took out their entrails, and then had them carried and burned outside the city, in the place where the ashes of the altar were usually taken. It was signalled to the High Priest from the watchers, by waving a cloth, that the goat for Azazel had reached the wilderness.

units.la: §. Quo tempore Iuvencus & hircus cremabantur, S.Sacerdos publicè legebat; vid. Sotah. etiam benedicebat, v. S.Sacerdos. vesperi huius diei suffitum adolebat, & amicis, cum salvus evasit, convivium instruxit. In die expiationis exceptis puerulis omnes ieiunare, & a lotione & unctione abstinere debuerunt. Vid. haec omnia prolixius in tratt. Ioma Mischna & Maymon.
units.tr: §. At the time the bullock and the goat were being burned, the High Priest read aloud in public (see Sotah); he also gave the blessing (see High Priest). On the evening of this day he burned incense, and when he had escaped safely, he prepared a feast for his friends. On the Day of Atonement, all were to fast except the little children, and they were to abstain from washing and anointing. See all these things at greater length in the tractate Yoma of the Mishnah and Maimonides.

units.la: §. In Expiationis die egressus est Ismael Ben Camithi summus Sacerdos, ut cum Duce quodam Ethnico colloqueretur; inter confabulandum sparsa est saiva ab istius Ducis ore in eius vestes, unde pollutus non potuit illo die ministerium obire, sed fratri suo hanc Spartam committere debuit. Etiam alia vice contigit, ut cùm in die expiationis summus Sacerdos ob contractam immunditiem ministerio fungi non posset, ingressus sit Ben Elam מציאורין è Zippori, & cultu functus sit. Hierof. Ioma folio 38. 4. Hierof. Megillah folio 72. 1.
units.tr: §. On the Day of Atonement the High Priest Ismael ben Camithi went out to speak with a certain heathen leader; during the conversation, some of the spittle from that leader's mouth was splashed onto his garments, and being thereby defiled he could not perform the service that day, but had to hand this charge (sparta) over to his brother. On another occasion it also happened that, when the High Priest on the Day of Atonement could not serve because of an uncleanness he had contracted, Ben Elam, מציאורין [Metsiaurin], from Zippori, went in and performed the worship. Jerusalem Yoma fol. 38.4. Jerusalem Megillah fol. 72.1.

units.la: §. Quamdiu Simeon iustus vixerat, caper qui die expiationis emittebatur, deiectus de præcipitio semper comminuebatur, sed post obitum eius, aufugit vivus in desertum, & fuit à Saracenis comestus; sors etiam quæ illo die projici solebat, non semper ad dexteram ut solebat, sed etiam ad sinistram prodiit: Hierof.Ioma sol. 43.3. Quæ manifesta erant signa deficientis cultus Ceremonialis appropinquante Christo.
units.tr: §. As long as Simeon the Just lived, the goat that was sent out on the Day of Atonement, when it was thrown from the precipice, was always torn to pieces; but after his death it escaped alive into the wilderness and was eaten by the Saracens. Also, the lot which was usually cast on that day did not always come up on the right hand, as it usually did, but also came up on the left: Jerusalem Yoma fol. 43.3. These were plain signs of the failing of the ceremonial worship as Christ drew near.

units.la: F.
units.tr: F.

units.la: FABIS vescebantur iuvenes formosi, Daniel. 1. 12. ut per eructationes crepitusque (earum effectus) à concubitu eorum masculo arcerentur Chaldæi. R. Saadias in loc. faba fressa somnum inducit, idcirco eius usus S. Socerdoti prohibita in die Expiationis v. L.T.B. pag.480.
units.tr: Beautiful young men were fed on beans, Daniel 1:12, so that the Chaldeans might be kept from intercourse with them by the belching and wind (their effect). R. Saadias on the passage: boiled beans induce sleep. For this reason their use was forbidden to the holy priest on the Day of Atonement. See L.T.B., p. 480.

units.la: FACULTATES הגוים Christianorum sunt instar solitudinis, (communes & expositæ omnibus) primus qui eas occupat, earum Dominus est. Bab. Batra sol.54.
units.tr: The possessions of the Christians [הגוים] are like a wilderness, common to all and open to all. Whoever first takes possession of them is their lord. Bab. Batra, fol. 54.

units.la: §. Ob quatuor res facultates Patrumfamilias traduntur fisco regni. 1. Quòd detineant obligationes iam solutas; 2. Quòd mutuò dent in usuram. 3. Quòd peccantes non castigent; 4. Quòd decernentes, ut Eleemosynæ publicè dentur, ipsimet nullas dent. Succah sol. 29.1. de bonis immobilibus & mobilibus vid. Buxt. L.T. in קירף.
units.tr: §. For four reasons the property of a householder is handed over to the king's treasury: (1) because he withholds debts already paid; (2) because he lends at interest; (3) because he does not punish sinners; (4) because, although he decrees that alms be given publicly, he gives none himself. Succah, fol. 29.1, concerning movable and immovable goods. See Buxtorf, L.T., under קירף.

units.la: FOEMINÆ immunitatem à pluribus ritibus habent; hinc illæ indulsiones. Fœminæ, servi & parvuli ad hæc non tenentur. Beracot cap.3.3. Fœminæ, servi & parvuli non tenentur ad recitanda phylacteria nec ad gestanda. H.Kiddufchin f.61.3. Omnes debebant in festo magno comparêre, excepto Androgyno, surdo, parvulo, mulieribus, &c. Chagiga c.1.1. Ad Siclum solvendum non tenentur mulieres, servi, parvuli, Schekalim c.1. פסחים של נשי ישר Pafchata fœminarum sunt ex Arbitrio, i.e. ea etiam absque reatu omittere possunt.
units.tr: WOMEN have exemption from many rites; hence those indulgences. Women, slaves and children are not bound to these. Berachot, ch. 3.3: Women, slaves and children are not bound to recite the phylacteries, nor to wear them. H. Kiddushin, f. 61.3: All were obliged to appear at the great festival, except the hermaphrodite, the deaf, children, women, etc. Chagigah, ch. 1.1. Women, slaves and children are not obliged to pay the shekel. Shekalim, ch. 1. The Passover of women is at their discretion [פסחים של נשי ישר], that is, they may omit it even without guilt.

units.la: §. Matronæ cuidam, de peccato quod Israelitæ in confectione vituli comiserunt, quærenti, Respondit R.Eleasar, Ne doceat fit mulier nisi quoad colum. Dixit ei Hyrcanus filius eius, Eò quòd ei non respondetur verbo uno è lege, detrahet ea à nobis trecentos coros decimales annuatim. Cui ille, in ignem eant potius, quàm tradantur verba legis fœminæ. Bab.Sotah f.21.2. in Gloss. v. etiam Bammidbar R.f.135.
units.tr: §. When a certain matron asked about the sin which the Israelites committed in making the calf, Rabbi Eleazar answered: Let not a woman be taught anything except the distaff. His son Hyrcanus said to him: Because you do not answer her a single word from the law, she will take from us three hundred tithe-measures of corn every year. He replied: Let them rather go into the fire than that the words of the law be delivered to a woman. Bab. Sotah, f. 21.2, in the Gloss, s.v.; see also Bammidbar Rabbah, f. 135.

units.la: §. De Mulierum loquacitate vid. Cabi.
units.tr: §. On the talkativeness of women, see Cabi.

units.la: §. Mulierum quatuor sunt species, gulosa, aufcultatrices, pigra, Zelotypa. Berefchit Rab. Sect.45. Qui mulieres multiplicat, multiplicat veneficas. Avot. c.2.7. Earum non valet testimonium q.d. & mentita est Sara &c. Gen. 18.15. Opifices omnes, qui pro eis laborant, apostatæ sunt. Kiddufchin 82.1. Ex iis Rex elegi non debet. Maymon.Hal.Melachim c.1.
units.tr: §. There are four kinds of women: greedy, eavesdropping, lazy, jealous. Bereshit Rabbah, sect. 45. Whoever multiplies women multiplies sorceries. Avot, ch. 2.7. Their testimony is not valid, as in Sarah lied, etc., Gen. 18:15. All craftsmen who work for them are apostates. Kiddushin, 82.1. A king ought not to be chosen from among them. Maimonides, Hilchot Melachim, ch. 1.

units.la: §. Qui mulierem aspicit cum intentione, perinde est ac si rem habuisset cum ea. Tract. כלה post init. Nedar.20.1, Sanhed. f.97.2. Confer Matth.5.28.
units.tr: §. He who looks at a woman with desire is just as if he had lain with her. Tract. Kallah, after the beginning; Nedarim, 20.1; Sanhedrin, f. 97.2. Compare Matt. 5:28.

units.la: §. Vxori hæc officia debet maritus: curare ægrotam, redimere captivam, sepelire mortuam, sustentare ipsam filiasque eius ex bonis suis, & filios ad dotis eius hæreditatem admittere. Maym.Hal. אישות c.12.1. Qui tractatus tibi etiam plura alia circa mulieres suppeditare poterit.
units.tr: §. A husband owes these duties to his wife: to nurse her when sick, to ransom her when captive, to bury her when dead, to support her and her daughters from his own goods, and to admit her sons to the inheritance of her dowry. Maimonides, Hilchot Ishut, ch. 12.1. The same treatise can supply you with many other things about women.

units.la: §. Ioh.iv.27. discipuli mirantur, quòd cum fœmina colloquium Christus haberet, præcipuè verò quòd cum Samaritana: Expresse enim Sapientes statuunt in Erubbin sol. 53.2. אל תרבה שיחה עם אשה Ne multiplices colloquium cum fœmina: Rigidiores adhuc sunt in Kiddufchin sol.70.1. Samuel dicit, non salutant fœminam omnino. Et in Ioma sol.240 2. Ne colloquatur quis cum fœmina in platea, imò ne quidem cum propria uxore.
units.tr: §. John 4:27: the disciples marvelled that Christ held converse with a woman, and especially that he did so with a Samaritan. For the wise men expressly lay down, in Erubin, fol. 53.2: [אל תרבה שיחה עם אשה] Do not multiply conversation with a woman. They are stricter still in Kiddushin, fol. 70.1: Samuel says, they do not greet a woman at all. And in Yoma, fol. 240.2: Let no one converse with a woman in the street, nor even with his own wife.

units.la: §. De Mulierum ob adulterium suspectarum potatione vid. Aqua amara. Illum ritum Deus instituit, ut mulier viro iuncta exactè sibi caveret, ne eor mariti ægritudine afficeret: nam etiam innocentes mulieres pleraq; omnibus suis facultatibus actionem illam ignominiosam redimerent. Hac ratione etiam magni & exitiales morbi ordinem domesticum destruentes impediti fuerunt. More Nevoch. III. 49.
units.tr: §. On the drinking of bitter water by women suspected of adultery, see Aqua amara. God instituted that rite so that a woman joined to a husband would guard herself carefully and not bring sickness upon him. For many women, even innocent ones, would have bought off that shameful procedure with all their possessions. By this means also great and deadly diseases, which destroy domestic order, were prevented. More Nevochim, III. 49.

units.la: FAMILIA materna אין קרויה משפחה non vocanda est familia. Iuch. f.55.2. hinc etiam genealogia Christi à marito Mariæ derivatur.
units.tr: FAMILY: the maternal line [אין קרויה משפחה] is not to be called a family. Yevamot, f. 55.2. Hence also the genealogy of Christ is traced through the husband of Mary.

units.la: §. De familiis, quæ officia templi obtinebant vid. Schekalim c.5.1. de illis vero quarum officium erat templo circa lignum prospicere vid. Taanith cap.3.5.
units.tr: §. On the families who held the offices of the temple, see Shekalim, ch. 5.1. On those whose office was to provide wood for the temple, see Ta'anit, ch. 3.5.

units.la: §. De familiis illis, quæ à tempore Esræ usque ad devastationem templi & urbis floruerunt, vide Historiam nostram Doct. Mishnicorum.
units.tr: §. On those families which flourished from the time of Ezra until the destruction of the temple and city, see our History of the Mishnic Teachers.

units.la: §. Bab. Erubbin sol.51.1. Laudantur familiæ Mamal, & Gorionis Arumæ in Galilæa, ob singularem suam liberalitatem. Ad familiarum conservationem apud Synedrium depositi fuerunt libri genealogici; de quibus vid. f.1.
units.tr: §. Bab. Erubin, fol. 51.1. The families of Mamal and Gorion of Arumah in Galilee are praised for their singular liberality. For the preservation of the families, genealogical books were deposited with the Sanhedrin; see on these, f. 1.

units.la: FANA celebriora olim hæc quinque fuerunt; fanum scilicet Bel Babylone; Fanum Nebo in Cursi; Tirathæ in Mapheg; Zeriphæ in Alcalone; & Nisræ in Arabia. Bab. Avoda Zarah f.11.2.
units.tr: TEMPLES: the most famous of these were once five: the temple of Bel at Babylon; the temple of Nebo at Cursi; that of Tirathah in Mapheg; that of Zeriphah in Alcalon; and that of Nisra in Arabia. Bab. Avodah Zarah, f. 11.2.

units.la: FEBRIS ardens curatur calculo, qui prodit è vesica, Gittin 69.2. Febris internæ & externæ medicamenta ibidem narrantur. Pro calculo recipe tres guttas olei Cypri. Ibid. Febris hyemalis gravior est febri æstiva. Ioma sol.29.1.
units.tr: FEVER: a burning fever is cured by a stone which comes out of the bladder. Gittin, 69.2. The remedies for internal and external fever are related ibidem. For the stone, take three drops of Cyprian oil. Ibid. A winter fever is more severe than a summer fever. Yoma, fol. 29.1.

units.la: FERMENTUM. De fermenti & fermentati eiectione vid. בִּיעוּר. Exeunte die decimo tertio ante Pascha בּוּרְקִין אֶת חֲמֵץ לְאוֹר הַנֵּר Investigant fermentum per lucem candela. Pefachin c.i.i. E verbis Scribarum. Investigant atque amovent fermentum initio noctis diei decimo quarti, idque per lucem candelæ &c. Maymon. in חָמֵץ וּמְצִיא cap.2. Idem ibid. cap.1. Prohibitum est comedere fermentatum die decimo quarto à meridie, & porrò viz. ab initio horæ septimæ. Prohibuerunt etiam Sapientes nostri comestionem eius ab initio horæ sextæ. Nec hora quinta comedunt fermentum, ne forte nubilus sit dies, & sic circa tempus error committatur. Ecce discis,quòd licitum sit fermentum comedere die decimo quarto, ad finem usque horæ quartæ, at quintâ non edendum. Vid. plura apud Pascha. §. Matth. 16. 6. dicit Christus Ὁρᾶτε καὶ προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων, quæ verba Discipuli proprie, non Metaphoricè de fermento doctrinæ, intellexerunt: Fuit quidem frequens usus Metaphoricus huius vocis in malam partem, de affectibus scilicet malis, & cordis pravitate, at rarior aut nullus de prava doctrina. De pravis affectibus sonat locus Bab. Berac. sol.17.1. Domine Seculorum, libenter voluntatem tuam perficeremus; ast illud quod impedit tu subde שְׁאוֹר שְׁבִעִיסָה וּשְׁעֻנּוֹ מִלִּיךְ Fermentum scilicet, quod est in massa, & tyrannidem regnorum (Ethnicorum) Gloss. Fermentum quod in massa, sunt pravi affectus, qui in cordibus nostris nos fermentant. Idem sensus est loci Bab.Rosch Haschana f.3.2. N התבור כורש Cyrus fermentatus est, id est, deteriorior & peior evasit. De deliberatione in iudicio, non autem de doctrina intelligendus locus Kimchi in Esai.1.17. Dicunt Rabbini; beatus est ille Iudex, qui fermentat iudicium suum.
units.tr: LEAVEN. On the removal and destruction of leaven, see בִּיעוּר. On the thirteenth day before Passover, they search for leaven by the light of a candle. Pesachim, ch. 1.1. From the words of the Scribes: they search out and remove the leaven at the beginning of the night of the fourteenth day, and this by the light of a candle, etc. Maimonides, on Chametz u-Matzah, ch. 2. The same, ibid., ch. 1: It is forbidden to eat leavened food on the fourteenth day from noon onward, and further, namely from the beginning of the seventh hour. Our wise men also forbade eating it from the beginning of the sixth hour. Nor do they eat leaven at the fifth hour, lest perhaps the day be cloudy and so error be committed about the time. Behold, you learn that it is lawful to eat leaven on the fourteenth day until the end of the fourth hour, but not after the fifth. See more under Pesachim. In Matt. 16:6 Christ says, Ὁρᾶτε καὶ προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων [Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees]; the disciples understood these words properly, not metaphorically, of the leaven of doctrine. There was indeed a frequent metaphorical use of this word in a bad sense, namely of evil affections and perversity of heart, but a rarer one, or none, of bad doctrine. The passage in Bab. Berachot, fol. 17.1, speaks of evil affections: Lord of the ages, we would gladly do your will; but what hinders, you subdue [שְׁאוֹר שְׁבִעִיסָה וּשְׁעֻנּוֹ מִלִּיךְ], that is, the leaven which is in the dough, and the tyranny of kingdoms (of the Gentiles). Gloss: The leaven which is in the dough are the evil affections which leaven us in our hearts. The same sense belongs to the passage in Bab. Rosh Hashanah, f. 3.2: [כורש התבור] Cyrus was leavened, that is, he became worse and more wicked. The passage in Kimchi on Isaiah 1:17 must be understood of deliberation in judgment, not of doctrine: The rabbis say: blessed is that judge who leavens his judgment.

units.la: §. Quo fermento utendum, quo non, anxiè definitur Hierof.Schabbat sol.3.3.
units.tr: §. The Hierosolymitan Shabbat, fol. 3.3, carefully defines what leaven may be used and what may not.

units.la: de Festis generalia quaedam. In festo fossam novam האפר non faciunt, corruptam verò instaurant; reparant etiam vias & plateas & aquaeductus, quaeque deinde publicam utilitatem spectant. Sepulchra etiam consignant, & exeunt ad eradicanda mixta. Moed Katon c. 1.2. Agrum siticulosum in festo irrigare licet, v.f.1. licet fornacem, foculos, & molas erigere. Moed. Katon c. 1.9. vid. sepulchra fodere, Qui olivas suas &c. Hos Radunt &c. Haec scribi in festo &c. Lutlum &c. Cardinem, Canalem, vectem, serram vel clavem, si forte fortuna frangantur, redintegrant in festo, hac tamen conditione, ne quis talium reparationem ex intentione differat ad festum. Condire etiam licet ea condimenta quae in festo edi possunt. Licet unicuique fructus suos in festo in domum introducere, ne illos subducant fures; extrahere etiam linum ex areolis in quibus iacet, ne corrumpatur, modo id data opera in festum non differerit. Servos, iumenta in festo non nisi ad usum festi comparare & conducere licet. Illicitum est in festo removere vasa ex domo in domum, sed in atrium licet. Abscissas ficos, in festo stramine obtegere licet. Qui fructus tegmina & vasa vendunt, id secreto ad necessitatem festi facere possunt. Moed Katon c.1.10. & c.3.1. Ex quo devastatum est Sanctuarium, עזרת feria eodem modo se habent ac Sabbathum. Et nunc Sapientes feriam festis solennibus, initium anni autem & diem expiationis Sabbatho assimilant. Simeon Cyrenæus ἀπ' ἀγρῶ in festo ligna attulit, quod illicitum non fuit. Betsah sol.31.1. die festo מניאים עצים מן השדה Important ligna ex agro vel collecta in unum, vel מן הקרקף a loco aliquo circumsepto, vel sparsa: Si scilicet, ut Gloss. notant, locus ille ultra limites Sabbathicos non distet.
units.tr: Some general points about festivals. On a festival they do not dig a new trench [האפר], but they do repair a ruined one; they also repair roads, streets and aqueducts, and whatever then serves public use. They also mark sepulchres, and go out to root out mixed seed. Moed Katan, ch. 1.2. On a festival it is lawful to irrigate a thirsty field, and to set up an oven, hearths and mills. Moed Katan, ch. 1.9. See digging up sepulchres; those who press their olives, etc. Those who sweep, etc. Writing on a festival, etc. Mud, etc. A hinge, a channel, a bar, a saw or a key, if by chance they are broken, may be mended on a festival, on this condition only: that no one postpone such repair on purpose until the festival. It is also lawful to season those seasonings which may be eaten on a festival. Everyone may bring in his fruits into the house on a festival, lest thieves carry them off; he may also draw out flax from the threshing-floors where it lies, lest it spoil, provided he has not deferred this on purpose until the festival. Servants and beasts may be hired or bought on a festival only for the use of the festival. It is unlawful on a festival to move vessels from house to house, but it is lawful into the courtyard. It is lawful on a festival to cover cut figs with straw. Those who sell fruit, coverings and vessels may do so privately for the needs of the festival. Moed Katan, ch. 1.10, and ch. 3.1. Since the sanctuary was laid waste, the feria [עזרת] stands in the same position as the Sabbath. And now the wise men treat the feria of the solemn festivals alike, but they liken the beginning of the year and the Day of Atonement to the Sabbath. Simeon of Cyrene carried wood from the field [ἀπ' ἀγρῶ] on a festival, which was not unlawful. Betzah, fol. 31.1. On a festival they bring in wood from the field [מניאים עצים מן השדה], either gathered into one place, or [מן הקרקף] from some enclosed place, or scattered: that is, if, as the Gloss notes, that place is not further than the Sabbath limits.

units.la: §. Ob infinitam multitudinem populi ad festa confluentis, ( vide Comparere in festo &c.) tentoria circa urbem Hierosolymitanam fixerunt, ast intra terminos Sabbathicos, ne nimis coarctarentur ex angustia urbis. Gloss. in Pesachin sol.95.2. Maneque convertens te redibis ad tentoria tua. Deut. xvi.7. Nocte festi prima pernoctandum erat intra Hierosolymam. Exinde licitum erat commorari extra mænia; ast intra terminos Sabbathicos. Illud ergo quod dicitur, Ibis ad tentoria tua, hoc vult, Ibis ad tentoria tua, quæ extra mænia Hierosolymæ, at nequaquam in domum tuam. Vid. Aben Efram in Deut. xvi. Hæc lucem afferunt profectionibus illis, quas Christum in festis ad montem olivetum fecisse legimus. De annuntiatione festorum per nuntios vid. Rosch Haschana cap. i. verf.3.
units.tr: §. Because of the immense multitude of people flocking to the festivals (see Comparere in festo, etc.), they pitched tents around the city of Jerusalem, but within the Sabbath limits, so that they would not be too cramped by the narrowness of the city. Gloss. on Pesachin, fol. 95.2: "And in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents," Deut. 16:7. On the first night of the festival one had to spend the night within Jerusalem. After that it was permitted to stay outside the walls, but within the Sabbath limits. So when it says, "You shall go to your tents," it means: go to your tents, which are outside the walls of Jerusalem, and not at all to your house. See Aben Ezra on Deut. 16.
