These things throw light on those journeys which we read that Christ made to the Mount of Olives at the festivals. On the announcement of the festivals by messengers, see Rosh Hashanah ch. 1, v. 3.

units.la: de Festo Expiationis. vid. Expiationis &c.
units.tr: On the Feast of Atonement, see Expiationis &c.

units.la: de Festo Paschatis vid. Pascha. de Festo Tabernaculorum vid. More Nevoch. iii.21. Buxtorf. Synag. c.21. Schindler ad ססה. Ioseph Antiq.iii. c.11. Machsor Hispanorum Iudæorum & Germanorum fermè clauditur hoc festo, propter Hosannas sive Eucharistias; nec non Ecclesiarum Orientalium. Offic. Maron.55.
units.tr: On the Feast of the Passover, see Pascha. On the Feast of Tabernacles, see More Nevochim iii.21; Buxtorf, Synagogue ch. 21; Schindler on ססה; Josephus, Antiquities iii. ch. 11; Offic. Maron. 55. The Machsor of the Spanish and German Jews is almost closed by this feast, on account of the Hosannas or thanksgivings; and likewise that of the Eastern Churches.

units.la: §. Festum Tabernaculorum insequebatur festum Expiatorium, sed in illo tanta solicitudine Sūmo Sacerdoti munia non erant obeunda, maiori etiam lætitiâ erat celebrandum. Die xi.mensis Tisri turbæ, quę Hierosolymâ confluxerunt, se ante festum purificabant, & parabant ad festum necessaria, qualia erant tentoriola, poma citrea, fasciculi palmarum & salicum. Die xiv. vulgo tondebantur in honorem festi. Dies xv. Mensis Tisri erat primus Scenopegiæ. Summa cultus omnium dierum Scenopegiæ recensetur in Hierof.Succah c.5. Summo mane offerebatur sacrificium iuge, deinde sacrificia additionalia, deinde oblationes votiva. Post hæc ad prandium se conferebant; Prandio peracto ad studium legis.Hocinsequebatur sacrificium vespertinum. Tandem dies claudebatur libatione & effusione aquæ. In additionalibus illis sacrificiis notandum 1. maximum ipsorum numerum suisse, ita ut cum sacrificiis iugibus 215. pro ratione annorum, quibus Israelitæ in Ægypto degerunt, fuerint. 2. oblationes illas semper inæquali numero factas fuisse; nam die primâ festi oblati fuerunt tredecim iuvenci, die secundâ verò solummodò duodecim, & sic semper decrescendo: Cuius diminutionis ratio non ita facilè reperiri potest. R. Sal. in Num.29. dicit id faétum esse, ad significandum 7o.nationes,qua per 7o. Iuvencos denotantur, semper diminui & in peius ire debere. Abarb. verò in eund. l. 7o.illos Iuvencos denotare atatem hominis, qua singulis annis aliquid de suo vigore amittit. In his sacrificiis offerendis ita versati sunt ut omnes 24. stationes singulis diebus aliquid haberent, quod offerrent, vid.Succah.c.5. Maym.in Tamid.c.5.
units.tr: §. The Feast of Tabernacles followed the Feast of Atonement, but during that feast the High Priest was not to perform his duties with such anxiety, and it was to be celebrated with greater joy. On the eleventh day of the month Tishri, the crowds who had gathered in Jerusalem purified themselves before the feast and prepared what was needful for the feast, such as little tents, citrons, bundles of palm and willow. On the fourteenth day they commonly had their hair cut in honour of the feast. The fifteenth day of the month Tishri was the first day of Sukkot. The sum of the worship of all the days of Sukkot is set out in Jerusalem Sukkah ch. 5: Early in the morning the continual sacrifice was offered, then the additional sacrifices, then votive offerings. After these they betook themselves to dinner; when dinner was over, to the study of the law. This was followed by the evening sacrifice. At last the day was closed with a libation and the pouring out of water. In those additional sacrifices we should note, first, that their number was very great, so that together with the continual sacrifices there were 215, corresponding to the number of years the Israelites spent in Egypt. Second, those offerings were always made in an unequal number; for on the first day of the festival thirteen bullocks were offered, but on the second day only twelve, and so always decreasing. The reason for this diminution cannot be found so easily. R. Solomon on Num. 29 says that this was done to signify that the seventy nations, which are denoted by the seventy bullocks, must always be diminished and go to the worse. But Abarbanel, on the same passage, says that the seventy bullocks denote the age of man, which each year loses something of its vigour. In offering these sacrifices they were so arranged that all twenty-four courses each had something on each day to offer; see Sukkah ch. 5; Maimonides on Tamid ch. 5.

units.la: §. Lev. 23. 40. Præcipit Deus, ut ad hoc festum celebrandum sumant termites arborum speciosarum, palmas & salices torrentis; Sadducæi (inquit Aben Esra in h.loc.) existimarunt ramos & palmarum spathas ad tentoria applicandas esse; sed Pharisæi constituerunt, ut manibus ferrentur. Postquàm itaque primus dies festì illuxit, ramos palmarum, myrti, salicumque parabant, & illos colligabant aureo vel argenteo aut etiam alius generis filo, semperque eos in manu gestabant. Si quis petit Synagogam, aut visitat ægrotantem, aut alia charitatis officia obit, hunc לולב fasciculum in manu habere debet. Templum absque illo non adeunt, imò singulis diebus expressè illum in templum portant. Maym. in Succah c.7.
units.tr: §. Lev. 23:40. God commands that for the celebration of this feast they take branches of goodly trees, palm fronds, and willows of the brook. The Sadducees (says Aben Ezra on this passage) thought that palm branches and palm sheaths were to be attached to the tents; but the Pharisees decided that they were to be carried in the hands. So when the first day of the festival dawned, they prepared branches of palm, myrtle and willow, and bound them together with gold or silver thread, or with thread of some other kind, and always carried them in the hand. If someone went to the synagogue, or visited a sick person, or performed some other office of charity, he had to have the bundle, lulab [לולב], in his hand. They did not approach the Temple without it; indeed, every day they carried it into the Temple. Maimonides on Sukkah ch. 7.

units.la: §. Erat quidā locus non multū distans Hierosolymâ, qui vocabatur אחנוא, eò descenderunt in festo tabernaculorum, & decerpserunt ramos salicum perlongos, atque abeuntes locarunt eos iuxta latera altaris, incurvatos, ita ut capita eorum in verticem altaris declinarent.Succah c.4.5. Salix dicit Hierof. Succah f. 55.1. יסוד הנבואה est fundamentum prophetiæ: Quod ita intelligendum, Salices illæ maximo cum gaudio & cædebantur,& gestabantur,at(uti alibi dicunt) Spiritus Sanctus non descendit, nisi supra gaudentes.
units.tr: §. There was a certain place not far from Jerusalem, called Ahnoa [אחנוא]. They went down there at the feast of tabernacles and cut off very long willow branches, and on returning they laid them beside the sides of the altar, bent over so that their tops leaned towards the top of the altar. Sukkah ch. 4, 5. The willow, says Jerusalem Sukkah fol. 55.1, is the foundation of prophecy [יסוד הנבואה]. This is to be understood thus: those willows were both cut and carried with the greatest joy; for, as they say elsewhere, the Holy Spirit does not descend except upon those who rejoice.

units.la: §. Postquàm prospexerant sibi de fasciculo, quem manu gestarent, & alio, quem ad altare collocarent, semel singulis diebus atrium ingrediebantur, & fasciculos manibus tenentes altare circumibant hoc occinentes הוה יהוה אנא Salva, obsecro, nunc Domine,prospera,obsecro,Domine. At die festi septies circuiverunt. Maymon. in Succah c.6.
units.tr: §. After they had provided themselves with the bundle which they would carry in the hand, and another which they would place by the altar, they entered the court once each day, and holding the bundles in their hands they went around the altar, singing this: "Ana Adonai, hoshia na" [הוה יהוה אנא]: Save us, we beseech you, now, O Lord; prosper us, we beseech you, O Lord. But on the day of the festival they went around seven times. Maimonides on Sukkah ch. 6.

units.la: §. In festo Scenopegiæ cani solitum est Hallel magnum, id est Psalmi 113.114.115.116.117.118. Dumque ab uno occinerentur verba Psalmorum, à toto cœtu aliquando responsum est ad quasdam clausulas Halleluiah, aliquando agitati & quassati sunt fasciculi, ad clausulas istas הורו נא Gratias agite Domino, in initio Psal. 118. & fine. Item ad clausulam salva obsecro. Succah cap.3.9. Agitatio fasciculorum fuit dextrorsum, sinistrorsum, sursum, deorsum. Bab. Succah sol.27.2. Ratio horum fasciculorum fuit mystica; in initio anni in iudicium prodeunt Israel & nationes mundi, cumque ignorent quinam iustificandi,quinam rei,præcepit Deus ut latarentur cum fasciculis bisce, sicut homo exiens è conspeƈtu iudicis iustificatus lætatur. Rab. Ascher in Succah sol. 66.2.3.
units.tr: §. At the Feast of Tabernacles it was customary to sing the Great Hallel, that is, Psalms 113, 114, 115, 116, 117, 118. While the words of the Psalms were sung by one man, the whole assembly sometimes responded with Hallelujah at certain closing phrases, and sometimes the bundles were waved and shaken at those closing phrases, "Give thanks to the Lord" [הורו נא], at the beginning of Psalm 118 and at its end. Likewise at the closing phrase salva obsecro. Sukkah ch. 3, 9. The waving of the bundles was to the right, to the left, upward, and downward. Babylonian Sukkah fol. 27.2. The reason for these bundles was mystical: At the beginning of the year Israel and the nations of the world come forth to judgment; and since they do not know who will be justified and who guilty, God commanded that they rejoice with these bundles, just as a man who comes out from the presence of the judge rejoices when he has been justified. R. Asher on Sukkah fol. 66.2.3.

units.la: §. Vidimus ipsos in festo hoc unâ manu gestare fasciculum; sed traditione receperunt altera manu לולב malum citreum ferendum esse. In lege nullum expressum de hoc ritu extat præceptum, sed credunt citreum intelligi per הדר ער פרי fructus arborum speciosarum. Lev. 23.40. Ita Ta'm. Hierof. in Succah sol.53.2. rem ita proponunt; per הדר יו intelligitur & fructus elegans & lignum speciosum, at ambo habet Citrus. R.Levi inquit (citrus ibi vocatur הדר יו quia רד flat & permanet ramis appensa ab uno anno ad alterum. vid. Aruch in הדר Bab. Succah sol.35. R. Salomoh & Baal Turim in Lev.23. Et certè Paraphrasis Chaldaica per הדר יו l. c. etiam citrum intellexit. Quales qualitates mala haec citrea habere debuerint, longum hic esset referre, omnes illas curiositates apud Maymon. in Succah velulabb c.8. reperies. Memorabilis est historia illius Sadducaei in Bab. Succah sol.35. & Tosapht. ibid. c.3. qui cùm in festo tabernaculorum aliquam partem cultus non observassset, aliantium malis citreis obrutus (vel ut Talmudici se exprimunt) lapidatus fuit. Cuius facti tamen deinde quidam Regi Iannaeo Sadducaeis addicto poenas dederunt. Iuchasin sol.15.
units.tr: §. We have seen that they carried the bundle in the one hand at this feast; but by tradition they received that in the other hand the citron [לולב] was to be carried. Nothing explicit about this rite is found in the law, but they believe that the citron is meant by "the fruit of goodly trees" [הדר ער פרי], fruit of trees, Lev. 23:40. So the Talmud of Jerusalem in Sukkah fol. 53.2 proposes the matter thus: by "goodly" [הדר] is understood both an elegant fruit and a beautiful wood, and the citrus has both. R. Levi says (the citron is there called "goodly" [הדר] because it [רד] blows and remains, hung on the branches, from one year to the next; see Aruch under הדר, Babylonian Sukkah fol. 35; R. Solomon and Baal Turim on Lev. 23). And indeed the Chaldee paraphrase, rendering "goodly" [הדר יו], also understood the citron. It would be long to relate here what qualities these citron apples ought to have; you will find all those curiosities in Maimonides on Sukkah velulab ch. 8. Memorable is the story of that Sadducee in Babylonian Sukkah fol. 35, and Tosephta ibid. ch. 3, who, when during the feast of tabernacles he had not observed some part of the rite, was pelted with citrons by the people (or, as the Talmudists put it, stoned). Yet some of those who did this were afterwards punished by King Jannaeus, who was devoted to the Sadducees. Yuchasin fol. 15.

units.la: §. Singulis diebus cùm sacrificium matutinum offerebatur, Sacerdos aliquis vase aureo ex fonte Siloah aquam petiit, & vino mixtam, post dispositia membra sacrificii, libavit; populus adstans ipsi solebat acclamare effundenti, tolle manus; ne forte aquam ad pedes suos ejiceret, sicuti fecerat Sadducaeus ille malis citreis trucidatus, cuius modò mentionem fecimus. vid. Tosapht. in Succah c.3. Mischnam c.4. ad hanc libationem ordinariè canebatur Hallel magnum, de quo etiam iam diximus.
units.tr: §. Each day, when the morning sacrifice was offered, a priest drew water in a golden vessel from the fountain of Siloam and poured it out, mixed with wine, after the parts of the sacrifice had been arranged; and the people standing by were accustomed to shout to the one pouring out, "Lift up your hands," lest perhaps he should cast the water at his feet, as that Sadducee had done, who was slain with citrons, of whom we have just spoken. See Tosephta in Sukkah ch. 3; Mishnah ch. 4. At this libation the Great Hallel was ordinarily sung, of which we have also already spoken.

units.la: §. Postquam ita dies transactus erat ordinariis & additionalibus sacrificiis, noếte appropinquante sese accinxerunt ad lætitiam. ניסוך המים effusionis aquæ; quæ ceremonia tanto gaudiô fiebat, ut dicant in Succah c.5. מי שלא ראה שמחת בית השואבה לא ראה שמחה מימיו Qui nun-quam vidit lætitiam effusionis aquæ, non vidit unquam ullam lætitiam. Manè quidem cùm aqua effundebatur, cultus reverentia non permi-sit, ut talem lætitiam ostenderent, quali erant delibuti sub vesperam,omni cultu peracto. Fiebat autem ille ritus hunc in modum, sicuti ex Succah cap.5. & Maym.Succah c.8.apparet. In exitu diei primi festi, descenderunt in atrium mulierum, & scenam magnam ibi ordinarunt, in cuius tabulatis fœminæ supra & viri infra stare poterant. Candelabra aurea erant ibi parietibus affixa, & super ea simpula aurea : erantque quatuor scalæ, quibus ascendebant ad ea : quatuorque Iuvenes sacerdotum in manibus habentes ampullas continentes centum & viginti logos, infundunt in unumquodque fimpulum. Ex lacernis vestimentorum cingulorumque Sacerdotum, ellychnia fecerunt, quibus accenderunt istas lampades, & non erat totis Hierosolymis platea ulla, quæ non corusca-retex ista irradiatione. Viri magnates, religiosi & devoti saltarunt coram iis, in manibus habentes ardentes faces, decantaruntque cantica & doxologias. Levitæ cum cytharis, nabliis, cymbalis aliisque instrumentis Musicis absque numero steterunt in xv. gradibus, quibus defcenditur ab atrio Israelis in atrium mulierum, atque ediderunt canticum. Steterunt etiam duo Sacerdotes in porta superiore,quâ defcenditur ab atrio Israelis in atrium mulierum,cum duabus tubis in manibus. Signo dato cecinerunt tubâ & clanxerunt, & clangendo perrexerunt, donec pervenirent ad portam atrii Orientalem. Cùm illuc perventum, facies suas converterunt ab Oriente in Occidentem, & dixerunt, Patres nostri hoc in loco, versis ad templum dorsis & faciebus ad orientem, adorarunt solem : Nos autem facies & oculos nostros ad Deum convertimus.Hæc omnia in feram noctem protrahebantur, donec tandem sopor & lætitiæ satietas unumquemque domum traherent.
units.tr: §. After the day had passed in this way with the ordinary and additional sacrifices, and as night drew near, they got ready for joy at the pouring out of water [ניסוך המים]. This ceremony was performed with such great gladness that they say in Sukkah ch. 5: "He who has never seen the joy of the place of drawing water has never seen joy in his life" [מי שלא ראה שמחת בית השואבה לא ראה שמחה מימיו]. He who has never seen the joy of the pouring out of water has never seen any joy. In the morning, when the water was poured out, reverence for the worship did not permit them to show such joy as they were filled with in the evening, after all the worship was finished. That rite was performed in the following manner, as appears from Sukkah ch. 5 and Maimonides, Sukkah ch. 8. At the end of the first day of the festival they went down into the court of the women and set up a great platform there; on its planks women could stand above and men below. There were golden candelabra fixed to the walls, and upon them golden bowls; there were four ladders by which they climbed to them; and four young priests, holding jars containing 120 logs, poured them into each bowl. From the cloaks of the priests' garments and their girdles they made wicks, with which they lit these lamps; and there was no street in all Jerusalem that did not shine with that illumination. Leading men, pious and devout, danced before them, holding burning torches, and they sang songs and doxologies. Levites with lyres, harps, cymbals and other musical instruments, without number, stood on the fifteen steps by which one goes down from the court of Israel to the court of the women, and they sang a hymn. Two priests also stood at the upper gate, by which one goes down from the court of Israel to the court of the women, each with two trumpets in his hands. At a signal they sounded the trumpet and blew, and as they blew they went on until they reached the eastern gate of the court. When they arrived there, they turned their faces from the east to the west and said: Our fathers, in this place, with their backs to the temple and their faces to the east, worshipped the sun; but we turn our faces and eyes to God. All these things were drawn out into the late night, until at last sleep and satiety of joy drew each one home.

units.la: §. Huius lætitiæ causam affert Maymon Hal. Succah Velulabh cap. 8. שהשמחה שישמח אורם בעשיית חמצות ובאהבת האל שצוה בהן עבודה גדולה היא Quia magnum Dei cultus erat cum laetitia praeceptum legis implere. Quare etiam non quivis בן עם הארץ ex plebeiis coram Deo actor illius lætitiæ esse poterat, sed solùm Magnates, Synedrii & Academiarum præsides; viri denique insigni pietate celebres. Reliqui verò spectatorum solummodò partes explebant. Tradit porrò Maymon in Succah sol.51.1. Libationem illam aquæ esse traditionem à monte Sinai; & Ionam Prophetam Spiritu Sancto suisse afflatum ex lætitia ob libationem hanc aquæ. vid. reliq. Gloss. in loc. At si quæras, quonam fundamento nitatur hic ritus, in antecessum respondet Maymon. quòd sint abstrusa quaedam signa eius in lege : Verum illi qui non credunt legi traditionali, non credent hunc articulü de libatione aqua. In specie autem I. producunt authoritatem Prophetæ Esaiæ. Succah sol.50.2. Vocatur hæc actio שואבין בית locus haustionis, quia sic scribitur; Et haurietis aquas cum lætitia &c. Esai.xii.3. hinc lætitia illa vocatur שמחת תורה lætitia legis: vel propter legem, Esai. enim lv.1. aquas interpretantur de lege.
units.tr: §. Maimonides, in Hilchot Sukkah ve-Lulav ch. 8, gives the cause of this joy: [שהשמחה שישמח אורם בעשיית חמצות ובאהבת האל שצוה בהן עבודה גדולה היא] because great worship of God is joy in fulfilling the commanded law. For this reason, not every common man (ben am ha-aretz) could lead that joy before God, but only the magnates, the presidents of the Sanhedrin and of the academies, and men famed for singular piety. The rest only played the part of spectators. Maimonides further relates, in Sukkah fol. 51.1, that this libation of water is a tradition from Mount Sinai, and that the prophet Jonah was inspired by the Holy Spirit out of joy at this libation of water; see the other glosses on the passage. But if you ask on what foundation this rite rests, Maimonides answers beforehand that certain hidden signs of it are in the law; yet those who do not believe the traditional law will not believe this article about the libation of water. In particular, they produce the authority of the prophet Isaiah. Sukkah fol. 50.2: this action is called [בית השואבין] the place of drawing, because it is written thus: And you shall draw water with joy, etc., Isaiah 12:3. Hence that joy is called [שמחת תורה] the joy of the law, either on account of the law, since in Isaiah 55:1 they interpret the waters as the law.

units.la: II. Addunt, quòd haustio & libatio denotarit effusionem Spiritus Sancti. Bereschit Rabb. folio 70. 1. Quare vocant eam בית השואבין locum haustionis? Quia inde hauriunt Spiritum Sanctum. Gloss. in Succah sol.50.2. In Talmude Hierosolymitano (Succah sol.55.) exponitur, quòd inde hauriant Spiritum Sanctum. Nam insidet homini divinus afflatus per lætitiam. Haustio ergo aquæ erat propter verba Esaiæ: lætitia pro aquis, ut symbolo legis, exspectatio Spiritus Sancti ex hac lætitia.
units.tr: II. They add that the drawing and the pouring out signified the effusion of the Holy Spirit. Bereshit Rabbah fol. 70.1: Why do they call it the place of drawing? Because from there they draw the Holy Spirit. Gloss on Sukkah fol. 50.2: In the Jerusalem Talmud (Sukkah fol. 55) it is explained that from there they draw the Holy Spirit, for the divine breath dwells in a man through joy. The drawing of water therefore was on account of the words of Isaiah: joy stood for the waters, as a symbol of the law, and from this joy came the expectation of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: III. Adjiciunt tamen porrò in Rosch Haschana sol.16.1. Quare dicit lex, libate aquam in festo Tabernaculorum? Dicit Sanctus Benedictus, Libate coram me aquas in festo Tabernaculorum כדי שיתברכו להם גשמי שנה Ut benedicantur vobis pluvia anni. Nam autumarunt, (notat Cl. Leigtfoot.) Deum in isto festo decrevisse & determinasse de pluviis futuris anno sequenti. Hinc illud loco iam allegato, & Taanith sol.2.1. כחג נירוגין על המים In festo Tabernaculorum indicantur circa aquas.
units.tr: III. They add further, in Rosh ha-Shanah fol. 16.1: Why does the law say, pour out water at the feast of Tabernacles? The Holy One, blessed be He, says: Pour out water before me at the feast of Tabernacles [כדי שיתברכו להם גשמי שנה] so that the rains of the year may be blessed for you. For they thought (as Lightfoot notes) that God in this feast decreed and determined concerning the rains of the following year. Hence that passage already cited, and Taanith fol. 2.1: [כחג נירוגין על המים] At the feast of Tabernacles they are indicated concerning the waters.

units.la: §. Ioh. vii. 37. Cùm ultimam diem festi μεγάλην vocat Evangelista, loquitur secundùm opinionem gentis: nam ex institutione Dei, non apparet aliqua dignitas huius diei supra primam; imò si consideretur multitudo sacrificiorum, vltima festi dies omnibus inferior dici debet, utpote in qua agni solùm septem & iuvencus unus oblatus fuerit, die primâ verò tredecim iuvenci & quatuordecim agni. Loquitur, inquam, Iohannes ex mente gentis: quia cæteris diebus supplicationes & sacrificia fieri arbitrabantur, non tam pro se ipsis, quàm pro reliquis gentibus, at die festi octavâ solùm pro se ipsis. Hoc est quod dicunt in Succah sol. 55.2. Erant septuaginta Iuvenci, (qui in hoc festo offerebantur) secundùm septuaginta nationes mundi At ad quid Iuvencus singularis? Pro gente singulari. (Iudaica sc.) Secundùm Gloss. Deus non dispensabatur à sacrificiis illis & oblationibus pro gentibus factis, sed tantùm oblatione pro Israele. Hinc æstimarunt diem octavam non includi intra festum, sed considerarunt ipsam ut diem festum per se separatim. Succah sol 48.1. Dies octavus est festum per se ipsum. In quo tamen homo tenetur ad decantandum Hallel, ad offerendum sacrificia Eucharistica in lætitiam festi, ad honorandum ipsum sicuti reliquos dies festi. In eo tamen non adhibuerunt tentoriolum, nec Ramos palmarum, nec mala Citrina: ast adhibuerunt libationem aquæ sicuti in reliquis diebus festi. §. In Exitu festi Tabernaculorum observabant tempestatem, omen ex illa pro toto anno desumentes. Vid. Tempestates &c.
units.tr: §. John 7:37. When the Evangelist calls the last day of the feast [μεγάλην] great, he speaks according to the opinion of the nation. For by God's institution no dignity of this day above the first appears; indeed, if the number of sacrifices is considered, the last day of the feast ought to be called inferior to all, since on it only seven lambs and one bullock were offered, whereas on the first day there were thirteen bullocks and fourteen lambs. John speaks, I say, from the mind of the nation: because they supposed that on the other days supplications and sacrifices were made not so much for themselves as for the other nations, but on the eighth day for themselves alone. This is what they say in Sukkah fol. 55.2: There were seventy bullocks (offered at this feast) according to the seventy nations of the world. But why one single bullock? For the one singular nation (namely the Jewish). According to the Gloss, God was not relieved of those sacrifices and offerings made for the nations, but only of the offering for Israel. Hence they judged the eighth day not included within the feast, but considered it a feast day in its own right, separately. Sukkah fol. 48.1: The eighth day is a feast in itself. On it, however, a man is bound to chant the Hallel, to offer thank-offerings for the joy of the feast, and to honour it just as the other days of the feast. On it, however, they did not use the booth, nor palm branches, nor citrons; but they used the libation of water, as on the other days of the feast. §. At the end of the feast of Tabernacles they observed the weather, taking from it an omen for the whole year. See Tempestates etc.

units.la: de Festo Pentecostes.
units.tr: On the Feast of Pentecost

units.la: Inceperunt Iudæi à secundo die festi Paschatis septem numerare septimas, quibus elapsis Festum erat Pentecostes, quod à Scriptura Exod.23. 16. vocatur festum messis; item festum septimanarum Deut.16. 10. à Iudæis verò יום הבכורים Pentecostes. Maym. in Tamid cap. 8. Rabb. Salom. in Lev.23. ut plurimùm etiam עצרת Paraph. Chald. Num. 28.26. Abarbenel Lev.23. Cuius nomenclationis probabilissima ratio est, quòd omnes oblationes primitiarum fructuum retentæ fuerint usque ad hoc festum. vid. Maymon. in Biccurim cap.2.
units.tr: The Jews began to count seven weeks from the second day of the feast of Passover; when these had elapsed, the feast was Pentecost, which Scripture (Exod. 23:16) calls the feast of harvest, and likewise the feast of weeks (Deut. 16:10); but the Jews call it [יום הבכורים] the day of the firstfruits. Maimonides, Tamid ch. 8; Rabbi Solomon on Lev. 23; and mostly also [עצרת] Atzeret, in the Chaldee paraphrase on Num. 28:26; Abarbanel on Lev. 23. The most probable reason for this naming is that all the offerings of firstfruits were kept back until this feast; see Maimonides, Bikkurim ch. 2.

units.la: §. Huius diei solemnitas hæc erat. 1. omnes masculi in eo comparere debebant, eadem ratione ac in Paschate & festo Tabernaculorum. Exod.23.16. 2. Offerebant duas placentas fermentatas de novo illius anni tritico. Causam, cur in hoc festo fermentatos offerre debuerint panes, in Paschate autem azymos, hanc reddit Abarbenel, uti supra; Quia illi panes oblati in hoc festo repræsentabant ordinarium ipsorum panem ad quotidianum usum destinatum, panes Paschales verò memorativi erant celerrimæ & improvisæ ipsorum profectionis, quæ non permittebat, ut panes fermentarent. Panes Paschales erant loco signi & memorialis, sed non ita panes Pentecostes. In Paschate solùm dicere poterant הילך מצה Hic est panis azymus, at in Pentecoste dicere poterant הילך מצה וחמץ Hic est panis azymus, (talis enim ad oblationem מחמת adhibebatur, ) & simul fermentatus. vid.Talm. Ierus. Succah.cap.5. Placentæ autem illæ quadratæ erant, septem palmos in longitudine, & quatuor in latitudine & altitudine habentes.
units.tr: §. The solemnity of this day was as follows. 1. All males had to appear on it, for the same reason as at Passover and the feast of Tabernacles, Exod. 23:16. 2. They offered two leavened loaves made of the wheat of that new year. Abarbanel, as above, gives the reason why they were to offer leavened loaves at this feast but unleavened ones at Passover: the loaves offered at this feast represented their ordinary bread, destined for daily use, whereas the Passover loaves were memorials of their very swift and unforeseen departure, which did not allow the bread to leaven. The Passover loaves were in place of a sign and memorial, but not so the Pentecost loaves. At Passover they could only say [הילך מצה] This is the unleavened bread, but at Pentecost they could say [הילך מצה וחמץ] This is the unleavened bread (for such was used for the leavened offering), and at the same time leavened. See Talmud of Jerusalem, Sukkah ch. 5. Those loaves were square, having seven palms in length and four in breadth and height.

units.la: 3. Cum illis placentis etiam offerebantur septem agni, juvencus unus, arietes duo pro holocausto, hædus unus pro oblatione pro peccato, & duo agni pro sacrificio pacifico. Hi duo agni debebant à Sacerdote cum placentis agitari, quod secundùm Maymon. in Tamid cap. 8. ita fiebat : Sacerdos agnos adhuc vivos sursum & deorsum agitabat, deinde illos mactabat, excoriabat, & unius aut alterius armum aut pectus sumens propè panes collocabat, omniaque ita unà sursum deorsum, hinc illinc, & Orientem versùs agitabat: Intestina comburebat, & reliquum carnis comedebat. Summus Sacerdos autem unam ex placentis pro se desumebat, altera verò inter משמרות Ordinem Sacerdotum tunc cultui vacantem dividebatur.
units.tr: 3. With those loaves there were also offered seven lambs, one bullock, two rams for a burnt offering, one goat for the sin offering, and two lambs for a peace offering. These two lambs were to be waved by the priest together with the loaves. According to Maimonides, Tamid ch. 8, this was done thus: the priest waved the lambs, still alive, up and down; then he slaughtered them and flayed them, and taking the foreleg or the breast of one or the other, he placed it near the loaves, and waved everything together up and down, this way and that, and towards the east. He burned the entrails and ate the rest of the flesh. The high priest took one of the loaves for himself, and the other was divided among the order of priests then serving in the ministry.

units.la: §. Huius festi celebritatem non sacrificiorum multitudo, sicuti in aliis festis, præcipuè autem tabernaculorum, faciebat, sed memoria promulgationis Legis in Sinai.
units.tr: §. The celebration of this feast was made not by the multitude of sacrifices, as in the other feasts, especially that of Tabernacles, but by the memory of the promulgation of the law at Sinai.

units.la: FESTUM חנוכה Encæniorum originem suam habuit ab historia quam 1. Macchab. iv. 52. legimus. Super quam sic Iosephus Αρχαιολογ. lib.12. cap.11. Tantâ voluptate capti sunt in restauratione rituum sacrorum, post tantum temporis, ut lege sancirent posteris, festo celebrandum esse restitutionem rituum templi, per dies octo. Exindè ergo usque nunc, festum celebramus, illud vocantes lumina. Nomen tale indentes festo, ut opinor, quia præter ipsem talem libertatem sumus adepti. Talmudici in Schabbat sol.21.2. aliam rationem huius nominis repererunt, dicendo: Asmonaos devicit Regibus Graecis quasivisse oleum, sed non nisi unam phialam, quae reposita erat sub sigillo summi Pontificis, reperiisse, nec in ea satis fuisse, nisi in accensionem pro die una. Factum autem esse miraculum: nam accenderunt de ea in dies octo; Anno vero postero instituerunt & fecerunt dies ipsos dies festos.
units.tr: The feast of [חנוכה] Chanukah, the Feast of Dedications (Encaenia), had its origin in the history which we read in 1 Macc. 4:52. Concerning this Josephus, Antiquities book 12 ch. 11, writes thus: They were so delighted at the restoration of the sacred rites after so long a time that they decreed by law for posterity that the restoration of the temple rites should be celebrated for eight days. Hence we still celebrate the feast to this day, calling it the lights. I think the feast received this name because we obtained such liberty beyond it itself. The Talmudists in Shabbat fol. 21.2 found another reason for this name, saying: The Hasmonean, having conquered the Greek kings, sought oil, but found only one flask, which had been laid aside under the seal of the high priest, and in it there was not enough except for one day's lighting. A miracle, however, took place: for they lit from it for eight days. In the following year they established those very days and made them festival days.

units.la: §. Incipiebat hoc festum à 25. mensis Chislev, qui nostro Decembri & Novembri aliquomodo respondet; in diebus eius octo decantandum erat Hallel, de quo plurima apud Maymon. Prohibitum erat in illis lugere aut ieiunare. Vespere ad ostia domuum unaquaque nocte istarum octo, lucernas accendere debent; Praeceptum est ut unaquaeque domus accendat lucernam unam. At ille qui magis honorat praeceptum, accendit lucernas secundùm numerum personarum, quae sunt in domo. Ille vero qui & ulterius honorat praeceptum, accendit lucernam pro unoquoque qui in domo nocte primâ, & duplicat nocte secundâ. Si sint decem personae in domo, accenduntur nocte primâ decem lucernae, nocte secundâ viginti, tertiâ triginta, ita ut nocte octavâ sint lucernae octoginta. Maymon Hal. (hanniha c. 3. & c. 4. Mortuus erat filius uxoris Tarquinii in festo dedicationis; accenderunt Iudaei tamen lucernas, quod ipsis male cessit, quia imputatum ipsis est, quasi ob mortem filii laetarentur. Echa Rabboti sol 80.1. Hinc iudicat Maymon. tempore periculi & persequutionis lif\ere lucernas intra domum collocare.
units.tr: §. This festival began on the 25th of the month Chislev, which roughly corresponds to our December and November. During its eight days the Hallel was to be sung, on which Maimonides has much to say. It was forbidden to mourn or to fast during them. On the evening of each of these eight nights, they must light lamps at the doors of their houses. The command is that each house light one lamp. But the one who honours the commandment more lights lamps according to the number of persons in the house. And the one who honours it even further lights a lamp for each person in the house on the first night, and doubles that number on the second night. If there are ten persons in the house, ten lamps are lit on the first night, twenty on the second, thirty on the third, so that on the eighth night there are eighty lamps. Maimonides, Hilchot Hanukkah, chapters 3 and 4. The son of Tarquin's wife had died during the feast of dedication, yet the Jews lit lamps, and this turned out badly for them, because it was imputed to them as if they rejoiced at the son's death. Echa Rabbati, fol. 80.1. From this Maimonides concludes that in a time of danger and persecution one should not light the lamps outside but place them inside the house.

units.la: §. Pascha, Pentecoste, Scenopegia, non
units.tr: §. The Passover, Pentecost and Tabernacles could be celebrated only at Jerusalem,

units.la: poterant nisi Hierosolymis celebrari: verùm Encænia celebrabantur ubivis per totam regionem: Hinc illud in Rosch Haschana sol.18. 2. גזרו תעניה בהנוכ' בלוד Indixerunt aliquando ieiunium intra Festum Encæniorum, in Lydda. Et Maymon. 1. m.c. Itinerans,pro quo accendunt lucernam domi suæ, non opus habet ut pro se accendat ibi,ubi itineratur.
units.tr: but the Encaenia were celebrated everywhere throughout the whole country. Hence that passage in Rosh Hashanah, fol. 18.2: "They once appointed a fast during the Festival of Encaenia, in Lydda" [gezeru ta'anit ba-hanukkah bi-Lod]. And Maimonides, Hilchot Megillah, chapter 1: "One who is travelling, for whom a lamp is lit at home, has no need to light one for himself where he is travelling."

units.la: de Festo Purim vid. Buxtorfi Synag. c.29. dicitur Heb. פורים Sortium; celebratur 14. & 15. Februarii; Hodiernis Iudæis non tam festum est quàm Bacchanalia; nec à festivitatibus abhorruerunt Prisci, hinc illud Megilla sol.7.2. tenetur homo in festo Purim eò usque inebriari, ut nullum discrimen norit, inter hæc: Maledictus Haman, & Benedictus Mardochai.
units.tr: On the Festival of Purim, see Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica, chapter 29. It is called in Hebrew Purim, "of lots"; it is celebrated on 14 and 15 February. For the Jews of today it is less a festival than a Bacchanalia, and the ancients did not shrink from festivities either. Hence that saying in Megillah, fol. 7.2: "A man is bound on the feast of Purim to drink until he cannot distinguish between 'Cursed be Haman' and 'Blessed be Mordecai.'"

units.la: §. In festo Purim prisco rum iuvenes & pueri fecerunt effigiem Hamanis, eamque primò posuerunt in tectis ædium, (in memoriam patibuli in quo fuit suspensus) deinde faciunt rogum, & effigiem projiciunt in ignem, lætique circumstantes vociferantur, canunt & hilariter instrumentis Musicis ludunt; Habuerunt etiam latum annulum, qui in igne suspensus est, per quem saliunt, ab una parte ignis ad aliam. vid. Jalkut in leg.171.
units.tr: §. At the feast of Purim the young men and boys of old made an effigy of Haman, and first set it up on the roofs of the houses (in memory of the gallows on which he was hanged). Then they make a pyre and throw the effigy into the fire, and standing around it in joy they shout, sing and make merry with musical instruments. They also had a broad ring, hung over the fire, through which they leapt from one side of the fire to the other. See Jalkut, on Leviticus, section 171.

units.la: de Festis minoribus
units.tr: On the Minor Festivals

units.la: de Festis minoribus, qualia sunt initium anni novi, & noviluniorum, vid. ex Rosch Haschana apud Novilunia.
units.tr: Concerning the minor festivals, such as the beginning of the new year and the new moons, see from Rosh Hashanah in the entry Novilunia.

units.la: Ficus. Fuerunt ficus in Iudæa, quas vocarunt שיתין דופרא Quia bis in anno fructus suos proferebant; פיגא autem dixeru it quasi duplices fructus, ex ון quod pro duo sumunt & פיג fruEius. Demai cap. 1. §. 1. in Maymon. (om.
units.tr: Figs. There were figs in Judaea which they called "shittin dufra" [שיתין דופרא], because they put forth their fruit twice in the year; they called them "pigga" [פיגא] as if the fruit were double, taking the (Aramaic) "pi" for "two" and "giga" for "fruit." Demai, chapter 1, §1, in Maimonides (omitted).

units.la: §. Varia memorantur genera ficuum à Talmudicis, præter vulgares illas, quæ in hortis crescebant & paradisis. 1. יתין שיתין de quibus modò ex Demai. Glossa dicit, fuisse תאני מרבריו ficus silvestres. 2. fit loco citato mentio ficuum, quæ בנות שקמה ab ipsis nominabantur, & quæ secundùm aliquos fuerunt fici Platano insitæ. 3. Aliud genus ficuum erat, quod פרסאות, & aliud quod בנות שוח appellabatur, quæ species posterior erat fructificationis admodùm inusitatæ. Nam de illis sic infit Glossa ad Scheviit c. 5.v.1. שוח בנות protrudunt fructus unoquoque anno; at non ad maturitatem perducunt nisi anno tertio. Ita ut in arbore ista conspici possit unoquoque anno triplex fructus, anni scilicet præsentis & prateriti, atque anni ipsum præcedentis. Sic ficus פרסאות fructum perducunt ad maturitatem duorum annorum spatio &c. Addit Gemara Hier. uniusque cuiusque anni fructus dignosci potuisse per appensa licia & affixa appendicula. Nisi dicamus Matth.xxi.19. & Marci xi.13. arborem illam, cui Christus maledixit, ex hoc genere ficuum των שוח בנות scilicet fuisse, nulla ratio illum locum explicandi nobis remanet. Nam si communis fuit ficus, & secundùm Marcum tempus ficuum nondum aderat, cur quæso Christus arboris maledixisset pro sua natura agenti? Christus reperit καὶ φύλλα, at in ordinariis arboribus mense Nisan, cuius die undecimo, Christus hanc maledictionem fecit, nulla adhuc folia erant, sed solùm prorepere incipiebant, vid.Gloss.in Bab.Pesachim sol.52.2. ad hæc
units.tr: §. The Talmudists record several kinds of figs, besides the common ones which grew in gardens and orchards. (1) "Shittin," of which we have just spoken from Demai. The Gloss says these were "wild figs" [tha'ne midbera]. (2) At the place cited there is mention of figs called "benot shiqmah," named after the sycamore, which some think were figs grafted onto a plane tree. (3) Another kind of fig was called "parsa'ot," and another "benot shuach," a later kind which bore fruit in a quite unusual way. For the Gloss on Shevi'it, chapter 5, verse 1, says of the latter: "benot shuach put forth fruit each year, but do not bring it to maturity until the third year. So on this tree one can see each year a threefold fruit: that of the present year, of the past year, and of the year before that." Likewise the "parsa'ot" bring their fruit to maturity over a span of two years, etc. The Gemara of Jerusalem adds that the fruit of each year could be told apart by the attached threads and the fastened little tags. Unless we say that the tree which Christ cursed (Matthew 21:19 and Mark 11:13) was of this kind, of the "benot shuach," there remains for us no reasonable way to explain that passage. For if it was an ordinary fig tree, and according to Mark "the time of figs was not yet," why, I ask, would Christ have cursed a tree for acting according to its nature? Christ found "leaves" [φύλλα]; but on ordinary trees in the month of Nisan, on whose eleventh day Christ uttered this curse, there were as yet no leaves, but they had only begun to sprout. See the Gloss on the Babylonian Pesachim, fol. 52.2, on these words:

units.la: hæc verba משיזציאו כל האילנות. Verùm si dicamus hanc ficum ex genere שוח כנות fuisse, omnia clara fiunt; Per lementiam aëris huic ficui adhæserunt, ut diximus, trium annorum fructus, simul cum foliis; Christus ambulans ὃςπ τῆς ὁδῶς in loco publico (quem Talmud. מפקר nominant contradistincté ad שבו quod locum ad peculiarem aliquem Dominum pertinentem denotabat.) vidit arborem ἐχόντα φύλλα folia habentem, (quod præsupponit, reliquas ficus istius loci foliis caruisse;) folia præterebant spem ficuum ab annis præcedentibus iam existentium, nam præsentis anni ficus Christus nec exspectavit, nec exspectare potuit, cùm tam parùm adesset καιρὸς σύκων, ut abesset ferè per spatium quinquemestre. Si itaque hæc ficus secundùm suam naturam egisset, debuisset duorum saltem annorum præcedentium fructus exhibere Christo; at ut discipulis effet Emblema pœnæ infligendæ Iudæis ob eorum spiritualem sterilitatem ac hypocrisin, divina ordinatio voluit, ut quidem folia signa fructus præ se ferrent, fructu tamen arbor careret omninò. Quare quoque iustam passa est vindictam, postquam (si ita loqui licet) Domini spem fefellerat. Marcus ergo in clausula ista, quæ maximè interpretes torquet, ἦν γὰρ ἢν καιρὸς σύκων non strictè & solùm rationem reddit, cur ficus non invenerit Christus: Sed rationem reddit totius actionis, cur scilicet in monte isto ficubus abundanti, unam tantùm viderit, cui folia talia, eamque conspectam è longinquo adierit. Ratio inquit hæc erat; Quia O non erat tempus ordinarium ficuum: quod si fuifset, à ficubus undique circunstantibus decerpere potuissët; at cum non esset, ab hac sola erat exspectatio, quæ de genere ימאם aut תוש videbatur; quæ nunquam foliis ac ficubus caruerunt. Hanc huius loci explicationem à Cl. D. Leigtfooto didicimus.
units.tr: These are the words mishetzi'u kol ha'ilanot [משיזציאו כל האילנות]. But if we say that this fig tree was of the kind sichnut [שוח כנות], everything becomes clear. Through the mildness of the air, as we have said, the fruit of three years clung to this fig tree together with its leaves. Christ, walking along the road [ὡς ἐπὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ] in a public place (which the Talmud calls mefukar [מפקר], in contrast to shavu, which denoted a place belonging to some particular owner), saw a tree having leaves [ἔχοντα φύλλα]. This presupposes that the other figs in that place had no leaves. The leaves promised figs from the earlier years, which already existed, for Christ neither looked for nor could look for the figs of the present year, since the season of figs was so far off that it was about five months away. If, then, this tree had behaved according to its nature, it ought at least to have shown Christ the fruit of the two preceding years. But in order that it might be a picture for the disciples of the punishment to be inflicted on the Jews for their spiritual barrenness and hypocrisy, divine providence willed that the tree should indeed display leaves as signs of fruit, yet be altogether without fruit. Therefore it also suffered just vengeance, after (if I may so speak) it had disappointed the Lord's hope. Mark, then, in that clause which most torments the interpreters, for it was not yet the season of figs [ἦν γὰρ καιρὸς σύκων], does not merely give the reason why Christ did not find figs. Rather, he gives the reason for the whole action: why, on that mountain abounding in fig trees, he saw only one, and that one with such leaves, and why he went to it after seeing it from a distance. The reason, he says, was this: because it was not the ordinary season for figs. Had it been, he could have plucked figs from the trees standing round on every side; but since it was not, his expectation rested on this one alone, which seemed to be of the kind [ימאם] or [תוש], trees which never lack leaves and figs. We learned this explanation of the passage from the distinguished Mr. Leightfoot.

units.la: Filius immoriger Heb. בן מות Reus est lapidationis; ætas autem eius quâ immorigerus fieri capax est, ita definitur. Filius immorigerus talis declaratur quando duos pilos produxerit, quando vestitus est barbâ תתתתת; si comedere potest carnis dimidiatam minam, & bibere potest vini Italici sextarium dimidiatum. Non declaratur immorigerus nisi furatus patri apud exteros voret. Alterutro parentum nolente non declaratur filius immorigerus, usquedum ambo id petant. Si mater eius patri non conveniat, aut si alteruter parentum sit mancus, aut claudus, aut cæcus aut surdus, non declaratur talis. Si admonitus aut virgis cæsus coram triumviris ad ingenium redit, iudicio xxiii.iudicandus stiftitur. Filius immoriger iudicatur propter ממון Id quod tandem deveniet, si nullâ censurâ corriperetur. Sanhed. cap. 8.
units.tr: A stubborn and rebellious son, Heb. "ben mot" [בן מות], is liable to stoning. The age at which he is capable of becoming rebellious is defined thus. A rebellious son is declared such when he has grown two hairs, when he is clothed with a beard, and when he can eat half a mina of meat and drink half a sextarius of Italian wine. He is not declared rebellious unless he has stolen from his father and eaten abroad. If either parent is unwilling, the son is not declared rebellious, until both ask for it. If his mother does not agree with his father, or if either parent is maimed, lame, blind or deaf, such a son is not declared rebellious. If, when admonished or beaten with rods before the three judges, he returns to his senses, he is to be judged by the court of twenty-three and is set free. A stubborn son is judged on account of his property, that is, what he would eventually come to, if he were not corrected by any censure. Sanhedrin, chapter 8.

units.la: Flagellatio.
units.tr: Flogging.

units.la: Hi flagro percutiuntur. Qui concubit cum sorore sua, vel amita, vel matertera, vel sorore uxoris, vel glore, vel uxore patrui, vel cum menstruata, vel cum vidua, si sit Sacerdos Summus; vel cum repudiata & cui calceus traditus est, si sit Sacerdos gregarius; vel cum spuria & Nethinæa, si sit Israelita, vel cum Israelitide, si sit spurius vel Nethinæus.
units.tr: These are punished with the scourge: he who lies with his sister, or his aunt, or his mother's sister, or his wife's sister, or his daughter-in-law, or his uncle's wife, or with a menstruating woman, or with a widow, if he is the High Priest; or with a divorced woman to whom the shoe was given, if he is an ordinary priest; or with a bastard or a Nethinite woman, if he is an Israelite, or with an Israelite woman, if he is a bastard or a Nethinite.

units.la: Ob viduam & eandem repudiatam tenentur duplici nomine. Pollutus qui sacrum comederit, qui in Sacrarium se immundum intulerit, qui adipem, sanguinem, immundumque comederit. Plura alia quibus supersedemus, reperies in Maccoth c. 3.
units.tr: For the widow, and for the same divorced woman, they are liable on a double count. Also liable are the one who has eaten the sacred food while defiled, the one who has entered the sanctuary while unclean, and the one who has eaten fat, blood, or unclean food. You will find many other cases, which we pass over, in Maccoth, chapter 3.

units.la: §. Sontem quadraginta, uno minùs, verberibus afficiunt, nam illud Deut.xxv.2.3. exponendum est numero, qui proximus est quadragenario. Hinc patet quid velit Paulus, dum 2. Cor.11.24. se à Iudæis quinquies accepisse quadragenas plagas, unâ minùs, asserit. Non adiudicatur plagis, nisi quæ trifariam dividi possint. Si xl. ferre posse æstimatus fuerit, & parte toleratâ, videatur reliquum sustinere non posse, dimittitur.
units.tr: §. They inflict forty stripes less one on the guilty party, for the passage at Deut. 25:2-3 must be explained by the number nearest to forty. Hence it is clear what Paul means when, at 2 Cor. 11:24, he asserts that he received from the Jews five times forty stripes less one. Stripes are not adjudged unless they can be divided into three parts. If a man is judged able to bear forty, and after bearing part of them it appears that he cannot endure the rest, he is released.

units.la: §. Flagellatio ita fit: Astringuntur manus rei ambæ ad columnam; Tum minister publicus vestem eius arreptam detrahit, sive rumpatur, sive diffluatur, usquedum denudet pectus. Lapis ponè illum collocatus est, in quo stat lictor, manu tenens lorum bubulum complicatum, primò ut ex simplici fit duplex; iterum ut ex duplici fiat quadruplex. In illo duo lora sunt quæ ascendunt & descendunt. Manubrium palmi longitudinem habet, latum est palmum; extremitas eius ad os ventris pertingit. Hoc cum ferit trifariam, ita ut trientem cituum adverso, bessem averso infligat. Maccot c.3. v.12.13.14.15. Vid. Maymon. Hal. Sanhed. cap.17. Buxtorf. Epist. Ded. Abbreviat. Si quis flagellatus fuerit, & deinde reciderit, iussu iudicum arcæ inditur, & hordeo cibatur, donec rumpatur venter eius. Sanhed. cap. 9.5.
units.tr: §. Flogging is carried out thus. Both hands of the accused are bound to a pillar. Then the public servant seizes his garment and tears it off, whether it rips or comes apart, until the chest is bared. Behind him is placed a stone on which the lictor stands, holding a bull's whip folded, first so that from a single thong it becomes double, and again so that from a double it becomes fourfold. In it are two thongs, which go up and down. The handle is a palm in length and a palm in breadth; its end reaches the belly. When he strikes in three parts, so that he inflicts a third on the front and two thirds on the back. Maccot, chapter 3, verses 12-15. See Maimonides, Hilchot Sanhedrin, chapter 17; Buxtorf, Epistola dedicatoria, Abbreviatio. If anyone has been flogged and then relapses, he is placed by order of the judges in a chest and fed barley until his belly bursts. Sanhedrin, chapter 9, section 5.

units.la: §. Qui flagellabatur ad numerum 39.plagarum vocatur flagellatio eius מלקות; sed si quis rebellis esset in verba legis & scribarum, nulla denique admonitione à mala sua via deterreri posset, ille percutitur מרדות במכת percussione contumacia, sine mensura aut æstimatione, sine numero tripertito, donec animam exhalet. Malkut infligitur propter transgressionem præceptorum negativorum, & מכת מרדות propter transgressionem præceptorum affirmativorum. vid. Aruch in לקה & Maymon. in Sanhed. c.16.§.3. & c.18.5.
units.tr: §. One who was flogged up to the number of thirty-nine blows has his flogging called malkut [מלקות]. But if anyone was rebellious against the words of the law and of the scribes, and could finally not be deterred from his evil way by any admonition, he is struck with the stroke of rebellion [מכת מרדות], a blow of stubbornness, without measure or estimate, without a threefold number, until he breathes out his soul. Malkut is inflicted for transgressing the negative precepts, and the stroke of rebellion for transgressing the affirmative precepts. See Aruch under לקה, and Maimonides in Sanhedrin, chapter 16, section 3, and chapter 18, section 5.

units.la: FOENORARIA negotiatio apud Iudæos à duplici genere hominum peracta est,1.à שולחנים Mensariis τραπεζίταις (Matth.25 27.)qui מכרו מטבעות vendebant nummos; & Mensarii nominabantur, quia coram ipsis semper erat mensa, super quam emebant & vendebant. Aruch. 2. à חנוניים Tabernarii, qui suum fœnus præcipuè exercuerunt in fructibus vendendis & emendis; horum sæpius mentio fit, dum Talmudici de decimis tractant, magnum numerum tabernarum suarum habebant in atrio exteriori templi. vid. Tabernas.
units.tr: Moneylending among the Jews was carried on by two kinds of men. (1) The money-changers [שולחנים], τραπεζῖται (Matt. 25:27), who sold coins [מכרו מטבעות]; they were called money-changers because a table was always before them, on which they bought and sold coins (Aruch). (2) The shopkeepers [חנוניים], tabernarii, who practised their usury chiefly in buying and selling produce. Mention of these is frequent when the Talmudists treat of tithes; they had a great number of shops in the outer court of the Temple. See Tabernas.

units.la: FORMULÆ loquendi variæ ad quas sæpius in novo testamento alluditur. §. Ev. Marci c.iv.1. ἰρξαῖς διδάσκων est phraseologia, quæ usitatissima genti Iudaicæ. Hierof.Sanhed. sol.18.3. שרי רב כהנא מארץ בצלותיות Incipit R.Chana prolixus esse in oratione sua: i. e. prolixus fuit. Ibid. sol.23.3. שרי ההוא תלמידא בכי Incipit scholaris ille flere. i. e. flevit. Berefchit Rab. Sect. 33. שרי גיי Ince-
units.tr: Various forms of speech, to which the New Testament often alludes. §. Mark 4:1, "ἤρξατο διδάσκειν", is a phrase most common among the Jewish nation. Jerusalem Sanhedrin, fol. 18.3: שרי רב כהנא מארץ בצלותיות, "R. Chana began to be lengthy in his prayer," that is, he was lengthy. Ibid., fol. 23.3: שרי ההוא תלמידא בכי, "that scholar began to weep," that is, he wept. Bereshit Rabba, section 33: שרי גיי, "The ox began-

units.la: Incepit bos mugire. i. e. mugiit.
units.tr: to low," that is, it lowed.

units.la: §. In eodem capite v. 11. extat Phrafeologia τῶν ἐξω pro Ethnicis, omnes enim regiones & terras præter suam Iudæi vocarunt ארץ לאוח Extra terram. Iflius nomenclationis exempla occurrunt ubique. vid. Sanhed. Maymon. cap.1. Bava Bathra sol.27.2. Ad illa verba : Arbor cuius pars dimidia nascitur intra terram Ifraeliticam, & dimidia pars extra terram &c. vid. apud חיצונים in C.
units.tr: §. In the same chapter, verse 11, there is the phrase τῶν ἐξω, "those outside," for the Gentiles, for the Jews called all regions and lands except their own ארץ לאוח, "outside the land." Examples of this usage occur everywhere. See Sanhedrin; Maimonides, chapter 1; Bava Bathra, fol. 27.2, on the words: "A tree of which half grows within the Israelite land and half outside the land," etc. See under חיצונים in C.

units.la: §. παση τῆ κτίσει Marci 16.15. est phrafeologia usitatissima, quâ i. omnes homines denotantur. Bab.Chetubb sol.17.1. dicunt sapientes: sit semper animus hominis הבריות עם הבר ויו מעורבת complacens creaturis. Gloff. ut faciat cum unoquoque homine ad complacentiam. Maymon in Sanhed.cap.2. requiritur in unoquoque iudice, prudentia, clementia, religio, odium pecunia, amor veritatis, ואהבת הבריות & amor Creaturarum. i.e. φιλανθρωπία. 2. præcipuè verò intelliguntur gentiles. Bab.Chagiga sol.12.2. אוי להם לבריות Væ creaturis quæ vident, & non norunt quid videant: quæ stant & non norunt super quid stent &c. Berefchit Rabba fect. Sermo & preces של בריות Creaturarum sunt tantum pro rebus terrenis, preces verò Israelitarum pro loco Sancto &c. Hunc sensum etiam habent verba citata Marci, ut ex parallelis Matth. xxviii. Μαθητευσατε παντα τα ἔθνη, apparet.
units.tr: §. "Πάση τῇ κτίσει" in Mark 16:15 is a most common phrase by which all men are denoted. Babylonian Chetubboth, fol. 17.1: the sages say, "let the mind of a man always be" הבריות עם הבר ויו מעורבת, pleasing to creatures; the gloss explains: that he should act toward each man so as to please him. Maimonides in Sanhedrin, chapter 2: in every judge there is required prudence, clemency, piety, hatred of money, love of truth, and ואהבת הבריות, love of creatures, that is, φιλανθρωπία. (2) But chiefly the Gentiles are meant. Babylonian Chagiga, fol. 12.2: אוי להם לבריות, "Woe to the creatures who see and do not know what they see, who stand and do not know upon what they stand," etc. Bereshit Rabba, section: the prayers of the creatures [של בריות] are only for earthly things, but the prayers of the Israelites are for the holy place, etc. The cited words of Mark have this same sense, as appears from the parallel at Matt. 28:19, "Μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη."

units.la: §. Matth. iii. 2. regnum cœlorum est מלכות שמים Iudæorum; quæ formula loquendi occurrit in Beracot cap.2. v.2.5. & Gemara Babyl. illius tractatus sol.13.2. sol.15 1. Zohar in Levit. sol.53. Servire Domino in timore, est iugum regni cælorum. Hierof Kiddußchin sol.59.4. Quare servus per aurem terebrandus potius, quàm per aliquam aliam partem corporis? Respondit ille. Cum aure audiret hæc in monte Sinai, Non erit tibi Dominus alius coram facie mea, rupit ille à se iugum regni cælorum, & suscepit in se iugum carnis & sanguinis. In quibus locis suscipere iugum regni cælorum, aliquando significat externos ritus legis diligenter observare, utplurimùm verò secundùm sensum Evangelii, se ad internum Dei amorem ac timorem applicare.
units.tr: §. At Matt. 3:2, "the kingdom of heaven" is the Jews' מלכות שמים [malkut shamayim]. This formula occurs in Berakot, chapter 2, verses 2 and 5, and in the Babylonian Gemara of that tractate, fol. 13.2 and fol. 15.1; in the Zohar on Leviticus, fol. 53: "To serve the Lord in fear is the yoke of the kingdom of heaven." Jerusalem Kiddushin, fol. 59.4: "Why is a servant to be bored through the ear rather than some other part of the body? He answered: when with his ear he heard on Mount Sinai, 'You shall have no other lord before my face,' he broke from himself the yoke of the kingdom of heaven and took upon himself the yoke of flesh and blood." In these places, "to take upon oneself the yoke of the kingdom of heaven" sometimes means to observe diligently the external rites of the law, but for the most part, according to the sense of the Gospel, it means to apply oneself to the inward love and fear of God.

units.la: §. Amen Amen in Evang.respondent frequentissimæ formulæ היכנותא quæ est Phraseologia iuramenti, secund.Gl.Bab.Berac. f.55.1. ad hæc verba, Dicit R. Iuda Bar Allai היכנותא לדידי תרויהי אסורין In veritate utrumque est mihi prohibitum. vid. plura apud Amen in l. A.
units.tr: §. The "Amen, amen" of the Gospels corresponds to the very frequent formula היכנותא [hikhnota], which is a formula of oath, according to the gloss on Babylonian Berakot, fol. 55.1, on these words: "R. Judah bar Allai says: היכנותא לדידי תרויהי אסורין," "in truth both are forbidden to me." See more under Amen in the letter A.

units.la: §. Ioh.1.9. πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ἐρχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον plane respondet phrasi כל באי עולם quâ omnes homines qui sunt in mundo, denotant. Hierof.Sanhed. sol.26.3. Nonne Sol oritur כל באי עולם Super omnes venientes in mundum? Ibid. sol.25.4. כל באי עולם Omnes venientes in mundum non possunt creare unam muscam. Rosch Haschana cap.1.1. In initio anni כל באי עולם omnes venientes in mundum transeunt coram facie Dei. Quæ Phraseologiæ non de nascentibus sed in mundo iam existentibus intelligi debent.
units.tr: §. John 1:9, "πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ἐρχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον," plainly corresponds to the phrase כל באי עולם, by which all men who are in the world are denoted. Jerusalem Sanhedrin, fol. 26.3: "Does not the sun rise upon כל באי עולם, all who come into the world?" Ibid., fol. 25.4: "All who come into the world cannot create one fly." Rosh Hashanah, chapter 1, section 1: "At the beginning of the year, all who come into the world pass before the face of God." These phrases must be understood not of those being born but of those already existing in the world.

units.la: §. Ioh 1.47. occurrit Phrasis Ἐρχόμενος תא חזי, quæ ipsissimum Talmudicorum est תא חזי & תא חמי; aliquando איתא חמי, & בוא וראה.
units.tr: §. At John 1:47 occurs the phrase "come and see" (Ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε), which is exactly the Talmudists' תא חזי [ta chezi], and sometimes איתא חמי and בוא וראה [bo u-re'eh].

units.la: §. Per τὸν κόσμον Mundum, de cuius vocabuli restrictione & extensione disputatur in controversia de gratia universali, Iudæi 1. magnam multitudinem & magnum numerum denotant. Bava Metzia sol.33.2. שבקי כולי עלמא Reliquit totus mundus Mischnas, & secutus est Gemaram. Innumeris vicibus occurrit כולי עלמא מידי Totus mundus fatetur, & פליגי לא עלמא כולי Totus mundus non dissentit.
units.tr: §. By "τὸν κόσμον," the world (on whose restriction and extension dispute is had in the controversy about universal grace), the Jews (1) denote a great multitude and a large number. Bava Metzia, fol. 33.2: כולי עלמא שבקי משניות, "the whole world left the Mishnah and followed the Gemara." Countless times occurs כולי עלמא מידי, "the whole world confesses," and פליגי לא עלמא כולי, "the whole world does not dissent."

units.la: 2. Per hominem mundi intelligunt quemvis cuiusvis ordinis. Rosch Hafchana sol. 22. Non requirit R. Ulla, ut vir magnus folium sit fide dignus, sed ut homo mundi אבלם עינו sit etiam credibilis. Sic cum de Eleemosynis loquuntur, semper distinguunt inter עניי אותו העיר Pauperes propria civitatis, & עניי העולם , Pauperes mundi, id est undecunque aliunde adventantes.
units.tr: (2) By "a man of the world" they understand anyone of any rank. Rosh Hashanah, fol. 22: "R. Ulla does not require that a great man be trustworthy, but that a man of the world, אבלם עינו, be also credible." Thus when they speak of alms, they always distinguish between עניי אותו העיר, "the poor of that city itself," and עניי העולם, "the poor of the world," that is, those arriving from anywhere else.

units.la: §. Ioh. VIII. 25. την αρχην οτι και λαλω υμιν Optime vertitur, Illud quod a principio dico vobis; vel ita, illud quod precipue vobis advertendum; ut αρχην respondeat ראש Iudæorum; quo denotant rem primariam & præcipuam, sicuti è contra per סיפו rem secundariam aut minorem intelligunt. vid. Tamid sol. 61. Beracot sol.53.1.
units.tr: Concerning John 8:25: "τὴν ἀρχὴν ὅτι καὶ λαλῶ ὑμῖν" is best rendered "That which I say to you from the beginning," or thus, "that which is chiefly to be attended to by you," so that ἀρχήν corresponds to the Hebrew ראש [rosh] of the Jews. By this they denote the primary and principal matter, just as, on the contrary, they understand the secondary or lesser matter by סוף [sof]. See Tamid fol. 61; Berachot fol. 53.1.

units.la: §. Ioh.XIX.22. ὁ γέγραφα γέγραφα ; repetitio talis admodum usitata fuit. Chetubbot sol.96.1. Vidua si prehendat vel occupet bona mobilia mariti sui defuncti in alimoniam suam כה שתפסה Illud quod prehendit, prehendit, quod fecit, stat & obtinet. Menachot sol.3.1. Si quis se obligat ad offerendum oblationem de fartagine, offert autem de craticula מה שהביא הביא .
units.tr: Concerning John 19:22, "ὃ γέγραφα γέγραφα": such a repetition was quite common. Chetubbot fol. 96.1: "If a widow seizes or takes possession of the movable goods of her deceased husband for her maintenance, what she has seized, she has seized" [כה שתפסה], that is, what she has seized stands and holds good. Menachot fol. 3.1: If someone binds himself to offer an offering from the frying pan but offers from the gridiron, "what he has offered, he has offered" [מה שהביא הביא].

units.la: Illud quod obtulit, obtulit. Ita etiam sæpissime dicunt שעש עשוי ה Quod faction, factum est. v.d. Hebba not f.106.2.
units.tr: What he has offered, he has offered. So they also very often say: "What has been done has been done" [מה שעשה עשוי], that is, what has been done is done. See Hebba, note f. 106.2.

units.la: §. Matth. vi. 22 23. Oculus malus & oculus bonus animum avarum & non avarum denotant, ex usitata formula loquendi. Terumot cap. 4 3. Hæc est mensura oblationis Sacerdotibus concessa עין יפה א׳ מארבעים Oculus bonus concedit partem quadragesimam. Oculus medius unam ex quinquaginta. והרעה א׳ ששים Et oculus malus unam ex sexaginta. Hieros. Bava Bathra fol.14.4. נותן מתנה נותן בעין יפה Qui dat donum det oculo bono &c.
units.tr: Concerning Matthew 6:22–23: "the evil eye" and "the good eye" denote a greedy mind and a generous one, from the common manner of speaking. Terumot ch. 4, 3: "This is the measure of the offering granted to the priests: the good eye gives the fortieth part; the middling eye one fiftieth; and the evil eye one sixtieth." [עין יפה, "the good eye"]. Jerusalem Talmud, Bava Bathra fol. 14.4: "He who gives a gift, let him give with a good eye" [נותן בעין יפה], etc.

units.la: §. I i eodem cap. Matth. v. 34. legimus ἀρχιτὴν τ᾽ ἡ λέξει ἡ καιρὸς ἀυτῆς, cui respondet illud in Bab, Beracot fol.9.2. דיה לצרה בשעתיה:
units.tr: In the same chapter, Matthew 5:34, we read "ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς" (Matt. 6:34), to which corresponds that saying in Berachot fol. 9.2: Let its trouble suffice for its hour [דיה לצרה בשעתה].

units.la: §. Matth. c. v. 1.2 ὅς ἂν μίνξῳ μιτροῦ eft vulgatissimum apud Iudæos adagium במרה שאורם מורד כה מורדי לו: Quâ mensurâ quis mensurabit, ea atque mensurabitur ipsi. Bab. Sanhed. fol. 100 1. Sotah c. 1 v. 7 8.9.
units.tr: Matthew 7:1–2: "ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε" is a most common adage among the Jews: By whatever measure a man measures, by that it is measured to him [במדה שאדם מודד בה מודדין לו]. Sanhedrin fol. 100.1; Sotah ch. 1, vv. 7, 8, 9.

units.la: § ἓ βὰ ὠ τὸ κ̓ἁῤφ̓ &c. in eodem cap. v. 4. etiam notum est adagium. Bab. Bava Batra fol 15 2. In generatione quæ iudicavit iudices suos אומר לו טול קיסם כעין עיניך Cum diceret quis (Iudex) alicui, Ejice festucam ex oculo tuo. אומר לו מול קורה מבין עיניך Respondit ille, Ejice & tu trabem ex oculo tuo &c. Vide etiam Erachin fol. 16.2. & Aruch in voce קסם.
units.tr: The saying about the mote in the eye, "τὸ κάρφος," in the same chapter, v. 4, is also well known. Bava Batra fol. 15.2: In the generation that judged its judges, one who said to another, "Take the splinter out of your eye" [קיסם], received the answer, "Take the beam out of your own eye" [קורה], etc. See also Erachin fol. 16.2 and the Aruch under the word קסם.

units.la: §. Ibid. v. 12. Quod tibi fieri non vis alteri ne feceris. Bab. Schabbat fol. 31.1. eadem ratione gentilem proselytum alloquitur Hillel דעלך סני לחברך לא תעביד: Quod tibi ipsi odiosum est, est, proximo ne feceris.
units.tr: Ibid., v. 12: "Whatever you do not want done to you, do not do to another." Shabbat fol. 31.1. Hillel addresses a Gentile proselyte in the same way: What is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbour [דעלך סני לחברך לא תעביד].

units.la: §. In cómunem usum etiam receptæ fuerunt quædam Phraseologiæ, ut in vulgari sermone obviam sit tur hæresi Sadducæorum immortalitatem negantium. Eius farinæ fuerunt עולם הבא ג֣ן עדן (Confer Matth.12.32.) ἀιὼν ὁ μέλλων ... מן העולם ועד עולם. à Seculo in Seculum. Bab. Berecot fol.54.1. עולם הבא duo præcipuè innuit I. Tempora Messiæ. Beracot c.1.v.ult. Dicunt Sapientes, Diebus vitæ tuæ, innuitur Hic Mundus; Omnibus diebus vitæ, superinducuntur dies Messiæ. 2. Statum post mortem, Tanchum. fol.52. עה"ב לאחר שיצא האדם מ"ע Mundus futurus, est, cùm iam exiit homo ex hoc mundo. vid.infra ap. Mundum.
units.tr: Certain phrases were also received into common use, so that in ordinary speech they would meet the heresy of the Sadducees, who denied immortality. Of this kind were "olam haba," "gan eden" (compare Matt. 12:32), "ὁ αἰὼν ὁ μέλλων," and "from age to age" [מן העולם ועד עולם]. Berachot fol. 54.1. "Olam haba" chiefly signifies two things: 1. The times of the Messiah. Berachot ch. 1, last verse: "The wise say, 'In the days of your life' signifies this world; 'all the days of your life' includes the days of the Messiah." 2. The state after death: Tanchuma fol. 52, "olam haba (the world to come) after a man has departed from this world," that is, when he has already gone out of this world. See below under "Mundus."

units.la: §. Matth.xvi. 17. σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα. illam formam sæpissimè adhibent, cùm homines Deo opponunt. Bab. Beracot fol.28.2. Si mè adduƈturi essent לפני מלך בשר ודם Coram Rege carnis & sanguinis, &c. At me adduƈturi sunt coram Rege Regum. vid. Tanchum fol.12.4. in qua columna ista Phraseologia quinquies occurrit. Item fol. 18.3. eiusdem tractatus hæc leguntur : לא כמרת מדת בשר ודם Deus Sanƈtus Benedictus non agit, prout agit caro & sanguis.
units.tr: Matthew 16:17: "σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα" (flesh and blood). The Jews very often use this form when they set men against God. Berachot fol. 28.2: "If they were to bring me before a king of flesh and blood [לפני מלך בשר ודם], that is, before a human king... but they bring me before the King of kings." See Tanchuma fol. 12.4, in which column this phrase occurs five times; also fol. 18.3 of the same treatise: "The Holy One, blessed be he, does not act as flesh and blood acts."

units.la: §. Matth. xix. 24. legimus Phraseologiam quæ apud Iudæos ufitatissima est, ad rem difficillimam ac insusitatissimam innuendam. Bab. Beracot f. 55. 2. לא מחוו לאינש לא רקלא דדהנרה ולא פילא דעייל בקופא דמחטא Non ostendunt homini Palmam ex auro, nec elephantem incedentem per foramen acus. Gloss. Rem quam non soliitus est videre, nec de qua unquam cogitavit. In
units.tr: Matthew 19:24: we read a phrase in use among the Jews, very common, to indicate a thing most difficult and most unusual. Berachot fol. 55.2: "They do not show a man a palm of gold [לא מחוו לאינש לא רקלא דדהבא], nor an elephant walking through the eye of a needle [ולא פילא דעייל בקופא דמחטא]." Gloss: a thing one has never been able to see, nor ever thought of.

units.la: Bava Metzia sol.38.2. R. Schefchet 7☥ R. Amram incongruum quid afferenti, sic respondit דילמא מפומבדיתא את דמעיילין פילא בקיפא דמחטא
units.tr: Bava Metzia fol. 38.2: R. Sheshet and R. Amram, to one who brought forward something incongruous, replied thus: dilma mefumbedita at de-maʿeilin pila be-qippa de-mahta [דילמא מפומבדיתא את דמעיילין פילא בקיפא דמחטא].

units.la: Forte tu è Pombedithanis es, qui introducere pofsunt elephantem per foramen acu. Id est interprete Aruch. Qui dicunt impossibilia. Plura alia passim in hoc opere annotavimus. Frater quo sensu fumatur vid. Proximus.
units.tr: Perhaps you are from Pumbedita, you who can bring an elephant through the eye of a needle. That is, according to the interpretation of the Aruch: those who say impossible things. We have noted many other things here and there throughout this work. As to the sense in which the word "brother" is used, see Proximus.

units.la: FORNICATIO. Ante datam legem non fuit flagitium adolescentulum scortari, ut loquitur Terent. Adelph. Act.i.Sc.2. Sic enim diserte Maymon in Hal. אישו cap.1. Ante legem datam, occurrente viro fœmina in publico, si ita ex pacto convenirent, mercede data concubuit cum ea atque abiit, hæc autem dicta est קרשה seu meretrix. Hoc alii probant exemplo Iudæ & Tamaris; Genef. 38 14. Quod hic Maymon de simplici fornicatione dixit, Sixtus Senensis Biblioth. Sacræ lib.v. Annot. 94. imperitè ita intellexit, quasi Maymonidis Sententia fuisset, ante datam legem ipsa adulteria licita fuisse; cùm ipse tamen contrarium non semel claris verbis doceat; vid. Halach. Melachim cap.9. ubi inter illicita genera concubitus etiam refert concubitum באשת איש Cum uxore viri, seu aliena.
units.tr: FORNICATION. Before the law was given, it was no disgrace for a young man to consort with prostitutes, as Terence says in the Adelphi, Act 1, Scene 2. For Maimonides says exactly this in Hal. (אישו) ch. 1: Before the law was given, if a woman met a man in public, and they agreed so by contract, he lay with her for a fee and went away; and she was called קדשה [qedeshah], that is, a harlot. Others prove this by the example of Judah and Tamar, Genesis 38:14. That Maimonides here spoke of simple fornication, Sixtus of Siena, Bibliotheca Sacra, book 5, Annotation 94, understood unskilfully, as if Maimonides' opinion had been that adultery itself was lawful before the law was given; yet he himself teaches the contrary in plain words more than once. See Halachot Melachim ch. 9, where among the illicit kinds of intercourse he also includes intercourse with a man's wife, that is, another's wife [באשת איש].

units.la: De fornicatione vid. etiam quædam apud Adulterium.
units.tr: On fornication see also certain passages under "Adulterium."

units.la: Quidam ad dictum Deut.xxiii.17. Non erit קדשה Meretrix de filiabus Israel &c. notant, non necessarium esse ut קדשה de quavis meretrice exponatur, sed Deum illa voce etiam innuere meretricem sacram, quales olim fuerunt apud Phœnices, Babylonios aliosque gentiles, quas ιερόδουλοι Ministras sacras vocat Strabo lib.8. & quales fuisse in templo Veneris Corinthi refert Athenaeus lib.13.6. Quod acuminis aliquid, fundamenti parum habet, verba enim in eodem versu sequentia & Comment. Iudaeorum clare contrarium probant. Nec Veneris numen inter Iudaeos ante tempora Gamalielis notum fuit. vid. Venus.
units.tr: Some, on Deuteronomy 23:17, "There shall be no קדשה (harlot) of the daughters of Israel," note that qedeshah need not be explained as any harlot whatever, but that God by that word also points to the sacred harlot, such as once existed among the Phoenicians, Babylonians, and other Gentiles, whom Strabo (book 8) calls ἱερόδουλοι (sacred ministers), and such as Athenaeus (book 13, ch. 6) reports to have been in the temple of Venus at Corinth. This has some cleverness but little foundation; for the words that follow in the same verse and the Jewish commentaries clearly prove the contrary. Nor was the deity Venus known among the Jews before the times of Gamaliel. See Venus.

units.la: de FUNERALI Iudaeorum caeremonia vid. Lu-cium.
units.tr: On the funeral ceremony of the Jews see Lucium.

units.la: FUR. Maymon in Genebba cap.1. Quisnam est fur? ille qui clam surripit opes cuiusquam, possessore ignorante. Veluti si manum extendat in loculum vicini sui, & nummum auferat eo non vidente. At vero si palam auferat & aperte Hic non est fur sed latro. Non κλέπτης sed λῃστής.
units.tr: THEFT. Maimonides in Gneviah ch. 1: Who is a thief? He who secretly steals the goods of anyone, the owner not knowing: as if he stretches his hand into his neighbour's purse and takes a coin while he is not looking. But if he takes openly and in plain sight, this is not a thief but a robber. Not κλέπτης [kleptes, thief] but λῃστής [leistes, robber].

units.la: §. Qui oblationem offert, non restituto quod iniuste rapuerat, non quod officii est facit. Bava Kama cap.9.v.12. Et rursus v.5, Qui surripit quicquam proximo, etiam vel quadrantem, & falso iurat, tenetur ad restituendum &c. Ita & Maym. in Gezelah cap.8. Non offertur oblatio pro reatu, nisi prius restituatur ablatum, vel possessori vel Sacerdoti.
units.tr: He who offers a sacrifice without restoring what he has unjustly seized does not do what is his duty. Bava Kama ch. 9, v. 12. And again, v. 5: he who steals anything from his neighbour, even a farthing, and swears falsely, is bound to make restitution, etc. So also Maimonides in Gezelah ch. 8: An offering is not brought for guilt unless the thing taken is first restored, either to the owner or to the priest.

units.la: §. Fur vocatur quis, sive facultatem Israelitae sive gentilis furatus sit, modo quis surripuerit ad valorem Peruta (minuti.) Qui furtum sponte confitetur ad retributionem dupli non tenetur, sicuti ille qui factum non sponte confessus est. Retributio dupli in omnibus facultatibus in usu est exceptis ove & bove, respectu illorum vero si quis ovem furatus fit & illam inactaverit, pro illa quadruplum, si bovem quintuplum retribuere debet.
units.tr: A person is called a thief whether he has stolen the property of an Israelite or of a Gentile, provided he has stolen to the value of a peruta (a small coin). He who confesses the theft of his own accord is not bound to double restitution, just as one who did not confess of his own accord is. Restitution of double applies to all kinds of property, except sheep and ox. With regard to these, if a man has stolen a sheep and slaughtered it, he must repay fourfold; if an ox, fivefold.

units.la: §. Dominus ad retributionem ob furtum fervi sui non tenetur, בפני שיש בהן דער quia quoque mente valent nec servi semper custodiri possunt: deinde Domino infensi maximum damnum ipsi inferre possent. Si quis puerulus furetur, retributionem dupli quidem non facit, interim tamen à Senatu verberibus excipitur, ne furto afflictat. Maym. Hal. Genebba c.1
units.tr: §. The master is not bound to make restitution for theft committed by his servant, because they too have their wits [בפני שיש בהן דעת], and servants cannot always be kept under guard. Moreover, a master angered against them could inflict the greatest damage on him. If a little boy steals, he does not make double restitution, but he is nevertheless flogged by the Senate so that he does not make a habit of stealing. Maym. Hal. Genebba c.1

units.la: §. בתר גנבא גנוב ושעשא טעים Qui post furem furatur, (vel qui à fure furtum accipit,) & ipse gustum furti accipit, (i.e. ipse fur est.) Berach. sol.5.2. fur etiam in ipsa effossione Deum invocet; Berac. cap.1. Propter duo triave furta fur non occiditur. Sanhed. sol.7.col.1.
units.tr: §. Whoever steals after a thief (or who receives stolen goods from a thief) also takes a taste of the theft (that is, he is himself a thief). Berach. sol.5.2: even the thief should call on God while he is digging through the wall. Berac. cap.1: A thief is not put to death for two or three thefts. Sanhed. sol.7 col.1.

units.la: §. De restitutione in furto sic loquitur Taanith sol.61 1. Si quis surripuerit tignum, & aedificando illud etiam in maximo palatio adhibuerit, diruere tenentur palatium, ut tignum restituat Domino.
units.tr: §. Concerning restitution in theft, Taanith sol.61 1 speaks thus: If someone steals a beam and uses it in building, even in a very large palace, they must tear the palace down so that the beam may be returned to its owner.

units.la: § In Bab. Bava Metzia sol.83.2. praescribitur regula detegendi fures. Adi tabernas horâ quartâ (quae erat hora comestionis, & quâ omnes tabernas adibant ut comederent,) fique ibi hominem videris bibentem vinum, & manu tenentem poculum, dormientemque &c. fur ille est, eum prehendito.
units.tr: § In Bab. Bava Metzia sol.83.2 a rule is laid down for detecting thieves: Go to the taverns at the fourth hour (which was the hour for eating, when everyone went to the taverns to eat), and if you see a man there drinking wine, holding a cup, and asleep, etc., he is the thief; seize him.

units.la: G.
units.tr: G.

units.la: GADARA etiam erat una ex urbibus decapolitanis, & proinde Ethnici iuris, ut patet ex Iosepho in vita sua pag. 654. ubi dicitur, Magnates Decapoleos Syriæ Vespasiano hanc querelam deposuisse, quod Iustus Tiberiensis oppida ipsorum incenderit; quænam autem illa oppida fuerint, recensetur ibidem p.628. Cogit Iustus concives suos arma capere, & cum illis egressus ἐπὶ μαχαιραις τὰς τὴ Ταδαρηνῶν καὶ Ἱππηνῶν κώμας. Illud porrò adstruere licet ex eo quòd porci illic tanto numero alerentur Matth.viii.Quorum nutritio Iudæis per Canones Talmudicos æquè prohibita erat, ac comestio per Mosen.
