Regio Gadarena in regione Girgesenorum quasi fuit inclusa: Erat enim illa latioris spatii. Hinc concludi potest Marci v. Gadarenum illum fuisse Ethnicum, & à Marco & Luca præcipuè memorari, quia quid extraordinarium erat, quòd Christus circa hominem Ethnicum miraculum facere voluerit.
units.tr: Gadara too was one of the Decapolitan cities, and therefore under Gentile law, as appears from Josephus in his Life, p. 654, where it is said that the magnates of the Decapolis in Syria lodged this complaint with Vespasian, that Justus of Tiberias had burned their towns; what those towns were is listed in the same place, p. 628: Justus forced his fellow citizens to take up arms, and with them went out against the villages of the Gadarenes and Hippenes [ἐπὶ μαχαίρας τὰς τῆς Ταδαρηνῶν καὶ Ἱππηνῶν κώμας]. This may further be inferred from the fact that pigs were reared there in such numbers (Matth. viii.), and the Jews were forbidden by the Talmudic canons to rear them just as they were forbidden by Moses to eat them. The Gadarene district was, as it were, enclosed within the region of the Gergesenes, for that was of wider extent. Hence it can be concluded (Marci v.) that the Gadarene man was a Gentile, and that Mark and Luke especially mention him because it was something extraordinary that Christ should wish to work a miracle on a Gentile man.

units.la: GALILÆA est vel inferior, vel superior, vel convallis; à Caphar Chanania & supra, quæcunque non producit Sycaminos, est Galilæa superior. Ast à Caphar Chanania & infrà, quæcunque producit Sycaminos, est Galilæa inferior. Scheviit c.9.v.2. Betschean est principium Galilææ. Ioseph. de bello lib.3.c.4. nam Scythopolis ibi est Betschean. Antiq. lib.12. c.12. Caphar Chanania (v. הנכפר) est medium, ut etiam ex loco cit. videtur.
units.tr: Galilee is either lower, upper, or the valley. From Caphar Chanania upwards, wherever sycamores are not produced, is Upper Galilee; but from Caphar Chanania downwards, wherever sycamores are produced, is Lower Galilee. Scheviit c.9 v.2. Beth-shean is the beginning of Galilee: Josephus, de bello lib.3 c.4, for Scythopolis is Beth-shean there. Antiq. lib.12 c.12. Caphar Chanania (or הנכפר) is the middle, as also appears from the place cited.

units.la: §. Galilæi fuerunt generosiores ipsis Iudæis incolis, hinc in Pesachin c.4.§.5. In Iudæa opera servilia fecerunt vesperis Paschatis usque ad meridiem. In modo dotalem denotationem scribendi convenerunt Hierosolymitani & Galilæi; at incolæ Iudææ aliquid variarunt. Galilæis cura fuit de fama non de nummis; Incolis Iudææ cura fuit de nummis non de fama,Hierof. Chetubbot sol.29. 2.
units.tr: §. The Galileans were more noble than the Jews who lived in Judea itself, hence in Pesachin c.4 §5: In Judea they did servile work from the evening of Passover until midday. In the manner of recording the dowry, the Jerusalemites and the Galileans agreed, but the inhabitants of Judea differed somewhat. For the Galileans the concern was for reputation, not money; for the inhabitants of Judea the concern was for money, not reputation. Hierof. Chetubbot sol.29.2.

units.la: §. Galilæi non obligabantur ad Trumam הלשכה Thesauri sacri.vid.votum. De ritu ipsorum circa sponsum vid. de Sponsa.
units.tr: §. The Galileans were not obliged to the Truma [הלשכה], the treasury of the sanctuary; see votum. Concerning their custom regarding the bridegroom, see de Sponsa.

units.la: §. Galilæi corrupte loquebantur, & plane aliam, quam reliqui Iudæi dialectum habebant. Erubbin sol.53. Hominibus Iudææ qui accurati fuerunt in lingua sua, confirmata est lex in manibus ipsorum, hominibus Galilææ, qui non accurati fuerunt, in lingua sua, non confirmata est lex eorum. Gloff. Accurati fuerunt homines Iudææ in lingua sua, ut loquerentur sermone puro, non fordido. Hinc cum quidam Galilæus dixisset אמר למאן Quis est qui dixit? Exclamarunt o Galilææ fatue: quia litteram א in אמר tam vage pronuntiaverat, ut auditores nescirent, an vellet dicere חמר למאן, vel מאן עמר vel מאן אימר למאן. Anicula quædam volebat alium invitare ad potum lactis, cum deberet dicere, תאי דאוכליך חלבא Veni & cibabo te laste, dixit תוכליך לבא devoret te Leo. Alia coram iudice dicere voluit, Domine here, tabula mihi fuit; quam furati sunt. Eaque tanta fuit, ut si te in eam collocarent, non attingerent pedes tui terram. Sed hæc sua verba permutando gutturales, & alias confundendo ita fœdavit, ut astantes hunc sermonis eius sensum collegerint. Domine Serve, tignum mihi fuit, te furati sunt, fuitque illud tam magnum, ut si te in illo suspenderent, non attingerent pedes tui terram. Quam dialecti Galilææ à Iudaica discrepantiam qui consiliderabit, videbit, Petrum ex Galilaea esse, non difficile à famulis Summi Sacerdotis agnosci potuisse.
units.tr: §. The Galileans spoke corruptly and had a quite different dialect from the other Jews. Erubbin sol.53: For the men of Judea, who were careful in their language, the law was confirmed in their hands; for the men of Galilee, who were not careful in their language, their law was not confirmed. The gloss: The men of Judea were careful in their language, so that they spoke pure speech, not foul. Hence when a certain Galilean had said אמר למאן [Who is it that said?], they cried out, O foolish Galilean! because he had pronounced the letter א in אמר so vaguely that his hearers did not know whether he meant חמר למאן, or מאן עמר, or מאן אימר למאן. An old woman wanted to invite someone to drink milk, and was to say תאי דאוכליך חלבא [Come, I will feed you with milk], but said תוכליך לבא [may a lion devour you]. Another woman wanted to say before a judge, Lord here, I had a board, which they stole; and it was so large that if they had placed you on it, your feet would not have touched the ground. But by swapping these words, confusing the gutturals and others, she so mangled them that the bystanders gathered this sense of her speech: Lord Serve, I had a beam, they stole you, and it was so large that if they had hanged you on it, your feet would not have touched the ground. Whoever considers how far the Galilean dialect differs from the Judaean will see that Peter, being from Galilee, could easily have been recognized by the servants of the High Priest.

units.la: §. In adventu Messiæ Galilaea devastanda est. Meslec. ארץ דרך cap. 6. In ista generatione, in qua veniet filius Davidis, Galilaea devastabitur, & Galilæi vagabuntur de civitate in civitatem, & misericordiam non consequentur.
units.tr: §. At the coming of the Messiah, Galilee is to be laid waste. Meslec. [ארץ דרך] cap. 6: In that generation in which the son of David comes, Galilee will be laid waste, and the Galileans will wander from city to city and will not obtain mercy.

units.la: §. Erat regio Galilaeæ fertilissima. Bereschit. Rabba sect. 20. Rab. Eliezer Ben Simeon dicit נוח לו לארם לגדל לגיון אחד של זיתים בגליל Facilius est homini legionem olivarum enutrire in Galilaea, quàm puerulum unum educere in terra Israelis. De Galilaea vid. Lex. Talm. Buxtorf. p. 434.
units.tr: §. The region of Galilee was very fertile. Bereschit Rabba sect. 20: Rabbi Eliezer ben Simeon says [נוח לו לאדם לגדל לגיון אחד של זיתים בגליל], It is easier for a man to rear a legion of olive trees in Galilee than to bring up one little child in the land of Israel. On Galilee see Buxtorf, Lex. Talm., p. 434.

units.la: GALLICINIUM. De eo sic Magistri Bab. Ioma sol. 21.1.
units.tr: GALLICINIUM. Concerning this, the masters say as follows, Bab. Ioma fol. 21.1.

units.la: Dicit R. Schillah, Quicunque iter aggreditur ante galli cantum, sanguis eius sit in caput eius. R. Iosia dicit si ante cantum secundum: as sunt qui dicunt, si ante tertium. Ex quibus apparet, istos gallicinium distinguere in cantum primum, secundum, & tertium. Primum vocant simpliciter הגבר קריאת Cantum galli: secundum כשישנה Cum iterat: Tertium כשישלש cum tertiat.
units.tr: R. Schillah says, Whoever sets out on a journey before the cock crows, let his blood be on his own head. R. Josiah says: if before the second crowing; but there are those who say, if before the third. From these words it appears that they distinguish the crowing of the cock into a first, second and third crowing. The first they call simply הגבר קריאת, the crowing of the cock; the second כשישנה, when it repeats; the third כשישלש, when it triples.

units.la: §. תרנגול בינוני Gallus Medianus est qui suum cantum nec nimis accelerat, nec nimis differt. Gloss. in Bab. Ioma sol. 21. Cineres ab altari unoquoque die removerunt circa galli cantum, ac die expiationis à media nocte. Ibid.
units.tr: §. תרנגול בינוני, the medial cock, is one that neither hastens its crowing too much nor delays it too much. Gloss on Bab. Ioma fol. 21. They removed the ashes from the altar every day around the cock's crowing, and on the Day of Atonement from midnight. Ibid.

units.la: §. Mirum est quomodo factum sit, ut gallinacei reperirentur Hierosolymis, cùm expressis canonibus prohibitum fuerit gallos ibi alere. Maymon.Beth Habech. cap.7. Bava Kama cap. 7. v. ult. אין מגדלין תרנגולין בירושלם מפני קרושים ולא כהנים בארץ ישראל מפני הטהרות: Non alunt gallos Hierosolymis propter sacra, nec sacerdotes eos alunt per totam terram Israeliticam propter puritatem. Glossa. Etiam Israelitis prohibitum est gallos alere Hierosolymis propter sacra; nam Israelita comederunt illic carnem sacrificiorum pacificorum, atque Eucharisticorum; at galli gallinacei in usu habent vertere stercoraria, & ex illis educere reptilia, à quibus pollui possent sacra ista comedenda.
units.tr: §. It is strange how it came about that fowls were found at Jerusalem, since it was expressly forbidden to keep cocks there. Maimonides, Beth Habechirah, ch. 7; Bava Kama ch. 7, last verse: They do not keep cocks in Jerusalem on account of the holy things, nor do priests keep them anywhere in the land of Israel on account of purity. Gloss: Israelites too are forbidden to keep cocks at Jerusalem on account of the holy things; for the Israelites there ate the flesh of the peace-offerings and of the thank-offerings; but cocks are accustomed to scatter dung heaps and to bring out from them creeping things, by which those holy things to be eaten could be defiled.

units.la: §. Memorabilis est Historia de gallo, ex sententia Synedrii lapidato ob interfectum ab eo puerulum. Hieros. Erubbin. sol.26.1.
units.tr: §. The story about the cock is memorable: by the sentence of the Sanhedrin it was stoned because it had killed a little boy. Jerusalem Talmud, Erubin fol. 26.1.

units.la: R. GAMALIEL.
units.tr: R. GAMALIEL.

units.la: Huius nominis duo praecipuè inter Iudaeos claruerunt; R.Gamaliel Senex, & R. Gamaliel Iabbnensis. Prior principatum Synedrii obtinuit, cùm Dominus noster summo senatui Hierosolymitano sisteretur: & post Christi in coelos ascensionem adhuc 22. annos vixit, fuitque secundùm communem sententiam Divi Pauli praeceptor. Sub finem vitae eius confecta est à Samuele Parvo (de quo in Iuchas. sol.21.1. Avoda Sarah sol.42.3.) illa orationis formula, quâ Christianos, & alios secum non sentientes, execrationi devovere solent, & quam ברכת המינים Orationem contra Haereticos appellant. vid. Maymon.Hal.Tephillah cap.7. Hic Gamaliel Aconc lavans aliquando cum Proculo Philosophi filio disputavit. Avoda Sarah c.3.4. Postquam mortuus est R.Gamaliel, ablata fuit puritas & Pharisaismi rectitudo, cessavit etiam כבוד התור gloria legis. Sotah c. 9. Onkelos proselytus in huius Gamalielis funere celebrando magnos adhibuit sumptus. Avoda Zarah pag.11. Tosipht. Schabbat cap.7.
units.tr: Two men of this name were especially famous among the Jews: R. Gamaliel the Elder, and R. Gamaliel of Jabneh. The former held the presidency of the Sanhedrin when our Lord was brought before the supreme senate at Jerusalem. After Christ's ascension into heaven he lived for 22 more years, and according to the common opinion he was the teacher of the apostle Paul. Near the end of his life, that form of prayer was composed by Samuel the Little (on whom see Iuchas. fol. 21.1; Avoda Sarah fol. 42.3) by which they usually curse Christians and others who do not agree with them, and which they call Orationem contra Haereticos (the blessing against the heretics). See Maymon. Hal. Tephillah ch. 7. This Gamaliel once bathed at Acco and disputed there with Proclus, a philosopher's son. Avoda Sarah ch. 3.4. After R. Gamaliel died, the purity and uprightness of Pharisaism were removed, and the glory of the law also ceased. Sotah ch. 9. Onkelos the proselyte spent large sums in celebrating this Gamaliel's funeral. Avoda Zarah p. 11. Tosipht. Schabbat ch. 7.

units.la: §. Gamaliel Iabhnensis fuit huius ex filio Simeone nepos: & post Iochanan Ben Saccai principatum in Iabhne obtinuit. Cùm Titus urbe Hierosolymitanâ potitus esset, etiam hunc Gamalielem ad necem quaesivit: sed R. Iochanan pro eius salute supplicavit. Iuchasin f.52.2. In maximo quoque periculo erat, cùm Turnus (vel Terentius) Russus arcam templi aratro devastaret. Iuch.l.c. & Bab. Taanit sol. 29.1. Akibham sua praefectura Lyddensi amovere curavit. Rosch Hafchana cap. 1. Ipse tamen quoque tandem suâ privatus fuit. Hierof.Taanit sol.67.4. Si non fallimur habuit R.Gamaliel servum illum famosissimum apud Talmudicos, quem טבי vocant, & טביתא Tabitam ancillam huius nominis, qui tam bene se gesserunt in familitio, ut illud nomen omnibus domesticis eius, & etiam aliis impositum fuerit. Beracot cap.2. Hierof.Nidda sol.49 4.
units.tr: §. Gamaliel of Jabneh was the grandson of this man through his son Simeon, and after Johanan ben Zakkai he held the presidency at Jabneh. When Titus had taken the city of Jerusalem, he also sought this Gamaliel for execution, but R. Johanan pleaded for his safety. Iuchasin fol. 52.2. He was also in the greatest danger when Turnus (or Terentius) Rufus ploughed up the ark of the temple with a plough. Iuch. l.c., and Bab. Taanit fol. 29.1. He took care to remove Akiba from his office at Lydda. Rosch Hafchana ch. 1. Yet he himself was in the end deprived of his own office. Hierof. Taanit fol. 67.4. If I am not mistaken, R. Gamaliel had that most famous servant among the Talmudists, whom they call Tabi, and the maidservant Tabita of that name, who conducted themselves so well in his household that the name was given to all his household servants and to others besides. Beracot ch. 2. Hierof. Nidda fol. 49.4.

units.la: GAZA. De ea vide Iosephum Antiq. lib.11.cap.18. Strabonem lib.16. Diodorum Siculum lib.19. עטלוא של עוזי in Bab. Avoda Zarah sol. 11. 2. erat quaedam platea extra urbem Gazam, ubi erat macellum & idoleum. Gazae forum erat unum e tribus foris celebrioribus. Hierof. Avoda Zarah sol. 39. 4. Erat & extrà urbem locus, qui vocabatur חורבתא סגירתא Solitudo leprosorum. Bab. Sanhed.sol.71.1.
units.tr: GAZA. On it see Josephus, Antiquities book 11 ch. 18; Strabo book 16; Diodorus Siculus book 19. The place called Atloa shel Uzi [עטלוא של עוזי] in Bab. Avoda Zarah fol. 11.2 was a certain square outside the city of Gaza, where there was a meat market and an idol temple. The forum at Gaza was one of the three more famous markets. Hierof. Avoda Zarah fol. 39.4. There was also a place outside the city called Solitudo leprosorum [חורבתא סגירתא]. Bab. Sanhed. fol. 71.1.

units.la: Γαζοφυλάκιον templi. Variæ erant in eo Corbonæ קורבנות i.e. oblationum loca. 1. Erat Corbona לבדק הבית ad restaurationem ipsius ædificii templi, & Corbona לעבודת הקרש ad parandum ea quæ necessaria erant ad cultum divinum in templo. Vtraque etiam duplex erat. Duplicitatem prioris habes in hac traditione. Duo conclavia erant in templo, Vnum vocabatur לשכת חשאים (conclave clandestinorum, ubi viri pii obtulerunt clanculùm, unde enutrirentur filii piorum parentum etiam clanculùm. Alterum vocabatur לשכת הכלים (conclave vasorum, ubi quicunque vas aliquod obtulit, illud proiecit. Et post triginta dies thesaurarii conclave aperuerunt, & quodcunque vas in eo repertum est, quod ad templi reparationem conducebat, illud seponebatur, reliqua vero vendebantur, & pretium eorum cessit in Conclave reparationis templi: Ex quo vela templi etiam suppeditabantur. Schekalim cap.ʼ. Maymon. in Schekalim c. 4.
units.tr: The Gazophylacium of the temple. Within it there were various Corbonae (קורבנות), that is, places of offerings. (1) There was a Corbona for the repair of the temple building itself (לבדק הבית), and a Corbona for providing those things which were necessary for divine worship in the temple (לעבודת הקרש). Each of these was also twofold. You have the duplication of the first in this tradition. There were two chambers in the temple. One was called the chamber of the secret ones (לשכת חשאים), where pious men gave in secret, and from which the sons of pious parents were likewise supported in secret. The other was called the chamber of vessels (לשכת הכלים), where whoever offered some vessel threw it in. After thirty days the treasurers opened the chamber, and whatever vessel was found in it that was useful for the repair of the temple was set aside, while the rest was sold, and its price went into the chamber for the repair of the temple, from which the veils of the temple were also supplied. Schekalim ch. 4. Maimon. in Schekalim ch. 4.

units.la: §. Duplex etiam erat Corbona unde suppetiit sumptus pro rebus ad cultum divinum necessariis. Prima erat שופרות Cistula quædam, de quibus sic Magistri in Schekalim cap.6.5. א״ש שופרות היו בסקדש וכתוב עליהן תיקלין חדתין ותיקלין עתיקין קינין וגוזלי עולת Tredecim arcula erant in templo, quibus inscriptum erat תיקלין חדתין Sicli novi (i.e. anni præsentis, תיקלין עתיקין Sicli veteres,) vel anni præteriti, קינין turtures, גוזלי עולת pulli columbarum pro oblatione &c. Hæc paulò clariùs proponit. Maymon in Schekalim cap.2. In Sanctuario tredecim fuerunt cistulæ, quævis figuram tubæ habebat, (id est superiùs angustiores, inferiùs verò dilatatæ erant.) prima erat ו שנה לשקלי pro Siclis anni præsentis. Secunda pro Siclis שנה שעברת anni prateriti. Tertia injici debebat illa pecunia quam debuit, cui incubuit oblationem adducere duorum turturum, aut columbarum. Quarta recipiebat pretium oblationis ex avibus. Quinta ædeunda erat ei, qui voluntariè numnum obtulit, ad emenda ligna pro altari; Sexta ei qui nummum obtulit ad emendum thus. Septima ei וחב שהתנדב לכפורת qui aurum obtulit pro propitiatorio. Octava למותר חטאת pro quod supererat de Sacrificio pro peccato. Si scilicet empto Sacrificio ex dicta pecunia ipsi aliquid residuum erit, illud in hanc cistam projicere debet. Nona למותר אשם pro quod supererat de sacrificio pro transgressione. Decima למותר קיני וכי Pro quod supererat de columbis pro profluviosis & puerperis. Undecima pro quod supererat de oblationibus Nasirai. Duodecima pro quod supererat de Sacrificio leprosi. Decima tertia למי שהתנדב מעות לעולה בהמה Et qui nummos dicaverat pro holocaufto è iumentis. ושם כל דכר שיהיו מעותיו בתוך התיבה כתוב על התיבה מכחוץ Et unicuique cistæ ab extra inscriptum erat, quid in ea recondendum. In unam harum arcularum projecit suas prutas פרוטות vidua laudata à Salvatore.
units.tr: §. There was also a double Corbona from which funds were supplied for the things necessary for divine worship. The first was the chests (שופרות), small boxes, concerning which the Masters speak thus in Schekalim ch. 6.5: there were thirteen chests in the temple, and on them were written new shekels, old shekels, turtle-doves, young pigeons for the burnt offering, and so on. Maimonides sets this out a little more clearly in Schekalim ch. 2: In the Sanctuary there were thirteen chests, each shaped like a trumpet (that is, narrower above and wider below). The first was for shekels of the present year. The second was for shekels of the past year. The third was to receive the money of a man who had vowed to bring a pair of turtle-doves or pigeons. The fourth received the price of bird offerings. The fifth was to be given to one who voluntarily offered money to buy wood for the altar; the sixth to one who offered money to buy incense; the seventh to one who offered gold for the propitiatory. The eighth was for what was left over of the sin offering: if, after buying the sacrifice with that money, anything remained to him, he was to throw it into this chest. The ninth was for what was left over of the guilt offering. The tenth was for what was left over of the doves for those with a discharge and for women after childbirth. The eleventh was for what was left over of the offerings of the Nazirite. The twelfth was for what was left over of the sacrifice of the leper. The thirteenth was for one who had vowed money for a burnt offering of cattle. On the outside of each chest it was written what was to be put into it. Into one of these little chests the widow praised by the Saviour cast her two mites.

units.la: §. Erat & Conclave, in quo in tres cistas evacuabatur quidquid nummi colligebatur in his Corbonis de quibus diximus illudque καὶ ἐξοχὴν לשכה Conclave vocabatur. Ioma sol.46.1.
units.tr: §. There was also a chamber in which whatever money was collected from these Corbonas we have described was emptied into three chests; it was called, par excellence, the Chamber (ἐξοχήν, לשכה). Yoma fol. 46.1.

units.la: Schekalim c. 3. Modus huius evacuationis cistarum recensetur à Gl.in loc.alleg.cuius verba Cl. Leigtfootus hunc in modum transtulit. Cista ista in quibus repositus erat nummus, continebant seas viginti septem (unaquæque novem) & cooperta erant linteo. Ingressus est ille qui evacuaturus erat, cum cistulis tribus continentibus novem seas, (& literis N. ɔ. ꞏ. notatis;) Replevit primo cistulam illam cui inscribebatur N. e prima inter tres cistas magnas, & deinde cooperuit eam linteo suo. Deinde detexit seu aperuit cistam secundam inter magnas; atque ex ea replevit cistulam secundam cui inscriptum erat ɔ; & rursus cooperuit eam. Deinde detexit cistam tertiam, & cistulam replevit, cui inscriptum erat ꞏ. Sed alteram non iterum cooperuit. Hæc cistarum evacuatio,verbo תרם denotatur & ordinariè fiebat à spatio semestri ante Pascha, ante Pentecosten, & ante Scenopegiam. Schekalim cap.3. Notatur ibi etiam, quòd ille qui ad evacuandum ingrediebatur Conclave, ut amoveretur opportunitas & suspicio aliquid subtrahendi, ingressus fit neque cum veste complicata, nec cum calceis, nec cum Sandaliis, nec cum Phylacteriis, nec cum amuletis.
units.tr: Schekalim ch. 3. The manner of emptying these chests is recounted by the Gloss on the passage cited, whose words Cl. Lightfoot rendered thus: "These chests in which the money was placed held twenty-seven seahs (nine each), and they were covered with linen. The man who was to empty them entered with three little chests, each holding nine seahs, marked with the letters N, ɔ, ꞏ. He first filled the little chest marked N from the first of the three large chests, and then covered it with his linen. Then he uncovered the second of the large chests, and from it filled the little chest marked ɔ, and covered it again. Then he uncovered the third chest and filled the little chest marked ꞏ. But the other he did not cover again." This emptying of the chests is denoted by the word תרם, and it was ordinarily done at half-yearly intervals: before Passover, before Pentecost, and before the Feast of Tabernacles. Schekalim ch. 3. It is also noted there that the man who entered the chamber to empty it, so that the opportunity and suspicion of taking anything away might be removed, went in neither with a folded garment, nor with shoes, nor with sandals, nor with phylacteries, nor with amulets.

units.la: §. Ex hac לשכה conclavis, pecunia suppeditabatur, quicquid necesse erat ad cultum & ministerium templi. גזברי Iudices etiam de rebus raptis (vel ut mihi videtur) viri mandata & decreta publica constituentes, nisi forte legendum fit גזילות qui erant Hierosolymæ, stipendium suum 99. minas ex reditu conclavis habuerunt. (hetubb. sol.105. 1. Suppedanea illa quæ singulis annis magno sumptu ad educendam vaccam rufam & hircum emissarium extruebantur, etiam pecuniâ Conclavis parabantur.
units.tr: §. From this chamber (לשכה) money was supplied for whatever was needed for the worship and service of the temple. The treasurers (גזברי), judges concerning things seized (or, as it seems to me, men who issued public orders and decrees, unless גזילות should be read), who were at Jerusalem, had their salary of 99 minas from the income of the chamber. Hetubb. fol. 105.1. The structures which were built each year at great expense for bringing out the red heifer and the scapegoat were also provided from the money of the chamber.

units.la: §. Gazophylacium fuit in atrio mulierum Ioseph. de bello. lib.5. cap.14. Hinc illud atrium sæpius simpliciter Gazophylacium dicitur Ioh. VIII.20. Hæc dixit Iesus in Gazophylacio; non certè quod Christus in Gazophylacium ingressus fuerit, nam nunquam hoc ipsi licuisset; sed quòd in loco aliquo atrii in quo Gazophylacium erat, hæc dixerit. Sic cùm Marcus dicit, Sedit Iesus καπέναντι τῆς Γαζοφυλακίου solùm hoc vult, Christum sedisse sub porticu, ante quam positæ erant istæ arculæ τῶν שופרות. Certè si Gazophylacium fuisset in atrio Israelis, Christus ibi sedere absque scandalo non potuisset; Quoniam sessio in illo atrio nemini licuit nisi Regi ex familia Davidis nato, & aliquando etiam Summo Sacerdoti: Sicuti iam supra apud Atrium innuimus.
units.tr: §. The Gazophylacium was in the court of the women. Josephus, de bello, book 5 ch. 14. Hence that court is often simply called the Gazophylacium, John 8:20: "Jesus spoke these things in the Gazophylacium." Certainly this does not mean that Christ entered the treasury, for that would never have been permitted him; it means that he spoke these words in some part of the court where the treasury stood. So when Mark says that "Jesus sat over against the treasury" [κατέναντι τοῦ Γαζοφυλακίου], he means only that Christ sat under the portico, in front of which those chests (שופרות) were placed. Certainly, if the treasury had been in the court of Israel, Christ could not have sat there without scandal, since sitting in that court was permitted to no one except a king born of the family of David, and at times also the high priest, as we have already indicated above under Atrium.

units.la: גבורת הגשמים Gebhurat haggeshamim, seu Robur pluviarum, significat necessarias illas pluvias, quas ineunte Octobri petunt, sic sumitur in Taanit, & Beracot. cap.5.1. ubi dicitur בזכירין גבורת גשמים בתחיית המתים Ipsos commemorare imbrium vim, unâ cum vivificatione mortuorum. Putabam primitus 'גשמי גבורת fumi pro corporum restaurati-one, quæ in resurrectione fieri debet; sed aliud me Commentatores docuerunt.
units.tr: Gebhurat haggeshamim, or Robur pluviarum, signifies those necessary rains which they seek at the beginning of October. It is used in this sense in Taanit, & Beracot, chap. 5.1, where it is said: They make mention of the might of the rains together with the revival of the dead [בזכירין גבורת גשמים בתחיית המתים]. At first I thought that the phrase "גשמי גבורת" [the might of the rains] meant the restoration of bodies, which is to take place in the resurrection; but the commentators have taught me otherwise.

units.la: GEHINNOM. Vid. Hinnom. de Gehenna vid.Cl. Buxt.L.T.231.395.
units.tr: GEHENNA. See Hinnom. On Gehenna see the learned Buxtorf, L.T. 231, 395.

units.la: GENEALOGIAM incorruptam conservatam fuiffe, postquàm è Babel venerant, in tanta Iudaici populi colluvie, non ita facilè sciri potuit; Vide quæ diximus apud Babylonios. Hinc quærela R. Iochananis; Per templum? in manu nostra est eos detegere, qui non purifanguinis sunt in Israel: at quid faciam? cùm viri primarii huius seculi lateant, i. e. cùm non puri sanguinis sint; palam tamen de iis non prædicetur. Hierof. Kiddufchin sol.65.3. Bab. Kiddufchin sol. 71. Plurimæ familiæ tamen suum splendorem confervarunt, ex libellis genealogicis apud Synedrium, cui hæc cura demandata erat, depositis. Vnum vidit Simeon Ben Azai Bab. Ievamot sol. 49. 2. In codice quodam Hierosolymis invento scriptum erat; Hillel ortus est à Davide. Ben Iatsuph ab Asapho. Ben Zizit est ab Abner &c. Hierof. Thaanit. sol. 68.1 V.Buxt.L.T.202.
units.tr: That the genealogy remained uncorrupted after they had come back from Babylon, amid such a mass of the Jewish people, could not easily be known. See what we have said under Babylonians. Hence the complaint of R. Iochanan: "By the Temple? It is in our hands to expose those who are not of pure blood in Israel. But what am I to do? For the leading men of this age lie hidden, that is, since they are not of pure blood; yet they are not to be named openly." Jerusalem Kiddushin fol. 65.3; Babylonian Kiddushin fol. 71. Yet very many families preserved their splendour, from the genealogical books deposited with the Sanhedrin, to which this care was entrusted. Simeon Ben Azai saw one (Babylonian Yevamot fol. 49.2). In a certain codex found at Jerusalem it was written: "Hillel was descended from David. Ben Iatsuph from Asaph. Ben Zizit is from Abner," etc. Jerusalem Taanit fol. 68.1. See Buxtorf L.T. 202.

units.la: GENNESARETICUM mare Heb. vocatur ים כנרת Num.34.1. Item ים טיבריא Mare Tiberiadis; aliquando כנרות in plurali dicitur: ut Iof.xii.3. Cuius rei rationem reddunt Hierof. Megillah sol.70.1. Quia fuerunt ב' אנטונית dua arces Chinnerethis, vel Eparchiæ; (vid.Aruch in אנטוליות) Buxt. L.T.p.461.
units.tr: The Sea of Gennesaret is called in Hebrew ים כנרת (Num. 34.1). Likewise ים טיבריא, the Sea of Tiberias. Sometimes it is called כנרות in the plural, as in Josh. 12.3. The reason for this is given in Jerusalem Megillah fol. 70.1: because there were two citadels [ב' אנטונית] of Chinnereth, or of the Eparchy (see Aruch under אנטוליות; Buxtorf L.T. p. 461).

units.la: §. Mare Gennefaret accensetur aquis fluentibus; (i.e. non stagnantibus aquis sed labentibus accensetur.) Hierof.Avoda Zarah sol.42.1. Septem maria creavit Deus; ex omnibus autem noa elegit nisi mare Gennefarethicum. Midrasch Tillim sol 4.1. Certè Christus apud nullum mare ac apud hoc versatus est. Mare Tiberiadis est portionis Naphtalicæ. Bava Kama sol.15 1. Ergo lapsum committunt mappæ noštræ, qui eum extra ponunt.
units.tr: The Sea of Gennesaret is reckoned among waters that flow; that is, it is counted as having not stagnant but running water. Jerusalem Avodah Zarah fol. 42.1. God created seven seas, but of all of them he chose only the Sea of Gennesaret (Midrash Tillim fol. 4.1). Certainly Christ spent time by no other sea than this one. The Sea of Tiberias belongs to the portion of Naphtali (Bava Kama fol. 15.1). Therefore those of our maps which place it outside the land commit a slip.

units.la: §. Regio Gennesaretica ita vocatur, quasi hortos principum diceres, quia Magnates ibi plurimos hortos & bona habuerunt. Aruch in גנסר Ad id eos commoverunt elegantes fr. Ɛtus, qui ibi creverunt. Hinc Bab.Pesachim f. 1.8.1. Quare non sunt è fructibus Gennesaritici Hierosolymis? Ne dicant accedentes ad festa, non venissemus nisi ad comedendos fructus Gennesaritícos. &c. Hac ratione elegantissimam Lacus Lemanni ripam & tractum quem La Cosse nominant, non inconcinnè גנסר appellare possemus. Nihil enim vinetis, Paradisis, fructibus eius cultius & fertilius, prospectu viciniæ gratius, aëre salubrius.
units.tr: The region of Gennesaret is so called as if you were to say the gardens of princes, because many magnates had very many gardens and estates there (Aruch under גנסר). Elegant fruit trees which grew there moved them to this. Hence Babylonian Pesachim fol. 1.8.1: "Why are there no fruits from Gennesaret in Jerusalem? Lest those who come up to the festivals say: We came only to eat the Gennesaret fruits." etc. By this reasoning we could not inappropriately call by the name גנסר the most elegant bank of Lake Geneva and the tract which they call La Cosse. For nothing is more cultivated or fertile than its vineyards and gardens and fruits, more pleasing to the eye in its surroundings, or more healthful in its air.

units.la: Gentes Iudæi vocant הגוים οἱ ἐξω, vid. in C. apud חיצונים. Plurimi sunt admodum venenati canones quibus in æternum odium gentilium instruuntur, ut & eorum Iudæorum qui in iisdem traditionibus cum ipsis non consentiunt. Maymon. in Hal. הוצא cap. 4. Hæretici Israelitici, id est, qui idola colunt ex Israele, aut qui transgrediuntur ut irritent, itemque Israelitæ qui negant legem & prophetas, ex præcepto sunt occidendi, si potest quis eos occidere, idque palam; si autem non aperte, clàm & astutè machinari eis mortem licet. Et paulo post. Gentilibus verò quibus nobiscum non est bellum, itemque pastoribus בהמה דקה pecorum minutiorum, aliisque iistiusmodi non mortem quidem ita machinantur, ut prohibitum tamen est eos à morte liberare, si de morte periclitantur. Vt si quis Iudaus Ethnicum videret in mare delapsum, eum nullo modo inde tollere, debet.
units.tr: The Jews call the Gentiles הגוים [οἱ ἐξω]; see under חיצונים in C. There are very many thoroughly poisonous canons by which perpetual hatred of the Gentiles is taught, and likewise of those Jews who do not agree with them in these traditions. Maimonides in Hal. הוצא, chap. 4: Israelite heretics, that is, those who worship idols from Israel, or who transgress in order to provoke, and likewise Israelites who deny the law and the prophets, are by precept to be killed, if one can kill them, and this openly; but if not openly, it is lawful to plot their death secretly and craftily. A little later: But as for Gentiles with whom we are not at war, and likewise shepherds of small cattle and others of that kind, they do not indeed plot their death, yet it is forbidden to free them from death if they are in danger of dying. So that if a Jew saw a Gentile fallen into the sea, he ought by no means to take him out.

units.la: §. Ethnicos non reputarunt pro fratribus aut proximis. Aruch in ביר בן Si cornu percusserit bos cuiusvis bovem proximi. Proximi non Ethnici: cum dicit Proximi, excludit Ethnicos.
units.tr: §. They did not regard Gentiles as brothers or neighbours. Aruch under ביר בן: "If an ox gores the ox of someone," neighbour, not Gentile: when it says neighbour, it excludes Gentiles.

units.la: §. Officia etiam fraterna negarunt Ethnicis. Prohibitum est reducere deperditum quid Ethnici: Maymon. Gezelah. c.11. Prohibitum est Iudaeo solum esse cum Ethnico, itinerari cum Ethnico.&c. Maym. Rozeach c.12.
units.tr: §. They also denied fraternal duties to Gentiles. It is forbidden to return a lost thing of a Gentile (Maimonides, Gezelah, chap. 11). It is forbidden for a Jew to be alone with a Gentile, to travel with a Gentile, etc. (Maimonides, Rozeach, chap. 12).

units.la: §. Qui admonitus noluit resipiscere reputatur pro Ethnico. Maym. in Girufchin cap. 3. Iudaus Apostatam agens, aut violans ex praesumptione Sabbathum, est omnino sicut Ethnicus.
units.tr: §. One who, when admonished, refuses to repent is regarded as a Gentile. Maimonides, in Girushin, chap. 3: A Jew who treats an apostate as such, or who presumptuously violates the Sabbath, is altogether like a Gentile.

units.la: §. Docent Iudaei nationes & gentes Mundi, a Messia non solum non redimendas, sed vastandas & destruendas esse. Ramban in Gen. XLIX. Videtur mihi hic sensus. Non recedet virga exactoris a Iudah, donec veniat filius eius, cuius erit debellatio populorum, atque eorum confractio, nam ille debellabit eos omnes ore gladii. Hieros. Taanith sol.64.1. Israeli erit aurora (cum advenerit Messias,) at nox nationibus Mundi. Midrasch Tillim in Psal.11. Nationes mundi erunt conflagratio furni, Ad Israel servabitur solum.
units.tr: §. The Jews teach that the nations and peoples of the world are to be not only not redeemed by the Messiah, but laid waste and destroyed. Ramban on Gen. 49: It seems to me that this is the sense: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah until his son comes, whose will be the subduing of the peoples and their breaking, for he will subdue them all by the edge of the sword. Jerusalem Taanit fol. 64.1: To Israel there will be a dawn (when the Messiah has come), but night to the nations of the world. Midrash Tillim on Psalm 11: The nations of the world will be a furnace's conflagration; Israel alone will be preserved.

units.la: GENVFLEXIO ficebat etiam in cultu quotidiano templi. vid. Cultum. προσκυνεῖν varia significare potest; Procidere ad pedes genu flexo, genu petere, ad genua procidere. Nam primò in more fuit sic adorantibus genua aut crura prehendere. 2.Reg.iv.27. Matth.xxviii.9. Secundò Genua aut pedes exosculari. Hierof.Kiddufchin sol.61.3. R. Iannai & R.Ionathan considebant, accessit homo quidam atque exosculatus est pedes R. Ionathanis. Bab.Chetubhot f.63.1. Aberat R.Akiba duodecim annis ab uxore, redeunti prodiit ea in occursum, & procidens in faciem קא מנשקה ליה לכרעיה exosculata est eius genua. Bab.Bava Bathra de Iobo loquens sic infit, Venit Sathan ונשק ה לכרעיה atque is exosculatus est eius genua. Sanhed. sol. 28.2. Cùm quidam Rabbinus de variis rebus disseruisset קא כר חמא ונשקיה אכרעיה Surrexit Bar Chama, atque exosculatus est eius genua.
units.tr: GENUFLECTION was also practised in the daily worship of the Temple. See Cultum. προσκυνεῖν. The word προσκυνεῖν [to worship] can signify various things: to fall down at the feet, to seek the knees, to fall down on the knees. For first, it was the custom among those worshipping to lay hold of the knees or legs (2 Kings 4.27; Matt. 28.9). Secondly, to kiss the knees or feet. Jerusalem Kiddushin fol. 61.3: R. Jannai and R. Jonathan were sitting, and a certain man came up and kissed the feet of R. Jonathan. Babylonian Ketubot fol. 63.1: R. Akiba had been away from his wife for twelve years; when he returned she came out to meet him and, falling on her face, kissed his knees [קא מנשקה ליה לכרעיה]. In the Babylonian Bava Bathra, speaking of Job, it begins thus: Satan came and kissed his knees [ונשקה לכרעיה]. Sanhedrin fol. 28.2: When a certain Rabbi had discoursed on various matters, Bar Chama rose and kissed his knees [ונשקיה אכרעיה].

units.la: Gerizim mons distans sexaginta milliaria à Iordane Bab. Sanhed. sol. 44. 1. in Gl. Bab. Sotah sol. 36. 1. habebat duo Cacumina quorum unum vocabatur <bl>גריזים</bl>, quod erat fontibus & hortis admodum amœnum: alterum vocabatur <bl>עיבל</bl> locus saxosus, & lapidibus deformatus. Prioris cacuminis natura apta & digna erat, ut in illo benedictiones promulgarentur, ob quam rationem Samaritani etiam templum in illo erexerunt, Iuchas. p.14.2. Ex altero autem quid aliud quàm maledictiones exspectandæ erant.
units.tr: Gerizim, a mountain sixty miles distant from the Jordan (Babylonian Sanhedrin fol. 44.1, in the gloss; Babylonian Sotah fol. 36.1), had two peaks. One was called <bl>גריזים</bl>, which was very pleasant, with springs and gardens. The other was called <bl>עיבל</bl>, a rocky place disfigured by stones. The nature of the former peak was apt and worthy for blessings to be proclaimed on it, and for this reason the Samaritans also erected their temple on it (Juchas p. 14.2). From the other, however, what else were curses to be expected?

units.la: §. In Gerizim Israëlitæ pro se invicem sposponderunt עובו, indequoque unus ob alterius culpam pleditur. Rafchi Deut.28.29. Sanhed. sol. 27. 2. Existimarunt aquas diluvii ipsum non inundasse; hinc in Berefchit Rabba Sect.23. quidam Samaritanus eius sanctitatem exinde arcessit. Samaritani templo suo ultra 200. annos fruiti non sunt, devastavit enim ipsum Iohannes Hyrcanus. vid. Cl.Castelli Lex. in יריח. Vid. & Historiam nostram Doct. Misn. p.18.
units.tr: §. On Gerizim the Israelites stood surety [עובו] for one another, whence one is also called to account for another's fault (Rashi on Deut. 28.29; Sanhedrin fol. 27.2). They thought the waters of the flood had not inundated it; hence in Bereshit Rabba, sect. 23, a certain Samaritan drew its holiness from this. The Samaritans did not enjoy their temple for more than 200 years, for John Hyrcanus laid it waste. See Castelli Lex. under יריח. See also our history of the Doctrina Mishnica, p. 18.

units.la: עיבוך Gnibbur, Intercalatio. Vide si lubet in I.
units.tr: Intercalation [עיבוך], Gnibbur. See under I, if you like.

units.la: Gihon fons. vid.Siloah.
units.tr: Gihon, a spring. See Siloah.

units.la: Gladii supplicium. vid.Supplicia.
units.tr: Punishment by the sword. See Punishments.

units.la: Græciæ Regnum in tribus præcedit regnum impium (Romanum) inlegibus, libris, & lingua. Berefchit R. Sect. 16.
units.tr: The kingdom of Greece precedes the impious kingdom (the Roman) in three respects: in laws, in books, and in language. Bereshit Rabba, sect. 16.

units.la: §. Permiserunt Sapientes ut libri Sacri scriberentur Græcâ linguâ; quia secundum prædictionem Dei ipsius, verba Iapheti erunt in tentoriis Semi, at (ut dicit Glossa) decor Japheti est lingua Græca, pulcherrima ex iis linguis quæ sunt filiorum Iapheti. Bab. Megillah sol.9.
units.tr: §. The Sages permitted the sacred books to be written in the Greek language, because according to God's own prediction "the words of Japheth shall be in the tents of Shem"; and, as the Gloss says, the beauty of Japheth is the Greek language, the most beautiful of those languages which belong to the sons of Japheth. Babylonian Megillah fol. 9.

units.la: 2. Hierof. Megillah sol.71.3. vid. etiam Massechet Sopherim c.1. v.7.
units.tr: 2. Jerusalem Megillah fol. 71.3. See also Massechet Sopherim, chap. 1, vers. 7.

units.la: §. Quatuor sunt linguæ nobiles, quibus utitur mundus; vernacula ad Cantum; intelligitur græca quæ ita vocatur in Bab. Megillah. sol.18. 1.) Romana ad bellum, Syriaca ad luctum, Hebrææ ad elocutionem. His quidam addunt Assyriacam ad scripturam. Hierof. Megillah sol. 71. cap.2.
units.tr: There are four noble languages used by the world: the vernacular for singing; the Greek, which is so called in the Babylonian Talmud, Megillah, fol. 18.1; the Roman for war; the Syriac for mourning; and Hebrew for speech. To these some add the Assyrian for writing. Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, fol. 71, ch. 2.

units.la: Græci sacra legere in Synagogis fuit permissum B.Sotah c.7. & Hierof. R. Levi ivit Cæsaream audiensque eos legentes, lectionem Audi Israel אלינסתין Helleneflice, voluit impedire ipsos. R. Iose id animadvertens irascebatur, dicens: Qui non potest legere Hebraicè, num omnino non leget? imo leget quacunque lingua, quam intelligit ac novit, & sic officio suo satisfaciet.
units.tr: It was permitted for the Greeks to read the sacred books in the synagogues (Babylonian Talmud, Sotah, ch. 7). In the Jerusalem Talmud, R. Levi went to Caesarea, and, hearing them read the Shema, "Hear, O Israel," in Greek [אלינסתין, Hellenistin], wished to stop them. R. Yose, noticing this, grew angry and said: "Whoever cannot read Hebrew, shall he not read at all? Indeed he shall read in whatever language he understands and knows, and so he will discharge his duty."

units.la: עם הארץ Gnam haarets; Est ille qui legit Scripturam, & recitat Mifchnam, & tamen non famulatur discipulis sapientum; item ille qui Phylacteria non recitat manè & vesperi cum orationibus; item ille cui non est fimbria in veste sua, item ille qui non erudit filios suos in doctrina legis. Gemara in Sotah sol.22.1. הארץ עם is est qui suspectus est, ne rite decimet, & rite curet mundationes; עם הארץ plebeio vel populo terræ adhuc vilior est בור Rudis. Gloss.in 1.
units.tr: עם הארץ [am ha-aretz]: this is one who reads Scripture and recites the Mishnah, yet does not serve the disciples of the wise; likewise one who does not recite the phylacteries morning and evening with the prayers; likewise one who has no fringe on his garment; likewise one who does not teach his sons the doctrine of the Law. Gemara in Sotah, fol. 22.1. The am ha-aretz is one who is suspected of not tithing correctly and of not observing the purifications properly; the am ha-aretz is still more contemptible than a plebeian, or a man of the people of the land, [בור, boor], a rude fellow. Gloss on the passage.

units.la: עובר לפני התיבה Transiens ante arcam, est Phrasis admodum obscura. Vocatur autem ita, si non fallor, שליח הציבור Minister Ecclesiæ, qui è regione Sacerdotum in publico conspectu stat, & tum illis cùm populo Amen succinentibus, benedicendo aut orando præcedit. vid. Megillah c.4.3.5.8. Vt etiam Beracot cap.5.3.1. Transiens ante arcam si erraverit, transeat alius loco eius, nec contumax fit in illa hora. Post Sacerdotes non respondebit Amen, confusionis vitandæ causâ.&c. Vid.Lex.Buxtorf.Talm. pag. 419.
units.tr: עובר לפני התיבה [oveir lifnei ha-teivah], "passing before the ark," is a very obscure phrase. It is, if I am not mistaken, so called because of the "minister of the congregation" [שליח הציבור], who stands opposite the priests in full view of the people and, while the priests and people say "Amen," leads them by blessing or praying. See Megillah ch. 4, 3, 5, 8; also Berakhot ch. 5, 3, 1: "If the one passing before the ark has made a mistake, let another pass in his place, and let him not be contumacious at that hour. After the priests he shall not answer Amen, to avoid confusion," etc. See the Talmud lexicon of Buxtorf, p. 419.

units.la: עונה חעונה אחד מעשרים וארבעה בשעה Est una ex 24. hora partibus: עת tempus verò quid? Vna ex 24.partibus עונה. Vicesima quarta pars verò רגע vocatur Momentum. Hierof. Berac. sol. 2. col.4.
units.tr: עונה [onah] is one of the twenty-four hour-parts [of the day]. But what is a time [עת]? One of the twenty-four parts is an onah. The twenty-fourth part, however, is called a moment [רגע]. Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, fol. 2, col. 4.

units.la: GONORRHÆUS.Non interest inter Gonorrhæum duas visiones videntem (i.e. duplicem impuritatem sentientem,) & illum qui tres, præter
units.tr: GONORRHAEUS. There is no difference between a gonorrhaeus who sees two discharges (that is, who feels a double impurity) and one who sees three, apart from ## G

units.la: G

קירִבּ oblationem. Megillah c. 1. v. 7. Vir gonorrhaicus lavandus est in fonte, fœmina verò profluvio laborans in מִקְוֶה collectione aquarum ad 40. seas aquæ continente. Maymon. Hal מִקְוָאוֹת cap. 1. & 4. Esra fancivit Gonorrhaicis ablutionem. Hierof.Megillah. sol.75.1.
units.tr: קרבן [korban], offering. Megillah ch. 1, v. 7: A man with a gonorrhoea must be washed in a spring, but a woman suffering a flux in a מקוה [mikveh], a gathering of waters, containing forty seahs of water. Maimonides, Hilkhot Mikvaot, chs. 1 and 4. Ezra prescribed washing for those with gonorrhoea. Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, fol. 75.1.

units.la: עַרְבּוֹ vid. Elias.
units.tr: ערבו [Arvo]: see Elias.

units.la: גּוּשׁ חַלָּב Gusch chalabh, Erat in Aferitide, Menachot sol.85.2. ibi enim exstat historia pretiosissimi olei empti in Gusch Chalabh. vid. Loca terræ Israelis.
units.tr: גוש חלב [Gush Chalav]: it was in Aferitis, Menachot fol. 85.2, for there is recorded the story of a very precious oil bought in Gush Chalav. See the places of the Land of Israel. ## H

units.la: H.

HÆRETICUS Heb. מִין est ille, qui vel sine lege Dei vivit, vel specialiter errores amplectitur & docet. V.L.Talm.Buxt. p.1100. Principes Hæreticorum fuerunt Zadok & Baithos: Rosch Haschana sol.17.1. Iuchasin sol.59.1. Hæreticos vocant Mainnichæos quòd duo statuant rerum principia; Christianos quòd Trinitatem agnoscant personarum, Karraitas, quòd traditiones orales rejiciant. Rabbi Salomoh Psal.21.2. Deut. 32.22. Oratio quibus à Lege Iudaica ad Christianos aut Turcas deficientibus exitium imprecantur, facta est A.M. 4385. Zemach David p.1.f.36.2. Kad.Hakkemach 80.1. de Hæreticis vid. plura apud Epicureum. HALLEL Iudæorum. De eo iam quædam diximus apud Festum Tabern. Cantabatur etiam in principio mensis, in festo dedicationis, in festo septimanarum, & festo Paschatis: Sicuti respectu Paschatis in Christi exemplo videre est, cui
units.tr: HAERETICUS. Heb. מין [min] is one who either lives without the law of God or specifically embraces and teaches errors. See Buxtorf's Talmud lexicon, p. 1100. The leaders of the heretics were Zadok and Baithos: Rosh ha-Shanah, fol. 17.1; Yevamot, fol. 59.1. They call heretics Minim because they posit two principles of things; Christians, because they acknowledge a Trinity of persons; Karaites, because they reject oral traditions. Rabbi Solomon on Psalm 21.2 and Deut. 32.22. The prayer by which those who fall away from the Jewish Law to the Christians or Turks are cursed with destruction was made in the year of the world 4385. Zemach David, p. 1, fol. 36.2; Kad ha-Kemach, 80.1. On heretics see more in Epicureus. The Hallel of the Jews. Of this we have already said some things under Feast of Tabernacles. It was also sung at the beginning of the month, at the feast of dedication, at the feast of weeks, and at the feast of Passover; as may be seen with respect to the Passover in the example of Christ, to whom

units.la: cum aliis Pafchatis ritibus, & hunc in inftitutione facræ Cœnæ retinêre placuit. Obfervandum tamen in Pafchate Iudæos fuos hymnos diftinxiffe in Hallel fimplex, & Hallel magnum: prius dixerunt ad quartum poculum, pofterius verò ad quintum poculum, fi aliquem adhibebat, quoniam hoc ex ipforum arbitrio pendebat. Pefachim fol. 118. In Pafchate primi Menfis (vid. Num. 9.) unusquisque tenetur ad hymnum cum comedit Pascha, at in Pafchate secundi menfis, non tenetur ad hymnum cum comedit; In utroque tenetur ad hymnum dum maflat. Pefachin c.9. v.3.
units.tr: (it pleased him to retain it) along with the other Passover rites, and in the institution of the holy Supper. It is to be observed, however, that in the Passover the Jews distinguished their hymns into the Simple Hallel and the Great Hallel: the former they sang at the fourth cup, the latter at the fifth cup, if they used one, since this depended on their own judgment. Pesachim, fol. 118. "At the Passover of the first month (see Num. 9), each one is bound to the hymn when he eats the Passover; but at the Passover of the second month he is not bound to the hymn when he eats; in either case he is bound to the hymn while he slaughters." Pesachim ch. 9, v. 3.

units.la: §. Iam diximus hymnum Hallel fuiffe ab initio Pfalmi cxiii. ad finem Pfal. cxviii. In Pafchate illum interfecuerunt, partemque eius recitarunt in ipfo medio convivii, & partem rejecerunt ad finem. De extenfione prioris portionis difceptatum eft inter Hillelis & Schammæi fectatores; Schammæani volunt, ufque ad finem Pfal. cxiii. Hilleliani verò ad finem Pfal. cxiv. Hymnus quem cecinit Chriftus cum difcipulis fuis, poft facram Eucharistiam erat pars posterior. In qua memorabantur hæc quinque; Exitus in Ægypto. Scifsio maris rubri. Traditio legis. Refurrectio mortuorum, & dolores Meffiæ. Pefachin fol. 118.1. vid. Cl. Buxtorf. Lex. Talm.614.
units.tr: §. We have already said that the Hallel hymn was from the beginning Psalm 113 to the end of Psalm 118. At the Passover they interrupted it, reciting part of it in the middle of the meal and reserving the rest for the end. About the extent of the first portion there was dispute between the followers of Hillel and of Shammai: the Shammaites wanted it to extend to the end of Psalm 113, while the Hillelites wanted it to the end of Psalm 114. The hymn which Christ sang with his disciples after the holy Eucharist was the latter part, in which these five things were recalled: the exodus from Egypt; the parting of the Red Sea; the giving of the Law; the resurrection of the dead; and the pangs of the Messiah. Pesachim fol. 118.1; see Buxtorf's Talmud lexicon, p. 614.

units.la: הפטרות Haphtarot, sunt sectiones Biblicæ, quas in Synagogis legere consueve- runt.
units.tr: Haphtarot [הפטרות] are the sections of Scripture which they customarily read in the synagogues.

units.la: Illas in quinque Sabbathis menfis Adar ceffare faciunt, ut & etiam in omnibus novilunijs, in festo dedicationis, in Purim, in Ieiuniis, in מעמדות stationibus, & in die expiationum, nam ut observat Maym. neglecta observatione ordinis leguntur Haphtarot, pro ratione temporis. In Pascha te legunt sectionem מעמדות Conventum ex Levitico. In feria ultima septem septimanarum, in novi anni initio, in mense septimo, in Novilunio, & die expiationum legunt sectionem אחרי מות. In Festi Tabernaculorum feriâ primâ, legunt sect. מעמדות ex Lev. in cæteris omnibus diebus vero de oblationibus quæ in festo fieri debent. In festo dedicationis legunt de משיאי principibus; in festo Purim sect. פתל ויבא עמלק Exod.17.8. In Noviluniis וברא חדשים Exod.10.10. & 28.11. In stationibus legunt Historiam creationis. In ieiuniis benedictiones & maledictiones; nullas intermissiones faciunt in maledictionibus legendis, sed unus omnia legit.
units.tr: On the five Sabbaths of the month Adar they cause these to cease, as also on all the new moons, at the feast of dedication, at Purim, at the fasts, at the stations, and on the Day of Atonement. For, as Maimonides observes, when the order is neglected the Haphtarot are read according to the circumstances of the time. At Passover they read the section Conventum [מעמדות] from Leviticus. On the last day of the seven weeks, at the beginning of the new year, in the seventh month, at the new moon and on the Day of Atonement they read the section "After the death" [אחרי מות]. On the first day of the Feast of Tabernacles they read the section Conventum [מעמדות] from Leviticus; on all the other days they read about the offerings which ought to be made at the feast. At the feast of dedication they read about the princes [משיאי]. At the feast of Purim they read the section "Amalek came" [ויבא עמלק], Exodus 17:8. At the new moons they read "And at the beginnings of months" [וברא חדשים], Exodus 10:10 and 28:11. At the stations they read the history of creation. At the fasts they read the blessings and the curses; they make no pauses in reading the curses, but one man reads them all.

units.la: §. Die Hebdomadis secundo & quinto, tempore sacrificii vespertini legunt sectiones secundùm ordinem suum, nec constituunt earum lectionem, pro ratione supputationis. Megillah cap.3.4.5.6.
units.tr: On the second and fifth days of the week, at the time of the evening sacrifice, they read the sections in their own order, and they do not fix their reading according to a reckoning of days. Megillah, chapters 3, 4, 5, 6.

units.la: §. In Noviluniis & diebus profestis solennitatis (בחולו מועד) legunt quatuor, nec fas est vel diminuere vel adjicere: nec Haphtaram ex Propheta desumunt. Generalis regula hæc est. Omni die cui preces sunt additionales, nec tamen fit טוב יום dies feriatus, legunt quatuor; die festo quinque; die expiationum sex; Sabbatho septem, non pauciora. Addere tamen licet, ut & sectionem ex Propheta aliquo legere. Megillah cap.4.
units.tr: On new moons and on the weekdays of a festival (בחולו מועד) they read four sections, and it is not lawful either to diminish or to add to them; nor do they take a Haphtarah from the Prophets. This is the general rule: on any day to which additional prayers belong, but which is not a holiday [טוב יום], they read four sections; on a festival five; on the Day of Atonement six; on the Sabbath seven, no fewer. It is nevertheless permitted to add, and also to read a section from some Prophet. Megillah, chapter 4.

units.la: §. Hæ sectiones legi possunt in omni lingua, Sectio Mulieris ob adulterium suspecta, vid. Aquas amaras. Confessio decimarum; lectio Schema, preces & benedictiones ciborum, iuramentum teslimonii & iuramentum depositi. Hæ autem solum in lingua sanctæ legi possunt. Lectio primogenitorum, extractionis calcei; Maledictiones & benedictiones (quæ factæ sunt in Gerizim.) Benedictiones Sacerdotum, Benedictiones Sacerdotis magni; sectio quam Rex legere debuit; sectio Iuvenca decollata, & Sacerdotis unctii ad bellum. Sotah c.7. 1.2. V.Leusden Philol.Hebr.p.26.
units.tr: These sections may be read in any language: the section on the woman suspected of adultery, see "the bitter waters"; the confession of tithes; the reading of the Shema, the prayers and blessings over food; the oath of testimony and the oath of deposit. These, however, may be read only in the holy tongue. The reading of the firstborn, the loosing of the sandal; the curses and blessings (which were pronounced on Gerizim); the blessings of the priests, the blessing of the high priest; the section which the king ought to read; the section on the beheaded heifer, and the section on the priest anointed for war. Sotah, chapter 7, 1, 2. See Leusden, Philologus Hebraeus, p. 26.

units.la: HEBDOMADIS sic numerant dies Iudæi, diem primum septimanæ vocant אחד בשבת, diem secundum vero תרי בשבת. Exemplum habes in Bab. Maccot sol.5.1. Adveniunt duo testes, dicuntque בחד בשבא Prima Sabbathi suratus est ipse, &c. ובתרי בשבא & fecunda Sabbathi consummatum est iudicium eius. Dies tertius appellatur שלישי בשבת. Exemplum legimus in Bab. Chetubhot. sol.2.1. Virgo ducitur in uxorem die hebdomadis quarto, nam curari de Convivio אחד בשבת die primo hebdomadis שני בשבת die secundo ושלישי בשבת & die tertio. Dies quartus est רביעי בשבת illo die separabant illum qui vaccam rufam combusturus erat. Gloss in Parah c.3. Dies quartus septimanæ infaustus est infantibus ob Synanchen, (vid. Morbos.) hinc etiam vox מארת Genes.1.14. caret vau; R. Salomoh in loc. Dies quintus erat חמישי בשבת. Illo die voluit Esra ut legem publice legerent. Hierof. Megilah sol.75.1. Sextum diem vulgo vocarunt ערב השבת Vesperam Sabbathi; in illo die ex ordinatione Efræ cepas comedere debebant. Bab. Bava Kama sol.82.1.
units.tr: The Jews count the days of the week thus. They call the first day of the week one of the Sabbath [אחד בשבת], and the second day two of the Sabbath [תרי בשבת]. You have an example in the Babylonian Makkot, folio 5, column 1: "Two witnesses come and say: On the first of the Sabbath he was tried himself," and "on the second of the Sabbath his judgment was completed." The third day is called third of the Sabbath [שלישי בשבת]. We read an example in the Babylonian Ketubot, folio 2, column 1: "A virgin is taken in marriage on the fourth day of the week," for the banquet is to be prepared on the first day of the week [אחד בשבת], the second day [שני בשבת], and the third day [ושלישי בשבת]. The fourth day is fourth of the Sabbath [רביעי בשבת]; on that day they used to set apart the one who was to burn the red heifer. Gloss on Parah, chapter 3. The fourth day of the week is unlucky for infants because of quinsy (see Morbos); hence also the word [מארת] in Genesis 1:14 lacks the vav; R. Solomon on the passage. The fifth day was fifth of the Sabbath [חמישי בשבת]. On that day Ezra wished that they should read the law publicly. Jerusalem Megillah, folio 75, column 1. The sixth day they commonly called the eve of the Sabbath [ערב השבת]; on that day, by the ordinance of Ezra, they were to eat onions. Babylonian Bava Kama, folio 82, column 1.

units.la: §. Dies primus Hebdomadis, qui Dominico respondet, & in illum transfiit, à Iudæis vocatur Dies Christianorum. Bab. Avoda Sarah sol.6.1. & 7.2. Die Christianorum semper prohibitum est. (Iudæo cum Christiano negotiari.) De Die vid. f. 1. in D.
units.tr: The first day of the week, which corresponds to the Lord's day and passes into it, is called by the Jews the day of the Christians. Babylonian Avodah Zarah, folio 6, column 1, and folio 7, column 2: "It is always forbidden to trade with a Christian on the day of the Christians." On this day see above, under the letter D.

units.la: Hebron. Non est locus in tota terra Israelitica magis saxosus quàm Hebron, inde illic sepultura mortuorum. Bab. Sotah sol.34.1. Non est terra aliqua excellentior quam Ægyptus; nec est in Ægypto locus excelientior Zoane, & tamen septem vicibus nobilior erat Hebron quàm Zoan, utcunque saxosa. R. Salomoh Num: XIII.22. Chetubbot 112.1.
units.tr: Hebron. There is no place in the whole land of Israel more rocky than Hebron; hence burial of the dead takes place there. Babylonian Sotah, folio 34, column 1: "There is no land more excellent than Egypt, and there is no place in Egypt more excellent than Zoan; yet Hebron was seven times more noble than Zoan, however rocky it was." R. Solomon on Numbers 13:22; Ketubot 112, column 1.

units.la: §. Tenuis gleba erat Hebrone, gramen ovibus gratum proferens, & proinde illinc agnos pro sacrificiis, tanquam optimos petebant, hinc hæc traditio Arietes à Moab agni ab Hebron.
units.tr: Hebron was a thin clod of earth which produced grass pleasing to sheep, and therefore they sought lambs from there for sacrifices, as the best; hence the tradition: "Rams from Moab, lambs from Hebron."

units.la: §. Ex tecto templi potuerunt conspicere Hebronem. Glossa in Tamid c.3.v.2. Et quando oriens Lucescebat usque ad Hebronem, sciebant auroram ingruisse, & tempus mactationis sacrificii iugis adesse. Ioma cap.3. v.2. & Tamid l.c. Erat Hebron respectu Hierosolymæ orientem versus, & eius in speculatione aurorae mentionem fecerunt, ut occurreret memoria meriti sepultorum Hebrone ad sacrificium iuge. Iuchasin sol.63 1.
units.tr: From the roof of the Temple they could catch sight of Hebron. Gloss on Tamid, chapter 3, verse 2. And when the dawn in the east shone as far as Hebron, they knew that the morning had come and that the time for the slaughter of the continual sacrifice was at hand. Yoma, chapter 3, verse 2, and Tamid, ibid. Hebron lay to the east in relation to Jerusalem, and they mentioned its watching for the dawn so that the memory of the merit of those buried at Hebron might come to mind at the continual sacrifice. Yuchasin, folio 63, column 1.

units.la: Herbam Heliotropicam quam vocant, habuerunt in Iudæa Schabb. sol.35.2. vid. R. Salom. in l.
units.tr: In Judea they had the plant which they call heliotrope. Shabbat, folio 35, column 2. See R. Solomon in the same place.

units.la: Herodiani, quinam fuerint apud doctos disceptatur. Probabilissima sententia est, illos ita vocari, qui partibus Herodis adhæserant, & eius conatui suffragabantur, cùm Asmonæis depulsis regnum invaderet, oraculo quodam ad id facinus commotus, sicuti legere est in Bava Batra sol.3.2. Fieri etiam potest, ut ita nominarentur viri illi docti qui Hillele præsidè cum Menachemo se in aulam Herodis contulerunt, ut eò liberius Sadducæam doctrinam (quæ Marco est fermentum Herodis, Marci viii. 15.) fovere possent; historiam refert Iuchasin sol.19.1. de Hillele loquens & Schammæo. Antea, inquit, fuerant Hillel & Menachemus præsides Synedrii; at recesserat Menachemus ad famulitium Herodis Regis, unâ cum octoginta viris splendidè vestitis. De columbis Herodis. V.Cl.Buxt. L.T.p.630.
units.tr: Herodians: who they were is disputed among the learned. The most probable opinion is that they were so called who adhered to the party of Herod and supported his attempt, when, the Hasmoneans having been driven out, he seized the kingdom, moved to that deed by a certain oracle, as may be read in Bava Batra, folio 3, column 2. It may also be that those learned men were so named who, with Hillel as president and Menahem, betook themselves to the court of Herod, so that they might more freely foster the Sadducean doctrine (which for Mark is the leaven of Herod, Mark 8:15). Yuchasin, folio 19, column 1, relates the story, speaking of Hillel and Shammai: "Previously," it says, "Hillel and Menahem had been presidents of the Sanhedrin; but Menahem had withdrawn into the service of King Herod, together with eighty men splendidly dressed." On the doves of Herod, see Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 630.

units.la: Heterogenea. De iis multa & Mischna & Maym. in כלאים retulerunt, pauca hic attulisse sufficiet. Hæc non sunt Heterogenea. החשים Tritica, הכוסמים Spelta השיפון Secale Rogken. שיעורים Hordea, שבולת שועל Avena הזונין Species tritici degeneris, הפורקים fructus pretiosi, השופה והפול Pisi & lentes. Lupus vero & Canis; Canis הכופרי Cypricus (ita Cl. Castellus reddit, sed secundum Maymonidem simpliciter Canem venaticum significat, quasi diceres כפרי agrestem.) & vulpes, hircus & rupicapra, equus & mulus; mulus & asinus, asinus & onager, sunt heterogenea, etiamsi aliquam similitudinem habeant. Q
units.tr: Heterogeneous things. The Mishnah and Maimonides, in the treatise Kilayim, have related much about them; it will suffice to bring forward a few here. These are not heterogeneous: wheat [החשים], spelt [הכוסמים], rye [השיפון], rye (Rogken); barley [שיעורים]; oats [שבולת שועל]; the degenerate kind of wheat [הזונין]; precious fruit [הפורקים]; vetch and bean [השופה והפול]: peas and lentils. But wolf and dog; the dog [הכופרי] Cypriot (so Castellus renders it, but according to Maimonides it simply means a hunting dog, as if you were to say rustic, כפרי); and fox, goat and chamois, horse and mule; mule and ass, ass and onager, are heterogeneous, even if they have some likeness.

units.la: §. Non inferunt arborem in arborem diversæ speciei, non olus in olus, non arborem in olus, nec olus in arborem. Si quis feminaverit agrum suum tritico, & vellet illum de novo hordeis sem nare, ne transgrediatur præceptum de heterogeneis, debet agrum invertere, occare, ut semen tritici eruatur & arescat, & deinde illum potest arare & seminare hordeo. Si ager seminatus est, & ille confilium sumit in illo aliquid plantandi, non debet 1. plantare & deinde semen eruere, sed semen debet primò evellere, & deinde plantare.
units.tr: They do not graft a tree onto a tree of a different kind, nor a herb onto a herb, nor a tree onto a herb, nor a herb onto a tree. If anyone has sown his field with wheat and wishes to sow it anew with barley, then, lest he transgress the precept about heterogeneous things, he must turn over the field and harrow it, so that the wheat seed is dug out and dries up, and then he may plough it and sow it with barley. If a field has been sown and its owner resolves to plant something in it, he must not first plant and then dig out the seed; rather he must first pull out the seed and then plant.

units.la: §. Qui intendit agrum suum diversis speciebus seminare, debet facere ארנ areolas, & illas distinguere à se invicem spatio trium porcarum (sive ut est in Hierof. spatio duarum ulnarum) vel tantum quantum spatii aratrum Saaroniticum in una porca facit. Kilaim cap.1. & 2.
units.tr: Whoever intends to sow his field with different kinds must make small beds [ארנ], and separate them from one another by a space of three furrows (or, as in the Jerusalem Talmud, a space of two cubits), or as much space as a Saaronitic plough makes in one furrow. Kilayim, chapters 1 and 2.

units.la: Hierosolyma vid. Ierofolyma. Hiericho vid. Iericho.
units.tr: See Jerusalem. See Jericho.

units.la: Hillel fuit ex familia Davidis Hierof. Taanith f.68.1. Hillel & filii eius Simeon, Gamaliel & Simeon gesserunt Synedrii principatum à centum illis annis,qui devastationem templi præcesserunt. Bab.Schabbat sol.15. Hillel fuit homo mansuetissimus. Cl. Hotting. Thef. Phil. p. 42. A filiis Bethiræ è Babylonia veniens ad præfeēturam promotus fuit, quia illos docuerat Pascha pellere Sabbatum, in cuius rei decisione laborabant. Hierof.Pefachim sol.33.1. Octoginta habuit Hillel discipulos, quorum minimus fuit maximus ille vir Iochanan Ben Saccai. Iuchasin in Hillel, vid. etiam Cl. Buxtorf. Lex.T. in rad. הרל.
units.tr: Hillel was of the family of David (Hierof. Taanith f.68.1). Hillel and his sons Simeon and Gamaliel, and Simeon, held the presidency of the Sanhedrin for the hundred years that preceded the destruction of the Temple (Bab. Schabbat sol.15). Hillel was a most gentle man (Cl. Hotting. Thef. Phil. p. 42). Coming from the Bethyrians in Babylon, he was promoted to the presidency, because he had taught them to set aside the Sabbath in celebrating the Passover, a matter over which they were in difficulty (Hierof. Pefachim sol.33.1). Hillel had eighty disciples, the least of whom was the great man Johanan ben Zakkai. See Juchasin under Hillel, and also Cl. Buxtorf, Lex. T. under the root הרל.

units.la: §. Inter Hillelem & Schammæum semper maxima fuerunt dissidia in doctrina & traditionibus; Exempla odii & insidiarum harum duarum partium habes in Hierof.Schabbat sol. 33. & Hierof. Scheviit sol.35.2. Ibi enim recensetur quomodo Schammæani quosdam Hillelianos in Camera Ben Goronis interfecerint,& quòd R.Tarphon in maximo vitæ periculo fuerit,quia ficus comederat, secundum traditiones Scholæ Schammæanæ. Post multas altercationes Bath Kol in Iafne pro Hillele sententiam pronuntiavit, omnibus notum faciens ipsius sententiam in determinationibus sequendam esse. Hierof. Beracot sol.3.2.
units.tr: §. Between Hillel and Shammai there were always the greatest disputes over doctrine and traditions. You will find examples of the hatred and plotting of these two parties in Hierof. Schabbat sol.33 and Hierof. Scheviit sol.35.2. For there it is recounted how the Shammaites killed some Hillelites in the chamber of Ben Goron, and that R. Tarphon was in the greatest danger of his life because he had eaten a fig, according to the traditions of the school of Shammai. After many disputes, a Bath Kol at Jafne pronounced in favour of Hillel, making known to all that his opinion was to be followed in decisions (Hierof. Beracot sol.3.2).

units.la: §. Hilleliani noluerunt fidem adhibere disputanti Eleazaro quamvis suas opiniones miraculis probare conatus esset. Bava Metzia sol.59.2. quia ille Eliefer erat שמש Schammaanus Hierof.Trumah f.43.3. Iom. tebh f.60.3.&c.
units.tr: §. The Hillelites refused to give credence to Eleazar in debate, although he tried to prove his opinions by miracles (Bava Metzia sol.59.2), because that Eliezer was a Shammaite (Hierof. Trumah f.43.3; Iom. tebh f.60.3, etc.).

units.la: §. De his duabus Sectis in communi transsiit adagium. Controversiae inter discipulos Hillelis & discipulos Schammai nec ipsum Eliam Thisbiten dirimere posse.
units.tr: §. A proverb has passed into common use concerning these two sects: "Controversies between the disciples of Hillel and the disciples of Shammai cannot even be settled by Elijah the Tishbite."

units.la: HINNOM vallis. Magna pars vallis Kedron vocata est vallis Hinnom בני הנם quasi vallis filiorum Hinnom. In ea erat Tophet, (alii tophel, sed non ita bene,) locus excelsus in quo hominum liberi Molecho immolabantur, quasi præceptum Dei ad Abrahamum Gen.22.2. de eo sonaret; eum locum Rex Iosias cadaverum proiectione polluit, R. D. Kimchi in Pfal.27.13.
units.tr: HINNOM, valley. Much of the valley of Kidron was called the valley of Hinnom, בני הנם [the sons of Hinnom], as if it were the valley of the sons of Hinnom. In it was Tophet (others say Tophel, but not so well), a high place where the children of men were sacrificed to Molech, as if the command of God to Abraham (Gen. 22.2) sounded about that place. King Josiah polluted that place by casting corpses there (R. D. Kimchi on Ps. 27.13).

units.la: Erat Hinnom communis totius urbis sentina, & ut probabile est urbis fepulchretum. Vid. Ierem. vii. 32. de perpetuo igne qui ibi erat, ad offa & reliquam spurcitiem consumendam sonat illud Bab. Erubbin sol.19. 1. Tria sunt ostia Gehenna, unum in Eremo fecundum Num. xvi 33. Alterum in mari sicut fc-iptum Ion.11.2. tertium apud Hierosolymas, fecundum illud Efai. xxxi.9. Cuius ignis est in Sione &c. Item. Traditio est fecundum Scholam R. Iochanan Ben Saccai; duae palmae sunt גניא כן הנום in valle Hinnom, inter quas ascendit fumus &c. & hoc est ostium Gehenna. Hinc Iudæi locum damnatorum usitatissimè per vocem גהינום designant: exempla ubique scatent. Chaldæus Paraph. in Esra. xxxiii.14. גהינום יקידו עלם Gehenna ignis aeternus.
units.tr: Hinnom was the common sewer of the whole city and, as is likely, the city's burial ground. See Jer. 7.32 concerning the perpetual fire that was there. That saying in Bab. Erubbin sol.19.1, about consuming bones and other filth, points the same way: "There are three gates of Gehenna: one in the wilderness, according to Num. 16.33; another in the sea, as is written, Jon. 2.2; and a third at Jerusalem, according to that of Isa. 31.9, Whose fire is in Zion, etc." Likewise there is a tradition according to the school of R. Johanan ben Zakkai: "There are two palms, גניא כן הנום [Gehinna ben Hinnom], in the valley of Hinnom, between which the smoke rises, etc., and this is the gate of Gehenna." Hence the Jews very commonly designate the place of the damned by the word גהינום [Gehinnom]; examples are everywhere. The Chaldee paraphrast on Isa. 33.14 has גהינום יקידו עלם [Gehinnom yequdu alam], "Gehenna, eternal fire."

units.la: de Hircis in die Expiationis vid. ad Festum diei expiationis. Ille qui hircum emissarium eduxit immundus fuit Bab. Ioma sol.66.2. Iudæi Alexandrini vellicare consueverant hircum, & ipsum ad egrediendum urgere & incitare, dicendo מה שהי צפירא דין וחובי דרא סגיאין Quare moratur hic hircus, cùm huius generationis peccata sint tam multa? Bab. Ioma sol.66,
units.tr: On the goats on the Day of Atonement, see under the Feast of the Day of Atonement. He who led out the scapegoat was unclean (Bab. Ioma sol.66.2). The Alexandrian Jews used to pluck at the goat and urge and incite it to go out, saying, מה שהי צפירא דין וחובי דרא סגיאין [Why does this goat delay, since the sins of this generation are so many?] (Bab. Ioma sol.66).

units.la: Holocausta
units.tr: Burnt offerings

units.la: vid. Sacrificia.
units.tr: See Sacrifices.

units.la: Homicida est qui proximum suum percussit lapide aut ferro, aut in aquam aut ignem intruferit, unde exire nequeat, ac moriatur. Quòd fi quem impulerit in aquam aut ignem, fi inde exire aliquis potuisset, ille autem moriatur liber est. Si canem aut serpentem in quem inciderit, non tenetur. Si quispiam proximum perpercusserit lapide pugnóve, & ista plaga lethalis æstimata sit; si melius habere cæperit, malum vero postmodum iterum ingravescat, ita ut moriatur, reus est.
units.tr: A homicide is one who has struck his neighbour with a stone or iron, or has thrust him into water or fire, from which he cannot escape, and he dies. But if he has pushed someone into water or fire, and that person could have got out from there but dies, the pusher is free. If he has thrown him to a dog or a serpent, he is not liable. If someone has struck his neighbour with a stone or fist, and the blow is judged mortal; if he then begins to recover, but the injury later grows worse again, so that he dies, the striker is liable.

units.la: §. Si quis in animo habuerit ferire bestiam, atque interemerit hominem, aut intenderit ferire peregrinum, & interfecerit Israelitam, liber est. Si intenderit femur cuiuspiam percutere, ubi ictus lethalis non fuisset; & telum in pectus inciderit, lethalemq; plagam fecerit,& moriatur,liber est. Si intenderit pectus lethali plaga ferire, ictusque in femur delatus lethalis non fit, etiamsi moriatur alter,liber est. Verum si intenderit quempiam ferire in lumbis, tam fortiter ut illo ictu interfici potuisset, isque deferatur in pectus, vitamque ei eripiat, tenetur. Homicida si admisceretur aliis reis, omnes liberi sunt. R. Iehuda ait carcere includuntur cuncti. Sanhed.c.1.
units.tr: §. If someone intended to strike a beast and killed a man, or intended to strike a stranger and killed an Israelite, he is free. If he intended to strike someone's thigh, where the blow would not have been mortal, and the weapon struck the chest and made a mortal wound, and the man dies, he is free. If he intended to strike the chest with a mortal blow, and the blow that was aimed there fell on the thigh and was not mortal, he is free even if the other dies. But if he intended to strike someone in the loins, so forcefully that the blow could have killed him, and it slipped to the chest and took his life, he is liable. If a homicide is mixed in with other guilty persons, all are free. R. Judah says that all are shut up in prison (Sanhed. c.1).

units.la: §. Hos licet occidere, ut alios liberemus; qui alterum prosequitur animo occidendi, qui insectatur masculum, aut puellam desponsatam. Sed qui sectatur bestiam, Sabbathum violat, idolo divinos honores defert, haud sunt occidendi ne peccent. Sanhed. cap.8.7. Maymon. Hal. Rotzeach.c.1.
units.tr: §. These may be killed to save others: one who pursues another with intent to kill, one who chases a male or a betrothed girl. But one who pursues a beast violates the Sabbath, and one who pays divine honour to an idol; they are not to be killed, lest they sin (Sanhed. c.8.7; Maimonides, Hal. Rotzeach c.1).

units.la: §. Si quis occiderit absque testibus inditur לכיפה arca, & cibatur pane ærumnæ & aqua angustiæ.Sanhed.c.9.5.
units.tr: §. If someone has killed without witnesses, he is put into a chest, לכיפה [lekippah], and is fed the bread of affliction and the water of distress (Sanhed. c.9.5).

units.la: §. Quod de duplici homicida, & duplici eius iudicio modò innuimus clarius à Maymon. proponitur in Rotzeach cap.2. Quicunque proximum occiderit manu sua, gladio scilicet percutiens aut lapide, ita ut ipsum interficiat: aut strangulaverit aut combusserit, ita ut moriatur, quocunque modo in propria persona interficiens. Ecce talis morte mulctandus a Synedrio: at ille qui mercede conducit alium, ut occidat proximum, aut qui servos suos mittit, & illi occidunt, aut violenter in aliquam bestiam protrudit, aut qui fe ipsum interimit כל אחר מאלו שומר דמים Vnuiquisque horum est effafor sanguinis, & damnas est Mortis לשמים per manum Dei, at non pleƈtendus est à Synedrio. Christus Matth. v.22. Iudæis ostendit ipsos malè homicidas ita distinguere,& solùm ad hos duos casus restringere, cùm & ille homicida fit, qui temerè fratri suo iratcitur.
units.tr: What we have just hinted at, concerning the twofold homicide and his twofold judgment, Maimonides sets out more clearly in Rotzeach c.2: whoever kills his neighbour with his own hand, that is, striking him with a sword or stone so that he dies, or strangles or burns him so that he dies, in whatever way killing him in his own person, is to be punished with death by the Sanhedrin. But one who hires another to kill his neighbour, or who sends his servants, and they kill him, or who pushes him violently into some beast, or who kills himself, כל אחר מאלו שומר דמים [each of these is a keeper of blood], and is condemned to death by heaven, לשמים [lashamayim], at the hand of God, but is not to be punished by the Sanhedrin. Christ, in Matt. 5.22, shows the Jews that they distinguish homicides in this way and restrict it to these two cases, since he also is a homicide who angrily calls his brother a fool.

units.la: HONORUM in gente Ifraelitica hi erant gradus & subsellia. Hierof. Horaioth sol.84.2. Sapiens præferendus Regi: Rex summo Pontifici: Summus Pontifex Prophetæ: Propheta Sacerdoti unƈto in bellum: Sacerdos unƈtus in bellum Præfecto Ephemeriæ: Præfectus Ephemeriæ capiti familiæ: caput familiæ Consiliario: Consiliarius Thefaurario: Thefaurarius Sacerdoti privato: Sacerdos privatus Levitæ: Levita Israelitæ: Israelita Notho: Nothus Nethinæo: Nethinæus Proselyto: Proselytus servo manumisso. At quando hoc? Nempe cùm cætera sunt paria: At verò si nothus sit discipulus sapientis, & Sacerdos Summus sit indoƈtus, Nothus ei præferendus. Sapiens est præferendus Regi: nam si moriatur sapiens, non est ei par; At si moriatur Rex, quivis Israelita lita Rex efle potest.
units.tr: HONOURS. Among the Israelite people these were the grades and seats of honour (Hierof. Horaioth sol.84.2): the wise man is to be preferred to the king; the king to the high priest; the high priest to the prophet; the prophet to the priest anointed for war; the priest anointed for war to the prefect of the course; the prefect of the course to the head of a family; the head of a family to the counsellor; the counsellor to the treasurer; the treasurer to a private priest; the private priest to the Levite; the Levite to the Israelite; the Israelite to the bastard; the bastard to the Nethinim; the Nethinim to the proselyte; the proselyte to the freed slave.
