So too the power of those promoted can be restricted to a certain time; e.g. "you may dispense from vows, and judge [דיני קיסות] cases in many matters, for as long as you remain in that province, or until the prince of the Senate comes here," and so on. Maimonides, Hilchot Sanhedrin cap. 4. See also on the form and rites of promotion, Juchasin fol. 60, Abravanel cap. 1, Avot. On the imposition of hands in sacrifices, see Sacrificia, and Maimonides, Corban cap. 3.

units.la: IMMUNDITIEI causæ principaliores recensentur à R. Salomone in Kelim cap. 1. Homo & vasa non contrahunt immunditiem מאם אלא התומאת Nisi à patre immunditiei (sic vocant causas principales.) Quales sunt: Immunditia à reptili, à concubitu feminis, à polluto per mortuum, à leproso, ab aqua purificationis, à coeunte cum menstruosa, à fluxu feminisi, à sputo eius, ab urina eius, à sanguine menstruosa, à profluvio &c. Qui illis pollutus erat ad purificationem sui totius corporis immersione opus habebat; at ob immunditias inferiores satis erat manus lavare.
units.tr: The principal causes of uncleanness are listed by Rabbi Solomon in Kelim cap. 1. Man and vessels do not contract uncleanness [מאם אלא התומאת], except from a father of uncleanness (this is what they call the principal causes). These are: uncleanness from a creeping thing, from intercourse with a woman, from pollution by a dead body, from a leper, from the water of purification, from one who has intercourse with a menstruating woman, from a woman's discharge, from her spittle, from her urine, from menstrual blood, from a flux, and so on. Whoever was defiled by these needed immersion of his whole body for purification; but for the lesser uncleannesses it was enough to wash the hands.

units.la: §. Mortuus immunditiem affert במגע במשא ובאהל Cum tangitur, fertur, & in tentorio reponitur. Ratione quidem secundi modi quamvis aliquis medium aliquod interponeret, ita ut mortuum non immediatè tangeret, tamen immundus redditur. v. g. fumat aliquis decem vasa & mortuum imponat vasi superiori; ille immundus fiet; ex vasibus vero nullum erit immundum, nisi quod Cadaver immediatè tetigit. Ratione tertii modi omnia immunda fiunt quæ cum cadavere sub eodem tentorio reperiuntur, sive vasa sive homo sit; imò etiam ille qui tentorium ingressus fuerit, aut caput vel digitos immiserit. Maymon. Hal. מומאה מה cap.1. Apud quem etiam curiosâ diligentiâ plurimi casus immunditiei notantur; in balaceot quæ citatam proximè insequuntur.
units.tr: A dead body conveys uncleanness [במגע במשא ובאהל] by touch, by carrying, and in a tent. In the second manner, even if someone interposed some medium so that he did not touch the dead body directly, he is nevertheless made unclean. For example, if someone holds ten vessels and places the dead body on the upper vessel, he will become unclean; but none of the vessels will be unclean except the one the corpse touched directly. In the third manner, all things that are found together with a corpse under the same tent become unclean, whether vessels or a man; indeed even one who entered the tent, or merely put in his head or fingers. Maimonides, Hilchot Tumat Met cap. 1, where many cases of uncleanness are also carefully noted, in the Baraita which follows immediately after the cited passage.

units.la: §. Lecti immunditiem contraxerunt, vel istam quam מרוש מומאת vocarunt, vel istam quam מרוש מגע מומאת. Lectus prioris generis erat, in quem vel sederat, vel steterat, vel se reclinaverat, vel innixus fuerat, vel pependerat profluviosus, aut profluviola, aut menstruosa, aut puerpera, aut leprosus. Lectus posterioris generis erat, quem tetigerat aliquid quod hi tetigerant. Vid. Maymon. in Hal. משכב ומושב.
units.tr: Beds contracted uncleanness either of the kind called [מרוש מומאת], or of the kind called [מרוש מגע מומאת]. The bed of the first kind was one on which a person with a flux, or a menstruating or puerperal woman, or a leper, had sat, stood, reclined, leaned or hung. The bed of the second kind was one that had been touched by anything these had touched. See Maimonides, in Hilchot [משכב ומושב].

units.la: §. De Immundorum purificatione & Lotione. Vid. suo loco. in L. & P. de pollutis aliquid. V. f. 1.
units.tr: On the purification and washing of the unclean, see its place in L. and P.; on things polluted, see f. 1.

units.la: §. Si quis immundus Sanctuarium ingressus fuerit incurrit pœnam כרת & מיתה בידי שמים Excidii & mortis per manum Dei; (vid. כרת in C.) Maymon. Biath Hamikd. c.4. Sacerdos qui cultui Dei vacat & non singulis horis matutinis manus & pedes laverit, in se arcessit pœnam מיתה בידי שמים Idem. ibid. cap. 5. Nota tamen hic, illum immundum fuisse, & immundum atrium ingressum esse qui hircum emissarium in desertum educebat. Bab. Ioma sol. 66.2. Sed hæc regula generalis solùm respe-ctu âtu illius exceptionem admisit.
units.tr: If an unclean person entered the sanctuary, he incurred the penalty of [כרת], excision, and death [מיתה בידי שמים] by the hand of Heaven (see [כרת] in C.). Maimonides, Hilchot Bi'at Hamikdash cap. 4. A priest who attends to the worship of God and does not wash his hands and feet every morning at each hour incurs death by the hand of Heaven. Ibid. cap. 5. Note here, however, that he was unclean who had entered the unclean court and led the scapegoat out into the wilderness. Babylonian Talmud, Yoma fol. 66.2. But this general rule admitted an exception only with respect to that case.

units.la: §. Quænam aquæ ad aspersionem immundorum idoneæ sint definitur in Parah cap. 8. 10. inter alia ibi notatur, Aquas fluvii קרמיון Kirmion (qui secundùm Aruch situs est in via, quæ tendit ad Damascum.) & fluvii פיגה non esse idoneas ad aspersionem immundorum. Nec aquas Iordanis aut ירמוך Iarmochi ad aspersionem idoneas & aptas esse, quia aquæ Kirmionis & Pigæ sunt admodum lutosæ, Iordanis verò & Iatmochi mixtæ cum aquis aliorum fluviorum: uti observat Giossa. Qui mundus fieri vult, à stercoribus se per quatuor cubitos removëre debet, nec se lavare in aquis corruptis, donec eas aliis infusis diluerit. Beracot cap.3.6.
units.tr: Which waters are suitable for sprinkling the unclean is defined in Parah cap. 8, 10. Among other things it is noted there that the waters of the river Kirmion [קרמיון] (which, according to Aruch, lies on the road that leads to Damascus) and of the river [פיגה] are not suitable for sprinkling the unclean. Nor are the waters of the Jordan or of [ירמוך] Jarmochi suitable and fit for sprinkling, because the waters of Kirmion and Piga are very muddy, while those of the Jordan and Jarmochi are mixed with the waters of other rivers, as Gloss observes. Whoever wishes to become clean must remove himself four cubits from filth, and not wash himself in corrupt waters until he has diluted them by pouring in others. Berachot cap. 3, 6.

units.la: INCANTATIONES vid. Amuleta & Magicae Artes.
units.tr: On incantations, see Amulets and Magic Arts.

units.la: INFANTES in utero matris irregulariter se gerere, & aliquid facere posse, quod non vacaret culpâ autumarunt Iudæi. In Vaikra Rabba introducitur in Parabola fœmina filium serió accusans coram Iudice כרהוא בנעי הוה מכוע Quod inordinatè calcitaret cum esset in utero. In Midrasch Ruth in cap 111. 13. Refertur historia de Elifcha Ben Abuiah qui factus est Apostata, illius apostasiæ ratio inter alias hæc redditur. Sunt qui dicunt, quòd mater eius cum gravida foret transiverit persanum Ethnicum, & odorata sit nidorem, simulque de eo quod olfecerat comederit; A quo ille in utero calefactus est, & in bullas intumuit, acsi esset in utero serpentis.
units.tr: The Jews thought that infants in the womb behave irregularly and can do something that is not free from fault. In Vayikra Rabba a woman is introduced in a parable seriously accusing her son before the judge [כרהוא בנעי הוה מכוע], because he kicked in disorderly fashion while he was in the womb. In Midrash Ruth on chapter 3.13 there is reported the story of Elisha ben Abuyah, who became an apostate; among other explanations of his apostasy this one is given: "Some say that his mother, when she was pregnant, passed by a heathen temple and smelled its fumes, and at the same time ate something from what she had smelled; from which he was warmed in the womb and swelled into bubbles, as if he were in the womb of a serpent."

units.la: §. In Bammidbar Rabba sol.230.2. Absolvitur Iacob quod prehenderit calcem Esavi, sed vix absolvitur Esau quod insurrexerit contra Iacobum.
units.tr: In Bammidbar Rabba, fol. 230.2, Jacob is acquitted for having seized Esau's heel, but Esau is barely acquitted for having risen up against Jacob.

units.la: §. Quaesivit Antoninus à R. Iehuda Sancto; A quonam tempore incipiat malus affectus pravalere in homine; An à tempore formationis eius in utero, an à tempore exitus eius ex utero? Respondit Rabbi, יצירת עובר מעת צירתו à tempore formationis eius. Ex quibus patet primaevam Iudaeorum sententiam fuisse infantes à prima sua animatione esse peccaminosos, & in utero aliquando se irregulariter gerere posse. Quis autem illius inordinationis fons, quàm peccatum originale?
units.tr: Antoninus asked Rabbi Judah the Holy: From what time does the evil inclination begin to prevail in a man? From the time of his formation in the womb, or from the time of his emergence from the womb? Rabbi replied: The formation of the embryo from the time of its formation [יצירת עובר מעת צירתו]. From this it is clear that the earliest Jewish opinion was that infants are sinful from their first animation, and that they can sometimes behave disorderly while still in the womb. Yet what is the source of that disorder, if not original sin?

units.la: §. Vt quivis infantes suos nutriret, de novo decretum est à Synedrio in Vscha; Hierof. Cheduhbot sol. 28. 4. Si verò accideret ut aliquis sua bona filiis concederet, illi patrem & matrem ex illis sustentare debent. Ibid. de filio immorigero V. in F.
units.tr: So that everyone would support their own infants, the Sanhedrin decreed afresh at Usha; Jerusalem Talmud, Kethuboth, fol. 28.4: if someone were to give his goods to his sons, they must support their father and mother from them. Ibid., concerning the disobedient son, see below.

units.la: Insomnia magnoperè curârunt Iudaei; hinc 1. sibi indixerunt ieiunia, ut insomnia felicia adipiscerentur. Vid. Ieiunia. 2. plurimas regulas inde de tractandis insomniis habent: Beracot sol. 14.1. יצאה ארם לחלום טוב עד כ"ב שנה Observet homo insomnium bonum usque ad annos viginti duos, exemplo Iosephi. Item in Schabbat sol.30.2. in Gl. Si cubtum eas latabundus, fruēris insomniis bonis &c. 3. Hinc quoque inter Iudaeos non ignobilis professio & ars fuit, insomnia interpretari. Bab. Beracot sol. 55. 2. introducitur quidam senex hunc in modum verba faciens. Viginti quatuor insomniorum interpre-tari terpretes eram Hierosolymis: atque ego cum aliquando somniarem somnium omnes de eius interpretatione consului; quod interpretatum est hic non interpretatur est ille; & tamen evenerunt omnia, quae interpretati sunt omnes, &c. Vide etiam Hierof. Maaser Scheni sol.52.2 3. ibi enim plurimae de insomniis referuntur historiae: R. Iose Ben Chelpetha, R. Ismael, R. Lazar & Akibha tanquam insomniorum interpretes adducuntur.
units.tr: The Jews took great pains over dreams. Hence, first, they appointed fasts for themselves, so that they might obtain good dreams (see Fasts). Second, they have many rules about dealing with dreams: Berakhoth, fol. 14.1: A man should observe a good dream up to the age of twenty-two, after the example of Joseph [יצאה ארם לחלום טוב עד כ"ב שנה]. Likewise in Shabbath, fol. 30.2, in the gloss: If you go to bed joyful, you will enjoy good dreams, etc. Third, among the Jews the interpreting of dreams was also a not inconsiderable profession and art. In Babylonian Berakhoth, fol. 55.2, an old man is introduced speaking in this way: I was one of twenty-four interpreters of dreams in Jerusalem. Once when I dreamed a dream, I consulted all of them about its interpretation; what one interpreted, another did not interpret; and yet everything they interpreted came true, all of it. See also Jerusalem Talmud, Maaser Sheni, fol. 52.2–3, for there many stories about dreams are told: R. Jose ben Chelpetha, R. Ismael, R. Lazar and Akiba are brought forward as interpreters of dreams.

units.la: INTERCALATIO.
units.tr: INTERCALATION.

units.la: Qui annus fit uno mense longior is intercalaris appellatur: sed nullus additur unquam anno mensis alius quàm Februarius: Itaque anno intercalari Februarii bini continuantur. Quid ita verò? Nimirum ut habeatur unà cum messe Pascha; secundùm dictum Deut. 16. 1. Observa mensem novarum frugum. i.e. tene temporis observandi rationem, quae mensem hunc ad messem adducat; atqui nisi alterum Februarium anno adducas, tum Pascha hybernis, tum aestivis acciderit temporibus.
units.tr: A year that is made longer by one month is called intercalary; but no month is ever added to a year other than February, so in an intercalary year two Februaries follow one another. Why is this so? Clearly so that the Passover falls together with the harvest, according to the saying in Deut. 16:1, Observe the month of new fruits, that is, keep the reckoning of the time that brings this month into line with the harvest. Indeed, unless you add a second February to the year, the Passover would fall sometimes in winter, sometimes in summer.

units.la: §. Tribus de causis intercalatur annus ע"ם ... ob spicas virorum, ob fructus arborum (quae debebant primitias in Pentecoste.) ... ob solis conversionem, (sive aequinoctium autumnale circa quod festum tabernaculorum peragi debebat.) Si duo illorum concurrant intercalant, ob unum verò non item.
units.tr: A year is intercalated for three reasons: for the ears of grain (of the men), for the fruit of the trees (which had to bring the firstfruits at Pentecost), and for the turning of the sun (or the autumnal equinox, around which the Feast of Tabernacles had to be celebrated). If two of these coincide they intercalate; but for one alone they do not.

units.la: §. Non intercalatur annus, nisi necesse sit propter itinera, (ab imbribus corrupta,) pontes (fractos,) furnos agnorum Paschalium (quàm reparandi sunt,) aut Israelitas qui extrà terram Israeliticam habitant ex sedibus suis obaliquod festum egressos, si nondum ad urbē pervenerint.
units.tr: A year is not intercalated unless it is necessary because of the roads (spoiled by rains), the bridges (broken), the ovens for the Passover lambs (which must be repaired), or Israelites living outside the land of Israel who have set out from their homes for some feast, if they have not yet reached the city.

units.la: §. Annus non intercalatur ob nivis copiam aut fr͏g.bus, nec ob hædos aut agnos (macros,) nec propter pullos avium involucres (quales non poterant à puerperis offerri;) Sed si aliqua alia intercalandi causa esset, talia facerent, ut eò magis ad intercalationem impellerentur.
units.tr: A year is not intercalated because of an abundance of snow or of frogs, nor on account of goats or lambs (that are thin), nor because of the young birds in their nests (of the sort that could not be offered by women after childbirth). But if there were some other reason for intercalating, they would do such things, so that they might be all the more driven to intercalation.

units.la: §. Non intercalatur nisi per eos qui sunt ad id officii electi. Itaque Synedrii Princeps deligit nonnullos, quibus ita dicit. Curate parati sitis in loco illo uti deliberemus ac consultemus, utrum annus intercalaris oporteat constitui nec ne. Atqui ab his solis qui sunt ad id invitati intercalatur. Ad hanc deliberationem, neque Rex admittitur unquam, nec Summus Sacerdos. Ille, ne forte propter delectum habendum, aut belli administrationem ad alterutram partem vel intercalandi vel non intercalandi convocatos impellat: hic, ne ab intercalandi consilio deterreat ideò, quòd si intercalaretur, mensis septembris in dies iam frigidos magno ipsius incommodo incurreret; quippe qui obligatur in die expiationis (qui est dies eius mensis decimus) quinquies se abluere. Si Præses Synedrii abest, annus intercalatur eâ conditione si Principi placuerit.
units.tr: Intercalation is carried out only by those who have been chosen for this office. So the Prince of the Sanhedrin selects certain men and says to them: Take care to be ready in that place, so that we may deliberate and consult whether a leap year ought to be established or not. Yet intercalation is made only by those who have been invited to it. Neither the King nor the High Priest is ever admitted to this deliberation: the former, lest perhaps he should drive those summoned to one side or the other, whether to intercalate or not, by the holding of a levy or the conduct of war; the latter, lest he should be deterred from the counsel to intercalate, because if the year were intercalated, the month of Tishri would fall in days already cold, to his great discomfort, since he is bound to wash himself five times on the Day of Atonement (which is the tenth day of that month). If the President of the Sanhedrin is absent, the year is intercalated on condition that it pleases the Prince.

units.la: §. Cùm venerit Februarii dies tricesimus, necdum sit intercalatum, omninò intercalandum non est: quippe cùm possint illo die Calendæ Nisan haberi. Mensis vero Nisan cum venit necdum intercalatum est, intercalari porrò non est integrum. Verumtamen ipso die Februarii si intercalatur ratum,habetur. Ergo si postquàm est intercalatum, lunæ novæ nu atius afferatur, Calendæ celebrantur non Martiæ; sed denuò Februariæ.
units.tr: When the thirtieth day of February has come and the year has not yet been intercalated, it must not be intercalated at all, since the Calends of Nisan can be held on that day. But when the month of Nisan comes and the year has not yet been intercalated, it is no longer lawful to intercalate. Nevertheless, if it is intercalated on the very day of February, the decision stands. Therefore, if after the intercalation a new moon is reported later, the Calends are celebrated not in March but again in February.

units.la: §. Cùm est intercalatum à Senatu literæ mittuntur in omnes Provincias, ut longinqui annum intercalarem factum esse cognoscant; Atque literæ scriptæ sunt verbis Principis Senatus in hunc modum. Notum vobis facio decrevisse me unà cum meis sociis, ut hic annus augeretur triginta, vel 29. diebus. Licet enim Senatui mensem vel cavum vel plenum constituere. Maymon Hal. Kid.Chodefch c.4.
units.tr: When the Senate has intercalated, letters are sent to all the provinces, so that those far away may learn that an intercalary year has been made. The letters were written by the Prince of the Senate in these words: I make known to you that I, together with my colleagues, have decreed that this year be lengthened by thirty, or by 29 days. For the Senate may establish a month either hollow or full. Maimonides, Hilchot Kiddush ha-Chodesh, c. 4.

units.la: §. Quandiu Synedrium fuit in terra Israelis, ab eo ut iam diximus aliquando pro necessitate, aliquando iuxta apparitionem Lunæ, capita mensium & annorum fixa & constituta fuerunt, at ex quo tempore illud abolitum est, Iudæi certam quandam rationem accommodatam luminarium motui medio (מחלך אסטר) certisque regulis astricam sequuntur. Maymon t. c. c.8.
units.tr: As long as the Sanhedrin was in the land of Israel, the beginnings of months and years were fixed and established by it, as we have already said, sometimes out of necessity, sometimes according to the appearance of the moon. But since that time, when this was abolished, the Jews follow a certain fixed reckoning, adapted to the mean motion of the luminaries (mechalech astar) and bound by certain rules. Maimonides, ibid., c. 8.

units.la: §. De intercalatione habe tohistoriolas. Cùm annum non licèret intercalare nisi in Iudæa, (Maymon Kidd.Chod.c.2.) Plurimi Lyddam adierunt è Schola Rabbi Iehudæ sanċti (è Galilæa scilicet) ut intercalarent, at occurrit ipsis oculus aliquis malus (infortunium) atque omnes simul sunt mortui. Exinde anni intercalationem transtulerunt è Iudæa in Galilæam &c. Hieros.Sanhed.sol.18.3.
units.tr: Concerning intercalation there is a little story. Since a year could be intercalated only in Judea (Maimonides, Kiddush ha-Chodesh, c. 2), many went to Lydda from the school of Rabbi Judah the Holy (that is, from Galilee) in order to intercalate; but some evil eye (a misfortune) fell upon them, and they all died together. After that they transferred the intercalation of the year from Judea to Galilee, etc. Jerusalem Sanhedrin, fol. 18.3.

units.la: §. Septem Seniores congressi sunt ad intercalandum annum פנחס בפעם in valle Rimmon; videlicet R. Meir. R. Iuda, R. Iosi, R.Simeon, & Nehemia, R.Lazar Ben Iacob, Ec R. Iochanan Sandelar; Eratque illic rupes niarmorea, cui unusquisque infixit clavum : hinc quoque hucusque rupes clavorum vocatur. Hierof. Chagigah sol. 78. 4. Vid. etiam Novilunia.
units.tr: Seven elders met to intercalate the year at Phinehas in Bemoth [פנחס בפעם]? in the valley of Rimmon; namely R. Meir, R. Judah, R. Jose, R. Simeon, and Nehemiah, R. Lazar ben Jacob, and R. Jochanan Sandelar. There was there a marble rock, into which each one fixed a nail; hence also the rock is called the rock of nails to this day. Jerusalem Chagigah, fol. 78.4. See also Novilunia.

units.la: INTERPRETES Orientales cómutant sæpè nomina propria per transpositionem literarum & vocalium. Sic Arabs Esai.xxvii.12. Pirokopipwr transtulit פורן pro כורה mutando ד. in ג. Interpreti Syro Schur Exod. 15. 20. est שור Sud, Puncto notificativo in litera ultima male disposito. Sic eodem errore Gen.xvi. 7. & 14. Schur & Bared vertit Gedar, pro Gerar. Bared Arabi ibi est Iared duobus punctulis sub litera prima, pro uno tantum subiectis.
units.tr: Eastern interpreters often change proper names by transposing letters and vowels. Thus the Arab, at Isaiah 27:12, Pirokopipwr, rendered פורן for כורה, changing ד into ג. For the Syriac interpreter Schur at Exod. 15:22 is שור Sud, with the pointing mark in the last letter wrongly placed. So by the same error at Gen. 16:7 and 14, the Syriac Schur and Bared renders Gedar for Gerar; the Arabic Bared there is Iared, with two little points under the first letter instead of only one.

units.la: §. Soliti sunt interpretes Græci nomina locorum non raro eo nomine reddere, non quo vocantur in textu Hebreo, sed quo nuncupabantur temporibus posterioribus sub templo secundo, quod & à Chaldæis Targumistis scripius etiam factum. Huius farinæ Καπνωδους pro Caphtarim Πιτοκοφιδ pro נחל מצרים fluvio Ægypti. sed clarum Exemplum habes ex collatione Loci Hierof. Megillah sol. 70.1. in quo Talmudistæ urbes quasdam quarum mentio in Iosua xix. & vetustis & præsentibus nominibus appellant. קטפ Kattat est Katinot Schimron est Simonia Irala est Chiriah. lxx interpretes retinuerunt non nomina vetusta sed recentiora dum loc. illum Iosuæ exposuerunt Καδαρα, Συμεων, Ιεχωθ. τιεσχω. Sic quoque 1.Reg. ix. 11. 12. Regionem illam Galilææ quæ olim כבור vocabatur (V.fl. in C.) ὁ͵ιον nomine recentiore transtulerunt: nam ex Hierof. Demai sol.22.4. Ista urbes prohibitæ sunt בתחום in termino &c. suspicari licet תחום reg onem כבור designare,optimè autem תח Graeè ὁ͵ιον redditur. Ex quibus versionem istam non redolere vetustatem temporum Ptolomæi Philadelphi videtur.
units.tr: The Greek interpreters were accustomed to render the names of places not rarely by the name not by which they are called in the Hebrew text, but by which they were known in later times under the second temple; which was also done by the Chaldean Targumists. Of this kind are Kapnōdous for Caphtorim, and Pitokophid for the river of Egypt [נחל מצרים]. But you have a clear example from a comparison of the passage in Jerusalem Megillah, fol. 70.1, in which the Talmudists call certain cities mentioned in Joshua 19 by both their old and their present names: Kattat is Katinot, Shimron is Simonia, Irala is Chiriah. The Seventy retained not the old names but the more recent ones, when they rendered that passage of Joshua as Kadara, Symeon, Iechōth [יחות]. So too at 1 Kings 9:11–12 they rendered by the more recent name Ion that region of Galilee which was formerly called Cabul (see Fl. on C.): for from Jerusalem Demai, fol. 22.4, These cities were forbidden [בתחום], in the border, etc., we may suspect that תחום designates the region of Cabul, and indeed תח is rendered in Greek as Ion very well. From these examples it appears that this version does not smell of the antiquity of the times of Ptolemy Philadelphus.

units.la: §. Sed insuper probabile est septuaginta Interpretes non nisi legem in sermonem Græcum transtulisse, 1. enim sic loquuntur Magistri in Massecet Sopherim cap.1. v.8. שוב מעשה בתלמי המלך שכנס שבעים ושנים זקנים והוש כם בשבעיים ושנים בתים ולא גלה להם על מה כנסם נכנס לכל אחד ואחד מהם אשר אמר להם כתבו לי תורת משה ובכם נתן המקום עצה בלב כל אחד ואחד והסכימו דעתן לדעת אחד וכתבו לו תורה כפני עצים : Historia est de Ptolomæo Rege, quòd LXXII. duos senes convocaverit, & eos in 72. domos collocaverit, causam verò cur eos convocaverat ipsis non indigitaverit; sed ad unumquemque ingressum ipsi dixerit, verte mihi legem Mosis Magistri vestri. Dedit Deus unicuique robur & consilium ut omnes in versione consenserint, & a se ipsis legem Mosis verterint. Observa hic in eodem cap.v.7. numerum LXXII. sanum ad quinque restringi & diminui; & proinde hanc contradictionem satis arguere, numerum LXXII. etiam fictitium esse. 2. Ipsa temporis ratio non videtur plura pati posse, Nam ab ἀντίῤῥ Aristæa 72 diebus, ad personarum numerum hoc pensum absolvisse memorantur, quo angusto dierum spatio vix describi, multo minus verti in alium sermonem vetus testamentum potuisset. 3. Incredulos constringet Iosephi authoritas in praef. Antiq. Iudaic. Ptolomaeus II., Rex Ægypti magnopere contendit legem nostram in Graecum elogium transferri &c. Eleazar Pontifex Summus Regi hanc utilem tatem non invidit, reclamaturus omnino nisi consuetudinem haberemus iam a maioribus acceptam, res bonas celare nemini nem &c. Neque vero totam Scripturam occupavit, sed legem solum ei tradiderunt interpretes, qui ideo, Alexandriam missi fuerant.
units.tr: Moreover, it is probable that the Seventy Interpreters translated only the Law into Greek. (1) For the Masters speak thus in Massechet Sopherim, chapter 1, verse 8: "It happened that King Ptolemy gathered seventy-two elders and placed them in seventy-two houses, but did not tell them why he had gathered them. He went in to each one and said to them, 'Write for me the Law of Moses your teacher.' God put counsel into the heart of each one, and they agreed in one opinion and wrote for him a Law before the wise men" [שוב מעשה בתלמי המלך שכנס שבעים ושנים זקנים והושיבם בשבעים ושנים בתים ולא גלה להם על מה כנסם נכנס לכל אחד ואחד מהם ואמר להם כתבו לי תורת משה רבכם נתן המקום עצה בלב כל אחד ואחד והסכימו דעתן לדעת אחת וכתבו לו תורה לפני חכמים]. This is the story of King Ptolemy, who gathered seventy-two elders and placed them in seventy-two houses, but did not tell them why he had summoned them. He went in to each one and said, "Translate for me the Law of Moses, your teacher." God gave each one strength and counsel, so that all agreed in the translation and rendered the Law of Moses by themselves. Observe here that in the same chapter, verse 7, the number seventy-two is reduced and cut down to five; and so this contradiction sufficiently shows that the number seventy-two is also fictitious. (2) The very chronology does not seem to allow more: the seventy-two are said to have completed this task in seventy-two days, from the time of Aristeas; in so narrow a span of days the Old Testament could hardly have been written out, much less translated into another language. (3) The authority of Josephus in the preface to the Antiquities of the Jews will constrain unbelievers: Ptolemy II, King of Egypt, very eagerly desired that our Law be translated into the Greek language, etc. Eleazar, the High Priest, did not begrudge the king this useful service, though he would have objected altogether unless we had a custom received from our ancestors, not to hide good things from anyone, etc. Nor did he take up the whole of Scripture, but the interpreters who had been sent to Alexandria delivered only the Law to him.

units.la: §. Sed nec hodierna expositio Graeca LXX. senium est, nam in Massilia Sopherim loco m. c. dicitur ipsos tredecim loca mutasse, (quae recenset Iosippus in historiae suae exordio, & ex eo Schikkardus in Bechinat Happer.) at illa loca non mutata repriuntur in hodierna editione. De hac versione etiam aliquid diximus ap. Lexem. De Interprete Synagogae. Vid. Synagogam.
units.tr: Nor is the present Greek version truly that of the Seventy, for in Massechet Sopherim, in the passage cited, it is said that they changed thirteen places (which Josippon lists at the beginning of his history, and from him Schickard in Bechinat Happer). Yet those places are found unchanged in the present edition. We have said something about this version also under Lexem. On the Interpreter of the Synagogue, see Synagogam.

units.la: Iobus, de eo ferme integrum conscripsit caput Maymon in More Nevoch. III. 22. 1. dicit Mirabilem esse historiam Iobi Et exemplum ad explicandum opiniones hominum de providentia. 2. Quorundam esse sententiam Iobum nunquam exstitisse, sed omnia parabolica esse. 3. Illos qui credunt Iobum revera fuisse, nescire neque locum neque tempus quo historia illa acciderit: Quosdam esse qui dicunt illum vixisse tempore Patriarcharum, alios ipsum in diebus Moisis exstitisse, aut DaDavidis; alios censêre illum fuisse מעולים מכבל ex ascendentibus è Babylone : illamque sententiarum diversitatem facere, ut plurimi confirmentur in sua opinione ipsum nunquam extitisse. 4. Quamvis fuerit vel non fuerit Iobus, tamen certum esse apparitionem illam Satanæ & eius cum Deo colloquium parabolicum esse: sed obscuriori & mirabiliori modo quàm vulgò parabolæ sint. 5. Nomen Huts esse 1. nomen proprium ut Gen.22.21. 2. esse imperativum verbi עוץ ut Iesai. 8.10. Quasi Spiritus Sanctus indigitasset הסתכל בזאת העצה והתבונן בו והעלה בידך עניינו והבינים ורא הרעות האמתיות מן Considera hoc consilium (Dei) & illud perpende, ut sum eius tibi applica, vrue ex eo scientiam veram. 6. In historia filiorum Dei non dicitur, & venerunt filii Dei & Satan ut adstarent coram Deo לפני יהוה האלהים ואתו השטן Ita enim videri potuisset ac si omnium una eademque fuisset ratio. Sed dicitur, Et venerunt filii Dei, ut adstarent coram Domino & venit etiam Satan in medio eorum. Hæc enim loquendi ratio dicitur tantùm de eo שבא בלתי מכון ולא מבוקש Qui non petitus & non rogatus venit, sed qui venientibus illis qui rogati sunt se ingerit &c. Reliqua quæ ex Orientalium scriptis de Iobo referri possent recensuit Clariff. Spanhemius in Hist. Iobi.
units.tr: Job. Maimonides wrote almost an entire chapter about him in More Nevochim III, 22. (1) He says the history of Job is wonderful, and an example for explaining people's opinions about providence. (2) It is the view of some that Job never existed, but that everything is a parable. (3) Those who believe Job really existed do not know the place or the time when that history happened. Some say he lived in the time of the patriarchs, others that he existed in the days of Moses or of David, others think he was one of those from Babylon who came up (from Babylon) (מעולים מכבל). This diversity of opinions makes most people confirmed in their view that he never existed. (4) Whether or not Job existed, that appearance of Satan and his conversation with God is certainly a parable, but in a more obscure and wonderful manner than parables usually are. (5) The name Huts is either (1) a proper name, as in Genesis 22:21, or (2) the imperative of the verb עוץ, as in Isaiah 8:10, as if the Holy Spirit had said: Consider this counsel (of God) and weigh it, apply its meaning to yourself, and from it draw true knowledge (הסתכל בזאת העצה והתבונן בו והעלה בידך עניינו והבינם ורא הרעות האמתיות מן). (6) In the history of the sons of God it is not said, and the sons of God came and Satan came to stand before God (לפני יהוה האלהים ואתו השטן), for that would seem to imply that all had one and the same reason. But it is said, And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord, and Satan also came among them. For this manner of speaking is used only of him who came not summoned and not asked, but who, while the others were called, thrust himself in (שבא בלתי מכון ולא מבוקש). Clarius Spanheim, in Historia Iobi, has listed the rest of what could be related about Job from Oriental writings.

units.la: IOHANNES Baptista natus est Hebrone, civitate Aaronitica, in montano Iudæ Iosuæ xxi. 2. Luc.15. Vtroque parente Aaronita. In Eremo, id est in montano Iudæ iuventutem transe- git ut vir privatus, non ut eremita sed in opifi-
units.tr: John the Baptist was born at Hebron, an Aaronite city in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 21:2; Luke 1). Both parents were Aaronites. He spent his youth in the wilderness, that is, in the hill country of Judah, as a private man and not as a hermit, but busy with some trade or study, and he took on no austerity for himself, except a Nazirite vow before the thirtieth year of his age. See Eremum.

units.la: cio aliquo aut studio versatus, nec quidquam austeritatis sibi aflumens, præter N.firæatum ante annum ætatis tricesimum. Vid. Eremum.
units.tr: On the trade or study, see above; the rest of this unit is as in [4].

units.la: §. Iohannes Baptista non habuit votum de carne non comedenda, aliàs nec locustas comedere potuisset, fecundùm Canonem in Hierof. Nedarim sol.40 2. הנודר מן הבשר יהא אסור : בכשר דגים וחגבים Qui voto se obligat de carne (non comedenda) in erdicatur carne piscium & locustarum. Illi boni homines nondum tantùm in natura profecerant, ut potuissent scire piscium venis inesse sanguinem frigidum, & proinde inter carnis species non numerandos, ut nudipedes & cucullati hodierni fratres!
units.tr: John the Baptist was not bound by a vow not to eat meat; otherwise he could not have eaten locusts either, according to the canon in the Jerusalem Talmud, Nedarim, folio 40, column 2: "Whoever binds himself by vow not to eat meat is forbidden fish and locusts" (הנודר מן הבשר יהא אסור בכשר דגים וחגבים). Whoever binds himself by vow to abstain from meat is forbidden meat of fish and locusts. Those good men had not yet advanced so far in natural knowledge as to know that fish have cold blood, and so are not counted among the kinds of meat, like the barefoot and hooded brothers of today!

units.la: Iohannes Ben Saccai fuit R. Simeonis, Hillelis filii coætaneus & cum ipso Cabbalam accepit Abhot c.2. Vixit 120. annos sicuti Moses, per 40. annos se exercuit in Pragmatica, Quadraginta annos alios singulari diligentia ad studia adhibuit, & per quadraginta annos docuit: nec ad principatum venit nisi sub finem vitæ eius; Rofch Hafchana folio 20. 2. Iuchasin folio 20. 2.
units.tr: John ben Zakkai was a contemporary of Rabbi Simeon, son of Hillel, and received the Cabbalah along with him (Avot c. 2). He lived 120 years, like Moses; for forty years he occupied himself with practical affairs, for another forty years he applied himself with singular diligence to study, and for forty years he taught. He did not come to the leadership until near the end of his life (Rosh Hashanah, folio 20, column 2; Yuchasin, folio 20, column 2).

units.la: §. Principatum gessit in Iabhnè, quo excisis laribus Synedrium se contulit, sed non nisi veniâ primò à Tito Imperatore impetrata. Avot R.Nathan cap.4. Iuchasin ipsius præsidiatui tribuit annos duos, Zemach David verò quinq;. Quadraginta ante vastatum templum annis, cùm eius portæ sponte se aperuissent, desolationem eius prædixit. Hierof. Ioma f.43.3. Quomodo populum in magna ætate sub umbra templi docuerit, reperies in Pesachin f.26.1.
units.tr: He held the leadership at Jabneh, and when the houses had been destroyed he moved the Sanhedrin there, but only after first obtaining permission from the Emperor Titus (Avot de Rabbi Nathan c. 4). Yuchasin assigns two years to his presidency, but Zemach David assigns five. Forty years before the temple was destroyed, when its gates opened of their own accord, he foretold its desolation (Jerusalem Talmud, Yoma, folio 43, column 3). How he taught the people in his great old age under the shadow of the temple, you will find in Pesachim, folio 26, column 1.

units.la: §. Cùm Vespasianus Hierosolymas obsidione cingeret, prædixit ipsi R. Iochanan in feretro tanquam mortuus extra Hierosolymas delatus, quod Imperator futurus esset. Historiam reperies in Gittin sol. 56. 1. & Echa Rabbeti sol. 64. 2. Fuit deinde etiam in castris Titi, & ab ipso multo favore & benignitate accumulatus; sed cùm tandem lethali morbo decumberet, admodum animi eius fortitudo elanguit, ita ut tremebundus de salute sua expiraverit. Bab. Beracot. sol. 28. 2. Et certè quæ spes supererat homini Pharisaico operibus suis confidenti, postquàm templum devastatum erat, lares excisi, Christus quidem ab ipso visus, sed non fide receptus!
units.tr: When Vespasian was besieging Jerusalem, Rabbi Yochanan, carried out of Jerusalem on a bier as though dead, foretold to him that he would become emperor. You will find the story in Gittin, folio 56, column 1, and Eicha Rabbati, folio 64, column 2. He was then also in the camp of Titus and was loaded with great favour and kindness by him. But when at last he lay down with a deadly sickness, the strength of his spirit wilted altogether, so that he expired trembling for his salvation (Babylonian Berakhot, folio 28, column 2). And surely what hope remained for a Pharisaic man confident in his works, after the temple was laid waste and the houses destroyed, when Christ indeed was seen by him, but not received in faith!

units.la: Iohanna filia Retibi fuit vidua quædam præstigiatrix, quæ cùm mulierum appropinquaret pariendi tempus, magicis artibus parturientis uterum occludebat, ut parere non posset. Cumque diu puerpera cruciatibus laboraret, dicebat illa, ibo ego & pro te supplicabo; profecta verò solvebat præstigias, & illicò nascebatur infans, tandem artes eius patefactæ fuerunt. Sotah c. 3. 4. in Gloss. ad Gemaram.
units.tr: Johanna, daughter of Retibus, was a certain widow and sorceress who, when women drew near the time of giving birth, would close the womb of the woman in labour by magic arts so that she could not bring forth. And when the woman in childbed had suffered long in agony, she would say, "I will go and pray for you"; but when she had gone, she would undo her spells, and the infant was immediately born. At last her arts were brought to light (Sotah c. 3, 4; in the Gloss. on the Gemara).

units.la: יום הכניסו Iom haccenifa In cap. 1. Megillah & alibi est dies secundus & quintus septimanæ in quibus legere possunt, nam in Sabbatho מגילות legere non licet.
units.tr: Iom haccenifa (יום הכניסו). In chapter 1 of Megillah and elsewhere it means the second and fifth days of the week, on which they may read; for on the Sabbath it is not permitted to read the Megillot.

units.la: Ionam R. Salomoh in Jon. 2. in ventre Ceti e mari Phœnicao ducit in mare rubrum, quâ arte dissicile videre est, nisi forte eadem ratione quâ Hierosolymitani in Taanith sol. 69. 2. Septi genera genera piscium mundorum migrasse dicunt cum
units.tr: R. Solomon leads Jonah in Jon. 2., in the belly of the whale from the Phoenician sea into the Red Sea. By what method this is done is hard to see, unless perhaps by the same reasoning by which the Jerusalemites in Taanith fol. 69. 2. say that the seven kinds of clean fish migrated with Israel

units.la: Israele in Babylonem. Et quando ab ipsis illius migrationis modus petitur, respondent דיך תהום גלו Per viam profundi migrarunt, & per viam profundi redierunt.
units.tr: into Babylon. And when they are asked how that migration was made, they answer: they went into exile by the way of the deep [דיך תהום גלו], and by the way of the deep they returned.

units.la: §. Ionas patriam habuit את החפר Gath Hachofer. Non probabile est illum aliam praeter quàm in Ninivitas habuisse prophetiam: Nam quamvis videatur ex libro Regum concludi posse ipsum etiam in Ieroboamum prophetasse, tamen secundùm Kimchium verba illa, sicuti Dixit Iehova per servum suum Ionam &c. Sic explicari possunt; Sicuti Prophetia cessit in bonum ex malo Ninevitis, ita tempore Ieroboam prophetia quoque cessit מרע לטובה ex malo in bonum. Ionas noluit primitus Ninivitis praedicare, שתבע ככוד הבן ולא תבע ככוד האב quia praculit & quasivit gloriam filii [populi Israelis,] non autem gloriam patris, [Dei.] Sic enim cogitabat, Ninivitae qui gentiles, sunt conversioni proximi, Israel verò cui singulis diebus concionantur Prophetae non resipiscit; si itaque illuc irem maximum contraheret probrum. Kimchi & Aben Esra, in Ionam c.1. Ratio cur fugerit Ionas מלפני à coram Domino [è terra Israelitica, quae illo termino designantur,] est, quia secundùm communem traditionem credidit השכינה gratiosam Dei praesentiam & prophetiam extra terram Israeliticam non habitare, & proinde Deum ipsum ibi non alloquuturum. Sic commentantur omnes. Notat insuper Kimchi ipsum omnem dedisse navis mercedem, ut eò expeditiùs fugere posset, ne exspectatione mercatorum fuga eius retardaretur:
units.tr: §. Jonah had his homeland at Gath Hachepher [את החפר]. It is not probable that he had any prophecy other than that to the Ninevites. For although it may seem to follow from the book of Kings that he also prophesied against Jeroboam, yet according to Kimchi those words, as the LORD spoke by his servant Jonah, can be explained thus: just as the prophecy turned out for good, from evil, for the Ninevites, so in the time of Jeroboam the prophecy also turned from evil into good [מרע לטובה]. Jonah at first did not want to preach to the Ninevites, because he sought and asked for the glory of the son [of the people of Israel], and not the glory of the father [of God]. For he reasoned thus: the Ninevites, who are Gentiles, are close to conversion, but Israel, to whom the prophets preach every day, does not repent; so if he went there he would incur the greatest disgrace. Kimchi and Aben Ezra, on Jonah ch. 1. The reason why Jonah fled from before the LORD [from the land of Israel, which those terms designate] is that, according to common tradition, he believed that the gracious presence of God [השכינה] and prophecy do not dwell outside the land of Israel, and that therefore God would not speak to him there. All commentators say this. Kimchi further notes that he paid the whole fare of the ship, so that he might flee the more quickly and his flight not be delayed by waiting for merchants.

units.la: & hoc mirandum non esse, quia receptus est Canon traditionis ; Prophetiam שאן נביא non habitare nisi in viris divitibus. Lubet hic quoque aliquas in Iona prophetiam commentationes annotare.
units.tr: And this is not to be wondered at, because the canon of tradition is received: prophecy [שאן נביא] does not dwell except in rich men. It pleases me here also to note some commentaries on prophecy in Jonah.

units.la: Cap.I.v.5. R. Sal. textus dicit, inclamarunt unusquisque Deum suum. Quia ibi è septuaginta populis nautæ & vectores erant.
units.tr: Ch. 1, v. 5. R. Solomon: the text says, each cried to his own God. This is because there the sailors and passengers were from the seventy peoples.

units.la: אל ירכתי ad latera; idem est ac si diceret ad unum ex lateribus, sic aliquis dicitur sepultus בערי גלעד in Urbibus Gilead, cùm tamen solùm in una sepeliri potuit. D. Kimchi.
units.tr: To the sides [אל ירכתי]: this is the same as if it said to one of the sides. Thus someone is said to be buried in the cities of Gilead [בערי גלעד], although he could be buried in only one of them. D. Kimchi.

units.la: V.7. Ratio cur ad sortem projiciendam se accinxerint, est, quia reliquas naves videbant in salvo esse, & pacatè suum cursum prosequi, & proindè cogitarunt, aliquem inter ipsos esse, propter cuius peccatum soli periclitarentur. R. S. Iarchi.
units.tr: V. 7. The reason why they prepared themselves to cast lots is that they saw the other ships were safe and continuing their course in peace, and so they thought that someone among them was the cause, on account of whose sin they alone were in danger. R. S. Iarchi.

units.la: V.8. Quaest ars tua? i.e. cuius iniquitatis reus es, forsan Ars tua est מלאכת רמאות est ars fraudum & rapinæ. Propter quam tu reus factus es. Vnde venis? i.e. forsan tu fugisti inde propter scelus quod commisisti : Forsan populus ex quo es, sunt impii, & quos Deus excindere vult. R.D.K.
units.tr: V. 8. What is your business? That is, of what wickedness are you guilty? Perhaps your business is a business of deceit and robbery [מלאכת רמאות], on account of which you have become guilty. Whence do you come? That is, perhaps you fled from there because of a crime you committed; perhaps the people you come from are wicked, and God wishes to cut them off. R.D.K.

units.la: V.9. R.D.K. Quando dicit Hebraeus sum, respondet ipsis ad duo, scil. ex qua regione & populo sit; verbis autem se timere Deum respondet ad quæstionem quam habeat artem. Insuper expresse meminit Deum aridam & mare fuisse, ut nautas aliquâ ratione erigeret, cogitatione, quòd Deus mare fecerit, & proinde quòd eius fluctus quoque facilè compescere possit.
units.tr: V. 9. R.D.K. When he says I am a Hebrew, he answers them on two points, namely from what region and people he is; but by the words that he fears God he answers the question what his business is. Moreover, he expressly mentions that God made the dry land and the sea, so as to raise up the sailors by some reasoning: since God made the sea, he can also easily calm its waves.

units.la: V. 16. R.D.K. dicitur ipsos sacrificasse, non quasi in ipsa navi sacrificaverint, sed quod sacrificia promiserint, ea soluturi postquam ad portum pervenissent. Per vota intelligitur reliquum quod à Sacrificantibus fieri debuit; ut Eleemosyna pro pauperibus.
units.tr: V. 16. R.D.K. It is said that they sacrificed, not as if they had sacrificed on the ship itself, but that they promised sacrifices, which they would pay once they had reached port. By vows is understood what remained to be done by those offering sacrifices, such as alms for the poor.

units.la: Cap. II. דגה Est nomen quòd fœmellæ & masculo tribuitur. Kimchi. R.Salom. dicitur in v.1.7. & in v.2. דגה, quia Deus primitus præparaverat piscem masculum ut ipsum è navi proiectum devoraret; sed cum Ionas in illo esset דגה in lato & libero spatio de oratione & precibus nihil cogitavit. Fecit Deus ut piscis masculus Ionam ejiceret in os piscis fœmellæ, in cuius intestinis in spatio admodum iniquo & ob fœmellæ graviditatem angusto, coactus fuit animum ad preces applicare: & idcircò textus dicit, è visceribus הדגה illius piscis. Kimchi notat magnum miraculum fuisse quòd Ionas per tres dies & noctes fuerit in ventre ceti, sed adhuc maius quòd non obstupuerit, & quòd ad Deum adhuc mentem suam componere potuerit.
units.tr: Ch. II. Dag [דגה] is a noun applied to both female and male. Kimchi. R. Solomon: it is said in v. 1, 7 and in v. 2 dag [דגה], because God had at first prepared a male fish to swallow him once he had been thrown from the ship; but when Jonah was in it, in a broad and free space, he thought of nothing of prayer and supplication. God caused the male fish to cast Jonah into the mouth of a female fish, in whose intestines, in a very confined space, narrowed also by the female's pregnancy, he was forced to turn his mind to prayer; and therefore the text says from the bowels of that fish [הדגה]. Kimchi notes that it was a great miracle that Jonah remained for three days and nights in the belly of the whale, but a greater one that he was not stunned and could still direct his mind to God.

units.la: V.3. Et exaudivisti vocem meam. D.Kimchi. Postquam Ionas vidit se in illo ventre & angustiis tamdiu in vita mansisse, de salute sua bene sperare incepit, & quod illinc mox liberandus esset.
units.tr: V. 3. And you heard my voice. D. Kimchi. After Jonah saw that he had remained alive for so long in that belly and in such distress, he began to hope well for his own safety, and that he would soon be set free from there.

units.la: V.4. יסובבני נחר Fluvius circumdedit me &c. Aben Esra notat Ionam in mare proiectum fuisse. בתחנכו' הים עם הנהר in Ostio Euphratis, (quem Hebraei καr' ἐξοχὴν נהר nominant) & ita in coniunctione eius cum mari: & proinde Ionam per mare, fluvium Euphratem intellexisse.
units.tr: V. 4. The river surrounded me [יסובבני נחר], etc. Aben Ezra notes that Jonah was cast into the sea at the mouth of the Euphrates (which the Hebrews call the River [נהר] par excellence), and so at its junction with the sea; and therefore by river he understood the Euphrates, through the sea.

units.la: V. 6. סוף חכוש לראשי Alga alligata est ca iti meo. Hic R. Sal. ut supra diximus, vult, mare illud fuisse Mare rubrum, quia mentio fit algae, & Deum Ionae ostendisse viam illam quam Israelitae tenuerunt dum illuc transfibant, oculos ceti Ionae fuisse tanquam חלונות fenestras, per quas ubi esset speculari potuit; quod ille parum Phycè. Kimchi dicit, algam etiam in fluminibus & alio mari reperiri, nec proinde necessario mare algosum hic intelligendum: illos vero qui in illa sunt sententia ad tollendam difficultatem ponere: כיים סוף נכנס בים יאו Quod mare rubrum aliquam cum mari Iapho communicationem habeat.
units.tr: V. 6. The weed was wrapped around my head [סוף חבוש לראשי]. Here R. Solomon, as we said above, holds that this sea was the Red Sea, since mention is made of weed, and God showed Jonah the way that the Israelites took when they crossed there; the eyes of Jonah's whale were like windows [חלונות] through which he could look out wherever he was. This, he little... Kimchi says that weed is also found in rivers and in other seas, and so it is not necessary to understand a weedy sea here; but those who hold this view, to remove the difficulty, assume that the Red Sea has some communication with the Sea of Joppa [כיום סוף נכנס בים יאפו].

units.la: V. 9. Kimchi ex Capit. Rab. Eliezeri plane aliam expositionem habet, quam nostra Lat. versio. Postquam, inquit, nautae Niniven appulsi viderunt omnia miracula quae Deus fecit cum Iona, unusquisque Deum suum proiecit in mare, sicuti scriptum est משמרי הבלי שוא חסרם יעזובו Qui observabant vanitates mendaces, opprobrium suum reliquerunt. Et Iapho reversi ascenderunt Hierosolymam, & se circumciderunt, sicuti dicitur, & timuerunt viri illi timore magno, & sacrificarunt sacrificia, quae erant sanguis sua circumcisionis. Et voverunt se & liberos & uxores ad conversionem ductuos.
units.tr: V. 9. Kimchi, from Chapter of Rabbi Eliezer, has an explanation quite different from our Latin version. After the sailors, he says, landed at Nineveh and saw all the miracles that God did with Jonah, each one threw his God into the sea, as it is written [משמרי הבלי שוא חסדם יעזובו] those who observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy. And they returned to Joppa and went up to Jerusalem, and circumcised themselves, as it is said, and those men feared with great fear, and offered sacrifices, which were the blood of their circumcision. And they vowed themselves and their children and their wives to conversion.

units.la: V. 10. Et dixit Iehova &c. Kimchi, non quasi Deus externo sermone piscem alloquutus sit, sed, sed העיר את רצונו excitavit solùm voluntatem eius ad Ionam eiaculandum.
units.tr: V. 10. And the LORD spoke, etc. Kimchi: not as if God addressed the fish with an external speech, but he only stirred up his will to cast Jonah out.

units.la: Cap. III. v. 3. Ninive autem erat עיר גדולה לאלהים Vrbs magna Deo &c. Si Sacer textus alicuius rei vult indicare magnitudinem in usu habet adiungere אל Deum, ut הרי אלהים Montes Dei, pro montibus altissimis. Kimchi.
units.tr: Ch. III, v. 3. Now Nineveh was a great city to God [עיר גדולה לאלהים], etc. If Scripture wishes to indicate the greatness of something, it has the habit of adding God [אל], as mountains of God [הרי אלהים] for very high mountains. Kimchi.

units.la: V. 4. Ninive subvertetur &c. instar Sodomæ & Gomorrhæ, quarum incolis, suis peccatis similes facti erant. K.
units.tr: V. 4. Nineveh shall be overthrown, etc., like Sodom and Gomorrah, whose inhabitants had become like them in their sins. K.

units.la: V. 5. (rediderunt &c. Erant enim Ninive nautæ qui Ionam præcipitaverant in mare, & qui ipsis totam recensebant historiam : quod fecit ut Prophetiæ eius citiùs fides adhibita. K.
units.tr: V. 5. They believed, etc. For the Ninevites were the sailors who had thrown Jonah into the sea, and they related to them the whole story; which made them more quickly believe his prophecy. K.

units.la: V. 10. Et pænituit Deum &c. Decreta Dei in hoc casu sunt conditionata, si homines non resipiscant, quare factâ resipiscentiâ etiam mutantur. K.
units.tr: V. 10. And God repented, etc. The decrees of God in this case are conditional, that is, if men do not repent; therefore, when repentance has taken place, they are also changed. K.

units.la: Cap. IV. v. 1. quæritur quomodo Ionas sciverit Deum nolle Ninivitas exscindere, cùm tamen 40. dies nondum præteriissent ? Kimchi, Deum hoc ipsi per spiritum Prophetiæ significasse. Accensa autem est Ira eius propter Israelem cui semper Prophetæ concionabantur absq; ullo fructu. Idem. Vel ut R. Sal. gentes porrò dicent me esse Prophetam Mendacem.
units.tr: Chapter 4, verse 1: the question is how Jonah knew that God was unwilling to destroy the Ninevites, since the forty days had not yet passed. Kimchi answers that God indicated this to him by the spirit of prophecy. His anger was kindled because of Israel, to whom the prophets always preached without any fruit. Idem. Or, as R. Sal. has it, the nations will say that I am a lying prophet.

units.la: V. 6. קיקיון est planta cuius folia sunt magna, & quæ Vmbram præbent : illius etiam fit mentio in Mischna vid. Oleum, nam ex fructu & granis eius conficiebant Oleum. Arabicè illam vocant אלכרוע. Kimchi.
units.tr: Chapter 4, verse 6: קיקיון [qiqayon] is a plant with large leaves that give shade. It is also mentioned in the Mishnah; see Oleum, for oil was made from its fruit and seeds. In Arabic they call it alkharua. Kimchi.

units.la: Iosua fil. Perachiæ cum Rex Alexander (vel Iannai) sapientes interficeret Alexandriam Ægypti commune Iudæorum receptaculum autugit. Sed hoc turbine sedato, iterum in gratiam Regis rediit, & à Simeone Ben Schetah tali epistola domum revocatus fuit עיר ירושלם מני הקדושה ליכי אליכסנדריא של מצרים בעלי שרוי A me Ierusalem civitate Sancta tibi Alexandriæ in Ægypto (salutem) Maritus meus apud te habitat, dum ego interea sedeo sola. Iuchasin f.18.2.
units.tr: Joshua son of Perachiah, when King Alexander (or Jannai) was putting the wise men to death, fled to Alexandria in Egypt, the common refuge of the Jews. But when the storm had calmed, he returned to the king's favour, and was brought home by a letter from Simeon ben Shetach: From me, Jerusalem, the holy city, to you, Alexandria in Egypt: peace. My husband dwells with you, while I sit alone. [עיר ירושלם מני הקדושה ליכי אליכסנדריא של מצרים בעלי שרוי] Iuchasin f. 18.2.

units.la: §. Iudæi hunc Ioluam fil. Perachiæ D.N.I. Christi præceptorem faciunt, & volunt Christum se illi comitem in Ægypto petenda præbuisse Bab. Sanhed. sol.107. 2. Sed certè Parachronismum committunt, nec consentiunt ipsi in sua Chronologia, nam secundum Zemach David Alexander potitus est imperio anno mundi 3660. R. Iosua filius Perachiæ verò in Ægyptum fugit anno 3560. quâ ratione non solùm tempora turbant, sed etiam Dominum nostrum Centenarium facere debent. Taceo æræ nostræ anticipationem, quæ nativitatem Christi fermè ad Pompeii tempora rejicit.
units.tr: The Jews make this Joshua son of Perachiah the teacher of our Lord Jesus Christ, and they want Christ to have accompanied him into Egypt. Bab. Sanhed. fol. 107. 2. But they certainly commit an anachronism, and they do not agree with themselves in their own chronology. For according to Zemach David, Alexander obtained the kingdom in the year of the world 3660, while R. Joshua son of Perachiah fled into Egypt in the year 3560. By this reckoning they not only confuse the times but must also make our Lord a centenarian. I say nothing of the anticipation of our era, which pushes the birth of Christ back almost to the time of Pompey.

units.la: IosES Ben Ioëser & Iosephfil. Iohannis floruerunt anno 3500. & in illorum temporibus inceperunt הוגות paria virorum illorum, quorum prior semper fuit princeps senatus, alter verò secundus à principe. Iuchasin p.18.1. R. Iose fuit è צרדה de qua 1.Reg.11.26. & pessimos filios habuit. Secundùm ipsum consituenda est הלכה fi aliqua inter magistros est disceptatio. Hal.Olam p.201. Cum ipso etiam cessarunt Botri sive איש כל בו Viri illi præstantes in quibus omnes tum eruditionis cum virtutis cumuli erant.
units.tr: Jose ben Joezer and Jose ben Johanan flourished in the year 3500, and in their times the pairs (zugot) of those men began; the first of each pair was always the prince of the senate, the second was the deputy of the prince. Iuchasin p. 18.1. R. Jose was from Zeredah, of which see 1 Kings 11:26, and he had very wicked sons. According to him, a halakah is to be settled if there is any dispute among the teachers. Hal. Olam p. 201. With him also ceased the Botri, or איש כל בו [ish kol bo], those outstanding men in whom were heaped all the learning and virtue of that time.

units.la: Voluit R. Iofes Chephara Elecmosynarios constituere, sed nemo erat qui munus suscipere voluisset. Hieros. Peah sol.21.1. Amabat imò deperibat R.Iofe. R. Chaia Rubba, & ut ipsum videre posset ieiunavit octoginta ieiunia. Hieros.Kilaim 32.2. Perduxit suos dies R.Iofe dies suos usque ad tempus Iannai Regis, & interfectus est à Græcis. Zemach David. pag.70.
units.tr: R. Jose Chephara wished to appoint almoners, but there was no one willing to accept the office. Hieros. Peah fol. 21.1. Indeed R. Jose loved and doted on R. Chaia Rubba, and so that he might see him he fasted eighty fasts. Hieros. Kilaim 32.2. R. Jose spent his days until the time of King Jannai, and was killed by the Greeks. Zemach David p. 70.

units.la: Iordanes è spelunca Vanneadis oritur, & fluit in mare, ita lacum vocant Sibhchæum, Bava Batra sol.74.2. Non magnam habuit latitudinem, nam aliquando flamma incendii in hac Iordanis ripa accensa ad aliam transiit. Quousque autem fertur flamma? R. Eleazar dicit ut plurimum ad sedecim cubitos, at ferente vento ad triginta. R. Iehuda dicit ad cubitos triginta & spirante vento ad quinquaginta. R. Akibha ad 100. Hieros.Baua Kama sol.5.3. De Iordane vid. Mapparum erroris.
units.tr: The Jordan rises from the cave of Vanneas and flows into the sea; they call the lake Sibhchaeum. Bava Batra fol. 74.2. It did not have a great width, for once the flame of a fire kindled on one bank of the Jordan passed over to the other. How far, however, is it said that the flame would reach? R. Eleazar says usually sixteen cubits, but with the wind blowing, thirty. R. Jehudah says thirty cubits, and with the wind blowing, fifty. R. Akiba says a hundred. Hieros. Baba Kama fol. 5.3. On the Jordan see Mapparum erroris.

units.la: §. In Iordane erexit Iosua lapides, super quos steterunt Abba Chalaphta, & Eleafar Ben Mathia, atque eos æstimarunt unumquemque ponderis quadraginta Satorum. Bab.Sotah 34.2. Tosaphr. c.8.
units.tr: In the Jordan Joshua set up stones, on which stood Abba Chalaphta and Eleazar ben Mathia, and they estimated each one at forty seahs of weight. Bab. Sotah 34.2. Tosaphot ch. 8.

units.la: §. Iordanica Scapha immunda æstimatur, quia eam fructibus implent & deducunt à mari in aridam, & ab arida in mare. Hieros. Schabbat f.7.1.
units.tr: A boat on the Jordan is considered unclean, because they fill it with fruits and carry them from the sea to the dry land, and from the dry land to the sea. Hieros. Shabbat fol. 7.1.

units.la: §. Beraeot sol 55.1. Dicit Rabbah verbis R. Iochanan אין ידין אלא מנית יריחו ולמטה Non est Iordanes nisi intus ab Hierichunte & infra; Glossator unus secundum literam hoc effatum intelligit, & proinde inquit, si quis voverit se non bibiturum ex aqua Iordanis, ex illis tamen bibere potest supra Ierichunta, quia scilicet ibi Iordanes non amplius Iordanes æstimatur. Alius vero hæc intelligit de Iordane terræ Israeliticæ adiacente, & quidem infra Hierichunta solùm.
units.tr: Berachot fol. 55.1. Rabbah says, in the words of R. Johanan: אין ידין אלא מנית יריחו ולמטה [ein yardin ela minit Yericho ulmatah], that is, the Jordan is only from Jericho downward. One commentator takes this saying literally, and therefore says: if someone has vowed not to drink from the water of the Jordan, he may nevertheless drink from it above Jericho, because there the Jordan is no longer considered the Jordan. Another, however, understands this of the part of the Jordan that borders the land of Israel, and indeed only below Jericho.

units.la: ISCARIOT. Illud nomen duplicem originem habere potest; 1. ut denotat Iudam cum cinctorio. Germ. Judas mit dem Gürtel. Nam קוריטיאו vel אסקוריטאס secundùm Gloss.& Gem. in Bab. Nedarim sol. 55. 2. indumentum est Coriaceum, vel Cinctorium coriaceum indutum à Coriariis supra vestes suas. Forsan enim antequàm discipulus factus esset, exercuit artem Coriarii; Simonem certè quendam legimus Coriarium Act. ix. 43. Atque hunc Iudam filium Simonis Ioan. xii. 14. Aut quamvis Coriarius non fuerit, tamen poterit Iudas אסקריוטס cum Cinctorio vocari, si observaverimus Iudam fuisse gestatorem glossocomi, Iudæos verò in eiusmodi cinctoriis confutas habuisse crumenas, & in illis suos nummos circumgestasse, sicuti docet Aruch in vocibus אמנור & תרפיי. Ita ut hoc sensu Iudas Iscariotes idem sit ac Germ. Judas mit dem Geltsak. Et Gall. Judas le boursier.
units.tr: ISCARIOT. This name can have a twofold origin. 1. It may denote Judas with the girdle (German: Judas mit dem Gürtel). For according to the Gloss and the Gemara in Bab. Nedarim fol. 55. 2, the word קוריטיאו or אסקוריטאס [koriṭiau or askoriṭas] means a leather garment, or a leather girdle worn by tanners over their clothes. Perhaps before he became a disciple, Judas practised the trade of a tanner; we certainly read of a certain Simon the tanner, Acts 9:43, and this Judas was the son of Simon, John 12:4. Or, even if he was not a tanner, Judas could still be called Iscariot, with the girdle, if we observe that Judas carried the money-box, and that the Jews had purses in such girdles, carrying their coins about in them, as Aruch teaches under the words אמנור and תרפיי. So in this sense Judas Iscariot would be the same as German Judas mit dem Geltsack (Judas with the money-bag), and French Judas le boursier (Judas the purse-bearer).

units.la: 1. Iscariot potest derivari ab אסכרא angina, ita ut hoc tituli ipsi post mortem tanquam stigma inustum fuerit. אסכרא enim secundùm Bab. Beracot sol. 8. 1. est asperrima mors inter omnia genera mortis, & à Gloss. vernaculè redditur strangulament. Sive nunc Iudas proprio suspendio se strangulaverit, sive à Diabolo strangulatus disruptus fuerit, (quod probabilius est, & magis correspondet verbis Petri Act. 1. 18. ἀρηνὴς χωρίον non mirum est si nomini eius inureretur hæc mortis infamia, ut vulgò diceretur Iudas Iscariotes, quasi Iudas ille, qui periit מכסא à strangulatione. Germ. Der von dem Teuffel erwurgte Judas.
units.tr: 1. Iscariot may be derived from אסכרא [askara], quinsy, so that this title would have been branded on him after his death like a stigma. For according to Bab. Berachot fol. 8.1, אסכרא is the most harsh death of all kinds of death, and the Gloss renders it in the vernacular as strangulation. Whether Judas hanged himself, or whether he was strangled by the devil and burst open (which is more probable, and better agrees with Peter's words, Acts 1:18: the field of blood), it is no wonder if this infamy of death was stamped on his name, so that he was commonly called Judas Iscariot, as if to say that Judas who perished מכסא [makhsa] by strangulation. German: Der von dem Teufel erwürgte Judas (Judas strangled by the devil).

units.la: §. De Iuda Iscariot vid. Osculum. vid.etiam Proditor.
units.tr: On Judas Iscariot see Osculum. See also Proditor.

units.la: IUBILÆUM יובל & annus septimus instituta sunt, partim propter Misericordiam erga homines omnes in universum, illorumque refocillationem & ut terra ita relicta eò uberiores fructus proferat: partim in specie in gratiam servorum & pauperum, in remissione argenti & manumissione servorum; partim ad perpetuam familiarum conservationem, facultates enim tunc ad hæredes & dominos ipsarum iterum redibant. More Nevoch. iii. 29.
units.tr: The Jubilee, יובל [yovel], and the seventh year were instituted partly out of mercy towards all men in general, for their refreshment, and so that the land, thus left fallow, might bring forth more abundant fruit; partly in particular for the benefit of servants and the poor, in the remission of debts and the manumission of slaves; and partly for the lasting preservation of families, for their property then returned again to their heirs and owners. More Nevochim iii. 29.

units.la: §. Qui in anno Iubilæo, arat, fodit, fundi maioris utilitatis causâ, item qui insitionem facit arborum, aut eos plantat, percutitur מכה percussione rebellionis (V. flagellationem,)ut & ille qui arbores à verrucis, vermibus & ramis siccis purgat, aut aliud quid facit, quod ad maiorem ipsarum utilitatem conducit. Licet tamen agri partem siccitate laborantem irrigare, arbores in prædiis, & vineas factis fossis aquâ refocillare, ne arbores & vineæ exarescant & ita pereant.
units.tr: In the Jubilee year whoever ploughs or digs for the greater usefulness of the land, likewise whoever grafts trees or plants them, is struck with the מכה [makkah], a stroke of rebellion (that is, a flogging), and so too is he who cleans trees of warts, worms and dry branches, or does anything else that serves their greater usefulness. It is nevertheless permitted to water the part of a field that suffers from drought, and to refresh trees on estates and vines by digging ditches with water, so that the trees and vines do not dry up and so perish.

units.la: § Postquàm Reges extranei Israelitis præter alia onera etiam imposuerunt exercitus suos nutrire, licèt anno septimo seminare quantum ad hoc requiritur. Extra eiusmodi casus si quis per errorem vel ex intentione in anno septimo aut Iubilæo(quorum jura fermè æqualia sunt) seminaverit, aut plantaverit, illud iterum evellere & eradicare debet.
units.tr: When foreign kings, besides other burdens, also imposed on the Israelites the duty of feeding their armies, it is allowed to sow in the seventh year as far as this requirement demands. Outside such cases, if anyone in the seventh year or the Jubilee (whose laws are nearly equal) sows or plants, whether by mistake or on purpose, he must pull it up again and root it out.

units.la: §. Ab initio simpliciter constitutum erat, ut quivis ligna, herbas, ex agro suo legere posset, sed solùm obiter, in alius agro verò etiam accuratè, sed postquàm multiplicati fuerunt transgressores, constituerunt, ut nemo amplius ex proprio agro colligeret, ex proximi verò non nui obiter, ne dicere possit se illius agrum purgasse. Maymon. Hal. Schemita vejobel. c.1.
units.tr: From the beginning it was simply laid down that anyone could gather wood and herbs from his own field, but only in passing; in another's field, however, he could gather them even thoroughly. But after transgressors multiplied, it was decided that no one should gather anything any longer from his own field, and from his neighbour's only in passing, lest he be able to say that he had cleaned his neighbour's field. Maimonides, Hilchot Shemitah ve-Yovel ch. 1.

units.la: §. In tribus diebus ultimis anni sexti terram colere non licet, quia tunc ad annum septimum iam præparata & destinata videtur. Ibid. c.2.
units.tr: §. In the last three days of the sixth year it is not permitted to till the ground, because by then the land is considered already prepared and set aside for the seventh year. Ibid. c.2.

units.la: §. Omnia quæ crescunt in anno septimo, sive crescant ex semine iam anno sexto sparso, sive ex radicibus succisis vocantur שמיטה; Ea ad esum ex lege licita sunt, sed non debent eo modo aut abscindi aut colligi quo vulgò fit, sed obiter & paulatim &c. Scribarum verò constitutionibus ea comedere non licet, ne aliquis occultè agrum seminet aut plantet, & deinde dicat, Illa שמיטה sunt. Excipiuntur tamen והיבוין הפיגם Et השושים Asparagorum hortensium & campestrium genera, & omnia talia quæ nec in omnium potestate sunt, nec à multis possidentur, ut & alia quæ Maymon. tr. cit. c.4. recenset. Syria ad annum septimum tenetur. V.f.1. in S.
units.tr: §. Everything that grows in the seventh year, whether it springs from seed sown in the sixth year or from roots cut off, is called shemita [שמיטה]. By the law these things may be eaten, but they ought not to be cut off or gathered in the usual way, but casually and gradually, etc. By the enactments of the scribes, however, it is not permitted to eat them, lest anyone secretly sow or plant a field and then say, These are shemita. Excepted are [והיבוין הפיגם] and [השושים], the kinds of asparagus, garden and field, and all such things as are neither in everyone's power nor possessed by many, and others which Maimonides, in the treatise cited, c.4, enumerates. Syria is held to the seventh year. V.f.1. in S.

units.la: §. Vrbibus in limitibus fitis imponunt præfidia,ne gentes irrumpant,& fruɑtus anni septimi devorent. Idem ibid. c.4. Fruɑtus anni septimi non extra terram Ifraeliticam, ne quidem in Synedrium ferendi sunt; ibid. c. 5. Non ex illis facienda est mercatura. cap. 6. Tandiu ab initio anni de illis edere licet, quandiu illa species fruɑtus in agro reperitur; sed postquàm cessavit in agris,fruɑtum illius speciei debet לבער excutere è domo sua, vel comburendo fruɑtum, vel להשליך אותו ליום הבלה ipsum in mare mortuum projiciendo : (i.e. illo nullo modo amplius utendo. Vid. mare mortuum.) ibid. c. 5.
units.tr: §. In cities situated on the borders they set guards, lest the nations break in and devour the produce of the seventh year. Idem ibid. c.4. The produce of the seventh year may not be carried outside the land of Israel, not even into the Sanhedrin. Ibid. c.5. Trade in such produce is not to be made. c.6. From the beginning of the year one may eat of these things as long as that kind of produce is found in the field; but once it has ceased in the fields, the owner must [לבער] remove the produce of that kind from his house, either by burning it or by [להשליך אותו ליום הבלה] casting it into the Dead Sea (that is, by making no further use of it in any way. See mare mortuum). Ibid. c.5.

units.la: §. Prohibitum est vendere in anno septimo illa instrumenta, quibus ea opera fieri possunt, quæ in anno septimo prohibita sunt; ne ad peccandum hominum manus corroborentur. Gentiles verbis corroborare licet, ut fi quis arantem viderit, & dixerit תצליח felix fauftumque fit ! non autem opere ipsos adiuvare, quia illis præceptum de anno septimo non incumbit. ibid. c. 8.
units.tr: §. It is forbidden to sell, in the seventh year, those implements with which those works can be done that are forbidden in the seventh year, lest the hands of men be strengthened for sinning. Gentiles may be encouraged with words, so that if someone sees a man ploughing and says [תצליח], May it be prosperous and fortunate!, that is allowed; but they may not be helped by deed, because the commandment concerning the seventh year does not bind them. Ibid. c.8.

units.la: §. In anno septimo ex præcepto etiam esse debet שמיטת כספים remissio debitorum; Et illa etiam obtinet sed tamen ab aliquibus ad illa solum tempora restringitur, in quibus Iubilæum obtinet, cùm tamen illa debeat & hoc tempore locum habere, quamvis Iubilæum non amplius in usu fit: ne scilicet beneficia Iubilæi ex hominum mente excidant.
units.tr: §. In the seventh year there ought also to be, by precept, [שמיטת כספים], the remission of debts. This too holds good, though by some it is restricted to those times in which the Jubilee holds; yet it ought to have place at the present time as well, although the Jubilee is no longer in use, lest the benefits of the Jubilee fall out of people's minds.

units.la: §. Remissio debitorum obtinet solùm in fine anni septimi, hinc qui proximo suo aliquid mutuò dedit, illud per totum annum exigere potest, postquàm autem occidit sol nocte egressus anni septimi perdidit debitum. Nisi forte Syngtapham suam tradiderit Synedrio, & illud rogaverit, velit debitum exigere, aut habeat <bl>פרוטול</bl> ( de quo V. L.T. Buxt. p.1806.) in quo ipsi aliquis fundus annotatus sit. Ibid. c.9.
units.tr: §. The remission of debts holds only at the end of the seventh year. Hence, one who has lent something to his neighbour may demand it throughout the whole year, but once the sun has set on the night after the seventh year has ended, he has lost the debt. Unless perhaps he has handed his syngrapha over to the Sanhedrin and asked that it be allowed to exact the debt, or has a [פרוטול] (on which see L.T. Buxt. p.1806), in which some estate of his is noted. Ibid. c.9.

units.la: §. Septendecim Iubilæa numerarunt Israelitæ, ab eo quo ingressi sunt terram Canaan, usque ad egressum ipsorum in excidio templi primi, quod accidit in exitu anni septimi, anni Iubilæi verò 36. postquàm templum 410. annos steterat; ( templum secundum verò stetit 420.annos. ) Priora Iubilæa inceperunt numerare ab anno 14. ingressus eorum in terram Canaan. Iubilæa verò quæ sub templo secundo,ab anno septimo restaurationis templi inceperunt. אפ״עי שלא היתה שם יובל בבית שני טונין היו אותו כרי לקדש שמישוור Et quamvis templo secundo anno quinquagesimo re ipsa nullum Iubilæum fuerit, 50. annum tamen numerarunt, ad observandas remissiones anni septimi.
units.tr: §. The Israelites counted seventeen Jubilees, from the time they entered the land of Canaan until their exile at the destruction of the first temple, which happened at the end of the seventh year; the Jubilee years, however, number 36, since the temple had stood 410 years (the second temple stood 420 years). The earlier Jubilees they began to count from the fourteenth year of their entry into the land of Canaan. The Jubilees under the second temple they began from the seventh year of the restoration of the temple. [אפ״עי שלא היתה שם יובל] [בבית שני טונין היו אותו כרי לקדש שמישוור] And although under the second temple there was in fact no Jubilee in the fiftieth year, they nevertheless counted the fiftieth year, in order to observe the remissions of the seventh year.

units.la: §. Vna eademque est tuba novi anni & Iubilæi, nisi quòd tuba Iubilæi clangat tum in illo Synedrio cuius curâ intercalatio mensis fa&ta est,cùm in aliis, & quòd unusquisque privatus clangere teneatur.
units.tr: §. The trumpet of the new year and of the Jubilee is one and the same, except that the trumpet of the Jubilee sounds then in that Sanhedrin by whose care the intercalation of the month was made, whereas in other places it sounds elsewhere, and every private person is bound to sound it.

units.la: §. In tribus moras neƈtunt Iubilæi tempore,in clangendis tubis, dimissione servorum, & in agris pristinis dominis reddendis. Ab initio novi anni, usque ad diem expiationis non dimittebantur servi in domos suas, nec tamen Dominis suis inserviebant, sed comedebant, bibebant, pergræcabantur, genio indulgebant, Capita ipsorum corona redimiebat. Adveniente vero die expiationis, Synedrium tubâ clangebat, & tunc demum servi suas petebant domos, & fundi ad Dominos suos revertebantur. Ibid. cap.10.
units.tr: §. In the time of the Jubilee there are three things that cause delay: the sounding of the trumpets, the release of the slaves, and the return of the fields to their former owners. From the beginning of the new year until the day of atonement the slaves were not dismissed to their homes, nor did they serve their masters, but ate, drank, lived luxuriously, indulged their fancy, and had their heads crowned with garlands. But when the day of atonement arrived, the Sanhedrin sounded the trumpet, and then at last the slaves sought their homes, and the fields returned to their lords. Ibid. cap.10.

units.la: §. De anno septimo vid. plura in A. apud Annum sept.
units.tr: §. On the seventh year see more under Annum sept.

units.la: Iudæa quadripartiti potest: scilicet in regionum quæ olim Philistæorum fuit & versus partem Occidentalem se extendebat. In montanam Iudææ quæ erat orientem versus & vocabatur הר המלך Mons regalis. In שפלה שבהר planitiem Montanam ab oriente excipientem, & in convallem oram scilicet Maris Sodomitici & Iordanis. Vide Hierof. Scheviit sol.38.4. de monte regali vid. f. 1.
units.tr: Judaea can be divided into four parts: namely, the region that once belonged to the Philistines and extended towards the west; the hill country of Judaea, which lay towards the east and was called [הר המלך], the mountain of the king; the [שפלה שבהר], lowland, the plain which receives the hill country from the east; and the valley, namely the shore of the Sea of Sodom and of the Jordan. See Hierof. Scheviit sol.38.4. On the royal mountain see f.1.

units.la: §. Privilegia Iudææ præ omnibus terræ Israeliticæ partibus fuerunt, quòd in ea sita Hierosolyma, Templum, Synedrium; Quòd annus extrà Iudæam intercalari non debuerit, dum licuit in ea. Hierof. Nedarim sol. 40.1. Quòd manipulus hordei primitialis non nisi ex Iudæa afferri debuit. Bab.Sanhed.f.11.2.
units.tr: §. The privileges of Judaea above all other parts of the land of Israel were these: that Jerusalem, the Temple and the Sanhedrin were situated in it; that the year was not to be intercalated outside Judaea, as long as it was permitted within it. Hierof. Nedarim sol.40.1. That the first sheaf of barley was not to be brought from anywhere but Judaea. Bab. Sanhed. f.11.2.

units.la: § Iudæa דרום Austrum vocatur respectu Galilææ; R. Iofua Ben Levi in Hierof. Chalah sol.57.2. vocatur דרומיא Australis, & pro Australibus pluviam impetravit, Hierof. Taanit sol.66.3. & tamen in Hierof. Trumot sol. 46. 2. dicitur ipsum Lyddensem fuisse. Sic in Hierof. Erubbin sol. 23.3. discipulus quidam devotus potuit intercalare pro Galilæa, sed non sufficiens fuit ut intercalaret pro Austro, i.e. Iudæa; erant enim ibi multò accuratiores. Hinc etiam intelliges quo fensuRabbini quidam vocentur ײַנִּ Aust·ales. Vt R. Iacob Australis Hierof. Succah f.53.4. R.Samlai Australis; Hierof.Berac. sol.11.4
units.tr: § Judaea is called [דרום], the south, in relation to Galilee. R. Joshua ben Levi, in Hierof. Chalah sol.57.2, is called [דרומיא], a southerner, and obtained rain for the southerners, Hierof. Taanit sol.66.3; and yet in Hierof. Trumot sol.46.2 he is said to have been a man of Lydda. Thus in Hierof. Erubbin sol.23.3 a certain devout disciple could intercalate for Galilee, but was not competent to intercalate for the south, that is Judaea, for the men there were far more exact. From this you will also understand in what sense certain rabbis are called [דרומאי], southerners: as R. Jacob the Southerner, Hierof. Succah f.53.4, and R. Samlai the Southerner, Hierof. Berac. sol.11.4.

units.la: §. In Iudæa plurima se aliter habuerunt quàm in Galilæa; Vid. Galilæa.
units.tr: §. In Judaea many things were otherwise than in Galilee. See Galilaea.

units.la: §.
