Papus & Lulienus sunt Iudæorum martyres; cùm enim filia Regis in Lydda cæsa reperta esset, & fama fuisset, Iudæos ipsam occidisse, & latum esset acre decretum in Iudæos, se prodiderunt hi duo, atque Israelem liberarunt; dixerant enim se cædis authores esse, & proinde à rege quoque soli occisi fuerunt. Vide Hierof. Taanith sol.66.1. & Megillah. sol. 70.3. Bab. Taanith sol.18.2. Bab. Bathra sol. 10.2.
units.tr: §. Papus and Lulianus are the martyrs of the Jews. For when the daughter of the king was found slain in Lydda, and a rumour arose that the Jews had killed her, and a harsh decree was issued against the Jews, these two gave themselves up and freed Israel; for they had said that they were the authors of the murder, and accordingly they alone were put to death by the king. See Hierof. Taanith sol.66.1 and Megillah sol.70.3; Bab. Taanith sol.18.2; Bab. Bathra sol.10.2.

units.la: §. Splendidum est mendacium Manethonis historiographi, quo finxit ref. Iofepho Antiq. lib 3. Iudæos ex Ægypto expulsos esse, quia leprosi erant, ut reliqui ab illis non inficerentur. Vid. Fagium in Deut. Lev.14.
units.tr: §. The splendid lie of the historian Manetho is that, as Josephus reports in Antiq. book 3, the Jews were expelled from Egypt because they were lepers, so that the rest might not be infected by them. See Fagius on Deuteronomy and Leviticus 14.

units.la: §. Alexander Macedo in Iudæa existens Iudæis admodum benignus fuit. Vid. Alexander Mag. Inter alia etiam ab ipso impetrarunt, ne rex septimi anni tributa exigeret.
units.tr: §. Alexander the Macedonian, while in Judaea, was very kind to the Jews. See Alexander Magnus. Among other things they obtained from him that the king should not exact tribute in the seventh year.

units.la: § Iudæi intra terræ suæ fines inclusi & iis contenti opibus, quas illic natura producebat, vitam procul commerciis agitarunt. Vide Iofeph Apolog. contra Apionem 1.
units.tr: §. The Jews, shut up within the borders of their land and content with the resources which nature produced there, passed their lives far from commerce. See Josephus, Against Apion, book 1.

units.la: §. Cum summa inscitia coniunctum est quod Aristoteles apud Clearchum autumavit, Iudæos esse ab Indiæ sapientibus propagatos, sed nomen mutavisse. Ratio eius est, quia Philosophi illi, qui apud Iudaeos Callani appellantur, in Cava Syria Iudaei dicuntur.
units.tr: §. Joined to the greatest ignorance is what Aristotle, as reported by Clearchus, supposed: that the Jews were descended from the wise men of India but had changed their name. The reason for this is that those philosophers who among the Jews are called Calani are said to be Jews in Coele-Syria.

units.la: §. Iudaei à Romanis nubium & incerti numinis cultores habiti sunt; sic Tacitus inquit, ex illo tempore quo Cn. Pompeius, per Asiam victrices circumagit copias, & Iudaeis victis, in templi intimos recessus penetravit, vulgatum esse, vacuam esse sedem & inania arcana. Credebant enim mortales, fore intus numen aliquod. Sic Lucanus Et dedita sacris, incerti Iudaea Dei. Petronius in Cataleetis Iudaeos sic perstringit.
units.tr: §. The Romans regarded the Jews as worshippers of a cloudy and uncertain deity. So Tacitus says that from the time when Gnaeus Pompey, leading his victorious forces through Asia, and having defeated the Jews, penetrated into the innermost recesses of the temple, it became widely known that the seat was empty and the hidden things were nothing: for mortals believed that some divinity was present within. So Lucan: and devoted to sacred rites, the Jewish God unknown. Petronius, in the Catalecta, lashes the Jews thus.

units.la: Iudaeus licet, & porcinum numen adoretEt cœli summas advocet auriculas.
units.tr: Though he is a Jew, he worships a pig-god, and summons the highest ears of heaven.

units.la: §. Vide de Iudaeis in genere ap. Israelitas.
units.tr: §. See on the Jews in general under Israelitas.

units.la: IUDICIA CAPITALIA [Hebrew] à tribus & 20. viris exercentur ut etiam iudicium de Homine qui cum bestia se commiscuit; Item de Bove lapidando; de Lupo, Leone, urso, pantera, vipera, serpente, non nisi Iudicium xxiii. habetur. Sanhed. c. 1. de retractatione in Iudiciis vid. Sanhed. c. 3. 2.
units.tr: CAPITAL JUDGMENTS are conducted by a court of three and twenty men, as is also the judgment on a man who has had intercourse with a beast; likewise on an ox to be stoned. For a wolf, lion, bear, panther, viper or serpent, only a court of twenty-three is held. Sanhed. c. 1. On retrial in judgments see Sanhed. c. 3. 2.

units.la: §. Iudicia pecuniaria [Hebrew] diiudicari possunt à tribus, ut & etiam iudicia de rapinis, laesione, damno, restitutione dupli, & quadrupli, de [Hebrew] vi & seductione; sed [Hebrew] [Hebrew] [Hebrew] aliena fama violator, secundum Sapientes à xxiii. diiudicari debet, quia est species capitalis Iudicii. Sanhed. c. 1. In causis pecuniariis partium quaeque unum arbitrum deligit, & pariter adscisecunt tertium. Pars quaeque iudicem ab adversario delectum repudiandi ius habet, si ullum ob propinquitatem aut aliam causam ad hoc ineptum esse demonstrare potest. Qui dixerit, Ego causam meam patri meo vel etiam tuo detulero fidei, imò etiam בקר רועי שלושה על tribus bubulcis, secundùm Sapientes retractare non potest. Sanhed. c.3.
units.tr: §. Pecuniary judgments may be decided by three, as may also judgments on robbery, injury, damage, restitution of double and fourfold, violence and seduction. But a slanderer of another's good name, according to the Sages, must be judged by twenty-three, since it is a kind of capital judgment. Sanhed. c. 1. In pecuniary cases each party chooses one arbitrator, and the two together then appoint a third. Each party has the right to reject a judge chosen by the opponent, if it can show that he is unfit for this on account of kinship or some other cause. Whoever says, "I will entrust my case to my father, or even to yours," or even "to three herdsmen," may not, according to the Sages, retract it. Sanhed. c. 3.

units.la: §. Si mutuò dans velit ut debitor compareat coram Synedrio magno ut ibi de eorum causa iudicetur, debitorem cogunt cum mutuò dante Hierosolymas ascendere. Atqui ita fit in omnibus istiusmodi naturæ. Maym.in Sanh. c.6.
units.tr: §. If a lender wishes the debtor to appear before the Great Sanhedrin, so that the case may be judged there, they compel the debtor to go up to Jerusalem with the lender. And this is done in all cases of this kind. Maym. in Sanh. c. 6.

units.la: §. Ad iudicandum & testimonium dicendum hi censentur פסולין Reieštanei; Aleator, fenerator, מוריתי יונים Qui columbas volare docent (qui quaestum volatu columbarum quaerunt, sicuti faciunt illi qui tales columbas vendunt, quas ad pristina columbaria rediturus esse sciunt.) Nundinatores fructuum anni septimi. (qui vix ad usum multò minus ad quaestum concessi.) Priorum respectu hoc obtinet semper nisi à vitæ instituto in melius redeant; Posteriorum verò si præter hanc non aliam artem exercent. Sanhed. cap.3.3. Mulier Iudicis personam sustinêre non potest. Maymon. Hal. Melachim c.9.
units.tr: §. For judging and for giving testimony these are held disqualified: gamblers and usurers; those who teach doves to fly (that is, who make their gain from the flight of pigeons, as do those who sell such pigeons, which they know will return to their former dovecote); and dealers in the produce of the seventh year (who are scarcely permitted for use, much less for profit). With the first two this always holds, unless they change their way of life for the better; with the last, if they practise no other trade. Sanhed. c. 3. 3. A woman cannot sustain the person of a judge. Maymon. Hal. Melachim c. 9.

units.la: §. In Iudiciis hi ex propinquis censentur: frater, patruus, avunculus, maritus amitæ, & materteræ, vitricus, socer, uxoris sororis vir; Illi nempe cum filiis & generis suis: at privignus solus; Amicus & inimicus, qualis æstimatur, si tribus diebus ad ipsum non verba feceris odii causâ. Sanhed. c.3.4.
units.tr: §. In judgments these are counted as relatives: brother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, the husband of a paternal or maternal aunt, stepfather, father-in-law, and the husband of one's wife's sister; namely, together with their sons and their kin. But a stepson alone. A friend or enemy is judged as such if you have not spoken to him for three days out of hatred. Sanhed. c. 3. 4.

units.la: §. Quid sit <bl>כריתא & חקירה</bl> in Iudiciis vid.
units.tr: What keritha and chaqirah [Hebrew] are in judgments, see.

units.la: Bedika. Qualis fiat processus in testibus examinandis. Vid. Testes.
units.tr: Bedika: how the process of examining witnesses is conducted. See Testes.

units.la: §. In Iudiciis pecuniariis nihil refert, in quam partem suffragia colligi incipiant; in iudiciis capitalibus vero tantùm ab absolventibus incipiunt, non autem à condemnantibus: in iudiciis pecuniariis sententia decernitur vel ad absolutionem vel ad condemnationem, unico suffragio præponderante. In capitalibus verò absolutio fieri potest, modò unius suffragium præponderet, condemnatio verò non nisi duobus præponderantibus suffragiis. Illa, sive absolvendi sive condemnandi causâ, revocantur, hæc, non nisi absolvendi gratiâ. In illis quilibet ad indicium sive innocentiæ sive debiti admittitur. In his quivis ad indicium innocentiæ, non omnes ad indicium culpæ (qui in defensionem accusati aliquid profert, dicitur [Hebrew] , & qui in condemnationem [Hebrew] ) Illa iudicia agitantur de die & etiam vel de noĉte deciduntur; hæc de die agitantur & de die concluduntur. Iudicia de pecuniariis absolvunt eodem die, sive sint mulĉatitia, sive absolutiva. Iudicia de capitalibus finiunt eodem die, si sint ad absolutionem; si verò sint ad damnationem finiuntur die sequente. Sanhed. cap.4. Rationem diversitatis huius reddunt Gemaristæ, quando dicunt [Hebrew] [Hebrew] Beatus est Iudex qui fermentat iudicium suum. i. e. secundùm Gloss. Qui iudicium suum moratur, & pernoĉtare facit, ut ventilet veritatem. In iudiciis pecuniariis ætate & prudentiâ maior primus sententiam dicit, in capitalibus verò à latere fit exordium. Quilibet de pecunia iudicare potest; de capite non nisi Sacerdotes, Leviræ & Israelitæ, & ii qui filiam Sacerdoti elocare possunt (vid. Kidduschin c.4.1.4.5.) Sanhed. ibid.
units.tr: §. In pecuniary judgments it makes no difference in which direction the votes begin to be collected; in capital judgments, however, they begin only with those who acquit, not with those who condemn. In pecuniary judgments the sentence is decided either for acquittal or for condemnation by a single preponderating vote. In capital judgments acquittal may be pronounced if a single vote preponderates, but condemnation only by two preponderating votes. The former, whether for acquittal or for condemnation, are reopened; the latter only for acquittal. In the former anyone is admitted to indicate either innocence or debt; in the latter anyone may indicate innocence, but not everyone may indicate guilt. (Whoever brings forward something in defence of the accused is called [Hebrew], and whoever speaks for condemnation [Hebrew].) The former judgments are conducted by day and may even be decided by night; the latter are conducted by day and concluded by day. Pecuniary judgments are concluded the same day, whether they end in a fine or in acquittal. Capital judgments are concluded the same day if they are for acquittal; if they are for condemnation, they are concluded the following day. Sanhed. c. 4. The Gemarists give the reason for this difference when they say: "Blessed is the judge who ferments his judgment," that is, according to the Gloss, "who delays his judgment and keeps it overnight, so that the truth may be sifted." In pecuniary judgments the eldest in age and prudence gives the first sentence; in capital judgments the beginning is made from the side. Anyone may judge about money; about life only priests, Levites and Israelites, and those who may give a daughter in marriage to a priest (see Kidduschin c. 4, 1, 4, 5). Sanhed. ibid.

units.la: §. In lectione tractatus Sanhedrin diligenter observanda est illa distinctio quam ponunt inter ניו & גומרין. Sub voce ניו totum iudicii processum innuunt; examen actoris, rei, testium, receptionem suffragiorum Synedrii, atque eorum conscriptionem per scribas. גומרין vero nihil aliud designat quàm processum ad sententiam definitivam.
units.tr: §. In reading the tractate Sanhedrin one must carefully observe the distinction they draw between [Hebrew] and [Hebrew]. Under the first word they refer to the whole process of the trial: the examination of the plaintiff, the defendant and the witnesses, the receiving of the votes of the Sanhedrin, and their recording by the scribes. The second, however, designates nothing other than the process up to the definitive sentence.

units.la: §. In Iudicio Domini N.I.C. Synedrium non observavit ordinarios suos de iudiciis canones. 1. Iudicia capitalia, ut diximus, non debebant noête fieri; at ex Evangelio discimus Patres hos iudicium de Christo noctu incepisse, & per totam ferè noctem agitasse; Quid enim aliud agitabant, quàm opus tenebrarum!
units.tr: §. In the trial of our Lord N.I.C., the Sanhedrin did not observe its ordinary canons on judgments. 1. Capital judgments, as we have said, ought not to be held by night; yet from the Gospel we learn that these judges began the judgment on Christ at night and carried it on through almost the whole night. For what else were they doing but the work of darkness!

units.la: 2. Nox hæc erat vespera diei festi primi scilicet hebdomadis Paschalis, quo tempore prohibitum erat iudicia exercere, secundùm Moed Katon c.5.2. Non iudicant die festo. At illi non solùm totâ festi diei vesperâ & nocte consilium habuerunt, sed etiam (Matt. 27.1.) in ipso die festo iudicium de capite Christi absolverunt; contra ea quæ leguntur in Bab. Sanhed. sol. 35.1. Hierof. (hetubhot sol. 24. 4. Moed Katon sol.63.1. Ne iudicent vesperâ Sabbathi; nec vesperâ diei festi; ne scilicet iudicia inchoata vespera finiantur vel concludantur die Sabbatho aut festo. 3. Summo mane à prima aurora usque ad horam tertiam erat tempus recitandi Phylacteria. Beracot. cap.1.2. At omnes primarii Sacerdotes & seniores de precibus parum aut non cogitant, confluunt enim summo mane primaque aurorâ apparente ad Christum morti adiudicandum. 4. Cùm Christus crucifigebatur erat dies primus Paschatis, quo se debebant sistere in templo & munera sua offerre. (v.f.) At quando & quomodo hoc ab ipsis praestitum illo die? quem integrum ad Christum malè perdendum insumpserunt. 5. Bab.Sanhed. sol.63.1. hunc habemus Canonem; Quod Synedriales Viri eo die, quo aliquem ad mortem diiudicarunt, nihil degustare debeant. At illi clamant ad Pilatum se non posse in praetorium ingredi, ut possent comedere Chagigam. Supplicium Christi non impedivit, quominus affatim se implerent.
units.tr: 2. That night was the eve of the first day of the Paschal week, when it was forbidden to hold judgments, according to Moed Katon c. 5. 2: "They do not judge on a festival day." But they not only held their council through the whole evening and night of the festal day, but also (Matt. 27. 1) on the festival day itself they brought the judgment on Christ's life to a conclusion. This is contrary to what is read in Bab. Sanhed. fol. 35. 1; Hierof. (hetubhot fol. 24. 4; Moed Katon fol. 63. 1): "They shall not judge on the evening of the Sabbath, nor on the evening of a festival day," that is, lest judgments begun in the evening be finished or concluded on the Sabbath or the festival day. 3. From early morning, from first dawn until the third hour, was the time for reciting the Phylacteries (Beracot c. 1. 2). But all the chief priests and elders think little or not at all of prayers, for they gather very early in the morning, as soon as dawn appears, to have Christ adjudged to death. 4. When Christ was crucified it was the first day of the Passover, on which they ought to present themselves in the temple and offer their gifts (v.f.). But when and how did they do this on that day, which they spent entirely on the wicked destruction of Christ? 5. In Bab. Sanhed. fol. 63. 1 we have this canon: "That members of the Sanhedrin, on the day on which they have judged someone to death, must taste nothing." Yet they cry out to Pilate that they cannot enter the praetorium, so that they may eat the Chagigam. The execution of Christ did not prevent them from filling themselves abundantly.

units.la: §. Sed pergimus de Iudiciis. Ad mortem condemnatorum propinqui, iudices ut & testes salutant, quasi dicerent. Persuasum vobis sit, nos nullo modo vobis succensère, quippe rectè iudicastis. Propinquos verò suos morte affectos non plangunt sed lugent. (Vid. Lutlum) Sanhed. c.6.
units.tr: §. But we return to judgments. To those condemned to death their kinsmen, the judges and the witnesses bid farewell, as if to say: "Be persuaded that we are in no way angry with you, since you have judged rightly." Their kinsmen who have been put to death they do not lament (plangunt) but mourn (lugent). (See Lutlum.) Sanhed. c. 6.

units.la: §. Iudex qui dona sumit, non morietur ex senectute Ufquedum oculi eius lippiant; dicuntur enim munera exoculare sapientes. Peah c.8.9. Non iudicandum est antequàm audiverimus aut rem perceperimus, ne in nos congruat illud in Ketubhot sol.112.1. Populus עמו praeceps est iis, qui praemittit os vestrum ante aures vestras.
units.tr: §. A judge who takes gifts will not die of old age until his eyes grow dim (Ufquedum oculi eius lippiant); for they say gifts blind the eyes of the wise (munera exoculare sapientes). Peah c. 8. 9. One must not judge before we have heard the matter or grasped it, lest that saying in Ketubhot fol. 112. 1 fall upon us: "The people (ammo) is hasty toward those who put their mouth before their ears."

units.la: §. De Iudiciis capitalibus plura vid. apud
units.tr: §. More on capital judgments see in

units.la: Supplicia; de Synedriis vid. suo loco. de Iudicis qualitatibus V. Cl.Buxt. L.T. p.512. De Iudicio Seductoris vid. Seductor. de Processu Senioris refragantis. Vid. Senior.
units.tr: Punishments; on the Sanhedrins see in their place. On the qualities of judges see V. Cl. Buxt. L.T. p. 512. On the judgment of the seducer see Seductor. On the process against a dissenting elder see Senior.

units.la: IURAMENTA. Sic incipit Maymonides suum tra- ctatum de iuramentis. ארבעה מיני שבועות הן
units.tr: OATHS. Thus Maimonides begins his treatise on oaths: There are four kinds of oaths [ארבעה מיני שבועות הן]

units.la: שבועת ביטוי שבועת שוא שבועת הפקדון ושבועת העדן Quatuor sunt iuramentorum classes, est Iuramentum promissorium, Iuramentum vanum; Iuramentum de deposito; Iuramentum testimoniale. De unoquoque genere pauca referemus.
units.tr: There are four classes of oaths: the promissory oath, the vain oath, the oath concerning a deposit, and the testimonial oath. We shall give a brief account of each kind [שבועת ביטוי שבועת שוא שבועת הפקדון ושבועת העדן].

units.la: §. Iuramentum promissorium est, quando aliquis dicebat & iurabat, se hoc vel illud facturum vel non facturum; להרע או להשיב sive malum sive bonum effecturis sit. Dividebatur in quatuor partes שתים להבא ושתים לשעבר Due erant de futuro, & duae de praeterito: v. g. si aliquis iurasset de re praeterita; illam ita factam fuisse, vel non factam: Aut de re futura, se illam facturum vel non facturum: ואין שבועת ביטוי נוהגת אלא כדברים שאיפשר לו לעשות בין להבא בין לשעבר Neque Iuramentum promissorium versatur nisi circa illa quae hominis vel respectu futuri possibilia sunt, aut respectu praeteriti fuerunt. Quicunque ergo aliquo horum quatuor modo iurat, & ita res se non habet prout iurat; (exempli gratia, se non iecisse lapidem in mare, cum iecerit: se iecisse cum non iecerit, se non comesturum & tamen comederit, se comesturum; & tamen non comederit;) הרי זו שבועת שקר Ecce hoc est iuramentum falsum; sive periurium. Maymon Schebbuot c. 1. Quicunque iurat se non comesturum, & tamen quaedam comedit, quæ quidem esui non fatis sunt idonea, hic reus non est. Talmud in Schebbuot cap.3. de his & similibus iuramentis loquitur Deus, quando inquit ne iurate in nomine meo vane. Qui iuraverit vane במיר petulanter, vapulat. Qui ex errore debet afferre oblationem &c. Maym.l.c.
units.tr: §. A promissory oath is when someone says and swears that he will or will not do this or that, whether he is going to bring about evil or good [להרע או להשיב]. It was divided into four parts: two concerning the future and two concerning the past. For example, if someone swore about a past matter that it was done or not done, or about a future matter that he would or would not do it. A promissory oath applies only to those things that are possible for a man to do, whether in the future or in the past [ואין שבועת ביטוי נוהגת אלא כדברים שאיפשר לו לעשות בין להבא בין לשעבר]. Therefore whoever swears in any one of these four ways, and the matter is not as he swears (for example, swearing that he did not throw a stone into the sea when he had thrown it; swearing that he had thrown it when he had not; swearing that he will not eat and yet eats; swearing that he will eat and yet does not), this is a false oath, that is, perjury [הרי זו שבועת שקר]. Maimonides, Shebuot ch. 1. Whoever swears that he will not eat, and yet eats some things which are not really fit for food, is not guilty. The Talmud in Shebuot ch. 3 speaks of these and similar oaths when God says, "Do not swear in my name vainly." Whoever swears wantonly [במיר] is flogged. Whoever swears in error must bring an offering, etc. Maimonides, ibid.

units.la: §. Iuramentum vanum est etiam quadripartitum (sed non eodem modo quo prius.) הנשבע על דבר ירוע שאין כן כגון על איש שהוא איש Cùm quis iuramento asserit quod notissima veritati est contrarium. Veluti si iuraret virum esse fœminam; fœminam esse virum, Columnam lapideam esse columnam auream &c. Vel cùm quis iuraret id esse vel fuisse, quod omnino impossibile, ut se vidisse camelum in aëre volitantem.
units.tr: §. The vain oath is also fourfold (though not in the same way as the former). When someone swears concerning a well-known fact to the contrary [הנשבע על דבר ידוע שאין כן כגון על איש שהוא איש], as if he swore that a man is a woman, that a woman is a man, that a stone column is a golden column, etc. Or when someone swears that something is or was altogether impossible, such as that he saw a camel flying in the air.

units.la: 2. Cùm quis iureiurando id assereret שאין כו ספק לארם de quo nemo dubitaret. v. g. Cœlum esse Cœlum, lapidem esse lapidem, duo esse duo. In quibus hominï, nullum est dubium, ut iuramentum ad eius confirmationem requireretur. 3. שנשבע לבטל את המצוות Cùm quis iurat se velle abstinere ab eo quod præceptum est; verbi gratiâ se nolle sua ציצית aut phylacteria gestare, se nolle in tugurilo festum Tabernaculorum transfigere, in Paschate azymum comedere; se velle ieiunare in Sabbathis & diebus festis. &c. 4. שנשבע על דבר שאין כוח בו לעשות Cùm id se factùrum iuraret, quod omnino ipsi impossibile, v.g. se per triduum & trinoctium non dormiturum, per plenam septimanam se nihil gustaturum &c. Qui ex his quatuor speciebus falsò iurat peccat contra præceptum negativum, & si petulanter iuraverit vapulat.
units.tr: 2. When someone confirms by oath what no one could doubt [שאין כו ספק לארם], for example, that heaven is heaven, a stone is a stone, two is two. In such cases there is no doubt for anyone, so an oath is not required for their confirmation. 3. When someone swears that he wishes to abstain from what has been commanded [שנשבע לבטל את המצוות]: for example, that he does not wish to wear his tzitzit or phylacteries, that he does not wish to dwell in a booth at the Feast of Tabernacles, that he does not wish to eat unleavened bread at Passover, that he wishes to fast on the Sabbaths and festival days, etc. 4. When he swears that he will do what is altogether impossible for him [שנשבע על דבר שאין כוח בו לעשות], for example, that he will not sleep for three days and three nights, that he will taste nothing for a full week, etc. Whoever falsely swears in any of these four kinds sins against a negative precept, and if he swears wantonly he is flogged.

units.la: §. Iuramentum de deposito est; quando quis iurat socium suum nihil apud ipsum de posuisse, aut se quicquam habere quod ad ipsum pertineat; aut quando assevérat iuramento se depositum non habere; sed illud surreptum, fractum, aut perditum esse. Propter hanc praecepti negativi transgressionem non vapulant. Qui vero de depósito falsò iuraverit, debet restituere substantiam quam se habere iuramento negavit, cum additione quintupli & oblatione pro reatu.
units.tr: §. The oath concerning a deposit is when someone swears that his companion has deposited nothing with him, or that he has nothing belonging to him; or when he solemnly asserts by oath that he does not have the deposit, but that it was stolen, broken, or lost. For the transgression of this negative precept they are not flogged. But whoever falsely swears about a deposit must restore the property which he swore he did not have, with the addition of a fifth, and bring an offering for his guilt.

units.la: §. Iuramentum testimoniale est, quando testes sciunt de depósita pecunia, & deinde cùm coram magistratu sunt, iurant se nescire an aliqua pecunia depósita sit nec ne. Qui ita iurant pro suo delicto oblationem afferre debent. Maymon & Mischna l.c.
units.tr: §. The testimonial oath is when witnesses know about money deposited, and then, when they are before the magistrate, swear that they do not know whether any money was deposited or not. Those who so swear must bring an offering for their offence. Maimonides and the Mishnah, ibid.

units.la: §. In tribus ex his iuramenti generibus de veritate rei iuratae solùmodò cautum est, non de vanitate iurandi; Cautionem quidem aliquam adhibère videntur circa iuramentum vanum & temerarium, primò quatenus exis-timarunt illum qui sic iuraret exsecrabilem fieri, & flagellandum esse, & quamvis oblationem offerret, tamen solùm respectu hominum purgari, non statim etiam in conspectu Dei; Maymon Hal.Schebbuot c.12. Ita etiam talem flagellationi adiudicant Gemarista Hier. in Schebbuot sol.34.4. qui iurat duo esse duo vapulat ob vanum iuramentum. Secundò quatenus terrorem addiderunt ex feralibus exemplis, quale est illud 1. m.c. Viginti quatuor coetus fuerunt in Austro, atque omnes vastati sunt ob iuramentum vanum. Incerim tamen ad periurium quod prohibetur Lev.xix.12. omne de iurando peccatum Iudæi reduxerunt, de iuramento vano parum curantes; imò illud in tam arctum circulum conclusêrunt, ut quis millies vane iurare possět, & tamen intrà limites cautionis de vano iuramento non includi, sicuti ex innumeris illis restrictionibus quas Maymonides affert videre est. Quare non mirum, si Christus Matth.v. Iudæos circa hanc materiam perstringat.
units.tr: §. In three of these kinds of oath, precaution is taken only regarding the truth of the thing sworn, not regarding the vanity of swearing. They do seem to have taken some precaution regarding the vain and rash oath. First, inasmuch as they judged that the one who so swears becomes accursed and must be flogged, and that although he offers a sacrifice, he is cleansed only in the sight of men, not immediately in the sight of God. Maimonides, Hal. Shebuot ch. 12. So also the Jerusalem Gemara in Shebuot fol. 34.4 assigns such flogging: whoever swears that two is two is flogged for a vain oath. Secondly, inasmuch as they added terror by dreadful examples, such as that found in the Mishnah, ch. 1: "Twenty-four companies were in the south, and all were destroyed on account of a vain oath." Yet they reduced almost every sin of swearing to the perjury forbidden at Leviticus 19:12, caring little about vain swearing. Indeed, they confined it within so narrow a circle that a man could swear vainly a thousand times and yet not be included within the limits of caution concerning vain oaths, as may be seen from the countless restrictions which Maimonides cites. So it is no wonder that Christ, in Matthew 5, rebukes the Jews on this point.

units.la: §. Iudai in usu habuerunt iurare per creaturas.Maymon ubi supra cap.12. מי שנשבע בשמים בארץ ובשמש וכיוצא בהן Si quis iurat per cœlum, terram, solem & similia: sit licet animus iurantis sub his verbis per illum iurare qui hæc creavit, hoc tamen non est iuramentum. Aut si quis iuret per aliquem ex Prophetis, aut per aliquem librum è libris scripturæ, sit licet sensus iurantis per illum iurare, qui ipsum Prophetam misit, aut qui ipsum librum dedit, nihilominus hoc non est iuramentum. (Notat tamen etiam author noster in seq. Populum edoceri debere ne illis formulis abutatur שלא ינהוג קלות ראש בשבועות ne tandem usu veniat, ut desultorie de quovis iuret.) Sic quoque Mischna in Schebbuot c.4. Si quis alium adiuret per cœlum aut terram reus non est.
units.tr: §. The Jews were in the habit of swearing by creatures. Maimonides, ubi supra, ch. 12: "If someone swears by heaven, earth, the sun, and the like, even if the intention of the one swearing under these words is to swear by Him who created these, this is nevertheless not an oath. Or if someone swears by one of the Prophets, or by some book of Scripture, even if the sense of the one swearing is to swear by Him who sent the Prophet or gave the book, this is nevertheless not an oath." (Our author, however, also notes in what follows that the people ought to be taught not to abuse these formulas, lest it come in time to be the practice to swear carelessly about anything [שלא ינהוג קלות ראש בשבועות].) So too the Mishnah in Shebuot ch. 4: If someone adjures another by heaven or earth, he is not guilty. [מי שנשבע בשמים בארץ ובשמש וכיוצא בהן]

units.la: §. Iurarunt per cœlum. Bab. Beracot.folio 55. השמים כן הוא Per cœlum res ita se habet.
units.tr: §. They swore by heaven. Babylonian Talmud, Berachot, fol. 55: "By heaven, the matter stands thus" [השמים כן הוא].

units.la: §. Iurarunt per templum. Cheritut cap.1. v. 7. Cùm venderentur aliquando Hierosolymis turtures & pulli columbarum denario aureo, dixit RabbanSimeon BenGamaliel המעון הוה לא אליך הלילה עד שיהוא בדינרין Per habitationem hanc (i.e. ( i. e. per templum hoc V. templi nomina.) Hac notle non quiescam nisi vaneant denario argenteo.
units.tr: §. They swore by the temple. Cheritut ch. 1, v. 7: When turtledoves and young pigeons were once being sold at Jerusalem for a gold denarius, Rabban Simeon ben Gamaliel said: "By this habitation (that is, by this temple) I will not rest tonight until they are sold for a silver denarius" [המעון הזה לא אליך הלילה עד שיהוא בדינרין]. (See the names of the temple.)

units.la: Ketubbot cap.3. & Tofapht. ibid. Dixit R.Zechariah Ben Ketfab הזה המעון Per templum hoc, non recefjio manus mulieris e manu mea. Bab. Kiddufchin sol.71.1. Dixit R. Iochanan היכלא Per templum, est in manu nostra monstrare, quinam legitimae stirpis sint &c. Sed luculentiffimum de hoc iuramento dictum habemus apud Iuchafin sol.56.col.1. Bava Ben Butah iuravit, per templum in fine traditus Cheritut, & RabbanSimeon Ben Gamaliel in initio ישראל בישראל מנהג וזה Et talis fuit mos in Israele.
units.tr: Ketubbot ch. 3, and Tosafot ibid.: "Rabbi Zechariah ben Ketsab said: By this temple, I will not withdraw my hand from the woman's hand." Babylonian Kiddushin, fol. 71.1: Rabbi Johanan said: "By the temple, it is in our power to point out who are of legitimate stock," etc. [היכלא]. But we have a most clear statement about this oath in Jochasin, fol. 56, col. 1: "Bava ben Buta swore by the temple at the end of the Cheritut tradition, and Rabban Simeon ben Gamaliel at the beginning" [ישראל בישראל מנהג וזה], and such was the custom in Israel.

units.la: §. Iurarunt per Hierosolymam. Tofapht. ad Nedarim cap.1. Dicit R. Iudah, Qui dicit per Hierosolymam, nihil dicit, nisi intentio animo voverit Hierosolymam versus. Vbi etiam post duas lineas interiectas adduntur hae iurandi vel vovendi formulae : ירושלם לירושלם בירושלם ירושלם היכל להיכל בהיכל Hierosolyma, pro Hierofolyma, per Hierosolymam.Templum,pro Templo, per Templum. Altare,pro Altari,per Altare. Agnus, pro Agno,per Agnum; Pastophoria, pro Pastophoria,per Pastophoria. Lignum, pro Ligno,per Lignum. Sacrificia ignita, pro ignitis, per ignita. Patina, propatinis, per patinas: hac omnia quod ego hoc faxo tibi.
units.tr: §. They swore by Jerusalem. Tosafot on Nedarim ch. 1: Rabbi Judah says: "Whoever says 'by Jerusalem' says nothing, unless in intention he has vowed toward Jerusalem." Where also, after two intervening lines, these formulas of swearing or vowing are added: "Jerusalem, for Jerusalem, by Jerusalem; Temple, for Temple, by Temple; Altar, for Altar, by Altar; Lamb, for Lamb, by Lamb; Pastophoria, for Pastophoria, by Pastophoria; Wood, for Wood, by Wood; burnt sacrifices, for burnt sacrifices, by burnt sacrifices; Pan, for pans, by pans: all these things, I will make this so for you." [ירושלם לירושלם בירושלם ירושלם היכל להיכל בהיכל מזבח למזבח במזבח כבש לכבש בכבש פסטופוריא לפסטופוריא בפסטופוריא עץ לעץ בעץ עולה לעולה בעולה מחבת למחבתות במחבתות]

units.la: §. Iurarunt per capita sua. Sanhed. cap.3.1. Tenetur quis proximo iurare, & dicit ille דור לי Vove (vel iura) mihi per vitam capitis tui. ראשך בחיי
units.tr: They swore by their heads. Sanhedrin ch. 3.1. A person is bound to swear to his neighbour, and the other says: [דור לי] "Vow (or swear) to me by the life of your head." [ראשך בחיי]

units.la: §. Claudit Maymonides suas de hac materia velitationes hoc effato היא גדולה טובה V 3
units.tr: Maymonides ends his discussions of this subject with this saying [היא גדולה טובה]:

units.la: : Magnum bonum homini est si ab omni iuramento possit abstinere: Christus voluntario & arbitrario iuramento plane nullum locum permisit, interim tamen legitimum non exclulit; dehortantur Iudæi suos ne nimis sint in iuramentis, quia impossibile est ne multum iurando non aliquando profanent, sicuti monent in Demai c.2.3. in Gloss.R.Salom. Salvator noster plane prohibet ullo modo aut per creaturas, aut per alias vanas rationes iurare. Quæ prohibitio interea iuramentum legitimum præsupponit; Christi enim intentio est abusum corrigere.
units.tr: It is a great good for a man if he can abstain from every oath. Christ allowed no place at all for a voluntary and arbitrary oath, yet he did not exclude a lawful one. The Jews warn their people not to swear too much, because it is impossible that by swearing often they will not at some time profane it, as they advise in Demai c.2.3 in the Gloss of R. Salom. Our Saviour plainly forbids swearing in any way, whether by creatures or by other vain reasons. This prohibition presupposes a lawful oath, for Christ's intention is to correct the abuse.

units.la: §. Iuramentum administrationis, quo iurabant se fideliter administraturos, quod ipsis commissum erat, vocant שבועת אפיטרופסות Pesach sol.68.2. in Com. Cl. Buxtorf. Lex. T. 183. Qui est suspectus de pecunia, est etiam suspectus de iuramento. Metzia f.6.1. de Iuramento Iudicum & Rabbinorum vid. Cl. Buxt. L.T. p.626. licet fallere publicanos Iuramento. Nedarim c.3. v.4.
units.tr: The oath of administration, by which men swore that they would faithfully administer what had been committed to them, they call שבועת אפיטרופסות [shevuat apitropsut]. Pesachim 68.2 in the Commentary; Buxtorf, Lex. T. 183. He who is suspected concerning money is also suspected concerning an oath. Bava Metzia f.6.1. On the oath of judges and rabbis, see Buxtorf, L.T. p. 626. It is permitted to deceive tax-collectors by an oath. Nedarim c.3 v.4.

units.la: de IUVENCÆ DECOLLATIONE hæc habet Codex Sotah in cap.9. Sectio de עגלה ערופה de decollatione iuvenci legitur (in Synagoga) in lingua Sancta. Ex Deuteronom. xxi.1. Ad illum actum celebrandum tres vel secundùm R. Iehudam quinque Senatores Hierosolymitani se conferre debent. Si reperitur Cadaver (cuius cædis author ignotus est) sub aliquo acervo absconditum aut arbori suspensum,aut aquis innatans iuvencam non decollant, quia Deut.21.1. dicitur in terra. Si cadaver reperitur propè littus
units.tr: On the beheading of the heifer, the tractate Sotah in chapter 9 has the following. The section on the heifer whose neck is broken (עגלה ערופה), the beheading of the heifer, is read (in the synagogue) in the holy tongue, from Deuteronomy 21:1. For that rite to be performed, three, or according to R. Judah five, senators of Jerusalem must gather. If a corpse is found (whose slayer is unknown) hidden under a heap, or hanging from a tree, or floating in water, they do not behead the heifer, because Deuteronomy 21:1 says "in the land". If a corpse is found near the shore

units.la: aut propè aliquam urbem, in qua plurimi gentiles sunt, si illa nullum senatum habet non decollant. Cadavere reperto ad vicinas urbes mensurationem instituunt, ut sciant quænam propior sit, nam ex illa vitula afferri debet. Non metiuntur nisi ab illa urbe in qua Senatus aliquis est. Si cadaver æqualiter distans à duabus urbibus reperitur, tunc ambæ civitates iuvencam afferre debent. Mensura illa fiebat fune quì vocabatur Aphaskima, & qui debebat esse quinquaginta cubitorum Bab. Erubhin sol. 58.1. tales funes ex palmæ foliis conficiebant. Plin. lib. 16. c. 24. Hierosolyma verò hoc fruebatur privilegio, ut ad vitulum afferendum non obligaretur.
units.tr: or near some city in which many Gentiles live, and that city has no senate, they do not behead the heifer. When a corpse is found, they measure to the neighbouring cities, so that they may know which is nearer, for the heifer must be brought from that city. They measure only from a city in which there is some senate. If the corpse is found equally distant from two cities, then both cities must bring a heifer. The measurement was made with a rope called Aphaskima, which had to be fifty cubits long (Bab. Erubin 58.1); such ropes were made from palm leaves (Pliny, lib. 16, c. 24). Jerusalem, however, enjoyed this privilege: it was not obliged to bring a heifer.

units.la: §. Si caput hominis confossi reperitur in loco uno, corpus verò eius in loco altero, caput ad corpus devolvunt. Mensuratio incipitur secundùm R. Eliefer ab umbilico eius, secundùm Akibam à naso eius. Secundùm alium à collo eius.
units.tr: If the head of a slain man is found in one place and his body in another, they roll the head down to the body. The measurement begins, according to R. Eliezer, from his navel; according to Akiba, from his nose; according to another, from his neck.

units.la: §. Mensuratione factâ & dimissis Senatoribus Hierosolymitanis, qui mensurationi præesse debebant, adducitur Iuvenca bovis, quâ nullum officium aut labor adhuc factus est, carens omni vitio, & illam deducunt ad locum occisi (qui à S. Scriptura vocatur ײַ אִיתְנַחַל vallis Æthan.) Posteà illam securi à posteriori parte decollant; locusque ille illicitus fit ad sementem & cultum; poterit tamen ibi linum excuti & lapides effodi.
units.tr: When the measurement is made, and the Jerusalem senators who were to preside over the measuring have been dismissed, a heifer is brought, a young cow on which no work or labour has yet been done, free from every blemish. They lead it down to the place of the slain man, which Holy Scripture calls the valley of Eithan (נַחַל אֵיתָן). Afterwards they behead it from behind with an axe. That place becomes unlawful for sowing and cultivation, though flax may be beaten out there and stones dug up.

units.la: §. Vrbis illius (ex qua vitula adducta) Seniores debent manus suas lavare aquâ in loco decollationis eius, & dicere את שפכו ידינו לא הדם הזה ועינינו לא ראו : Manus nostræ nonfuderunt hunc sanguinem, nec oculi nostri viderunt. Et quia in mentem venire posset Seniores illius Senatus esse homicidas (saltem per accidens,) his addunt. Hic non venit in manus nostras, ut nos ipsum dimiserimus absque alimento, non ipsum vidimus, ut ipsum absque comitatu reliquerimus. Sacerdotes vero huic ceremoniæ præsentes dicunt. Propitius esto populo tuo Israel, quem redemisti, Domine, & non reputes sanguinem innocentem, in medio populi tui Israel.
units.tr: The elders of that city from which the heifer was brought must wash their hands in water at the place of its beheading, and say: "Our hands have not shed this blood, nor have our eyes seen it" [ידינו לא שפכו את הדם הזה ועינינו לא ראו]. And because it might come into someone's mind that the elders of that senate were murderers (at least by accident), they add: "It did not come into our hands, so that we would have let him go without food; we did not see him, so that we would have left him without an escort." The priests present at this ceremony say: "Be merciful to your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, O Lord, and do not impute innocent blood in the midst of your people Israel."

units.la: §. Si homicida invenitur antequam Iuvenca decollata fuerit, illam iterum ad suæ gregis pascua dimittunt. Postquàm autem decollata est, in loco decollationis etiam inhumatur, utpote quæ ab initio propter dubium adducta fuit, postquàm autem dubium expiatum est, illa sibi permittitur. Si vero decollatâ iuvencâ homicida reperitur omninò occiditur.
units.tr: If the killer is found before the heifer has been beheaded, they send it back again to the pasture of its flock. But once it has been beheaded, it is also buried in the place of beheading, since it had been brought in the first place because of the doubt; but once the doubt has been atoned for, it is left to itself. If, however, the killer is found after the heifer has been beheaded, he is put to death without fail.

units.la: §. משרבו הרציחנים כשלא עגלה ערופה Postquam numerus homicidarum multiplicatus fuit, cessavit iunicis decollatio. Nempe à quo venit Eliefer filius Dinai, quem antea Techinam filium Pharifæ vocaverant, deinde autem (ob sua latrocinia) בן רצחן filium homicidam nominarunt. (Postquàm enim tales scelerati ingruissent, non difficile erat cognoscere quinam illarum cædium Authores erant, ad quos alias in dubia cæde investigandos Iuvenca decollabatur.) Vide plura in Gem. ad Sotah c. 9.
units.tr: When murderers multiplied, the beheading of the heifer ceased [משרבו הרציחנים כשלא עגלה ערופה]. That is, from the time when Eliezer son of Dinai came, whom they had earlier called the son of Techina the Pharisee, and afterwards, because of his robberies, named "son of a murderer" [בן רצחן]. For once such wicked men had multiplied, it was not difficult to know who were the authors of those killings, and the heifer was otherwise beheaded for the investigation of a doubtful slaying. See more in the Gemara on Sotah c. 9.

units.la: §. Hæc vitulæ in folenni cæremonia decollatio à summo legislatore ob sapientissimas sanctissimaque causas instituta est, ut omnia, quamvis nos homunciones illas adeò complecti non queamus; probabilissimæ tamen nobis videntur illæ, quas Dodissimus Maymonides rufpatus est in More Nevoch. iii 40. & quas iam aliquo modo innuimus; Affert autem ille præcipuè duas rationes; 1. est [Hebrew] Quoniam vitula adduci debuit ex civitate proxima, ex qua ut plurimum erat qui eadem commiserat, & ita facilius dignosci potuit. 2. est. Quia propter istam in factum inquisitionem, seniorum ad id negotii egressionem, propter populi adstantis coronam, vitula acceptionem & decollationem, plurimi necessario iuter homines feruntur sermones; ac ita publica ista actione, vel cadis author invenitur, vel ab alio qui vel rei conscius est, vel famâ de eo audivit, proditur, vel ex signis cognoscitur, quod N. sit interfector. His adde quòd in publicis actionibus & animadversionibus homines multò vehementiùs à talibus facinoribus deterreantur, quàm si inquisitio simpliciter inter parietes fiat. Hinc publicam indagationem etiam gentes retinuerunt, quam Nostrates [Greek] nominant, & non exigui usus in Politia esse iam sæpius experientiâ comprobatum est.
units.tr: The beheading of the heifer in this solemn ceremony was instituted by the supreme lawgiver for most wise and most holy causes. Though we poor mortals cannot fully grasp all of them, those seem most probable to us which the most learned Maymonides set out in More Nevochim iii. 40, and which we have already hinted at in some way. He brings forward chiefly two reasons: (1) because the heifer had to be brought from the nearest city, from which for the most part came the one who had committed the deed, and so he could more easily be identified; (2) because on account of this inquiry into the deed, the going out of the elders on this business, the crowd of the people standing by, and the taking and beheading of the heifer, much talk necessarily passes among men; and so by this public action either the author of the killing is found, or he is betrayed by someone who either knows the matter or has heard of it, or is recognised from signs as the killer, N. To these add that in public proceedings and punishments men are far more strongly deterred from such crimes than if the inquiry were made simply behind closed doors. Hence even the nations have kept public inquiry, which the Greeks call by their own name, and experience has often proved that it is of no small use in the state.

units.la: §. Notatu insuper dignum est, quod Deus prohibuerit vallem in qua vitula decollata fuit, aut ut propriam possidendi, aut denique ulla ratione colendi; Magistratus enim cuius intererat summâ curâ impedire, ne aliqua suæ ditionis pars profana & inutilis redderetur, ita
units.tr: It is also worth noting that God forbade the valley in which the heifer was beheaded to be either possessed as one's own or cultivated in any way. The magistrate, whose concern it was, had to take the greatest care that no part of his territory was rendered profane and useless, and so

units.la: omnem operam ad homicidam detegendum collocare cogebatur, quod innuit R. David Kimchi, in lib. rad. ad vocem איתן. Illud fit ut cauti sint in regionibus & terminis suis, ut non inveniatur ibi interfectus כדי שלא יאבד מהם בכחר אחות Ut non pereat ab eis loco eleCtus possessionis eorum. Observa hic vallem איתן (sive ut Mischna exponit) נשפ asperam dici, non quod tunc talis erat, ut nonnulli existimarunt, sed quia talis futura erat, propter sublatum cultum, quo antea fertilis & pinguis florescebat. Nota etiam Iuvencam debuisse esse absque macula, quamq; nullus adhuc labor fatigaverat. Euripidi in Phoenissis etiam laudatur ποικίλος βόες, ἀδάμαστον πόλμα. Et Senecæ. Vacca quam non flexerat, Vomer, aut tardi iuga plaustri.
units.tr: he was compelled to devote every effort to detecting the killer. R. David Kimchi indicates this in the book of Roots, under the word איתן: "This is done so that they may be careful in their regions and borders, so that the slain man is not found there" [כדי שלא יאבד מהם בחר אחוזתם], "so that the chosen place of their possession does not perish from them." Observe here that the valley is called איתן (or, as the Mishnah explains it, נשף), "rough", not because it was such at that time, as some have thought, but because it was going to be such, on account of the abolished cultivation by which it had earlier flourished, fertile and rich. Note also that the heifer had to be without blemish, and one on which no labour had yet been done. Euripides in the Phoenissae also praises "a dappled heifer, an unbroken yoke" [ποικίλος βόες, ἀδάμαστον πόλμα]. And Seneca: "A cow which the ploughshare or the yoke of a slow wagon had not bent."

units.la: K.
units.tr: K.

units.la: קבים Kabim vide Cabi. de KARRÆIS vid. Buxt. Lex. Talm. p. 2113.
units.tr: Kabim [קבים], see Cabi. On the Karaites see Buxtorf, Lex. Talm. p. 2113.

units.la: KEDRON Vallis. De ea vide Ioseph. de bello lib. 5. c. 8. Singulis vicibus ac vacca rufa comburenda erat, ædificabant suppedaneum arcubus fulcitum à templo in montem Oliveti trans vallem Kedron. Maymon in Schekalim cap. 4. 8.
units.tr: KEDRON, Valley. On it see Josephus, De bello, bk. 5, ch. 8. Whenever a red heifer was to be burnt, they built a causeway, supported on arches, from the temple to the Mount of Olives across the valley of Kedron. Maimonides on Shekalim ch. 4, sect. 8.

units.la: §. E valle cineracea torrentis Kedron demessus fuit manipulus primitialis, tota ceremonia describitur in Menachot cap. 10. (vid. f. 1.) Sordes Hierosolymæ deducebantur Canali in vallem Kedron. Hieros. Nasir sol. 57. 4. Vt & sordes templi, quæ deinde hortulanis vendebantur, ad stercorandos hortos. Bab. Iom& sol.58. 2.
units.tr: §. From the ash-filled valley of the torrent Kedron the first-fruits sheaf was reaped; the whole ceremony is described in Menachot ch. 10 (see f. 1). The filth of Jerusalem was carried away by a channel into the valley of Kedron. Jerusalem Talmud, Nazir, sol. 57.4. Likewise the filth of the temple, which was afterwards sold to gardeners for manuring their gardens. Babylonian Talmud, Yoma, sol. 58.2.

units.la: קנים Kinnim Significat illas scutellas in quibus placentas & alia in templo exponebant, in mensa propositionis. Maymon. Beth Habech. cap.2. Sub finem.
units.tr: Kinnim [קנים] signifies those dishes in which the cakes and other things were set out in the temple, on the table of showbread. Maimonides, Beth Habechirah ch. 2, near the end.

units.la: קרי וכתיב Keri ucetif Quomodo ortum sit varię sunt sententię, sed probabilissima hæc est. Hieros. Taanit sol. 68. 1. dicitur שלש ספרים מצאו בעזרת tres libros inveniruntʒ in atrio, Librum מעוני, Librum ועשוי, & Librum היא. In uno invenerunt scriptum מעון אלהי קדם & in duobus מעונה אלהי קדם (Deut. 33. 27.) Hæc duo posteriora approbarunt, alterum vero reiecerunt. Rationi consentaneum est, hos tres libros triplici cœtui Iudæorum, in Iudæa, Babylonia, & Ægypto respondisse, præcipuè cum vox ועשוי, idem fermè sonet quàm septuaginta: vel saltem illum interpretem olcat. Nam in Massecet Sopherim cap. 1. 8. expressè dicitur ועשוי esse ex immutationibus istis, quas LXX. in legem invexerunt. Quid ni autem nobis Keri & Cetib ex hac exemplarium collatione ortum sit? præcipuè cùm ita conferre maximè in usu habuerint; ut ex exemplis quæ in loco citato proferuntur videre est.
units.tr: Keri and Ketiv. There are various opinions on how this arose, but this is the most probable. The Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit, sol. 68.1, says: they found three books in the court, the book "meoni," the book "veasui," and the book "hia." In one they found written "maon elohei kedem," and in two "meonah elohei kedem" (Deut. 33:27). These last two they approved, but the first they rejected. It is consistent with reason that these three books corresponded to the threefold assembly of Jews in Judaea, Babylon and Egypt, especially since the word "veasui" sounds almost the same as "septuaginta," or at least smells of that interpreter. For in Massechet Soferim ch. 1, sect. 8, it is expressly said that "veasui" is among those alterations which the Seventy introduced into the law. Why should not Keri and Ketiv also have arisen from this collation of copies? Especially since they made the greatest use of such comparison, as can be seen from the examples brought forward in the passage cited.

units.la: קטון Katon Minorennis quis sit. Vide Adolescentulam & Trumam.
units.tr: Katon [קטון]: who is a minor. See Adolescentula and Trumah.

units.la: קרקע בית רובק Karkang beth robbang Est fundus in quo quarta pars Cabi seri potest. Peah. 3. 6.
units.tr: Karkang beth robbang [קרקע בית רובק] is a plot of ground on which a fourth part of a kab of seed can be sown. Peah 3.6.

units.la: קפוטקיא Kapputkia Quid? Vid. in Q.
units.tr: Kapputkia [קפוטקיא]: what is it? See under Q.

units.la: L.
units.tr: L.

units.la: LABRUM הכיור erat inter propylæum sive porticum & altare, ac protrahebatur versus austrum, Middot cap.3.6. Vt plures Sacerdotes possent unâ manus & pedes abluere, pro duobus Epistomiis eius Ben Katin fecit duodecim. Ioma cap.3. Aruch. in דרים. Fecit hic Ben Katin insuper Labro Machinam, ne aquæ eius nocte polluerentur; ( Cl. Buxtorf. vertit, ne aquæ corrumpantur; An rectè vid. apud Scheringh mium Ioma pag. 70.) De Labri loco accuratè Maymon Hal. Beth Habbech c. 1. & c. 2.
units.tr: The LAVER, הכיור, stood between the portico (propylaeum) and the altar, and extended towards the south. Middoth ch. 3, sect. 6. So that several priests could wash their hands and feet together, Ben Katin made twelve spouts for its two taps. Yoma ch. 3; Aruch, under דרים. Ben Katin also fitted the laver with a covering, so that its waters would not be polluted at night. (Buxtorf translates this as "not be corrupted"; whether that is right, see Scheringham on Yoma, p. 70.) On the position of the laver, see Maimonides, Hal. Beth Habbechirah ch. 1 and 2 in detail.

units.la: LACERATIO vestium fieri potest, excepto סרבל pallio exteriori, & בגד הויעה Interula, in omnibus reliquis vestis partibus, etiamsi decem essent, sed vix ultrà palmæ longitudinem lacerant. Laceratio quæ propter parentes fit, nunquam resuitur; quæ autem propter alios post trigesimum diem &c.
units.tr: Garments may be torn, except the outer cloak (sarbal) and the inner tunic (begad hayoah), in all the other parts of the garment, even if there were ten of them; but they are torn scarcely more than a palm's length. A tear made for one's parents is never sewn up again; but those made for others may be repaired after thirty days, etc.

units.la: §. Laceratio vestium fit 1. in Lusu ob mortem parentum, principis, prætoris summi &c. statim ad egressum animæ si quis præsens sit, aut in primis septem diebus, si quis non peregrè est, vel triginta si procul abest, ad primam de mortuo famam. 2. in Blasphemiis & convitiis ad Deum, de hoc processu iudicantium Blasphemantem & vestes lacerantium vid. Blasphemum & Gemaram Babyl. ad Sanhed. c. 7. 10. 3. Si quis audiat videatve verba legis flammis ::bfumi, si audiat, urbes, templa, scholas vastari, aut comburi, populumque Iudaicum trucidari. §. Laceratio fit stando anteriùs tantùm non a latus, neque ad simbrias inferiores. Mayn. Hal. חאכ c.9. Vid.Cl.Buxt. L. T. p. 47.
units.tr: §. Garments are torn: (1) in mourning for the death of a parent, a prince, or a chief judge, etc., immediately at the departure of the soul if someone is present, or within the first seven days if one is not away from home, or within thirty days if one is far off, counted from the first report of the death; (2) in cases of blasphemy and abuse directed at God (on this procedure, in which judges condemn the blasphemer and those present tear their garments, see the tractate on blasphemy and the Babylonian Gemara on Sanhedrin ch. 7 and 10); (3) if someone hears or sees the words of the law burned in flames, or hears that cities, temples or schools are being laid waste or burned, or that the Jewish people are being slaughtered. §. The tearing is done standing, and only at the front, not at the side nor at the lower hem. Maimonides, Hal. ch. 9. See Buxtorf, L.T. p. 47.

units.la: LAMECH : Vide de eo plura in אבות ראשי Cl. Heideggeri. D. Leigtfootus locum Gen. ix. "sic explicat; Introduxerat Lamechus Bigamiam; vastaverat ea etiam universum mundum Gen.vi. Ob scelus tam nefarium, & exemplo suo homines infinitos perdens, percutit & pungit eum iustitia & vindicta divina, horrore & aculeo conscientiæ, ita ut gemens & eiulans coram bigamis suis, Adah & Zillah queratur & fateatur, se homicidam esse Caino longè cruentiorem. Is enim unum Abelem tantum occiderat, ille autem iuvenes senesque exemplo suo scelerato infinitos.
units.tr: LAMECH: see more about him in the Patriarchs of the learned Heidegger. Dr. Lightfoot explains the passage Gen. 9 thus: "Lamech had introduced bigamy, and by it he had also laid waste the whole world (Gen. 6). Because of so impious a crime, and by his example destroying countless men, he is struck and pierced by divine justice and vengeance, with the horror and sting of conscience, so that, groaning and wailing before his two wives, Adah and Zillah, he complains and confesses that he is a murderer far more bloody than Cain. For Cain had killed only one man, Abel, whereas Lamech, by his wicked example, destroyed countless young and old."

units.la: LAMPADES; & earum adoratio Vid. Cultus Templi.
units.tr: LAMPS, and their worship: see Temple worship.

units.la: LANIONUM PEDES practidit plantatio, ut & eorum qui comprimunt menstruatas. Hoc dictum exstat Bab. Beza sol. 25.2. Quæritur quomodo intelligendum sit? Mihi placet expositio Cl. Castelli. Ille qui vineam plantavit ex illa fructus non sumit, nisi præterierint tres anni præputii, & adveniat annus quartus, in quo fructus liciti fiunt: at Laniones non exspectant, donec bestiæ & pecora ad maturum tempus pervenerint & licita fiant, ut & nec Dominus menstruata donec purificata sit; illi deberent à plantatione suum officium petere & discere, qui sensus eò plausabilior est, quod ipsum etiam Aruch in ערוך referat, de Laniis vid. Kiddufchin sol.82.1.
units.tr: "Planting declares the feet of butchers, as also of those who press menstruating women." This saying is found in the Babylonian Talmud, Beza, sol. 25.2. The question is how it is to be understood. The explanation of the learned Castellus pleases me: "He who has planted a vineyard does not take its fruit until three years of uncircumcision have passed and the fourth year arrives, in which the fruits become lawful. But butchers do not wait until beasts and cattle reach maturity and become lawful, and likewise a husband does not wait for a menstruating wife until she is purified. They ought to seek and learn their duty from planting." This sense is the more plausible because Aruch, under ערוך, reports the same thing. On butchers see Kiddushin, sol. 82.1.

units.la: LAPIDATIO ita fiebat. Vnus officialium stabat ad ostium curiæ, tenens manu sudarium: unus item equo insidens, tantum inter ipsum & se intervalli relinquebat, ut eum commodè videre posset. Tum si quis se offerat, qui damnatum insontem esse doceat; iste sudarium quatit, eques concitato cursu damnatum retrahit, quin etiam si ipse quid solidi ad suam innocentiam demonstrandam afferat, quatuor aut quinquies reducitur. Si hoc modo innocentia eius comprobetur, liberum dimittunt; sin minus prodit ad lapidandum, (nam locus supplicii debuit esse extra locum iudicii; ne senatus videretur cædibus delectari) antecedente præcone atque clamante Vir iste N.N. prodit lapidandus,ob culpam hanc; testes faẗi sunt N.N. Quicunque demonstrare potest ipsum insontem esse, accedat. Quando decem cubitis abest à loco lapidationis iubetur confiteri; si nescit confiteri sic iubetur dicere תהא מתתי כפרה על כל עונותי Mors mea sit expiationi pro omnibus peccatis meis. Si sciat, se testium mendacio gravatum dicit. Sit mors mea expiationi pro omnibus peccatis meis, hoc uno excepto crimine. Quando à loco lapidationis abest quatuor cubitis, vestes ei detrahuntur; Maris anteriora velantur: mulieris & posteriora; secundùm sapientes verò mas etiam nudus lapidibus obrui potest.
units.tr: Stoning was carried out thus. One of the officials stood at the door of the court holding a handkerchief in his hand; another, mounted on a horse, kept such a distance between himself and the first that he could see him conveniently. Then, if someone offers himself who can show the condemned man to be innocent, the first shakes the handkerchief, and the horseman, riding hard, brings the condemned man back. Indeed, even if the man himself brings forward something solid to prove his innocence, he is brought back four or five times. If his innocence is proved in this way, they release him. If not, he goes out to be stoned. (The place of execution had to be outside the place of judgment, so that the court should not seem to take pleasure in bloodshed.) A herald goes before, crying: "This man N.N. goes out to be stoned for this offence; N.N. are the witnesses. Whoever can show that he is innocent, let him come forward." When he is ten cubits from the place of stoning, he is ordered to confess. If he does not know how to confess, he is ordered to say: "Let my death be an atonement for all my sins" [תהא מתתי כפרה על כל עונותי]. If he knows, he says that he is burdened by the lie of the witnesses: "Let my death be an atonement for all my sins, with this one crime excepted." When he is four cubits from the place of stoning, his garments are taken off. A man's front parts are covered, a woman's back parts; but according to the wise, a man may be stoned even naked.

units.la: §. Locus lapidationis altus erat שתי קומות geminam hominis longitudinem. Testium alter inde reum detrudebat ut in lumbos caderet. Si conversus in pectus esset, in lumbos convertebatur; si hac ratione mortuus esset, satisfa{ctum} erat legi, sin; alter lapidem sublatum in pedius immittebat; Si hoc ictu moreretur satisfactum erat legi, sin minus à toto Israële lapidabatur. Et deinde suspendebatur. Sanhed. cap.6.1.2.3.
units.tr: §. The place of stoning was high, "two men's heights" [שתי קומות]. One of the witnesses pushed the accused from it so that he fell onto his loins. If he fell onto his chest, he was turned over onto his loins. If he died in this way, the law was satisfied. If not, the second witness took a stone and dropped it on his chest. If he died from this blow, the law was satisfied; if not, he was stoned by all Israel. And then he was hanged. Sanhedrin ch. 6, sect. 1, 2, 3.

units.la: §. Hi lapidationis supplicio afficiuntur; Qui rem habet cum matre, uxore patris sui, nuru, mare, iumento; Blasphemus, idololatra; qui dedit ex semine suo Molecho, Pythomantis, hariolus, profanator Sabbathi, qui maledicit Patri, itemque matri suæ, qui violat puellam desponsatam, seductor qui ad apostasiam impellit, Magus, filius contumax. Sanhed. cap.7.4.
units.tr: §. These are liable to the punishment of stoning: whoever has intercourse with his mother, his father's wife, his daughter-in-law, a male, or a beast; a blasphemer; an idolater; he who gives of his seed to Molech; a necromancer, a soothsayer; a profaner of the Sabbath; he who curses his father or likewise his mother; he who violates a betrothed girl; a seducer who drives others to apostasy; a magician; a stubborn and rebellious son. Sanhedrin ch. 7, sect. 4.

units.la: §. Qui lapidatur illius bona evadunt, sed qui gladii supplicio afficitur, illius bona ad fiscum veniunt. Sanhed. c.11.4.
units.tr: §. The goods of one who is stoned pass to his heirs; but the goods of one who is put to death by the sword come to the fisc. Sanhedrin ch. 11, sect. 4.

units.la: §. De Lapidatione vide etiam Supplicia.
units.tr: On stoning, see also Supplicia.

units.la: LAPIDES varii memorantur apud Talmudicos. Bava Metzia sol.28.2. legitur de lapide erratum, qui erat lapis satis magnus, ad quem accurrebat qui aliquid perdiderat, & qui invenerat; prior ibi rem amissam signis describebat, posterior verò rem repertam publicabat. Bab. Scheviit cap.3. legitur de lapidibus humeri, i. e. qui aliter quàm humeris portari non poterant. De Lapidibus templi Kolis vid. Markolu. Magnes Iudæis non ignotus fuit, dicunt enim in Gem. Sanhed. sol.107.2. Ieroboamum vi huius lapidis vitulum suum in aere suspendisse. De lapide Lorarum vid. Horas. In Schabbat folio 66. fit mentio lapidis תקומה Resurrectionis, quem mulieres gravidæ collo gestabant ne abortirent. In Ioma sol.52. col.2. fit mentio lapidis שתיה fundamenti ex quo fundatum esse mundum & in quo Arcam constitisse putant. De eo V. Buxtorf: Differt. de Petra & Lex.Tal.p.2541.
units.tr: Various stones are mentioned among the Talmudists. In Bava Metzia fol. 28.2 we read of the erratum stone (lapis erratum), a fairly large stone to which both the one who had lost something and the one who had found it ran. The former described the lost object by its marks there, while the latter made the found object public. In Bab. Scheviit chap. 3 we read of shoulder stones, that is, stones which could be carried only on the shoulders. On the stones of the temple, Kolis, see Markolu. The magnet was not unknown to the Jews, for in Gem. Sanhed. fol. 107.2 they say that Jeroboam suspended his calf in the air by the power of this stone. On the stone of Lorarum see Horas. In Schabbat fol. 66 mention is made of the stone of resurrection [תקומה], which pregnant women carried around their necks so that they would not miscarry. In Ioma fol. 52 col. 2 mention is made of the foundation stone [שתיה], from which they think the world was founded and on which the Ark stood. On this see Buxtorf, Dissertation on the Rock, and the Lex. Tal. p. 2541.

units.la: de Læsionibus vid. Bava Kama c.8. & Maym. in Halacot חובל ומזיק. Generalis regula est, Qui ladit sociumsuum, tenetur ei satisfacere pro quinq; rebus, pro Damno, Dolore, Neglectione, Cessatione & Ignominia.
units.tr: On injuries, see Bava Kama chap. 8 and Maimonides in Halacot, "The one who wounds and the one who damages" [חובל ומזיק]. The general rule is: He who injures his neighbour is bound to make amends under five heads: for damage, pain, neglect, loss of work, and disgrace.

units.la: Lavare vid. Lotio:
units.tr: Lavare: see Washing.

units.la: Lazarus est nomen abbreviatum ab Eleazar, sæpius enim in dialecto Hierosolymitana, א in vocibus illa litera incipientibus eliditur, ut בר בא pro אבא אר, Item מר מי pro מאי אמר. Lazarus sive לעזר sæpius memoratur. Vt in Taanith sol.68.2. R. יסי בן ר' לעזר Lazar Ben R.Iosè. Chagigah sol.78.4. ר' לעזר בן יעקוב R. Lazar Ben Iacob. Qui deinde in Sotah sol.23; & 20.2. vocantur nomine suo non abbreviato. R. Eleazar.
units.tr: Lazarus is a name abbreviated from Eleazar, for in the Jerusalem dialect the letter א is often elided at the beginning of words, as בר בא for אבא אר, and likewise מר מי for מאי אמר. Lazarus, or לעזר, is mentioned often, as in Taanith fol. 68.2: R. Yose ben R. Lazar [ר' יסי בן ר' לעזר]. In Chagigah fol. 78.4: R. Lazar ben Jacob [ר' לעזר בן יעקוב]. These same men are then called by their unabbreviated name, R. Eleazar, in Sotah fol. 23 and 20.2.

units.la: Lectiones Biblicæ. Iudæi annuatim quinque legunt מגילות volumina in suis Synagogis, & quidem integra; primum est Canticum Canticorum, quod legunt in 8. die Paschatis, propter exitum ex Ægypto, & commonefactionem liberationis futuræ per Messiam, & quia materia hæc læta huic festo apprimè convenit. Secundum est Ruth, die secundo Pentecostes, ob Genealogiam Davidis, & quia in hoc libro agitur de frugibus terræ, quarum primitias offerre tum temporis soliti fuerunt. Tertium Threni Ieremiæ, quas die 9. mensis quinti ob captivitatem Babylonicam, & templi utriusque devastationem quæ hac die accedit, legunt. Quartum est Ecclesiastes, quem legunt 3. die festi Tabernaculorum, in memoriam nubium quæ operiebant tabernaculum. Adde quòd sicuti hoc festum memoriale est quòd Patres læti & contenti fuerint habitare in tabernaculis, ita hic liber docet omnia esse vana, ac unumquemque debere lætari & contentum esse iis quæ Deus ipsi largitur. Quintum est volumen Esthera, quod legi potest à die undecimo mensis Adar, usque ad diem 16. exclusivè in memoriam liberationis à crudeli voluntate Hamanis qui omnium Iudæorum exitium devoverat. In urbibus mœnibus cinctis communiter illám Megillam legebant die 15. mensis Adar, in pagis verò die 14.
units.tr: Biblical readings. The Jews read five volumes [מגילות] annually in their synagogues, and indeed whole. The first is the Song of Songs, which they read on the eighth day of Passover, because of the exodus from Egypt and the reminder of the future deliverance through the Messiah, and because this joyful material suits this festival very well. The second is Ruth, read on the second day of Pentecost, on account of the genealogy of David, and because this book deals with the fruits of the land, the firstfruits of which were customarily offered at that time. The third is the Lamentations of Jeremiah, which they read on the ninth day of the fifth month, on account of the Babylonian captivity and the devastation of both temples, which fell on this day. The fourth is Ecclesiastes, which they read on the third day of the Feast of Tabernacles, in memory of the clouds which covered the tabernacle. Add that just as this feast is a memorial that the fathers were glad and content to dwell in booths, so this book teaches that all things are vain, and that each person ought to rejoice and be content with what God grants him. The fifth is the volume of Esther, which may be read from the eleventh day of the month Adar up to the sixteenth day, exclusive, in memory of the deliverance from the cruel purpose of Haman, who had devoted all the Jews to destruction. In walled cities they commonly read that Megillah on the fifteenth day of the month Adar, but in villages on the fourteenth.

units.la: §. Si legerunt Megillam in Adar primo, & Annus intercalatus sit, illam iterum legunt in Adar secundo. (vid. Adar.) Megillah non legenda est memoriter, aut præposterè &c. non legenda est in libro vel charta pergamena, quæ scripta est auripigmento, minio, gummi, calacantho, sed in libro qui Assyriacè atramento scriptus est. Suo officio satisfecit, qui in libro Esther incepit ab init. 2. aut 3. capitis.
units.tr: §. If they read the Megillah in first Adar, and the year is intercalated, they read it again in second Adar (see Adar). The Megillah must not be read from memory, or out of order, etc. It must not be read from a book or a parchment scroll written with orpiment, red lead, gum or chalcanthum, but from a book written in Assyrian script with ink. He has discharged his duty who, in the book of Esther, began from the start of the second or third chapter.

units.la: §. Omnes idonei sunt ad legendam Megillam, excepto surdo, stulto & minorenni; Megillah non legitur, nec etiam circuncidunt, aut lavant, donec illucescat sol. Tota autem dies ad eius lectionem idonea est. Qui Megillam legit potest vel sedere vel stare; ubi benedicere soliti sunt benedicit. Diebus secundo & quinto septimanæ, (qui vocantur ימי הנסיסה) Tres sunt qui legunt. Qui aperit & convolvit librum legis, benedicit ante apertionem & postquàm clausit. Megillah c. 1. & 2. 4.
units.tr: §. All are fit to read the Megillah except the deaf, the fool and the minor. The Megillah is not read, nor do they circumcise or wash, until the sun has risen. The whole day is suitable for its reading. He who reads the Megillah may either sit or stand; where they are accustomed to bless, he blesses. On the second and fifth days of the week (which are called ימי הנסיסה [yemei hanesisah]) three read. He who opens and rolls up the book of the law blesses before the opening and after the closing. Megillah chap. 1 and 2, and 4.

units.la: §. De Lectionibus Biblicis plura vid. in הפטרות in H. In Megillah cap.4. adhuc hi generales Canones exstant. Qui legit legem, ne minus legat quàm tres versus ne prælegat interpreti plusquàm unum, vel in Prophetis (si vult) tres. Si tres illi sunt in tribus diversis sectionibus, legunt eas sigillatim. Transiliunt in lectione Prophetica, non legali. Historia Rubenis legitur non autem licet interpretari; Historiam Tamaris legunt & interpretantur. Historiam vituli priorem legunt & interpretantur. Historiam vero vituli secundam, (quæ incipit v.21. Cap.31. Exod.) legunt, at non interpretantur. Benedictionem Sacerdotum, historiam Davidis & Amnonis nec legunt nec interpretantur. Non legunt Haphtaram c. 16. Ezech.
units.tr: §. More on the biblical readings is found under הפטרות [haftarot] in H. In Megillah chap. 4 there still survive these general rules. He who reads the Law must not read fewer than three verses, and must not translate for the interpreter more than one verse; or, in the Prophets, if he wishes, three. If those three are in three different sections, they read them separately. They skip in the prophetic reading, but not in the legal. The history of Reuben is read, but it is not permitted to translate it; the history of Tamar they read and translate; the earlier history of the calf they read and translate. But the second history of the calf (which begins at v. 21 of Exodus chap. 31) they read but do not translate. The priestly blessing, and the histories of David and Amnon, they neither read nor translate. They do not read the Haphtarah of Ezekiel chap. 16.

units.la: Lecti, de ipsorum immunditie Vid.f.1. in I. Antiquitus lectum splendidum singuli in ædibus suis stratum habebant, nec ulli serviebat, nisi לשר הבית Principi vel Angelo domus, five laribus. Hic lectus vocatur ערש רגרא lectus bonæ fortunæ, Nedarim sol 56.1. Sanhed. sol.20.1. Inter diversas species lectorum celebrantur משה גלילית Lectus Galilæus, qui per partes complicari, & ab uno loco in alterum deferri solebat. Schabbat sol.47.2.
units.tr: On beds, and on their uncleanness, see f. 1 in I. Formerly each person had a splendid couch spread in his house, and no one used it except the Prince or Angel of the house, that is, the household gods. This couch is called ערש רגרא [ʿeres regara], the couch of good fortune; Nedarim fol. 56.1, Sanhed. fol. 20.1. Among the various kinds of couches the מטה גלילית [mittah galilit], the Galilean couch, is celebrated, which was customarily folded into parts and carried from one place to another. Schabbat fol. 47.2.

units.la: LEPROSUS.
units.tr: THE LEPER.

units.la: Nulla est differentia inter צרעת בסוד Leprosum inclusum & טהור מצורע leprosum absolutum, nisi נריעה ופריעה denudatio capitis, & discessio future vestis. Nulla est differentia inter leprosum post inclusionem mundum pronuntiatum, & eum qui antea absolute immundus pronuntiatus, iam mundus evadit, praeter rationem & oblationem avium. Megillah c.1.v.7.
units.tr: There is no difference between a leper who is shut in for observation (צרעת בסוד) and a leper who is pronounced clean outright (טהור מצורע), except the uncovering of the head and the tearing of the garments. Nor is there any difference between a leper who after his period of confinement is pronounced clean and one who was earlier pronounced unclean without qualification and now becomes clean, apart from the reckoning and the offering of birds. Megillah c.1.v.7.

units.la: §. Lepræ plagam in festo secundum R. Meir (Sacerdos) poterat להקל in meliorem partem diiudicare (ut dicat Tu mundus es,) sed non poterat להחמיר illam aggravare, (ut dicat immundus es,) sed secundum Sapientes, nec hoc nec illud licet. Moed Katon cap.1.5.
units.tr: §. According to R. Meir the priest, on the feast, he could judge a plague of leprosy more leniently, to the better part (saying, "You are clean"), but he could not make it more severe (saying, "You are unclean"). But according to the Sages, neither this nor that is permitted. Moed Katon cap.1.5.

units.la: §. In Leprosi mundatione haec peragenda erant; Afferre debuit Sacerdos pro Leproso tria pecora; sacrificium scilicet pro peccato (חטאת) & Sacrificium pro transgressione(אשם) & holocaustum. Pauper autem attulit sacrificium pro peccato e volucribus & holocaustum e volucribus. Deinde Sacerdos adstitit Sacrificio pro transgressione, atque ambas ei manus imposuit, atque mactavit. Duo autem Sacerdotes sanguinem excipiebant, unus in vasculo alter in manu; Hic posterior ad leprosum accedebat in conclave leprosorum (quod erat in angulo atrii mulierum occasum aestivum spectante Middot cap. 2.) eumque sistebat in porta orientali atrii Israelis quae Nikanoris appellata, caputque eius extendebat intra atrium, sanguinemque dabat super infimum auris eius; manum etiam intra atrium extendebat; & sanguinem pollici eius inspergebat, Idem faciebat respectu pedis. Alius deinde iisdem membris oleum infundebat. Ratio autem cur Leprosus exerto collo caput & aures protruserit in atrium redditur à Glossatore.
units.tr: §. In the cleansing of a leper these things had to be carried out. The priest had to bring three animals for the leper: a sin offering (חטאת), a guilt offering (אשם) and a burnt offering. A poor man, however, brought a sin offering of birds and a burnt offering of birds. Then the priest stood by the guilt offering and laid both hands upon it, and slaughtered it. Two priests received the blood, one in a small vessel and the other in his hand. The latter approached the leper in the chamber of the lepers (which was in the corner of the women's court facing the west, Middot cap. 2.), and set him in the eastern gate of the court of Israel, which is called Nicanor's, and he stretched out the leper's head within the court, and gave blood upon the lowest part of his ear; he also stretched out his hand within the court, and sprinkled blood upon his thumb. He did the same with respect to his foot. Another priest then poured oil upon the same limbs. The reason why the leper put his neck out and thrust his head and ears into the court is given by the glossator.

units.la: Porta Nikanoris fuit inter atrium mulierum & atrium Israelis. Iam verò in atrium Israelis non licuit cuiquam ingredi, pro quo non perfecta esset expiatio; atque è contra non licuit extra illud atrium proferre sanguinem sacrificii pro transgressione. Vide omnia accuratius in Negaim c. 14. & Maymon in מחוסרי כפרים cap. 4. & eius Glossa ad Sotah c. 1.
units.tr: The Gate of Nicanor was between the court of the women and the court of Israel. Now no one was allowed to enter the court of Israel for whom the atonement had not been completed; and conversely, it was not lawful to carry the blood of the guilt offering outside that court. See all these things more exactly in Negaim c. 14, and Maymon in "Those lacking atonements" cap. 4, and his gloss on Sotah c. 1.

units.la: §. Leprosi cultui divino interesse poterant in Synagogis civitatum moenibus non cinctarum, ita tamen ut semper aliqua esset differentia, inter ipsorum locum & aliorum, sed non poterant ingredi urbes muro cinctas, multò minus templum. Maymon Hal. Tephillah. Hinc primò à Sacerdote aliquo in provinciis visitabantur & purgabantur, & deinde die septimo mundationis suae iterum se monstrabant, aqua se abluebant, & tum demum Hierosolymas accedere poterant ad complementum purificationis suae perficiendum. Vid. Maymon in משנה ערוך c.11. Ordinariè omnes impuri summo mane se ante atria conserebant, & deinde post auditum sonum campanae à Praeside stationis ad portam Nikanoris deducebantur. Tamid. c.5.
units.tr: §. Lepers could attend divine worship in synagogues of the towns that were not walled, yet always with some difference between their place and that of others; but they could not enter walled cities, much less the temple. Maymon, Hilchot Tephillah. Hence they were first visited and cleansed by some priest in the provinces, and then on the seventh day of their cleansing they showed themselves again, washed themselves in water, and only then could they come to Jerusalem to complete their purification. See Maymon in the Mishneh Torah c.11. Ordinarily all the unclean gathered before the courts very early in the morning, and then, after the sound of the bell was heard, they were led by the overseer of the watch to the Gate of Nicanor. Tamid c.5.

units.la: §. De variis Leprae speciebus videatur Maymon in Hal. Tumneat. Tzor. Inter alia ibi haec habemus. צרעת est Nomen quod ὁμωνύμως dicitur citur & completitur species multas, quarum nulla similis est alteri. Nam 1. Albedo cutis vocatur nyx. 2. Casus pilorum quorundam capitis aut barbæ vocatur nyx. 3. Mutationem in vestibus & ædibus Lex etiam nyx vocat; illa autem non fuit res ordinaria in mundo, sed miraculum & portentum in Israele.
units.tr: §. On the various species of leprosy see Maymon in Hilchot Tumneat Tzora'at. There, among other things, we have the following: צרעת is a name that is used homonymously [ὁμωνύμως], and comprises many species, none of which is like another. For, first, the whiteness of the skin is called nega. Second, the falling of certain hairs of the head or beard is called nega. Third, the law also calls a change in garments and houses by the name nega; but that was not an ordinary thing in the world, but a miracle and a portent in Israel.
