units.la: §. Addamus hic illud quod in Ialkut in Iobum 28. 25. legitur. Homo constat ex dimidia aqua & dimidio sanguine. Quamdiu iustè vivit, non plus est aquæ in homine, quàm sanguinis; Quando peccat tunc vel aqua exuberat, & fit hydropicus, vel sanguis superat aquam, & fit leprosus.
units.tr: §. Let us add here what is read in Ialkut on Job 28:25. Man consists of half water and half blood. As long as he lives righteously, there is no more water in man than blood. When he sins, either the water overflows and he becomes dropsical, or the blood surpasses the water and he becomes a leper.

units.la: Leviathan Judæis est Balæna portentæ magnitudinis. Vid. Cl. Buxtorf. Synag. Iud. c. 36. & Lex.Talm. p. 1128.
units.tr: Leviathan to the Jews is a whale of prodigious size. See the most learned Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica c. 36, and Lexicon Talmudicum p. 1128.

units.la: Levitæ 4000 deputati erant ut essent portarii & custodes templi, & 4000 qui cantarent in templo; hi ita dividebantur ut per hanc hebdomadam illi, per aliam vero alii ministrarent; postquàm autem à Sabbatho ad Sabbathum ministrassent, & ministerio hebdomadario vesperâ Sabbathum præcedente absoluto, domum redibant vocabantur יוצאי השבת, illi vero qui his succedebant באי השבת Vid. Schindl. in Lex.
units.tr: The Levites, 4000 of them, were appointed to be gatekeepers and guardians of the temple, and 4000 to sing in the temple. These were divided so that one group served in one week and another in another. After they had served from Sabbath to Sabbath, and when their weekly duty was finished on the evening before the Sabbath, they returned home. Those who had gone off duty were called יוצאי השבת [yotze'ei hashabbat, "those going out of the Sabbath"], and those who succeeded them were called באי השבת [ba'ei hashabbat, "those coming in for the Sabbath"]. See Schindler in the Lexicon.

units.la: §. Levitarum urbium suburbia erant 3000 cubitis ab unoquoque latere, à mœnibus scilicet urbis & extrà, Num.35.4.5. Mille priores suburbia complectebantur, & bis mille posteriores erant pro agris & vineis; non licuit iflis civitatibus, mortuos intra hos terminos sepelire, Maym. Hal.Schemita vejobel Cap.13. Omnes civitates Levitarum erant civitates refugii; cum hac distinctione tamen à sex istis, proprie sic vocatis, quòd sex istæ refugium semper præberent & omnibus, suppeditabantque victum gratis; At Leviticæ non ita. Maym. Hal. Rozeach c.8.
units.tr: §. The suburbs of the Levitical cities extended 3000 cubits from each side, that is, from the walls of the city outwards, Num.35.4.5. The first thousand comprised the suburbs, and the second two thousand were for fields and vineyards. These cities were not permitted to bury the dead within these boundaries. Maym. Hal. Shemitah, chapter 13. All the Levitical cities were cities of refuge, but with this distinction from those six that are properly so called: the six always offered refuge to all, and supplied food free of charge, but the Levitical cities did not. Maym. Hal. Rozeach c.8.

units.la: §. Officium Portariorum erat aperire & claudere portas montis templi & atrii mulierum(reliquas portas enim per Sacerdotes aperiebantur) & per totum diem ibi curam adhibêre ne aliquid impuri templum ingrediatur, aut. quid fieret quod sanctitatem illius loci non decéret. Noctu verò debebant in 24 locis excubias agere in honorem templi (Maymon Beth Habech.cap.8) 1. Custodia erat in omnibus portis montis templi, in porta orientali, in porta septentrionali Tedi, in duabus portis Meridionalibus Hulda. in porta occidentali Copponiu: custodia etiam erat in angulis magni huius spatii quadrati Sancta loca cingentis. Portæ Parbar & Asuppim in plaga occidentali custodiâ opus non habebant. 2. Circa murum atria cingentem duæ erant Custodiæ in duobus angulis orientalibus, & duæ in duobus angulis occidentalibus. Erant deinde duæ portæ sed Levitæ in illis non excubabant, scil. Porta aquæ in cuius camera Abhtines custodiam curabant Sacerdotes, & Porta פרן in cuius conclavi Beth Mokad etiam Sacerdotes excubias agebant. In loco Septentrionali (orban vocato, è regione Sancti Sanctorum etiam Levitarum custodia erat, Item in parte meridionali è regione veli, item à tergo Sancti Sanctorum. Porta Nitsots custodiam habebat partim ex Levitis partim vero ex Sacerdotibus constantem. Singulis noctibus Præfectus custodum visitabat omnes custodias. Vid. הר איש הביח in A.
units.tr: §. The office of the gatekeepers was to open and shut the gates of the temple mount and of the women's court (for the other gates were opened by the priests), and throughout the whole day they took care there that nothing unclean should enter the temple, or anything else that would not befit the holiness of that place. By night, however, they had to keep watch in 24 places in honour of the temple (Maymon, Beth Habechirah, cap.8). 1. There was a guard at all the gates of the temple mount: at the eastern gate, at the northern gate Tedi, at the two southern gates Hulda, and at the western gate Copponiu. There was also a guard at the corners of this large square space surrounding the holy places. The gates Parbar and Asuppim on the western side had no need of a guard. 2. Around the wall enclosing the courts there were two guard posts at the two eastern corners and two at the two western corners. Then there were two gates, but the Levites did not keep watch at them, namely the Water Gate, in whose chamber the priests kept guard, called Abhtines, and the gate פרן, in whose room the priests also kept watch, called Beth Mokad. In the northern place, called orban, opposite the Holy of Holies, there was also a guard of Levites; likewise on the southern side, opposite the veil, and likewise behind the Holy of Holies. The Gate of Nitsots had a guard consisting partly of Levites and partly of priests. Each night the commander of the guards visited all the guard posts. See הר איש and הביח in A.

units.la: §. De Levitis Cantoribus vid. Musica.
units.tr: §. On the Levite singers see Musica.

units.la: §. Recensèt Ialkut in Psalm.137. Babylonios petiisse à Levitis ut carmen aliquod testudine psalterent, sed pramorderunt sibi pollicem manus dextera, dicentes אין נשיר Quomodo canemus? Sapit historia fabulam. Causa cur Levitæ non etiam in divisione terræ recensiti fuerint, est, quia Deus est Hæreditas ipsorum, nec debent in bellum ire quia sunt חיל ה. Maym.H.Schemita c. ult.
units.tr: §. Ialkut on Psalm 137 relates that the Babylonians asked the Levites to play some song on the lyre, but they bit off the thumb of their right hand, saying אין נשיר "How shall we sing?" The story smacks of fable. The reason why the Levites were not also counted in the division of the land is that God is their inheritance, and they ought not to go to war, because they are the army of the Lord. Maym. H. Shemitah last chapter.

units.la: LEVIRATUS. De hoc iure vid. Calcei extraßionem.
units.tr: LEVIRATE. On this law see Calcei extractionem.

units.la: Erat etiam in usu apud Patres qui ante datam legem vixerunt, ut patet exemplo filiorum Iudæ, Er, Onan & Schela. Genes. xxxviii. 7. 8. Probabile est ipsos hanc consuetudinem habuisse מבית דינו של שם à Consistorio Semi, non autem ex moribus Cananæorum, ut alii volunt.
units.tr: This custom was also in use among the Fathers who lived before the law was given, as is clear from the example of the sons of Judah, Er, Onan and Shelah. Genesis xxxviii. 7, 8. It is probable that they had this custom from the consistory of Shem, and not from the morals of the Canaanites, as others want.

units.la: Fratres uterini ex eadem matre non eodem patre progeniati, ad hoc ius non obligantur. Maym.in Hal.Iabom Vechaliza. cap.1. Fratres ex matre tantùm non censentur pro fratribus, aut in materia leviratus, nam illi sunt quasi non essent fratres, cùm non sit fraternitas quæ à patre non est. Nec contrarium probat exemplum Noemi Ruth. i. ii. quæ nutus suas ita alloquitur, an in utero meo adhuc sunt filii, Respondet enim Aben Esra illud ex ingenti amore erga nurus dici; quasi diceret, si ego unquam filios haberem, ego illos vobis traderem.
units.tr: Brothers born of the same mother but not of the same father are not bound to this law. Maym. in Hilchot Yibbum ve-Chalitzah cap.1. "Brothers only by the mother are not counted as brothers in the matter of levirate, for they are as if they were not brothers, since there is no brotherhood that does not come from the father." Nor does the example of Naomi in Ruth i. 11 prove the contrary, where she addresses her daughters-in-law thus: "Are there yet sons in my womb?" For Aben Ezra replies that this is said out of great love for her daughters-in-law, as if she were saying, "If I ever had sons, I would give them to you."

units.la: Data lege accedit Leviratui circumstantia de Extractione Calcei, quæ si fuisset ante legem Onan Thamarem non duxisset, cum illud invitus fecerit.
units.tr: The law is accompanied by the circumstance of the drawing off of the shoe. Had this existed before the law, Onan would not have taken Tamar as his wife, since he did it unwillingly.

units.la: Lex distinguitur in תורה שבכתב legem scriptam, & תורה שבעל פה oralem vid. Schaare Orah in lit. ה. sol. 4. Quicunque remittit studium legis, non erit in eo facultas consistendi in die angustiæ Beracot sol. 36. Non confirmantur verba legis nisi in eo שמשים עצמו כמי שאינו qui se ipsum ducit quasi pro nihilo. Sotah sol. 21. 2. Vid. Cl. Buxtorf. Florileg. & Lex. Talm. p. 983.
units.tr: Law is divided into the written law [תורה שבכתב], the written law, and the oral law [תורה שבעל פה], the oral law. See Schaare Orah under the letter ה, fol. 4. "Whoever neglects the study of the law will have no ability to stand firm in the day of distress." Berachot, fol. 36. "The words of the law are not confirmed unless he makes himself as one who regards himself as nothing. Sotah, fol. 21.2." See Cl. Buxtorf, Florilegium, and Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 983.

units.la: §. Legis lucem infinitis encomiis celebrant vid. Berefchit Rabba fect. 3. ubi dicitur, In historia creationis quinquies scribitur lux; secundum quinq, quintades legis.
units.tr: § The praises of the light of the law are sung in countless ways. See Bereshit Rabba, section 3, where it is said: In the account of creation, light is written five times; this corresponds to the five books of the law.

units.la: §. De legis studio plura habemus in Hierof. Beracot p. 3. c. 2. Inter alia R. Simeon Ben Iochai dicit; Si fuissemus in monte Sinai hora illa qua lex data fuit, petiissemus à Deo, ut homini creasset תרין מופין duo ora, unum ad perpetuum studium legis, alterum vero ad vitæ necessitates. Et R. Ismael loco citato non tantâ erga legem religione ducitur, sic enim de illa loquitur; In verbis legis est איסור prohibitio, & היתר perhibitio sive permissio, item levia & gravia, sed verba nostrorum Doctorum כולם חמורים omnia gravia sunt.
units.tr: § We have more on the study of the law in Jerusalem Berachot, p. 3, ch. 2. Among other things, R. Simeon ben Yochai says: If we had been on Mount Sinai at the hour when the law was given, we would have asked God to make for man two mouths [תרין מופין], one for constant study of the law and the other for the needs of life. R. Ishmael, in the place cited, does not hold the law in such reverence; for he speaks of it thus: In the words of the law there is prohibition [איסור] and permission [היתר], likewise light and heavy; but the words of our teachers, all of them [כולם חמורים], are heavy.

units.la: §. Liber legis in quo sunt duo errata in unaquaque pagina, emendabitur: si tria reponetur, vel occultabitur. Menachot sol.29.2. Omnia corpora hominum vaginæ sunt: beatum illud corpus לדוכי דהוי דהופתקי דאוריתא quod meretur ut sit vagina legis. Sanhed. sol.39.2.
units.tr: § A book of the law in which there are two errors on each page will be corrected; if three are put in, or it is hidden. Menachot, fol. 29.2. "All human bodies are sheaths: blessed is that body [לדוכי דהוי דהופתקי דאוריתא] which deserves to be a sheath for the law." Sanhedrin, fol. 39.2.

units.la: §. Legem Græce scripserunt quibusque Seniores pro Rege Ptolomæo, fuitque ille dies acerbus Israeli sicuti dies quo factus est vitulus, eò quod lex non potuit verti, secundùm quòd ei est necessarium. Maff.Sopherim c.1. Hoc etiam labefactat quæ vulgo de LXX. Interpretibus dicuntur, de quibus vid. Interpretes.
units.tr: § The law was written in Greek for King Ptolemy by the elders, and that day was as bitter for Israel as the day the calf was made, because the law could not be translated as it needed to be. Maff. Sopherim, ch. 1. This also overturns what is commonly said about the Seventy translators; on these see Interpreters.

units.la: §. Incolæ civitatis, si vendiderint plateam civitatis, pecuniis eius comparare tenentur Synagogam, si vendiderint Synagogam comparare arcam: si arcam, comparare מטפחות ventralia (ita vocant pretiosa illa lintea quibus librum legis involvere solebant, vid. Sanhed. 100.1. & Kilaim cap.9.) si vendiderint ventralia, debent comparare libros, si libros vendiderint debent comparare librum legis; at si vendiderint legem, ne comparent libros, & ita de cæteris. Megillah c.2.1.
units.tr: § If the inhabitants of a city sell the city square, they are bound to buy a synagogue with the money; if they sell the synagogue, they must buy the ark; if the ark, they must buy the wrappings [מטפחות] (so they call those precious linen cloths in which they used to wrap the book of the law; see Sanhedrin 100.1 and Kilayim ch. 9). If they sell the wrappings, they must buy books; if they sell the books, they must buy the book of the law; but if they sell the law itself, they need not buy books, and so on for the rest. Megillah ch. 2.1.

units.la: §. In Bereschit Rabba §.20. fit mentio תורה מאיר ר' legis R. Meir, & dicitur in illa quædam aliter se habuisse quàm in lege Mosis, (vid. Adam.) quæritur quid illa lex R. Meir fuerit? Nobis videtur per legem R. Meir solum intelligi volumen aliquod legis, in cuius margine vel chartulis interfertis, criticas suas nugas & argutias Rabbinus ille scripserat. Vel ita vocari ipsius commentarium quem in legem scripsit.
units.tr: § In Bereshit Rabba §20 there is mention of the Torah of R. Meir [תורה מאיר ר'], and it is said that in it some things were otherwise than in the law of Moses (see Adam). The question is what the law of R. Meir was. It seems to us that by the law of R. Meir we should understand only some volume of the law, in whose margins or inserted sheets that rabbi had written his critical trifles and subtleties. Or else it is so called because it is his commentary on the law that he wrote.

units.la: §. De Promulgatione decem præceptorum vid. Decem.
units.tr: §. On the promulgation of the ten commandments, see Decem.

units.la: §. Quo charactere Lex Dei digito tabulis lapideis insculpta, atque adeò tota sacra Biblia exarata fuerint, disceptatur inter doctos. Quidam literas Hebraicas hodiernas quibus sacer codex iam ubique descriptus est, esse genuinas ac primigenias illas quibus Deus Scriptoresque sacri usi fuère, existimant; Atq; in hanc sententiam descendunt ferè omnes, aut saltem præcipui inter Hebræorum Magistros. Alii hanc prærogativam deferunt characteribus Samaritanis, quos Esdram abrogasse in reditu captivitatis Babylonicæ ac in eorum locum hodiernos ab Assyriis mutuatos substituisse asserunt; Atque huius sententiæ inter Hebræos pauciores sunt Patroni. Rationes pro & contrà Videsis apud Cl. Buxtorf. differt. de literis Hebræorum & Ioh. Leusden. de literarum Hebraicarum antiquitate.
units.tr: § It is debated among the learned in what character the law of God was inscribed by the finger of God on the stone tablets, and indeed the whole holy Bible written. Some think that the Hebrew letters now in use, in which the sacred codex is now everywhere copied, are the genuine and original ones that God and the sacred writers used; and almost all, or at least the leading masters among the Hebrews, go along with this view. Others grant this privilege to the Samaritan characters, asserting that Ezra abolished them at the return from the Babylonian captivity and substituted in their place the present letters borrowed from the Assyrians; and there are fewer defenders of this view among the Hebrews. For the arguments for and against, see Cl. Buxtorf, the dissertation on the letters of the Hebrews, and Johannes Leusden on the antiquity of the Hebrew letters.

units.la: Libamen vid. Sacrificia.
units.tr: Libation: see Sacrifices.

units.la: Lychni vid. Lampades.
units.tr: Lamps: see Lampades.

units.la: Lilith Lamia nocturna. Vid. Buxtorf. Synag. Jud. 80. Lex. Talm. p.1140. Nidda sol. 24. 2. Erubbin sol. 100 2. Kircheri Oedip. I. 1321. Selden. de Diis Syris 249. Gregorii Opus p.97.
units.tr: Lilith, a night-demon or lamia. See Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica, 80; Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 1140; Nidda, fol. 24.2; Eruvin, fol. 100.2; Kircher, Oedipus, I, 1321; Selden, De Diis Syris, 249; Gregory, Opus, p. 97.

units.la: Ligna. Apud Talmudicos multa genera lignorum sunt quæ vocantur תמר vid. L.Talm. Buxt. p.788. Memoratur etiam in Schabbat sol.54.2. in Mischna quædam ligni vel radicis species תמן vocata, quam ovibus in nares ingerebant, ut sternutarent, & vermes quas in cerebro habent ejicerent. In Targum Ionathanis Gen. 50.1. legitur tur de pretiosissimo quodam lignorum genere, quod שנדפין vocatur, & ex quo vult factum fuisse lectum Iacobi.
units.tr: Wood. Among the Talmudists there are many kinds of wood called [תמר]; see Lexicon Talmudicum, Buxtorf, p. 788. There is also mention in Shabbat, fol. 54.2, in the Mishnah, of a certain species of wood or root called [תמן], which they used to push up the nostrils of sheep so that they would sneeze and expel the worms they have in their brains. In the Targum of Jonathan on Genesis 50.1 there is a reading about a very precious kind of wood, called [שנדפין], from which Jacob's bed is said to have been made.

units.la: §. Referemus hic quomodo versati sint circa ligna altaris. Præceptum expressum exstat Lev.6.13. ignem altaris nunquam extingui debère. Videtur etiam divinam providentiam Iudæos in illo exequendo adiuvasse, notat enim Talmud in Avoth cap. 5. pluviam ignem altaris nunquam extinxisse. Certè secundum Maym. in Tamid. Umusaph cap.2. ille vapulare debuit, qui præsumpsisset ignem illum ex intentione extinguere: quod satis offendit ipsos non negligenter hoc præceptum de ignis perpetuitate observasse. De Festo ξυλοφορίαι quo ligna de quibus loquimur afferebantur vid. Ioseph. de bello libro 2. cap. 31. Maffecet Taanit cap.4. recenset novem dies speciales in anno, ad hoc destinatos ut novem familiæ in illis ligna afferrent. 1. die Nisan afferebant Arahi filii; die 2. Tammus filii Davidis, filii Iudæ; die 5. mensis Abh filii Parosch; die 7. eiusdem mensis filii Ionadab filii Rechab: & die 10. filii Senaah; die 15. filii Zattu; die 20. filii Paleoth Moab. Die 20. mensis Elul filii Addin; 1. Thebet iterum familia Parosch.
units.tr: § Here I shall relate how they dealt with the wood for the altar. An express precept exists at Leviticus 6.13 that the fire of the altar must never go out. It also seems that divine providence helped the Jews in carrying this out, for the Talmud in Avoth, ch. 5, notes that the rain never put out the fire of the altar. Certainly, according to Maimonides in Tamid, Umusaph, ch. 2, anyone who presumed to put out that fire on purpose ought to be flogged; which sufficiently shows that they did not neglect this precept about the perpetuity of the fire. On the festival of wood-carrying [ξυλοφορίαι], at which the wood we are speaking of was brought, see Josephus, On the War, book 2, ch. 31; Massechet Taanit, ch. 4. It lists nine special days in the year, set apart so that nine families might bring wood on them: on the 1st of Nisan the sons of Arah brought it; on the 2nd of Tammuz the sons of David, the sons of Judah; on the 5th of the month Av the sons of Parosh; on the 7th of the same month the sons of Jonadab, son of Rechab; and on the 10th the sons of Senaah; on the 15th the sons of Zattu; on the 20th the sons of Paleth-Moab. On the 20th of the month Elul the sons of Addin; and on the 1st of Tevet again the family of Parosh.

units.la: §. Ligna hac ratione allata primum seponebantur in לשכת דיר העציס (onclave lignorum quod erat in angulo septentrionali atrii mulierum, & deinde ab illis Sacerdotibus qui ob aliquod vitium ad sanctiorem cultum ineptiores erant perscrutabantur an nulli inessent vermes, (Middot c.2.) quæ ab illis immunia erant deinde transportabantur in aliud conclave, quod in Middot cap. 5. etiam לשכת העץ vocatur, item conclave Parhedrin, ut deinde ligna ad continuum usum ad manus effent. Illa ligna vero quæ vermibus corrosa erant, poterant adhiberi ad assationes, coctiones & alias præparationes carnium sacrificiorum; item pro igne quo se refocillabant tempore brumæ Sacerdotes & Levitæ.
units.tr: § The wood brought in this way was first stored in the [לשכת דיר העציס], the wood-store chamber (onclave lignorum), which was in the north corner of the women's court. Then the priests who were less fit for the holier service because of some defect examined it to see whether any worms were in it (Middoth ch. 2). What was free of them was carried into another chamber, which in Middoth ch. 5 is also called [לשכת העץ], the wood chamber, and also the chamber of Parhedrin, so that the wood would then be at hand for continual use. But the wood that was eaten away by worms could be used for roasting, boiling and other preparations of the sacrificial meat, and also for the fire by which the priests and Levites warmed themselves in winter.

units.la: LINGUÆ an æternæ sint disputatur in Cofri p.25. Plurimarum peritiam maximè necessariam esse ostendit Seld. Syned.11.244.395. præcipuè autem Hebraicam utilem & necessariam esse probat Cofri 131.303. Cl. Buxt.VIII. Differt.I. De Linguarum confusione varietate, numero; Idem. VII. Differt.52. Seniores Synedrii magni debebant plurimarum linguarum, 70.nempe,cognitionem habere,ne opus haberet Senatus audire quenquam ex ore interpretis. Vid. Maym.Sanhed. cap.1. §. LXX. linguas calluit Mardochai unus ex magnis Senatoribus, illud ignorarunt שני שרפיים Duo Tarfii (vel æriffices) & loquuti sunt in lingua Tursi. Megillah. sol.13.2.
units.tr: TONGUES. Whether languages are eternal is disputed in Cofri, p. 25. Selden, Synedrion, 11.244.395, shows that knowledge of many languages is especially necessary; Cofri, 131.303, proves that Hebrew in particular is useful and necessary. Cl. Buxtorf, Dissertation VIII, I, on the confusion, variety and number of languages; the same author, Dissertation VII, 52. The elders of the great Sanhedrin were to have a knowledge of very many languages, namely seventy, so that the Senate should not need to hear anyone through an interpreter. See Maimonides, Sanhedrin, ch. 1. Mordecai, one of the great senators, knew seventy languages; but they did not know that two Tarsians (or soothsayers) spoke in the language of Tursi. Megillah, fol. 13.2.

units.la: §. De Linguis vid. Gracia.
units.tr: § On languages, see Gracia.

units.la: לקט Leket Specilegium, eius definitio est הנותר בשעה הקצירה illud quod decidit cùm seges demetitur, omne itaque illud quod ex manibus messorum violentia quadam excussum est לקט esse non potest, nisi forsan illud quod intra manus messoris est. Vid. Bartenoram ad Peah. 4.10. Si pauperes post messores incedentes, reperiunt foramina formicarum in quæ congestum est frumentum, spicæ superiores sunt pauperum, quia præsumuntur ex hac messe decidisse; inferiores verò & quæ iam nigrescunt sunt Domini agri. Ibid.v.11.
units.tr: לקט [Leket], gleaning. Its definition is [הנותר בשעה הקצירה], that which is left behind at the time of harvest. Therefore everything that falls out of the reapers' hands through some violence is not leket, unless perhaps it is what is still within the reaper's hand. See Bartenora on Peah 4.10. If the poor, coming after the reapers, find grain heaped into the holes of ants, the upper ears belong to the poor, since they are presumed to have fallen from this harvest; but the lower ones, and those already turning black, belong to the owner of the field. Ibid., v. 11.

units.la: §. Omnia quæ in loco acervi frumenti, in quo pauperes nihil adhuc legerunt, in terra iacentia reperiuntur, pauperibus cedunt. Peah. s.1. si ventus quædam ex manipulis dispergit, metiuntur illa an possint mensuram spicilegii conficere, si possunt, relinquunt pauperibus. Mensura autem illa est quatuor Cabi ex Coro, sive 30. seæ. Culmus sive spica quæ cum vicina non demetitur, sed sola relicta erecta stat, Domini agri est, si modò ad reliquarum spicarum magnitudinem creverit, sin pauperum est. Ibid.
units.tr: §. Everything that lies on the ground in the place of a heap of grain, where the poor have not yet gathered anything, belongs to the poor. Peah s.1. If the wind scatters some of the sheaves, they measure whether those can make up a gleaning measure; if they can, they leave them to the poor. That measure is four cabs of the cor, or 30 seahs. A stalk or ear which is not reaped with its neighbours but stands alone, left upright, belongs to the owner of the field, if indeed it has grown to the size of the other ears; otherwise it belongs to the poor. Ibid.

units.la: §. Si commixtæ fuerint quædam spicæ cum acervo frumenti, pater familias profert duas spicas, (secundum Ionathan Gen. 41. 47. talis spica facit duos pugillos) & ad unam dicit, Si tu ad spicilegium pertinet bene est, & hac altera erit decima eius. Deinde primam tradit pauperi, alteram Sacerdoti. Peah.s.2. Maym. Com. Non demetendum est unà cum frumento leguminis illud genus quod נזיו vocatur, ne spicilegium illius pauperes impediat. Si quis Paterfamiliâs ipsemet opus habet angulo agri & spicilegio, in itinere constitutus, aut aliâ necessitate adactus, domum reversus illud iterum restituere debet. Secundùm Maymonidem verò dare poterit, quod libuerit. Peah.5.4.
units.tr: §. If some ears are mixed in with a heap of grain, the householder brings out two ears (according to Jonathan on Gen. 41.47, such an ear makes two handfuls) and says to one of them, "If you belong to the gleaning, well and good; and this other will be its tithe." Then he gives the first to the poor man and the other to the priest. Peah s.2. Maym. Com. The kind of pulse called [נזיו] should not be reaped together with the grain, lest it hinder the poor from gleaning. If a householder himself needs a corner of the field and the gleaning, being on a journey or compelled by some other necessity, he must restore it again when he returns home. According to Maimonides, however, he may give whatever he pleases. Peah 5.4.

units.la: §. Nemo debet operarios conducere, eâ conditione, ut filii ipsorum post ipsos spicilegium colligant. Ille qui non permittit pauperibus colligere, aut permittit huic & non alteri, aut unum ex illis adiuvat, æstimatur defraudare pauperes. ibid.v.6.
units.tr: §. No one should hire workers on the condition that their sons gather the gleaning after them. He who does not allow the poor to glean, or allows it to one and not to another, or helps one of them, is judged to defraud the poor. Ibid. v.6.

units.la: A quo tempore הנמושות Senes incipiunt ad spicilegium ire, & postquàm descendit pluvia fecunda (postquàm appropinquaverit dies 7. Octob.) cuivis spicilegium facere licet. Quia præsupponitur tunc pauperes sufficienter collegisse,& deinde ne ea quæ ab ipsis telinquuntur corrumpantur. Peah.8.1.
units.tr: From the time when the aged [Senes, הנמושות] begin to go out to the gleaning, and after the fruitful rain has come down (when the 7th of October draws near), it is permitted to anyone to make a gleaning. For it is then presupposed that the poor have gathered sufficiently, and this is done so that what is left by them is not spoiled. Peah 8.1.

units.la: Lotio. Erat Lavacrum in Bethania. Vid. Bethania. Sacerdotes ante cultûs templi inchoationem aquis se purificare debebant. Vid. Labrum & Cultum Templi. De Summi Sacerdotis quinque lotionibus in die Expiationis vid. Expiationis festum, & Iomá c.3.
units.tr: Washing. There was a laver in Bethany. See Bethany. Priests had to purify themselves with water before the beginning of the temple service. See Laver and Temple Worship. On the five washings of the high priest on the Day of Atonement, see Feast of Atonement and Yoma c.3.

units.la: §. In nuptiis adhibuerunt diversa vasa ad lavandum manus, erat כולא משי Vas maiusculum ex quo se lavabant omnes & משכילתא כלתא משיא Vas minusculum ex quo se lavabat Sponsa, & ut Gloss. etiam digniores convivæ. Schabb.sol.77.2.
units.tr: §. At weddings they used different vessels for washing the hands: there was the [כולא משי], a larger vessel from which all washed, and the [משכילתא כלתא משיא], a smaller vessel from which the bride washed, and, as the Gloss says, the more honourable guests too. Schabb. sol.77.2.

units.la: §. Quando totum corpus inter lavandum immergebatur, lotio vocatur טבילה (vid. Baptismus.) Si autem pedes & manus simpliciter abluuntur, tunc illa lotio vocatur קירוע, quæ fiebat secundùm Iarchi ad Exod.30.19. Imponendo manum dexteram, super dexterum pedem, manum sinistram super sinistrum pedem, & ita lavando.
units.tr: §. When the whole body was immersed in washing, the washing is called [טבילה] (see Baptism). If, however, the feet and hands are simply rinsed, then that washing is called [קירוע], which, according to Jarchi on Exod. 30.19, was done by placing the right hand on the right foot and the left hand on the left foot, and washing thus.

units.la: §. De manuum lotione eleganter disseruit Cl.Pocok. in porta Mosis 376. Miscel. Item Cl. Buxt.vIII. differt.397. de illa quoque tractat codex Iadaim.c.2. Scaliger contra Serrarium c.7. Drusius Marci 7. §. Qui-
units.tr: §. The washing of hands has been discussed elegantly by Cl. Pocock, Porta Mosis 376, Miscel. Likewise Cl. Buxtorf, VIII, differt. 397, and the tractate Iadaim c.2 also treats of it. Scaliger against Serrarius c.7. Drusius on Mark 7. §. Qui-

units.la: §. Quicunque comedit panem absque lotione manuum, perinde est אישׁ על באלו בא ... ac si rem haberet cum muliere meretrice. R. Eliezer dicit, quicunque vilipendit lotionem manuum extirpatur ex hoc mundo; In lotione manuum autem Raf obvervari vult, ut in aquis purioribus (h.e. ante cibum sumptum) eleventur manus sursum, ut aquæ usque ad brachia defluant, ne à coniunctura revertantur, & iterum manus polluant: Aquam autem secundam purificare aquam primam, & ut aqua ante prandium super manus effundatur duabus vicibus. Sotah. sol.4.2. Non lavabant manus super terram, i.e. ut aqua decidant in terram, sed in vas. Schylchan Aruch p.1.sol.3, col.3.
units.tr: §. Whoever eats bread without washing his hands is as though [אישׁ על באלו בא ...] he had to do with a harlot. R. Eliezer says, whoever despises the washing of hands is cut off from this world. Raf, however, wishes that in the washing of hands one observe that, with purer water (that is, before the food is taken), the hands be lifted up so that the water flows down to the arms, lest it run back from the joints and pollute the hands again; and that the second water purifies the first; and that the water be poured over the hands twice before the meal. Sotah sol.4.2. They did not wash hands over the ground, that is, so that the water falls on the ground, but into a vessel. Shulchan Aruch p.1, sol.3, col.3.

units.la: §. In festis manus tenentur lavare, ante profanorum esum, ut & decimarum & Trumæ, ante esum vero sancti & sacrificii pro peccato manus intingere; cuius manus immundæ sunt, immundum est & corpus. Chagigah cap.2. Qui lavavit cum intentione profana solum comedendi, decimas edere non debet; qui cum intentione edendi decimas, Trumam edere non debet; Qui lavavit respectu ad gravius habito, levius eadem actione licitum sibi fecit. Ibid.
units.tr: §. On festivals the hands must be washed before eating ordinary food, as well as tithes and Terumah; before eating holy food and the sacrifice for sin, the hands are to be dipped. Whose hands are unclean, his body is unclean too. Chagigah ch.2. He who washed with the profane intention of merely eating may not eat tithes; he who washed with the intention of eating tithes may not eat Terumah; he who washed with regard to the weightier matter has made the lighter permitted to himself by the same action. Ibid.

units.la: §. In Babyl. Beracot. sol. 46.2. refertur vilipensionem lotionis manuum ex iis rebus esse, pro quibus Synedrium excommunicat, & re ipsa ab eo ideo excommunicatum fuisse R. Eleazar Ben Hazar, שפיקפן Quod vilifaceret lotionem manuum. Lotio Manuum & earum immersio est institutio Scribarum May-
units.tr: §. In Bab. Berachot sol.46.2 it is reported that despising the washing of hands is among the things for which the Sanhedrin excommunicates, and that R. Eleazar ben Hazar was in fact excommunicated for this reason, [שפיקפן], "because he despised the washing of hands." The washing of hands and their immersion is an institution of the Scribes. May-

units.la: mon. in Mikvaoth cap.11. Et fecundum Hierof. Schabbat sol.3.4. ab Hillele & Schammaeo. De origine huius consuetudinis loquitur Maym. in טומאת אוכלין cap.16. Quamvis permissum fit edere edulia immunda, & poculenta immunda bibere, religiosi tamen antiqui comederunt communem victum suum in munditia; Atque illi vocabantur Pharifaei. Atque res hac est summa sanctitatis, & via summa religionis, ut se homo segreg[e]t a vulgo, utq; illud nec tangat, nec cum eo comedat, nam separatio talis induxit in puritatem corporis &c.
units.tr: mon. in Mikvaoth ch.11. And according to the Hierosolymitan Shabbat sol.3.4, it came from Hillel and Shammai. Maimonides speaks of the origin of this custom in [טומאת אוכלין] ch.16: "Although it is permitted to eat unclean foods and drink unclean drinks, the ancient religious nevertheless ate their common food in cleanness; and these were called Pharisees. This is the sum of holiness and the highest way of religion, that a man separate himself from the common people, so that he neither touches it nor eats with it, for such separation led to purity of body," etc.

units.la: §. Bab.Taanith sol.20.2. מילתא דשיבתא הוא Res Schibbt a fuit. Gloff. Schibbta ex Demonibus est, qui iis nocent, qui non lavant manus ante cibum. An non hoc satis terriculamenti, ne lotionem manuum negligamus ! Memorabilis etiam est Canon Hierof.Challah. sol. 58. 3. Ad placentam & manus lotionem, ambulet homo, usque ad quatuor milliaria.
units.tr: §. Bab. Taanith sol.20.2: [מילתא דשיבתא הוא], "It is a matter of Shibta." The gloss says: Shibta is one of the demons, who harm those who do not wash their hands before eating. Is this not enough of a scare, that we should neglect the washing of hands? Also memorable is the canon of the Hierosolymitan Challah sol. 58.3: "For a cake and for the washing of hands, let a man walk up to four miles."

units.la: §. Cùm manus lavarent, ut iam innuimus, lavarunt pugnum עד הנורק usque ad Iunƈturam Lacerti. Iadaim c.2.v.3. Mundificatio manuum & pedum in templo erat usque ad iunƈturam. Cholin sol.106. נטילת ידים respondet Marc.7. & טכילת ידים ipsius βαπτισμοί. Manus illas quæ opus habuerunt טנילת, non tinxerunt nisi loco idoneo, ubi scilicet congregabantur quadraginta seæ aquarum. Maym.in Mikvaoth cap.11. In quo Maymonidis tractatu, plurima adhuc de manuum lotione reperies. Vid. etiam Bab.Beracot sol.46.2.
units.tr: §. When they washed their hands, as we have already hinted, they washed the fist [עד הנורק], up to the joint of the forearm. Iadaim c.2 v.3. The cleansing of hands and feet in the temple was up to the joint. Cholin sol.106. [נטילת ידים] corresponds to Mark 7, and [טכילת ידים] itself to "baptisms" [βαπτισμοί]. Those hands which needed [נטילה] did not dip them except in a suitable place, namely where forty seahs of water were gathered. Maim. in Mikvaoth ch.11. In this tractate of Maimonides you will find very much more on the washing of hands. See also Bab. Berachot sol.46.2.

units.la: §. Ad lotiones corporis habebant Balnea (Vid. f. 1. in B.) item Cupas, hinc illud. R.Sira jedebat באגנר in Cupa aqua ad se lavandum. Bab.Beracot.sol.22.1. Cupas maiores & minores etiam vocabant אבנשו Nedarim folio 41. Mikvaot cap. 6. Homo Gonorrhæus non nisi in fonte lavabatur. At fœmina profluvio laborans, ut & omnes alii immundi, abluebantur בסקוות in collectione aquarum, in qua tantum aquæ esse debebat, quantum requiritur ad totum corpus abluendum merfione una; qualis locus in profunditate tres cubitos habere, & ad 40.seas aquæ continere potest, Maymon. in Hal. Mikvaot cap.1. & 4. Mifchna in Mikvaot cap. 2. 3. de Lotione Proselytorum vid. Baptisfmum.
units.tr: §. For washings of the body they had baths (see f.1 under B.), likewise tubs; hence that saying: "R. Sira used to sit in a tub [באגנר] of water" to wash himself. Bab. Berachot sol.22.1. Larger and smaller tubs they also called [אבנשו]. Nedarim folio 41. Mikvaot ch.6. A man with a gonorrhoea was washed only in a spring. But a woman suffering from a flux, as also all other unclean persons, was washed in [בסקוות], in a collection of water, in which there had to be as much water as is needed to wash the whole body in one immersion; such a place, which can be three cubits deep and hold up to 40 seahs of water, is described by Maimonides in Hal. Mikvaot ch.1 and 4. Mishnah Mikvaot ch.2, 3. On the washing of proselytes see Baptism.

units.la: §. Si quis contraxit immunditiem באט המובאתה A Patre immunditiei, (vid. Immunditties) est טיבול יום (v.f.1.) & opus habet immersione totius corporis. At ob immunditias inseriores satis erat mundificare manus. Vid. R. Salomoh in Kelim cap.1.
units.tr: §. If anyone contracted uncleanness from [אב הטומאה], a father of uncleanness (see Uncleannesses), he is [טבול יום] (see f.1), and needs immersion of the whole body. But for the lesser uncleannesses it was enough to cleanse the hands. See R. Solomon in Kelim ch.1.

units.la: §. Quomodo ירות של כלים manubria, ansæ, & partes externæ vasorum domesticorum rite emundari & fricari debebant. Vid. Mikvaot cap.10. quædam adduxit Cl.Buxt. L.Talm.p. 644. Vid.etiam סר טהרות. Abluunt omnia vasa ante Sabbathum Betza sol.17.2. Post celebrationem festorum omnia lavabant vasa (vid. Atrium) Hos licet in festo lavare, qui veniunt ex provincia maritima (vid. ברית הים) Captivitate, carcere, excommunicatione. Item linstea manuum, lintea tonsorum, balneatorum, Gonorrhææ laboratium, omnes de ique inmunditie affeʒos lavare licet; reliqui autem à lotione prohibentur. Moed Katon c.3.2. Quæ in lotione obstacula esse poterant, cum curâ semovebant. Beza sol.17.2. Succah sol.36.2.
units.tr: §. How the handles [ירות של כלים] of vessels, the handles and external parts of household vessels, were to be properly cleansed and scrubbed. See Mikvaot ch.10; Cl. Buxtorf has adduced some of these in L. Talm. p. 644. See also [סר טהרות]. They wash all vessels before the Sabbath, Betza sol.17.2. After the celebration of the festivals they washed all vessels (see Atrium). It is permitted to wash on a festival for those who come from a maritime province (see [ברית הים]), from captivity, from prison, from excommunication. Likewise the linen cloths for hands, the cloths of barbers and bathers, the workshop of the gonorrhoeic; in short, it is permitted to wash those affected by any uncleanness; the rest, however, are forbidden to wash. Moed Katon c.3.2. Whatever could be obstacles to washing they removed with care. Beza sol.17.2. Succah sol.36.2.

units.la: §. In lotione vestimentorum hoc observarunt, ut sanctiores habiti semper illa lavarent, si profluvio vel aliâ impuritate immunda facta erant. De vestimentis illis hæc scribitur regula in Chagiga cap. 2. v.7. Vestimenta plebeiorum sunt בורש causa vel origo impuritatis Pharisæis, Pharisæorum edentibus Trumam, Edentium Trumam Edentibus Sanctum; Edentium Sanctum edentibus sacrificium pro peccato. Iose Ben Ioeser pientissimus fuit inter Sacerdotes, peplum tamen eius immundum redditum est ab edentibus Sanctum.
units.tr: In washing garments they observed this rule: those regarded as more holy always washed those garments if they had become unclean through a discharge or some other impurity. On such garments this rule is written in Chagigah ch. 2, v. 7: "The garments of common people are a source or origin of uncleanness for the Pharisees; Pharisees who eat Terumah make those who eat Terumah unclean, and those who eat Terumah make those who eat holy things unclean; those who eat holy things make those who eat the sacrifice for sin unclean." Jose ben Joezer was the most pious of the priests, yet his cloak was made unclean by those who ate holy things.

units.la: §. De Pelvi in qua pedes lavabantur hæc habet Iadaim cap.4.1. Isto die (quo præfecerunt Synedrio R. Elieserem Ben Asariæ,) numerata sunt suffragia, & determinarunt על עריבת de pelvi quâ lavandi pedes, illam nempe continere debere à duobus logis usque ad decem logos.
units.tr: On the basin in which feet were washed, Iadaim ch. 4.1 has this: "On that day (when they placed R. Eliezer ben Azariah over the Sanhedrin) votes were counted, and they determined concerning the basin for washing feet, that it must hold from two logs up to ten logs."

units.la: §. Circa lotionem pedum quam Christus discipulis fecit, hæc observanda. 1. Fuisse rem inusitatam, ut superiores lavarent pedes inferiorum. Inter officia præstanda ab uxore erga maritum hoc unum erat, ut lavaret faciem eius, & manus, & pedes, Maymon in איסות cap.31. Eadem præstanda à filio Patri. Tosaphta in Kidduschin cap.1. Eadem etiam à servo erga herum Kidduschin f.22.2. At non vice versa.
units.tr: Concerning the washing of feet that Christ performed for his disciples, note the following. 1. It was an unusual thing for superiors to wash the feet of inferiors. Among the duties a wife owed her husband, this alone was included: that she wash his face, his hands and his feet (Maimonides, in Ishot ch. 31). A son owed the same to his father (Tosephta in Kiddushin ch. 1), and a servant owed it to his master (Kiddushin f. 22.2). But not the reverse.

units.la: 2. Observat Cl. Leigtfootus nunquam lotos fuisse pedes solùm sub notione purificationis legatis. Lotas quidem fuisse manus solùm à Pharisæis, sub ea notione,sed non pedes,& manus &pedes àSacerdotibus, at non pedes solùm. Quo longiùs ergo hæc actio Christi recessit à communi more, eo altius assurgit ad erudiendum suos, proposita non solum in exemplum, sed & in doctrinam.
units.tr: 2. The distinguished Lightfoot observes that feet were never washed merely under the notion of purification. Among the Pharisees, hands alone were washed under that notion, but not feet; hands and feet were washed by the priests, but not feet alone. Therefore, the further this action of Christ departed from common custom, the higher it rises to instruct his own, being set forth not only as an example but also as a teaching.

units.la: Loca quædam terræ Israeliticæ recensêre ad intelligentiam plurimorum locorum Talmud. non incongruum erit. Vid. in genere de regione Israelitica f.l. de Bethphage, Bethoron, Emmaunta, Beth Chadudo, Dalmanuta, Gadara, Galilæa, Gaza, Gehinnom, Gennesaret; Gerizim, Gusch chalab. Iabhne, Lydda, Iericho, Ierosolyma, de loco אונו מויב, Alexandria vid. in suis locis. De נמר בית vid. in N. de מודעיה in M. מוצא est locus prope Kedronis vallem, ex quo decerpserunt ramos salicum in festo Tabernaculorum Succah cap.4.5. Zuphim צופים est collis à septentrione Hierosolymam aspiciens. Hierof. Beracot fol.13.2. Bab. Beracot fol.49.2. Pirke R. Eliefer cap. 31. Noba locus fuit non remotus Hierosolyma, nam urbs illinc commodè conspici potuit, illuc venit Sancherib & urbem consideravit despiciendo. Chald. Esai: x. 31. Kimchi in loc. Bab. Sanhed. fol. 94. 2. Hebron vid.f.l. Beth Cherem v. f. 1. de Monte Simeonitidis vid. in S.
units.tr: Some places in the land of Israel should be listed, since this will not be unhelpful for understanding many places in the Talmud. On the region of Israel in general, see under its own heading. See Bethphage, Bethoron, Emmaus, Beth Chadudo, Dalmanutha, Gadara, Galilee, Gaza, Gehinnom, Gennesaret, Gerizim, Gush Chalab, Iabne, Lydda, Jericho, Jerusalem; for the place Ono and for Alexandria, see in their own places. On Beth Nimra, see under N. Mutza (מוצא) is a place near the valley of Kidron, from which they cut branches of willows at the Feast of Tabernacles (Succah ch. 4.5). Zuphim (צופים) is a hill from the north facing Jerusalem (Jerusalem Berachot f. 13.2; Babylonian Berachot f. 49.2; Pirke R. Eliezer ch. 31). Nob was a place not far from Jerusalem, for the city could be conveniently seen from there; Sennacherib came there and looked at the city with contempt (Chaldee on Isa. 10.31; Kimchi on the passage; Babylonian Sanhedrin f. 94.2). Hebron, see in its place. Beth Cherem, see f. 1. On Mount Simeonitis, see under S.

units.la: §. De הר צבועים Vid. Challah cap.4.10.Tres urbes vastatæ sunt כנוד propter discordiam, שיחין propter artes magicas, & מגדל צבעיא Turris Zebaia propter fornicationem. Hierof.
units.tr: On Mount Tzeboim (הר צבועים), see Challah ch. 4.10. Three cities were destroyed: Kinnud (כנוד) because of discord, Sheichin (שיחין) because of magic arts, and the Tower of Zebaia (מגדל צבעיא) because of fornication (Jerusalem Talmud).

units.la: Taanit f.69.1. De תרי כי & כי ip V.Sanh.f.95 1.de GophnaHier.Taan.f.69.1.Ofloginta paria franu Sacerdotu, duxerunt in uxores oftogiuta paria Sacerdotiffarum in Gophna,nofte una.Vallis Rinmon, in ea femel feptem feniores intercalarunt annum. Hierof. (hagiga fol.78.4. עקרבת diftabant Hierofolymis fpatio itineris unius diei verfus feptentrionem Maafer Scheni cap.5. v.2. Neapolis v.f.1. Cafarea v.f.1. Bethfchean v. f.1. Tiberias v. f.1. de סוכר עין aliquando afferebantur duo panes offerendi a Summo Pontifice,Bava Kama f. 81.2. §. De quibufdam Pagis vid.in כפר.De Capernaum vid. etiam in C. de נבוריא כפר Urbe Navoria mentio fit Megillah f.18.1.de כפר ברקאי Vrbe Barkai loquitur Kerithut fol.28.2. de כפר פאני Meilahfol.71. de עין כפר Kilaim c.6. de Caphar שכניא Secania Avoda Zarah f.17.1.
units.tr: Taanit f. 69.1. On the pairs of priests' sons... Sanhedrin f. 95.1 on Gophna. The Jerusalem Taanit f. 69.1 says: eighty pairs of priests' sons took to wife eighty pairs of priests' daughters in Gophna, all in one night. In the valley of Rimmon, seven elders once intercalated a year there (Jerusalem). Hagigah f. 78.4. Akrabat (עקרבת) was a day's journey north of Jerusalem (Maaser Sheni ch. 5 v. 2). Neapolis, see f. 1. Caesarea, see f. 1. Beth-shean, see f. 1. Tiberias, see f. 1. On Ein Sukar: at times two loaves to be offered were brought by the High Priest (Bava Kama f. 81.2). On certain villages, see under Kaphar. On Capernaum, see also under C. Kaphar Navoria: mention is made in Megillah f. 18.1. The city Barkai is spoken of in Kerithut f. 28.2 under Kaphar Barkai. Kaphar Pani: Meilah f. 71. Ein Kaphar: Kilaim ch. 6. Caphar Secania: Avodah Zarah f. 17.1.

units.la: Locusta. Illas venabantur in efcam, quibus non nobilior victus. Species mundarum locuftarum Gemariitæ fingunt effe octingentas Hierof.Taanith fol.69.2. labore & acumine opus effet, omnes illas fuis nominibus defcribere. Bab. Schabbat fol.106.2. Tradunt Rabbini הצר והגוין הגבי Qui venatur locuftas, bruchos, crabrones &c. in Sabbatho rem eft; Secundùm Gloff. הגוין funt de genere locuftarum mundarum quæ comeduntur; excipit Gemara, quòd fcilicet etiam in Sabbatho locuftas venari liceat, modò fit tempore roris, quia tunc gradum fiftere folent, aut gregatim eunt, unde abfque magno labore capi poffunt. In Sabbatho enim quicquid laborem fecum fert, fugiendum.
units.tr: Locusts. They hunted these for food, since there was no more noble fare. The Gemarists imagine there are eight hundred kinds of clean locusts (Jerusalem Taanit f. 69.2), and it would require labour and keen discernment to describe them all by their names (Babylonian Shabbat f. 106.2). The rabbis teach that whoever hunts locusts, bruchi, hornets, and so on, on the Sabbath, is doing a forbidden thing. According to the Gloss, these are kinds of clean locusts that are eaten. The Gemara makes an exception: it is lawful to hunt locusts even on the Sabbath, provided it is at the time of dew, because then they tend to halt their march or move in flocks, so they can be caught without great labour. For on the Sabbath, whatever involves labour is to be avoided.

units.la: §. Pro Locuftis (intellige ad cibum aptis) benedicunt benedictione quæ incipit, שהכל Per cuius verba omnia. Beracot c.5. Locustæ annumerantur etiam carni, vid. Ioh. Bapt. in I. quænam esui idoneæ sint lege in Cholin f. 65.1.
units.tr: For locusts (meaning those fit for food), one says the blessing that begins "shehakol," by whose word all things come to be (Berachot ch. 5). Locusts are also counted as flesh. See John the Baptist in I. For which creatures are fit to eat, see Chullin f. 65.1.

units.la: Loth fuit Princeps iudicum, primus est summus prætor Berefch. Rabba fect.59. Vid. Sodomah. Quicunque ardet post concupiscentiam libidinum ושמאכלין אותו מכשרו סופו Eius finis est ut vescatur propria carne sua; Talis fuit Loth, ideoque filiarum suarum scortatione se tandem explevit, Filiæ autem appellantur Caro Parentum. Berefch. Rabba. sect.51.
units.tr: Lot was prince of judges; he was the first chief praetor (Bereshit Rabba sect. 59). See Sodomah. Whoever burns after lustful desires, "they feed him from his own flesh; that is his end." Such was Lot, and therefore he at last satisfied himself by the fornication of his daughters, and daughters are called the flesh of their parents (Bereshit Rabba sect. 51).

units.la: לשכות Vid. Conclavia
units.tr: Chambers (לשכות). See "Conclavia."

units.la: Lucernæ. In templo vid. Cultus quotid. Temp. de loco Lucernarum vid. Maym. Hal. Beth. Habech. c.1. sub sin c. 2. ab init. de structura Candelabri vid. eiusdem tract.cap.3.
units.tr: Lamps. In the temple, see "Daily worship in the Temple." On the place of the lamps, see Maimonides, Hal. Beth Habechirah ch. 1, end of ch. 2 at the beginning. On the structure of the lampstand, see the same treatise ch. 3.

units.la: Luctus. De morte vid. suo loco. In usu est claudere defuncti oculos; & si os apertum habeat, alligare maxillas ut claudatur, & obturare maiores meatus eius, postquam ipsum (si ita visum fuerit) aromatibus condiverunt. Abscindunt etiam capillos eius, & ipsum involucris albis ex lino contextis, & non magni pretii involvunt; Sudarium quod vulgò adhibent ultra denarium non valet, ne pudorem faciant illis, in quorum facultate non est, pretiosius habere. Faciem denique mortui tegunt, ne pudore afficiantur pauperes, quorum facies ut plurimùm nigrescunt. Prohibitum est sepelire aliquem involucris שד כבי Byssinis, aut vestimentis deauratis & acu pictis, licet mortuus præses Synedrii fuisset, hoc enim argueret גמות רוח Supe rbiam & morem gentilem. Ille qui in agone constitutus est consideratur adhuc ut perfecte vivens, hinc nec vasa umbilico eius imponunt, nec meatus eius obturant, nec eum aromatibus ungunt; oculos vero eius non claudunt cum animæ egressu, sed paululum exspectant; qui aliter fecerit, æstimatur quasi ipsum interfecisset, Maym.Hal.Ebhel.c.4.
units.tr: Mourning. On death, see in its place. It is customary to close the eyes of the dead; and if the mouth is open, to tie up the jaws so that it closes, and to stop its larger openings, after they have (if it seems fit) anointed the body with spices. They also cut off the hair and wrap the dead in white shrouds woven of linen, of no great price. The cloth commonly used is not worth more than a denarius, so that they do not put to shame those who cannot afford something more costly. Finally, they cover the face of the dead, lest the poor, whose faces mostly turn dark, be put to shame. It is forbidden to bury anyone in byssus shrouds or in garments gilded and embroidered with needlework, even if the dead man was president of the Sanhedrin, for this would show pride and pagan custom. One who is in the agony is still considered fully alive; hence they do not place vessels on his navel, nor close his openings, nor anoint him with spices. They do not close his eyes at the moment the soul departs, but wait a little. Whoever does otherwise is judged as though he had killed him (Maimonides, Hal. Ebhel ch. 4).

units.la: §. In mortuo sepeliendo non moras nectunt,sed funus accelerant, nisi forte instet festum aut Sabbathum, aut pluviæ locum sepulchri aquâ impleverint, aut mortuus sit pater vel mater, ad parentum enim honorem facit sepulturam retardare. In reliquis verò casibus המלין את מתו qui mortuum suum per noctem insepultum relinquit, transgreditur præceptum affirmativum. Maym. l. m.c.
units.tr: In burying the dead they do not delay but hasten the funeral, unless perhaps a feast or the Sabbath presses, or they have filled the grave with rainwater, or the dead person is a father or mother, for to delay burial would dishonour the parents. In other cases, "whoever leaves his dead unburied overnight" transgresses an affirmative precept (Maimonides, loc. cit.).

units.la: §. De vestium Laceratione in luctu,vid.Laceratio. De ingenti quodam luctu legitur in Bava Kama sol. 17. 1. dicitur enim 36000 qui luctus causâ vestes suas dilaceraverant feretrum antecessisse.
units.tr: On tearing the garments in mourning, see "Laceration." Of a huge mourning we read in Bava Kama f. 17.1: it is said that 36,000 men, who had torn their garments for grief, went before the bier.

units.la: §. Mortuum ferunt humeris usque ad sepulchretum. Qui humeris feretrum sustinent, sandalia sua induere non debent, ne forte uni aut alteri ligamina disrumpantur, & ille in cadendi periculo sit; deinde in aliqua speluncæ parte foveam adaptant, ipsum facie sursum versâ demittunt, terram quam effoderunt ipsi injiciunt, & tandem lapides imponunt; Qui ipsum comitati sunt, dicunt לך בשלום Abi in pace. (Maym. Hal. Ebhel c. 4.) Horum comitantium cœtus vocatur שלום quasi lineam dicens: res : huius lineæ ordo primus fuit proximorum (quales sunt maritus, uxor, liberi) secundus, amicorum specialium, tertius communis cætus Ecclesiæ : (Beracot.c.3.)Cùm ita cum sunere progrediebantur per septem vices conseederunt לכבוד המת in honorem defuncti, & dixerunt ad unumquodque caput planctus עכרו Surgite pretiosi, surgite; Sedete pretiosi,sedete; &c. (Gloss. ad Megillah c.43.) Talia erga mortuos officia vocarunt גמילות חסרים Exhibitionem misericordiarum.Hieros.Sanhed. sol.23.3. Vbi etiam de ingrata quadam urbe recensetur, illam præstanti cuidam discipulo sapientum fato suo functo, non exhibuisse misericordias, sed contrà, cùm. quidam publicanus mortuus esset, ab operibus cessasse, ut ritè bellum hominem lugere posset. Quomodo Summus Sacerdos funus comitetur vid. Sanhed.c.1. quando ipse consolationem accipiebat, tum totus populus ipsi dicebat, Simus nos expiatio tua (Gloss. In nobis fiat expiatio tua, nosque subeamus tuo loco quidquid tibi evenire debet.) Et ipse respondebat eis תתברכו מן השמים Benedicti sitis cœlitus. Rambam c. 2. Negajim notat priorem loquutionem esse formulam, quâ quis magnitudinem amoris sui testabatur; illamque imitatus est Paulus ad Rom.9.3. quando optat ut Anathema fiat pro ipsis.Sanhed.18.1. in Mischna.
units.tr: The dead are carried on the shoulders to the burial place. Those who bear the bier on their shoulders must not put on their sandals, lest perhaps a strap break on one or the other and he be in danger of falling. Then they fit a pit in some part of the cave, lower the body face upward, throw in the earth they dug out themselves, and at last lay stones upon it. Those who accompanied him say "Go in peace" (Maimonides, Hal. Ebhel ch. 4). The company of those accompanying is called "shalom," as though the line of things said. The order of this line was: first the nearest relatives (husband, wife, children), second special friends, third the common company of the Church (Berachot ch. 3). When they thus advanced with the funeral, they sat down seven times in honour of the dead, and at each one they said to the mourners, "Arise, precious ones, arise; sit, precious ones, sit," and so on (Gloss on Megillah ch. 43). Such services toward the dead they called "gemilut chasadim," the exercise of kindnesses (Jerusalem Sanhedrin f. 23.3). There it is also recorded of an ungrateful city that, when an outstanding disciple of the wise died, it did not show kindnesses; on the contrary, when a certain publican died, it ceased from its work so that it could properly mourn that man. As for how the High Priest accompanies a funeral, see Sanhedrin ch. 1: when he himself received consolation, the whole people said to him, "May we be your atonement" (Gloss: may atonement be made in us, and may we take your place in whatever ought to befall you). He answered them, "May you be blessed from heaven" (Rambam ch. 2). Negaim notes that the first expression was a formula by which someone attested the greatness of his love; Paul imitated it in Rom. 9.3, when he wishes that he himself might become an anathema for them (Sanhedrin 18.1, in the Mishnah).

units.la: §. Postquàm mortuus terræ mandatus est, pingunt sepulchrum הקבר על נפש וכונים ædificant ipsi monumentum super sepulchrum; iusti tamen sibi monumenta non ædificare curant; quia verba sunt μνημεῖα ipsorum. Hal. אכל c. 4. Schekalim cap.4. Berefchit Rabba fecl. 82.sol. 92.1. Hieros Schekalim cap. 2. in Gem. Sepulchrorum cippis inscribunt adhuc hodierni ut prisci: Quies eius sit in fasciculo viventium, cum reliquis iustis, Amen, Amen, Amen, Selah. Item Anima eius sit colligata בגן ערן A.A.A.S. Midrasch Cohelet 3. 21. Duo Epitaphia viri & foeminae habes apud Cl.Buxt.Lex.Talm. p.971.
units.tr: §. After the dead have been committed to the earth, they inscribe the grave [הקבר על נפש וכונים], that is, they build a monument over the sepulchre. The righteous, however, take care not to build monuments for themselves, because their words are their memorials [μνημεῖα]. Hal. אכל c. 4. Schekalim cap. 4. Bereshit Rabba fol. 82, sol. 92.1. Hieros Schekalim cap. 2. In Gem. Even today, as in antiquity, people inscribe the stones of graves: "May his rest be in the bundle of the living, with the other righteous, Amen, Amen, Amen, Selah." Likewise: "May his soul be bound up in the garden of Eden," A.A.A.S. Midrash Kohelet 3. 21. You have two epitaphs, of a man and of a woman, in Buxtorf's Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 971.

units.la: §. De sepeliendi antiquitate, ritu, legibus v. Sanhed. 46.2. Buxt. Syn.Iud.701. Leo Modena. H. Iud. v.c.8. Sepulchra quaedam extraordinaria erant, 1. Erat קבר הנכרי Sepulchrum inventum, cum in alicuius praedio Domino inscio aliquis sepultus fuerat. 2. Erat קבר מויק את הרבים Sepulchrum nocens publico, qualia erant quae in loco publicae ambulationis effossa. Bab. Sanhed. folio 47. 2. Hierof. Nedarim folio 57.4. Talia sepulchra fuerunt sepulchra familiae Davidis & sepulchrum Huldae, intra Hierosolymam sita, in qua tamen sepulchra fieri non debebant, quare etiam sepulchra domus Davidis suo loco moverunt, filiorum Huldae vero reliquerunt, certas ob causas vid. Hierof. מויר sol.57.4. His sepulchris extraordinariis accensé etiam duo illa sepulchreta, in quae ponebantur illi qui à synedrio morte affecti erant, non quidem quasi extra ordinem suissent, sed quia pro tempore solum cadavera retinebant, & tanquam publica Carcinomata aestimabantur; relinquebantur autem ibi intersecti donec caro consumpta erat, deinde ossa effodiebantur, & in sepulchra patrum ipsorum rum recondebantur. Sanhed. cap.6.5. In uno ex illis sepeliendus erat ex more D. N. I. Christus, nisi Iosephus pie audax à Pilato impetrasset, ut honestius humaretur.
units.tr: §. On the antiquity, ritual and laws of burial, see Sanhedrin 46.2; Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica, 701; Leo Modena, Historia Judaica, c. 8. Some sepulchres were extraordinary: (1) there was the "grave of the stranger" [קבר הנכרי], a sepulchre found when someone had been buried on another's estate without the owner's knowledge; (2) there was the "grave that harms the public" [קבר המזיק את הרבים], such as those dug in a place of public walking. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 47.2; Hierosolymitanum Nedarim fol. 57.4. Such were the sepulchres of David's family and the sepulchre of Huldah, situated within Jerusalem, where tombs ought not to have been made. Therefore they moved the sepulchres of David's house to another place, but left those of Huldah's sons, for certain reasons; see Hierosolymitanum, Moed fol. 57.4. To these extraordinary sepulchres I also reckon the two burial grounds in which those put to death by the Sanhedrin were laid. They were not extraordinary in the sense of being outside the ordinary arrangement, but because they held the corpses only for the time being, and were regarded as public carrion pits. The condemned were left there slain until the flesh was consumed; then the bones were dug up and laid in the sepulchres of their fathers. In one of these our Lord Jesus Christ was to be buried according to custom, had not Joseph, a devout and bold man, obtained from Pilate that he might be buried more honourably.

units.la: Tradunt etiam Rabbini, Iudæos qui Pisæ in Italia sepeliuntur, triduo consumi, propterea quod eo olim vasculum terræ cæmeterii sive urbis Ierusalem allatum fit, & in eum locum evacuatum, ubi mortui sepeliebantur, unde postea observatum, carnem mortuorum tribus diebus fuisse consumptam. Vid. Iuchafin f.136.1.
units.tr: The rabbis also relate that Jews buried at Pisa in Italy are consumed within three days, because a small vessel of earth from the cemetery, or city, of Jerusalem was once brought there and emptied into the place where the dead were buried. Hence it was later observed that the flesh of the dead was consumed in three days. See Juchasin f. 136.1.

units.la: §. Generales regulæ sepulchrorum hæ erant.
units.tr: §. These were the general rules concerning sepulchres.

units.la: 1. Per locum sepulchrorum canalis aquarum non est derivandus, non ducenda via publica, non pascenda illic pecora, nec colligenda illinc ligna. Maffeceth Schabbath. cap.44.2. 2. Nemo debet inter sepulchra cum Phylacteriis capiti affixis, & libro legis brachio appenso ambulare Bab. Beracot sol.18.1.3. 3. Homines unius familiæ non sparsim sed in uno loco sepeliendi sunt; hinc vulgo in usu habuerunt conficere interiora speluncæ quatuor cubitorum, atque aperire intra eam octo sepulchra, ita ut tria hinc, tria illinc, & duo iuxta illa fuerint, & iuxta ostium, atriolum. Alii concavum speluncæ fecerunt sex atque octo cubitorum, & in ea aperuerunt tredecim sepulchra: sed in omnibus his se dirigere debuerunt pro conditione petra, secundum quam hi plura illi vero pauciora repositoria fuerunt. B. Batra c.6.v.8.
units.tr: 1. A channel of water must not be diverted through the place of the sepulchres; a public road must not be led through it, animals must not be pastured there, and wood must not be gathered from there. Mass. Shabbath cap. 44.2. 2. No one should walk among the sepulchres with phylacteries fixed to his head and a book of the law hung on his arm. Bab. Berakhot sol. 18.1. 3. The men of one family are to be buried not scattered about but in one place. Hence it was common practice to make the inner part of a cave four cubits deep and to open eight tombs within it, three on one side, three on the other, and two beside them near the entrance, forming a little court. Others made the hollow of the cave six or eight cubits and opened thirteen tombs in it. But in all these cases they had to adapt themselves to the condition of the rock, according to which some cells were more numerous and others fewer. B. Bathra c. 6, v. 8.

units.la: §. Luctus pro mortuis distinguitur in Aninut & Abelut. Aninut erat in diem funeris tantum; exinde autem cæpit אבלות in dies triginta. In אבלות habuerunt epulas lugubres de quibus Hierof.Beracot f.6.1.& Sanhed. c.1.Item חלילי & המאונן tibicines & plangentem. Etiam pauperrimus inter Israelitas non præbuit uxori mortuæ minus quàm duos tibicines, & unam lamentatricem. Chetubhot c.4.6. vid. etiam Maym.Hal. אישות c.14. Bava Me'zia c.6.1. Schabbat c.13.4. Qui ad defunctum plangendum conducitur his utitur verbis בואו בכו עמי כל מרי לב ומי שלכו דוה עליו הולך ומספיד על קרוכו Accedite ad me omnes vos quorum cor amarum & languidum est; ad plangendum super proximum vestrum. Bartenora ad Moed Katon c.1.5.
units.tr: §. Mourning for the dead is distinguished into aninut and abelut. Aninut lasted only until the day of the funeral; after that abelut began, for thirty days. During abelut they held mournful feasts, about which see Hieros. Berakhot f. 6.1 and Sanhedrin c. 1. There were also flute-players [חלילי] and the mourner [המאונן], the wailing man. Even the poorest of the Israelites did not provide for a dead wife fewer than two flute-players and one female lamenter. Ketubot c. 4.6; see also Maim. Hal. Ishut c. 14; Bava Metzia c. 6.1; Shabbat c. 13.4. Whoever is hired to lament the dead uses these words: "Come to me, all you whose hearts are bitter and languid, to lament over your neighbour, and he who goes about and makes lament for his kinsman." Bartenora on Moed Katan c. 1.5.

units.la: §. Qui habet mortuum suum ante se proiectum,& cui incumbit sepulturam curare, prohibetur carnem edere, vinum bibere: liber est etiam ab oratione,recitatione phylacteriorum, à consecratione cibi, & benedictione post ipsum. Bab.Beracot sol.8.1. Maym. Hal. Ebhel. cap. 4.
units.tr: §. Whoever has his dead lying before him, and whose duty it is to see to the burial, is forbidden to eat meat and to drink wine. He is also free from prayer, from the recitation of the phylacteries, from the consecration of food, and from the blessing after it. Bab. Berakhot sol. 8.1. Maim. Hal. Evel cap. 4.

units.la: §. כפיית המטות Inclinatio lectorum (quæ fit ad imitandum amicos Iobi, qui consederunt cum illo ad terram, Iobi.ii.13.) fit, ex quo mortuus effertur ex porta atrii domus, aut ex quo imponunt lapidem sepulchralem. Maym. l.c. & c.1. Beracot sol.6.1.
units.tr: §. The inclination of the couches [כפיית המטות] (done in imitation of Job's friends, who sat down with him on the ground, Job 2:13) is performed from the time the dead man is carried out through the gate of the court of the house, or from the time they set the sepulchral stone in place. Maim. l.c. and c. 1. Berakhot sol. 6.1.

units.la: §. Hæc sunt ad quæ obligatur המתאבל lugens, die primò luctus ex lege, & in reliquis diebus ex sapientum præceptis, non debet se radere, lavare nec ungere oleo, nec mariti ossicium præstare, nec sandalia induere, aut opus suum peragere, sive sit paterfamilias, sive filius aut filia, aut servus &c. nec legere in lege , nec elevare lectum suum, aut aperire caput suum, aut pacem alicui precari. Maym. אבל c.5. Muff. Semachot c.5.
units.tr: §. These are the duties to which the mourner [המתאבל] is bound. On the first day of mourning he is bound by law, and on the remaining days by the precepts of the sages. He must not shave, wash, or anoint himself with oil; he must not perform the duty of a husband; he must not put on sandals or carry on his work, whether he is the head of the household, or a son or daughter, or a servant, and so on. He must not read in the law, lift his bed, uncover his head, or wish peace to anyone. Maim. Avel c. 5; Mufflaeus, Semachot c. 5.

units.la: §. Incipiunt האבל luctum, ut iam indigitavimus, ex quo funus e domo elatum est; aut secundum Maym. ex quo obturatur הגולל lapis sepulchri, si nimirum morte communi defunctus est mortuus; aliàs si quis à Rege interfectus est, & ipsum sepelire non permiserit, incipiunt ipsum lugere ex quo diffid… [illegible, ~3 letters] se à Rege impetraturos, illius corpus sepeliendi veniam licet non desperent se illud furari posse. Similiter si quis submersus aut à fera dilaceratus fuit, dies luctus non numerare incipiunt, nisi caput eius reperierint, licet membra invenerint, aut de ipso reperiendo plane desperaverint. Hal. Ebbel. c.1.
units.tr: §. Mourning begins, as we have already indicated, from when the funeral has been carried out of the house; or, according to Maimonides, from when the stone [הגולל] of the sepulchre is closed, provided the dead man died a common death. Otherwise, if someone was killed by the king and the king did not permit him to be buried, they begin to mourn him from the time they despair of obtaining from the king leave to bury his body, although they do not despair of being able to steal it away for burial. Likewise, if someone was drowned or torn apart by a wild beast, they do not begin to count the days of mourning unless they find his head, even if they find his limbs, or have altogether despaired of finding him. Hal. Evel c. 1.

units.la: §. Non lugent abortus; etiamsi embryo novem menses compleverit, si tamen ex ventre matris aut contusus aut frustatim egreditur, propter ipsum luctum non instituunt. Quos Rex interfecit מתאבלין עליהן lugent eos, & ossa eorum in sepulchris patrum ipsorum recondunt, bona vero eorum cedunt Regis fisco. At à quibus synedrium supplicium sumpsit, eos non lugent sed אנגין plangunt, quia planctus talis non nisi in corde est, luctus autem communis in gestibus, quem si publice ita edidisfent, Synedrium quasi iniustitiae accusassent, quod tamen semper studuit iudicia incorrupta administrare; in corde vero licuit ipsis tristitiam fovere, ad commiserationem erga personas ita infami morte è medio sublatas oftendendam: Quod autem lugere potuerint propter interfectos המלכות בן הרשעה. A Rege, externis etiam gestibus, id inde est, quia Reges in usu habuerunt, pro libitu suo, homines ad supplicia adigere, absque praevio iustitiae processu, sola se vindicandi cupiditate, aut quia ita ipsorum intererat: quod Iudaei saepius cum lachrymis aspicere debuerunt, cum sub propriis principibus, tum sub iugo Romanorum, quod ut plurimum nomine המלכות denotant. His adde, Synedrium se ab omni suspicione sinistri iudicii liberasse, eo quod bona Reorum non ut Rex fisco applicabat, sed ad haeredes transmittebat. Vid. Hal.Ebbel.c.1.
units.tr: §. They do not mourn miscarriages. Even if the embryo has completed nine months, if it comes forth from the mother's womb bruised or in pieces, they do not institute mourning for it. Those whom the king has put to death they mourn [מתאבלין עליהן], and they gather their bones into the sepulchres of their fathers, but their goods pass to the king's treasury. For those on whom the Sanhedrin has inflicted punishment, however, they do not mourn but "lament" [אנגין], because such lament is only in the heart, whereas common mourning is shown in gestures. Had they displayed it publicly in that way, they would have been accusing the Sanhedrin of injustice, though it always strove to administer incorrupt judgments. In the heart, however, they were permitted to cherish sadness, to show compassion towards persons removed from the midst by so infamous a death. That they could mourn, even with outward gestures, those killed by "the kingdom, the son of wickedness" [המלכות בן הרשעה], that is, by the king, is because kings were accustomed to drive men to punishment at their pleasure, without any prior process of justice, from the sole desire of vengeance or because it suited their own interest. The Jews were often obliged to look upon this with tears, both under their own princes and under the yoke of the Romans, which they commonly denote by the name "the kingdom". Add to this that the Sanhedrin freed itself from every suspicion of an unjust trial, because it did not apply the goods of the accused to the fisc as the king did, but passed them on to their heirs. See Hal. Evel c. 1.

units.la: §. Propter Haereticos, separatistas, excommunicatos, non luget Ecclesia, sed propinqui & consanguinei ipsorum vestimentis albis velantur & vestiuntur, edunt bibunt & hilares sunt, quia Dei ofores sublati sunt. Non legunt eum qui אבר עשנו לדעת ex intentione mortem sibi consciivit, & violentas manus intulit. Ibid.
units.tr: §. Because of heretics, separatists and the excommunicated, the Church does not mourn. Their kinsmen and relatives, however, wrap themselves in white garments and dress in them, eat, drink and are cheerful, because the enemies of God have been removed. They do not hold the lament over one who has deliberately [אבר עשנו לדעת] taken his own life and laid violent hands upon himself. Ibid.

units.la: §. Hi sunt quos ex lege lugere debemus, Patrem, matrem, filium, filiam, fratrem & sorores, maritus uxorem, & uxor maritum; sapientes deinde luctum etiam ad alios extenderunt &c. quomodo Sacerdos possit lugere, & se ob mortuum immundum reddere explicatur prolixè in eadem Hal.c.2.3.
units.tr: §. These are the people whom by law we must mourn: father, mother, son, daughter, brother and sisters; a husband mourns his wife, and a wife her husband. The sages afterwards extended mourning to others as well, etc. How a priest may mourn, and make himself unclean for the dead, is explained at length in the same Hal. c.2.3.

units.la: §. Quomodo lugentes templum ingrediebantur vid. Excommunicatio. & Maym.Bet.Habech. c.7.
units.tr: §. On how mourners entered the temple, see Excommunication, and Maim. Bet Habechirah c.7.

units.la: §. R. Meir existimat aliquem absque luctu & cum gaudio, patris fui & matris suæ ossa colligere posse, & proinde id licitum esse in festo. Sed contrarium existimat R.Iose. Nemo debet conducere ןשמ Plangentem propter iam diu defunctum, ut eius memoriam propinquis refricet. Nec propter illum qui tribus ante festum diebus mortuus est: ( tunc enim pecunia ad præparationem pro festo & lætitia adhibenda, non autem pro luctu.) Moed Katon c.1.5.
units.tr: §. R. Meir holds that a man may gather the bones of his father and mother without mourning and with joy, and that this is therefore lawful on a festival. But R. Jose holds the contrary. No one should hire a wailer [mesapped] for one who died long ago, to stir up his memory among the relatives. Nor should one be hired for a man who died three days before the festival, for then the money is to be spent on preparing for the festival and for joy, not on mourning. Moed Katon c.1.5.

units.la: §. In festo non licet vestimenta lacerare,aut humerum denudare , aut epulo funerali aliquem excipere, nisi sit ex propinquis. Cibare autem non licet, nisi incumbat lecto erecto. Non licet cibum inferre in domum luctus super tabulam aut scutellam,sed licet in canistro. Non dicunt in festo consuetam lugentium benedictionem , sed stantes ordine consolantur & multitudinem dimittunt. In festo mortui feretrum non collocant in platea , ne festum luctuosum reddatur. Licet mulieribus se affligere in festo, non autem complodere manus. R. Ifmael dicit,proximi feretro manibus complodant. In Noviluniis, festo dedicationis, & פורים se affligere licet, & complodere manus, non autem lamentari: Postquàm autem mortuus inhumatus est, nec se affligere nec manus complodere licet. Quid est עיוי affliction? Vbi omnes lugent simul. קינה lamentatio verò est, ubi una incipit, reliquæ verò lamentatrices in luctu edendo eam sequuntur, secundùm Ierem. 9.19. Moed. Katon c.3.7.8.9.
units.tr: §. On a festival it is not lawful to tear one's garments, or bare the shoulder, or receive anyone at a funeral meal, unless he is a relative. It is lawful to feed someone only if he reclines on a raised couch. It is not lawful to bring food into a house of mourning on a table or a dish, but it is lawful in a basket. On a festival they do not say the customary blessing over the mourners, but they console them standing in a row and dismiss the crowd. On a festival they do not set the bier down in the street, lest the festival be turned into mourning. Women may lament on a festival, but may not clap their hands. R. Ishmael says that those next to the bier may clap their hands. On the new moons, at the feast of dedication, and at Purim, one may lament and clap the hands, but not wail. But once the dead man has been buried, it is lawful neither to lament nor to clap the hands. What is ʿiyyui, affliction? It is where all mourn together. A qinah, lamentation, is where one begins and the other wailing women follow her in raising the cry of mourning, according to Jer. 9.19. Moed Katon c.3.7.8.9.

units.la: §. Quædam Epicedia retulit Cl. Buxt. Lex. Talm.1524. in ןשמ. Lamentatrices ad plangendum utebantur tympanis Vid. Kelim c.1ȝ. in fine. & Sisbro quod Heb. מנעים & Targ. רביען vel רביעית vocatur. Kelim c.16.
units.tr: §. Buxtorf, in Lex. Talm. 1524 under "mesapped", has reported certain funeral songs. Wailing women used drums in their lamentation; see Kelim c.13 at the end; and Sisbro, which in Hebrew is called mena'im, and in the Targum ravi'an or ravi'it. Kelim c.16.

units.la: §. De חיבוט הקבר Percussione qua fit in sepulchro vid. Buxt. L.Talm.p.698. Obtectio Barbæ & capitis est signum luctus, Kimchi Ezech.24.17. אגרא דבי טמא שתיקותא Optimum domus luctus est silentium, h.e. ut patienter feramus. Adag.
units.tr: §. On the striking that is done in the grave see Buxt. L. Talm. p.698. Covering the beard and head is a sign of mourning, Kimchi on Ezek. 24.17. "The best of a house of mourning is silence", that is, that we bear it patiently. Adag.

units.la: §. Circa suam sepulturam anxius erat ille de quo legimus in Nidda sol. 20. 1. & Schabbat sol. 114. 1. ibi enim sic loquens introducitur. Ne sepelite me vestibus albis, neq; vestibus nigris; sed בכלי האולירים vestibus Vliarimis, qua per more advehuntur. Acumine opus est, ut odoremur, quænam illæ vestes sint, Ego certè illas non assequor.
units.tr: §. Anxious about his own burial was the man of whom we read in Nidda fol. 20.1 and Shabbat fol. 114.1. For there he is introduced speaking thus: "Do not bury me in white garments, nor in black garments, but in Vliarim garments, which are commonly brought in." One needs sharp wits to work out what those garments were; I certainly cannot make them out.

units.la: §. אנינות לילה mæror noctis non est ex lege (Mosis) sed ex statutis scribarum. Zevachin sol. 101. 1.
units.tr: §. The mourning of the night is not from the law (of Moses) but from the statutes of the scribes. Zevachin fol. 101.1.

units.la: §. De שדה כוכים agro stentium vid.Lex.Talm. Buxt. p.304.
units.tr: §. On the field of caves see Lex. Talm. Buxt. p.304.

units.la: §. Duo mortui qui unà sepulti sunt nudi נעשו גלגלי זה לוה fiunt convolutiones sibi invicem: i. e. perindè habentur, ac si quilibet eorum cum involucris sepultus esset. Nasir sol.51.1. Similem locum citat Baal Aruch ex Nidda sol. 27. 2.
units.tr: §. Two dead men buried together naked "become rolls to one another", that is, they are regarded as if each had been buried wrapped in shrouds. Nazir fol. 51.1. Baal Aruch cites a similar passage from Nidda fol. 27.2.

units.la: §. De Tibiis in luctu adhibitis consule Cl. Buxt. L.Talm. p.766.
units.tr: §. On the flutes used in mourning, consult Cl. Buxt. L. Talm. p.766.

units.la: §. Nubilis puella non habet licentiam deturpandi se ipsam tempore luctus propter patrem suum, id est, squalido vestitu se odiosam procis exponere, quibus potiùs placëre stude-
units.tr: §. A marriageable girl has no licence to disfigure herself in time of mourning for her father; that is, she must not expose herself to suitors, in squalid clothing, as repellent. Rather she should take care to please them with becoming adornment.

units.la: bit decenti ornatu. Taanith fol.13. 2.
units.tr: Taanith fol. 13.2.

units.la: Ludi varii fuerunt apud Judæos. Ludebant פּספּס Calculis five latrunculis, fritillis Sanhed. fol.25.2. Aruch in rad. Ludebant etiam בצוחם הקוביאות Lusu alearum, & כמחום הקלפים Lusu Chartarum Vid. Sanhed. fol.24 2. Schabbat c. 23. in Mischna.Cl.Buxt. in קלף de Ludo Schach scripsit tract.Erud.D.Hyde.Bibliot.Oxoniensis.
