units.tr: There were various games among the Jews. They played with pebbles or draughtsmen [Hebrew], with dice, Sanhedrin fol. 25.2; Aruch in the root. They also played at dice-throwing [Hebrew] and at the game of cards [Hebrew]; see Sanhedrin fol. 24.2 and Shabbat c.23 in the Mishnah. Cl. Buxtorf, under qelef, wrote on the game of chess; Dr Hyde wrote a tract on it in the Bibliotheca Oxoniensis.

units.la: Lunatici vid. Daemoniaci.
units.tr: On lunatics see Demoniacs.

units.la: Lydda fuit vicus, civitati magnitudine non cedens Ioseph. Antiq. lib.20. c.5. Lydda distabat Hierosolymis spatio iteneris diarii, quod elicitur ex Maaser Scheni cap.5.2. ibi enim dicitur fructus vineæ annum quartum agentis ab illis civitatibus quæ uno solùm die distabant Hierosolymas afferri debuisse, in ipsarum autem numero recensetur Lydda. Certè magnam non fuisse distantiam videtur ex hoc dicto. Fœmina Lyddanæ deposunt massam, ascendunt ad templum, orant, & redeunt, priusquam fermentetur. Gemar. Hierof. in Maaser Scheni ubi supra. Vbi quidem aliquid hyperbolici est, interea semper manet scopus, illis scilicet fœminis per illam distantiam nihil detrimenti accrevisse.
units.tr: Lydda was a village, not inferior to a city in size. Josephus, Antiq. lib. 20 c.5. Lydda was a day's journey from Jerusalem, as is gathered from Maaser Scheni 5.2. For there it is said that the fruit of a vineyard in its fourth year had to be brought up from those cities which were only one day distant from Jerusalem, and Lydda is counted among them. From this saying it seems certain that the distance was not great. "The women of Lydda knead the dough, go up to the temple, pray, and return before it is leavened." Gemara Hierosolymitanum on Maaser Scheni, as above. There is certainly something hyperbolical here, but the point always remains that those women suffered no loss from that distance.

units.la: §. Præfecturam Scholæ Lyddanæ tempore Rabban Gamalielis gessit Akiba, Rosch Hafschana cap.1.7. Gamaliele amoto à præfectura Iabhnensi successit Akibæ in Lydda. R.Tarphon Vid. Hierof.Iom tobh fol.62.1. & Taanith c.3.41.
units.tr: §. Akiba held the headship of the school at Lydda in the time of Rabban Gamaliel, Rosh Hashanah c.1.7. When Gamaliel was removed from the headship at Jabneh, Akiba succeeded him at Lydda. On R. Tarphon see Jer. Yom Tob fol. 62.1 and Taanith c.3.41.

units.la: §. De variis historiis quæ acciderunt בלוד in Lydda vid. Hierof. Succah fol. 51.4. Hierof. Nedarim fol.40.4. Ben Sadta ibi insidiis interceptus fuit. H.Sanhed. f.52.4. vid. Hierof.Taanith fol.66.1. Megillah fol.70. 3. in quibus locis dicitur Papum & Lulienum martyrium ibi subiisse. Intendebant semel quidam Galilaei Lyddae intercalare annum, sed res male ipsis cessit Hierof. Sanhed. fol. 18. 3. A Romanis fugiens Lyddam se proripuit Kosba Bar Vlla. Hierof. Trumot fol.46.1.
units.tr: §. On the various stories that happened in Lydda [Hebrew], see Jer. Succah fol. 51.4, Jer. Nedarim fol. 40.4. Ben Sadta was there intercepted by an ambush. Sanhedrin fol. 52.4. See Jer. Taanith fol. 66.1 and Megillah fol. 70.3, where it is said that Papus and Julianus underwent martyrdom there. Once certain Galileans tried to intercalate a year at Lydda, but the matter turned out badly for them, Jer. Sanhedrin fol. 18.3. Fleeing from the Romans, Kosba Bar Kochba hurried himself to Lydda, Jer. Trumot fol. 46.1.

units.la: §. Lyddae plurimae Scholae,ut Camera Beth Aram. Hierof. Schekalim fol.30.2. Camera Beth Lebaz'ah, Hierof.Scheviit fol.35.1. Camera Beth Netheza Bab.Sanhed. f.74.
units.tr: §. Lydda had very many schools: the Chamber of Beth Aram, Jer. Shekalim fol. 30.2; the Chamber of Beth Lebaz'ah, Jer. Shevi'it fol. 35.1; the Chamber of Beth Netheza, Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 74.

units.la: 1. De quibusdam Rabbinis Lyddensibus v. Hierof. Schekalim fol.49.2. Hierof. Succah fol.53.1.
units.tr: 1. On certain Lydda rabbis see Jer. Shekalim fol. 49.2 and Jer. Succah fol. 53.1.

units.la: R. Eliefer Caesareae moriens Lyddae voluit fepeliri. Bab.Sanhed. fol.68.1. De Villa Lyddensium mentio fit in Gittin c.1.1. Villa Tebi erat fita ab oriente Lyddae Bab. Rosch Hafchana fol. 13.2. de celebri illa Medicorum consultatione in Lydda circa arcam offibus repletam Vid. Hierof. Beracot fol.3.1.
units.tr: R. Eliezer, dying at Caesarea, wished to be buried at Lydda. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 68.1. Mention is made of a village of the Lyddans in Gittin c.1.1. The village of Tebi lay east of Lydda, Bab. Rosh Hashanah fol. 13.2. On the famous consultation of physicians at Lydda concerning an ark filled with bones, see Jer. Berakot fol. 3.1.

units.la: M.
units.tr: M.

units.la: MActationis locus in templo vid. Maym. Hal. Beth Habech c. 5. circa finem.
units.tr: Mactationis locus in templo: see Maym. Hal. Beth Habech ch. 5, near the end.

units.la: MACULAS septem res aufferunt; fputum icium, aqua fabarum, urina, nitrum, fapo,cimolia, Afchlcg. Nidda c.9.6. Maym. Kelim c.2.
units.tr: Seven things remove stains: spittle, bean-water, urine, natron, soap, cimolia (fuller's earth). Afchlcg. Nidda ch. 9.6. Maym. Kelim ch. 2.

units.la: MAGDALA erat urbs prope Hierosolymam. Echa Rabbati fol. 75.2. Clericus Magdala, ordinavit candelas unaquaque vesperaSabbathi, ascendit Hierosolymam, oravit,& rediit,& accendit eas cum iam ingrederetur Sabbathum. Glossa dicit fuisse מגדל צבעים Magdala Zebaim vocata, de qua dicunt in Echa Rabbethi fol.71.4. & Taanith Hierof. fol.69. 1. quòd destructa sit propter adulteria.
units.tr: Magdala was a city near Jerusalem. Echa Rabbati fol. 75.2: A priest of Magdala lit lamps each Sabbath eve. He went up to Jerusalem, prayed, returned, and lit them just as the Sabbath was about to begin. The Gloss says it was called Magdala Zebaim [מגדל צבעים], of which they speak in Echa Rabbathi fol. 71.4 and Taanith Hierosolymitanum fol. 69.1, that it was destroyed on account of adulteries.

units.la: §. Ad אבעיא מגדל se contulit aliquando R. Ionathan, ut medelam aliquam acquireret calvitiei suæ. Midrasch Cohelet. fol.84.2.
units.tr: §. Concerning the question [אבעיא מגדל], R. Jonathan once went to obtain some remedy for his baldness. Midrasch Cohelet fol. 84.2.

units.la: §. Erat deinde quædam Magdala propè Tiberiadem, ut elicitur ex Hierof.Maaserot fol.50. 3. Si quis duas habeat areas, unam Magdalæ, alteram Tiberiade, fructus amovere licet ab illa qua Magdala, comedendos in illa qua Tiberiade. Et Hierof.Scheviit fol 38 4. Qui Magdala transfit, potuit praconis Tiberiade clamantis vocem audire.
units.tr: §. There was then a certain Magdala near Tiberias, as is drawn from Hierosolymitanum Maaserot fol. 50.3: "If anyone has two fields, one at Magdala and the other at Tiberias, he may remove the produce from the one at Magdala, to be eaten in the one at Tiberias." And Hierosolymitanum Scheviit fol. 38.4: "He who passed Magdala could hear the voice of the herald calling at Tiberias."

units.la: §. De מגדל שיר. Vid. Hierof.Scheviit fol.36. ambiguum est an sit Turris Stratonis vel Cæsarea.
units.tr: §. Concerning Migdal Shir, see Hierosolymitanum Scheviit fol. 36; it is uncertain whether it is the Tower of Straton or Caesarea.

units.la: §. מגדל עדר Turris gregis non longè Hierosolymis distabat, sita erat à latere urbis meridionali, omnia enim iumenta quæ reperiebantur Hierosolymis usque ad Migdal Eder, sacrificanda erant, Hierof. Kiddushin fol.63 1. Bab. Kiddushin fol.55.1. nam (notat Gloss.) supponi potuit ea ex Hierosolymis fuisse evagata, plurima enim iumenta inde exeuntia fuisse sacrificanda. Quod in locis diffitioribus locum habere non poffet. Vid. Cl. Leigtfoot Chor. Marci p.36.
units.tr: §. Migdal Eder [מגדל עדר], "the Tower of the Flock," was not far from Jerusalem; it lay on the southern side of the city. For all the cattle found at Jerusalem up to Migdal Eder had to be sacrificed (Hierosolymitanum Kiddushin fol. 63.1; Bab. Kiddushin fol. 55.1). The Gloss notes that one could suppose they had strayed from Jerusalem, since most cattle leaving there were to be sacrificed; this could not hold in more distant places. See Cl. Lightfoot, Chor. Marci p. 36.

units.la: Magistratus vid.Synedrium. Cavete ab iis qui constituti sunt in potestate, non enim adiunguntur sibi hominem, nisi cogat aliqua necessitas. Pirke avot. 2. אהוב את המלאכה ושנא את הרבנות Ama opus & laborem, & odi officia Magistratus; Illis enim adhærent sua onera & periculà. Pirkę Avoth. c.1. Interim nisi Magistratus effet,unus alterum vivum devoraret. Ibid. Va potestati quasepelit Dominos suos. Pesachim sol.87.2. Pœnæ indicium est quando Magistratus citiùs è vivis abripiuntur. Apud Iudæos olim Personæ munera publica obtinentes cāstigabantur. Maymon. lele Hamikd. cap. 4. sub finem.
units.tr: Magistratus: see Synedrium. "Beware of those who hold power, for they do not draw near to a man unless some necessity compels them." Pirke Avot 2: "Love work, and hate lordship [אהוב את המלאכה ושנא את הרבנות]" ("love labour and hate the office of magistrate"), for its burdens and dangers cling to those who hold it. Pirke Avoth ch. 1. Indeed, if there were no magistrate, one would devour the other alive. Ibid. "Woe to the authority which buries its masters." Pesachim fol. 87.2. It is a sign of punishment when magistrates are snatched from the living more quickly. Among the Jews of old, persons holding public offices were punished. Maymon. Hilchot Hamikdash ch. 4, near the end.

units.la: MAGIA. Magus is est, qui rem patrat non autem qui solum oculis imponit: qui rem patrat tenetur pœnâ lapidationis, qui verò oculis imponit liber est.Sanhed.c.7.1.
units.tr: MAGIC. A magus is one who performs the thing, not one who merely deceives the eyes. He who performs it is liable to the penalty of stoning, but he who merely deceives the eyes is free. Sanhed. ch. 7.1.

units.la: §. De Infusurrationibus, amuletis, Vid. Amuleta. De miris magicis plurima extant in paginis Talmudicis, In vestibulo hæc duo admirationem merentur. 1. Quòd Senator Synedrii Magni debuerit esse instructus artibus Astrologorum, Præstigiatorum, Divinantium, Venefcorum &c. ut de iis deinde reos iudicare possit. Maym. Sanhed. c.2. 2. Quòd Camera quædam in ipso templo àMago condita fuerit. Gloss. in Middot c.5.3. Camera Happarva condita fuit à mago quodam, cui nomen Parvah, arte Magicâ.
units.tr: §. On incantations and amulets, see Amuleta. Much about magical marvels is found in the Talmudic pages. At the threshold, two things deserve our wonder. (1) That a member of the Great Sanhedrin ought to have been instructed in the arts of astrologers, illusionists, diviners, poisoners, and so on, so that he could then judge the accused in such matters. Maym. Sanhed. ch. 2. (2) That a certain chamber in the temple itself was founded by a magus. Gloss on Middot ch. 5.3: "The chamber Happarva was founded by a certain magus named Parvah, by magical art."

units.la: §. Nunc indiscriminatim referemus illa loca, in quibus de Magis & Præstigiatoribus eorumque artibus mentio fit. Hierof.Sanhed. sol. 18.3. Iverunt viginti quatuor ex schola Rabbi (ex Galilæa,) ut intercalarent annum Lydda, sed omnes perierunt oculo malo, GlossVeneficiis &c. Ibid.sol.25.4. R. Iofua Magum magicâ superat arte, & submergit in mare. Hierof.Sanhed. sol. 23.2. Bab.Sanhed. f.44.2. in Glossa refertur historia de oɗoginta fœminis veneficis Ascalone tunâ die suspensis à Simeone Ben Schetach: quia fœminæ proruperant ad veneficia.
units.tr: §. Now we will list, without distinction, the passages in which mention is made of magi and illusionists and their arts. Hierosolymitanum Sanhedrin fol. 18.3: "Twenty-four men from Rabbi's school (from Galilee) went to intercalate the year at Lydda, but all perished through the evil eye," the Gloss says, by poisonings, etc. Ibid. fol. 25.4: R. Joshua surpassed a magus in magical art and drowned him in the sea. Hierosolymitanum Sanhedrin fol. 23.2; Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 44.2: the Gloss relates the story of eighty poisoning women at Ascalon, hanged on one day by Simeon ben Shetach, because the women had rushed into poisonings.

units.la: §. Bab.Taanith fol.24. varia referuntur miracula à Rabbinis edita. Vid. N'kodemus. De Miris in disputatione publica editis, à Rabbi Eliesere filio Hyrcani vid. Bava Metzia f.59.2. Plurimi Rabbini memorantur quòd essent [illegible, ~3 letters] Periti in edendis miraculis, ut Abba Chelchia & Chanina in Ɩuchas. fol.20.1. & R. Chanina Ben Dufa, de quo admiranda referuntur in Bab. Beracot fol.33.34. Vid. Iuchasin fol.56.2. Quidam precibus pluvias impetrarunt vid. Trac. Taanith, & Ieiunia. Quidam authoritatem suam stabiliverunt voce cœlitus edita, vid. Bath Kol. Quæ omnia magis sapiunt artes præstigiarum & magiæ, quàm vim Spiritus Sancti.
units.tr: §. Bab. Taanith fol. 24: various miracles performed by the Rabbis are related. See Nkodemus. Concerning the miracles performed in public disputation by Rabbi Eliezer son of Hyrcanus, see Bava Metzia fol. 59.2. Many Rabbis are recorded as being [illegible, about three letters], skilled in performing miracles, such as Abba Chelchia and Chanina in Iuchasin fol. 20.1, and R. Chanina ben Dosa, of whom wonderful things are related in Bab. Beracot fol. 33–34. See Iuchasin fol. 56.2. Some obtained rain by prayer; see the tractate Taanith, and Fasts. Some established their authority by a voice sent from heaven; see Bath Kol. All of these smack more of the arts of illusion and magic than of the power of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: §. Ad magicas incantationes [illegible, ~2 letters] utebantur, quæ erat cutis à capite alicuius mortui detracta. Vid.Gloss. in Cholin fol.123.1. & Aruch in Rad. De Præstigiatore arte magica thefaurum quærente vid. Midrasch Tillim Psalm.68. Effodiebant magi mortuos ad detrahendas ipsis vestes. Bava Bathra fol.58.1. Nomina Diabolorum per quæ artes magicæ fiunt dicuntur Nomina impuritatis, oppositè ad Nomina Spiritus Sancti. R. Salomo in Sanhed. fol.91.1. De Pythone vid. f.1. vocabantur Scifcitantes os Ieddoah. Ionath. Lev.20.6. Habebant in usu os illud quod secund. Scholiasten ex quodam animante defumebatur, ponere in os fuum, & illud deinde ex fe loquebatur. Sanhed.fol.65.1. De illo animali vid. in A. Animal. Vid. etiam Maym. in Avoda Zarah.cap.6.fol.32. Quid fint Præftigiæ difputat Bechai in Legem fol. 95. 4. 96. 1. Vid. Buxt.Lex.Talm. p.1102.
units.tr: §. For magical incantations they used [illegible, about two letters], which was the skin stripped from the head of a dead man. See the Gloss on Cholin fol. 123.1 and Aruch under Rad. On an illusionist seeking treasure by magical art, see Midrasch Tillim on Psalm 68. Magi dug up the dead in order to strip them of their garments. Bava Bathra fol. 58.1. The names of devils through which magical arts are performed are called "names of impurity", in contrast to the "names of the Holy Spirit". R. Solomon on Sanhed. fol. 91.1. Concerning the Python, see f. 1; they were called "those who consult the bone of Jeddoah" (Jonathan on Lev. 20.6). They used to place in their mouth that bone which, according to the scholiast, was taken from a certain animal, and it would then speak out of itself. Sanhed. fol. 65.1. On that animal, see under Animal. See also Maim. in Avoda Zarah ch. 6, fol. 32. Bechai, on the Law, fol. 95.4 and 96.1, discusses what illusions are. See Buxt. Lex. Talm. p. 1102.

units.la: §. ישן idem eft quod magus Sotah. fol.22.1. Pharao qui fuit in diebus Mofis Magus fuit. Moed Katon fol.18.1. Qui difcit verbum unum à Mago reus eft mortis. Schabbat fol.75.1.
units.tr: §. ישן is the same as magus. Sotah fol. 22.1: Pharaoh, who was in the days of Moses, was a magus. Moed Katon fol. 18.1: whoever learns one word from a magus is liable to death. Schabbat fol. 75.1.

units.la: MALEDICTA, iniuriæ, patienter funt ferendæ. Berefchit R. Sect. 45. Si dicat tibi quifpiam una auris tua,efl auris afini, וחיחו לא Ne cures,ambo (aures tuæ funt aures afini,) parato tibi frænum. Item Bava Kama fol.92.2. Si fo.ius tuus te vocet afinum, etiam fellam afini fuper te admove. In eundem fenfum Chriftus, Matth.5.39. De Calumniis v. f. 1.
units.tr: MALEDICTA: insults and injuries are to be borne patiently. Berefchit Rabba sect. 45: "If someone says to you, 'One of your ears is an ass's ear,' [וחיחו לא] do not heed it; both (your ears are an ass's ears) — prepare a bridle for yourself." Likewise Bava Kama fol. 92.2: "If your companion calls you an ass, put the saddle of an ass on yourself too." To the same effect Christ, Matt. 5.39. On Calumniis see f. 1.

units.la: de MANIPULO עומר & שכחה vid. in S. שכחה.de MANETE Hæretico vid. Buxt. Lex. Talm.1165.de MANUUM lotione vid. LOTIO.
units.tr: On the MANIPULUS [עומר] and [שכחה], see under S. שכחה. On the heretic MANETE see Buxt. Lex. Talm. 1165. On the MANUUM washing, see LOTIO.

units.la: §. Notandum ipfos Iudæos in quibufdam actionibus religionem fpectantibus, non admiffe concurfum manus finiftræ cum dextra. Exempla funt in Schabbat Maym. c.29. Poculum vini, ad fanctificandum ingreffum Sabbathi adhibitum, dexterâ manu fumendum erat, auxilio finiftræ non admiffo. Item in Babyl. Ioma fol.49.1. Ne quis fanguinem Sacrificii recipiat in vafculum, adducat ad altare, vel fpargat manu finiftra. Schammæus fe noluit cibare nisi manu unâ. Ibid.fol.77.2. Confer Matth.6.3.
units.tr: §. It should be noted that the Jews themselves, in certain actions concerning religion, did not admit the joining of the left hand with the right. Examples are in Schabbat Maym. ch. 29: "A cup of wine, used to sanctify the entrance of the Sabbath, was to be taken in the right hand, the left hand not being admitted to help." Likewise in Bab. Ioma fol. 49.1: "No one should receive the blood of the sacrifice in a vessel, bring it to the altar, or sprinkle it with the left hand." Shammai would not eat except with one hand. Ibid. fol. 77.2. Compare Matt. 6.3.

units.la: MANUUM Impofitio. Vid. Sacrificia.
units.tr: MANUUM imposition: see Sacrificia.

units.la: §. Australem Galilææ regionem excepit Isacharitis : eam nonnullæ collocant ab Austro maris Gennefaritici non male; at male, dum eam ad istud ipsum protendunt, aliæque pessimè dum ab Occidente istius maris eam statuunt. De ea sic Josephus Antiq. lib. 5. cap. 1. Καὶ μετὰ τὰς Ισαχαρεις Καρμηλὸν τὴ ὀρ@ καὶ τὴν πεδιάδα τὰ μέρη ποιησαμένη τρόμοντα, τὸ δὲ Ιταβυρ ὄρ@ τὶ πλατις.
units.tr: §. The southern region of Galilee was received by Issachar. Some place it not badly on the south of the Sea of Gennesaret; but badly, insofar as they extend it right up to that sea, and others very badly when they set it to the west of that sea. Concerning it, Josephus says thus, Antiq. bk. 5, ch. 1: Καὶ μετὰ τὰς Ισαχαρεις Καρμηλὸν τὴ ὀρ@ καὶ τὴν πεδιάδα τὰ μέρη ποιησαμένη τρόμοντα, τὸ δὲ Ιταβυρ ὄρ@ τὶ πλατις [And after the Issacharites, the region which made Carmel a mountain and the plain its parts ... and Mount Tabor, broad ...].

units.la: §. Isacharitidi à septentrione contigua erat Zabulonitis ; eam tabulæ quædam iuxta mare Gennefaretieum expandunt, quædam longè supra Mare istud disponunt versus aquilonem, priores secundùm Cl. Leigtfootum Chor. Mt. 17. non bene, posteriores pessimè; vid. Joseph. l. c. quando inquit, Ζαβυλωνίτ) τὴν μέχει γε-ιωσφίτιδ, κωδηματαν δὲ τὰς κάρμηλον καὶ διὰ λεσσαν, ἐλαχιον.
units.tr: §. Adjacent to Issachar on the north was Zabulon. Some maps spread it out beside the Sea of Gennesaret, others set it well away from that sea towards the north. The former, according to Cl. Lightfoot, Chor. Matt. 17, is not right; the latter is very wrong. See Josephus, l.c., where he says, Ζαβυλωνίτ) τὴν μέχει γε-ιωσφίτιδ, κωδηματαν δὲ τὰς κάρμηλον καὶ διὰ λεσσαν, ἐλαχιον [the Zebulonites reaching to Gennesaritis, ... Carmel ... lesser].

units.la: §. Duplicem Iordanis fontem assignant tabulæ, non absque insigni errore; nulla alia ratione duƈti, quàm quòd Joseph de bello lib.4. c.1. mentionem faciat, Iordanis minoris & maioris, cùm tamen Iordanes maior & minor dicatur, non ratione duorum fontium, aut duorum rivorum discretorum, sed ratione distinctæ magnitudinis eiusdem rivi. Oricebatur Iordanes פמיאו מעית E spelunca Panneadis: Bab.Bava Bathra sol.74.2. Gloss. in Bab. Megillah sol. 6. 1. ad פמיו וו ביול. ( not. non è spelunca sed è spelunca.) Et vocabatur Parvus, ufquedum sueret in lacum Samochonitin, ex illo vero fluens, cum incremento magno vocatur Iordanes Maior. De Iordane vid. f. 1.
units.tr: §. The maps assign a double source to the Jordan, not without a notable error. They were led to this by no other reason than that Josephus, in de bello bk. 4, ch. 1, mentions the Lesser and the Greater Jordan; yet the Jordan is called greater and lesser not on account of two sources or two separate streams, but on account of the distinct size of the same stream. The Jordan rose "from the cave of Panias" [פמיאו מעית], Bab. Bava Bathra fol. 74.2; Gloss on Bab. Megillah fol. 6.1 at [פמיו וו ביול] (note: the reading should be "from the cave," not as printed). It was called Small as long as it flowed into the lake Samochonitis; flowing out from there with great increase, it is called the Greater Jordan. On the Jordan see f. 1.

units.la: §. Collocant tabulæ mare Gennesareticum extra tribum Nephtalitican, Talmudici verò ponunt illud intra eam. Bab.Bava Kama f.81.
units.tr: §. The tables place the Gennesaretic Sea outside the tribe of Naphtalitic, but the Talmudists place it within that tribe. Bab. Bava Kama f.81.

units.la: 2. Traditio eft ... Mare Tiberiadis eft portionis Nephtalitica. Hierof. Bava Bathra fol.15.1. Dederunt τῷ Nephtali plenum funiculum (ut extrahere posset retia) ab ora maris australi. His adde Ioseph. Antiq.lib. 5. c. 1. Νεφθαλίν πεφίλαβον τὰ φεὺς τὰς ἀνατολὰς τὰς πεςαμμένα μέχρι Δαμασκοῦ πόλεως.
units.tr: 2. The tradition is: The Sea of Tiberias is of the portion of Naphtali. Hierosolymitan Talmud, Bava Bathra fol.15.1. They gave to Naphtali the full cord (to draw nets) from the southern shore. To these add Josephus, Antiquities, book 5, chapter 1: Naphtali possessed the lands toward the east, extending as far as the city of Damascus [Νεφθαλίν πεφίλαβον τὰ φεὺς τὰς ἀνατολὰς τὰς πεςαμμένα μέχρι Δαμασκοῦ πόλεως].

units.la: §. Vifcheri Tabula ubi Tiberiadem, urbem tantâ famâ celebrem, poneret, dubia hærere videtur, an in effluxu vel inflexu Iordanis in mare Gennesareticum, vel an sequeretur illas, quæ in maris Gennesaretici medio littore hallucinantes illam posuerunt. Tutissimum est illam collocare ad effluxum Iordanis, ad littus lacus Meridionale, nam ad influxum eius eam statuere non potes, quia Iosephus dicit in vita sua p.650. Edit. Froben. Tiberiada non distare à Scythopoli nisi cxx. stadiis; iam verò lacus Gennesareticus ipse erat longitudinis stadiorum C. Et Scythopolis erat limes ultimus Galilææ versus austrum. Vid. Bethschean & Galilæa.
units.tr: §. Vischer's table, where it places Tiberias, a city of such fame, seems uncertain whether to put it at the outflow or the inflow of the Jordan into the Sea of Gennesaret, or whether to follow those who, wandering in their thoughts, placed it on the middle of the shore of the Sea of Gennesaret. It is safest to place it at the outflow of the Jordan, on the southern shore of the lake, for you cannot place it at the inflow, because Josephus says in his Life, p.650, Edit. Froben., that Tiberias was not more than 120 stadia from Scythopolis; and the Sea of Gennesaret itself was 100 stadia long. Scythopolis was also the last boundary of Galilee toward the south. See Bethschean & Galilæa.

units.la: §. Iulia Beth-aramphta sita erat, ad ipsissimum influxum Iordanis. Secundùm illa Iosephi de bello lib.3. cap.35. Iordanes à lacu Samochonite centum alia stadia emensus, μετὰ πόλιν Ἰουλιάδα ἀπὸ τὴν Γεννησὰρ μίσλω. Quæ arguunt Iuliada præterlabi Iordanem antequàm Gennesareticum lacum ingrediatur.
units.tr: §. Julias, Beth-aramphta, was situated at the very inflow of the Jordan. According to Josephus, De bello, book 3, chapter 35: The Jordan, having traveled one hundred other stadia from the Lake Samochonitis, past the city of Julias, from Gennesar [μετὰ πόλιν Ἰουλιάδα ἀπὸ τὴν Γεννησὰρ μίσλω]. These passages show that Julias lies beside the Jordan before the river enters the Sea of Gennesaret.

units.la: §. Non probabile est Chorazin Matth. xi. 21. fuisse urbeculam, & sitam prope vel trans Iordanem ut tabulæ volunt; חורשין Chorafchin enim loca saltuosa denotat, quibus maximè abundabat regio Nephtalica Hierof. Bava Bathra sol.15.1. illa itaque citius in Galilæa quam in Peræa collocanda erit.
units.tr: §. It is not probable that Chorazin, Matt. xi. 21, was a small town situated near or beyond the Jordan, as the tables want; for חורשין [Chorafchin] denotes wooded places, of which the Naphtalite region had a great abundance (Hierosolymitan Talmud, Bava Bathra sol.15.1). It is therefore better to place it in Galilee than in Peraea.

units.la: §. Sodoma malè pingitur in finibus Aquilonaribus maris Asphaltitis,nam potiùs in extremitate eius australi collocanda est, vid. Gen.x. 19. Termini (ananæorum erant à Sidone (ab Aquilone) ad Gazam, (ab Austro) ut pergis vel donec accedas ad Sodomam. Insuper ultima extensionis eius ora austrum versus, fuit Zoar, ut elicitur ex verbis Iosephi de bello lib. 4. cap. 5. Longitudo (maris Asphaltitis) est dlxxx. stad. Prout extenditur usque ad Zoarem Arabiæ. At Zoar à Sodoma distabat solummodò quatuor milliaribus. Hierof. Beracot sol. 2. 3. consentit hist. Gen.xix. 23. Iudica hinc quâ authoritate Tabulæ Zoarem & speluncam Lothi collocent in Iudæa, ad oram Borealem Asphaltitis.
units.tr: §. Sodom is wrongly depicted on the northern borders of the Dead Sea; it should rather be placed at its southern extremity. See Gen. x. 19: The borders of the Canaanites were from Sidon (toward the north) to Gaza (toward the south), as you go until you come to Sodom. Moreover, the farthest extent of its shore toward the south was Zoar, as is gathered from the words of Josephus, De bello, book 4, chapter 5: The length of the Dead Sea is 580 stadia, as it extends as far as Zoar of Arabia. But Zoar was only four miles from Sodom. The Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot sol.2.3, agrees with the history in Gen. xix. 23. Judge from this by what authority the tables place Zoar and the cave of Lot in Judea, on the northern shore of the Asphaltite Lake.

units.la: §. Finxerunt sibi Tabulæ Adrichomii,Tirini, longissimum montium dorsum, ab ipso fere mari rubro, ad terram fere Cananitidem & illum nominarunt Montem Amorrhæum : Cùm tamen mons Amorrhæus solùm initium sumferit à Cadesch Barneah vid. Deut. 1. 19. 20. Cl. Leigtfoot Chor. Matth. 23.
units.tr: §. The tables of Adrichomius and Tirinus have invented a very long ridge of mountains, reaching from almost the Red Sea to nearly the land of Canaan, and they called it the Amorite Mountain. Yet the Amorite mountain began only at Kadesh-barnea; see Deut. 1. 19, 20. Cl. Lightfoot, Chor. Matth. 23.

units.la: §. Insignem insicitiam arguit quòd quædam Tabulæ Lod & Lyddam pro duobus oppidis habeant; Lod non longè à Iordane, Lyddam Z 4
units.tr: §. It shows remarkable carelessness that some tables take Lod and Lydda to be two towns: Lod not far from the Jordan, Lydda

units.la: non longè à Mari Mediterraneo ; cùm tamen Lod & Lydda nihil difcriminis habeant, nisi quòd illud sit Hebraicum, alterum Græcum.
units.tr: not far from the Mediterranean Sea; yet Lod and Lydda differ in nothing, except that the one is Hebrew and the other Greek.

units.la: §. Ex hiltoria vaccæ Rufæ & eius suppedaneo exstructo à porta orientali in Montem Olivetù patet,monte Olivetum fuiíle è regione templi; at Tabula impreffa à Mariette Parisiis ipsum ad latus collocat. Ex hiftoria Simeonis Iufti loma f. 69.1 videtur adhuc aliam fuiffe propè Hierosolymas apud locum סיפ, Antipatridam, præter illam quam tabulæ in Samaritano tradtu ponunt. An Bethphage urbecula fuerit, vel tractus folùm montis oliveti, vid. in Bethphage. De errore Baronii circa Regionem Decapolitanam vid. Cl.Leigtfooti Chorog. Marci p.54.
units.tr: §. From the story of the red heifer, and of the causeway built from the eastern gate to the Mount of Olives, it is clear that the Mount of Olives lay opposite the temple; yet the table printed by Mariette at Paris places it at the side. From the history of Simeon Justus, Yoma f.69.1, it seems there was another, near Jerusalem, at the place סיפ [Sip], Antipatris, besides the one the tables put in the Samaritan district. Whether Bethphage was a small town or only a stretch of the Mount of Olives, see under Bethphage. On Baronius's error concerning the Decapolitan region, see Cl. Lightfoot, Chorographia Marci, p.54.

units.la: MARIA feptem ambiunt terram Ifraeliticam. 1. יםא רבא Mare Mediterraneum. 2. יםא דטיבריא Mare Tiberiadis. 3. יםא דמלח Mare Sodomiticum. 4. יםא דסמכי Mare (lacus) Samochonitis. 5. יםא דחולטה Mare arenosum i.e. lacus Sirbonis. 6. יםא רשלחת Quod quid sit ignoramus, nisi sit forsan lacus Cendevii. 7. יםא ראפמיא Mare Apamia. Hierof.Kilaim fol.32.1. Bab. Bava Bathra fol 74.2.
units.tr: The seven seas surround the land of Israel: (1) the Great Sea [יםא רבא], the Mediterranean Sea; (2) the Sea of Tiberias [יםא דטיבריא], the Sea of Tiberias; (3) the Salt Sea [יםא דמלח], the Sea of Sodom; (4) the Sea of Samochonitis [יםא דסמכי], the Sea (lake) of Samochonitis; (5) the Sandy Sea [יםא דחולטה], the sandy sea, that is, the lake of Sirbon; (6) [יםא דשלחת], what this is we do not know, unless perhaps it is the lake of Cendevius; (7) the Sea of Apamea [יםא דאפמיא], the Sea of Apamea. Hierosolymitan Talmud, Kilaim fol.32.1; Bab. Bava Bathra fol.74.2.

units.la: §. Ora maritima maris mediterranei vocatur מדינת הים Gemaristæ ad Hierof. Scheviit fol.36.3.4. dicunt in mari mediterraneo הניסים שבים Insulas videri, ac fi linea dudla effet a montibus Amanæ ad fluvium Ægypti. In Chartis & tabulis certè nullæ videntur insulæ, in illo loco positæ.
units.tr: §. The coastline of the Mediterranean is called the region of the sea [מדינת הים]. The Gemarists, in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shevi'it fol.36.3.4, say that in the Mediterranean there are the islands in the sea [הניסים שבים], islands which appear as if a line were drawn from the Amanus mountains to the river of Egypt. In the charts and tables, however, no islands are shown at all in that place.

units.la: §. המלח ים Vocatur Mare Sodomiticum; המלח ibi magis Bitumen quàm Sal denotat;
units.tr: §. The Sea of Salt [ים המלח] is called the Sea of Sodom; there, המלח [ha-melach] denotes bitumen rather than salt;

units.la: apud Maym. certè in Kele Mikdafch מלח סרוםB tumen est. Distabat Hierosolymis stadiis ccc. Ioseph. Antiq. lib.15.9. Longitudine extenditur DLXXX. stad. (LXXII. M. past.) Id. de bello lib.4.c.27. de eius longitudine paulò aliter sentit Plinius Nat. Hist. lib.5.cap.16. Projicere vel abdicare aliquid המלח הים in Mare Sodomiticum; (cuius Phraseos mentio fit Hierof. Avoda Zarah sol.39.2 Hierof. Sotah sol.19.1. Nazir cap.4.4. Hierof. Demai sol.25.4. de Aquila Proselyto &c.) significat aliquid execrationi devovere, seu ab omni usu removere.
units.tr: as in Maimonides, in Kele Hamikdash, where "salt of Sodom" [מלח סדום] is bitumen. It was 300 stadia from Jerusalem (Josephus, Antiquities, book 15, chapter 9). Its length extends 580 stadia (72 Roman miles). Josephus, De bello, book 4, chapter 27. Pliny (Natural History, book 5, chapter 16) judges its length somewhat differently. To cast or renounce something into the Sea of Sodom [הים המלח] (a phrase mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud, Avodah Zarah sol.39.2, Sotah sol.19.1, Nazir chapter 4.4, Demai sol.25.4, concerning Aquila the proselyte, etc.) signifies to devote something to execration, or to remove it from all use.

units.la: §. De mare Gennesaret: Vid. apud Tiberiadem & Gennesareth.
units.tr: §. On the Sea of Gennesaret, see under Tiberias and Gennesareth.

units.la: §. De lacu Sirbonis vid. שרבון in S.
units.tr: §. On the lake of Sirbon, see שרבון [Sirbon] under S.

units.la: MARIA MAGDALENA fecundùm Baronium Lazari soror fuit. (Annal. ad annum Christi 31. pag.147.148.&c.) Magdalena dici potuit, vel quia fuit ex urbe Magdala (de qua suprà,) vel à voce מגדלא, quæ plicaturam, vel cincinnationem crinium meretricibus præcipuè usitatam significat. De Maria illius nominis legitur in Bab. Sanhed. sol. 67.1. Mater Ben Sadta fuit מרים מגדלא נשיא Maria plicatrix capillorum mulierum Chagigah sol.4.2. Rabb Bibai, cùm esset quondam apud eum Angelus mortis, dixit ad legatum suum, Abi אייתי לי מרים מגדלא שיער נשיא Adduc mihi Mariam plicatricem (capillorum) mulierum &c. Glass. in Gittin sol. 90.1. Papa Ben Iuda fuit maritus נשיא מגדלא מרים Maria plicatricis capillorum mulierum &c. Vid. etiam Bab. Schabbat sol.104.2. Probabile est Iudæos sub hoc nomine opprobrium inurere velle
units.tr: MARY MAGDALENE, according to Baronius, was the sister of Lazarus (Annals, year of Christ 31, pp.147, 148, etc.). She could be called Magdalene either because she came from the city of Magdala (mentioned above), or from the word מגדלא [migdala], which denotes the plaiting or curling of hair, a fashion especially common among prostitutes. Of a Mary of that name we read in Bab. Sanhedrin sol.67.1 that the mother of Ben Sadta was מרים מגדלא נשיא [Miriam, the hair-plaiter of women]. In Chagigah sol.4.2, Rabbi Bibai, when once the Angel of Death was with him, said to his messenger: "Go, bring me מרים מגדלא שיער נשיא [Mary, the hair-plaiter of women's hair]," and so on. Gloss on Gittin sol.90.1: Papa Ben Judah had as husband a מרים מגדלא נשיא [Mary, a hair-plaiter of women's hair], and so on. See also Bab. Shabbat sol.104.2. It is probable that the Jews wished by this name to brand her with disgrace

units.la: {*} Ies.
units.tr: {*} Jesus.

units.la: Maria Magdalena, sicuti Christo sub nomine Ben Sadta faciunt.
units.tr: Mary Magdalene, just as they do to Christ under the name Ben Sadta.

units.la: §. Mariæ matris Iesu mentionem facit Iu-chasin, & recenset, quòd etiam אשתוניפוס Promethei neptis, duos filios pepererit Aphkon & Schalzebin, & tamen ante & post partum virgo manserit ורה קשה נגד הנוצרי & hoc exemplum grave esse Christianis. Vtpote qui existimant, miraculum in Maria factum esse. Muhammedani Religiosius de virgine Matre sentiunt, credunt enim illam sine ope viri filium peperisse. Alcoran. Surata 3.35. Sur.4.155. Sur.5.19. 46.72. Surata 6.87. & 19.
units.tr: §. The Jewish author Juchasin mentions the mother of Jesus, and relates that Ashtoniphus, granddaughter of Prometheus, also bore two sons, Aphkon and Schalzebin, and yet remained a virgin before and after childbirth. ורה קשה נגד הנוצרי [This is a hard thing against the Christian]. This example is grave for Christians, inasmuch as they think a miracle was wrought in Mary. The Muslims hold more religiously about the Virgin Mother; for they believe she bore a son without the help of a man. Alcoran, Sura 3.35; Sura 4.155; Sura 5.19; 46.72; Sura 6.87; and 19.

units.la: §. Maria filia Amram, sic vocata est, ab amaritudine, quia vixit in plagarum seculo, Olam Rabba 19.
units.tr: §. Mary, daughter of Amram, was so called from bitterness, because she lived in an age of plagues. Olam Rabba 19.

units.la: §. De Puteo eius vid. Buxtorf. Exerc. VI.414. 418. De illa etiam hæc leguntur in Bab. Megillah sol.14.1. Mirjam ante nativitatem Mosis prophetaverat, Mater mea pariet filium, qui liberabit Israelem. Cum foret natus, repleta est tota domus luce. Projitit pater atque eam exosculatus est super caput, & dixit, adimpleta est prophetia tua. At cum eum abjicerent in fluvium טשחה על ראשו Eam contudit super caput.
units.tr: §. On her well, see Buxtorf, Exercitationes VI, pp.414, 418. Concerning her these things are also read in Bab. Megillah sol.14.1: Miriam had prophesied before the birth of Moses: "My mother will bear a son who will deliver Israel." When he was born, the whole house was filled with light. The father leapt up, kissed her on the head, and said, "Your prophecy is fulfilled." But when they cast him into the river [טשחה על ראשו; he struck her on the head] he struck her on the head.

units.la: §. De Maria filia Baithos Vid. Echa Rabbeti sol.67.2.
units.tr: §. On Mary, daughter of Baithos, see Echa Rabbati sol.67.2.

units.la: MARTHA Nomen est muliebre apud Talmudi- cos satis notum.
units.tr: MARTHA: a woman's name, well known among the Talmudists.

units.la: Hierof.Schabbat sol.3.4. Isaac Bar Samuel, Bar Martha. Bab. Ievamoth f.120.1. Abba Bar Martha &c. Ibid.cap.6.4. Iosua Ben Gamla desponsavit מרתא בת בישוש Martham filiam Baithos, quæ erat vidua ditissima, Iucha-
units.tr: Hierof. Schabbat sol. 3.4: Isaac bar Samuel, bar Martha. Bab. Ievamoth f. 120.1: Abba bar Martha, etc. Ibid. cap. 6.4: Joshua ben Gamla betrothed Martha (מרתא בת בישוש), the daughter of Baithos, who was a very wealthy widow. Iuchasin sol. 57.2.

units.la: sin sol. 57. 2. Eius etiam fit mentio in Succah sol. 52. 2. & dicitur habuisse filium robustif-simum.
units.tr: She is also mentioned in Succah sol. 52.2, where she is said to have had a very strong son.

units.la: Marcolis vid. Mercurius.
units.tr: Marcolis: see Mercurius.

units.la: Matrimonia. De iis Buxt.in Synag. Leusden in Philol. mixto f. 173. Vid. Nuptiae.
units.tr: Marriages. On these see Buxtorf in Synagoga; Leusden in Philologus mixtus f. 173. See Nuptiae.

units.la: Masculus. Quando masculus venit in mundum, venit salus in mundum, habetque talentum in sua manu, Nidda f.31.2. felix ille cuius liberi sunt masculi; væ illi cuius liberi sunt foemellæ. Kiddushin sol.82.2.
units.tr: Male. When a male comes into the world, salvation comes into the world, and he has a talent in his hand. Niddah f. 31.2. Happy is he whose children are male; woe to him whose children are female. Kiddushin sol. 82.2.

units.la: מדינת הים Medinath hajam, Quæritur quid fit? R. Salomoh in Gittin inquit כל ח"ל קרי מדינת הים לבד מבנרי Omnis regio extra terram Israeliticam, vocatur מדינת הים Regio maris, exceptâ Babylonia. In quæ Rabbi Salomonis verba sic commentatur R. Nissim loco cit. Durius est (inquit) omnem regionem quæ est extra terram, pro regione maris habere; nam tum sub isto nomine concludentur loca omnia vicina, & quæ quasi absorbentur iuxta terram. Nec possunt loca remotiora מדינת הים vocari. Nam non tanta distantia opus est, ut dicatur locus aliquis regio maris &c. At dicitur in relatione ad oram Occidentalem terræ Israelis (labii scilicet maris mediterranei) Sensu itaque R. Salomonis est, quod omnis regio vocatur מדינת הים, quæ similis est regioni isti (oræ maritimæ.)
units.tr: Medinath hajam (מדינת הים). The question is what this means. R. Solomon in Gittin says: every foreign land is called medinath hajam, "region of the sea," except Babylonia. On these words of Rabbi Solomon, R. Nissim comments as follows, loc. cit.: "It is harsher," he says, "to take every region outside the land as a region of the sea; for under this name are included all the places nearby, which are, as it were, absorbed alongside the land. Remoter places cannot be called medinath hajam, for no great distance is needed for a place to be called a region of the sea, etc. But it is said in relation to the western shore of the land of Israel" (namely the coast of the Mediterranean). "So the sense of R. Solomon is that every region which is similar to that region (the maritime coast) is called medinath hajam."

units.la: §. De מדינת הים in pluribus locis mentio fit; vid. Gittin per totum cap. primum. Moed Katon cap. 3. versu primo & secundo: ubi de rasura & lotione ex illa provincia venientium agitur.
units.tr: Mention of medinath hajam is made in several places: see Gittin throughout chapter 1, and Moed Katon chap. 3, verses 1 and 2, where it deals with those coming from that province who are shaved and washed.

units.la: MEDICUS. Afflicta est civitas cuius Medicus est פודגריס Podagricus. Vaikra Rabba Sect.5. אסי אסי חגרתך Medice cura te ipsum. Tanchuma in Gen. Sect.1. conf. Luc.4.23. Ne habites in urbe cuius caput Medicus est. Pesachin sol.113.1. Civilibus enim negotiis intentus, aegrotorum curam negligit. Medici Iudaei merita festive describuntur in Kiddushin sol. 82.1. טוב שכרופא לגיהנם Optimus medicorum meretur Gehennam. Gloss. multos enim incaute occidit; multos pauperes quos servare potuisset negligit. Prohibitum est Iudaeis uti medicis & medicamentis Christianorum, quia sunt משורר בדמים suspecti de sanguine. Ammude Gozah folio 37. num. 100.
units.tr: PHYSICIAN. A city whose physician is a podagricus is afflicted. Vayikra Rabba sect. 5. "Physician, heal yourself" (אסי אסי חגרתך). Tanchuma on Genesis sect. 1; cf. Luke 4:23. "Do not live in a city whose head is a physician." Pesachim sol. 113.1. For, being occupied with civil affairs, he neglects the care of the sick. Jewish physicians are wittily described in Kiddushin sol. 82.1: "The best of physicians is destined for Gehenna." Gloss: for they carelessly kill many, and neglect many poor people whom they could have saved. Jews are forbidden to use the physicians and medicines of Christians, because they are suspected of blood. Ammude Gozah folio 37, num. 100.

units.la: §. Medicamenta quaedam referemus apud priscos usitata. Bab.Schabb. sol.110. Varia Medicinarum genera praescribuntur foeminae profluvio laboranti. Dicit R. Iochanan. Recipe מתקל זוא קומא אלכסנדריא Gummi Alexandrini pondus Sufai, Et pondus Sufai גביא גילא Aluminis. כורכמא רישקא (roci hortensis, pondus Sufai. Conterantur haec una, & in vino dentur foeminae hamorrhoidae.
units.tr: We will mention some medicines used by the ancients. Bab. Schabbat sol. 110: various kinds of medicine are prescribed for a woman suffering from a flux. R. Johanan says: take gum of Alexandria, a weight of a sufai, and a weight of a sufai of alum, and a weight of a sufai of garden rocket (roci hortensis). Let these be crushed together and given in wine to the woman with hemorrhoids.

units.la: Si haec non prosint.
units.tr: If these do not help.

units.la: Recipe תלחא קפיו שמכי פרסאי Ceparum Persicarum ter tria log, vino coquantur, atque inde eam potare debes, dicasque מוביך קום Surge a profluvio tuo.
units.tr: Take Persian onions, three times three logs; boil them in wine, and she must drink it, and you should say, "Arise from your flux."

units.la: Si hoc non valeat.
units.tr: If this does not work.

units.la: Siste eam in aliquo bivio, manuque teneat poculum vini: Veniatque aliquis a tergo eius, eamque terreat, dicens מוביך קום Surge a profluvio tuo. Aliud
units.tr: Let her stand at some crossroads, holding a cup of wine in her hand; let someone come up behind her and frighten her, saying, "Arise from your flux." Another remedy.

units.la: Aliud remedium si precedentia nihil obtinuerint.
units.tr: Another remedy, if the preceding have achieved nothing.

units.la: Recipe [?] Manipulum Cymini, [?] manipulum Croci, [?] manipulum fœni Graci; coquantur vino, & dentur ei potanda, cum clausula ordinaria, surge à profluvio tuo.
units.tr: Take [?] a handful of cumin, [?] a handful of saffron, [?] a handful of Greek hay; let them be boiled in wine and given to her to drink, with the usual formula, "Arise from your flux."

units.la: Alia Dosis.
units.tr: Another dose.

units.la: Fodiant septem foveas, in quibus comburant sarmenta quædam vitium non circuncisarum i.e. quæ nondum quadriennium attigerunt. Accipiatque in manu sua poculum vini; Deinde illam in unaquaque fovea sedere faciunt, & dum illam ex una in aliam amovent, dicunt, surge à profluvio tuo.
units.tr: Let them dig seven pits, in which they burn certain vine cuttings from uncircumcised vines, that is, vines that have not yet reached four years. She takes a cup of wine in her hand; then they make her sit in each pit, and while they move her from one to the next, they say, "Arise from your flux."

units.la: §. In Bab. Gittin sol. 69. præscribuntur varia medicamenta variis morbis; inter alia [?] pro Pleuritide (vel secund.alios, morbo quodam capitis) recipe ad quantitatem glandis [?] de Ammoniaco. de medicina pro febri vid. in F. Febris.
units.tr: In Bab. Gittin sol. 69, various remedies are prescribed for various diseases. Among others, for pleurisy (or, according to others, a certain disease of the head), take an amount the size of an acorn [?] of ammoniac. On medicine for fever see under Febris.

units.la: §. Potum medicinalem ex succo [?] lacerpitii sæpius conficiebant; hæc herba quæ in officinis Assa fœtida nominatur, erat laudatissima in Syria, præcipuè in provincia Cyreniaca; Hinc Catullus ad Lesbiam Cyrenas nominat, Lasser-pitiferas. De potu hoc loquuntur in Schabbat sol. 140.
units.tr: They often made a medicinal drink from the juice of [?] lacerpitium. This herb, called asafoetida in the shops, was highly praised in Syria, especially in the province of Cyrenaica; hence Catullus, addressing Lesbia, names the Cyrenes "laserpitifera." They speak of this drink in Shabbat sol. 140.

units.la: §. Contra suffusionem oculorum, fumatur scorpio [?] septem internodiorum, & exsiccetur in umbra. Gittin sol. 69. 1. Pro morbo oculorum etiam prodest sputum ieiunum; Maym. Schabbat cap. 21. patet etiam ex historia
units.tr: Against cataract of the eyes, smoke a scorpion [?] of seven internodes, and let it dry in the shade. Gittin sol. 69.1. Fasting spittle is also good for eye disease: Maimonides, Shabbat chap. 21; it is also clear from the story

units.la: R. Meir in Vajikra Rabba. fol.175.2.
units.tr: of R. Meir in Vayikra Rabba fol. 175.2.

units.la: §. Appendebant mulieres ova locustarum ad aures suas, si dolorem in illis sentiebant,aut illæ sanie diffluerent. Vid.Schabbat fol. 67.1. de vomitoriis אפיקטויין vid. Schabbat fol.123.2. & fol.147.in Mifchna.
units.tr: Women hung locust eggs at their ears if they felt pain in them, or if they discharged pus. See Shabbat fol. 67.1. On emetics, apiktoyin: see Shabbat fol. 123.2 and fol. 147, in the Mishnah.

units.la: §. Pro tuffi vehementiori ordinarunt Medici, ut ægrotus bibat lac caprinum calidum mane. Temura fol.15. 2. Bava Kama fol.80.1. de Magica curatione morsus canis Rabidi,vid. Cl.Buxt.Lex.Talm.fol.2063.
units.tr: For a violent cough, physicians prescribed that the patient drink warm goat's milk in the morning. Temurah fol. 15.2. Bava Kama fol. 80.1. On the magical treatment of the bite of a rabid dog, see Buxtorf, Lex. Talm., fol. 2063.

units.la: §. Habebant etiam Medicos peritos exscindendi pelliculas oculi, quas Germ. vocant Staar. Illos vocabant איקופוס. Vid. Vajikra Rabba fe&t.5. in Gloff. & Ialkut fol.124. 2. de curatione vid. Ægrotos. de morbis periculosioribus, & quibus omni tempore adhibenda medicina vid. Hierof.Avoda Zarah f.40.4.
units.tr: They also had skilled practitioners for cutting out the membrane of the eye, which the Germans call Staar. These they called ikopos (איקופוס). See Vayikra Rabba sect. 5, in the Gloss, and Yalkut fol. 124.2. On treatment see Aegroti. On more dangerous diseases, and those for which medicine must be applied at all times, see Hierosolymitanus Avoda Zarah f. 40.4.

units.la: מגילה Megillah Vid. leci. Biblica.
units.tr: Megillah. See Lex. Biblica.

units.la: R. Meir floruit anno 3881. Erat Vicepræses Rab. Simeonis tertii Iuchafin pag. 67. libenter Simeonem cum Rab. Nathan de gradu deiecifset; historia narratur in cap.3.tractatus Horaioth. De pœna ipsorum vid. Buxt. Lex. Talm. p.61. propter ipsum absolvit R. Beth Schean à decimatione, Cholin fol.6.2. R. Meir dispensavit de nimis rigida observatione curationis ægrotorum in Sabbatho. Hierof.Berac. fol.3.1. de volumine Critico Bibliorum R. Meir vid.apud legem. Historia ridenda de ipso extat in Vajikra Rabba f.175.2. vid. Sputum. Nomen R. Meir erat Nehorai. Quare ergo vocatur R. Meir ? שמאי עיני חכמי בהלכה Quia illuminat
units.tr: R. Meir flourished in the year 3881. He was deputy president under Rabban Simeon III (Iuchasin p. 67), and had gladly deposed Simeon from his office together with Rabban Nathan; the story is told in chap. 3 of the tractate Horaioth. On his punishment see Buxtorf, Lex. Talm., p. 61. Because of him, R. Beth Schean was absolved from tithing (Cholin fol. 6.2). R. Meir dispensed with an overly rigid observance of the care of the sick on the Sabbath (Hierosolymitanus Berachoth fol. 3.1). On R. Meir's critical volume of the Bible, see under Lex (legem). A ridiculous story about him is in Vayikra Rabba f. 175.2; see Sputum. R. Meir's name was Nehorai. Why, then, is he called R. Meir? "Because he illumines the eyes of the wise (שמאי עיני חכמי בהלכה) with the traditions," etc. Erubin folio 13.2.

units.la: oculos sapientum traditionibus &c. Erubbin folio 13. 2.
units.tr: "...for he illumines the eyes of the sages in the halakhah," etc. Erubin folio 13.2.

units.la: MEL. Deus promisit populo Israelitico terram fluentem lacte & melle ; hinc primo intuitu quidam concludunt Totam terram sic fluxisse, Item infinita alvearia in illa fuisse. At aliter Talmudici. Hierosf. Biccurim sol.64.2. Dicit R. Ionah, Terra fluens lacte & melle, est terra, cuius aliqua pars, fluit lacte & melle. Partem autem illam ponunt in Galilaea, nam sic aiunt. Per sedecim milliaria undiquaque à Zippore est terra fluens lacte & melle. Hinc etiam illud R. Iose Galilaei in Biccurim c. 1. v.15. Non afferunt primitias è regione quae trans Iordanem, quia ea non est terra fluens lacte & melle.
units.tr: MEL (honey). God promised the Israelite people a land flowing with milk and honey; hence at first sight some conclude that the whole land flowed thus, and that there were countless beehives in it. But the Talmudists think otherwise. Hierosolymitanus Bikkurim sol. 64.2: "R. Jonah says: a land flowing with milk and honey is a land of which some part flows with milk and honey." They place that part in Galilee, for they say: "For sixteen miles on every side of Zippori is a land flowing with milk and honey." Hence also that saying of R. Jose the Galilean in Bikkurim chap. 1, v. 15: "They do not bring firstfruits from the region beyond the Jordan, because it is not a land flowing with milk and honey."

units.la: Quomodo autem illa pars quae fluxit melle illud produxerit diximus ex Maymon.in locum modo citatum. Cum dicit, & melle, intelligit mel palmarum. Nam palmae quae sunt in planitie, & in convallibus, abundant melle admodum. Habebant ergo in palaestina & mel Palmarum, quod sine dubio abundantissimè proveniebat in tractu Hierichuntino qui locus commorationis erat Iohannis Baptistae; Hiericho enim à multitudine palmarum vocabantur Urbs Palmarum. Sed praeter mel palmarum erat etiam mel distillans à ficubus: ut eruitur ex Chetubh. sol.3.2. Dixit R. Iacob Ben Dosithai, profectus fuit tempore quodam à Lydda ad Ono ante diluculum, ad talos usque in melle ficuum.
units.tr: How that part which flowed with honey produced it, we have said, following Maimonides in the place just cited: "When he says 'and honey,' he understands date-honey, for the palms in the plain and in the valleys abound greatly in honey." So in Palestine they had date-honey, which without doubt was most abundant in the district of Jericho, the place where John the Baptist lived; for Jericho was called the City of Palms because of the multitude of its palm trees. But besides palm-honey there was also honey dripping from figs, as is clear from Chetubhoth sol. 3.2: "R. Jacob ben Dosithai said: on one occasion he went from Lydda to Ono before dawn, up to his ankles in fig-honey."

units.la: MELCHISEDECH. De eo plura habent Gregorius in praef. ad sua opera. p.2. Cunaeus de repub. Hebraeorum lib. iii. c.3. Cl. Leigtfootus etiam existimat ipsum Semum fuisse; Chor. Marci pag. 80.
units.tr: MELCHIZEDEK. Gregory has more on him in the preface to his works, p. 2. Cunaeus, De republica Hebraeorum, book 3, ch. 3. Cl. Lightfoot also thinks he was Shem; Chor. Marci, p. 80.

units.la: MENDACIUM. Doce linguam tuam dicere Ego nescio, ne forte mendacii arguaris, & capiaris. Beracot sol.4 1. Hæc est pœna mendacii, ut etiamsi dicat verum, tamen ei fidem non adhibeant. Sanhed.sol.89 2. Quicunque interpretatur textum Biblicum secundum literam, is est mendax. R. Asaria in Meor Enaim sol.145. ex Kidduschin cap.2. vix enim cavebit, quin aliquando sensum corrumpat.
units.tr: LYING. "Teach your tongue to say, 'I do not know,' lest perhaps you be convicted of lying and caught." Berachot fol. 4.1. "This is the punishment of a liar: even when he tells the truth, people will not give him credence." Sanhedrin fol. 89.2. Whoever interprets a Biblical text according to the letter is a liar. R. Asaria, Meor Enaim, fol. 145, from Kiddushin ch. 2: for he will hardly take care not to corrupt the sense at some point.

units.la: MENDICANTES distinguuntur in pauperes mundi, i.e. Mendicos ostiatim petentes Elcemosynam, sive sint Ethnici vel Israelitæ, & ex quacunque sint regione; & in Pauperes uniuscuiusque urbis. Vid. Eleemosyna. Verba mendicantium usitatissima hæc erant, Merere in me. i.e. meritum acquire tibi, per eleemosynam mihi datam. Item O homo teneri cordis, in me benefac tibi ipsi. Aliquando Respice me quis fuerim, aspice iam qualis sim. Vajikra Rabba f. 204.3. Sect.34.
units.tr: BEGGARS are divided into the poor of the world, that is, beggars who ask for alms from door to door, whether they are Gentiles or Israelites and from whatever region they come; and the poor of each city. See Almsgiving. The most common words of beggars were these: Merit in me, that is, acquire merit for yourself through the alms given to me. Likewise: O man of tender heart, do good to yourself in me. Sometimes: Look at me, who I was; behold now what I am. Vayikra Rabba, fol. 204.3, sect. 34.

units.la: MENSÆ ordinariæ descriptio. Vid. Accumbendi ritus.
units.tr: A description of the ordinary table. See Ritual of reclining at table.

units.la: MENSES sic numerant. Ian. ipsis est Schebhat, Februar. Adar, Martius Nisan, Aprilis Iar. Majus Sivan. Iunius Tammus, Iulius Ab. Augustus Elul, September Tisri, Octobèr Marchesvan, November Cislev. December Tebbet. Observandum hic, quod duplicem annum olim habuerint, Ecclesiasticum & Politicum.Annus Ecclesiasticus instituente Mose in memoriam exitus ex Ægypto incepit à ניסן Martio, vid.Ionathan & R.Salomoh in Exod. 12.1. Politicus incipiebat à Tisri sive Septembri, quia credunt in eo olim Mundum fuisse creatum, vid. Kimchi 1.Reg.8.2. Berefch. Rabba sect.22. Ex quibus affertur lux loco aliàs satis obscuro in Rosch Hashchana cap.1. v.1. באחר כתשרי ראש השנה לשנים ולשמיטין וליובלות ולנטיעה וליקורית Quæ paraphrasticè reddita sic sonant. Mensis Tisri die primo computatio annorum à creatione mundi pertexitur. A Mense Tisri etiam computant annos pro determinatione Iubilaeorum, remissionis agrorum in anno septimo. Sic à Mense Tisri numerant annos illos tres à plantatione fructuum, in quibus fructus præputiati & illicitì erant, ut anno quarto redimi possent. Item annos plantationis olerum, quia ex illis decima & oblationes erant conferenda. Mensis Tisri vocatur etiam ירח האתנים Mensis robustorum. 1.Reg.8.2. propter perfectionem fructuum in illo mense. In illo mense erat festum illud magnum הכפורים Expiationis. Vid.f.1. de mense אב vid.A. De Februario vid.אדר in A.
units.tr: MONTHS are counted thus. January is for them Shevat; February Adar; March Nisan; April Iyar; May Sivan; June Tammuz; July Av; August Elul; September Tishri; October Marcheshvan; November Kislev; December Tevet. Here observe that they once had a double year, ecclesiastical and civil. The ecclesiastical year, instituted by Moses in memory of the exodus from Egypt, began in March, in ניסן [Nisan]; see Jonathan and R. Solomon on Exod. 12.1. The civil year began in Tishri, that is September, because they believe the world was created in that month; see Kimchi on 1 Kings 8.2, and Bereshit Rabba, sect. 22. From these a light is shed on a passage otherwise rather obscure, in Rosh Hashanah ch. 1, v. 1: באחד בתשרי ראש השנה [Be-echad be-Tishri, rosh ha-shanah], which, paraphrased, reads thus: "On the first day of the month Tishri the reckoning of years from the creation of the world is carried on. From the month Tishri they also reckon the years for fixing the Jubilees and the remission of the fields in the seventh year. So from the month Tishri they count those three years from the planting of fruit trees, in which the fruit is uncircumcised and forbidden, so that in the fourth year it may be redeemed. Likewise the years of planting of vegetables, because tithes and offerings were to be given from them." The month Tishri is also called ירח האתנים [yerach ha-ethanim], the month of the strong (1 Kings 8.2), on account of the perfection of the fruits in that month. In that month was the great feast הכפורים [ha-kippurim], of Atonement. See fol. 1. On the month אב [Av], see A. On February, see אדר [Adar] in A.

units.la: MENSURA.
units.tr: MEASURE.

units.la: In mensuratione Iudæi admodum delectantur numero quadringentarum Parsarum; Gloss. in Bava Metzia sol.28.1. Terra Israelitica fuit quadratura quadringentarum Parsarum. Megillah sol.3.1. Ionathan Ben Vziel interpretatus est ab ore Haggai, Zachariæ & Malachiæ, & commota est terra Israelitica quadringentis Parsis undiquaque. Bava Kama sol. 82.2.
units.tr: In matters of measurement the Jews take great delight in the number four hundred parasangs. Gloss on Bava Metzia fol. 28.1: The land of Israel was a square of four hundred parasangs. Megillah fol. 3.1: Jonathan ben Uzziel interpreted, from the mouth of Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi, that the land of Israel was shaken on every side for four hundred parasangs. Bava Kamma fol. 82.2.

units.la: Cum porcus sursum traheretur super muros Hierosolyme, & infigeret ungues, quassata est terra Israelitica, per quadringentas Parsas undiquaque.
units.tr: When a pig was dragged up over the walls of Jerusalem and sank its claws in, the land of Israel was shaken on every side for four hundred parasangs.

units.la: Maymon in Hal. Melachim cap. 5. Licitum est habitare in universo mundo, excepta terra Ægypti, (quæ se extendit,) à mari magno versus occasum ארבע מאות פרסה ad quadringentas Parsas. Parsa autem intra se continuit quatuor milliaria, & decem Parsæ, milliaria 40. fecerunt. Gloss. in Pesach. sol.93.2.
units.tr: Maimonides, Hilchot Melachim ch. 5: "It is lawful to dwell in the whole world, except the land of Egypt" (which extends) "from the great sea towards the west, ארבע מאות פרסה [arba meot parsah], to four hundred parasangs." A parasang contains four miles, and ten parasangs make forty miles. Gloss on Pesachim fol. 93.2.

units.la: §. Mensurarunt etiam per Milliaria & dietas. De Milliari referunt in Bava Metzia sol. 33.1. constitisse illud, (non octo ut Romanum & Græcum sed) septem מיל stadiis cum dimidio. Alias מיל distinguitur in maius & minus, maius completitur gressus bis mille, minus gressus mille. Vid. Sanhed. sol.96.1. Megillah sol. 6.1. Maymon. Hal. Tephillah cap.4. Supra fidem est quod de itinere Saulis & Israelitarum refertur in Midrasch Tillim sol.7.4. Gloss. in Sanhed. sol. 44.1. nimirum Saulem una die sexaginta milliaria peragrasse; & Israelitas una die ad Iordanem ad montem Gerizim pervenisse. Nam de dieta five itinere diario notant, illud ultra quadraginta milliaria se non extendisse. Scil. a prodeunte primum aurora ad ortum solis, quinque milliaria; ab occasu solis donec appareant stellæ, quinque milliaria; quindecim a mane ad meridiem, & quindecim a meridie ad vesperam. Pesachin sol.93.1. Intra spatium itineris trium dierum aliquis Hierosolymâ, ad ultimam limitem terræ Israeliticæ pervenire poterat; quod eruitur ex Bava Metzia f.28.1. tenetur ille qui amissum repererit, rem repertam manifestare publico præconio, tribus festis, & septem diebus post festum ultimum. Nempe ut triduo quis domum redeat, quæsitum an aliquid perdiderit, triduo redeat (Hierosolymam,) & supersit adhuc dies unus publico præconio.
units.tr: §. They also measured by miles and days' journeys. Concerning the mile, they report in Bava Metzia fol. 33.1 that it was (not eight, as the Roman and Greek mile, but) seven and a half stadia, מיל [mil]. Otherwise the mil is distinguished into greater and lesser: the greater consists of two thousand paces, the lesser of one thousand. See Sanhedrin fol. 96.1; Megillah fol. 6.1; Maimonides, Hilchot Tefillah ch. 4. What is reported of the journey of Saul and the Israelites in Midrash Tillim fol. 7.4 is beyond belief; Gloss on Sanhedrin fol. 44.1 says that Saul walked sixty miles in a single day, and that the Israelites reached the Jordan and Mount Gerizim in one day. For concerning a day's journey, or daily stage, they note that it did not extend beyond forty miles: namely, from first dawn to sunrise, five miles; from sunset until the stars appear, five miles; fifteen from morning to noon, and fifteen from noon to evening. Pesachim fol. 93.1. Within the space of a three days' journey one could reach from Jerusalem the furthest border of the land of Israel. This is gathered from Bava Metzia fol. 28.1: the one who finds a lost thing is bound to make the find known by public proclamation over three festivals and seven days after the last festival. That is, so that a man who returns home in three days, and asks whether he has lost anything, may return (to Jerusalem) in three days, and there remain one day for the public proclamation.

units.la: §. De Mensura longitudinis & intervallorum vid. Cl. Leusdenii Philol. Mixtum. p. 201. 212. 112. Mensura ciborum illicitorum est aliquando כית Instar olivæ, vel כאפן instar fabæ, vel נכוככ inster Dactyli. Vt in Toma c. 8. §. 2. Seah Hierofolymitana amplior erat Seah rustica sexta parte; & Seah Zipporiensis Hierofolymitana sexta parte. Menachot. cap. 8. Erubbin. f. 83. 1.
units.tr: §. On the measure of length and intervals see Cl. Leusden, Philologus Mixtus, pp. 201, 212, 112. The measure of forbidden foods is sometimes כזית [kezayit], like an olive; or כאפן [kaphan], like a bean; or נכוככ [nekhuqaq], like a date. As in Yoma ch. 8 §2. The Jerusalem seah was larger than the rustic seah by a sixth part, and the Zipporite seah was smaller than the Jerusalem seah by a sixth part. Menachot ch. 8; Eruvin fol. 83.1.

units.la: §. Mensuræ aridorum duæ fuerunt in templo, & septem mensuræ fluidorum. Maymon Kele Hamikdasch c. 1. circa finem. Illas pluribus descripsit; Cl. Leusdenius l. c. p. 204. 205. 207. 208.
units.tr: §. There were two measures for dry things in the Temple and seven measures for liquids. Maimonides, Kelei Hamikdash ch. 1, near the end. He described these at greater length; see Cl. Leusden, l.c., pp. 204, 205, 207, 208.

units.la: MERCURII idoleum prisci בית קולים Domus Kolis, ité מרקולים Marcolis vocarunt. In eo positi erant tres lapides, quorum unus hinc, alter illinc positus, & tertius super eos utrumque tegens. Metzia sol. 25. 2. Ad hos tres lapides projiciebantur alii lapides certo ritu, quam proiectionem idololatriam esse dicunt in Sanhed. cap. 7. f. 60. Vid. Scaliger de Emendatione temporum lib. 5. p. 486. Seld. de Dis Syriis. 11. c. 14. Kircheri Oedip. l. 388.
units.tr: MERCURY. The ancients called the idol of Mercury בית קולים [Beth Kolis], the House of Kolis, and also מרקולים [Merkolis], Markolis. In it were placed three stones, one here, another there, and a third laid over both. Metzia fol. 25.2. Other stones were thrown at these three stones with a certain rite, which throwing they call idolatry in Sanhedrin ch. 7, fol. 60. See Scaliger, De emendatione temporum, book 5, p. 486; Selden, De diis Syris, ch. 14; Kircher, Oedipus, p. 388.

units.la: MESSIAS. Messiæ adventum præcurret Armillus, immanis Iudæorum Hostis. Vid. Cl. Buxt. lex. Talm. p. 221. De duplici Messia, filio Iofeph, qui & filius Ephraim dicitur; & filio Davidis
units.tr: MESSIAH. Armillus, the monstrous enemy of the Jews, will precede the coming of the Messiah. See Cl. Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 221. On the twofold Messiah: the son of Joseph, who is also called the son of Ephraim; and the son of David.

units.la: Vid. Rabbi Salomoh Iarchi Esai.24.18. Cantic.7.
units.tr: See Rabbi Solomon Jarchi on Isa. 24.18; Song of Songs 7.

units.la: 3. Succah 52.1. Avoda Zarah 5.1. Priori Iudæi tribuunt quæ humilia de Messia in Scripturis dicuntur; alteri quæ gloriosa. Vid. Abarbanel in Esai.53. R. Salomoh Esai.11.13. etiam de Messia Ben Iehuda loquitur.
units.tr: 3. Sukkah 52.1; Avodah Zarah 5.1. The Jews assign to the first Messiah what is said humbly of the Messiah in the Scriptures, and to the other what is glorious. See Abarbanel on Isa. 53. R. Solomon on Isa. 11.13 also speaks of the Messiah ben Jehuda.

units.la: §. Eius adventus erit inexspectatus; Sanhed.sol.97.1. Tria veniunt הרעת כחמ per abreptionem mentis (inopinato) Messias, Res inventa, & ictus scorpionis. Messias Sanhed.96.2. vocatur בר נפלי quia adventus eius tam in Macrocosmum quàm in Microcosmum erit cùm res maximè collapsæ. Et sanè Dominus noster Iesus Christus in hunc mundum venit, rebus Iudæorum admodùm debilitatis, & ipsorum privilegiis ablatis. Referemus pauca ad hæc facientia. Tempore Simeonis Iusti, qui vixit & floruit A.M.3448. Prophetia ablata fuit,ut expresse Iuchafin sol.15.2. Caper emissarius in die expiationis à rupe deiectus, non ampliùs comminuebatur in frusta, ut antea factum, sed vivus aufugit in desertum & à Saracenis fuit comestus. Post mortem Simeonis Sors Dei in Die Expiationis iacta, non ampliùs ad manum dexteram solùm prodiit ut antea, sed aliquando ad dexteram, aliquando ad sinistram. Lucerna Occidentalis sæpius extincta est, cùm antea perpetuò arderet. Ignis struis non conservabatur nisi per totum diem ligna supplerent; lingua coccinea dealbescebat aliquando, aliquando vero non. Ablata etiam fuit benedictio panum propositionis, illis enim nunquam satiabantur Sacerdotes, ut anteà factum. Lege de his prolixius Hierosol. Ioma sol. 43. 3. Paulò ante Christi adventum ita multiplicatus erat homicidarum numerus, sub famoso illo latrone Eliefere fil. Dinai, (quem ob sua facinora בן הרצין Homicidam κατ' ἐξοχὴν vocarunt,) ut iunicis decollatio (v.fl.) abroganda fuerit. R. Iochanan Ben Saccai noluit amplius permittere, ut uxores suspectæ ob adulterium aquarum potatione probarentur; quia in illud vitium ita proruperant, ut nec castigari ob ingentem multitudinem, nec probari potuissent. Cum Iose filio Ioeser cessarunt viri præstantes & pii. Sublata puritas, sustulerat gustum & saporem fructuum & decimarum fraus, pinguedinem frumenti, fornicatio & præstigiæ omnia corruperant. Ita habes confitentes Magistros in Elegantissimo tractatu Sotah c. ult. Addamus quæ in Bab. Sanhed. sol. 99 1. & 97. 1. dicuntur, R. Iuda inquit, In generatione ista, cum filius Davidis advenerit, Schola erunt Meretrices, Galilæa vastabitur, Gablan excidetur, & incola terræ (Gloss. Synedrium) circumvagabuntur ab urbe in urbem, & misericordiam non assequentur, sapientia scribarum fœtida erit, & qui peccare timent spernentur, eruntque facies generationis istius, sicut facies canum, & deficiet veritas, &c. Quæ non quæso! fuerunt dissensiones inter Schammæanos & Hillelianos. (vid. Hillel.) ante & post Christi adventum? quæ non cædes & rapinæ in historia quadraginta istorum annorum, qui à morte Christi ad excisas Hierosolymas excurrerunt?
units.tr: §. His coming will be unexpected. Sanhedrin fol. 97.1: three things come (הרעת כחמ, garbled in the printed text) by a sudden seizing of the mind, unexpectedly: the Messiah, a found thing, and the sting of a scorpion. The Messiah is called בר נפלי [bar nafli] in Sanhedrin 96.2, because his coming, both into the macrocosm and into the microcosm, will be when things have fallen most low. And indeed our Lord Jesus Christ came into this world when the affairs of the Jews were very much weakened and their privileges taken away. Let us relate a few things pertinent to this. In the time of Simeon the Just, who lived and flourished in A.M. 3448, prophecy was taken away, as Yuchasin fol. 15.2 expressly says. The scapegoat on the Day of Atonement, thrown down from the cliff, was no longer cut into pieces as before, but escaped alive into the desert and was eaten by the Saracens. After the death of Simeon, the lot of the LORD cast on the Day of Atonement no longer came up only in the right hand as before, but sometimes in the right and sometimes in the left. The western lamp was often extinguished, whereas before it burned continually. The fire of the wood-pile was not kept up unless the wood was replenished through the whole day. The scarlet thread sometimes turned white, and sometimes not. The blessing of the showbread was also taken away, for the priests were never satisfied with it, as had been the case before. Read more fully on these matters in Jerusalem Yoma fol. 43.3. Shortly before Christ's coming the number of murderers had so multiplied, under that notorious robber Eliezer son of Dinai (whom, on account of his crimes, they called בן הרצין [Ben Harazin], the murderer κατ' ἐξοχὴν [kat' exochēn], by way of eminence), that the breaking of the heifer's neck (variant reading) had to be abolished. R. Johanan ben Zakkai was unwilling to permit any longer that suspected wives accused of adultery be tested by drinking the waters; for people had broken out into that vice to such an extent that they could neither be punished, because of the huge multitude, nor proven guilty. With Joseph ben Joezer the outstanding and pious men ceased. Purity was taken away; fraud had removed the taste and savour of fruits and tithes; fatness of grain, fornication and sorcery had corrupted everything. So you have the masters confessing this in the most elegant tractate Sotah, last chapter. Let us add what is said in Babylonian Sanhedrin fol. 99.1 and 97.1: "R. Judah says: In that generation, when the son of David comes, the schoolhouses will be brothels, Galilee will be laid waste, Gablan will be destroyed, and the inhabitants of the land (Gloss: the Sanhedrin) will wander from city to city and will find no mercy; the wisdom of the scribes will stink, those who fear sin will be despised, and the faces of that generation will be like the faces of dogs, and truth will fail," etc. What, I ask, were not the dissensions between the Shammaites and the Hillelites (see Hillel) before and after Christ's coming? What were not the slaughters and robberies in the history of those forty years, which ran from the death of Christ to the destruction of Jerusalem?

Solomon on Isaiah 11:13 also speaks of the Messiah ben Jehudah.
