Nazirææatus extra terram Ifraeliticam non obtinet, si quis vero extra terram Ifraeliticam votum Nazirææatus fuscepepit ינחפ ץלמ Mullant eum, & ipsum cogunt ire in terram Israeliticam,& ibi suum Nazirææatum peragere; cum vero hodie sanctuarium ædificatum non fit, debet ibi per integram suam vitam manere, & exspectare donec reædificetur; quamdiu vero extra terram est, nihilominus ab omnibus abstinere debet, quæ Nazirææo prohibita sunt. Maymon Hil. Nazir. cap. 2.
units.tr: §. The Nazirite vow is not fulfilled outside the land of Israel. If anyone has undertaken a Nazirite vow outside the land of Israel, they fine him [ינחפ ץלמ] and compel him to go into the land of Israel and there complete his Nazirite vow. But since today the sanctuary is not built, he must remain there for his whole life and wait until it is rebuilt. As long as he is outside the land, nevertheless he must abstain from all the things forbidden to a Nazirite. Maimonides, Hilchot Nazir ch. 2.

units.la: §. Non minus quàm triginta dies, quis Nazirææus esse potest, etiamsi vovisset solùm per unum diem: & in quibusdam casibus etiam ultra hunc terminum non extenditur.
units.tr: §. No one can be a Nazirite for less than thirty days, even if he vowed for only one day; and in certain cases the term is not extended beyond this limit.

units.la: §. Simson non erat Nazirææus perfectus, quia ipse Nazirææatum non voverat, sed ab Angelo separatus fuit, quare etiam solùm observare debuit, ne vinum biberet, aut se raderet; at
units.tr: §. Samson was not a perfect Nazirite, because he had not vowed the Nazirite vow himself, but was set apart by the angel. Therefore he was bound only to observe that he should not drink wine or shave himself; but

units.la: ab immunditie mortuorum liber fuit; poterat enim se propter ipsos inquinare; si quis dixerit הריני נויר כשמשון Ecce ego sum Naziræus qualis Simson fuit: ille non plura cogitur observare, quam Simson observavit. Sunt quidam נזירים עולם Nazirei in æternum: quidam vero נזירים לזמן קצוב Nazirei ad certum tempus; illi quorum votum ad certum tempus se extendit, se radere non possunt, nisi cum illud tempus advenerit. Priores vero si capillitium ipsorum nimis creverit, & ipsis grave & molestum est; possunt illud à duodecim mensibus ad alios duodecim menses semel abscindere; singulis vicibus vero quibus raduntur, debent tria iumenta in sacrificia dare. Talis נזיר עולם fuit Absalom, ut ex traditione accepimus; ut & Samuel Propheta. Quando autem aliquis ad horum virorum exemplum, se Nazirææum facere vult; debet ipsos circumscribere nominibus patronymicis & gentilitiis ipsorum, ne aliquis exi&imet, alios esse, quos imitari velit. Maymon. Hal. נויר cap.3.
units.tr: he was free from defilement by the dead, for he could make himself unclean on their account. If someone says הריני נזיר כשמשון [Behold, I am a Nazirite like Samson], he is not compelled to observe more than Samson observed. There are some נזירים עולם [Nazirites forever], and some נזירים לזמן קצוב [Nazirites for a fixed time]. Those whose vow extends to a fixed time may not shave until that time has come. The former, if their hair has grown too much and is grievous and troublesome to them, may cut it off once, from twelve months to another twelve months; but at each shaving they must give three animals for sacrifices. Such a Nazirite forever was Absalom, as we have received by tradition, and also the prophet Samuel. When anyone wishes to make himself a Nazirite after the example of these men, he must distinguish them by their patronymics and gentilics, lest anyone think that they are others whom he wishes to imitate. Maimonides, Hilchot Nazir ch. 3.

units.la: §. Postquàm votum solutum est, Nazirææus in conclavi ad hoc destinato, (quod situm erat in atrio mulierum ad ortum solis brumalem Middot cap.2.5. Bab. Ioma sol.16.1.) debet de allatis eucharisticis carnes coquere, capillos detondere, & eos ollæ submittere. Maymon cap.8. tra&. supra cit.
units.tr: §. After the vow has been fulfilled, the Nazirite, in a chamber set apart for this purpose (which was situated in the women's court, toward the winter sunrise; Middot ch. 2.5; Babylonian Yoma fol. 16.1), must boil the flesh of the thank-offerings, shave off his hair, and put it under the pot. Maimonides, ch. 8, the treatise cited above.

units.la: NAZARETH
units.tr: NAZARETH

units.la: forsan suum nomen obtinuit à בן נצר quod vid. in בן in B. Quod locum Matth. 2.23. attinet; non spernendum pondus habent quæ de נצר adducuntur ex Esaiæ xi.1. & de Samsone Naziræo. Interim Matthæus etiam intelligi potest, quasi loqueretur de humili & vili salvatoris conditione externa, quam omnes Prophetæ prædixerunt; ita ut Ναζωραῖο ipsi sit idem ac נזיר vel מור separatus, alienus ab aliis hominibus, (vid. Psal. lxix. 6) Sicut etiam in Galilæa regione à Iudæis satis contempta, erat urbs Nazareth, locus vilissimus in quo Messias noster נזיר alienus & separatus ab hominibus, ac si societate ipsorum indignus esset, degere debuit.
units.tr: It perhaps took its name from בן נצר [ben netser], which see under בן in B. As for the passage at Matt. 2.23, the arguments brought from נצר in Isaiah 11.1 and from Samson the Nazirite are not to be despised. Meanwhile Matthew may also be understood as speaking of the humble and lowly external condition of the Saviour, which all the Prophets foretold, so that Ναζωραῖος [Nazōraios] itself means the same as נזיר [nazir] or מור, separated, a stranger from other men (see Ps. 69.6). Just as in the region of Galilee, which the Jews despised enough, there was the town of Nazareth, a most lowly place in which our Messiah, a נזיר, a stranger and separated from men, as if he were unworthy of their company, had to dwell.

units.la: נחל מצרים Nachal misraim terminus extremus terræ Israeliticæ, versus austrum, non est Nilus in Ægypto, sed Schihor in via ad Ægyptum. Iosua xiii. Ierem. ii. 18. lxx. interpretibus est Rhinocorura vid. eos in Esai. xxvii. 12. de eo vid. quædam apud Diod. Siculum lib. 1. & quæ apud Interpretes, adducta.
units.tr: The נחל מצרים [Nachal Misraim], the extreme boundary of the land of Israel towards the south, is not the Nile in Egypt but Shihor on the road to Egypt. Josh. 13; Jer. 2.18. For the Septuagint translators it is Rhinocorura; see them on Isa. 27.12. On it see some things in Diodorus Siculus, book 1, and what is brought forward by the commentators.

units.la: Neapolis est Sychem Samariæ Metropolis; Benjam. Itiner. p. 60. Hieros. Avoda Zarah sol. 44. 4. R. Ismael adiit נאפולי Neapolim, accesserunt ad eum Cuthæi; quibus ille. Video quòd vos non adoratis ad montem istum, sed ad idola, quæ sub eo sunt; sicuti dicitur, Et abscondit Iacob idola sub luco, qui erat iuxta Sychem. Reliqua quæ hic adduci possent vid. apud Buxt. in Lex. Talm. pag. 1369.
units.tr: Neapolis is Sychem, the metropolis of Samaria. Benjamin, Itinerary, p. 60. Jerusalem Talmud, Avodah Zarah, fol. 44.4: R. Ismael came to Neapolis (נאפולי), and Cuthaeans approached him, to whom he said: "I see that you do not worship at this mountain but at the idols which are under it, as it is said: And Jacob hid the idols under the oak which was by Shechem." The remaining things that could be adduced here see in Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 1369.

units.la: Necromantes Vid. Demonstratio. Magia. Pytho. Nikanoris porta Vid. Porta.
units.tr: Necromancers: see Demonstration, Magic, Python. Nicanor's Gate: see Gate.

units.la: Nikodemus filius Gorionis erat senator Hierosolymitanus. Medrasch Echa cap. 1. 5. de eius pietate & miraculis tractatur in Taanith f. 19. 20. 1. & R. Nathan in Avoth cap. 7. tempore quo-dam. dam ascendit totus Israel Hierosolymam ad feftum & non fupperiit ipsis aqua. Adit Nicodemus Ben Gorion, Magnatem quendam, & dixit ei, Mutuo da mihi duodecim puteos aquarum, pro ascendentibus ad festum, & ego reddam tibi duodecim puteos (plenos aqua,) aut solvam tibi duodecim talenta argenti. Constituerunt diem, & Nikodemus precibus in sacello fusis pluvias obtinuit, quibus omnes 12. putei repleti sunt. Cum vero Magnas cavillaretur, solem iam occidisse, (& tamen constituta die pluvias non afcendiffe.) Nikodemus iterum fe velavit, & oravit, & dispersa fuerunt nubes, & sol eluxit. Inde nomen ei נקידימון Nikodemus. שנקרה לו חמה quia sol ei emicuit. An hic Nikodemus fuerit discipulus Christi magna fundamenta non sunt ad manus, dicitur quidem in Taanith loc. cit. ipsius nomen verum fuisse בוני qualis nominis discipulum attribuunt Christo in Sanhed. f. 43.1. (Vid. Christum.) at plures eiusdem nominis esse potuerunt. Aliud argumentum etiam pro affirm. esse potest, quia cum ditissimus fuisset, (ut dicitur Gittin sol. 56.1.) tandem familia eius ad summam inopiam redacta fuerit, ita ut R. Iochanan Ben Saccai viderit filiam eius colligentem hordea ex stercore iumentorum Arabum, ut dicitur in Chetubh. sol.66.2. Cum fecundum R. Nathan in Abbot cap.7. Antea eius lectus stratus fuisset duodecim mille denariis. Ex quo quidam eliciunt, Nikodemi familiam ob perfequutionem propter fidem in Christum in illam penuriam incidisse. Sed hoc argumentum pondus haberet, fi solus ad illam paupertatem venisset, cùm in publica clade urbis, cui supervixit R. Iochanan Ben Saccai, omnes honestæ & opulentæ familiæ fortunas suas amiserint. Si certè Christianus fuisset ipsum non semper ita cum laude memorarent.
units.tr: Nicodemus son of Gorion was a senator of Jerusalem. Midrash Echa, ch. 1 §5, treats of his piety and miracles, as do Taanith fol. 19.20.1 and R. Nathan in Avoth ch. 7. At one time all Israel went up to Jerusalem for the feast, and water failed them. Nicodemus ben Gorion went to a certain magnate and said to him: "Lend me twelve wells of water for those going up to the feast, and I will return to you twelve wells (full of water), or I will pay you twelve talents of silver." They fixed a day, and Nicodemus, having poured out prayers in a shrine, obtained rains by which all twelve wells were filled. But when the magnate mocked him, saying that the sun had already set (and yet on the appointed day the rain had not come), Nicodemus covered himself again and prayed, and the clouds were scattered and the sun shone out. Hence his name נקידימון [Nikodimon], because שנקרה לו חמה [the sun shone for him]. Whether this Nicodemus was a disciple of Christ, there are no great foundations at hand. It is indeed said in Taanith, loc. cit., that his real name was בוני [Bunai], which name they assign to a disciple of Christ in Sanhedrin fol. 43.1 (see Christ). But several men of the same name could have existed. Another argument for the affirmative can also be made: although he was very rich (as is said in Gittin fol. 56.1), his family was at last reduced to the utmost poverty, so that R. Johanan ben Zakkai saw his daughter gathering barley from the dung of the Arabs' beasts of burden, as is said in Ketubot fol. 66.2; whereas according to R. Nathan in Avoth ch. 7, his bed had formerly been spread with twelve thousand denarii. From this some infer that Nicodemus's family fell into that penury because of persecution for their faith in Christ. But this argument would carry weight if he alone had come to that poverty, whereas in the public ruin of the city, which R. Johanan ben Zakkai survived, all honourable and wealthy families lost their fortunes. Certainly if he had been a Christian, they would not always have remembered him with such praise.

units.la: §. De eo tractat etiam Iuchasin pag.19. Echa Rabbeti sol.64.1.
units.tr: §. This is also treated by Juchasin p. 19 and Echa Rabbeti fol. 64.1.

units.la: בית נמר Beth-namar, est locus cuius incolæ laudantur, quia spicilegium reliquerunt in omnibus lineis quibus agrum distinxerunt. Peah cap.4.5.
units.tr: בית נמר [Beth-namar] is a place whose inhabitants are praised, because they left gleanings in all the rows into which they divided their field. Peah ch. 4 §5.

units.la: NOACHIDÆ. Proselytus duplex est, vel גר צדק Proselytus iustitiæ, qui baptizatus circuncisus & in numerum Israelitarum receptus est. Et גר תושב Inquilinus proselytus יעבוד שלא עליו שקבל :עבודה זרה עם שאר המצות שנצטוו בני נח qui idololatriæ renuntiavit, reliquaque præcepta filiorum Noæ infe recepit. Maymon.Hal Issure Biah cap.14. Doctrinam de posteriori proselytorum genere, quos proprie Noachidas appellamus diducit Maymon in Hal. Melach. cap.ix. cuius verba sicuti ea olim reddidimus, dum Aureliæ dulcissimo otio fruebamur, hic notabimus.
units.tr: NOACHIDES. There are two kinds of proselyte: either גר צדק [ger tzedeq], a righteous proselyte, who has been baptized, circumcised and received into the number of the Israelites; or גר תושב [ger toshav], a resident proselyte, who has renounced idolatry and accepted the remaining precepts given to the sons of Noah (יעבוד שלא עליו שקבל עבודה זרה עם שאר המצות שנצטוו בני נח). Maimonides, Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah ch. 14. Maimonides, in Hilchot Melachim ch. 9, sets out the doctrine of the second kind of proselyte, whom we properly call Noachides; since we once rendered his words while we enjoyed the sweetest leisure at Orléans, we shall note them here.

units.la: §. Sex præcepta data sunt, Adamo primævo, de idololatria, de benedictione numinis; de effusione sanguinis, de revelatione turpitudinum, de rapina, de iudiciis administrandis, quamvis hæc ipsa acceperimus à Mose nostro Doctore. Additum verò fuit Noacho mandatum de membro vivi animalis, secundùm illud Gen.9.4. Carnem in sanguine non comedatis. Ita facta sunt in universum septem præcepta. Sic erat res in universo mundo usque ad Abrahamum, cui venienti additum fuit praeceptum circuncisionis; & ipsemet introduxit preces matutinas, Isaac vero separavit decimas,& preces addidit לפנות היום dicendas in meridie. Jacob superaddit morem גיד הנשה de nervo luxato non comedendo: precatusque est vesperi. In Ægypto postea degentibus, plura praecepta ab Amramo iniuncta fuerunt; donec tandem sub Mose lex tota consummatur.
units.tr: §. Six precepts were given to Adam the first man: concerning idolatry, concerning the blessing of the Deity, concerning the shedding of blood, concerning the uncovering of nakedness, concerning robbery, and concerning the administration of justice; although we have received even these from our teacher Moses. To Noah was added the command concerning a limb of a living animal, according to Gen. 9.4: You shall not eat flesh with its blood. Thus there were seven precepts in all. So matters stood throughout the whole world until Abraham, to whom, when he came, the precept of circumcision was added; he himself introduced the morning prayers, and Isaac set apart the tithes and added prayers to be said לפנות היום [at the turning of the day], that is, in the afternoon. Jacob added the custom of not eating the גיד הנשה [sinew of the hip], the sinew that is dislocated, and he prayed in the evening. When they later dwelt in Egypt, more precepts were enjoined by Amram, until at last under Moses the whole law was completed.

units.la: §. Noachida qui idola secundum idololatrici cultus ritus colit reus fit. Propter quam idololatriam, Synedrium Israelitas mortis supplicio afficit, propter eam Noachida quoque occiditur. Et etiamsi non occideretur manet tamen omnibus excommunicatus. Neque permittunt ipsi statuas erigere, aut lucum plantare, aut imagines conficere, & similia quae ad pulchritudinem idolorum faciunt.
units.tr: §. A Noachide who worships an idol according to the rites of idolatrous cult is guilty. On account of this idolatry the Sanhedrin puts Israelites to death; on account of it a Noachide too is killed. And even if he is not killed, he remains excommunicated by all. Nor do they permit them to erect statues, plant a grove, make images, or do anything similar that contributes to the beauty of idols.

units.la: §. Si Noachida Deum blasphemaverit, sive id fecerit blasphematione, nominis proprii (Iehova,) sive cognominis cuiusdam, imo quomodocunque id factum fit, reus fit. Quod respectu Israelitarum non ita se habet; (nam quod הכינוים cognomina attinet, propter ea Magistri (excepto R. Meir) blasphemum, non quidem morte plectendum esse senciverunt, sed tamen volunt ut באורה acri increpatione, talis excipiatur. Vid.Sanhed. c.7.)
units.tr: §. If a Noachide blasphemes God, whether by blaspheming the proper name (Jehovah) or some epithet, or indeed however it is done, he is guilty. This is not so with respect to Israelites. For as regards the הכינויים [epithets], the Masters (except R. Meir) have judged that a blasphemer of these is not to be punished with death, yet they wish that such a one be dealt with by באורה [sharp rebuke]. See Sanhedrin ch. 7.

units.la: §. Noachida qui hominem interfecit, etiamsi esset solum embryo in visceribus matris, propter hoc facinus, quoque occidi debet. Ita si animal aliquod occiderit, & illud sinat discerptum fieri, aut illud Leoni prostituerit, aut fame perire permiserit, quoniam illud perdidit in omnibus locis interfici debet. Ita fi occiderit persequentem fe, à quo fe uno ex eius membris læso liberare potuisset, quoque interficitur. מה שאין כן בישראל Quod non ita fe habet in Israele. Vid. Homicidium.
units.tr: §. A Noachide who has killed a man, even if he was only an embryo in its mother's womb, must also be put to death for this crime. Likewise, if he has killed some animal and allowed it to be torn in pieces, or has thrown it to a lion, or allowed it to perish of hunger, he must be killed in every place, since he has destroyed it. Likewise, if he has killed one who was pursuing him, when he could have freed himself by injuring one of his limbs, he too is put to death. מה שאין כן בישראל [This is not so in Israel.] See Homicide.

units.la: §. Sex turpitudines prohibitæ sunt Noachidis; Mater, & Vxor patris, Vxor viri aliûs, Soror eius, Matertera eius; Masculus & beftia. Noachida non tenetur propter uxorem proximi fui, nisi ad illam accesserit, postquàm iam à marito compressa fuit, propter defponfatam verò, & cum qua sponsus non concubuit, non reus fit. Hæc omnia intelligenda sunt de Noachida, qui rem habet, cum Noachitida; nam fi Noachida rem haberet cum Ifraelitida, five id fieret more consueto five non, reus fit.
units.tr: §. Six shameful unions are forbidden to Noachides: a mother; a father's wife; another man's wife; his sister; his father's sister; a male, and a beast. A Noachide is not bound on account of his neighbour's wife unless he has had intercourse with her after she was already violated by her husband; but he is not guilty on account of a betrothed woman with whom the bridegroom has not lain. All these things are to be understood of a Noachide who has intercourse with a Noachite woman; for if a Noachide had intercourse with an Israelite woman, whether it happened in the usual manner or not, he is guilty.

units.la: §. Noachida qui congredi facit servum cum ancilla sua, propter id occidi debet, fi scilicet res tota divulgata fit.
units.tr: §. A Noachide who causes his male slave to lie with his female slave is to be put to death for this, provided of course the whole affair has been made public.

units.la: §. Noachida ob furtum tenetur, five illud commiserit in bonis Iudæi, five gentilis; idem deinde est, five furatus fit pecuniam five hominem, aut suppresserit mercedem mercenarii, aut similia. Ita quoque tenetur על מנה quando aliquid surripuit, quod minus quàm Pruta valet, ( quod in respectu Ifraelitarum non est in usu, vid. Furtum.)
units.tr: A Noachide is liable for theft, whether he commits it against the property of a Jew or of a gentile. It is the same whether he steals money or a person, or withholds a hired labourer's wages, or does anything similar. Likewise he is liable when he has taken something worth less than a pruta [על מנה], which is not in use with regard to Israelites (see Theft).

units.la: §. Noachida etiam tenetur ob membrum animalis vivi, in omni genere animantium; licita tamen est iis effusio sanguinis animalis vi-vi; vi; in his autem idem est membrum aut caro quæ à iumento separatur, aut ab animali vivo. Quod volatilia attinet, non videtur Noachidam ob membrum eius vivum occidi debere. In genere, quod Israelitis circa membrum animalis vivi prohibitum; tale quoque respectu Noachidarum est; imò Noachidæ aliquando rei fiunt, non vero Israelitæ, quia Noachidæ tenentur, cùm circa iumenta tum reliqua animalia, sive sint pura, sive impura.
units.tr: A Noachide is also liable for a limb cut from a living animal, in every kind of creature. It is nevertheless lawful for him to shed the blood of an animal while it is alive. In this case, the limb or flesh cut from a beast is the same as that cut from a living animal. As for birds, it does not seem that a Noachide must be put to death for taking a limb from one while it is alive. In general, what is forbidden to Israelites concerning a limb cut from a living animal is likewise forbidden to Noachides. Indeed, Noachides sometimes become guilty when Israelites do not, because Noachides are bound with respect to beasts of burden and other animals, whether they are clean or unclean.

units.la: §. Quoniam Noachidis illa præcepta data sunt, obligantur idcirco ad constitutionem iudicum in omni tractu, qui ipsos secundùm septem illa præcepta diiudicent, & dirigant. Et quicunque ex Noachidis unum ex his septem præceptis transgressus est, supplicio gladii affici debet. Hinc quoque omnes incolæ Sichem rei facti sunt mortis, quia Sichemo furtum committente, illi facti conscii ad istud conniverunt, nec in iudicium illum vocarunt.
units.tr: Since those precepts were given to the Noachides, they are for that reason bound to appoint judges in every district, who shall judge and direct them according to those seven precepts. And whoever among the Noachides has transgressed one of these seven precepts must be punished by the sword. Hence also all the inhabitants of Shechem were made liable to death, because when Shechem committed theft, they, being aware of it, connived at it and did not summon him to judgement.

units.la: §. Noachida interficitur teste uno, & iudice uno, absque clarâ demonstratione, ex ore solùm proximorum, non autem ex testimonio mulieris; neque unquam Mulier Noachidarum iudex esse poterit.
units.tr: A Noachide is put to death on the testimony of one witness and the verdict of one judge, without clear demonstration, on the word of neighbours alone, but not on the testimony of a woman; and a woman can never be a judge of Noachides.

units.la: §. Noachida qui erravit (inquit Maym. in cap.10.) in uno ex præceptis suis, à pœna nunquam immunis fit, nisi forte imprudenter illud commisisset, & absque ulla errandi intentione. Si alicui Noachidæ vis afferretur, ut aliquod ex suis violaret, vel ut cultum Diis fictitiis exhiberet, à pœna immunis est.
units.tr: §. A Noachide who has transgressed (says Maimonides in chapter 10) in one of his precepts is never exempt from punishment, unless perhaps he committed it inadvertently and without any intention of wrongdoing. If force is applied to a Noachide so that he violates one of his own precepts, or so that he offers worship to fictitious gods, he is exempt from punishment.

units.la: §. Si Noachida qui proselytus Iustitiæ faërus est, seque circuncidere & lustrare curavit, deinde à Iehova regredi vellet, & solùm proselytus inquilinus esse d. fideraret, si iam in religione aliquem progressum fecerit, ipsum non audiunt: sed debet similis esse reliquis Israelitis in omnibus.
units.tr: If a Noachide who has become a proselyte of righteousness has been circumcised and purified, and then wishes to turn back from Jehovah, and to be a proselyte-sojourner only, they do not listen to him if he has already made some progress in the religion; rather he must be like the rest of the Israelites in all things.

units.la: §. Si accidit ut Senatus Noachidam aliquem pupillum baptizare curet, postquàm ille ad maturam ætatem pervenit, quod factum est, delere poterit, ita ut solùm maneat proselytus inquilinus. Si verò Maiorennis declaratus tacta non delet, deinde nihil amplius mutare poterit.
units.tr: If it happens that the court has a Noachide boy baptized, after he reaches adult age he may undo what was done, so that he remains only a proselyte-sojourner. But if, once declared of age, he does not undo what was done, he can change nothing further after that.

units.la: §. Noachida qui maledixit Deo aut fictitios Deos coluit, aut cum uxore proximi rem habuit, aut aliquem interfecit, si Iudæus fit à poena liberatur. At hoc illi nihil proderit si Iudæum interfecisset, aut alicui Iudææ vim intulifset; quamvis enim tunc sacra Iudaica amplecteretur, nihilominus occideretur.
units.tr: A Noachide who has cursed God, or worshipped fictitious gods, or had intercourse with his neighbour's wife, or killed someone, is freed from punishment if he becomes a Jew. But this will do him no good if he has killed a Jew or used violence against a Jewess; for even if he then embraces Jewish rites, he will nevertheless be put to death.

units.la: §. Noachida בתורה חייב מיתה פסיו qui legi operam dat, reus est mortis. (Vid. Sanhed. in ענין הדין) non itaque aliud quid studere debet quàm septem præcepta, quæ ad ipsum pertinent. Si aliquis ex ipsis sibi Sabbathum faceret, in aliquo die pro selto reus fit mortis; in genere non permittendum est, ut ipsi sibimet ipsis novam aliquam cudant legem, aut fabricent præcepta pro lubitu. Debent enim vel planè proselyti iustitiæ fieri, vel in suis septem præceptis absque diminutione aut additione manere.
units.tr: A Noachide who occupies himself with the Torah [בתורה חייב מיתה] is liable to death (see Sanhed. under the heading of judgement). He ought therefore not to study anything other than the seven precepts that pertain to him. If any of them keeps the Sabbath on some day, he becomes liable to death as a transgressor. In general it must not be permitted that they forge some new law for themselves or make up precepts at will. For they must either become fully proselytes of righteousness, or remain in their seven precepts without diminution or addition.

units.la: §. Noachida qui desiderat aliquod aliud legis præceptum observare præter illa septem שכר לקבל כרי ut mercedem promereatur, ipsum non impediunt quin id debito modo faciat. ita si offert holocaustum, omnino ab illius manibus id acccipiunt. Si eleemosynam erogare vult, eam quoque recipiunt.
units.tr: A Noachide who wishes to observe some other precept of the Law besides those seven, in order to earn a reward [שכר לקבל שכר], they do not prevent him from doing it in the proper manner. Thus, if he offers a burnt offering, they accept it entirely from his hands. If he wishes to give alms, they receive that too.

units.la: §. Si duo Noachidæ coram iudice comparent, petentes ut iudicentur secundùm statuta Israelis; si ambo id voluerint, secundùm legem eos diiudicant. Secus fit si non ambo consenserint. Cæterùm Gentiles qui Noachidæ sunt debent humaniter & cum benignitate excipi, ut ipsimet Israelitæ, quia clarè nobis iniunctum est, ut ipsos sustentemus Deut.14.21. Israelitæ debent ipsorum ægrotos visitare, mortuos sepelire, ipsorum pauperes nutrire, ad communem pacem confervandam.
units.tr: If two Noachides appear before a judge, asking to be judged according to the statutes of Israel, then if both wish it, they judge them according to the Law; otherwise it is not so if they do not both agree. Moreover, Gentiles who are Noachides must be received humanely and kindly, just as Israelites themselves are, since it is clearly enjoined on us that we should sustain them (Deut. 14:21). Israelites ought to visit their sick, bury their dead, and feed their poor, in order to preserve the common peace.

units.la: NoBA. Vid. Loca terræ Ifraelitica. in L.
units.tr: NoBA. See Places of the Land of Israel under L.

units.la: NoVILUNIA vid. Intercalationem. De Noviluniis sequentia habet tractatus Rosch Haschana. c. 1. & 2. & 3. Primo die mensis Tisri est caput anni ad fingendos annos & intermissiones, & Iubilæa. Propter duos menses Sabbathum non observant (i.e. Sabbathum non impedit quominus Neomenias figant.) Propter Nisan & propter mensem Tisri, quia in iis nuncii egrediuntur in Syriam, & in illis festa ordinant.
units.tr: NOVILUNIA: see Intercalation. On new moons the tractate Rosh Hashanah, chapters 1, 2 and 3, contains the following. The first day of the month Tishri is the head of the year, for fixing years and intercalations, and jubilees. On account of two months they do not observe the Sabbath (that is, the Sabbath does not prevent them from fixing the new moons): on account of Nisan and on account of the month Tishri, because in those months messengers go out into Syria, and in them the feasts are arranged.

units.la: Ad testimonium de novilunio dicendum legitimus est Pater & filius, & omnes alii propinqui, ipse servus Tobiæ Medici à Synedrio extra ordinem quidem fuit exclusus. Illegitimi autem sunt illi qui ludunt aleâ, qui usuram exercent, qui columbas volare docent, qui fruɗus anni septimi divendunt & qui in statu servili sunt.
units.tr: For testimony about the new moon, a legitimate witness is a father, a son, and all other close relatives; a slave of the physician Tobias was indeed excluded by the Sanhedrin outside the ordinary course. Those are illegitimate who gamble with dice, who practise usury, who teach doves to fly, who sell the produce of the seventh year, and who are in servile condition.

units.la: Illum qui novilunium observavit,& ad illud significandum pedibus ire non potest, asino deducunt aut lectulo; si insidias timent spiculis se munire poterunt, & ne in itinere moras nectant commeatum secum sumere debent.
units.tr: If a man who has observed the new moon cannot go on foot to give notice of it, they bring him by donkey or by litter. If they fear ambushes, they may arm themselves with spears, and so as not to delay on the journey they must take provisions with them.

units.la: Si testem non norunt, alium cum ipso mittunt, ut ille deinde de ipso testimonium reddat. Ab initio receperunt testimonia de quovis indiscriminatim, postquàm autem omnia ab Epicuræis corrupta fuerunt, statuerunt ne ullum testimonium reciperetur, nisi à probè notis.
units.tr: If they do not know the witness, they send another with him, so that he may afterwards give testimony about him. At first they received testimony about anyone indiscriminately; but after everything had been corrupted by the Epicureans, they decreed that no testimony should be received except from those who were well known to be upright.

units.la: Olim ad novilunium indicandum flammas elevarunt, at cùm Cuthæi malitiosè idem intempestivo tempore facerent, decretum est, ut nuntii ad illud significandum egrederentur. Flammas autem sic extulerunt. Acceperunt bacillos longos è cedro, & cannas, & ligna pinguia, & stupam lini, atque hæc filo colligarunt; Deindè unus in fastigium montis oliveti ascendebat, ignem admovebat, flammamque hinc illinc, sursum deorsumque agitabat, usquedum videret alium idem in proximi montis cacumine facientem sicque fiebat in monte tertio & cæteris.
units.tr: Formerly they raised fires to announce the new moon; but when the Cuthaeans maliciously did the same at an unseasonable time, it was decreed that messengers should go out to announce it. They raised the fires as follows. They took long rods of cedar, and reeds, and fat wood, and linen tow, and bound these together with thread. Then one man climbed to the top of the Mount of Olives, applied the fire, and waved the flame from side to side and up and down, until he saw another doing the same on the summit of the next mountain; and so it was done on the third mountain and the rest.

units.la: Vnde autem has flammas primò elevarunt? A monte Oliveti ad Sartabam, à Sartaba ad Grophinam, à Grophina ad Houran, ab Houran ad Beth Balthin, atque illi qui in Beth Balthin flammas extulerunt, sursum ac deorsum agitarunt, donec tota captivitas fuit instar pyræ ignis.
units.tr: Whence, then, did they first raise these flames? From the Mount of Olives to Sartaba, from Sartaba to Grophina, from Grophina to Houran, from Houran to Beth Balthin; and those who raised the flames in Beth Balthin waved them up and down, until the whole exile was like a pyre of fire.

units.la: Atrium magnum fuit Hierosolymis quod פיץ יית בית vocabatur, illud ingredi solebant omnes testes, & ibi Synedrium illos examinare circa lunæ apparentias, & in sabbatho convivio excipere in usu habebat, ut eò libentius accederent.
units.tr: There was a great courtyard at Jerusalem called the House of Ya'aze (Beth Yaaz)... the place which they called "Pits"; all the witnesses were accustomed to enter it, and there the Sanhedrin examined them concerning the appearances of the moon, and it was their custom to entertain them at a Sabbath feast, so that they would come more willingly.

units.la: Examen testium ita fit; par illud testium quod omnium primò accessit accersitur,illumque qui natu maior est ingredi faciunt, & ipsum sic alloquuntur. Dic quomodo vidisti lunam? Fuitne illa ante solem vel post solem? Septentrionem versus aut meridiem versus? Quanta fuit eius altitudo? Sic etiam examinatur secundus; reliquos verò solum obiter examinant, ne ipsos neglexisse videantur. R. Gamaliel ut examen idiotarum facilitaret Lunæ Phasès habuit in tabula conclavis sui, & deinde illas ipsis ostendens interrogavit, an Lunam ita vel ita vidisti?
units.tr: The examination of witnesses is conducted thus. The pair of witnesses who came first of all is summoned, and they have the elder of the two come in, and they address him thus: Tell how you saw the moon. Was it before the sun or after the sun? Toward the north or toward the south? What was its height? In the same way the second is examined; the rest, however, they examine only briefly, so that they may not seem to have neglected them. Rabban Gamaliel, to make the examination easier for the unlearned, had the phases of the moon on a board in his room, and then, showing them these, asked: Did you see the moon thus or thus?

units.la: Postquam testimonia convenerunt, Præses Synedrii clamat, Sanctus est, totusque populus respondet, Sanctus est, Sanctus est. Si ipsam lunam Synedrium & totus Israel viderit, examinantur quidem testes, sed tamen non possunt dicere mensem sanctificatum esse donec noctescat, deinde verò initiatus est. Si Synedrium solum lunam viderit, duo coram ipsis surgunt,& testimonium dicunt,& tunc proclamatur, Sanctificatus es, Sanctificatus est.
units.tr: After the testimonies have been heard, the president of the Sanhedrin cries, He is holy, and the whole people answers, He is holy, he is holy. If the Sanhedrin and all Israel have seen the moon itself, the witnesses are examined, but they still cannot declare the month sanctified until it is night, and only then is it initiated. If the Sanhedrin alone has seen the moon, two men rise before them and give testimony, and then it is proclaimed, Thou art sanctified, It is sanctified.

units.la: His peractis etiam tuba clangunt, de quo ritu vid.loc. citato.
units.tr: When these things are done, they also sound the trumpets. On this rite see the place cited above.

units.la: Nox. Iudæi tres tantùm vigilias noctis agnoscunt,nam hoc apud eos tritum אשמורת שליש
units.tr: Night. The Jews recognise only three watches of the night, for this is a common expression among them: [אשמורת שליש]

units.la: הא של לילה Vigilia est tertia pars noctis. Gloss. in Beracot cap.i.v.i. Commentatores in Iudic.vii. v.19. non quod non noctem in quatuor partes diviserint, sed quod quartam partem, aut vigiliam, non tam pro nocturna, quam pro matutina aestimarint; sic Marci 13.35. spatium illud post Gallicinium כוכב est. Erant ergo revera quatuor noctis vigiliae, at tres tantum profundae noctis. Cl. Lightfoot.
units.tr: [הא של לילה] A watch is the third part of the night. Gloss. on Berakhot ch. 1, v. 1. Commentators on Judges 7:19. They did not fail to divide the night into four parts, but they reckoned the fourth part, or watch, as belonging to the morning rather than to the night. So in Mark 13:35 the period after cockcrow is called [כוכב]. There were therefore really four watches of the night, but only three of deep night. Lightfoot.

units.la: §. Nocte quae fieri possunt, Vid. Diem. Vt nox fit, quot stellae requiruntur? quaerunt in Hierof. Beracot f.1.col.1. Respond. כוכב אחד ודאי יום שנים פעם לילה שלשה ודאי לילה Si adhuc una solum apparet stella, manifeste adhuc dies est, si duo appareant, dubie adhuc nox est; si tres tunc manifeste nox est.
units.tr: §. What may be done at night. See Day. When does night begin? How many stars are required? They ask this in Jerusalem Berakhot fol. 1, col. 1. The answer: If only one star is still visible, it is certainly day; if two appear, it is still doubtfully night; if three, then it is certainly night [כוכב אחד ודאי יום שנים פעם לילה שלשה ודאי לילה].

units.la: Nummi vide Moneta.
units.tr: On coins see Money.

units.la: Numerus. Vid. Mensurationes. Numero Denario gavisa est plurimum gens Iudaica, & in sacris & in civilibus. אין עירה פחותה עשרה Non constituit Synagoga nisi è decem ad minimum. Maymon. Hal. thephilla cap. ii. Vid. etiam Sanhed. cap.i. v.ult. Quaenam est civitas magna? כל שיש בה י בטלין Ea in qua sunt decem homines otiosi. Megillah cap.i.v.3. Hoc etiam apud eos obtinuit אין שורה פחותה מעשרה Corona (vel linea, quam faciunt in funerali pompa,) hominum non constat, nisi è decem ad minimum. Gloss. in Bab. Beracot sol.16.2. Item עשרה יוחסין עלו מנכרי Decem stirpes asfenderunt è Babylone. &c. Massecet Kiddushin cap.4. v.1. Decem qui sedent & discunt legem, Divinitas quiescit inter eos. Pirke avoth c.3. Ad quae sic commentatur Paulus lus Fagius, vir in his eruditissimus. Est certè numerus denarius admodum sacer Hebrais, unde puerum non circumcidunt, nulla connubia stabiliunt, libellus repudii non datur, & solenniores quasdam preces ad Deum non fundunt, nisi Decem personæ affuerint. Hunc numerum itaque κατ' ἐξοχὴν מניין nominant; & novum Testamentum videtur ad illum alludere, Matt.25.1. de hoc numero vid. Decem.
units.tr: Number. See Measurements. The Jewish people greatly favoured the number ten, both in sacred and in civil matters. A synagogue is not established unless it has ten members at least [אין עירה פחותה עשרה]. Maimonides, Hilchot Tefilah ch. 2. See also Sanhedrin ch. 1, last verse. What is a great city? That in which there are ten idle men [כל שיש בה עשרה בטלין], Megillah ch. 1, v. 3. This also prevailed among them: a row (or line, which they form in a funeral procession) of men does not consist unless of ten at least [אין שורה פחותה מעשרה], Gloss. on Bab. Berakhot fol. 16.2. Likewise ten families went up from Babylon [עשרה יוחסין עלו מנכרי], etc., Massechet Kiddushin ch. 4, v. 1. Ten who sit and study the law, the Divine Presence rests among them, Pirke Avot ch. 3. On this Paulus Fagius, a man most learned in these matters, comments: Certainly the number ten is very sacred to the Hebrews. Hence they do not circumcise a boy, do not contract marriages validly, do not give a bill of divorce, and do not pour out certain more solemn prayers to God unless ten persons are present. They therefore call this number by eminence [מניין]; and the New Testament seems to allude to it, Matt. 25:1. On this number see Ten.

units.la: §. Numerus septenarius & quaternarius etiam Mystici sunt, de quartenario vid. Maymon.More Nevoch.II.10. De Septenario sic inquiunt דרך הטקרא לוכור שבע ושבעה לחשבון רב לפי שכל ימי העולם שבועות Mos est scriptura, septenarium numerum, pro multo usurpare, eo quod omnes dies seculi in hebdomadas distribuuntur.
units.tr: The numbers seven and four are also mystical. On four see Maimonides, Guide of the Perplexed II. 10. Of seven they say: It is the manner of Scripture to use the number seven for a large number, because all the days of the world are distributed into weeks [דרך הכתוב לומר שבע ושבעה לחשבון רב].

units.la: §. Adeò hæsit animis Iudæorum devastatio Sacrorum, quam per annos tres & dimidium continuavit Antiochus (vid.1.Maccab.1. Ioseph. Archaiolog.lib.12.cap.7.) ut numerum istum, ut celebrem & memorabilem retinerent, præsertim cum sermo est de rebus tristibus & afflictis. Echa Rabbethi sol.60.4. Venit quidam Athenis Hierosolymam, atque ibi transegit tres annos & dimidium, ut disceret linguam sapientia, sed non didicit. Ibid.sol.641. Vespasianus obsedit Hierosolymam tribus annis & dimidio: & cum eo erant Dux Arabia, Dux Africa, Dux Alexandria, & Dux Palestina.
units.tr: §. The devastation of the sacred things by Antiochus, which he continued for three and a half years (see 1 Macc. 1; Josephus, Antiquities 12.7), so stuck in the minds of the Jews that they kept that number as famous and memorable, especially when the talk is of sad and afflicted matters. Echa Rabbathi fol. 60.4: A certain man came from Athens to Jerusalem and spent three and a half years there, in order to learn the wisdom of the language, but did not learn it. Ibid. fol. 64.1: Vespasian besieged Jerusalem for three and a half years, and with him were the Duke of Arabia, the Duke of Africa, the Duke of Alexandria, and the Duke of Palestine.

units.la: Ibid. sol.71.1. Tribus annis & dimidio obsedit Adrianus Betharam.
units.tr: Ibid. fol. 71.1: Hadrian besieged Bethar for three and a half years.

units.la: Ibid. sol. 66.2. Iudicium generationis diluvii, erat duodecim mensibus. Totidem quoque erant Iudicia Ægyptiorum, Iobi, Gog & Magog; At Iudicium Nebucadnezaris, tribus annis & dimidio, Iudicium Vespasiani tribus annis & dimidio.
units.tr: Ibid. fol. 66.2: The judgment on the generation of the flood lasted twelve months. So too were the judgments on the Egyptians, on Job, and on Gog and Magog. But the judgment of Nebuchadnezzar lasted three and a half years, and the judgment of Vespasian three and a half years.

units.la: Ibid. sol.79 2. Nebucadnezar commoratus est in Daphne Antiochia per tres annos & dimidium. In quibus omnibus numerus non intelligendus est praecisè talis, sed allusivus: qualis etiam aliquando ponendus est in Apocalypsi. De numero Septuagenario vid. Leusdenii Philolog. Heb. Mixt. p.11. ubi pluribus exemplis probat numerum illum aliquando mysticum fuisse.
units.tr: Ibid. fol. 79.2: Nebuchadnezzar dwelt in Daphne near Antioch for three and a half years. In all these cases the number is not to be understood as precisely such, but as allusive, as it sometimes must be taken in the Apocalypse. On the number seventy see Leusden, Philologus Hebraeo-Mixtus, p. 11, where by many examples he proves that this number was sometimes mystical.

units.la: §. De Computatione ipsorum vid. אב.
units.tr: §. On their reckoning see Ab [אב].

units.la: §. Existimant Rabbini nemini licere, homines numerare, ne quidem ad divinum mandatum exequendum. Cùm verò numerum scire desiderabant, à singulis aliquid capiebant, & res istas numerabant, ex quibus deinde numerus hominum ipsis innotuit. Sic Maymon ad cap.2. Ioma. Et Gemar. ibid. Dixit R.Eliefer כל המונה את ישראל עובר כלא תעשה Quisquis numerat Israelem peccat contra praeceptum negativum &c. Hinc Praefectus cultus templi, ad ossicia distribuenda, non Sacerdotes sed digitos ipsorum numeravit: illeque officium habuit, in quem ultima unitas ceciderat. Circa numerum etiam habent formulam usitatissimam, quae respondet formulae quâ Christus usus est Matth.18.v.12. Si erraverit unavelitlis nonaginta novem &c. Peah cap.4. v.2. In distribuendo uvas quasdam & dactylos pauperibus, etiamsi dicant nonaginta novem sparge, & unus tantum divide &c. Hierof. Schabbat sol.14.3. Si moriantur nonaginta novem a fascinatione unus autem ille Dei &c.
units.tr: §. The rabbis think that no one is permitted to number people, not even to carry out a divine command. When they wished to know the number, they took something from each and counted those things, from which the number of men then became known to them. So Maimonides on Yoma ch. 2, and the Gemara there: R. Eliezer said: whoever numbers Israel transgresses a negative precept [כל המונה את ישראל עובר כלא תעשה], etc. Hence the prefect of the temple worship, in distributing the offices, counted not the priests but their fingers, and the office fell to him on whom the last unit came. They also have a very common formula about number, which corresponds to the formula Christ used in Matt. 18:12: If one of them has gone astray, does he not leave the ninety-nine, etc. Peah ch. 4, v. 2: In distributing some grapes and dates to the poor, even if they say "Scatter ninety-nine, and divide only one", etc. Jerusalem Shabbat fol. 14.3: If ninety-nine die of the evil eye, but that one belongs to God, etc.

units.la: Nuptiæ. Indiscriminatim referemus quæ de iis nunc nobis ad manus. In Iudæa circa sponsum & sponsam examen habuerunt, at in Galilæa non ita. In Iudæa permiserunt privatum consortium sponsi cum sponsa per horam unam ante nuptias, at sic non in Galilæa. In Iudæa mos fuit, ut essent duo חבריא amici maritatorum (in vernacula nostra Knabenlader.) Unus è familia sponsi, alter è familia sponsæ; at non sic in Galilæa. In Iudæa dormiverunt, ubi sponsus & sponsa etiam isti amici, & in Galilæa non ita. Tosiphta ad Cethubhot cap.1.
units.tr: Weddings. We shall report, without any particular order, what now comes to hand concerning them. In Judea they had an examination concerning the bridegroom and bride, but not so in Galilee. In Judea they permitted the bridegroom a private meeting with the bride for one hour before the wedding; not so in Galilee. In Judea it was the custom to have two friends of the married [חבריא] (in our vernacular, Knabenlader), one from the bridegroom's family and the other from the bride's; not so in Galilee. In Judea the bridegroom and bride, together with these friends, slept in the same place; in Galilee not so. Tosephta on Ketubot ch. 1.

units.la: §. De Nuptiis vid. Vxor.
units.tr: §. On weddings see Wife.

units.la: §. Quomodo in Nuptiis sponsa dignosci potuit, an esset virgo vel vidua. Vid. Vidua.
units.tr: §. How, at a wedding, the bride could be distinguished as a virgin or a widow. See Widow.

units.la: §. Tempore persequutionis, non potuerunt celebrare nuptias publicè; clanculum ergò id præstiterunt. Vbicunque itaque erant candelæ lucentes in superliminari; noverunt, quòd illic foret convivium nuptiale. Aruch in אור.
units.tr: §. In a time of persecution they could not celebrate weddings publicly, so they did it secretly. Wherever there were lamps shining over the lintel, therefore, they knew that a wedding feast was being held there. Aruch under [אור].

units.la: §. Nuptias semper præivit desponsatio. Ante legem quivis poterat privatim uxorem ducere, sed data lege præcipitur, ut si quis velit uxorem ducere, recipiat eam prius coram testibus, & deinceps sit illa ei in uxorem. Maymon. in משנה cap. 1. In locis plurimis vir sibi fœminam desponsat, ad se autem non ducit, nisi interposito aliquo temporis spatio. Maymonides Comment. in Hal. משנה cap. 3.
units.tr: §. Betrothal always preceded the marriage. Before the law, anyone could take a wife privately; but once the law was given, it was commanded that if anyone wished to take a wife, he should first receive her before witnesses, and thereafter she should be his wife. Maimonides on the Mishnah, ch. 1. In many places a man betroths a woman to himself but does not take her to his home until some interval of time has passed. Maimonides' commentary on Hal. ch. 3.

units.la: §. De Desponsatione vid.f 1. in D. Non nubit nec desponsatur illa fœmina, quæ à viro dimissa vel repudiata est, nisi post moram nonaginta dierum,ut dignoscatur, utrum sit gravida nec ne; atque ut inter sobolem primi mariti distinguatur & fecundi. Idem observatur respectu uxoris illius qui proselytus factus est, ut inter infantes in vera religione conceptos & reliquos discrimen poni possit. Maymon. in Girujchin c.11.Talmud in Iebhamot c.4. Chetubhot cap.5.
units.tr: §. On betrothal see f. 1 in D. A woman who has been dismissed or repudiated by her husband may not marry or be betrothed until after a delay of ninety days, so that it may be known whether she is pregnant or not, and so that the offspring of the first husband may be distinguished from that of the second. The same rule is observed with regard to the wife of a man who has become a proselyte, so that a distinction can be drawn between children conceived in the true religion and the rest. Maimonides on Gerushin ch. 11; Talmud on Yebamot ch. 4; Ketubot ch. 5.

units.la: §. In modo Dotalem donationem scribendi convenerunt Hierosolymitani & Galilæi; at incolæ Iudææ aliquid variarunt. Gemara. Galilæis cura fuit de fama, non de nummis; at Incolis Iudææ cura fuit de nummis non de fama. Hierof. (Chetubhot sol.29.2. Simeon Ben Schetach dotes ordinavit. Schabbat sol.14.2. Ab antiquitate virgini constituti erant 200. Numni, viduæ centum. Chetubhot cap. 8. in fine.
units.tr: §. In the manner of writing the dowry gift, the Jerusalemites and the Galileans agreed, but the inhabitants of Judea varied somewhat. Gemara: The Galileans cared about reputation, not money; the inhabitants of Judea cared about money, not reputation. Jerusalem Ketubot fol. 29.2. Simeon ben Shetach ordained dowries. Shabbat fol. 14.2. From antiquity, 200 coins were assigned for a virgin and 100 for a widow. Ketubot ch. 8, at the end.

units.la: §. In more fuit cum educerent sponsum & sponsam, ante eos ducere gallum & gallinam: ac si dicerent, Crescite, & Multiplicamini. Bab. Gittin sol.57.1. Habebant etiam in usu Betharæ, ut cum infans nasceretur, plantarent cedrum, cum infantula, pinum, & deinde ex iis conficere thalamum cum nati contraherent matrimonium. Gittin l. cit. His ritibus tam ardenter adhæserunt, ut illi cautæ excidii fuerint, montis regalis & Betharæ; noluerunt enim connivere ad factum illorum Romanorum Militum, qui in transitu talem gallum ab ipsis extorserant, & cedrum exciderant. Vid. historiam loco modò notato.
units.tr: In former times, when they led the bridegroom and bride out, they had a cock and a hen walk before them, as if to say, "Increase and multiply." Bab. Gittin fol. 57.1. They also had the custom at Bethar that when a boy was born they planted a cedar, and when a girl was born a pine, and later made a bridal chamber from these trees when the children married. Gittin, loc. cit. They clung so tenaciously to these rites that they became the cause of the destruction of the royal mountain and of Bethar. For they refused to overlook the deed of those Roman soldiers who, on their march, had seized such a cock from them and cut down the cedar. See the history mentioned just above.

units.la: §. Tenebatur maritus pro proportione dotis uxori præbere קופת הכשרי Arculam Aromatum, ut apparet ex Bab. Chetubh. sol. 66. 2. At hoc non dicitur, inquit Rabh Ischai, nisi de Hierosolymitanis. Extat exemplum filiæ Nicodemi Ben Gorion, cui allocarunt sapientes quadringentos aureos pro area aromatum in unumquemque diem. Glossa. A marito dandi erant decem Sufai uxori pro unaquaque Manah, quem ea secum attulit, ad comedenda aromata, quibus uteretur ad se lavandum.
units.tr: The husband was bound, in proportion to the dowry, to provide his wife with an ark of spices (קופת הכשרי), as appears from Bab. Chetubh. fol. 66.2. "But this is said," says Rabh Ischai, "only of the Jerusalemites. There is the example of the daughter of Nicodemus ben Gorion, for whom the sages assigned four hundred gold pieces for an ark of spices each day." Gloss: "The husband had to give ten sufai to his wife for each manah she brought with her, for spices to be consumed, which she would use to wash herself."

units.la: §. Nemini licet ante annum decimum tertium coniugium contrahere, quia ante illud tempus ad coniugium & generandos filios est inidoneus. Sanhed. sol. 51. 1. filia vocatur בוגרת pubescens à duodecimo & dimidio anno; & tunc quando pubuit non amplius patri est potestas in eam, Nidda f. 47. 1. hinc illud dictum, si filia tua ad pubertatem pervenerit, manumitte servum tuum, & dato eum ipsi. Pesachim f. 113. 1.
units.tr: No one may contract marriage before the thirteenth year, because before that time a person is unfit for marriage and for begetting children. Sanhed. fol. 51.1. A girl is called pubescens (בוגרת) from the age of twelve and a half years; and once she has reached puberty, her father no longer has power over her. Nidda fol. 47.1. Hence that saying: "If your daughter has reached puberty, manumit your slave and give him to her." Pesachim fol. 113.1.

units.la: §. De coniugio satis honesta ubique fermè fit mentio. Berefchit Rabba sect. 58. in princip. dixit R. Pinchas, invenimus in lege, in Prophetis, & in Hagiographis שאין הגו של איש אלא מן הק"בה Quod coniugium hominis à Deo tantum fit. Est qui quærit coniugium, & est ad quem coniugium venit. Quæsivit quadam mulier; Quid faciat Deus post absolutam creationem? Resp. ישוב ויושב Sedet & coniungit coniugia, p r a.&c. Benedictionem coniugii ablatam esse credunt cum templi devastatione. Sanhed. sol. 75. in fine cap.
units.tr: Marriage is mentioned almost everywhere in fairly respectable terms. Bereshit Rabba sect. 58, at the beginning: "R. Pinchas said, 'We find in the Law, in the Prophets, and in the Writings' that the marriage of a man comes only from the Holy One, blessed be He" (שאין הזיווג של איש אלא מן הקב"ה). "There is one who seeks a wife, and there is one to whom a wife comes. A certain woman asked: What does God do after the completion of creation? Answer: He sits and joins marriages" (ישוב ויושב), "etc." They believe that the blessing of marriage was taken away with the devastation of the Temple. Sanhed. fol. 75, at the end of the chapter.

units.la: A tempore quo vaslatum est templum Hierosolymitanum ניטלה טעם ביאה ablata est voluptas cohabitationis coniugalis, & data est scortatoribus & adulteris.
units.tr: From the time the Temple of Jerusalem was laid waste, the pleasure of cohabitation was taken away (ניטלה טעם ביאה), and it was given to fornicators and adulterers.

units.la: §. Prohibitum viro est desponsare sibi uxorem antequàm viderit eam; Kiddufchin c.2. Mulier desponsatur tribus rebus, argento, scripto & coitu. Schulchan Aruch par. 4. num. 26. Talmud. Kiddufchin cap. 1. Sapientes tamen postea vetuerunt desponsare per coitum ad protervam lasciviam vitandam. Pecuniâ uxor desponsatur, quando dicit dans ei pecuniam, vel æquivalens pecuniæ, Ecce mihi desponsata es. Kiddufchin sol. 5. 2. Non desponsant sibi uxorem minus quàm quod valet Pruta. Schulchan Aruch parte 4. num. 31. Si quis non expressè dixerit, desponsata es ללי mihi, desponsatio valida non est. Si desponset annulo commodato illa non est desponsata. Innumeros alios Casus vid. in Kiddufchin.
units.tr: A man is forbidden to betroth to himself a wife before he has seen her. Kiddufchin ch. 2. A woman is betrothed in three ways: by money, by writing, and by intercourse. Schulchan Aruch part 4, num. 26. Talmud, Kiddufchin ch. 1. Nevertheless the sages later forbade betrothal by intercourse, to avoid shameless lewdness. A wife is betrothed with money when the man gives her money, or something equivalent to money, and says, "Behold, you are betrothed to me." Kiddufchin fol. 5.2. They do not betroth a wife with less than the value of a pruta. Schulchan Aruch part 4, num. 31. If someone does not expressly say, "You are betrothed to me" (לי), the betrothal is not valid. If he betroths her with a borrowed ring, she is not betrothed. For countless other cases see Kiddufchin.

units.la: §. Consuetudo sponsorum est, post desponsationem per datam arrham, ut crastino mane mittant ad domum soceri sui, in honorem uxoris sponsæ monilia sive ornamenta muliebria, species fructuum, vascula vini aut olei. R.Salomoh in Bava Bathra cap.9. sol.146. col.1. hæc munera vocantur סיבלונות vid. loc.
units.tr: The custom of bridegrooms is that, after the betrothal by the giving of an earnest, the next morning they send to the house of the bride's father, in honour of the betrothed wife, necklaces or women's ornaments, samples of fruit, and small vessels of wine or oil. R. Salomoh in Bava Bathra ch. 9, fol. 146, col. 1. These gifts are called סיבלונות; see the passage.

units.la: In terra Ismaelitica mos erat, ut sponsam ducerent à domo patris sui in domum sponsi, ante introductionem in thalamum, ferrentque ante eam circiter decem baculos ligneos, in uniuscuiusque summitate vasculum instar scutellæ habentes, in quo est segmentum panni cum oleo & pice. Ex his accensis facem ei præferunt. Aruch in לפר. R. Salom. in Kelim c. 2. v.8. tales lampades habere dicuntur 10.Virgines in Parabola Mat h.25.v.1.
units.tr: In the Ishmaelite land the custom was to lead the bride from her father's house into the bridegroom's house, and before she was brought into the bridal chamber they carried in front of her about ten wooden staves, each having at its top a little vessel like a dish, in which there was a piece of cloth with oil and pitch. Having lit these, they carried the torch before her. Aruch under לפר. R. Salom. on Kelim ch. 2, v. 8. Such lamps are said to have been carried by the ten virgins in the parable, Matt. 25.1.

units.la: §. Consuetudo communis est in plerisque nationibus, ut cùm quis ducit uxorem, & nuptias celebrat, proximi agnati & amici mittant dono pecunias quasdam ad sublevandos sumptus nuptiarum; veniunt etiam plerumq; amici isti dona mittentes ad nuptias & convivantur cum sponso, vel septem nuptiarum diebus, vel aliquot tantum. Isti שושבנין vocantur; Socii, hospites nuptiarum. Maymon Iad Chasaka parte 4. sol.103. col.2. in princip. cap.7. de illis vid.Cl.Buxt.Lex.Talm.f.2.535.
units.tr: It is a custom common among most nations that when someone takes a wife and celebrates the wedding, near relatives and friends send some money as a gift to help with the expenses of the wedding. These friends who send gifts to the wedding often also come and feast with the bridegroom, either for the seven days of the wedding or for only a few of them. They are called שושבנין, companions, guests of the wedding. Maymon, Iad Chasaka part 4, fol. 103, col. 2, in princip. ch. 7. On them see Cl. Buxt. Lex. Talm. p. 2535.

units.la: §. Nuptiæ virginis celebrabantur die quarto Septimanæ, Chetubhot sol.2.1. חופה dies thalami amicis & familiaribus, fuerunt septem; hinc frequens memoria septem dierum convivii nuptialis: at verò sponsæ dies thalami fuerunt triginta. Ioma cap.1.v.1. in die expiationis nemo debet edere, bibere, aut se lavare, at reg' & sponsa permissum est lavare facies suas. Glossa. Sponsa enim venustanda est, ut amabilis sit marito וכל ל' יום לחופתה היא קויה כלה Atq; omnibus triginta diebus thalami sui vocatur sponsa. Sponsæ virgines, ut & aliæ honoratiores mulieres in nuptiis aliisque festivitatibus, gestabant coronam auream, ad formam urbis Ierusalem factam, & quàm propterea עיר של זהב urbem auream vocabant Nedarim sol.50.1.
units.tr: The wedding of a virgin was celebrated on the fourth day of the week. Chetubhot fol. 2.1. The days of the bridal chamber (חופה) for friends and relatives were seven; hence the frequent mention of the seven days of the wedding feast. But the bride's days of the bridal chamber were thirty. Ioma ch. 1, v. 1: On the Day of Atonement no one may eat, drink, or wash; but the bridegroom and the bride are permitted to wash their faces. Gloss: "For the bride must be made lovely so that she may be pleasing to her husband." And throughout all thirty days of her bridal chamber she is called a bride (וכל ל' יום לחופתה היא קוייה כלה). Virgin brides, like other more honoured women at weddings and other festivities, wore a golden crown made in the form of the city of Jerusalem, and for this reason called it "the golden city" (עיר של זהב). Nedarim fol. 50.1.

units.la: §. Ingenti lætitiâ perstrepuerunt nuptiæ eorum; præter varia instrumenta Musices,
units.tr: Their weddings resounded with great rejoicing, besides various musical instruments,

units.la: D d etiam utebantur tympanis, ut ex hoc loco disci potest. Nidda sol. 61. 2. In bello Vespasiani decretum ediderunt עַל עִטְרוֹת חִתָּנִים וְעַל הָאִירוּם Super coronis sponsorum, & super tympanis (fecund.R.Salom. tintinnabula erant)ne scilicet ulterius pulsarentur, in publica illa miseria. De מוּטוּתִין ludis quæ coram sponso & sponsa fiebant, Vid. Chagigah. sol.14.2. Memorabilis est ille ritus quô נהגו לשבר זכוכית בנישואין soliti suunt frangere vasa vitrea in nuptiis. Gloff. in Bab. Beracot sol. 31.1. ut scilicet illâ ratione modum & frænum inderent hilaritati, ne nimis luxuriarentur. Historiam unam & alteram producit illic Gemara. Mar filius Rabbena fecit convivia nuptialia filio suo, atque invitavit Rabbinos, cumque videret, illos supra modum lætitiæ locum dare איתי כסא רבוקרא Adduxit poculum vitreum valens quadringentos fuscos, atque illud coram iis confregit, unde contristabantur. Idem refertur de Rabb Ifchai, & ratio redditur; quia prohibetur homini os suum risu implere in hoc mundo.
units.tr: they also used drums, as can be learned from this passage. Nidda fol. 61.2. "In the war of Vespasian they issued a decree: concerning the crowns of the bridegrooms and concerning the drums" (עַל עִטְרוֹת חִתָּנִים וְעַל הָאִירוּם), (according to R. Solomon, the drums were little bells), "namely that they should no longer be struck in that public misery." Concerning the games (מוּטוּתִין) that were performed before the bridegroom and bride, see Chagigah fol. 14.2. Memorable is that custom by which they were accustomed to break glass vessels at weddings (נהגו לשבר זכוכית בנישואין). Gloss in Bab. Beracot fol. 31.1: namely, to set a measure and a bridle on merriment, so that they would not indulge too much. The Gemara there produces one story and another. "Mar, son of Rabbena, made a wedding feast for his son and invited the Rabbis; and when he saw them giving place to joy beyond measure, he brought a glass cup worth four hundred fusci (איתי כסא רבוקרא) and broke it before them, whereupon they were saddened." The same is related of Rabbi Ischai, and the reason given is because a man is forbidden to fill his mouth with laughter in this world.

units.la: §. In Babylonia in usu erat in nuptiis virginum, capita Rabbinorum ungere; Bab.Chetubbot sol.17.2. Quænam sunt testimonia quòd fœmina nupta sit viro? Si prodierit peplo super oculos demisso, capite tamen non velato. Sparsio nucum est etiam testimonium. Hac in Iudea. At quaenam in Babylonia? Dicit Rabb דמשתא אריש דרבנן Si unguentum fuerit super caput Rabbinorum, Gloffa, fœminæ unguentum dederunt in capita תלמידין Studiosorum, & unxerunt.) Dicit Rabb Papa ר' Abbai, num Doctor iste loquitur de unguento aromatico, usitato in thalamis? Respondit ille יתמא O Orphane, (i. e. inscie confuetudi- num) לא עברא לך אפך דדרוגי משחא אריש־ דרבן Nonne mater tua effudit pro te (in nuptiis tuis) unguenta super capita Rabbinorum ? Item fecit Rabba Bar Ulla, & effudit unguentum super capita Rabbinorum. An hoc etiam apud Hierofolymitanos in usu fuerit dubitari potest, praecipuè cùm ipsimet dicant in Hierof. Beracot sol.11.2. Indecorum esse discipulo sapientum olere aromata: & insuper ex exemplo discipulorum Christi Marci 14.3. Satis apparet, ipsos (excepto Iuda, qui lucro inhiabat) profusionem unguenti idcirco ægre tulisse, quia non poterant approbare, morem tam delicatum, & apud Magistros Iudæorum invisum, adhiberi Magiftro suo.
units.tr: In Babylonia it was the custom at the weddings of virgins to anoint the heads of the Rabbis. Bab. Chetubbot fol. 17.2: "What are the testimonies that a woman is married to a man? If she goes out with her veil lowered over her eyes but her head not covered. The scattering of nuts is also a testimony; this is in Judea. But what in Babylonia? The Rabbi says: If there is ointment on the head of the Rabbis (דמשתא אריש דרבנן)." (The gloss: women gave ointment to the heads of the students (תלמידין) and anointed them.) "Rabba Papa says: Rabbi Abbai, does this teacher speak of aromatic ointment used in bridal chambers? He replied: O orphan (יתמא), i.e., ignorant of the custom, did not your mother pour ointment on the heads of the Rabbis for you (לא עברא לך אפך דדרוגי משחא אריש דרבן) at your wedding? Likewise Rabba bar Ulla did, and poured ointment on the heads of the Rabbis." It may be doubted whether this was also in use among the Jerusalemites, especially since they themselves say in Hierof. Beracot fol. 11.2 that it is unseemly for a disciple of the sages to smell of spices; and moreover from the example of Christ's disciples, Mark 14.3. It is quite clear that they (except Judas, who was greedy for gain) took the pouring of the ointment badly precisely because they could not approve of so luxurious a custom, one hateful among the Jewish masters, being applied to their own Master.

units.la: §. De Nuptiis plura habet Cl. Buxtorf. in Synagog. Iud. & tractat. de sponsalibus, quem lector adire poterit.
units.tr: §. Cl. Buxtorf has more on weddings in Synagoga Judaica and in his treatise on betrothals, which the reader may consult.

units.la: §. Quæritur apud Iudæos quomodo פרו ורבו Crescite & multiplicamini Gen.1.28. Primi homines intellexerint, an perceperint illud mandatum ad se pertinêre? Resp. R. Levi Barzelonita, Deum hoc præcepto obligasse omnes homines masculos, sed non fœminas. Obtinet omni loco, inquit, & tempore, ita ut teneatur et homo dare operam, primum atque aptus consecutus fuerit terminum, quem præfixerunt Magistri nostri. ומצוה זו אינה מטלת על הנשים Hoc autem præceptum mulieribus non est impositum. Maymonides, Bartenora, Iarchi in Comment. ad Iebhamot cap.6. R. Levi assentiunt, hoc argumento nixi, quia terram subjiciendi præceptum præcipuè mascülis datum in verbis in Genesi seq. Implete terram ac subijcite eam, nec proinde præceptum connexum de fructificatione, nisi ad mares extendi oportère; hoc præcipuè Gloss. Iarchi ex Vau in חנכנ elicit. V. Gloss. R. Iochanan verò non solum hoc tribuit masculo. Sed & fœminæ vid. Massec.Iebhamot cap.6. ratio eius est plausibilis, sc. quia Deus marem & fœminam, qui tunc soli erant in mundo alloquutus est, cur præceptum non quoque ad ambos extenderetur. Hæc Iudæorum commentatio non placet, Bellarmino & Torniello, qui volunt matrimonium tunc esse præceptum, cùm mundus exhaustus esse incolis, quod quidem non ita male dicerent, nisi scopus ipsorum esset impuro lenocinari cœlibatui; nam ἀπρ γεαφὴς est, quod Hebræi existimant, unumquemque masculum, & quidem sub ratione pœnæ [ut notat R. Levi] ad coniugium alligari & obligari. Taceo iam quòd de exclusione mulierum absque ratione referunt.
units.tr: §. Among the Jews it is asked how the first humans understood the command Be fruitful and multiply [פרו ורבו] (Gen. 1.28), and whether they took it to apply to themselves. The answer: R. Levi Barzelonita held that God bound all men, but not women, by this precept. It holds in every place and at every time, so that a man is bound to take pains over it as soon as he has reached the first suitable age that our masters have set. This commandment, however, has not been laid upon women [ומצוה זו אינה מטלת על הנשים]. Maimonides, Bartenora and Rashi, in their commentary on Yebamot ch. 6, agree with R. Levi, resting on this argument: since the command to subdue the earth was given chiefly to males in the words that follow in Genesis, Fill the earth and subdue it, the connected command about fruitfulness must likewise extend only to males. Rashi's gloss draws this especially from the vav in the word in question; see the gloss. R. Johanan, however, does not assign it to males alone but to females as well; see Massekhet Yebamot ch. 6. His reasoning is plausible: because God addressed the male and the female, who alone were then in the world, why should the command not extend to both? This Jewish interpretation does not please Bellarmine and Tornielli, who want marriage to have been commanded only once the world had been emptied of its inhabitants. They might say this well enough, were it not that their aim is to flatter unclean celibacy. For the view that every male is bound to marriage under penalty, as the Hebrews hold, is not from Scripture [ἀπὸ γραφῆς], as R. Levi notes. I say nothing yet of the fact that they report the exclusion of women without any reason.

units.la: De Nuptiis Patriarcharum notamus 1. Ipsos in delectu coniugum sanguinis etiam rationem habuisse, ne scilicet incestum committerent, erant enim sex coniugia ante legem præcipuè talia. 1. cum matre sua, 2. cum noverca. 3. cum uxore viri, i. e. aliena. 4. cum sorore uterina. 5. cum masculo. 6. cum bestia. Vid. Gemaram ad Babil. Sanhed. cap.7. talia enim sunt coram oculis Domini ut & reliqua memorata Levit. 18. תועבות abominationes, ob quas Deus Gentes Cananeas evomuit. Levit. xviii.27.28.
units.tr: On the marriages of the patriarchs we note: 1. that in choosing spouses they also took account of kinship, so that they would not commit incest. For before the law there were six kinds of such unions in particular: (1) with one's mother; (2) with a stepmother; (3) with another man's wife; (4) with a full sister; (5) with a male; (6) with a beast. See the Gemara on Babylonian Sanhedrin ch. 7. Such things are an abomination in the eyes of the Lord, as are the other abominations listed in Lev. 18 (תועבות), on account of which God vomited out the Canaanite nations: Lev. 18.27, 28.

units.la: Secundò, illos adhibuisse consensum parentum; Sic Abraham, Isaac, Iacob, Iuda, filiis suis de coniugio prolpexerunt. Ipse Laban, a'iàs parum tidelis, satis ostendit, parentibus solis ius competere τὴ ἐχγαμίζειν, quando dicit, Melius est ut eam dem tibi quàm alii; Genes. xxix. 19. hoc ius etiam tradit Aristot. Ethic. viii. 1. φύσει ἀρχικὸν πατὴρ υἱῶν. Natura pater imperat filiis.
units.tr: Second, that they sought the consent of their parents. Thus Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Judah provided spouses for their sons. Laban himself, not a very faithful man, shows well enough that the right to give a daughter in marriage belongs to parents alone, when he says, It is better that I give her to you than to another (Gen. 29.19). Aristotle also grants this right in Ethics viii.1: The father by nature rules over the sons [φύσει ἀρχικὸν πατὴρ υἱῶν].

units.la: Tertiò, in ipsis nuptiis sequentia obseruasse, x. Vt solenni benedictione seu εὐλογία mulier traderetur viro; talem benedictionem dedit Deus Gen. 2. 22. & adduxit Evam ad Adamum, & benedixit ipsis. Gen. 1. 28. Sic in historia Rebeccæ ipsi benedicunt, vid. Gen. 24. 60. hunc ritum quoque in posterioribus seculis retinuerunt, Vid. R. Eliefer in Pirke cap. 16. Minister Synagoga stat & benedicit sponso in thalamo suo. &c.
units.tr: Third, that in the marriage itself they observed the following. First, that the woman was given to the husband with a solemn blessing, or eulogia. God gave such a blessing: He brought Eve to Adam, and blessed them (Gen. 2.22; 1.28). So in the story of Rebekah they bless her (Gen. 24.60). They kept this rite also in later centuries; see R. Eliezer in Pirke ch. 16: The minister of the synagogue stands and blesses the bridegroom in his bedchamber, etc.

units.la: 2. Sponsam in aedibus paternis ante consummationem matrimonii aliquam moram traxisse, sic in historia Rebeccæ Genes. xxiv. 55. dicunt, maneat puella nobisçum dies aut decem. i. e. annum aut decem menses. 2. Sponsas in usu habuisse theriftero, palliolo scilicet se obvelare, ut patet ex exemplo Rebeccæ, quæ appropinquans se opperuit τῷ Σηρίφῳ, Heb. בצעי Ionath. ירידו Onkelofo עיפא, Arab. ורא, Rabb. ירד quod secundùm R. Nathan erat velum tenue, mulieribus usitatum, ad cooperiendum caput.
units.tr: 2. That the bride stayed some time in her father's house before the marriage was consummated. Thus in the story of Rebekah they say (Gen. 24.55), Let the girl stay with us for ten days or so, that is, a year or ten months. 2. That brides used a veil, namely a little cloak with which to cover themselves, as is clear from the example of Rebekah, who, when she drew near, covered herself with the veil [Greek σηρίφῳ]. The Hebrew word is betsa'i; Targum Jonathan has yeridu, Onkelos 'ippa, the Arabic wara', and the rabbis yarad. According to R. Nathan this was a thin veil, used by women to cover the head.

units.la: 3. Nuptias absque solenni convivio non fuisse celebratas. Sic Laban instruxit convivium, Genes. xxix. 22. hoc convivium verò per integrum septiduum durabat; ut probant & explicant ex Genes. xxix. 27. ex verbis בלא שבע ואת
units.tr: 3. That weddings were not celebrated without a solemn feast. Thus Laban arranged a feast (Gen. 29.22), and this feast lasted a full seven days, as they prove and explain from Gen. 29.27, from the words, fulfil the week of this one [בלא שבע ואת].

units.la: Exple hebdomadam huius &c. R. Eliezer in Pirke cap. 16. Targum Hierof. Ionathan & Onkelos in loc.
units.tr: Fulfil the week of this one, etc. R. Eliezer in Pirke ch. 16; the Jerusalem Targum; Jonathan and Onkelos on the passage.

units.la: O.
units.tr: O.

units.la: OBLATIONES frumentariae vocantur מנחות vid. Sacrificia. De oblatione frugum iam praeparatarum vid. Truma. Qui oblationem offert, non restituto quod iniuste rapuerat, non quod officit est faci. Bava Kama cap.9.v.12. אין מקריבין את המנחה Non offertur oblatio pro reatu, nisi prius restituatur ablatum, vel possessori vel sacerdoti. Maymon in Gezelah cap.8.
units.tr: OBLATIONS of grain are called מנחות [minchoth]; see Sacrifices. On an offering of produce already prepared, see Terumah. One who brings an offering without first restoring what he has unjustly seized does not do what is right. Bava Kama, chapter 9, verse 12: An offering is not brought for guilt unless what was taken is first restored, either to the owner or to the priest. אין מקריבין את המנחה [ein makrivin et ha-minchah]. Maimonides, in Gezelah, chapter 8.

units.la: §. De oblatione nummorum in templo tractatur in Schekalim sol.8. 4. Vid. Sicles & Gazophylacium. Glosa loc.cit. Pro arbitrio suo potuit quisquam in arculas projicere quantum voluit: Nempe in cistam quae pro auro, tantillum auri quantum pendebat granum hordei: & in cistam pro thure, quantum pendebat granum hordei thuris. &c.
units.tr: §. On the offering of money in the Temple, see the tractate Shekalim, folio 8, column 4. See Shekels and Gazophylacium. The gloss on the same passage: Anyone could cast into the chests as much as he wished: namely, into the chest for gold, a little gold equal in weight to a grain of barley; and into the chest for incense, as much incense as weighed a grain of barley. etc.

units.la: OBOLUS Vid. Monetam.
units.tr: OBOLUS: see Coin.

units.la: OBSCURA dilucidabantur ab Elia. Vid. Eliam.
units.tr: OBSCURE passages were made clear by Elijah; see Elijah.

units.la: OCCASIONE uti debemus, quando se offert, secundùm illud in Ialkut in Leg. 279.1. Dum calceus est in pede, conculca stinas.
units.tr: OPPORTUNITY should be used when it presents itself, according to the saying in the Yalkut on the Law, 279.1: While the sandal is on your foot, trample the stones.

units.la: ODIUM. Tria se invicem odio habent, Canes, Galli, Socii, (Genef. 3. 4. in Ionath.) addunt etiam, scorta & Discipulos Sapientum. Megillah sol.25.2. Pesachim f.113.2. Tres odio habet Deus, qui aliud ore loquitur, aliud sentit; qui testimonium pro socio suo scit, & id non testatur, qui proximum solus in scortatione deprehendit, & solus contrà eum testatur. ibid.
units.tr: HATRED. Three things hate one another: dogs, cocks and partners (Genesis 3:4 in Jonathan). They add also harlots and disciples of the wise. Megillah, folio 25, column 2; Pesachim, folio 113, column 2: God hates three: he who speaks with his mouth one thing and thinks another; he who knows a testimony for his partner and does not bear it; and he who alone catches his neighbour in fornication and alone bears witness against him. Ibid.

units.la: §. Pulchrum est illud Hillelis in Schabbat f. 31.1. דעלך סני לחכיך לא העביד ו הוא כל התורה כולה Quod odiosum est tibi proximo tuo ne feceris. Hac est lex tota, cetera nihil sunt nisi eius explicatio. Confer Matth.7.12. de odio non fovendo Vid. offensio.
units.tr: §. Hillel's saying in Shabbat, folio 31, column 1, is fine: דעלך סני לחכיך לא העביד [da alach sani lechavrach la ta‘avid], What is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbour. This is the whole Law; the rest is only its explanation. Compare Matthew 7:12 on not nourishing hatred; see Offence.

units.la: OFFENSIO. Si quis te offenderit aut peccaverit corripies eum, inquit Christus Matth.18.15. & Moses Lev.xix.17. Idem Talmudici in Bab. Erachin sol.16. Tradunt Rabbini, Non odio habebis fratrem tuum in corde tuo. Forte eum non tundit, non vellicat, non ei maledicit: Tertius dicit in corde tuo; loquens de odio in corde. Unde autem adstruitur quod videns fratrem suum turpe aliquid perpetrantem, teneatur illum corripere? quia dicitur תוכיח תוכיח Corripiendo corripies. Ex cuius iteratione etiam videtur corripientem ad secundam correptionem teneri. Et paulò post, Rabb dicit, fratrem corripiendum esse usque ad ictus. Samuel dicit, usquedum irascatur. Vide etiam Maymon in Peah cap. 6.
units.tr: OFFENCE. "If anyone offends you or sins against you, correct him," says Christ, Matthew 18:15, and Moses, Leviticus 19:17. The Talmudists say the same in Bab. Erachin, folio 16: The rabbis teach: You shall not hate your brother in your heart. Perhaps he does not strike him, pinch him or curse him? The third says: in your heart, speaking of hatred in the heart. But whence is it established that one who sees his brother committing some shameful act is bound to rebuke him? Because it is said, תוכיח תוכיח [tokhiach tokhiach], you shall surely rebuke. From this repetition it seems also that the one rebuking is bound to rebuke a second time. And a little later: Rabbi says the brother is to be rebuked even to the point of blows. Samuel says, until he is angry. See also Maimonides in Peah, chapter 6.

units.la: §. In culpa offensionis ad fratrem redarguendum praecipit Christus, ut unum vel alterum secum sumat, idem exigunt Iurisconsulti Hebraei à peccante in fratrem. Hierof. Ioma f. 45.3. & Babyl.Ioma 87.1. Samuel dicit, quicunque peccat in fratrem suum, necesse habet, ut ei dicat in te peccavi. Si audiat, bene. Si non; adducat alios, & placet eum coram iis, si forsan moriatur, placet eum ad sepulchrum suum, & dicat, in te peccavi.&c. Sic Synedrium semper duos discipu-
units.tr: §. In a fault of offence, Christ orders that one or two others be taken along to rebuke the brother; the Hebrew jurists require the same of one who sins against a brother. Jerusalem Yoma, folio 45, column 3, and Babylonian Yoma 87.1: Samuel says: whoever sins against his brother must say to him, "I have sinned against you." If he listens, well. If not, let him bring others, and let him make peace with him before them; if perhaps he dies, let him make peace with him at his grave and say, "I have sinned against you," etc.

units.la: los sapientum adhibuit, quando civitatem ad idololatriam prolapsam ad refipiscentiam vocavit. Maymon Avodah Zarah cap.4. Ita maritus Zelotypia motus, coram duobus testibus uxorem admonere debuit, ut colloquium viri suspecti vitaret. Sotah. c. 1.
units.tr: So the Sanhedrin always called two disciples of the wise when it summoned a city that had fallen into idolatry to repentance: Maimonides, Avodah Zarah, chapter 4. So too a husband moved by jealousy ought to admonish his wife before two witnesses, that she avoid conversation with a suspect man: Sotah, chapter 1.

units.la: §. Christus iussit,ut indicaretur Ecclesiae, si frater in viam non posset reduci; apud Iudaeos etiam uftatiffimum erat, obstinatos in hac vel illa perverfitate post indultam admonitionem, publico praeconio in Synagoga notare. De hac הכרוה בנית רין publica proclamatione, respectu pastorum minoris pecoris, exactorum,publicanorum agit Bab Sanhed. sol.26.2. Vt& Maymon in אישור cap.12. quando infit.
