Si quis renuit alere liberos suos, arguunt ipsum, pudefaciunt eum, urgent eum: fi adhuc renuit, publice in eum proclamant in Synagoga, dicentes, N. crudelis est, & non vult alere liberos suos, vel ipsis volucribus immundis crudelior.&c. Sic idem ibid. cap.14. recenset, quomodo uxor vexatrix, fi marito molestiam creare sibi proposuerit, primo per nuntios a senatu admonetur, quod fi in mala sua perfliterit intentione, omnem suam perdet dotem,& deinceps,quomodo בכתי עליה בכרזין וכנתי מדרשות כנסיות publicum preconium per quatuor Sabbatha in Synagogis & Medrafchot in eam edant.
units.tr: §. Christ commanded that the matter be told to the Church if the brother could not be brought back to the way. Among the Jews also it was most usual, when people persisted obstinately in this or that wickedness after an admonition had been given, to note them by public proclamation in the synagogue. Of this public proclamation (הכרוה בנית רין [hakhrazah binit din]), with respect to ministers of the lesser flock, tax collectors and publicans, speaks Bab. Sanhedrin, folio 26, column 2; and Maimonides in אישור [isur], chapter 12, where he begins: If anyone refuses to feed his children, they reprove him, shame him and press him. If he still refuses, they make a public proclamation against him in the synagogue, saying, "N. is cruel and does not wish to feed his children, more cruel than the unclean birds themselves," etc. Likewise the same author, ibid., chapter 14, relates how a quarrelsome wife, if she has set out to make trouble for her husband, is first admonished through messengers from the court; and if she persists in her evil intention, she loses her whole dowry; and then how they make a public proclamation for four Sabbaths in the synagogues and houses of study (בכתי עליה בכרזין [bekhetei alah bekhrazin], וכנתי מדרשות כנסיות [ukhnatei midrashot knesiyot]).

units.la: OFFICIARII varii. Nullum tam exiguum ossicium esse, quod non a Deo homini commendetur, docent hoc suo dicto: Etiam ריש גרונתא Praefectus cisternis coelicus constituitur. Bava Bathra sol. 91.2. Erat autem minimum officiolum esse praefectum aequaductis aut cisternis, ut etiam ex his Maymonidis verbis elicitur, quae leguntur in Hal. Melachim cap.1. Non eligunt Regem ex peregrinis, nisi mater ipsius Iudaea sit; nec hoc solum circa regnum observatur, sed etiam circa omnia reliqua munia quae in Israele exercentur. Ita talis non esse potest Dux exercitus, aut Centurio imo nec מטונה על אמת המים Praefectus ille qui aquas in agros distribuit. Habebant enim praecipue in Babylonia cisternas communes ad irrigandos agros. Illis praefecti erant certi homines, qui aquas cuique pro proportione agri sui distribuebant, hodie haustus huic,cras alii concedebatur. Bava Bathra sol. 12.1. Bava Metzia sol.77.1.
units.tr: OFFICIALS of various kinds. They teach, from this saying of theirs, that no office is so small that it is not commended by God to a man: Even the overseer of the cisterns is appointed by heaven. Bava Bathra, folio 91, column 2. The smallest office was thought to be that of overseer of the aqueducts or cisterns, as is also gathered from the words of Maimonides in Hilchot Melachim, chapter 1: They do not choose a king from foreigners unless his mother is a Jewess; nor is this observed only for the kingship, but also for all the other offices exercised in Israel. Thus such a man cannot be commander of an army, or a centurion, nor even מטונה על אמת המים [meshagiah al emat ha-mayim], the overseer who distributes water to the fields. For in Babylonia especially they had common cisterns for irrigating the fields. Over these there were appointed men who distributed water to each according to the proportion of his field: today one was given a draw, tomorrow another. Bava Bathra, folio 12, column 1; Bava Metzia, folio 77, column 1.

units.la: §. Habebant etiam Magnates Iudaeorum Praefectos stabuli, quos אהווירא nominant. Talem habuit Raf, qui ditior erat, quàm Schabhor Rex Persiae. Schabbat sol. 113.2. Metzia sol. 55.1.
units.tr: §. The leading Jews also had overseers of the stable, whom they call אהווירא [ahavira]. Raf had one such, who was richer than Shapur, King of Persia. Shabbat, folio 113, column 2; Metzia, folio 55, column 1.

units.la: §. Praefectus Cursorum vocatur רואר, de eo fit mentio in Schabbat sol. 19.1. Maym. Hal. Schabbat cap. 6. Avoda Zarah sol. 26.1. Bava Kama sol.114.1.
units.tr: §. The overseer of couriers is called רואר [ru'ar]; mention is made of him in Shabbat, folio 19, column 1; Maimonides, Hilchot Shabbat, chapter 6; Avodah Zarah, folio 26, column 1; Bava Kama, folio 114, column 1.

units.la: §. Praetor urbis qui ius dicebat nominatur פטירא Zohar sect. תצות in Fxod. Ita hoc nomine etiam designant custodem urbis & custodem limitum (Germ. Bannwarth) Sanhed. sol. 98.2.
units.tr: §. The city praetor who pronounced judgment is called פטירא [pateira]; Zohar, section Tetzaveh, on Exodus. So they also use this name for the guard of the city and the guard of the boundaries (German Bannwart): Sanhedrin, folio 98, column 2.

units.la: §. Officiarii templi quindecim numero erant.
units.tr: §. There were fifteen officials of the Temple.

units.la: Primus erat ממונה של זמנים Qui debebat observare tempus munera adeundi, & Sacerdotes & alios admonendi,qui proinde etiam clamabat, cùm illud advenerat, O vos Sacerdotes ad cultum vestrum; O vos Levitæ ad loca vestra; O vos Israelitæ ad stationes vestras.
units.tr: The first was the ממונה של זמנים [memunneh shel zemanim], who had to watch for the time of duty and remind the priests and others; so he also cried out, when that time had come: "O you priests, to your service! O you Levites, to your places! O you Israelites, to your posts!"

units.la: Secundus erat 'שערי נעילת על ad aperiendas & claudendas portas; hoc munus præcipuè obtinebat unus ex אברכלין (de quibus vid. in A.) qui etiam cùm portæ aperiebantur, tubâ signum dare curabat. (Vid. Musicam.)
units.tr: The second was the one for 'שערי נעילת על [she'arei ne'ilah], to open and close the gates; this office was held chiefly by one of the אברכלין [avarkhelin] (about whom see under A.), who also, when the gates were opened, took care to give the signal with a trumpet. (See Music.)

units.la: Tertius erat השומרים על Præfectus excubiarum; Vid. Excubias, & Levitas.
units.tr: The third was השומרים על [ha-shomerim al], the prefect of the watches; see Watches and Levites.

units.la: Quartus erat, 'המשררי על Cantor, cuius erat singulis diebus nominare illos, qui tum cantare, cùm instrumentis ludere debebant.
units.tr: The fourth was 'המשררי על [ha-meshorerim al], the Cantor, whose duty was to name each day those who had to sing and those who had to play the instruments.

units.la: Quintus erat præfectus הצלצל illius musices quæ cymbalis siebat. Vid. Musica.
units.tr: The fifth was the prefect of הצלצל [ha-tzaltzal], that kind of music which was made with cymbals. See Music.

units.la: Sextus erat הפיס על Præfectus sortium, vid. Sors.
units.tr: The sixth was הפיס על [ha-pis al], the prefect of the lots; see Lot.

units.la: Septimus 'הקיני המכוכנה על ille qui dedebat providere illis qui se purificare intendebant, de turturibus & columbis.
units.tr: The seventh was הקיני המכוכנה על [ha-kinnei ha-mekhuvanah al], the one who had to provide for those who intended to purify themselves, with turtle-doves and pigeons.

units.la: Octavus erat החותמות על 'המסר Sigillorum custos, cuius munus intelliges ex iis quæ apud Sigillum posuimus.
units.tr: The eighth was החותמות על [ha-hotamot al], the custodian of the seals, whose office you will understand from what we have set out under Seal.

units.la: Nonus erat præfectus הנסכים על circa libamina, qui hæc de quibus modò diximus sigilla recipiebat, & unicuique illa libamina, quæ illius sigillo inscripta erant tradebat.
units.tr: The ninth was the prefect of הנסכים על [ha-nesakhim al], concerning the drink offerings; he received those seals of which we have just spoken and handed to each the drink offerings inscribed with his seal.

units.la: Decimus erat ille, qui sacerdotes ægrotos curabat, qui pluribus morbis, propter continuum carnis esum, vestitum levem, pedes nudos infestabantur.
units.tr: The tenth was the one who looked after the sick priests, who, because of continual eating of flesh, light clothing and bare feet, were afflicted with many diseases.

units.la: Undecimus ille erat, qui de aquis profpiciebat, ut cisternæ, aquæ ductus bene se haberent, ne aquæ templo deessent. Vocatur ille חופר יחיו Fossor puteorum in Schekalim cap.5.1.
units.tr: The eleventh was the one who saw to the waters, that the cisterns and aqueducts were in good order and that the Temple did not lack water. He is called חופר יחיו [chofer yechiv], the digger of wells, in Shekalim, chapter 5, verse 1.

units.la: Duodecimus erat ille qui panes propositiones conficiebat. Vid. f.1. & in Middot cap.1. vocatur עושה הכיתין.
units.tr: Twelfth was the one who prepared the showbread. See f.1, and in Middot ch.1 he is called the one who makes the kittin [עושה הכיתין].

units.la: Decimus tertius qui aromata ad suffitum parabat. Vid. Suffitum.
units.tr: Thirteenth was the one who prepared the spices for the incense. See Suffitum.

units.la: Decimus quartus qui vela confici curabat.
units.tr: Fourteenth was the one who saw to it that the curtains were made.

units.la: Decimus quintus qui Sacerdotum vestimenta custodiebat, & curabat.
units.tr: Fifteenth was the one who guarded and looked after the priests' vestments.

units.la: Vid. Shekalim cap.6. & 5. Maymon in Kele Hamikdasch cap. 7. His omnibus præpositus erat ō סגן Summi Sacerdotis Vicarius. Ibid. c. 4.
units.tr: See Shekalim ch.6 and 5; Maymon in Kele Hamikdasch ch.7. Over all of these was set the deputy [סגן] of the High Priest. Ibid. ch.4.

units.la: §. Officiolum administrare cum aliquo fructu, utilius est, quàm otiosum & famelicum expectare, donec offeratur lautius, hoc exprimunt in fine tractatus Succah, quando dicunt כוצינא טבא סקרא Cucumis præstat Cucurbitâ. In omnibus officiis, observandum vulgatum illud גרמא דנפיל כחלוך גרדיה Os quod cecidit in sorte tua rode illud. Ἐπαῖδεν ἐλαχὺς, κείναν κίτρεσ.
units.tr: §. It is more useful to carry out a small duty with some profit than to sit idle and hungry, waiting until something more lavish is offered. They express this at the end of tractate Succah, where they say: "A good cucumber is better than a gourd" [כוצינא טבא סקרא]. In every duty the common saying should be observed: "Gnaw the bone that has fallen to your lot" [גרמא דנפיל כחלוך גרדיה]. The Greek proverb, hard to read in the scan, runs: [Ἐπαῖδεν ἐλαχὺς, κείναν κίτρεσ].

units.la: OLEUM. Primò de olivis dicamus, deinde de oleo ipso.
units.tr: OIL. First we shall speak of olives, then of the oil itself.

units.la: §. Olæ vocantur שמנונים quando pingues & grahdes olivas ferunt; quando autem tantùm olei dant, ut videantur aliquâ ratione exsiccare proximè adsitas, vocantur בישנים Peah 7. 1. quanquam etiam dici posset, quod sic vocatæ fuerint à loco elegantissimarum olivarum fertilissimo בית שאן (v.f.1. in 2.) abiectâ litera ב, secundùm assuetam dialectum, quâ etiam dicunt ביתר Be-tar, pro Beth tar, quam alii malè ביתר Bitter vocant. Erant quædam olivarum species, quæ certo quodam anni tempore emittebant oleum, & dum ita oleum stillabant, vocarunt illas זית הנוטף. Tempore Imperatoris Adriani, paucæ admodùm olivæ in Iudæa reperiebantur, quia ille fermè omnes exciderat, quod in causa fuit, quod olivarum tunc nulla fuerit שכחה, quod quid fit apud Cl. Buxtorf. in Lex. Talm. reperies. Vid. etiam in lit. S. In festo licet ea circa olivas facere, quæ ad ipsarum conservationem conducunt, reliquis verò debet supersedère donec festum transfierit. Moed Katon cap.2. §.1. Olivas illas quæ ad plenam maturitatem non pervenerant, ponebant in מעין vas oleare, ut mollescerent, alii faciebant foveam, in quam tales olivæ recondebantur.Bab.Metzia f.72.2. Olivas non licet vendere, nisi illi qui est נאמן in puritate; (i.e. de quo non dubitatur, quòd non omni munditiei studeat.) ne forte oleum impurum fiat. Hilleliani existimant, sufficere si emptor נאמן fit, respectu decimationis. De hoc נאמן habes plura apud Decimas.
units.tr: §. Olives are called שמנונים [shemanunim] when they bear plump and large fruit. When they yield so much oil that they seem in some way to dry up the trees growing near them, they are called בישנים [bishanim], Peah 7.1. It could also be said that they were so called from the place of the finest and most fertile olives, בית שאן [Beth Shean] (see f.1 on 2), with the letter ב dropped according to the customary dialect; in the same way they say ביתר [Be-tar] for Beth tar, which others wrongly call Bitter. There were certain kinds of olives which at a certain time of year gave out oil, and because they dripped oil in this way they were called זית הנוטף [zait hannotef, the dripping olive]. In the time of the Emperor Hadrian very few olives were found in Judea, since he had almost all of them cut down; this was the reason there was then no שכחה [shikhah, the forgotten sheaf], which you will find explained in Cl. Buxtorf in his Lexicon Talmudicum. See also under the letter S. On a festival it is permitted to do with olives those things that help preserve them, but other work must be put off until the festival has passed. Moed Katon ch.2 §1. Olives that had not reached full ripeness were put into a מעין [vat for oil] to soften them; others dug a pit in which such olives were stored. Bab. Metzia f.72.2. Olives may not be sold except to one who is נאמן [trustworthy] in puritate, that is, one of whom it is not doubted that he takes every care for cleanness, lest perhaps impure oil results. The Hillelites think it is enough if the buyer is trustworthy with respect to tithing. You will find more on this נאמן under Decimas.

units.la: §. Quodnam optimum terræ Israeliticæ oleum fuerit. Vid. Israelita terra &c. De oleo quod in oblationibus frumentariis adhibebatur Vid. Sacrificia. Triplex habebant oleum; Primum & optimum erat ex olivis maturis sponte fluentibus: alterum ex illarum granis five residuo, leviter expressum: tertium ex immaturioribus & deciduis, idque omnium erat vilissimum, & vocabatur אמפיקינון Omphacinum; Menachot cap.8. hoc oleum hanc habebat vim, ut effluere faceret pilos, & delicatam redderet carnem. Pesachim folio 43. 1. Vajikra Rabba sect. 5.
units.tr: §. As to which oil was the best of the land of Israel, see Israelita terra etc. On the oil used in the grain offerings, see Sacrificia. There were three kinds of oil. The first and best was from ripe olives that flowed out of their own accord; the second was from their seeds or residue, lightly pressed; the third was from less ripe and fallen olives, and this was the cheapest of all and was called אמפיקינון [Omphacinum]; Menachot ch.8. This oil had the power to make hair fall out and to make flesh tender. Pesachim f.43.1. Vajikra Rabba sect. 5.

units.la: §. פרסמון שמן Oleum Balsaminum excellebat inter omnia olea, de eo sic Kimchi ad illud אפרסמון שמן הטוב ואת 2.Reg.20.13 Hoc est oleum Balsaminum, quod non fuit in toto mundo, nisi in Iericho, unde etiam women eius יריח est ab odore eius.
units.tr: §. Balsam oil [פרסמון שמן] excelled among all oils. Of it Kimchi says on 2 Kings 20:13, "the good balsam oil and..." [אפרסמון שמן הטוב ואת]: "This is balsam oil, which was not in the whole world except in Jericho, and so its name, יריח [Yericho], is from its fragrance."

units.la: §. קיק שמן Oleum cicinum, erat cibis foedum, etiam non adhibebatur ad accendendas lucernas Sabbathinas. Schabbat cap.2. in principio.
units.tr: §. Castor oil [קיק שמן] was foul for eating, and was not even used for lighting the Sabbath lamps. Schabbat ch.2 at the beginning.

units.la: §. משחת המשחה שמן Oleum unctionis, erat oleum illud quod conservabatur in Sanctuario: de eo sic Maymon cap.1. Hal.Melach. אין מושחין מלכי ישראל בשמן המשחה אלא בשמן אפרסמון Reges Israelis non unguntur oleo unctionis, sed tantum oleo balsamino; nam nemo oleo unctionis ungi debebat, nisi esset vel ex familia Davidis vel Summus Sacerdos. Vid. Vngere. Modum hoc oleum conficiendi refert Maymon. in Cele Hamikdafch "cap.1. Expressum praeceptum datum est, ut "oleum unctionis conficiatur, quo ea quae ungi "oportebant illiniri possent, secundum illud "Exod.30.18. Moses autem Magister nostER il"lud ita paravit in deserto: accepit Myrrhae, "Cinnamomi, & Casiae, uniusque speciei, quin"gentorum siclorum pondus, & ex Calamo "odorato, ducenta quinquaginta. Postquam "haec separatim in pulverem redegit, omnia "commiscuit, & aquae dulci & purae immersit, "donec omnis aromatum vis extracta fuit. "Deinde infudit olei olivae Hinnem sive duo-
units.tr: §. Anointing oil [משחת המשחה שמן] was the oil that was kept in the Sanctuary. Of it Maymon says in Hal.Melach. ch.1: "The kings of Israel are not anointed with the anointing oil, but only with balsam oil" [אין מושחין מלכי ישראל בשמן המשחה אלא בשמן אפרסמון]; Kings of Israel are not anointed with the anointing oil, but only with balsam oil. For no one was to be anointed with the anointing oil except one of the house of David or the High Priest. See Vngere. Maymon in Cele Hamikdafch ch.1 describes how this oil is made: "An express command was given that the anointing oil should be made, with which the things that were to be anointed could be smeared, according to Exod.30.18. Moses our Teacher prepared it thus in the desert: he took myrrh, cinnamon and cassia, of each species five hundred shekels' weight, and of fragrant calamus two hundred and fifty. After he had reduced these separately to powder, he mixed everything together and steeped it in sweet, pure water until all the virtue of the spices had been drawn out. Then he poured in olive oil, a hin, or twelve

units.la: “decim Logos; (quantùm 72. ova caperent) & “tamdiu igni impositum coxit, donec exhala“verit aqua, & solùm oleum superfuerit. Quod “deinde in vas condidit & reservavit posterita“ti. המור Myrrha הוא הרם כחייה שכהודו Est “sanguis concretus in quodam animali India, quod “omnibus notum est, quia eo mortuos ubique “ungunt; הקנמון (inamomum est illud lignum, “quod ex Insulis Indicis venit, & ob fragran“tiam ad suffitum faciendum adhibetur, הקידה “היא הקושט Casia est radix illa odoratissima, “quam Kost nominant. (alamus odoratus est “arundo illa tenuis, rubris paleis similis, quæ “ex India adsertur, & suavissimi est odoratùs.
units.tr: logs (as much as 72 eggs would hold); and he cooked it over the fire until the water had evaporated and only the oil remained. This he then put into a vessel and kept for posterity. Myrrha [המור] is the thick blood of a certain animal in India, Est sanguis concretus in quodam animali India, which everyone knows, since they anoint the dead with it everywhere. Cinnamomum [הקנמון] is that wood which comes from the Indian islands and is used for incense because of its fragrance. Casia [הקידה] is the most fragrant root, which is called Kost [הקושט]. Calamus odoratus is that slender reed like red chaff, brought from India, and it has the sweetest smell.

units.la: §. Oleum adhibebant in Medicinis pro ægrotis. Vid.Ægroiuin & Sabbathum. De olco ex צלוליבא confecto vid. Kimchi in Ionam.4.6.
units.tr: §. Oil was used in medicines for the sick. See Aegrotum and Sabbathum. On the oil made from צלוליבא [tzelulivah], see Kimchi on Jonah 4:6.

units.la: §. Olivetus mons vocatur à Iudæis הר הזיתים & הר הוחשה quæ ambo nomina ipsi ab olivis data sunt, non quòd non alii etiam fructus ibi essent, (in una enim eius parte erat tractus Bethphage,cuius nomen à ficuum grossis derivatum ; & insuper secundùm Hieros. Taanith sol. 69. 1. in illo duo immensæ magnitudinis cedri fuerunt.) sed quòd olivarum maior numerus & fructus dignior. Targum Cant.8. 1. dicit, Cùm revivificent mortui dirumpendus est mons Olivetus, atque omnes mortui Israelis inde exibunt &c. In hoc monte comburebatur à Sacerdote vacca rufa. Middot c 1. v. 3. Parah c. 3.9. Item flammæ signales in vertice illius, ad signum iam statæ Neomeniæ, agitabantur, Rofch Hafchana cap.2.2.3. Vid.Messiam. Vbi collocandus fit Mons Olivetus in Mappis vid. Mappas.
units.tr: §. The Mount of Olives is called by the Jews הר הזיתים [Har HaZeitim] and הר המשחה [Har HaMashchah], both names given to it from the olives. This is not because there were no other fruits there (for in one part of it was the district of Bethphage, whose name is derived from the unripe figs; and moreover, according to Hieros. Taanith f.69.1, there were two cedars of immense size on it), but because the olives were more numerous and of worthier fruit. The Targum on Cant.8.1 says: "When the dead are revived, the Mount of Olives must be split, and all the dead of Israel will come forth from it," etc. On this mount the red heifer was burned by the priest. Middot ch.1 v.3; Parah ch.3.9. Likewise, signal flames were waved on its summit to announce the New Moon, once it had been fixed; Rosh Hashanah ch.2.2.3. See Messiam. For where the Mount of Olives should be placed on maps, see Mappas.

units.la: ONO urbs. Vid. יָנוֹחַ.
units.tr: ONO, a city. See יָנוֹחַ [Yanoach].

units.la: ONIAS fil. Simeonis Iusti, erat testamento & ultimâ Patris voluntate ad summum Sacerdotium dominatus, sed invidit hoc ei Simeon frater eius, & ita incruduit contentio, ut Onias tandem ad montem Regium, & deinde in Ægyptum fugeret, ubi condidit Sanctuarium, recitans illud Prophetæ. In die illo erit altare Domini in medio Ægypti. Vid. Iuchasin pag.15. Hieros. Ioma sol.43. An Ecclesia Alexandrina commune Iudæorum in persequutionibus Asylum, ab illo iustituta fuerit, vel aucta; ita definiri non potest. Vid. Alexandriam.
units.tr: ONIAS, son of Simeon the Just. By his father's will and final wish he was entitled to the high priesthood, but his brother Simeon envied him this, and the dispute grew so bitter that Onias at last fled to the royal mountain and then to Egypt, where he founded a sanctuary, citing the prophet: "In that day there shall be an altar to the Lord in the midst of Egypt" (Isa. 19:19). See Iuchasin p.15; Hieros. Ioma f.43. Whether the Alexandrian congregation, as a common refuge for the Jews in persecutions, was founded by him or only enlarged by him, cannot be determined. See Alexandriam.

units.la: §. De Onia חוֹנִי Hammagal הַמַּגָּל refert Iuchasin pag.17. ipsum per 70. annos dormivisse. Et ipsum interfectum esse in illo bello, quod Hyrcanus & Aristobulus fratres sibi invicem intulerunt. De illo historiam habes in Massec. Taanit cap.3. v.8.
units.tr: §. Concerning Onias, Choni the Hammagal [חוֹנִי הַמַּגָּל], Iuchasin p.17 reports that he slept for seventy years, and that he himself was killed in that war which the brothers Hyrcanus and Aristobulus waged against each other. You have his story in Massec. Taanit ch.3 v.8.

units.la: ONKELOS vocatur ut plurimùm הַגֵּר proselytus. de eius versione legis vid. Hottingeri Thesaurum & Leusdenii Philologum. Rabban Gamalielem senem, tali honore & amore prosequutus est, ut cùm eo defuncto suppellex eius ordinario ritu, paucis solùm aromatibus comburi deberet, largos adhibuerit sumptus, ad ipsam honorificentiùs cremandam. Dicunt in Avoda Zarah p. 11. & Tosaphot. Schabb. cap.7. ipsum ultra 80. Minas Tyrias in bustum profusisse.
units.tr: ONKELOS is usually called הַגֵּר [ha-ger], the proselyte. On his version of the Law see Hottinger's Thesaurus and Leusden's Philologus. He showed such honour and affection to the aged Rabban Gamaliel that, when at his death his household goods were to be burned according to the usual rite with only a few spices, he spent large sums to have them burned with greater honour. They say in Avoda Zarah p.11 and Tosaphot. Schabb. ch.7 that he himself poured more than 80 Tyrian minas into the funeral pyre.

units.la: §. De Vnkelo disputatur an idem fit cùm Talmudicorum עֻקְלוֹס, quo etiam Græcum Paraphrasten denotarunt. Vid. Drufium in Ep.41. Meor Enaim cap. 45. Schikkard. in BechinatHapperufchim Disp.2. Certè in Hierof. Demai sol.25.4. Onkelos intelligitur, quando sic inquiunt; Onkelos Proselytus divisit haereditatem cum fratre suo gentili, atque usum srutium eius abdicavit ad mare salsum.
units.tr: §. Some dispute whether Onkelos is the same person as the Talmudists' עֻקְלוֹס [Ukelos], which they also used to denote the Greek paraphrast. See Drusius on Ep. 41; Meor Enaim ch. 45; Schickard in Bechinat Happerufchim, Disp. 2. Certainly in Hierosolymitan Demai fol. 25.4 Onkelos is meant where they say: Onkelos the proselyte divided the inheritance with his gentile brother, and renounced the dried fruit of his [property] to the salt sea.

units.la: Orare Vid. Preces.
units.tr: Praying. See Prayers.

units.la: Operariis licet de illis edere in quibus laborant; In vindemia possunt edere uvas; In collestione ficuum ficus, In messe spicas; imò Operario in istis rebus operanti, licet edere peponem valentem Denarium (Ein halb orth eines Reichsthalers) & dactylos valentes Denarium. Bava Metzia sol.83.1. Sic operamini cibo permanenti in vitam aeternam, qui est Christus, & de Christo edetis.
units.tr: Workers may eat from what they labour on: at the vintage they may eat grapes, at the gathering of figs they may eat figs, at the harvest they may eat ears of grain. Indeed, a worker engaged in such things may eat a melon worth a denarius (half an orth of a Reichsthaler) and dates worth a denarius. Bava Metzia fol. 83.1. So you labour for the food that endures to eternal life, which is Christ, and you will eat of Christ.

units.la: §. In conducendis operariis valuit plurimùm mos loci, hinc illud circa operarios axioma in Bab. Bava Metzia sol.11.2. Observa morem vbi. Hoc etiam probatur exemplo desumpto ex Hierof. Metzia sol.11 2. Tiberienses ascendentes in Beth-Meonem, locum vicinum, non aliter conducebantur, quàm secundùm morem Beth-Meonis, & è contra Beth-Meonenses inTiberiade, non aliter conducebantur, quàm pro more Tiberiensium. In Parabola de Operariis Matth.20. dicit Dominus respiciens morem loci, Quodcunque iustum fuerit dabo vobis. Reliquum quod est in v.13. Οὐχὶ δηνάριϊ συνφωνήσας μοι dilucidatur ex Canone Majmon, in cap.9. Dicit Paterfamilias servo, Ito, conduc mihi servos quatuor denarius, & conducit eos tribus; quamvis labor eorum mereatur quatuor denarios, non reddentur tamen iis nisi tres, eo quod ex compacto hoc in se susceperunt, & יגיעומיס תרעומת iis est adversus servum.
units.tr: §. In hiring workers, the custom of the place counted for much; hence that saying about workers in Babylonian Bava Metzia fol. 11.2: Observe the custom where you are. This is also shown by an example from Jerusalem Metzia fol. 11.2: The Tiberians who went up to Beth-Meon, a neighbouring place, were hired only according to the custom of Beth-Meon, and conversely the Beth-Meonites in Tiberias were hired only according to the custom of the Tiberians. In the parable of the workers, Matthew 20, the Lord, looking to the custom of the place, says: Whatever is just I will give you. The rest, in v. 13, Did you not agree with me for a denarius? [Οὐχὶ δηνάριϊ συνφωνήσας μοι], is explained by the Canon of Maimonides, ch. 9: The householder says to his servant, Go, hire me four workers for a denarius; and he hires three. Although their labour deserves four denarii, they will be given only three, because they accepted this by the agreement they made, and their complaint [יגיעומיס תרעומת] is against the servant.

units.la: §. De conducendis operariis prolixè Maymonides loco modò cit. Distinguunt etiam Canones Hæbræorum inter יום שכיר Conductum in diem, & שעור שכיר & Conductum in horas quasdam eadem ratione ac parabola Christi: quam imitati sunt in Bera Acot Talmud. Hierosol.sol.5.3. quando inquiunt. Cuinam fuit R. Bon Bar Chaia similis? Regi שכר פועלי qui conduxit operarios multos, inter quos fuit unus conductus, qui opus suum praestitit extraordinarie. Quid facit Rex, cum secum duxit, & cum eo ambulavit hinc illinc. עיר לעיתותי ... venerunt operarii isti, ... ... de-ditq; isti mercedem completam cum iis. והיו nos laboravimus per totum diem, hic autem non nisi per duas horas, & data est ei merces aequalis nostra: dixit iis Rex, plus ille laboravit unâ horâ, quàm vos totâ die. Sic plus legi incubuit R. Bon; annis viginti octo, quàm alius annus centum.
units.tr: §. On hiring workers, Maimonides in the place just cited is full. The Hebrew canons also distinguish between a hire by the day [יום שכיר] and a hire for certain hours [שעור שכיר], on the same principle as Christ's parable. They imitated it in Jerusalem Talmud, Bera Acot, fol. 5.3, where they say: To whom was R. Bon bar Chaia like? To a king who hired many workers [שכר פועלי], among whom was one hired man who performed his work extraordinarily. What did the king do? He took him with him and walked with him here and there. [עיר לעיתותי] ... these workers came, ... and he gave them their full wage with them. And [והיו] we laboured the whole day, but this man only two hours, and he is given a wage equal to ours. The king said to them: He laboured one hour more than you did the whole day. So R. Bon applied himself to the Law more in twenty-eight years than another did in a hundred.

units.la: §. Operarii suum opus incipiunt ab exortu solis, hinc etiam conducebantur; ante ortum solis ad laborem nunquam egressi sunt. Vid. Gloss. in Bab.Bava Metzia sol. 83.a.
units.tr: §. Workers begin their work at sunrise, and so they were hired; they never went out to labour before sunrise. See the Gloss on Babylonian Bava Metzia fol. 83.a.

units.la: §. De mercede operantis addamus Maymonidis in שכיורות cap.11. E præcepto legis affirmativis est, ut detur merces operario conducto
units.tr: §. On the wage of the worker, let us add Maimonides in Sechirut, ch. 11: By an affirmative precept of the Law, the wage must be given to the hired worker.

units.la: E e Editio tempore suo; sicut dicetur, In die suo dabis ei mercedem suam: Si verò detineatur post tempus suum, peccatur in præceptum negativum; sicut dicitur: Non occidet sol super eum.
units.tr: It is to be paid at its own time, as it is said: On his day you shall give him his wage. But if it is withheld beyond its time, one transgresses a negative precept, as it is said: The sun shall not go down upon him.

units.la: Opificium aliquod pater filium docere debet.
units.tr: A father ought to teach his son some craft.

units.la: Tosapht. in Kidduschin cap. 1. Patri incumbit circuncidere filium, redimere eum, docere eum legem, & docere eum aliquod opificium: R. Iudah dicit, quicunque filium suum non docet aliquod opificium, est ac si doceret eum latrocinium. De opificiis plura habes in Kidduschin cap. 4. in v. undecimo hoc dicitur R. Meir dicit, Det semper homo operam ut doceat filium suum אומנות נקייא Artem honestam. Talia inter suos recepta axiomata considerans Iosephus, Christum in arte sua tectonica, educavit & instruxit.
units.tr: Tosefta, Kiddushin ch. 1: It is incumbent on the father to circumcise his son, to redeem him, to teach him the Law, and to teach him some craft. R. Judah says: whoever does not teach his son some craft is as if he taught him robbery. You will find more on crafts in Kiddushin ch. 4; in the eleventh verse it is said: R. Meir says: let a man always take pains to teach his son an honest craft [אומנות נקייא]. Considering such maxims as were received among his own people, Joseph educated and instructed Christ in his craft as a carpenter.

units.la: §. Non docebit homo filium suum artificium aliquod inter mulieres: quia conversatio ipsarum prava est. Nunquam doceat homo filium suum, ut sit mulorum vel camelorum ductor, tonsor, nauta, pastor, hospes שאומנתם אומנות ליסשים quod opificium ipsorum sit opificium latronum. His addunt etiam Medicos & Laniones. Vid. Bab. Kidduschin sol.82.1. Hierof. Kidduschin sol.66.
units.tr: §. A man shall not teach his son a craft among women, because their conversation is depraved. A man should never teach his son to be a driver of mules or camels, a barber, a sailor, a shepherd, or an innkeeper, because their craft is the craft of robbers [שאומנתם אומנות ליסשים]. To these they also add physicians and butchers. See Babylonian Kiddushin fol. 82.1; Jerusalem Kiddushin fol. 66.

units.la: 2. Vbi etiam hoc legitur: Beatus ille qui videt natos suos, באומנות מעולה in opificio honesto; & Infelix ille qui eos videt in opificio פגומה sordido. Sicuti enim dicunt in Nedarim sol.49.2. Magnum est illud opificium שמכבדת ומחמת בעליה quod honorat & calefacit dominos suos.
units.tr: 2. Here too this is read: Blessed is he who sees his sons in a noble craft [באומנות מעולה], in an honest trade; and Unhappy is he who sees them in a sordid [פגומה] trade. For, as they say in Nedarim fol. 49.2: That is a great craft which honours and warms its masters [שמכבדת ומחמת בעליה].

units.la: §. Multi ex Sapientibus Israelis היו בעלי כלאכה artifices fuerunt, & artem aliquam exercuerunt, ne opus habèrent donaria accipere ab hominibus, & ex fifco Ecclefiaftico ali. Vid. Abarbenel in Abbot fol. 35. 1. Drufium Aftor. 18.
units.tr: §. Many of the wise men of Israel were artisans [היו בעלי כלאכה] and practised some craft, so that they should not need to accept gifts from men, nor be supported from the ecclesiastical treasury. See Abarbanel on Avot fol. 35.1; Drusius on Acts 18.

units.la: Osculum. Ofculari genua olim in ufu fuit, Vid. Genuflexio; item Hierof. Chagiga fol. 77. 1. Nedarim 36. 4. Megillah 14. 1. De pede ofculando reverentiæ causa vid. Hierof. Kiddufchin fol. 61. 3. Ofculatio omnis eft ad fatuitatem exceptis tribus. 1. נשיקה של גדולה Ofculo magnificentiæ. 1. Sam. 10. 1. 2. נשיקה של פרקים Ofculo Compitorum Exod. 4. 27. 3. נשיקה של פרישות Ofculo feparationis. Ruth. 1. 14 Berefch. Rabba fect. 17. His addit R. Tanchuma ofculum propinquitatis. Gen. 29. 11.
units.tr: Kiss. Kissing the knees was once in use; see Genuflexion. Likewise Jerusalem Chagigah fol. 77.1; Nedarim 36.4; Megillah 14.1. On kissing the foot out of reverence, see Jerusalem Kiddushin fol. 61.3. Every kiss tends to foolishness, except three kinds: 1. a kiss of greatness [נשיקה של גדולה], 1 Samuel 10.1; 2. a kiss of meeting [נשיקה של פרקים], Exodus 4.27; 3. a kiss of separation [נשיקה של פרישות], Ruth 1.14; Bereshit Rabbah sect. 17. To these R. Tanchuma adds the kiss of kinship, Genesis 29.11.

units.la: §. Ofculatio capitis in ufu erat, cùm alicui oftendere volebant, ipfius actiones non parùm placuiffe, fe ipfum non parum æftimare: exempla quæ ad manus funt affremus.
units.tr: §. Kissing the head was in use when they wished to show someone that his actions had pleased them, and that they esteemed him not a little. I shall add examples that are at hand.

units.la: Hierof. Chagigah fol. 77. 1. Eliefer Ben Erech veniam impetravit à Rabban Iochanan Bén Saccai ut de nonnullis coram eo differeret: differuit de מעשה מרכבה (Ezech. cap. 1.) cùm finiiffet exfurrexit Rabban Iochanan ונשקיה בראשיו & Caput eius ofculatus eft.
units.tr: Jerusalem Chagigah fol. 77.1: Eliezer ben Arach obtained leave from Rabban Johanan ben Zakkai to speak about certain matters in his presence. He spoke about the work of the chariot [מעשה מרכבה] (Ezekiel ch. 1). When he had finished, Rabban Johanan rose and kissed his head [ונשקיה בראשיו].

units.la: Idem Horajoth fol. 48. 3. Cum R. Levi finiiffet differere, exfurrexit R Abba atque caput eius eft ofculatus.
units.tr: The same, Horayot fol. 48.3: When R. Levi had finished speaking, R. Abba rose and kissed his head.

units.la: Idem Nedarim fol. 36. 4. legitur hiftoria de quodam iuvene, qui in refponfione fua ita complacuit Simeoni Iufto, vt eum amplexus fit atq; caput eius exofculatus.
units.tr: The same, Nedarim fol. 36.4, contains the story of a certain young man who so pleased Simeon the Just by his answer that he embraced him and kissed his head.

units.la: Bab. Megillah fol. 14. 1. dicitur: Miriam prophetaffe matrem fuam parituram illium, qui Ifraelem liberaturus effet. Cum foret natus Moses, profitit pater eius ונשקה על ראשה Atque eam exosculata est super caput ; dicens adimpleta est prophetia tua. Ex quibus patet, non fuisse inusitatum Magistris suos discipulos osculari : At non ita fuisse in more ut discipulus magistrum oscularetur, saltem ad caput : sed osculari ad genua quia maiorem humilitatem præ se tulit, magis licuit. Videtur itaque Iudæ proditoris osculum quô Christum καταφίλησεν excepit, non tam ex prætextu officii, quam aperta derisione & contemptu fuisse.
units.tr: Babylonian Megillah fol. 14.1 says that Miriam prophesied that her mother would bear the one who was to deliver Israel. When Moses was born, his father rose and [ונשקה על ראשה] kissed her on the head, saying: your prophecy is fulfilled. From these things it is clear that it was not unusual for teachers to kiss their disciples; but it was not the custom for a disciple to kiss his teacher, at least on the head. Kissing at the knees, since it displayed greater humility, was more permissible. It seems, therefore, that the kiss by which Judas the traitor kissed warmly [καταφίλησεν] Christ was not so much a matter of the pretext of his office as an open mockery and contempt.

units.la: OVES. Distinguunt in oves חריפות primores quæ mense Februario nascuntur, & validiores sunt, & in oves אפליתא Serotinas, quæ in Martio proveniunt & imbecilliores sunt. Rosch Haschana sol. 8.
units.tr: SHEEP. They distinguish among sheep the early [חריפות] ones, which are born in the month of February and are stronger, and the late [אפליתא] ones, which appear in March and are weaker. Rosh Hashanah fol. 8.

units.la: In Ægypto habebant oves , quibus erant caudæ magnæ & graves, proinde ipsis conficiebant plaustra parva, ut illis sustinerentur, ne in terra attererentur & exulcerarentur : talibus plaustris oves in Sabbatho egredi non poterant. Maymon in Schabbat sol. 54. 2.
units.tr: In Egypt they had sheep whose tails were large and heavy; therefore they made small carts for them, so that the tails would be supported and not dragged on the ground and chafed. Sheep of this kind could not go out on the Sabbath in such carts. Maimonides in Shabbat fol. 54.2.

units.la: §. De ovibus quæ apud Talmudicos ואת בּרוּך nominantur vid. Cl. Buxt. Lex. Talm. p. 1879. de agnorum decimatione Vid. Decimas. Caula ovium Talmudicis est דיר Becoreth sol. 58.2. כונסין לדיר Congregant gregem in ovile. Erat autem solùm septum aliquod in quo congregabantur oves noctu ne vagarentur, & ut incolumes essent à furibus & feris. Mulgebantur etiam interdiu ut sonat illud Iliad. δ.
units.tr: On sheep, which the Talmudists call [ואת בּרוּך], see Cl. Buxt. Lex. Talm. p. 1879. On the tithing of lambs, see Decimas. The sheepfold among the Talmudists is [דיר] Becoreth, sol. 58.2, where [כונסין לדיר] means they gather the flock into the fold. It was simply an enclosure in which the sheep were gathered at night, so that they would not wander and would be safe from thieves and wild beasts. They were also milked by day, as the line of the Iliad δ suggests:

units.la: Τράεc δ' ὤςε οἷςε πολυπαμμονῳ- ἀνδρὸς ὧ ἀυλὰ Μυρίαι ἰςηκαζιν ἀμελγομέναι γάλα λεύκον.
units.tr: "Three times as many flocks of a rich man's sheep stand milking white milk." [Τράεc δ' ὤςε οἷςε πολυπαμμονῳ- ἀνδρὸς ὧ ἀυλὰ Μυρίαι ἰςηκαζιν ἀμελγομέναι γάλα λεύκον.]

units.la: §. Locum Misna in Rosch Haschana cap. I.
units.tr: A passage of the Mishnah in Rosh Hashanah, chap. 1.

units.la: de בני מרון Cl. Buxt. de ovibus in decimatione peͤdetentim, ex caula & porta parva egredientibus intelligit; Gemara vero sol. 16. 1. de מעלות בית מרון Vid. Beth Maron in B.
units.tr: Buxtorf takes the "sons of Maron" [בני מרון] to be sheep that go out on foot from the fold and the small gate for tithing. The Gemara, however, at sol. 16.1, speaks of the ascents of Beth Maron [מעלות בית מרון]. See Beth Maron in B.

units.la: P.
units.tr: P.

units.la: PALMÆ & rami salicum in usu erant, in festo Tabernaculorum vid. suo loco. in F.
units.tr: Palms and willow branches were in use at the Feast of Tabernacles; see suo loco under F.

units.la: Panis non raro apud scriptores Iudaicos sumitur pro doctrina. Chagigah sol. 14. 1. כל משען לחם Omne fulcimentum panis, Esai. iii. 1. אלו בעלי תלמוד Hi sunt Magistri Doctrinae: sicut dicitur, venite & comedite de pane meo. Prov. ix. 5. Gloss. in Succah f. 52. האכילו לחם Ciba eum pane; i. e. fac eum laborare in lege, sicut dicitur, venite, comedite, de pane meo. Moses pavit doctrina & Manna, Christus fideles pane coelesti, doctrina & Carne sua.
units.tr: Among Jewish writers, bread is often taken to mean teaching. Chagigah, sol. 14.1: [כל משען לחם], "every stay of bread" (Isa. 3.1). [אלו בעלי תלמוד], "These are the masters of doctrine, as it is said, come and eat of my bread" (Prov. 9.5). The Gloss. on Succah, f. 52: [האכילו לחם], "Feed him with bread; that is, make him labour in the law, as it is said, come, eat of my bread." Moses fed the people with doctrine and manna; Christ feeds the faithful with heavenly bread, that is, with doctrine and his flesh.

units.la: §. Mulieres Iudaeae coctura panem, decerpunt a Massa particulam instar ovi, aut plus minusve, Eam particulam vocant חלה Challa, & projiciunt in furnum, ac comburunt igne. Quandoque reservant & tempore oborti incendii inscribunt ei certas litteras, vocabula angelorum, & notas superstitiosas. Eã in ignem proiectã, credunt extingui incendium. De hoc integer exstat tractatus Talmudicus, qui vocatur חלה.
units.tr: Jewish women, when they bake bread, pinch off from the dough a piece about the size of an egg, or more or less. They call this piece [חלה] Challa and throw it into the oven and burn it in the fire. Sometimes they keep it, and when a fire breaks out they mark it with certain letters, the names of angels, and superstitious signs. When it is thrown into the fire, they believe the blaze will be put out. A whole Talmudic tractate on this exists, called [חלה].

units.la: §. Panes propositionis pinsuntur vel in atrio, vel in Bethphage; duo singulis diebus a Summo Sacerdote offerebantur. Panes propositionis, habuerunt tres ססמו formae (ʃʃtoʃ Dell Germ. vel simpliciter סיעף Scutellas) in altera imponebantur cùm conficiebantur, In altera cùm coquebantur, In tertia cùm ex furno eduſebantur. Menachot c. ii. v. i. 2. in Maym. Com. S‐mel duo panes (propositionis) affſrebantur ex סוכר עין loco fatis ab Hierosolymis remoto, cùm ordinariè vel ab ipsa urbe vel ex locis vicinis asportabantur. Sed illo tempore circa Hierosolymam hostes omnia devaftarunt. Mena hot cap.10.
units.tr: The showbread was ground either in the court or in Bethphage; two loaves were offered every day by the High Priest. The showbread had three forms (dishes, or simply scutellas): one was used for placing the dough when it was made, one when it was baked, and one when it was taken out of the oven. Menachot ch. 2, v. 1–2, in the Maym. Com. Once the two loaves of showbread were fetched from a place [סוכר עין] far from Jerusalem, whereas ordinarily they were carried from the city itself or from nearby places. But at that time the enemies laid waste everything around Jerusalem. Menachot ch. 10.

units.la: §. De panum propositionis patinis vid. Maymon in Ha'.Beth Habech.cap 2. sub finem. De duodecim panibus propositionis vid. Sacrisi ia. & Templum.
units.tr: On the dishes of the showbread, see Maimonides in Ha' Beth Habech, chap. 2, near the end. On the twelve loaves of showbread, see Sacrificia and Templum.

units.la: PARADISUS פרדס ja. De eo sic loquitur R. Lachifch in Bab.Erubhin sol.19.1. Si Paradisus fit in terra Ifraelitica, Beth Schean est ostium eius (Gloff. fructus Beth Scheanenfes fuerunt pulcherrimi) Si in Arabia, Beth Geram est ostium eius; fi inter fluvios Damascus.
units.tr: PARADISE [פרדס]. R. Lachisch speaks of it thus in the Babylonian Erubhin, sol. 19.1: "If Paradise is in the land of Israel, Beth Shean is its door (the Gloss says the fruits of Beth Shean were most beautiful). If it is in Arabia, Beth Geram is its door; if it is between the rivers, Damascus."

units.la: PARADISUS collocatur à Cl.Heidegg.Exerc. iv.42. in eo terrae sanctae tractu, qui regionem & locum Gennesar, quem Mare Tiberiadis (V. f.1.) nominant, campum magnum, convallem illustrem, vallem Ierichuntinam, mare denique mortuum sive Sodomiticam regionem complectitur; quam suam sententiam novem argumentis, dodiffime ut omnia, probat. Decem cum corpore & anima ingressi sunt paradisum, inter quos Elias & Enochus. Menasse Ben Israel de fragilit. Human. fect. xii. 7. ex Medrasch & Kimchi ii.Reg ii.1.
units.tr: PARADISE is placed by Cl. Heidegg, Exerc. iv.42, in that tract of the Holy Land which takes in the region and place of Gennesar, which they call the Sea of Tiberias (V. f. 1), the great plain, the famous valley, the valley of Jericho, and finally the Dead Sea or the Sodomitic region. He proves this opinion with nine arguments, most learnedly as always. Ten entered Paradise alive, body and soul, among them Elijah and Enoch. Menasseh Ben Israel, De fragilitate humana, sect. xii.7, from the Medrash and Kimchi on 2 Kings 2.1.

units.la: PARABOLA. Iudaicae oratoriae nullum Schema familiarius Parabolismo; ille qui in eo genere præcipuè excelluit erat Rabbi Meir de quo dicunt in Sotah cap.9. משמת ר' מאיר נישלו משלים משלים Ex quo cessavit R. Meir cessa-unt Parabolyzantes. Non quasi illis flosculis non amplius usi sint, sed quia nullus amplius fuit qui in illis ita excelleret ut fecit R. Meir de quo dicit Gloss. in Sanhed. q od tertia pars orationum eius erat traditio,tertia pars allegoria,& tertia pars Parabolismus.
units.tr: PARABLE. No figure of Jewish oratory is more familiar than the parable. The one who excelled especially in this kind was Rabbi Meir, of whom they say in Sotah ch. 9: [משמת ר' מאיר נישלו משלים], "From the time R. Meir died, the parable-makers ceased." This does not mean they no longer used those flowers of speech, but that there was no longer anyone who excelled in them as R. Meir did. Of him the Gloss on Sanhedrin says that a third part of his discourses was tradition, a third allegory, and a third parable.

units.la: PARASCEVE vid. Sabbatum.
units.tr: PARASCEVE: see Sabbatum.

units.la: PARENTES quid infantibus debeant, vid. Infantes, & Opificium, qui parentes suos ita pulsaverit, ut livorem illis effecerit, strangulari debet. Hoc gravius est in eo qui maledixit, quàm qui pulsat: quòd qui execratur illos, post funera, reus fit, qui verò eos mortuos ferit, haud tenetur. Sanhed. cap.10.1.
units.tr: PARENTS: for what children owe their parents, see Infantes and Opificium. One who has struck his parents so as to leave a bruise on them must be strangled. It is more serious in one who curses than in one who strikes, because one who curses them is guilty after their death, whereas one who strikes them when they are dead is not liable. Sanhedrin ch. 10.1.

units.la: §. De casu illo, an mater salvâ conscientiâ possit embryonis mortem poculis vel alio modo promovere, si sentiat se aliter non posse in vivis manère, sic ratiocinantur Maymon. in Hal. Rozeach cap. 1. Mulier gravida, qua in partu ob enitendi difficultatem periclitatur, embryonem in suis visceribus interficere potest, vel veneno vel manu sua, quia embryo est instar persequutoris ad occidendam eam: ( qualem etiam adstantibus interficere licet, si oppressum & persequutum ab ipso aliter liberare non possunt.) Postquàm autem infans prodiit caput suum, ipsi amplius nocere non possunt שאין רוחין נפש מפני נפש quia non pellunt animam propter animam. (i. e. non licet matrem iuvare morte infantis, cùm spes est illam facilè liberari posse, ut est dum infans iam aliquas ex suis partibus exeruit.)
units.tr: On the case whether a mother may, with a clear conscience, bring about the death of the embryo by drinks or some other means, if she feels that otherwise she cannot remain alive, Maimonides reasons thus in Hal. Rozeach ch. 1: "A pregnant woman who is in danger in labour because of the difficulty of bearing down may kill the embryo in her womb, either with poison or by her own hand, because the embryo is like a pursuer intent on killing her" (just as bystanders may kill one who, if they cannot otherwise free the person oppressed and pursued by him). "But after the infant has come forth with its head, they can no longer harm her, for [one does not push aside a soul for the sake of a soul]." That is, it is not lawful to help the mother by the death of the infant, since there is hope she can easily be freed, as is the case while the infant has put forth some of its parts.

units.la: §. De officio infantum erga parentes, sonat Tosaphta in Kiddufchin cap. 1. filium tenetur ad cibandum patrem, ad potandum, vestiendum, tegendum, inducendum & educendum, & ad lavandum eius faciem; manus & pedes. Et Hierof. Kiddufchin sol.61.2.3. Tenetur filius patrem nutrire,imo pro eo mendicare. Intempestivum zelum arguit ille Canon Maymonidis in Gezelah cap.12. Vilipendendum esse patrem, pro Rabbino legem nos docente. Satis enim natura infantes inclinant ad reverentiam parentum excutiendam, licèt talibus monitis ipsis prætextum nullum suppeditaretur.
units.tr: On the duty of children towards their parents, the Tosaphta in Kiddufchin ch. 1 says: "A son is bound to feed his father, to give him drink, to clothe, cover, bring in and take out, and to wash his face, hands and feet." And the Jerusalem Kiddufchin, sol. 61.2.3: "A son is bound to nourish his father; indeed, to beg for him." That canon of Maimonides in Gezelah ch. 12 condemns untimely zeal: "The father is to be despised, on the authority of a rabbi who teaches us the law." For nature already inclines children enough to cast off reverence for their parents, even though no pretext would be supplied to them by such warnings.

units.la: Parsa vid. Mensurationes.
units.tr: Parsa: see Mensurationes.

units.la: Pascha in illo tria potissimùm sunt. agnus indicans Deum transiliisse ædes Israelitarum, trucidatis Ægyptiorum primogenitis. Amaram indicans Israelitarum in Ægypto servitutem, azymum, indicans Israelitarum liberationem divinam. Buxt.Cosri 250.252.
units.tr: In the Passover there are three things of chief importance: the lamb, showing that God passed over the houses of the Israelites when he struck down the firstborn of the Egyptians; the bitter herb [Amaram], showing the Israelites' servitude in Egypt; the unleavened bread [azymum], showing the divine deliverance of the Israelites. Buxt. Cosri 250–252.

units.la: §. De Paschate notabimus præcipua quæ in hanc materiam faciunt, omnia enim referre magni laboris esset.
units.tr: On the Passover we shall note the chief points that bear on this subject, for to report everything would be a great labour.

units.la: §. Tempore Salvatoris nostri, Pascha non ampliùs omnibus illis ritibus celebrabant, quibus celebrabatur ab initio; differentiam discimus ex Tosaphta in Pefachim cap.8.
units.tr: In the time of our Saviour, the Passover was no longer celebrated with all those rites with which it was celebrated from the beginning. We learn the difference from the Tosaphta in Pefachim ch. 8.

units.la: Pascha in Ægypto separabatur à grege die decimo, & mactabatur die 14. Nec pro Paschate incurrebant in poenam excidii, sicuti ti incurrebant in generationibus sequentibus.
units.tr: In Egypt the Passover lamb was separated from the flock on the tenth day and slaughtered on the fourteenth. Nor did those who failed to keep the Passover incur the penalty of excision, as they did in later generations.

units.la: De Pafchate in Ægypto dicitur, fumat ille & vicinus eius proximus agnum: quod locum non habuit in pafchatibus sequentibus.
units.tr: Of the Passover in Egypt it is said, "let him and his nearest neighbour take a lamb"; this did not apply to the Passovers that followed.

units.la: Pascha in Ægypto non annexam habuit sanguinis sparsionem, & adipis positionem in altari. Aliterautem res se habuit in temporibus posterioribus.
units.tr: In Egypt the Passover had no attached sprinkling of blood or placing of fat on the altar. It was otherwise in later times.

units.la: In posterioribus Pafchatibus non rigidè observabant aspersionem postium & liminum sanguine.
units.tr: In later Passovers they did not rigidly observe the sprinkling of the doorposts and lintels with blood.

units.la: De Pafchate in Ægypto dicitur, ne egrediemini domibus vestris usque ad mane. At non ita erat in sequentibus.
units.tr: Of the Passover in Egypt it is said, "you shall not go out of your houses until morning." But it was not so in the following Passovers.

units.la: Pascha in Ægypto unusquisque macabat paterfamilias; sed deinde omnes Israelitæ illud macabant in loco uno.
units.tr: In Egypt each head of a household slaughtered the Passover; but afterwards all the Israelites slaughtered it in one place.

units.la: Olim ubi comedebant Pascha, ibi etiam diversabantur, at deinde in uno loco illud comedebant & in alio diversorium sive hospitium habebant.
units.tr: Formerly, where they ate the Passover, there they also lodged; but afterwards they ate it in one place and had their lodging or inn in another.

units.la: In his verò conveniebat Pascha Ægypti cum Pafchatibus posterioribus. 1. illud poterat comedi a pluribus familiis simul iunctis. 2. in utroque agnus debebat esse à grege desumptus, masculus, absque ullo vitio, & annum unum solum habere. 3. Fermentum in utroque excuti debebat. 4 Pafchata utraque debebant non absque Cantico celebrari.
units.tr: In these, the Egyptian Passover agreed with the later Passovers in four points: (1) it could be eaten by several families joined together; (2) in both, the lamb had to be taken from the flock, be male, be without any defect, and be only one year old; (3) leaven had to be removed in both; (4) both Passovers had to be celebrated with singing.

units.la: §. De vitiis quæ agnum Paschalem ineptum reddunt vid. Majm. in Iffure cap.2. Abarbenel in Exod.12. recensed illos qui decem diebus ante festum agnos suos segregaverant, illos deinde ad lectorum suorum pedes alligasse, ut continuò in ipsorum essent oculis.
units.tr: §. On the defects that make a Paschal lamb unfit, see Majm. in Iffure ch. 2. Abarbanel on Exodus 12 records that some men set apart their lambs ten days before the feast and then tied them to the feet of their beds, so that they would always be before their eyes.

units.la: §. Post comparatum agnum Paschalem prima cura erat, ut abstinerent ab esu omnis generis fermentati, & illud ex domibus suis excuterent, vid. Fermentum. Antequàm fermentum quærere inciperent, hanc eiaculati sunt oratiunculam, Benedictus sis ô Deus & Rex noster æterne, qui sanctificasti nobis præceptum de repurgatione fermenti. Quo dicto statim se ad excussionem parabant, & quicquid fermentati reperiebant, indebant in aliquam cistulam, vel in aliquem alium locum in quem Mures venire non poterant, & hanc ceremoniam claudunt his verbis: כל חמירא דאיכא ברשותי דחמיתי ודלא חמיתיה ליבטל ולהוי כעפרא דארעא Omne fermentum quod fuit & est in potestate mea, illud quod vidi & illud quod non vidi, sit ut pulvis terra. Maymon in מצרי cap.3. Et Seder Haggada Schel. Pesach. sol.1.
units.tr: §. After the Paschal lamb had been acquired, the first concern was to abstain from eating anything leavened of any kind and to remove it from their houses; see Fermentum. Before they began to search for leaven, they uttered this short prayer: Blessed are you, O God and eternal King, who have sanctified for us the commandment concerning the removal of leaven. As soon as this was said, they prepared for the clearing out, and whatever leaven they found they put into some small chest or some other place where mice could not get in. They close this ceremony with these words: כל חמירא דאיכא ברשותי דחמיתי ודלא חמיתיה ליבטל ולהוי כעפרא דארעא [Kol chamira, etc.] Let all the leaven that is or was in my possession, whether I have seen it or not, be nullified and become like the dust of the earth. See Maymon in Mitzri ch. 3, and Seder Haggada Schel. Pesach. p. 1.

units.la: §. Diem Pascha antecedentem quem vocant הפסח ערבי Vesperas Paschatis, quædam populi pars totum festivum celebrabat, uti incolæ Galilææ, altera verò sic in Iudæa solum à meridie à laboribus cessabat. Pesachim cap.4. Hoc die horâ quintâ quæ 12. nostræ respondet unusquisque fermentum suum quod alicui cistulæ indidisse modò diximus, vel igne concremabat, vel in aërem projiciebat, vel extraneis divendebat. Vid. Maymon in Chametz uMatza cap.1. & 2. Pesachim c.2.
units.tr: §. On the day before the Passover, which they call הפסח ערבי [erev ha-pesach], the Vespers of the Passover, one part of the people kept the whole day as a feast, as the inhabitants of Galilee did, while others in Judea ceased from work only from midday. Pesachim ch. 4. On this day, at the fifth hour, which corresponds to our twelfth, each person either burned the leaven that he had just said he put into a chest, or threw it into the air, or sold it to outsiders. See Maymon in Chametz uMatza ch. 1 and 2, and Pesachim ch. 2.

units.la: §. Dies mactationis Paschatis, erat dies decimus quartus mensis primi. Adducendus erat agnus in atrium, ubi altare. Maymon in Korban Pesach. cap. 1. Non mactandum erat Pascha nisi in atrio, ubi reliqua sacrificia mactantur: mactandumque die decimo quarto, post meridiem, post iuge sacrificium, post oblatum thymiama, horâ secundâ nostrâ & dimidiâ. Sunt quidam qui existimant Christum in Pafchate suo celebrando unum diem anticipasse, hoc argumento nixi quòd Iudæi noluerint ingredi tribunal Pilati, ne immundi fierent, & proinde inepti ad comedendum Pascha. Sed præterquàm quòd illi non agnum Paschalem sed Chagigah, (de quo infra) intellexerunt, Maymonides expressis verbis docet, illum pœnam excidii incurrisse qui solus in aliquo loco Pascha mactasset, & non cum totol fraele in atrio templi, aut qui unum diem anticipasset, & non præcisè diem decimum quartum observasset. In Corban Pesach cap 1. Christus certè nunquam contra receptas regulas ivit, ut egisset, quod apud populum summum nefas erat. Videtur quidem locum Tosaphs. ad Pesathim cap.1. ad med. Quando inquit, Cuthaei aliquando suum Pascha celebrarunt ante diem quo Israelita, & aliquando post, aliquo modo illorum opinionem plausibilem reddere, quia per מ"נכ etiam Christiani sæpius designantur. Sed qui locum inspiciet, facilè videbit, ipsum de Samaritanis loquii, qui in suo Monte Gerizim agebant quod lubebat.
units.tr: §. The day of the slaughter of the Passover was the fourteenth day of the first month. The lamb had to be brought into the court where the altar was. See Maymon in Korban Pesach. ch. 1: The Passover was not to be slaughtered except in the court where the other sacrifices are slaughtered, and it was to be slaughtered on the fourteenth day, after midday, after the continual sacrifice, after the incense had been offered, at about half past the second hour of our reckoning. There are some who think that Christ anticipated one day in celebrating his Passover, relying on this argument: that the Jews did not want to enter the tribunal of Pilate, lest they become unclean and so unfit to eat the Passover. But apart from the fact that they understood this not of the Paschal lamb but of the Chagigah (about which see below), Maimonides teaches in express words that he who slaughtered the Passover in some place alone, and not with the whole of Israel in the court of the temple, or who anticipated one day and did not observe precisely the fourteenth day, incurred the penalty of extermination. In Corban Pesach ch. 1. Christ certainly never went against the accepted rules in such a way as to do what was thought the greatest sin among the people. Indeed, the passage of the Tosaphoth on Pesachim ch. 1, about the middle, seems to make their opinion somewhat plausible, since it says: The Cuthaeans sometimes kept their Passover before the day on which the Israelites did, and sometimes after. For under the term מ"נכ [minim] Christians are also often meant. But whoever looks at the passage will easily see that it speaks of the Samaritans, who on their mountain Gerizim did as they pleased.

units.la: §. Antequam mactarent Agnum Paschalem, ante omnia conveniebant de numero illorum qui ipsum comedere debebant, secundùm illud Maymonidis in Corban Pesach. cap. 2.
units.tr: §. Before they slaughtered the Paschal lamb, they first of all agreed on the number of those who were to eat it, according to the saying of Maimonides in Corban Pesach. ch. 2.

units.la: אין שוחשין את הפסח אלא למנויין Non poterant mactare Pasch,nisi personas antea numeraverint. Si quis vellet deinde ad aliam societatem se conferre, id facere debet ante mactationem agni, nam postea id ipsi non licet. R.Salomoh in Exod.12. hae societates vocabantur חבורות Συναξεις vel φρατριαι: numerusque personarum illas constituentium definitus non erat: ut plurimum illum ordinabant pro constitutione edentium, si membra societatis erant valida & robusta, pauci solum ad pascha comedendum constituebantur; e contra si comedentes senes aut invalidi erant. Quamvis Mulieres non obligabantur ad omnes comparitiones festorum, nihilominus ad celebrandum Pascha obstrictae erant. Maymon. Korban Happesach. cap 2. tota Congregatio Israelis illud mactare debet, ואחר איש ואחר אשה חייבי במצוה זו Et viri & foemina ad illud praeceptum aequaliter obligabantur. Non autem permittebant ob reverentiam actionis ut illae societates vel ex solis mulieribus, aut infantibus, aut proselytis, aut senibus conflarentur: sed familias integras coniungebant. Dominus noster Iesus Matth.26.20. Luc.22.14. suam paschalem societatem cum duodecim discipulis habuit.
units.tr: אין שוחטין את הפסח אלא למנויין [Ein shochtin et ha-pesach ella le-minuyin] They could not slaughter the Passover unless they had first numbered the persons. If anyone wished afterwards to join another company, he had to do so before the lamb was slaughtered, for afterwards it was not permitted to him. R. Solomon on Exodus 12. These companies were called חבורות [chavurot], Greek συναξεις [synaxeis] or φρατριαι [phratriai]. The number of persons forming them was not fixed; generally they arranged it according to the number of those eating: if the members of the company were strong and robust, only a few were assigned to eat the Passover; on the other hand, if those eating were old or infirm, more were assigned. Although women were not bound to attend all the feasts, nevertheless they were bound to celebrate the Passover. Maymon. Korban Happesach. ch. 2: The whole congregation of Israel must slaughter it, ואחר איש ואחר אשה חייבים במצוה זו [ve-achar ish ve-achar isha chayavim be-mitzvah zo] and men and women were equally bound by this precept. They did not permit these companies to be made up only of women, or of children, or of proselytes, or of old men, out of reverence for the action; rather, they joined whole families together. Our Lord Jesus had his Paschal company with the twelve disciples: Matth. 26:20; Luke 22:14.

units.la: §. Pascha נשרש כשלש כיתור Mactabatur in tribus coetibus. Pesach. cap. 5. quoniam enim agnus debebat in atrio mactari, illud vero tantum numerum una vice capere non poterat, omnem multitudinem in tres dividebant coetus, & unus post alterum sua paschata mactavit. Cur autem tres coetus fecerint, & non plures aut pauciores, rationem petunt Gemarijs in Pesach. l.c. & R. Salomoh in Exod.11. ex ipsis institutionis Paschatis verbis. Totus Cœtus & congregatio Israelis illud matlare debet. Tria illa Cœtus, Congregatio, Israel, triplicem mactandi vicem designant. In unoquoque cœtu ad minimum triginta homines esse debebant, si itaque casu eveniret, ut in universum ultra quinquaginta non adessent, constitutum est, ut triginta primò ingrederentur & deinde mactato paschate viginti manerent, & decem egrederentur, quos deinde alii decem secundâ & tertiâ vice exciperent. Vid. Maymon in Korban Pesach. cap. 1. Gemaram Bab. in Pesachim sol. 64.
units.tr: §. The Passover was נשחט בשלשה כיתות [nishchat be-shelosha kitot] slaughtered in three groups. Pesachim ch. 5. For since the lamb had to be slaughtered in the court, and that court could not hold so great a number at one time, they divided the whole multitude into three groups, and each in turn slaughtered its Passover, one after another. Why they made three groups, and not more or fewer, the Gemarists on Pesachim ibid. and R. Solomon on Exodus 11 seek the reason from the very words of the institution of the Passover: The whole assembly and congregation of Israel must slaughter it. These three words, assembly, congregation, Israel, designate a threefold turn of slaughter. In each group there had to be at least thirty men. If it happened that, in total, there were not more than fifty, it was arranged that thirty should enter first, and after the Passover had been slaughtered twenty should remain and ten should go out, and these ten were then received by another ten in the second and third turn. See Maymon in Korban Pesach. ch. 1, and the Gemara Babylonica in Pesachim p. 64.

units.la: §. Modum Mactandi paschata habes in Pesachim cap.5.v.5.6. his verbis. Pascha mactatur in tribus turmis, sicut dicitur, Atque agnum mactabit, omnis cœtus congregationis Israelis; cœtus & congregatio & Israel. Ingreditur cœtus primus, & repletur totum atrium: portæ atrii serrant: tubis canunt: Sacerdotes stant seriatim, atque pro manibus habent phialas aureas, & argenteas: series altera argenteas, altera aureas; & non confunduntur: & non erant לכוכי שולייס Phialis fimbria, ne eas seponerent, & sic condensaretur sanguis. Israelita mactat & sanguinem recipit Sacerdos, & proximè adstanti dat, & ille proximo, qui phialam plenam recipiens vacuam ei dat. Sacerdos qui altari proximus stat, sanguinem spargit aspersione unâ iuxta fundamentum altaris, יצאה כת ראשונה Exit turma prima, & ingreditur secunda, & post secundam tertiam, semperque eadem ratione proceditur.
units.tr: §. The manner of slaughtering the Passover you have in Pesachim ch. 5, sections 5 and 6, in these words: The Passover is slaughtered in three companies, as it is said: "And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it" (assembly, congregation, and Israel). The first company goes in, and the court is filled completely; the gates of the court are shut; trumpets are sounded; the priests stand in rows, holding in their hands golden and silver bowls, one row silver and the other gold, and they do not get mixed up; and the bowls had no לכוכי שוליים [lechuchei shulayim, rims], so that they could not be set down, and the blood would thereby coagulate. The Israelite slaughters, and the priest receives the blood and passes it to the one standing next to him, and he to the next, who, receiving a full bowl, gives back an empty one. The priest who stands nearest the altar throws the blood with a single sprinkling at the base of the altar. יצאה כת ראשונה [yatza kat rishona] The first company goes out, and the second enters, and after the second the third; and always the procedure continues in the same way.

units.la: Agnos in atrium vulgò humeris portarunt, quæ portatio vocatur הרכבה in Pesachin c. 6. v.1. Vbi Gloss, Portatio eius in humeris hominis, ut eum afferat in atrium tanquam in locum publicum. Eo tempore quo Israelitæ occupabantur circa agni mactationem, Levitæ canebant Hallel, si illud iam absolverant, Israelitæ verò mactationem non perfecerant, illud iterum de novo repetebant. Maymon in Korban Pesach. cap.1. Gloss. in Succah sol.54. Pesachim cap.5. De Hallel iam quædam diximus suo loco; plura de eo habes in Hierof. Pesachim cap.5. Maym. in Megillah cap.3. Gloss. in Succah sol.38. Succah cap. 5. Taanith cap.3.
units.tr: The lambs were commonly carried into the court on the shoulders, and this carrying is called הרכבה [harkavah] in Pesachim ch. 6, section 1, where the Gloss says: its carrying on a man's shoulders, so that he may bring it into the court as into a public place. At the time when the Israelites were occupied with the slaughter of the lamb, the Levites sang the Hallel; if they had already finished it, but the Israelites had not yet completed the slaughter, they repeated it again from the beginning. See Maymon in Korban Pesach. ch. 1, Gloss. in Succah p. 54, Pesachim ch. 5. Some things about the Hallel we have already said in its place; more about it you have in the Jerusalem Pesachim ch. 5, Maimonides in Megillah ch. 3, Gloss. in Succah p. 38, Succah ch. 5, Taanith ch. 3.

units.la: §. Sparso sanguine ad pedem altaris, excoriato agno, exsecto ventre, extracto adipe, atque in ignem altaris reiecto, fertur Cadaver ad hospitium ubi cœnandum: caro assanda, corium tribuendum hospiti. Vid. Pesachim c.5.8.9. Bab.Ioma sol.12.1.
units.tr: §. The blood is sprinkled at the foot of the altar, the lamb is skinned, its belly is opened, the fat is drawn out and cast on the fire of the altar. The carcass is then carried to the lodging where it is to be eaten: the flesh is to be roasted, and the hide is given to the host. See Pesachim c.5.8.9. Bab.Ioma sol.12.1.

units.la: §. Omittimus hic curiosas & anxias illas observationes quibus agnum assabant, & quæ in cap.7. Pesachim describuntur; solummodò notamus illos sumsisse שפור של ריבון baculum ligni Malogranati, & per os agni ad posteriora eius protrusisse, illoque agnum assasse. Item quod agnus Paschalis vocetur מקולס Galeatus, quia cùm totus assabatur, cum capite, cruribus, & intestinis, pedes autem & intestina ad latera ligabantur inter assandum, agnus ita quasi armatum repræsentaverit, qui galeâ in capite & ense in latere est munitus. Baba Beracoi folio 19. 1. Pesachim folio 53. 2.
units.tr: §. We pass over here the fussy and anxious rules by which they roasted the lamb, which are described in Pesachim cap.7. We note only that they took a staff of pomegranate wood (שפור של ריבון [shafur shel rimmon]), thrust it through the lamb's mouth down to its hindquarters, and roasted the lamb on it. Likewise the Paschal lamb is called מקולס [mekulas], Helmeted, because, when it was roasted whole with head, shins and entrails, its feet and entrails were tied to its sides during roasting, so that the lamb appeared as if armed, protected by a helmet on its head and a sword at its side. Baba Beracoi folio 19. 1. Pesachim folio 53. 2.

units.la: §. Tempus quo agnum comedebant erat, cùm nox ingruerat, secundùm illum Canonem in Pesachim cap. 10. ערבי פסחים סבוך לבנתה לא In vespera Paschatis nemo debet pascha comedere à tempore Mincha usque dum noctescceret. Notat etiam Glossa Alphesi & R. Salomonis, ipsos à sacrificio vespertino usque ad ipsam coenam nihil degustare debuisse, ut eo acutiori stomacho & appetitu ad agni esum accederent.
units.tr: §. The time for eating the lamb was when night had come on, according to that canon in Pesachim cap. 10: ערבי פסחים סבוך לבנתה לא [On the eve of Passover no one should eat the Passover until the time of Minchah, until it grows dark]. The gloss of Alphesi and of R. Solomon also notes that from the evening sacrifice until the supper itself they ought not to taste anything at all, so that they might come to the eating of the lamb with a keener stomach and appetite.

units.la: §. De accubitu diximus in A. In Cœna paschali ipsum summè necessarium & requisitum existimarunt. Gloss. in Beracot cap.6. v.6. Nos recubitum non abhibemus nisi ad buccellam folium; & certè iis qui ederunt recumbentes, necessarium fuit recubitus &c. Pesachim cap.10.v.1. אפילו עני שבישראל לא יאכל עד שיסב Etiam pauperrimus Israelita, nè comedat antequam accumbat. Causa verò cur in accubitu tantam religionem posuerint, fuit quia signum prae se ferebat libertatis. Hierof. Pesachim sol.37.2. R. Levi dicit, Mos servorum est, ut edant stantes: at nunc comedant recumbentes, ut dignoscatur exiisse eos ex servitute in libertatem.
units.tr: §. We have spoken about reclining at A. At the Paschal supper they judged it absolutely necessary and required. Gloss. in Beracot cap.6. v.6. We do not use reclining except for eating a morsel of bread; and certainly for those who eat, reclining was necessary, etc. Pesachim cap.10.v.1. אפילו עני שבישראל לא יאכל עד שיסב [Even the poorest Israelite should not eat until he reclines]. The reason why they attached such great religious importance to reclining was that it was a sign of freedom. Hierof. Pesachim sol.37.2. R. Levi says: It is the custom of slaves to eat standing; but now they eat reclining, so that it may be recognised that they have gone out from slavery into freedom.

units.la: Bab. Pesachim sol.108. 1. Azyma opus habent recubitu, herba amara opus non habent. Duo pocula priora opus habent recubitu, sed non duo posteriora. Glossa, Azyma comedunt nocte prima recumbentes, quia recordatio est redemptionis. Herba amara non opus habent recubitu, quia memoriam ferunt servitutis.
units.tr: Bab. Pesachim sol.108. 1. The unleavened bread requires reclining; the bitter herb does not require reclining. The first two cups require reclining, but not the last two. Gloss: They eat the unleavened bread on the first night reclining, because it is a remembrance of redemption. The bitter herb does not require reclining, because it bears the memory of servitude.

units.la: Maymon Comment. in Mischn. Tenemur ad accubitum dum comedimus, ut comedamus more Regum & Magnatum.
units.tr: Maymon Comment. in Mischn. We are bound to recline while we eat, so that we may eat in the manner of kings and great men.

units.la: §. Iam ipsam cœnam referemus. 1. Exordium cepit cœna Paschalis à poculo vini. Pesachin cap. x. v. 2. Miscent ei poculum primum, Schola Schammaana dicit, Benedicit primo super die, deinde super vino: at Schola Hillelíana aicit, primo super vino benedicit, ac deinde super die, quia dies in causa est, cur adsit vinum: id est, ut explicat Gloss. עוזרה סעודה קורם שיבא ut adsit ante Cibum.
units.tr: §. Now we shall relate the supper itself. 1. The Paschal supper began with a cup of wine. Pesachin cap. x. v. 2. They mix for him the first cup. The School of Shammai says: He blesses first over the day, then over the wine; but the School of Hillel says: He blesses first over the wine, and then over the day, because the day is the reason why wine is present; that is, as the gloss explains, עוזרה סעודה קורם שיבא [that it may be there before the meal].

units.la: Maymon in Chamets uMatsa cap. 8. Miscent primo poculum unicuique, & benedicit (Paterfamilias) Benedictus sit qui creavit fructum vitis, & recitat insuper consecrationem diei, ןובן & pro toto cætu gratias agit, ac poculum ebibit, & postea benedicit super lotione manuum & lavat. Confer hoc poculum cum illo Luc. xxii. 17.
units.tr: Maymon in Chamets uMatsa cap. 8. They first mix a cup for each person, and the head of the household blesses: Blessed be he who created the fruit of the vine; and he further recites the sanctification of the day, ןובן and gives thanks on behalf of the whole company; he drinks the cup, and afterwards blesses over the washing of the hands and washes. Compare this cup with that in Luke 22:17.

units.la: II. Apponuntur deinde Herbæ amaræ. Maymon. Inferunt mensam stratam, super quam est מרור וירק אחר Embamma amarum, atque Herba alia. Bab. Pesachin sol. 114. 1. Non apponunt mensam, nisi post consecrationem diei: & mensa apponitur lactuca. Postquam benedixit super vino apponunt herbas, atque edit ille lactucas intinctas: at non in חרוסת Embammate; nam illud adhuc non adducitur.
units.tr: II. Then bitter herbs are set out. Maymon. They bring in a spread table, on which there is מרור וירק אחר [a bitter relish and another herb]. Bab. Pesachin sol. 114. 1. They do not set out the table except after the sanctification of the day; and the table is set with lettuce. After he has blessed over the wine they set out the herbs, and he eats the lettuce dipped; but not in the חרוסת [charoset] relish, for that is not yet brought.

units.la: III. Apponuntur postea Azyma, atque Embamma חרוסת, atque agnus, & caro etiam Chagigæ diei decimi quarti. Maymonides nullam notat interpositionem, inter appositas herbas amaras atque appositá Azyma, At Misna illam notat his verbis הביאו לפניו מצה & Apponunt coram eo Azyma. Vt enim notat Glossa tollebant & reducebant mensam, ut filius occasionem haberet interrogandi, quare bis intingimus?
units.tr: III. Afterwards the unleavened bread is set out, and the charoset relish, and the lamb, and also the flesh of the Chagigah of the fourteenth day. Maimonides notes no interruption between the setting out of the bitter herbs and the setting out of the unleavened bread. But the Mishnah notes it in these words: הביאו לפניו מצה [They bring before him unleavened bread]. For, as the gloss notes, they removed and brought back the table, so that the son would have an occasion to ask: Why do we dip twice?

units.la: IV. Incipit & benedicit. Benedictus sit qui creavit fructum terrae: ac herbas accipit, atque intingit in embammate (charoseт, & comedit pro quantitate olivae, ille (Paterfamilias) atque omnes eum eo accumbentes. Et tunc removent mensam à patrefamiliás. Maymon.
units.tr: IV. He begins and blesses: Blessed be he who created the fruit of the earth. He takes the herbs and dips them in the relish (charoset), and eats the amount of an olive, he (the head of the household) and all who recline with him. And then they remove the table from the head of the household. Maymon.

units.la: V. מוגי לו כוס שני Iam misćent ei poculum secundum: atque iam filius interrogat patrem: vel si filius non norit interrogare ipse eum docet. Quantum differt hac nox ab aliis omnibus noctibus? Aliis noctibus non intingimus nisi semel; hac nocte bis: Alia comedimus vel fermentatum vel Azyma; hac Azyma solum &c. aliis comedimus vel sedentes vel recumbentes, hac nocte omnes recumbimus.
units.tr: V. מוגי לו כוס שני [They mix for him the second cup]. Now the son asks the father; or, if the son does not know how to ask, the father teaches him. How does this night differ from all other nights? On other nights we do not dip even once; on this night twice. On other nights we eat either leavened or unleavened bread; on this night only unleavened bread, etc. On other nights we eat either sitting or reclining; on this night we all recline.

units.la: V I. Admovetur iterum Mensa, & tum dicit ille, Hoc est Pascha, quod comedimus ideo, quia Deus transiit per domos Patrum nostrorum in Ægypto. Tunc elevat manu sua herbas amaras & dicit, herbas has amaras nos comedimus ideo, quòd amaras fecerunt vitas patrum nostrorum in Ægypto. Elevat manu sua Azyma & dicit, Azyma hac comedimus, quia non fuit tempus sufficiens quo farina à Patribus nostris subacta fermentaretur, antequàm se ipsum revelaret Deus, eosque redimeret. Debemus ergo nos laudare, celebrare, honorare, magnificare, &c. illum qui patribus nostris, nobisque haec omnia miranda fecit, nosque eduxit è servitute in libertatem, è dolore in gaudium, è tenebris in lucem magnam. Dicimus ergo HalleIuiah (ab initio Psal.113. ad finem Psal.114.) Et claudit, Benedictus tu Domine Deus noster Rex æterne nos redimens, patresque redimens ex Ægypto, atque ad noctem hanc nos perducens; ut comedamus Azyma atque herbas amaras: & iam ebibit poculum secundum.
units.tr: VI. The table is brought back again, and then he says: This is the Passover which we eat, because God passed over the houses of our fathers in Egypt. Then he raises the bitter herbs in his hand and says: These bitter herbs we eat because the Egyptians made the lives of our fathers bitter in Egypt. He raises the unleavened bread in his hand and says: This unleavened bread we eat because there was not enough time for the dough kneaded by our fathers to become leavened, before God revealed himself and redeemed them. We ought therefore to praise, celebrate, honour, magnify, etc., him who did all these wonderful things for our fathers and for us, and led us out of servitude into freedom, from sorrow into joy, from darkness into a great light. Therefore we say Hallelujah (from the beginning of Psalm 113 to the end of Psalm 114).
