And he concludes: Blessed are you, Lord our God, eternal King, who redeemed us and redeemed our fathers from Egypt, and brought us to this night, that we may eat unleavened bread and bitter herbs. And now he drinks the second cup.

units.la: VII. Deinde manus lavans, & duos panes accipiens, unum frangit, (Ratio fractionis apud Maymon. est, quia hic panis vocatur לחם עוני Panis paupertatis. Pauperibus autem res est cum frustis, atque hic pariter sunt frusta.) & fractum in mensa reponit, & benedicit, Benedictus sit ille qui producit panem e terra: & complicans panem, cum herbis amaris, intingensque in embamma חרוסת , benedicensque, azymas atque herbas amaras simul comedit. Posteaque gratias pari modo agens circa carnem Chagiga diei decimi quarti, de ea etiam comedit: & pari modo benedicens super carne agni, de ea comedit.
units.tr: VII. Then, washing his hands and taking two loaves, he breaks one. (The reason for the breaking, according to Maimonides, is that this bread is called לחם עוני [bread of affliction]. The poor have to do with broken pieces, and here likewise there are pieces.) He places the broken piece on the table and blesses: Blessed be he who brings forth bread from the earth. Folding the bread together with the bitter herbs and dipping it in the charoset relish, and blessing, he eats the unleavened bread and the bitter herbs together. Then, likewise giving thanks over the flesh of the Chagigah of the fourteenth day, he eats of it too; and in the same way, blessing over the flesh of the lamb, he eats of that.

units.la: VIII. Inde porrò cœnam protrahit, hoc vel illud edens bibensve, prout lubet: ultimoque de carne Paschatis edit, saltem pro quantitate olivæ, atque exinde nec quicquam cibi gustat omnino. Hanc cœnæ Paschalis rubricam hoc modo quo eam repræsentavimus, ex Maymonide & cap. ult. Pefachin adornavit Cl. Ligtfootus.
units.tr: VIII. Then he prolongs the supper, eating or drinking this or that as he pleases; and at the end he eats of the flesh of the Passover, at least the amount of an olive, and after that he tastes nothing of food at all. Cl. Lightfoot arranged this rubric of the Paschal supper in this way, as we have presented it, from Maimonides and the last chapter of Pesachin.

units.la: §. Postquàm in cœna Paschali eousque quò notavimus pervenerant, Paterfamilias deinde lavabat manus המים וגו ברכת הפתן Et benedicit benedicens cibo, (sive gratias agit post cibum.) Et super poculo vini tertio, atque ebibit. Maymonides. De hoc poculo benedictionis decem res dicuntur in Bab. Berac. sol.51.1. חרחה ושטיפה Lotio & proluvio (i.e. ut lavetur intus & extra, ne scilicet in eo maneat quid vini poculorum praecedentium ) חי Vinum purum infundatur in poculum, & fiat commistio aquae in poculo : ובלא plenum sit, עשוך Coronatu n.e.dum ille hoc agit circum sint discipuli instar coronae. עיטוף obvelatum, i.e. velat se & confidet. נוטלו בשתי ידיו Poculum accipit manu utraque, ac manui dexterae tenendum tradit, oculos in illud figit, sunt qui dicunt, dono impertit suis.
units.tr: §. When the Paschal supper had reached the point we have noted, the head of the household then washes his hands: המים וגו ברכת הפתן [the water, etc., the blessing of the meal]. And he blesses the one who gives food (or gives thanks after the meal). And over the third cup of wine he blesses, and drinks it. Maimonides. Ten things are said about this cup of blessing in Bab. Berac. sol.51.1: חרחה ושטיפה [cleaning and rinsing] (that is, that it be washed inside and out, so that nothing of the wine of the previous cups remains in it); חי [pure wine] is poured into the cup, and water is mixed into the cup; ובלא [it is full]; עשוך [crowned], while he does this the disciples sit around him like a crown; עיטוף [wrapped], that is, he covers himself and reclines; נוטלו בשתי ידיו [he takes the cup in both hands], and gives it to be held in the right hand, fixing his eyes upon it; some say he gives it as a gift to his people.

units.la: §. Erat & calix quartus, de quo Maymonides in Chamets &c. & Mischna in Pesachin. c. ult. Deinde miscet poculum quartum, & super illo perficit Hallel : additque insuper ברכת השיר Benedictionem Cantici, quod est, Laudent te, Domine, omnia opera tua &c. & dicit Benedictus sit, qui creavit fructum vitis, & postea non quiequam gustat ista nocte. Perficit Halleli e. incipit inde ubi desitum est ante videl. ab initio Psal.115. ad finem Psal.118.
units.tr: §. There was also a fourth cup, of which Maimonides writes in Chametz etc., and the Mishnah in Pesachin, last chapter. Then he mixes the fourth cup, and over it completes the Hallel. He adds besides the Blessing of the Song [ברכת השיר], that is, "Let all your works praise you, O Lord," etc., and says, "Blessed be he who created the fruit of the vine," and afterwards tastes nothing else that night. He completes the Hallel, that is, he begins where it was left off before, namely from the beginning of Psalm 115 to the end of Psalm 118.

units.la: §. Panis in Coena Paschali erat ex institutione divina, at vinum solum ex traditione. Hierof. Pesachin sol.37.2. Traditio. Necesse est ut homo exhilaret uxorem suam & filios ad festum. At quomodo exhilarant? Vino. Vide etiam Bab. Pesach. sol.109.1.
units.tr: §. At the Paschal supper, bread was by divine institution, but wine only by tradition. Jerusalem Talmud, Pesachin, fol. 37.2. Tradition: "A man must gladden his wife and children for the feast. But how do they gladden them? With wine." See also Babylonian Talmud, Pesach, fol. 109.1.

units.la: Vnusquisque debebat ebibere quatuor pocula. Hierof. Pesachin ubi supra. הכל חייבין כוס Omnes tenentur ad quatuor pocula, viri, foemina, & pueri. At quid pueris cum vino inquit R. Iehuda. Illis distribuunt triticum & nuces.
units.tr: Everyone was obliged to drink four cups. Jerusalem Talmud, Pesachin, as above: [הכל חייבין כוס] All are bound to the four cups, men, women and boys. "But what have boys to do with wine?" says R. Jehuda. "They are given wheat and nuts."

units.la: De Mensura horum poculorum sic determinatur, in Hierof.Schabbat sol.11.1. ארבעה כוסות שאמרו ישנן רבעית יין כאישלקי Quatuor pocula continent, quartanam Vini Italicam.
units.tr: The measure of these cups is determined thus in Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, fol. 11.1: [ארבעה כוסות שאמרו ישנן רבעית יין כאישלקי] The four cups contain a quarter of Italian wine.

units.la: Vinum adhibebant Rubrum Hierof. Pesachim sol.37.2. כיין ארום סצות לצאת Praeceptum est, ut vino rubro praestet hoc officium. Sic Bab. צריך שיהא כו טעם ומראה Necesse est, ut sit in eo sapor & apetitus vini. Gloss. ארום שיהא Ut sit rubrum.
units.tr: They used red wine. Jerusalem Talmud, Pesachim, fol. 37.2: [כיין ארום סצות לצאת] It is commanded that this duty be performed with red wine. So the Babylonian: [צריך שיהא כו טעם ומראה] It is necessary that it have in it the taste and appearance of wine. The gloss: [ארום שיהא] that it be red.

units.la: Traditio est in Bab.Beracot sol.50.2. quod super vino cui non immisceatur aqua, non benedicant, quia secundum glossam vinum ipsorum strenuum erat, & potationi absque immixtione aquae, non ita idoneum. Interim tamen in Pesachin dicunt שתאן חי יצא Si quis vinum purum biberet, & non aquâ commixtum, officium tamen praestitit. Ex his etiam rationem habes, cur in cap.ult. Pesachim & in tota huius festi rubrica, quando de infundendis poculis loquuntur, semper adhibeant simpliciter verbum מוג quia scilicet utplurimum pocula haec absque dilutione cum aqua, non ebiberunt, hoc innuit etiam Maymon in Chametz u Matza cap.7. quando inquit ארבע כוסות האלו צריך לשתות : מוג
units.tr: There is a tradition in Babylonian Berakhot, fol. 50.2, that they do not say the blessing over wine into which water is not mixed, because according to the gloss their wine was strong, and drinking it without admixture of water was not so suitable. Meanwhile, however, they say in Pesachin: [שתאן חי יצא] If someone drank undiluted wine, and not mixed with water, he nevertheless discharged the duty. From these you also have the reason why, in the last chapter of Pesachim and in the whole rubric of this feast, when they speak of pouring the cups, they always simply use the word [מוג], because most of the time these cups were not drunk without dilution with water. Maimonides in Chametz u Matza, ch. 7, also points to this when he says: [ארבע כוסות האלו צריך לשתות מוג] These four cups must be drunk mixed.

units.la: §. Addamus hic quasdam observatiunculas indifferenter in Paschalis ritus notatas. Herbae illae quibus utebantur in coena erant חורת Haluca, יולשין Intybus, Endivien / velut Aruch Germ. Körblin Kraut. תכנא de la (hicorée, vel Marrubium. חרחבינה Beta. מרור Prasium vel linostrophon. Parum referebat sive illae herbae essent virides aut aridae, modo non fuerint coctae, aut conditæ. Vid. Pesachim cap .2. verf. 6. De causâ illâ cur has herbas comederint vid. R.Salomoh in Exod. 12. Aben Esra in eundem locum, citat quendam ludæum Hispanum, qui in illa fuit ententia, illas herbas amaras in ordinariis ꝸ yptiorum epulis usitatas fuisse, propter humiditatem aëris, ut illis se contra ipsius vitium tuerentur.
units.tr: §. Let us add here some small observations, noted without any particular order, on the Paschal rite. The herbs they used at the supper were: [חורת] Haluca; [יולשין] Intybus, endive, as the Aruch German "Körblin Kraut"; [תכנא] de la chicorée or Marrubium; [חרחבינה] Beta; [מרור] Prasium or linostrophon. It made little difference whether these herbs were green or dried, provided they were not cooked or pickled. See Pesachim, ch. 2, v. 6. On the reason why they ate these herbs, see R. Solomon on Exod. 12. Aben Ezra on the same place cites a certain Spanish Jew who held that those bitter herbs were in use at the ordinary meals of the Egyptians, because of the humidity of the air, so that they might protect themselves against its harmful effects.

units.la: In Cœna Pa[s]chali non solum agnum habebant, sed etiam alias Carnes vid. Maymon in Corban Pesach. cap.8. Mischna in cap.10. Pesachin illas designat cùm dicit הביאו לפניו מצה ושני תבשילין וחזרת ושני תבשילין adducent coram eo Azyma, lactucas & duo Cocta.
units.tr: At the Paschal supper they had not only the lamb but also other meats; see Maimonides in Corban Pesach, ch. 8. The Mishnah in ch. 10 of Pesachin indicates them when it says: [הביאו לפניו מצה ושני תבשילין וחזרת ושני תבשילין] They shall bring before him unleavened bread and two cooked dishes, lettuce, and two cooked dishes.

units.la: חרוסת Erat Embamma factum ex amaris & dulcibus, qualia sunt dactyli, ficus, uvæ passæ, acetum. Aruch in rad. Maymon Corban Pesach. cap. 8. adhibebatur in memoriam argillæ, ex qua lateres compositi patres in Ægypto. Vid. Haggada Schel. Pesach.
units.tr: [חרוסת] was an embamma made of bitter and sweet things, such as dates, figs, raisins and vinegar. Aruch, in the root; Maimonides, Corban Pesach, ch. 8. It was used in memory of the clay from which our fathers made bricks in Egypt. See Haggada Schel Pesach.

units.la: De numero Panum vel placentarum disputatur, probabilissimum est, illos ante devastationem templi adhibuisse placentas duas, & postea tres. Vid. Maymon.in Chamets &c. c.8. Cl.Buxt.Lex.Talm. in אפיקומן.
units.tr: There is debate about the number of loaves or cakes. It is most probable that before the destruction of the temple they used two cakes, and afterwards three. See Maimonides in Chamets, etc., ch. 8; Buxtorf's Lexicon Talmudicum under [אפיקומן].

units.la: In conviviis ordinariis adhibebant etiam אפיקומן Bellaria, (Nachtracht) sed in cœna Paschali obtinuit hic Canon אין מפטירין אחר הפסח אפיקומן non dimittunt convivium in Pascha bellaria. Pesachim cap. ult. ultimum enim quod degustare volebant erat caro agni Paschalis & frustulum Azymi, quod proinde ipsorum erat אפיקומן bellaria. De hoc sonat ille locus Maymonidis Glossatoris in loc. ubi supra, quando infit, אחת פורס לשנים ושאר חצי לאפוקי frangit unam placentam in duas partes, & unam ser-vat pro bellariis. Quoniam enim ipsis non licebat frustus adhibere pro bellariis; Azymi frustum bellaria fecerunt. Quod observandum, ne existimemus Talmudicos sibi invicem contradicere.
units.tr: At ordinary banquets they also used [אפיקומן] bellaria (Nachtisch, dessert), but at the Paschal supper this canon held: [אין מפטירין אחר הפסח אפיקומן] they do not end the meal after the Passover with bellaria (Pesachim, last chapter). For the last thing they wished to taste was the flesh of the Paschal lamb and a morsel of unleavened bread, which therefore was their [אפיקומן], bellaria. To this refers that passage of Maimonides' glossator on the same place, where it begins: [אחת פורס לשנים ושאר חצי לאפוקי] he breaks one cake into two parts and keeps the remaining half for bellaria. Since they were not allowed to use a piece of bread for dessert, they made the piece of unleavened bread into dessert. This should be noted, lest we think the Talmudists contradict one another.

units.la: Repetamus & contrahamus hic quæ nunc prolixius de Cœna paschali diximus. Confidebant inclinando, incipiebant cœnam poculo vini, benedicebant illo, diei lavabant manus; tabula parabatur. Primò comedebant de lactuca (de la falade,) secundum deinde poculum implebatur, quo impleto recitabant historiam & Psalm. 113. 114. quibus peractis poculum exhauriebant. Manus denuò lavabant. Azyma frangebantur & benedicebantur, & quædam ipsorum partes cum herbis amaris comedebantur, postquàm & panem & herbas in Embammate tinxerant. Deinde edebant carnes oblationis pacificæ, & post illas, carnes agni. Quibus peractis iterum se lavabant. Poculum tertium sequitur, quod ebibunt post gratiarum actionem pro cibo & vino. Poculo quarto absolvunt suum Hallel, & deinde addita una vel altera benedictione cœna peracta est.
units.tr: Let us now repeat and summarise, more briefly, what we have said at greater length about the Paschal supper. They reclined, leaning, and began the supper with a cup of wine, blessing it; they washed their hands; the table was prepared. First they ate lettuce (de la salade); then a second cup was filled, and when it was filled they recited the story and Psalms 113 and 114, and when this was done they drained the cup. They washed their hands again. The unleavened bread was broken and blessed, and some parts of it were eaten with the bitter herbs, after they had dipped both the bread and the herbs in the embamma. Then they ate the flesh of the peace offering, and after it the flesh of the lamb. When these were finished they washed themselves again. The third cup follows, which they drink after the thanksgiving for food and wine. With the fourth cup they finish their Hallel, and then, after adding one or another blessing, the supper is ended.

units.la: §. Notandum hic etiam totum festum Paschatis septiduum, aliquando translatum fuisse in alium mensem, non tantùm ex illa lege quæ extat Num. ix. sed ex causis etiam aliis de quibus Hierosol. in Maaser Scheni sol. 56.3. Maymon. in Kiddusch.Chodesch cap. 4. Interim tamen
units.tr: §. Note also here that the whole seven-day feast of Passover was sometimes transferred to another month, not only by that law in Num. ix but also for other causes, of which see Jerusalem Talmud, Maaser Scheni, fol. 56.3; Maimonides, Kiddush Chodesh, ch. 4. Meanwhile

units.la: nunquam non mactatus fuit agnus, dum præsente festo dies decimus quartus aderat. Hinc hæc traditio in Pesachin cap.7.v.4. Quinque res si veniunt in immunditia, non comeduntur in immunditia. Manipulus,& duo panes,& panes proposi ionis, sacrificia pacifica congregationis,& hirci Neomeniorum. At Pascha quod venit in immunditia comeditur in immunditia. Quia non venit originaliter, nisi ut comedatur. Hierof. Sotah sol.16.3. Comperimus quod congregatio facit Pascha suum in immunditia, eo tempore quo plurimi eorum sunt immundi. Quæ observanda contrà illos qui volunt Christum suum Pascha celebrasse decimo quarto die, at Iudæos non ante decimum quintum, quia illo anno ipsorum Pascha reiectum erat in diem decimum quintum, ob insequens Sabbathum, quod asseritur absq; ullo fundamento. Si certè Pascha rejici potuisset in diem 15. filii Bethiræ in Hierof. Pesachin sol.33. facilè se ex illa sollicitudine in quam ipsos iecerat dubium, an Sabbathum Pascha pelleret nec ne, liberassent, ipsum Pascha ex die 14. in diem 15. rejiciendo.
units.tr: the lamb was never not slaughtered whenever the feast fell on the fourteenth day. Hence this tradition in Pesachin, ch. 7, v. 4: "Five things, if they come in uncleanness, are not eaten in uncleanness: the sheaf, the two loaves, the showbread, the peace offerings of the congregation, and the goats of the New Moons. But the Passover that comes in uncleanness is eaten in uncleanness, because it comes only to be eaten." Jerusalem Talmud, Sotah, fol. 16.3: "We have found that the congregation keeps its Passover in uncleanness, at a time when most of them are unclean." This must be noted against those who want Christ to have celebrated his Passover on the fourteenth day, and the Jews not before the fifteenth, because in that year their Passover was put off to the fifteenth day on account of the following Sabbath. This is asserted without any foundation. For if the Passover could indeed have been put off to the fifteenth day, the sons of Bethira in Jerusalem Pesachin, fol. 33, would easily have freed themselves from the anxiety into which their doubt had cast them, whether the Sabbath drove out the Passover or not, by postponing the Passover from the fourteenth to the fifteenth day.

units.la: §. Pascha duplex esse potest, discrimen inter primum & secundum hoc esse potest. In primo (in pascha te mensis primi Num. ix.) obligatur quisque sub ista lege. Fermentum non videbitur apud vos nec invenietur. In secundo, fermentum & azymum possunt esse cum homine in domo sua. In primo, tenetur ad hymnum dum comedit, at non in secundo, in utroq; tenetur ad hymnum dum mactat. Vtrumq; comedendum est assatum & cum Azymis, & herbis amaris, & utrumque pellit Sabbathum. Pesachin cap.9.v.3. Pafchate primo quivis tenetur ad pernoctationem intra Hierosolymam, ut & Paschate secundo Pesachin sol.95.2 Glossa illum canonem solum ad noctem primam festi restringit: Christus ipsum non observavit; egressus enim est ἐις Ꝺ ὁρ@ τῶν ἰλεάων.
units.tr: §. The Passover can be of two kinds, and the difference between the first and the second can be stated thus. In the first (the Passover of the first month, Num. ix) each person is bound by this law: "Leaven shall not be seen among you, nor found." In the second, leaven and unleavened bread may be in a man's house with him. In the first he is bound to the hymn while he eats, but not in the second; in both he is bound to the hymn while he slaughters. Both must be eaten roasted, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, and both put off the Sabbath. Pesachin, ch. 9, v. 3: "At the first Passover everyone is bound to stay overnight within Jerusalem, as also at the second Passover." Pesachin, fol. 95.2. The gloss restricts that canon to the first night of the feast. Christ did not observe it, for he went out [εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν ἐλαιῶν] to the Mount of Olives.

units.la: §. In festo Pafchatis ad duo præcipue obligabantur, בראיה Ad comparendum coram Domino in atrio, idque cum sacrificio, secundo ad חגיגה folennem lætitiam, & festivitatem, idque etiam cum sacrificiis. Ex his huobus maius quid erat (chagigah, nam I. ad Chagigam quidam tenebantur, qui non obligabantur ad comparitionem. Chagigah, sol.2.2. Is qui surdus quidem est, at tamen non mutus est, non tenetur ad comparitionem, at tenetur tamen לשמחה ad lætitiam sive Chagigam.
units.tr: On the feast of Passover they were bound chiefly to two things: to appear before the Lord in the court, and that with a sacrifice; and secondly to the chagigah, the solemn joy and festivity, also with sacrifices. Of these two, which was the greater? The chagigah, for some were bound to the chagigah who were not bound to appear. Chagigah, sol. 2.2: He who is deaf but not mute is not bound to appear, but is bound to joy (לשמחה), that is, to the chagigah.

units.la: II. Non tam strictè requirebatur Comparitio ad diem primum festi ac Chagigah, Vid. Chagigah sol.7.2.
units.tr: II. Appearance was not required as strictly on the first day of the feast as at the chagigah. See Chagigah, sol. 7.2.

units.la: III. Offerebant oves pro Pafchate, pro Chagigah verò Boves. Pesachin sol.70.2. ות אך נפ Oves pro Pafchate חגיגה בקר ו Boves pro Chagigah, Vid. Comment R. Salom. & Beck. in Deut. xvi.2. Hæc Sacrificia vocabantur שלמי שמחה Sacrificia pacifica.
units.tr: III. They offered sheep for the Passover, but oxen for the chagigah. Pesachin, sol. 70.2: Sheep for the Passover (צאן לפסח), oxen for the chagigah (בקר לחגיגה). See the commentary of R. Solomon and Beckius on Deut. 16.2. These sacrifices were called שלמי שמחה, sacrifices of peace.

units.la: IV. Proprium tempus adducendæ Chagigæ erat dies decimus quintus. Aruch in אח. Edebant, bibebant & lætabantur, & sacrificium Chagiga, ad quod adducendum tenebantur die decimo quinto; i. e. die festi primo. Quando Iudæi Ioh.xviii.28. negant se in Prætorium in-
units.tr: IV. The proper time for bringing the chagigah was the fifteenth day. Aruch in אח: They ate, drank and rejoiced, and the chagigah sacrifice, which they were bound to bring on the fifteenth day, that is, on the first day of the feast. When the Jews in John 18.28 refuse to enter the praetorium,

units.la: ingredi posse, ἵνα φάγωσι ͏ πάσχα, ne immundi fierent ad Pascha comedendum; non intelligunt agnum Paschalem sed Chagigam, quam Evangelista cum vulgo vocat πάσχα. Zevachim sol.7.2. Scriptum est, observa mensem Abib ועשית שיהו כל עשיותיו לשם פסח ut facias Pascha. פסח Ut sint omnia quæ facis sub nomine Paschatis. Menachot sol.3.1. עגל ופר ששחטן לשום פסח Vitulus & Iuvenis quem mactant nomine Paschatis. Vel pro Paschate. Nota vitulus & Pascha uti & agnus.
units.tr: that they might not be defiled, ἵνα φάγωσι τὸ πάσχα, so that they might eat the Passover, they do not mean the Paschal lamb but the chagigah, which the Evangelist, with the common people, calls the Passover. Zevachim, sol. 7.2: It is written, observe the month of Abib, and "you shall make" that all your works be for the name of Passover (לשם פסח), that all that you do be under the name of the Passover. Menachot, sol. 3.1: a calf and a bullock which they slaughter in the name of the Passover, or for the Passover. Note that calf and Passover, as also lamb.

units.la: PAUPERES. De eorum privilegiis respectu Spicilegii & anguli agri vid. לקט & שכחה Item angulus agri. De distinctione mendicantium, & de mendicandi modo, Vid. Mendicantes. Qui suspendit corbem, (ut à pauperibus abscondat micas,) is suspendit alimentum suum. (i.e. pauper erit.) Pesachin. iii.2. Vid. Eleemosynas. De Racematione pauperibus relinquenda vid. f.1.
units.tr: POOR. On their privileges with respect to the gleaning and the corner of the field, see לקט and שכחה. Likewise corner of the field. On the distinction of beggars and the manner of begging, see Beggars. He who hangs up a basket (so that he hides the crumbs from the poor) hangs up his own food, that is, he will become poor. Pesachin iii.2. See Alms. On leaving the grape-gleanings to the poor, see f.1.

units.la: Iudæis visum est perfectionem esse omnia dare pauperibus. Peah cap.i.v.i. Istis rebus non est stata mensura, Angulo agri pauperibus relinquendo, Primitiis, & Comparitioni, (vid. Exod. 23.15.) exhibitione misericordiæ, & studio legis. Glossatores in locum dicunt, non præscribi statam mensuram ad auxiliandum pauperibus corpore tuo, at quoad nummos, aliquem non teneri ex opibus suis dare pauperibus ultra partem quintam, nisi hoc fecerit במרת חסידות Ex extraordinaria devotione; tentat itaque Christus Matt. 19.21. an Pharisæus ad illam perfectionem aspirare velit, quam tantopere laudant sui, non quòd Christianis novam regulam præscribat.
units.tr: The Jews thought it perfection to give everything to the poor. Peah ch. 1 v. 1. For these things no fixed measure is set: the corner of the field left for the poor, first-fruits, and appearance (see Exod. 23.15), the showing of mercy and the study of the law. The glossators on the passage say that no fixed measure is prescribed for helping the poor with one's body; but as to money, no one is bound to give to the poor from his means more than a fifth part, unless he does so במדת חסידות out of extraordinary devotion. Thus Christ tests (Matt. 19.21) whether the Pharisee is willing to aspire to that perfection which his people praise so highly, not because he prescribes a new rule to Christians.

units.la: Pastores pecoris parvi הקה בחמה sunt illiciti ad testimonium dicendum, quia tales gregem suum in aliorum agris pascebant, & ita גולי proximum defraudabant, proinde ille qui חבר religiosus esse voluit, non debuit educare הקה בחמה parvum pecus, sine dubio ne deinde in aliorum praediis illud pascere cogatur. Ex Maym. in Demai ad cap.2.3.
units.tr: Shepherds of small cattle (בהמה דקה) are unfit to give testimony, because such men pastured their flock in the fields of others, and so defrauded their neighbour. Therefore he who wished to be religious ought not to rear small cattle, undoubtedly lest he later be compelled to pasture them on others' estates. From Maimonides on Demai, ch. 2.3.

units.la: Patriarchæ Heb. vocantur ראשי אבות ἀρχηγοὶ πατριάδες Exod.vi.25. Post excidium Hierosolymitanum Iudæi etiam habuerunt Patriarchas in Babylonia, alias Æchmalotarchas nominatos ראשי גליות vel ראשי גלויות ut in Gem.Sanhed. c.1. & ראשי ישיבות ἀρχοντες τῆς παροικίας, quales vidit Benjamin Tudelensis in itin. Roma, Narbona & alibi. Ita Patriarchæ Iudæorum Alexandriam incolentium meminit Hadrianus ad Severianum Cos. apud Vopiscum in Saturnino. Ita præsulem Iudæorum Tiberiade habitantium vocat Patriarcham Epiphan. in diɛp. adversus Ebionit.
units.tr: The patriarchs are called in Hebrew ראשי אבות, [ἀρχηγοὶ πατριάδες], Exod. 6.25. After the destruction of Jerusalem the Jews also had patriarchs in Babylonia, otherwise named Exilarchs, ראשי גליות or ראשי גלויות, as in Gem. Sanhedrin c.1, and ראשי ישיבות [ἄρχοντες τῆς παροικίας], such as Benjamin of Tudela saw in his Itinerary at Rome, Narbonne and elsewhere. So Hadrian mentions the patriarch of the Jews living in Alexandria, in his letter to Severianus the consul, cited by Vopiscus in Saturninus. So Epiphanius, in his letter against the Ebionites, calls the head of the Jews living in Tiberias the patriarch.

units.la: Peccatum. Duo proxenetæ peccati sunt cor & oculus; secundum illud Hierof.Berac. sol.3. c.3. א״ר לוי ליבא ועינא תרין סרסורי דחטאה Dixit R. Levi. Oculus & cor duo peccati proxeneta &c.
units.tr: Sin. The two go-betweens of sin are the heart and the eye, according to that saying in Jerusalem Berakhot, sol. 3 c.3: R. Levi said: the eye and the heart are two go-betweens of sin (א״ר לוי ליבא ועינא תרין סרסורי דחטאה), etc.

units.la: In Chagigah cap.1.v.7. quæritur, quis Eccles. 1.15. vocetur מעוות perversus? R. Manasse respondit esse illum qui ex inceptu genuerit spurium: nam si ad raptorem vel furem referatur, ipsum redire posse & corrigi negari nequit. Secundum Ben Iochai vero perversus vocatur discipulus sapientis a lege recedens, qui ab initio bene institutus postea pervertitur.
units.tr: In Chagigah ch. 1 v. 7 it is asked who is called perverse (מעוות) in Eccles. 1.15. R. Manasseh answered that it is he who from the beginning has begotten a bastard; for if it is referred to a robber or thief, it cannot be denied that he may return and be corrected. According to Ben Iochai, however, the perverse is the disciple of a sage who turns aside from the law, who was well instructed at the beginning but afterwards is perverted.

units.la: Qui quatuor non perpendit ראוי לו כאלו Bene ipsi fuissent si nunquam in mun- דום ... לא נא בעולם dum venissent. Quod supra est, & quod infrà, quod antea fuit, & quod posteà futurū est. Quicunque non par- it gloriae Cre- ationis sui נוחי שלא נברא Melius ipsi fuisset, nunquam creatum fuisse. Si non esset peccatum praevaricationis, non nota esset praestantia condonationis. Mifchar Happenini n.
units.tr: He who does not weigh four things, it would have been better for him if they had not come into the world (ראוי לו כאלו לא נא בעולם): what is above, what is below, what was before, and what will be after. Whoever does not weigh the glory of his Creator, it would have been better for him not to have been created (נוחי שלא נברא). If there were no sin of transgression, the excellence of forgiveness would not be known. Mishchar Happeninim n.

units.la: Non punit Deus hominem donec impleta fuerit Seah eius; extat in Sotah 9.1.
units.tr: God does not punish a man until his seah is full; this is found in Sotah 9.1.

units.la: Tria sunt peccata, à quibus homo nulla die liberatur, cogitationes peccati, יין oculatio (meriti praesumptio,) orationis divagatio, & lingua mala. Bab. Batra f. 134.2.
units.tr: There are three sins from which a man is freed on no day: sinful thoughts; oculation (presumption of merit); wandering of prayer; and an evil tongue. Bab. Batra f. 134.2.

units.la: Pi- tas semper senescit, secundùm illud in Ioma f. 9. 2. prisorum sub templo secundo unguis melior fuit quàm venter posteriorum.
units.tr: Piety always grows older, according to that saying in Yoma f. 9.2: the nails of the earlier men under the second temple were better than the belly of the later ones.

units.la: Illi reputantur in numerum ἀμεψὶ ωλῶν peccatorum apud Iudaeos. Qui sunt aleatores, foeneratores, praedones, publicani, pastores pecorum minutiorum, vendentes fructum anni septimi, pugnis avium lucrum facientes. Sanhed. f. 25. 2.
units.tr: Among the Jews these are counted among the sinners (ἁμαρτωλῶν): gamblers, usurers, robbers, publicans, shepherds of small cattle, those who sell the fruit of the seventh year, and those who make gain by fighting birds. Sanhedrin f. 25.2.

units.la: Qui non potest remittere peccata, ille recipiendus non est Sanhed. f. 38. 2. Gloss. ad haec verba אפיל בפרונקא נמי לא קבלניו Nam eum ne pro nuntio quidem recepimus. Si ille non potest remittere peccata vestra, quid tum ab eo emolumenti? Nam penes eum non erat potestas remittendi peccata nostra, nos ergo eum repudiavimus. Ex circumstantiis elicitur ipsos loqui de Christo, quem magno suo malo repudiarunt.
units.tr: He who cannot remit sins is not to be received. Sanhedrin f. 38.2. Gloss on these words: For we did not even receive him as a messenger. If he cannot remit your sins, what advantage is he to you? For the power of remitting our sins was not with him; we therefore rejected him. From the circumstances it is gathered that they are speaking of Christ, whom they rejected to their great harm.

units.la: אין כור ירא חטא Nullus bardus peccare erubefcit, Pirke avot c.2. הכושת םביא ליד ירא חטא Pudor facit ut quis metuat peccare : Nedar. sol. 20. 1.
units.tr: A boor does not fear sin (אין כור ירא חטא), Pirke Avot ch. 2; shame makes a man fear sin (הבושה מביא ליד ירא חטא), Nedarim sol. 20.1.

units.la: Deus non cogit hominem ut peccet ושמיו sed posuit eum dominium electionis (liberi arbitrii) ut liberaretur à pœnis spiritualibus & corporalibus, & eccc fi non potuisset liberari ab istis, non fuisset æquum ut punitus fuisset propter eà. R. Levi 1.Reg.17 1. Kimchi 1. Reg.18.57. פתש יצרת עקפי cap.8. Doctrina Iudæorum de peccatorum remissione est, illa vel in hac vita per pœnitentiam remitti, vel in fœculo futuro per mortem inflictam à Synedrio. Vid. Hieros. Vid. Sanhed. sol.37.3. & Bab. Ioma f.86.
units.tr: God does not compel man to sin, but has given him the dominion of choice (free will), so that he might be freed from spiritual and bodily punishments; and if he could not be freed from these, it would not be just that he be punished for them. R. Levi on 1 Kings 17.1; Kimchi on 1 Kings 18.57; פתש יצרת עקפי ch. 8. The Jewish doctrine of the remission of sins is that they are remitted either in this life through repentance, or in the age to come through death inflicted by the Sanhedrin. See Hieros.; see Sanhedrin sol. 37.3 and Bab. Yoma f. 86.

units.la: 1. Confer Matth. 12.32.
units.tr: 1. Compare Matt. 12.32.

units.la: §. De Peccato originali quædam diximus apud Infantes. In Sepher Ikkarim lib.4. cap.13. illud ita innuitur. Trahitur pœna peccati in omne semen eius, tam in iustos quam in impios. Vid. etiam Targum Ruth cap.4. v.ult. Cl.Buxt. Lex. Talm. in ארץ יצר הרע Naturæ vitiositatem etiam agnovit R. Alexander ut patet illo dicto, quod in שלום נוח sol.191.2. legitur. R. Alexander posse preces dicere folebat. Domine Mundi, notum tibi est, quod voluntas mea sit, ut faciam voluntatem tuam, quid autem retarda? שאר שבעה fermentum in massa (sive היצר הרע vitiositas naturæ,) quod corrumpit totum hominem.
units.tr: §. We have said some things about original sin under Infants. In Sepher Ikkarim book 4, ch. 13, this is hinted thus: The punishment of sin is drawn over all his seed, both on the just and on the impious. See also Targum Ruth ch. 4, last verse. Buxtorf, Lex. Talm., under יצר הרע. R. Alexander also acknowledged the vitiosity of nature, as appears from the saying read in Shabbat sol. 191.2: R. Alexander used to say in his prayers: Lord of the world, you know that my will is to do your will; but what hinders it? The leaven in the dough (שאר שבעה) (that is, the evil inclination, the vitiosity of nature), which corrupts the whole man.

units.la: Pella urbs Decapolitana, Epiphanius de mensuris & ponderibus cap.15. Olim erat habitata ab Ethnicis. Iosephus Antiq. lib.13. c.23. Moabitica has urbes recuperarunt Iudai H-sbonem, Pellam, illam autem exciderunt, quia incolæ eius recusarunt in patrios mores transformari. Historia est, Christianos ab obsidione & clade Hierosolymae sugisse Pellam: cur illuc se contulerint haec ratio esse potest.Ex textu Iebhamot sol.16.1. & Glossa apparet, terra Ammonitica & Moabitica sanctitatem esse sub templo secundo, & proinde ipsos ibi in anno septimo servere, & angulum agri pro pauperibus relinquere potuisse, & revera reliquisse. Traditio autem communis est excidium Hierosolymitanum contigisse בשביעית in anno septimo; in quo cis Iordanem nec severant nec segetes sponte natas colligere poterant. Nullibi itaque melius pauperculi illi homines & laribus suis deiecti suam sustentationem quam in regione Pella reperire poterant, utpote in qua esset messis & decimatio pro pauperibus.
units.tr: Pella, a city of the Decapolis. Epiphanius, on Weights and Measures, ch. 15. It was once inhabited by Gentiles. Josephus, Antiquities, bk. 13, ch. 23: The Jews recovered from the Moabites the cities Heshbon and Pella, but they destroyed that one, because its inhabitants refused to be transformed to the customs of their ancestors. It is a historical fact that the Christians fled from the siege and destruction of Jerusalem to Pella, and this may be the reason why they betook themselves there. From the text of Yebamot 16a and the Gloss it appears that the land of Ammon and Moab had holiness under the second temple, so that they could there let the fields lie fallow in the seventh year and leave a corner of the field for the poor, and indeed they did leave it. The common tradition, however, is that the destruction of Jerusalem happened in the seventh year, bishvi'it, when on this side of the Jordan they could neither sow nor gather the crops that grew of their own accord. Nowhere, then, could those poor people, driven from their homes, find their sustenance better than in the region of Pella, since there was a harvest there and tithes were set aside for the poor.

units.la: PENTECOSTE vid. Festa.
units.tr: PENTECOST: see Festivals.

units.la: PERA & BACULUM erant usitatissima viatorum instrumenta sive viatica. Addebant religiosires librum.
units.tr: The SCRIP and STAFF were the most common instruments, or provisions, of travellers. Religious men added a book.

units.la: Ievamoth cap.16. v.ult. Profecti sunt Levita quidam Zoarem civitatem palmarum: cumque exiis unus in via aegrotaret, adduxerunt eum ad diversorium. Redeuntes ab hospitio quaesiverunt de collega. Mortuus est,inquit ea,eumque sepelivi. Et paulo post להם הוציאו Ad eos protulit מקלו ותרמילו וספר תורה שבידו : baculum eius, peram eius, atque librum legis, qui fuerat in eius manu.
units.tr: Yevamot ch. 16, end. Some Levites set out for Zoar, the city of palms. When one of them fell ill on the way, they brought him to an inn. Returning from the inn, they asked about their companion. "He is dead," she said, "and I have buried him." And shortly afterwards they brought out to them his staff, his scrip, and the book of the law that had been in his hand. [מקלו ותרמילו וספר תורה שבידו]

units.la: Quid autem תרמיל fit docet Maymon in Kelim cap.16. v.4. תורפ est pera coriacea, quam a collo suo appendunt pastores, in qua viElualia sua reponunt. Idem fermè habet R. Salomoh & Aruch, nisi quod illas non solis pastoribus tribuunt.
units.tr: What a tarmil is, is explained by Maimonides on Kelim ch. 16, v. 4: a tarmil is a leather bag which shepherds hang from their necks, and in which they put their food. Rabbi Solomon and the Aruch say much the same, except that they do not assign these bags only to shepherds.

units.la: Græco ζων respondet Talmudicorum אפונדה quod sic à Glossatore definitur in Bab. Beracot sol.62.2. פונדתו אזור חלול שנותנין בו מעות פונדא Est cingulum cavum in quo repositerunt nummos suos. Aruch dicit אפונדה esse speciem חלוק קשן induisi parvi תפורים בקיסו' הרכה בו יש cui multi loculi sunt affuti, quibus imponunt quicquid obvenit ipsis.
units.tr: The Greek zōnē (belt) corresponds to the Talmudic apundah, which the glossator defines in Bava Berakhot 62b thus: its apundah is a hollow belt in which they put their coins. The Aruch says that an apundah is a kind of small tunic with many pockets sewn on it, in which they put whatever they have received.

units.la: Adducamus nunc alia loca in quibus gestationis baculi, pera, & zonæ mentio fit.
units.tr: Let us now adduce other passages in which mention is made of carrying a staff, a scrip, and a girdle.

units.la: Beracot cap 9.v.5. Ne ingrediatur quis montem templi ולא במנעל בבקלו cum baculo suo ולא nec cum calceis suis, nec נתדו בב cum crumena sua, nec pulvere in pedibus suis. Non debebant enim coram summo numine ut viatores comparere.
units.tr: Berakhot ch. 9, v. 5: No one may enter the mount of the temple with his staff, nor with his shoes, nor with his purse, nor with dust on his feet. For they ought not to appear before the supreme Deity like travellers.

units.la: Bab.Schabb. sol.31. Introducitur Proselytus sic dicens, si Israelita ad sacra veniens moriatur, quanto magis advena שבא בבקלו ותרמיל qui venit cum baculo suo & pera sua.
units.tr: Bab. Shabbat 31. A proselyte is introduced, speaking thus: If an Israelite who comes to the holy things dies, how much more a stranger who comes with his staff and his scrip.

units.la: Bava Batra sol.133.2. Tradunt Rabbini.
units.tr: Bava Batra 133b. The rabbis relate:

units.la: Historia est de homine quodam, cuius filii se bene non gesserunt. Profitit ille, atque opes suas assignavit Ionathani Ben Vziel. Quid fecit Ionathan Ben Vziel? tertiam partem vendidit, tertiam dicavit, & tertiam reddidit filiis defuncti.
units.tr: This is a story about a man whose sons did not behave well. When he was dying, he assigned his goods to Jonathan ben Uzziel. What did Jonathan ben Uzziel do? He sold a third, dedicated a third, and gave a third back to the sons of the deceased.

units.la: Venit ad eum Schammæus (qui erat Vicepræfectus) בבקלו ותרמיל cum baculo suo & pera sua. Gloss. ut cum eo contenderet, quia testatestamentum defuncti violaverat.
units.tr: Shammai (who was vice-prefect) came to him with his staff and his scrip, in the gloss, in order to contend with him, because he had violated the will of the deceased.

units.la: DE BACULO vid. Rofch Hafchana cap. II.
units.tr: On the STAFF see Rosh Hashanah ch. 2.

units.la: PERFECTIONES Iudæorum quomodo paulatim cessaverint Vid. cap.ult. tractSotah. Quædam citata habes in Meffia.
units.tr: On how the privileges of the Jews gradually ceased, see the last chapter of the tractate Sotah. Some cited passages you will find in Messia.

units.la: PESTIS. Si illa in aliquo loco ingruit אותה תעיר ומתרעות ומתענה illius incolæ debent se ieiunii affligere, & tubis clangere, omnesque loci vicini ad ieiunia obligantur sed non ad clangendum. Taanith. cap.3.4. Quærit autem ibi Mifchna איתר דבר quando pestis esse dicitur? חמש עיר חמוציאה מאות רגלי ויצאו ממנה שלשה סתים בשלושה ימים זה אחר זה Quando ex aliquo loco qui 500 pedites educere potest, intra triduum, tres mortui unus post alterum efferuntur.
units.tr: PESTILENCE. If it breaks out in some place, its inhabitants must afflict themselves with fasting and sound the trumpets, and all the neighbouring places are bound to fast, but not to sound the trumpets. Taanit ch. 3, mishnah 4. There the Mishnah asks: When is a pestilence said to be? When from a town which can send out five hundred foot soldiers, three dead are carried out, one after another, within three days.

units.la: Bava Kama sol. 60. 2. בשעת דבר כנוס רגליך tempore pestis collige pedes tuos, contine te domi, & hominum fuge commercium.
units.tr: Bava Kama 60b: In time of pestilence, gather in your feet: keep yourself at home, and flee the company of men.

units.la: PHOENIX de eo vid. Lex. Talm. Buxtorf. pag. 720.
units.tr: PHOENIX: on this see Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 720.

units.la: PHARAO. Miracula quæ Deus fecit Mosi sunt, quòd quidam satellites Pharaonis facti sunt muti, quidam cœci, alii surdi. Debbarim Rabba sol. פתחאו f.290. col.4.
units.tr: PHARAOH. The miracles God worked through Moses included this: some of Pharaoh's attendants became mute, some blind, others deaf. Devarim Rabba, f. 290, col. 4.

units.la: Ialkut Exod. 13. in Parascha בשלח ויאמר Rex quidam dixit servo suo: Ito affer mihi piscem ex foro: Ivit, attulit piscem fœtidum; Tunc Rex, quàm vivis, unum ex his tribus non evades! Aut fœtida comedes, aut centum ictibus fuste vapulabis, aut facultates tuas dabis. Servus dixit comedam fœtida; at cùm tæderet animam eius, dixit; subibo fustigationem, at cùm nec illam ferre posset, dixit, bona mea dabo &c. Sic Pharaoni & Ægyptiis contigit cum decem plagis.
units.tr: Yalkut, Exodus 13, in the parashah Beshallach: A certain king said to his servant: "Go and bring me a fish from the market." He went and brought a stinking fish. Then the king said: "As I live, you will not escape one of these three: either you will eat the stinking fish, or you will be beaten with a hundred blows of the rod, or you will give up your goods." The servant said, "I will eat the stinking fish"; but when it sickened him, he said, "I will submit to the flogging"; but when he could not bear that either, he said, "I will give my goods," and so on. So it happened to Pharaoh and the Egyptians with the ten plagues.

units.la: PHARISÆI. Religiosus stultus, improbus astutus, fœmina Pharisæa, ac illisio Pharisæorum in lapides perdunt mundum; Sotah. cap.3.4. Fœminæ Pharisææ fuerunt virgines & viduæ, sub velo sanctitatis omnem nequitiam exercentes, ut videtur ex Gemara in locum & Gl.
units.tr: PHARISEES. A foolish religious man, a crafty wicked man, a Pharisaic woman, and the dashing of the Pharisees on stones destroy the world. Sotah ch. 3, mishnah 4. Pharisaic women were virgins and widows who practised all wickedness under the veil of holiness, as appears from the Gemara on that passage and from the Gloss.

units.la: Pharisæi sunt האוכלי חוליהן כטהרות Illi qui comedunt communem victum suum in munditia. Gloss. in Chagig.sol.18.2.
units.tr: The Pharisees are those who eat their ordinary food in cleanness. Gloss on Chagigah 18b.

units.la: Pharisæorum septem sectæ sunt, secundùm Hierosol. Beracot folio 13.2. Sotah. folio 20.3. Bab. Sotah. folio 22.2. Aruch in פירוש 1. פרוש שכמי Pharisæus Sichemita. Gloss. qui circuncisus est, sed non in honorem Dei &c. 2. פרוש נקיפי Pharisæus illidens, Gloss. qui ob insignem humilitatem ita incedit, ut nec pedes efferat, ita ut illiderentur pollices pedum ad saxa. 3. פרוש קואי Pharisæus sanguinem eliciens. Gloss. qui ita se præltitit ac si obturatis esset oculis, ne aspiceret fœminam, atque hinc in parietes caput allisit. 4. Pharisæus מדוכיא Mortarii, qui in tunica fluente incedens mortarii instar erat. 5. Pharisæus ארעה מה חובתי ואעשה qui dicit, noscam meum officium & illud faciam. 6. Pharisæus ירא timoris sicuti Iobus. 7. Pharisæus אהבה Amoris sicut Abraham. Hic solus pharisæus est amore dignus. Hieros. cit.
units.tr: According to the Jerusalem Berakhot, folio 13b, the Sotah, folio 20c, and the Babylonian Sotah, folio 22b, there are seven sects of Pharisees. The Aruch, under peirush: (1) the Shechemite Pharisee [שכמי]. Gloss: one who is circumcised, but not for the honour of God, etc. (2) The stumbling Pharisee [נקיפי]. Gloss: one who, from remarkable humility, walks in such a way that he does not lift his feet, so that his toes are struck against the stones. (3) The blood-drawing Pharisee [קואי]. Gloss: one who conducts himself as if his eyes were shut, so that he would not look at a woman, and for this reason dashes his head against the walls. (4) The mortar Pharisee [מדוכיא], who, walking in a flowing tunic, was like a mortar. (5) The Pharisee who says: Let me know my duty, and I will do it. (6) The Pharisee of fear, like Job. (7) The Pharisee of love, like Abraham. He alone is the Pharisee worthy of love. Jerusalem Talmud, loc. cit.

units.la: De Pharisæis egerunt Viri Doctissimi. Hottingerus in suo Thesauro. Leusdenius in Philologo. Cl. Buxt. in Lex.Talm. pag.1851. Cl. Ligifootus Ev.Matth. pag.51.
units.tr: Learned men have treated of the Pharisees: Hottinger in his Thesaurus; Leusden in his Philologus; the learned Buxtorf in the Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 1851; and the learned Lightfoot on Matthew, p. 51.

units.la: Phraseologiæ vid. Formulas loquendi.
units.tr: Phraseology: see Formulas of speech.

units.la: Pisces. Apud Talmudicos mentio fit piscis קולִיף Kolia, quem Thunnum esse existimant; solet salese condiri in vasculis. Schabb.c.22. In Berefchit Rabba Sect. 7. dicitur inter pisces quoque dari כלאים diversa genera quæ copulari non debent. Habebant etiam vivaria piscium. Betza f.23.2. Non capiunt pisces הכיכרים מן è vivariis die festo. Erat & piscis magni nominis qui libra vendebatur cuius nomen בניתא Beza sol.28.1. Bava Kama sol.19.1. Piscículos qui nunquam maiores fiunt, & qui ordinariè nascuntur in luto maris, vocant גלוגה Tamid. cap.3. in fine.
units.tr: Fish. Among the Talmudists mention is made of a fish, Kolia, which they think is the tuna; it is commonly preserved in salt in small vessels. Schabb. c.22. In Bereshit Rabba, Sect. 7 it is said that among fish too there are diverse kinds that ought not be coupled. They also had fish ponds. Betza f.23.2: they do not take fish from the ponds on a festival day. There was also a fish of great renown, sold by the pound, whose name is benita. Beza fol.28.1; Bava Kama fol.19.1. Small fish that never grow larger, and which are commonly born in the mud of the sea, they call gelugah. Tamid ch.3, at the end.

units.la: De Delphino notavit quædam Cl. Buxt. in Lex. Talmud. pag. 545. Tria sunt quæ quando senescunt fiunt fortiora, nempe pisces, serpens, & porcus. Schabbat f.77.2.
units.tr: Cl. Buxtorf noted some things about the dolphin in Lex. Talmud. p.545. There are three things which, when they grow old, become stronger, namely fish, serpent and pig. Schabbat f.77.2.

units.la: De piscium in Babylonia migratione elegantem habent fabulam in Hierof. Taanith sol. 69.2: Septingenta genera piscium mundorum, & octoginta genera locustarum mundarum, & volucrium numerus infinitus migrarunt cum Israele Babylonem, & cum eo redeunte redierunt, excepto pisce שבוע. At quomodo pisces migrarunt? R. Houna Bar Iosephe dicit גלי תהום per viam profundi migrarunt, & per profundum redierunt. Quænam autem illa via profundi sit libenti animo intelligerem.
units.tr: They have a charming tale about the migration of fish to Babylon in Jerusalem Taanith fol.69.2: "Seven hundred kinds of clean fish, and eighty kinds of clean locusts, and an infinite number of birds, migrated with Israel to Babylon, and when it returned, they returned with it, except the fish shabua. But how did the fish migrate? R. Huna bar Yosef says: 'by the way of the deep (galei tehom) they migrated, and through the deep they returned.'" I would gladly learn what that way of the deep is.

units.la: De piscinis quæ circa Hierosolymam vid.: Iosephe. de excidio lib.5.c.13. Vid. etiam Cl. Ligtfooti Chorog. Ioh. pag.33. De Piscatione quædam extant in Bava Kâ-ma f.81.1. Permisit Iosua ut מתכין ביטה של טיבריא indifferenter quivis retia mittat ad piscandum in mare Tiberiadis. At sub hac conditione, ne maceriam aliquam struat, quæ remora sit navigibus; nam ut notat Glossa, Moris iam olim erat piscatoribus sudes figere in aqua, & sepes struere è cannis & calamis, in quibus capiebantur pisces. Apostoli in illo mari retibus proinde in piscando usi sunt.
units.tr: On the pools near Jerusalem see Josephus, On the Destruction, book 5, ch. 13. See also Cl. Lightfoot, Chorographia on John, p.33. Some things about fishing are in Bava Kâma f.81.1. Joshua permitted that anyone indifferently may cast his nets for fishing in the sea of Tiberias. But on this condition: that he not build any wall which would be a hindrance to ships. For, as the Gloss notes, it was already long the custom for fishermen to fix stakes in the water and to build fences of reeds and canes, in which fish were caught. The apostles therefore used nets in fishing in that sea.

units.la: PLAGIARIUS non reus fit strangulationis nisi hominem furto surreptum ad se deduxerit. Sanhed.cap.9. §.1. Si quis furetur eum,qui dimidiâ parte servus, dimidiâ vero parte liber est, non tenetur. Ibid.
units.tr: A kidnapper is not liable to strangulation unless he has led to himself a man stolen by theft. Sanhed. ch.9 §1. If someone steals one who is half slave and half free, he is not liable. Ibid.

units.la: PLANETÆ V. Astrologia. Quivis inter gentiles habet suum מזל יום נativitatis planetam. Qui sub Sole nati sunt, futuri sunt formosi & aperti, sub Venere divites & libidinosi; sub Mercurio memoriâ valentes,& sapientes; sub Luna valetudinarii & inconstantes; sub Saturno infelices,sub Iove iusti, sub Marte felices; Israelitis אין מזל Non est planeta qui eos regat. Schabbat f. 156. 1.Vid.Stellas.
units.tr: PLANETS: see Astrology. Everyone among the gentiles has his planet of the day of birth. Those born under the Sun will be handsome and open; under Venus, rich and lustful; under Mercury, strong in memory and wise; under the Moon, sickly and inconstant; under Saturn, unhappy; under Jupiter, just; under Mars, happy. But for Israelites there is no mazal; there is no planet which rules them. Shabbat f.156.1. See Stars.

units.la: PLATEÆ Hierosolymitanæ. De illis quædam apud Hierosolymam reperies. Platea superior Hierosolymis erat solùm ab alienigenis habitata. Vid. Schekalim cap.8.v.1. Erat etiam platea quæ vocabatur שוק של בשמים Platea macellariorum, item שוק של צמרים Lanariorum Platea, de quibus in Erubbin cap.10. v 9. In platea Macellariorum, occluserunt ostium in Sabbatho ומניחין את המפתח Et reposuerunt clavem in senes. fenestra, quæ erat supra ostium; R. Iose dicit, erat hoc in Platea Lanariorum.
units.tr: PLAZAS of Jerusalem. You will find some things about these at Jerusalem. The upper plaza at Jerusalem was inhabited only by foreigners. See Shekalim ch.8 v.1. There was also a plaza called Platea macellariorum, the Butchers' Plaza, and likewise the Lanariorum Platea, the Wool-workers' Plaza, of which see Erubbin ch.10 v.9: In the Butchers' plaza they closed the door on the Sabbath, and put the key in the window which was above the door; R. Yose says this was in the Wool-workers' plaza.

units.la: Pluviam quæ incipiente Octobri decidit vocant רביעה, rationem illius nomenclationis tradit Bartenora ad Peah cap.8.1. מני שהוא רובע את הרוץ ומוליד ומליחה כופר הרובע את הנקבה: Quia pluvia illa terram inundo illam prægnantem & fertilem reddit, prout fœmella à masculo prægnans fit. Illam pluviam autem distinguunt tripliciter. In רביעה ראשונה Pluviam primam, quæ cadit tertio octobris; רביעה שניה In pluviam secundam, quæ die septimo illius mensis, & in tertiam quæ decimo septimo, vel secundum R. Iehuda vicesimo tertio descendit. Vid. Taanith sol.6.1. Postquam pluvia secunda decidit, licitum est omnibus ad spicilegiū ire Peahc.8.1.
units.tr: The rain that falls beginning in October they call rabiah. Bartenora, on Peah ch.8.1, gives the reason for this name: because that rain soaks the earth and makes it pregnant and fertile, as a female is made pregnant by a male. They distinguish that rain in three ways. The first rain, Pluviam primam, falls on the third of October; the second, in pluviam secundam, falls on the seventh day of that month; and the third, tertiam, falls on the seventeenth, or according to R. Yehuda on the twenty-third. See Taanith fol.6.1. After the second rain has fallen, it is lawful for everyone to go out to gleaning. Peah 8.1.

units.la: De ieiuniis quæ celebrare solebant, si pluvia pro segetibus suo tempore non descenderit, Vid. Ieiunia. de miraculis circa pluviam factis vid. Taanith cap.3 v.8. item sol.5.1. quæ & à Buxt. in Lex.Talm. p.2195. recensentur.
units.tr: On the fasts they used to observe if rain did not come down for the crops at its proper time, see Fasts. On miracles connected with rain see Taanith ch.3 v.8, also fol.5.1, which are listed by Buxtorf in Lex. Talm. p.2195.

units.la: Pœnitentia.
units.tr: Repentance.

units.la: De eius partibus, conditionibus, utilitate & necessitate conscripsit Maymon. tractatum תשובה. De ea etiam tractatur Sanhed. f.97.2.99.1. Ioma f.86.1. Avoth c.4.11. 12.17. Pœnitenti non est exprobranda vita antea acta. Meizia sol.58 2. Vid. etiam Hakspan. Cab.375. Buxt.Synag.Iud cap 25.
units.tr: On its parts, conditions, usefulness and necessity Maimonides wrote a treatise, Teshuvah. It is also treated in Sanhed. f.97.2, 99.1; Ioma f.86.1; Avoth ch.4.11, 12, 17. A penitent is not to be reproached with his former life. Meizia fol.58.2. See also Hakspan, Cab. 375; Buxt., Synag. Iud. ch.25.

units.la: Præcipua dicta de pœnitentia sunt. Magna est pœnitentia, quæ ducit hominem ad folium gloria: Magna est pœnitentia שכרת תגאולה quæ appropinquare facit redemptionem. Magna est pœnitentia, nam propter unum quem facit pœnitentem siam, condonatur ipsi & toto mundo. Pœnitentia est fundamentum mundi, ין&כ & columna eius, nec consistit mundus nisi propter pœnitentiam. Vid. Ioma & Maym.loc.cit.
units.tr: The principal sayings about repentance are these: "Great is repentance, which brings a man to the throne of glory. Great is repentance, which hastens the redemption. Great is repentance, for on account of one man who repents God forgives him and the whole world. Repentance is the foundation of the world and its pillar, and the world does not stand except on account of repentance." See Ioma and Maimonides, loc. cit.

units.la: Pœnitentiæ causâ celebris est אתן רע"ע, ad carnis enim mortificationem, præter reliquam vitæ austeritatem; indutus erat indusio ex pilis caprarum contexto. Schabb. f.56.2.
units.tr: Famous for the sake of repentance is Atan Raʿa, for, besides the rest of his austere life, he wore a garment woven of goats' hair, in mortification of the flesh. Shabbat f.56.2.

units.la: De Charitate quam requisiverunt in pœnitentia loquitur dictum Tanchuma folio 5. col.
units.tr: The charity they required in repentance is spoken of in the saying in Tanchuma, folio 5, col. 2.

units.la: 2. Rediit quidam ad pœnitentiam. Dixit ei uxor ריקה Raca, si statuum est tibi pœnitentiam agere, ipsum quo te accingu cingulum non erit suum.
units.tr: 2. A certain man returned to repentance. His wife said to him, Raca: "If you have resolved to do penance, the girdle with which you gird yourself will not be your own."

units.la: Videtur tamen ad μετάνοιαν pœnitentiam, ipsos præter oralem confessionem non multa alia desiderasse; Maymon in Teschubha cap.
units.tr: It seems, however, that for metanoia, repentance, they asked for little beyond oral confession. Maimonides in Teshuvah ch.

units.la: 1. Præcepta legis, sive præceptiva sive prohibitiva, quicunque transgressus fuerit, sive errans sive prasumens, cum pœnitentiam agit, ac à peccato suo revertitur, confessionem edere tenetur. Quicunque oblationem pro peccato attulerit, expiatum per oblationem non habet peccatum, unde dum oralem edat confessionem. Et quicunque reus est mortis aut flagellationis à Synedrio, non tollitur eius peccatum, per mortem eius aut per flagellationem, si pœnitens non edat confessionem. Hinc quoque quia hircus emissarius est expiatio pro toto Israele, Summus Sacerdos super eo confessionem edit, pro toto Israele.
units.tr: 1. The precepts of the law, whether commands or prohibitions: whoever has transgressed them, whether in error or in presumption, when he does penance and turns from his sin, is bound to make confession. Whoever has brought an offering for sin does not have the sin expiated by the offering unless he also makes oral confession. And whoever is liable to death or flogging by the Sanhedrin, his sin is not removed by his death or by his flogging, if the penitent does not make confession. Hence also, because the scapegoat is an atonement for all Israel, the High Priest makes confession over it on behalf of all Israel.

units.la: Quicquid sit de natura Pœnitentiæ, illam tamen ad Messiæ receptionem necessariam crediderunt. Vid. Sanhed. sol. 98. Kimchi in Esai LIX.16. Quaeritur apud Rabbinos an Israel sit redimendus poenitens an sine poenitentia? Ex Esaia adducuntur loca pro & contra, quae tamen ita reconciliantur; Multos ex Israele poenitentiam ag- alluros, cum signa viderint redemptionis. Clarum de hac re testimonium exstat in Hierof. Taanith sol 64.1.
units.tr: Whatever the nature of repentance, they nevertheless believed it necessary for the reception of the Messiah. See Sanhed. fol.98; Kimchi on Isaiah 59:16. Among the rabbis it is asked whether Israel is to be redeemed penitent or without penitence. Texts from Isaiah are adduced for and against, which are, however, reconciled thus: many of Israel will repent when they have seen the signs of redemption. A clear testimony on this matter exists in Jerusalem Taanith fol.64.1.

units.la: Si Israel resipuerit vel una die, illico adveniet redemptor. Merito proinde Iracurfor Messiae poenitentiam ut sit.
units.tr: "If Israel repents even for one day, the redeemer will come at once." Rightly, therefore, the one named Iracurfor wished the Messiah to come through repentance.

units.la: POLLUTIONES. Vid. Atrium. Item. Immunditia.
units.tr: POLLUTIONS. See Atrium. Likewise Uncleanness.

units.la: POLYGAMIA usi sunt, eadem licentia qua uxorum repudio & dimissione. Maymon in nwr k cap. 10.14. Multas simul uxores habere licet, etiam quotquot velit: at decreverunt sapientes nostri, ne quis ultra quatuor habeat. Ne scilicet pluribus oneratus, eas sustentare nequeat.
units.tr: POLYGAMY was practised with the same license as the repudiation and dismissal of wives. Maimonides in Ishut, ch.10 §14: "It is permitted to have many wives at once, as many as one wishes; but our wise men decreed that no one should have more than four." Namely, so that a man burdened with more could not support them.

units.la: Ante diluvium mos erat unam ducere uxorem prolis gratia, altera vero bibebat poculum sterilitatis. Iarchius ad Genes. IV. 19. Bereschit Rabba sect. 23.
units.tr: Before the flood the custom was to take one wife for the sake of offspring, while the other drank the cup of barrenness. Jarchi on Genes. 4:19. Bereshit Rabba sect.23.

units.la: In Gemara Bab. ad Iebhamot cap. 6. etiam post legem permittunt plures ducere uxores, modo quis supra recitatum Maymonidis temperamentum retinuerit, id est, non plures sumat quam alere poterit. Hanc Iudaeorum sententiam etiam fovent Selden in Uxore Hebraica, & de Iure naturae & gentium Heb. lib. V. cap. 6. Item Grotius de Iure Belli & Pac. lib. II. cap. 5. §. 8, 9.
units.tr: In the Gemara Babylonica on Yevamot ch.6 they allow that, even after the law, many may take wives, provided only that one keeps the moderation of Maimonides recited above, that is, does not take more than he can support. This opinion of the Jews is also favoured by Selden in Uxore Hebraica and in de Iure naturae et gentium Hebraeorum, book 5, ch.6; likewise Grotius in de Iure Belli et Pacis, book 2, ch.5, §§8, 9.

units.la: Locum Malach. II.13. qui de Polygamia sonat, R. David Kimchi ita explicat non quasi ibi sermo esset de Deo creante duo in unam carnem, & hoc demum modo quaerente semen Dei; sed de Abrahamo magno illo Patre, cuius exemplum respectu Hagaris vel Deus objiciat Iudaeis, vel Iudaei Deo. Sed si hoc esset, cur Propheta Abrahamum non diserte nominasset? Cur dixisset unum? cur factum eius excusasset?
units.tr: Kimchi, Rabbi David, explains the passage in Malachi 2:13, which speaks of polygamy, not as if the text were about God creating two into one flesh and so seeking a seed of God in this way. He takes it to be about Abraham, that great Father, whose example in regard to Hagar God either sets before the Jews or the Jews set before God. But if this were so, why would the prophet not have named Abraham plainly? Why would he have said "one"? Why would he have excused Abraham's deed?

units.la: de Pomis citreis. Vid. Festum Tabernaculorum.
units.tr: On citrons. See Feast of Tabernacles.

units.la: Pompeius devicta Iudaea, in ipsa sacraria templi penetravit, & tunc demum notum factum est, vacuam esse sedem & inania arcana. Tacitus. Pompeius omnes cives de gente Cassia ex oraculo quodam suspectos habuit, tandem a nemine Cassio insidiis petitus, sed apud Casium montem, eā ipsa die quā quondam de Mithridate & piratis triumphaverat, caesus periit, & tumulatus fuit. Dion Cassius lib. 24.
units.tr: After Judaea was conquered, Pompey entered the very sanctuaries of the temple, and only then was it made known that the seat was empty and the inner shrine void. Tacitus. Pompey had held all the men of the Cassian family under suspicion because of a certain oracle. At last, though no Cassius attacked him by treachery, he was slain near Mount Casius on the very day on which he had once triumphed over Mithridates and the pirates, and he died and was buried there. Dio Cassius, book 24.

units.la: Porci recensentur inter החזיר pecus parvum, & proinde dedecus erat Iudaeo porcos alere. Hieros. Sekekalim sol. 47.3. R. Ionah erat rubentis admodum faciei, quam videns mulier quaedam sic dixit Domine, Domine aut tu es divoriens, aut foenerator, aut altor porcorum.
units.tr: Swine are counted among the small cattle [החזיר], and so it was a disgrace for a Jew to rear pigs. Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim, p. 47.3. Rabbi Jonah had a very ruddy face, and seeing him a certain woman said: "Lord, Lord, you are either a divorcer, or a usurer, or a breeder of pigs."

units.la: Canone expresso probibitum est porcos alere. Maymon in הלכות cap. 5. Prohibuerunt sapientes ut ut pian nutrire porcos, & canem nisi catena ligatum. Rationes prohibitionis duae sunt, 1. quia prohibitum est pecora minutiora nutrire in Iudaea, qualia sunt porci. 2. quia prohibitum est mercaturam facere rei cuiusvis immundae. Bava Kama c.7.v.7. & Gloss. in illum locum.
units.tr: The prohibition on rearing pigs was laid down as an express rule. Maimonides, in the Laws, chapter 5: The sages forbade rearing pigs in any place, and dogs unless they are kept tied. There are two reasons for the prohibition: (1) because it is forbidden to keep smaller livestock in Judaea, such as pigs; (2) because it is forbidden to trade in any unclean thing. Bava Kamma, chapter 7, section 7, and the Gloss on that place.

units.la: Maledictio prohibitioni addita est. Maymon ubi ante. Dicunt sapientes, maledictus sit qui alit canes & porcos, eo quod ex iis sint nocumenta multa.
units.tr: A curse was added to the prohibition. Maimonides, as above: The sages say, cursed be he who feeds dogs and pigs, because they cause much harm.

units.la: Bava Kama sol. 82.2. & Menachot sol.64.2. recensetur historia belli familiae Asmonea, & quomodo milites Aristobuli indiderint arculae (quam de Muro Hierosolymitano ad sacrificium petendum demiserant) porcum, & qua ratione tunc de novo constitutum sit Quod maledictus sit ille qui alit Porcos.
units.tr: Bava Kamma, page 82.2, and Menachot, page 64.2, record the history of the war of the house of the Hasmoneans, and how the soldiers of Aristobulus put a pig into a chest (which they had let down from the wall of Jerusalem to ask for a sacrifice), and by what reasoning a new rule was then laid down: Cursed be he who feeds pigs.

units.la: Quando itaque legimus in Evangelica historia de porcis, illi qui ipsos aluerunt non erant Judaei, sed Ethnici inter Judaeos habitantes.
units.tr: When therefore we read in the Gospel story about the pigs, those who reared them were not Jews, but Gentiles living among the Jews.

units.la: Sed si Judaei porcos non aluerunt, quid dicemus ad illud in Bab. Taanith sol.21.2. Dixerunt aliquando Rabbi Juda, Pestis est inter porcos. Ille ergo indixit ieiunium. Cur ille doctor de peste porcorum sollicitus fuit, ut etiam ieiunium decerneret, cum tamen ipsos parum curare ob recensitas rationes debuisset. Sed ratio illius ieiunii statim loc. cit. subditur. Timuit Rabbi Judah plagam in unam pecorum speciem infllictam, invasoram etiam omnes.
units.tr: But if the Jews did not rear pigs, what shall we say to that passage in the Babylonian Taanith, page 21.2: Once Rabbi Judah said: "There is a plague among the pigs." He therefore proclaimed a fast. Why was that teacher so anxious about a plague among pigs that he even ordained a fast, when, given the reasons already recited, he ought to have cared little for them? But the reason for that fast is given at once in the same place: Rabbi Judah feared a plague inflicted on one kind of livestock, which would afterwards attack them all.

units.la: Per carnem suillam iam olim Judaeos Ethnici irriserunt, ut hodie adhuc plurimi faciunt. Tanchuma sol.18.col.4. Dixit Ethnicus Israelita, Paratum tibi apud me est esculentum appositissimum. Qualenam illud, inquit alter, Caro suilla. Raca (inquit Judaeus) de bestiis etiam mundis apud vos non comedendum.
units.tr: Through the pork the Gentiles already long ago mocked the Jews, as very many still do today. Tanchuma, page 18, column 4: A Gentile said to an Israelite: "I have a most delicious dish ready for you." "What is it?" said the other. "Pork." "Raca!" (said the Jew) "Among you not even clean beasts are to be eaten."

units.la: Decem Cabi leprarum descenderunt in mundum, novem acceperunt porci. KidduSchin sol. 49. R. Bechai in Pentateuch. sol. 132, col 3. scribit in quibusdam libris Medicinalibus reperiri, infantem fieri leprosum si lac suillum sugat. De Carnibus suillis cur prohibitæ sint Iudæo, disserit etiam Maymon in More→ Nevoch. lib. 3. c. 48.
units.tr: Ten measures of leprosy came down into the world; nine were taken by pigs. Kiddushin, page 49. Rabbi Bechai, in his commentary on the Pentateuch, page 132, column 3, writes that in certain medical books it is found that an infant becomes leprous if it sucks swine's milk. Maimonides, in the Guide of the Perplexed, book 3, chapter 48, also discusses why the eating of pork is forbidden to the Jew.

units.la: Portæ Templi. In muro atrium gentium ambiente erant quinque portæ, Middot cap. 1. v. 3. Porta orientem versus una tantum erat, eaque cognominata porta Sufan, ideo quod in ea sculpta erat figura Sufan Metropoleos Persicæ, in subiectionis signum, (Glossa ad Middot loc. cit.) Vocabatur hæc porta porticus Salomonis, & in ea sessiones suas habuit Sanhedrin cap. 11. in Sanhed. Hanc portam respexit Sacerdos cùm comburebat vaccam rufam, debebat enim sanguinem spargens respicere Sanctum Sanctorum. Parah cap. 3. v. 9. Porta ergo Sufan ne prospectum eius impediret, reliquis portis erat humilior. Middet c. 2. v. 3.
units.tr: The Gates of the Temple. In the wall surrounding the court of the Gentiles there were five gates, Middoth, chapter 1, section 3. The gate facing east was the only one, and it was called the Gate of Shushan, because on it was carved the figure of Shushan, the Persian metropolis, as a sign of subjection (Gloss on Middoth, loc. cit.). This gate was also called the Portico of Solomon, and the Sanhedrin had its seats in it, Sanhedrin, chapter 11. The priest looked toward this gate when he burned the red heifer, for in sprinkling the blood he had to face the Holy of Holies, Parah, chapter 3, section 9. Therefore the Gate of Shushan, so that it would not block the view, was lower than the other gates, Middoth, chapter 2, section 3.

units.la: Ab austro erant duæ portæ, utraque vocata porta Hulda; porticus, latus hoc australe decorans, vocabatur Σὰ ἀπλαυ. Ioseph. Antiq. lib. 15. cap. 4. De Portis Huldæ exstat dictum satis obscurum in Schir Rabba sol. 16. 4. Ecce ille stat post parietem nostrum. Post murum scilicet templi Occidentalem: quia iuravit Sanctus Benedicti. quod ille nunquam destruetur. שער הכהן & porta Sacerdotis (in qua fuit conclave Buleutõn) & porta Hulda nunquam erant destruenda, donec eas renovaturus esset Deus.
units.tr: On the south there were two gates, each called the Gate of Huldah; the portico that adorned this southern side was called the Royal Portico [Στοὰ βασιλική]. Josephus, Antiquities, book 15, chapter 4. There is a rather obscure saying about the Gates of Huldah in Song of Songs Rabbah, page 16.4: Behold, he stands behind our wall. That is, behind the western wall of the temple, because the Holy One, blessed be he, swore that it would never be destroyed. The Gate of the Priest [שער הכהן] (in which was the chamber of the council) and the Gate of Huldah were never to be destroyed until God should restore them.

units.la: Ab occidente erat Porta Kipponi, forte à Coponio procuratore Iudeæ denominata. Idem ibid. lib. 18. cap.1.
units.tr: On the west was the Gate of Kiponi, perhaps named after Cuspius Fadus, the procurator of Judaea. The same, ibid., book 18, chapter 1.

units.la: Ab aquilone erat porta שרי quæ nullius erat usus. Mifnah in Middot. cap.1.
units.tr: On the north was the gate [שרי], which had no use. Mishnah, Middoth, chapter 1.

units.la: Ab Oriente Atrii mulierum erat porta tantum una 'Ωραία dicta Act. iii. 2. & Corinthiaca Iosephi de bello lib. 5. c.14.
units.tr: On the east of the Women's Court there was only one gate, called the Beautiful Gate [Ὡραία], Acts 3:2, and the Corinthian Gate of Josephus, Jewish War, book 5, chapter 14.

units.la: Ab Austro erat etiam porta tantùm una, unaque ab Aquilone. Idem ibid.
units.tr: On the south there was also only one gate, and likewise one on the north. The same, ibid.

units.la: Porta Orientalis atrii Israelis vocabatur Porta Nikanoris, quæ ex auro non erat ut reliquæ Middot c.2. v.3. in illa potum dederunt uxori suspectæ, purificarunt puerperas & leprosos. Sotah. cap.1.v.5. De hac porta vid. Bab.Taanith sol.18.2. Iosephi antiq. lib.12.17. Middot Cl. l'Empereur pag.57. Iuchasin sol.65.2. Sedit in ista Synedrium xxiii. prout alterum in porta Sufan Sanhed. cap.11. v.2. Nulli è portis templi erat מנה scheda postibus affixa, nisi portæ Nicanoris. Bab.Ioma sol.11.1.
units.tr: The eastern gate of the Court of Israel was called the Gate of Nicanor, which was not of gold like the others, Middoth, chapter 2, section 3. At it they gave a drink to the suspected wife, and they purified women after childbirth and lepers, Sotah, chapter 1, section 5. On this gate see Babylonian Taanith, page 18.2; Josephus, Antiquities, book 12, chapter 17; Middoth, Cl. l'Empereur, page 57; Yoma, page 65.2. In this gate the Sanhedrin of twenty-three sat, just as the other one sat in the Gate of Shushan, Sanhedrin, chapter 11, section 2. No gate of the temple had a tablet [מנה] fixed to its posts except the Gate of Nicanor. Babylonian Yoma, page 11.1.

units.la: In latere huius atrii Meridionali erat porta aquarum, sic dicta vel quòd per hanc inferretur aqua in altari libanda in festo Scenopegiæ, aut quòd per illam iret aquæ ductus à fonte Etam in conclave scaturiginis. Vid. Bab. Ioma sol.31. Erant etiam deinde in illo Atrio שער קורבן Porta oblationis, & postea-m שער הרלקת Porta accensionis.
units.tr: On the south side of this court was the Water Gate, so called either because water was brought through it to be poured on the altar at the Feast of Tabernacles, or because through it ran the conduit from the spring of Etam into the chamber of the spring. See Babylonian Yoma, page 31. There were then also in that court the Gate of the Offering [שער קורבן] and afterwards the Gate of the Burning [שער הרלקת].

units.la: A latere Septentrionali erat Porta & Camera Nitsots, Middot cap.1.v.5. ut & Porta בית מוקד de his portis vid. Maymon. in Hal. Beth Habechech. cap 4. circa med. cap.6. sub init. & cap.7. De portis templi & Portariis seu Ianitoribus; Vide plura in voce Levita.
units.tr: On the north side were the Gate and Chamber of Nitsots, Middoth, chapter 1, section 5, and also the Gate [בית מוקד]. On these gates see Maimonides, Laws of the Vessels of the Temple, chapter 4, near the middle, chapter 6 at the beginning, and chapter 7. On the gates of the temple and the gatekeepers or doorkeepers, see more under the word Levite.

units.la: §. Vrbis Hierosolymæ portæ. 1. שער הצאן Probatica porta (Nehem. cap. iii.) erat sita à parte Aquilonis; intus erat Piscina Bethesda sanationibus celebris. 2. שער הדגים Porta Piscium (Sophon. i. 10.) sic dicta à foro piscium, quod erat in ea, sicuti in probatica forum pecorum. 3. שער העופות Porta volucrum, eius facit mentionem R. Salomoh ad cit. loc. Sophon. Erat fortasse porta illa vetus apud Nehem. 3. 6. 4. שער הגיא Porta vallis, quæ cum duabus sequentibus sita erat ab Occidente, ad basin montis Acræ. 5. שער האשפות Porta Esquilina, distabat à præcedente mille cubitis. 6. שער העין Porta fontis, an fontis Siloami vel Draconis ita non patet. Vid. Nehem. l. c. 7. Ab oriente erat porta Aquarum cuius mentio Neh. xii. 37. 8. Porta equorum Nehem. iii. 27. 28. Hierem. xxxi. 40. porta equorum duxit in vallem Hinnomis, porta aquarum in vallem Kedronis. 9. Porta שער הדגה Iudicialis. De porta Ephraim & porta angulari. Vid. 2. Reg. xiiii. 13.
units.tr: §. The gates of the city of Jerusalem. 1. The Sheep Gate [שער הצאן], the Probatic Gate (Nehemiah 3), was situated on the north side; inside it was the Pool of Bethesda, famous for its healings. 2. The Fish Gate [שער הדגים] (Zephaniah 1:10), so called from the fish market which was in it, just as in the Probatic Gate there was a cattle market. 3. The Gate of the Birds [שער העופות]; Rabbi Solomon mentions it at the cited place in Zephaniah. Perhaps it was the old gate in Nehemiah 3:6. 4. The Valley Gate [שער הגיא], which, with the two following, was situated on the west, at the foot of the hill Acra. 5. The Dung Gate [שער האשפות], the Esquiline Gate, was a thousand cubits distant from the preceding. 6. The Fountain Gate [שער העין]: whether it was the gate of the spring of Siloam or of the Dragon is not clear. See Nehemiah, loc. cit. 7. On the east was the Water Gate, mentioned in Nehemiah 12:37. 8. The Horse Gate, Nehemiah 3:27-28. Jeremiah 31:40: the Horse Gate led into the valley of Hinnom, the Water Gate into the valley of Kidron. 9. The Judgment Gate [שער הדגה]. On the Gate of Ephraim and the Corner Gate, see 2 Kings 14:13.

units.la: §. Sub nomine Porta πύλης apud Sacram Scripturam in religione plurima exprimuntur. Gen. xxviii. 17. Psal. cxviii. 19. 20. Matth. vii. 14. xvi 18. Idem fit apud Scriptores Iudaicos. Porta pœnitentiæ memoratur à Chaldæo Paraphraste in Ierem. xxxiii. 6. & porta precum & porta lachrymarum. Bab. Beracot sol. 32. 2. Ex quo excisum est templum, occlusæ sunt ianuæ orationis, & non occlusæ sunt ianuæ lachrymarum. Vid. Defraudatio.
units.tr: §. Under the name Gate (Porta, πύλη), Sacred Scripture expresses many things relating to religion: Gen. 28:17; Ps. 118:19, 20; Matt. 7:14; 16:18. The same usage occurs among the Jewish writers. The gate of repentance is mentioned by the Chaldee paraphrast on Jer. 33:6, and also the gate of prayers and the gate of tears: Bab. Berachot fol. 32.2: From the time the temple was destroyed, the doors of prayer were shut, but the doors of tears were not shut. See Defraudatio.

units.la: Talmudicorum ψψψ optimè redditur per Græcorum Σπλαν πύλαν. De eo mentio fit in Tamid Tamid cap. I. v.3. פתח את השער Clavi aperit ostiolum, atque e Beth Mokad ingreditur in atrium. Aruch שער est porta parva in medio porta magna.
units.tr: The Talmudic shaar (שער) is well rendered by the Greek Spilan pylan [Σπλαν πύλαν]. It is mentioned in Tamid ch. 1, v. 3: He opens the wicket with the key and enters from Beth Mokad into the court. Aruch: a shaar is a small gate within a large gate. [פתח את השער: "he opened the gate"]

units.la: Porticus Salomonis, cuius fit mentio Ioh.x.23. Act. v.12. Erat teste Iosepho Antiq. lib. 15. 14. "Ἐρμῶν ἀξιαφυλάκων τῶν ὑπ' ἰλίῳ Antiq. lib.15. cap. 14. Porticus regalis erat a latere templi meridionali, sub se in muro habens שני שערי חולה duas portas Hulde Middot cap.1. sed non erat porticus Salomonis; illa enim sita erat ad murum templi extimum versus Orientem. Vid. Ioseph Archaiol. lib.20. cap.8. ubi dicitur "Ἀναλωκὴν σοὰν esse "Ἐρμῶν Σολομῶνος". Introeunti itaque in atrium per portam Susan apparebat a dextra laevaque porticus columnis sustentata, duplici ordine dispositis, ita ut fieret duplex ambulacrum. Atque intra vel circa hanc porticum erant חנויות Tabernae, ubi vendebantur sal, oleum, thus, aliaque altari necessaria.
units.tr: Solomon's Portico, mentioned at John 10:23 and Acts 5:12. According to Josephus, Antiq. book 15, ch. 14, it was the royal portico on the south side of the temple, which had beneath it in the wall the two gates of Hulda (Middot ch. 1). But it was not Solomon's Portico, for that was situated along the outer wall of the temple toward the east. See Josephus, Archaeol. book 20, ch. 8, where the [Greek] is said to be Solomon's Portico. Thus, for one entering the court through the Susan Gate, there appeared on the right and left a portico supported by columns, arranged in a double row, so that there was a double walkway. In or around this portico were the shops (chanuyot), where salt, oil, incense and other things needed for the altar were sold.

units.la: §. In Porticu templi contignationibus erant infixae catenae aureae, quarum ope Sacerdotes iuniores ascendebant ad coronas quae in fenestris conclavium supra contignationem suspensae erant. In porta porticus expansa fuit vitis aurea, erigebaturque super canterios; quicunque folium aut uvam vovebat, illic eam suspendebat Middot cap.3. v.8.
units.tr: In the portico of the temple, golden chains were fixed to the beams, by means of which the younger priests climbed up to the crowns hung in the windows of the chambers above the beams. In the gate of the portico a golden vine was spread out, raised above the pillars; whoever vowed a leaf or a grape hung it there. Middot ch. 3, v. 8.

units.la: Prandendi tempus apud לוריח (an Lyddenses vel Antropophagi intelligantur diiudicet lector) hora prima; hora secunda vero est tempus prandendi latronum; tertia haeredum, quarta operariorum, quinta omnium hominum. Schabbat folio 10. 1.
units.tr: The time for dining among the [Lydians?] (let the reader judge whether Lyddenses or cannibals are meant) is the first hour; the second hour is the dining time of robbers, the third of heirs, the fourth of workers, the fifth of all men. Shabbat fol. 10.1.

units.la: De Præceptis affirmativis & negativis vid. Buxt. Synag. Lex Talm. sol. 1114.
