units.tr: On affirmative and negative precepts see Buxtorf, Synagoga, and Lex Talmudica, p. 1114.

units.la: Præceptores olim sedentes discipulis stantibus docebant & prælegebant: qui mos honorificus, ad mortem Gamalielis Senioris continuatus, tunc periit, eoúsque ut sederent etiam discipuli, sedente Magistro, hinc illud Sotah 9. hal. 15. Ex quo obiit Rabban Gamaliel Senex, pe-rit honor legis, & mortua est puritas, & Pharisaismus: ubi Glossa ex Megillah. Ante eius mortem fuit sanitas in Mundo, & non didicerunt legem nisi stando; ast eo defuncto, descendit agritudo in mundum, & coactli sunt discere legem sedendo.
units.tr: Teachers once sat while their disciples stood and were taught or read aloud to. This honorable custom continued until the death of Gamaliel the Elder, and then perished, so that even the disciples sat while the master sat. Hence Sotah 9, hal. 15: From the time Rabban Gamaliel the Elder died, the honour of the Law perished, and purity died, and Pharisaism. Where the gloss from Megillah says: Before his death there was health in the world, and they did not learn the Law except standing; but when he died, sickness descended into the world, and they were compelled to learn the Law sitting.

units.la: De discipulis Sapientum vid. suo loco. in D.
units.tr: On the disciples of the wise, see in its place under D.

units.la: Synedrium vigesies quater quosdam excommunicavit qui suos Rabbinos vel præceptores debito honore non afficerant. Bab. Beracot sol. 19. 1. vid. etiam Rabbi.
units.tr: The Sanhedrin excommunicated twenty-four people who had not shown their Rabbis or teachers the proper honour. See Bab. Beracot fol. 19. 1; also see Rabbi.

units.la: PRAEFECTI Templi vid. Officiarii.
units.tr: PREFECTS of the Temple: see Officers.

units.la: PRAEPUTIUM Vid. Circuncisio. De attractione præputii cuius mentio fit 1. ad Corinth. 7. 18. V. Cl. Buxt. Lex. Talm. pag. 1274.
units.tr: FORESKIN: See Circumcision. On the drawing back of the foreskin, which is mentioned in 1 Cor. 7. 18, see the most learned Buxtorf, Lex. Talm. p. 1274.

units.la: PRAESTIGIAE Vid. Magiam.
units.tr: MAGIC TRICKS: see Magic.

units.la: PRECES off-rendæ sunt versus Sanctum Sanctorum, & ab exulibus Iudæis versus terram Israeliticam. Beracot cap. 4. sol. 30. 1. Maymon Hal. Tephil. cap. 5. sol. 42. 1. Orach Chaijm Num. 94. Schulchan Aruch Num. eod. sol. 40. Vt autem illuc orans respicere possit, requiritur ut camera fenestras habeat quæ versus urbem Sanctam aperiri possint. Berac. c. 5. f. 13. a. & 34. b.
units.tr: Prayers are to be offered facing the Holy of Holies, and by Jews in exile facing the land of Israel. Berachot ch. 4, fol. 30.1; Maimonides, Hal. Tephil. ch. 5, fol. 42.1; Orach Chaijm num. 94; Schulchan Aruch num. 40 of the same. So that one praying there may look toward it, a room needs windows that can be opened toward the Holy City. Berachot ch. 5, fol. 13a and 34b.

units.la: Iudæi Babylonienses non solùm orarunt in כנסיות S. nagogis, sed aliquando etiam iverunt לעליית דרניאל in (onclave Danielis, quod secundùm Beniamin Bar Iona, qui vixit anno 933. sive æræ nostræ 1173. erat in veteri quadam lapidea domo, quam ipse Propheta ædificaverat. Vid. Iuchasin sol. 131. Tsemach David sol. 55.
units.tr: Babylonian Jews prayed not only in the synagogues but sometimes also went to the upper room of Daniel (לעליית דניאל). According to Benjamin of Tudela, who lived in 933 or in the year 1173 of our era, this was in an old stone house which the prophet himself had built. See Iuchasin fol. 131; Tsemach David fol. 55.

units.la: In templo & Synagogis orabant stantes, Hierof. Beracot sol. 20.1. Ingreditur quis in Synagogam ובמצאן עוברין לתפלת invenitque illos stantes in oratione. Maymon Hal. Tephill. cap. 5. Sequentia oraturus observare debet, stare, faciem suam templo obvertere, componere decenter corpus suum, ut & vestimenta: constituere locum suum, ordinare vocem suam, incurvare se & adorare.
units.tr: In the temple and synagogues they prayed standing. Jerusalem Berachot fol. 20.1: One enters a synagogue and finds them standing in prayer (ובמצאן עומדין לתפלת). Maimonides, Hal. Tephill. ch. 5: One who is about to pray must observe the following: stand, turn his face toward the temple, compose his body decently, as also his garments; set his place, order his voice, bow down and worship.

units.la: Corpus autem ita concinnare debet. Pedes suos æqualiter unùm apud alterum disponet, oculos suos versus terram demittet, cor verò elevet sursum: manum imponet peɛtori, dexteram supra sinistram, ut servus stare solet coram Domino suo, omni reverentiâ & decore.
units.tr: He ought to compose his body in this way: he shall set his feet evenly, one beside the other; he shall lower his eyes to the ground but raise his heart upward; he shall lay his hand on his breast, right over left, as a servant usually stands before his lord, with all reverence and decorum.

units.la: In Precibus fugienda Battologia, non agendum ut stulti quidam homines faciunt, qui in orationibus, multa elogia, epitheta, verba, Rythmos & carmina componere & congerere solent, quæ si hominem aliquem respicer nt, dignitatem eius imminuerent, atque iis ad Deum, ut sibi imaginantur, appropinquare satagunt. Maymon. More Nevoch. l. 59.
units.tr: In prayers, vain repetition (battologia) must be avoided, and one should not do as some foolish men do, who in their prayers are accustomed to compose and heap up many eulogies, epithets, words, rhythms and songs, which, if they were addressed to some human being, would diminish his dignity; yet they strive to approach God with them, as they imagine. Maimonides, More Nevoch. l. 59.

units.la: De Precibus in cultu quotidiano faƈtis vid. Cultum quotid. Preces piorum sunt כעיר i star pala, ut hæc vertit frumentum de loco in locum; sic illæ vertunt proprietates Dei, ex iracundia v. 9. in Misericordiam. Ievamot f.64.r. Isaac dicitur אתרא דהפיך ארא vertens granarium, quasi precibus vertens fatum divinum, f. d. Gen. 25. 21. Berefchit Rabba Sect.36.2. Orationis שחרית matutinae author est Abraham; illius quae tempore oblationis minchae fundenda Isaac. Orationis vespertinae ערבית Iacob. Maymon Hal.Melachim c.9.
units.tr: On prayers made in the daily worship, see Cultus quotidianus. The prayers of the pious are like grain moved from place to place (כעיר); so they turn the attributes of God from wrath (v. 9) to mercy. Ievamot f. 64r. Isaac is called one who turns the granary (אתרא דהפיך ארא), as if by prayer he turned the divine decree, f. d. Gen. 25:21; Bereshit Rabba sect. 36.2. The author of the morning prayer (shacharit) is Abraham; of the prayer to be poured out at the time of the minchah offering, Isaac; of the evening prayer (arvit), Jacob. Maimonides, Hal. Melachim ch. 9.

units.la: De תפילין quae oraturi sibi applicant vid. suo loco. De decem nominibus precum vid. Devarim Rabba sect.23. Plantavic. Fl. Bibli.1394. Cofri 171. De efficacia orationis, praesertim publicae vid. Cofri pag.160. 82.
units.tr: On the tefillin which those who pray apply to themselves, see in its place. On the ten names of prayers, see Devarim Rabba sect. 23; Plantavit, Flor. Bibl. 1394; Cosri 171. On the efficacy of prayer, especially public prayer, see Cosri pp. 160, 82.

units.la: Orationis Dominicae petitiones petitae sunt ex antiquiore Leiturgia.
units.tr: The petitions of the Lord's Prayer were taken from an older liturgy.

units.la: Christus nos iubet orare in numero plurali; fuit hic etiam canon in Bab.Berarot sol.30 1. לעולם לישתף אינש נפשיה כהדי ציבורא Orantem oportere semper, cum orat, se cum Ecclesia consociare. Quod non stricte intelligendum est solum de praesentia sua in Synagoga, sed ut ubicunque terrarum positus, etiam cum solus preces suas effundat numero plurali. Sic enim explicat Glossa אל יתפלל ה"ק בלשון יחיד אלא בלשון רבים Ne oret quis orationem brevem (i.e. aliam à precibus statis) numero singulari, sed plurali.
units.tr: Christ bids us pray in the plural number. There is also this rule in Bab. Berachot fol. 30.1: A man must always, when he prays, associate himself with the congregation (לעולם לישתף אינש נפשיה כהדי ציבורא). This is not to be understood strictly only of one's presence in the synagogue, but that wherever on earth a person is placed, even when he pours out his prayers alone, he should do so in the plural number. For so the gloss explains: One should not pray a brief prayer (i.e., one other than the fixed prayers) in the singular number, but in the plural.

units.la: Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς est notissimum apud Iudaeos Dei Epithethon. Maymon in Tephillot אבינו שבשמים Pater noster qui es in coelis, sic nobiscum agas sicuti promisisti per Prophetas. In Sotah cap.9.15. Ter hoc recitatur. Quemnam habemus cui innitamur? על אבינו שבשמים Super
units.tr: Our Father who art in heaven (Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς) is the best-known epithet of God among the Jews. Maimonides, in Tephillot: Our Father who art in heaven, deal with us as you promised through the prophets (אבינו שבשמים). In Sotah ch. 9, fol. 15, this is recited three times: Whom have we to lean upon? Upon Our Father who is in heaven.

units.la: per.
units.tr: Through

units.la: Patri vestro qui est in cœlis non dedistis, sed mihi Sacerdoti.
units.tr: "Your Father who is in heaven": you did not give it, but to me, the priest.

units.la: ΕΛΑΣΙΤΩ ἡ βασιλεία σου. Axioma hoc obtinuit.: בל ברכה שאין כה מלכות אינה ברכה Ista oratio in qua non est memoria regni Dei, non est oratio. Bab.Berac. sol 40.2.
units.tr: Let your kingdom come (ἐλθάτω ἡ βασιλεία σου). This maxim prevailed: Any prayer in which there is no mention of the kingdom of God is not a prayer (בל ברכה שאין בה מלכות אינה ברכה). Bab. Berachot fol. 40.2.

units.la: Γεωσ ... Confer illud in Bab. Berac. sol.29.2. Quanam est oratio brevis? R. Eliezer dicit עשה רצונך בשמים Voluntatem tuam fac in cœlis, & dato quietem spiritus,timentibus te infrà, i.e. in terris.
units.tr: Compare what is said in Bab. Berachot fol. 29.2: What is a short prayer? R. Eliezer says: "Do your will in heaven, and give rest of spirit to those who fear you below", i.e., on earth (עשה רצונך בשמים).

units.la: Τὸν ἀρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον. Bab. Beracot ubi suprà. Necessitates populi tui Israelis sunt multæ, & cognitio ipsorum tenuis (ita ut non noriñt necessitates suas patefacere) sit beneplacitum tuum, ut des unicuique כדי פרנסתו quod sufficit in alimentum.
units.tr: "Our daily bread" [τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον]. Babylonian Berachot, as above. May it be your good pleasure: your people Israel has many needs, and its knowledge is slight, so that it does not know how to set out its needs. Grant to each one what suffices for his sustenance [kedei parnasato].

units.la: Ῥῦσαί ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ. Beracot sol. 16.2. R. Iudah sic solitus fuit precari. Sit beneplacitum tuum, ut liberes nos ab impudentibus & impudentia, ab homine malo, & occursu malo, ab effectu malo, à socio malo, à vicino malo, à Satana destruente, à Iudicio duro, & adversario duro.
units.tr: "Deliver us from evil" [Ῥῦσαί ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ]. Berachot 16.2. R. Judah was accustomed to pray thus: May it be your good pleasure to free us from the shameless and from shamelessness, from an evil man and an evil encounter, from an evil outcome, from an evil companion, from an evil neighbour, from the destroying Satan, from a harsh judgment and a harsh adversary.

units.la: Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία Vid. Amen in A.
units.tr: For yours is the kingdom [Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία]. See Amen under A.

units.la: Quæritur cur Christus discipulos suos orare docuerit, cùm iam alias preces sciverant? Respondetur Doctoribus Iudæorum usitatum fuisse, orationculorum formulas sibi ipsis struere, discipulisque suis tradere. Vid. exempla in Gemara Babylonica ad tractatum Beracot. Illas autem proponebant tanquam additicias ordinariis, & conclusivas, non autem ut stataspreces illis enervarent. De precibus illis addititiis loquuntur in Bab.Berac: sol.16.2. אליעור ר' R. Eliefer cùm orationes suas finisset, sic dicere est solitus, sit beneplacitum tuum, Domine, ut habitet in sorte nostra amor & fraternitas &c. R. Iochanan cùm finisset orationes suas, sic dicere est solitus, sit beneplacitum tuum Domine, ut observet contumeliam nostram.
units.tr: It is asked why Christ taught his disciples to pray, since they already knew other prayers. The answer is that it was customary among the Jewish teachers to compose short formulas of prayer for themselves and hand them on to their disciples. See examples in the Babylonian Gemara on the tractate Berachot. They offered these, however, as additions to the fixed prayers, and as concluding ones, not so as to weaken the fixed prayers by them. The additional prayers are spoken of in Berachot 16.2. R. Eliezer, when he had finished his prayers, was accustomed to say: May it be your good pleasure, Lord, that love and brotherhood dwell in our portion, etc. R. Iochanan, when he had finished his prayers, was accustomed to say: May it be your good pleasure, Lord, that you observe our reproach.

units.la: Cùm Christus discipulis suis illam orationem præscriberet, Iudæi statas preces numero octodecim habuerunt. Hierof.Taanith sol.65.3. Preces quotidianæ sunt octodecim, pro numero octodecim Psalmorum, &c. Vid. etiam Bab. Beracot sol. 28.2. ubi dicitur Simeonem הפקולי Pekolaum in ordinem redegisse octodecim orationes seriatim: coram Rabban Gamaliele in Iafne. Ita tamen, ut ipsis etiam brevis istarum precum epitome adesset, quâ uti posset ille, cui in promptu non erat omnes illas numerosas preces memoriter recitare; hanc summulam vocarunt מעין. Bab.Beracot ubi supra. Dixit R.Gamaliel, unoquoque die oret unusquisque octodecim orationes; R.Iofua dicit, יתפלל מעין יח Oret summulam istarum octodecim. R. Akiba dicit, si expedita sit oratio in ore eius, oret octodecim, sin minus oret summulam istarum octodecim. Talem summulam imitatus est Salvator noster, comp ingendo omnium orationum medullam in paucissimas lineas. De Orationis Dominicæ partibus in veterum Liturgia exstantibus, vid.Sanhed.f 42.1. Selaen.
units.tr: When Christ prescribed that prayer to his disciples, the Jews had fixed prayers, eighteen in number. Jerusalem Taanit 65.3: The daily prayers are eighteen, corresponding to the number of the eighteen Psalms, etc. See also Babylonian Berachot 28.2, where it is said that Simeon Pekolaum arranged the eighteen prayers in order, in the presence of Rabban Gamaliel at Jabneh. Yet there was also a brief summary of these prayers, which a person could use if he could not recite all those numerous prayers from memory. They called this little summary [מעין]. Babylonian Berachot, above: R. Gamaliel said, each day let each person pray the eighteen prayers; R. Joshua says, let him pray the summary [מעין] of the eighteen; R. Akiba says, if his prayer comes readily to his lips, let him pray the eighteen, but if not, let him pray the summary of these eighteen. Our Saviour imitated such a summary, compressing the marrow of all the prayers into a very few lines. On the parts of the Lord's Prayer found in the liturgies of the ancients, see Sanhedrin 42.1. Selaen.

units.la: Selden. de Or. Eutych. 41. Mufar 49.1. & 78. 2. Machfor Hifpan. 1.142.129.143. Machfor Germ. 10. 6.
units.tr: Selden, de Or. Eutych. 41. Mufar 49.1 and 78.2. Machfor Hispan. 1.142.129.143. Machfor Germ. 10. 6.

units.la: §. Hypocritis exprobrat Christus quòd ament in Synagogis angulis, & Plateis stantes orare. 1. Orabant in Synagogis quia ipsis persuasum erat preces Synagogæ certò exaudiri. Tanchum.sol.35.1. Pergit ad Synagogam ad orandum. Hierof. Beracot sol.2.1. Quare recitant Phylacteria in Synagoga? &c. Raabenu A'ch r in Beracot sol. 69. 3. Cùm quis vespere ab agro fe domum confert, primò fe conferat ad Synagogam, & filegere potest, legat quid, deinde recitet phylacteria & precetur. Christus non improbat morem hunc in Synagogis orandi, ipsemet enim illis precibus interfuit; sed redarguit quorundam consuetudinem, quâ vanam gloriam venantes, preces privatas & à Synagoga discretas mussitabant, qualis fuit R. Nechoniæ Ben Hakana in Beracot cap.4.2. qui in ingressu & egressu Synagogæ præter solitum morem, breves orationculas dixit. Quales etiam fuerunt illi qui inceptis iam publicis & ordinariis precibus Synagogam ingrediebantur, & nihilominus suas preces recitabant ab initio, ne nihil neglexisse viderentur; quæ recitatio etiam nunquam non facta est; cum insigni præcipitatione, quoniam cum reliquis finita oratione Amen dicere debebant. Vid. Hierof Beracot sol.8.3. 2. Quòd orationes ipsorum in Publicis angulis & plateis attinet, erant illæ duplicis generis; vel publicæ vel personarum privatarum; de publicis precibus in plateis factis sonant sequentia loca. Maymon in Tephillah c. 11. Orabant in Plateis in festis & publicis ieiunii. Taanith cap.2.v.1.2. Quisnam ritus ieiuniorum? Arcam produxerunt in plateas urbis, cineremque sparserunt in arcam ftetterunt orantes&c. Vide etiam Maymon. in Taanith cap.3. Quamvis illæ omni plane hypocrisi non caruerint, non tamen illas primario redarguit Christus, sed tantum preces personarum privatarum, qualis fuit R. Iannai in Hierof.Berac.f.8.3. Dixit Rabbi Iochanan, vidi ego R. Iannai stantem atque orantem in plateis Tfipporis, & progredientem ad quatuor cubitos atque orantem orationem addititiam. Præextextum & occasionem se ita oftentandi dederunt ipsimet Canones Iuris Hebræorum, quando de precum tempore loquuntur. Volunt enim ut unusquisque phylacteria sua recitet accuratè appropinquante tempore, insidens asino descendat & recitet, operarii recitent suas preces vel in culmine arboris. Vid. Beracot cap.1.2.3.4. flatuosi itaque homines libenter à tempore precum in plateis deprehendebantur, ut se ostendere possent. His adde, Christum etiam respicere potuisse ad duplicem in precibus ipsorum excessum, in quibus non parva latebat Hypocrisis. Prior erat, quòd uterentur longissima pausatione ante & post finitas orationes, ita ut aliquando per tres horas conspicerentur in habitu precatorio positi. Vid. Bab.Beracot sol.30.2. & 32.2. cap.5. hoc exstat. Preces non incipiunt nisi [Hebrew: מחוך כובד ראש] Ex reverentia animi. Sancti prisci post hora moram precabantur, ut animum ad Deum intendere possent. Et deinde ita attenti fuerunt, ut nec regi eos salutantes respondissent.
units.tr: §. Christ reproaches the hypocrites for loving to stand and pray at the corners of the synagogues and in the streets. (1) They prayed in the synagogues because they were persuaded that the prayers of the synagogue were certainly heard. Tanchuma 35.1: He goes on to the synagogue to pray. Jerusalem Berachot 2.1: Why do they recite the phylacteries in the synagogue? etc. Rabbeinu Asher on Berachot 69.3: When someone returns home from the field in the evening, let him first go to the synagogue, and if he is able to read, let him read something, then recite the phylacteries and pray. Christ does not disapprove of this custom of praying in the synagogues, for he himself took part in those prayers; but he rebukes the habit of some who, hunting after vainglory, muttered private prayers apart from the synagogue, such as R. Nehunia ben Hakana in Berachot ch. 4.2, who, on entering and leaving the synagogue, contrary to his usual custom, said brief little prayers. Such too were those who, when the public and ordinary prayers had already begun, entered the synagogue and nevertheless recited their own prayers from the beginning, lest they seem to have neglected anything. This recitation too was always done with remarkable haste, since they had to say Amen together with the rest when the prayer was finished. See Jerusalem Berachot 8.3. (2) As for their prayers at public corners and streets, these were of two kinds: either public, or those of private persons. The following passages speak of public prayers made in the streets. Maimonides, Tefillah ch. 11: They prayed in the streets on feast days and on public fast days. Taanit ch. 2 v. 1–2: What is the custom of fasts? They brought the ark out into the streets of the city, sprinkled ashes on the ark, and stood praying etc. See also Maimonides, Taanit ch. 3. Although those prayers were not wholly free of hypocrisy, Christ does not chiefly rebuke them, but only the prayers of private persons, such as that of R. Yannai in Jerusalem Berachot f. 8.3: Rabbi Iochanan said, I saw R. Yannai standing and praying in the streets of Tsippori, and walking four cubits and praying an additional prayer. The canons of Hebrew law themselves, when they speak of the time of prayer, gave the pretext and occasion for such display. For they want each person to recite his phylacteries carefully as the time approaches: sitting on a donkey, let him dismount and recite; labourers should recite their prayers even from the top of a tree. See Berachot ch. 1–4. Vain men therefore gladly let themselves be caught in the streets at the time of prayer, so that they could show themselves. Add to this that Christ may also have had regard to the double excess in their prayers, in which no small hypocrisy lay hidden. The first was that they used very long pauses before and after their prayers, so that sometimes they were seen for three hours in a posture of prayer. See Babylonian Berachot 30.2 and 32.2; ch. 5 contains this: Prayers do not begin unless [מתוך כובד ראש] in gravity of mind. The holy men of old waited an hour before praying, so that they could direct their minds to God. And then they were so attentive that they did not even answer the king when he greeted them.

units.la: Posterior quod in excessum formare soliti sint eiaculationes, preces, benedictiones, ex occursu cuiuslibet rei, sive illud fuerit publice vel privatim. Hierof. Avoda Zarah sol. 40. 1. Rabban Gamaliel ambulans in atrio gentium, vidit foeminam Ethnicam, ac ei benedixit; De benedictionibus varia habes apud Benedictiones.
units.tr: The second was that they were accustomed to pour out ejaculations, prayers and blessings to excess, on the occasion of anything that met them, whether in public or in private. Jerusalem Avodah Zarah 40.1: Rabban Gamaliel, walking in the court of the Gentiles, saw a heathen woman and blessed her. On blessings you will find various things under "Benedictiones".

units.la: §. Adiungamus breviter quaedam de precibus in genere.
units.tr: §. Let us briefly add some things about prayers in general.

units.la: Oratio matutina fieri potest usque ad meridiem, Oratio vero Minchæ usque ad vesperam, Beracot cap. 4. 1. Qui preces ut pensum respicit, oratio illius minime supplex est. Ibid. v. 4. Preces illius qui inter pericula versatur hæ sunt: הושיעה״ את עמך את ישראל בכל פרשת העיבור יהיו צרכיהם לפניך Salva Domine populum tuum Israelem, omnibus momentis sint necessitates ipsorum coram oculis tuis. Preces additiciæ non nisi cum Doctore urbis faciendæ sunt. Ibid. v. 7. Si quis erraverit inter precandum סיון דע לו Malum ei portendit. Si legatus fuerit, portentum malum est iis, qui ipsum miserunt. Beracot. cap. 5. 5. Preces vanæ sunt, si quis deprecatur, quod iam praeteritum est, ut si quis uxore iam gravida dixerit. Faxit Deus, ut uxor mea masculum pariat. Beracot. c. 9.
units.tr: Morning prayer may be said until midday, but the afternoon prayer (Minchah) until evening. Berachot ch. 4.1. He who regards prayer as a task, his prayer is by no means supplicating. Ibid. v. 4. The prayer of one who is in dangers is this: Save, Lord, your people Israel; in every critical moment let their needs be before your eyes. Additional prayers are to be said only with the teacher of the city. Ibid. v. 7. If someone makes a mistake while praying, let him know that evil is portended for him. If he is a messenger, it is an evil omen for those who sent him. Berachot ch. 5.5: Prayers are vain if someone prays for what is already past, as when someone whose wife is already pregnant says: May God grant that my wife bear a male. Berachot ch. 9.

units.la: Omnis multiplicans orationes exauditur Hierof. Taanit f. 67. 3 ubi videt ipsos existimasse repetitionibus inesse quandam vim, ut Deus ipsas citius audiat; Christus quando reprehendit battologias, non tam intelligit, nudas earundem petitionum reiterationes, quàm hanc ipsorum opinionem, de virtute repetitionum, quasi illæ apud Deum plurimùm valêrent.
units.tr: Everyone who multiplies prayers is heard. Jerusalem Taanit f. 67.3, where you see that they thought there was a certain power in repetitions, so that God would hear them the sooner. When Christ censures vain repetitions, he means not so much the bare reiteration of the same petitions as this their opinion about the power of repetitions, as if these counted for much with God.

units.la: Qui orat ןיכרצ שיך incurvare se debet usquedum conspiciantur omnes vertebræ quæ sunt in spina dorsi. Beracot sol.28.2. tam profundè se incurvare debet, ut vidêre possit assarium è regione cordis sui.
units.tr: He who prays must bend himself until all the vertebrae in the spine can be seen. Berachot 28.2: he must bend so deeply that he can see a small coin opposite his heart.

units.la: Religiosi Prisci insumserunt unoquoque die novem horas immorando precibus, Bab. Beracot sol.32.2. Prolixa oratio vitam protrahit. Ibid. sol.54.2.
units.tr: The men of old spent nine hours each day in prayer. Bab. Beracot sol.32.2. A long prayer prolongs life. Ibid. sol.54.2.

units.la: Elias extracto gladio confodit illum, qui inter orandum tergum Sanctuario obvertit; facies enim non posteriora versus templum vertenda sunt. Beracot sol.6.2.
units.tr: Elijah drew his sword and struck down the man who, while praying, turned his back on the Sanctuary, since one must not turn the face toward the temple and the back toward it. Beracot sol.6.2.

units.la: PRIMITIÆ. Lege divina cautum est, ut offerretur Manipulus primitialis secundâ die Hebdomadæ Paschalis. Lev. xxiii. 10. 11. ubi R. Salomoh מסח ממחרת יום טוב הראשון של פסח Crastinâ à prima die festi Paschatis. Quær. autem num segetes maturæ fuerint ad festum Paschatis? Satio hordei fuit illicò post medium mensem Marcheswan, id est, circa ineuntem Novembrem nostrum. B. Beracot sol. 18. 2. Audivit semen ad pluviam primam satum grandine perditum, ivit ille, & seminavit ad pluviam secundam &c. Pluvia prima erat decimâ septimâ die mensis Marcheswan. Secundâ die eiusdem mensis vicesimo tertio. Quod si cùm iustum adventaret tempus Paschatis, hordea non maturuerant, addito ad annum istum mense emboly-mæo, mæo, exspe&atum est, ufquedum maturescerent. Vid. Intercalatio & Maymon in Kiddufch Chodefch cap. 4. & quòd re ipsa aliquando annum intercalarint ob hanc necessitatem apparet ex Hierof. Maaser Scheni sol.56.3. Sanhed. sol.18.4. Bab. Sanhed. sol.11.2. ubi hoc exstat diploma Synedrii. Rabban Gamaliel cum senioribus Synedrii magni, fratribus nostris in Iudea & Galilæa salutem. Innotescat vobis, quòd cum agni nimu sint teneri, & columbæ implumes, & non adsint fruges recentes, visum est nobis addere huic anno dies triginta.
units.tr: FIRST FRUITS. By divine law it was ordained that the first sheaf be offered on the second day of the Passover week, Lev. xxiii. 10, 11, where R. Solomon renders [ממחרת יום טוב הראשון של פסח] on the morrow after the first day of the festival of Passover. One may ask whether the crops were ripe by the Passover festival. The sowing of barley took place just after the middle of the month Marcheshvan, that is, about the beginning of our November. Beracot sol.18.2: He heard that seed sown at the first rain was destroyed by hail, so he went and sowed again at the second rain, etc. The first rain fell on the seventeenth day of the month Marcheshvan; the second on the twenty-third day of the same month. But if, when the proper time of Passover came, the barley had not ripened, a thirteenth month was intercalated into that year, and they waited until it ripened. See Intercalatio and Maimonides in Kiddush Hachodesh ch. 4. That they did sometimes intercalate a year for this necessity is clear from Jerusalem Talmud, Maaser Sheni sol.56.3; Sanhedrin sol.18.4; Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin sol.11.2, where this decree of the Sanhedrin survives: Rabban Gamaliel, with the elders of the great Sanhedrin, to our brethren in Judea and Galilee, greeting. Be it known to you that since the lambs are too tender, the doves unfledged, and fresh crops are not available, it has seemed good to us to add thirty days to this year.

units.la: Primitiarum manipulus, demessus fuit è valle Kedron tanquam loco urbi omnium proximo, ex quo illum secundùm Maymonidem afferre debuerunt. Semel tamen ipsum derheffuerunt ex hortúZeriphæis, loco quodam ab Hicrofolymis satis remoto, quia exercitus sementem circa urbem devastaverat. Ceremonia demessionis ita peragebatur. Legati Synedrii vesperà primi diei festi Paschatis, egrediebantur, & spicas in manipulos colligabant, & versus terram incurvabant, ut deinde eò commodiùs abscindi possent. Ex omnibus autem vicinis urbibus illuc confluebant, quasi res magno molimine peragenda esset. Cùm iam vesperasceret, dixit ille qui ad demetendum constitutus erat. Occidit sol. Responderunt illi, benè. Item, hac falce ? responderunt Benè. Hoc Sabbatho ? responderunt, hoc Sabbatho. Metam? Responderunt, mete. Hæc ter ille, atq; illi ter responderunt. Omnia hæc tanta fecerunt propter
units.tr: The sheaf of first fruits was cut from the valley of Kidron, as the place nearest to the city, from which, according to Maimonides, they ought to have brought it. Once, however, they fetched it from the garden of Zeriphus, a place quite far from Jerusalem, because an army had laid waste the sowing around the city. The ceremony of reaping was performed thus. On the evening of the first day of the Passover festival, the envoys of the Sanhedrin went out, gathered the ears into sheaves, and bent them toward the ground so that they might afterward be cut more conveniently. People came flocking to it from all the neighbouring towns, as if a great undertaking were to be carried out. When evening came, the man appointed to reap asked: "Has the sun set?" They answered: "Yes." He asked: "With this sickle?" They answered: "Yes." "On this Sabbath?" They answered: "On this Sabbath." "Shall I reap?" They answered: "Reap." He asked this three times, and they answered three times. They did all these things so elaborately because of

units.la: אוּרִים אֵין קִצִיר הָעוֹמֶר בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב : propter
units.tr: Urim: "There is no reaping of the omer at the close of the festival day." [אוּרִים אֵין קִצִיר הָעוֹמֶר בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב] Because of

units.la: Baithofaos ( Sadducæos ). qui negabant manipulum in vespera diei festi demeti debere. Consule de his Menachot c.10.
units.tr: the Boethusians (Sadducees), who denied that the sheaf might be reaped in the evening of the festival day. Consult on these matters Menachot c.10.

units.la: §. Ex quibus rebus, primitiæ ad templum afferendæ sunt Vid. Tractatum Bicurim; referemus nos ex illius capite tertio pompam, quæ primitiarum adductionem comitata est.
units.tr: §. From these matters, the first fruits were to be brought to the temple. See the tractate Bikkurim; from its third chapter I shall recount the procession that accompanied the bringing of the first fruits.

units.la: Omnes urbes שבטיעבר quæ erant unius stationis (i.e. ex quibus prodiit una ἐφημερία Sacerdotum) collectæ sunt in urbem stationariam, & pernoctarunt in plateis : Manè is qui primus inter eos fuit, dixit, Exsurgite, ascendamus ad Sionem, ad domum Domini Dei nostri.
units.tr: All the cities of the district that belonged to one station (that is, from which one course of priests came forth) were gathered into the station city and spent the night in the squares. In the morning the one who was first among them said: "Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the house of the Lord our God."

units.la: Bos præivit cornibus deauratis, & coronâ in capite oleaginâ. ( Gloss. Bos iste erat in sacrificium pacificum ) cecinit & tibia ante eos, usquedum appropinquarent Hierosolymam : cùm Hierosolymam appropinquatum effet, coronarunt primitias suas, (i.e. speciosas quantum fieri potuit conspectui exposuerunt.) Et prodierunt in occursum iis primates, & summi officiarii, & thesaurarii templi, idque in honorem accedentium. Atque omnes opifices Hierosolymæ assurrexerunt iis (in ossicinis suis) atque eos salutarunt hoc modo, : אחינו אנשי מקום פלוני באתם לשלום O fratres nostri incolæ urbis N. grati advenistis מכה החליל לפניהם Tibia coram iis canebatur, usquedum perventum foret in montem templi אפילו אגריפס המלך נושל הסל על כתפו Etiam ipse Rex Aggrippa canistrum (plenum vel ficubus vel uvis viridibus fi loca non longinqua, vel ficubus aridis & uvis passis, si remota) suscepit in humerum suum, & progressus est donec pervenniret ad atrium, Levitae occinuerunt. Exaltabo te Domine, quia exaltasti me, & non laetificasti inimicos meos super me, (Psal.xxx.1.) Dum adhuc Canistrum est in humero eius recitat periochen illam (Deut.xxvi.3.) Profiteor hodie Domino Deo meo. R. Iehuda dicit, Cum haec verba recitat, Aramaeus periturus erat pater meus &c. (v.f.) demittit canistrum ab humero, יאומון נשמתיהן & labiis tenet, dum Sacerdos illud huc illuc agitat. Recitatâ totâ periochâ ad verf.10. caniftrum disponit iuxta altare, & adorat & exit.
units.tr: An ox went before them, its horns gilded and an olive wreath on its head (the gloss says this ox was for the peace offering). A flute played before them until they drew near Jerusalem. When they drew near Jerusalem, they decked their first fruits with garlands (that is, they displayed them as beautifully as possible to view). The chief men and the chief officers and the treasurers of the temple came out to meet them, in honour of those approaching. And all the craftsmen of Jerusalem rose before them (in their workshops) and greeted them in this manner: [אחינו אנשי מקום פלוני באתם לשלום] O our brethren, men of such-and-such a place, you have come in peace. [מכה החליל לפניהם] The flute was played before them, until they reached the mount of the temple. [אפילו אגריפס המלך נושל הסל על כתפו] Even King Agrippa lifted the basket (full of figs and green grapes if the place was near, or of dried figs and raisins if it was far) onto his shoulder, and went on until he came to the court. The Levites sang: I will extol you, O Lord, for you have lifted me up, and have not let my enemies rejoice over me (Ps. xxx. 1). While the basket was still on his shoulder, he recited that passage (Deut. xxvi. 3): I profess today to the Lord my God. R. Judah says: when he recited these words, My father was a wandering Aramaean, etc. (to the end), he lowered the basket from his shoulder, and held it by the lips, while the priest moved it to and fro. Having recited the whole passage down to verse 10, he set the basket beside the altar, worshipped, and went out.

units.la: §. Placentam Hierosolymam attulit Nittai Tekoita è Bittur, ast eam non receperunt. Alexandrini placentas suas attulerunt Alexandria sed illas non receperunt; (quia illa loca sunt extra terram Israeliticam, ex qua sola placenta offerri debuerunt.) Incolae הר צבוע Montis Zeboim, attulerunt primitias suas ante pentecosten, sed eas non receperunt, (quia tempore illegitimo illas attulerunt.) Challah cap.4. v.10.
units.tr: §. Nittai of Tekoa brought a cake from Bitter to Jerusalem, but they did not accept it. The Alexandrians brought their cakes from Alexandria, but these too were not accepted (because those places lie outside the land of Israel, from which alone cakes ought to be offered). The inhabitants of Mount Zeboim [הר צבוע] brought their first fruits before Pentecost, but these were not accepted either (because they brought them at an unlawful time). Challah ch. 4, v. 10.

units.la: PRIMOGENITUS. In eo vitium faciunt, caput crassum vel nimis magnum; oculi nimis rotundi; aures tumescentes inflar spongiae. Beracot sol.44.1.
units.tr: FIRSTBORN. They find fault with him: a head too thick or too large; eyes too round; ears swollen like a sponge. Beracot sol.44.1.

units.la: De primogenitorum redemptione à patre vid. Synag.Iudaicam Buxt.p.114. de primogenitis animalium ibid. p.612.
units.tr: On the redemption of the firstborn by the father, see Synagoga Judaica of Buxtorf, p. 114; on firstborn animals, ibid. p. 612.

units.la: Primogenitus respectu patris vocatur ראשית און Principium roboris eius. Genef.xlix.3. Respectu matris vero רחם בשר δαvoιγον μητραν apeperiens vulvam. Exod. xiii. 12.
units.tr: The firstborn, with respect to the father, is called [ראשית און] the beginning of his strength, Gen. xlix. 3. With respect to the mother, he is [פטר רחם] the one opening the womb (Greek [διανοιγον μητραν] opening the womb), Exod. xiii. 12.

units.la: Primogenitus erat aliorum fratrum Dominus, sic Deus ipse Caino potestatem eius in fratrem confirmat, quando ipsi dicit, ad te appetitus eius, & tu illi dominabteris.Gen.f.iv.7. Et Iacob servire debebat Esavus cum tamen ex iure naturae ipsi E avo obedire debebat. Genef. xxv 23.
units.tr: The firstborn was lord over his other brothers. Thus God himself confirmed Cain's authority over his brother when he said to him: Its desire is toward you, and you shall rule over it, Gen. iv. 7. And Esau was to serve Jacob, although by the law of nature Jacob ought to have obeyed Esau. Gen. xxv. 23.

units.la: Dicitur primogenitus in distributione hereditatis paternae nomine πρωτοτόκια seu praerogativa, sumebat שנים פי διπλα portionem duplicem, vel ut notat Archius in Deuter. xxi. 17. quantum ad duos spectat fratres. Ita ut fires fuerint fratres (verba sunt Aben Esrae) שנים יחשבו consiciabantur quasi essent quatuor, & primogenitus sumat partes duas, reliqui unam.
units.tr: In the division of the paternal inheritance the firstborn took the privilege called [πρωτοτόκια] or prerogative, and received [שנים פי] a double portion, or, as Aben Ezra notes on Deut. xxi. 17, a share as large as that of two brothers. Thus, if there were two brothers (in the words of Aben Ezra) [שנים יחשבו] they were reckoned as though they were four, and the firstborn took two parts and the rest one.

units.la: Primogenito cedebat ius in eadem familia sacrificandi; hinc Iacob נתן נפשו על הבכורה deferavit primogenituram, ut sacrificare posset. Bereschit Rabba sol.71. E Mishna in זבחים c. 14. Antequam tabernaculum exstructum erat, licita erant loca excelsa ועבודה בבכורות Et cultus a primogenitis peragebatur. Sic Exod.xxiv.5. Sacerdotes iuniores filiorum Israel vocantur, & sunt secundum Onkelos, primogeniti Israel qui immolarunt. De primogeniti privilegiis quoad Sacerdotium, & haereditatem vid. Caput octavum. Tit. בכורות. De Disputatione inter Israelitas & Arabes circa haereditatem Ismaëlis praesente Alexandro Magno Vid. Alexander & Bereschit Rabba sol.68.
units.tr: The right of sacrificing within the same family belonged to the firstborn; hence Jacob [נתן נפשו על הבכורה] sold the birthright so that he might be able to sacrifice. Bereshit Rabba sol.71; from the Mishnah in [זבחים] c. 14: Before the tabernacle was built, high places were lawful, and the service of the firstborn [ועבודה בבכורות], and worship was performed by the firstborn. So in Exod. xxiv. 5, the priests are called the young men of the sons of Israel, and according to Onkelos they are the firstborn of Israel who offered sacrifices. On the privileges of the firstborn with regard to the priesthood and the inheritance, see Caput octavum, title [בכורות]. On the dispute between the Israelites and the Arabs concerning the inheritance of Ishmael, in the presence of Alexander the Great, see Alexander and Bereshit Rabba sol.68.

units.la: Processus Iudicialis. Vid. Iudicia. Item Testes.
units.tr: Judicial Process. See Judgments. Also Witnesses.

units.la: PRODITOR. Prohibitum est, Israelitam in manus Ethnicorum prodere,vel quoad personam suam, vel quoad bona sua &c. Et quicunque Israelitam ita tradiderit partem nullam habebit in seculo suturo. Maymon in פירוש חובל ומזיק cap. 8. Ex quo apparet quid de Proditore Iuda, ipsimet senserint patres conscripti. Ex sententia gentis locutus est Petrus Apostolus de Iuda Actor.1 25. quando inquit, abiit in locum suum. Idem enim de Bileamo dixit Baal Haturim Num.24. 25. Abiit Bileamus in locum suum; hoc est, inquit ille, ירד לגיהנום Descendit in Gehennam.
units.tr: TRAITOR. It is forbidden to hand over an Israelite to Gentiles, whether as to his person or as to his goods, etc. And whoever has so delivered an Israelite shall have no portion in the world to come. Maimonides, Commentary on Chovel u-Mazzik [פירוש חובל ומזיק], ch. 8. From this it is clear what the conscript fathers themselves thought of Judas the traitor. Peter the Apostle spoke in the sense of his nation about Judas, Acts 1:25, when he said, he went to his own place. For the same was said of Balaam by Baal Haturim on Num. 24:25: Balaam went to his place; that is, he says, he descended into Gehenna [ירד לגיהנום].

units.la: PROMOTIO Vid. impositio manuum.
units.tr: PROMOTION. See laying on of hands.

units.la: PROFLUVIOSA. De remediis pro profluvio laborantibus vid. Medicina. De זבה גדולה profluviosa magna, & זבה קטנה profluviosa minori vid. Nidda cap.2. Hal.4. Maymon. Iffure Biah cap.5. & 6.
units.tr: FLUX. For remedies for those suffering from a flux, see Medicine. On the great zavah [זבה גדולה] and the small zavah [זבה קטנה], see Nidda ch. 2, Hal. 4; Maimonides, Issurei Bi'ah, ch. 5 and 6.

units.la: PROPHETA. In quonam honoris gradu sit, vid. Honores. Seniorem ex sapientibus prophetae praeferunt in Hierof. Beracot pag.3. col.2. in sin. Propheta & senex similes sunt Regi שלוח כ' פלמטרין duos legatos suos in unam regionem; de uno ex ipsis scripsit אם אינו פראה לכם חותם Si vobis non ostenderit sigillum & signum meum, ne fidem ipsi adhibeatis; de altero vero, credite ipsi quamvis nec sigilla nec signa mea ostenderit. Prior est Propheta, alter senior.
units.tr: PROPHET. For the rank he holds in honour, see Honours. In the Jerusalem Talmud, Berachot, p. 3, col. 2, near the end, the prophets prefer the elder of the wise. A prophet and an elder are like a king who sent two envoys to one region. Of one of them he wrote: "If he does not show you my seal and my sign" [אם אינו פראה לכם חותם], "do not give him credence"; but of the other: "believe him, even though he shows neither my seal nor my signs." The first is the prophet, the other the elder.

units.la: Omnes Prophetae in universum לא נתנבאו אלא ליוות המשיח non prophetarunt nisi de diebus Messia. Dixit R. Iochanan. Omnes Prophetae non prophetarant nisi de iis qui poenitentiam egerunt. Sanhed. sol. 99. 1. Per decem אספקלריות Specula viderunt Prophetæ; Moses autem vidit tantum per speculum unum; Omnes Prophetæ viderunt per speculum maculatum; sed Moses vidit per speculum nitidum. Vaikra Rabba sect 1.
units.tr: All the prophets in general prophesied only of the days of the Messiah [לא נתנבאו אלא ליוות המשיח]. R. Yochanan said: All the prophets prophesied only concerning those who repented. Sanhedrin fol. 99.1. The prophets saw through ten mirrors [אספקלריות]; Moses saw only through one mirror. All the prophets saw through a clouded mirror, but Moses saw through a bright mirror. Vayikra Rabba, sect. 1.

units.la: Crediderunt Iudæi in adventu Messiæ, resuscitandos fore Prophetas. Sanhed. sol. 91. 2. Vox speculatorum tuorum, vocem exultaverunt. Iubilabunt simul. Esai. LII.8. Dicit Rabbi Chaia Bar Abba, Dicit R. Iochanan, omnes Prophetæ edunt canticum simul voce una. Ibid. sol. 92. 2. Omnes iusti quos resuscitabit Deus a mortuis, non redibunt in pulverem. Gloss. quos resuscitabit in diebus Messiæ. Succah sol. 51. 2. Suscitabimus septem Pastores. Davidem in medio, Adamum, Sethum, Methuselemum a dextra eius. Abraham am, Iacobum & Mosen a sinistra. Atque octo primates hominum. Iesse, Saul, Samuel, Amos, Zephaniam, Ezechiam (ut notat Kimchi) Messiam & Eliam.
units.tr: The Jews believed that at the coming of the Messiah the prophets would be raised. Sanhedrin fol. 91.2: The voice of your watchmen; they lift up their voice, together they sing for joy. Isa. 52:8. Rabbi Chiya bar Abba says, R. Yochanan says: all the prophets will sing a song together with one voice. Ibid. fol. 92.2: All the righteous whom God raises from the dead will not return to dust. The gloss: whom he raises in the days of the Messiah. Succah fol. 51.2: We shall raise up seven shepherds: David in the middle, Adam, Seth and Methuselah on his right, Abraham, Jacob and Moses on his left; and eight chief men of mankind: Jesse, Saul, Samuel, Amos, Zephaniah, Hezekiah (as Kimchi notes), the Messiah and Elijah.

units.la: §. De Prophetarum vestitu particulari vid. Leusd. Philol. Mixtum pag. 151.
units.tr: On the particular dress of the prophets, see Leusden, Philologus Hebraeo-Mixtus, p. 151.

units.la: §. נביא שקר Pseudo Propheta est, qui vaticinatur quod non audivit, & quod ipsi dictum non est. Si quis verò Prophetiam supprimat, aut addiderit ad verba Prophetæ, ipsiusque verba non observaverit, is à Deo punietur (מיתתו בידי שמים Mors eius erit per manus cœli, homines ipsum non puniunt, sed iudicio Dei relinquitur.) qui prophetat in nomine idoli, his verbis, sic dicit Iupiter, etiamsi nihil in receptis statutis mutet, sed omnia secuncundùm ius iudicet, tamen strangulatur. Sanhed.cap.10.5.6. Pseudo-Prophetæ & summi Sacerdotes, à nemine nisi Synedrio magno diiudicari possunt. Sanhed.1.5.
units.tr: A false prophet [נביא שקר] is one who prophesies what he has not heard, and what has not been said to him. If anyone suppresses a prophecy, or adds to the words of a prophet, or does not observe his words, he is punished by God; his death is by the hand of heaven [מיתתו בידי שמים]: men do not punish him, but leave him to the judgment of God. Whoever prophesies in the name of an idol, with these words, thus says Jupiter, is strangled, even if he changes nothing in the accepted statutes but judges everything according to the law. Sanhedrin ch. 10, §§ 5, 6. False prophets and high priests can be judged by no one but the Great Sanhedrin. Sanhedrin 1.5.

units.la: Post obitum Prophetarum ultimorum, qui fuerunt Haggai, Zacharias, Malachias, discessit Spiritus Sanctus ab Israele, veruntamen exinde usi sunt τῆ Bath Kol. Bab Sanhed. sol.11.1. Iuchafin sol.15.2. Post integros mille annos à legis promulgatione, ablata est prophetia ab Israele, & Alexander Hierosolymæ venit.
units.tr: After the death of the last prophets, who were Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi, the Holy Spirit departed from Israel; nevertheless, from then on they made use of the Bath Kol. Babylonian Sanhedrin fol. 11.1; Yuchasin fol. 15.2. After a full thousand years from the promulgation of the Law, prophecy was taken from Israel, and Alexander came to Jerusalem.

units.la: Notam circa citationem Prophetarum in N. T. Vid. apud Ieremiam.
units.tr: A note on the citation of the Prophets in the New Testament: see under Jeremiah.

units.la: Proselytismus. Vid. Noachida. Item Baptismus. Proselyti Tadmorai sunt idonei ut introeant in congregationem. Hieros. Ievamot sol.3.2.
units.tr: Proselytism. See Noachida. Also Baptism. Proselytes of Tadmor are fit to enter the congregation. Jerusalem Yevamot fol. 3.2.

units.la: Mirum est quòd Pharisæi Proselytos tam anxiè & sedulò captaverint (Matth.23.15.) cùm tamen apud Talmudicos pessimè audiant. Bab. Niddafol.13.2. גרים והמקשים היונוקות מעכבין את המשיח Tradunt Rabbini nostri Proselyti & Paderasta impediunt adventum Messiæ. גרים לישראל כספחת Proselyti sunt sicut scabies Israeli. (Glossa) Ideò quòd non essent periti mandatorum, quodque inducerent vindictas, atque insuper, quod fortè eorum opera imitarentur Israelitæ. Vid. Proximus.
units.tr: It is remarkable that the Pharisees sought proselytes so anxiously and diligently (Matt. 23:15), although among the Talmudists they are spoken of very badly. Babylonian Nidda fol. 13.2: Our rabbis teach: proselytes and pederasts delay the coming of the Messiah [גרים והמקשים היונוקות מעכבין את המשיח]. Proselytes are like a scab to Israel [גרים לישראל כספחת] (Gloss): because they were not skilled in the commandments, and would bring on vengeance, and moreover because Israelites might perhaps imitate their works. See Neighbour.

units.la: Genes.xii.2. Dicuntur Abraham & Loth fecisse animas in Charan: quæ verba Interpretes non intelligunt de generatione animarum vel hominum, sed de hominibus, quos illi ab Idololatria conversos Deo lucrifecerunt. Sic Aben Esra, sunt anima quas docuerunt veritatem, ut colerent verum Deum. Salomoh Iarchi, נשׂשות שהכניסון כתחת כנפי השכינה אנרהם מגייך את האנשים ושרה מגיירת את הנשים : Animas quas congregarunt sub alas Maiestatis Dei. Abraham proselytos fecit viros, Sarah fœminas. Ita ut secundum Aben Esram עשו fecerunt, idem sit ac קנו acquisiverunt.
units.tr: Gen. 12:2. Abraham and Lot are said to have made souls in Haran. The interpreters do not understand these words of the generation of souls or of men, but of men whom they won to God from idolatry. So Aben Ezra: they are souls whom they taught the truth, that they might worship the true God. Solomon Jarchi [Rashi]: souls whom they gathered under the wings of the Divine Presence [נשׂשות שהכניסון כתחת כנפי השכינה]: Abraham made proselytes of the men, and Sarah of the women. So, according to Aben Ezra, made [עשו] is the same as acquired [קנו].

units.la: De Proselytis vid. Clariss. Leusdenium in Philolog. Hebr. Mixto. Lex. Buxt. Talmud. in rad. גור.
units.tr: On proselytes, see the most distinguished Leusden in his Philologus Hebraeus Mixtus; the Lexicon of Buxtorf; the Talmud, under the root גור.

units.la: PROXIMUS, est Israelita religione & cultu, hoc est Proselytus; Frater vero Israelita genere & sanguine; Hinc Aruch in בן ברית excludit ethnicos in illo dicto, Si bos tuus ferierit bovem proximi &c. quoniam illi sub nomine קרוב non veniunt. Ita Maymonides Hal. Rozeach cap.2. dicit, Israelitam qui interficit advenam inquilinum, qui proselytus factus non est, morte mulctandum non esse, quia praeceptum Exod.21. 14. solum de eo sonat qui proximum occiderit, quales tales inquilini, ut & reliqui Ethnici non sunt. Sub Evangelio eadem latitudine adhibetur frater, quâ apud Iudaeos & frater & proximus, id est pro omnibus Evangelium prositentibus, & contradistinguitur Ethnicis 1.Cor. v. 11. Proximus autem ad omnes extenditur, etiam à religione nostra alienos. Luc.x.29.30.
units.tr: NEIGHBOUR [PROXIMUS] is an Israelite by religion and worship, that is, a proselyte; brother, however, is an Israelite by descent and blood. Hence Aruch, under בן ברית, excludes the Gentiles from that saying, If your neighbour's ox gores your ox, etc., since they do not come under the name קרוב. So Maimonides, Hilchot Rotzeach, ch. 2, says that an Israelite who kills a resident alien who has not become a proselyte is not to be punished with death, because the precept at Exod.21. 14 speaks only of one who has killed his neighbour, and such resident aliens, like other Gentiles, are not neighbours. Under the Gospel the word brother is used with the same breadth as among the Jews, both brother and neighbour, that is, for all who profess the Gospel, and it is contrasted with Gentiles, 1 Cor. v. 11. The neighbour, however, extends to all, even those alien to our religion. Luke 10:29–30.

units.la: PROVIDENTIA duplex est השגחה הכוללת Providentia generalis, & פרטית particularis. R. Levi in Iob. 3. scribit, Iobum sensisse, quod ההשגחה האלוהית איננה באישי האדם כלל כל שכן בשאר בעלי חיים Providentia Divina se non extendat, ad singularia hominis, multò minus ad singularia reliquorum animantium, quae reguntur partim naturalibus, partim cœlestium influentiarum motibus & inclinationibus. Etiam alii fuerunt in hac sententia. Vid. פתי עקרה sol.145. col. More Nevoch. p.3. cap.17.18.
units.tr: PROVIDENCE is twofold: general providence [השגחה הכוללת] and particular providence [פרטית]. R. Levi, on Job 3, writes that Job thought divine providence does not extend to the individual persons of men at all, much less to the individual other living creatures, which are governed partly by natural causes, partly by the motions and inclinations of heavenly influences. Others also held this opinion. See Peti Akara, fol. 145, col. [פתי עקרה]. Guide of the Perplexed, part 3, chs. 17–18.

units.la: PUBERTAS incipit in puellis ab anno duodecimo & sex mensibus; in masculis verò ab anno decimo tertio & sex mensibus; etsi non in articulo isto temporis sita sit hæc res, sed præcipuè in productione duorum pilorum וגאו מקום Aruch & Nidda sol.65.1. Kiddufchin sol. 79.1. Pub.r Masculus vocatur בגר, fœmella verò בוגרת, quæ ad annum 12. completum vocatur קטנה, ab anno duodecimo & die uno verò vocatur נערה, ufquedum sex menses effluxerint, à quibus deinde בוגרת nominatur. Maymon. in Hal. Ifchut cap. 2. Filia quando pubuit, libera est à potestate patris. Nedarim 47.1. Vid. Adolescentula.
units.tr: PUBERTY begins in girls at twelve years and six months, and in boys at thirteen years and six months; though this matter is not fixed at that moment of time, but depends chiefly on the appearance of two hairs [שני שערות] (Aruch and Nidda fol. 65.1; Kiddushin fol. 79.1). A male is called bagar [בגר], a female bogeret [בוגרת]. A girl who has not yet completed twelve years is called qetanah [קטנה]; from twelve years and one day she is called naarah [נערה], until six months have passed, after which she is called bogeret. Maimonides, Hilchot Ishut, ch. 2. When a daughter has reached puberty, she is free from her father's authority. Nedarim 47.1. See Adolescentula.

units.la: PUBLICANI genti Iudaicæ admodùm fuerunt odiosi. Maymon in Gezelah cap. 5. Homines quibus præsumitur eos fures esse, præsumiturque omnes eorum opes per rapinas congestas esse, opusq; totum suum esse opus rapacium, veluti Publicanorum & latronum, quibus uti non licet, nec est eorum numerus cum tuo commiscendus, eòquòd præsumitur ex rapina acquisitus.
units.tr: PUBLICANS were very hateful to the Jewish nation. Maimonides, Hilchot Gezelah, ch. 5: People who are presumed to be thieves, and whose whole wealth is presumed to have been gathered by robbery, and whose entire business is plunder, like publicans and robbers, are not to be dealt with, nor are they to be counted together with your own people, because it is presumed that what they have was acquired by rapine.

units.la: Bab. Sanhed. sol.25. 2. recensentur illi, qui nec ad iudicandum nec ad testimonium dicendum idonei sunt, & in ipsorum numerum recensentur etiam הגבאין והמוכסין Exactores & publicani.
units.tr: Bab. Sanhedrin, fol. 25, col. 2: those who are not fit either to judge or to give testimony are listed, and among their number are counted הגבאין והמוכסין [the collectors and the publicans], that is, tax-collectors and publicans.

units.la: Nedarim cap.3. v.4. Coniunguntur Publicani cum sicariis & latronibus לְהַרְגִּין גּוֹיִם וּלְמוֹכְסִין Iurant Sicariis, latronibus & publicanis. Hac est oblatio, quamvis oblatio non fit; Et ita licet eos fallere: idque iuramento.
units.tr: Nedarim, ch. 3, v. 4: publicans are joined with assassins and robbers: לְהַרְגִּין גּוֹיִם וּלְמוֹכְסִין [they swear by assassins, robbers and publicans]. This is an offering, although no offering is made; and so it is permitted to deceive them, and that by oath.

units.la: Nec immeritò tam ignominiosè de ipsis loquuntur,oneri enim addiderunt onus.
units.tr: Nor do they speak so contemptuously of them without reason, for they have added burden to burden.

units.la: Maym. ubi supra. Quando Publicani reputandi sunt profuribus? Quando scilicet publicanus est gentilis: vel quando ex se ipso illud munerū usurpat, vel quando à Rege deputatus non definitam summam exigit, sed pro arbitrio.
units.tr: Maimonides, loc. cit.: When are publicans to be counted as thieves? Namely, when the publican is a Gentile, or when he takes up that office on his own authority, or when, appointed by the king, he exacts not a fixed sum but whatever he pleases.

units.la: Bab.Sanhed.sol.25.2. Aruch in דכם. Cum Rex tributum definiret à Iudaeis exigendum,ab unoquoque secundum facultates suas, hi Publicani ad rem ordinandam deputati, seuꝛmoλiꝓ facti sunt, hos onerantes illis indulgentes, & sic facti sunt depredatores.
units.tr: Bab. Sanhedrin, fol. 25, col. 2; Aruch, under דכם: When the king fixed the tax to be exacted from the Jews, from each one according to his means, these publicans, appointed to arrange the business, became a band of robbers [συμμορία]: burdening some and favouring others, they became plunderers.

units.la: Laudandus est Pater R. Zeirꝛ,qui, cùm publicanus foret per annos tredecim, onera tributorum non gravavit sed emollivit.
units.tr: Praise is due to Rabbi Zeira, who, though he was a publican for thirteen years, did not make the burdens of the taxes heavier but lighter.

units.la: Publicanos nullo modo reputarunt intra societatem religiosam. Hieros.Demai sol. 23.3. Religiosus qui evadit publicanus, pellendus est è societate religiosa.
units.tr: They did not count publicans at all within the religious fellowship. Jerusalem Demai, fol. 23, col. 3: a religious man who becomes a publican is to be expelled from the religious fellowship.

units.la: Ex Maymonide modò citato vides publicanum duplicem esse, spontaneum scilicet & à Rege constitutum. Vid. etiam Nedarim sol.28.1.
units.tr: From the Maimonides just cited you see that there are two kinds of publican: the voluntary, namely, and the one appointed by the king. See also Nedarim, fol. 28, col. 1.

units.la: Publicani specialem signaturam habebant, quæ Schabbat cap.8. vocatur קשר מוכסין, & erat duarum litterarum maiuscularum in chartulâ aut alia materia, quæ dabatur illi qui vectigal totum solvebat ab una fluminis parte, quâ ostensâ, in altera liber erat. Tali signaturç etiam utebantur qui decimas recipiebant. Maymon in locum.
units.tr: Publicans had a special mark, which in Shabbat, ch. 8, is called קשר מוכסין [the publican's knot]. It was a pair of capital letters on a small slip of paper or other material, which was given to the man who had paid the whole toll for one side of the river; when this was shown, he was free on the other side. Tax-collectors also used such a mark when receiving tithes. Maimonides on the passage.

units.la: PULVEREM terræ Ethnicæ ex contactu inquinare docuerunt Scholæ scribarum.
units.tr: The schools of the scribes taught that dust of the Gentile land defiles by contact.

units.la: Tofaph. ad Kelim cap. 1. Pulvis Syriæ inquinat æque ac pulvis reliquarum religionum Ethnicarum.
units.tr: Tosafot on Kelim, ch. 1: the dust of Syria defiles just as the dust of the other Gentile religions does.

units.la: Bab. Sanhed. sol. 12. 1. Traditionalis quidam ait, non afferunt olera è terra Ethnica in terram Israeliticam; at Rabbini nostri permiserunt. Quidnam est inter ipsos discrepantia? R Ieremiah dicit חושיין לגושיהן איכא בניימיהן Cura de pulvere eorum est inter eos. Glossa, Cavent, ne cum oleribus afferatur aliquid de pulvere terra Ethnica, quod inquinet in tentorio, & inquinet puritatem terra Israelitica.
units.tr: Bab. Sanhedrin, fol. 12, col. 1: A certain traditionalist says they do not bring vegetables from the Gentile land into the land of Israel, but our rabbis permitted it. What is the disagreement between them? R. Jeremiah says: חושיין לגושיהן איכא בניימיהן [care for their dust lies between them]. The gloss: they take care lest, along with the vegetables, anything of the dust of the Gentile land be brought in, which would defile in the tent and defile the purity of the land of Israel.

units.la: Bab. Schabbat sol. 15. 2. Ob sex dubia comburunt Trumam: ob dubium agri in quo olim sepulchrum, ob dubium pulveris allati è terra Ethnica &c. Glossa. Quia de omni pulvere terra Ethnica dubitari potest, an non fuerit de sepulchro mortui.
units.tr: Bab. Shabbat, fol. 15, col. 2: On six doubts they burn the terumah: from doubt about a field in which there was once a grave; from doubt about dust brought from the Gentile land, etc. Gloss: because one may doubt concerning all dust of the Gentile land whether it came from a grave of the dead.

units.la: Gloss. in Sanhed. sol. 5. 2. Nonne de terra Ethnica determinatum est, quod immunda æquè sit ac sepulchretum.
units.tr: Gloss on Sanhedrin, fol. 5, col. 2: Has it not been determined that the Gentile land is as unclean as a burial place?

units.la: Ex quibus clarè intelligere possumus, quid voluerit Christus Matth. 10. 14. ἐξινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν. Scilicet, Ubicunque vos non exceperit urbs Israelitica, eum inde discederis, excutiendo pulverem à pedibus vestris demonstrate, vos urbem istam, utcunque Israelitican, pro Ethnica, profana, & impura reputare atque abominari.
units.tr: From these things we can clearly understand what Christ meant in Matt. 10:14: ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν [shake off the dust from your feet]. That is, wherever a Israelite city does not receive you, depart from it, shaking the dust from your feet, to show that you count that city, however Israelite it may be, as Gentile, profane and impure, and abominate it.

units.la: De Sanctitate pulveris terræ Israeliticæ vid. Ægyptios. Maymon in Hal. Melach. c.5. בדולי Hebrew Præstantiores ex sapientibus, exfculati sunt fines terra Israelitica, exfculati sunt lapides eius, & se circumvolverunt in pulvere eius. f. d. Psal 2.15.
units.tr: On the holiness of the dust of the land of Israel see Maimonides, Hilchot Melachim, ch. 5: The most eminent of the wise have kissed the borders of the land of Israel, have kissed its stones, and have rolled themselves in its dust. Cf. Psalm 102:15.

units.la: De pulvere adhibito in potatione Sota, vide Aqua amara potatio.
units.tr: On the dust used in the drink of the suspected wife (Sota), see "Aqua amara potatio" [the bitter water drink].

units.la: Purgatorium vocant Iudæi בית צירוף, quasi domum, ubi animæ à peccatis ut aurum ab igne per liquefactionem à scoriis purgatur. De hoc Iudæorum purgatorio vid.Cl. Buxt. Synag. 331. Voisin.pug.fid.136.141.
units.tr: The Jews call purgatory בית צירוף [the house of refining], as if a house where souls are purged of sins as gold is purged of dross by fire, through melting. On this Jewish purgatory see the learned Buxtorf, Synagoga, p. 331; Voisin, Pugio fidei, pp. 136, 141.

units.la: Puritas, Purificatio. De puritate vid. Lotio. Immundities. Incolæ urbis מודעית Modaith in urbe sua existimantur puri circa vasa fictilia, sed non extrà ipsam. Exactores qui in domum ingressi sunt, & fures qui reddiderunt vasa surrepta, creduntur dicentes non tetigimus. Chagiga cap.3. de illis qui in omnibus de puritate creduntur, vid. נאמן. de Societatibus religiosis puritatem voventibus, vid. חבר. Pharisæi. De oblationibus leprosorum postquàm mundi facti sunt. vid. Leprosu. De puerperarum oblationibus vid. Sacrificia. In monte oliveti erant duo cedri tantæ magnitudinis, ut sub unâ illarum quatuor fuerint tabernæ, in quibus omnia ad purificationem necessaria vendebantur. Ex altera verò unoquoque mense, circa quadraginta Seas columbarum produxerunt, in usum fœminarum purificandarum. Hieros.Taanith. sol.69.1. De pueris aquam purificationis aspergentibus vid. Atrium magnum. De Hyssopo quâ aquæ aspersionem faciebant. Vid. suo loco. de cineribus vaccæ rufæ, quæ ad aspersionem adhibebantur Vid. Vacca Rufa.
units.tr: Purity, purification. On purity see "Lotio" and "Immunditiae". The inhabitants of the city מודעית [Modaith] are thought to be clean as regards earthenware vessels, but not outside the city. Tax-collectors who entered a house, and thieves who gave back stolen vessels, are believed when they say, "We have not touched them." Chagigah, ch. 3. On those who are believed in all matters of purity, see נאמן [trustworthy]. On religious societies that vow purity, see חבר [fellowship], the Pharisees. On the offerings of lepers after they have been made clean, see "Leprosy". On the offerings of women after childbirth, see "Sacrifices". On the Mount of Olives there were two cedars of such size that under one of them were four shops in which everything needed for purification was sold. From the other, each month, they produced about forty seahs of doves for the use of women being purified. Jerusalem Taanith, fol. 69, col. 1. On boys sprinkling the water of purification see "Atrium magnum". On the hyssop with which they sprinkled water, see in its place. On the ashes of the red heifer, which were used for sprinkling, see "Vacca rufa".

units.la: PYTHON Python Heb. פיתום divinator qui admiculo mali spiritus vaticinia edit. Maymon Avoda Zarah cap. 6. sol. 32. האוב זה שהוא עומר ומקטיר קטורת ידועה ואוחז שרביט של הרס בידו ומניפו : Python fuit, qui stubat & adoleb at suffitum certum & notum, tenebatque v rgam ex myrto in manu sua, & agitabat eam. Ipse verò murmurabat submisse verba quædam nota apud ipsos, donec audiret ea interrogans, quasi aliquis loqueretur cum ipso, & responderet ei ad id, quod quærebat ipse verbis, quasi ex terra, voce depressa admodum, ut fere auribus percipi non posset, sed cogitatione perciperet eam. וכן הלוקח גולגולת המת ומקטיר לה ומנחש ברוח Ille quoque Python est, qui accipiebat cranium mortui, ac suffitum faciebat ei, mussitabat eo donec audiretur, voce quasi ex axillis prodeunte ,submisse admodum. & respondebat ei. כל אלו מעשה אוב Omnia illa sunt opera Pythonis, & qui unum faciebat ex illis lapidabatur.
units.tr: PYTHON. Python, in Hebrew פיתום, a diviner who utters prophecies by the aid of an evil spirit. Maimonides, Avodah Zarah, ch. 6, fol. 32: האוב זה שהוא עומר ומקטיר קטורת ידועה ואוחז שרביט של הרס בידו ומניפו [The Python is one who stands and burns a known incense, and holds in his hand a rod of myrtle, and waves it. He himself murmurs in a low voice certain words known among them, until he hears them asking him, as if someone were speaking with him, and he answers their question in words, as if from the earth, in a voice so low that it can scarcely be perceived by the ears, but is grasped by the mind.] וכן הלוקח גולגולת המת ומקטיר לה ומנחש ברוח [Likewise he who takes the skull of a dead man, burns incense to it, and divines by the spirit.] He too is a Python: he took the skull of the dead, burned incense to it, and muttered into it until he was heard, in a voice very low, as if coming from the armpits, and it answered him. כל אלו מעשה אוב [All these are the works of a Python], and whoever did any of them was stoned.

units.la: Bartenora in Sanhed. sol. 65. 1. ubi de Pythonibus agitur sic infit. Sunt Pythones, qui accipiunt cranium hominis mortui, cuius caro iam absumpta est, eique suffitum faciunt; postea quæruntex eo futura, & cranium illud respondet, nempe per spiritum in illud arte magicâ inductum.
units.tr: Bartenora on Sanhedrin, fol. 65, col. 1, where he treats of Pythons, begins thus: There are Pythons, who take the skull of a dead man whose flesh has already been consumed, and burn incense to it; then they ask it about the future, and that skull replies, namely through a spirit drawn into it by magical art.

units.la: De Pythonibus vid. Aruch in אוב. Aben
units.tr: On Pythons see Aruch, under אוב [ob]. Aben ...

units.la: Efram inIob.32. 19. Seldenum de Diis Syrii pag. 39. de Magis & Daemoniacis vid. suo loco.
units.tr: Ephraem on Job 32:19. Selden, De diis Syris, p. 39. On magi and demoniacs see in their place.

units.la: Q.
units.tr: Q.

units.la: קפוטקיא Quapputkia, seu Cappadocia, apud Talmudicos significat Pelusium.(Chetubhot sol. 110.2. & 120. 2. נשא בקפוטקיא וגירשה Si quis uxorem ducat in Cappadocia, eamque dimittat in Cappadocia det ei nummum Cappadocia. Rambam in loc. קפוטקיא est Caphtor, vocaturque ab Arabibus דמיאטא Damiata quam eandem esse cum Pelusio nemo ignorat.
units.tr: Qapputkia [קפוטקיא], or Cappadocia, among the Talmudists means Pelusium (Chetubhot fol. 110.2 and 120.2). If anyone marries a wife in Cappadocia and divorces her in Cappadocia, let him give her a Cappadocian coin [נשא בקפוטקיא וגירשה]. Rambam on the passage: Cappadocia is Caphtor, and it is called by the Arabs Damietta, which everyone knows is the same as Pelusium.

units.la: Quadrans. Marcus cap.12.42. sic infit. Κόδραντης, ὁ ἐς· ἐν Confer Hierof.Kidduschin sol.58.4. ב"מרוטות קרוינגס Dua pruta sunt quadrans. Bava Metzia sol.44.2. Pruta est octava pars Assarii Italici. Assarium est vicesima quarta pars denarii argentei. Vid. Denarius & Moneta.
units.tr: Quadrans. Mark 12.42 begins thus: kodrantēs [κόδραντης], which is a quadrans. Compare the Jerusalem Talmud, Kiddushin fol. 58.4: Two pruta make a quadrans. Bava Metzia fol. 44.2: A pruta is the eighth part of an Italian as. An as is the twenty-fourth part of a silver denarius. See Denarius and Moneta.

units.la: R.
units.tr: R.

units.la: Rabbi. De origine huius tituli sic Aruch in voce אבי. Secula vetustiora, qua digniora erant, non opus habuerunt titulo vel Rabban, vel Rabbi, vel Rabb, sive ad Sapientes Babylonicos, sive ad Sapientes terra Israelitica cum honore designandos: Hillel ascendit Babylone & tamen non vocatus fuit Rabbi Hillel, sic nec Haggai nec Esra titulo Rabbinatus insigniti fuerunt. Titulus Rabban autem incepit in praefectis Synedrii; a
units.tr: Rabbi. On the origin of this title, Aruch in the word אבי says thus: The earlier ages, which were more worthy, had no need of the title Rabban, or Rabbi, or Rabb, to designate with honour either the Sages of Babylon or the Sages of the land of Israel. Hillel went up from Babylon, and yet he was not called Rabbi Hillel; nor were Haggai and Ezra marked with the title of Rabbinate. The title Rabban, however, began with the presidents of the Sanhedrin: with Rabban Gamaliel the elder, and Rabban Simeon his son, and likewise with Rabban Johanan ben Zakkai.

units.la: Rabban Gamaliele sene, & Rabban Simeon filie eius, itemque a Rabban Iohanan Ben Saccai. Ti- tulus Rabbi vero incipit a promotis (ad Presby- teratum) a Rabbi Zadok & R. Eliefer Ben Ia- cob.
units.tr: Rabban Gamaliel the elder, Rabban Simeon his son, and likewise Rabban Johanan ben Zakkai. The title Rabbi, however, begins with those promoted (to the presbyterate): Rabbi Zadok and R. Eliezer ben Jacob.

units.la: Reperiuntur tamen exempla in quibus videmus etiam ante illa tempora nomen Rabbi usitatum. Bab. Maccot sol. 24.1. Iosaphat introducit sic discipulum Sapientis alloquens אבי אבי רבי רבי מרי מרי O Pater Pater, Rabbi, Rabbi, Domine, Domine, In Sanhed. sol.107.3. Iosua Ben Perachiae appellatur Rabbi Iosua. Sed non ita frequens in ore hominum fuit ac post Schisma Hillelianorum & Schammaeanorum.
units.tr: Yet there are examples in which we see the name Rabbi in use even before those times. Bab. Maccot fol. 24.1: Jehoshaphat addresses a disciple of a Sage in this way: O Father, Father, Rabbi, Rabbi, Master, Master. [אבי אבי רבי רבי מרי מרי] In Sanhedrin fol. 107.3, Joshua ben Perachiah is called Rabbi Joshua. But it was not so frequent on people's lips as after the schism of the Hillelites and Shammaites.

units.la: De gradu horum titulorum sic loquitur Aruch ubi supra. Maior est Rabbi quam Rabh, & maior est Rabban quam Rabbi, & maior est qui nomine suo (simplici vocatur, quales sunt Antigonus Sochaeus, Schemaja, Abtalion, Gebhina Ben Pesisa, Schammai Gaiba Suava, Admon, Chanan) quam qui appellatur Rabban.
units.tr: On the rank of these titles, Aruch speaks thus in the passage above: Rabbi is greater than Rabh, and Rabban is greater than Rabbi, and greater than one who is called by Rabban is he who is named by his simple name (such as Antigonus of Sochoh, Shemaiah, Avtalion, Gebhina ben Pesisa, Shammai, Gaiba, Suava, Admon, Hanan).

units.la: Quod titulum Rabbi attinet, in more fuit; illo tanquam honorario alios salutare, sic Discipuli salutabant suos Magistros, sic etiam Magistri se invicem.
units.tr: As for the title Rabbi, it was the custom to greet others with it as a title of honour: thus disciples greeted their masters, and masters greeted one another in the same way.

units.la: Quod Discipuli sic magistros salutaverint; patet ex Bab. Beracot sol. 27.1. Qui orat post tergum magistri sui, & qui salutat Magistrum suum aut resalutat Magistrum suum, & qui discedit a schola magistri sui, & qui aliquid docet, quod non audivit a Magistro suo, facit ut discedat Maiestas divina ab Israele. Glossa in verba, qui salutat ea forma verborum, qua alios homines salutat,& non dicit ei שלום עליך רבי Salve Rabbi&c. Vid. etiam Hierof.Schevuot sol.34.1.
units.tr: That disciples greeted masters in this way is clear from Bab. Berachot fol. 27.1: He who prays behind his master, and he who greets his master or returns his master's greeting, and he who leaves his master's school, and he who teaches something he did not hear from his master, causes the divine Majesty to depart from Israel. The gloss on the words "who greets in the form of words with which he greets other men, and does not say to him, Peace be upon you, Rabbi" [שלום עליך רבי] adds: "Hail, Rabbi," etc. See also Hierosolymitanum Shevuot fol. 34.1.

units.la: De Magistris fe mutuò sic salutantibus sonat Hierof. Moed Katon sol.81.1. R. Akiba dixit B. Eleafaro Rabbi, Rabbi. Bab. Taanith legitur historia de homine quodam deformi qui erat Magister & qui R. Elieferem sic salutavit שלום עליך רבי Salve Rabbi, & qui deinde à concivibus suis cum magna admiratione R.Elieferis etiam salutatus fuit שלום עליך רבי מורי Salve Rabbi & Magister; non enim hunc deformem Rabbinatus capacem credebat.
units.tr: Concerning masters greeting one another in this way, Hierosolymitanum Moed Katan fol. 81.1 says: R. Akiba said to R. Eleazar, Rabbi, Rabbi. In Bab. Taanith we read the story of a certain deformed man who was a master and who greeted R. Eliezer: "Peace be upon you, Rabbi" [שלום עליך רבי]; and then R. Eliezer was also greeted by his fellow citizens with great admiration: "Peace be upon you, Rabbi and Master" [שלום עליך רבי מורי]. For they did not believe this deformed man capable of the rabbinate.

units.la: §. De Rabbinorum distinctionibus in גאונים & אמוראי vid. Cl. Buxt. in Rad. de סבוראי vid. Voisin pug. fid. pag. 62. Schalfchelet Hakab. p. 34. 2. De Misnicis Doctoribus iam quaedam in historia nostra complexi sumus: plurima huic operi in suis locis inspersa reperies.
units.tr: § On the distinctions among the Rabbis into Geonim and Amoraim, see Cl. Buxtorf in Radice. On Sabboraim, see Voisin, Pugio fidei, p. 62; Schalschelet Hakabbala, p. 34. 2. On the Mishnic doctors we have already gathered some matters in our history; you will find much scattered through this work in its proper places.

units.la: §. Vocantur in Talmude quidam Rabbini דרומאי Australes, ut ר' יעקוב דרומי R. Iacob Australis in Hierof.Succah sol.53.4. & R. Samlai דרומי Australis in Hierof. Berac. sol. 11. 4. Si quaeris rationem illius nomenclationis, Observa illos fuisse è Iudaea, quae דרום Auster respectu Galilaeae vocatur, Vid. Iudaea.
units.tr: § Some Rabbis in the Talmud are called Southerners [דרומאי], as R. Jacob the Southerner in Hierosolymitanum Sukkah fol. 53.4, and R. Samlai the Southerner in Hierosolymitanum Berachot fol. 11.4. If you ask the reason for this name, observe that they were from Judaea, which is called the South [דרום] with respect to Galilee. See Judaea.

units.la: RACEMATIO quae pauperibus relinquenda vocatur עוללות & פרט & definitur per הנותר בשעה הבציר id quod decidit vel remanet tempore vindemia. Debent autem baccae vel grana feparatim decidere si פרט esse debent, secundum hanc regulam שני גרגרין פרט שלשה אינה Duo grana racematio sunt, sed non tria. Si quis cani-
units.tr: GLEANING, which is to be left for the poor, is called olelot [עוללות] and peret [פרט], and is defined as what falls or remains at the time of the vintage [הנותר בשעה הבציר]. Grapes or grains must fall separately if they are to be peret, according to this rule: Two grains are gleaning, but not three. If someone

units.la: strum supponeret ad recipienda decidua grana, ille est ⵙⵏⵉ defraudans pauperes. Peah 7. 3.
units.tr: were to set a basket beneath to catch the falling grains, he is defrauding the poor. Peah 7.3.

units.la: Omnes uvæ quibus non est קוח nec קוח (Vid. Buxtorf. in Lexic.) ad racemationem pertinent. Si in tota vinea solummodò tales uvæ reperiruntur, imò vineatam paucas produxisset, ut iam videmiata esse videretur, Akiba illam totam pauperibus attribuit. Si quis vineam suam sanctificaverit, ut fructus eius in templi usum cedant, antequàm scire potuerit an illo anno parvulas tantùm uvas quæ ad racemationem pertinent produētura sit, tunc vinea illa pauperibus non datur, At si illam sanctificat postquam viderit illam racemos tantùm aliquos habere; pauperibus relinquitur. Peah ubi supra v.4.5. & ult.
units.tr: All grapes which have neither [קוח] nor [קוח] (see Buxtorf in the Lexicon) belong to gleaning. If only such grapes are found in the whole vineyard, indeed if the vine has produced so few that it already seems to have been gleaned, Akiba assigns the whole vineyard to the poor. If someone consecrates his vineyard so that its fruit may be used for the temple, before he can know whether in that year it will produce only the small grapes that belong to gleaning, that vineyard is not given to the poor. But if he consecrates it after seeing that it has only some clusters, it is left to the poor. Peah ubi supra, v. 4, 5, and last.

units.la: RASURA. Hos radebant in festo, qui veniunt ex provincia maritima, (si illuc negotii vel mercaturæ causâ se contulerant) qui veniunt ex captivitate, aut ex carcere dimittuntur. Qui excommunicatus erat, sed per sapientem solutus est; Nasiræus etiam postquàm votum suum exequutus est. Moed Katon cap.3.1.
units.tr: SHAVING. At the festival they shaved those who came from the maritime province (if they had gone there on business or trade), those who came out of captivity, or those released from prison. Also one who had been excommunicated but was absolved by a sage, and a Nazirite after he had fulfilled his vow. Moed Katan ch. 3.1.

units.la: Summus Sacerdos radebatur rasurâ illâ quæ לוליניית ωχλιωδης vocatur Nedar. sol.51.1. Sanhed. sol.22.2. æstimabatur illa pulcherrima, & ita se habebat, ut caput pili unius pertingeret ad radicem pili alterius.
units.tr: The high priest was shaved with that shaving which is called luliniyit [לוליניית] and ōchliōdēs [ωχλιωδης]. Nedarim fol. 51.1; Sanhedrin fol. 22.2. It was judged most beautiful, and was such that the root of one hair reached to the root of another.

units.la: De rasura Vid. Comm.
units.tr: On shaving, see Comm.

units.la: Raca est vox contemnentis summo contemptu, & apud Hebræos usitatissima.
units.tr: Raca is a word of contempt, of the utmost scorn, and most frequent among the Hebrews.

units.la: Tanchum sol.5. col. 2. Rediit quidam ad pænitentiam: Dixit ei uxor ריקה Raca, si statutum est pœnitentiam agere, ipsum quo te accingis cingulum non erit tuum.
units.tr: Tanchum fol. 5, col. 2: A certain man returned to repentance. His wife said to him, Raca! If it is decided that you repent, the belt with which you gird yourself will not be yours.

units.la: Idem sol. 18 col. 4. Dixit Ethnicus Israelita, paratum tibi apud me est esculentum appositissimum. Quale nam est illud? inquit Iudæus, respondit alter, Caro suilla, ad quod Iudæus ריקה Raca, etiam de mundis apud vos non est comedendum.
units.tr: The same, fol. 18, col. 4: A Gentile said to an Israelite, A most suitable dish is ready for you at my place. "What is it?" said the Jew. The other replied, Pork. To which the Jew replied, Raca! Even of the clean things among you, it is not to be eaten.

units.la: Midrasch Tillim in Psal. cxxxvii. Nupta est Regis filia sordido cuidam nebuloni; imperat illE ut sibi adstaret ut servula. (ui illa, Raca, ego sum filia Regis. Vid. idem sol. 38. col. 4.
units.tr: Midrash Tillim on Psalm 137: A king's daughter was married to some filthy good-for-nothing, who ordered her to stand before him as a servant girl. She said, Raca, I am the king's daughter. See the same, fol. 38, col. 4.
