units.la: Bab. Beracot sol. 32.2. Religiosus quidam in via orans salutatus a duce non resalutavit, exspectavit ille donec orationem finiisset, Deinde ei dixit, ריקה Raca, scriptum est in lege vestra &c.
units.tr: Bab. Berachot fol. 32.2: A certain pious man, praying on the road, was greeted by a leader but did not return the greeting. The other waited until he had finished his prayer, and then said to him, Raca! It is written in your law, etc.

units.la: REFUGII urbes vid. Asylum.
units.tr: Cities of REFUGE: see Asylum.

units.la: REPUDIUM. Vix copiosius ullum caput doctrinæ Talmudicæ tractatur ac illud de repudio. In omnibus autem præcipua ipsorum sollicitudo est, ut legitimam formam & modum determinent repudii, de iusta causa parum anxii.
units.tr: DIVORCE. Scarcely any head of Talmudic doctrine is treated more fully than that of divorce. In all of them their chief concern is to determine the lawful form and manner of divorce; they are little anxious about a just cause.

units.la: Gloriantur sibi solis datum esse hoc privilegium, repudiare uxores. Hierof. Kiddushin sol. 583 Malach. 2. per totum capitulum Deus vocatur Dominus exercituum, vocatur autem Deus Israelis quando inquit שלח כי שנא Si odio habes dimittere illam, ut innotesceret Deum nomen suum repudii non subscripsisse, nisi solum inter Israelitas. Quasi dicat, Israelitis concessit uxorum dimissiones, non concessi gentilibus. Dicit Rabbi Chaja Rabba, Nationibus Mundi non concedantur repudia.
units.tr: They boast that this privilege of divorcing wives was given to them alone. Hierosolymitanum Kiddushin fol. 58.3. In Malachi 2, throughout the chapter God is called the Lord of hosts, but the God of Israel is named when he says, If you hate, send her away, [שלח כי שנא] so that it might be made known that God did not subscribe his name to a bill of divorce, except only among the Israelites. As if he were saying: the dismissal of wives was conceded to Israelites, not granted to the Gentiles. Rabbi Chaja Rabba says: Divorces are not to be granted to the nations of the world.

units.la: De causis repudii variè loquuntur, sunt qui graviores requirunt, alii verò etiam ob leviores id fieri posse credunt. Qui graviores postulant, locum Deut.24. de causa solum adulterii interpretantur.Gittin c.9.v.ult. Qui disciplinam Schammaana sequuntur, dicunt, לא יגרש ארם את אשתו אלא אם כן מצא בה דבר ערות Non expellet homo uxorem suam, nisi invenerit in ea rem nuditatis (i.e. adulterium.)
units.tr: They speak variously about the causes of divorce. Some require weightier causes, while others believe it may be done even for lighter ones. Those who demand weightier causes interpret Deut. 24 as referring only to the cause of adultery. Gittin ch. 9, last verse. Those who follow the school of Shammai say: A man shall not divorce his wife unless he finds in her some matter of nakedness [לא יגרש אדם את אשתו אלא אם כן מצא בה דבר ערות], i.e. adultery.

units.la: Gemara ibid. Illinc de re propositá edoceris, quòd si non invenerit in uxore turpitudinem, non licet dimittere.
units.tr: Gemara ibid.: From this you learn the matter at hand: if he does not find indecency in the wife, it is not lawful to divorce her.

units.la: Maymon in Hal. Girufchin. cap.10. 21. id quod dictum, restringit ad uxorem primam. Non expellit homo uxorem suam primam, nisi inveniat in ea ערות דבר rem aliquam turpem; ואין ראוי למהר לשלח אשתו ראסונה אגל שניה אם שנא' ישלחנה Neque decet ut festinet, & precipitanter dimittat uxorem suam primam, sed secundam si oderit eam, dimittere potest. Ita etiam Gittin ubi supra. R.Eliefer dicit, de dimissione uxoris prima, vel ipsum altare fundit lachrymas. Hanc Glossam sumunt ex Mal. 11. 15. Ne quis perfidè agat in uxorem iuventutis suæ.
units.tr: Maimonides, in Hal. Girushin ch. 10.21, restricts what was said to the first wife: "A man does not expel his first wife unless he finds in her ערות דבר [some shameful thing]." "It is not fitting to hurry or to dismiss one's first wife rashly, but a second wife, if he hates her, he may dismiss." So also the Gittin passage cited above. "R. Eliezer says that over the dismissal of a first wife even the altar sheds tears." They take this gloss from Malachi 2:15: "Let no one deal treacherously with the wife of his youth."

units.la: Illorum verò, qui ob quamvis fermè causam uxorem repudiare licitum esse existimarunt, ingentem faciunt numerum.
units.tr: Those who thought it lawful to repudiate a wife for almost any cause make up a very large number.

units.la: Abarbenel ex loco Deuteronomii duas generales repudii causas elicit. 1. est ערות דבר Turpitudo sive ea consistat in scortatione & adulterio ipso, sive in aliis, pudicitiam mulierum parum decentibus. 2. est, תלוף המוגים temperamenti & natura diversitas, ex qua ordinarię odia, displicentiæ,nauseæ,oriuntur.
units.tr: From the passage in Deuteronomy, Abarbanel draws two general causes of repudiation. (1) ערות דבר, turpitude, whether it consists in fornication and adultery itself or in other things that scarcely befit the chastity of women. (2) תלוף המוגים, diversity of temperament and nature, from which ordinary hatreds, dislikes and nausea arise.

units.la: Maiorem licentiam permittunt sequentes. Maymon ubi ante. Uxorem non bene moratam, & quæ non modesta fit, ut decet filiam Israelitica̅m, præceptum est ut dimittat. Idem habet Gittin ubi supra.
units.tr: Those who follow permit a greater licence. Maimonides, in the place cited above: "A wife who is not well behaved, and who is not modest as befits an Israelite daughter, he is commanded to dismiss." The Gittin passage cited above has the same.

units.la: Si quis uxorem odio habeat, (si non sit prima) eam dimittat. Maymon. Et R. Salomoh in loc. Malach. Vxorem dimittere præcipitur, si in oculis mariti gratiam non assequatur.
units.tr: "If someone hates his wife (if she is not the first), let him dismiss her." Maimonides; and R. Solomon on the passage. Malachi: "A wife is commanded to be dismissed if she does not win favour in her husband's eyes."

units.la: Gittin cap. 9. & comment. R. Salom. & R. Nissin. Hillelis sectatores dicunt, אפילו הקריאה תבשילו Expellere eam etiam potest, si edulium duntaxat ipsi adduslerit. Hi subtiliùs duo ista verba עורות דבר examinantes, voluerunt divisim esse exponenda, ut sensus illorum sit ac si dictum esset או ערוה או דבר Aut turpitudinem aliquam, aut rem aliam fœdam.
units.tr: Gittin ch. 9, with the commentary of R. Solomon and R. Nissim. The followers of Hillel say: "He may expel her even if she has only burnt his food." These men, examining the two words ערות דבר more subtly, wished them to be explained separately, so that their sense is as if it had been said: "either some turpitude, or some other foul thing."

units.la: Gemara in Gittin l. c. docet, causas repudii esse poss., si uxor in platea neverit, aut sila duxerit, sicque nuda brachia ostentarit, ורמה ופרומה משני צדדיה aut aperto pectore incesserit, aut laverit cum viris in eodem lavacro, vel in loco ubi viri lavare solent, aut si luserint cum iuvenibus.
units.tr: The Gemara in Gittin, in the place cited, teaches that the causes of repudiation may be: if the wife goes out into the street spinning thread, and so shows her bare arms; or walks out with her chest open, [ורמה ופרומה משני צדדיה]; or bathes with men in the same bath, or in a place where men are accustomed to bathe; or if she plays with young men.

units.la: In libro Kol Bo כל בו sol.88. col.3.4. Quid est עירות דבר ? Veluti si transgrediatur legem Mosis: Ex. gr. Si præbeat marito cibum qui non est decimatus; si menstruis laborans ministraverit ei. Si non abscindat particulam de massa ex qua panem faciunt: si votum faciat & id non observet: si transgrediatur leges verecundiæ, & honestatis, mulierum Iudaicarum; veluti si detecto capite exeat in plateam, si suco faciem suam pingat, si cum iuvenibus ludat.
units.tr: In the book Kol Bo, fol. 88, col. 3–4: "What is ערות דבר? For example, if she transgresses the law of Moses: e.g. if she gives her husband food that has not been tithed; if, while suffering her menstruation, she waits on him; if she does not separate the portion from the mass from which they make bread; if she makes a vow and does not keep it; if she transgresses the laws of modesty and decorum of Jewish women; for example, if she goes out into the street with her head uncovered, if she paints her face with juice, if she plays with young men."

units.la: Gioff. in Ammude Golah. Si fuerit exigens debitum coniugale a marito suo voce clara, ita ut eius vicina eam de hac re loquentem audire potuerint, aut si maledixerit socero suo, praesente marito suo.
units.tr: Joffe, in Ammude Golah: "If she demands the marital debt from her husband in a loud voice, so that her neighbours could hear her speaking of this matter; or if she cursed her father-in-law in her husband's presence."

units.la: Sic Maymon cit.tract. recenset, sufficientem repudii causam esse si sit rebellis marito suo, officium coniugale ipsi deneget, ipsum fastidiat, vel irritet. Si Sponsa quae completo tempore, quo nuptiae celebrandae sunt, refragatur; repudiari poterit. Sic si uxor se suspectam reddidit de re aliqua vehementer foeda ut si sola fuerit in cubiculo, & visus fuerit vir egredi, eoque egressio, illa statim visa fuerit de lecto surgere &c. De indifferenti dimissione festivus est R. Akiba in v.ult. c.9. Gittin. Si quis videat mulierem uxore formosiorem, uxorem dimittere licet; quia dictum est, si gratiam non assequatur in oculis eius.
units.tr: Thus Maimonides, in the tract cited, lists as a sufficient cause of repudiation that she is rebellious toward her husband, denies him conjugal duty, loathes him or provokes him. If a betrothed woman refuses when the time fixed for the wedding has come, she may be repudiated. So too if a wife has made herself suspected of some very foul act, as when she is alone in a bedroom and a man is seen leaving, and at his departure she is at once seen rising from the bed, and so on. On repudiation for no particular reason, R. Akiba is witty in the last section of ch. 9 of Gittin: "If someone sees a woman more beautiful than his wife, he may dismiss his wife, since it is said, if she does not find favour in his eyes."

units.la: In his casibus liberum est marito uxorem repudiare vel non repudiare, at si uxor deprehensa fuerit corpus suum prostituere, vel a marito vel a testibus fide dignis, tum nolens volens cogitur, etiam Iudicis authoritate interveniente, ipsam repudiare, sic tamen ut ipsi dare teneatur dotem propter nuptias, quam tamen admitteret uxor si propria eius confessio accederet. Maymon in Hal. cap. 24. 16.17.
units.tr: In these cases it is up to the husband whether or not he repudiates his wife. But if the wife is caught prostituting her body, whether by her husband or by trustworthy witnesses, then, willing or unwilling, she is compelled, even with the authority of a judge intervening, to be repudiated; yet he is bound to give her the dowry, which the wife would forfeit if her own confession were added. Maimonides in Hal. ch. 24.16–17.

units.la: Lepidae sunt istae historiolae quas de repudiantibus uxores quavis de causa legimus; Afferamus duas. Prima extat in Bava Metzia sol.101.2. Mercator quidam advenebat navem repletam dolijs vini, in locum quendam, & non inveniebat cellam in quam ea reponeret. Alloquitur mulierem quandam quae habebat cellam, ut eam sibi pro vino suo elocaret. Illa recusat. Ipse ut rebus suis consuleret, desponsat istam mulierem: mulier desponsata concedit ipsi locum pro vino: Ipse nactus loco statim domum abit, & scribit libellum repudii, eumque ad ipsam mittit: Mulier offensa conducit baiulos, & vinum eius iterum curat e cella extrahi, & in plateam reponi &c.
units.tr: Ridiculous are the little stories which we read of men repudiating wives for any cause. Let us bring forward two. The first is in Bava Metzia, fol. 101.2. A certain merchant was arriving at a certain place with a ship loaded with casks of wine, and he did not find a cellar in which to store it. He addressed a certain woman who had a cellar, asking her to let it to him for his wine. She refused. He, to look after his goods, betrothed this woman; the betrothed woman granted him a place for the wine. He, having secured the place, at once went home, wrote a bill of divorce and sent it to her. The woman, offended, hired porters and had his wine taken out of the cellar again and placed in the street, and so on.

units.la: Altera extat in Gittin sol. 34.1. R. Gidol Ben Reilai, mittebat sine ulla causa libellum repudii uxori suae; cum vero ipsa nollet statim acceptare, sed iuberet latorem crastino die redire, R. Gidol poenitentia ductus, Deo gratias egit, quod non acceptasset libellum.
units.tr: The other is in Gittin, fol. 34.1. R. Gidol ben Reilai sent a bill of divorce to his wife without any cause; but when she was not willing to accept it at once, and told the bearer to return the next day, R. Gidol, moved by repentance, gave thanks to God that she had not accepted the bill.

units.la: Pro talibus quibus repudiare uxores in deliciis fuit, factus est ille Canon qui legitur in Iebham. sol.52. & quo permittitur sponso ut si ita lubuerit ante nuptias libellum repudii scribendum curet ut illum deinde statim tradere queat, ubi ipsi placuerit repudium facere. Verba sic sonant: St quis Scriba dixerit, scribe libellum repudii sponsae meae לכשאכנוסנה אגרשנה quo eam postquam duxero dimittam, גט הרי זה גט talis libellus est legitimus.
units.tr: For such men, who took delight in repudiating wives, that canon was made which is read in Yebamot, fol. 52, by which it is permitted to a betrothed man, if he so wishes, to have a bill of divorce written before the wedding, so that he may afterwards hand it over at once whenever he pleases to divorce. The words run thus: "If a scribe says, write a bill of divorce for my betrothed, [לכשאכנוסנה אגרשנה] that I may divorce her after I have married her, [גט הרי זה גט] such a bill is a valid bill of divorce."

units.la: Recensebimus nunc quaedam alia defectus naturales praecipue spectantia quae occasionem vel marito vel uxori repudiandi dare possunt.
units.tr: We shall now recount certain other natural defects, chiefly those which can give occasion for repudiation either to the husband or to the wife.

units.la: Si quis מוּם Apostata & Hæreticus factus elt cogitur maritus uxori libellum repudii dare, tunc enim ut mortuus consideratur. Akedath Izchak sol.152.col.3. Abarbenel Coment.in Deut. f.383.col.1.Schulchan Aruch p. 4.ad Num.154.§.1.
units.tr: If anyone becomes an apostate and heretic, [מוּם], the husband is compelled to give his wife a bill of divorce, for then he is regarded as dead. Akedath Izchak, fol. 152, col. 3; Abarbanel's commentary on Deuteronomy, f. 383, col. 1; Shulchan Aruch, part 4, on Num. 154, §1.

units.la: Ob hæc vitia Vxor virum libellum repudii sibi dandi coram iudice, si velit, cogere potest. Fœtor oris: Fœtor narium: Impotentia: Si mutato mundo & honesto opificio immundum tractare coeperit, veluti si lucri causâ converrat fimum, si fiat coriarius, metallarius. Si accideret ut maritus esset מוּם ויחין שׁ Malignus ulceribus laborans, aut alio contagioso & insanabili morbo esset affectus, ipsos etiam invitos separant.
units.tr: For these defects the wife may, if she wishes, compel her husband before a judge to give her a bill of divorce. Bad breath; a foul smell from the nostrils; impotence; if, having changed his trade and honourable occupation, he begins to handle filth, as when for gain he sweeps up dung, or becomes a tanner or a metalworker. If it should happen that the husband is [מוּם ויחין], a malignant sufferer from ulcers, or is affected with some other contagious and incurable disease, they separate them even against their will.

units.la: Omnia vitia naturalia quæ prophanum & illegitimum reddunt Sacerdotem, prophanam quoque reddunt mulierem,& præter illa adhuc sequentia. Fœtidus sudor, fœtor oris, Cicatrix ex morsu canis, verruca in fronte; si decem annis cum marito habitarit, & ille nullos ex ea liberos suscep… Si ter abortiverit הוחוקה לנפלים inepta iudicatur ad liberos in lucem edendos. Vid. Maym.Hal. אשות cap.15.& 11.
units.tr: All natural defects that make a priest profane and unfit also make a woman profane, and besides these the following: foul sweat, bad breath, a scar from a dog's bite, a wart on the forehead; if she has lived with her husband for ten years and he has had no children by her; and if she has miscarried three times she is judged unfit to bring children into the light. See Maimonides, Hal. Ishut, ch. 15 and 11.

units.la: Libellus repudii apud Iudæos vocatur ספר אגרת & גט פשורין, & גט, & ספר תיוכין & כריתו שנוקין Vxor dimitti non potuit, nisi dato libello repudii: vocatur ergo (inquit Baal Turim in Deut. xxiv.) ספר כריתות libellus abscissionis, eò quod nih l aliud sit, quod eam à marito exscindat.
units.tr: Among the Jews a bill of divorce is called ספר אגרת, גט פשורין, גט, ספר תיוכין, and כריתו שנוקין. A wife could not be dismissed unless a bill of divorce was given; therefore it is called (says Baal Turim on Deuteronomy 24) ספר כריתות, "book of cutting off," because it is nothing other than that which cuts her off from her husband.

units.la: Vxor non dimittebatur nisi libenter volente marito; reluctante enim non erat repudium: at velit, nolit uxor, repudianda est, si velit maritus. Maymon in Girufchin cap.1.
units.tr: A wife was not dismissed unless the husband was willing; for if she was unwilling there was no repudiation. But whether the wife is willing or not, she must be repudiated if the husband wishes it. Maimonides, Girushin, ch. 1.

units.la: Libellus repudii duodecim lineis debet conscriptus esse, nec pluribus nec paucioribus. Rafchba in Tikkun Get. Rationem huius numeri duplicem habent, 1. quia talis est valor numericus literarum in voce ꝏ. 2. quia illo linearum numero separantur libri legis: quatuor enim lineæ intercedunt inter librum Geneseos & librum Exodi, & totidem inter Exodi librum & Leviticum, & inter Leviticum & librum Numerorum. At quatuor inter librum Numerorum & Deuteronomii non reputantur, eò quòd liber iste sit tantum repetitio legis. Vid. R. Mardochai in cap.1. in tractatum Git- tin .
units.tr: A bill of divorce must be written in twelve lines, neither more nor fewer. Rafchba in Tikkun Get. They give a twofold reason for this number: (1) because the numerical value of the letters in the word Get [גט] is twelve; (2) because the books of the Law are separated by this number of lines. For there are four lines between the book of Genesis and the book of Exodus, as many between Exodus and Leviticus, and as many between Leviticus and Numbers. But no four lines are counted between Numbers and Deuteronomy, because that book is merely a repetition of the Law. See R. Mardochai on chapter 1 of the tractate Git-tin.

units.la: Exemplar libelli repudiatorii habes apud Alphesium Maymonidem in Girufchin f. 273. Alphesii verba sic Latinè reddidit Cl. Ligtfootus.
units.tr: You have a copy of the bill of divorce in Alphesius Maimonides, Girufchin, f. 273. Cl. Lightfoot rendered the words of Alphesius into Latin as follows.

units.la: LIBELLVS REPVDII.
units.tr: THE BILL OF DIVORCE.

units.la: DIE Hebdomadis N. Mensis N. anni à condito mundo N. computo quo numerare consuevimus in provincia N. Ego N. filius N. quocunque nomine vocitor, de civitate N. cum summo animi consensu, atque absque ulla coactione urgente, repudiavi, dimisi, atque expuli te, te, inquam, N. filiam N. quocunque nomine vociteris, de civitate N. ita ut libera & de iure tuo sis, nuptum iri cuicunque placuerit, & nemo te reprimat, ab hodierno die usque in perpetuum. Libera es ergò cuivis homini: Atque hic esto tibi à me libellus repudii, literæ divortii, & schedula expulsionis, secundùm legem Mosis atque Israëlis.
units.tr: On the day of the week N., the N. day of the month N., in the year N. from the creation of the world, reckoned as we are accustomed to count in the province of N., I, N., son of N., by whatever name I am called, of the city of N., with the fullest consent of my mind and without any urgent compulsion, have divorced, dismissed and cast out you, you I say, N., daughter of N., by whatever name you are called, of the city of N., so that you are free and at your own disposal, to marry whomever you please, and let no one restrain you, from this day forever. Therefore you are free to be married to any man. And let this be to you from me a bill of divorce, a letter of separation and a writ of dismissal, according to the law of Moses and of Israel.

units.la: Ruben fil. Iacobi testis. Eliezer filius Gilead testis.
units.tr: Reuben son of Jacob, witness. Eliezer son of Gilead, witness.

units.la: Libellus hic, sigillo mariti roboratus & subscriptione testium, in manus uxoris tradendus erat, aut ab ipso marito, aut ab aliquo in hoc munus deputato. De subscriptione, nota illud quod exstat in Gittin sol.36.1. scilicet, Rabbinos quosdam in libellis divortii non semper nomina sua expresse scripsisse, cùm illos subsignabant: sed certa quædam signa habuisse quæ apponerent, veluti unus appingebat piscem, alter ramum dactyli. Et deinde literis significabant qualia signa haberent, illis quorum hoc scire intererat.
units.tr: This bill, sealed with the husband's seal and signed by the witnesses, was to be handed into the wife's hands either by the husband himself or by someone appointed for this task. Concerning the signing, note what is found in Gittin fol. 36.1, namely that some rabbis, when they signed bills of divorce, did not always write out their names in full, but had certain marks which they put down; one would draw a fish, another a branch of a date palm. And afterwards they indicated by written notes what marks they had, for the benefit of those who needed to know.

units.la: Libellus repudii uxori tradendus non erat, nisi duobus præsentibus, qui libellum perlegerent: & antequàm libellus in manus uxoris daretur & etiam post, cumque dabatur, maritus si præsens erat sic inquiebat. Ecce hic est tibi libellus repudii.
units.tr: A bill of divorce was not to be given to a wife unless two people were present to read through the bill. Both before the bill was put into the wife's hands and afterwards, and while it was being handed over, the husband, if he was present, spoke thus: Behold, here is your bill of divorce.

units.la: Vxori dimissæ licuit, si visum esset, libellum hunc ad Synedrium adducere, & rogare ut in rei memoriam inter archiva conscriberetur. Si deinde alicui denuò nubere vellet, id facere ipsi licuit, modò maritus clausulâ aliquâ in libello repudii ipsi obicem non posuerit.
units.tr: A divorced wife was permitted, if she wished, to bring this bill before the Sanhedrin and ask that it be recorded among the archives as a memorial of the matter. If she then wished to marry again, she was free to do so, provided the husband had not placed some obstacle in the bill of divorce by a clause.

units.la: Plurimi fuerunt quibus satis grave erat suas uxores dimittere, ita ut à Synedrio aliquando verberibus ad illam dimissionem adigi debuerint. De hoc fonat Maymonidis locus in cap.2. Girufchin. מי שהרין נותן שכופין אותו לגרש את אשתו ולא רצה לגרש בית דין של ישראל בכל מקום וככל וכן מכין אותו עד שיאמר רוצה אני Illum de quo Senatus decrevit quod debeat dimittere uxorem, si illud facere renuerit, omni tempore & loco ad illud faciendum verberibus adigunt.
units.tr: There were many men for whom it was hard enough to dismiss their wives, so that at times the Sanhedrin had to compel them to that dismissal with blows. Maimonides' passage in chapter 2 of Gittin speaks to this: [מי שהרין נותן שכופין אותו לגרש את אשתו ולא רצה לגרש בית דין של ישראל בכל מקום וככל וכן מכין אותו עד שיאמר רוצה אני]. Anyone of whom the court has decided that he must divorce his wife, if he refuses to do so, they compel him to do it, at any time and in any place, by blows.

units.la: Superfunt plurima alia, quibus recenfendis brevitatis causâ fuperfedêmus, adeat qui volet Maymonidis tractatum modò citatum, in quo ad naufeam ufque circa hanc materiam curiofus eft.
units.tr: There are very many other matters, which for the sake of brevity I pass over. Whoever wishes may consult the treatise of Maimonides cited just now, in which he is curious about this subject to the point of nausea.

units.la: Notat Cl. Caftellus in rad. שהר, quòd ille qui apud Arabes uxorem repudiare volebat, illam fic alloqueretur fit עלי אנת כטהר אמי Abi, namitu mihi es ut dorfum matris mee.
units.tr: Cl. Castellus, in the root shhr, notes that a man among the Arabs who wished to divorce his wife addressed her thus: ['alayya anta ka-zahri ummi] Go away, you are to me as the back of my mother.

units.la: Hebraeorum mens eft Repudium uxorum ex iure naturali ab ipfis rerum primordiis licitum fuiffe, & proinde nec infolitum Patriarchis. Sic enim inquiunt בני נוח אין להן קידושין אין להן גירושין Noachidae [fic indigitant eos, qui partim ante, partim poft legem Mofis, eiufdem legi non fubfuerunt] nec fiunt nuptiae, fcil. folennes, nec divortia, qualia interveniente iudicii fententia apud Hebraeos in ufu erant: שניהם מגרשין זה את זה fed alteruter copiagum pro lubitu coniugium folvit. Vide Gemaram Hierof. ad Sanhed. cap. 7. & Maymon in Halac. Melacim cap.9. Sic apud Romanos olim & Graecos, tam mulier quàm vir alter alteri dicere potuit, ut res fuas fibi habeat: Si vir uxorem dimiffiet, difcelfio illa
units.tr: The mind of the Hebrews is that divorce of wives was lawful from the beginning of things by the natural law, and therefore not unusual even for the patriarchs. For they say: [Bnei Noach, ein lahem kiddushin, ein lahem gerushin] Noachides (so they designate those who were not under the law of Moses, whether before or after it) have no marriages, that is, no solemn ones, and no divorces, such as were in use among the Hebrews, with a judicial sentence intervening; [shenehem megarshin zeh et zeh] but either of the pair dissolved the union at will. See the Jerusalem Gemara on Sanhedrin chapter 7, and Maimonides in Hilchot Melachim chapter 9. Thus among the Romans and Greeks of old, both wife and husband could say to each other that each should keep their own goods. If a husband dismissed his wife, that parting was called apomomi; if a wife bade farewell to her husband, it was called apeleusis. See Scaliger on Eusebius, number 2015.

units.la: vocabatur ἀνπομμι, si mulier viro valedixisset, ἀπέλευσις. Vid. Scaliger. Animad. Euseb. num. 2015.
units.tr: (Continued from the previous unit: such a parting was called apomoi, and a wife's farewell apeleusis.)

units.la: Resurrectio. De illa vide Sanhed. sol. 90. 2. sol.92.1. Cl. Cocceium in Sanhed. 317. Cl. Buxt. Cofri 73. Amama Antib. Biblic. 967. Biblic. 967. Buxt. Synag. Iud. cap. 31. Cl. Pocockii Portam Mosis. n. 180.
units.tr: Resurrection. On this see Sanhedrin fol. 90.2 and fol. 92.1; Cocceius on Sanhedrin 317; Buxtorf, Cosri 73; Amama, Antibiblicus 967; Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica chapter 31; Pocock, Porta Mosis, number 180.

units.la: Sadducæi λέγουσιν μὴ ἐἶναι ἀνάστασιν. Sic Tanchum sol.3.1. Sadducæi negant, dicuntque deficit nubes, atque abit; sic descendens in sepulchrum non redit.
units.tr: The Sadducees say [λέγουσιν μὴ ἐἶναι ἀνάστασιν] that there is no resurrection. So Tanchuma fol. 3.1: The Sadducees deny it, and say that a cloud fails and passes away; so one who goes down into the grave does not come back.

units.la: Argumentationes pro resurrectione mortuorum sunt variæ, illæ quæ propius accedunt ad argumentationem Christi Matth. 22. sunt sequentes.
units.tr: The arguments for the resurrection of the dead are various; those which come closest to the argument of Christ in Matthew 22 are the following.

units.la: Init. cap. Chelek in Bab. Sanhed. Dixit R. Eliesser Ben Rabbi Iose. Hac in re ego falsitatis incusavi Scribas Samaritanorum, qui dicunt, resurrectionem mortuorum non probandam esse e lege: Dixi illis vos falsificatis legem vestram (vos legem vestram false interpretamini,) nec quicquam reportatis in manibus vestris; nam dicitis, resurrectio mortuorum non est e lege, cum dicat, Excidendo excidetur anima ista, iniquitas eius super eam. Num. 15.31. Excidendo excidetur nempe ab hoc mundo. Iniquitas eius super eam: quando? Nonne in mundo futuro?
units.tr: At the beginning of the chapter Chelek in Bab. Sanhedrin. Rabbi Eliezer ben Rabbi Jose said: In this matter I charged the scribes of the Samaritans with falsehood, who say that the resurrection of the dead cannot be proved from the law. I said to them: You falsify your law (you misinterpret your law falsely), and you gain nothing in your hands; for you say that the resurrection of the dead is not from the law, when it says, That soul shall utterly be cut off, her iniquity shall be upon her. Numbers 15:31. Utterly be cut off, namely from this world. Her iniquity shall be upon her: when? Is it not in the world to come?

units.la: Christus dicit ὃν ἐγὼ ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ ... Confer R. Tanchum sol.13.3. Deus sanctus Benedictus nomen suum iustus non adiungit dum vivunt, sed tamen post mortem eorum, postquam eos dereliquit malus affectus) Reperitur quidem nomen suum adiunxisse Isaaco cum viveret, (Gen. scil.28.13.) sed respiciebatur pulvis eius, ac si collectus super altare. R.Berachia dixit, à quo cacus factus est, fuit sicut mortuus.
units.tr: Christ says [ὃν ἐγὼ ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραάμ] "I am the God of Abraham..." Compare Rabbi Tanchuma, fol. 13.3: God, blessed be his holy name, does not join his name to the just while they live, but only after their death, when the evil disposition has left them. It is indeed found that he joined his name to Isaac while he was alive (Genesis 28:13), but his dust was regarded as if it were gathered upon the altar. Rabbi Berachiah said: he from whom the blind man was made was like a dead man.

units.la: Item Hierof.Berac.sol.5.4. Iusti etiam in morte dicuntur vivi, & impii etiam in vita dicuntur mortui, hoc probant ex quod dicitur, Et dixit ei, Hac est terra de qua iuravi Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Iacobo, לאמור Quid sibi vult vox לאמור? Dicit ei abi & dic patribus quodcunque promisi vobis, prastiti filiis vestris.
units.tr: Likewise the Jerusalem Berachoth fol. 5.4: The just are said to be alive even in death, and the wicked are said to be dead even in life; they prove this from what is said: And he said to him, This is the land of which I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, [lemor] What does the word [lemor] mean? It says to him: Go and tell the fathers, whatever I promised you, I have performed to your sons.

units.la: In Zohar in Gen. 206. & 324. item Berefchit Rabba f.28. pro resurrectione argumentantur ex eo, quia תרוד דקב os spina dorsi est incorruptibile. Illud argumentum pluribus exstat in Midrasch Cohelet sol.114.3. Adrianus cuius ossa conterantur, & nomen deleatur, inteergavit R. Iosuam Ben Chanania: Vnde homo revivisci tempore futuro? Respondit ille, à Luz in spina dorsi. Dicit ille, demonstra hoc mihi. Accepit ille Luz officiculum de spina dorsi & indidit aqua, & non fuit humiditate aqua emollitum: Indidit igni & non fuit adustum; subiecit mola, & non fuit contritum; positum in incude percussit malleo, scissa est incus, & ruptus malleus. Sit tibi ô Iudæe Luz origo & semen resurrectionis tuæ; nostrum est Christus qui se ipsum suscitavit à mortuis & factus est nobis primitiæ dormientium.
units.tr: In the Zohar on Genesis, pages 206 and 324, and likewise Bereshit Rabba fol. 28, they argue for the resurrection from the fact that the luz, the bone of the spine, is incorruptible. This argument is found at greater length in Midrash Qohelet fol. 114.3: The emperor Hadrian, whose bones were to be ground up and whose name was to be blotted out, asked Rabbi Joshua ben Hananiah: How will a man be revived in the time to come? He answered: from the luz in the spine. He said: Show me this. He took a little bone from the spine of a luz and put it in water, and it was not softened by the moisture of the water; he put it in fire, and it was not burnt; he put it under a millstone, and it was not crushed; he placed it on an anvil and struck it with a hammer, and the anvil was split and the hammer broken. Be it so, O Jew: the luz is the origin and seed of your resurrection; ours is Christ, who raised himself from the dead and became to us the firstfruits of those who sleep.

units.la: Resurrectionem nullam fore credunt nisi in terra Israelis, Vid. Ægyptus. qui extra illam moriuntur, debent per infimos terræ meatus in terram Canan revolvi.
units.tr: They believe there will be no resurrection except in the land of Israel. Those who die outside it, must be rolled through the lowest passages of the earth into the land of Canaan. See Egypt (?).

units.la: Hierof. Kilaim cap.ult. An Rabbini qui moriuntur in captivitate pereunt ? Dixit R. Ibb S. Imai, Deus perfo. at ipsis terram, & illi devolvuntur instar Doliorum vini, postquàm in terram pervenerunt, Spiritus ipsorum redit ad ipsos. Vid. etiam Ketubbot sol. iii. i. R. Salomoh Gen. 47. 29. ad verba Ne sepelias me in Ægypto. Kimchi ad Ezech. 37.12. Tanchum princip. seet. ויחי יעקוב.
units.tr: Jerusalem Kilaim, last chapter: Do the rabbis who die in captivity perish? Rabbi Ibbo, son of Rabbi Imi, said: God brings them to the land, and they are rolled along like barrels of wine; after they have reached the land, their spirit returns to them. See also Ketubbot fol. 3.1. Rabbi Solomon on Genesis 47:29, on the words Do not bury me in Egypt. Kimchi on Ezekiel 37:12. Tanchuma, beginning of the section Vayechi Yaakov.

units.la: Zohar col. 206. Non dat Deus mortuis animas nisi in terra Israelis, q. d. Ezech. 37.13. Cùm aperuero sepulchra &c.
units.tr: Zohar page 206: God does not give souls to the dead except in the land of Israel, as if to say Ezekiel 37:13: When I have opened your graves, etc.

units.la: Sanhed. sol. 91. 1. ווי לכון חייביא דאמר יתון ד מיתי לא חיין Vae vobis improbi (Sadducaei) qui dicitis mortuos non revicturos: Cùm illi qui antea non vixerunt facti sunt vivi, an non illi qui vixerunt multò magis?
units.tr: Sanhedrin 91.1: "Woe to you, wicked ones (Sadducees), who say that the dead will not live again! When those who did not live before have become alive, will not those who lived much more?" [ווי לכון חייביא דאמר יתון ד מיתי לא חיין]

units.la: Fovent quidam ut Bechai paras. זאת הכרכ f. 227. col.3. Caphtor sol.51. 2. in Comment μετεμψύχωσιν, & dicunt animam hominis etiam in avem migrare posse. Probabile tamen est illorum authorum mentem fuisse ἀνασπάσεις, & aliquid ad terrendum peccatorem effingere.
units.tr: Some, such as Bechai on the parashah ... (f. 227, col. 3) and Caphtor (Sanhedrin 51.2, in the commentary), favour metempsychosis [μετεμψύχωσιν] and say that the soul of a man can also pass into a bird. It is probable, however, that these authors meant anaspaseis [ἀνασπάσεις] and invented this to frighten the sinner.

units.la: Rex. Tria praecepta data sunt Israelitis, tempore ingressus ipsorum in terram Canaan, למנות להם מלך ut constituerent sibi Regem. (Deut.17 15.) Ut exciderent semen Amalek', & ut aedificarent בית הבחירה domum Sanctuarii. Si itaque electio Regis ordinata fuit, quare Deo displicuit cùm Israelitae à Samuele Regem petebant? לפי ששאלו בהדעובת ולא שאלו לקיים המצוה אלא ספני שקצן בשמואל הנביא ? Quia regem concupiverunt per querelas & seditiosas voces, non uti legis praeceptum peragerent, sed quia ipsis displicebat vates Samuel.
units.tr: Kings. Three commands were given to the Israelites when they entered the land of Canaan: to appoint a king over themselves (Deut. 17.15) [למנות להם מלך]; to destroy the seed of Amalek; and to build the house of the Sanctuary [בית הבחירה]. If, then, the choice of a king was ordained, why did it displease God when the Israelites asked Samuel for a king? [לפי ששאלו בהדעובת ולא שאלו לקיים המצוה אלא ספני שקצן בשמואל הנביא] Because they desired a king through complaints and seditious cries, not to carry out the precept of the law, but because they disliked the prophet Samuel.

units.la: K k
units.tr: K k

units.la: [Hebrew: אין מעמידין מלך בתחילה] Non constituibant regem ab initio nisi ex sententia Synedrii magni, & ex ore Prophetæ, sicuti Iosua quem præfecit Moses Senatusque eius. Et sicuti Saul & David, qui per Samuelem & Senatum eius electi fuerunt.
units.tr: [Hebrew: אין מעמידין מלך בתחילה] They did not set up a king at the beginning except by the decision of the great Sanhedrin and at the word of a prophet, as Joshua, whom Moses appointed, with his council. And as Saul and David were chosen through Samuel and his council.

units.la: Non eligunt regem ex peregrinis ; etiam post plurimorum seculorum decursum [Hebrew: עד] [Hebrew: שתהיה אמו משראל] nisi mater ipsius Iudaea sit, Nec hoc solum circa regnum observatur, sed etiam circa omnia reliqua munia, quæ in Israele sunt obeunda.
units.tr: They do not choose a king from foreigners, not even after many centuries have passed, unless his mother is a Jewess [עד שתהיה אמו משראל]. Nor is this observed only in regard to the kingship, but also in regard to all the other offices that are to be discharged in Israel.

units.la: Ad regnum non eligunt fœminam, quia dicitur statuito super te regem, non reginam. Regem non faciunt, Lanium, Tonsorem, Balneatorem, Textorem aut Coriarium, non quia tales per se ad regnum omnino inepti sint, sed quoniam ob vilitatem horum opificiorum à populo perpetuò sannis excipiebantur. Qui per unicum diem uni ex his opificiis adhæserit, iam ineptus est ad regnum.
units.tr: For the kingship they do not choose a woman, because it is written "set a king over you," not a queen. They do not make a king of a butcher, barber, bath-attendant, weaver or tanner. This is not because such men are altogether unfit for kingship, but because, on account of the lowliness of these trades, they were constantly mocked by the people. Anyone who has followed one of these trades for even a single day is already unfit for kingship.

units.la: Postquàm Rex electus est ungitur oleo [Hebrew: המשחה] Unctionis, si scilicet ex familia Davidis fuerit, alias simpliciter adhibent [Greek: ἀρόματος] Oleum Balsaminum. Vid. Oleum.
units.tr: After the king is chosen he is anointed with oil of unction [המשחה], if he is of the family of David; otherwise they simply use balsam oil [ἀρόματος]. See Oil.

units.la: Quando ungunt reges ex familia Davidis [Hebrew: אין משחין אותן אלא על הנעין] ungunt nisi apud fontem. [Cuius ritus aliam non invenio probabilem rationem, quàm ut ille locus Regi novo aliquod bonum omen præberet, & subditi hanc spem de illo conciperent, quod sicuti fons & rivulus prata arvaque quæ alluit & irrigat proventu læta reddit, ita fore ut Rex suo prudenti regimine regnum stabiliret, illos omnes varia felicitate beatos redderet, hoc videntur Talmudici voluisse in Crituth cap.5.
units.tr: When they anoint kings of the family of David, they anoint only at a spring. [I find no other probable reason for this rite than that the place gave the new king a good omen, and that his subjects conceived this hope about him: just as a spring and a stream make the meadows and fields they water fruitful and happy, so the king by his prudent rule would establish the kingdom and make all his people happy with varied prosperity. This the Talmudists seem to have meant in Crituth ch. 5.]

units.la: תנו רבנן אין מושחין את המלכים אלא על המעיין כרי שתמשך מלכותן שנא והורדתם אותו גיחון וגו׳
units.tr: תנו רבנן אין מושחין את המלכים אלא על המעיין כרי שתמשך מלכותן שנא והורדתם אותו גיחון וגו׳

units.la: Tradunt Magistri nostri reges non unqi nisi iuxta fontem, ut extrahatur (dilù firmum sit) regnum ipsorum; prout dicitur. 1.Reg.1.33. deducatis eum ad Gichon.]
units.tr: Our teachers hand down: kings are anointed only beside a spring, so that their kingdom may be drawn out (that is, made firm), as it is said: 1 Kings 1.33, "bring him down to Gihon."

units.la: Non ungitur Rex qui filius Regis est, nisi forte orta sit dissensio aut bellum, tunc ungunt ipsum ad omnem controversiam tollendam, ita unctus fuit Salomoh propter Adoniam; Ioas propter Athaliam, Iehoachas propter Iehoiakim.
units.tr: A king who is the son of a king is not anointed, unless perhaps a dissension or war has arisen; then they anoint him to remove every controversy. Thus Solomon was anointed on account of Adonijah, Joash on account of Athaliah, and Jehoahaz on account of Jehoiakim.

units.la: Rex qui unctus est, regnum cum posteris suis, perpetuò possidet, quia regnum hereditarium est. Si Rex mortuus filium reliquit minorennem, regnum ipsi custodiunt, donec maturam aetatem attigerit, ita fecit Iehoiada Ioaso. Ille qui in divisione hereditatis praecederet, praecedit quoq; in hereditate regni: ita praecedit maior natu minorennem. Ita David postquàm unctus fuit, coronà regni d' gnus cum omnibus liberis suis masculis fuit: nemo autem regno dignus est nisi sit probus. Et quamvis regno nemo dignus sit nisi probus, regnum tamen numquam aufertur à semine Davidis secundum dictum Psal.89.31. & 110. Solium tuum erit stabile in aeternum. Si accideret ut aliquis alius quam ex familia Davidis Rex fieret, vel à Propheta aliquo ex aliqua alia tribu constitueretur, cessaret quidem regnum ipsorum, ut in Hieroboamo
units.tr: A king who has been anointed possesses the kingdom perpetually, together with his posterity, because the kingdom is hereditary. If a dead king has left a minor son, they keep the kingdom for him until he reaches maturity; so Jehoiada did for Joash. He who would precede in the division of an inheritance also precedes in the inheritance of the kingdom; thus the elder by birth precedes the younger. So, after David was anointed, the crown of the kingdom was due to him together with all his male children. Yet no one is worthy of the kingdom unless he is upright. And although no one is worthy of the kingdom unless he is upright, the kingdom is nevertheless never taken from the seed of David, according to Psalm 89.31 and 110: "Your throne shall be stable forever." If it happened that someone other than of the family of David became king, or was appointed by some prophet from another tribe, their kingdom would indeed cease, as appears in the case of Jeroboam;

units.la: [Remaining marginal notes and catchword illegible.] apparet; sed id non perpetuò sed tantùm ad tempus fit. Maym. Hal. Melachim c.1.
units.tr: [Remaining marginal notes and catchword illegible.] but this is not perpetual, only for a time. Maym. Hal. Melachim c. 1.

units.la: Regem magno afficiunt, honore, & ponunt terrorem & reverentiam eius in corda omnium. Regis equo non insident (Vid. Caput 2. Sanhed.) folium eius non occupant, nec utuntur ipsius sceptro, aut coronâ aut alio vase utensilium eius. Nam illo mortuo hæc omnia comburuntur.
units.tr: They hold the king in great honour, and place his terror and reverence in the hearts of all. They do not sit on the king's horse (see ch. 2 of Sanhedrin), they do not occupy his throne, nor do they use his sceptre, his crown, or any other of his vessels or utensils. For when he dies, all these things are burned.

units.la: [illegible, ~12 letters] Famulitio autem eius ut & Gynecæo, aut aliis ancillantibus, nemo utitur nisi Rex qui succedit; hac ratione Abisag licita fuit Salomoni, & prohibita Adoniæ. Regis uxor verò nunquam ab alio duci potest, etiam non licet Regi viduam aliam ducere, aut repudiatam Regis præcedentis.
units.tr: [illegible, about 12 letters] No one uses his household servants, nor his harem or other attendants, except the king who succeeds him. On this ground Abishag was lawful for Solomon and forbidden to Adonijah. The king's wife, however, can never be taken by another; nor may a king marry another widow, or a divorced woman of the previous king.

units.la: Prohibitum est regem videre cùm nudus est, aut cùm raditur, aut in balneo est, aut à sudore abstergitur.(Hæc enim omnia Regis Maiestatem diminuunt, & reverentiam in alpicientibus tollunt.)
units.tr: It is forbidden to see the king when he is naked, or when he is being shaved, or when he is in the bath, or when he is wiping away sweat. (For all these things diminish the majesty of the king and take reverence away from those who look upon him.)

units.la: Regi Calceus non extrahitur, nec ille præstat ius leviri, & quamvis Rex id facere vellet ipsum tamen non audiunt: Et quamvis Rex de honore suo remisisset, remissus tamen non est.
units.tr: A shoe is not taken off the king, nor does he perform the duty of a levir. And although the king might wish to do so, they would not listen to him. And although the king had remitted something of his honour, nevertheless it was not remitted.

units.la: Rege mortuo, vidua eius quia Leviro nubere non potest, perpetuò in suo conclavi sedet. Si aliquis ex familia regia fato fungitur, Rex extrà portam Palatii non egreditur. Cùm ipsi exhibetur epulum funerale omnis populus humi recumbit, ille verò in lecto accumbit. Si Rex in templo, Israelis atrium ingreditur & est ex familia Davidis, ibi sedêre potest: quia nullis aliis regibus quam illis ex stirpe Davidis sessio in atrio licita est.
units.tr: When the king dies, his widow, since she cannot marry a levir, sits perpetually in her chamber. If someone of the royal family dies, the king does not go out through the gate of the palace. When a funeral feast is set before him, the whole people recline on the ground, but he reclines on a couch. If the king enters the court of Israel in the temple and is of the family of David, he may sit there, because sitting in the court is permitted to no kings other than those of the stock of David.

units.la: Rex singulis diebus tondetur, ornatque seipsum & induitur pulchris vestimentis. In Palatio suo sedet in solio regni, caput coronâ redimitum habens. Omnes deinde coram ipso comparent quando ipsi placet, stantes coram illo, & ad terram se incurvantes. At Sacerdos magnus ad Regem non venit, nisi voluerit: nec coram Rege stat, sed Rex stat coram ipso, sicuti dicitur Numer. 27. 1. Coram Eleasaro Sacerdote stabit. Interim tamen etiam præceptum est Summo Sacerdoti honorare regem, & ipsum dum ad se venit ad sedendum invitare, & coram ipso stare. Stat autem Rex præcipuè coram Summo Sacerdote, quando Vrim & Thummim consulitur.
units.tr: The king is shaved every day, adorns himself and puts on fine garments. He sits in his palace on the throne of the kingdom, his head crowned. Then all come before him whenever it pleases him, standing before him and bowing down to the ground. But the high priest does not come to the king unless he wishes to; nor does he stand before the king, but the king stands before him, as it says Numbers 27.21: "He shall stand before Eleazar the priest." Meanwhile, however, it is also commanded that the high priest honour the king, invite him to sit when he comes to him, and stand before him. The king stands especially before the high priest when Urim and Thummim are consulted.

units.la: Præceptum est Regi honore excipere doctores legis, quare si ad ipsum accedunt Senatores Synedrii,& Sapientes Israelis, coram ipsis assurgit & ad latus suum assidére iubet; ita fecit Asa Rex Iehudæ (in Sanhed. id dicitur de Josaphat) discipulum sapientis enim è solio suo assurgens exosculatus est, & ipsum Dominum & Rabbi vocavit.
units.tr: It is commanded that the king receive the teachers of the law with honour. So if the senators of the Sanhedrin or wise men of Israel approach him, he rises before them and bids them sit at his side. So King Asa of Judah did (in Sanhedrin it is said of Jehoshaphat): rising from his throne, he kissed a disciple of a wise man and called him Lord and Rabbi.

units.la: Talem humanitatem autem Rex solùm adhibet remoris testibus & in occulto, nam publicè coram nemine assurgit, neminem tenerè aut molliter alloquitur: Ut timor eius in omnium corde sit.
units.tr: The king grants such courtesy only to a few witnesses and in secret; for publicly he rises before no one, and he speaks tenderly or gently to no one, so that fear of him may be in everyone's heart.

units.la: Sicuti Scriptura vult ut Rex maximo honore afficiatur, ita viceversa vult, ut cor regis humile sit; sit & erga omnes gratiosus & misericors, propendeat semper ad manfuetudinem; nam (ut notat R. Levi Ben Gerfom) Israelitarum conditio non est, ut rex aliquis eos iudicet profua voluntate, ut faciunt imperatores gentium, qui constituunt populis suas leges prout libuerit. Vid. Maymon ubi supra cap. 2.
units.tr: Just as Scripture wills that the king be honoured with the greatest respect, so conversely it wills that the heart of the king be humble; let him also be gracious and merciful towards all, and always inclined to gentleness. For (as R. Levi Ben Gershom observes) the condition of the Israelites is not such that a king should judge them by his own will, as the emperors of the nations do, who lay down laws for their peoples as they please. See Maimonides, above, chapter 2.

units.la: Rex debet legem describere, quamvis antecessor eius codicem ipsi reliquisset, & illam corrigere ex authentico codice conservato in Sanctuario; illum librum legis semper secum habere in bello & in pace, nec ullo tempore illum seponere, nisi in illis locis in quibus in lege studere prohibitum est, qualia sunt balnea, secreta.
units.tr: The king ought to copy out the law, even though his predecessor had left him a codex, and to correct it from the authentic codex kept in the Sanctuary; he is to keep that book of the law always with him, in war and in peace, and never to put it aside, except in those places where it is forbidden to study the law, such as baths and privies.

units.la: Rex ultra octodecim uxores, sive sint concubinae sive uxores rite ductae, non habeat. (Vid. Gemaram Sanhed. Cohen Gadol.) Equos ultra quos currus eius requirunt non multiplicet; imo prohibitum est ut ullum habeat equum, qui (pompae gratia) vacuus ante ipsum currat: ut mos est caeterorum regum: si unum superaddit, vapulat, (de iure, nam de facto quis verbera inflixisset?)
units.tr: The king shall not have more than eighteen wives, whether they are concubines or lawfully married wives. (See the Gemara, Sanhedrin, Cohen Gadol.) He shall not multiply horses beyond those which his chariots require; indeed it is forbidden for him to keep any horse which runs empty before him for show, as is the custom of other kings. If he adds one, he is beaten (by law; for who in fact would inflict the blows?).

units.la: Argentum ultra quod necessarii requirunt usus ne multiplicet, collectum in thesauro templi deponat: ut inde depromatur cum usus feret. Prohibetur autem multiplicatio argenti praecipue respectu propriorum thesaurorum in quibus Reges gloriari solent.
units.tr: He shall not multiply silver beyond what necessary uses require; he shall deposit what is collected in the treasury of the Temple, so that it may be drawn out as use demands. The multiplication of silver is forbidden chiefly with regard to private treasuries, in which kings are wont to glory.

units.la: Rex non debet esse vinolentus, & bibere more inebriantium: Nec se amoribus nimium dare, aut ita deperire aliquam ex suis uxoribus, ut semper apud ipsam reperiatur כשאר הטשפים ut alii fatui in usu habent.
units.tr: The king ought not to be a drunkard, nor to drink in the manner of those who become intoxicated; nor should he give himself too much to loves, or so dote upon any of his wives that she is always found with him, as other fools are wont to do.

units.la: Reges ex familia Davidis iudicant & iudicantur, de ipsis etiam testimonium dicitur. Sed de Regibus Israelis qui non ex stirpe Davidis sunt, decreverunt sapientes, ne iudicentur, aut testimonium de ipsis dicatur מפני שלבן גם כהים quia cor ipsorum elatum est, & ab illis scandalum & damnum legi oriri posset. (causa decreti huius reperitur in Sanhed. Cohen gadol cap.2. ubi Rex Iannæus in ius vocatus Synedrio non debitam reverentiam exhibuit.)
units.tr: Kings of the house of David judge and are judged, and testimony may be given about them. But concerning kings of Israel who are not of the stock of David, the sages decreed that they should not be judged, nor that testimony be given about them, because their heart is lifted up, and scandal and loss could arise for the law from them. (The reason for this decree is found in Sanhedrin, Cohen Gadol, chapter 2, where King Jannaeus, summoned to judgment before the Sanhedrin, did not show the due reverence.)

units.la: Rex interficere potest illos qui ipsi rebelles sunt, aut qui ipsum contemp serunt, sed supplicium nullum adhibere potest, præter gladii supplicium. Potest etiam scutica percutere ob honorem suum, sed non publicare opes, ne audiat raptor. Deo tamen magis obediendum est quàm Regi, si aliquid contrà legem eius præciperet. דברי חרב ודברי העבד ודברי הרב קודשין Habemus verba Domini & servi, sed Domini verba semper precedunt.
units.tr: The king may kill those who rebel against him, or who despise him, but he may apply no punishment except the sword. He may also strike with the whip for the sake of his honour, but he may not make his wealth public, lest the robber hear of it. Yet God is to be obeyed rather than the king, if he should command anything contrary to his law. We have the words of the Lord and the words of the servant, and the words of the master are holy; but the words of the Lord always precede.

units.la: Homicidas absque demonstratione & processu prævio interficere potest. Potest occidere plures unà die (quod Synedrio non licuit, vid. Sanhed. cap.14.) & patibulo suspendere, suspensosque relinquere per plures dies להשיל אימה ולשבר יד רשעי העולם ad terrorem incutiendum & frangendam manum improborum mundi. Maymon Hal. Melach. cap. 3.
units.tr: He may put murderers to death without proof and without prior trial. He may slay several in one day (which the Sanhedrin was not permitted to do; see Sanhedrin, chapter 14), and hang them on a gibbet, leaving them hanging for several days, to strike terror and to break the hand of the wicked of the world. Maimonides, Hilchot Melachim, chapter 3.

units.la: Potestatem habet Rex tributum imponendi, telonia ordinandi, ad suam & bellorum necessitates. Potest legere undiquaque ex terra Israelitica viros fortes in militiam suam. Ita ad opera sua adhibēre potest omnes opifices, servos & ancillas; at dando ipsis mercedem promeritam.
units.tr: The king has the power of imposing tribute and of establishing tolls, for his own needs and those of wars. He may levy from the whole land of Israel strong men for his army. Likewise he may employ all craftsmen, male and female servants for his works; but he must give them their earned wages.

units.la: Vxores ducit Rex literis dotalibus & sponsalibus, pellices vero absque illis ;& per solam cohabitationem. Illas pellices si lubuerit in coquas & famulas iterum ordinare poterit. Si in bellum egressus fit Rex, vicina prædia in suum usum convertere poterit, si aliunde non suppetat victus.
units.tr: The king takes wives by marriage contracts and betrothal documents, but concubines without those, and by cohabitation alone. If he wishes, he may again appoint those concubines as cooks and maidservants. If the king goes out to war, he may convert neighbouring estates to his own use, if sustenance is not otherwise available.

units.la: Decimas habet Rex, ex seminibus & arboribus, iumentisque, & de omnibus terris quas subigunt Israelitæ, tollit partem unam e tredecim. Qui à Rege occiduntur, bona ipsorum veniunt in ipsius fiscum.Si quę regna subiugantur, Regni illius thesauri & suppellex,Regi accedunt in solidum, cæteris vero prædas bonorum mobilium quas prædantur dividunt: ipse dimidiam partem primò sumit, altera deinde pars inter Duces suos & populum tum præsentem, cùm castra & sarcinas custodientem æqualiter distribuitur. Ex regione ipsa potest servis suis distribuere & sibi reservare sicuti bonum ipsi visum fuerit: Modò omnia opera eius tendant ad res rite componendas. שאין ממליכין מלך תחילה אלא לעשות משפט ומלחמה Nam Rex ab initio non in alium finem constitutus est, nisi ut faciat iudicium & gerat bellum. Maym.cit.tracl.c.4.
units.tr: The king has tithes from seed and trees, from beasts of burden, and from all lands which the Israelites subdue, he takes one part in thirteen. Goods of those who are put to death by the king pass into his treasury. If any kingdoms are subdued, the treasures and furnishings of that kingdom fall wholly to the king; but of the spoils of movable goods which they plunder, they divide the rest: he first takes half for himself, and the other half is then distributed equally among his leaders and the people, both those present and those guarding the camp and baggage. From the land itself he may distribute to his servants and reserve for himself as seems good to him; provided that all his acts tend to the rightful ordering of affairs. For a king was not appointed at the beginning for any other end than that he should do judgment and wage war. Maimonides, cited treatise, chapter 4.

units.la: De bellis Regis vld. Bella. Rex Messias qui venturus est, restituet regnum Domus Davidis in integrum ad dignitatem pristinam. Maym. ubi supra cap. 9
units.tr: On the wars of the king see Bella. The Messiah King who is to come will restore the kingdom of the house of David to its former dignity in full. Maimonides, above, chapter 9.

units.la: In ulu erat apud reges plantare arbores, sub quibus ambulando possent umbram captare. Gloss. in Erubhin sol. 25. 2. ad verba אנרנקא חני לית
units.tr: It was the custom among kings to plant trees, under which they might walk and seek shade. Gloss on Eruvin, folio 25, on the words anrnqa chni lit.

units.la: Si essent omnia maria atramentum, & omnes iunci calami, & coelum pelles, & omnes homines scribæ, non sufficerent describere profunditatem cordis potestatis regiæ. Schabbat f. 11.
units.tr: Even if all the seas were ink, and all the reeds pens, and the heavens skins, and all men scribes, they would not suffice to describe the depth of the heart of royal power. Shabbat, folio 11.

units.la: Rex similis est vestimento, quod si breviores fimbrias habeat, turpitudinem hominis eo induti revelabit, cum in publicum prodierit; si vero longiores, in iis intercipiuntur pedes eius, ut ad lapsum impellatur: postquàm autem ceciderit, quis ipsum sublevabit. Cl.Castell. cit. in בלש.
units.tr: The king is like a garment: if it has shorter hems, it will reveal the shame of the man who wears it when he comes out in public; if longer, his feet are caught in them, so that he is driven to a fall; and once he has fallen, who will raise him up? Castell, cited work, under bls.

units.la: Memorabilis est ille ritus, quo Rex in solenni panegyri in lege legere debebat. Ceremoniam integram apponemus. Præceperat Moses lectionem regis Deut.13.10.11. Circunstantiæ loci, temporis, personæ ita referuntur in Sotah cap.7. R.Salom. in Deut.31. Maymon in Chagigah per. 1. Qui legere debebat Rex erat; locus in quo lectio fieri debebat, erat atrium mulierum, ut eò mulieres & infantes se conferre possent, & lectioni interesse, nam in atrium Israelis ipsis venire non licuit. Paratum erat ibi ידי שלמה Suggestum ligneum quod Rex ascendebat, & in illo considebat. Minister congregationis חזן הכנסת sumebat librum legis, & illum tradebat capiti congregationis. Ille Præsul libērum deferebat ad סגן Summi Sacerdotis vicarium. Vicarius ad Summum Sacerdotem, qui illum Regi porrigebat. Rex surgens illum recipiebat, & stans fundebat preces, sicuti in usu habent illi qui se ad lectionem accingunt. Si sedens legere voluisset id ipsi licebat, magis honorificum tamen ipsi erat si stans legeret: sicuti fecit Rex Agrippa.
units.tr: Memorable is that rite by which the king was obliged to read the law at the solemn festival. We shall set out the whole ceremony. Moses had prescribed the reading of the king, Deut. 31:10-11. The circumstances of place, time and person are related in Sotah, chapter 7; Rabbi Solomon on Deut. 31; Maimonides on Chagigah, chapter 1. The one who was to read was the king; the place where the reading was to be made was the court of the women, so that women and infants might betake themselves there and be present at the reading, for they were not permitted to enter the court of Israel. There was prepared there a wooden platform, the bema of Solomon, which the king ascended, and on it he sat. The minister of the synagogue, chazzan, took the book of the law and handed it to the head of the congregation. That president handed the book to the deputy of the High Priest, the vicar. The vicar passed it to the High Priest, who presented it to the king. The king, rising, received it, and standing poured out prayers, as those who prepare themselves for reading are accustomed to do. If he wished to read sitting, this was permitted him; yet it was more honourable for him to read standing, as King Agrippa did.

units.la: Lectionem incipiebat ab init. Deut. ad verf. 10. cap.6. Deinde à versu 13. cap. undecimi ad v.22. eiusdem capitis legebat. Inde iterum pergebat ad v.22. cap.14. & legebat usque ad versum 2. cap. 29. Sufficere enim exiftimarunt si præcipuè illas legeret petiochas quæ maximè ad obseruationem legis ipsum exstimulare possent. Memoratur loco Sota citato de Rege Agrippa, ipsius oculos stillasse lachrymas cùm illum uersum legisset Deut.xvii.15. Non poteris tibi præficere virum extraneum qui non frater tuus sit. Sibi enim conscius erat, quòd non ex stirpe Iudaica esset: populus tamen ipsum consolari voluit, triplici blandâ allocutione, dicendo אל תירא אגריפס אחינו אחרי Ne timeas Agrippa, frater noster es.
units.tr: He began the reading at the beginning of Deuteronomy, to verse 10 of chapter 6. Then from verse 13 of chapter 11 to verse 22 of the same chapter he read. Thence he went on again to verse 22 of chapter 14 and read as far as verse 2 of chapter 29. For they judged it sufficient if he read especially those sections which could most stimulate him to the observance of the law. It is recorded in the Sotah passage cited that of King Agrippa, tears fell from his eyes when he read the verse Deut. 17:15: Thou shalt not set a stranger over thee, who is not thy brother. For he was conscious that he was not of Jewish stock; but the people wished to console him with a threefold kindly address, saying: Fear not, Agrippa, our brother, you are our brother.

units.la: Hæc regis lectio vocatur פרשת המלך & debebat necessario in lingua Hebraea fieri. Vide Haphtarot.
units.tr: This reading of the king is called the portion of the king, and it had of necessity to be made in the Hebrew language. See Haphtarot.

units.la: RHINOCORURA. Vid. Interpretes.
units.tr: RHINOCORURA. See Interpreters.

units.la: ROMA. החשובה של אדום היא רומי Roma est urbs præstantissima regni Edom. R.Salom. Num.24.19. (Qui locus tamen in editione Basil. ut & plurimi alii, nescio quo zelo omissus fuit: optarem ego ut nobis libros integros ac non castratos reliquissent.)
units.tr: ROME. [החשובה של אדום היא רומי] Rome is the most eminent city of the kingdom of Edom. R. Salomo. Num. 24.19. (This passage, however, like many others, has been omitted from the Basel edition through some zeal I cannot account for. I wish they had left us the books whole and not mutilated.)

units.la: Quicquid Prophetæ dixerunt de vastatione Edom in ultimis diebus id de Roma intellexerunt. Kimchi in Obadiam c. 1. Iesai;34.1. in prima edit. Venet. quæ omnium laudatissima.
units.tr: Whatever the prophets said about the devastation of Edom in the last days, they understood of Rome. Kimchi on Obadiah, ch. 1; Isa. 34.1, in the first Venice edition, which is the most highly praised of all.

units.la: Servator egressurus est ex Roma Metropoli & vastaturus est eam. Bechai (ad Hakkemach cap. ult. lit.3. In vastatione Romæ illico erit Redemptio nostra. Zeror Hamor sol. Schophetim. Sunt plurima alia in scriptis Hebræorum quæ abundè malig:num ipsorum in Romam assectum testantur.
units.tr: The Saviour is going to come out of Rome, the metropolis, and will lay it waste. Bechai (on Hakkemach, last chapter, letter 3): In the destruction of Rome our redemption will come at once. Zeror Hamor, fol. Schophetim. There are very many other things in Hebrew writings which abundantly attest their malice towards Rome.

units.la: De origine Romæ loquitur Sanhed. edit. Venet. sol.21.2. Eâ horâ quâ Salomoh duxit filiam Pharaonis, descendit Gabriel, & fixit Calamum in mare, qui ascendere fecit canem, & in eo edificata est, civitas magna quæ est Roma.
units.tr: The origin of Rome is discussed in Sanhedrin, Venice edition, fol. 21.2: At the hour when Solomon took the daughter of Pharaoh, Gabriel descended and fixed a reed in the sea, which brought up a dog, and on it was built the great city which is Rome.

units.la: Item Hieros. cap. 1. Die quo erexit Jeroboam duos vitulos, venerunt Remus & Romulus, & adificarunt duo tugurria Romæ. Vid. Schabbat sol. 56.2. Medrasch Rabba Cant. Cant. sol.9.3. ubi dicitur locum illum in quo duo illi fratres sua tuguriola ædificarunt, vocari רומי בבלי Roma Babylon. Consule etiam Medrasch Psal.10.
units.tr: Likewise the Jerusalem Talmud, ch. 1: On the day Jeroboam set up the two calves, Remus and Romulus came and built two huts at Rome. See Shabbat, fol. 56.2; Midrash Rabba on the Canticles, Cant. fol. 9.3, where it is said that the place in which those two brothers built their little huts is called Rome Babylon. Consult also the Midrash on Psalm 10.

units.la: S.
units.tr: S.

units.la: SABBATHUM quando principium sumserit vid. Cosri sol. 88. Quæ beneficia observatio illius nobis afferat exponuntur in En Israel 73.1. Baal Hatturim Exod.35.3. Abrahamum Sabbathum non observasse dicit Berefchit Ketanna Genef. 2.3. Patres in deserto illum quoque non observarunt. Siphre num.9.5. Gentiles ad Sabbathum observandum non obligantur. Sanhed. sol.58.2.
units.tr: For when the Sabbath began, see Cosri, fol. 88. What benefits its observance brings us is explained in En Israel 73.1. Baal Hatturim, Exod. 35.3, says that Abraham did not observe the Sabbath; Bereshit Ketanna, Gen. 2.3. The Fathers in the wilderness did not observe it either: Siphre, Num. 9.5. Gentiles are not obliged to observe the Sabbath: Sanhedrin, fol. 58.2.

units.la: Vesperà Sabbathum præcedente si quis confspeƈtâ stellâ unâ laborare pergit, liber est à reatu, si verò conspeƈtis duabus, laborem continuet, reatum contrahit: si exspeƈtát donec conispiciantur tres, tunc planè peccat. Hieros. Berachot sol.2. col.2.
units.tr: If on the evening before the Sabbath someone, having seen one star, continues to work, he is free from guilt; but if he continues after seeing two, he incurs guilt; if he waits until three are visible, then he plainly sins. Jerusalem Talmud, Berachot, fol. 2, col. 2.

units.la: Nemo vesperà Sabbathum antecedente ante sacrificium vespertinum coram tonsore sed at, aut balneum ingrediatur, donec preces peregerit. Tria dicenda sunt unicuique in vespera Sabbathi domui suæ, postquàm tenebræ obortæ sunt: Decimastis e? Parastisne mixtionem ciborum? Accendite lucernam.
units.tr: No one on the evening before the Sabbath, before the evening sacrifice, should sit before a barber or enter a bath until he has finished his prayers. Three things are to be said by each man in his house on the Sabbath eve, after darkness has fallen: Have you tithed? Have you prepared the mixture of food? Light the lamp.

units.la: In Sabbatho non licet canalem frigidæ, calidæ immittere. Non subjicere licet vas lucernæ ad oleum excipiendum. Camelus cum capistro, Camelus fœmina cum annulo, asinus Lydius cum fræno, equus cum catena, alia animalia cum suis retinaculis egredi possunt.
units.tr: On the Sabbath it is not lawful to direct a channel of cold or hot water into a place. It is not lawful to set a vessel under a lamp to catch the oil. A camel may go out with its halter, a female camel with its ring, a Lydian ass with its bridle, a horse with its chain, and other animals with their own fastenings.

units.la: Mulier exire non potest in Sabbatho, cum tæniis laneis & lineis, neque cum frontalibus, aut genarum ornamentis, nisi assuta fuerint: neque cum corona, neque cum acu perforata, neque cum annulo in quo est sigillum: Exire tamen potest secundùm Sapientes cum globulo Balsami, cum filis comæ, cum pipere & grano salis in ore; modò non indiderit primùm in Sabbatho. Dentem verò sive aureum sive alìûs alius materiae ori impositum Sabbatho ferre Sapientes vetant.
units.tr: A woman may not go out on the Sabbath with woollen or linen ribbons, nor with frontlets or cheek ornaments, unless they are sewn on; nor with a crown, nor with a pierced pin, nor with a ring that bears a seal. She may, however, according to the Sages, go out with a ball of balsam, with threads for her hair, with pepper, and with a grain of salt in her mouth, provided she did not first put them in on the Sabbath. But a tooth, whether of gold or of some other material, placed in the mouth, the Sages forbid to be carried on the Sabbath.

units.la: Viro in Sabbatho egredi non licet cum foleis clavis plenis, neque cum lorica, neque Calside, neque cum gladio aut arcu, aut scuto aut lancea, mutilus exit cum fulcro suo filii cum corrigiis alligatis, filii regum cum tintinabulis. Maffecet Schabbat cap. 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6.
units.tr: A man may not go out on the Sabbath with shoes full of nails, nor with a breastplate, nor with a helmet, nor with a sword, bow, shield or spear. A cripple goes out with his crutch; the sons of kings go out with bells on. Maffecet Schabbat, ch. 1–6.

units.la: Regulam generalem de Sabbatho hanc definierunt Rabbini; Quicunque oblivisciitur fundamenti Sabbathi, & facit opera multa in Sabbathis multis, non est reus nisi peccati unius, quicunque vero sciens fundamentum Sabbathi, multa opera in Sabbathis multis fecerit, reus est de unoquoque Sabbatho.
units.tr: The rabbis laid down this general rule about the Sabbath: Whoever forgets the foundation of the Sabbath and does many works on many Sabbaths is guilty of only one sin; but whoever knowingly, knowing the foundation of the Sabbath, does many works on many Sabbaths is guilty for each and every Sabbath.

units.la: Opera per quae reus fit homo lapidationis atque excisionis, si ex praesumptione ea faciat, sacrificii autem pro peccato si ex ignorantia מהן אבות ובהן תולדות sunt vel primitiva vel derivativa. (Maim.Schabbat cap.8.) Ex primitivis enumerantur triginta novem, ex quibus sunt, Arare, serere, metere, manipulos colligare, triturare, cribrare, commolere, pinsere &c. tondere oves, lanam fingere &c. Derivativa vel species iistorum generum sunt ea quae eiusdem cum iis sunt classis & similitudinis. Ex. gr. Fossio est eiusdem generis cum aratione; olerum in fructula dissectio eiusdem classis cum commolitione; & spicarum avulsio eiusdem rationis cum messione. Hinc Maym. l. m. c. Maeens Sabbatho vel tantillum reus est קוצר תולש ותולש תולדות Et vellere spicas est species messionis: (patet hinc ratio, cur Matth. 12.2. causam discipulorum tam ardenter agat, Salvator, agebatur enim de capite.)
units.tr: The works by which a man becomes liable to stoning and excision, if he does them presumptuously, or to a sin offering if he does them in ignorance, [מהן אבות ובהן תולדות] are either primary or derivative. (Maimonides, Shabbat, ch. 8.) Thirty-nine primary works are listed, among them: ploughing, sowing, reaping, binding sheaves, threshing, winnowing, grinding, sifting, kneading, and so on; shearing sheep, spinning wool, and so on. Derivative works, or species of these kinds, are those that belong to the same class and resemblance. For example, digging is of the same kind as ploughing; cutting vegetables into small pieces is of the same class as grinding; and plucking ears of grain is of the same nature as reaping. Hence Maimonides, in the same place: One is guilty of even a little reaping on the Sabbath. [קוצר תולש ותולש תולדות] Reaping, uprooting and plucking are derivatives; and plucking ears is a species of reaping. (From this it is clear why our Lord, in Matt. 12.2, argues so vehemently for the disciples' cause, for the matter at issue was a capital one.)

units.la: Prolixi sunt admodum in recensione casuum quæ in Sabbatho licent vel non licent; pauca solum adhuc notabimus. In Sabbatho non licet viris uxores ducere aut fœminis nubere. Maymon Hal. אישות c.10.14. Sani Medicinam ne adhibento Sabbatho. (confer Matth. 12.10.) Qui æger est lumbis ne oleo vel aceto locum assectum ungat: ast oleo licet modo non rosaceo, &c. Dolens dentibus acetum ne absorbeat, iterum exsputurus: at absorbere licet, modo deglutiat. Gutture dolens oleo ne gargarizet: at oleum deglutire licet, unde si fanetur, bene est. Ne mastichen quis masticet, aut dentes aromatibus confricet in medela; si vero hoc faciat ad suaveolentiam oris, permittitur. Vinum oculo dolenti non indunt. Fomentationes, aut olea, loco affecto, non applicant. Maymon in Schabb. c. 21.
units.tr: They are very lengthy in enumerating the cases which are or are not permitted on the Sabbath; we will note only a few more. On the Sabbath it is not lawful for men to take wives, nor for women to marry. Maimonides, Hal., ch. 10, 14. Healthy people must not apply medicine on the Sabbath (compare Matt. 12.10). One who is sick in the loins must not anoint the affected place with oil or vinegar; but oil is permitted, provided it is not rose oil, etc. One who suffers in the teeth must not swallow vinegar, since he would have to spit it out again; but swallowing it is permitted, provided he swallows it down. One who has a sore throat must not gargle with oil; but it is permitted to swallow oil, so that if he recovers, all is well. One must not chew mastic, or rub the teeth with spices as a remedy; but if he does so for sweetness of breath, it is allowed. They do not put wine into a painful eye. They do not apply fomentations or oils to the affected part. Maimonides, in Shabbat, ch. 21.

units.la: Qui duas literas scribit, sive dextra sive sinistra sua, sive de nomine uno, sive de nominibus duobus, reus est violati Sabbath. Qui venatus fuerit avem in aviarium magnum abigendo, & capream in domum, reus est. Omnes scripturas Sanctas eripiunt die Sabbathi ab incendio, sive in illis legant sive non; si gentilis accenderit lucernam, poterit eius lumine Israelita uti, ut etiam gradibus quos sibi fecit, aut ad aquandum, aut ad descendendum.
units.tr: Whoever writes two letters, whether with his right hand or his left, whether of one name or of two names, is guilty of breaking the Sabbath. Whoever hunts a bird by driving it into a large aviary, or a roe into a house, is guilty. On the Sabbath they snatch all the holy Scriptures from a fire, whether they read them or not. If a Gentile lights a lamp, an Israelite may use its light; and likewise the steps which the Gentile made for drawing water or for going down.

units.la: Non obstetricantur bestiæ die Sabbathi, adjuvant tamen. At fœminæ obstetricantur in Sabbatho, & obstetrici licet umbilicum ligare, & venam abscindere: omnia quoque facere licet in Sabbatho quæ ad circumcisionem pertinent. Operarii in Sabbatho conducendi non sunt. Mortuo omnia necessaria fieri possunt Schabbat à cap.11. ad 23.
units.tr: Animals do not act as midwives on the Sabbath, though they help. But women may act as midwives on the Sabbath, and it is lawful for the midwife to tie the umbilical cord and to cut a vein. It is also lawful to do on the Sabbath everything that pertains to circumcision. Workers are not to be hired on the Sabbath. For the dead, all necessary things may be done. Shabbat, from ch. 11 to 23.

units.la: Innuit D. N. I. Matth.12.11. ipsos in Sabbatho etiam animalia si in foveas incidissent extrahere in usu habuisse. De illo casu sic loquuntur Hierof. in Iom.tobh sol.62. Si bestia atque eius fœtus incidant in foveam die festo; R. Lazar dicit, priorem elevet, eo fine ut occidat; & occidat, alteri autem pabulum ministret ne moriatur. R.Iosua dicit elevet utramque &c.
units.tr: Our Lord, in Matt. 12.11, hints that they were accustomed on the Sabbath to draw out even animals which had fallen into pits. The Jerusalem Talmud, Yom Tob, fol. 62, speaks thus of that case: If a beast and its young fall into a pit on a festival day, R. Lazar says: lift up the first, with the aim that it be killed; and let it be killed; but feed the other so that it does not die. R. Joshua says: lift up both, etc.

units.la: Maymon. in Schabb. cap.25. Si bestia incidat in foveam, aut in stagnum aquarum, alimenta ei possessor in ipso loco ministret, si possit: sin minus pannos & stramenta afferat, & bestiam suffulciat; unde si possit ascendere ascendat.
units.tr: Maimonides, in Shabbat, ch. 25: If an animal falls into a pit or into a pool of water, the owner shall provide it with food in that very place, if he can; if not, let him bring cloths and straw and prop up the beast; and so, if it can climb, let it climb up.

units.la: Sed videtur insuper hanc ipsorum praxin non parum ponderis ex hoc Canone habuisse. Tenere admodum curandum est de bonis & facultatibus Israelitarum, Hierof.ubi modo.
units.tr: But it seems that this practice of theirs derived no little weight from this canon: One must take the greatest care of the goods and property of the Israelites. Jerusalem Talmud, where above.

units.la: §. Circuncisio & Sabbathum fuerunt ante legem, Midrasch Tillim sol.15. Redempti sunt Israelitæ ex Ægypto, ob observatam illic Circuncisionem & Sabbathum. Baal Hatturim Exod.1. Fuit Sabbathum iam ab initio mundi. R. Salomoh Efai.lviii.14. Adamus creatus est vespere Sabbathi, ut illico subiret præceptum. Bab.Sanhed.sol.38.1. Nihil interest inter diem festum & Sabbathum Nisi quòd in eo pro cibo sint carnes animalium.Nihil interest inter Sabbathum & diem expiationis, nisi quòd contemptus illius ab hominibus vindicetur,huius verò per manum Dei.
units.tr: §. Circumcision and the Sabbath existed before the law. Midrash Tillim, fol. 15. The Israelites were redeemed from Egypt on account of circumcision and the Sabbath observed there. Baal Hatturim, Exod. 1. The Sabbath existed from the beginning of the world. R. Solomon on Isa. 58.14. Adam was created on the evening of the Sabbath, so that he might at once undergo the command. Bab. Sanhedrin, fol. 38.1. There is no difference between a festival day and the Sabbath, except that on the former there is meat of animals for food. There is no difference between the Sabbath and the Day of Atonement, except that contempt for the former is avenged by men, but contempt for the latter by the hand of God.

units.la: Traditio est שאין שבות אסור בםקרש In Sanctuario nullas prohibitiones respectu Sabbathi esse, si itaque accideret ut festi Paschatis primus dies in quo agnus macta-batur, incideret in Sabbathum, nulla Sabbathi consideratione habità omnes Paschatis requisita fecerunt. De hac permissione in Sabbatho necessitates templi faciendi, loquitur Christus Matth.12 5.
units.tr: There is a tradition, that in the Sanctuary there are no prohibitions with respect to the Sabbath [שאין שבות אסור במקדש]. So if it happened that the first day of the Passover feast, on which the lamb was slaughtered, fell on the Sabbath, they performed all the requirements of the Passover without any regard for the Sabbath. Christ speaks of this permission to do the necessary work of the temple on the Sabbath in Matt. 12. 5.

units.la: §. Conclusum est à Iudæis Sabbathum cœnâ vel convivio. In quo candelam adhibuerunt (sicuti etiam faciunt ad ingressum Sabbathi) & vinum & aromata, & formulam benedictionis super poculo vini, & deinde super candela, & deinde super aromatibus. Si Sabbathum exit cum est in medio convivii sui, (Paterfamilias nempe vel Rabbinus) finem imponit comestioni, manus lavat, & super poculo vini gratias agit pro vitu, & postea super poculo illo formulâ orationis utitur in separationem Sabbathi à die communi. &c. Maymon Hal.Schabbat c.29.
