units.tr: §. It is settled among the Jews that the Sabbath is ended with a supper or banquet. For this they used a candle (as they also do at the beginning of the Sabbath), wine and spices, and a formula of blessing over the cup of wine, then over the candle, and then over the spices. If the Sabbath departs while he is in the middle of his feast (namely the head of the household or a rabbi), he brings the eating to an end, washes his hands, and gives thanks over the cup of wine for the food, and afterwards uses over that cup a formula of prayer for the separation of the Sabbath from an ordinary day. etc. Maimonides, Hilchot Shabbat ch. 29.

units.la: Proprii limites Sabbathi erant à Sole occidente ad solem occidentem: hinc nemo aliquod opus die Sabbathum antecedente inchoare debet, nisi illud perficere queat מכעור יום Dum adhuc est dies. i. e. (ut ipsi explicant) עם יום שמש dum adhuc sol non occidit. Schabbat cap.1. Idem vult Hierof.Scheviit sol.33 1. Vespere Sabbathi permittitur opera incumbere, usquedum sol occidat. Sed sicuti post occasum solis
units.tr: The proper limits of the Sabbath ran from sunset to sunset; hence no one ought to begin any work on the day before the Sabbath unless he could finish it while it is still day [מבעוד יום], that is (as they themselves explain) while the sun has not yet set [עם יום שמש]. Shabbat ch. 1. The Jerusalem Talmud, Shevi'it fol. 33 col. 1, holds the same. On the evening of the Sabbath it is permitted to apply oneself to work, until the sun sets.

units.la: nullus labor fieri debuit Sabbato ingrediente, ita quoque nullus fieri debebat Sabbatho egrediente nisi iam sol occidisset. Non autem opera facere licuit statim post occasum solis, sed solum postquam illud tempus praeteriisset, quod vocant בין השמשות & quod proprie significat inter soles, phraseologia deducta a duplici שקיעות occasu solis. De illo tempore sic disputant in Hierof. Beracot sol.2.2. Quid est בין השמשות ? Dicit Rabbi Tanchuma; est instar guttae sanguinis cadentis in aciem gladii, quae se dividit utrinque. Quid est בין השמשות ? Est ab eo tempore, quo occidit sol, usquedum ambulet quis ad dimidium miliaris. R. Iose dicit, est sicut illus oculi. Clarius, quid בין השמשות sit & quando opera incipere liceat, definit Maymon. in Schabbat c.5. Ab eo tempore quo occidit sol, usquedum appareant tres stellae mediana, vocatur בין שמשות Inter soles: & dubium est num tempus illud sit de die, an de nocte. Utcunque de eo ubique iudicant להחביר ad gravandum officium. Intra illud tempus ergo non accenduntur lucernam Sabbathicam: & quicunque servile aliquod opus fecerit vesperâ Sabbathi, aut exitu Sabbathi, tenetur ad Sacrificium pro peccato. Haec eo diligentius notanda sunt, quo maiorem lucem foenerantur loco Matth.8.16. obtulerunt Daemoniacos & alios aegrotos Christo ὀψὲ δὲ γενομένης sive ut Marcus dicit ὅτι ἐδύ ὁ ἥλιος: observare enim voluerunt Canones de Sabbatho.
units.tr: Just as no labour ought to be done when the Sabbath was entering, after sunset, so too none ought to be done when the Sabbath was leaving, unless the sun had already set. Nor was it lawful to do work immediately after sunset, but only after that interval had passed which they call בין השמשות, which properly means between the suns, a phrase derived from the double setting [שקיעות]. They dispute about that time thus in the Jerusalem Berakhot fol. 2 col. 2: What is בין השמשות? Rabbi Tanchuma says: it is like a drop of blood falling on the edge of a sword, which divides on either side. What is בין השמשות? It is from the time the sun sets until a man walks half a mile. R. Yose says, it is like the twinkling of an eye. More clearly, Maimonides defines what בין השמשות is and when it is permitted to begin work, in Shabbat ch. 5: From the time the sun sets until three middle stars appear it is called בין שמשות, between the suns; and it is doubtful whether that time belongs to the day or to the night. However, they everywhere judge it so as to make the obligation heavier [להחמיר]. Within that time, therefore, the Sabbath lamp is not lit; and whoever does any servile work on the evening of the Sabbath, or at its close, is bound to a sin-offering. These things must be noted all the more carefully because they yield more light for the passage Matt. 8. 16, where they brought demoniacs and other sick people to Christ, ὀψὲ δὲ γενομένης [ὀψὲ δὲ γενομένης], or as Mark says, ὅτι ἐδύ ὁ ἥλιος [ὅτι ἔδυ ὁ ἥλιος]: for they wished to observe the canons about the Sabbath.

units.la: §. In Schabbat sol.118.1. sic inquiunt, qui ter convivatur Sabbatho, liberabitur à tribus miseriis, à doloribus Messiae, à iudicio Gehennae, à bello Gog & Magog. Facilè itaque ipsis erat satisfactione culinaria ex opere operato hæc beneficia acquirere.Illas luxurias etiam approbant Kimchi in Esai. lviii.13. & Maymon in Schabbat cap.30. cuius hæc sunt verba. Prohibitum est ieiunare Sabbatho: At verò è contra tenentur homines cibo & potu se oblectare: lautius enim convivandum est Sabbatho quàm diebus aliis; summeque est laudandus, qui parat in illum diem dapes maximè opiparas. Omnes, etiam ipsi pauperes, qui Eleemosyna vivitant, ter in Sabbatho comedere debent. Quantum ab illis dapibus distabant discipulorum Christi spicæ aridæ! Et tamen non caruerunt invidiâ.
units.tr: §. In Shabbat fol. 118 col. 1 they say thus: Whoever is feasted three times on the Sabbath will be freed from three miseries: from the pangs of the Messiah, from the judgment of Gehenna, and from the war of Gog and Magog. It was therefore easy for them to acquire these benefits by culinary satisfaction ex opere operato. Kimchi on Isaiah 58. 13 and Maimonides in Shabbat ch. 30 also approve those excesses. Maimonides' words are these: It is forbidden to fast on the Sabbath. On the contrary, people are bound to delight themselves with food and drink; for one ought to feast more lavishly on the Sabbath than on other days, and he is most to be praised who prepares the most sumptuous dishes for that day. All, even the poor who live on alms, ought to eat three times on the Sabbath. How far those banquets were from the dry ears of grain of Christ's disciples! And yet they did not escape envy.

units.la: §.Festivum est illud quod Cl.Castellus cit.in ערב Sex dies Septimanæ constituunt tria paria coniugalia: Sabbathum autem est solitarium & viduatum, unde Deus ipsi addixit Israelitas quasi coniugem, ut eum Precibus Cantionibus, Concionibusque honorent, ipsique adhæreant toti, ut uxor marito.
units.tr: §. That is a fine comparison which the learned Castellus cites under [ערב]: the six days of the week make up three conjugal pairs, but the Sabbath is solitary and widowed; whence God joined the Israelites to it as a wife, so that they might honour it with prayers, songs and sermons, and cling to it wholly, as a wife to her husband.

units.la: §. Quousque extensi fuerint limites Sabbatici itineris neminem latet; observatu autem dignum est, in usu fuisse spatium illud undiquaque extrà urbes metiri, ut certos statuere possent terminos: quos præterea certis signis notabant, ne dubii hæsitarent.
units.tr: How far the limits of the Sabbath journey extended is known to no one. It is worth observing, however, that it was customary to measure that space on all sides outside the towns, so that they could set fixed boundaries, which they also marked with certain signs, lest the doubtful should hesitate.

units.la: De mensura bis mille cubitorum has habet regulas Maymon in Schabb.cap.28. Civitatem, quae longa est, vel quadrata, si ei sint quatuor anguli iusti, sinunt esse ut est, & metiuntur bis mille cubitos ab uno quoque eius latere. Si sit rotunda formans ei quadraturam, & à lateribus istius quadraturae metiuntur. Idem faciunt si sit triangularis. Mensurationem autem illam non faciunt nisi funiculo quinquaginta cubitorum eoque lineo.
units.tr: Concerning the measure of two thousand cubits, Maimonides in Shabbat ch. 28 gives these rules: A city which is long or square, if it has four right angles, they let stand as it is, and measure two thousand cubits from each of its sides. If it is round, they form a square for it and measure from the sides of that square. They do the same if it is triangular. They make that measurement only with a cord of fifty cubits, and that a linen one.

units.la: De signis limitum sonat Canon in Beza sol. 36.2. Nullus vehuntur animalibus (Sabbatho aut die festo) ne scilicet exeant ultra limites. Gloss. Quia qui pedibus non ambulat אין רואה את סימני חומה Non videt signa limitum. Discipuli à Christo missi reperierunt τὴν πῶλον διὰ μέσου δύο ἐπὶ ἀμφότερα, in loco scilicet ubi se mutuò contingebant via Sabbathica ab urbe protensa, & via communis inde rus ducens, & ubi statum erat signum itineris Sabbathici ab urbe. Si rectius quid habes candide imperti.
units.tr: Concerning the signs of the boundaries, the canon in Beza fol. 36 col. 2 says: No one is carried on animals (on the Sabbath or a feast day), namely lest they go out beyond the limits. The gloss adds: because one who does not walk on foot does not see the signs of the wall [אין רואה את סימני חומה]. The disciples sent by Christ found the colt [τὴν πῶλον διὰ μέσου δύο ἐπὶ ἀμφότερα] in the place where the Sabbath road, extended from the city, touched the common road which leads from there into the countryside, and where the sign of the Sabbath journey from the city was set up. If you have anything more correct, please share it frankly.

units.la: §. Quid sit Sabbathum Σαββάτον tot sententiæ fermè sunt quot capita. Paucis hoc tene. Manipulus Primitialis offerri debuit, ad supplicandum Deo, ut benediceret, novis frugibus, & ut venia impetraretur ad falcem in segetes immittendam; Oblatio illius fiebat secundo die Hebdomadæ Paschalis Lev. 13. 10. 11. qui dies fuit Sabbaticus Exod.12.16. Sicuti autem ab initio messis oblatio fiebat manipuli, ita post peractam messem hordeaceam, post numeratas septem ab illa die oblationis manipuli hebdomadas, in gratiarum actionem offerebantur panes primitiales. Lev.23.15.16.17. Ad computationem autem illarum hebdomadum & temporis interlabentis inter oblationem manipuli & oblationem panum, non alio calculo usi sunt, nisi ut per Sabbatha numerum septimanarum designarent, hoc modo: Hoc est Σαββάλον Δευτερ-πεσέτου Sabbathum à secunda die Paschatis primum. Hoc est Δευτερο-πρωτος ā secunda ista die secundum. Occurrit tamen etiam mentio computationis illius temporis per dies. Iuchasin sol.36.1. Mortui sunt plurimi sapientum discipuli quindecim diebus ante pentecosten, hoc est triginta tribus à manipulo. Sub finem Midrasch Samuelis sic concluditur. Finitum est hoc opus die tricesimo tertio à manipulo.
units.tr: §. As for what the Sabbath (Σαββάτον) is, there are almost as many opinions as there are heads. Briefly, hold to this: the first-fruits sheaf had to be offered, to beg God to bless the new crops, and so that pardon might be obtained for putting the sickle to the standing grain. Its offering was made on the second day of the Passover week, Lev. 13. 10. 11., which day was a Sabbath, Exod. 12. 16. But just as at the beginning of the harvest the sheaf was offered, so after the barley harvest was finished, and seven weeks had been counted from the day of the sheaf offering, loaves of first-fruits were offered in thanksgiving, Lev. 23. 15-17. For the reckoning of those weeks and of the time elapsing between the offering of the sheaf and the offering of the loaves, they used no other method than to designate the number of weeks by Sabbaths, in this way: this is Σαββάτον Δευτερ-πεσέτου [Σαββάτον Δευτεροπρώτου], the first Sabbath from the second day of Passover. That is Δευτερο-πρωτος [Δευτεροπρῶτος], the second from that second day. Yet mention also occurs of computing that time by days. Juchasin fol. 36 col. 1: Many of the wise men's disciples died fifteen days before Pentecost, that is, thirty-three days from the sheaf. At the end of Midrash Samuel it is concluded thus: This work was finished on the thirty-third day from the sheaf.

units.la: SABBATION Talmudicis סבבתיון , fluvius qui omnibus siccatur Sabbathis. Sanhed. sol. 65.2. Quaesivit Turnus Rufus ab Akiba: Quis probaret quod hic dies esset Sabbathum? (forte enim aliquis alius dies Sabbat. esse posset.) Respondit R. Akiba נהר סבשיון יוכיח fluvius Sabbathicus hoc probabit. Glossa. Fluvius Sabbaticus probabit. Ipse fluvius est saxosus: qui omnibus diebus septimanae fluit & labitur, at Sabbatho intermittit & quiescit.
units.tr: SABBATION: in Talmudic usage סבבתיון, a river which dries up on every Sabbath. Sanhedrin fol. 65 col. 2: Turnus Rufus asked Akiba: What would prove that this day is the Sabbath? (for perhaps some other day might also be a Sabbath.) Rabbi Akiba answered: the Sabbatical river will prove it. Gloss: The Sabbatical river will prove it. The river itself is stony; it flows and runs on all the days of the week, but on the Sabbath it stops and rests.

units.la: Iosephus de bello lib.7. 6.13. contrarium scribit, & dicit, illum Sabbaticum vocari, quia fluvius ille quamvis aquis satis abundans, nec segniter labens, totus à fontibus deficiens siccum per sex dies exhibet locum. Deinde vero quasi nulla mutatione facta septimo die similis exoritur.
units.tr: Josephus, De bello book 7, ch. 6 section 13, writes the opposite, and says that it is called Sabbatical because that river, though abundant enough in water and not sluggishly flowing, is wholly drawn from its sources and presents a dry place for six days. Then, however, on the seventh day it rises again, as if no change had been made.

units.la: Situm eius Iosephus loco citato collocat, inter Arcaas & Raphanaas regni Agrippa civitates. Plinius Nat. Hist. lib.31.c.2. ipsum in Iudaea collocavit, quando inquit, In Iudaea rivus Sabbathis omnibus siccatur.
units.tr: Josephus places it in the place cited above, between the Arcaean and Raphanaean cities of King Agrippa. Pliny, Nat. Hist. book 31, chapter 2, locates it in Judaea, when he says: In Judaea a stream dries up on every Sabbath.

units.la: De hoc fluvio consule (l.Buxtorf.in Rad.Fulleri Miscel. l. c. 9. Fagium Deut. 31. Galatinum xi. c.9. Ionathan Exod.34.10. Berefchit R. sect. 11.&73. Schalsehelet Hakkabala p.36. Iuchasin 155. 155. Beniamin itin. 205.
units.tr: On this river, consult Buxtorf (in the Radices of Fuller's Miscellanea, l. c. 9), Fagius on Deuteronomy 31, Galatinus book 11, chapter 9, Jonathan on Exodus 34:10, Bereshit Rabbah sections 11 and 73, Shalshelet ha-Qabbalah p. 36, Yuchasin 155, and Benjamin of Tudela's Itinerary p. 205.

units.la: Sacerdotes הוכדלו לעבודת הקרבנות ordinati & electi fuerunt ad officia Sacrificiorum facienda. Proinde singuli ipsis debitum honorem exhibere debent, & ipsos omnibus reliquis praeferre. Maymon Hal. Cele Hamikd. c. 4.
units.tr: The priests, set apart for the service of the sacrifices [הוכדלו לעבודת הקרבנות], were ordained and chosen to perform the duties of the sacrifices. Accordingly, each person ought to show them the honour owed to them and prefer them to all the rest. Maimonides, Hilchot Klei ha-Mikdash, chapter 4.

units.la: Recepta est opinio ordines Sacerdotum primo a Mose constitutos esse, ipsumque quatuor sumsisse ex filiis Eleazaris & quatuor ex progenie Ithamaris. Samuelem Prophetam deinde addidisse a Ihuc octo, ita ut ipsius tempore 16. ordines fuerint: Tandem Davidem adhuc octo huic numerum auxisse, & ita 24. ordines fecisse. Sunt qui Mosi attribuunt 16. ordines, & constitutioni Davidis & Samuelis solum octo; sed tanti non est ut huic computationi immoremur, modo in eo sit consensus 24. Sacerdotum ordines fuisse. Vid. Ierof. Taanith c. 4. Maymon. Kele Hamikd. c. 4. Kimchi in I. Chron. 24. R. Salomoh ibid.
units.tr: It is the accepted opinion that the orders of priests were first established by Moses, who took four of them from the sons of Eleazar and four from the family of Ithamar. The prophet Samuel then added eight more, so that in his time there were sixteen orders. Finally David increased the number by a further eight, and so made twenty-four orders. Some attribute sixteen orders to Moses and only eight to the arrangement of David and Samuel; but it is not worth dwelling on this reckoning, provided there is agreement that there were twenty-four orders of priests. See Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit chapter 4; Maimonides, Kele ha-Mikdash chapter 4; Kimchi on 1 Chronicles 24; Rabbi Solomon ibid.

units.la: Videndum autem primo tempus ingressus ipsorum in Sacerdotium & ordines; deinde ordines ipsos inspiciemus.
units.tr: We must consider first the time when they entered the priesthood and the orders, and then we shall examine the orders themselves.

units.la: Tempus fixum & constitutum ordines ingrediendi erat cum 30. annos attigissent; Num. 4. 3. (Sic Christus anno 30. suum sacerdotale munus incepit.) Legimus quidem Num. 8. 25. quod iam ab anno 25. cultui interesse caeperint, sed tunc nondum ut Sacerdotes, sed ut Sacerdotio initiati & novitii (ut in Papismo loquuntur) considerabantur: poterant aliqua officia facere, sed non omnia, poterant (ut notat Aben Esra Num. 8.) excubias facere circa tabernaculum, sed non arcam ferre. Ita David tandem permisit ut iam anno vigesimo ad initiationem accederent 1.Chron.23.24.27. Et quoniam illo tempore iuvenes pubescere & producere barbam incipiunt, hos novitios Talmudici vocant פרחי כהונה Pubem Sacerdotalem, ut in Ioma cap.1. Si Summus Sacerdos dormire gestiebat iuvenes Sacerdotales coram ipso digitis percutiebant. Glossa פרחי כהונה sunt iuvenes quibus barba efflorescere incipit. Vid. etiam Tamid cap.1. ubi dicuntur dormire in pavimento Beth Mokad: & à Glossa describuntur quòd sint שהגיעו לעבודה illi qui non ita pridem ad cultum accesserunt: sive qui non ita pridem Sacerdotii candidati facti erant. Initiatio Samuelis dum adhuc puerulus erat, fuit casus extraordinarius. Kimchi in 1. Sam. 2.
units.tr: The fixed and appointed time for entering the orders was when they had reached thirty years of age (Numbers 4:3). Thus Christ began his priestly office in his thirtieth year. We read indeed in Numbers 8:25 that they began to take part in the worship from the age of twenty-five, but at that time they were not yet regarded as priests, but as initiates and novices (as they say in Papistry). They could perform some duties, but not all; they could (as Aben Ezra notes on Numbers 8) keep watch around the tabernacle, but they could not carry the ark. So David at last allowed them to be admitted to initiation in the twentieth year (1 Chronicles 23:24, 27). And since young men at that age begin to reach puberty and grow a beard, the Talmudists call these novices the priestly youth [פרחי כהונה], as in Yoma chapter 1: If the High Priest wished to sleep, the young priests would snap their fingers in front of him. The Gloss says: the priestly youths are young men whose beards are beginning to grow. See also Tamid chapter 1, where they are said to sleep on the pavement of the Beth Mokad; and the Gloss describes them as those who have not long since come to the service [שהגיעו לעבודה], that is, those who have recently become candidates for the priesthood. Samuel's initiation while he was still a little boy was an extraordinary case. Kimchi on 1 Samuel 2.

units.la: Modus inaugurationis & admissionis ipsorum ad omnes partes cultus talis erat. Synedrium magnum singulis diebus sedens in conclave Gazit iudicabat de Sacerdotibus qui ad legitimam aetatem pertigerant, an ex legitima orti essent prosapia, & ita an admittendi ad cultum essent, nec ne. Si probarunt se legitimè natos esse, (De Sacerdotum matribus legitimis Vid. Kiddushin c.4.5. Generalem de illis hunc habuerunt Canonem. Ne inquiratur ulterius, si pater eius conscriptus fuit in catalogo leschah a Zipporiensis; il e leschana enim accuratam Genealogiam conscripserat.) Inquisitio deinde facta est, an nullo laborarent vitio; vitia autem numero erant 140.(vid.Maymon in Biat Mikdashcb c.8.) Si aliquis perfectè non poterat probare se ex stirpe Sacerdotali natum esse, induebatur vestimento nigro, & obvolvebatur velo nigro,& ita pullatus dimittebatur, nec unquam reverti poterat. Si vero sufficienter probasset legitimum suum ortum,& tamen aliquo laboraret vitio relegabatur ad conclave lignorum, & ad ligna à vermibus purganda adhibebatur. (Vid. Conclavia.) Ille vero qui & bene natus & recte constitutus erat, sive vitio carebat, induebatur vestimentis albis & velo albo, matriculæ Sacerdotum inscribebatur, & ad cultum cum reliquis faciendum amandabatur. Middot cap.5. Maymon ubi sup. c. 6. Ad hunc ritum alluditur Apocal.3.5. Qui vicerit amicietur vestimentis albis.
units.tr: The manner of their inauguration and admission to all parts of the worship was as follows. The Great Sanhedrin, sitting daily in the chamber Gazit, judged concerning the priests who had reached legitimate age, whether they were born of a lawful lineage, and so whether they were to be admitted to the worship or not. If they proved that they had been born lawfully (on the lawful mothers of the priests, see Kiddushin chapters 4 and 5; they had this general rule: Let no further inquiry be made, if his father was enrolled in the catalogue of Zipporiensis of Leschah; for the Leschah had drawn up an accurate genealogy), then an inquiry was made whether they suffered from any defect; there were 140 defects (see Maimonides, Beit ha-Mikdash chapter 8). If anyone could not fully prove that he was born of priestly stock, he was dressed in black clothing and wrapped in a black veil, and so dismissed in mourning, and could never return. But if he had sufficiently proved his lawful birth and yet suffered from some defect, he was relegated to the chamber of wood, and was employed to clean the wood of worms (see Conclavia). But the one who was both well born and properly qualified, or free from defect, was clothed in white garments and a white veil, was enrolled in the register of priests, and was sent to perform the worship with the rest. Middot chapter 5; Maimonides, loc. cit. chapter 6. Revelation 3:5 alludes to this rite: He who overcomes shall be clothed in white garments.

units.la: De viginti quatuor ἐφημερίαις abductis in Babel solummodo quatuor ex captivitate reductes facta sunt, scilicet ordo Ieddaja, Harim, Paschur, Immer. Ex illis deinde, forte iacta iterum, 24. constituerunt, Iedaia ex urna 5. fumebat, & unam pro se; sic fecerunt & Harim & Pafchur & Immer. Vide Tosapht. ad Taanith cap.4. Talm.Bab. ibid. Notandum autem illos fortibus illis inscriptisse nomina capitum 24. ordinum, ut scirent quales ordines unaquaeque ex his familiis residuis explere deberet. Hinc ratio patet cur Zacharias dicatur esse ex ordine Abia Lucæ 1.5. Licet illa familia iam desiisset; quia scilicet ἐφημερία illa respondens ordini prisco Abiæ, semper antiquum nomen obtinuit.
units.tr: After the twenty-four courses [ἐφημερίαις] were carried off into Babylon, only four orders were brought back from captivity, namely the orders Jedaiah, Harim, Pashhur and Immer. From these, then, by casting lots again, they made up twenty-four: Jedaiah drew five from the urn and one for himself; and Harim, Pashhur and Immer did the same. See Tosefta on Taanit chapter 4; Babylonian Talmud, ibid. It should be noted that they inscribed on the lots the names of the heads of the twenty-four orders, so that each of the surviving families would know which order it ought to fill. Hence the reason is plain why Zechariah is said to be of the order of Abijah (Luke 1:5), although that family had already ceased to exist; for that course, corresponding to the old order of Abijah, always kept the ancient name.

units.la: Vnusquisque ordo Sacerdotalis ita erat divisus ut dimidia ad minimum pars eius perpetuo
units.tr: Each priestly order was so divided that at least half of it always

units.la: Hierosolymis habitaverit, vel circa eam, ut alii qui saltem certò parati essent, tempore officii ipsorum appropinquante; reliqua verò pars ἐφημερίαις dispersa erat undiquaque per omnes tractus Iudeæ: magna autem multitudo ipsorum residebat Ierichunte (Vid. f. 1.) ex quibus plurimi accedere debebant cum tempus cultus ordinis ipsorum adesset; Qui non adhibebantur ad ipsum altaris cultum מתקיים לאחיהם curabant pro fratribus suis cultui vacantibus victualia, & quæ ipsis opus erant. Sacerdotes verò illi qui neque Hierosolymis nec Ierichunte degebant, & qui tamen illius ordinis qui tunc in officio erat membra erant, cum Levitis & viris stationariis (de quib. v. f. 1.) Synagogas ingrediebantur, iciunabant, orabant & lectioni legis incumbebant, Deumque supplicabant ut cultus qui tunc in fratrum suorum manibus erat, ipsi gratus atque acceptus esset. Taanit cap. 3.
units.tr: lived in Jerusalem, or near it, so that others at least would be certainly ready when their time of service drew near; but the remaining part was scattered on all sides throughout all the regions of Judaea. A great multitude of them, however, dwelt in Jericho (see f. 1), and many of these were bound to come when the time for the worship of their order arrived. Those who were not called to the altar service itself took care to provide food and whatever else was needed for their brothers who were occupied in the worship. Those priests who lived neither in Jerusalem nor in Jericho, but who were nevertheless members of the order then on duty, entered the synagogues together with the Levites and the men of the stations (on whom see f. 1); they fasted, prayed and devoted themselves to the reading of the law, and implored God that the worship which was then in the hands of their brothers might be pleasing and acceptable to him. Taanit chapter 3.

units.la: Ordines hi Sacerdotum etiam in semet ipsis aliquos gradus honorum habuerunt. Totus ordo habebat caput sive Præsulem qui vocatur ראש הפנה & qui repræsentabat personam illam à qua ordo nomen sumpserat. Erant illi præsides membra Synedrii, & in novo Testamento ἀρχιερεῖς vocantur. Sicuti deinde ordo plurimas comprehendit familias ita quoque illæ familiæ ita divisæ erant, ut unaquæque diebus sibi constitutis cultus vacaret; ita autem ordinis divisio se habuit, ut recenset Hierof. Taanit cap. 4. sol. 68. & Tosapht. Ordo ille qui quinque familias paternas habuit, tres familias cultui vacantes habuit per tres dies, & duas per quatuor. In ordine illo qui habuit sex familias paternas, una cultum fecit per duos dies, & quinque per quinque dies. In ordine qui habebat septem familias unaquaque per suum diem officium faciebat. In ordine qui octo habebat familias, sex ministrabant per 6. dies, & dua per diem unum. Qui novem, per 1, ministrabant dies, & 4. per dies duos.
units.tr: These orders of priests also had certain degrees of honour among themselves. The whole order had a head or president, who is called the head of the corner [ראש הפנה], and who represented the person from whom the order took its name. These presidents were members of the Sanhedrin, and in the New Testament are called chief priests [ἀρχιερεῖς]. Again, just as the order comprised many families, so these families were divided in such a way that each of them was assigned days on which to perform the worship. The division of the order was as Jerusalem Taanit chapter 4, fol. 68, and the Tosefta recount: That order which had five paternal families had three families serving for three days, and two for four days. In the order which had six paternal families, one served for two days and five for five days. In the order which had seven families, each family performed its office for its own day. In the order which had eight families, six ministered for six days, and two for one day each. Those with nine ministered for one day each, and four for two days each.

units.la: Quivis itaque ordo solùm per unam ministrabat septimanam; cultum incipiebat in Sabbatho, & Sabbatho insequente finiebat; vid. 2. Reg.11.7. 2. Chron.23.4. Ille qui familiæ minifiranti præerat vocatur אב בית ראש Caput familia paterna. Vid אב in A. De aliis honoribus & officiis Sacerdotum vid. אבריכליך in A. & Ossiciarii.
units.tr: Thus each order ministered for only one week; it began the worship on the Sabbath, and finished it on the following Sabbath; see 2 Kings 11:7; 2 Chronicles 23:4. The one who presided over the family on duty is called the head of the paternal house [אב בית ראש]. On the term אב see under A. On other honours and offices of the priests, see אבריכליך under A, and Officiarii.

units.la: Viri ordinis ministerio vacantis poterant bibere vinum noctu sed non interdiu, si enim accideret ut cultus diei gravior esset quàm ut familia paterna illi sustinendo par esset, ad illam iuvandam se accingere debebant, quod facere non possent si vinum bibissent: qui enim circa cultum occupati erant, ipsis vinum degustare non licuit. Tosaphi. Hierof. ubi supra.
units.tr: Men of a course that was free from ministry could drink wine at night but not by day. If the day's service happened to be too heavy for the father's house to bear, they had to gird themselves to help with it, and they could not do that if they had drunk wine, since those occupied with the service were not allowed to taste wine. Tosaphoth, Jerusalem Talmud, loc. cit.

units.la: §. De munditia & puritate Sacerdotum vid.: Immunditiis, & Lotio. Dabantur tamen certi casus in quibus Sacerdotibus licuit, licet immundis cultum facere. Maymon in Biat Mikdafch cap.4. Si tempus oblationis alicuius sacrificii advenerit dispensans de Sabbatho, (si scilicet in illud inciderit,) & de immunditia, sed solum si congregatio aut Sacerdotes aut vasa ministerii impura facta sunt, propter aliquem mortuum, alias Sacerdotibus alia immunditia affectus ad cultum accedere non licet.
units.tr: §. On the cleanness and purity of the priests, see: Uncleanness and Washing. Yet there were certain cases in which priests were allowed to perform the service even while unclean. Maimonides, in Biath Mikdash ch. 4: "If the time for the offering of some sacrifice has come, the one dispensing it may (on the Sabbath, if it should fall on one) and may (in uncleanness), but only if the congregation, or the priests, or the vessels of ministry have become unclean on account of some dead person. Otherwise a priest affected by some other uncleanness may not approach the service."

units.la: §. De Cultu Sacerdotum quibus ritibus peragebatur quotidie vid. Cultum quotidianum. Erat aliquis qui Sacerdotes singulis horis matutinis excitabat: vocatur ille in Tamid c.3.8. גביני הכרוז Gevini Praeco. Sic autem clamabat, עמדו הכהנים על עבודתכם ולוים כרוכניכם Surgite Sacerdotes ad cultum vestrum, & vos Levita ad loca vestra. De benedictione Sacerdotum vid.Benedictiones. De ea sic loquitur cap.8. Sotah. Benedictio Sacerdotum debet fieri in lingua sancta. Quomodo autem fit? In provinciis ipsam dicunt ut tres benedictiones, in Sanctuario vero ut unam. In Sanctuario dicunt nomen (Iehova) ut scribitur, In provinciis vero per cognomina eius: In provinciis Sacerdotes manus suas ad humeros tollunt; sed in sanctuario supra capita sua, excepto summo Sacerdote, qui manus suas ultra laminam non elevat.
units.tr: §. On the service of the priests, and with what rites it was carried out each day, see: The daily service. There was someone who woke the priests at each morning hour. In Tamid ch. 3 §8 he is called the Herald of Gevini (גביני הכרוז). He cried out thus: "Rise, priests, to your service, and you Levites to your posts" [עמדו הכהנים על עבודתכם ולוים כרוכניכם]. On the blessing of the priests see: Blessings. Of it ch. 8 of Sotah speaks thus: "The blessing of the priests must be given in the holy tongue. How is it done? In the provinces they say it as three blessings, but in the Sanctuary as one. In the Sanctuary they say the name (Jehovah) as it is written; in the provinces they say it by its substitute names. In the provinces the priests raise their hands to the shoulders, but in the Sanctuary above their heads, except the high priest, who does not raise his hands above the plate."

units.la: §. Sacerdotibus incubuit Liturgia, in illa singulis diebus destinatos Psalmos cantarunt; Primo die habebant Psalm.24 Secundo Psalm. 48. Tertio Psalm.82. Quarto Psalm.94. Quinto Psalm. 81. Sexto Psalm. 93. Septimo Psalm.92. ab ipso Adamo contextum,Tamid f.67.2. Kimchi inpraefat. Psalm.
units.tr: §. The liturgy was the priests' charge, and in it they sang the psalms appointed for each day. On the first day they had Psalm 24; on the second, Psalm 48; on the third, Psalm 82; on the fourth, Psalm 94; on the fifth, Psalm 81; on the sixth, Psalm 93; on the seventh, Psalm 92, said to have been composed by Adam himself. Tamid f. 67.2; Kimchi in the preface to the Psalms.

units.la: §. בית דין של כהנים Senatus Sacerdotum cuius mentio fit in Ketubh. cap. 1. constabat ex superioris ordinis sacerdotibus, quales ראשי ראשי משמר ביתאב, Immarcalin &c. De hoc fenatu intelligendus est locus Maym. in מחוסי אין בית דין של כהנים עומדין משם כפרת cap.1. עור
units.tr: §. The court of the priests (בית דין של כהנים), the Senate of the Priests, mentioned in Ketubhoth ch. 1, consisted of priests of the higher order, such as the heads of the courses, the heads of the fathers' houses, the Immarcalin, and so on. The passage of Maimonides beginning "The court of the priests stands there" (ch. 1) is to be understood of this senate.

units.la: שיכלו עד Non recedit illinc senatus Sacerdotum &c. De loco huius senatus. Vid. Conclave Βυλωτων.
units.tr: "The senate of the priests does not withdraw from there," etc. On the place of this senate see: Conclave [βουλευτήριον].

units.la: §. De Sacerdotum luctu, quomodo & à quibus mortuis immundi fiant, tractat Maymon, Hal אבל c. 2. & 3.
units.tr: §. On the mourning of the priests, and how and by whom dead persons make them unclean, Maimonides treats in Hilchoth Avel ch. 2 and 3.

units.la: §. Colligamus nunc ea quæ de Sacerdotum distinctionibus teneri debent. Sacerdotes illi qui ex stirpe quidem Sacerdotali erant orti, sed educatione Scholastica carebant, vocarunt כהני עם הארץ Sacerdotes plebeios. Et quoniam tales ut plurimum pauperes erant, permissum est ipsis reliquis pauperum privilegiis frui, qualia sunt spicilegium, rarematio &c. Vid. Hierof. Trumot sol. 44. 1. Tali Sacerdoti plebeio non dabatur Trumah sive oblatio, quia incertum erat an comesturus esset in munditia vel immunditia; Sanhed. sol. 90. sicuti enim indoctus erat, ita præipponebatur omnes puritatis regulas observare non posse.
units.tr: §. Let us now gather what must be held about the distinctions among the priests. Those priests who were indeed born of priestly stock but lacked scholastic education were called "priests of the common people" (כהני עם הארץ). And since such men were for the most part poor, they were allowed to enjoy the other privileges of the poor, such as gleaning, rarematio, and so on. See Jerusalem Terumoth, p. 44. To such a common priest the Terumah, or offering, was not given, because it was uncertain whether he would eat it in cleanness or uncleanness (Sanhedrin p. 90). For just as he was unlearned, so it was presumed that he could not observe all the rules of purity.

units.la: Erant deinde Sacerdotes qui vocabantur כהנים הדיוטית Sacerdotes Idiotæ, sive privati, qui quamvis docti erant, ita tamen nominabantur quandiu ordinis inferioris Sacerdotes manebant.
units.tr: Then there were priests called "ordinary priests" (כהנים הדיוטית), or private priests, who, although learned, were so named as long as they remained priests of the lower order.

units.la: Ordinis superioris id est honorificentioris erant ראשי המשמר Præsides ἡγούμενοι, ראשי בית אב Capita familiarum quæ unâ die cultui vacabant; ממני במקרש variorum officiorum præfecti in templo; Sacerdos unctus ad bellum. הסגן Vicarius summi Pontificis; & Summus Pontifex. De tribus prioribus iam quædam dicta; de posterioribus paucis agendum.
units.tr: Of the higher, that is the more honourable, order were: the heads of the courses (ראשי המשמר), the presidents (ἡγούμενοι); the heads of the fathers' houses, who alone were free for service on one day; the prefects of the various offices in the temple (ממני במקרש); the priest anointed for war; the deputy of the high priest (הסגן); and the high priest himself. Of the first three something has already been said; of the last few things must be discussed.

units.la: §. Summum Sacerdotium ordinarie obtinere debuit primogenitus, ut elicit Rafchi in 1.Chron.24.1. ad verba Nadab & Abihu mortiebantur &c. Ante datam legem etiam primogenitus familiæ Sacerdos esse debeit, hinc Chaldaus Gen.49.3. introducit Iacobum,Rubeni primogenituræ, sacerdotium & regnum tribuente. Hinc etiam Simeon iustus nihil obtinere potuit cùm primogenitum suum Schimæi exclusò Omnia ad Sacerdotium promovere voluit.Iuch.f.15.
units.tr: §. The high priesthood ought ordinarily to be held by the firstborn, as Rashi draws out in 1 Chron. 24.1, on the words "Nadab and Abihu died," etc. Even before the law was given, the firstborn of a family ought to be the priest; hence the Chaldee on Gen. 49.3 introduces Jacob assigning the priesthood and kingship to Reuben, the firstborn. Hence too Simeon the Just could obtain nothing when, with Shimei excluded, he wished to advance his firstborn to the priesthood. Juchasin f. 15.

units.la: Hæc successionis necessitas fecit ut aliquando ad Sacerdotium promoverentur illi qui plane indocti erant. Vid.Ioma c.1.ubi plura dicuntur quæ præsupponunt, plurimos Summos Sacerdotes non חכמים sed עם הארץ plebeios & indoctos fuisse, quædam dedimus de Expiationis die. Nota etiam Maymonidis dictum in Talm. Torah cap. 3. quando sic loquitur ... Discipulus sapientis quamvis spurius sit, tamen præferendus est Summo Sacerdoti indocto.
units.tr: This necessity of succession caused some men who were quite unlearned to be advanced to the priesthood. See Yoma ch. 1, where many things are said which presuppose that most high priests were not sages (חכמים) but common and unlearned men (עם הארץ); we have given some remarks on the Day of Atonement. Note also the saying of Maimonides in Talmud Torah ch. 3, where he speaks thus: "A disciple of a sage, though he be a bastard, is still to be preferred to an unlearned high priest."

units.la: Summi Sacerdotis initiatio fiebat per Synedrium magnum, quod ante Iosiæ tempora cùm oleum unctionis nondum absconditum erat, ipsum per octo dies oleo illo ungebat; illique Sacerdotes vocantur כהנים משוחי בשמן המשחה Vncti oleo unctionis. De modo ungendi Vid. f.1. Postquam autem oleum unctionis defecit, Sacerdos Summus initiabatur, induendo per octo dies eius vestes: qui ita initiatus erat, vocabatur מרובה כגדים Vid Maym.in Kele Hamikd.c. 4 Qui ita initiatus erat, Summus Sacerdos erat omni vita sua.Iosep.Antiq.lib.15.c.3.Sed tandem fraus & pecunia nihil stabile hic reliquerunt, V. Gem. Gem. in Ioma & Iofeph. De frequenti enim mutatione in Pontificatu, Nota loca sequentia.
units.tr: The initiation of the high priest was carried out by the Great Sanhedrin. Before the time of Josiah, when the anointing oil was still not hidden, the Sanhedrin anointed him with that oil for eight days; and those priests are called "anointed with the oil of anointing" (כהנים משוחי בשמן המשחה). On the manner of anointing see f. 1. After the anointing oil failed, the high priest was initiated by putting on his garments for eight days; one so initiated was called "the one of many garments" (מרובה כגדים). See Maimonides in Kele Hamikdash ch. 4. One so initiated was high priest for the whole of his life. Josephus, Antiquities bk. 15 ch. 3. But in the end fraud and money left nothing stable here; see the Gemara, the Gemara in Yoma, and Josephus. For the frequent change in the pontificate, note the following passages.

units.la: Ioma sol.9.1. In templo secundo quod tantùm stetit 410. annis, ministrarunt plures quam trecenti Pontifices. De his 410. annis deme 40. annos quibus ministravit Simeon Iustus, & 80. quibus ministravit Iochanan, & 10. quibus Ismael fil. Pabhi, & ut dicitur 11. quibus Eleasar Ben Harsum, & tum computa, & quisque Pontisex non complevit annum suum. Forsan Gemaris cum Summis Pontificibus etiam ipsorum vicarios complectuntur. Sed audiatur locus alius.
units.tr: Yoma 9.1: "In the second temple, which stood only 410 years, more than three hundred pontiffs ministered. From these 410 years subtract the 40 years in which Simeon the Just ministered, the 80 in which Johanan ministered, the 10 in which Ishmael son of Phabi ministered, and, as is said, the 11 in which Eleazar ben Harsum ministered; then count, and each pontiff did not complete his year." Perhaps the Gemaras include with the high priests their deputies as well. But let another passage be heard.

units.la: Vajikra Rabba sol.189.1. In templo primo quoniam in eo ministrarunt in veritate, ministrarunt tantum octodecim pontifices, pater & filius & nepos successive. At sub templo secundo, cum Pontificatum pecuniâ obtinerent (sunt etiam qui dicunt, quòd alter alterum incantationibus interimeret) ministrarunt octoginta Pontifices, sunt qui dicunt 81. alii 82. alii 84. Inter eos ministravit Simeon Iustus per 40. annos. At cùm Pontificatum emerunt nummis, abbreviati sunt anni eorum. Historia est de quodam qui misit per filium suum duos modios argenti (ad emendum Pontificatum) atque modii ipsi erant argentei. Erat etiam alius qui misit per filium suum duos modios auri, atque ipsi modii erant aurei. Si res ita se habuit, ut tam frequenter Summum Sacerdotium alium possessorem nancisceretur; verba Iohannis 18.13. ὁς ἦν ἀρχιερεὺς τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου, intelligenda sunt de tempore quo Caiphas S. Sacerdotium obtinuerat, ipsum scil. non anno precedente sed isto ad illum honorē pervenisse: & certè quantū ex temporis illius constitutione elicere licet, anno sequenti forsan
units.tr: Vayikra Rabba 189.1: "In the first temple, since they ministered in truth, only eighteen pontiffs ministered, father, son and grandson in succession. But under the second temple, when they obtained the pontificate by money (there are also those who say that one would kill another by incantations), eighty pontiffs ministered; some say 81, others 82, others 84. Among them Simeon the Just ministered for 40 years. But when they bought the pontificate with coins, their years were shortened. There is a story of a certain man who sent through his son two measures of silver (to buy the pontificate), and the measures themselves were of silver. There was also another who sent through his son two measures of gold, and the measures themselves were of gold." If the matter stood so, and the high priesthood so often passed to another possessor, the words of John 18.13, "who was high priest that year" (ὃς ἦν ἀρχιερεὺς τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου), must be understood of the time in which Caiaphas had obtained the high priesthood: namely, that he had come to that honour not the year before but in this one; and certainly, as far as can be drawn from the arrangement of that time, the following year perhaps

units.la: illo caruit. Vid. Ioseph. Antiq. lib.18. cap.6. Anna enim socer eius non fuit Sacerdos Summus, ut infrà patebit.
units.tr: he lacked it. See Josephus, Antiquities bk. 18 ch. 6. For Annas, his father-in-law, was not high priest, as will appear below.

units.la: Quoad Qualitates requisitas in Summo Sacerdote ut legitimus esset, aliquas recenset Maymon in Cele Hamikdasch cap. 5. Summus Sacerdos inquit debet omnes reliquos Sacerdotes superare בגוי בכח בעוזו pulchritudine, robore, & divitiis; item Sapient à & externo aspectu. Si pecuniâ non habet, omnes reliqui Sacerdotes ex suo aliquid conferre debent, donec inter ipsos sit ditissimus. Debet Summus Sacerdos decus conservare םעה שאר םע בעצמו יקל לא cum aliis nimium familiariter non gerere; non nudus videri in balneo &c.
units.tr: As for the qualities required in the high priest if he was to be lawful, Maimonides in Kele Hamikdash ch. 5 lists some. "The high priest," he says, "must surpass all the other priests in body, strength and might [בגוי בכח בעוזו], and likewise in beauty, wisdom and outward appearance. If he has no money, all the other priests must contribute something of their own, until he is the richest among them. The high priest must keep his dignity and not behave too familiarly with others; he must not appear naked in the bath, and so on."

units.la: Pergit Maymon. In convivia publica se conferre non debet, adest tamen epulo funerali, in quo totus populus humi accumbit, ipse vero sedet in folio.(vid.Sanhed.c.2.)Si quis ipsi propinquus mortuus est, post feretrum non incedit, nisi ita ut illis qui feretrum succollant tectis aliquâ porticu ipse detectus sit: illis retectis tegatur. Cum funere ultrà portas urbis non procedit. Cùm alios consolatur, vicarius eius ipsum medium facit inter se & populum. Q; ando ipse consolationem accipit; dicit populus אנו כפרך Nos tibi piaculo! Ille verò ipsis respondet, bened Eli fitis coelitus. Ob mortuum non debet vestimenta lacerare instar reliquorum Sacerdotum: & si lacerat, fissuram faciet in parte inferiori versus pedes. Caput suum detegere non debet, quamvis non esset tempus ingrediendi in Sanctuarium. (de modo ipsum radendi vid. Rasura.) Habet in Sanctuario domum quam vocant לשכת כהן גדול Conclave Sacerdotis Summi, in illa habitare debet interdiu, noctu vero potest se conferre in propriam domum, quæ extra Hierosolymam esse non debet. Summus Sacerdos iudicat, & iudicatur, testimonium dicit, ac de ipso dicitur; Calceo se exuit, aliique id faciunt ob uxorem eius. Si quid Summus Sacerdos commiserit, quod vapulationem mereatur, à Synedrio magno vapulat, & deinde pristinæ suæ dignitati restituitur. (vid. Maymon in Biat Mikdafch cap.4.) Virginem in uxorem sumere debet; duas uxores simul ipsi habere non licet; Cùm in Sanctuarium ingreditur ad se incurvandum, tres ipsum comitantur unus à dextra, alter à sinistra, tertius à tergo eius: ipso egresso deinde etiam reliqui ingrediuntur Sacerdotes. Summus Sacerdos nullum officium per sortem aggreditur, sed offert ex sacrificiis quæ vult, adolet thymiama,quando ipsi lubet. Non tamen ipsi permittitur aliquam partem cultus facere, antequàm annum vigesimum attigerit. Hactenus Maym.
units.tr: Maimonides goes on: He must not take part in public banquets, but he attends the funeral feast, at which the whole people reclines on the ground while he himself sits on a throne. (See Sanhedrin ch. 2.) If someone close to him dies, he does not walk behind the bier, unless he is under a porch so that, while those who carry the bier are covered, he himself is uncovered; when they are uncovered, he is to be covered. He does not go beyond the city gates with the funeral. When he consoles others, his deputy stands between him and the people. When he himself receives consolation, the people say, "We are your atonement!" [אנו כפרך] and he answers them, "May you be blessed from heaven." On account of the dead he must not tear his garments as the other priests do; and if he tears them, he makes the rent in the lower part, towards the feet. He must not uncover his head, even when it is not the time for entering the sanctuary. (On the manner of shaving him, see Rasura.) In the sanctuary he has a house which they call the chamber of the high priest [לשכת כהן גדול]; he must live there by day, but at night he may go to his own house, which must not be outside Jerusalem. The high priest judges and is judged, gives testimony and has testimony given about him. He takes off his shoe, and others do so on account of his wife. If the high priest has done anything deserving a flogging, he is flogged by the Great Sanhedrin, and afterwards restored to his former dignity. (See Maimonides on Beth Habechirah ch. 4.) He must take a virgin as his wife; he may not have two wives at once. When he enters the sanctuary to bow himself, three accompany him, one on the right, one on the left and a third behind him; when he has come out, the other priests then enter. The high priest undertakes no duty by lot, but offers from the sacrifices whichever he wishes and burns incense whenever he pleases. Yet he is not permitted to perform any part of the worship until he has reached his twentieth year. Thus far Maimonides.

units.la: Nihil discriminis erat quoad executionem officii Sacerdotalis inter Summum Pontificem & reliquos Sacerdotes nisi in his duobus. i. in fcifcitatione per Urim & Thummim. ii. in praftando officio diei expiationis. Evanescente spiritu prophetiæ, (quod factum est in excessu prophetarum posteriorum Haggai, Malachiæ &c.) etiam evanuerat scifcitatio per Vrim & Thummim, & proinde nihil ipsis supererat tempore
units.tr: There was no difference in the performance of priestly office between the high priest and the other priests except in these two things: (1) in inquiring by the Urim and Thummim; (2) in performing the office of the Day of Atonement. When the spirit of prophecy faded (as happened after the later prophets, Haggai, Malachi and the rest), the inquiry by Urim and Thummim also faded, and so nothing remained to them in the time

units.la: {y} Vide supra. Christi præter cultum diei expiationis. Præcipua pars cultus diei expiationis erat, ferre sanguinem in Sanctum Sanctorum: at cùm summus noster Pontifex per proprium sanginem sanctissimum introiisset, quid tum reliquum Pontifici?
units.tr: {y} See above. of Christ, apart from the worship of the Day of Atonement. The principal part of the worship of the Day of Atonement was carrying the blood into the Holy of Holies; but when our supreme High Priest entered through his own most holy blood, what then remained for the priest?

units.la: Sed adhuc nihil diximus de eius vestimentis. Sacerdos magnus in octo vestibus minis- rabat, Sacerdos verò vulgaris in quatuor; כתונת in tunica, מכנסיים femoralibus, מצנפת Cidari, ואבנט & Cingulo. Et hæc erant vestimenta Sacerdotis vulgaris. Summus Sacerdos insuper habebat חושן Pectorale, אפוד Amiculum, מעיל pallium וציץ & laminam. Vid. Ioma cap. 7. Vaiikrâ Rabba sect. 10.
units.tr: But we have still said nothing about his vestments. The high priest ministered in eight garments, while the ordinary priest used four: the tunic [כתונת], the breeches [מכנסיים], the mitre [מצנפת] and the girdle [ואבנט]. These were the garments of the ordinary priest. The high priest additionally wore the breastpiece [חושן], the ephod [אפוד], the robe [מעיל] and the plate [ציץ]. See Yoma ch. 7; Vayikra Rabba sect. 10.

units.la: Notandum autem hæc verba mischnæ intelligenda esse de ministeriis in sanctuario peractis; nam cùm Sanctum Sanctorum intraverit Sacerdos magnus, quatuor tantùm vestibus usus est, quæ à Talmudicis albæ appellantur. (R. Levi in Parafch תצוה Maymon Kele Hamikd. cap. 8.) illaque finito festo expiationis depositit, nec unquam denuò in iisdem ministravit. Octo autem illæ vestes quibus Summus Sacerdos ordinariè sacris interfuit vocantur aureæ. Si quis sive Sacerdos magnus sive gregarius, plures vel pauciores vestes quam lex imperat induisset, si emplastrum vulneri impositum inter carnem eius & vestes abscondisset, si vestes fuissent sordidæ & laceratæ, ministerium eius irritum fuisset. Gemara Zebachim cap. 2.
units.tr: It should be noted, however, that these words of the Mishnah are to be understood of the ministries performed in the sanctuary. For when the high priest entered the Holy of Holies, he used only four garments, which the Talmudists call white. (R. Levi on Parashat Tetzaveh; Maimonides, Kele Hamikdash ch. 8.) He laid these aside when the festival of atonement was over and never again ministered in them. The eight garments in which the high priest ordinarily took part in the sacred rites are called golden. If anyone, whether high priest or ordinary priest, had put on more or fewer garments than the law prescribes, if he had hidden a plaster placed on a wound between his flesh and his garments, or if the garments had been dirty and torn, his ministry was void. Gemara Zebachim ch. 2.

units.la: De vestibus recensitis observandum כתונת tunicam Sacerdotalem indumentum lineum fuisse, totius corporis velamen. Latini vulgò Camisiam vocant & Græci χιτὼν. Plautus in Trinummo כתונת Hebræorum expressit, quando infit. Tunica propior pallio est. Quod formam attinet, fuit illa manicata, strictimque corpori adhæsit. Talaris insuper erat & in longum porrecta, ut totum corpus operiret. Iosephus lib. 3. 8. Antiq. Iudaic.
units.tr: Concerning the garments listed, observe that the priestly tunic [כתונת] was a linen garment, a covering for the whole body. The Latins commonly call it camisia and the Greeks χιτών. Plautus in the Trinummus rendered the Hebrew כתונת when he began, "The tunic is closer than the cloak." As to its form, it had sleeves and fitted closely to the body. It was also reaching to the ankles and extended to full length, so as to cover the whole body. Josephus, Jewish Antiquities, book 3, ch. 8.

units.la: כסות מכנסים Femoralia lineæ braccæ erant, quibus femora & pudenda Sacerdotes velabant. Supernè circa cor constringebantur, ut videtur ex Jonath. ad Ezech. 44.18. Vel circa ilia ut Iosephus Ant. I. lib. 3. 8. totum enim spatium ab axillis ad coxendicem huic rei liberum fuit. Loca verò quibus copiosus sudor excutrit, qualia sunt axillæ & imus venter, prohibita erant, ne sacræ vestes inde attracto sudore inquinarentur. Kimchi ad Ezech. 44.18.
units.tr: The breeches [כסות מכנסים] were linen drawers with which the priests covered their thighs and private parts. They were fastened above, about the heart, as appears from Jonathan on Ezekiel 44.18; or about the loins, as Josephus says (Ant. 3.8), for the whole space from the armpits to the hip was left free for this purpose. But the places where copious sweat breaks out, such as the armpits and the lower belly, were forbidden, lest the sacred vestments be soiled by sweat drawn in from there. Kimchi on Ezekiel 44.18.

units.la: מצנפת Tiara ut quidam contendunt non solùm Summo Sacerdoti, sed etiam cuivis Sacerdoti gregario competebat. Erat autem fascia linea quæ multis contorta voluminibus caput cinxit, & in occipitio redimiculo constricta fuit, in arcuatam galeæ formam flectebatur unde ipsum Græci nonnulli τιάρας κορυβαντίων appellant: quia Corybantes inter Sacrificia saltantes ita velati erant. Vid. Strabonem lib. 10. Geograph.
units.tr: The mitre [מצנפת], as some contend, belonged not only to the high priest but to any ordinary priest. It was a linen band wound round the head in many coils, fastened with a tie at the back of the head, and shaped into the arch of a helmet. Hence some Greeks call it the mitre of the Corybantes [τιάρας κορυβαντίων], because the Corybantes, leaping during their sacrifices, were veiled in this way. See Strabo, Geography, book 10.

units.la: אבנט Balhem erat, quo tunicas cingebant Sacerdotes, ut magis agiles & expediti esset. Latus erat quatuor digitis, & variis floribus figurisque instar operis plumarii acupictus. Contextura cava erat, ut serpentis exuvium, aut marsupium longius putares. Ioseph.A.I. lib.3.8. יהוה in sacra scriptura vocatur ככן חשן pectorale iudicii ; quia per ipsum Sacerdos magnus divinum responsum accepit, & iudicium de rebus salutem Reipublicæ spectantibus edidit. Ornamentum erat pretiosissimum, luculentissimum, collo appensum, & ad pectus usque pendulum,ut observat R.Salomoh ad Exod. 28.4. Ad eundem fere modum triumphantes & pueri prætextati Romanorum bullas aureas collo appensas ad pectus gestabant. Macrob. Saturn. lib.1. cap 6. Ornamenta illa dicta sunt bullæ à Græco βυλὴ quia ad cor sedem humani consilii propendebant, ut inquit Festus, ob eandem forsan rationem Græci ἡ λόγιον rationale vocarunt.
units.tr: The girdle [אבנט] was the belt with which the priests bound their tunics, so that they might be more nimble and unencumbered. It was four fingers wide and embroidered with various flowers and figures, like featherwork. Its weave was hollow, so that you would take it for a serpent's slough or a long purse. Josephus, Ant. 3.8. In Holy Scripture the breastpiece is called the breastpiece of judgment [חשן המשפט], because through it the high priest received the divine answer and gave judgment on matters concerning the safety of the commonwealth. It was a most precious and splendid ornament, hung from the neck and reaching down to the breast, as R. Solomon observes on Exodus 28.4. In much the same way Roman boys of triumphant and praetexta rank wore golden bullae hung from the neck to the breast. Macrobius, Saturnalia, book 1, ch. 6. Those ornaments were called bullae from the Greek βουλή, because they hung down over the heart, the seat of human counsel, as Festus says; perhaps for the same reason the Greeks called it the oracle [λόγιον], that is, the rational.

units.la: אפוד Hellenistis ἐπωμὶς dicitur, hinc latinorum superhumerale; melius ἡμιφόριον quam ἀμφιφόριον appellatur,quia vestis erat brevis & quasi dimidiatum pallium, non absimile sago militari, nisi quòd ex variis coloribus, intermixto auro, contexebatur, & quòd ipsi circa medium pectus erat lacuna, spatium pectoralis. Vid. Ioseph.ubi suprà.
units.tr: The ephod [אפוד] is called ἐπωμίς by the Hellenists, whence the Latin superhumerale (shoulder-piece). It is better called ἡμιφόριον than ἀμφιφόριον, because it was a short garment and, as it were, half a cloak, not unlike a soldier's cape, except that it was woven of various colours mixed with gold, and that there was an opening at the middle of the chest, the space for the breastpiece. See Josephus, as above.

units.la: בגדי Pallium, vestis erat exterior, ut מעיל interior. Erat referente Iosepho vestis oblonga & talaris, quæ ad maiorem Summi Sacerdotis honorem adhibebatur. Maymon Kele Hamikd. cap.8. Pallio huic appensa erant mala punica & tintinnabula, ut eius sonus audiretur cum adiret Sanctuarium. Cum hoc pallio Sanctum Sanctorum non ingressus est, sed tantùm cum vestimentis lineis; quod notandum, lapsus est enim in hoc casu Hieronymus ad Fabiolam.
units.tr: The robe [בגדי / Pallium] was an outer garment, as the me'il [מעיל] was the inner one. According to Josephus it was a long garment reaching to the ankles, used to add to the greater honour of the high priest. Maimonides, Kele Hamikdash ch. 8. Pomegranates and little bells were hung from this robe, so that its sound could be heard when he approached the sanctuary. He did not enter the Holy of Holies in this robe, but only in the linen garments. This must be noted, for Jerome erred on this point in his letter to Fabiola.

units.la: יץ Lamina duos digitos lata erat, frontemque ad aures usque cinxit. R. Salomoh in Exod. 28.36. idcirco Exod.39.30. Coronafanella dicitur. Eiusmodi laminas Latini corollaria vocarunt. Vid. Plin.lib.21.cap.2.de coronis sacrificulorum gentilium loquitur Tertullianus lib.15. Ipsa fores, ipsa hostia & ara, ipsi Ministri & Sacerdotes Gentilium coronantur. Lamina haec ad tiaram pontificiam vitta hyacintina astringebatur Exod.28.37. unde à quibusdam διάδημα dicitur; ita enim Graece vittae sonant.
units.tr: The plate [ציץ] was two fingers wide and girded the forehead as far as the ears. R. Solomon on Exodus 28.36; for this reason Exodus 39.30 calls it a holy crown. The Latins called plates of this kind corollaria. See Pliny, book 21, ch. 2. Tertullian, speaking of the crowns of the pagan sacrificers, says in book 15: "The very doors, the very victim and altar, the ministers and priests of the Gentiles themselves are crowned." This plate was fastened to the high priestly mitre with a hyacinth-coloured band, Exodus 28.37; whence some call it a diadem (διάδημα), for that is what the Greek word vittae means.

units.la: §. Ille qui Summo Sacerdoti in die expiationis substituebatur vocatur ןמכ Ioma. c.1. Si accidisset ut Pontifex aliqua immunditie commaculatus fuisset, ille ןמכ ipsius obivit vices.
units.tr: The one who was substituted for the high priest on the Day of Atonement is called the deputy [ממונה]. Yoma ch. 1. If it happened that the high priest had been stained by some impurity, that deputy took over his duties.

units.la: ןמכ etiam nominatur qui Candidatus erat Summi Sacerdotii, ita R. Salomoh in Num.19. Eleasarum filium Aaronis ןמכ vocat, & notant Iuchasin sol.57. & Aruch in rad. כי לא היה ממונה illum non fuisse rite ad Pontificatum promotum, qui prius non erat Sagan. Providebatur enim ita, ut in Saganatu experientiam in legibus & ritibus acquireret candidatus, ut deinde ad Pontificatum eo aptior esset. Pecuniae vis tandem hunc ordinem etiam perturbavit.
units.tr: ןמכ is also the name given to the man who was the candidate for the high priesthood. So R. Salomoh, on Num.19., calls Eleazar son of Aaron ןמכ, and Iuchasin fol.57 and Aruch in the root כי לא היה ממונה note that he had not been properly promoted to the high priesthood, since he had not previously been Sagan. Provision was made so that the candidate would gain experience of the laws and rites while serving as Sagan, and so be better fitted for the high priesthood. The power of money eventually upset this order too.

units.la: Ille Sagan vocatur sapius ממונה Praefectus cultus, ut in Ioma cap.3.1. אשר להם הממונה dixit ipsis praefectus. Gloss. סגן ממונה הוא Praefectus est Sagan. Item Sanhed. sol.19.1. סגן היינו ממונו Sagan est praefectus. Appellatur etiam סגן הכהנים Sagan Sacerdotum in Ioma sol.8.2. Schekalim cap.3. & 6.1. Chald.Ierem.52.14. Rationem dat Maymon in Kele Mikd. cap.4. Quia omnes Sacerdotes illi ut Pontificis vicario fungebantur.
units.tr: That one is often called ממונה, Prefect of the worship, as in Ioma cap.3.1: אשר להם הממונה he said to them, the prefect. The Gloss: סגן ממונה הוא The prefect is the Sagan. Likewise Sanhed. fol.19.1: סגן היינו ממונו Sagan is his prefect. He is also called סגן הכהנים, Sagan of the priests, in Ioma fol.8.2, Shekalim cap.3 and 6.1, and Chald. Ierem. 52.14. Maimonides gives the reason in Kele Mikd. cap.4: Because all those priests acted as the vicar of the high priest.

units.la: Frequentissima est mentio R. Ananiæ פּןּ הכהני Sagan Sacerdotum, vid.loc.m.cit. periit in obsidione urbis cum Rabban Simeone Luchasin sol.57. An ille fuerit Annas socer Caiphæ, vel Iudex Pauli Actor.23. diiudicet lector. Lucas cap.iii. Annam summum Pontificem nominat, non quòd revera summus Pontifex suisset ut Caiapha, sed quia erat הכהנים פּןּ Sacerdotum præfectus & primus à Caiapha. Hinc etiam Salvator noster prius ad Annam deducitur quàm ad Caiapham, partim quia Caiaphæ erat socer, partim verò quia grandævior erat, maioris experientiæ & scientiæ, qualibus vicariis indocti & imperiti illorum temporum Sacerdotes ad expedienda negotia opus habebant; Erat ipse Caiaphas non omnium mortalium doctissimus, & qui proinde consilio Annæ dirigebatur.
units.tr: Frequent mention is made of R. Ananias, פּןּ הכהני Sagan of the priests; see the place cited above. He perished in the siege of the city together with Rabban Simeon, Luchasin fol.57. Whether he was Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas, or the judge of Paul in Acts 23, let the reader decide. Luke 3 calls Annas the high priest, not because he truly was high priest in the way Caiaphas was, but because he was הכהנים פּןּ the prefect of the priests and first after Caiaphas. Hence also our Saviour was taken first to Annas before Caiaphas, partly because Annas was Caiaphas's father-in-law, and partly because he was older, of greater experience and knowledge. Such vicars were needed by the unlearned and inexperienced priests of those times to manage affairs. Caiaphas himself was not the most learned of all mortals, and was therefore guided by the counsel of Annas.

units.la: §. De modo quo Summus Sacerdos solenniter in die expiationis administraverit, Vid. Expiationis festum. Retinenda est hic methodus quâ publicè in illo die legerit in lege. Sicuti illam referunt Ioma cap.7. & Sotah cap.7. Pontisex legebat vel in vestibus byssinis vel in stola alba; ordo autem talis erat. Minister publicus deprompsit librum legis, & tradidit illum archisynagogo; Caput Synagogæ tradebat illum summi Sacerdotis vicario, ille verò summo Sacerdoti, qui stabat, & accipiebat, & legebat; legebat autem sècl. אחרי מות Lev.16. & volvebat librum legis (non enim possumus dicere claudebat, quia libri ipsorum non erant ut nostri, ) & illum ad suumpestus collocans dicebat, plusquàm id quod legi vobis est hic. 'בחומש הפקודי in Pentateucho Numerorum (sectionem scilicet Num.29.27.) memoriter recitabat. Postea benedicebat osto benedictionibus, super lege & super ministerio, super confessione, remissione peccatorum sanctuario, Israele, Sacerdotibus,& super oratione reliqua.
units.tr: §. On the manner in which the high priest solemnly performed the rites on the Day of Atonement, see Feast of Atonement. The method by which he publicly read the law on that day should be retained here, as they relate it in Ioma cap.7 and Sotah cap.7: The high priest read either in linen garments or in a white stole. The order was as follows. A public minister took out the book of the law and handed it to the head of the synagogue; the head of the synagogue handed it to the deputy of the high priest, and he to the high priest, who stood and received it and read. He read Lev.16, "after the death," and rolled up the book of the law (for we cannot say he closed it, since their books were not like ours), and placing it at his side he said, more than what has been read to you here. He recited from memory in the Pentateuch [בחומש הפקודי] of Numbers (namely the section Num.29.27). Afterwards he pronounced eight blessings: over the law and over the ministry, over the confession, the remission of sins, the sanctuary, Israel, the priests, and over the remaining prayer.

units.la: §. Summi Sacerdotis mors sive fuerit oleo unctionis sive vestimentis initiatus, homicidas in asylis exsulantes liberabat. Vid. Asyla.
units.tr: §. The death of the high priest, whether he had been initiated by anointing with oil or by vestments, set free the manslayers who were in exile in the cities of refuge. See Asyla.

units.la: §. De Sacerdote qui est מלחמה כשוח unctus in bellum Vid.ap. Bellum.
units.tr: §. On the priest who is [משוח מלחמה] anointed for war, see War.

units.la: SACRIFICIA & oblationes, erant vel rerum animatarum vel inanimatarum. Creaturæ animatæ quæ offerebantur erant numero 5. Juvenci, oves, capri, turtures, columba. Inanimatæ erant, primitiæ frugum, flores, vinum, oleum, thus, & sal.
units.tr: Sacrifices and offerings were either of living or of inanimate things. The living creatures that were offered were five in number: young bulls, sheep, goats, turtledoves, pigeons. The inanimate ones were first fruits of grain, flour, wine, oil, incense, and salt.

units.la: Sacrificia rerum animatarum iterum distinguuntur in קדשי הקדשים Sacrificia Sanctissima, & קדשי קלים Sacrificia minoris valoris. Sacrificia Sanctissima erant עולות holocausta, חטאות Sacrificia pro peccato, אשמות Sacrificia pro reatu & שלמים Sacrificia Eucharistica, sive pacifica. (Vid. Maymon in קרבנות מעשה cap. 1.) Sacrificia minoris æstimationis erant Particularium & Privatorum oblationes eucharistica, agni Paschales, primogenitorum animalium oblationes, & decima.
units.tr: Sacrifices of living things are again divided into קדשי הקדשים [most holy sacrifices] and קדשי קלים [sacrifices of lesser value]. The most holy sacrifices were עולות burnt offerings, חטאות sin offerings, אשמות guilt offerings, and שלמים thank offerings, or peace offerings. (See Maimonides in קרבנות מעשה cap.1.) Sacrifices of lesser estimation were the thank offerings of individuals and private persons, the Passover lambs, the offerings of firstborn animals, and tithes.

units.la: De quibusdam Sacrificiis dicitur, quòd sint זבחי חובה Sacrificia debita, de aliis verò quòd sint 'ודבי ו־נדר Sacrificia volumaria. Nunc de singulis in specie.
units.tr: Of some sacrifices it is said that they are זבחי חובה debt sacrifices, and of others that they are ודבי ו־נדר, voluntary sacrifices. Now let us consider each in particular.

units.la: De עולות Sacrificiis ascensus, sive holocaustis.
units.tr: On the עולות ascending sacrifices, or burnt offerings.

units.la: Disputatur inter Hebraeorum magistros, quaenam holocaustorum ordinationis fuerit occasio, & quo modo debita facta sint. Tandem autem ita definiunt, holocausta instituta esse vel ad expiationem malarum cogitationum cordis, sicuti sacrificia pro peccato erant pro malis actionibus: vel ad expiationem peccati commissi contra aliquod praeceptum affirmativum, sicuti reliqua erant ad expianda peccata negativa. Sic Aben Esra in Lev.1. Animal illud quod offertur ad expiationem illius quod nobis in cor ascendit vocatur עולה; sicuti oblationem pro peccato patrato vocamus חטאת & אשם. Et Akiba in Tosaphot. Menachot cap.10. Item Ionathan & Gloss.Heb. in ipsum ad Levit.6.9.
units.tr: Among the Hebrew masters there is dispute about what was the occasion for the institution of burnt offerings, and how they came to be owed. In the end they define them as having been instituted either for the expiation of evil thoughts of the heart, just as sin offerings were for evil deeds, or for the expiation of a sin committed against some affirmative precept, just as the rest were for expiating negative sins. So Aben Esra on Lev.1.: The animal which is offered for the expiation of what has come into our heart is called עולה; just as we call the offering for a sin committed חטאת and אשם. Also Akiba in Tosaphot. Menachot cap.10. Likewise Ionathan & Gloss.Heb. on the same passage, Levit.6.9.

units.la: Holocausta fieri poterant ex omnibus quinque speciebus animalium viventium. Oblatio autem eorum fiebat hunc in modum.
units.tr: Burnt offerings could be made from all five kinds of living animals. Their offering was made in this manner.

units.la: Sacrificium holocausti allaturus de juvencis, poterat vitulum accipere qui octo dies & supra agebat. Idem poterat facere respectu agnorum & haedorum. Sed semper in hunc usum debebat segregare masculum: quoniam enim nulla oblatio excellentior erat holocausto, merito ad illam adhibebatur, quod inter animantia excellentissimum. Aben Esra ubi supra.
units.tr: One who was bringing a burnt offering of the herd could take a calf that was eight days old or more. He could do the same with regard to lambs and goats. But he must always set apart a male for this purpose. Since no offering was more excellent than the burnt offering, it was rightly used for the most excellent of living creatures. Aben Esra, as above.

units.la: §. 1. Vitulum electum debebat in atrium afferre : Expressa enim exstat lex Lev.1.3. ut oblationem suam quivis afferat coram Domino. Phrasi autem ilâ coram Domino, intelligitur spatium templi à Porta Nikanoris intus versum, ( Hierof.Sotah c.1.) Et certè hoc tam strictè observari debuit,ut ipsæ mulieres, quæ aliàs in atrium Israelis venire non poterant, in illud tamen ingredi cogerentur, si sacrificium holocausti offerre intendebant. Vid. Tosapht. in Erachin cap. 2.
units.tr: §. 1. He had to bring the chosen calf into the court, for the law is expressly given at Lev.1.3, that each one should bring his offering before the Lord. By the phrase before the Lord is understood the space of the temple inward from the Gate of Nicanor (Hierosolymitan Sotah cap.1). And indeed this was to be observed so strictly that the women themselves, who otherwise could not enter the court of Israel, were nevertheless compelled to go in if they intended to offer a burnt offering. See Tosapht. in Erachin cap.2.

units.la: §. 2. Manum suam capiti holocausti imponere debebat. Lev.1.4. Maymon in Corbanot cap. 3. Omnibus Sacrificiis quæ privatus aliquis de animalibus offert,sive sint oblationes debitæ sive voluntariæ,manus impositionem est dû adhuc vivit animal, exceptis oblationibus primogenitorum, decimatarum,& agni Paschalis. Hac manuum impositione transmittebat in animal sua peccata , & morte eius instanti confitebatur se morte dignum esse. Quæ omnia Christum ut figuræ spectabant. §. Circa hanc manuum impositionem sequentes traditiones habent patres Mischnici & Maym. a. Debebat illa fieri in atrio, & si manus animali imposuisset antequàm in atrium pervenïsset, illam ibi repetere debebat. ß. In Sacrificiis privatorum nemo poterat per vicarium manus imponere; in publicis sacrificiis id fieri poterat per viros stationarios de quibus infrà.
units.tr: §. 2. He had to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, Lev.1.4. Maimonides in Corbanot cap.3: In all sacrifices which a private person offers from animals, whether they are debt offerings or voluntary, laying on of hands is required while the animal is still alive, except for the offerings of firstborn animals, tithes, and the Passover lamb. By this laying on of hands he transferred his sins onto the animal, and at its death confessed that he deserved to die. All these things looked to Christ as the figure. §. Concerning this laying on of hands, the Mishnic fathers and Maimonides have the following traditions. a. It had to be done in the court; and if he had laid his hand on the animal before reaching the court, he had to repeat it there. ß. In the sacrifices of private persons no one could lay on hands through a substitute; in public sacrifices this could be done through stationary men, about whom more below.

units.la: γ. Si diversi convenerunt ut pro omnibus Sacrificium unum offeratur,(sicuti etiam id fieri poterat docente Maymon in Corbanot cap.3. & R. Salomoh in Lev.1.) unusquisque unus post alterum viftima manus imponere debuerunt. δ. Disputatur inter Doctores an solum una vel ambæ manus imponendæ essent, & hoc & illud suos habet assertores, omnes autem in hoc consentiunt, quòd manus imponendæ sint omnibus viribus. Ionathan qui vult ut una solum imponatur manus sic inst. Manum suam dextram imponere debet omni tempore sine virium. Idem dicit Maymon quamvis ambas intelligat. ε. Vbi manus imponebatur erat ordinarie in loco mactationis (sive ut vocant annulorum, ab infixis ibi annulis ad alligationem sacrificiorum destinatis:) qua occasione Israelita ingredi poterat atrium Sacerdotum; cùm alias hoc ipsi prohibitum esset. ζ. Modus impositionis manuum hic erat. Victima ita collocabatur ut offerens facie orientem versus conversa, manus suas intrà animalis cornua ponere poterat: Deinde illis positis confitebatur sua peccata quæ vel contrà affirmativa vel negativa præcepta commiserat, si scilicet sacrificium eius holocaustum esse debebat. Confessio talis erat: Peccavi, Perversè egi, rebellus fui & hoc & illud commisi; sed pœnitens ad te convertor, sit hoc mea expiatio. Statim autem ac confessio hæc absoluta erat, victima macta batur.
units.tr: γ. If several persons agreed that one sacrifice should be offered for all (as could be done, teaches Maimonides in Corbanot cap.3, and R. Salomoh on Lev.1.), each one had to lay his hand on the victim one after another. δ. Disputes arise among the teachers as to whether only one hand or both were to be laid on. Each opinion has its advocates, but all agree that the hands must be laid on with all one's strength. Ionathan, who wants only one hand laid on, puts it thus: He must lay his right hand on it at all times, with all his strength. Maimonides says the same, although he understands both hands. ε. The place where the hand was laid on was ordinarily the place of slaughter (or, as they call it, of the rings, from the rings fixed there for tying the sacrifices). On this occasion an Israelite could enter the court of the priests, which was otherwise forbidden to him. ζ. The manner of laying on the hands was this. The victim was placed so that the offerer, facing east, could put his hands between the animal's horns. Then, with his hands so placed, he confessed the sins he had committed against either affirmative or negative precepts, if his sacrifice was to be a burnt offering. The confession was as follows: I have sinned, I have acted perversely, I have rebelled, and I have done this and that; but penitent I turn to you; let this be my atonement. As soon as this confession was finished, the victim was slaughtered.

units.la: §. 3. Sacrificii mactatio propriè ad Sacerdotes pertinuit, interim tamen propter locum Lev.1. Et ille mactare debet invencum coram Domino, filii Aaronis vero spargent sanguinem &c. permissum fuit ut etiam alii mactarent, & sufficiebat Sacerdotibus, si ipsorum officium in excipiendo sanguine inciperet. Hoc notarunt
units.tr: §3. The slaughter of the sacrifice properly belonged to the priests. Nevertheless, on the basis of Lev. 1, "And he shall kill the bullock before the LORD; and the sons of Aaron shall sprinkle the blood, etc.", others were also permitted to slaughter, and it was enough for the priests if their own service began with receiving the blood. The Hebrews noted this.

units.la: Maymon in Biath Mikdasch cap.9. & in Corbanoth cap.5. in his verbis שחיטת הקרשים כשירה בור ם אפי' קודשי הקדשים Mactatio sacrificiorum legitima erat saëta ab aliis quàm Sacerdotibus, licet fuerint sacrificia sanctissima, vel personæ privatæ vel publicæ alicuius congregationis. Vid. etiam R. Salomoh in Levit.1.
units.tr: Maimonides, in Biath Mikdasch ch. 9 and in Corbanoth ch. 5, in these words: שחיטת הקדשים כשירה בזר אפילו קדשי הקדשים [Shechitat hakodashim kesherah bazar afilu kodshei hakodashim]. "The slaughter of sacrifices was lawful when performed by others than priests, even if they were most holy sacrifices, whether by private persons or by public persons of some congregation." See also R. Solomon on Leviticus 1.

units.la: §. 4. Excoriatio viltima secundùm Maymonidem etiam ab alio quàm à Sacerdote fieri poterat item dissectio eius, & lignorum ad altare delatio. In mactatione agnorum Paschalium ad quam ob ingentem numerum Sacerdotes non sufficiebant, præcipuè in usu erat alios adhibêre. De loco excoriationis loquitur Middot cap.3.§.5. Ad septentrionem altaris erant annu'orum sex ordines (non erant proprie integri annuli, sed potius annulorum dimidiata segmenta) quorum singguli continebant quatuor. בית המטנחים locus mactationis erat ad Septentrionem altaris, atque in eo osto columnæ humiles, quibus erant imposita quadrata è cedro ligna: his verò unci ferrei ita infixi erant, ut ligna singula haberent ordines eorum tres, è quibus Sacrificia suspendebantur, ac pelle nudabant ad mensas marmoreas quæ inter columnas erant. Si non plures victimæ erant, quàm quòd illi unci capere poterant, omnes in illis suspendebant; at notat Maymon quòd in Paschate in quo ingens multitudo agnorum erat, sumserint baculos ibi in hunc finem paratos, illosque humeris imponentes, agnum ad excoriandum suspenderint; aut si Pascha incidisset in Sabbathum, ipsos loco baculorum manus sibi invicem humeris imposuisse, in illisque agnum suspendisse, quia tunc ipsis ob observationem Sabbathi non ita licitum erat baculos ferre. Vellera & pelles Sacrificiorum Sanctissimorum cedebant Sacerdotibus, qui illas condiebant singulis diebus, & in fine septimanæ dividebant inter se invicem. Reliquorum vero sacrificiorum pelles erant, vel reliquis officiariis, vel illis qui sacrificaverant propriæ.
units.tr: §4. According to Maimonides, the flaying of the victim could also be done by someone other than a priest, and likewise its dissection and the carrying of wood to the altar. In the slaughter of the Passover lambs, for which the priests were not enough because of their huge number, it was especially customary to employ others. Middot ch. 3 §5 speaks of the place of flaying: "On the north side of the altar there were six rows of rings (they were not properly whole rings but rather half-segments of rings), each row containing four." בית המטבחיים [Beit hamitbachayim]: "The place of slaughter was on the north side of the altar, and in it were low columns, on which were laid squared beams of cedar; in these were fixed iron hooks, three rows for each beam, from which the sacrifices were hung, and they were stripped of their skin at the marble tables that stood between the columns."
