If there were not more victims than those hooks could hold, they were all hung on them; but Maimonides notes that at the Passover, when there was a huge multitude of lambs, they took staves prepared there for this purpose, laid them on their shoulders, and hung the lamb from them for flaying. Or, if the Passover fell on the Sabbath, they laid their hands on one another's shoulders in place of the staves and hung the lamb on these, because then it was not so lawful for them to carry staves on account of the observance of the Sabbath. The fleeces and skins of the most holy sacrifices went to the priests, who salted them each day and divided them among themselves at the end of the week. The skins of the other sacrifices went either to the other officials or to those who had offered them, as their own.

units.la: §. 5. Sanguinis sparsio debebat fieri antequàm Sacrificium excoriaretur, secundùm Canonem m אין משׁשׁיטין אותן עד שיורק הדם Victimas non denudant pelle, donec sanguis sparsus fuerit, quia Lev.1. 5. 6. Sanguinis sparsio detractioni pellis præponitur.De spargendo sanguine in altari observa seq. x. Sanguis spargendus excipi debebat vasculo ad cultum destinato, non autem aliquo quod ad ipsum pertinebat offerentem. Vascula illa vocant כלי שרת vid. Zebbachin c. 5. per tot. cap. ɔ. Sequentes sanguinem excipere non poterant; 1. Ille qui non erat Sacerdos. 2. Sacerdos qui erat אנו i.e. cui, illo die ex familiaribus eius aliquis morte defunctus erat. 3. qui immundus erat & יום טבול illo die ad se purificandum lavare debebat. 4. ille qui maiori & longiori impuritate laborabat, quàm ut lotione adhuc illo die mundus fieri potuisset. 5. ille qui non indutus erat omnibus illis vestimentis quæ habere debebat. 6. ille qui incircuncifus erat. 7. ille qui immundus erat. 8. ille qui non stabat in pavimento soli templi, sed sup. r aliquo ligno, aut strato, aut pede sui proximi. 9. ille qui suistrâ sanguinem excipiebat; bat; quamvis in hoc casu inter doctores non sit universalis consensus. Vid. Zebbachin cap.2. & Gloss.in Mischn. 1. In altaris medio erat linea rubra quæ tafin & extremitatem eius æqualibus spatiis dividebat. Quorundam sacrificiorum sanguis prope illam lineam erat spargendus, aliorum vero supra illam. Si hoc accurate non observabatur aspersio illegitima erat. Zebbachin ibid.
units.tr: §5. The sprinkling of blood had to be done before the sacrifice was flayed, according to the canon: "They do not strip the victims of their skin until the blood has been sprinkled" (אין משמיטין אותן עד שיזרק הדם [Ein meshamitin otan ad sheyizrok hadam]), because of Lev. 1:5, 6. The sprinkling of blood takes precedence over the removal of the skin. Concerning the sprinkling of blood on the altar, see the following. The blood to be sprinkled had to be received in a vessel dedicated to the service, not in anything that belonged to the person offering. These vessels they call כלי שרת [keli sharet]; see Zebachim ch. 5 throughout. The following could not receive the blood: (1) one who was not a priest; (2) a priest who was an onen, that is, one of whose close relatives had died that same day; (3) one who was unclean and had to wash that day to purify himself (יום טבול [yom tevul]); (4) one who was afflicted with a greater and longer uncleanness, which could not be cleansed by washing on that same day; (5) one who was not clothed in all the garments he was required to wear; (6) one who was uncircumcised; (7) one who was unclean; (8) one who did not stand on the bare pavement of the temple court, but on some wood, or a mat, or the foot of his neighbour; (9) one who received the blood with his left hand, although in this case there is not universal agreement among the teachers. See Zebachim ch. 2 and the Gloss on the Mishnah. In the middle of the altar there was a red line which divided its ledge and its edge into equal spaces. The blood of some sacrifices was to be sprinkled near that line, and of others above it. If this was not observed exactly, the sprinkling was unlawful. Zebachim, ibid.

units.la: 7. Aspersio Sanguinis Sacrificiorum sanctissimorum (excepto sacrificio pro peccato,) similis erat, nec discrepantiam habebat. Maym. in Corbanot cap.5. Sic autem fiebat. Sacerdos ille qui sanguinem exceperat, illum ad altare ferebat & infrà lineam rubram illam spargebat כזין ין instar Γ Græcorum. Id est, stabat primò à parte altaris orientali prope angulum eius Orientalem, & sanguinem ita effundebat, ut pars eius aspergeret latus vergens versus orientem, altera verò pars latus septentrionale; secundò stabat à parte occidentali & adhibebat iterum diligentiam, ut uno ictu duo latera aspergeret: quâ ratione in modum L sanguis spargebatur, quod denotarunt Græcorum Gammâ: interim illo modo quoque satisfactum est legi præcipienti Lev.1.5. & 3.8. ut altare circumcirca aspergeretur. Ictus vel vices illas expellendi sanguinem vocant מתנה dationem. Quædam sacrificia ut illa de quibus nunc nobis sermo דמן שתי מתנות שתן ארבע opus habebant duabus solùm dationibus, quæ tamen æstimabantur ut quatuor; alia verò opus habebant ictibus quatuor, pro numero quatuor altaris angulorum. Vid. Zevachin sol. 55. in Gem. & c. 5. in Mifna. Maymon in Corbanot c. 5.
units.tr: 7. The sprinkling of the blood of the most holy sacrifices (except the sin offering) was similar and showed no difference. Maimonides, Corbanot ch. 5. It was done as follows. The priest who had received the blood carried it to the altar and sprinkled it below that red line, כזין [kazayin], like the Greek Γ (gamma). That is, he first stood on the east side of the altar near its eastern corner and poured out the blood so that one part of it struck the side facing east and the other part the northern side. Secondly, he stood on the west side and took care again, so that with one throw he sprinkled two sides; by this method the blood was sprinkled in the shape of an L, which the Greeks denoted by gamma. In this way too the law was satisfied, which requires (Lev. 1:5 and 3:8) that the altar be sprinkled all around. These throws or actions of pouring out the blood they call מתנה [mattanah], "a giving." Some sacrifices, such as those we are now discussing, שתי מתנות שתן ארבע [needed only two givings, which were nevertheless reckoned as four], while others required four throws, corresponding to the number of the altar's four corners. See Zevachim fol. 55 in the Gemara, and ch. 5 in the Mishnah; Maimonides, Corbanot ch. 5.

units.la: De aspersione sanguinis in Paschate vid. f. 1. De illa quæ fiebat in Sacrificio pro peccato mox dicendum.
units.tr: On the sprinkling of blood at the Passover, see f. 1. What was done in the sin offering will be discussed presently.

units.la: §. 6. Iam referendus ritus, agnum mactatum vel qualecunque animal fuerit, dissecandi, sicuti respecta Sacrifici iugiter offerendi illum tradit MassecetTamid c. 4. Agni qui mactari debuit pedes ligabantur, anteriores cum posterioribus; ligatus illum in modum, ita disponebatur, ut facies eius orientem respiceret: qui ipsum mactaturus erat stabat a parte orientali facie in Occidentem versâ. Mactato & iugulato agno excipiebatur sanguis & spargebatur; deinde uncis ipsum suspendentes excoriabant. Perrexit Sacerdos in excoriatione donec perventum ad pectus; postquàm eò usque processum, abscidit caput, & dedit illi cui forte contigit illud ad altare deferre. Deinde abscindebat crura cique dabat, cuius erat illa deferre; quo facto ipsum excoriare pergebat, donec tota pellis detracta. Cordis exsectio sequebatur, illud aperiens purgabat sanguine. Posteà exscindebat armos & Sacerdoti exhibebat, pedem dextrum cum testiculis sumebat & separato adipe, illum imponebat tabulæ mactatoriæ. Viscera extrahebat & alicui lavanda tradebat, qui illa primò accuratè purgabat in conclavi lavantium, deinde obiter super tabulas marmoreas. Sumpto Cultro dividebat pulmones & iecur, nondum autem plane tollebat. Tandem pectus exsecabat, &per spinam dorsi descendens unumquodque separans illis dabat qui ordinati erant ad Sacrificium ad altare deferendum, ut notavimus ap. Cultum.
units.tr: §6. Now the rite is to be related: how the lamb, or whatever animal it was, was dissected once it had been slaughtered; this is what the Mishnah tractate Tamid ch. 4 hands down concerning the continual burnt offering. The feet of the lamb that was to be slaughtered were tied, the front ones together with the back ones. Bound in this way, it was arranged so that its face looked toward the east, and the one who was to slaughter it stood on the east side, facing west. When the lamb had been slaughtered and its throat cut, the blood was received and sprinkled. Then, hanging it on hooks, they flayed it. The priest proceeded with the flaying until he reached the breast; after going this far, he cut off the head and gave it to whoever happened to be assigned to carry it to the altar. Then he cut off the legs and gave them to the one whose task was to carry them; having done this, he continued flaying until the whole skin was removed. Next came the cutting out of the heart, which he opened and cleansed of blood. Afterwards he cut off the shoulders and gave them to a priest; he took the right foot with the testicles and, once the fat was separated, placed it on the table of slaughter. He removed the entrails and handed them to someone to be washed, who first cleansed them carefully in the room of the washers, and then briefly over the marble tables. Taking a knife, he divided the lungs and the liver, but did not yet remove them entirely. At last he cut open the breast, and, descending along the backbone, separated each part and gave them to those who had been appointed to carry the sacrifice to the altar, as we have noted under Cultus.

units.la: §. 7. Sacerdotes illi cum suis frustis in manibus ad gradum altaris accedebant, ibique ea deponebant, & sale condiebant. Maymon in Corban. c.6. ad hoc obligabantur expresso praecepto Lev. 2. 13. cum omnibus tuis sacrificiis sal offerre debes. Hinc Maynon in Ifsure מוּבח cap.5. אין דבר שקרב למזבח בלא מלח חוץ מיין הנסכין והרם והעצים Nihil in altari offerebatur quod non salitum erat, excepto vino libaminis, sanguine aspersionis, & ligns pro ignis conservatione. In tribus autem locis utebantur sale בלשכת המלח in conclavi salis ad pelles saliendas; in gradu altaris ad saliendas partes Sacrificii, & in summitate altaris condiebant sale flores, oleum & thus, ובנחור oblationes quae comburebantur, & oblationes avium. Sal illud non poterat a privato afferri sicuti nec ligna; sed funebatur de sale של הצבור quod commune erat in templo, & ad totam congregationem pertinebat. Ad hunc saliendi ritum respiciens Salvator Marci 9. 49. dicit, omnis homo igne salietur. i.e. quivis qui vera Dei victima est condietur sale gratiae ad incorruptionem gloriae: ignem autem adhibet, quia in versu praecedenti aluserat ad ignem perpetuum in valle Hinnom, quo absumebantur cadavera. Quasi innueret, Cadavera igne salita a corruptione sunt immunia, sed quamvis impii salientur igne inextinguibili, vermis ipsorum non morietur. De Sacrificiorum falitione videfis Menachot folio 21. 2.
units.tr: §7. Those priests, with their pieces in their hands, came up to the step of the altar, and there they set them down and seasoned them with salt. Maimonides, Corbanot ch. 6, shows that they were bound to this by the express precept of Lev. 2:13: "With all your offerings you shall offer salt." Hence Maimonides in Isure Mizbeach ch. 5: אין דבר שקרב למזבח בלא מלח [Ein davar shekarav lamizbeach belo melach]: "Nothing was offered on the altar that was not salted, except the wine of the libation, the blood of sprinkling, and the wood for keeping the fire. In three places they used salt: in the chamber of salt, for salting the hides; on the step of the altar, for salting the parts of the sacrifice; and on the top of the altar they seasoned with salt the flour, oil and frankincense, the offerings that were burnt, and the offerings of birds. That salt could not be brought by a private person, nor could the wood; but it was taken from the salt of the community (של הצבור [shel hatzibur]), which was common in the temple and belonged to the whole congregation." Looking at this rite of salting, the Saviour says (Mark 9:49), "Every one shall be salted with fire"; that is, whoever is the true victim of God shall be seasoned with the salt of grace unto the incorruption of glory. He uses the word fire because in the preceding verse he had alluded to the perpetual fire in the valley of Hinnom, in which corpses were consumed. As if to indicate that corpses salted with fire are immune to corruption, but although the wicked are salted with unquenchable fire, their worm will not die. On the salting of sacrifices see Menachot fol. 21 (2).

units.la: Partes sacrificii salitas ab ordinatis in eum finem Sacerdotibus, deferebant ad fummitatem Altaris, ubi primò nervum contrahentem in cineres projiciebant, deinde omnes reliquas partes incomptè & inconditè, ut proiectione illa partium aspersionem sanguinis aliquo modo imitarentur. Sed partes ita disjectas secundâ diligentiâ in illum redigebant ordinem, qui ad formam agni maximè accedebat. v. g. caput primum disponebant, addebant humeros & partes anteriores, & sic de cæteris. Dispositus illum in modum agnus igni committebatur.
units.tr: The parts of the sacrifice, once salted by the priests appointed for that purpose, were carried up to the top of the altar. There they first threw the sinew that shrinks into the ashes, and then all the remaining parts, placed carelessly and without order, so that by this scattering they might in some measure imitate the sprinkling of the blood. Afterwards, with careful attention, they set the scattered parts again in the order that came closest to the shape of a lamb. For example, they first arranged the head, then added the shoulders and the forequarters, and so on with the rest. Arranged in this manner like a lamb, the offering was committed to the fire.

units.la: De sacrificio holocausti adde quæ in D. apud Ṡpor פורון posuimus.
units.tr: On the burnt offering, add what we have set out under Ṡpor פורון in the D. section.

units.la: De חטאת Sacrificio pro peccato.
units.tr: On the sin offering, חטאת

units.la: §. De illo vid. Lev.4.2.13.22.27. In quibus locis generaliter definitur, sacrificia pro peccato offerenda esse, pro peccatis sive omissionis, sive commissionis, modò ex ignorantia patrata sint. Hebræi verò definiunt illa adducenda esse pro peccatis ex ignorantia commissis contrà præceptum negativum, cuius negletti conscius merebatur excidium. Sic R. Salomoh in Lev.4. אין חטאת כאה אלא על שודונו לאו וכרת ושגגתן חטאת Sacrificium pro peccato non offerebatur propter peccatum conscie & ex petulantia commissum contra præceptum negativum, & quod inducebatur in reatum excidii, sed pro peccato ex ignorantia commisso. Kerithut cap. 1. על כל אלו חייבין דרונם כרת ועל שגגתן חטאת Omnia illa (peccata quæ numero 36. ibi recensentur) si petulanter commissa sunt, reatum excidii attrahunt; exignorantia vero commissa requiruntur Sacrificium pro peccato. Idem dicit Maymon in משנה cap.1. Et Aben Efra in Lev.1. nisi quòd in hoc ab aliis dissentiat, quòd existimet, sacrificium pro peccato afferri propter peccatum commissum contra tale praeceptum negativum, quod petulanti negligentiae meretur excidium vel vapulationem; addit ille excidio vapulationem, quod alii non faciunt, plurimis enim peccatis debebatur vapulatio, quibus non debebatur כרת excidium. Et Maym. l. cit. solùm 45. peccata recensef pro quibus sacrificium חטאת afferendum, cùm tamen praeceptorum negativorum numerus in genere fuerit 365. Maym.praef. ad Iad Chafaka. Quod diximus clarum fiet allatis his duobus exemplis.
units.tr: §. On this see Lev. 4:2, 13, 22, 27. In these passages it is laid down in general that sin offerings are to be brought for sins, whether of omission or of commission, provided they were committed through ignorance. The Hebrews, however, define that these offerings are to be brought for sins committed in ignorance against a negative precept, the one who knew of the transgression deserving excision. So R. Solomon on Leviticus 4: A sin offering was not brought for a sin committed knowingly and wilfully against a negative precept, for which the penalty was excision, but for a sin committed in ignorance. [אין חטאת באה אלא על שודונו לאו וכרת ושגגתן חטאת] Kerithut, chapter 1: For all those (sins which are listed there under number 36), if they were committed wilfully, they bring the guilt of excision; but if committed in ignorance, a sin offering is required. [על כל אלו חייבין דרונם כרת ועל שגגתן חטאת] Maimonides says the same in the Mishnah, chapter 1. And Aben Ezra on Leviticus 1 agrees, except that he differs from the others in holding that a sin offering was brought for a sin committed against such a negative precept as deserved excision or flogging for wilful negligence. He adds flogging to excision, which the others do not do; for many sins carried the penalty of flogging but not the penalty of כרת excision. Maimonides in the same place lists only 45 sins for which the חטאת sin offering was to be brought, although the number of negative precepts in general is 365 (Maimonides, preface to Yad Chazakah). What we have said will become clear from the following two examples.

units.la: Praeceptum negativum est de violatione Sabbathi (Maymon in Schabbat cap.1.) Si itaque aliquis esset qui petulanter Sabbathum violasset, reus erat excidii: si Sabbathum violasset praesentibus testibus, lapidabatur; si autem ex ignorantia Sabbathū violasset, afferebat sacrificium pro peccato, postquàm lapsum se comisisse meminerat. Praeceptum negativum est, ne ullus immundus in Sanctuarium ingrediatur. Si quis petulanter se ingerat in Sanctuarium cùm immundus est, & praesentibus testibus id fiat, fit flagellationis מרדות rebellionis (v.fl.) si nemine praesente חייב לכרת reus fit excidii. Si ex ignorantia ingreditur, affert sacrificium pro peccato. Aben Efra fine dubio de his posterioribus peccatis loquitur, sed non debebat excludere priora.
units.tr: The negative precept concerns the violation of the Sabbath (Maimonides on Shabbat, chapter 1). If, then, someone wilfully violated the Sabbath, he was liable to excision; if he violated the Sabbath in the presence of witnesses, he was stoned; but if he violated it through ignorance, he brought a sin offering after he remembered that he had fallen into error. The negative precept is that no unclean person should enter the sanctuary. If someone wilfully pushed himself into the sanctuary while unclean, and this was done in the presence of witnesses, he incurred the flogging of rebellion (מרדות, as some read it); if it was done with no one present, he became liable to excision. If he entered through ignorance, he brought a sin offering. Aben Ezra without doubt speaks of these latter sins, but he should not have excluded the former.

units.la: §. Sacrificia pro peccato distinguuntur in
units.tr: §. Sin offerings are distinguished into

units.la: sacrificia totius congregationis, & in sacrificia privatorum: Sacrificia totius congregationis offerebantur aliquando in nomine Synedrii, quod tamen populum integrum simul etiam repræsentabat, aliquando vero simpliciter in nomine congregationis. Synedrium illa afferebat Sacrificia, si per inadvertentiam male circa aliquam legis partem determinasset; vocant illa sacrificia הָעֽלָם דבר invencos pro re gnota oblatos. Oblationum pro tota congregatione mentio fit. Lev.16.15. Lev.4.13. De hac acceptione nominis קהל Congregationis vid. R.Salomoh in Lev.4. Maymon. in Schegagah cap.12. Targum Ionath. in Lev.4. Sanguis horum sacrificiorum congregationis allatus fuit in sanctum sanctorum, illoque digitis septies coram velo aspergebat Sacerdos; aliquid deinde affundebat cornubus altaris, residuum vero ad basin altaris. Aliquid de adipe in altari comburebat; sed vellus & caro, intestina, lingua, consumebantur in campo extra Sanctuarium. Christus factus est ἁμαρτία peccatum pro nobis, id est sacrificium pro peccato; & sicuti sacrificia in die expiationis ut & agnus qui quotidie offerebatur, erant oblationes pro tota congregatione, ita Christus qui est agnus Dei Ioh.1. facta est expiatio pro omni suo populo. Sacrificiorum in die expiationis carnes cur extra castra combustæ fuerunt, nisi ad significandum Christum à gentilibus & propter Gentiles mori debere, qui חיצונים ἔξω respectu Iudæorum nominantur?
units.tr: offerings for the whole congregation, and offerings for private persons. Offerings for the whole congregation were sometimes made in the name of the Sanhedrin, which nevertheless also represented the whole people at once; sometimes, however, simply in the name of the congregation. The Sanhedrin brought these offerings if, through an oversight, it had decided wrongly on some part of the law; they call such offerings הָעֽלָם דבר, bullocks offered for a matter unknown. Mention is made of offerings for the whole congregation (Lev. 16:15; Lev. 4:13). On this meaning of the word קהל, congregation, see R. Solomon on Leviticus 4, Maimonides in Shegagah chapter 12, and the Targum of Jonathan on Leviticus 4. The blood of these sacrifices of the congregation was brought into the Holy of Holies, and the priest sprinkled it with his finger seven times before the veil. Then he poured some on the horns of the altar, and the rest at the base of the altar. Some of the fat he burnt on the altar; but the hide and the flesh, the entrails and the tongue, were consumed in a clean place outside the sanctuary. Christ was made sin [ἁμαρτία] for us (2 Cor. 5:21), that is, a sin offering; and just as the sacrifices on the Day of Atonement, and also the lamb which was offered daily, were offerings for the whole congregation, so Christ, who is the Lamb of God (John 1), became the atonement for all his people. Why were the flesh of the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement burnt outside the camp, unless to signify that Christ had to die outside the city and for the Gentiles, who are called חיצונים, outside, with respect to the Jews?

units.la: Sacrificia pro peccato personarum privatarum erant 1. Iuvencus quem pro se offerebat summus Sacerdos in die expiationis. Lev.16.6. 2. Iuvencus quem summus Pontifex offerebat pro peccato ab ipso ex ignorantia commissio. Ille Iuvencus vocatur Iuvencus qui ob omnia praecepta offertur Maymon in Schegagah cap. 12. Secundum Aben Esram Lev.4. talem oblationem pro peccato summus Sacerdos semel in anno faciebat: ut alii pudorem sua peccata confitenti abjicerent, ut notat Baal Hatturim in Lev.4. 3.De duobus aliis sacrificiis pro peccato vid. Lev.4.22. v.23.25. & cap.4. v.27.
units.tr: Sin offerings for private persons were these: 1. The bullock which the high priest offered for himself on the Day of Atonement (Lev. 16:6). 2. The bullock which the high priest offered for a sin committed by himself through ignorance. This bullock is called the bullock offered for all the commandments (Maimonides in Shegagah chapter 12). According to Aben Ezra on Lev. 4, the high priest made such a sin offering only once a year, so that others, confessing their sins, might cast off shame; as Baal Hatturim notes on Leviticus 4. 3. On the two other sin offerings see Lev. 4:22, v. 23, 25, and chapter 4, v. 27.

units.la: §. De his Sacrificiis porro sequentia observanda.
units.tr: §. On these sacrifices the following points are further to be observed.

units.la: 1. Locum & modum sacrificia pro peccato offerendi, mactandi, eundem fuisse, cum illo quo offerebantur holocausta.
units.tr: 1. The place and manner of offering, slaying, and so forth, for sin offerings were the same as for the burnt offerings.

units.la: 2. Iuvencorum combustorum & hircorum combustorum (pro congregatione) Sanguis opus habet sparsione in Sancto ante velum ad altare aureum. Zebhachim cap. 5.
units.tr: 2. The burnt bullocks and burnt goats (for the congregation) needed the sprinkling of blood in the Sanctuary before the veil, at the golden altar (Zebahim chapter 5).

units.la: 2. Sanguinem qui in Sanctum non delatus fuit ex parte cornibus altaris fuisse illinitum, ex parte vero ad basin altaris effusum: sanguinem digito illiniebat cornibus Sacerdos incipiens à cornu quod inter orientem & meridiem erat. Vid. Maymon ubi supra v. 5. Talm. in Zevachin c. 5.
units.tr: 2. The blood which was not carried into the Sanctuary was partly smeared on the horns of the altar and partly poured out at the base of the altar. The priest smeared the blood on the horns with his finger, beginning from the horn which was between east and south (see Maimonides, loc. cit. v. 5; Talmud, Zebachim chapter 5).

units.la: 3. Hircos & Iuvencos qui extra castra comburebantur fuisse dissectos in frusta & in igne dispositos holocaustorum instar. Maymon ubi supra cap.1.
units.tr: 3. The goats and bullocks which were burnt outside the camp were cut into pieces and arranged on the fire in the manner of burnt offerings (Maimonides, loc. cit. chapter 1).

units.la: 4. Illorum Sacrificiorum carnes quæ non extrà castra fuêre absumptæ, debebant à Sacerdotibus comedi. Lev.6.25.26. Hinc dictum Hosea 4.8. Peccatum populi mei comedunt. Id est sacrificia pro peccato populi mei comedunt, non tam ex devotione quàm ut ventres opleant.
units.tr: 4. The flesh of those sacrifices which were not consumed outside the camp was to be eaten by the priests (Lev. 6:25, 26). Hence it is said in Hosea 4:8: They eat the sin of my people. That is, they eat the sin offerings of my people, not so much from devotion as in order to fill their bellies.

units.la: De אשם Sacrificiis pro reatu.
units.tr: On the asham, the Sacrifices for Guilt.

units.la: §. Sacrificia pro peccato & pro reatu in multis conveniebant. Sicuti enim Sacrificia pro peccato offerebantur, si aliquis contra præceptum negativum ex ignorantia peccasset, ita & sacrificia pro reatu. Sicuti illa relationem vel respectum habebant ad periculum excidii, ita & illa. Est tamen aliqua differentia ut ex sequentibus patebit.
units.tr: §. Sin offerings and guilt offerings agreed in many respects. Just as a sin offering was brought if anyone sinned through ignorance against a negative precept, so too was a guilt offering. As the former had reference to the danger of being cut off, so did the latter. There is, however, some difference, as will be clear from what follows.

units.la: §. Sacrificia pro reatu distinguuntur in אשם תלוי suspensa vel dubia, & ודאי אשם certò debita. Cur תלוי אשם sacrificium aliquod pro reatu suspensum nominetur videre poteris ex Maymon in Corbanoth cap. 9. Glossa in Misnaioth dicit hanc nomenclationis rationem esse לאי שתול ומנין עליו מן היסורי quia Sacrificium pro reatu reum suspendit & liberat à pœna. Sed meliorem rationem exhibet Kerithut cap. 1. sect. 2. postquàm enim recensuit 36. transgressiones quæ excidium merentur, ita concludit כל אלו חייבין על ודגם כרת על שגגתן חשאת ועל לא הורע שלהם אשם תלוי Omnes illi si petulanter peccaverint incurrunt pœnam excidii: si ex ignorantia, afferre debent sacrificium pro peccato, si verò dubitant an peccaverint nec ne, afferent sacrificium pro pro reatu. Vult Misna quòd si quis nescìat an certò peccaverit nec ne, & tamen aliqua apparentia adsit quòd peccare potuerit, ut sacrificium pro reatu dubitans afferat: hoc dinucidari potest historiâ quam lector de Baba Ben Butah in Kerithut c.6. seƈt.3. reperiet: & positione horum duorum exemplorum.
units.tr: §. Guilt offerings are divided into the asham talui, the suspended or doubtful guilt offering, and the asham vaddai, the certain guilt offering. You may see from Maimonides, in Corbanoth ch. 9, why a guilt offering is called suspended. The gloss on the Mishnah says the reason for the name is that the guilt offering holds the guilty party in suspense and frees him from punishment [לאי שתול ומנין עליו מן היסורי]. But Kerithut ch. 1, sect. 2, gives a better reason. After listing the 36 transgressions that deserve being cut off, it concludes: "All these, if they sin wilfully, incur the penalty of being cut off; if through ignorance, they must bring a sin offering; but if they doubt whether they sinned or not, they bring a suspended guilt offering" [כל אלו חייבין על ודגם כרת על שגגתן חשאת ועל לא הורע שלהם אשם תלוי]. The Mishnah means that if someone does not know for certain whether he has sinned or not, yet there is some appearance that he could have sinned, he brings a guilt offering in doubt. This can be explained by the story of Baba ben Butah, which the reader will find in Kerithut ch. 6, sect. 3, and by the setting of these two examples.

units.la: Kerithut cap.3. & Tosapht. in Kerithut cap.2. אמרו לו אכל חלב מבּיא חטאת עד אובר אכל ועד אומר לא אכל מביא אשם תלוי Id est per paraphrasin. Licitum erat ipsis comedere adipem sed non intestinorum, debebat enim ille comburi, posito ita casu ut aliquis credens se comedere adipem qui licitus erat, comedisset illicitum, & deinde ille testimonio astantium certus de suo errore factus fuisset, incubuit ipsi offerre sacrificium pro peccato. Si verò ipsi dubitaret sine ullo signo evidente, aut testibus sibi invicem contradicentibus, an revera comedisset nec ne, afferre debuit אשם תלוי Sacrificium pro reatu suspensionis vel dubitationis.
units.tr: Kerithut ch. 3, and the Tosephta on Kerithut ch. 2, say: "They said to him: if he ate fat, he brings a sin offering; until one says he did not eat, he brings a suspended guilt offering" [אמרו לו אכל חלב מביא חטאת עד אומר לא אכל מביא אשם תלוי]. In paraphrase: it was permitted to eat fat, but not the entrails, which had to be burned. Suppose someone, believing he was eating permitted fat, actually ate what was forbidden, and then, certain of his mistake through the testimony of bystanders, was obliged to offer a sin offering. But if he doubted, with no clear sign and with witnesses contradicting one another, whether he had really eaten or not, he had to bring an asham talui, a guilt offering of suspicion or doubt.

units.la: Glossa in Misnaioth ubi ante, & Tosaphta ubi modo. Si aliquis intendens concumbere cum uxore sua, rem habuisset cum sua sorore in eodem lecto dormiente, si sciens id fecerit, incurrit reatum excidii, si ex ignorantia, debet afferre Sacrificium pro peccato; si dubitat an non forsan hoc ipsi acciderit, neque tamen plenarie de facto certus sit, offerre debet תלוי אשם Sacrificium pro reatu dubio.
units.tr: The gloss on the Mishnah, where mentioned above, and the Tosephta where mentioned now, say: If someone intending to lie with his wife had had relations with his sister, who was sleeping in the same bed, then if he did so knowingly, he incurs the guilt of being cut off; if through ignorance, he must bring a sin offering; if he doubts whether this may have happened to him, and is not fully certain of the fact, he must bring a doubtful guilt offering, an asham talui.

units.la: §. ואשם תלוי Certi reatus oblatio nominatur, quia lex determinavit, quæ sacrificia, quomodo, & à quibus pro reatu offerenda sint. Ea sequentia erant, ut recensentur à Tosapht. ubi supra, Zevachin cap.5. & Maym. in מזבח c.9.
units.tr: §. The asham vaddai is named the offering of certain guilt, because the law determined which sacrifices were to be offered for guilt, how, and by whom. These were as follows, as listed by the Tosephta above, Zevachin ch. 5, and Maimonides in Mizbeach ch. 9.

units.la: 1. אשם גזילות Sacrificium pro reatu rei furto surreptæ, aut iniuste detentæ. Lev.6.2.3.6.
units.tr: 1. Asham gezilot: a guilt offering for guilt concerning a thing stolen or unjustly withheld. Lev. 6.2, 3, 6.

units.la: 2. אשם מעילה Sacrificium pro reatu sacrilegii Lev.5.16.
units.tr: 2. Asham me'ilah: a guilt offering for the guilt of sacrilege. Lev. 5.16.

units.la: 3. אשם תלוי Sacrificium pro reatu circa ancillam despectam de qua Lev.9.20.
units.tr: 3. Asham talui: a guilt offering for guilt concerning a despised maidservant. Lev. 19.20.

units.la: 4. אשם נזיר Sacrificium pro reatu Nasiræorum. Num.6.12.
units.tr: 4. Asham nazir: a guilt offering for the guilt of Nazarites. Num. 6.12.

units.la: 5. אשם metzora Sacrificium pro reatu Leprosorum. Lev.14.12.
units.tr: 5. Asham metzora: a guilt offering for the guilt of lepers. Lev. 14.12.

units.la: §. Dispositio horum Sacrificiorum quando offerebantur erat similis oblationi sacrificiorum pro peccato. Macta-bantur, excoriabantur, & interstina eximebantur, lavabantur, saliebantur & comburebantur, carnesque ipsorum comedebantur à Sacerdotibus. Aliquod tantum discrimen erat in sparsione sanguinis ipsorum: sicuti enim sanguis sacrificiorum pro peccato illiniebatur ex parte cornibus altaris, ita horum sanguis instar Gamma lateribus altaris aspergebatur, sicuti supra innuimus. Illorum sanguis spargebatur supra lineam rubram altaris, horum infra. Item differebant in eo quòd non omnia sacrificia reatûs numerabantur inter קדשי הקדשים Sacrificia sanctissima, sicuti Sacrificia pro peccato, oblatio enim Nazi-æorum numerabatur inter קדשים קלים Sancta levia.
units.tr: §. The arrangement of these sacrifices when they were offered was similar to that of sin offerings. They were slaughtered, skinned, and their entrails removed, washed, salted and burned, and their flesh was eaten by the priests. There was only a slight difference in the sprinkling of their blood. Just as the blood of sin offerings was smeared on the horns of the altar, so the blood of these was sprinkled on the sides of the altar in the shape of a gamma, as we hinted above. The blood of the former was sprinkled above the red line of the altar, that of the latter below it. They also differed in that not all guilt offerings were counted among the kodshei hakodashim, the most holy sacrifices, as sin offerings were; the offering of a Nazarite, for instance, was counted among the kodashim kalim, the lesser holy things.

units.la: De illa Sacrificiorum sanctissimorum comestione à Sacerdotibus Nota, quòd à Iudæis vo-
units.tr: Concerning that eating of the most holy sacrifices by the priests, note that by the Jews it is

units.la: cetur אכילת לפנים מן הקלעי comestio intra vela, allusione facta ad tabernaculum, quod velis ab aliis castris distinctum erat. Sicuti enim intra illa vela erant castra Domini, ita in templo spatium internum a Porta N kanoris castra Domini vocabatur, & in illo ut in sanctiore loco omnia Sacrificia sanctiora comedi debebant. Vid.Num.18.10. David Kimchi ad Ezech.42.13. Commentatur, fuisse quaedam conclavia quae in ipsum atrium Sacerdotum se extendebant, in quibus Sacerdotes, suas תרומות res sanctas comedebant. Sed praeterquam quod a nullis aliis haec conclavia designata fuerint, non opus est ut illa comestio plane ad Sacerdotum atrium constringatur; secundum praeceptum Dei sufficit si illa in Israelis atrio facta fuerit: & si loca ipsa designanda sunt, probabile est Sacerdotes aestivis temporibus sub porticu in libero aere, hybernis temporibus vero vel in conclavibus, Gazith, Mokad, aut Nitsots sua sancta comedisse, נאכלים על חצות Non comedebant omni tempore illas carnes, sed versus vesperam. Post mediam noctem illas edere amplius non potuerunt. Quod autem sub vesperam ad esum solum se accinxerint Sacerdotes, apparet ex primo versu qui in codice Misnico legitur. מאימתי קורין את שמע בערבית משעה שהכהנים נכנסים לאכול בתרומתן: Quando Phylacteria versperi recitanda sunt? Ab eo tempore, quo Sacerdotes ingrediuntur ad trumam suam comedendam. At an Sacerdotes nihil prandere soliti sint, definire non possumus.
units.tr: called [אכילת לפנים מן הקלעי], "eating within the curtains," an allusion to the tabernacle, which was separated from the other camps by curtains. Just as the camp of the Lord lay within those curtains, so in the temple the inner space from the Nicanor Gate was called the camp of the Lord, and in it, as in the holier place, all the most holy sacrifices had to be eaten. See Num. 18.10. David Kimchi, on Ezek. 42.13, comments that there were certain chambers that extended into the priests' court itself, in which the priests ate their terumot, their holy things. But apart from the fact that no other writers designate these chambers, it is not necessary to restrict that eating strictly to the priests' court; according to God's precept it is enough if it was done in the court of Israel. And if the places are to be specified, it is probable that the priests ate their holy things in summer under the portico in the open air, and in winter either in the chambers, gazith, mokad or nitsots. [נאכלים על חצות] They did not eat those flesh at all times, but towards evening; after midnight they could no longer eat them. That the priests only prepared themselves to eat at evening appears from the first verse as it is read in the Mishnaic text: "From when may the Shema be recited in the evening? From the time when the priests go in to eat their terumah" [מאימתי קורין את שמע בערבית משעה שהכהנים נכנסים לאכול בתרומתן]. But whether the priests were accustomed to eat anything at midday we cannot determine.

units.la: De שלמים Sacrificiis Pacificis.
units.tr: On the Shelamim [שלמים], or Peace Offerings.

units.la: §. Ita nominantur, quòd sicuti holocausta, sacrificia pro peccato & reatu offerebantur sub respectu alicuius commissi peccati, vel dubitationis, ita Sacrificia pacifica offerebantur, vel ad solutionem voti, vel ad gratiarum actionem testandam, vel denique ad Deum propitium reddendum, quod non male Heb. להשלים exprimit. R.Salomoh in Lev.3. hanc nomenclationis rationem habet: quia sacrificia illa dabant, pacem mundo, pacem altari, pacem Sacerdotibus, pacem offerentibus.
units.tr: §. They are so called because, just as burnt offerings and sin and guilt offerings were offered with respect to some sin committed or some doubt, so peace offerings were offered either to fulfil a vow, or to testify thanksgiving, or finally to render God propitious. The Hebrew word להשלים [lehashlim] expresses this not badly. R. Solomon, on Leviticus 3, gives this reason for the name: "because those sacrifices gave peace to the world, peace to the altar, peace to the priests, and peace to the offerers."

units.la: §. Inter Sacrificia Pacifica referuntur etiam illa quæ gentiles afferebant: de illis sic Maymon in Corbanot cap. 3. A Gentilibus & Ethnicis non recipiunt nisi solum illa quæ holocausta fieri possunt. Illius generis autem recipiunt oblationem avium, etiamsi illi Ethnicus idololatra essent. Non autem recipiunt ab ipsis sacrificia pacifica, nec libamina, nec sacrificia pro reatu aut peccato, nec sacrificia holocausti, nisi voluntarie ea attulerint, & in modum voti. Si Ethnicus afferat sacrificia pacifica, illa offerri debent in modum holocaustorum, quia animus Ethnici est versus cælum. A Iudæo Apostata nullum recipiunt sacrificium.
units.tr: §. Among the peace offerings are also counted those which Gentiles brought. Maimonides on this in Corbanot, chapter 3, says: "From Gentiles and heathens they accept only those offerings which may be made as burnt offerings. Of this kind they accept the offering of birds, even if the heathen was an idolater. But they do not accept from them peace offerings, nor drink offerings, nor sin or guilt offerings, nor burnt offerings, unless they brought them voluntarily and by way of a vow. If a heathen brings a peace offering, it must be offered in the manner of a burnt offering, because the heathen's mind is turned towards heaven. From a Jewish apostate they accept no sacrifice at all."

units.la: Ad quæ nota quòd non potuerint Ethnicorum sacrificia offerri, nisi essent לנחם לשמים eorda ipsorum aliqua devotione ealentia. 2. quòd non potuerint sacrificia ipsorum venire sub nomine sacrificii pro peccato aut reatus, quia non sub iisdem erant legibus cum Iudæis. 3. quòd non potuerint offerre panem, partim ob expressum Dei mandatum, partim verò quia panis non poterat holocaustum fieri, quæ in Sacrificio Gentilis erat conditio requisita. 4. quod oblationes Ethnici, sub altera harum duarum Sacrificii pacifici notionum, venire debuerint, ut vel offerrentur ex libera voluntate, vel ex consequentia alicuius voti. 5. Gentilis oblatio veniens sub nomine sacrificii Pacifici debuit tamen holocaustum fieri; quia carnes sacrificii Pacifici debebant comedi à Sacerdotibus; at cùm Ethnicus sacrificat, studet solum Deum pacificare, non autem cogitat de Sacerdotibus. Si verò eveniret ut amans unum vel alterum Israelitam ipsorum gratiâ sacrificium afferret Ethnicus, & Sacerdotes & Israelitæ carnes comedere possent; ut loco citato notavit Eruditissimus noster Maymonides.
units.tr: On these points it should be noted: (1) Gentile sacrifices could not be offered unless their hearts were glowing with some devotion, לנחם לשמים [lenoach lashamayim]. (2) Their sacrifices could not come under the name of a sin or guilt offering, because they were not under the same laws as the Jews. (3) They could not offer bread, partly because of God's express command, and partly because bread could not be made into a burnt offering, which was the required condition in a Gentile sacrifice. (4) Gentile offerings had to come under one of these two senses of a peace offering: either they were offered of free will, or in fulfilment of some vow. (5) A Gentile offering that came under the name of a peace offering nevertheless had to be made a burnt offering, because the flesh of a peace offering had to be eaten by the priests; but when a Gentile sacrifices, he seeks only to appease God and does not think of the priests. If, however, it happened that a Gentile, loving one or another Israelite, brought a sacrifice for their sake, both the priests and the Israelites might eat the flesh, as our most learned Maimonides noted in the place cited.

units.la: §. Sacrificia pacifica Israelitarum erant vel totius congregationis, vel persona alicuius privata. Prioris speciei erant duo agni qui unâ semel in anno offerebantur, scilicet in Pentecoste. Lev. 23.19. in illorum oblatione versabantur ut in Sacrificiis pro peccato. Ex Sacrificiis Eucharisticis, solummodò hoc numerabatur inter קדשים הקדשים Sacrificia Sanctissima. Maymon in Corbanoth cap.1. & cap. 9. Zevachin cap. 5. R. Salomoh Lev.23.20.
units.tr: §. The peace offerings of the Israelites were either those of the whole congregation or those of a private person. Of the former kind were the two lambs which were offered once a year, namely at Pentecost (Lev. 23.19). In their offering they were treated as sin offerings. Among the thanksgiving offerings, this alone was counted among the קדשים הקדשים [kodashim hakodashim], the most holy sacrifices. Maimonides in Corbanoth, chapter 1 and chapter 9; Zevachin, chapter 5; R. Solomon on Lev. 23.20.

units.la: Sacrificia personarum privatarum Eucharistica triplicia erant.
units.tr: The thanksgiving peace offerings of private persons were of three kinds.

units.la: 1. Sacrificia pacifica quæ absque pane offerebantur; tales erant oblationes quas offerebant in tribus solemnibus festis ad gaudium testandum.
units.tr: 1. Peace offerings which were offered without bread. Such were the offerings which they brought at the three solemn feasts to testify joy.

units.la: 2. Sacrificia pacifica quae eum pane offerebantur: illorum fit mentio Lev.7. poterant fieri ex Iuvencis ex agnis & hircis Lev.3. & hebant vel ex occasione voti, vel gratiarum actionis, vel merae & lib. rae devotionis: si aliquis salvus ex navigatione periculosa evaserit, ץי si non absque insigni aliquo miraculo liberatus, fuisset ex aliqua angustia, talem oblationem afferre debebat. Vid. R. Salomoh & Aben Esram in Lev.7.
units.tr: 2. Peace offerings which were offered with bread. Mention of these is made in Lev. 7. They could be made from bullocks, from lambs and from goats (Lev. 3). They were offered either on the occasion of a vow, or of thanksgiving, or of pure and free devotion. If someone had escaped safely from a perilous voyage, or had been freed from some distress without a remarkable miracle, he ought to bring such an offering. See R. Solomon and Aben Ezra on Lev. 7.

units.la: Haec Sacrificia personarum privatarum macari poterant in quavis atrii Israelis parte,(vid. Zevachin cap.5. sect.7.) ut plurimum caedebantur in latere Meridionali. Sanguis ipsorum spargebatur in modum sanguinis holocaustorum, scilicet שתי מתנות שתן ארבעה instar Gamma r. Pectus & armus dexter sacrificii pacifici pertinebant ad Sacerdotem offerentem, vocabanturque Rabbinicè מורם. Pectus debebat agitari coram Domino: ritus autem ille talis erat. Offerens debebat ingredi atrium Sacerdotum; ibi Sacerdos manui offerentis adipem cum pectore & armo dextro imponebat, item renes & omentum iecoris, & si ad gratias agendas mactatum effet Sacrificium, massam panis. Deinde Sacerdos manum suam infra manum offerentis ponens, illam cum rebus impositis huc illuc, sed praecipuè Orientem versus agitabat. Hic agitatione facta interstina aspergebat sale & in altari concremabat. Agitatum vero pectus & armum & panem pro sua parte fumebat Sacerdos, reliqua offerens. Licitum autem erat offerenti partem suam Sacrificii allati comedere in quacunque parte Hierosolymæ ipsi lubuerit, ita intelligendum hoc axioma נאכלין בכל העיר Poterant (partes Sacrificiorum)comedi (non in quavis urbe) sed in quavis parte Urbis: erat enim hoc unum ex Hierosolymæ privilegiis, quod קדשים קלים Sacrificia minus sanctla, in nulla alia urbe quam in illa comedi poterant. Kelim cap.1. sect.8. hinc intelliges quid sibi velit locus in Bab Berachot sol.49.2. Si quis post Sacrificium peractum domum revertitur & egressus Hierosolymâ recordatus fuerit, se adhuc apud se habere aliquam partem de carne Sacra; si iam ultra Zuphim progressus sit, qui erat locus ex quo urbs & templum conspici poterant, carnem illam comburat in illo loco ubi est; si non ultra Zuphim redeat & comburat in templo. Sed ad rem regredimur. Offerentes suas partes in aliquo angulo atrii mulierum coquebant. vid.2.(Chron. 35.13. cum tabernaculum adhuc in Schiloh erat, in illo etiam fiebat coctio Sacrificiorum. Hinc filiorum Eli fraudes, qui cum pectore & armo quæ Sacerdotibus cedebant, non contenti, uncinulis ex olla surripiebant, quæ extrahere poterant.
units.tr: These private sacrifices could be slaughtered in any part of the court of Israel (see Zevachin, chapter 5, section 7), but most were slaughtered on the south side. Their blood was sprinkled in the manner of the blood of burnt offerings, namely שתי מתנות שתן ארבעה [shtei matanot, shetan arba'ah], two sprinklings making four, in the form of a gamma. The breast and the right shoulder of a peace offering belonged to the priest who offered it, and are called in rabbinic language מורם [murom]. The breast had to be waved before the Lord. The rite was as follows: the offerer had to enter the court of the priests, where the priest placed upon the offerer's hands the fat with the breast and the right shoulder, likewise the kidneys and the caul of the liver, and, if the sacrifice had been slaughtered for thanksgiving, a cake of bread. Then the priest, placing his own hand under the offerer's hand, waved it with the things laid upon it, this way and that, but especially towards the east. After this waving, he sprinkled them with salt, and burned them on the altar. The priest took for himself the waved breast, the shoulder and the bread, and returned the rest to the offerer. The offerer was allowed to eat his portion of the sacrifice brought in any part of Jerusalem he pleased. This saying, נאכלין בכל העיר [nei'okhalin bekhol ha'ir], must be understood thus: the portions of sacrifices might be eaten not in any city, but in any part of the city. For this was one of the privileges of Jerusalem: the קדשים קלים [kodashim kalim], the lesser holy sacrifices, could be eaten in no other city than that one (Kelim, chapter 1, section 8). From this you will understand what the passage in Bab. Berachot, fol. 49.2, means: "If someone, after a sacrifice has been completed, returns home, and having left Jerusalem he remembers that he still has some part of the holy flesh with him, if he has already gone beyond Zuphim, which was the place from which the city and the temple could be seen, he shall burn that flesh in the place where he is; if he has not gone beyond Zuphim, he shall return and burn it in the temple." But let us return to the matter. Those offering their portions cooked them in some corner of the women's court (see 2 Chron. 35.13). When the tabernacle was still in Shiloh, the cooking of sacrifices was also done in it. Hence came the frauds of the sons of Eli, who, not content with the breast and shoulder which belonged to the priests, snatched away from the pot with little hooks whatever they could draw out.

units.la: Sacrificium pacificum personarum privatarum, quod offerebatur in gratiarum actionem eodem die quo offerebatur comedi debuit, at si oblatum fuisset ex voluntaria devotione poterat die crastino comedi. Levit.7.15.16. Et Sacerdotum & offerentium familiæ ad illorum Sacrificiorum esum admittebantur, mulieres, infantes, servi, &c. Sacerdos suam partem poterat in urbe comedere, & offerens in templo, & vice versa.
units.tr: A peace offering of a private person offered in thanksgiving had to be eaten on the same day on which it was offered; but if it had been offered from voluntary devotion, it could be eaten on the following day (Lev. 7.15, 16). Both the families of the priests and of the offerers were admitted to eat of these sacrifices: women, children, servants, and so on. A priest could eat his portion in the city, and the offerer in the temple, and vice versa.

units.la: 3. Sacrificium pacificum persona privata etiam erat Aries Nazirei, de cuius oblatione vid. Num.6.17. pectus & armus cum intestinis & aliqua portione panis etiam agitabantur, & exceptis intestinis quæ in altari comburebantur, cedebant Sacerdoti. Naziræus verò reliquam partem carnis habebat, quam ollæ immittebat in conclavi Nazirææorum, de quo Vid. si lubet.
units.tr: 3. A private person's peace offering was also the ram of the Nazirite, concerning whose offering see Num. 6.17. The breast and shoulder, together with the entrails and some portion of bread, were also waved; and, apart from the entrails, which were burned on the altar, they went to the priest. The Nazirite, however, had the rest of the flesh, which he put into a pot in the chamber of the Nazirites; on which see, if you please, ...

units.la: De Sacrificiis Eucharisticis quæ in festis offerebantur Vid. Festa. Item Pascha.
units.tr: For the thanksgiving sacrifices which were offered at the feasts, see Festa. Likewise Pascha.

units.la: De Avium oblatione.
units.tr: On the offering of birds.

units.la: §. Haētenus loquuti sumus de oblatione juvencorum, arietum, hædorum, agnorum &c. nunc etiam aliquid de avium oblatione dicendum. Cur Deus illarum oblationes instituerit Vid. Aves. Ex omnibus avium speciebus àDeo solùm turtures & columbæ fuërunt electæ: quæ vocantur Talmudicè nidi, expressum de illis tractatum habet Mischna. Ordinariè vendebantur in templo Ioh.2.14. ut & monte Oliveto sub duobus immensæ magnitudinis Cedris, vid. Talm. Hieros. Taanith sol.69.1. Columbæ præcipuè à mulieribus (non enim solis) offerebantur, quia ob impuritates, fluxus, puerperia, abortus, tam frequenter oblationes offerre debebant, ut sumptus ipsarum in immensum crevisset, si ex aliis animantibus sacrificia afferre debuissent. Audiatur in hunc finem Keritbut cap 1. Mulier quæ in dubio est, (Confer quæ supra prà apud Sacrificium de reatu de תלי אשם dixit mus, ad illa Sacrificia enim hæc avium proprie pertinent) de quinque paribus & quinque fluxibus unum solum exetur offerre Sacrificium, & de illo comedere potest. Si vero de quinque partubus & quinque fluxibus e rta est, tenetur ad unum sacrificium והשאר חובה עליה & reliqua debet. Historia est, שעמרו קנים בירושלם כנרי זהב Semel Hierosolymis columbas prostitisse, sed non nisi pro denario aureo. Iurav t Rabban Simeon Ben Gamaliel, המעון דוה Per templum hoc! Hæc noste non requiescam, donec ve neant denario argenteo; Intravit Synedrium & constituit, ut mulier quæ certa erat de quinque partubus & quinque fluxibus, unum solum afferret Sacrificium, de illo comederet, & quoad reliqua, soluta esset. Et columbæ iterum denario argenteo vendebantur: quia non erant quæ illas emerent. Hoc etiam exstat in Iuchasin sol.68.
units.tr: Up to now we have spoken of the offering of young bulls, rams, goats, lambs and so on. Now something must also be said about the offering of birds. For why God instituted their offerings, see Birds. Of all the species of birds, only turtledoves and pigeons were chosen by God. The Talmud calls them nidi, and the Mishnah has a whole tractate about them. They were ordinarily sold in the temple (John 2:14), and also on the Mount of Olives under two cedars of immense size; see Talm. Hieros. Taanith, fol. 69.1. Pigeons were offered especially by women (not only by them), because for uncleanness, discharges, childbirth and miscarriage they had to bring offerings so often that the cost would have grown enormous if they had had to bring sacrifices from other animals. On this point hear Keritbut, chapter 1: "A woman who is in doubt" (compare what we said above under the guilt offering, of which these bird offerings are properly a part) "about five births and five discharges must offer only one sacrifice, and may eat of it. But if she is certain of five births and five discharges, she is bound to one sacrifice, and the rest is owed by her as a debt." There is a story: "Once in Jerusalem the pigeons were sold for a gold denarius. Rabban Simeon ben Gamaliel swore, 'By this temple! I will not rest tonight until they are sold for a silver denarius.' He entered the Sanhedrin and decreed that a woman certain of five births and five discharges should bring only one sacrifice, of which she might eat, and that as to the rest she was released. And pigeons were again sold for a silver denarius," because there were no others who might buy them. This is also found in Iuchasin, fol. 68.

units.la: §. Oblationis avium ritum describit Zevachin cap.6. Si pro holocausto afferebantur, Sacerdos ascendens gradus altaris, & per circuitum ibat donec ad Angulum perveniebat qui inter orientem & meridiem erat, ibique ipsorum præscindebat capita, aperiebat, sanguinem ipsorum ad latus altaris effundebat, saliebat capita in loco ubi aperta, & ea in ignem proiiciebat; eximebat intestina & in cumulum cinerum projiciebat; avium ipsa corpuscula salo aspergebat, & igni immittebat. Si aves allatæ fuissent ad sacrificium pro peccato, capita abscindebat, sanguinem ad latus altare spargebat ex parte, ex parte vero effundebat ad basim altaris, ubi canales ad deglutiendum sanguinem erant; Deinde aves sibi reservabat Sacerdos, & in cibum adhibebat. Differentia itaq;e in aspersione sanguinis avium & reliquorum sacrificiorum,notantc tract. Kinnim c.1. hæc erat. Sanguis animalium in holocaustis spargebatur infrà lineam rubram altaris, in sacrificiis pro peccatis supra lineam. Sanguis avium verò si in holocaustum off rebantur, spargebatur superius, si in sacrificium pro peccato, inferius.
units.tr: The rite of offering birds is described in Zevachin, chapter 6: "If they were brought for a burnt offering, the priest went up the steps of the altar and walked around until he came to the corner which lay between east and south. There he cut off their heads, opened them, poured their blood out at the side of the altar, squeezed the heads at the place where they were opened and threw them into the fire; he removed the entrails and threw them on the heap of ashes; he sprinkled the little bodies of the birds with salt and put them into the fire. If the birds were brought for a sin offering, he cut off their heads and sprinkled the blood partly at the side of the altar, but partly poured it out at the base of the altar, where there were channels for draining the blood. Then the priest kept the birds for himself and used them as food." The difference in the sprinkling of the blood of birds and of the other sacrifices is noted in the tractate Kinnim, chapter 1, and was this: the blood of animals in burnt offerings was sprinkled below the red line of the altar, in sin offerings above the line. But the blood of birds, if they were offered as a burnt offering, was sprinkled higher up, and if as a sin offering, lower down.

units.la: De Oblatione מנחות, & נסך libamine.
units.tr: On the offering of meal (מנחות) and the drink offering (נסך).

units.la: §. Duodecim species מנחות erant, tres ex parte totius congregationis, & novem ex parte personarum privatarum. Maymon in Corbanot cap.2. Menachot 6.
units.tr: There were twelve kinds of meal offerings: three on behalf of the whole congregation and nine on behalf of private persons. Maimonides, in Corbanot, chapter 2; Menachot 6.

units.la: Menachot quæ à tota congregatione offerebantur, erant 1. Duodecim illi panes propositionis, qui coram Domino singulis Sabbathis ponebantur. Exod. 25.3. Levit. 24.5.6. & cedebant in esum Sacerdotum poltquàm remoti erant. 2. Omer primitiarum messis. Levit. 23.9. nempe manipulus ille desumptus ex hordeo, quia inter fruges frumentis omnium primò maturum est. Reliquæ autem Menachot desumebantur ex tritico, unicà solùm adhuc exceptâ Fasciculus hic agitabatur coram Domino, huc illuc, sursum deorsum, pars comedebatur, & pars offerebatur. Agitatio huc illuc fiebat (notante R. Salom. in Lev.23.) ad actionem gratiarum, quòd Deus cohibuit malignos ventos, agitatio verò sursum & deorsum, quòd segetes custodivit à malignis roribus.
units.tr: The meal offerings brought by the whole congregation were: (1) the twelve loaves of the showbread, which were set before the Lord every Sabbath (Exod. 25:30; Lev. 24:5-6), and which, after they had been removed, went to the food of the priests. (2) The omer, the first-fruits of the harvest (Lev. 23:9), namely that handful taken from barley, because barley ripens first of all the grains. The other meal offerings, however, were taken from wheat, with one exception. This sheaf was waved before the Lord, here and there, up and down; part was eaten and part was offered. The waving here and there was done (as R. Solomon notes on Lev. 23) as an act of thanksgiving, because God restrained the harmful winds; the waving up and down was because He had guarded the crops from harmful dews. (3) The two loaves of waving, offered at the feast of Pentecost (Lev. 23:17).

units.la: 3. Duo panes agitationis oblati in festo Pentecostes. Lev.23.17.
units.tr: The meal offerings brought by private persons were as follows.

units.la: Menachot quæ à personis privatis offerebantur sequentes erant.
units.tr: (1) The חביתין, pans, which were offered every day by the High Priest.

units.la: 1. חביתין Sartagines quæ quotidie à Summo Sacerdote offerebantur.
units.tr: 1. Chabitin [חביתין], frying pans, which were offered daily by the High Priest.

units.la: 2. מנחת חנוך Mincha sive oblatio Initiationis, quam manu sua afferebat quivis Sacerdos in primo suo ingressu ad officium Sacerdotale.
units.tr: 2. Mincha of initiation [מנחת חנוך], or the offering of initiation, which any priest brought with his own hands on his first entry into priestly office.

units.la: 3. מנחת חוטא Oblatio peccatoris; quando enim aliquis, qui sacrificium pro peccato afferre debebat tam pauper erat, ut illud præstare non posset, solùm ad talem Mincham offerendam tenebatur. Misna etiam loquitur de מנחת חוטא של הכהנים Mincha pro pauperculo peccante inter Sacerdotes; quod satis arguit, non omnes fuisse Croesos inter Sacerdotes.
units.tr: 3. Mincha of the sinner [מנחת חוטא], the offering of a sinner. For when someone who ought to bring a sin offering was so poor that he could not provide it, he was bound to offer only such a Mincha. The Mishnah also speaks of the Mincha of the sinning priests [מנחת חוטא של הכהנים], the Mincha for a poor sinning priest among the priests, which sufficiently shows that not all the priests were Croesuses.

units.la: 4. מנחת קנאות Oblatio propter uxorem suspectam ob adulterium (vid. Aquas amaras) Numer.5.15.
units.tr: 4. Mincha of jealousy [מנחת קנאות], the offering for a suspected wife accused of adultery (see Bitter Waters), Num. 5.15.

units.la: Illa erat ex farina hordeacea.
units.tr: That was made of barley flour.

units.la: 5. מנחת סולת Oblatio similia vel purissima farina, hæc non coćta erat. Quæ in templo offerri debuit erat מככם & מוניחה, secunda ab illis est ista quæ ex valle Ephraim venit. Menachot c.8. Aruch in מככם.
units.tr: 5. Mincha of fine flour [מנחת סולת], the offering of fine or purest flour. This was not cooked. What was to be offered in the temple was [מככם and מוניחה]; the second of these is the one that comes from the valley of Ephraim. Menachot ch. 8. Aruch under [מככם].

units.la: 6. מנחת המחבת oblatio coćta in patella. (poële.)
units.tr: 6. Mincha cooked in a pan [מנחת המחבת], an offering cooked in a pan. (Fr. poêle.)

units.la: 7. מנחת המרחשת oblatio frixa in sartagine. (Gall. dans une poële à frire.)
units.tr: 7. Mincha fried in a pan [מנחת המרחשת], an offering fried in a frying pan. (Fr. in a frying pan.)

units.la: 8. תנוך מנחת מאפת כתנור oblatio cocta in furno.
units.tr: 8. Mincha baked in an oven [תנוך מנחת מאפת כתנור], an offering cooked in an oven.

units.la: 9. רקיקין Placenta tenues & contorta.
units.tr: 9. Thin wafers [רקיקין], thin and twisted cakes.

units.la: In Talmudicis sæpè etiam mentio fit מנחת גויים oblationis Gentilu, מנחת נשים oblationis mulierum, מנחת נסכים oblationis fa-inacea fa-cta cum libamine. Sed re ipsa cum recensitis conveniunt, quamvis nomine discrepent.
units.tr: The Talmudists also often mention the Mincha of the Gentiles [מנחת גויים], the offering of the Gentiles; the Mincha of women [מנחת נשים], the offering of women; and the Mincha of libations [מנחת נסכים], a flour offering made with a libation. But in reality they agree with those listed above, although they differ in name.

units.la: §. Circa confectionem & adornationem hatum Menachot sequentia sunt observanda.
units.tr: §. Concerning the preparation and arrangement of these Menachot, the following points must be observed.

units.la: 1. Nullam Mincham minus decimâ parte Ephæ (εἰνεὸ Μάβες) tritici, habere debuisse, nec minus Logo olei, id est, non infrà tredecim uncias. Decima illa pars Ephæ vocatur עומר Exod.16.36. Maymon in Corbanoth c.13.
units.tr: 1. No Mincha was to have less than a tenth part of an ephah [ἐφά] of wheat, nor less than a log of oil, that is, not less than thirteen ounces. That tenth part of an ephah is called omer. Exod. 16.36. Maimonides, Corbanoth ch. 13.

units.la: 2. Si Mincha ex quatuor illis speciebus erat quæ coqui debebant, ordinariè ex decima parte Ephæ decem placentas conficiebant, & sic si plus quàm decima pars Ephæ offerebatur, ex unaquaque decem pinsebant placentas. Mincha sola Summi Sacerdotis distribuebatur in duodecim placentas, quæ postquàm coctæ erant frangebantur in duo frusta, ut manè duodecim frusta possent offerri, & vesperi duodecim. Maymon. ubi modò.
units.tr: 2. If the Mincha was of one of those four kinds which had to be cooked, they ordinarily made ten cakes from a tenth part of an ephah; so if more than a tenth part of an ephah was offered, they pounded ten cakes from each such portion. The Mincha of the High Priest alone was made into twelve cakes, which, once baked, were each broken into two pieces, so that twelve pieces could be offered in the morning and twelve in the evening. Maimonides, ibid.

units.la: 3. יש שעונות שמן ולבונה שמן ולא לבונה Quædam Menachot requirebant & oleum & thus quædam requirebant oleum sed non thus, quædam thus sed non oleum, quædam nec thus nec oleum. Illa quæ simul oleum & thus requirebant, erant, Mincha similæ, quæ non coquebatur: quatuor illæ Menachot quæ coquebantur; Mincha Summi Sacerdotis; Mincha initiationis Sacerdotum; Omer primitiarum; Mincha Gentilis; Mincha Mulieris. Mincha quæ coniunctum habebat כף libamen requirebat oleum sed non thus. Panes propositionis requirebant thus sed non oleum. Oblationes verò pauperis peccantis & mulieris ob adulterium suspectæ nec oleum nec thus habebant. Vid. tractat. Menachot cap.5. fect.3.
units.tr: 3. Some Menachot required both oil and frankincense, some required oil but not frankincense, some frankincense but not oil, and some neither frankincense nor oil. Those Menachot which required both oil and frankincense were the flour offering, which was not cooked; the four Menachot which were cooked; the Mincha of the High Priest; the Mincha of the initiation of priests; the omer of firstfruits; the Mincha of a Gentile; and the Mincha of a woman. The Mincha which had the handful of libation (kaf) required oil but not frankincense. The showbread required frankincense but not oil. But the offering of the poor sinner and of the woman suspected of adultery had neither oil nor frankincense. See tractate Menachot ch. 5, sect. 3.

units.la: 4. כל המנחות הנעשות בכלי שלש מתנות : שמן Omnes oblationes frumentariæ sive Menachot quæ conficiuntur in vase opus habent triplici olei affusione. Verbi gratiâ, si offerenda מנחת הסולת purissimæ farinæ oblatio, primò oleum in vas infunditur, deinde immittitur ipsamet farina, & farinæ denuò affundunt oleum, oleumque cum farina commiscent. Hoc facto farinam ita præparatam ponunt in כלי השרת vase illo Ministerii, in quo ad altare deferri debebat oblatio, iterumque affundebatur oleum, & tandem addebatur quoque thus: Similiter, si offerenda aliqua Mincha quæ in patella coqui debebat, patellæ primò immittebant oleum, deinde farinam, & supra farinam iterum oleum, postquàm autem hæc commixta & cocta erant, placentis iterum oleum & deinde thus imponebatur. הרקיקין משיחה כיצר מושחין כפין כי Quomodo verò ungunt liba contorta & tenuia? Ungunt ea in modum X. Gracorum; vel ut Tosaphta dicit instar Kappa Græcorum, ut oleum huc & illuc fuerit dispersum. Vid. Menachot cap. 6. verf.3.
units.tr: 4. All grain offerings, or Menachot, which are prepared in a vessel, require three pourings of oil. For example, if a flour offering of fine flour is to be offered, first oil is poured into the vessel, then the flour itself is put in, and oil is poured over the flour again, and the oil is mixed with the flour. Once this is done, they place the flour so prepared in the vessel of ministry, in which the offering was to be carried to the altar, and oil is poured again, and finally frankincense is added too. Similarly, if some Mincha that had to be cooked in a pan is to be offered, they first pour oil into the pan, then the flour, and oil again over the flour; and once these are mixed and cooked, oil is put on the cakes, and then frankincense. How, then, do they anoint the twisted and thin cakes? They anoint them in the shape of the Greek X; or, as the Tosefta says, in the likeness of the Greek kappa, so that the oil is spread here and there. See Menachot ch. 6, verse 3.

units.la: 5. Quædam Menachot integræ fuerunt in altari combustæ; nec Sacerdos ullam partem pro se habebat; De quibusdam verò solummodò plenam volam manus Sacerdos comburebat, reliqua pars ipsi cedebat. Prioris generis erant Mincha Sacerdotum vulgarium, & Mincha Sacerdotis Summi unëti, item Mincha quae offerebatur cum libamine. Posterioris generis verò, Mincha Similae, Menachot illae quatuor, quae coquebantur; Mincha gentilis, Mincha mulieris, Omer primitiarum; oblatio pa peris peccantis, & oblatio Sotae sive mulieris suspectae. Ex oblatione duorum panum, & panum propositionis nihil cedebat altari, sed omnia pertinebant ad Sacerdotes. Vid. Menachot c. 6 v. 1. 2.
units.tr: 5. Some menachot were burned whole on the altar, and the priest kept no portion for himself. From others the priest burned only a full handful, and the rest fell to him. The first kind were the meal offering of the common priests, and the meal offering of the anointed high priest, likewise the meal offering that was offered with a drink offering. The second kind were the meal offering of fine flour, the four menachot that were baked, the gentile's meal offering, the woman's meal offering, the omer of firstfruits, the offering of a sinner who was poor, and the offering of the suspected wife, the sotah. Nothing of the offering of the two loaves or of the showbread went to the altar; all of it belonged to the priests. See Menachot ch. 6, vv. 1, 2.

units.la: §. Modus offerendi has oblationes Menachot hic erat. Postquàm Mincha posita erat in vase ministerii, sanctificabatur in eo, oleum affundebatur, imponebaturque thus. Deinde illud deferebatur ad cornu altaris quod inter Orientem & meridiem erat, & stabat Sacerdos à parte cornu meridionali. Posito autem thure à Sacerdote in aliqua parte vasculi collectimi, sumebat ex illa parte ubi non sparsum erat, quantum volà manus capere poterat, & illud ponebat in medio alius vasculi ministerii, deinde etiam colligebat thus & illud sepositae Massae imponebat, tandem illam ad superficiem altaris deferebat, sale condiebat, & igni immittebat; residuum autem comedebatur à Sacerdotibus. Vid. Tosaphta Menachot c. 1.
units.tr: §. This was the manner of offering these menachot. After the meal offering had been placed in the vessel of ministry, it was sanctified in it, oil was poured over it, and frankincense was laid on it. Then it was carried to the horn of the altar that lay between east and south, and the priest stood on the south side of the horn. The priest then put the frankincense in some part of the collecting dish, and took from that part where it had not been scattered as much as his hand could hold, and put this in the middle of another vessel of ministry. Then he also gathered up the frankincense and laid it on the separated portion, and at last carried this up to the top of the altar, salted it, and cast it into the fire. The remainder was eaten by the priests. See Tosefta Menachot ch. 1.

units.la: §. Quod םנ libamen attinet, sacrificium quotidianum semper illud coniunctum habebat. Vid. Cultus &c, illud etiam habebant aliae sacrificia. Num. 15. Illud autem nihil aliud erat quàm certa vini quantitas, quae variabatur pro ratione sacrificiorum, ut ibi videri potest. Vinum Jibaminis, docente R. Salomoh in Num.15. nunquam miscebatur, nec aliquid de eo arfundebatur igni, ut fiebat in Mincha, sed effundebatur ad basin altaris, & cum eius effusione Musica incipiebat.
units.tr: §. As for the libation [נסך], the daily sacrifice always had it joined to it. See Cultus, etc.; the other sacrifices also had it. Num. 15. It was nothing other than a fixed quantity of wine, which varied according to the kind of sacrifice, as can be seen there. According to R. Solomon on Num. 15, the wine of the libation was never mixed, and none of it was poured on the fire as was done with the meal offering, but it was poured out at the base of the altar, and with its pouring out the music began.

units.la: §. Mane & vesperi cum sacrificio iugi osserebatur Mincha interim tamen solum tempus sacrificii vespertini vocatur חנכה Mincha. Vid. 1. Reg. 18.29. certa ratio huius appellationis non patet. Forsan ett idcirco, quia personarum privatarum oblationes, ut plurimum tempore vespertino fiebant, vel quia sufsitus adolebatur vesperi una cum Mincha, quod aliter erat mane.
units.tr: §. Morning and evening the meal offering was offered with the continual sacrifice. Yet the time of the evening sacrifice alone is called Mincha [חנכה]. See 1 Kings 18:29. The reason for this name is not clear. Perhaps it is so called because the offerings of private persons were mostly made in the evening, or because the incense was burned in the evening along with the meal offering, which was otherwise done in the morning.

units.la: De Primitiis, Pasc hate, & Decimis Vid. suo loco.
units.tr: On firstfruits, Passover, and tithes, see in their proper places.

units.la: De publicis legatis ad offerenda Sacrificia Vid. Stationarii Viri.
units.tr: On the public envoys sent to offer sacrifices, see Stationarii Viri.

units.la: Addemus quaedam generalia de Sacrificiis. Quaeritur quomodo processum, fi aliquis Sacrificia, quae debebat, ex obstinatione afferre noluerit? ¶. Qui Religiosi erant in hoc peccatum non incidebant, poena enim excidii ipsos satis urgebat ad solutionem sacrificiorum, quoad reliquos vero respondet R. Salomoh in Levit.1.4. Traditio est, quod ipsum nolentem volentem. At Lex (loco cit.) dicit, quod sponte debeat afferre sacrificium? Resp. cogant ipsum tamdiu, donec dicat, ego voluntarie afferam.
units.tr: We shall add some general points about sacrifices. It is asked how one proceeds if someone, out of obstinacy, refuses to bring the sacrifice he owes? ¶. Pious people did not fall into this sin, for the penalty of being cut off pressed them hard enough to pay their sacrifices. As for the rest, R. Solomon answers on Lev. 1:4: There is a tradition that they compel the unwilling man until he is willing. But the Law (in the place cited) says that he must bring the sacrifice willingly? The answer: they compel him for so long until he says, "I will bring it willingly."

units.la: Quaer. an qui peccaverat statim obligatus fuerit ad immediatam Sacrificii oblationem; an debuerit degens in remotiore aliqua provincia, relinquere omnia sua negotia & confestim Hierosolymam advolare ad expiandum suum reatum? Ex loco Deut.12.5.6. eliciunt, quòd suffecerit si oblationem suam attulerit primo insequente festo magno, qualia fuerunt Pascha, Pentecoste, Scenopegia. Maymon in praefat. ad lad Chafaka. Hoc unum ex 248. praeceptis affirmantis est להכיא כל הקרבנות שיש על האדם כחוב או בנדר ברגל ראשון שפגע בו : quòd unusquisque debeat afferre illa sacrificia ad quae vel voto vel reatu obligatur, in festo proximo sequente. Bab.Sanhed.sol.11.1. Puerperae feminiflux, & feminiflui, columbas suas reservarunt usque dum ascenderent ad festum. Item Hierof. Rosch Haschana f.56.2. Oblationes quae sacrata sunt anse festum, offerantur in festo, nam dicitur est, hae faciet in solemnitatibus vestris. Vid. etiam Baal Hatturim in Deut.12.
units.tr: It is asked whether one who had sinned was at once bound to offer the sacrifice immediately, or whether, living in some distant province, he had to leave all his business and fly at once to Jerusalem to atone for his guilt. From the place in Deut. 12:5, 6 they infer that it was enough if he brought his offering at the first following great feast, such as Passover, Pentecost, or Tabernacles. Maimonides, in the preface to the Book of Commandments, says that this is one of the 248 affirmative precepts: [להכיא כל הקרבנות שיש על האדם כחוב או בנדר ברגל ראשון שפגע בו], that everyone must bring those sacrifices for which he is bound either by debt or by vow, at the first festival that comes upon him. Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 11.1: A woman after childbirth, and a woman with a flux, and a man with a flux, kept their doves until they went up to the feast. Likewise Jerusalem Talmud, Rosh Hashanah fol. 56.2: Offerings that were vowed before the feast are to be offered at the feast, for it is said, "you shall do this at your solemn feasts." See also Baal Haturim on Deut. 12.

units.la: Quaer. Quomodo Christus Matth.5.v.24. dicere & praecipere poterit, ut munus ιμᾶες ... relinqueretur, & offerens ad reconciliandum fratrem se conferret? R. 1. Fatendum, hoc in muneribus ad Altare oblatis in tali causa omnino insolitum fuisse libamen post oblatum Sacrificium, quia Sacrificium offerre licuit hodie v.g. ac differre libamen ab hinc viginti diebus. Tosaphta ad Corbanot cap.5. Poterat etiam Sacrificium ipsum differri, imò planè rejici poltquàm iam ad altare allatum vel adductum erat, si scilicet vel labes in victima, vel immunditia in offerente reperta. Sed de hoc casu silent paginae Talmudicae. 2. Intentio Christi est docere, quòd Deus frustrà colatur absque vera charitate in fratrem, eadem mens est Gemaristis in Bab. Ioma sol.87.1.Si itaque moram in allato sacrificio fecerunt ob quaedam minutiora, qualia aut offerentis immunditia, aut victimae aliquod vitium erat, cur non similem curiositatem in placando fratre, absque cuius reconciliatione, oblatio Deo non poterat grata esse, adhibêrent, quod tacitè ipsis exprobravit Christus. Innuit itaque, satius esse relinquere sacrificium extra morem apud altare, & ad fratrem reconciliandum currere, quàm strictâ observatione Paternorum rituum, absque reconciliatione fratris, ad sacrificandum accedere. Praesupponit insuper Christus illud quod de reiectione sacrificiorum in proximum festum supra diximus. Si enim personarum privatarum sacrificia non fuissent in festo oblata, quomodo Christus dixisset, relinquat Sacrificium coram altari & abeat ad reconciliandum sibi fratrem: poterat ille frater longissimè abesse; at in festo non longè ab altari remotus erat quivis frater in quem quis peccaverat. Obligabatur enim quivis Masculus ad festum ascendere. Vid. Comparitio.
units.tr: It is asked how Christ, Matt. 5:24, could say and command that the gift [δῶρον] be left, and that the one offering should go first to reconcile himself to his brother. Answer 1: It must be admitted that in gifts offered at the altar, in such a case, it was altogether unusual for the libation to be made after the sacrifice had been offered, since it was permitted to offer the sacrifice today, for example, and to defer the libation for twenty days. Tosefta on Qorbanot ch. 5. The sacrifice itself could also be postponed, indeed clearly rejected, after it had already been brought or led to the altar, if a blemish were found in the victim or an uncleanness in the offerer. But the Talmudic pages are silent about this case. 2. Christ's intention is to teach that God is worshipped in vain without true love for one's brother. The Gemarists in Bab. Yoma fol. 87.1 have the same mind. If, then, they delayed over a sacrifice already brought because of some smaller matters, such as the offerer's uncleanness or some defect in the victim, why did they not use a similar care in appeasing a brother, without whose reconciliation the offering could not be pleasing to God? Christ tacitly reproached them for this. He therefore hints that it is better to leave the sacrifice before the altar, contrary to custom, and run to reconcile one's brother, than to approach to sacrifice with strict observance of the fathers' rites, without reconciliation with the brother. Christ also presupposes what we said above about the deferral of sacrifices to the next feast. For if the sacrifices of private persons had not been offered at the feast, how could Christ have said, "leave the sacrifice before the altar and go to reconcile yourself to your brother"? That brother could have been very far away; but at the feast any brother against whom one had sinned was not far from the altar, for every male was obliged to go up to the feast. See Comparitio.

units.la: SADDUCAEI. Ipsorum haeresis de nullo futuro seculo, iam Esrae tempore fuit, quod patet, quia ab illo & consessu eius decretum factum est, ut ad Coronidem omnium orationum diceretur מן העולם עד עולם. Ad innuendum duplicem esse mundum, & ad extirpandam è corde opinionem negantium resurrectionem mortuorum. Vid. Beracot sol.54. & Gloss.
units.tr: THE SADDUCEES. Their heresy about no future age existed already in the time of Ezra, as is clear, because from him and his council a decree was made that the conclusion of all prayers should be said: [מן העולם עד עולם], "from the world to the world," to indicate that there are two worlds, and to root out of the heart the opinion of those who deny the resurrection of the dead. See Berakhot fol. 54 and the Gloss.

units.la: Efræ tempore, hunc errorem foventes simpliciter מינים Hareticos vocarunt, ut ex loc. modò cit.videtur, sed postquàm Zadok & Baithos Antigoni Sochæi (qui post mortem Simeonis Iusti Synedrii præses fuit;) discipuli, hoc dogma pro αἱρέσει Sectæ audaciter usurpassent, vocabantur Sadducæi. De causa ipsorum defectionis vid. Pirkę Avoth cap.1. R.Nathan cap.5.
