units.tr: In Ezra's time those who fostered this error were simply called [מינים] heretics, as appears from the place just cited. But after Zadok and Boethus, disciples of Antigonus of Sokho (who was president of the Sanhedrin after the death of Simon the Just), boldly took up this doctrine as a αἱρέσει [haeresis], a sect, they were called Sadducees. On the cause of their secession see Pirqe Avot ch. 1 and R. Nathan ch. 5.

units.la: Semel Synedrium ex meris Sadducæis conflatum erat. Vid.Synedrium.
units.tr: Once the Sanhedrin was made up entirely of Sadducees. See Synedrium.

units.la: In rubrica & ratione faciendi cultum in die expiationis hoc semel mutaverant, quòd licèt thymiama secundùm Lev.16.12.13 intra velum adoleri deberet, illi ἀδιάφορον iudicaverint, vel intrà vel extrà adoleri, imò adhibuerint suffitum extrà. Hinc illæ adiurationes Legatorum Synedrii ad Pontificem maximum in Ioma c.1. Vid. Expiationis diem.
units.tr: In the rubric and manner of performing worship on the Day of Atonement they changed this one thing: although, according to Lev. 16:12, 13, the incense ought to be burned within the veil, they judged it ἀδιάφορον [adiaphoron], a matter of indifference, whether it was burned within or without, and indeed they used the censer outside. Hence those adjurations of the envoys of the Sanhedrin to the high priest in Yoma ch. 1. See Expiationis diem.

units.la: SADTA Vid. Ben Sadta. in B.
units.tr: SADTA. See Ben Sadta, under B.

units.la: SALAMANDRA est reptile lacerti figurâ, ex igne generatum. Ionath.Levit.11.30. Cholin sol.127.1. Schemot Rabba sect.15. Tanchuma sol.16.2. Chagiga sol.27. Sanhed.sol.63.2. Ezechias à matre lua sanguine Salamandræ inunctus fuit, ita ut cum Achaz eum traduceret per ignem, comburi non potuerit. Ialkut Psalm.1. Reg.21.6. Vid. Cl. Buxt. in Rad. Fuller Miscell. vi.9. Bochard. de animal. 1.4.4.
units.tr: THE SALAMANDER is a reptile in the shape of a lizard, generated from fire. Jonathan on Lev. 11:30; Chullin fol. 127.1; Shemot Rabbah sect. 15; Tanchuma fol. 16.2; Chagigah fol. 27; Sanhedrin fol. 63.2. Hezekiah was anointed by his mother with the blood of a salamander, so that when Ahaz made him pass through fire he could not be burned. Yalqut on Ps. 1; 1 Kings 21:6. See the learned Buxtorf in Radices; Fuller, Miscellanies vi. 9; Bochart, De animalibus 1.4.4.

units.la: SAL adhibebatur in Sacrificiis Vid. Sacrificia. Duæ celebres Salinæ fuerunt in ludæa, unaSodomæ & altera Iftaroki. Hinc tam frequens mentio illorum locorum talis, מלח סרומית Salis Sodæ. Sodomitici, quod ad suffitu m conficiendum requirebatur, & מלח אסתרונית Salis Iflarokini. Vid. Bava Batra sol.20. 2.
units.tr: SALT was used in sacrifices. See Sacrificia. There were two famous salt-pits in Judea, one at Sodom and the other at Istarok. Hence the frequent mention of these places in such phrases as [מלח סרומית], salt of Sodom, Sodomitic salt, which was required for making the incense, and [מלח אסתרונית], salt of Istarok. See Bava Batra fol. 20.2.

units.la: Samaritani in Iudæos odio plusquàm Vatiniano flagrabant, hinc videtur ipsos expressè in dialecto Iua,tam varia deflexione & immutatione uiros esse, ne plane eandem cum Iudæis linguam habere existimarentur.
units.tr: The Samaritans hated the Jews more than Vatinius did, and so it seems they deliberately differed from them in dialect, altering and inflecting the language in so many ways that they would not be thought to speak the same tongue as the Jews.

units.la: Legem Mosaicam quidem per Dosithæi ministerium amplexi sunt, sed cum ingenti in vocabulorum scriptione,mutatione. Vide textum Samaritanum ad Deut.xi.30. Hinc exprobratio R. Elieseris in Hieros. Sotah sol.21 3. Bab.Sotah sol.33.2. Dixi ego (inquit R. Eliefer) Scribæ Samaritanorum, Vos falsificatis legem vestram, absque vllo inde vobis advenientte commodo. Nam in lege vestra scripsistis אצל אלוני מורה שכם Iuxta quercetam Moreh, quae est Sichem (Sichem enim superadditum est.)
units.tr: The Samaritans did indeed embrace the Mosaic Law through the ministry of Dositheus, but with a great deal of alteration in the writing of words. See the Samaritan text at Deut. 11.30. Hence the reproach of R. Eliezer in Hieros. Sotah fol. 21.3 and Bab. Sotah fol. 33.2: "I said," says R. Eliezer, "to the scribes of the Samaritans: You falsify your law, and gain nothing from it. For in your law you have written [אצל אלוני מורה שכם] 'Beside the oak of Moreh, which is Shechem' (for 'Shechem' has been added as a gloss)."

units.la: Ab Idololatris non multùm differebant Samaritani, cùm nescirent quid adorarent. Iohan. 4.22. De templo ipsorum Vid. Gerizim. De idolis & simulachris abscondit is sub hoc monte Vid. Epiphanium 1. contrà Hæret. 9. de illis etiam sermo est Hieros. Avoda Zarah, sol.44.4. ubi in idololatriæ ipsorum convitium sic inquiunt. R.Ismael Ben R.Iosi adiit Neapolin (i.e.Sichem.) Accesserunt ad eum Samarita: quibus sic ille, Video ego; quod vos non adoratis hunc montem, sed Idola quae sub eo: nam scribitur, Abscondit Iacobus Deos alienos sub luco qui iuxta Sichem.
units.tr: The Samaritans did not differ much from idolaters, since they did not know what they worshipped. John 4:22. On their temple see Gerizim. On the idols and images they hid under this mountain, see Epiphanius, Against Heresies 1.9. The passage is also discussed in Hieros. Avoda Zarah, 44.4, where, in mocking their idolatry, they say: R. Ismael ben R. Jose went to Neapolis (that is, Shechem). Samaritans came to him, and he said to them: "I see that you do not worship this mountain but the idols beneath it; for it is written, 'Jacob hid the strange gods under the oak which is near Shechem.'"

units.la: Hinc Iudæi Samaritanos, quamvis illi non plane Ethnici fuerint, saltem non maioris æstimarunt ac si integri & absoluti Ethnici essent. Hieros.Schekalim sol.46.2. Negat R.Simeon Samaritanum Ethnicum esse, affirmat id Rabbi Iehuda cum aliis. Schekalim cap. 1. v.5. Si (uthai afferrent bemisiclos aut columbas puerperarum, ab illis eas non reciperent. אין עונין אמן אחר כותי הסבור Posi Samaritanum orantem non dicunt Amen. Adæg. desumptum ex Beraco'h cap.8. v.8. ubi tamen hoc non absolutè sed solùm respectu benedictionis Israelitæ intelligitur, ad illam Amen dicendum absque precum consideratione, sed non ita respectu Samaritani.) Hieros. Pesachim sol 27.2. Si Cuthai Azyma susa fauciunt cum Israelitis, credendi sunt de exterminatione fermenti alias non. Cum Cuthei diffusi erant, in villis, sicut bene praecepta observabant, nunc vero suspecti sunt. Hieros. Avoda Zarah ubi suprà. Samaritani Cæsarienses interrogarunt Rabh Abhu, Patres vestri ανγκων patribus nostris, vos igitur, quare non etiam cum nobis conversamini ? Resp. Patres vestri non corruperunt opera tua (religiosius munditiem observabant) vos autem corrupistis. Vid. etiam Tanchuma sect. ישו & Vaiikra Rabba 291.1.
units.tr: Hence the Jews esteemed the Samaritans no more highly than if they were complete and absolute Gentiles, though they were not altogether Gentiles. Hieros. Shekalim 46.2: R. Simeon denies that a Samaritan is a Gentile; R. Judah, with others, affirms it. Shekalim ch. 1, v. 5: If Cuthites brought shekels or the doves of women in childbirth, they would not accept them from them. One does not say Amen after a Samaritan who blesses [Posi Samaritanum orantem non dicunt Amen]. This is taken from Berakhot ch. 8, v. 8, where, however, it is understood not absolutely but only with regard to an Israelite's blessing: one should say Amen to that without considering the prayers, but not so with regard to a Samaritan. Hieros. Pesachim 27.2: If Cuthites keep unleavened bread along with Israelites, they are to be trusted about the removal of leaven, otherwise not. When the Cuthites were scattered in villages, they observed the precepts well; but now they are suspect. Hieros. Avoda Zarah, as above. The Caesarean Samaritans asked Rabbi Abhu: "Your fathers [ἀνγκων] to our fathers, why then do you not also associate with us?" He answered: "Your fathers did not corrupt your works (they observed cleanliness more religiously), but you have corrupted them." See also Tanchuma, section ישו, and Vayikra Rabba 29.1.

units.la: Ita Regio Samaritana pro conditione gentis, nec merè Ethnica erat, nec verè Israelitica. Non æstimabatur Israelitica; quia hemisiclos ab ipsis non recipiebant, nec utebantur ipsorum cibis, si acetum aut vinum ipsorum commixta fuissent. (Avod.Zarah. ubi sup.) nec comedel ant cum illis, secundùm illud לא יאכל אדם משרא פת כותי Ne comedat quispiam busellam Samaritani (cui est benedicendum.) Non poterat Samarita Israeliticus proselytus fieri, secundum excommunicationem, quam in ipsos vibrarunt viri הגדולה כנסת Confessus magni, tempore Esra. Tanchum sol.17. 4. Quamvis Akiba in Hieros. Schekal. sol.64.2. ipsos in numerum verorum Proselytorum in posterioribus temporibus retulerit. At nec merè Ethnica erat, nam ארץ כותיים שהורה ובקוותיה והרוותיה ושבילית שהוריך Terra Samaritica reputata est munda, collectiones aquarum eius munda, atque habitationes munda, & semita munda. Quod curiositas Magistrorum de terra merè Ethnica nunquam dixerit. Vid. Avod Zarah. ubi sup.
units.tr: Thus the Samaritan region, by the standing of its people, was neither purely Gentile nor truly Israelite. It was not regarded as Israelite, because they did not accept shekels from them, nor did they use their food if vinegar or wine of theirs had been mixed in; nor would one eat with them, according to the saying: "A man should not eat a loaf of a Samaritan" (who is to be blessed). A Samaritan could not become an Israelite proselyte, because of the excommunication which the men of the Great Assembly, the Great Synagogue, hurled against them in the time of Ezra (Tanchuma, 17.4), although Akiba, in Hieros. Shekalim 64.2, counted them among true proselytes in later times. Yet it was not purely Gentile either, for the land of the Samaritans is pronounced clean: "The land of the Samaritans is clean, its valleys and its caves are clean, its dwellings are clean, and its paths are clean" [ארץ כותיים שהורה ובקוותיה והרוותיה ושבילית שהוריך]. This shows that the scrupulosity of the Masters never called the land purely Gentile. See Avoda Zarah, as above.

units.la: Quando Evangelista Ioh. 6. 9. dicit ἐν ᾧ οὐ χρῶνται Ἰουδαῖοι Σαμαρείταις, non vult, ipsos nullum commercium cum ipsis habere, ludaei enim mercaturam non abnuerunt cum quibusvis gentibus; nec intelligit, Iudaeos non uti Samaritanis nam in Gloss. in Kiddushin sol.76.1. & Hieros. Ievamnot sol.9.1. dicitur Samaritam farinam suam depsere posse in domo Israelita, & Israelitam Cuthaeum circuncidere posse, quae praesupponunt quod cum Cuthaeis aliquis usus fuerit. Sed probabiliter hoc intelligit Iohannes, quod Iudaei non utantur Samaritanis, ita ut iis devinciantur ob aliquod beneficium, quod noluerint ipsis obligari, quod ab illis nihil accipiant gratis, aut petant mutuo, sicuti illis, respectu aliarum gentium secundum Avoda Zarah c.1. v.1. licitum fuit.
units.tr: When the evangelist John (4:9) says that the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans [ἐν ᾧ οὐ χρῶνται Ἰουδαῖοι Σαμαρείταις], he does not mean that they had no commerce with them at all, for the Jews did not refuse trade with any nation. Nor does he mean that Jews did not use Samaritans, for the Gloss on Kiddushin 76.1 and Hieros. Yevamot 9.1 say that a Samaritan woman may knead her dough in an Israelite's house, and an Israelite may circumcise a Cuthite; these presuppose that some dealings took place with the Cuthites. John probably means rather that the Jews did not make use of the Samaritans so as to be bound to them by some favour; that they did not wish to be obligated to them, did not receive anything gratis from them, nor borrow from them, as they were permitted to do with respect to other nations, according to Avoda Zarah 1.1.

units.la: De literis quas Samaritani non habent Vid. Itiner. Beniamini p.66. An Characteribus Samaritanis exaratum fuerit Vetus Testamentum
units.tr: On the letters which the Samaritans do not have, see Itinerarium Beniamini, p. 66. Whether the Old Testament was written in Samaritan characters.

units.la: V.Cl. Buxtorf & Leusd. de literis Hebraeorum, S- ANCTUM. De Sancto Sanctorum Vid. Templum.
units.tr: Cf. Buxtorf and Leusden on the letters of the Hebrews. SANCTUM. On the Holy of Holies, see Temple.

units.la: In Sanctitate locorum, numerant undecim gradus, in Kelim cap. 1. Maymon in Beth Habechira cap. 1.
units.tr: They count eleven degrees of holiness of places, in Kelim ch. 1, and Maimonides in Beth ha-Behirah ch. 1.

units.la: 1. ארץ ישראל מקדשת מכל הארצות Terra Israelitica sanctior est omnibus terris aliis. De eius privilegiis Vid. Israelitica terra.
units.tr: 1. The Land of Israel is holier than all other lands [ארץ ישראל מקדשת מכל הארצות]. On its privileges, see Land of Israel.

units.la: 2. עיירות החוקפות חומה מקודשות מסנה Urbes muris cinctae sanctiores erant quam reliquae partes terrae. Nam α. in illis Leprosi non tolerabantur, sed extra muros dimittebantur, quae dimissio vocatur שלוח Siloah. Maymon in Biath Mikdasch cap. 3. (hinc forsan a tali loco ad quem miseri illi homines amandabantur, nomen fonti Siloa.) β. Cadaver demortui extra muros elatum iterum in civitatem reportari poterat, מסבבין בתוכה יד מה שירצו יצא אין כמוזירין אותו Poterant mortuum per urbem circumducere, quantum lubuerit, at semel elatum extra muros reducere non potuerunt. Vid. Kelim. c. 1. γ. intra vallum nulla demortuis permittebatur sepultura; ita intra Hierosolymam exceptis sepulchris Regum ex familia Davidis & Prophetiae Huldae, nulla erant sepulchra. Vid. R. Nathan in Avoth cap 34.
units.tr: 2. Cities walled in from the time of Joshua were holier than the rest of the land [עיירות החוקפות חומה מקודשות מסנה]. For (α) lepers were not tolerated in them but were sent outside the walls, and this sending out was called Siloah [שלוח]. Maimonides in Biath Mikdasch ch. 3. (Perhaps for this reason the spring Siloam took its name from the place to which those wretched men were sent away.) (β) A corpse carried out beyond the walls could be brought back into the city. They could lead a dead body around the city as far as they wished, but once carried out beyond the walls they could not bring it back in [מסבבין בתוכה יד מה שירצו יצא אין כמוזירין אותו]. See Kelim ch. 1. (γ) Within the wall no burial was permitted to the dead; so within Jerusalem there were no tombs, except the tombs of the kings of David's line and of the prophetess Huldah. See R. Nathan in Avoth ch. 34.

units.la: 3. לפנים מן התוכה כקודש מתם Intra (Hierosolymae) muros locus sanctior erat, quam in omnibus reliquis urbibus. Poterant enim Hierosolymae comedere sancta leviora (Vid. Sacrificia.) Item decimas secundas, quas in nulla alia civitate comedere poterant. Ita etiam quandiu Hierosolyma stetit, in nullo alio loco quam in illa Pascha comedere ipsis licuit. Vid. Com. Maym. in Kelim c.1.
units.tr: 3. Within the walls of Jerusalem the place was holier than in all other cities [לפנים מן התוכה כקודש מתם]. For in Jerusalem they could eat the lesser holy things (see Sacrifices); likewise the second tithes, which they could eat in no other city. Also, as long as Jerusalem stood, they were allowed to eat the Passover in no other place than there. See Commentary of Maimonides on Kelim ch. 1.

units.la: 4 מנו הר הבית מקודש מכון Mons templi (atrium gentium, quamvis aliquando etiam latius sumatur) erat sanctior reliquis Vrbis Hierosolymitanae partibus. Seminibus enim & Seminiflux, puerp ræ & menstruatæ poterant per Hierosolymam ire, in illa degere; At in montem templi ipsis venire non licuit, quia omnia illa immunda astimabantur, quibus vel insistebant, vel insidebant, Maymon ubi supra. Imo citius permisisset mortuum in montem templi inferri, quàm ut aliquis tali immunditiâ commaculatus ingrederetur. Sic dicunt Mosen Iosephi ossa secum cum ipso tentorio deportasse absque crimine, quia illud ad vindicationem honoris illius viri magni cinerum fiebat.
units.tr: 4. The Mount of the Temple [מנו הר הבית מקודש מכון] (the court of the Gentiles, although sometimes taken more broadly) was holier than the other parts of the city of Jerusalem. For those with seminal emission, women with a discharge, women after childbirth and menstruating women could go through Jerusalem and dwell there, but they were not allowed to come onto the Mount of the Temple, "because all those things are considered unclean on which they stood or sat" (Maimonides, loc. cit.). Indeed, they would sooner have permitted a corpse to be carried onto the Mount of the Temple than let anyone defiled by such uncleanness enter it. Thus they say that Moses carried the bones of Joseph with him, together with the tent itself, without sin, because this was done to vindicate the honour of that great man.

units.la: 5 מנו החיל מקודש מכון Antemurale(vid. Atrium) erat sanctius monte templi. In illud enim qui ob mortuum immundus erat ingredi non potuit; uti nec Alienigena qui non esset factus Proselytus, hinc ille tumultus contra Paulum Act.21. crediderunt enim Paulum, Trophimum quem cum ipso in urbe viderant intra חיל duxisse, cùm in atrio mulierum cum quatuor aliis, oblationem suam pro Nazireatu exsolveret.
units.tr: 5. The Chel [מנו החיל מקודש מכון], or antemurale (see Court), was holier than the Mount of the Temple. For one who was unclean because of a corpse could not enter it, nor could a foreigner who had not become a proselyte. Hence that uproar against Paul in Acts 21: for they believed that Paul had brought Trophimus, whom they had seen with him in the city, into the Chel, when he was paying his offering for the Nazirite vow in the women's court with four others.

units.la: 6. מנו עזרת נשים מקודש מכון Atrium mulieris sanctius erat antemurali; quia nullus טבול יום in illud ingredi potuit: i. e. quia nemo in illud se conferre potuit, si tali immunditiâ immundus factus fuisset, quæ opus habebat lotione adhuc illo die quo illam contraxerat; quamvis enim talis se lavisset non tamen ipsi fuit integrum in atrium mulierum ingredi, quandiu luceret sol.
units.tr: 6. The women's court [מנו עזרת נשים מקודש מכון] was holier than the antemurale, because no one who was tebul yom could enter it, that is, no one who, having become unclean by such uncleanness as required washing even on the day on which he had contracted it, could betake himself into it. For although such a person had washed, it was still not lawful for him to enter the women's court as long as the sun shone.

units.la: 7. עזרת ישראל מקודשת מסנה Atrium Israelis erat sanctius atrio Mulierum. In illud non licuit introire טהורים מטומאתם כפורי i.e. illis qui re ipsa quidem ablutionibus & aliis purificationibus se mundaverant, sed nondum attulerant sacrificia debita pro reatu: aut qui ab immunditie sua liberati, nondum tamen in genere consuetas ceremonias transfegerant, quales Maym. in Mekhuššare Cappera c.1. dicit esse leprosos, qui à Sacerdote aliquo aut alia ratione purgabantur, mulieres menstruatas & puerperas. Mulieres in hoc atrium venire non poterant. Ioseph. de bello 5. c.14. Excipe, nisi sacrificium attulerint. Tosaphta in Erachin cap.2.
units.tr: 7. The court of Israel [עזרת ישראל מקודשת מסנה] was holier than the women's court. Into it were not allowed to enter those who were clean from their uncleanness but had not yet brought the sacrifices due for guilt [טהורים מטומאתם כפורי]: that is, those who indeed had cleansed themselves by ablutions and other purifications, but had not yet brought the due sacrifices for guilt; or those who, freed from their uncleanness, had not yet completed the customary ceremonies in full. Maimonides in Mekhuššare Cappera ch. 1 says these are lepers who were cleansed by a priest or in some other way, and women who are menstruating or who have just given birth. Women could not come into this court. Josephus, Jewish War 5, ch. 14. Excepted are those who have brought a sacrifice. Tosefta in Erachin ch. 2.

units.la: 8. עזרת כהנים מקודשת מסנה Atrium Sacerdotum sanctius erat atrio Israelis, quia in illud Israelita non poterat ingredi nisi in his tribus occasionibus; aut ad imponendum manus animali sacrificando, aut ad illud excoriandum postquàm mactatum erat, aut ad agitanda frusta coram Domino sacrificii dissecti.
units.tr: 8. The court of the priests [עזרת כהנים מקודשת מסנה] was holier than the court of Israel, because an Israelite could enter it only on these three occasions: either to lay hands on the animal when sacrificing it, or to flay it after it had been slaughtered, or to wave the pieces of the dissected sacrifice before the Lord.

units.la: 9. בין האולם ולמזבח מקודש מסנה Spatium inter altare & Pronaon erat sanctius reliqua parte atrii Sacerdotum. Eò enim nullus venire poterat Sacerdos qui aliquo laboraret vitio, aut caput non pileo vel velo tectum haberet, id quod nec in aliis partibus templi Sacerdotibus licitum fuit, sed praecipuè cautio adhibenda in illo loco.
units.tr: 9. The space between the altar and the porch [בין האולם ולמזבח מקודש מסנה] was holier than the rest of the court of the priests. For no priest who was suffering from any blemish could come there, nor one whose head was not covered with a cap or veil; a thing not permitted to the priests even in other parts of the temple, but especially to be guarded against in that place.

units.la: 10. ההיכל מקודש מסנו Sanctum sanctius erat illo loco. Nemo enim illuc accedere potuit nisi lotis manibus & pedibus; at per atria illis ambulare absque hac rigida observatione licuit,modo non aliquid quod ad cultum pertinet, attingerent.
units.tr: 10. The holy place [ההיכל מקודש מסנו] was holier than that place. For no one could approach it unless his hands and feet had been washed; but they were allowed to walk through the courts without this strict observance, provided they did not touch anything pertaining to the worship.

units.la: II. קדש הקדשים מקודש מרם Sanctum Sanctorum hac omnia Sanctitate superat. Ratio, שאין נכנס לשם אלא כהן גדול ביום הכפורים כשעת העבודה Quia illud nemo ingrediebatur, nisi Summus Sacerdos in die expiationis, eâ horâ quâ cultus templi peragebatur.
units.tr: 11. The Holy of Holies [קדש הקדשים מקודש מרם] surpasses all this holiness. The reason is: "No one entered there except the High Priest on the Day of Atonement, at the hour when the temple service was performed" [שאין נכנס לשם אלא כהן גדול ביום הכפורים כשעת העבודה].

units.la: Si quis petulanter se in templum in sua immunditia intruserit, si nemo adfuerit, incurrit poenam כרת excidii. Vid. כרת si aliquis affuerit & testis sit illius petulantiæ, percutitur מלקות & מכות מרדות (Vid. flagellatio.) si ignorantia illud fecerit, afferre debet sacrificium pro peccato. Vid. Maymon in Biat Mikdasch cap.4.
units.tr: If anyone presumptuously intruded into the temple in his uncleanness, and no one was present, he incurred the penalty of excision [כרת]. See כרת. If someone was present and was a witness of that presumption, he was beaten with stripes [מלקות] and with rebellious blows [מכות מרדות] (see flagellation). If he did it in ignorance, he had to bring a sacrifice for sin. See Maimonides in Biat Mikdasch ch. 4.

units.la: §. Quem Rabbini intelligant per Sanctum fatuum Vid. Cl. Buxtorf. Lex.Talm. pag.799. Quomodo Iudæi Sanctis probrosa dent nomina Vid. apud eundem pag.1088. De Sanctorum invocatione quædam habemus apud Lipman in Nizachon sol.16.
units.tr: §. What the rabbis understand by a holy fool, see the learned Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 799. How the Jews give shameful names to saints, see the same, p. 1088. We have some remarks on the invocation of saints in Lipman in Nizachon, fol. 16.

units.la: Sanguis Sacrificiorum partim spargebatur ad altaris latera, partim vero ad basin altaris per destinatos in hunc finem canales. Vid. Sacrificia. Maymon in More Nevochim III. 46. refert, Deum Sanguinis esum prohibuisse propter Zabæos, qui sanguine vescebantur, ut possent communicationem habere cum Diabolo, vel Dæmonibus, quorum cibum Sanguinem esse crediderunt.
units.tr: The blood of the sacrifices was partly sprinkled on the sides of the altar, and partly at the base of the altar through channels set aside for this purpose. See Sacrifices. Maimonides in More Nevochim III, 46, reports that God forbade the eating of blood on account of the Sabaeans, who fed on blood so that they might have communion with the Devil or the demons, whose food they believed blood to be.

units.la: Sandalia, inter ipsa & calceos satis evidens faciunt discrimen: Proferamus loca. Extraētio calcei (dǫ qua si fiat בנעל calceo legitima & recta est; נסגר si fiat Sandalio & ei adsit calx, legitima est, sin minus, non recta.
units.tr: Sandals: between these and shoes they make a clear enough distinction. Let us quote the passages. The removal of a shoe (if it is done in a shoe [בנעל], it is lawful and correct; if it is done in a sandal and there is a heel on it, it is lawful; otherwise it is not correct).

units.la: Dicit R.Iosi, Profeētus sum Nisibin, vidique illic seniorem quendam, dixique ei, Num bene nosti R.Iudam, num unquam eum difcalceantem vidisti, in quonam difcalceat, Calceo an Sandalio? Respondit ille, numnam Rabbi sunt Sandalia hic apud nos? Et paulò infrà, Viplurimum hic usitatum est extrahere Sandalium contra communem tamen traditionem &c.
units.tr: R. Jose says: "I went to Nisibis and saw there an elder, and I said to him, 'Do you know R. Judah well? Have you ever seen him take off his shoes? In what does he take them off, in a shoe or in a sandal?' He replied, 'Are there sandals here among us, Rabbi?'" And a little further on: "It is very commonly practised here to take off the sandal, contrary nevertheless to the common tradition," etc.

units.la: Gloss in Ievamot sol.101.1. Calceus מנעל של עור erat e corio molliori. סנדל של עור קשה Sandalium verò e corio duriori.
units.tr: Gloss on Yevamot fol. 101.1. A shoe [מנעל] was of softer leather; but a sandal [סנדל] was of harder leather.

units.la: His adde,quod quædam Sandalia ita confecta fuerint, ut ex utraque parte indui potuerint.Vid.Schabbat sol.60.1.Erant quædam Sandalia,quorum solea è ligno erat, superior è corio,atque hæ clavis compaginatæ. Gloss in loc. modo cit.Erant etiam Sandalia quædã è iuncis confecta, aut è cortice palmarum. Ioma f.78.2.
units.tr: To these add that some sandals were so made that they could be put on from either side. See Shabbat fol. 60.1. There were certain sandals whose sole was of wood and whose upper was of leather, and these were fastened with nails. Gloss on the same passage. There were also sandals made of rushes, or of palm bark. Joma fol. 78.2.

units.la: In Kelim cap 9. fit mentio calcei עמיקי Imkani vel vallensis. Christus discipulis suis Matt. 10. v.10. interdicit cum tunicis etiam ὑποδήματα calceos, non Sandalia, scopus enim est ipsi prohibêre vestitum delicatiorem ad quem pertinebant calcei, non certè Sandalia, utpote quæ sæpius ligneas soleas habebant. De Calceo aliquid in C. diximus.
units.tr: In Kelim ch. 9 mention is made of a shoe of the Imkani [עמיקי], or valley, kind. Christ forbids his disciples to take with them shoes [ὑποδήματα] together with tunics, Matt. 10:10, not sandals; for his aim is to forbid the more luxurious clothing to which shoes belonged, not certainly sandals, since these often had wooden soles. We have said something about the shoe in C.

units.la: erat vallis cuius fundus tenerrimus erat, hinc quoque de עור השרוני aratro Saaronitico dicitur, quod tantæ magnitudinis porcam fecerit, quantum aliorum locorum aratra vix in tribus vicibus faciebant: quod observ. ad explic.loci Kelaim cap.2.v.6.
units.tr: It was a valley whose floor was very soft. Hence also of the Saronite plough [עור השרוני] it is said that it made a furrow of such size that other ploughs in those places could hardly do the same in three passes. Observed for the explanation of the passage in Kelaim ch. 2, v. 6.

units.la: SCHEDA מזוה Mesusa, est scheda membranacea quam affigunt postibus ıanuarum.De illa disputatur in Tractat. Menachot c. 3. f.33.2. apud Maymonidem in Halac.Tephillin c.1.c.5.c.6. Vid. Synag. Iud. Buxtorf. pag.m.583.
units.tr: The SCHEDA [מזוזה] Mezuzah is a parchment scroll that they fix to the doorposts of houses. This is discussed in the tractate Menachot ch. 3, f. 33.2, and in Maimonides, Hilchot Tefillin ch. 1, 5 and 6. See Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica, p. 583.

units.la: SCHEMAIA שמעיה & Abhtalion אבשלין floruerunt anno Mundi 3722. Schemaia fuit Princeps Senatus, alter vero secundus ab ipso. Non erant Iudæi nati, sed גרי צדק Proselyti iustitiæ, ex Sancheribi nepotibus, ita tamen ut mulierem Israelitidam matrem habuerint כדי שיוכלו לרון Vt idonei ad iudicandum essent. Nam apud Rambam in Sanhed. expresse definitur, neminem inter Israelitas Iudicis munus administrare posse,nisi mater eius ab Israele oriunda esset.
units.tr: SCHEMAIA [שמעיה] and Abtalion [אבטליון] flourished in the year of the world 3722. Shemaiah was the president of the Sanhedrin, and Abtalion was second after him. They were not born Jews but proselytes of righteousness [גרי צדק], descended from the grandsons of Sennacherib, yet they had an Israelite mother, so that they might be fit to judge. For in Rambam, Sanhedrin, it is expressly laid down that no one among the Israelites can exercise the office of judge unless his mother was of Israelite origin.

units.la: Ornavit Iuchasin p.17. Schemaiam & Abthalionem hoc elogio, quod fuerint Sapientes maximi ובמעשיהם ככני אהרון & quod opera ipsorum fuerint ut opera filiorum Aaron (licet ex femine eius non effent) quodque Hillelem & Schammaeum præceptores habuerint.
units.tr: Iuchasin, p. 17, praises Shemaiah and Abtalion with this commendation: that they were very great sages, and [their works were] as the works of the sons of Aaron (although they were not of his seed), and that they had Hillel and Shammai as their teachers.

units.la: est manipulus cuius obliviscuntur messores שכחה Deut.24.19. Manipulus relictus Schekecha esse non potest, si quis pilei iustar manipulat, aut לכוםסאות ex parte caulium in terra ponit, aut לחורות iustar placentæ colligit, sed manipuli in agro relicti tum dimum שכרה fiunt, quando messis in horreum refertur & re ipsa deleta & seposita est, secundum hanc gene-
units.tr: There is a sheaf which the reapers forget [שכחה], Deut. 24:19. A sheaf left behind cannot be a shekhechah if someone binds it like a cap, or sets it on the ground on its end [לכוסאות] like a stalk, or gathers it like a cake [לחורות], but sheaves left in the field become a shekhechah only when the harvest has been carried into the barn and has in fact been cleared and set apart, according to this gen-

units.la: ralem regulam in Peah cap.8. כל העמר לםקום שהוא גמר מלאכה יש לו שכחה Manipulus fit Schekecha, postquàm messis deposita in locum in quem ultimò recondi solet.
units.tr: eral rule in Peah ch. 8: Every sheaf [becomes a shekhechah] when it is placed in the place where the work is finished, [כל העמר לםקום שהוא גמר מלאכה יש לו שכחה]. A sheaf becomes a shekhechah after the harvest has been deposited in the place where it is usually stored last.

units.la: Manipulus qui relinquitur propè גפה claustrum, propè Acervum frumenti, propè gregem aut vasa, secundùm Schammæanos non est שכחה. Manipulus ראש תשורה qui seriei caput est, non potest esse Schekecha, quia proximus ipsius signum est; ut nec ille quem quis humeris sublatum, in urbem ferre vult, & deinde illius obliviscitur. Peah c.6.
units.tr: A sheaf which is left near a gate [גפה], a closure, near a heap of grain, near a flock or vessels, is not a shekhechah according to the Shammaites. A sheaf which is the head of the row [ראש תשורה] cannot be a shekhechah, because it is a sign for the one next to it; likewise not one which a man has lifted on his shoulders and wants to carry into the city, and then forgets it. Peah ch. 6.

units.la: Manipuli שכחה hæc est generalis regu!a כל שהוא כבל תשוב שכחה ושאינו תשוב אינו שכחה: Omnis ille [manipulus] qui in tali loco relinquitur, ut ad eum venire non possint [à serie manipulorum,] nisi revertendo, [& ita transgredi debeant præceptum divinum quod dicit בל.תשוב] est Schekecha. Peah ubi supra.
units.tr: For sheaves of shekhechah this is the general rule: Every sheaf left in such a place that they cannot come to it [from the row of sheaves] except by turning back, [and so they would have to transgress the divine precept which says, לא תשוב (you shall not return)], is a shekhechah. Peah, as above.

units.la: Duo Manipuli sunt שכחה sed non tres; Duo olivarum & siliquarum ציבורי acerviculi sunt שכחה sed non tres. Seges etiam potest fieri שכחה, si Dominus eius illius obliviſcitur, si scilicet minus quàm duo Sata aut habeat, aut ferre possit. Ex fasciculis pabuli quod ex luxuriante semente demessum est, & manipulis allii & ceparum, quales sunt cæpæ illæ quæ תורת לאת & לוף vocantur, non fit Schekecha secundùm R. Iehudam. Ille qui nostu metit & manipulat, aut qui cæcus est, si intenderit tollere הגם, ea quæ protuberant non fiunt שכחה, Peah.c.6.
units.tr: Two sheaves are a shekhechah, but not three; two heaps of olives and carobs [ציבורי] small heaps are a shekhechah, but not three. A standing crop too can become a shekhechah, if its owner forgets it, that is, if he has less than two seahs of it or can carry less. From bundles of fodder cut from a lush crop, and from bunches of garlic and onions, such as those onions called teoret [תורת] and lof [לוף], no shekhechah is made, according to R. Judah. A man who reaps and binds at night, or one who is blind, if he intends to take up the hagam [הגם], those things that stick out are not made a shekhechah. Peah ch. 6.

units.la: SCHIBBOLETH De eo sic Kimchi in cap.12. Iud.
units.tr: SHIBBOLETH. Of it, thus Kimchi on Judges ch. 12.

units.la: Sicuti eos tentarunt hoc vocabulo, ita ipsos quoque probarunt pronuntiatione omnium vocabulorum in quibus שין reperitur, Ephraimitæ verò omnia protulerunt per Sin. Scriptura autem solùm unius vocis meminit, לפי שהיה שכולת הנהר בסקום שהיו עוברים בני אפרים quia Schibbolet erat nomen illius fluminis quod transfire debebant Ephraimita. Quod autem in pronuntiatione illius vocis balbutiverint, אולי היה אויר ארצם גורם לחם זרז certè ex climate ipsorum regionis arcefsendum; sic videmus Gallos שין ut plurimùm efferre in modum תיו רפה tanquam lenis.
units.tr: Just as they tested them with this word, so they also proved them by the pronunciation of all the words in which Sin [שין] is found, while the Ephraimites pronounced everything with Sin. Scripture, however, mentions only one word, because Shibboleth was the name of that river which the Ephraimites had to cross [לפי שהיה שכולת הנהר...]. As for the fact that they stammered in pronouncing that word, this must certainly be ascribed to the climate of their region [אולי היה אויר ארצם גורם לחם זרז]; so we see the French usually pronounce Sin like the soft Tav [תיו רפה], as a gentle sound.

units.la: SCORTATIO. In quocunque loco invenis fcortationem זנות, ibi peftis venit & occidit bonos & malos. Berefch.Rabba fect.26. R.Salom. Gen. 6.13. עליו כל המזנה אשתו מוננת Quicunque fcortatur, uxor eius quoque fcortatur poft ipfum. Succa in fin. Nam בסה שהוא עוסק היא Quod vir agit, eodem uxor eft occupata. Sotah. fol.10.1. In illos competit hoc Heb. proverb. איהו בקרי ואתתיה כבוציני Ipfe cucurbitis & uxor eius cucumeribus deleftatur.
units.tr: SCORTATIO. Wherever you find fornication [זנות], there pestilence comes and kills both good and bad. Bereshit Rabba sect. 26, R. Solomon on Gen. 6:13: [עליו כל המזנה אשתו מזנה] Whoever commits fornication, his wife also commits fornication after him. Sukkah at the end. For [בעה שהוא עוסק היא] what the husband does, the wife is occupied with the same. Sotah fol. 10.1. Against such people applies this Hebrew proverb: [איהו בקרי ואתתיה כבוציני] He himself delights in gourds, and his wife in cucumbers.

units.la: SCRIBERE. Hæc possunt scribi in festo. Vxoris sponsalia, Libellus repudii, Apochæ, ויתיקי מתנה Testamenta. מרוכולין debiti perpetui Syngrapha. אגרות שום litera positionales (five concessionis,) literæ alimoniæ [quibus à Synedrio uxori mariti decoctoris, & filiis suis, usufructus fundi attribuitur.] Instrumenta extractionis calcei: Literæ הנאין Recusationis, literæ declarationum [protocollum hodiè vocamus, Heb. שטרי בירורין] Decretalia Senatus, ושטרי הרשות & mandata Magistratus.
units.tr: SCRIBERE. These things may be written on a festival: the betrothal of a wife, a bill of divorce, receipts, [ויתיקי מתנה] testaments, a syngraphe of perpetual debt [מרוכולין], letters of position [אגרות שום] (or of concession), letters of maintenance [by which the Sanhedrin assigns to the wife of a bankrupt husband and to his sons the usufruct of a field], instruments for the removal of a shoe [חליצה], letters of refusal [הנאין], letters of declarations [which we today call protocol, Heb. שטרי בירורין], decrees of the Senate, [ושטרי הרשות] and mandates of the magistrate.

units.la: In festo autem scribere non licet Syngrapham Debiti. Si autem non fidat creditor, aut scriba non habet quod edat, scribere licet. Nec licet libros, phylacteria, aut postium ichedas scribere, nec corrigere vel unam literam, ne quidem in exemplari Bibliorum quod ordinarie in templo conservabatur. Moed K. ton cap.3.v.3.4. De Contractuum scriptione Vid. Contractus.
units.tr: On a festival, however, it is not lawful to write a syngraphe of debt. If, however, the creditor does not trust, or the scribe has nothing to publish, it is lawful to write. Nor is it lawful to write books, phylacteries, or the scrolls for doorposts, nor to correct even a single letter, not even in the copy of the Bible which was ordinarily kept in the temple. Moed Katan ch. 3, v. 3, 4. On the writing of contracts see Contractus.

units.la: Illos Scribas, qui agrorum, aedium, hominum summam notabant, ut inde tributum Regi legitime conferretur, vocabant אנקילמוס Bava Bathra sol.68.2. Quasi a Calamis.
units.tr: Those scribes who recorded the sum of fields, buildings and persons, so that a tax might lawfully be paid to the king from them, were called ankilmos [אנקילמוס]. Bava Bathra fol. 68.2. As if from calamus.

units.la: סופר Γεαμματεὺς generalius quemlibet doctum denotat, & opponitur רודי בור rudi Bab. Berac. sol.45.2. Sic סופרי כותיים Bab. Sotah sol.33. 2. i. e. Docti inter Sammaritanos. Spe ialius denotat Scribas phylacteriorum legis, & amanuenses quoslibet, de quibus vid. Maffec.Sopherim. Singulari etiam ratione ita vocantur Patres constitutionum, seniores Synedrii; si illi e Levitica prosapia orti non effent, vocabantur Scribae populi, illi vero qui ex illa erant nominabantur Scribae Cleri. Vid. Hierof.Beracot sol.3.cap.2. Vb. verba sunt constitutiones Synedrii.
units.tr: Scribe [סופר] [γραμματεύς] more generally denotes any learned man, and is opposed to the ignorant [רודי בור]. Bab. Berachot fol. 45.2. So the scribes of the Samaritans [סופרי כותיים], Bab. Sotah fol. 33.2, i.e. learned men among the Samaritans. More specially it denotes scribes of the phylacteries of the law, and any copyists, on whom see Maffec. Sopherim. By a singular usage they are also so called: fathers of the constitutions, elders of the Sanhedrin; if they were not of Levitical descent, they were called scribes of the people, but those who were of that descent were called scribes of the clergy. See Hierof. Beracot fol. 3, ch. 2. Where the words are the constitutions of the Sanhedrin.

units.la: Scythopolis Vid. Beth/chean.
units.tr: Scythopolis: see Beth-chean.

units.la: שמיר Schamir est vermiculus instar grani hordacei, cuius virtute & tactu pararunt, diviserunt, & dedolarunt lapides ad aedificium templi destinatos, nullum enim adhibuerunt ferrum. R. Salomoh Iesai.56. Kimchi 1. Regum 6.7. Quidam dicunt hunc vermem Salomonem ab Asmodaeo Diabolorum principe impetrasse, Gittin sol.68.1. Alii vero Aquilam illum ad Salomonem asportasse: ut Kimchi ubi supra. Creatus fuit Schamir cum decem aliis rebus vesperâ Sabbathi sub crepusculum Pirke avoth cap.5. משחרב בית המקדש נשל השמיר A quo devastatum fuit Sanctuarium ceßavit vermis Schamir. Sotah c. ult.
units.tr: Schamir is a little worm the size of a barley grain. By its power and touch they cut, split and dressed the stones destined for the building of the Temple, since they used no iron. R. Solomon Jarchi on Isaiah 56; Kimchi on 1 Kings 6:7. Some say Solomon obtained this worm from Asmodeus, prince of the demons, Gittin fol. 68.1. Others say that an eagle carried it to Solomon, as Kimchi says in the passage above. The Schamir was created, together with ten other things, on the evening of the Sabbath at twilight, Pirke Avoth ch. 5. "From the time the Sanctuary was destroyed, the worm Schamir ceased." A quo devastatum fuit Sanctuarium, cessavit vermis Schamir. Sotah last chapter. [משחרב בית המקדש נשל השמיר]

units.la: De hoc verme Vid.Cl.Bochart. de Animal.
units.tr: On this worm see the illustrious Bochart, De Animalibus.

units.la: Sectiones Biblicæ quas legunt in Synagogis Vid. משטרות in H. & Lectiones.
units.tr: Sections: the biblical passages read in the synagogues. See mishtarot [משטרות] in the H. and Lectiones.

units.la: Seductor הסית is est הרשע laicus, seducens alium laicum his verbis 'יש ירא נבמקום Est Deus in illo loco, cui talis cibus, talis potus prabetur, a quo talia bona vel mala expectari possunt. Ex omnibus qui morti adiudicantur in lege, nullæ insidiæ collocantur hoc excepto; nam Si ad binos sic loquutus sit, illique testimonium de eo dixerint, in iudicium vocatus lapidatur, si vero ad unum quempiam dixerit, Socios habeo, qui idem volunt, & deinde cautus sit, neque coram pluribus talia dicat, testes post parietem absconduntur; Tum qui ab ipso ad idololatriam invitatus fuit, iubet eum repetere in Secreto, quod ei dixerat. Is si repetat, ille dicet, Quomodo relinquemus Deum nostrum; ut colamus ligna & lapides? Si pœniteat illum bene est. At si dixerit, Hoc tenemur facere, hodecet nos. Testes occultati post parietem, abductum ad Iudices lapidibus cædunt. Sanhedrin cap.7. §.10.
units.tr: The seducer [הסית] is the wicked man [הרשע], a layman, who entices another layman with these words: "There is a God in that place, to whom such food and such drink are provided, from whom such good or evil may be expected." Of all who are condemned to death under the law, no snare is laid except for this one. For if he speaks thus to two men, and they testify against him, he is summoned to judgment and stoned. But if he speaks to a single person, saying, "I have companions who think the same," and then is cautious and does not say such things before several people, witnesses are hidden behind a wall. Then the man who was invited by him to idolatry is ordered to repeat in private what he had said to him. If he repeats it, the other will say, "How shall we forsake our God to serve wood and stones?" If he repents, it is well with him. But if he says, "We are bound to do this; it befits us," the hidden witnesses behind the wall lead him before the judges and stone him. Sanhedrin ch. 7 §10.

units.la: Sementis Vid. Agriculturam.
units.tr: Sowing: see Agriculture.

units.la: Initium messis hordeaceæ, erat à medio mensis Nisan Levit. 23. 10. Bava Metzia sol. 106.2. Dimidium Tisri, totus Marchesvan, & dimidium
units.tr: The beginning of the barley harvest was from the middle of the month Nisan, Lev. 23:10; Bava Metzia fol. 106.2. Half of Tishri, all of Marcheshvan, and half of

units.la: Pp Cifl ev, eft ירז Sementis. Dimidium Cifl·v, totum Tebhet& dimidium Schebat eft חורב Hyems. Dimidium Schebat, totus Adar, & dimidium Nifan eft ‏ריפ Bruma. Dimidium Nifan totus Iiar, & dimidium Sivan eft ריצפ. Dimidium Sivan, totus Tammus, & dimidium אב, eft ייפ eftas. Dimidium Ab, totus Elul, & dimidium Tifri eft םוח eftus.
units.tr: Half of Kislev is sowing [זרע]. Half of Kislev, all of Tebeth, and half of Shevat is winter [חורב]. Half of Shevat, all of Adar, and half of Nisan is bruma [ריפ]. Half of Nisan, all of Iyar, and half of Sivan is [ריצפ]. Half of Sivan, all of Tammuz, and half of Av is summer [ייפ]. Half of Av, all of Elul, and half of Tishri is heat [םוח].

units.la: Seminarunt triticum & fpeltam à Tifri & Marchefvan; Targ. in Ecclef.xi.2. Da portionem bonam feminis agro tuo in Tifri, & ne cohibearis à feminando etiam in Cifl ev.
units.tr: They sowed wheat and spelt from Tishri and Marcheshvan. Targum on Ecclesiastes 11:2: "Give a good portion of seed to your field in Tishri, and do not refrain from sowing even in Kislev."

units.la: Seminarunt hordeum in Schebat & Adar.
units.tr: They sowed barley in Shevat and Adar.

units.la: Gloff. in Rofch Hafchana fol.16.1. ארעא אפלא Semen Serotinum (vel abfconditum & fub terra latens) eft triticum & fpelta, quae non cito maturefcunt, feruntur in Marchefvan. חרפ ירזי Semen pracox, eft hordeum quod cito maturefcit, feruntur in Schebat & Adar.
units.tr: Gloss on Rosh Hashanah fol. 16.1. "Late seed [ארעא אפלא] (or hidden and lying under the ground) is wheat and spelt, which do not ripen quickly; they are sown in Marcheshvan. Early seed [חרפ ירזי] is barley, which ripens quickly; it is sown in Shevat and Adar."

units.la: Menachot fol. 85.1. Serunt 70. diebus ante Pafcha.
units.tr: Menachot fol. 85.1. They sow seventy days before the Passover.

units.la: Aliquando & frequenter fatis, fatio hordei fuit poft medium menfis Marchefvan. Vid. Primitias.
units.tr: Sometimes, and quite often, the sowing of barley was after the middle of Marcheshvan. See Firstfruits.

units.la: Seminandi duplicem rationem habuerunt, aliquando manu femen fparferunt, quam feminationem (venia verbo) vocant יד מעולת; aliquando vero indiderunt femen plauftro undiqque foraminibus oppleto, & bobus fuper agrum aratro verfum illud plauftrum trahentes femen foraminibus percolabant. Hunc modum appellant מעולת שוורים feminationem failam à bobus. Bava Metzia. fol.105. in Gemar. & Gloss. Vid. quæ apud Agriculturam diximus: Si dixerint tibi senes נזן destrue, Iuniores verò נב ædifica, destrue & ne ædifices; quia destructio senum ædificatio est, & ædi-ficatio iuvenum destructio. Plantav. Flor. 175.
units.tr: They used two methods of sowing. Sometimes they scattered the seed by hand, which kind of sowing they call, pardon the word, yad me'ulat [יד מעולת]. Sometimes they put the seed into a cart, filled with holes all over, and oxen drew the cart over the ploughed field, so that the seed trickled out through the holes. This method they call me'ulat shevarim [מעולת שוורים], sowing by oxen. Bava Metzia fol. 105, in the Gemara and Gloss. See what we said under Agriculture. "If old men say 'destroy' [נזן] to you, but young men say 'build' [נב], destroy and do not build; for the destruction of the old is building, and the building of the young is destruction." Plantavit, Flor. 175.

units.la: מסרר ןק Senior refragator, qui edicto Senatus parere renuit, & ex proprio cerebro traditiones sibi fabricare vult, primò adducitur ad illud Synedrium quod sedebat ad ascensum montis Sanctuarii; tum sic agebat Senior, ego hunc sensum ex sacra pagina depromp si, socii mei istum. Si iudices quid in illa causa tenendum esset, traditione accepissent, hoc illis cómunicabant: sin minus alteri Synedrio, & ab illo ad magnū pergebant. Reversus in urbem suam, si tradat doceatque sicut didicit (aut existimat) liber est. Si autem id etiam facere præceperit, reus fit. Non occiditur à iudicibus civitatis suæ: non à Synedrio quod Iasne est, sed ad magnum Synedrium Hierosol. adducitur, atque ibi in custodia asservatur usque ad sestum, in illoque interficitur. R. Ikhuda ait, non dilatant iudicium eius, sed ipsum quamprimùm interficiunt & literis publicant; N. N. ob hoc aut illud à Senatu supplicio affectus fuit. Sanhed. c.10.2.4.
units.tr: A stubborn elder [זקן ממרא], who refuses to obey the decree of the Senate and wants to fabricate traditions from his own mind, is first brought before that Sanhedrin which sat at the ascent of the Temple mount. The elder then says, "I will derive this sense from the sacred page; let my colleagues consider it." If the judges had received a tradition about that case, they communicated it to him; if not, they went to the other Sanhedrin, and from there to the great one. If he returns to his city and teaches as he has learned (or thinks he has learned), he is free. But if he has also been ordered to do this, he is guilty. He is not put to death by the judges of his own city, nor by the Sanhedrin at Jabneh, but he is brought before the great Sanhedrin at Jerusalem, kept in custody there until the feast, and killed during it. R. Judah says they do not delay his judgment, but kill him as soon as possible and publish it in writing: "N.N. was put to death by the Senate for this or that." Sanhedrin ch. 10 §§2, 4.

units.la: Bertramus de Rep. Heb. cap.5. existimat Iudæos in Ægypto possedisse aliquam politiam, quia dicitur Mosen adiisse הקנים Seniores; & illud probare vult ex Iarchio, qui illos vocat מיוחדי quorum munus fuit habere consefsum; sed consiliarii etiam confessum habent non solùm iudices. Ita ut hinc iurisdictio forensis concludi non possit. Nec aliud Aben Esra.
units.tr: Bertram, in De Republica Hebraeorum ch. 5, thinks the Jews in Egypt possessed some kind of polity, because it is said that Moses approached the elders [הקנים]. He wants to prove this from Jarchi, who calls them "those set apart, whose office was to hold a council." But counsellors also hold a council, not only judges, so no judicial jurisdiction can be inferred from this. Aben Ezra says nothing different.

units.la: Servi. Servus est vel Israelita vel Cananeus.
units.tr: Servants. A servant is either an Israelite or a Canaanite.

units.la: Servus Israelita duplici modo servus fit, vel quia Synedrium ipsum vendidit, vel quia vendidit se ipsum. Synedrium Israelitas in Servos vendit, quando furtum commiserunt, nec furreptum iterum per retributionem restituere valent; servos autem tales non nisi Israelitis vendunt, non autem gentilibus. Venduntur autem, aut pro argento, aut pro æquivalente, aut simplici instrumento venditionis. Talis servus anno septimo appropinquante iterum fit בן חורין liber. Synedrium propter nullum aliud facinus quàm propter furtum servos facit.
units.tr: An Israelite becomes a servant in two ways: either because the Sanhedrin has sold him, or because he has sold himself. The Sanhedrin sells Israelites into servitude when they have committed theft and cannot make restitution of the stolen goods. Such servants are sold only to Israelites, never to Gentiles. They are sold either for silver, or for an equivalent, or by a simple deed of sale. Such a servant becomes free again [בן חורין] as the seventh year draws near. The Sanhedrin makes servants for no other crime than theft.

units.la: Circa servos statuitur in Gem. ad Gittin c. 4. & Maym. Hal. עבדי cap. 9. Servitutem בגוף in corpore, id est personæ inhærentem sive personalem non esse ex Iure naturæ sed Iure Hebraico: & naturali iure servum Domino non esse acquisitum nisi ירי ידי לבעשה quoad ministerium & operam eius. Quæ distinctio ab aliis I.Consultis non est recepta.
units.tr: Concerning servants, see the Gemara on Gittin ch. 4, and Maimonides, Hilchot Avadim ch. 9. Servitude "in the body" (that is, adhering to the person, or personal) is not from the law of nature but from Hebrew law; by natural law a servant is not acquired by his master except as regards his service and labour. This distinction has not been accepted by the other jurists.

units.la: Ille qui se ipsum in servum vendit, ob nullam aliam rationem id facere potest, nisi ita fit pauper ut neque se nutrire neque sustentare possit. Israelita non debet se vendere בארץ ישראל ולא בסמוך Palàm aut in semita, ut alii faciunt. Non debet gentilis se vendere, si verò id fecerit cogit synedrium cognatos ut eum redimant; si non redimitur, ante Iubilæum è servitute egredi non poterit. Qui seipsum vendidit non po-teft teft ancillam Cananiticam in uxorem ducere. At Dominus qui servum è Synedrio emit, ipsi ancillam Cananiticam dare tenetur. Filia statim ac pubuit (pubertatis signa Vid. apud Puberta)à Patre amplius divendi non potest.
units.tr: One who sells himself into servitude can do so for no other reason than that he is so poor that he cannot feed or support himself. An Israelite ought not to sell himself in the land of Israel and "not in the open or in the street" [בארץ ישראל ולא בסמוך], as others do. A Gentile ought not to sell himself; if he has done so, the Sanhedrin compels his kinsmen to redeem him; if he is not redeemed, he cannot go free before the Jubilee. One who has sold himself cannot take a Canaanite maidservant as his wife. But the master who bought the servant from the Sanhedrin is bound to give him a Canaanite maidservant. A daughter, as soon as she has reached puberty (for the signs of puberty see under Puberty), cannot be sold again by her father.

units.la: Servus Cananiticus potest acquiri aut liber fieri. qɔɔɔ argento, בשער literis, (ut quando Dominus eius ipsi scribit השחרור גט libellum libertatis, cuius summa est, הרי את לעצמך Ecce, iam tui iuris es, vel אין לי פסץ כך Nihil mihi est tecum) בראשי אברים decurtatione membrorum, quando Dominus eius sui aliquod membrum praecidit, aut ita percussit ut membra eius insigne damnum passa sint, tunc enim sui iuris fit, & si ipsi placuerit se alii Domino addicere poterit, בחליפין Permutatione (durch einen Tausch.) His addunt, במשיכה tractione, ut bestias publici iuris nofi as trahendo facimus. Vid.Maymon. Hal. ערכי c.1.2.3.4.5.
units.tr: A Canaanite servant can be acquired or made free. He is acquired by money; by writing, as when his master writes him a bill of freedom [השחרור גט], the sum of which is "Behold, you are now your own master," or "I have nothing more to do with you"; by the mutilation of limbs, when his master cuts off some member of his or so beats him that his limbs suffer serious damage, for then he becomes his own master, and if it pleases him he may hand himself over to another master; by exchange; and by drawing, just as we make animals the property of the public by drawing them. See Maimonides, Hilchot Arachin ch. 1 to 5.

units.la: Quidam erant servi qui vocantur עבדי מלוג, servi usuarii, nam ipsorum operâ & officio Dominus quidem uti poterat, ipsi verò illos divendere non licuit, aut alienare. Ievamot f.66.1.
units.tr: There were slaves called עבדי מלוג, usufructuary slaves. Their master could make use of their labour and service, but he was not permitted to sell them or alienate them. Ievamot f.66.1.

units.la: Alii vocantur עבדי צאן ברזל, quia maritus eos sic suscipiebat, ut si morerentur, ipse teneretur certâ pecuniæ summâ, in literis matrimonialibus designatâ, eos redimere, eamque uxori pro iis solvere, ita ut illi tanquam ferrum uxori integri manerent. Bava Kama sol.89.1. Cl.Coccei Sanhed. sol.96.
units.tr: Others are called עבדי צאן ברזל, because the husband received them on the condition that, if they died, he himself was bound to redeem them for a fixed sum of money specified in the marriage contract and to pay that sum to his wife in their place. In this way they remained for the wife as sound as iron. Bava Kama sol.89.1. Cl. Coccei Sanhed. sol.96.

units.la: Qui servos olim vendebant, cogebantur emptori dare sponsionem, quòd eos non furati essent; Sub eiusmodi sponsionibus emit Potiphar Iofephum ab Ifmaelitis. Ionath. Gen.39.1. Berefch. Rabba fect. 86. Ordinariūm pretium servi erat פליין וTriginta Selaim argenti puri. Maymon. in מכון cap. ii. Christus à luda pretio itaque servi fuit divenditus. Servus quem Dominus hæredem constituit liber fit, si Dominus nullum fundum sibi reservaverit, aliàs non liber fit. Peah.3.8.
units.tr: Those who formerly sold slaves were obliged to give the buyer a guarantee that they had not stolen them. Under such a guarantee Potiphar bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites. Ionath. Gen.39.1. Berefch. Rabba sect. 86. The ordinary price of a slave was Triginta Selaim, thirty shekels of pure silver. Maymon. in מכון cap. ii. Christ was therefore sold by Judas for the price of a slave. A slave whom the master appointed heir becomes free, if the master reserved no field for himself; otherwise he does not become free. Peah.3.8.

units.la: עבד של רצועה Perforatio auris servi, fit coram triumviratu, Subulam Dominus ipse debet per aurem servi ad limina ianuæ premere. Maymon ubi supra cap.3. Servus per aurem potiùs terebrandus quàm per aliquam aliam partem corporis, quia aure audiverat in monte Sinai, solum iugum regni cœlorum esse suscipiendum, & tamen in se suscepit iugum carnis & sanguinis. B n Saceai in Kiddufchin sol. 59.4.
units.tr: עבד של רצועה: the piercing of a slave's ear, is performed before a triumvirate. The master himself must press an awl through the slave's ear against the doorpost. Maymon, ubi supra cap.3. The slave is to be pierced through the ear rather than any other part of the body, because he heard with his ear on Mount Sinai that only the yoke of the kingdom of heaven is to be taken up, and yet he took upon himself the yoke of flesh and blood. B n Saceai in Kiddufchin sol. 59.4.

units.la: De dimissione Servorum in Iubilæo Vid.Iubilæum
units.tr: On the release of slaves in the Jubilee, see Iubilæum.

units.la: Servus Regis Rex est, adhære Principi & honorabunt te. R.Salomoh.Gen.15 18. Servus Sacerdotis quem accepit ab Israele non comedet de oblatione Trumæ, propter defectum. Kethubbot sol. 57.2. tota enim oblatio propter talem convivam maculam contrahere posset.
units.tr: "The slave of a king is a king: cling to the prince and they will honour you." R.Salomoh.Gen.15 18. The slave of a priest, whom he acquired from Israel, shall not eat of the offering of Terumah, because of his defect. Kethubbot sol. 57.2. For the whole offering could contract a stain on account of such a guest.

units.la: SEPULTURAM, SEPULCHRA Vid. Mors & Lu-ctus. Sepulchreta non erant prope urbes לא היו קברות בתי Glossa in Kiddufchin sol. 80 2. A civitatibus Leviticis cœmeteria distabant bis mille cubitis; ab omnibus aliis civitatibus si non eodem spatio saltem non multò minori. Hæc autem intelligenda de sepulchris vulgaribus, nobiliora enim excisa erant in petra. tra, in propriis prædiis non modico sumptu. Illa ordinariè ita confecta erant ut in spelunca sepulchrali primò esset area in qua stare poterant illi qui feretrum succollabant, deinde area istâ quatuor cubitis profundior erat spelunca excavatio, & in illa plurimi כוכין loculi ad cadavera recipienda. Vid.Lucium. Marci 16.5. Mulieres introeuntes in monumentum viderunt, invenem sedentem à dexteris, scil. in ipsa area, illico post introitum in speluncam. Luc. 24.3. Mulieres & Petrus stant in area, facies inclinant in כוכין repositoria. Ipse Petrus Ioh.20.5. descendit ab area in excavationem, ubi sepulchrorum ordines. Maria stabat ad monumentum foris, intra speluncam quidem in area, at extra speluncam profundiorem, ubi ipsi loculi dispositi.
units.tr: BURIAL, SEPULCHRES. See Mors & Luctus. Sepulchreta non erant prope urbes: cemeteries were not near the cities. Gloss in Kiddufchin sol. 80.2. From the Levitical cities the cemeteries were two thousand cubits away; from all other cities, if not at the same distance, at least not much less. But this must be understood of ordinary tombs, for the more noble ones were hewn out of rock, on their own estates, at no small expense. These were ordinarily so made that in the sepulchral cave there was first an area in which those who carried the bier could stand. Then, four cubits deeper than this area, was the excavation of the cave, and in it many niches (loculi) for receiving the corpses. See Lucium, Marci 16.5. The women, entering the tomb, saw a young man sitting on the right, namely in the area itself, just after entering the cave. Luc. 24.3. The women and Peter stand in the area, bending their faces into the niches (repositoria). Peter himself, Ioh.20.5., descends from the area into the excavation, where are the rows of tombs. Mary stood at the tomb outside: within the cave, indeed, in the area, but outside the deeper cavity where the niches were set.

units.la: De Sepulchrorum distantia ab urbe consule Maym. in Hal Beth Habechira c.7. circa med.
units.tr: On the distance of tombs from the city, consult Maimonides in Hal Beth Habechira ch.7, about the middle.

units.la: De Sepulchrorum dealbatione fit sermo in Schekalim cap.1.v.1. die 15.mensis Adar emendant plateas מצייניך את הקברות ה pingunt sepulchra, scilicet כסיד ממחה ושופך calce, aquâ macerata ac infusâ, ut refert Maafer Scheni cap.5.1. Notat etiam Gloss. in Schekalim ipsos Sepulchra calce notasse ad formam ossium. Finem huius dealbationis eadem docet Glossa, ut scil. inquit inde omnes agnoscerent locum istum immundum esse, ideoque ab eo esse declinandum.
units.tr: The whitewashing of sepulchres is discussed in Shekalim ch.1 v.1. On the 15th of the month Adar they repair the roads, and they paint the sepulchres, namely with lime dissolved in water and poured on, as Maafer Scheni ch.5.1 reports. The Gloss on Shekalim also notes that they marked the sepulchres with lime in the form of bones. The same Gloss gives the purpose of this whitewashing: that all should recognise this place as unclean, and therefore avoid it.

units.la: SERPENS; Quidam ex maligno in Iudæos assectu scripserunt Serpentem esse ipsorum vitricum, quia scribunt Serpentem congressum esse cum Eva Ioma sol.28.2.
units.tr: THE SERPENT: Some, out of a malicious disposition towards the Jews, have written that the serpent was their stepfather, because they write that the serpent had intercourse with Eve. Ioma sol.28.2.

units.la: Serpens æneus nobilis erat Christi typus, ut patet ex Ioh.iii.14. ad illud myfterium tamen cæcutiunt Iudæi.
units.tr: The bronze serpent was a noble type of Christ, as is clear from John 3.14. Yet the Jews are blind to this mystery.

units.la: In Bammidbar Rabba feſt.19. opinantur, Serpentem æneum non fuiffe furca affixum, fed à Mofe iactatum in aërem, & fic illic hafiffe, abfque aliquo fulcro.
units.tr: In Bammidbar Rabba sect.19 they hold that the bronze serpent was not fixed on a fork, but was thrown by Moses into the air, and there hung without any support.

units.la: BaalTurim in Num.21. Mofes pofuit ferpentem in ligno, ficut qui caftigavit filium fuum, virgam collocat in loco aliquo editiori, ut filius videns reminiscatur.
units.tr: Baal Turim on Num.21: Moses set the serpent on a wood, just as one who has chastised his son places the rod in some higher place, so that the son, seeing it, may remember.

units.la: Nachmanides in loc. תסיר נוף בםויק ותרא חולי בםחלייא Amovebis nocumentum per illud quod nocuit, & sanabis agritudinem per illud quod fecit agros. Idem habet R. Bechai, & fatentur ambo, quod foret םנ בחוך םנ Miraculum intra miraculum.
units.tr: Nachmanides on the passage: You shall remove the harm by means of that which harmed, and you shall heal the sickness by means of that which made the fields sick. R. Bechai has the same, and both admit that it would be a miracle within a miracle.

units.la: De Serpente תברבנ Vid.Cl.Buxtorf. L.Talm. pag.706.
units.tr: On the serpent, see Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum, p.706.

units.la: De Serpente tentatore Vid. Eva.
units.tr: On the serpent as tempter, see Eve.

units.la: Sicli. Siclus est duplex, sacer vel communis, sacer est 20. obolorum, obolus autem 16. grana hordeacæa in pondere valebat, quæ per 20. multiplicata faciunt 320. grana hordei, sicli integri pondus. In argento continebat πηχῶν, vel 4. Sufæos. Communis vero solùm 10. obolos continebat. Præter hos siclos etiam habebant siclos המדינה Provincia, & siclos המלך Regios. De quibus Maymon in Schekalim ab init. vid. Schalschelet Hakabala parte II. sub fin. Waserum & Cl. Hotting. de nummis Heb. Cl. Buxt. in L.T. p.1489.
units.tr: Shekels. The shekel is of two kinds, sacred or common. The sacred shekel is twenty obols, and an obol was worth sixteen grains of barley in weight; multiplied by twenty, this makes 320 grains of barley, the full weight of the shekel. In silver it contained four sufos. The common shekel contained only ten obols. Besides these shekels there were also the shekels of the Provincia, and the royal shekels. On these see Maimonides in Shekalim, at the beginning; see Schalschelet Hakabala part II, near the end; Waserus; and Cl. Hottinger on Hebrew coins; Cl. Buxtorf in L.T. p.1489.

units.la: De Hemisiclorum persolutione, quam unusquisque debebat ad cultum templi & eius necessitates, sequentia ex Tratt. Schekalim notavimus.
units.tr: On the payment of the half-shekel, which each one was obliged to give for the worship of the temple and its needs, I have noted the following from the Tractate Shekalim.

units.la: Ad hemisiclum persolvendum omnes Israelitæ obligantur, Etiam pauperrimus qui Eleemosyna nutritur; si tantùm non habet, ab aliis petet, aut vestimenti venditione acquiret. A persolutione hemisicli liberantur fœminæ, servi,& parvuli, si tamen sponte aliquid attulerint, id ab ipsis recipitur, sic Pater qui incepit pro parvulo suo siclum pendere, semper pergat usquedum puer ipsemet pendere possit.
units.tr: All Israelites are obliged to pay the half-shekel, even the poorest, who is supported by charity. If he does not have it, he will ask others for it or get it by selling a garment. Women, slaves and small children are exempt from paying the half-shekel; yet if they have voluntarily brought something, it is received from them. So a father who began to pay a shekel for his small child should always continue until the boy himself can pay.

units.la: Subsistente Sanctuario hemisiclus solvi debebat extrà & intrà terram Israeliticam, at illo devastato nec in illa nec extrà illam amplius solvitur.
units.tr: While the Sanctuary stood, the half-shekel had to be paid both inside and outside the Land of Israel; but once it was laid waste, it is no longer paid either within it or outside it.

units.la: Primâ die Februarii, proclamant propter siclos, ut unusquisque suum paratum habeat. Die decimâ quintâ eiusdem mensis per omnes provincias ad menses sedent, & placidè ab unoquoque hemisiclum petunt, neque ullum ad solutionem eius cogunt. At Die vicesimâ quintâ eiusdem mensis sedent ad mensas in Sanctuario, & tunc illos qui nondum dederunt, ad solutionem cogunt, vel pignora sumendo, vel aliâ ratione oppignerando, & obligando. A Sacerdotibus pignora non sumunt, civilitatis causâ, sed siclos ab ipsis petunt donec persolverint. Ab Ethnicis & Gentilibus quamvis siclos afferrent, illos tamen non recipiunt.
units.tr: On the first day of February they proclaim concerning the shekels, that each should have his own ready. On the fifteenth day of the same month they sit at tables throughout all the provinces and quietly ask each person for the half-shekel, and compel no one to pay it. But on the twenty-fifth day of the same month they sit at tables in the Sanctuary, and then they compel those who have not yet given, either by taking pledges or by pledging and binding them in another way. They do not take pledges from priests, out of courtesy, but ask them for shekels until they pay. From Gentiles and foreigners, even if they bring shekels, they do not receive them.

units.la: In Provincia exactores Siclorum coram se habent duas arcas רחכן מלבטה ופיה צר מלכעלה quarum bases large erant, orificia vero angusta, ut sicli facilè indi sed difficulter eximi potuerint, in unam pendentes immittebant Siclos novos, i. e. illos qui pro illo anno debebantur; in alteram vero Siclos veteres, i. e. illos qui iam anno praeterito debebantur, sed nondum persoluti erant. In Sanctuario habebant tredecim cistulas,de quibus vid.Gazophylacion, ubi etiam usum Siclorum notavimus.
units.tr: In the province the collectors of shekels had two chests before them, whose bases were wide but whose mouths were narrow, so that shekels could easily be put in but with difficulty taken out. Into one they put the new shekels, that is, those owed for the current year; into the other the old shekels, that is, those already owed in the past year but not yet paid. In the Sanctuary they had thirteen chests, on which see Gazophylacion, where we have also noted the use of the shekels.

units.la: Sicli ita in Provincia collecti, per legatos in Sanctuarium mittebantur. אותם לצרף להם ויש בדינרי זהב מפני משואי הדרך Et ut facilius deferri possent, mutabantur in Denarios aureos, Mischna illam speciem monetae aureae vocat דרבונות Darbonoth.
units.tr: The shekels collected in the province were sent to the Sanctuary through envoys. And so that they could be carried more easily, they were exchanged for gold denarii on account of the dangers of the road. The Mishnah calls that species of gold coin Darbonoth.

units.la: Quoniam autem unusquisque tenebatur solvere hemisiclum, & facile accidere poterat, ut tunc hemisiclus ipsi non esset ad manus, monetam suam apud שולחני Mensarium, trapezitam mutare debuit, & aliquid ipsi pro mutatione dare ואותה התוספת נקראת קולבון & illud superadditum vocatur Collybum: & secundùm R. Meir est obolus argenteus, secundùm Sapientes verò, dimidia pars eius. A collybo exempti sunt Sacerdotes,mulieres,& parvuli. Qui affert siclum duplum & accipit siclos dimidios, tenetur dare duo Collyba. Qui permutat per pauperem, per vicinum suum, per concivem suum a Collybo liber est, si verò ipsis mutuò dedit, tenetur. Vid. plura apud Maymonidem.
units.tr: Since everyone was bound to pay the half-shekel, and it could easily happen that a half-shekel was not at hand, one had to exchange one's money with a money-changer, a mensarius or trapezite, and give him something for the exchange. This addition is called collybus. According to R. Meir it is a silver obol, but according to the Sages it is half of that. Priests, women and small children are exempt from the collybus. Whoever brings a double shekel and receives half-shekels owes two collybi. Whoever exchanges money through a poor man, through his neighbour, or through his fellow-citizen, is free from the collybus; but if he lent them the money, he is liable. More on this may be found in Maimonides.

units.la: SIGILLUM Dei vid. Deus.
units.tr: SEAL of God; see Deus.

units.la: Siloah שילוח fons situs à parte Hierosolymæ occidentali, at non longè ab angulo Occidentem & Aultrum respiciente. Vid.Ioseph. de bello lib. 5.cap.13 In tabulis itaque post Acram non post Sionem hic fons collocandus est, aliàs quomodo intelligeres illud Ioseph. lib.6.cap.38. Romani cùm subditiosos ex urbe inferiori abegissent, totam eam combusserunt μίχει ἐπὶ Σιλωὰμ usque ad Siloamum.
units.tr: Siloah [שילוח], a spring situated on the western side of Jerusalem, though not far from the corner that faces west and south. See Ioseph. de bello book 5, chapter 13. On the maps, then, this spring should be placed after Acra, not after Sion; otherwise how would you understand that passage of Ioseph. book 6, chapter 38: When the Romans had driven the seditious out of the lower city, they burned the whole of it [μέχρι ἐπὶ Σιλωάμ] as far as Siloam.

units.la: Vocatur hic fons etiam in Sacra Scriptura גיחון Gichon Vid.Paraph.Chald.ad 1.Reg.1.33.38. & Kimchium itl 1. erat itaque locus unctionis Regum, Vid.ap.Regem & Hierof.Sotah sol.22.3.
units.tr: In Sacred Scripture this spring is also called [גיחון] Gichon. See the Chaldee paraphrast on 1 Kings 1:33, 38, and Kimchi there. It was therefore the place where kings were anointed. See Regem and Hierosolymitanum Sotah, fol. 22.3.

units.la: Aquæ Siloami exhibuerunt typum regni Davidici. Chald. ad Esai.viii.6. Quia tedet hunc populum regni familiæ Davidicæ, quæ leniter illum traêtat, sicuti leniter labuntur aquæ Siloam.
units.tr: The waters of Siloam represented the kingdom of David. Chaldee paraphrast on Isaiah 8:6: Because this people despises the kingdom of the house of David, which treats them gently, just as the waters of Siloam flow gently.

units.la: Ex hoc fonte hauserunt Phialâ aureâ tria Log continente aquas in solenni lætitia festi Tabernaculorum. Vid. Festum Tabern.
units.tr: From this spring, with a golden flask holding three log, they drew water for the solemn rejoicing of the Feast of Tabernacles. See Festum Tabernaculorum.

units.la: Aquam etiam inde hauserunt, cùm aspergendus esset aliquis immundus admixto cinere. Parah cap.3.v.2. Sacerdotes etiam largiùs de sacris cibis comedentes, de huius fontis aquis biberunt concoctionis ergo. Aveth R.Nathan sol.9.1.
units.tr: They also drew water from it when someone unclean was to be sprinkled with water mixed with ash. Parah chapter 3, verse 2. Priests who ate large quantities of the holy foods also drank of the waters of this spring for the sake of digestion. Aveth R. Nathan fol. 9.1.

units.la: Simon שמעון est nomen Talmudicis usitatissimum pro שמעון. Notetur locus in Hierof. Schabbat sol.11.2. ר' אליעזר בעא מר סימון R. Eliefer quæsivit de re quadam à R. Simeone, at ille ei non respondit. Quæsivit à R.Iosua Ben Levi, atque ille respondit. Indignatus est R. Eliezer, quod R. שמעון Simeon non responderet &c.
units.tr: Simon [שמעון] is the most common name in the Talmud, in place of Shimon. Note the passage in Hierosolymitanum Schabbat fol. 11.2: R. Eliezer asked a certain matter of R. Simeon, but he did not answer him. He asked R. Joshua ben Levi, and he answered. R. Eliezer was angry that R. Simeon did not answer, etc.

units.la: Simeones celeberrimi fuerunt sequentes.
units.tr: The most famous Simeons were the following.

units.la: Simeon iustus qui floruit A. M. 3448. Hoc nomine insignitus fuit, ὃς ἦν ὁ ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν ... ἐπὶ τῆς ... ὁμολογίας ... ἱστορίας ... ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ... ὡς ἀναγεγραμμένος propter eius pietatem erga Deum, tum ob eius benevolentiam & humilitatem erga suos populares. Ioseph. Antiq. lib.12.c.2. Quòd Esræ successerit nemo dubitat, sed quidam dubitassent an Summus Sacerdos fuisset, nisi id asseruissent Iosephus & Inchasin p.13.2. Successit autem Esræ in præsideatu, Iehosuæ verò in Summo Sacerdotio: Esras enim Summi Pontificis munus nunquam obtinuit. Hic Simeon admodum longævus fuit: nam omnibus magnæ Synodi membris superstes fuit, & anno 40. post templi restaurationem, adhuc Alexandro magno in Palæstina vicrices copias circumagenti occurrere potuit. Historia exstat in Ioma sol.69.1. Ab ipso Alexander magnus petiit, ut in Sanctuario aureum sui monumentum collocaret, sed ob religionem id Simeon recusavit, ut tamen Alexandro aliquod μνημόσυνον poneret, promisit Iudæos ab illo die incepturos numerum in æra contractuum, & omnes filios illo anno nasciturōs, de nomine eius Alexandros appellaturos. Vid. Vorstii Zemach David p.59. Postquàm Simeon hic in Sacerdotio quadraginta circiter annos explevisset, dixit, Ego hoc anno sum moriturus. Petierunt abeo quem vellet in suum locum subrogari: respondit הנה בני נחונו Ecce filius meus Onias est coram vobis. Constituerunt ergo defunctō Simeone Oniam Summum Pontificem, sed invidit hoc ei Simeon frater eius,& ita incruduit contentio, ut Onias tandem ad montem regium & deinde in Ægyptum fugeret, ubi condidit Sanctuarium recitans illud Prophetæ; In die illo erit altare Domini in medio Ægypti. Iuchasin p.15. Hierof.lema sol.43. Quomodo post mortem Simeonis Iusti omnia in peius ruerint vid. Meffiam.
units.tr: Simeon the Just, who flourished in the year of the world 3448. He was marked with this name, [ὃς ἦν ὁ ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν ... ἐπὶ τῆς ... ὁμολογίας ... ἱστορίας ... ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ... ὡς ἀναγεγραμμένος], on account of his piety towards God and his kindness and humility towards his own people. Ioseph. Antiq. book 12, chapter 2. That he succeeded Ezra no one doubts, but some would doubt whether he was High Priest, were it not that Josephus and Iuchasin p. 13.2 affirm it. He succeeded Ezra in the leadership, but Jeshua in the high priesthood, for Ezra never held the office of High Priest. This Simeon was very long-lived: he outlived all the members of the Great Synod, and in the fortieth year after the restoration of the Temple he was still able to meet Alexander the Great, who was marching his victorious army through Palestine. The story is found in Yoma fol. 69.1. Alexander the Great asked him to set up a golden monument of himself in the Sanctuary, but Simeon refused on religious grounds; yet, so that Alexander might have some memorial, he promised that from that day the Jews would begin to number years in the era of contracts, and that all the sons born that year would be called Alexanders after his name. See Vorstius, Zemach David p. 59. After Simeon had spent about forty years in the priesthood, he said: I am going to die this year. They asked him whom he wished to be appointed in his place. He answered: [הנה בני חוניו] Behold, my son Onias is before you. So after Simeon's death they appointed Onias High Priest, but his brother Simeon envied him, and the quarrel grew so bitter that Onias at last fled to the royal mountain and then into Egypt, where he built a Sanctuary, citing the prophet's words: In that day there shall be an altar to the Lord in the midst of Egypt. Iuchasin p. 15; Hierosolymitanum fol. 43. On how everything went to worse after the death of Simeon the Just, see Messiam.

units.la: שמעון בן יוחנן Simeon fil. Schetah floruit A. M. 3621. fuit ille virtutis rigidus custos, & iustitiæ incorruptissimus administrator. Iuchasin p.15. Coram ipso rege Iannæo παρρησίαζων ausus est, & illius causa ab ordinaria regula ne latum unguem deflectere voluit. V.Sanhed. in Cohen gadol. Memorabile est ipsius factum,quo Ascalone uno die 80.fœminas veneficas suspendere curavit. Hierof.Sanhed. sol.23.3. & Bab. Sanhed. sol.44.2. in Gl. ædificatio Conclavis Gazith huic Simeoni tribuitur à pluribus, nos hactenus nullum huius assertionis fundamentum reperiimus.
units.tr: Shimon ben Yochanan [שמעון בן יוחנן], son of Shetach, flourished in the year of the world 3621. He was a stern guardian of virtue and a most incorruptible administrator of justice. Iuchasin p. 15. He dared to speak boldly before King Jannaeus himself, and for the sake of justice he would not deviate a hair's breadth from the ordinary rule. See V. Sanhedrin, under Cohen gadol. His famous deed was that at Ashkelon he arranged for eighty sorceresses to be hanged on a single day. Hierosolymitanum Sanhedrin fol. 23.3, and Babylonicum Sanhedrin fol. 44.2, in the gloss. The building of the upper chamber Gazith is attributed to this Simeon by many, but so far I have found no foundation for this assertion.

units.la: רבן שמעון בן של הלל Rabban Simeon filius Hillelis ad nominis celebritatem pervenit circa A. M. 3768. defuncto Patri in principatu successit circa annum Christi decimum tertium, quia pater eius à Chronologis tunc mortem oppetiisse dicitur. Notat tamen R. Gans in Zemach David sol. 36. neque initium neque tempus protractionis principatus eius hene notum esse, & verisimile esse ipsum diu non præsedisse. Ac sanè Iudæi admodum parcè de eo loquuntur, cùm aliàs Hillelis posteros diligenter satis recensere soleant; imò plàne ipsum reliquri
units.tr: Rabban Simeon [רבן שמעון בן של הלל], son of Hillel, came to fame about the year of the world 3768. When his father died he succeeded him in the leadership, about the tenth or thirteenth year of Christ, since his father is said by the chronologists to have met his death then. R. Gans in Zemach David fol. 36 notes, however, that neither the beginning nor the length of his rule is well known, and it is likely that he did not preside for long. Indeed the Jews speak of him very sparingly, although they are usually careful to list the descendants of Hillel; indeed they seem to have passed him over altogether,

units.la: videntur, nisi ad Genealogiam Hillelis contextendam ipso opus haberent. Quod fecit ut quibusdam suspicio inciderit, quasi ille Christum ulnis excepisset, & eius in Christum fides in causa fuisset quare deinde ipsum praeterierint.
