Addamus ad huius confirmationem, Chronologiae computum non refragari, & apud omnes receptum esse filium eius Rabban Gamalielem Apostoli Pauli praeceptorem fuisse. Hanc itaque sententiam sequi non dubitabimus, donec aliquis nos felicioribus maxillis mandere doceat.
units.tr: unless they needed him to complete the genealogy of Hillel. This has led some to suspect that he received Christ into his arms, and that his faith in Christ was the reason they afterwards passed him over. To confirm this, let us add that the reckoning of the chronology does not oppose it, and that it is generally accepted that his son Rabban Gamaliel was the teacher of the Apostle Paul. We shall therefore not hesitate to follow this opinion, until someone teaches us to chew it with better jaws.

units.la: R. Simeon Ben Gamaliel; post Patrem principatum obtinuit, sed ipso diu functus non est, fuit enim occisus in Hierosolymitana clade & devastatione, cum aliis novem itidem Doctissimis, quos ab Imperio occisos vocant. Iuchasf. f. 66.2 Zemach David ad A.3810. Boni publici sedulus fuit promotor Vid.cap.1.v.7. tradit. Ab eius morte aucta in funeralibus epulis sunt pocula, ita ut loco novem, tredecim deinde ebiberent, quem abusum Synedrium in lafne sedens correxit. Hierof.Beracot sol.6.1.
units.tr: R. Simeon ben Gamaliel obtained the leadership after his father, but he did not live long in it, for he was killed in the destruction and devastation of Jerusalem, together with nine other very learned men, whom they call those killed by the empire. Iuchasin fol. 66.2; Zemach David at the year 3810. He was a diligent promoter of the public good. See chapter 1, verse 7, tradition. After his death the cups at funeral feasts were increased, so that instead of nine they then drank thirteen; the Sanhedrin, sitting in the Lishkat ha-Gazit, corrected this abuse. Hierosolymitanum Berachot fol. 6.1.

units.la: De Simeone tertio Vid. Iuchasin p. 67. Vbique fermè intelligitur quando in Mishna, traditio absolute sub nomine R. Simeonis profertur. R. Meir eius Vice-praeses conatus est eum astu de gradu dejicere, sed irrito successu. Horaioth cap.3.
units.tr: On the third Simeon see Iuchasin p. 67. Almost everywhere when, in the Mishnah, a tradition is quoted absolutely under the name of R. Simeon, it is understood to be this one. R. Meir, his vice-president, tried by a trick to remove him from his rank, but with no success. Horaioth chapter 3.

units.la: SION. De eius situ Aben Esra ad Psalm. xlviii.
units.tr: ZION. On its location see Aben Ezra on Psalm 48.

units.la: 2. Mons Sion est a latere Hierosolyma Septentrionali, sic etiam lxx. Interpr. Iosephus etiam (qui eam non amplius Sionem, sed stylo post captivitatem Babylonicam usitato τὴν ἄνω πόλιν & τὴν ἄνω ἀγορὰν nominat) dicit turres Pse-phinum, Hippicum fuisse ab Aquilone, de bello lib.5. cap.12. & cap.13. & quidem adiunctas Regiæ,quæ in urbe superiore,Sione scilicet,erat,ut patet ex lib.2. de bello cap.39. quando infit Ioseph. Cestius venit tandem in urbem Superiorem (Sionem) & castra posuit contrà aulam Regiam.
units.tr: 2. Mount Zion lies on the northern side of Jerusalem; so also the Seventy translators. Josephus too (who no longer calls it Zion, but in the style used after the Babylonian captivity names it the upper city and the upper market) says that the towers Phasael, Hippicus lay to the north, de bello book 5, chapter 12, and chapter 13. Indeed they were joined to the palace which was in the upper city, that is Zion, as is clear from de bello book 2, chapter 39, where Josephus begins: Cestius finally came to the upper city (Zion) and pitched his camp opposite the royal palace.

units.la: Sionem cum templo coniungebat Pons Ioseph. de bello lib.2.cap.28. Antiq. lib.14.cap.8. In Sione etiam erat Domus Asmonæorum & Xystus. Idem ib.
units.tr: A bridge joined Zion with the Temple. Ioseph. de bello book 2, chapter 28; Antiq. book 14, chapter 8. In Zion there was also the house of the Asmoneans and the Xystus. The same, ibid.

units.la: שמע recitationem Phylacteriorum Vid. in Tephillin.
units.tr: Shema, the recitation of the Phylacteries. See under Tephillin.

units.la: בין השמשות Quid fit? Vid.Sabbathum. Possunt בין השמשות ✠ Demai decimas separare. Demai cap.1.4.
units.tr: בין השמשות: what is it? See Sabbath. They may [בין השמשות] separate tithes from demai produce. Demai chapter 1, section 4.

units.la: SODOMA. De eius legitimo situ vid. Mappa. A Sodoma ad Zoarem erant quatuor milliaria Hieros. Berac. fol.2.3. De ætate Sodomæ cùm periret vid. Bab. Schabb. fol.10. & 11.1. Iuchasin fol.8.1.
units.tr: SODOM. For its true location see the Map. From Sodom to Zoar there were four miles. Hierosolymitanum Berachot fol. 2.3. On the age of Sodom when it perished, see Babylonicum Schabbat fol. 10 and 11.1; Iuchasin fol. 8.1.

units.la: Lacus Sodomiticus distabat Hierosolymis stadiis ccc. i.e. circiter xxxviii. M.Pasl. Joseph. Antiq. lib.15. 9.
units.tr: The Sodomitic lake was three hundred stadia from Jerusalem, that is about thirty-eight Roman miles. Josephus Antiq. book 15, chapter 9.

units.la: Phrasis Talmudicorum Abdicare aliquid הים המלח in mare Sodomiticum; significat rem aliquam execrationi devotam, & qua nullâ ratione utendum exterminare, an proiectione ipsa in mare salsum, vel simplici sepositione ita non patet. Exempla huius locutionis habes in Hieros. Avoda Zarah fol.39.2. Hieros.Sotah sol.19.1. Nazir cap.4.4. Hierof. Demai sol.25.4.
units.tr: The Talmudic idiom to cast something away [הים המלח] into the Sodomitic sea means to devote a thing to execration, so that it must be destroyed and not used in any way; whether by casting it into the salt sea itself or by simply setting it aside, this does not clearly appear. Examples of this expression are found in Hierosolymitanum Avodah Zarah fol. 39.2; Hierosolymitanum Sotah fol. 19.1; Nazir chapter 4, section 4; Hierosolymitanum Demai fol. 25.4.

units.la: Ex Genef.xix.1. Et sedebat Loth in porta Sodomæ &c. eliciunt Hebræi, Lothum ibi sedisse ut Sodomæ Iudicem, sic Iarchius. Berefchit Rabba adhuc alios quinque Sodomæ Iudices facit יפ שקר Katz Sebakar, Rabb Schakar, Rabb מסשריך Misterin, Rabh גבל Gabal, & קלא מגרד Kola Pindar.
units.tr: From Genesis 19:1, And Lot sat in the gate of Sodom, etc., the Hebrews infer that Lot sat there as a judge of Sodom; so Jarchi. Bereshit Rabba makes five more judges of Sodom: Katz Sebakar, Rabb Schakar, Rabb Misterin, Rabh Gabal, and Kola Pindar. ## Dreams, see Insomnia.

units.la: Somnia vid. Insomnia.

Sorts. In officiis templi obeundis quævis munera ab initio obibant& distribuebant certando cursu (sed quoniam semel unus alterum de gradu altaris deturbaverat,ita ut cruseius fractum fuerit, & alia vice unus alterum cultro interfecerat, Synedrium ordinavit ut sorte ossicia distribuerentur, ut ita pacatius unusquisque suum munus capesseret Bab. Ioma sol.23.1.
units.tr: Lots. In performing the duties of the temple, the priests at first took up and distributed whatever tasks there were by competing in a race. But because on one occasion one man pushed another off the ledge of the altar, so that his leg was broken, and on another occasion one killed another with a knife, the Sanhedrin ordered that the duties be assigned by lot, so that each man might take up his task more peaceably (Bab. Yoma 23.1).

units.la: Locus ubi sortes projiciebantur erat Conclave Gazith, ea nimirum eius pars quæ in atrium extendebatur.
units.tr: The place where the lots were cast was the chamber Gazith, namely that part of it which extended into the court.

units.la: In cultu quotidiano ita sortem peragebant; Sacerdotes in unum collecti consentiebant de aliquo numero,qualiscunque placuerit. Deinde Præses cultus המונה alicuius Sacerdotis thiaram accipiens dicit, ab hoc incipiam numerare,elevate digitos; postquam sustulerunt digitos singuli,quot lubuerit, numerat digitos & illi addicit munus apud quem numerus finitus fuit. Maymon in Tamid cap.4. Vid. Cultus.
units.tr: In the daily service they carried out the lot as follows. The priests gathered together and agreed on some number, whatever number they liked. Then the president of the service, hamuneh [המונה], taking the turban of a certain priest, said: "I will begin counting from this man. Raise your fingers." After each of them had raised as many fingers as he wished, he counted the fingers, and assigned the duty to the man at whom the count ended (Maimonides on Tamid, ch. 4). See Worship.

units.la: In die expiationis verò Summus Sacerdos sumebat קלי κάλπιν & ipsi immitebat sortes aureas à Ben Katin confectas, nam anteà solùm erant אשכרינ ן Buxina (Ioma c.3.) & deinde שוף
units.tr: On the Day of Atonement, the High Priest took the urn [κάλπιν, kalpin] and put into it the golden lots made by Ben Katin; for before this they had been of boxwood (Yoma ch. 3), and then [...] [שוף].

units.la: טרף בקלפי Succussando urnam sortem eliciebat. Cùm sors projiciebatur pro duobus hircis, illa duplex erat, uni erat inscriptum לשם Domino i. c. hircus ille quem hæc sors diiudicat Deo debet offerri. Alteri verò inscriptum erat לעזאזל i. e. Hircus emissarius erit. Si Sors שלש Domini dexteram Summi Sacerdotis ascendisset, vicissius eius ipsi dicebat, dexteram in altum tolle, si verò ad sinistram ascendisset, dicebat sinistram tolle. Quo facto Summus Sacerdos sortes hircis imponebat dicens להשם Iomi c.4.1.
units.tr: By shaking the urn [bekalpi, בקלפי] he drew out a lot. When the lot was cast for the two goats, there were two lots. On one was inscribed for the Lord [לשם, lashem], that is, "The goat which this lot selects must be offered to God." On the other was inscribed for Azazel [לעזאזל], that is, "It shall be the scapegoat." If the lot for the Lord came up in the High Priest's right hand, his assistant said to him, "Raise your right hand on high"; if it came up in his left hand, he said, "Raise your left hand." When this was done, the High Priest laid the lots on the goats, saying for the Lord [להשם, lashem] (Yoma ch. 4, §1).

units.la: Spectacula etiam Iudæos habuisse ex his locis elici poterit, Avoda Zarah folio 16. in Misna, prohibetur ne Iudæi cum gentilibus tribunal aut אצרושא locum stadiorum coniunctâ operâ exstruant. At Gloss. Stadium est locus spectaculorum. Ita ibid. sol. 18. prohibent ne aliquis illa spectacula ingrediatur, in quibus præsligiatores suas ludicras artes exerunt, quod præsupponit ingressum aliorum spectaculorum fuisse permissum. Amphitheatrum splendidum, quod in Bab. Succah sol.51 2, vocatur דיפליוסטין habebant Iudæi Alexandriæ, quod qui non vidit לא ראה כבודן של ישראל Gloriam Israelis nunquam vidit.
units.tr: It may also be gathered from these passages that the Jews had spectacles. In the Mishnah of Avoda Zarah, folio 16, it is forbidden for Jews to build, in joint work with Gentiles, a tribunal or a place of games [אצרושא]. The Gloss says that a stadium is a place of spectacles. Likewise in the same tractate, folio 18, they forbid anyone to enter those spectacles in which conjurers perform their tricks, which presupposes that entry to other spectacles was permitted. The splendid amphitheatre, which in Bab. Sukkah folio 51b is called diplyston [דיפליוסטין], the Jews had at Alexandria; and whoever has not seen it has never seen the glory of Israel [לא ראה כבודן של ישראל].

units.la: Videtur tamen ludos illos publicos præcipuè institutos fuisse ab Ethnicis & Romanis postquàm Iudæos subegerant; & de illis sonat dictum in Avod.Zarah pag.18.2. Beatus ille vir. אשר לא הלך לשרטיאות ולקרקסיו של גוים Qui non ambit in theatra & circos gentilium. Ionatan in Deut. 28.19. videtur magis abusum quàm usum theatrorum reprehendere.
units.tr: Yet those public games seem to have been instituted especially by the Gentiles and the Romans after they had subdued the Jews; and a saying about them occurs in Avoda Zarah, page 18b: Blessed is the man [אשר לא הלך] who has not gone to the theatres and circuses of the Gentiles [לשרטיאות ולקרקסיו של גוים]. Jonathan on Deuteronomy 28:19 seems to rebuke the abuse of theatres rather than their use.

units.la: SPICILEGIUM Vid. ꝩ.
units.tr: SPICILEGIUM See ꝩ.

units.la: SPONSUS. Vid. Nuptiae.
units.tr: SPONSUS. See Nuptiae.

units.la: SPUTUM. Nemini licuit in monte templi sputum eiaculari. Maym. Hal. Beth Habech. cap.7. vid. Cultus.
units.tr: SPUTUM. No one was permitted to spit out saliva on the Temple Mount. Maim., Hal. Beth Habechirah ch. 7. See Cultus.

units.la: Si cui inter orandum obveniat sputum expuendum, excipiat illud palliolo Taller: si illud pulchrius & pretiosius fit, excipiat illud aut abstergat velo capitis, quod אפיקרסות & סודר nominatur. Beracot sol.24.2.
units.tr: If someone has to spit while praying, let him catch the spittle in his little cloak (Taller). If it would be more becoming and more costly, let him catch it, or wipe it off, with the head-veil called אפיקרסות and סודר. Berachot fol. 24.2.

units.la: Saliva quaevis in urbe inventa munda erat, exceptâ eâ quae in platea superiori reperiebatur, Schekalim cap.8.v.1. Ibi enim habitabant alienigenae qui aestimabantur immundi tanquam profluvio laborantes. Hinc patet sensus historiae quam refert R. Nathan in Avoth f.9.1. In die expiationis egressus est Israel Ben Camithi Summus Sacerdos, ut cum Duce quodam Ethnico colloqueretur; inter confabulandum sparsa est saliva ab ipsius Ducis ore in eius vestes; unde pollutus factus, non potuit illius diei ministerium subire, sed fratri suo hanc Spartam commitere debuit.
units.tr: Any saliva found in the city was clean, except that which was found in the upper street. For there lived foreigners, who were considered unclean like those suffering from a flux. Hence the sense of the story which R. Nathan relates in Avot fol. 9.1 becomes clear: On the Day of Atonement the High Priest Israel ben Camithi went out to speak with a certain heathen leader. While they were talking, saliva flew from the leader's mouth onto his garments. Made unclean by this, he could not perform the service of that day, but had to hand this duty over to his brother.

units.la: Ioh.ix.6. Christum adhibuisse salivam legimus, ad visum caeco restituendum, quia illa erat ordinarium pro aegris oculis remedium, ut patet ex Vaiikra Rabba sol.175.2. Nam ibi R. Meir simulans morbum oculorum, iubet foeminam pro remedio septies in ipsius oculos sputare. Item ex Maymonide cap.21. in Schabbat. ubi tradit illud remedium Sabbatho aegro applicare fuisse prohibitum, nec licuisse oculos nisi in diebus profestis salivâ illinire, ob reverentiam Sabbathi, quòd Medicinâ profanandum non erat. Sumsit Christus oculos sanaturus salivam, sed ut Iudæis ostenderet se plane aliâ vi & facultate sanare quam vulgò fieret, immiscuit salivæ pulverem terræ, quâ nihil magis oculis officit; & fecit ex his tale μύγμα quod etiam purissimum & optimum visum turbidum reddere & corrumpere potuisset, nisi Summi Medici omnipotens manus adfuisset, & miraculo hæc ita temperavisset, ut cæco salutaria fuerint.
units.tr: We read that Christ used saliva in John 9:6 to restore sight to the blind man, because this was the ordinary remedy for sore eyes, as is clear from Vayikra Rabba fol. 175.2. There R. Meir, pretending to have an eye disease, orders a woman to spit seven times into his eyes as a cure. Likewise from Maimonides ch. 21 on Shabbat, where he records that it was forbidden to apply that remedy to a sick person on the Sabbath, and that it was lawful to smear the eyes with saliva only on working days, out of reverence for the Sabbath, since it was not to be profaned by medicine. Christ, about to heal the eyes, took saliva, but to show the Jews that he healed by a power and virtue quite different from the usual one, he mixed dust of the earth with the saliva. Nothing harms the eyes more than this. From these he made such a mixture (myguma) that could have made even the purest and best sight cloudy and corrupt, had not the all-powerful hand of the supreme Physician been present and tempered this by a miracle, so that it was healthful for the blind man.

units.la: Conspuere aliquem erat signum comtemptûs. Vid. Calcei extraslio.
units.tr: To spit at someone was a sign of contempt. See Calceus, extraslio.

units.la: STATIONARII Viri. Sicuti ad cultum templi & oblationem sacrificiorum, viginti quatuor ordines tum Sacerdotum, tum Levitarum erant, ita quoque erant viginti quatuor ordines Israelitarum qui vocantur אנשי מעמד Viri stationarii. Et quamvis Sacra Scriptura illorum non fecerit mentionem, videntur tamen necessario requisitos fuisse ob sequentes rationes.
units.tr: STATIONARY men. Just as there were twenty-four orders of both priests and Levites for the worship of the Temple and the offering of sacrifices, so there were also twenty-four orders of Israelites called אנשי מעמד, stationary men. And although Holy Scripture makes no mention of them, they seem necessarily to have been required, for the following reasons.

units.la: I. Nemo poterat sacrificium offerre nisi ipse met adesset, & oblationi adstaret secundum Canon in Taanith cap. 4. & Maymon Kele Hamikdafch cap. 6. אין איפשר שיהיה קרבנו של אדם קרב והוא אינו עומד על גבין Impossibile est ut osseratur Sacrificium nisi adstet offerens. V. Sacrificia.
units.tr: I. No one could offer a sacrifice unless he himself was present and stood by the offering, according to the canon in Taanit ch. 4 and Maimonides, Kele Hamikdash ch. 6: אין איפשר שיהיה קרבנו של אדם קרב והוא אינו עומד על גבין, It is impossible for a man's sacrifice to be offered unless the offerer stands over it. See Sacrifices.

units.la: II. Erant Sacrificia pro integro populo oblata, qualia erant התמידין Sacrificia singulis diebus mane & vesperi offerenda, Hierof. Pesachim cap. 3. Quæ etiam ex publico thesauro comparabantur. Schekalim cap. 4. At quomodo omnes Israelitæ adesse potuissent in oblatione publicorum illorum Sacrificiorum? Plane itaque necessarium fuit, ut sicuti singulis diebus pro toto populo sacrificia offerebantur, ut etiam illis sacrificiis quidam à populo delegati adstarent; illi itaque erant Viri stationarii in 24. ordines distincti, & ex populo Ifraelitico lecti à Prophetis prioribus, ut notat Maymon ubi supra. Vnusquisque ordo habebat suum præsidem quem Talmudici vocant ראש המעמד Caput stationis.
units.tr: II. Sacrifices were offered on behalf of the whole people, such as the תמידין, the sacrifices to be offered every day morning and evening (Jerusalem Pesachim ch. 3), which were also paid for from the public treasury (Shekalim ch. 4). But how could all Israelites be present at the offering of these public sacrifices? It was therefore plainly necessary that, just as sacrifices were offered every day for the whole people, certain men chosen from the people should also stand by those sacrifices. These were the stationary men, divided into twenty-four orders and chosen from the Israelite people by the earlier Prophets, as Maimonides notes in the passage above. Each order had its own president, whom the Talmudists call ראש המעמד, head of the station.

units.la: Sicuti de Sacerdotibus retulimus quòd non omnes Hierosolymam simul ascenderint ad cultum peragendum unicâ, suo ordine officio fungentes, Ephemeria, sed quòd remotiores se conferrent in Synagogas, ut ibi lectioni & ieiuniis vacarent, idem nunc de his viris stationariis tenendum. Qui Hierosolymis erant & circa eas ad cultui vacandum in templum se conferebant, qui verò in locis magis dissitis, die secundo, tertio, quarto & quinto septimanæ in Synagogis collecti ieiunabant, & legebant cap. 1. & 2. Genef. ita illa dispescentes ut unicuique diei septimanæ suam assignarent partem; diebus autem 1. & 6. septimanæ ob Sabbathi gloriam non ieiunabant, quamvis scripturam in illis nihilominus legerint. Taanit cap.4. Maymon ubi supra.
units.tr: Just as we have said of the priests, that not all of them went up to Jerusalem together to perform the worship, but each order in its turn, which they called the ephemeria, while those who lived farther away gathered in the synagogues to devote themselves there to reading and fasting, the same must be held of these stationary men. Those who were in Jerusalem and nearby went to the Temple to attend to the worship, while those in more distant places gathered in the synagogues on the second, third, fourth and fifth days of the week, fasted, and read Genesis chs. 1 and 2, dividing these so that each day of the week had its own portion assigned. On the first and sixth days of the week, out of reverence for the Sabbath, they did not fast, though they nevertheless read Scripture on those days. (Taanit ch. 4; Maimonides, passage above.)

units.la: Hi viri stationarii itaque 1. ordinati erant ad repræsentandum populum in oblatione sacrificiorum: an etiam iacrificiis iugiter oblatis manus loco populi imposuerint in controversiam vocatum fuit; nos pro negativa stamus à Maymonide in cap.3. Corban. edocti, quòd sacrificiis pro tota congregatione oblatis nulla esset manus impositio, exceptis his duobus הער המשתלה
units.tr: So these stationary men were first appointed to represent the people in the offering of sacrifices. Whether they also laid hands on the continual sacrifices in place of the people has been disputed. We take the negative side, taught by Maimonides in ch. 3 of Corban, that in sacrifices offered for the whole congregation there was no laying on of hands, except in these two cases: the goat sent away (הער המשתלה, i.e. the scapegoat)

units.la: הטמאלה Hirco Emissario, הפר העלם ודבר & Iuvenco oblato pro peccato ignorantia. Hirco emissario manus imponebat Summus Sacerdos; Iuvenco vero tres viri à Synedrio ad id delegati Vid. Lev.4.13. Habent hanc regulam, quòd in publicis precibus & lectionibus in Synagoga ad minimum decem adesse debent, Megillah cap.4. Maymon in Tephillah cap.11. Quanto magis itaque in publicis actionibus templi semper honestus aliquis hominum numerus adesse debuit, ad Maiestatem cultus confervandam. Officium quidem erat uniuscuiusque Hierosolymae degentis his publicis orationibus & lectionibus interesse, interim timendum erat, ne si hoc inconstanti plebi simpliciter relinqueretur, ne forsan accideret, ut homines admodum rari adstarent. Consultissimum itaque visum est hos Viros Stationarios ordinare, qui semper & certò adessent. Adiuvabant insuper illos qui accedebant ad suas purificationes faciendas, ipsos partim dirigendo, partim verò in ipsum templum deducendo. Hoc praecipuè agebat stationis praeses audito instrumento quod Migrepha appellant Vid.Tamid. cap.5.
units.tr: and the bullock (הפר העלם ודבר) offered for a sin of ignorance. The High Priest laid his hands on the scapegoat, while three men appointed for this purpose by the Sanhedrin laid theirs on the bullock (see Lev. 4:13). They hold this rule: that at public prayers and readings in the synagogue there must be present at least ten persons (Megillah ch. 4; Maimonides, Tefillah ch. 11). How much more, then, must some respectable number of men always have been present at the public acts of the Temple, to preserve the majesty of worship. It was indeed the duty of every resident of Jerusalem to attend these public prayers and readings; yet they feared that if this were left simply to a fickle populace, it might happen that very few would stand by. It therefore seemed most advisable to appoint these stationary men, who would always and certainly be present. They also helped those who came to perform their purifications, partly by directing them and partly by leading them into the Temple itself. This was chiefly the task of the president of the station, who, upon hearing the instrument called Migrepha, did so. See Tamid ch. 5.

units.la: כל יום שיש בו הלל אין בו מעמד In illis diebus in quibus Cantant Hallel mane nulla est statio: itaque omnibus octo diebus festi Dedicationis à statione liberi sunt, quia in illis cantatur Hallel: vesperi etiam à statione liberi sunt, si sacrificio ordinario aliquod addebatur sacrificium. Taanith cap. 4.
units.tr: כל יום שיש בו הלל אין בו מעמד, On those days on which Hallel is sung in the morning there is no station. So during all eight days of the Feast of Dedication they were free from the station, because Hallel is sung on those days. In the evening too they were free from the station if some sacrifice was added to the ordinary sacrifice. (Taanit ch. 4.)

units.la: In illa Septimana qua viri stationarii vacabant cultui, non poterant à Tonsore radi, aut
units.tr: In that week in which the stationary men were devoted to worship, they could not be shaved by a barber, nor

units.la: lavare sua vestimenta; quia iam ante cæptum cultum hæc fecifle debebant.
units.tr: wash their garments, because they had to have done these things already before the worship began.

units.la: Stellas homines coluerunt tempore Enofi, ita ratiocinantes, Deus creavit stellas ad regendum mundum, honoris participes facit,& illis Ministris utitur; voluntas autem Dei est ut honoremus quem ipse evexit, Ergò ipsas laudare & honorare debemus; deinde templa iis ædificare ac sacrificare cœperunt. Progressu temporis etiam inceperunt, secundum Pseudoprophetarum effata, singulares revelationes mentientium, stellarum & syderum simulacra fabricare, & ea in templis adorare, ex huius cultus observatione omnia bona sperantes, & ex eius neglectu omnia mala metuentes. Ita ut tandem progressu temporis nomen venerabile(Iehovæ)ex omnium ore pericirit, exceptis illis Patribus quorum Sacra Scriptura mentionem facit: etiam Sapientissimi præter stellas alium Deum non noverant. Ita mundus volvebatur donec natus est columna Mundi, Abraham, qui anno ætatis 48. per idearum naturalium considerationem, verum Mundi Rectorem, Deum suum cognovit, contra Idololatriam incolarum Vr Chaldæorum disputavit, ipsorum simulacra confregit; tandem Rex ipsum occidere voluit, sed miraculo liberatus in Canaan venit, in qua plurimos in veram viam duxit, qui deinde vocabantur בית אברהם Domus Abrahami. Maymon in Hal. Avoda Zarah cap.1. Vid. Planetas.
units.tr: Men worshipped the stars in the time of Enosh, reasoning thus: God created the stars to rule the world, makes them sharers in his honour, and uses them as his ministers; but it is God's will that we honour whom he has exalted; therefore we ought to praise and honour them. Then they began to build temples for them and to sacrifice to them. As time went on, following the sayings of false prophets, the private revelations of liars, they also began to fashion images of the stars and planets and to worship them in temples, hoping for all good things from the observance of this cult and fearing all evils from its neglect. So that in time the venerable name (Jehovah) perished from everyone's mouth, except for those fathers of whom Holy Scripture makes mention; even the wisest men knew no god besides the stars. Thus the world went on until Abraham, the pillar of the world, was born. In the forty-eighth year of his life, through consideration of natural ideas, he came to know the true Ruler of the world, his God. He disputed against the idolatry of the inhabitants of Ur of the Chaldeans and broke their images. At last the king wished to kill him, but delivered by a miracle he came into Canaan, where he led very many into the true way; these were afterwards called בית אברהם, the house of Abraham. Maimonides in Hal. Avodah Zarah ch. 1. See Planets.

units.la: Sterilitas. De poculo tum contrà cùm pro sterilitate Vid. Schabbat folio 109. 2. & 110. 1. Rabbi
units.tr: Barrenness. On the cup, both against and in favour of barrenness, see Schabbat folio 109.2 and 110.1. Rabbi

units.la: Rabbi Salomoh Gen. 4. 23.
units.tr: Rabbi Solomon on Gen. 4.23.

units.la: אילונית sterilis est, quæ attigit annum vigesimum exceptis triginta diebus, & tamen nondum produxit duos pilos, & reliqua signa sterilitatis habet, quæ sunt אם אין לה דין Si nulla ubera habet, אם מתקשה בתשביש Si difficilis est in hora commixtionis, אם אין לה שיפולי מעים Si nulla est ipsi declivitas; & si tam crassa pollet voce ut à viro dignosci non possit. Maymon. Hal. אישות cap. 2. Alia sterilitatis signa circa ubera idem observat author, quæ in cap.cit. videre potes.
units.tr: An ailonit [אילונית] is a barren woman: one who has reached her twentieth year, not counting thirty days, and yet has not produced two pubic hairs, and has the other signs of barrenness. These are: if she has no breasts; if she is difficult during intercourse; if she has no curve of the hips or belly; and if her voice is so coarse that she cannot be told apart from a man. Maimonides, Hilchot Ishut ch. 2. The author notes other signs of barrenness concerning the breasts, which you may read in the same chapter.

units.la: De sterili Viro Vid. Eunuchus.
units.tr: On the barren man, see Eunuchus.

units.la: STERNUTATIO.
units.tr: SNEEZING.

units.la: Vsque ad tempora Iacobi fuit homo מה ומה עוטש Sternutans & moriebatur; posteà dixerunt homini sternutanti חיים טובים fit Salutiferum, & vivus mansit. Tanchuma Gen. 27. 1.
units.tr: Up to the time of Jacob there was a man who, when he sneezed, died [מה ומה עוטש, "sneezing and dying"]. Afterwards they said to a man who sneezed, "May you have a good life" [חיים טובים], and he remained alive. Tanchuma on Gen. 27.1.

units.la: Qui sternutat inter edendum, vetitum est dicere ipsi אסותא Salus, propter periculum Hierof. Berac. sol. 10. 4. Sternutatio prodest sanitati Beracot sol. 57. 2. Nisi sternutationes essent, homo egereret necessitates suas in vestimenta sua, nam admonetur illo eiaculandi impetu ut satisfaciat naturæ, ne pudefiat. Ben Sira Edit. Conft. sol. 27. 1. Quòd homines sternutando non amplius moriantur acceptum referunt precibus Iacobi. Chaskuni sol. 68. ad Genef. 48. 1. Cap. Eliezeris cap. 52.
units.tr: Someone who sneezes while eating must not be told "Health" [אסותא], because of the danger. Jerusalem Berakhot 10.4. Sneezing is good for health. Berakhot 57.2. If there were no sneezes, a man would soil his clothes with his necessities, for that ejaculatory impulse reminds him to relieve nature, so that he is not put to shame. Ben Sira, Constantinople edition, 27.1. The fact that men no longer die by sneezing is credited to the prayers of Jacob. Chaskuni, 68, on Gen. 48.1. Cap. Eliezer ch. 52.

units.la: STUDIA.
units.tr: STUDIES.

units.la: Quicunque nigredine afficit vultum suum ob studium legis in mundo hoc, Deus faciem eius lucere faciet in Mundo futuro. Sanhed. sol. 100. 1. מגמר בעתיקתא קשי מחדתא Discere antiquum difficilius est quàm novum. Ioma f.29.1. In studiis habendus unus præceptor, multitudo confusionem parit, Erubbin c.5. Hinc irridebatur Ioseph Bar Chaia כי מכוליה עלמא גמיר Quod בתרא זמור זמורתא à t o mundo disceret. Cholin c.1. תהא Doctrina perfecta (anticum est; i.e. famam ubique spargit. Beza sol.24.1. Manetque fama post mortem secundùm dictum כל תלמיד חכם שאומר דבר שמועה כפיו בעולם הוה שפתותיו דוממות נקבי Ievamot sol.97.1.
units.tr: Whoever darkens his face through devotion to the Law in this world, God will make his face shine in the world to come. Sanhedrin 100.1. Learning the old is harder than learning the new. Yoma f.29.1. In study one teacher should be had; a multitude of teachers brings confusion. Eruvin ch. 5. Hence Joseph bar Chaya was mocked, because he had learned from the whole world [כי מכוליה עלמא גמיר]. Chullin ch. 1. Perfect doctrine (it is the ancient one) spreads fame everywhere. Beza 24.1. And fame remains after death, according to the saying: every scholar who speaks a tradition from his mouth in this world, his lips move in the grave. Yevamot 97.1.

units.la: Studia nostra facienda sunt in Iuventute, quia tunc ingenium nostrum ita est comparatum, ut quicquid ipsi imprimitur simile sit לדיין על נייר חדש Atramento scripto in Charta nova. Avoth cap 4. Quamdiu quis quærit Sapientiam sapiens est æstimandus, כאשר יחשוב Cùm autem putat se ad finem eius perventsse stultus est. Ibid. שאלת החכמים חצי חכמה Interrogare Sapientes dimidia Sapientia est. Misch. Hapen. Ornatissimus Vir Rod. Rodolph harum literarum peritissimus, & olim noster præceptor, in Albo meo amicorum hanc elegantissimam de studiorum utilitate sententiam ex Schabbat sol.152.1. referente Elia in Thisbi apponere voluit. חכמים כל עור שהם מוקיניים חכמה נתוספת כהם ועשי הארץ כל עור שהם מוקינים טפשות נתוספת בהם; Bonarum literarum studiosi quò magis senescunt, eò quoque magis crescunt in scientia: At illiterati & plebei quò magis senescunt eò magis quoque stultescunt. De studiis plures sententias reperies apud Cl. Buxtorf. in Florileg.
units.tr: Our studies must be pursued in youth, because then our mind is so formed that whatever is impressed on it is like ink written on new paper. Avot ch. 4. As long as someone seeks wisdom, he is to be counted wise; when he thinks he has reached its end, he is a fool. Ibid. To ask the wise is half of wisdom. Mishnah Hapen. The most distinguished man Rodolph, most skilled in these letters and once our teacher, wished to write in my album of friends this most elegant saying on the usefulness of studies, taken from Schabbat 152.1 and quoted by Elijah in the Tishbi: "Learned men, the older they grow, the more wisdom grows in them; but the unlearned and common people, the older they grow, the more folly grows in them." More sayings on studies can be found in Buxtorf's Florilegium.

units.la: Suggestus. Quando in templo, scholis aut Syna- gogis,
units.tr: Platform. When they read, prayed, and blessed in the temple, schools or synagogues, they ascended the platform.

units.la: gogis, legebant, orabant, benedicebant, ascendebant suggestum. De benedicentibus in suggestu Levitis Vid. Targum in Cantic. 3.7. In Sotah foli.) 38 2. talis exstat Canon. Omnis Sacerdos שאינו עולה לדוכן Qui non ascendit suggestum po ulo benedicturus transgreditur tria praecepta affirmativa. Secundarius praeceptor in scholis, qui primarii Doctoris doctrinam diligentius observabat, & ab auditoribus repetebat vocatur ויש דוכנא in Bava Bathra folio 21. 1.
units.tr: (Synagogues.) They read, prayed, blessed, and ascended the platform. On the Levites who blessed from the platform, see the Targum on Cant. 3.7. In Sotah folio 38.2 there is this canon: every priest who does not ascend the platform [שאינו עולה לדוכן] to bless transgresses three affirmative precepts. The secondary teacher in the schools, who observed the chief teacher's doctrine more carefully and repeated it to the hearers, is called [ויש דוכנא] in Bava Bathra folio 21.1.

units.la: SUFFITUS definitur דבר שקושר ועולה וריחו נודף Res quae fumat & ascendit, cuiusque odor fragrans est Kerithut cap.1. sol.6.2.
units.tr: INCENSE is defined as "a thing that smokes and rises, whose odour is fragrant" [דבר שקושר ועולה וריחו נודף]. Keritot ch. 1, sol. 6.2.

units.la: Mosis non diserte expressit, quae & quot aromata ad suffitum sacrum adhibere debuerint, orali tamen traditione didicerunt ea esse undecim, nempe הצפורן צרי Resina praestans, Onyx, החלבנה Galbanum, הלבונה Thus, מר Myrrha, קציעה Casia, שבולת נרד Spica Nardi, כרכום Crocus, קושט Costum הקלופה Cortex odoratus, קנה Calamus odoratus, קנמון Cinnamomum. (eritur ubi supra; R. Salom. in Comm. his secundum Maymon. in Kele Hamikd. cap.2. addiderunt מלח סרומית Sal Sonomiticum, five Bitumen, כפת הירדן Ambram Iordanis, & מעלה עשן Herbam quae non ita nota est.
units.tr: Moses did not expressly state which and how many aromatics were to be used for the holy incense. By oral tradition, however, they learned that there were eleven: resin (tseri, צרי), onycha (הצפורן), galbanum (החלבנה), frankincense (הלבונה), myrrh (מר), cassia (קציעה), spikenard (שבולת נרד), saffron (כרכום), costus (קושט), cortex (הקלופה), sweet cane (קנה), and cinnamon (קנמון). R. Solomon, in his commentary on these, following Maimonides in Kele Hamikdash ch. 2, added salt of Sodom (מלח סרומית), that is bitumen, the balsam of Jordan (כפת הירדן), and the herb (מעלה עשן), which is not so well known.

units.la: Quomodo solebant fumigare in cultu ordinario templi Vid. Cultus. De thuribulo Vid. Templi vasa. Nemo poterat bis suffitum adolere, R. Chanina dicit, quia divitem facit, R. Papa vero illud ad benedictionem refert, qua ut omnes fruerentur, novi semper ad hoc ministerium antiquum difficilius est quàm novum. Ioma f.29.1. In studiis habendus unus praeceptor, multitudo confusionem parit, Erubbin c.5. Hinc irridebatur Ioseph Bar Chaia כי מכוליה עלמ גמיר Quod à tot mundo differet. Cholin c.1. במרא גמור זמורתא תהא Doctrina perfecta (anticum est; i.e. famam ubique spargit. Beza sol.24.1. Manetque fama post mortem secundum dictum כל תלמיד חכם שאומר דבר שמועה מפיו בעולם הוה שפתותיו דוכות :נקני levamot sol.97.1.
units.tr: On how they used to fumigate in the ordinary worship of the temple, see Cultus. On the censer, see Templi vasa. No one could offer incense twice. R. Chanina says this is because it makes one rich; R. Papa refers it to the blessing, so that all might share in it, and new men were always appointed to this ministry. Yoma f.29.1. In study one teacher should be had; a multitude brings confusion. Eruvin ch. 5. Hence Joseph bar Chaya was mocked, because he had learned from the whole world. Chullin ch. 1. Perfect doctrine (it is the ancient one) spreads fame everywhere. Beza 24.1. And fame remains after death, according to the saying: every scholar who speaks a tradition from his mouth in this world, his lips move in the grave. Yevamot 97.1.

units.la: Suggestus. Quando in templo, scholis aut Synagogis, legebant, orabant, benedicebant, ascendebant suggestum. De benedicentibus in suggestu Levitis Vid. Targum in Cantic. 3.7. In Sotah sol. 38 2. talis exstat Canon. Omnes Sacerdos שאינו עולה לדוכן Qui non ascendit suggestum po ulo benedicturus transgreditur tria praecepta affirmativa. Secundarius praeceptor in scholis, qui primarii Doctoris doctrinam diligentius observabat, & ab auditoribus repositus vocatur ויש דוכנא in Bava Bathra folio 21. 1.
units.tr: Platform. When they read, prayed, and blessed in the temple, schools or synagogues, they ascended the platform. On the Levites who blessed from the platform, see the Targum on Cant. 3.7. In Sotah folio 38.2 there is this canon: every priest who does not ascend the platform [שאינו עולה לדוכן] to bless transgresses three affirmative precepts. Salom. in Comm. his secundum Maymon. in Kele Hamikd. cap.2. addiderunt מלח סרומיר Sal Somomiticum, five Bitumen, כפת הירדן Ambram Iordanis, & מעלה עשן Herbam quae non ita nota est.
units.tr: Moses did not expressly state which and how many aromatics were to be used for the holy incense. By oral tradition, however, they learned that there were eleven: resin (tseri, צרי), onycha (הצפורן), galbanum (החלבנה), frankincense (הלבונה), myrrh (מר), cassia (קציעה), spikenard (שבולת נרד), saffron (כרכום), costus (קושט), cortex (הקלופה), sweet cane (קנה), and cinnamon (קנמון). R. Solomon, in his commentary on these, following Maimonides in Kele Hamikdash ch. 2, added salt of Sodom (מלח סרומית), that is bitumen, the balsam of Jordan (כפת הירדן), and the herb (מעלה עשן), which is not so well known.

units.la: Quomodo solebant fumigare in cultu ordinario templi Vid. Cultus. De thuribulo Vid. Templi vasa. Nemo poterat bis suffitum adolere, R. Chanina dicit, quia divitem facit, R. Papa vero illud ad benedictionem refert, quia ut omnes fruerentur, novi semper ad hoc ministerium designati fuerunt. Gemar.ad Ioma. cap.2.
units.tr: The manner in which they used to fumigate in the ordinary worship of the temple: see Cultus. On the censer see Templi vasa. No one could burn incense twice, R. Chanina says, because it makes a man rich. R. Papa, however, refers this to the blessing: so that all might share in it, new men were always appointed to this ministry. Gemara on Yoma ch. 2.

units.la: In aromatibus fufitus pugillandis admodum curiosi erant, hinc ut Summus Sacerdos illam accuratè disceret, pridie diei expiationis ducebatur in Conclave Abhtines, ut ibi in pugillatione se exerceret. Modus pugillationis recensetur à Gemara Bab.iii Ioma cap.4. Tribus digitis operuit Summus Sacerdos volam, & accepit pugillum; deinde ad craticulam aut patellam abrasit pollice quod supra, minimo digito verò quod infra erat.
units.tr: In the aromatic spices they were very particular about the handfuls to be pounded. Hence, so that the High Priest might learn this exactly, on the day before the Day of Atonement he was taken into the chamber Abhtines, to practise the pounding there. The method of pounding is recounted in the Babylonian Gemara on Yoma ch. 4: The High Priest covered his palm with three fingers and took a handful; then he scraped it onto the grate or pan with his thumb from above and his little finger from below.

units.la: Sadducæi in adolendo thymiamate innovationes introducere studuerunt. Vid. Sadducæi.
units.tr: The Sadducees tried to introduce innovations in the burning of incense. See Sadducees.

units.la: Supplicia. Poenæ quas inflixerunt iis qui licèt immundi ad sacrum cultum aut templum se ingerebant,sunt 1. מיתה בידי שמים Mors per manus Dei, 2. כרת Excidium, 3. מלקות flagellatio, 4. מכות כרדות flagellatio ob rebellionem, Vid. כרת in C. & fl gellatio.
units.tr: Punishments. The penalties they inflicted on those who, though unclean, pressed themselves into sacred worship or the temple are: (1) death at the hand of God (mors per manus Dei); (2) karet, excision; (3) malkot, flogging; (4) makkot marduot, flogging for rebellion. See karet under C., and flagellatio.

units.la: Supplicia capitalia quatuor Synedrio tradita sunt, Lapidatio, uslio, supplicium gladii & strangulatio. Sanhed.cap.7.
units.tr: Four capital punishments were handed over to the Sanhedrin: stoning, burning, the sword and strangling. Sanhedrin ch. 7.

units.la: De Lapidatione vid. in L.Supplicium omnium gravissimum est lapidatio. Qui duplici supplicio tenetur graviori plectitur. Sanhed. cap.9.3.4. Omnes lapidati secundùm R.Elieser em suspenduntur. Sanhed.cap.6. At Sapientes solummodò ad suspendium adiudicant Blasphemum & Idololatram ibid. & Maym. Sanhed.cap.15.
units.tr: On stoning see under L. Stoning is the most severe punishment of all. One who is liable to a double penalty is punished with the heavier. Sanhedrin ch. 9.3.4. All the stoned are, according to R. Eliezer, afterwards hanged. Sanhedrin ch. 6. But the Sages adjudge only the blasphemer and the idolater to hanging, ibid. and Maimonides, Sanhedrin ch. 15.

units.la: Vsitio ita fit, Damnatus fimo ad genua usque immergitur, tum collo eius circundatum סדר משה לתוך הרכת linteum durum molli involutum, hinc inde testes trahunt, donec aperiatur os eius, deinde ori eius infundunt liquefactum filum plumbi, quod descendens eius comburit intestina: hanc combustionem vocant combuftionem animae, & apud ipsos usitatior fuit combustione corporis quae appositis lignis fiebat. Vid. R. Levi in Levit.10. Si comburendus moriatur in manibus ipsorum qui eum strangulant, tum praecepto ustionis nondum est satisfactum, sed aperiunt os eius forcipe & metallum candens ori illiquant. Sanhed. c. 7. Hi decem rei sunt combustionis. 1. Sacerdotis filia quae fcortata est. 2. Qui concumbit cum propria sua filia.
units.tr: Burning is done thus: the condemned man is immersed in dung up to the knees; then a hard linen cloth wrapped in something soft is put around his neck. Witnesses drag him hither and thither until his mouth is opened. Then they pour molten lead into his mouth, which, going down, burns his intestines. They call this the burning of the soul. Among them the burning of the body, which was done by piling wood around the victim, was more common. See R. Levi on Leviticus 10. If the one to be burned dies in the hands of those who strangle him, the command concerning burning is not yet satisfied, but they open his mouth with tongs and pour molten metal into it. Sanhedrin c. 7. These are the ten who are liable to burning: (1) a priest's daughter who has played the harlot; (2) one who lies with his own daughter.

units.la: 3. Cum filia filiae suae. 4. Cum filia filii fui. 5. Cum filia uxoris. 6. Cum filia filii eius. 7. Cum filia filiae eius. 8. Cum socru sua. 9. Cum matre socrus. 10. Cum matre socceri. Sanhed. c. 9.
units.tr: (3) With the daughter of his daughter. (4) With the daughter of his son. (5) With the daughter of his wife. (6) With the daughter of her son. (7) With the daughter of her daughter. (8) With his mother-in-law. (9) With the mother of his mother-in-law. (10) With the mother of his father-in-law. Sanhedrin c. 9.

units.la: Supplicium gladii vocatur הרג & fit duplici modo, Aliquando caput ense secabatur כריך שהמלות עושה Sicuti more Regio fieri assolet, & in his regionibus in usu est; Aliquando vero caput impositum trunco securi praecidebatur, ut mos est Anglorum. Sanhed. cap. 7. Qui gladio puniuntur sunt Homicida, Incolae urbis ad idololatriam prolapsae; Homicida qui proximum suum percussit lapide ferrove, Sanhed. c. 9.
units.tr: Execution by the sword is called hereg and takes place in two ways. Sometimes the head was cut off with a sword, as is usually done by royal custom and is in use in these regions. Sometimes the head was placed on the trunk and cut off with an axe, as is the custom of the English. Sanhedrin ch. 7. Those punished by the sword are: the murderer; the inhabitants of a city that has fallen into idolatry; and the one who has struck his neighbour with stone or iron. Sanhedrin c. 9.

units.la: Strangulatio Heb. פנח fiebat ut dum de ustione, comburendum strangulari diximus. De illa habent hunc generalem Canonem כלמיתה אשור בחור פתם חנק Quando Scriptura non determinat poenam, sed simpliciter dicit morte morietur, illa poena de strangulatione intelligenda est. Maym. Sanhed. cap. 14. Sequentes strangulantur 1. Qui matrem patremve pulsavit. 2. Qui animam ex Israele furatus est. 3. Presbyter refragator, vid. Senex. 4. Vates mendax. 5. Qui vaticinatur in nomine idoli. 6. Qui cum alterius uxore concumbit. (at Ioh.8 5. volunt adulteram ex lege Mosis esse lapidandam? Vid. Adulterium. ubi haec difficultas solvitur.) 7. Qui familiam Sacerdotis falsò detulit. 8. Qui cum ea concumbit. Sanhed. cap.10.
units.tr: Strangling, Hebrew chenek (חנק), was done in the manner we said of burning, that the one to be burned was strangled. Concerning it they have this general canon: When Scripture does not determine the penalty, but simply says "he shall surely die", that penalty is to be understood as strangling. Maimonides, Sanhedrin ch. 14. The following are strangled: (1) one who strikes his father or mother; (2) one who steals a soul from Israel; (3) a stubborn elder, see Senex; (4) a false prophet; (5) one who prophesies in the name of an idol; (6) one who lies with another man's wife. (But in John 8:5 do they want the adulteress to be stoned by the law of Moses? See Adulterium, where this difficulty is resolved.) (7) one who falsely accuses a priest's family; (8) one who lies with her. Sanhedrin ch. 10.

units.la: Quod Suspendium attinet illud non nisi in lapidatis exercebatur; hoc modo. Trabs in terram depangitur, ex qua lignum extat, deinde revinctis manibus lapidatus suspenditur, & statim iterum tollitur, nec pernoctare sinunt: nisi quis id faciat honoris causâ ut paret ei capulum & involucra: sepeliebantur autem ordinarie in duobus Sepulchretis àSynedrio constitutis, ex quibus olim ipsorum, consumptâ carne, iterum in sepulchra patrum ipsorum deserebantur. Sanhed.cap.6. Secundùm Sapientes foemina non suspenditur, sed solummodò mas. ibid. Simeon Ben Schetach suspendit 80. venefica Ascalone unâ die Hierof. Sanhed. sol.23.3. & Bab.Sanhed. sol.44.2. In quo processu duo praecipuè notanda; Unum est, quod Simeon illas 80. mulieres supplicio suspendii puniverit, quod supplicium tamen in mulieribus exerceri non debuit, uti modò diximus & insuper apparet ex tradi. Sotah. Alterum verò est quòd Synedrium nunquam debuerit plures unâ die condemnare nisi velit perdendi auidum audiri; licebat quidem Synedrio, ut notat Maym. in Sanhed. c.14. singulis diebus aliquem suppli-cio cio afficere, & etiam condemnare; sed illum unitatis numerum in condemnatione transilire non debuit. At Simeon iudicavit,condemnavit, & supplicio affecit 80. homines unà die. Huius extraordinarii processus ratio tamen in promptu est : processerant enim fœminæ Ifraeliticæ ad talia flagitia,& tantoperead veneficia proruperant, ut necessarium omnino effet durum quid תעש pro temporis ratione, contra illud corruptum seculum decernere. Eas itaque suspendit ad exaggerationem exempli, & ad rem publicandam: atque hoc uno eodemque die,ne earum cognati aut alii homines, ad illas liberandas conspirarent.
units.tr: As for hanging, it was practised only on the stoned, and in this way: a beam is fixed in the ground, from which a piece of wood projects. Then the stoned man, with his hands bound, is hanged and at once taken down again; they do not allow him to stay overnight, unless someone does this for the sake of honour, to prepare for him a shroud and wrappings. They were ordinarily buried in two burial places appointed by the Sanhedrin, from which their bones, once the flesh was consumed, were later carried back to the tombs of their fathers. Sanhedrin ch. 6. According to the Sages, a woman is not hanged, but only a man. Simeon ben Shetach hanged eighty sorceresses at Ashkelon in one day: Jerusalem Sanhedrin fol. 23.3 and Babylonian Sanhedrin fol. 44.2. In this proceeding two things are especially to be noted. The first is that Simeon punished those eighty women by hanging, though that punishment ought not to be inflicted on women, as we have just said, and as also appears from the tradition in Sotah. The second is that the Sanhedrin ought never to condemn more than one in a single day, unless it wished to be heard as greedy for destruction. The Sanhedrin was allowed, as Maimonides notes in Sanhedrin ch. 14, to punish someone and even condemn someone each day; but in condemnation it ought not to skip over the number one. Yet Simeon tried, condemned and executed eighty men in one day. The reason for this extraordinary proceeding is nonetheless at hand. Israelite women had gone so far into such crimes, and had rushed so much into sorceries, that it was altogether necessary to decree something harsh [תעש] according to the circumstances of the time against that corrupt age. So he hanged them to make the example greater and to make the matter public; and this on one and the same day, lest their kinsmen or other people should conspire to free them.

units.la: Ceremoniæ ante & post supplicia adhibitæ sequentes fuerunt. 1. Deliberatio Iudicum debebat esse longa& matura. 2. Rei accusati collocabantur coram iudicibus in loco eminentiori, unde videri & audiri poterant, & testes accusantes è regione. Vid. 1. Reg. 21. 9. 10. hoc adhuc in usu in Anglia. 3. Iudices & testes imponebant manus suas capitibus damnatorum, & dicebant, Sanguis tuus fit super caput tuum. Confer Matth.27.25. 4. Damnatum præcedebat præco Vid. Lapidatio. 5. Antequàm damnatus occideretur,tenebatur confiteri sua peccata.
units.tr: The ceremonies applied before and after the punishments were as follows. (1) The judges' deliberation had to be long and mature. (2) The accused were placed before the judges in a more prominent place, from where they could be seen and heard, and the accusing witnesses opposite them; see 1 Kings 21:9-10. This is still the custom in England. (3) The judges and witnesses laid their hands on the heads of the condemned and said, Your blood be upon your head. Compare Matthew 27:25. (4) A herald went before the condemned man; see Lapidatio. (5) Before the condemned man was put to death, he was bound to confess his sins.

units.la: 6. Antequàm educeretur amarus quidam potus dabatur damnato איתא ליהרג משקין : קורט של לבונה בכוס של יין כדי שתשרף דעתו Ei qui ducitur ad mortem, prabetur granum thuris in poculo vini, ut alienetur mens eius, & ille ita pœnam minus sentiret. Maymon. Sanhed. cap. 13. Christo etiam dederunt ἐσμυρνισμένον οἶνον. olvot Marc.15. sed ipsum non sumpsit, uti nec acetum cum felle miscetum quod milites ad illudendum præbuerunt Matth. 27.34. 7. Omnia instrumenta, ut gladius quo aliquis fuit decollatus; arbor in qua aliquis fuit suspensus, linteum quo aliquis fuit strangulatus &c. fuerunt igne consumpta; ne aliquis posset diceret,hoc instrumento N. N. fuit interfectus. Vid. Misna & Maym. in Sanhed. 8. Extra urbem damnati puniebantur,ne Senatus videretur cædibus delectari, atque ut tractu temporis argumento innocentiæ reperto, posset liberari reus. Vid. Gloss.Bab.Sanhed.sol.42.2. Christus quoque extra Castra ad Crucifixionem deductus fuit. Interim tamen eius supplicium quoniam à tribunali Ethnico inflictum fuit in multis à Iudæorum more discrepabat.
units.tr: (6) Before he was led out, a bitter drink was given to the condemned man: one who is led to death is given a grain of frankincense in a cup of wine, so that his mind is dulled and he feels the punishment less. Maimonides, Sanhedrin ch. 13. They also gave Christ wine mixed with myrrh [ἐσμυρνισμένον οἶνον], Mark 15:23, but he did not take it; nor did he take the vinegar mixed with gall which the soldiers offered in mockery, Matthew 27:34. (7) All the instruments, such as the sword with which someone was beheaded, the tree on which someone was hanged, the linen with which someone was strangled, and so on, were consumed by fire, so that no one could say, "N.N. was killed with this instrument." See the Mishnah and Maimonides on Sanhedrin. (8) Those condemned were punished outside the city, so that the Senate might not seem to delight in bloodshed, and so that, with time passing and evidence of innocence found, the accused could be set free. See the Gloss, Babylonian Sanhedrin fol. 42.2. Christ too was led outside the camp to crucifixion. Yet, since his punishment was inflicted by a Gentile tribunal, it differed in many respects from the custom of the Jews.

units.la: 1. Enim flagellatus fuit, qui mos erat Romanis respectu crucifigendorum Vid. Iosephus de bello lib.2. cap.25.
units.tr: (1) For he was scourged, which was the Roman custom with regard to those to be crucified. See Josephus, De bello, book 2, ch. 25.

units.la: 2. Cum Christo duo Latrones fuerunt damnati, at ut iam innuimus אין דין שנים ביום אחד non iudicant duos eodem die, si legitimè condemnatio procedere debet. Sanhed.c.6.v.4.
units.tr: (2) Two robbers were condemned together with Christ; but, as we have already hinted, [אין דין שנים ביום אחד] they do not judge two on the same day, if the condemnation is to proceed lawfully. Sanhedrin c. 6, v. 4.

units.la: 3. Suspendendum non adegerunt ad suspendium, nisi propè adesset occasus solis, Gemara ibid. at Christus de capite iudicatus ante meridiem & meridie ad crucem actus. Ordinarie Synedrium suas incepit sessiones à tempore Minchæ matutinæ, & cum Mincha vespertina finiebat, & hac ratione exequutio iudicii ordinaria statim post finitum confessum sub vespera fiebat, ne esset הדין עינוי i.e. ne condemnatus longâ morâ affligeretur & languescaret,vid. Gloff.in Sanhed.sol.35.1. Interim Christus secundùm Marcum Hora tertia ad supplicium abigitur plane eo tempore quo Patres conscripti se ad Chagigæ festivitates parare debuissent. (Vid. Pascha.)
units.tr: 3. They did not compel anyone to hanging unless sunset was near (Gemara, ibid.). But Christ was condemned to death before noon and led to the cross at noon. Ordinarily the Sanhedrin began its sessions from the morning Minchah and finished at the evening Minchah, and so the ordinary execution followed immediately after the session ended, toward evening, so that the condemned would not be tormented and wither away through a long delay (ne condemnatus longâ morâ affligeretur & languesceret; see Gloss. in Sanhed. fol. 35.1). Meanwhile, according to Mark, Christ was led away to punishment at the third hour, precisely when the conscript fathers should have been preparing for the festivities of Chagigah (see Pascha.).

units.la: 4. Iudæi secundum Gem. sup.cit. מביתין אותו ואחר כך תולין אותו Damnatum primo morte assecerunt, & deinde in arbore suspenderunt; at mos Romanorum erat primò suspendere, & inde morte multare. Sic Christus primò in arbore fuit suspensus.
units.tr: 4. According to the Gemara cited above, the Jews first put the condemned to death and then hanged him on a tree; but the custom of the Romans was to hang first and then put to death. [מביתין אותו ואחר כך תולין אותו] Thus Christ was first hanged on the tree.

units.la: 5. Eduõos ad supplicium non aperte luxerunt, si scilicet Synedrium poenam infligebat. Vid. Lutum. At Christum luxerunt aperte. Luc. 23.27. Vna ratio discrepantiæ potest esse, quia interfectus fuit מהמלכות à Romanis, quò casu האבלות luctus licitus fuit. Altera ratio esse potest, quia secundùm Gloff. in Sanhed. c.6. v.ult. vulgò à Synedrio interfectos non publicè planxerunt, ut eius vilificatio, cùm nemo eum aperte plangeret, accrescere in interfectii expiationem. At qui Christum planxerunt melius de persona Christi edocti fuerunt. Sciebant summam eius iustitiam & integritatem expiatione opus non habere.
units.tr: 5. Those led to execution were not openly mourned, namely when the Sanhedrin inflicted the punishment (see Lutum.). But Christ was openly mourned (Luke 23.27). One reason for the difference may be that he was put to death by the Romans [מהמלכות], in which case mourning [האבלות] was lawful. Another reason may be that, according to the Gloss. in Sanhed. c.6 v.ult., those put to death by the Sanhedrin were commonly not mourned publicly, so that their contempt would, since no one mourned them openly, increase toward the expiation of the one killed. But those who mourned Christ were better taught about the person of Christ; they knew that his supreme righteousness and integrity needed no expiation.

units.la: An Poena כרת fuerit forensis an Stýλα@ vid. כרת in C. de vero sensu כרת & quotupliciter usurpetur vid.Cl.Heidegg. Exerc. de Vita Patriarch. pag. 64.
units.tr: Whether the penalty of כרת was a forensic one or [...]; see כרת in C., on the true sense of כרת and the many ways it is used; see Cl. Heidegg., Exerc. de Vita Patriarch. p. 64.

units.la: SUILLA CARO Vid. Porcos.
units.tr: SWINE'S FLESH. See Porcos.

units.la: SYNAGOGÆ non ædificari debuerunt nisi ubi essent decem literati, legis studiosi בשלין ostiantes, nullis mundanis negotiis distrifti sed ubi decem tales reperiuntur necessariò exstruenda est Synagoga. Maymon Tephillah cap. 11. talis locus deinde vocatus fuit עיר גדולה Vrbs magna &c. (vid. Urbes) Cur autem decem requirantur legis studiosi ut ibi esse possit Synagoga, rationem reddunt in Sanhed. cap. 4 6. quia עדה היא עשרה Omnis congregatio constat è decem, ut colligitur ex Num. 14. 17. nam deme Josuam & Calebum & restant tantùm decem.
units.tr: Synagogues were not to be built unless there were ten literate men, students of the Law, who were in attendance and not occupied with worldly business. But where ten such men are found, a synagogue must be built (Maymon Tephillah ch. 11). Such a place was then called עיר גדולה [ir gedolah] Vrbs magna, etc. (see Urbes). Why ten students of the Law are required for a synagogue to exist, they give as the reason in Sanhed. ch. 4 §6: Omnis congregatio constat è decem, ut colligitur ex Num. 14. 17. [עדה היא עשרה], nam deme Josuam & Calebum & restant tantùm decem. That is: an assembly consists of ten, as gathered from Num. 14:17, for take away Joshua and Caleb and only ten remain.

units.la: Ex his decem viris 1. tres Magistratum gesferunt, & vocabantur בית דין של שלושה Consessus triumviralis, qui in genere Synagogæ res procurabant, de minoribus litibus sententiam dicebant, vid. Sanhed. cap. 4. 1.2. Hi in Novo Testamento vocantur ἀρχισυνάγωγοι.
units.tr: Of these ten men: (1) three held the magistracy and were called בית דין של שלושה Consessus triumviralis [a triumviral court], who managed the affairs of the synagogue in general and pronounced sentence in minor lawsuits (see Sanhed. ch. 4 §§1–2). In the New Testament these are called archisynagogues [ἀρχισυνάγωγοι].

units.la: 2. Vnus ex his decem erat publicus Synagogæ minister, cuius officium erat publicè orare, de lectione legis curare, aliquando etiam concionari. Hunc communiter vocant שליח הצבור ὑπηρέτης τῆς συναγωγῆς, vel חזן הכנסת ὑπηρέτον τῆς συναγωγῆς, ὑπηρέτον autem five supervisorem ipsum vocarunt secundùm Aruch in חזן, quia ei incubuit animadvertere quomodo lector legeret, & quosnam ille evocaret ad legendum.
units.tr: (2) One of these ten was the public minister of the synagogue, whose office was to pray publicly, to see to the reading of the law, and sometimes also to preach. They commonly call him שליח הצבור [shaliach hatzibbur] or חזן הכנסת [chazzan hakkeneset], minister of the synagogue [ὑπηρέτης τῆς συναγωγῆς]. They called him ὑπηρέτης [hypēretēs], or supervisor, according to Aruch under חזן, because it was his charge to watch how the reader read, and whom he summoned to read.

units.la: 3. Post hunc considerandi veniunt tres פרנסים Eleemosynarii, quibus cura pauperum erat; duo ex illis vocantur שני גבאי צדק Exactores Eleemosynæ, (vid. Eleemos) non constituunt pauciores quam tres פרנסים, nam cùm iudicia pecuniaria transigantur à tribus, multò magis hæc, quæ vitam spirant à tribus fieri debent. Hierof. Peah. folio 21. 1.
units.tr: (3) After him come three פרנסים [parnasim], almoners, who had charge of the poor. Two of them are called שני גבאי צדק [two collectors of charity], (see Eleemos.). There are not fewer than three parnasim, for since monetary judgments are transacted by three, much more those which concern life must be done by three. Hierof. Peah. fol. 21.1.

units.la: 4. Octavus ex hoc decemviratu fuit התורגמן Interpres, qui verficulatim vernaculè reddebat quæ legebantur è fonte Hebræo. Ipsum instituit Esras postquàm populus in captivitate Babylonica ita Chaldeæ assueverat linguæ ut Hebræam non nisi cum difficultate intelligeret; vid. Hierof. Megillah sol. 7. 4. de Canonibus huius lectionis vid. Lectiones in L.
units.tr: (4) The eighth of this board of ten was the התורגמן [the targeman], Interpres, who rendered what was read from the Hebrew source into the vernacular, verse by verse. Ezra instituted him after the people, during the Babylonian captivity, had become so accustomed to the Chaldean language that they understood Hebrew only with difficulty (see Hierof. Megillah fol. 7.4). On the rules of this reading see Lectiones in L.

units.la: 5. Nonum & decimum Cl. Leigtfootus existimat fuisse Scholarcham Theologum & eius interpretem.
units.tr: (5) The ninth and tenth, Cl. Lightfoot thinks, were Scholarcham Theologum & eius interpretem: the theological head of the school and his interpreter.

units.la: §. In Synagoga conventum est die secundo & quinto septimanæ (de Sabbatho enim nulla est quæstio) quos dies deinde ימי הכנישה nominarunt, & fuerunt ex institutione Esræ Hierof. Megillah sol. 75. 1. Bab. Bava Kama f. 82. 1.
units.tr: §. In the synagogue they met on the second and fifth days of the week (for there is no question about the Sabbath), which days they then called ימי הכנישה [yemei hakhnisah]. They were instituted by Ezra (Hierof. Megillah fol. 75.1; Bab. Bava Kama fol. 82.1).

units.la: §. Antiquitus ædificabantur Synagogæ in agro Gemar. in Beracot sol. 2. 1. R. Afcher in eundem tractatum sol. 69. 3. sed sequentia tempora eas in urbes invexerunt.
units.tr: §. Formerly synagogues were built in the fields (Gemar. in Beracot fol. 2.1; R. Ascher on the same tractate fol. 69.3), but later times brought them into the cities.

units.la: §. Vnusquisque temporibus ad orationes statis frequentare debet Synagogam; Qui non orat cum congregatione vocatur שכן רע vicinus malus. Maymon in Tephillah cap. 8. Hinc nemo debet Synagogam præterire tempore orationum, nisi quid oneris in humeris portet; aut nisi sint plures in eadem urbe Synagogæ, nam tunc existimari potest eum ad aliam proficisci &c. Si verò capite gestet Phylacteria, tum ei præterire permissum est, eò quod illæ testentur eum non immemorem esse legis. Maymon Tephillah cap. 6. Beracot sol 8. 1.
units.tr: §. Each person should frequent the synagogue at the set times for prayer. Whoever does not pray with the congregation is called vicinus malus [שכן רע], an evil neighbour (Maymon in Tephillah ch. 8). Hence no one should pass by the synagogue at prayer time unless he is carrying some burden on his shoulders, or unless there are several synagogues in the same city, for then it may be supposed that he is going to another. If, however, he wears phylacteries on his head, it is permitted for him to pass by, since these bear witness that he is not unmindful of the Law (Maymon Tephillah ch. 6; Beracot fol. 8.1).

units.la: §. Diebus in quibus conventum est in Synagoga Minister Ecclesiæ septem, quos sibi visum est, ad lectionem evocat. Sacerdotem primò, deinde Levitam si modò adessent & post hos quinque Israelitas; sic Christus ad lectionem vocatus fuit Luc.iv.16. Aliquando etiam in Synagoga catechizabant. Gloss. in Bab. Beracot sol.17.1.
units.tr: §. On the days when the congregation meets in the synagogue, the minister of the church calls up for reading whomever he thinks fit, seven in all: first a priest, then a Levite if any are present, and after these five Israelites. Thus Christ was called up to read (Luke 4.16). Sometimes they also catechized in the synagogue (Gloss. in Bab. Beracot fol. 17.1).

units.la: §. In Sabbatho post prandium ibant ad בית מדרש Praelectionem Theologicam in qua aliquis Doctor auditoribus aliquid traditionale prælegebat & exponebat. Gloss. in Bab. Beracot sol.17.1. non quidem clara voce rem efferens, sed leni susurro Hebraicè in aurem interpretis mussitans, qui deinde id sonorè sermone vernaculo populo enuntiabat; ita Rabh fuit loco interpretis R.Schillæ, cùm alius nullus adesset Gloss. in Bab.Ioma sol.20.2. Confer Matth.x.27. De quæstionibus propositis cum R. Eliefer filius Asariæ ad principatum fuit promotus vid. Bava Metzia sol.59.2.Sotah cap.5. R. Eliefer filius Hyrcani in Beth Midrasch suas quæstiones thesium nostrarum instar suspenderat. De quæstionibus agitatis cùm R. Gamaliel à præfectura amoveretur Vid. Hierof.Berac. sol.7.4. Taanith sol.67.4. Bab. Beracot sol.27. Dum interpres sic perorabat sedit populus in terra, Gloss. ad Bab.Sanhed.sol.7.2. ad verba, Ne incedat index super capita populi sancti. Ad quorum verborum dilucidationem Nota, quòd ille qui feriùs in Synagogam veniebat, & classes illic ad pedes Doctoris sedentes circumibat, visus fuerit quasi per condiscipulorum suorum capita inceincedere, quod vituperio fuit, & talis vocabatur יום Megillah sol. 27.2. tardè venientem vero vocant יום in Beracot sol. 43.2.
units.tr: §. On the Sabbath, after the meal, they went to בית מדרש [beth midrash], the Praelectionem Theologicam, a theological lecture, in which some teacher read aloud and expounded something traditional to the hearers. He did not utter the matter in a clear voice, but murmured it softly in Hebrew into the ear of the interpreter, who then announced it resonantly in the vernacular to the people. Thus Rabh served in place of the interpreter R. Schilla when no one else was present (Gloss. in Bab. Ioma fol. 20.2). Compare Matt. 10.27. Concerning the questions proposed, when R. Eliezer son of Azariah was promoted to the principate, see Bava Metzia fol. 59.2 and Sotah ch. 5. R. Eliezer son of Hyrcanus had hung up his questions in the Beth Midrasch, like our theses. On the questions debated when R. Gamaliel was removed from office, see Hierof. Berac. fol. 7.4; Taanith fol. 67.4; Bab. Berachot fol. 27. While the interpreter thus harangued, the people sat on the ground (Gloss. on Bab. Sanhed. fol. 7.2) on the words ne incedat index super capita populi sancti, "let not the judge walk over the heads of the holy people." To clarify these words, note that the one who came late into the synagogue and walked around the classes sitting at the feet of the teacher seemed to walk over the heads of his fellow-disciples; this was a reproach, and such a person was given a special name (Megillah fol. 27.2). The one who came late they called by another name (Beracot fol. 43.2).

units.la: §. Synagogæ sexaginta & quadraginta erant Hierosolymis, quarum unaquæque habuit בית ספר למקרא Domum libri pro scriptura, id est, locum ubi legebatur Scriptura. Et בית תלמוד למשנה locum ubi docebantur traditiones. Vid. Megillah sol. 73.4. R. Salomoh in Esai. 2.1.
units.tr: §. Jerusalem had sixty or forty synagogues, and each of them had בית ספר למקרא Domum libri pro scriptura, that is, a place where Scripture was read, and בית תלמוד למשנה, a place where the traditions were taught (see Megillah fol. 73.4; R. Solomon on Isaiah 2.1).

units.la: Alexandrinorum Synagoga Hierosolymis erat celebris, de illa loquuntur in Hierof. Megillah sol. 73.4. Eleazar Ben Zadok accepit pretio Synagogam Alexandrinorum, atque in ea opera necessaria peregit. Alexandrini de suo illam exstruxerant. Erant autem illi Alexandrini artifices ærarii צורפי נחושת, & in templi usum si quid faciendum erat opera sua elocabant. Vid. Luchaf. sol. 26.2. Bab. Megillah sol. 26.1. Erachin sol. 10.2.
units.tr: The synagogue of the Alexandrians was famous at Jerusalem; they speak of it in Hierof. Megillah fol. 73.4. Eleazar ben Zadok took payment for the synagogue of the Alexandrians and carried out the necessary work in it. The Alexandrians had built it at their own expense. These Alexandrians were coppersmiths [צורפי נחושת], and if anything had to be made for the use of the temple, they let out their work for hire (see Luchaf. fol. 26.2; Bab. Megillah fol. 26.1; Erachin fol. 10.2).

units.la: §. Si incolæ alicuius civitatis vendiderint aliquam plateam, ex illa pecunia Synagogam ædificare possunt, sed non vice versa. Non vendunt Synagogam nisi sub hac conditione, ut si velint, illam iterum habere possint. Videntur Synagoga ad quasvis usus, præter quatuor, non venditur ut sit balneum, aut officina eoriarii; nec ad lotionem aut ut ibi sit congregatio aquarum. Si vastata fuerit Synagoga in ea lugere non licet; nec funus in ea suspendere, vel explicare retia, vel fructus super tectum eius expandere, nec per eam transire compendii causâ. Megillah cap 3.2.3.
units.tr: §. If the inhabitants of a city have sold some open space, they may build a synagogue with that money, but not the reverse. They sell a synagogue only on this condition, that they may have it back again if they wish. It is thought that a synagogue may be sold for any use except four: it may not be sold to become a bath, or a tanner's workshop, nor for washing, nor so that water may collect in it. If a synagogue has been laid waste, it is not lawful to mourn in it; nor to hang a corpse in it, or to spread out nets, or to spread fruit on its roof, nor to pass through it as a shortcut. Megillah cap. 3.2.3.

units.la: SYNEDRIUM. Præceptum de Synedriis obligabat solummodò quandiu Iudæi fuerunt in terra Sancta. Maymon.Sanhed.cap.i.
units.tr: SYNEDRIUM. The commandment concerning the Sanhedrins bound only as long as the Jews were in the Holy Land. Maymon. Sanhed. cap. i.

units.la: §. Hierosolymis erant tria Synedria; Primum erat Synedrium magnum סנהדרין הגדולה sedens in conclave Gazith (v.f.l.) & membra habens 71. Secundum erat in porta atrii Israelis, alterum vero בשער עזרת ישראל in porta atrii gentium; & hoc & illud senatores habebat xxiii. Extra Hierosolymam, in reliquis civitatibus etiam constituta erant בתי דינין Iudicia vel Sanhedrin modò 120. incolas locus habuerit, alias ipsis suffecit triumviratus. Ratio verò cur ad Synedrium xxiii. constituendum requiratur numerus 120. hæc est: quia primo 23. esse debent iudices, secundo tres series coram iudicibus sedentes numero 15, tertio decem בית הכנסת של בנלין sultu Synagoga vacantes. Quarto duo Scribæ. Quinto duo חזנים. ἄγγελοι τῆς ἐκκλησίας five ἀγγέλοι τῆς ἐκκλησίας. Duo item qui possint aliquam habere litem, duo testes, & duo qui testes falsi redarguere possint; tres qui Eleemosinas possint exigere & erogare. Vnus qui sit medicus, alius qui artifex, alius qui scriba, & unus qui fungatur officio Ludimagistri: qui omnes nisi ex numero 120. exsculpi non possunt. Maymon Sanhed. cap.i.
units.tr: §. At Jerusalem there were three Sanhedrins. The first was the great Sanhedrin [סנהדרין הגדולה], sitting in the chamber Gazith (so read) and having 71 members. The second sat at the gate of the court of the Israelites, and the other at the gate of the court of the Gentiles, [בשער עזרת ישראל]; each of these had 23 senators. In the other cities outside Jerusalem also, courts of judgment [בתי דינין] or Sanhedrins were established, of 120 inhabitants, where the place had that many; otherwise a triumvirate sufficed for them. The reason why a Sanhedrin of 23 requires the number 120 is this: first, there must be 23 judges; second, three rows of fifteen sitting before the judges; third, ten who sit idle in the synagogue [בית הכנסת של בנלין]. Fourth, two scribes. Fifth, two attendants [חזנים], the angels of the congregation [ἄγγελοι τῆς ἐκκλησίας]. Likewise two who may have some lawsuit, two witnesses, and two who can refute false witnesses; three who can collect and distribute alms. One who is a physician, another who is a craftsman, another who is a scribe, and one who performs the office of schoolmaster: all of whom cannot be picked out except from the number of 120. Maymon. Sanhed. cap. i.

units.la: §. In Senatum legebantur nobilissimi quique arte & doctrinâ celebres, moribus & legitimâ ætate prædicti. Quoad ortum legebantur ex Sacerdotibus, Levitis, ישראל הכהנים הראוין לשיא לכהונה Israelitæ quorum nobilitas ipsos aptos reddebat cum Sacerdotibus affinitatem contrahendi. Maymon Sanhed. c.2. Doctrinam quod attinet, debebant esse viri דיעה מרובה Scientia perfecta & multi linguae, debebant scire 70. linguas, Arithmeticam, Medicinam, Astronomiam, Astrologiam, Divinationes & Magicas artes, item cultus Idololatricos &c. ut de his omnibus accuratum edere possent iudicium. Maym. l. 9. Quoad staturam, Mores & aetatem secundum eundem authorem requirebatur 1. ut essent liberi ab omni vitio corporis, hinc claudi, lusci, monoculi erant incapaces huius supremae functionis. 2. ne essent nimis senes, senes enim saepe solent repuerascere, deinde יש בחן אכוריות ad crudelitatem magis vergunt quam ad humanitatem. 3. Ne essent Eunuchi ob eandem rationem. 4. Sed essent Patres liberorum, quia tales iudicabantur magis inclinare ad clementiam. Maymon. ibid. Quoad reliquas qualitates iudicum Vid. Exod. 18. 21. Deut. 1. 13. 16. Summus Sacerdos etiam potuit in Synedrium legi אם חיה ראוי בחכמה modo Sapientiâ praeditus esset. Rex vero non potuit membrum Senatus esse, שאסור לחלוק ולמרות את דברו quia prohibitum est ipsi in sententia dicenda contradicere. Maymon ubi supra. Caeremonia quâ hi seniores fuerunt electi & confirmati erat סמיכה quae fiebat carmine citato quod sonat הרי את סמוך ויש לך רשות לדון אפילו דיני קנסורת Ecce manus tibi imposita est, daturque potestas tibi iudicia exercendi etiam criminalia. Vid. Impositio manuum &c. & Maymon. Sanhed. cap. 4. Hi iudices promoti iam ante per aliquod tempus fuerunt separati ab aliis hominibus tali modo; Tres ordines Candidatorum (h. e. expectantium qui erant in singulis ordinibus viginti tres) coram Synedrio sedebant. Horum quisque suum sedes habebat locum. Si quem promoveri necesse fuit, exigeret ex primo ordine, is capiebatur. Tum primus secundi ordinis in primum ascendebat, ex tertio item in secundum; Denique ex coetu deletus aliquis in tertio ordine non quidem in locum primi, sed sibi convenientem collocabatur. Sanhed. c.4. §.4. Maym. c.1.
units.tr: §. The most noble men, distinguished for skill and learning, and endowed with good morals and lawful age, were chosen for the Senate. As to birth, they were chosen from the priests, the Levites, and the Israelites [ישראל הכהנים הראוין לשיא לכהונה] whose nobility made them fit to contract marriage with the priests. Maymon. Sanhed. c. 2. As to learning, they had to be men of [דיעה מרובה] perfect knowledge and many tongues; they had to know 70 languages, arithmetic, medicine, astronomy, astrology, divinations and magic arts, likewise idolatrous worship, etc., so that they could give an accurate judgment on all these things. Maym. l. 9. As to stature, morals and age, according to the same author, the following was required: 1. that they be free from every bodily defect; hence the lame, the blind in one eye, and the one-eyed were incapable of this supreme function. 2. that they not be too old, for old men often tend to become childish again, and then [יש בחן אכוריות] they incline more to cruelty than to humanity. 3. that they not be eunuchs, for the same reason. 4. but that they be fathers of children, because such men were judged to incline more to clemency. Maymon. ibid. For the other qualities of judges, see Exod. 18. 21; Deut. 1. 13, 16. The High Priest also could be chosen into the Sanhedrin, provided [אם חיה ראוי בחכמה] he were endowed with wisdom. But the king could not be a member of the Senate, [שאסור לחלוק ולמרות את דברו] because it was forbidden to him to contradict in giving sentence. Maymon, ubi supra. The ceremony by which these elders were chosen and confirmed was [סמיכה] the laying on, which was performed with the formula quoted, which runs [הרי את סמוך ויש לך רשות לדון אפילו דיני קנסורת] Behold, your hand is laid on, and you have authority to judge, even criminal cases. See Imposition of hands, etc., and Maymon. Sanhed. cap. 4. These judges, already promoted, had for some time before been separated from other men in this way. Three orders of candidates (that is, those awaiting, of whom there were twenty-three in each order) sat before the Sanhedrin. Each had his own seat. If someone had to be promoted, one was taken from the first order. Then the first of the second order moved up to the first, and likewise from the third to the second; finally, someone deleted from the assembly was placed in the third order, not indeed in the place of the first, but in a place suitable to him. Sanhed. c. 4. §. 4. Maym. c. 1.

units.la: §. In Synedrio tria officia praeter caetera admodum honorifica fuerunt;
units.tr: §. In the Sanhedrin there were three offices, besides the others, which were very honourable.

units.la: Primum erat principis הנשיא qui alias etiam מופלא dicitur propter insignem eruditionem qua praeditus esse debebat: eius definitio est בעל הרוש ובלמד תורה ברבים Ille qui legis publice interpretanda authoritatem habet. Quando in consessum ingrediebatur; non solùm capita aperiebant, sed & assurgebant, sicuti docet Mischna tract. Horaiot. cap.iii. Principe intrante omnis assurgit populus, nec iterum occupat locam nisi id dixerit. Quando Princeps è vivis discesserat, nudabant humerum utrumque, palàm in foro non spatiabantur, sed moesti apud familiares sedebant, ut refert Rambam in Hal. Ebhel. sepultura eius non vulgaris erat, comburebatur enim suppellex eius lignis odoratis condimentisque; Avoda Zarah p.11. Quemadmodum cremant propter reges, ita etiam propter Synedrii praesides: Quid autem comburunt? Lectum & utensilia ipsorum. Historia est, Onkelosum Proselytum propter R. Gamalielem 70. minas Tyrias combussisse.
units.tr: The first was that of the prince [הנשיא], who is also called [מופלא] on account of the outstanding learning he had to possess; his definition is [בעל הרוש ובלמד תורה ברבים] he who has authority to interpret the law publicly. When he entered the assembly, not only did they uncover their heads, but they also rose, as the Mishnah teaches in tract. Horaiot cap. iii.: When the prince enters, the whole people rises, nor do they sit again unless he has said so. When the prince had departed from the living, they bared both shoulders, did not walk about openly in the forum, but sat mournfully among their family, as Rambam reports in Hal. Ebhel. His burial was not ordinary, for his household goods were burned with fragrant woods and spices. Avoda Zarah p. 11.: As they burn for kings, so also they burn for the presidents of the Sanhedrin.
