What do they burn? His bed and his utensils. There is a story that Onkelos the proselyte burned seventy Tyrian minas for Rabban Gamaliel.

units.la: Secundum munus in Synedrio fuit אב בית דין Patris Senatus, qui sedebat ad principis dexteram; & eo absente præsidebat: definitio eius est הגדול שבדיינין והדיינין נפסקין על פי Judicum, antecessor, cuius ore lites decidiuntur; subintellige, fi absit princeps. Honore etiam magno prosequebantur ipsum, sed tamen non æquali cum Principe: quando enim intrabat senatum duabus solum surgentibus lineis excipiebatur, illis scilicet inter quas progrediebatur; contrà princeps Senatus ab omnibus surgentibus salutabatur. Item, Patre Senatus mortuo non humeros sed solùm sinistra denudabant brachia; insuper autem Academiæ vel Scholæ, quæ in illa urbe erant, vacabant, &, qui anteà Meridionalem locum obtinuerat, nunc ad septentrionalia pulpita demigrabat.
units.tr: The second office in the Sanhedrin was [אב בית דין] father of the court, who sat at the prince's right hand, and presided in his absence; his definition is [הגדול שבדיינין והדיינין נפסקין על פי] the greatest of the judges, the predecessor by whose mouth lawsuits are decided; understand, if the prince is absent. They also showed him great honour, but not equal to that of the prince: when he entered the Senate, he was received only by two lines rising, namely those between which he advanced; whereas the prince of the Senate was greeted by all who rose. Likewise, when the father of the court died, they bared only the left arm, not the shoulders; moreover, they left off the academies or schools that were in that city, and he who had previously held the southern place now moved to the northern benches.

units.la: Tertium honoris gradum possidebat ille quem Sapientem vocarunt; ille fuit ordinarie הגדול שנחכמים Doctorum præstantissimus, cum quo de agendis communicabant ut perito sensuum & rationum legis. In Senatu ad lævam principis sedebat: ingrediens verò itaexcipiebatur, ut unus surgeret alter verò sedéret.
units.tr: The third degree of honour was held by the one they called the Sage; he was ordinarily [הגדול שבחכמים] the most eminent of the teachers, with whom they consulted about matters to be transacted, as one skilled in the senses and reasons of the law. In the Senate he sat at the prince's left hand; and when he entered, he was received in such a way that one rose and the other remained seated.

units.la: Ninores Synedrii officiarii erant Scribæ & Littores. De Scribis loquitur Sanhed. c.4. Synedrium erat כחצי גורן instar areæ dimidiatæ orbicularent unus alterum contueri posset. Coram illis à dextra & læva stabant duo scribæ, qui absolventium & condemnantium annotabant sententias &c. De illis etiam fit mentio in Schabbat sol.56. 1. Littores triplici insigniuntur nomine, שוטר, סרדיוט, מנגרא De Schoterim sonat locus Maymon,Sanhed. cap.1. שוטרים sunt גוליירים חוכטין Lictores qui bacillis feriunt iussu iudicum inobedientes, proficiscuntur hi per vices & plateas, & diversoria, de ponderibus & mensuris curantes: verberantque prave agentes. Ast omne ipsorum opus est ex praescripto iudicum. Quemcunque male agentem vident, ad iudices adducunt &c. Ex quibus apparet falli Bertramum Rep.Heb.cap.5. quando vult שטרים vocari illos qui peritiores fuerunt & consultiores rerum iudicandarum reliquis senioribus. Et si ad hoc evincendum non sufficit dictum citatum, Vid. insuper Mosen Cotzeum ad Deut.xvi. Iudices, inquit, sunt senatores, qui decidunt causam, & שטרים הם הרודים את העם אחר מצותם במקל ורצועה Schoterim sunt illi qui regunt populum ex illorum praescripto cum bacub & loro. Vno verbo Schoterim Latinis sunt exactores, & Graeci illos vocarent ἐκβίβασ-ὰς & ἀράκτης. De סכרים loquuntur in Bab.Schabbat sol.32.1. Quicunque in Plateam egreditur דומה בעיניו כמי לסרדיוט de se reputet ac si iam raderetur lictori: Gloss. facile enim in aliquam incidere potest litem. De מנגרא Glossa loquitur in Bab.Ioma sol.15 1. quod sit lictor Synedrii ad flagellat. Romani lictores suum munus circumstantiis quibusdam oculis hominum magis ingerebant quam Iudaeorum ministri: Romani enim erant municipes, conditione libri, togâ ut reliqui Quirites utentes, sicuti ex Cicerone ad Pisonem apparet; Togula ad portas lictoribus praesto fuerunt, quibus illi acceptis fasces reiecerunt. At Iudaeos discrimen aliquod personarum habuisse, & conditionem in ministris publicis legendis respexisse, non constat. Huic adde lictorem Romanum in publicum præceßisse cum insignibus, maius quid simplici מקל baculo præscrentibus, illa erant fasces & virgæ; & si Dictator aliquis absque provocatione creatus erat, iubit ipsius Maiestas & in urbe fascibus iungere totidem tacito terrore secures. De simili maguificentia lictorum Synedrii quantum scio, nobis nihil relatum est.
units.tr: The lesser officers of the Sanhedrin were the scribes and lictors. The scribes are spoken of in Sanhed. c. 4.: The Sanhedrin was like a half-threshing floor [כחצי גורן], circular, so that one could see another. Before them, on the right and left, stood two scribes, who noted the sentences of those who acquitted and condemned, etc. They are also mentioned in Schabbat fol. 56. 1. The lictors are marked by three names: [שוטר], [סרדיוט], [מנגרא]. The place in Maymon, Sanhed. cap. 1 explains the [שוטרים]: they are [גוליירים חוכטין] lictors who strike with rods those disobeying the orders of the judges. They go about by turns through the streets, lodgings and inns, taking care of weights and measures, and they beat those who act wickedly. But all their work is according to the directions of the judges. Whomever they see behaving badly, they bring before the judges, etc. From this it appears that Bertram is wrong in Rep. Heb. cap. 5., when he wants those called [שטרים] to be those who were more skilled and more experienced in judging matters than the other elders. And if the quoted saying is not enough to prove this, see also Moses Kotzeus on Deut. xvi.: Judges, he says, are the senators who decide the case, and [שטרים הם הרודים את העם אחר מצותם במקל ורצועה] the Schoterim are those who rule the people according to their directions with a staff and thong. In one word, the Schoterim are in Latin exactores, and the Greeks would call them [ἐκβίβασ-ὰς] and [ἀράκτης]. The [סכרים] are spoken of in the Babylonian Schabbat fol. 32. 1.: whoever goes out into the street, let him think of himself [דומה בעיניו כמי לסרדיוט] as if he were already being shaved by a lictor; the Gloss says: for he can easily fall into some lawsuit. The Gloss speaks of [מנגרא] in the Babylonian Yoma fol. 15. 1., that it is the lictor of the Sanhedrin for flogging. The Roman lictors made their office more conspicuous to men's eyes by certain circumstances than the ministers of the Jews did: for the Romans were citizens, wearing the toga like the other Quirites by the condition of their freedom, as appears from Cicero to Piso: The lictors were present at the gates with togas, and when they received them, they threw aside the fasces. But that the Jews made some distinction of persons, and regarded rank in the choice of public ministers, is not established. Add to this that the Roman lictor went before the public with insignia, carrying something greater than a simple [מקל] staff; these were the fasces and rods; and if some dictator had been created without appeal, the majesty of his office was that, even within the city, the fasces were joined with as many axes, a silent terror. Of any similar magnificence of the lictors of the Sanhedrin, as far as I know, nothing has been reported to us.

units.la: §. De tempore sessionis Synedrii audiemus ipsum Maymonidem in Sanhed. cap.3. Quoto tempore sedent iudices in iudicio? Synedrium minus & consessus triumviralis, sedent à finitis precibus matutinis, usque ad finem horæ sexta: At Synedrium magnum sedet à sacrificio iugi matutino, ad sacrificium iuge pomeridianum. Atque Sabbathis & diebus festis sedit in בית Sacello, quod erat in atrio gentium. De conclavi Gazith in quo aliis temporibus sedebat vid. Conclave.
units.tr: §. On the time of the Sanhedrin's sitting, we shall hear Maimonides himself in Sanhedrin, chapter 3: For how long do the judges sit in judgment? The lesser Sanhedrin and the triumviral bench sit from the end of the morning prayers until the end of the sixth hour. But the great Sanhedrin sits from the morning continual sacrifice until the afternoon continual sacrifice. On Sabbaths and festival days it sat in the בית chamber, which was in the Court of the Gentiles. On the hall Gazith, in which it sat at other times, see Conclave.

units.la: De sessione ipsa pergit Maymon; Synedrium LXXI. non necesse habet ut sedeant omnes in loco suo qui est in templo. Cum vero necesse est ut congregentur omnes, congregantur omnes. Ast aliis temporibus, qui propria habet negotia, propriis negotiis vacet & tum redeat. Hoc provisio, quod non deficiat quid de numero viginti trium considentium continuo per totum tempus sessionis. Si cui necessarium sit exeundum, circumspiciat an collega sui sint viginti tres: si sint, exeat; sin minus, expectet usquedum intrat alter.
units.tr: Maimonides goes on to the sitting itself: The Sanhedrin of seventy-one is not obliged to have all of them sit in their place, which is in the Temple. But when all of them must be assembled, all are assembled. At other times, whoever has his own business attends to his own business and then returns. This is provided so that there is never a lack of the number of twenty-three sitting throughout the whole time of the session. If anyone needs to go out, let him look round to see whether his colleagues are twenty-three: if they are, let him go out; if not, let him wait until the other one comes in.

units.la: §. De actionibus Synedrii & earum modis Vid. Iudicia. Supplicia. הכחשה. Causa pecuniaria. בריקה.
units.tr: §. On the proceedings of the Sanhedrin and their modes, see Judgments, Punishments. הכחשה, refutation [hakhchashah]. Pecuniary cause. בריקה, beriqah [beriqah].

units.la: §. De Synedriis & consessibus quibusdam præstantioribus Vid. Consessu.
units.tr: §. On the Sanhedrins and certain more distinguished assemblies, see Assembly.

units.la: §. Discipulus Sapientis est sustentandus à concivibus suis. Bab.Ioma sol.72.2. Sic promotus in profecturam Synedrii à Synedrio est sustentandus & locupletandus. Vid.Gloss.in Bab. Taanith sol.21. Eligebant in præfecturam Synedrii non tam illum qui opibus aut dignitate antecelleret, quàm qui doctrinâ ac scientiâ: ita Hillel promotus fuit ad cathedram Synedrii, quia dubia quædam de Pascha solvere potuit. Hierof. Pesachin sol.33.1. sæpius etiam Summus Pontifex & Sacerdotes cùm is dignitate præcelleret & isti numero, acta in Synedrio præ omnibus aliis promoverunt, & omni nervositate prosecuti sunt, ut patet in actis Synedrii circa Christum, Paulum & Stephanum.
units.tr: §. A disciple of a sage is to be supported by his fellow citizens. Babylonian Yoma, folio 72.2. So one promoted to the presidency of the Sanhedrin is to be supported and enriched by the Sanhedrin. See the Gloss on Babylonian Taanith, folio 21. They chose for the presidency of the Sanhedrin not so much the one who excelled in wealth or rank as the one who excelled in learning and knowledge. Thus Hillel was promoted to the chair of the Sanhedrin because he was able to resolve certain doubtful points about the Passover. Jerusalem Pesachim, folio 33.1. Still more often the High Priest and the priests, when he surpassed them in rank and they in number, promoted the business in the Sanhedrin before all others and pursued it with all their vigour, as is evident from the acts of the Sanhedrin concerning Christ, Paul and Stephen.

units.la: §. Ex occasione verborum Iohan.xviii.31. Quando Iudæi dicunt Hμῖν ἀ ξεσιν ἀποκτεῖναι ἀ ἰδια &c. disputari potest, qualem Synedrium tempore Christi authoritatem habuerit, nam his verbis fatentur ipsi se capitale iudicium exercere non posse, & idem insuper faciunt in Hierof. Sanhed. sol.24.2. Traditio quadraginta annis ante vastatum templum ablata sunt iudicia capitalia ab Israele: Quæritur, quomodo illam potestatem amiserint? Non probabile est Romanos ipsos potestate illâ privasse, quomodo enim Pilatus ad ipsos dicere potuisset; Accipite eum, & secundum legem vestram iudicate eum. Serio loquitur, iocari aut iis irrideri non vult. Nos rem ita se habuisse credimus. 1. Certum est quòd ante Christi & circa ipsius tempora tam stolida fuerit lenitas Synedrii circa iudicia capitalia ut nunquam terme iudicium capitale exercuerit, præcipuè ob hanc rationem, quia horrendum videbatur Israelitam de femine Abrahami interficere. Sic Bava Metzia sol. 82.2. insurg t Iofua ben Korcha in R. Eliefer em, qui ceperat fures, dicens quousque tu tradis populum Dei nostri ad occisionem? relinque fentes erad candos Domino vinea. Huic fures erant populus Dei, relinquendi Dei iudicio, noli eos tangere. De tali lenitate quoque sonat locus in Maccoth sol.7.1. Synedrium a quo vel unus plectitur morte intra feptennium vocatur חבלין Destructorium. R. Eleafar dicit, imo a quo vel unus intra septuaginta annos.
units.tr: §. On the occasion of the words of John 18:31, When the Jews say, Ἡμῖν οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἀποκτεῖναι οὐδένα [It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death], etc., it may be debated what authority the Sanhedrin had at the time of Christ. For by these words they confess that they themselves cannot exercise capital jurisdiction, and they do the same in Jerusalem Sanhedrin, folio 24.2: Forty years before the temple was laid waste, capital judgments were taken away from Israel. The question is how they lost that power. It is not probable that the Romans themselves deprived them of it, for how could Pilate have said to them, Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law? He speaks in earnest; he does not wish to joke or be laughed at by them. We believe the matter stood thus. 1. It is certain that before Christ, and around his own time, the Sanhedrin was so foolishly lenient about capital judgments that it never once exercised capital jurisdiction, chiefly for this reason: it seemed a dreadful thing to kill an Israelite, a seed of Abraham. So in Babylonian Bava Metzia, folio 82.2, Joshua ben Korcha rose up against Eliezer, who had caught thieves, saying: How long will you hand over the people of our God to slaughter? Leave the thorns to be burned by the Lord of the vineyard. To him the thieves were the people of God, and they were to be left to God's judgment; he was not to touch them. The passage in Makkoth, folio 7.1, also speaks of such leniency: A Sanhedrin that puts even one man to death in seven years is called a destroyer (חבלין). Rabbi Eleazar says, nay, one that does so even once in seventy years.

units.la: 2. Hac ratione factum est,ut non solum omnibus vitiis laxata fuerit habena, præcipuè cùm accederent latrocinia militum, ut a Synedrio nec de incertis nec certis cædibus inquisitio fieri potuisset, ita enim creverat scelerum vis, ut leges silere debuerint; Tunc itaque cùm multiplicati essent homicidæ cessavit decollatio vaccæ rufæ. Sotah sol.47.1. Et cùm sub templo secundo multiplicati essent palam adulteri, dissolvit & abrogavit Synedrium probationem adulterae per aquas amaras. Maymon in Sotah cap.3.
units.tr: 2. For this reason it came about that not only was the reins loosened for all vices, especially when the robberies of soldiers were added, so that the Sanhedrin could make no inquiry into either uncertain or certain murders; for the force of crimes had so grown that the laws were bound to fall silent. Therefore, when murderers had multiplied, the ceremony of the broken heifer ceased. Sotah, folio 47.1. And when in the second temple adulterers openly multiplied, the Sanhedrin dissolved and abrogated the testing of the adulteress by the bitter waters. Maimonides, Sotah, chapter 3.

units.la: 3. Synedrium verò quandiu sedit in conclavi Gazith in ipso atrio Israelis coram altari, ipsa sanctitate & majestate loci quasi obligabatur ad rigidam iustitiam administrandam. Senatores itaque ut reatum effugerent, locum sessionis commutarunt a conclavi Gazith בחניות in Tabernas, quæ quidem quoque erant in monte templi, sed non ita prope apud Maiestastem divinam ac in conclavi Gazith. Statim itaque ac Synedrium non amplius sedit in Conclavi Gazith ceffarunt דיני קנסות Iudicia multitativa non solùm Hierosolymis sed & in tota terra Israelitica. Hoc nos docet Avoda Zarah sol.8.2. Chetubbot sol. 30.1. & Glossæ in utrumque loc. & hæc itaque est tatio consopitæ Synedrii authoritatis. Verba ergò ex Evangelista allata ita per paraphrasin sonant. Nofti ò Pilate, predecesforum nostrorum lenitate & hoc seculo malorum fertilissimo, ita nostram authoritatem propter intractabilem Sicariorum & latronum nequitiam vacillare, ut à sanguine & suppliciis nobis abstinendum sit.
units.tr: 3. But the Sanhedrin, as long as it sat in the hall Gazith in the very court of Israel before the altar, was bound, as it were, by the very holiness and majesty of the place to administer strict justice. The senators, therefore, in order to escape guilt, changed their place of sitting from the hall Gazith to the shops (בחניות), which were also on the Temple mount, but not so close to the divine Majesty as the hall Gazith. As soon as the Sanhedrin no longer sat in the hall Gazith, the fine cases (דיני קנסות) ceased, not only at Jerusalem but in the whole land of Israel. Avodah Zarah, folio 8.2, Ketubbot, folio 30.1, and the Glosses on both passages teach us this, and this is the reason for the decline of the Sanhedrin's authority. So the words quoted from the Evangelist, paraphrased, sound thus: You know, O Pilate, that through the leniency of our predecessors, and in this age most fertile of evils, our authority has so wavered because of the unmanageable wickedness of assassins and robbers, that we must abstain from blood and from punishments.

units.la: §. An autem Synedrium in conclavi Gazith nunquam redierit, ita definiri non potest: quantum ex Glossa in Chetubbot sol.30.1. patet, dicere possumus ipsum aliquando rediisse, sed nunquam משום דיני נפשות בירושלים propter capitale iudicium in causa homicidii. Tandem verò destructo templo & rebus conclamatis, ivit Synedrium Hierosolyma Iafnen: Iafne Vscham: Vscha Schepharamam: Schepharamà Beth Schaarim: Beth Schaarim Tsipporin: Tsippori Tiberiada. Bab.Rosch Hafchana sol.31.1.
units.tr: §. Whether the Sanhedrin never returned to the hall Gazith cannot be settled in this way. As far as the Gloss on Ketubbot, folio 30.1, makes clear, we may say that it did return at some time, but never on account of capital cases in Jerusalem [משום דיני נפשות בירושלים], that is, for a capital trial in a case of homicide. Finally, when the temple was destroyed and affairs were ruined, the Sanhedrin went from Jerusalem to Jabneh; from Jabneh to Ushah; from Ushah to Shefar'am; from Shefar'am to Beth Shearim; from Beth Shearim to Tsippori; from Tsippori to Tiberias. Babylonian Rosh Hashanah, folio 31.1.

units.la: T.
units.tr: T.

units.la: DE TABERNACVLORVM festo Vid. apud Festum.
units.tr: On the Feast of Tabernacles, see under Festum.

units.la: TABERNÆ תאניות erant in monte templi, & in illis sedit aliquandiu Synedrium. Rosch Hafchana sol.31.1. Avoda Zarah sol.8.2. Chetubbot thubhot £30.1. §. In monte Oliveto erant duæ cedri, sub una earum erant quatuor Tabernæ, ubi vendebantur omnia ad purificationes necessaria. Hierof. Taanith sol.69.2. illæ tabernæ in Hierof.Berachot sol.16.1. vocantur תניות בני חנן Taberna filiorum חנן Chanan. in Bab. Mezia sol.88.1. verò תניות של בית חינו Tabernæ ת Feth Heno, & si recte auguramur Bethaniæ, in qua tam frequenter versatus Christus.
units.tr: The TABERNAE (tenuoth) stood on the Temple Mount, and the Sanhedrin sat in them for some time. Rosch Hafchana fol. 31.1. Avoda Zarah fol. 8.2. Chetubbot fol. 30.1. In the Mount of Olives there were two cedars; under one of them were four shops, where everything needed for purifications was sold. Jerusalem Taanith fol. 69.2. In the Jerusalem Berachot fol. 16.1 these shops are called tenuoth bene Chanan, the shops of the sons of Chanan. In the Babylonian Mezia fol. 88.1 they are called tenuoth shel beth Chino, the shops of Feth Heno. If we guess rightly, this is Bethany, where Christ so often stayed.

units.la: Templum Hierosolymitanum.
units.tr: The Temple of Jerusalem

units.la: §. Nomina templi varia sunt, vocatur בית הקדש Domus sanctuarii, היכל Templum, בית הבחירה Domus electa; בית העולמים Domus seculorum, quia ex illo non fuit translata arca, ficuti ex Gilgal post annos 24. ex Siloh post 369. ex Nob post 13. ex Gibeon post annos 50. nominatur insuper מנין, ut in Cheritut cap.1.v.7. Ketubhot cap.3. Tosaphot.
units.tr: The Temple has various names. It is called beth hamiqdash, the house of the sanctuary; hekhal, the temple; beth habbechirah, the chosen house; and beth ha-olamim, the house of the ages, because the ark was never carried away from it, as it was from Gilgal after 24 years, from Shiloh after 369, from Nob after 13, and from Gibeon after 50. It is also named minin, as in Cheritut ch. 1 v. 7, Ketubhot ch. 3, Tosaphot.

units.la: §. Ædificatum fuit templum in monte Moriah, de quo vid. Montes. Spatium in quo stabat templum erat חמש מאות אמה Quingentorum cubitorum super quingentis cubitis, id est perfectum quadratum quod in summa continebat 2000. cubitos. Middot c. 2. Murus qui hoc cingebat spatium ex pulchris exstructus erat lapidibus: Ioseph. de bello lib.5. c.14. כותל המזרח Murus Orientalis ultra 6. cubitos altus non erat, ut Sacerdos comburens vaccam rufam in monte Oliveto, in Sanctuarium suprà hunc murum introspicere posset, at depressio illa muri non erat in omnibus eius partibus, sed tantùm in illis quæ respondebant portæ Orientali. Middot c.1.sec.1.& c.2.
units.tr: The Temple was built on Mount Moriah; see Montes. The enclosure in which the Temple stood was hamesh me'ot ammah, five hundred cubits by five hundred cubits, that is, a perfect square which in all contained 2000 cubits (Middot ch. 2). The wall that enclosed this space was built of fine stones (Josephus, Bellum lib. 5 ch. 14). The eastern wall was not more than six cubits high, so that the priest who burned the red cow on the Mount of Olives could look into the sanctuary over it. But this lowering of the wall did not apply to all its parts, only to those that faced the eastern gate (Middot ch. 1 sec. 1 and ch. 2).

units.la: §. De Portis templi Vid. Portas.
units.tr: On the gates of the Temple, see Portas.

units.la: §. Intrà Murum montis templi erant porticus in quibus poterant tempore pluviæ & caloris ambulare. Vid. Porticus. De his porticibus fit mentio in Schabbat sol.6.& sol.13. Maymon in Beth Habech. c.5. Ioseph. de bello lib.5.c.14.
units.tr: Within the wall of the Temple Mount there were colonnades where people could walk in rain and heat. See Porticus. These colonnades are mentioned in Schabbat fol. 6 and fol. 13, in Maimonides, Beth Habech ch. 5, and in Josephus, Bellum lib. 5 ch. 14.

units.la: §. In vel circa has porticus erant תחנות taberna (V.fl.) in quibus thus, oleum & sal vendebantur; & ne hoc nimio fieret pretio constituti erant quidam infpectores, de quibus Aruch in אגרטין.
units.tr: In or near these colonnades were the tanuoth, shops (taberna, V.fl.), where incense, oil and salt were sold. To keep these from being sold at too high a price, certain inspectors were appointed; see Aruch under agartin.

units.la: §. Structura templi Hierosolymitani à Salomone ædificati ex Sacra Scriptura patet, quare nos hic præcipuè ea dicemus quæ respiciunt templum ab Herode exstructum. Occasio cur Herodes illud opus fuscperit, erat, quia Senatores Synedrii interfecerat tempore Schammai & Hillelis, & hoc horribile factum aliquo beneficio expiare voluit. Vid. Baba Ben Butah. Tali itaque animi alacritate hoc opus aggressus est, ut templum fecerit μείζω τι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν largiori & ampliori circuitu, altitudine praestantiam, & novis fundamentis instructum. Ioseph. Antiq. lib.15.cap.14.
units.tr: The structure of the Temple built by Solomon is clear from Holy Scripture, so here we shall chiefly treat what concerns the Temple built by Herod. The reason Herod undertook the work was that he had put to death the senators of the Sanhedrin in the time of Shammai and Hillel, and he wished to atone for this horrible deed by some benefit. See Baba Ben Butah. He undertook the work with such eagerness that he made the Temple something greater in its assembly space [μείζω τι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν], with a larger and wider circuit, outstanding in height, and furnished with new foundations (Josephus, Antiquities lib. 15 ch. 14).

units.la: Anno ante natum Christum nono hoc ædificium fuit ad Colophonem perductum; octo annos ad ædificandum insumserunt, in quibus fi Iuchasin credendum sol. 19. nunquam illo in loco pluvia decidit, ne opera impedirentur. De huius ædificii magnificentia loquuntur in Succah.cap.5. in Gemara. Qui nunquam Hierosolymam vidit in gloria sua, nunquam vidit elegantem urbem; & qui nunquam vidit Sanctuarium, nunquam vidit pulchrum ædificium.
units.tr: In the ninth year before the birth of Christ this building was brought to completion. They spent eight years on the building, and, if we may believe Juchasin fol. 19, it never rained in that place during those years, so that the work would not be hindered. The Gemara in Succah ch. 5 speaks of the magnificence of this building: He who never saw Jerusalem in its glory never saw an elegant city; and he who never saw the Sanctuary never saw a beautiful building.

units.la: Huius templi mensura in longitudine habebat 200. cubitos & 100. cubitos in altitudine. Middot cap.4. repræsentabat formam Leonis, anteriora enim magis extendebantur quam posteriora. Middot ibid.Maymon in Beth Habbech.cap.4.5. Murus eius erat exstructus מאכני כחלא שו ex lapidibus marmoreis pulcherrimis colorum venis diversificatis. Gemara in Succah c.5. Vid. etiam Ioseph. Antiq. lib.15.c.14.
units.tr: The length of this Temple was 200 cubits and its height 100 cubits (Middot ch. 4). It represented the form of a lion, for its front parts extended further out than its back parts (Middot ibid.; Maimonides, Beth Habbech ch. 4, 5). Its wall was built of marble stones of the finest colours, with veins of varied hue (Gemara in Succah ch. 5). See also Josephus, Antiquities lib. 15 ch. 14.

units.la: Fundamentum האומ muri quod erat structura oppilata, extra terram prominebat altitudine sex cubitorum: sequebatur murus altitudine 40.cubitorum, (cuius lapides ita dispositi erant ut repræsentaverint אויתא דיפא Vndas maris. Gemara in Succah cap. 5. ) Deinde erat אמה כיור trabs inferior continuationis, obducta auro & figurata pulchris figuris latitudine & altitudine cubiti. [Aruch in כיור.] פלה אמתים בית הילפה Canalis ad pluviam derivandam duorum cubitorum. הקורה אמה locus coaptationis contignationis unicus cubiti. מעוברת אמה Contignatio ipsa unius cubiti.· In medio deinde surgebat העליית Cœnaculum altitudine quadraginta cubitorum, quod directè erat supra Sanctum & Sanctissimum. Hoc Cœnaculum etiam habebat הכיור trabem contignationis & canalem pluviatilem unius cubiti altam, ut & המעוברת laquear aut contignationem. מעקה Lorica verò erat trium cubitorum. Loricæ erat impositi tænia quæ erat lamina ferrea ad arcendas aves; Vid. כלח ערב in C. De his consule Middot c.4. v 6.
units.tr: The foundation of the wall, which was a solid structure, rose above the ground to a height of six cubits. Above it followed a wall forty cubits high, whose stones were so arranged that they represented the waves of the sea (Gemara in Succah ch. 5). Then came the lower beam of the continuation, amah kiyyor, covered with gold and adorned with fine figures, a cubit in breadth and height (Aruch under kiyyor). A canal to carry off rain, two cubits; the place where the beam was joined, one cubit; the contignation itself, one cubit. In the middle rose the upper chamber, ha-aliyah, forty cubits high, which lay directly above the Holy and the Most Holy Place. This upper chamber also had the beam of contignation, kiyyor, and a rain canal one cubit high, and the ceiling or contignation, ha-meubberet. The parapet, ma'aqeh, was three cubits high. On the parapet was placed a band, which was an iron plate to keep birds away; see Kelach Arav under C. On these matters consult Middot ch. 4 v. 6.

units.la: §. Latitudo templi erat 100. cubitorum
units.tr: The breadth of the Temple was 100 cubits.

units.la: Middot c.4. Crassities muri erat 5. cubitorum. Maymon in Beth Habech. c. 4.
units.tr: Middot ch. 4. The thickness of the wall was five cubits. Maimonides, Beth Habech ch. 4.

units.la: §. In medio Frontispicii templi erat Porta Porticus [Hebrew] altitudine 40. cubitorum & latitudine 20. Middot c.3. Maym.in Beth Habech. cap. 4. refert nullas ibi fuisse ianuas, sed quemvis per illum in templum introspicere potuisse : addit Ioseph. de bello lib.5. cap.14. [Greek] frontem totam fuisse deauratam. De reliquis portis vid. Portae.
units.tr: In the middle of the front of the Temple was the gate-porch, porta porticus, forty cubits high and twenty cubits wide (Middot ch. 3). Maimonides, Beth Habech ch. 4, reports that there were no doors there, but anyone could look into the Temple through it. Josephus, Bellum lib. 5 ch. 14, adds that the whole front was gilded. On the remaining gates, see Portae.

units.la: §. De Atriis & conclavibus templi Vid. Atria & Conclavia.
units.tr: On the courts and chambers of the Temple, see Atria and Conclavia.

units.la: Transfibimus nunc cogitatione nostra à parte templi Orientali occidentalem versus.
units.tr: Now in thought we shall pass from the eastern side of the Temple towards the west.

units.la: Primò ingredimur per Portam Susan & in ea observamus Figuram Susan Metropoleos Persicae, in subiectionis signum in illa sculptam suisse. Glosla in Middot cap.2. (V.f.l.) Ingressi videmus iuxta portam utrinque Tabernas, ab Austro nobis apparent portae Hulda, ab occidente porta Kipponos, ab aquilone porta Tedi.
units.tr: First we enter by the Susan Gate, and in it we observe a figure of Susa, the Persian metropolis, carved there as a sign of subjection (Gloss on Middot ch. 2). Once inside we see shops on either side of the gate. On the south appear the Hulda gates, on the west the Kipponos gate, and on the north the Tedi gate.

units.la: His consideratis in plano Atrii gentium ambulantes pergimus ad Portam Orientalem Atrii mulierum quae vocatur 'Ωραία. In hoc atrio etiam observamus porticus muro contiguas quales antea videramus in atrio gentium, sed hae non erant duplicatae sicuti in atrio exteriori. [Ioseph. de bello lib.5.cap.14.] In Austro huius atrii observamus portam unam, unamque ab Aquilone ; Ante Porticus posita erant Gazophylacia [vid.Gazophylacium] Quando respicimus ortum Brumalem in eo videmus Conclave Naziraeorum, siortum aestivum (conclave lignorum, si occasum æstivum, Conclave Leprosorum, si occasum Brumalem, conclave vini atque olei. Vid. atrium mulier. & Conclavia.
units.tr: Having noted these, we walk across the level of the court of the Gentiles to the eastern gate of the court of women, which is called Beautiful [Ὡραία]. In this court too we observe colonnades attached to the wall, like those we saw earlier in the court of the Gentiles, but these were not double as they were in the outer court (Josephus, Bellum lib. 5 ch. 14). On the south side of this court we observe one gate, and one on the north. In front of the colonnades stood the treasuries (see Gazophylacium). When we look towards the winter sunrise we see there the chamber of the Nazirites; towards the summer sunrise, the chamber of wood; towards the summer sunset, the chamber of lepers; and towards the winter sunset, the chamber of wine and oil. See atrium mulierum and Conclavia.

units.la: Perlustrato atrio gentium tendimus ad portam Orientalem atrii Israelis, ad illam ascendebatur ex atrio mulierum gradibus quindecim vid. Portas & Iosf. de bello lib. 5. cap. 14. Prope angulum orientalem ad latus meridionale huius atrii, erat Conclave Gazith; huic proximum fuit ab Occidente Conclave Scaturiginis: Huic contigua erat porta aquarum. Post hanc portam vero erat conclave ..., ulterius vero Porta Oblationis & Porta accensionis. A latere Septentrionali primò occurrebat Porta & Camera Nitsots, ubi Sacerdotes & Levitæ excubias egerunt. Proximum ei erat conclave lavantium & conclave Happarva: & deinde conclave Salis. Vid. conclavia. Per totum hoc atrium in plano pergimus & inde ascendimus in atrium Sacerdotum gradu uno altitudine cubitali: cui impositum pulpitum in quo cantabat chorus Levitarum, atque in eo erant etiam tres gradus, singuli cubiti dimidii, hoc atrium quoque dividebatur ab atrio Israelis capitibus trabium prominentibus.
units.tr: Having surveyed the court of the Gentiles, we make for the eastern gate of the court of Israel. One ascended to it from the court of women by fifteen steps (see Portas, and Josephus, Bellum lib. 5 ch. 14). Near the eastern corner, on the south side of this court, was the chamber of Gazith; next to it on the west was the chamber of the spring; adjoining it was the water gate. Behind this gate was a chamber ..., and further on the Gate of the Offering and the Gate of the Burning. On the north side, first we come to the Gate and Chamber of Nitsots, where the priests and Levites kept watch. Next to it were the chamber of the washers and the chamber of Happarva, and then the chamber of salt (see conclavia). Through this whole court we walk on level ground, and from there we ascend into the court of the priests by one step of a cubit's height. On this step was a platform on which the choir of Levites sang; on it were also three steps, each half a cubit high. This court too was divided from the court of Israel by the projecting heads of beams.

units.la: Per atrium Sacerdotum ambulantes reperimus altare, (Vid. Altare in A.) & deinde in spatio inter Altare & ... labrum (Vid. labrum in L.) Hoc spatium vero inter Altare & ... erat 22. cubitorum.
units.tr: Walking through the court of the Priests, we find the altar (see Altare in A.), and then, in the space between the altar and the ... laver (see labrum in L.). This space between the altar and the ... was 22 cubits.

units.la: Πρόναος est frontispicium templi de quo iam aliquid diximus. Ad Pronaon ex atrio Sacerdotum ascendebatur duodecim gradibus, singulis dimidii cubiti altitudine; Middot cap.3. de his gradibus sonat locus in Middot loco citato admodum difficilis; אמה אמה ורוב שלש אמה ואמה אמה רוב שלש והעליונה אמה אמה רבר ארבעה ad verbum, retraɛtio cubiti, retraɛtio cubiti, postea areola trium cubitorum; iterum retraɛtio cubiti, retraɛtio cubiti, deinde areola trium cubitorum, & supremus gradus post retraɛtionem cubiti, retraɛtionem cubiti, suit areola 4. cubitorum. Quæ per paraphrasin ita exponimus. Post unum cubitum erat spatiolum vel areola latitudine trium cubitorum, & ita post omnes, excepto ultimo, qui habebat areolam 4. cubitorum. Erat enim magnificum ut postquam gradus binos ascendisses, deinde aliquod haberes spatiolum in quo quasi requiesceres. Vid. Maymon. cap. 4. Beth Habechira versus finem. Ex his aliqua lux affertur verbis illis quæ in Ioma cap. 4. leguntur. מסרס בו על הרוב הרביעי של היכל quæ hoc sonant: Sacerdotem sanguinem miscuisse in areola quarta (graduum) templi. Iam hos gradus ascententes ingrediemur האולם pronaon cuius longitudo erat 100. cubitorum, altitudo 120. cubitorum, totam itaque reliquarum partium templi altitudinem superrabat 20. cubitis. Forsan apud Evangelistam Pronaon est πρόπυλον ιερόν, propter hanc suam eminentiam. Ex Iosepho iam retulimus Pronaon Ianuas non habuisse ut scilicet Cœlum apertum repræsentaret, totumque Portæ frontispicium fuisse deauratum. De Pronao itaque duo præterea notamus ; Primum est à Salomone in priori templo in eius introitu positas fuisse duas columnas Iachin & Boas de quibus Talmudici parùm aut nihil dicunt. Memorant solummodò inPronao ante portam Sanctuarii fuisse duas tabulas pro propositionis panibus; in marmorea ponebant panes in ingressu, & in aurea in egressu. In rebus sanctis enim ibant à minori ad maius. Beth Habech. Secundum est, Pronaon latius fuisse Templo quindecim cubitis à septentrione, & quindecim cubitis à Meridie, & spatium istud utrinque exuberans fuisse vocatum בית התליפות Locus cultrorum. Postquam enim Sacerdotes sacrificia mastaverant illic recondebant cultros & instrumenta ad mastationem inservientia. Vid. Middot c.4.v.7. Reconditoria illa in quibus cultri ponebantur erant numero 24. pro ratione viginti quatuor stationum Sacerdotum.Notat etiam Maymon in Kele Mikdasch cap.8. in templo adhuc 96. alias capsulas vel riscos intra parietem apparatos fuisse, ad recondenda vestimenta Sacerdotum, quos vocat תולות fenestras: & illis capsulis inscriptiones fuisse pictas hunc in modum מכנסים Caliga, אבנטים Cingula: אפנדה Infula. Vnaquæque Ephemeria Sacerdotum habebat suas capsulas assignatas, quas ad sacrum cultum feriâ diei Sabbathi accedentes aperiebant clavibus, necessaria vestimenta sumebant, ex hac femoralia ex illa cingula &c. & à cultu recedentes iterum claudebant. An verò illæ capsæ quoque in extremitatibus Pronai fuerint Maymon non notat; certè probabile non est, quo-
units.tr: The Pronaon (Πρόναος [Pronaos]) is the frontispiece of the temple, of which we have already said something. From the court of the Priests one ascended to the Pronaon by twelve steps, each half a cubit high. The passage in Middot chapter 3 about these steps, in the place cited from Middot, is very difficult. Word for word: a setback of a cubit, a setback of a cubit, then a landing of three cubits; again a setback of a cubit, a setback of a cubit, then a landing of three cubits; and the top step, after a setback of a cubit and a setback of a cubit, was a landing of four cubits [אמה אמה ורוב שלש אמה ואמה אמה רוב שלש והעליונה אמה אמה רבר ארבעה]. We explain these words by paraphrase thus: after every single cubit there was a little landing of three cubits in breadth, and so after all of them, except the last, which had a landing of four cubits. For it was a fine arrangement that, having climbed two steps, you had a little space on which you could, as it were, rest. See Maymon chapter 4, Beth Habechira, near the end. Some light is brought to this from the words in Ioma chapter 4 which read: מסרס בו על הרוב הרביעי של היכל [masras bo al ha-rov ha-revi'i shel hekhal], which mean: the priest mixed the blood on the fourth landing (of the steps) of the temple. Now, ascending these steps, we enter the האולם [ha-ulam], the pronaon, whose length was 100 cubits and height 120 cubits; it therefore rose 20 cubits above the height of the other parts of the temple. Perhaps in the Evangelist the Pronaon is the πρόπυλον ιερόν (sacred gateway), on account of this its prominence. From Josephus we have already reported that the Pronaon had no doors, evidently so that it might represent the open heaven, and that the whole frontispiece of the gate was gilded. Concerning the Pronaon, we note two further things. First: that in the former temple Solomon set two pillars, Jachin and Boaz, at its entrance, about which the Talmudists say little or nothing. They mention only that in the Pronaon before the gate of the Sanctuary there were two tables for the showbread: one of marble, on which they placed the loaves at the entrance, and one of gold, at the exit. For in holy things they went from the lesser to the greater. Beth Habech. Second: the Pronaon was wider than the temple by fifteen cubits on the north and fifteen cubits on the south, and this projecting space on either side was called בית התליפות [beth ha-taliphoth], the place of the knives. For after the priests had slaughtered the sacrifices, they stored there the knives and the instruments used in slaughtering. See Middot chapter 4, verse 7. These storerooms in which the knives were placed were twenty-four in number, according to the reckoning of the twenty-four stations of the priests. Maymon in Kele Mikdasch chapter 8 also notes that in the temple there were 96 other chests or recesses built into the wall, for storing the priests' garments, which he calls תולות [tolot], windows; and on those chests there were painted inscriptions in this manner: מכנסים [michnesayim], breeches; אבנטים [avnetim], girdles; אפנדה [efoddah], ephod. Each course of priests had its own assigned chests, which on the Sabbath day, when they came to the sacred service, they opened with keys; they took out the garments needed, from this one the breeches, from that one the girdles, and so on; and when they withdrew from the service they closed them again. Whether those chests were also at the ends of the Pronaon, Maymon does not say; it is certainly not probable, for

units.la: Sf 2 modo enim ad tam sanctum locum in quo nunc versamur absque vestibus sacris Sacerdotes ad illa induenda accedere potuissent?
units.tr: (for how could the priests have gone to put on their sacred vestments in so holy a place as the one where we now are, without the vestments?)

units.la: Memoriâ dignum est quod de חלנות capsula quibusdam in pronao referunt Middot cap.3. v.8. & Kimchi & Iarchi in Zachar.6. Scilicet in illis ad satisfaciendum textui Zach.6.14. quem literaliter intellexerunt, fuisse suspensas coronas, & Sacerdotes Iuvenes gestientes illas videre, repsisse per catenas aureas, in vestibulo Pronai suspensas, ut illas possent contemplari.
units.tr: It is worth remembering what some report about the חלנות [chalonoth], the chests, in the Pronaon: Middot chapter 3, verse 8, and Kimchi and Jarchi on Zech. 6. Namely, that in order to satisfy the text of Zech. 6:14, which they understood literally, crowns were hung up there, and young priests, eager to see them, crept up by golden chains suspended in the vestibule of the Pronaon, so that they could look at them.

units.la: Venimus nunc ad Portam templi, היכל dicunt scriptores Iudaei, strictius templi vocem intelligendo pro loco sanctiore. Porta templi altitudine erat 20. cubitorum, & latitudine 10. cubitorum, Middot cap.4.1. habebat quaternas valvas binas intus,& binas foris,exteriores aperiebantur intrà portam, tegendo muri crassitiem quae erat sex cubitorum; interiores verò aperiebantur intra aedem, obtegendo quod à tergo erat valvarum: quia tota aedes erat obducta auro,praeterquàm à tergo valvarum. Supra interiorem templi Ianuam erat aurea vitis quae mirè oculos aspicientium perstringebat, habebat notante Iosepho βότρυας ἀνάλογον ὕψος proportionem & magnitudinem hominis habentes. De bello lib.5. cap.14. haec vitis perpetuò augmentabatur, si quis enim uvas aut grana vitis voto voviisset, ex auro illa conficere curabat, & deinde supra hanc ianuam suspendebat. Supra hanc ianuam quoque pendebat aureum Candelabrum, quem templo dono dedit Helena Regina Adiabeni; Ioma cap.3. Exterior porta templi à Iudæis vocatur שער הגדול Porta magna : non quod interior non magna quoque essct, sed quia propter frontispicium maior videbatur. De hac porta duo præcipuè in scriptoribus Iudaicis obseruauimus. I. est Sacrificium iuge mane non fuisse mactatum, nisi cum mactator audiret stridorem & strepitum aperturæ Ianuæ magnæ.Tamid c.3. Maym.in Tamid. cap.6. II. Ipsos circa ipsius strepitum egregiè ὑπερβολίζειν; Vid. Hyperbole in H.
units.tr: We come now to the Gate of the temple, which the Jewish writers call היכל [hekhal], understanding the word temple more narrowly as the holier place. The gate of the temple was 20 cubits high and 10 cubits wide. Middot chapter 4, section 1, says it had four leaves, two inside and two outside. The outer leaves opened inside the gate, covering the thickness of the wall, which was six cubits; the inner leaves opened within the sanctuary, covering what was behind the leaves, because the whole building was overlaid with gold, except behind the leaves. Above the inner gate of the temple was a golden vine, which strikingly caught the eyes of those who looked at it; according to Josephus, it had clusters of grapes whose height and size were proportionate to a man. De Bello book 5, chapter 14. This vine was continually enlarged: for if anyone had vowed grapes or grape-berries, he took care to make them of gold and then hung them above this gate. Above this gate also hung a golden candelabrum, which Helena, queen of Adiabene, gave to the temple as a gift; Ioma chapter 3. The outer gate of the temple is called by the Jews שער הגדול [sha'ar ha-gadol], the great gate: not because the inner one was not also great, but because it seemed greater on account of the frontispiece. Concerning this gate we have noted two things especially in the Jewish writers. First: the continual morning sacrifice was not slaughtered until the slaughterer heard the creaking and noise of the opening of the great gate; Tamid chapter 3; Maymon in Tamid chapter 6. Second: they exaggerate greatly about its noise; see Hyperbole in H.

units.la: Intra has duas ianuas erat extensum velum; Vid. Vela. in V. & illo sublato apparebat locus Sanctus, qui quadraginta cubitos habebat in longitudine & viginti in latitudine, in hoc loco præter aurum splendescens nihil videbas; reliquum ornatum disce ex 1. Regum 6. & c. 7. & Kimchio in locos. Tria præcipuè memorabilia illic erant, Candelabrum totum aureum; Tabula in qua panes propositionis coram domino exponebantur, & altare suffitus: hæc duo erant solùm deaurata. De his tribus notandum quod dicit Iosephus de bello lib.5. c.14. Fuisse in Sancto τρία θαυμασιώτατα καὶ ἀξιόλογα πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἔργα, λυχνίαν, τράπεζαν, θυμιατήριον, Tria admirabilia opera & maximè apud homines celebrata, Candelabrum,mensam,altare suffitus.Septem Lampades Candelabri repræsentabant septem planetas; & duodecim panes in mensa propositionis referebant duodecim signa Zodiaci: altare suffitus qui partim ex mari partim è terra adferebatur denotabat omnia entia à Deo esse & ad ipsum respicere.
units.tr: Between these two gates a veil was stretched out; see Vela. in V. When it was lifted, the Holy Place appeared, which had forty cubits in length and twenty in breadth. In this place you saw nothing but shining gold; for the rest of the furnishings, learn from 1 Kings 6 and 7 and Kimchi on those passages. Three things especially worth remembering were there: the candelabrum, all of gold; the table on which the showbread was set out before the Lord; and the altar of incense. Only these two were merely gilded. Concerning these three, note what Josephus says in De Bello book 5, chapter 14: In the Holy Place there were three most admirable works, and especially celebrated among all men: the lampstand, the table, the altar of incense [τρία θαυμασιώτατα καὶ ἀξιόλογα πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἔργα, λυχνίαν, τράπεζαν, θυμιατήριον]. The seven lamps of the candelabrum represented the seven planets; and the twelve loaves on the table of the showbread represented the twelve signs of the zodiac; the altar of incense, which was brought partly from the sea and partly from the earth, signified that all things are from God and look back to him.

units.la: Quomodo candelabrum factum fuerit Vid. apud Maymonidem in Beth Habech. cap. 3. de modo Lucernas illas purgandi aliquid diximus apud Cultum templi in C. Vocantur candela Domini apud 1. Sam. 3. 3. Vid. Kimchium in 1. Sam. 3. R. L. B. & Gerfom ibid. His materialibus lucernis voluit Deus suum populum ad spiritualia lumina deducere; sed inter septem lampades nulla magis mystica erat quàm illa quæ appellatur Lucerna Occidentalis, quæ erat in medio omnium, vergens versus Sanctum Sanctorum; repræsentabat enim, inquit Baal Hatturim in Lev. 24. propter perpetuitatem sui luminis, Divinam præsentiam inter Israelitas habitare.
units.tr: How the candelabrum was made, see Maimonides in Beth Habechira chapter 3. We have said something about the manner of cleaning those lamps under Cultum templi in C. They are called the lamps of the Lord in 1 Sam. 3:3; see Kimchi on 1 Sam. 3, R. L. B., and Gersom there. By these material lamps God wished to lead his people to spiritual lights. But among the seven lamps none was more mystical than that called the Western Lamp, which stood in the middle of all, facing toward the Holy of Holies. For, says Baal Hatturim on Lev. 24, because of the perpetuity of its light, it represented the divine presence dwelling among the Israelites.

units.la: Candelabrum positum erat in latere meridionali sancti; ita tamen ut ramos suos in meridiem & septentrionem spargeret. In latere septentrionali vero collocata erat mensa panum propositionis; in Tabernaculo Mosis tabula illa in longitudine habebat duos cubitos, & in latitudine cubitum cum dimidio, Exodi 25. 23. in templo secundo vero in latitudine cubitum habebat; Maymon in Beth Habech. cap. 3. in sancto stabat secundùm suam longitudinem Orientem & Occidentem respiciens. Cincta erat coronâ aurea ad repræsentandam coronam regni. Baal Hatturim Exod. 25.
units.tr: The candelabrum stood on the south side of the Holy Place, yet so that its branches spread toward the south and the north. On the north side was placed the table of the showbread. In the Tabernacle of Moses that table was two cubits long and a cubit and a half broad (Exod. 25:23); in the second temple, however, it was one cubit in breadth. Maymon in Beth Habech. chapter 3: in the Holy Place it stood, according to its length, facing east and west. It was encircled with a golden crown, to represent the crown of the kingdom. Baal Hatturim on Exod. 25.

units.la: Panes propositionis pinsebantur ex 24. Seah nxd, figuram habebant quadratam, 10. palmas in longitudine, & 5. in latitudine, crassi erant 7. digitos: coquebantur in Beth Mokad. Maymon in Temidin cap. 5. Die Sabbathi illos tabulæ hunc in modum imponebant. Quátuor Sacerdotes ingrediebantur ad panes propositionis, qui per totam septimanam coram Domino positi erant, exportandos, & alii quatuor novos inferebant, dum illi quatuor veteres panes sumebant, hi 4. novos apponebant, ita ut tabula absque panibus nunquam relinqueretur. Sex ponebant in unum cumulum & deinde alios sex separatim accumulabant, sed observatis in utraque serie his duabus conditionibus. 1. est quòd posuerint panes fecundum longitudinem suam supra mensam, ita ut utrinque duarum palmarum latitudine extrà mensam prominerent. 2. est quòd primam placentam pofuerint immediatè supra mensam, sed inter reliquas posuerunt tres baculos ex auro factos ut impediretur mucor. &c.
units.tr: The showbread was kneaded from 24 seahs of flour. It was square, 10 palms long and 5 palms wide, and 7 fingers thick. It was baked in Beth Mokad, as Maimonides says in Temidin ch. 5. On the Sabbath day they set the loaves on the table in this manner. Four priests entered to take away the showbread, which had stood before the Lord all week, and four others brought in new loaves. While the first four took the old loaves, these four set the new ones in place, so that the table was never left without bread. They placed six loaves in one pile and then piled six others separately, but in each row two conditions were observed: (1) they laid the loaves lengthwise on the table, so that on each side they projected two palms beyond its edge; (2) they set the first cake directly on the table, but between the rest they placed three rods made of gold, so that mould would be prevented. Etc.

units.la: Consideravimus candelabrum cum mensa panum propositionis, nunc accedamus ad altare suffitus; illud erat בשלש התיכל in tertia parte loci sancti inquit Maymon in Beth Habech.c.3. id est, locus sanctus in longitudine habebat 40. cubitos, postquàm processisti per 26. cubitos reperis mensam cum candelabro; & paulò ultrà prope velum erat altare suffitus. Illud in altitudine duos habebat cubitos & in latitudine unum: ipsi quatuor erant anguli, & deinde in labris suis cingebatur corona, quam Iudæi dicunt retulisse coronam Sacerdotii. Maymon ubi supra. Singulis diebus supra hoc altare manè & vesperi offerebatur suffitus; in die expiationis verò Summus Sacerdos illius cornibus vel angulis illiniebat sanguinem. Vid. Cultum Templi, & Diem Expiationis.
units.tr: We have considered the lampstand with the table of showbread; now let us approach the altar of incense. It stood in the third part of the holy place, as Maimonides says in Beth Habechira ch. 3, that is, the holy place was 40 cubits long. After you have gone 26 cubits you find the table with the lampstand, and a little further on, near the veil, stood the altar of incense. It was two cubits high and one cubit wide, with four corners, and around its rim ran a crown, which the Jews say represented the crown of the priesthood. Maimonides, as above. Every day incense was offered on this altar morning and evening. On the Day of Atonement the High Priest smeared blood on its horns or corners. See Temple worship and Day of Atonement.

units.la: Tandem ad Sanctum Sanctorum appropinquamus, quod in templo primo à Sancto divisum erat muro, in templo secundo verò duobus velis, spatio unius cubiti distantibus quod spatium vocant ﬠּ Middot cap. 4. ex vocabulo Græco παραξὶς quod debilitatem visus significat; cùm enim templum secundum ædificarent, imperfectè solùm mensuram muri sciebant, quare eius loco vela substituerunt. Vide Talmud Hierof. in Middot cap.5. Maym. in Beth Habechira cap.4. Const. l'Empereur in Middot pag. 164.
units.tr: Finally we come to the Holy of Holies. In the first temple it was separated from the holy place by a wall, but in the second temple by two veils a cubit apart. This space they call the Middot in ch. 4 (the Hebrew term), from the Greek word [παραξίς], which means weakness of sight. When they built the second temple they knew the measure of the wall only imperfectly, so they put veils in its place. See the Talmud of Jerusalem in Middot ch. 5; Maimonides in Beth Habechira ch. 4; Constantin l'Empereur in Middot p. 164.

units.la: Longitudo Sancti Sanctorum erat 20. cubitorum. Parietes duobus Cherubinis erant ornati, quorum alæ se ab una extremitate ad aliam extendebant, omnia verò auro splendefcebant; in medio Cherubinorum ipsa arca fœderis erat, & prope ipsam urna cum baculo Aaronis : Arca stabat imposita lapidi qui tegebat orificium fluxuosæ spelunca quæ à Salomone in hunc finem facta dicitur, ut arca ibi poslet abscondi, & revera ibi positam fuisse referunt Maymon in Beth Habeeh.cap.4. & Kimchi in 2. Chron.35. Quid Summus Sacerdos dum semel in anno hunc locum ingrederetur faceret, apud Expiationis festum in E. diximus. In tabulato Sancti Sanctorum erant quædam valvulæ per quas immittebant chordis opifices si aliquid reparatione egeret, & ne oculos pascerent in considerando Sanctum Sanctorum, ipsos includebant cistis ex quibus solùm illum locum aspicere poterant, qui operâ ipsorum opus habebat. Middot c.4.sol.37. a. Quæ deinde de arca hic dici possent, ea recensuit Cl. Buxtorfius in Differt. defuit illa in templo secundo de quo proprie hic loquimur, una cum Urim & Thummim, Olea Vnctionis & Spiritu Sancto. Hierof. Taanith sol. 65.1. non quod nullam plane arcam habuerint, nam confecerunt unam ut partes cultus templi perficere possent, sicuti etiam duodecim lapides habuerunt in pectorali; sed quod Deus nec suâ שכינה illam cohonestaret, nec à Mose confecta esset. De Cherubinis vid. in lit. C.
units.tr: The Holy of Holies was 20 cubits long. Its walls were adorned with two cherubim, whose wings stretched from one end to the other, and everything shone with gold. In the middle of the cherubim stood the ark of the covenant, and near it the urn with Aaron's rod. The ark stood on a stone that covered the opening of a winding cave, said to have been made by Solomon for this purpose, so that the ark could be hidden there. Maimonides in Beth Habechira ch. 4 and Kimchi on 2 Chronicles 35 report that it was really placed there. What the High Priest did when he entered this place once a year, we have described under the Feast of Atonement in E. In the floor of the Holy of Holies were some small hatches through which workmen let down cords if anything needed repair. So that they would not feast their eyes on looking at the Holy of Holies, they were enclosed in boxes through which they could see only the part that needed their work. Middot ch. 4, sol. 37a. What else could be said here about the ark has been listed by the learned Buxtorf in his Dissertation. But the ark was absent from the second temple, which is what we are speaking of here, along with the Urim and Thummim, the anointing oil, and the Holy Spirit. Jerusalem Taanith sol. 65.1. Not that they had no ark at all, for they made one so that the parts of the temple worship could be completed, just as they also had twelve stones in the breastplate. Rather, God neither honoured it with his Shekinah nor was it made by Moses. On the Cherubim see under the letter C.

units.la: Nunc indiscriminatim de templo referenda sunt, quæ ad manus. Templum primum stetit 410. annos, Templum secundum verò 420. Vid. Iubilaa. Quæ in templo ædificando præcipuè observari debebant recenset Maymon in Beth Habech. c.1. debebat ædificari ex lapidibus non autem ex ligno; interdiu non nocturno in eius ædificatione laborandum; idem ibid. Quidam dicunt templi lapides absque ullo ferro sola applicatione vermiculi Schamir fuisse paratos. Vid. Sotah sol. 48. D. Kimchi cap. 6. lib. 1. Regum. Ædificatum templum bis in anno dealbabant. Beth Habech. c.4. Templi reverentia qualis fuerit? Vid. apud (ultum templi, in C. Sanctitatem templi cum variis eius gradibus innuimus apud Sanctum, in S. Templum ingrediuntur via dextra & egrediuntur via sinistrâ. Middot c. 2. §. 2. Vid. Lugentes.
units.tr: Now we must set down, without order, what concerns the temple as it comes to hand. The first temple stood 410 years, the second 420. See Jubilees. Maimonides in Beth Habechira ch. 1 lists what chiefly had to be observed in building the temple: it had to be built of stones, not wood; the work was to be done by day, not by night. Ibid. Some say the stones of the temple were prepared without any iron, merely by applying the worm Shamir. See Sotah sol. 48 D; Kimchi on 1 Kings ch. 6. The built temple was whitewashed twice a year. Beth Habechira ch. 4. What was the reverence due to the temple? See under Temple worship, in C. We have hinted at the holiness of the temple with its various degrees under Holy, in S. They enter the temple by the right-hand way and leave by the left. Middot ch. 2, §. 2. See Mourners.

units.la: §. De Templi custodiis Vid. Levitas. Portariis. ibid.
units.tr: §. On the guards of the temple, see Levites, gatekeepers, ibid.

units.la: §. Templi omnia vasa oleo unctionis sanctificata sunt. Kele Hamikdafsch c.1. circa med.
units.tr: §. All the vessels of the temple were consecrated with anointing oil. Kele Hamikdafsch ch. 1, about the middle.

units.la: §. Ascensus ad templum ex Vrbe Hierofolyma nec erat adeò difficilis quin eo possent agi pecora & boves, nec adeò facilis quin nixum aliquem requireret ab ascendentibus, hinc puerulus immunis erat à comparitione in tribus festis à Deo requisita, donec prehensâ patris manu cum ipso ascendere posset. Chagiga cap.1.
units.tr: §. The ascent to the temple from the city of Jerusalem was not so difficult that animals and oxen could not be driven up to it, nor so easy that it did not require some support from those climbing. Hence a little boy was excused from the appearance required by God at the three feasts, until he could go up with his father by holding his hand. Chagigah ch. 1.

units.la: §. In templi vasibus reficiendis utebantur operâ Alexandrinorum, qui Bab. Megillah sol. 26.1. סרפיים vocantur, id est artifices aris. Illi in integrum restituerunt Cymbalum æneum & Mortarium in quo contundebantur amorata, cùm fissuræ in illis essent. Bab. Erachin sol.10.2.
units.tr: §. For repairing the temple vessels they used the labour of Alexandrians, who in Bab. Megillah sol. 26.1 are called [סרפיים], that is, brass-workers. They restored to perfect condition a bronze cymbal and a mortar in which spices were pounded, when they had cracks. Bab. Erachin sol. 10.2.

units.la: §. De templi officiariis vid. officiarios. Item אמרכלין in A. de Templi Musicis vid. apud Musicam.
units.tr: §. On the temple officers see Officers. Likewise [אמרכלין] in A. On the temple musicians see under Music.

units.la: §. In templo erat locus excelsus,quò ascendit is qui spectatum missus an aurora ascenderit, cumque ille videret spatium orientis splendescens dixit ברקאי vel lucida est tota facies Orientis usque ad Hebronem. Vnoquoque mane id facere iussit Leithurgiæ præfectus, ut scirent an adesset tempus macândi sacrificium iuge. Ioma cap 3 2.Tamid.cap.3.v.2. Maym. ad loc. in Ioma.
units.tr: §. In the temple there was a high place to which he climbed who had been sent to watch whether the dawn was rising. When he saw the eastern sky brightening, he said [ברקאי], that is, "The whole face of the East is bright as far as Hebron." Every morning the overseer of the liturgy ordered this to be done, so that they might know whether the time had come to offer the continual sacrifice. Yoma ch. 3, 2. Tamid ch. 3, v. 2. Maimonides on the passage in Yoma.

units.la: §. De cultu quotidiano templi, vid. Sacrificia. Cultum templi in C.
units.tr: §. On the daily worship of the temple, see Sacrifices. Temple worship in C.

units.la: §. De Sacerdotibus & eorum variis ordinibus vid.Sacerdotes. סגן in S. אנשי בית אב in A.
units.tr: §. On the priests and their various orders, see Priests. [סגן] in S. [אנשי בית אב] in A.

units.la: §. In Bab. Ioma sol. 9. 2. quærunt propter quæ peccata templum primum fuerit devastatum? Respondetur propter Idololatriam, fornicationem & effusionem sanguinis. Quæritur, propter quænam sub secundo; respondetur Odium absque-causa,& secretam iniquitatem. Idem oraculum divinum ipsis exprobraverat Matth. 23. 28. ἐπωσὶν μισοὶ ἐςι ὑποκρισίαις καὶ ἀνομίας.
units.tr: §. In Bab. Yoma sol. 9.2 they ask for what sins the first temple was laid waste. The answer is: for idolatry, fornication and the shedding of blood. They ask for what sins the second was destroyed. The answer is: baseless hatred and hidden iniquity. The same divine oracle had rebuked them in Matthew 23:28: [μεστοί ἐστε ὑποκρίσεως καὶ ἀνομίας], "full of hypocrisy and iniquity."

units.la: §. Cùm templo secundo flammæ admoverentur, Sacerdotes ascenderunt in summitatem templi, & claves conclavium & camerarum templi, sursum, cœlum versus iecerunt, cum his verbis: O Domine noster æterne, quoniam nos digni non sumus, qui claves has retineamus, tibi traditæ sint. Et prodiit è cœlo quasi forma manus, atque eas ab illis recepit. Illi autem defultarunt & ceciderunt in ignem. Taanith sol. 25. 1.
units.tr: §. When flames were put to the second temple, the priests climbed to the top of the temple and threw up towards heaven the keys of the chambers and storerooms of the temple, saying: "O Lord our eternal God, since we are not worthy to keep these keys, let them be handed over to you." And from heaven there came forth something like the form of a hand, which took them from them. But they leapt about and fell into the fire. Taanith sol. 25.1.

units.la: §. De plenaria templi ruina sonat locus Maymonidis in Taanith cap. 5. Nonoisto die mensis Ab, qui ob vindictas fatalis fuit, Turnus Rufus impius è regionibus Edomæis, aratro templum fodit, & circumiacentia, ut adimpleretur illud, quod dictum est: Sion ut ager arabitur.
units.tr: §. Maimonides in Taanith ch. 5 describes the complete ruin of the temple: "On the ninth day of the month Ab, which was fatal because of the vengeance, the impious Turnus Rufus from the Edomite regions ploughed up the temple with a plough, and the surrounding ground, so that what was said might be fulfilled: Zion shall be ploughed like a field."

units.la: §. Inter illos qui aliquid ad templi usum contulerunt, aut eximii quid ad maiorem eius gloriam fecerunt, sequentes sunt. Laudatur Filius Catin quod fecerit 12. labri epistomia, & illam Machinam quæ impediebat ne labri aquæ noctu polluerentur. Celebratur Rex Monobazus quod illorum vasorum ansas quibus in die expiationis utuntur, ex auro fecerit. Memoratur Helena mater Monobazi, quod fecerit candelabrum aureum super ostium Sanctuarii, & illam tabulam cui sectio mulierū declinantis inscripta est. Fit etiam mentio Nicanoris, in cuius portis facta sunt miracula. Vicevversa, sequentes ignominiâ notantur, Familiæ
units.tr: Among those who contributed something to the use of the Temple, or did some outstanding thing for its greater glory, the following are named. The son of Catin is praised because he made the twelve spouts of the laver and that device which kept the water of the laver from being polluted at night. King Monobazus is celebrated because he made of gold the handles of those vessels which they use on the Day of Atonement. Helena, mother of Monobazus, is mentioned because she made a golden candelabrum over the door of the Sanctuary, and that tablet on which the section of the bending woman is inscribed. There is also mention of Nicanor, at whose gates miracles took place. Conversely, the following are marked with disgrace: the family

units.la: Garmo, quòd noluerit alios quædam docere, quæ spectabant ad modum conficiendi panes propositionis. (scil. panes è furno ita extrahendi, ut non frangerentur, quod cæteri artifices ignorabant; Item hæc familia sciebat panem ita coquere ut non mucidus fieret.) Familia Beth Abhtines,quòd noluerint docère quædam, quæ spectabant ad modum conficiendi suffimentum. (i. e. sciebat thymiama quibusdam herbis ita miscēre, ut fumus deinde non consusè sed baculi instar sursum ascenderet.) Item quòd Hogrus cantandi,& Ben Kamzar scribendi peritus, artem suam nemini monstrare voluerint. Vid.Ioma c.3 v.10.12.
units.tr: of Garmo, because it was unwilling to teach others certain things which concerned the manner of making the showbread (namely, drawing the loaves from the oven so that they were not broken, which other craftsmen did not know; this family also knew how to bake bread so that it did not become mouldy). The family of Beth Abhtines, because they were unwilling to teach certain things which concerned the manner of making the incense (that is, they knew how to mix the incense with certain herbs so that the smoke then rose upward like a staff, and not diffusely). Likewise, Hogrus, skilled in singing, and Ben Kamzar, skilled in writing, were unwilling to show their art to anyone. See Yoma ch. 3, vv. 10, 12.

units.la: De loco templi יף ור vocato Vid. יף ור in C. Tempestates curiosè observare Iudæis erat admodum assuetum.
units.tr: On the place of the Temple called יף ור; see יף ור in C. To observe the weather carefully was very customary among the Jews.

units.la: Bab. Ioma sol.21 2. In exitu diei ultimi Festi Tabernaculorum omnes observarunt ascensum sumi. Si fumus inclinaret septentrionem versus, pauperes gavisi sunt, at ditiores dolore sunt affecti; quia pluvia anni sequentis multa futura erant,srufiusque corrumpendi. Si austrum versus inclinaret, denotabat pluvias rariores. Si Orientem versus, omnes gavisi sunt: si Occasum versus, omnes sunt contristati. Glossa. In Festo Tabernaculorum indicatum est de iis quod pluvias attinet.
units.tr: Bab. Yoma, fol. 21.2. At the end of the last day of the Feast of Tabernacles, they all observed the rising of the smoke. If the smoke leaned toward the north, the poor rejoiced, but the richer were struck with grief, because there would be much rain in the following year, and the crops would be spoiled. If it leaned toward the south, it signified scarcer rains. If toward the east, everyone rejoiced; if toward the west, everyone was saddened. Gloss: At the Feast of Tabernacles it was indicated concerning the rains.

units.la: Hierof.Taanith sol.65.2. R. Acha dixit, si fuisset sapiens quis in Zippore, cùm descenderet pluvia prima, ex ipso pulveris odore prædicere poterat humiditatem anni.
units.tr: Hierosolymitanus Taanith, fol. 65.2. R. Acha said: if there were a wise man in Zippore, when the first rain came down he could foretell the moisture of the year from the very smell of the dust.

units.la: Terminus Sabbathi. De eo Vid. Sabba- thum.
units.tr: The boundary of the Sabbath. On this see Sabbathum.

units.la: TESTIMONIUM. Triplex illud præcipuè erat.
units.tr: TESTIMONY. There were especially three kinds.

units.la: I. Erat עדות בשילה Testimonium inane: quo audito nihil amplius cum eo est actum, sed amovebatur ut nihil ad rem faciens.
units.tr: I. There was the "empty testimony" [עדות בשילה], empty testimony. When this was heard, nothing further was done with the witness; he was simply removed, as irrelevant to the matter.

units.la: II. Erat עדות קיים Testimonium stans; quod ita vocatum fuit, non quasi in re nullum planè dubium relinqueret, sed quia non planè reiectum à iudicibus, & admissum ad examen erat, si scilicet alii essent qui illius improbationem suscipere vellent.
units.tr: II. There was the "standing testimony" [עדות קיים], standing testimony. It was so called not because it left nothing at all in doubt, but because the judges had not wholly rejected it and it was admitted to examination, provided that there were others who wished to undertake its disproof.

units.la: III. Erat testimonium כשורייהם מכוונים cum verba duorum testium congruerent & essent ad idem.Hoc testimonium vocatur Marci cap. 14.56. Μαρτυρία Ion. Vide Sanhed.cap.5.v.3.4. & Maymon in Edúth.
units.tr: III. There was testimony [כשורייהם מכוונים], when the words of two witnesses agreed and were to the same effect. This testimony is called Mark 14:56 ["Μαρτυρία Ion."]. See Sanhedrin ch. 5, vv. 3–4, and Maimonides in Eduth.

units.la: §. De diversis disquisitionum circa testes ventilationibus. Vid. בריקה in B. & הכחשה in C.
units.tr: On the various investigations concerning witnesses, see [בריקה] in B and [הכחשה] in C.

units.la: §. De Testibus sequentia observandum. 1. Testes non nisi præsente litigante audiuntur, nisi is æger sit, aut citatus non compareat. 2. In causis pœnalibus debent testes proprio ore testimonium dare; in pecuniariis verò licet scripto testimonium exhibère. Maymon Hal.Eduth cap.3. 3. Vir magnus in rebus vilibus, & in minori iudicio non tenetur testimonium dare. Sacerdos Summus non nisi in regem & coram magno Synedrio testimonium dicit. Idem cap.1. 4. Decem hominum genera testimonium dicere non possunt; mulier, & quæ dubii sexus est: servi, & semiliberi: minor 13. annis: delirus, stolidus, fatuus, insanus, epilepticus, mutus, cæcus, sceleratus, & illi qui sunt רועי בהמה דקה pastores parvi pecoris; id est qui nutriunt capras, & alia quæ fata carpendo corrumpunt. His accensetur יארhomo de fœce plebis: & alii contemptibiles; Necessarii, & decimo illorum quorum interest. Maymon ubi supra c.10.11.12.
units.tr: Concerning witnesses, the following should be observed. (1) Witnesses are heard only when the litigant is present, unless he is sick or, having been summoned, does not appear. (2) In criminal cases witnesses must give their testimony by mouth; in monetary cases, however, testimony may be presented in writing. Maimonides, Hal. Eduth ch. 3. (3) A great man is not bound to give testimony in trivial matters or in a lesser court. The High Priest testifies only before the king and before the great Sanhedrin. The same, ch. 1. (4) Ten kinds of men cannot give testimony: a woman, and one of doubtful sex; slaves and half-freed men; a minor under thirteen years; a madman, dullard, fool, lunatic, epileptic, mute, blind man, criminal, and those who are [רועי בהמה דקה], shepherds of small cattle, that is, those who keep goats and other animals that ruin crops by nibbling. To these are reckoned [יאר], a man of the dregs of the people, and others who are contemptible; also relatives, and those who have an interest in the matter. Maimonides, ubi supra, chs. 10–12.

units.la: §. Iam alia promiscuè referemus.Si quis teftis neget sibi constare, patente actore aut reo iurat. Schebhuot c.4.3.
units.tr: Further, we will set down other points without any order. If a witness denies that his testimony hangs together, he swears the oath, with the plaintiff or the defendant present. Schebhuot ch. 4, §3.

units.la: Falsi evictio fit ex circunftantia temporis & loci potissimum, Maymon Eduth c.1.Reiectanci per supplicium flagri, solutam mulctam, atque pœnitentiam integram restituuntur. Ibid.c.12. De supplicio ipsorum per flagrum plura dicit in c.18. & additur, quòd fi qui testes falsi pœnam luerint, missis literis in omnibus Synedriis id annuntiari debêre.
units.tr: Falsity is proved chiefly from circumstances of time and place. Maimonides, Eduth ch. 1. Those rejected as false witnesses are restored after they have suffered the lash, paid the fine and made full repentance. Ibid. ch. 12. He says more about their punishment by the lash in ch. 18, and adds that if any false witnesses have paid the penalty, notice of this should be sent by letter to all the Sanhedrins.

units.la: Qui capitis damnati sunt, à testibus interfici debent, & fi testes id non fecerint, fi reus homicida fuerit, à quibusvis interfici potest. Maymon Hal.Sanhed. c.13.
units.tr: Those condemned to capital punishment must be put to death by the witnesses; and if the witnesses have not done so, then, if the accused was a murderer, he may be put to death by anyone at all. Maimonides, Hal. Sanhed. ch. 13.

units.la: Vnus testis ad testimonium reddendum non admittitur,nisi in Sotah,ne bibat aquas amaras, & in iunice decollanda ne id fiat. Maym.Eduth cap.5.
units.tr: A single witness is not admitted to give testimony, except in the case of the suspected wife who must drink the bitter waters, and in the case of the heifer whose neck is broken, so that this may not be done. Maimonides, Eduth ch. 5.

units.la: Testibus in causa capitali ita terrorem incutiebant; Intrò vocatos admonebant,ne quid ex coniectura aut rumore dicerent;Item: forte ignoratis nos tandem vos pervestigaturos per inquisitionem & indagationem; ne sitis nescii, aliter se habere iudicia quæ de pecunia quàm de capite habentur. Nam in illa pecuniâ data peccatum expiari potest. In his si quid deliquerit,sanguis rei & seminum eius ad finem usque seculi tibi imputabitur. Sanhedrin cap. 4. 5.
units.tr: To witnesses in a capital case they used to put the fear of God thus. When they were called in, they were warned not to say anything from conjecture or rumour. Likewise: Perhaps you do not know that we shall at last investigate you by inquiry and search; be not unaware that judgments concerning money are different from those concerning a capital charge. For in that matter of money a sin can be expiated by payment; but in these cases, if he has offended, the blood of the accused and of his seed will be imputed to you until the end of the age. Sanhedrin ch. 4–5.

units.la: TIBERIAS olim fuit Rakath H. Megilla fol.7o.1. Bab. Megillah fol.5.2. Sita fuit ad mare quod fuit ipfi loco muri: ut elici poteft ex loco modo cit.
units.tr: TIBERIAS once existed. Rakath H. Megilla fol. 70.1; Bab. Megillah fol. 5.2. It was situated by the sea, which served it in place of a wall, as may be gathered from the passage just cited.

units.la: Olim Therma חמת vocatæ diftabant ab ipfa fpatio milliaris, Bab.Megillah fol.2.2. Tandem חמת Chamat & Tiberias conftituerunt civitatem unam. Hierof.Erubbin fol.23.4. Therma illæ aliquando vocantur חמת דגר Therma Gedara, propter loci viciniam. Bab.Megillah fol.6.1. Illas Thermas adierunt R. Ionathan & R. Iuda Hammafi. Hierof.Kiddufchin fol.64.3. Alia de Thermis Tiberiadis reperies in Hierof.Schabbat fol.3.1. Bab. Sanhed, 108. Hierof. Schabbat folio 6.1.
units.tr: Formerly the hot springs called [חמת] were a mile distant from it. Bab. Megillah fol. 2.2. At length Chamath and Tiberias formed one city. Jerus. Erubin fol. 23.4. Those hot springs are sometimes called [חמת דגר], Chamath Gedara, on account of the nearness of the place. Bab. Megillah fol. 6.1. R. Jonathan and R. Judah Hammafi visited those hot springs. Jerus. Qiddushin fol. 64.3. Other matters concerning the hot springs of Tiberias you will find in Jerus. Shabbat fol. 3.1, Bab. Sanhedrin 108, and Jerus. Shabbat fol. 6.1.

units.la: §. Prope Tiberiadem quoque erat Hippo סוסיו de qua Rofch Hafchana fol.54.4. Vt & מעין בית Hierof.Bava Metzia fol.11.2. Tiberias fuit ab Herode ædificata, Iofeph. Antiq. lib.18. cap.3. Tredecim Synagogas habuit Bab. Beracot f.30.2. inter quas celebratur סורוגן ביתן Antiqua Serongiana.
units.tr: Near Tiberias there was also Hippo, [סוסיו], of which see Rosh Hashanah fol. 54.4; likewise the spring of the house [מעין בית], Jerus. Bava Metzia fol. 11.2. Tiberias was built by Herod, Josephus, Antiquities, book 18, ch. 3. It had thirteen synagogues, Bab. Berachot fol. 30.2, among which the famous synagogue [סורוגן ביתן], the ancient Serongian one, is celebrated.

units.la: §. Tiberiade compegit R. Iehuda Hannafii Mifchnaiot in volumen unum. Zemach David. Sed non circa annum Chrifti 230. ut plurimi exiftimant, quoniam in eo mentio fit Imperatoris Diocletiani; (Vid.f.loco.)
units.tr: At Tiberias R. Judah Hannasi compiled the Mishnayot into one volume. Zemach David. But this was not around the year of Christ 230, as most suppose, since mention is made in it of the Emperor Diocletian (see the place cited).

units.la: Academia Tiberienfis maior erat Zipporitana.Gloffa in Bab.Sanhed. fol.32.1.
units.tr: The Tiberian academy was larger than the Zipporitan. Gloss on Bab. Sanhedrin fol. 32.1.

units.la: §. De mari Tiberiadis hanc conftitutionem fecit Iofua, ut indifferenter omnes Ifraelitæ in eo pifcari poffent, modò in eo non ftruant sepes ex cannis aut calamis ad capiendos pisces, quia illæ impedimento sunt navibus. Hierof. Megillah sol.75.1. Bava Kama sol.82.1.
units.tr: Concerning the Sea of Tiberias, Joshua made this rule: that all Israelites might fish in it without distinction, provided they do not build fences of reeds or canes in it for catching fish, since these are an obstacle to ships. Jerus. Megillah fol. 75.1; Bava Kama fol. 82.1.

units.la: תפיליז Tephillin est lorum coriaceum duplex של ראש Capitis, & של יד Manus, quod precaturi sibi alligant, primum circa caput, secundum circa brachium sinistrum; in eius medio cellula est, cui inclusa membranula continens 4. scripturæ versus, fc. Exod.13.2.5. Deuter. 6.4. c.11.13. Cellula ista in Oratorio capitis diftincta est in quatuor cellulas alias, quibus singulis una membrana convoluta includitur; hæc cellula arcte consuitur, ex qua lora utrinque exeuntia רציעות dicuntur. Hæc Tephilla alligatur circa caput ita ut cellula sit in media fronte, ubi pili desinunt, ut sit quasi ante oculos. Altera quæ manui applicatur, alligatur brachio sinistro ubi manui iungitur, quia vicinior est ea pars cordi, & sic preces putant magis è corde proficisci: Hæc in V.T. טוטפות in Novo φυλακτήρια dicuntur. De his vid. Maymon per totum tract. Tephillin præcip. cap.2. Buxt. Synag. Iud. cap.9.10.&13. Ita Phylacterium mihi explicare dignatus est Præstantissimus Toignardus, dum Aureliæ commorarer.
units.tr: [תפיליז], tephillin, is a double leather strap: one [של ראש], of the head, and one [של יד], of the hand, which those who pray fasten to themselves, the first around the head and the second around the left arm. In the middle of it is a little cell, in which is enclosed a small membrane containing four passages of Scripture, namely Exod. 13.2–5, Deut. 6.4 and 11.13. In the head-phylactery this cell is divided into four smaller cells, each enclosing one rolled-up membrane; the cell is sewn tightly, and the straps that come out on either side are called [רציעות]. The head-phylactery is bound so that the cell lies in the middle of the forehead, where the hair ends, so that it is, as it were, before the eyes. The other, which is applied to the hand, is bound to the left arm where it joins the hand, because that part lies nearer the heart, and so they think prayers come more from the heart.
