In the Old Testament these are called [טוטפות], and in the New [φυλακτήρια], phylacteries. On these see Maimonides throughout the tractate Tephillin, especially ch. 2; Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica, chs. 9, 10 and 13. Thus the most distinguished Toignard condescended to explain the phylactery to me while I was staying at Orléans.

units.la: De Curiosa Phylacteriorum scriptione plurima habet Maymon in loc. cit. c.1.2. necessariò debebant linguâ Assyriacâ illa exarare, cum aliàs Biblia etiam lingua Græca, aut ut quidam volunt, quâvis aliâ scribere poterant. Megillah cap.1.v.8.
units.tr: Maimonides has much on the curious writing of the phylacteries, loc. cit. chs. 1–2: they had necessarily to write them in the Assyrian language, whereas otherwise they could write the Bible in Greek or, as some want, in any other language. Megillah ch. 1, v. 8.

units.la: De Phylacteriorum ligamentis literulis quibusdam signatis, v. Tofaphot ad Megillah f.26.2.
units.tr: On the straps of the phylacteries marked with certain small letters, see Tosafot on Megillah f. 26.2.

units.la: De Phylacteriorum recitatione Vid. utrumque Talmud in Beracot c.1.2.3. Regulæ generales hæ sunt. 1. Schema legendum est mane à stantibus, vesperi verò illud legere possunt inclinati. 2. Schema vespertinum legitur ab illa horâ quâ Sacerdotes ingrediuntur ad תרומה trumam suam comedendam, (i.e. Sole occidente.) Cùm color cæruleus à prasino poteit distingui (aurora ingruente) legitur matutinum, quod legi poteit usque ad horam tertiam. 3. Operarii Schema legere possunt in cacumine arboris, si tempore orationis adhuc circa illud occupantur. 4. A lectione Schema liber est sponsus primâ nocte.
units.tr: On the recitation of the phylacteries, see both Talmuds in Berachot chs. 1–3. The general rules are these. (1) The Shema is to be read in the morning by those standing, but in the evening they may read it reclining. (2) The evening Shema is read from the hour when the priests go in to eat their terumah, that is, after sunset. When blue can be distinguished from green, as dawn comes on, the morning reading is recited, and it may be read until the third hour. (3) Workers may read the Shema at the top of a tree, if they are still occupied with it at the time of prayer. (4) A bridegroom is free from reading the Shema on the first night.

units.la: Iudæi iurarunt tactis Phylacteriis. Maymon in Schebbuot cap.11. Apud Tanchum.sol.6.3. ipse Deus per phylacteria iurans introducitur.
units.tr: The Jews swore with their hands on the phylacteries. Maimonides in Shebuot ch. 11. In Tanchuma fol. 6.3, God himself is introduced swearing by the phylacteries.

units.la: Christus non omnem Phylacteriorum sed Hypocriticam & fastuosam damnavit gestationem, nam probabile est Christum ipsum illa gestasse, ut reliqui Iudæorum pueri, qui statim ac chatechisationis erant capaces in recitatione Phylacteriorum erudiebantur. Baba Berac. sol.21.1. in Glossa.
units.tr: Christ condemned not all wearing of phylacteries, but the hypocritical and ostentatious kind. For it is probable that Christ himself wore them, like the other Jewish boys, who, as soon as they were capable of catechising, were trained in the recitation of the phylacteries. Baba Berachot fol. 21.1, in the gloss.

units.la: TRIBUS DECEM fecundùm Gemarisas in Sanhed. sol.110.2. nunquam convertentur. Decem Tribus nunquam redibunt, sicuti dicitur; Et proiecit eos in terram alienam, sicuti est hodie Deut. xxix. 28. Sicuti hic dies abit & non redibit, sic etiam illi abierunt & non redeunt.
units.tr: THE TEN TRIBES, according to the Gemara in Sanhedrin fol. 110.2, will never return. The ten tribes will never return, as it is said: "and he cast them into another land, as it is this day" (Deut. 29:28). As this day passes and does not return, so they too have departed and do not return.

units.la: TRADITIONES suas Iudæi præ verbo æstimarunt divino ut patet ex v. 2. Matth.15. & sequentibus Talmud. locis.
units.tr: The Jews esteemed their traditions above the divine word, as is clear from Matt. 15:2 and following, and from the passages of the Talmud.

units.la: Hierof. Beracot sol. 3. 2. חכיבים רבי סופרי מרבי תורה Amabilia sunt verba Scribarum prae verbis legis, nam verba legis sunt gravia & levia, at verba Scribarum sunt omnia levia.
units.tr: Hierosolymitanum Berachot, fol. 3, col. 2: "Lovely are the words of the Scribes beyond the words of the Law, for the words of the Law are weighty and light, but the words of the Scribes are all light." [חכיבים רבי סופרי מרבי תורה]

units.la: Qui dixerit, non esse Phylacteria, transgrediens verba legis, reus non est; at qui dixerit, Quinque esse Totaphot, addens ad verba Scribarum, hic reus est.
units.tr: "Whoever says that phylacteries are not required does not break the words of the Law and is not guilty; but whoever says that there are five Totaphot, adding to the words of the Scribes, he is guilty."

units.la: Quomodo verba ἀρτεβυτέρων graviora sint, & magis æstimanda, quam verba Prophetarum Vid. Propheta.
units.tr: How the words of the elders [πρεσβυτέρων] are weightier and to be valued more than the words of the Prophets. See Prophet.

units.la: תרומה Truma est oblatio elaboratarum frugum : Trumot sunt multiplices, prima est תרומה גדולה Truma magna, quae est pars pro Sacerdote separata ex sedecim fructuum ad usum hominis iam praeparatorum generibus. Alii est תרומת יהוה Oblatio Iehove, quae est decima quam Levitae ex מעשר ראשון Decima prima Sacerdoti dabant; Fuit deinde & תרומת מעשר quâ quisquis quantum allubebat decimabat. Haec omnia diducit Maymon in Hal.Trumot. Vid. etiam Decimas.
units.tr: Truma is an offering of prepared produce. There are several kinds of Trumot. The first is the great Truma [תרומה גדולה], which is the part set apart for the priest from the sixteen kinds of fruit already prepared for human use. Another is the offering of Jehovah [תרומת יהוה], which is the tithe that the Levites gave to the priest from the first tithe [מעשר ראשון]. Then there was also the tithe-offering [תרומת מעשר], by which anyone tithed as much as he pleased. Maimonides works all of this out in Hilchot Trumot. See also Tithes.

units.la: Turnus Rufus saepius apud Talmudicos memoratur, ut in Taanith cap. 4. v. 6. & apud Maymon. in Taanith cap. 5. Nono die mensis Ab, Turnus Rufus impius, è regionibus Edomaeis, aratro templum fodit. Item in Sanhedrin folio 65.2. Gloss. disputavit Akiba cum Turno Rufo &c. Probabile est hunc Turnum Rufum fuisse Τεραύνιον Ῥύφον apud Ioseph. de bello lib. 7. cap. 7. quem Titus reliquit exercitûs praefectum: hoc magis volumus quàm illum fuisse aut Annium Rufum, quo Iudaeae praefecto obiit Augustus: Ioseph. Antiq. lib.18. cap.3. Aut Turanium Rufum annonae praefectum, apud Tacitum lib. 1. ab init.
units.tr: Turnus Rufus is often mentioned among the Talmudists, as in Taanith, chapter 4, verse 6, and in Maimonides on Taanith, chapter 5: "On the ninth day of the month Av, the impious Turnus Rufus ploughed up the Temple with a plough, coming from the region of Edom." Likewise in Sanhedrin, folio 65, col. 2, in the Gloss: "Akiba disputed with Turnus Rufus," etc. It is probable that this Turnus Rufus was the Tineius Rufus [Τεραύνιον Ῥύφον] in Josephus, The Jewish War, book 7, chapter 7, whom Titus left as commander of the army. I prefer this to supposing that he was either Annius Rufus, the prefect of Judaea under whom Augustus died (Josephus, Antiquities, book 18, chapter 3), or Turanius Rufus, the prefect of the grain supply, mentioned in Tacitus, book 1, at the beginning.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: VACCÆ RUFÆ exustio.
units.tr: The burning of the red heifer.

units.la: Lex vaccam rufam comburendi, & cineribus eius illos qui ob mortuum impuri facti erant aspergendi, traditur Numer. 19. huiusce aspersionis significationes docet Apostolus ad Heb.9.13.
units.tr: The law for burning the red heifer, and sprinkling those who had become unclean through a dead body with its ashes, is given in Numbers 19. The Apostle explains the meaning of this sprinkling in Hebrews 9:13.

units.la: Ceremoniae in hac ustione adhibitae admodum magnae & curiosae fuerunt; magnis cautionibus eligi debebat vacca in hunc finem adhibita, ut videtur ex duobus primis capitibus tractatus Parah. Etiam disputatur, an ab unoquoque Sacerdote indiscriminatim comburi potuerit, an vero necessario hoc opus a Summo Sacerdote fieri debuerit. Vid. Iuchasin sol. 13. Rabbi Salomoh in Numer.19.
units.tr: The ceremonies used in this burning were very great and very exacting. The heifer chosen for this purpose had to be selected with great care, as appears from the first two chapters of the tractate Parah. It is also disputed whether any priest could burn it indiscriminately, or whether this work had to be done by the High Priest. See Yuchasin fol. 13; Rabbi Solomon on Numbers 19.

units.la: Qualiscunque autem fuerit, qui vaccam comburebat, septem diebus antequam illud fiebat, separabatur in conclave Templi, quod erat in atrio Israelis, & vocabatur בית האבן Domus lapidum: id est domus vasium lapideorum; illuc segregabatur in hunc finem, ne aliquo sepulchro aut cadavere polluteretur, quae conditio in hoc actu quam maximè requirebatur. Maimonides Parah cap.3.
units.tr: Whoever he was who burned the heifer, he was separated for seven days before the act was performed, into a chamber of the Temple that stood in the court of Israel and was called בית האבן [Beth ha-Eben], that is, "the house of the stone vessels." He was kept there for this purpose, so that he would not be defiled by any tomb or corpse, a condition that was required above all in this act. See Maimonides, Parah ch. 3.

units.la: Vacca Rufa debebat comburi extra montem templi, & proinde ut locum aliquem haberent qui à sepulchris esset immunis, elegerunt collem fornicibus suffultum in monte Oliveti, qui situs erat è regione portæ templi Orientalis; Eo die quo vacca comburi debebat, Sacerdos cum illis qui ipsum comitabantur, per portam orientalem trans vallem Kedron ibat; sed non ordinariâ viâ; ædificabant. enim singulis vicibus ac vacca comburi debebat suppedaneum arcubus suffultum, ita ut duobus arcubus unus suppositus esset; pecunia quâ hic fiebat sumptus, desumebatur ex conclavi לשכת Ροζοχυλακία. Hæc omnia fiebant פני קבר התהו propter sepulchra occulta, ne illis Sacerdos impurus redderetur, si forsan illa tangeret. Vid. Middot cap.1. Maymon in Parah cap.3. Schekalim cap.4.
units.tr: The red heifer had to be burned outside the Temple mount. So that they might have a place free from graves, they chose a hill supported by vaults on the Mount of Olives, which lay opposite the eastern gate of the Temple. On the day the heifer was to be burned, the priest went with his attendants through the eastern gate across the valley of Kidron, but not by the ordinary road. For each occasion when the heifer was to be burned they built a footbridge supported by arches, so that one arch was placed under two others. The money for this was taken from the chamber called Rhozochylakia [Ροζοχυλακία]. All this was done because of the hidden graves [פני קבר התהו], so that the priest should not be made unclean if he happened to touch one. See Middoth ch. 1; Maimonides, Parah ch. 3; Shekalim ch. 4.

units.la: Seniores populi per hoc suppedaneum Sacerdotem & comites eius præcedebant, & cùm in locum exustionis pervenisset Sacerdos ipsi imponebant manus, utque se ad lavandum accingeret monebant; quod etiam loco ad id destinato faciebat. Postea parabatur strues ligni, in qua vacca comburi debebat. Vacca ligatis cruribus imponebatur, facie occidentem versus disposita; Sacerdos verò stans in oriente vultu occidenti obverso, ipsam mactabat manu dextrâ, & sanguinem excipiebat manu sinistrâ.
units.tr: The elders of the people went before the priest and his companions along this footbridge. When the priest reached the place of burning, they laid their hands on him and reminded him to get ready to wash, which he also did in the place set aside for that. Afterwards a pile of wood was prepared on which the heifer was to be burned. The heifer, with its legs tied, was laid down facing west. The priest, standing in the east with his face turned toward the west, slaughtered it with his right hand and caught the blood in his left hand.

units.la: Iubet lex Num.19.4. ut Sacerdos de sanguine vaccæ septies aspergat versus anteriorem partem tentorii conventus, ad implendum itaque hoc mandatum Sacerdos de sanguine vaccæ iugulatæ septies spargebat recta ergà portam Susan conversus, & super ipsam in ipsum sanctuarii porticum inspiciens: in quem finem quoque porta illa facta erat aliis depressior. Vid. Templum.
units.tr: The law commands in Numbers 19:4, "that the priest shall sprinkle of her blood with his finger seven times toward the front of the tent of the congregation." So, to carry out this command, the priest sprinkled the blood of the slaughtered heifer seven times, turned straight toward the Susa gate, and looking up at the porch of the sanctuary itself. For this purpose that gate had also been made lower than the others. See Templum.

units.la: Sparso sanguine struem ligni incendebat, illique simul imponebat lignum cedrinum, hyssopum, & lanam Coccineam: adstantes vero antequàm ea igni injiceret de unoquoque ter interrogabat, an non hoc tale vel tale esset, v.g. an non hoc est lignum cedrinum? & illi etiam ter responderunt, Ita.
units.tr: After the blood was sprinkled, he set fire to the pile of wood, and at the same time placed on it cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet wool. Before he cast them into the fire, the bystanders asked each item three times whether this or that was such-and-such, for example, "Is this not cedar wood?" And they too answered three times, "Yes."

units.la: Postquàm ignis omnia consumpsit, colligebant cineres, ipsaque cribrabant, unam ex illis partem relinquebant in monte oliveto ad aspersionem populi; alteram tradebant 24. stationibus Sacerdotum ad Sacerdotum aspersionem. Tertiam vero reponebant in חיל antemurale Templi, in exuftionis memoriam. A Lege data usque ad templi devastationem novem solùm combustæ fuerunt vaccæ; una exusta fuit tempore Moisis, alia ab Esra; duas combussit Simeon Iustus, & duas Iohannes pater Mathiæ; Vna ab Elionai filio Hakkoph; una ab Hanamel Hamitzri, & una ab Ifmaele filio Fabi. Decima comburetur in diebus Meffiæ. Vid. Iuchasin sol.16. & tract. supra cit.
units.tr: When the fire had consumed everything, they gathered the ashes and sifted them. They kept one part on the Mount of Olives for sprinkling the people; they gave another part to the twenty-four stations of the priests for the sprinkling of the priests. They put the third part in the rampart [חיל] of the Temple, in memory of the burning. From the giving of the Law until the destruction of the Temple, only nine heifers were burned: one was burned in the time of Moses, another by Ezra; Simeon the Just burned two, and John, the father of Matthias, two; one was burned by Elioenai son of Hakkoph; one by Hanamel the Mitzrite; and one by Ishmael son of Phiabi. A tenth will be burned in the days of the Messiah. See Yuchasin fol. 16 and the tractate cited above.

units.la: Requirunt Iudæi ad legitimam purificationem faciendam, ut illa fiat à persona quæ nunquam immunda ob tactum mortui facta erat; de qua vid. Atriam Magnum in A.
units.tr: For the lawful purification to be performed, the Jews require that it be done by a person who had never become unclean through touching a dead body. On this see Atrium Magnum at A.

units.la: VELA, καταπετασμα in templo in universum erant tredecim, nempe septem ante 7. portas Atrii Israelis, unum in porta Portius, unum ante portam Sancti. Et duo inter Sanctum & Sanctissimum. Maymon in Kelî Hamikdafch cap.7. Duo illa erant loco unius, qui in Veteri Tabernaculo: spatium inter hæc duo vocatur παραξις, vid. Templum. Hæc duo vela singulis annis renovabantur, ita ut quæ per hoc annum suspensa fuerant, deinde tollerentur. Contexta erant ex quatuor coloribus, caruleo, purpureo, coccineo, & filo albo; unumquodque filum כפולים שש שש erat sexies duplicatum: & 72. pili intertexti erant unicuique filo. Maym. ubi sup. Evangelistæ dicunt in singulari, hoc velum disruptum fuisse, idem etiam infit Iosephus de bello lib.5. cap.14. quando Sanctissimum velo divisum fuisse dicit; non quasi unum solum fuerit velum, aut quasi unum solum disruptum fuerit; sed simpliciter indicant parietem intergerinum, repagulum istud intermedium fuisse dilaceratum, ad reliqua particularia non attendentes.
units.tr: VEILS. In the Temple there were thirteen veils in all: seven before the seven gates of the court of Israel, one at the Portius gate, one before the gate of the Holy Place, and two between the Holy Place and the Most Holy. See Maimonides, Kelei ha-Mikdash ch. 7. These two were in place of the one in the old Tabernacle. The space between these two is called paraxis; see Templum. These two veils were renewed every year, so that those hung up during the year were then taken down. They were woven of four colours: blue, purple, scarlet, and white linen; each thread was sixfold [כפולים שש שש], and seventy-two strands were woven into each thread. See Maimonides, loc. cit. The Evangelists say, in the singular, that "the veil" was torn. Josephus too says the same in Bellum bk. 5 ch. 14, when he says that the Most Holy Place was divided by a veil. This is not because there was only one veil, or because only one was torn; the writers simply mean that the middle partition, that intermediate barrier, was torn, without attending to the other particulars.

units.la: Inter officiarios templi, unus erat, qui curam gerere debuit velorum, ut nova, si necesse, suppeditarentur, & quævis legitimo loco suspenderentur. Si accidisset ut velum aliquod impurum factum fuisset, ipsum solvebant, lavabant, & lotum iterum in איל antemurali suspendebant, ad exsiccandum. Quando novum aliquod confectum erat velum, in podio vel xisto atrii mulierum alligabatur & suspendebatur, ut populus ipsum contemplari posset, & simul videre an legitimo modo factum esset. Schekalim c. 5. Maym. ubi supra.
units.tr: Among the Temple officials there was one whose duty was to take care of the veils, so that new ones could be supplied if necessary and each one hung in its proper place. If any veil had become unclean, they took it down, washed it, and after washing hung it again in the rampart [איל] to dry. When a new veil had been made, it was fastened and hung on the platform or terrace of the women's court, so that the people could look at it and at the same time see whether it had been made in the proper way. See Shekalim ch. 5; Maimonides, loc. cit.

units.la: Venam qui secat, non comedet pisces, lac, caseum, ova. Nedarim sol.54.2. Qui somniat sibi secari venam, peccata eius remittuntur. Berachot chot sol.57.1 & p.60.1. R.Acha ad venam secundam ingressus, dicebat, Sit voluntas tua Domine Deus Mi, ut negotium hoc mihi cedat ad sanitatem.
units.tr: Whoever has a vein opened shall not eat fish, milk, cheese, or eggs. Nedarim fol. 54.2. Whoever dreams that a vein is being opened for him has his sins forgiven. Berachoth fol. 57.1 and fol. 60.1. Rabbi Acha, when he entered for the second bloodletting, used to say, "May it be your will, Lord my God, that this business turn out well for me for my health."

units.la: VENERI dicatum erat Balneum Aconense sive Ptolemaidis, & in ea lavit aliquando Rabban Gamaliel,praesente Proculo filio Philosophi: de ipsorum disputatione vid. Avoda Zarah cap. 3. verf. 4.
units.tr: The bath at Accho, or Ptolemais, was dedicated to Venus, and Rabban Gamaliel once bathed in it, in the presence of Proclus, the son of the philosopher. For their dispute about this, see Avodah Zarah ch. 3, verse 4.

units.la: VESTES. De vestitu Iudaeorum vide Cl. Buxtorf. in Synag. Quicunque induet vestes suas absque benedictione, is induetur vermibus, qui moleftiores sunt quam acus in carne viva. Orchot Chajim. Quicunque contemnit vestes [Hebrew] [Hebrew] tandem nullum illarum usum habebit. Hinc etiam David tandem non calefiebat, quamvis ipsis imponerentur vestes, quia dilaceraverat pallium Saulis. Vid. Rabbi Salomoh ad 1.Reg.1.v.1. & Ialkut in lib. Reg.
units.tr: GARMENTS. On the dress of the Jews, see the distinguished Buxtorf in Synagoga. Whoever puts on his clothes without a blessing will be clothed with worms, which are more troublesome than needles in living flesh. Orchot Chajim. Whoever despises his garments will in the end have no use of them. Hence also David, though garments were put on him, could not get warm in the end, because he had torn Saul's mantle. See Rabbi Solomon on 1 Kings 1:1, and the Yalkut on the books of Kings.

units.la: Lugens non debebat lavare sua vestimenta, aut se iuduere vestibus dealbatis; Colbo cap.114. Maymon Halac. [Hebrew] cap. 5. non autem solum laetitiam denotabant vestimenta alba, sed etiam innocentiam: hinc locus in Middot cap.5. v.3. In conclavi Gazith etiam sedebat Synedrium, quando diiudicabat Sacerdotes; Sacerdos in quo inventum erat aliquod vitium, induebat sibi vestimenta [Hebrew] nigra, ac atris involutus egrediebatur; cui vero non inerat vitium, induebat sibi vestimenta [Hebrew] alba, & albis involutus ingrediebatur.
units.tr: A mourner was not to wash his garments, or put on white garments. Colbo ch. 114; Maimonides, Halachoth ch. 5. White garments denoted not only joy but also innocence. Hence the passage in Middoth ch. 5, verse 3: "In the chamber Gazith the Sanhedrin also sat when it judged the priests. A priest in whom some blemish was found put on black garments and went out wrapped in dark clothing; but one in whom there was no blemish put on white garments and entered wrapped in white."

units.la: Israelitae in deserto vestiti fuerunt ex eo quo Angeli ministeriales vestiverunt eos, ex purpura scil. Si quaeris, an non parvi facti sunt maiores? Respondetur, abi & discè à testudine, cum qua simul crescit concha vel testa eius. Nubesque gloriæ illas vestes commaculatas purificabat; vid. Talkut Psalm.23.98. col. 2. Midrasch Tillim Psalm. 23.
units.tr: The Israelites in the wilderness were clothed with the same clothing that the ministering angels had clothed them with, namely, purple. If you ask whether they did not become bigger, the answer is: go and learn from the tortoise, with which its shell grows at the same time. The clouds of glory purified those garments that had been stained; see Talkut on Psalm 23, 98, col. 2; Midrash Tillim on Psalm 23.

units.la: De vestimentis Sacerdotum vid. Sacerdotes.
units.tr: On the vestments of the priests, see Priests.

units.la: De vestium dilaceratione in Blasphemiis & luctu. Vid. Blasphemiam in B. & Laceratio in L.
units.tr: On the tearing of garments in blasphemy and mourning, see Blasphemy under B and Laceration under L.

units.la: Vestis interior Iudæi vocatur חלוק quod respondet Græco ἐνδύματι, exterior verò nominatur טלית; illi intextæ erant fimbriæ memorativæ de quibus mentio fit Numer.15.38. Græcè dicitur κρασπεδον, & de tali pallio loquitur Christus Matth.5.v.40. Loca in quibus de Tallit mentio fit, sunt Bab.Schabbat sol.23.2. Bab.Bava Metzia sol.78.2. Nedarim sol.33.1.
units.tr: The Jew's inner garment is called חלוק, which corresponds to the Greek ἐνδύματι [garment]. The outer garment is called טלית. Into it were woven memorial fringes, mentioned at Numbers 15:38. In Greek they are called κρασπεδον [fringes], and Christ speaks of such a cloak at Matthew 5:40. Places where the tallit is mentioned are Bab. Shabbat fol. 23.2, Bab. Bava Metzia fol. 78.2, and Nedarim fol. 33.1.

units.la: De Muliebribus ornamentis & vestimentis Vid. Mulieres.
units.tr: On women's ornaments and garments, see Women.

units.la: VIA per tectum (ad quam alluditur ab Evangelista Marci 11.4. quando inquit Ἀπογεύεσθε τὴν σεγλω &c.) à Talmudicis vocatur דרך גגין ;
units.tr: The way through the roof (to which the Evangelist Mark alludes at 11:4, when he says Ἀπογεύεσθε τὴν σεγλω etc.) is called by the Talmudists דרך גגין.

units.la: Bab. Moed Katon sol.25.1. Cum mortuus esset Rabh Houna, feretrum eius per ostium efferri non potuit סבור שלשולי דרך גגין Visum est ipsis illud per tectum extrahere &c.
units.tr: Bab. Moed Katan fol. 25.1: "When Rabbi Huna had died, his bier could not be carried out through the door. They thought it best to bring it out through the roof" [סבור שלשולי דרך גגין], etc.

units.la: Bava Metzia sol.88.1. Cum introitus in atrium est per portam גגות לאפיקי דרך Ad excipiendum viam per tectum. Illius locutionis exemplum habes etiam in sol.117.1. eiusdem tractat.
units.tr: Bava Metzia fol. 88.1: "When the entrance into the court is through the gate, one uses the way through the roof" [גגות לאפיקי דרך]. You will find an example of this expression also in fol. 117.1 of the same tractate.

units.la: Mensuræ viarum traduntur in Bava Bathra sol.100. Via privata (דרך היחיד) est lata quatuor cubitorum; via ab urbe in urbem, latitudinem habet octo cubitorum. דרך הרכים Via publica (illa scil. per quam non solùm una vel altera urbs transfivit, sed quæ erat communis omnibus.) lata est sedecim cubitorum. Via ad civitates refugii est lata triginta duorum cubitorum. דרך המלך Via Regis non habet mensuram, nam Rex quando cum exercitu egreditur potest sepes perfringere, & viam sibi struere ubi voluerit. Via ad sepulchrum etiam non habet mensuram, ob honore mortui: scilicet ne comitantes feretrū, ob angustiam viæ segregarentur.
units.tr: The measurements of roads are given in Bava Bathra fol. 100. A private way (דרך היחיד) is four cubits wide. A way from one city to another is eight cubits wide. A public way (דרך הרבים), that is, one through which not merely one or another city passes but which is common to all, is sixteen cubits wide. The way to the cities of refuge is thirty-two cubits wide. The king's way (דרך המלך) has no fixed measure, for when the king goes out with his army he may break through hedges and make a road wherever he wishes. The way to a sepulchre also has no measure, out of honour for the dead, so that those accompanying the bier are not separated by the narrowness of the road.

units.la: De via publica & privata in agris & sementibus vid. etiam Maym. in Peah cap. 2. 1.
units.tr: On public and private ways through fields and sown land, see also Maimonides in Peah ch. 2.1.

units.la: Vidua non adhibentur tosta, dicitur in Ketubbot sol. 17. 2.
units.tr: Roasted food is not served to widows; it is said in Ketubbot fol. 17.2.

units.la: id est secundùm Aruch, solebant coquere triticum & fabas, iniectis uvis passis, & sorbebant illud; Hoc in nuptiis faciebant virgini sponsæ, sed viduæ non faciebant. Hinc etiam cognosci poterat an sponsa virgo esset vel vidua.
units.tr: That is, according to the Aruch, they used to roast wheat and beans, add raisins, and drink the mixture. This they did for a virgin bride at her wedding, but not for a widow. By this means one could also tell whether a bride was a virgin or a widow.

units.la: De viduarum domiciliis v. Dalmanutha in D.
units.tr: On widows' dwellings, see Dalmanutha under D.

units.la: Vinea :
units.tr: Vineyard:

units.la: De illa memorabilem habemus Parabolam in c. 12. Marci. ad illius explicationem Nota quæ sunt apud Talmudicos.
units.tr: We have a memorable parable about it in Mark ch. 12. For its explanation, note what the Talmudists say.

units.la: Pharisæi facile intellexerunt Christum de ipsis loqui, nam hoc erat apud Judaicam gentem ordinarium assimilare se vineæ, & se vineam Dei dicere. Talis parabola exstat apud Tanchum folio 54. 3. Erat Regi vinea, atque tres ISTI inimicabantur; Quidnam illi fecerunt? Vnus excidit racemos, Secundus defalcavit botros, & tertius extirpavit vites. Rex ISTE est Rex Regum, Dominus benedictus; Vinea Domini est domus
units.tr: The Pharisees easily understood that Christ was speaking about them. For it was customary among the Jewish people to compare themselves to a vineyard and to call themselves the vineyard of God. Such a parable exists in Tanchuma fol. 54.3: "A king had a vineyard, and three enemies harmed it. What did they do? The first cut off the clusters, the second stripped off the grapes, and the third uprooted the vines. That king is the King of kings, the blessed Lord. The vineyard of the Lord is the house of

units.la: Israelis. Tres inimici sunt Pharao, Nebucadnezar & Haman.
units.tr: Israel. The three enemies are Pharaoh, Nebuchadnezzar and Haman.

units.la: 'Αμπελῶν כרם est, & dicitur secundùm Schammæanos, quando quis plantavit seriem unam quinque vitium, Hilleliani verò volunt nullam vineam esse, nisi in illa sint duo ordines vitium. Kilaim cap.4.v.5.
units.tr: A vineyard (ἀμπελῶν) is כרם. According to the Shammaites, something is a vineyard when someone has planted a single row of five vines. The Hillelites, however, hold that there is no vineyard unless there are two rows of vines. Kilaim ch. 4 v. 5.

units.la: Φραγμὸς sepes vitis debet esse alta decem palmos, his minus non est sepes. Ibid.v.3.
units.tr: A hedge (φραγμὸς) around a vine must be ten palms high; a hedge less than this is not a hedge. Ibid. v. 3.

units.la: Ὑπολήνιον גת Lacum Dominus vineæ facere debet profundum decem palmos, & latum quatuor. Ibi ubi sup.
units.tr: A wine-press (ὑπολήνιον, גת): the lord of the vineyard must make a pit for it ten palms deep and four palms wide. Ibid., as above.

units.la: שומרו ο πύργος Custodia in vinea, sit alta decem cubitos, & quatuor lata. Kilaim c.5.v.3.
units.tr: A watch-tower (שומרו or πύργος) in the vineyard should be ten cubits high and four cubits wide. Kilaim ch. 5 v. 3.

units.la: De כרמים quibus elocata vinea, quomodo diligenter illam curare debeant V. Maym. in שכירות c.2.
units.tr: On the כרמים to whom a vineyard is let, and how diligently they ought to tend it, see Maimonides in Schekhirut ch. 2.

units.la: Dicit etiam Evangelium, Dominum vineæ misisse legatum vel servum ad agricolas τῷ καιρῷ suo tempore: intellige Anno quarto à prima eius plantatione; ante hunc annum enim nullus erat fructuum usus. Vid. Annum quartum. in A.
units.tr: The Gospel also says that the lord of the vineyard sent a servant or messenger to the husbandmen at the proper time (τῷ καιρῷ). Understand this as the fourth year after the first planting, for before that year the fruit could not be used. See Fourth year under A.

units.la: VINUM Iudeæ optimum Vid. in Israelitica terra apud I.
units.tr: On the excellent wine of Judea, see Land of Israel under I.

units.la: Vini Italici quartanam inebriare docent Hierof. Avod. Zarah sol. 40. 1. & tamen Hierof. Schabbat sol. 11. 1. dicunt quatuor illa pocula quæ ebibenda sunt in epulis Paschatis & sacris continêre quartanam vini Italici. Sobriè ergo ab illis epulis discessum est.
units.tr: The Jerusalem Talmud, Avodah Zarah fol. 40.1, teaches that a quarter measure of Italian wine intoxicates. Yet the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat fol. 11.1, says that the four cups to be drunk at the Passover meals and sacred feasts contain a quarter measure of Italian wine. They therefore left those feasts sober.

units.la: Rabbini in dictum Prov.23.31. sic commentantur. Ne aspicias vinum rubrum, quia rubrum est: i.e. quia finis eius est sanguis; excitat enim
units.tr: The rabbis comment on Proverbs 23:31 as follows: "Do not look at the red wine, because it is red", that is, because its end is blood, for it stirs up quarrels and fights with the shedding of blood.

units.la: lites & pugnas cum sanguinis effusione ; Glossa alia. דרם נדר כי יתאוה לדם quia expetit sanguinem menstruate mulieris ; i.e. excitat libidines, ut homo ne menstruatæ mulieri parcat. Alius dixit, Quia rubram faciẽ faciem hominis. Vid.Tanchuma.
units.tr: Another gloss reads: "because it desires the blood of a menstruating woman" [דרם נדר כי יתאוה לדם]; that is, it stirs up lusts so that a man does not spare a menstruating woman. Another said: "because it makes a man's face red." See Tanchuma.

units.la: Vinum אספרגוס Asparaginum id est, vinum in quo Asparagum macerarunt, ieiuno stomacho bibebant sanitatis causâ. Beracot sol.51. in R. Salom.
units.tr: Asparagus wine (asparaginum), that is, wine in which asparagus had been steeped, was drunk on an empty stomach for the sake of health. See Berakhot fol. 51, in R. Solomon.

units.la: Amans חמרא וכספא Vinum & aromata non ditabitur. Chald. in Prov.21.17.
units.tr: One who loves wine and spices will not grow rich (חמרא וכספא). Chaldee on Proverbs 21:17.

units.la: הדבור רע ליין Locutio mala est vino: cùm nempe dolium vacuum repleto maiorem edet sonum, sonus ille malum est signum, docet enim vinum esse exhaustum. E contra הקול יפה לבשמ sonus pulcher est aromatibus, cùm tunduntur. Vid. etiam Menachot sol.87.1.
units.tr: "An evil sound is to wine" (הדבור רע ליין): when a cask is empty it gives a louder sound than when it is full, and that sound is a bad sign, for it shows that the wine has been drawn off. On the contrary, "a pleasant sound is to spices" (הקול יפה לבשמים) when they are pounded. See also Menachot fol. 87.1.

units.la: חמרא חמרא פמי דשתי חמרא Coram bibentibus vinum, vinum ponitur; Prov.est, denotans hominem esse ut suit eius educatio; delicatè nutritis delicias placere. Sotah sol.10 1.
units.tr: "Wine is set before those who drink wine": the proverb means that a man is as his upbringing was, and that delicacies please those who were delicately nurtured. Sotah fol. 10.1.

units.la: Ebibens calicem suum vice unâ est gulosus גרגר, duabus est דרך ארץ Politicum & civile. Tribus est rusticorum. Pesachim c.7. in sin.
units.tr: One who drinks his cup at one time is a glutton (גרגר). At two times it is good manners and civility (דרך ארץ). At three times it is the way of rustics. Pesachim ch. 7, at the end.

units.la: Iudæi etiam utebantur Syphonibus ad extrahendum vinum è dolio. Vid. Avoda Zarah sol.72. col.2.
units.tr: The Jews also used siphons to draw wine out of a cask. See Avodah Zarah fol. 72, col. 2.

units.la: חמרא פרוגי תא Vinum Prugiathinum & thermæ דיומסיר Diomafit, absciderunt decem tribus ab Israelitis. Id est, voluptates & delicię perdiderunt eos. Schabbat sol. 147. 2. Erat enim Prugiathinum vinum idem apud Iudæos ac Falernum apud Italos.
units.tr: "Prugiathine wine and baths" (דיומסיר): "the ten tribes were cut off from Israel." That is, pleasures and delights destroyed them. Shabbat fol. 147.2. For Prugiathine wine was among the Jews what Falernian was among the Italians.

units.la: Vinum de quo bibet Messias cùm venerit custoditur in uvis suis inde à sex diebus creationis mundi. Sanhed. sol.99.1.
units.tr: The wine which the Messiah will drink when he comes has been kept in its grapes since the six days of the creation of the world. Sanhedrin fol. 99.1.

units.la: נכנם יין יצא סוד Ingrediente vino, egreditur secretum. Quare vocatur vinum יין? Quia affert יללה eiulatum in mundum, suo abusu. Ioma sol.76.2. Pulchrum est vinum senibus sicut lac infantibus. Erubbin sol.65.
units.tr: "When wine goes in, secret goes out" (נכנם יין יצא סוד). Why is wine called יין? Because by its abuse it brings wailing (יללה) into the world. Yoma fol. 76.2. "Wine is pleasant to the old, as milk is to infants." Erubin fol. 65.

units.la: Habuerunt Iudæi etiam potus extraneos, artificialiter confectos, ut כותח הבבלי Kuttach Babylonicum, de quo 3. referunt in Pesa hin sol.42.1. Ipsum obstruere cor (abusivè sumptum) propter ferum lactis ipsi immixtum, excaecare oculos, propter Sal Sodomiticum ipsi immixtum cuius hæc erat proprietas; emaciare corpus, propter putredinem panis mucidi ipsi immixti. Alius potus erat שכר המדי Sicera vel Cerevisia Medæa, quæ ex aquis hordeorum ut cerevisia nostra confecta erat. Pesachin sol.42. col.2. Celebris etiam erat זיתוס המצרי Zythum Ægyptiacum, cuius tertia pars erat hordeum, tertia pars crocus sylvestris, tertia pars Sal. Schabbat sol.156.1. Ex Asia etiam liquor dulcis in Palæstinam afferebatur, cui nomen קרינא Avod. Zarah sol.30.1.
units.tr: The Jews also had other, artificially prepared drinks, such as the Babylonian kuttach (כותח הבבלי), of which three effects are reported in Pesachin fol. 42.1: it "stops up the heart" (a figurative use), because of the wild milk mixed into it; it "blinds the eyes," because of the Sodomitic salt mixed into it, whose property this was; and it "wastes the body," because of the rot of mouldy bread mixed into it. Another drink was the Median beer (שכר המדי), or sicera, made from barley water, like our beer. Pesachin fol. 42, col. 2. The Egyptian zythum (זיתוס המצרי) was also famous: one third of it was barley, one third wild saffron, and one third salt. Shabbat fol. 156.1. A sweet liquor was also brought into Palestine from Asia, called קרינא. Avodah Zarah fol. 30.1.

units.la: §. De vino adhibito ih epulo paschali vid. Pascha. De vino libaminis vid. Sacrificia.
units.tr: On the wine used at the paschal meal, see Passover. On the wine of libation, see Sacrifices.

units.la: VITULI Decollationem vid. Iuvenca &c. in I.
units.tr: On the beheading of the calf, see Heifer etc. under I.

units.la: VITAM æternam non possidebunt, qui dicunt nullam esse resurrectionem mortuorum. Qui negat legem à Cœlo esse. Qui Epicuream vitam agit. Qui legit ספרי החיצוני libros extraneos. Qui vulneri aut plagæ insusurrat. Qui Dei nomen tetragrammaton suis literis pronuntiat. Tres Reges & 4. Idiotæ vitæ æternæ exsortes erunt; Reges sunt Hieroboam, Achab, Manasses; Idiotæ sunt, Bileam, Doeg, Ahitophel, Gehasi. Qui diluvio perière vitæ futuræ exfortes erunt, neque etiam sistentur iudicio. Viris Sodomæ nulla pars erit in vita æterna, stabunt tamen in iudicio. Generatio quæ in deserto periit exsors erit vitæ futuræ, neque stabit in iudicio. Cives urbis ad Idololatriam delapsæ, carebunt sorte futuri seculi. Sanhed. cap.II.
units.tr: Those who say there is no resurrection of the dead shall not possess eternal life; so too those who say the law is not from heaven; those who live an Epicurean life; those who read the outside books (ספרי החיצוני); those who whisper over a wound or a blow; and those who pronounce the name of God, the tetragrammaton, as it is written. Three kings and four commoners will have no share in eternal life. The kings are Jeroboam, Ahab and Manasseh; the commoners are Balaam, Doeg, Ahithophel and Gehazi. Those who perished in the flood will have no share in the future life, nor will they stand in judgement. The men of Sodom will have no portion in eternal life, but they will stand in judgement. The generation that perished in the wilderness will have no share in the future life, nor will it stand in judgement. The citizens of a city that fell into idolatry will be deprived of their portion in the world to come. Sanhedrin ch. 11.

units.la: עולם הבא Seculum futurum duplici sensu à Iudæis sumitur; 1. de יום השנה Diebus Messiæ solùm, in quibus epulis exquisitissimis sunt opplendi, omnia abundabunt, & de hoc seculo futuro suum regnum formarunt Chiliastæ. 2. de æterna beatitudine, quæ convivium illud & dies Messiæ excipiet ævo infinito. Vid. Formul. loquendi in F.
units.tr: The Jews take the phrase world to come [עולם הבא] in two senses: (1) only of the days of the Messiah [יום המשיח], in which men will be filled with the choicest feasts and all things will abound; from this future age the Chiliasts formed their kingdom; (2) of eternal blessedness, which will follow that banquet and the days of the Messiah for an endless age. See Formul. loquendi under F.

units.la: VITULI conflati se adhuc hodie pœnas dare asserunt Iudæi. Sanhed.cap.ult. Nulla adhuc calamitas venit in mundum sc. post conflatum vitulum, in qua non fuit granum vel drachma in depressione libra, vituli illius adorati, quia ditlum est Exod.32.34. Quandocunque visitabo &c.Vid.Beth Israel pag.130 col.1.
units.tr: The Jews still today claim that they are paying penalties for the molten calf. Sanhed. ch. last: No calamity has yet come into the world since the molten calf, in which there was not a grain or a drachma's weight in the scale of that calf which was worshipped, since it is said Exod. 32:34, Whenever I visit, &c. See Beth Israel, p. 130, col. 1.

units.la: VNCTIO. Olim in bellis,clypei pinguedine ungebantur, ut nitida clypei superficies non facilè iacula susciperet. Kimchi 2.Sam.1.21.
units.tr: ANOINTING. In former times, in wars, shields were smeared with the fat of the shield, so that the polished surface would not easily take up missiles. Kimchi on 2 Sam. 1:21.

units.la: Vngebantur olim Reges,Prophetæ,& Summi Sacerdotes, quia erant custodes utriusque ta-
units.tr: Kings, prophets and high priests were anointed in former times, because they were the guardians of both tables.

units.la: bulæ. Abrabanel Exod.30.33. Eadem erat utrifque affusio יציקה, idem oleum,ex 4.aromatibus constans; Vid.verf.23.& Oleum in O. At regis tantùm erat ad fontem ungi, idque sibi & posteris, ad augurium felicis & diutinæ regni fubfistentiæ. Salomoh, Ioas, Ioachas proinde non ungi debebant ad fontem, quia patribus succedebant, nec novum instituebant regnum; unĉi tamen ad fontem sunt למלוּך המחלוּקת Ad controversiam tollendam. Cerithut cap.5.Maymon Hal. Melachim cap.1.
units.tr: (Abarbanel on Exod. 30:33.) The pouring [יציקה] was the same for each, and the same oil, made of four aromatic spices; see v. 23, and under Oil in O. But for a king it was only at the fountain that he was anointed, and that for himself and his posterity, as an omen of a happy and lasting continuance of the kingdom. Solomon, Joash and Jehoahaz therefore ought not to have been anointed at the fountain, because they succeeded their fathers and did not institute a new kingdom; yet they were anointed at the fountain to settle the controversy [למלוך המחלוקת]. Ad controversiam tollendam. Cerithut ch. 5. Maimonides, Hilchot Melachim ch. 1.

units.la: Rex deinde inter oculorum palpebras in formam coronæ, summus Sacerdos verò in formam X Græcorum ungebatur; Cerithut c.5. Maymon Hal. Kele Hamikdafch cap. 1. Pro X habet Abarbenel ׂ loco cit.quia eius erat Deo manibus servire.
units.tr: Then the king was anointed between the eyelids in the form of a crown, but the high priest in the form of the Greek letter X. Cerithut c. 5; Maimonides, Hilchot Kele Hamikdash ch. 1. For the X, Abarbanel in the passage cited gives the reason that the priest was to serve God with his hands.

units.la: Iehu & Saul è lenticula unẗi sunt, ideo non protraxerunt imperium : David verò & Salomon è cornu, & proinde quoque perpetuarunt regnum. Kimchi 2.Reg.9.1.
units.tr: Jehu and Saul were anointed from a little flask, and therefore they did not prolong their rule; but David and Solomon were anointed from a horn, and so they also perpetuated the kingdom. Kimchi on 2 Kings 9:1.

units.la: §. Olim apud Iudæos ægroti ungebantur; Vid. Ægrotum in A. quod confirmat ea quæ dicit Iacobus Apost. c.5.
units.tr: § Formerly among the Jews the sick were anointed; see Sick under A, which confirms what the Apostle James says in ch. 5.

units.la: §. Ieiunantes nec se unxerunt nec lavarunt; Ioma c.8.v.1. Die expiationis prohibitum est edere, bibere, lavare,ungere se, induere Sandalia. At rex & sponsa lavant facies suas. Consule etiam Gemar.Babil. sol.77.2. Christus iubet Matth.17. ut ieiunantes se ungant.
units.tr: § Those who fasted neither anointed nor washed themselves. Yoma ch. 8, v. 1: On the Day of Atonement it is forbidden to eat, drink, wash, anoint oneself, or put on sandals. But the king and the bride wash their faces. Consult also Gemara Babli, fol. 77.2. Christ commands in Matt. 17 that those who fast should anoint themselves.

units.la: §. Corpora & capita ungere soliti sunt triplici ratione.
units.tr: § Bodies and heads were customarily anointed for three reasons.

units.la: I. לתענוג In deces & delicias maiores.Hieros. in Maafer Scheni sol.53.2.& Schabb.sol.12.1. Unctio Sabbatho permittitur,sive sit in decorem,sive non in decorem. Die Expiationis, utraque prohibetur; Nono mensis Abh & in ieiuniis,unctio in decorem prohibetur, non in decorem permittitur.
units.tr: I. לתענוג For delight and greater pleasures. Jerusalem Talmud, Maaser Sheni, fol. 53.2, and Shabbat, fol. 12.1: Anointing is permitted on the Sabbath, whether for adornment or not for adornment. On the Day of Atonement both are forbidden; on the ninth of Av and in fasts, anointing for adornment is forbidden, but not anointing without adornment, which is permitted.

units.la: II. סיכה שלא לתענוג Erat unctio propter aliquem morbum,ad adiuvandam corporis sanitatem : uti iam supra monuimus & videtur ex Hierof. ubi supra ; Qui capite dolet, aut cui oritur scabies,ungat se oleo Vid.etiam Bab.Iema f.77.2.
units.tr: II. סיכה שלא לתענוג Anointing not for delight. This was anointing on account of some illness, to help the health of the body, as we have already noted above and as appears from the Jerusalem Talmud in the place cited: He who suffers in the head, or in whom scabies arises, let him anoint himself with oil. See also Babylonian Gemara, fol. 77.2.

units.la: III. Vsi sunt aliquando unctione superstitiosâ. Hierof.Maafer Scheni sol.52.2. Qui muffitat נותן שמן על גבי ראשו Det oleum super caput, & muffuet.
units.tr: III. They sometimes used superstitious anointing. Jerusalem Talmud, Maaser Sheni, fol. 52.2: He who mutters [נותן שמן על גבי ראשו] puts oil upon his head and mutters.

units.la: §. In Babylonia in usu erat capita Rabbinorum in nuptiis ungere, vid.Nuptiis. Pedes oleo ungere erat etiam vulgatissimum; at unguento aromatico, rarissimum; & in Schabbat sol.62.2. Gemaristæ reputant pro crimine,quòd fœminæ Hierosolymitanæ etiam calceos ungerent unguento odorifero, ut allicerent iuvenes ad lasci-viam. Extraordinarium ergo est factum Ioh. 12.3.
units.tr: § In Babylon it was the custom to anoint the heads of the rabbis at weddings; see Nuptials. To anoint the feet with oil was also very common, but with aromatic unguent very rare; and in Shabbat, fol. 62.2, the Gemarists count it a crime that the women of Jerusalem anointed even their shoes with fragrant unguent, so as to entice young men to lasciviousness. The deed in John 12:3 was therefore extraordinary.

units.la: §. Tempore Messiæ restituetur unctio Sacra Ecclesiæ. Abarbenel art. 13.
units.tr: § In the time of the Messiah the sacred anointing of the Church will be restored. Abarbanel, art. 13.

units.la: §. Tandem, usitatissimum erat, in epulis etiam sacris, non solum profanis, capiti alicuius præsentis oleum aromatibus conditum illinire. H. Beratot sol.11.2. Schola Schammaana dicit,Oleum suave dextra tenet, & poculum vini sinistra. Recitat primum benedictionem super oleo, & dein super poculo. Schola Hilleliana dicit, Oleum tenet dextra, poculum sinistra. Benedicit super oleo suave, atque illinit capiti ministrantis: si vero miniftrans fit discipulus Sapientis, illinit parieti; nam indecorum est discipulo sapientum olere aromata. Confer Matth.26.7.7.
units.tr: § Finally, it was very usual, even at sacred feasts and not only at profane ones, to smear oil seasoned with spices on the head of someone present. H. Berachot, fol. 11.2: The school of Shammai says: one holds the sweet oil in the right hand and the cup of wine in the left. He recites the blessing first over the oil, and then over the cup. The school of Hillel says: one holds the oil in the right hand, the cup in the left. He blesses over the sweet oil and anoints the head of the one serving; but if the one serving is a disciple of a sage, he anoints the wall, for it is unbecoming for a disciple of the sages to smell of spices. Compare Matth. 26.7.

units.la: Vngues comburit Sanctus, iustus sepelit eos, impius vero spargit in publicum, ut maleficae iis abutantur. Nidda 17.1.
units.tr: The Holy One burns the nails; the righteous bury them; but the wicked scatter them in public, so that witches may misuse them. Nidda 17.1.

units.la: Vota. Non sit leve in oculis tuis sectio de votis, quia propter sectionem de votis occisum est Synedrium magnum Ezechiæ &c. Echa Rabbeti Thren.2.v.10. Voisin pug.fid.716.
units.tr: Vows. Let not the section on vows be light in your eyes, because on account of the section on vows the Great Sanhedrin of Hezekiah was put to death, &c. Echa Rabbati, Lam. 2:10. Voisin, Pugio fidei, 716.

units.la: Præcipiunt sapientes, ne quis abstineat nisi ab iis, à quibus per legem iubetur abstinere. ולא יהא אוסר עצמן נדרים וכשבועות על הדברים המותרים Neque se voto aut iuramento privet illis, qua ipsi aliàs licita essent; quæ cum ita sint, qui se perpetuo ieiunio macerant, viâ rectâ non progrediuntur &c. Maymon in דעות cap.3. ubi plurima alia eiusdem argumenti tradit.
units.tr: The sages direct that no one should abstain except from those things from which the law orders abstinence. And let no one bind himself by vows and oaths concerning things that are permitted [ולא יהא אוסר עצמן נדרים וכשבועות על הדברים המותרים]: neither should he deprive himself by vow or oath of those things which would otherwise be lawful; and since this is so, those who wear themselves out with perpetual fasting do not advance by the straight path, &c. Maimonides, Deot, ch. 3, Maymon where he gives very many other things of the same kind.

units.la: Non interest inter votivum ex quo habetur usufructus, & votivum ex quo habetur cibus, præter conculcationem pedis. (i.e. admittitur ille qui votum habet circa cibum ad sua, non autem ille qui circa usumfructum vovit.)
units.tr: There is no difference between a vow by which the usufruct is had and a vow by which food is had, except for the trampling of the foot. (That is, one who has vowed concerning food is admitted to his own things, but not one who has vowed concerning the usufruct.)

units.la: Non interest inter נדרים & נדבות, nisi quoad in נדרים quis teneatur ad cautionem de futuro damno in נדבות voluntariis non item. (i.e. si quis agnum voverit in Holocaustum, agnus vero vel mortuus vel surreptus fuerit, debet alium substituere; ad quod tamen non tenetur si sponte מנרב ad holocaustum agnum obtulerit.) Megillah c.1.6.
units.tr: There is no difference between vows [נדרים] and freewill offerings [נדבות], except that in the case of vows a man is bound to give security against future loss, while in the case of voluntary offerings he is not. (That is, if someone has vowed a lamb as a burnt offering and the lamb has either died or been stolen, he must substitute another; yet he is not bound to do so if he offered the lamb for a burnt offering of his own accord.) Megillah ch. 1, 6.

units.la: Qui voverat se non dormiturum in lecto, ei licitum erat decumbere בערסא ריצלא in lecto coriaceo, (qui vilißimus æstimatus est.)
units.tr: One who had vowed not to sleep on a bed was permitted to recline on a leather couch [בערסא ריצלא], which was reckoned the cheapest kind.

units.la: Cùm quis votum generalibus terminis enuntiaret, e. g. dicendo, Hoc mihi estoficut truma, non nominata quali Truma, si vovens illâ ratione, habitabat in Iudæa, Trumam vel oblationem illam solvere debebat Thesaurario Templi; at si Galilæus voverit, voto solutus est,quia ille pro distantia loci, non novit Trumam הלשכה thesauri. Si generaliter quis voverit per Anathemata,solvitur in Iudæa,& ligatur in Galilæa, quia Galilæi non norunt anathemata Sacerdotum. i.e. Non erant Sacerdotes inter Galilæos, cùm itaque anathematizarent, anathematizarunt non nisi Deo. Nedarim cap.2.3.
units.tr: When someone expressed a vow in general terms, for example by saying, This is to me like the truma, without naming which truma, then if the one vowing lived in Judaea, he had to pay the truma or that offering to the treasurer of the Temple; but if a Galilean made the vow, he was released from it, because on account of the distance from the place he did not know the truma of the treasury [הלשכה]. If someone vowed generally by anathemata, the vow is loosed in Judaea and binds in Galilee, because the Galileans did not know the anathemata of the priests; that is, there were no priests among the Galileans, so when they pronounced an anathema, they pronounced it only to God. Nedarim ch. 2, 3.

units.la: §. De votis in specie observa, illa fuisse distincta in duas classes: In נדרי הקדש Vota consecrationis, & נדרי איסור Vota obligationis. Votum consecrationis fuit, cùm aliquid devoveretur in usus sacros, altaris scilicet, aut templi: veluti cùm quis voto hoc vel illud dicaret in Sacrificium,vel ad coquendum lignum,sal,vinum pro altari &c. Votum obligationis fuit, cùm se quis voto adstringeret ad hoc vel illud, quod in se erat licitum, veluti, se hoc vel illud non comesturum, non indueturum, non facturum.
units.tr: § Concerning vows in particular, note that they were divided into two classes: vows of consecration [נדרי הקדש] and vows of obligation [נדרי איסור]. A vow of consecration was when something was devoted to sacred uses, namely of the altar or of the Temple: as when someone by vow said that this or that would be for a sacrifice, or for wood, salt or wine for the altar, &c. A vow of obligation was when someone bound himself by vow to this or that which in itself was lawful, such as that he would not eat this or that, not wear it, not do it.

units.la: §. Nota etiam, Iudæis fuisse pro noto axiomate, כל כינוי נדרים כנדרים Omnia Fpitheta votorum sunt sicut ipsa vota. Nedarim. cap.1.v.1. Id est, non opus erat ut aliquid esset devotum, ut longâ circumscriptione significaretur, sed suffecit dixisse קונח Konah, vel כונס Konas, vel קרבן Δῶρον, hæc enim erant epitheta rei devotx. Nedar. cap.I. v.2. Confer Matth.15. v.5.
units.tr: § Note also that it was a well-known axiom among the Jews: All epithets of vows are like the vows themselves [כל כינוי נדרים כנדרים]. Nedarim ch. 1, v. 1. That is, it was not necessary that something be declared devoted in order to signify it by a long circumlocution; it sufficed to say Konah [קונח], or Konas [כונס], or korban [קרבן], which is gift [δῶρον]; for these were the epithets of a devoted thing. Nedarim ch. 1, v. 2. Compare Matt. 15:5.

units.la: VRIM & TUMIM. Pectorali Pontificis lapides inserti erant, qui vocabantur אורים ותומים Luces & perfectiones, ex hoc Vrim & Tummim Sacerdos magnus consulentibus responsum reddidit, atque inde oraculo nomina haec indicta sunt. Vocantur enim אורים quia illi מאורין לישראל Israelem illuminabant. תומים vero שהן מתיסין לגניהן את הדרך Quia coram ipsis perficiebant viam. i. e. viam indicabant quâ insistere oporteret.Gemar.Hierof.ad cap.7.Ioma.
units.tr: URIM AND THUMMIM. Stones were set into the high priest's breastplate, which were called lights and perfections [אורים ותומים]. By these the high priest gave responses to those who consulted him, and from this the oracle received these names. They are called lights because they illuminated Israel [מאורין לישראל], and perfections because they made the way perfect before them [שהן מתיסין לגניהן את הדרך], that is, they indicated the way in which one ought to walk. Gemara Jerusalem on ch. 7, Yoma.

units.la: Modus hoc oraculum consulendi hic erat. Pontifex arcam versus faciem inflexit; ille qui oraculum consuluit ei à tergo stetit, dixitque faciam hoc, aut non faciam? Tum Pontifex Vrim & Thumim inspexit & è vestigio responsum invenit. De duobus simul non inquisiverunt, nisi hoc temporis angustiae exegissent; Ordine etiam inverso non petiverunt, & si petiissent, oraculum ad quaesita ordine respondebat: & quod primum futurum erat primum praedixit. Vid. Gemaram Babyl. ad Ioma.7.
units.tr: The manner of consulting the oracle was this. The High Priest turned his face towards the ark, and the one who consulted the oracle stood behind him and said, "Shall I do this, or not?" Then the High Priest looked at the Urim and Thummim and at once found the answer. They did not ask about two matters at once, unless the shortness of time forced them to. Nor did they ask in an inverted order; and if they had, the oracle answered the questions in order, and it foretold first what was to happen first. See the Babylonian Gemara on Yoma 7.

units.la: Responsum divinum exilientes literae indicarunt, erant enim in pectorali nomina Abrahami, Isaaci, Iacobi, & duodecim tribuum, ut & verba כל אלה שבטי ישראל quibus totum continetur Alphabethum. Sed ne Pontifex erraret in combinatione literarum ex punctorum vocalium defectu, dicunt Talmudici Hierofol. l.c. vocem auditam esse, quae Pontificem docuit, quomodo illae coalescerent. Ex quo videtur responsum divinum per solum gemmarum fulgorem non innotuisse ut plurimi existimarunt; aliàs alià quomodo omnia illa poterant indicari, quæ extant 2.Sam.5.23?
units.tr: The letters that leapt out indicated the divine answer. For the names of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and of the twelve tribes, were on the breastplate, and so were the words kol elleh shivtei Yisrael ("all these are the tribes of Israel"), which together contain the whole alphabet. But so that the High Priest would not err in combining the letters, owing to the lack of vowel points, the Talmudists of Jerusalem (in the passage cited above) say that a voice was heard which taught the Priest how the letters should be joined. From this it seems that the divine answer was not made known by the brilliance of the jewels alone, as most have thought; otherwise how could all those things be indicated by different letters, which are found in 2 Samuel 5:23?

units.la: Per Vrim & Thumim non de quoyis privato, sed solum de Rege inquireba.t. Ioma cap. 7. Vide etiam Schikardum de iure Regis cap.1.
units.tr: Through the Urim and Thummim one inquired not about any private person, but only about the King. Yoma, chapter 7. See also Schickard, De iure Regis, chapter 1.

units.la: Vxor. De uxore Hebraica scripsit peculiarem tractatum Seldenus.
units.tr: Wife. Seldenus wrote a special treatise on the Hebrew wife.

units.la: De nuptiis & repudiis Vid.f.1. de Fornicatione in F. & Fœminas.
units.tr: On marriages and divorces, see the entry on Fornication and Women.

units.la: Nos sequentia ex Halaca 'אישׁ Maymonidis observata hic apponemus.
units.tr: Here we shall set out the following points noted from the Halakah of Maimonides, under the heading "Man."

units.la: Cap.I. §. Ante datam legem aliquis sibi uxorem acquirebat, modò illa consentiret, & in eius domum ingressa rem cum ipso habuisset. Sed lege data necessarium fuit ut observarentur 'הליקוחי rationes uxorem ducendi.
units.tr: Chapter 1, §. Before the Law was given, a man acquired a wife for himself, provided she consented, and he had relations with her after she had entered his house. But once the Law was given it became necessary to observe the halikhot, the rules for taking a wife.

units.la: §. Tres sunt modi uxorem ducendi ספר argentum, שטר litera matrimonialis, ובעילה congressus, quorum prior argenti scilicet est extraditione Scribarum: quæ unâ ex his rationibus acquisita est dicitur מאורסה desponsata, & quamvis nondum ad virum ingressa sit, perfectè tamen eius uxor censetur. Sic Maria solum desponsata, æstimata est uxor Iosephi &c.
units.tr: §. There are three ways of taking a wife: kesef, money; shetar, a marriage document; and bi'ah, intercourse. Of these, the first, namely by money, is completed by the handing over of the money before the scribes. A woman acquired by one of these means is said to be me'orasah, betrothed; and although she has not yet entered her husband's house, she is considered fully his wife. Thus Mary, merely betrothed, was reckoned the wife of Joseph, etc.

units.la: §. Ante datam legem unusquisque cum quavis potuit congredi, modò solverit mercedem, absque ulla consequentia, sed lex prohibuit ne sit fornicatrix in Israele.
units.tr: §. Before the Law was given, anyone could have intercourse with any woman, provided he paid her wage, and there was no further consequence; but the Law forbade that there be a harlot in Israel.

units.la: §. Gradus illiciti & quæ secum ferunt נרת excidium vocantur ערות nuditates, & recensentur in sacra Scriptura; Gradus vero etiam illiciti, sed de quibus excidium non pronuntiatum est, vocantur אִיסורי לאוין prohibitiones circa negativa, & sunt sequentes, 1. Viduæ summi Pontificis; 2. Repudiata, profana, scortum, respectu Sacerdotum, tales enim ducere nunquam poterant. 3. Spuria respectu Israelitæ: & filia Israelitæ, respectu nothi, Ammonitæ, Moabitæ. 4. Nethinæa, quæ non aliter ac spuria censetur, de illis quæ vocantur שניית Vid. ibid. & Buxtorf. in Lex.Talm. De gradibus illicitis ob sanguinis propinquitatem ratione Noachidarum Vid. Cl. Heidegg. de Vita Patriarch. Exer.1.13.
units.tr: §. Degrees of forbidden union, and those which carry karet (excision), are called 'ervot (nakednesses), and they are listed in Holy Scripture. But degrees which are also forbidden, yet for which no excision has been pronounced, are called issurei lavin, prohibitions of negative precepts, and they are as follows: (1) the widow of the High Priest; (2) the divorced woman, the profane woman and the harlot, with respect to priests, for priests could never marry such women; (3) for an Israelite, the bastard, and for a bastard, the daughter of an Israelite; for an Israelite, the Ammonite and the Moabite; (4) the Nethinah, who is reckoned no differently from a bastard, concerning those called she'iyit. See ibid., and Buxtorf, Lexicon Talmudicum. On the degrees of forbidden union on account of nearness of blood, with respect to the sons of Noah, see the distinguished Heidegger, De vita patriarcharum, Exercise 1, §13.

units.la: CAP. II. §. De tempore pubertatis vid.Pubertas, de sterilitatis signis, vid. Sterilitas.
units.tr: CHAPTER 2, §. On the age of puberty see Puberty; on the signs of barrenness see Barrenness.

units.la: CAP. III. Vxor acquiritur, modo quis mulieri Prutam, aut pretium Pruta æquivalens dederit, & simul coram testibus dixerit, tu mihi sis desponsata! Quamvis autem mulier viro Prutam aut aliam summam pecuniæ daret & ipsum dicto modo alloqueretur, nihil tamen inde sequeretur. Qui literis uxorem ducit, sufficit in Pergameno aut Charta scripsisse, Mihi desponsata es, aut similia, & coram testibus chartam mulieri dedisse. In quibus præsupponitur ipsum libellum nomine mulieris & ipsa conscia scripsisse, aliàs nihil ageret. Qui concubitu uxorem acquirit, debet etiam coram 2. testibus cum ipsa coniungi, & ipsi dicere, Desponsata mea es.
units.tr: CHAPTER 3. A wife is acquired if a man gives the woman a pruta, or a sum of money equal to a pruta, and at the same time says before witnesses, "Be betrothed to me." If, however, the woman gave the man a pruta or some other sum of money and addressed him in the said manner, nothing would follow from it. One who takes a wife by a document is sufficient if he writes on parchment or paper, "You are betrothed to me," or similar words, and gives the paper to the woman before witnesses. In this it is presupposed that he wrote the document in the woman's name and with her knowledge; otherwise he would achieve nothing. One who acquires a wife by intercourse must also be joined with her in the presence of two witnesses, and say to her, "You are my betrothed."

units.la: Epitheta desponsandi sunt, לי את מקודשת Desponsata mea es, לי את מאורסת idem; At non הריני ארוסיך Ecce me virum tuum. הריני בעלך Ecce me desponsum tuum, הריני איש Ecce me maritum tuum : Si enim quis ita diceret uxorem non desponsaret : requiritur itaque ut dicat expressis verbis ipsam esse suam desponsatam, non qualis ille sit ; tales legitimæ formulæ sunt, והרי את אשתי, הרי את Tu es uxor mea, את הרי ארוסתי Tu es sponsa mea, הרי את הקנויה לי הרי את Tu es illa quam mihi acquisivi. Item quando quis dixerit, הרי את שלי, הרי את לקוחתי, הרי את חרופתי, הרי את ברשותי, הרי את וקיקתי לי &c.
units.tr: The formulas of betrothal are: Li at mekudeshet, "You are consecrated to me"; Li at me'orasah, the same. But not Harini erusayikh, "Behold, I am your betrothed"; Harini ba'alekh, "Behold, I am your husband"; Harini ish, "Behold, I am your man"; for if someone spoke thus he would not betroth her. It is therefore required that he say in express words that she is his betrothed, not what he himself is. Such are the lawful formulas: Vehare at ishti, "Behold, you are my wife"; At harai arusati, "You are my betrothed"; Hare at hakeniyah li, "Behold, you are she whom I have acquired for myself." Likewise when someone says, "Behold, you are mine," "Behold, you are my taken one," "Behold, you are my ... ," "Behold, you are in my power," "Behold, you are for me," etc.

units.la: At si quis ad mulierem dixisset, aut scripsisset in Charta, הרי את מיוחדת לי, הרי את עורתי, הרי את נגדי, הרי את מיועדת לי, הרי את סגורתי, הרי את תחתי, צולעתי &c. Dubitare licèret an illam desponsassèt.
units.tr: But if someone said to a woman, or wrote on a paper, "Behold, you are set apart for me," "Behold, you are my help," "Behold, you are opposite me," "Behold, you are destined for me," "Behold, you are my enclosed one," "Behold, you are beneath me," "You are my lame one," etc., one might doubt whether he had betrothed her.

units.la: Quando Virgo non pubuit, pater potest ipsam despondere, sed postquàm maturam attigit ætatem, illa fui iuris fit : nec potest desponderi, nisi suam dederit voluntatem.
units.tr: When a virgin has not reached puberty, her father may betroth her; but after she has reached maturity of age she is her own mistress, and she cannot be betrothed unless she gives her consent.

units.la: Aliquis per legatum uxorem sibi despondere potest ; Etiam mulieri licet per legatum promissa recipere, qui tamen ipse hoc facere poterit, legato ne committat.
units.tr: A man may betroth a wife to himself through an agent; a woman may also lawfully receive a promise through an agent, although he may do this himself, so long as he does not entrust it to the agent.

units.la: Desponsationi præmittenda est benedictio cum poculo vini ; Benedictio sonat צ"א אמ' ק' כן והכנילנו מן הערויות ואסר לנו את האירוסות והתיר לנו את הנשיאות על ידי חופה : וקידושין בא'י מקדש ישראל Benedictus fis tu Domine Deus noster, rex huius mundi, qui sanctificafti nos præcepti tuis, & nos feparafti ab incesto congressu, qui prohibuisti nobis desponsatas, & permisit dullas per sponsalia, & folennia nuptialia, Benedictus fit Deus qui Israelem sanDificat. Hæc ex cap. tertio.
units.tr: A blessing with a cup of wine must precede the betrothal. The blessing runs: Baruch atah Adonai Elohenu melekh ha'olam, asher kiddeshanu bemitzvotav, vetzivanu al ha'arayot, ve'asar lanu et ha'erusot, vehitir lanu et hanesu'in al yedei huppah vekiddushin, "Blessed art thou, O Lord our God, King of the world, who hast sanctified us by thy commandments, and commanded us concerning incest, who hast forbidden us the betrothed women, and hast permitted us wives by the canopy and the nuptial rites. Blessed be God who sanctifies Israel." These things are from the third chapter.

units.la: Quandiu desponsata in paterna manet domo, non licet sponso cum ipsa rem habere, & si aliter fecerit à Synedrio verberibus excipitur tanquam rebellis, vel ut clarius dicam flagellatione vocata ‛מכת מרדות’. Ducta vero in connubialem thorum perfectè eius uxor fit.
units.tr: As long as the betrothed woman remains in her father's house, it is not lawful for the bridegroom to have relations with her; and if he does otherwise he is punished by the Sanhedrin with stripes, as a rebel, or, to speak more plainly, with the flogging called makkat meridut. But once she has been brought into the marriage bed, she becomes his wife in full.

units.la: Io thorum introducta iterum Benedictio recitanda, & scribendum instrumentum dotis. Virgini scribunt 200. Sufeos; illi quæ iam maritata 100. Qui minus dederit בעילתו בעילת זנות Concubitus eius est concubitus fornicationis. Instrumentum autem dotis institutum est שלא תהיה קלה בעיניו להוציאה Ne illa facile in oculis eius vilescat, aut ex quavis occasione illam expellat.
units.tr: Once she has been brought into the bed, the blessing is to be recited again, and the deed of dowry is to be written. For a virgin they write 200 zuzim; for one who is already married, 100. If he gives less, "his intercourse is intercourse of fornication." The deed of dowry was instituted so that she would not become cheap in his eyes, nor be dismissed for any chance reason.

units.la: Licitum est unâ die plures ducere uxores, sed propter maiorem lætitiam sufficit unam uno die duxisse, (Vid. Polygamiam.) & si virgo fuerit festum per septem dies continuasse.
units.tr: It is lawful to take several wives in one day, but for greater joy it suffices to have taken one wife in one day (see Polygamy); and if she was a virgin, the feast is to be kept for seven days continuously.

units.la: Nuptias faciunt omni tempore, die & nocte, etiam 9. mensis Iulii (vid. אב) excepto die Sabbathum præcedente, & Sabbathum insequente, ne præparationibus Convivii Sabbathum profanetur.
units.tr: Weddings are held at any time, by day or by night, even in the month of Av (see Av), except on the Sabbath before and the Sabbath after, lest the preparations for the feast profane the Sabbath.

units.la: Cap. XII. Vxori Maritus decem officia præsta- re debet;
units.tr: Chapter XII. A husband must render ten duties to his wife;

units.la: I. שאירה Alimenta eius. II. כסותה Vestes eius. III. Cohabitatio maritalis. IV. Promittere ipsi aliquam dotem. V. Sanare ipsam ægrotam. VI. Redimere captivam. VII. Sepelire mortuam. VIII. Alere ipsam ex bonis suis.
units.tr: I. Her food (she'erah) [שאירה]. II. Her clothing (kesuatah) [כסותה]. III. Marital cohabitation. IV. To promise her some dowry. V. To heal her when she is sick. VI. To redeem her if she is taken captive. VII. To bury her when she is dead. VIII. To feed her from his own goods.

units.la: IX. Præbere ipsi habitationem tempore eius viduitatis. X. Alere eius filias.
units.tr: IX. To provide her with a dwelling during her widowhood. X. To feed her daughters.

units.la: Maritus autem fruitur opere manuum uxoris, rebus ab ipsa inventis, usufructu bonorum eius; & ipsa mortua est proximus hæres.
units.tr: The husband, moreover, enjoys the labour of his wife's hands, the things she has acquired, and the usufruct of her goods; and when she is dead, he is her nearest heir.

units.la: De Vxore & marito pervicaci Vid. Offensio.
units.tr: On a wife and a stubborn husband, see Offence.

units.la: §. Qua ratione sub Incunabula mundi, præsente unicâ familiâ Adami, Cainus nativam sororem absque incestus crimine ducere in uxorem potuit variæ sunt sententiæ. Thalmudistæ plerique hic allegant חסד benignitatem Dei, iuxta illud Psalmi 89. 3. Benignitas ædificavit seculum. Sic Iarchius ad Levit. xx. 17. Si objicias Cainum in axorem duxisse sororem suam, חסר עשה המקום לבנות עולם ממנו Id ex Numinis indulgentia factum est, ut mundus eius ex eo ædificaretur. Eadem habet Gemara Hierof. ad Sanhed. cap. 16. & citatur à Seldeno, de Iure Nat. Gent. Heb. lib. 5. c. 8. Item Paraph.
units.tr: §. How, at the beginning of the world, when Adam's was the only family, Cain could take his own sister as wife without the crime of incest, opinions vary. Most of the Talmudists here cite chesed [חסד], the kindness of God, according to Psalm 89:3, "Kindness has built the world." Thus Jarchi on Leviticus 20:17: "If you object that Cain took his sister as wife, [חסר עשה המקום לבנות עולם ממנו]; this was done by the indulgence of the Divine Majesty, so that the world might be built from it." The Gemara of Jerusalem on Sanhedrin chapter 16 has the same, and it is cited by Selden, De Iure Naturali et Gentium Hebraeorum, book 5, chapter 8. Likewise the Paraphrase

units.la: · Ionath. ad verba חסר הוא Levit. xx. 17.
units.tr: · of Jonathan on the words "it is chesed" [חסר הוא] in Leviticus 20:17.

units.la: Z.
units.tr: Z.

units.la: ZABI quibusdam sunt Samaritani de quibus vid. Buxtorf. Lexi 109. Aliis veteres Chaldæi.
units.tr: Zabi are, according to some, the Samaritans, concerning whom see Buxtorf, Lexicon 109. According to others, they are the ancient Chaldeans.

units.la: Quænam fuerit fides Zabæana vid. Maymon in More Nevoch.
units.tr: For what the Zabian faith was, see Maimonides in the More Nevochim.

units.la: Arabibus [Hebrew] sunt pagani, qui in oriente respiciunt septentrionem; aliquando verò illi qui Noëmi religione adhæserunt; & illi qui primi Assyriæ Moss & Muhammedis fuerunt. Vid. Cl. Pocokii Hist. Dynast. 10.95. & 108. Hist. Arab. 38. Coran.Sur. 2.61.
units.tr: Among the Arabs they are pagans, who face north when they look east; and sometimes those who adhered to the religion of Noah, and those who were the first in Assyria, Moses and Muhammad. See Pococke's Historia Dynastiarum 10, 95 and 108; Historia Arabum 38; Koran, Sura 2.61.

units.la: ZACHARIA. De Zacharia filio Ioiadæ, quem Ioasus Rex occidit memorabilis locus est in Hierof. Taanith sol. 69.1.2. & Bab. Sanhedrin folio 96.2.
units.tr: Zachariah. Concerning Zechariah son of Jehoiada, whom King Joash killed, there is a memorable passage in the Jerusalem Talmud, Taanith, fol. 69.1.2, and in the Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin, fol. 96.2.

units.la: R. Ionathan dixit, octoginta mille Sacerdotes occisi sunt ob sanguinem Zachariæ. Rab. Iuda interrogavit Rab. Acham, Vbi interfecerunt Zachariam? An in atrio mulierum? an in atrio Israelis? Respondit ille, nec in atrio Israelis, nec in atrio mulierum, sed in atrio Sacerdotum &c.
units.tr: R. Jonathan said: eighty thousand priests were slain on account of the blood of Zechariah. Rab Judah asked Rab Achah: Where did they kill Zechariah? In the court of the women, or in the court of Israel? He answered: neither in the court of Israel nor in the court of the women, but in the court of the priests, etc.

units.la: Plura ibi de ebullitione sanguinis Zachariæ & illius vindicta exstant, quæ probabilem reddunt sententiam de hoc Zacharia Christum loqui Matth.23. v.35.
units.tr: There is more there about the boiling of Zechariah's blood and his vengeance, which makes the opinion probable that Christ, in Matthew 23:35, speaks of this Zechariah.

units.la: ZALMON Vid. DALMANUTA.
units.tr: ZALMON: see DALMANUTHA.

units.la: ZELOTÆ apud Iudæos fuerunt illi, qui transgredientem propriis manibus immediatè interfecerunt, non exspectato Iudicio Synedrii;
units.tr: Among the Jews the Zealots were those who immediately killed with their own hands a transgressor, without waiting for the judgment of the Sanhedrin;

units.la: ita in Sanhedrin folio 81. 2. recensetur, Sacerdotem in immunditia administrantem, non adduci ad Synedrium, sed a פקסp Zelotis ex atrio educi, & sarmentis ligni exterebrari.
units.tr: as is recorded in Sanhedrin, fol. 81.2: a priest who is serving in uncleanness is not brought before the Sanhedrin, but is led out of the court by the Zealots and pierced through with bundles of wood.

units.la: A talibus Pseudo-Zelotis quot non mala evenerunt? Novum Testamentum plurima exempla respectu Christi & Pauli exhibet.
units.tr: How many evils have not come from such pseudo-Zealots? The New Testament presents very many examples with respect to Christ and Paul.

units.la: De Zelotis Vid. Sanhed. cap.9.6.
units.tr: On the Zealots see Sanhedrin, chap. 9.6.

units.la: ZIPPORIS nomen habet a צפור avis, quia instar avis monti insidet. Bab. Megillah folio 6.1.
units.tr: Zippori takes its name from צפור [tsippor], bird, because it sits on the mountain like a bird. Babylonian Megillah, fol. 6.1.

units.la: Sedecim milliaribus undiquaque a Zippore erat terra fluens lacte & melle. Hierof. Bicurim sol.64.2.
units.tr: For sixteen miles on every side of Zippori was a land flowing with milk and honey. Jerusalem Bikkurim, fol. 64.2.

units.la: Plurimæ in Zippori erant Synagogæ, sed præcipuè duæ celebres erant.
units.tr: There were very many synagogues in Zippori, but two in particular were famous.

units.la: Synagoga דגונא Gophnitica, & Synagoga בבלי Babylonica. Hierof. Beracot folio 6.1. & folio 9.1.
units.tr: The Gophnitic synagogue [דגונא] and the Babylonian synagogue [בבלי]. Jerusalem Berakhot, fol. 6.1 and fol. 9.1.

units.la: De inquisitione facta in Zippori Vid. Hierof. Ievamot sol.15.3.
units.tr: On an inquiry made in Zippori, see Jerusalem Yevamot, fol. 15.3.

units.la: De persequutione aliqua sonat locus Bab. Ioma sol.11.1.
units.tr: A certain persecution is hinted at in the passage of the Babylonian Yoma, fol. 11.1.

units.la: Scribitur Zipporis aliquando per ץ, ut Hierof. sol.41 2.
units.tr: Zippori is sometimes written with the letter צ [tsade], as in the Jerusalem Talmud, fol. 41.2.

units.la: Zippori fuit propinqua urbecula ישוע Iefchana Kiddufchin cap.4.5. ut & קצרון Kezara. Gloss. in Erachin cap.9.6.
units.tr: Near Zippori there was a small neighbouring town, Iefchana [ישוע] (Kiddushin, chap. 4.5), and also Kezara [קצרון] (gloss on Eruvin, chap. 9.6).

units.la: ZIZITH Vid. Tephillin in T. Illorum præceptum extat Numerorum xv.38. Deuteronom. XXII.12.
units.tr: Zizith: see Tephillin in the Talmud. Their precept is found in Numbers 15:38 and Deuteronomy 22:12.

units.la: Apud ipsos receptum erat diligentem eorum observationem mereri retributionem.
units.tr: Among them it was accepted that diligent observance of them merits a reward.

units.la: Bab. Schabbat sol. 23. 2. Qui de candela Sabbatica curat, situri sunt eius filii discipuli Sapientum; qui de membranulis postibus affigendis, domum speciosam adipiscetur: quique de ציצית fimbriis vestimento attexendis, adipiscetur bonam tunicam.
units.tr: Babylonian Shabbat, fol. 23.2: Whoever takes care of the Sabbath candle, his sons will be disciples of the wise; whoever takes care to affix the little parchments to the doorposts will obtain a fine house; and whoever attends to the fringes [ציצית] attached to a garment will obtain a good tunic.

units.la: CAP. I. Verf. 1. Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Vid. Genealogiam in G. p.320 Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ vid. Christum in C. 108 v. 2. Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν vid. Abraham in A. p.3 v. 16. Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησε τὸν Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας &c. quare ad Iosephum genealogia descendat? vid. apud Christum. 108 v. 17. Πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες. In usu habuerunt numeros paritate aliqua se contingentes reducere ad idem. vid. Numerus in N. & ΙΝ in A. p.2 Βαβυλῶνος vid. Babylonios in B. 62 v. 18. Μνηστευθείσης &c. vid. Desponsationem & Nuptias. 158.413.414.675 εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα. Spatium requisitum ad detegendum an uxor prægnans sit. vid. Nuptias. 414
units.tr: CHAP. I. Verse 1. The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ [Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ]. See Genealogy in G, p. 320. Jesus Christ: see Christ in C, 108. Verse 2. Abraham begat [Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν]: see Abraham in A, p. 3. Verse 16. Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, etc. Why does the genealogy descend to Joseph? See under Christ, 108. Verse 17. All the generations are fourteen [Πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες]. They used to reduce numbers that touch each other by some parity to the same thing: see Number in N, and ΙΝ in A, p. 2. Babylon [Βαβυλῶνος]: see Babylonians in B, 62. Verse 18. When his mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, etc.: see Betrothal and Marriage, 158, 413, 414, 675. She was found with child [εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα]: the space of time needed to discover whether a wife is pregnant. See Marriage, 414.
