units.la: observato scilicet quod notatur Megillah sol.24.1. quod interim non liceat transfilire retrorsum : id est non à posteriori ad prius Marcus ut his canonibus non subiectus à Propheta unius classis, à Malachia transilivit ad Esaiam Prophetam alterius ordinis. Et forsan Christiano-Iudæi, quibus hic saltus non admodum placuit, pro Esaia aut Malachia Propheta, infuerunt in Prophetis, quod vocabulum in plurali positum dedit deinde occasionem disputationibus.
units.tr: This is to be observed, namely that Megillah 24b notes that one may not skip backwards, that is, from a later passage to an earlier one. Mark, not bound by these rules, passed from Malachi, a prophet of one class, to Isaiah the prophet of another order. And perhaps the Jewish Christians, to whom this leap did not much please, found in the phrase "in the Prophets", the plural word used for Isaiah or Malachi the prophet, an occasion for further disputes.

units.la: Oppositio Baptismi Christi & Iudæorum talis potest fieri. Baptizabant Iudæi aquâ frigidâ ita ut mulieres Galilææ ex illo frigore sterilescerent; Christus baptizat aquâ & igne, id est aquâ ignitâ, efficacissimâ, quæ nos in bonis operibus sobolescere facit. Iudæi baptizabant nudâ & simplici aqua, hinc proselyti ipsorum erant ut scabies (vid. Baptismum.) quatenus pristinorum morum & peccatorum semper tenaces alios inficiebant; Christus baptizat ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, vi flexanimâ, quæ non solùm externè purgat ut aquâ, sed etiam
units.tr: The contrast between the baptism of Christ and that of the Jews may be drawn thus. The Jews baptized with cold water, so that the women of Galilee became barren from that chill; Christ baptizes with water and fire, that is, with fiery, most effective water, which makes us fruitful in good works. The Jews baptized with bare and plain water; hence their proselytes were like scabies (see Baptism), as they always clung tenaciously to their former manners and sins and infected others; Christ baptizes in the Holy Spirit [ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ], with a soul-moving power, which cleanses not only externally, as water does, but also

units.la: ad mare מרינת אחר Provincia una. Gemara Hierosolymit. addit, hanc provinciam vocatam esse בורי quod vel est Περαία, vel Περαία, vel Περαία, Regio ulterior. Ioseph. Perœa. Nobis videtur περαίαν τῆ Ἰορδάνῃ nihil aliud esse quam spatium illud amœnum quod Μέγα πέδιον. Magna planities vocatur apud Iosephum de bello lib. 4. c. 27. quod medium erat inter duo montana quorum unum à Gemaristis vocatur הר אמאום Amaus mons; & quod in medio intersciindebatur per Iordanem.
units.tr: to the sea [מרינת אחר] One province. The Jerusalem Gemara adds that this province is called [בורי], which is either Peraea, or Peraea, or Peraea, the region beyond. Josephus has Perea. It seems to us that the Greek phrase "beyond the Jordan" [περαίαν τῆ Ἰορδάνῃ] is nothing other than that pleasant tract which is called the Great Plain [Μέγα πέδιον]. Josephus calls it the Great Plain in De Bello book 4, chapter 27: it lay between two mountainous districts, one of which the Gemarists call Mount Amaus [הר אמאום], and it was cut through the middle by the Jordan.

units.la: ἀρκοῦσ̈ τῆς ἐλωνίους ὑμῶν. Ἰώνιον etiam est vox nota Talmudicis sed cùm aliqua immutatione, Textus enim in Sanhed. f.21.2. habet אפנין, quam lectionem tamen Bartenora restituit in Commentario אופסניא. Opsonia verò notante Glossa est שכר חיילות Merces militum, & comprehendit in se quicquid militibus sub nomine stipendii, salarii, authoramenti, accedit.
units.tr: "Be content with your wages" [ἀρκεῖσθε τοῖς ὀψωνίοις ὑμῶν]. The word ōnion [ἐλωνίους] is also a word known to the Talmudists, though with some change: the text in Sanhedrin f. 21.2 has [אפנין], which Bartenora restores in his commentary as [אופסניא]. The Gloss notes that opsonia means [שכר חיילות], the wages of soldiers, and it comprises everything that accrues to soldiers under the name of pay, salary or enlistment bounty.

units.la: ἐοει ἐπὶ πεπώκασι. Sacerdotes ordinem ingrediebantur cùm 30. annos attigissent. vid. pag. 533. ita Christus anno 30. Sacerdotale munus suscepit: nam quamvis illos non plenè compleverat, tamen secundùm gentis consuetudinem ille æstimabatur iam 30. annos habere, qui illos incepisset, vid. Anni dies primus &c. 35.
units.tr: [ἐοει ἐπὶ πεπώκασι]. Priests entered the order when they had reached thirty years; see p. 533. So Christ took up the priestly office in the thirtieth year. For although he had not fully completed them, according to the custom of the nation he was reckoned to be thirty years old, since he had begun them. See Anni dies primus etc., 35.

At הכפיש significat, metiri menfurâ deprefsâ, accumulatâ, fuperabundanti. Vid. Rabbi Salomoh Thren.3.16.
units.tr: CHAP. VI. v.38. ... Among the ancients the liberal measure for dry goods was heaped up, pressed down, shaken, and then heaped again, so that something overflowed above the brim. ... For this is the same as [מרה כפושה] in Yebamot fol. 107.2. But [הכפיש] signifies to measure with a pressed-down, heaped-up, overflowing measure. See Rabbi Solomon on Thren. 3.16.

units.la: CAP. VIII. v.52. ... De Luctu vid. 346. feq. Notandum plan&tum de quo ibi loquimur non fimplici clamore & ciulatu, fed præcipuè cantionibus & epicediis ad honorem defun&torum, & confolationem lugentium inftitutis, factum fuiffe: ita cùm mortuus effet Rabbena quidam Siticen, plan&tum fuum ita exorfus eft, תמרים הניעו ראש על צריק כתמר נשים לילות כימי O Palmæ commoveie caput super iusto qui similis erat palmæ, infumamus dies & noctes [in lu&tu.] Videtur etiam officium Lamentatorum publicum & ftatum fuiffe; in illa Sparta verò excelluerunt Bar קיפוק Kippuk & בר אבין Bar Abhin, de quibus mentio fit in Moed Katon fol.25.2. & Iebhamot fol.103.1.
units.tr: CHAP. VIII. v.52. ... On mourning see pp. 346 ff. It should plainly be noted that what we speak of there was done not with mere shouting and wailing, but chiefly with songs and funeral poems established to honour the dead and console the mourners. So when a certain Rabbena Siticen had died, he began his lament thus: "O palms, bow your heads over the righteous one, who was like a palm; let us spend days and nights [in mourning]" [תמרים הניעו ראש על צריק כתמר נשים לילות כימי]. It seems also that the office of mourners was public and established; in that Sparta, however, Bar Kippuk [בר קיפוק] and Bar Abhin [בר אבין] excelled, of whom mention is made in Moed Katan fol. 25.2 and Yebamot fol. 103.1.

units.tr: CAP. XI. v.12. Every house divided against itself falls. Something similar is found in Derech Eretz ch. 5: "Every house in which there is dissension will in the end be laid waste" [כל בית שיש בו מחלוקת סופו ליחרב].

units.la: v.27. Beatus uterus qui te portavit, ἢ μακάριοι αἱ μαστοί ἐθήλασας. Erat hæc usitata formula benedictionis, ut è contra maledictionis erat, ליש ביוא רכן אייען Maledicta sint ubera quæ hunc lactarunt. Exstat illa Hierof. Kilaim cap.1. sub sin. Beresc. Rabba sect.5.
units.tr: v.27. Blessed is the womb that bore you, or blessed are the breasts that you sucked [ἢ μακάριοι αἱ μαστοί ἐθήλασας]. This was the usual formula of blessing, just as the opposite was the formula of cursing: Cursed be the breasts that nursed this one. It is found in Hierosolymitan Kilaim ch. 1, near the end, and in Bereshith Rabba sect. 5.

units.la: CAP. XII. v.3. ἐν τῇ ταμείῳ. Quando Syrum consulo quid ταμεῖον fit, refert, esse תונא ; illud verò originem sumit ex Hebraico תא, quod Thalamum, cubiculum, οἰκοῦ-τὸν, Excubitorium, significat. Insuper in Bava Bathra cap. 4. in Gemara, תא non in interioribus partibus Domus ponitur, sed annectitur exterioribus lateribus, & existimatur esse appendix principalis ædificii. Item תא etiam vocatur יציע quod substructionem denotat & stratum : vid.
units.tr: CAP. XII. v.3. "In the storeroom" [ἐν τῇ ταμείῳ]. When I consult the Syriac as to what ταμεῖον is, it gives tuna; but that word derives from the Hebrew taw [תא], which means a chamber, a small room, a guard-room, a watch-house. Moreover, in Bava Bathra ch. 4, in the Gemara, a taw is not placed in the innermost parts of a house but is attached to the outer sides, and is regarded as an appendix to the main building. Likewise the taw is also called yatzia [יציע], which denotes a substructure and a layer: see.

units.la: 1.Reg.6.5.His significationibus positis,sen‐ sus verborum Evangelistæ esse potest. Quod in interioribus vestris cubiculis, in Thalamis ipsis in quibus lingua liberè quaevis eloquitur, dixeritis, in publicis locis super ipso tecto domus manifestabitur, in om‐ nium conspectum veniet. Vel Talis: Quod in appendice, vestibulo, substructione, & infimo plane domus vestra strato dixeritis, in aurem loquuti estis, ut secretum deposueritis μυχοῖ‐σι ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων, יכרו וכריזון כו על הגג supra domos prædicabitur, promulgabitur; proclamabitur ; hanc enim vim habet כרו à quo profluit verbum κηρύσσω. Loco tecti domus Proverbiorum 1.21. Chaldæus habet fastigium & caput arcium ; בריש ביתא בכרזא (Summa sapientia) in capite arcium proclamat. Zohar exprimit δωμάτων per מלמעלה Cœlitus, superne, in his verbis אין דבר בא לעולם שאין מכריזין אותו מלמעלה Nulla res venit in mundum, quam non promulgent cœlitus; quæ non à Deo hominibus declaratur.
units.tr: 1 Reg. 6.5. With these meanings laid down, the sense of the Evangelist's words can be this: "What you have spoken in your inner chambers, in the very bedrooms where the tongue speaks freely, will be made known on the housetops in public places, and will come into the sight of all." Or it may be as follows: "What you have said in the porch, the vestibule, the substructure, and the very lowest floor of your house, whispering in the ear, you have put away as a secret" [μυχοῖσι ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων] "will be preached above the houses, published, and proclaimed" [יכרו וכריזון כו על הגג]; for כרו has this force, and from it the verb κηρύσσω derives. In place of "the housetop of the house" in Proverbs 1.21, the Chaldee has "the pinnacle and head of the gateways" [בריש ביתא בכרזא], "(Highest wisdom) proclaims at the head of the gateways." The Zohar renders δωμάτων by מלמעלה [from above], "from heaven, from on high," in these words: "No thing comes into the world which they do not proclaim from above" [אין דבר בא לעולם שאין מכריזין אותו מלמעלה], which is not declared to men by God.

Cæterùm in hoc versu nota vocem, ἐπιαπὼ magis ex Hellenismo quàm Latinismo explicandam esse; & quoniam apud Græcos διὰ ἐπιαπὼ denotat illum qui quæstum alicui exhibet, (quo sensu sumitur apud Nicarch. Moreover, in this verse note that the word ἐπιαπὼ is to be explained from Hellenism rather than from Latinism [ἐπιαπὼ]; for among the Greeks διὰ ἐπιαπὼ denotes one who furnishes a profit to someone [διὰ ἐπιαπὼ], in which sense it is used in Nicarchus, Anthologia, Epigrams book 6; likewise Athenaeus 16.v.16, 19; likewise chapter 19.24. units.tr: Go out into the highways and the hedges [Ἐξιλθε εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς καὶ φραγμοὺς]. In verse 21 the householder sent his servant [illegible] into the squares and streets of the city (see on the squares, Hicrof. p. 466). Now he bids the servant gather people of the very lowest condition; to this end he wills that he leave the city and go to [illegible], that is, to gardens and vineyards, in which the very poorest labourers hired out their work for wages, and which were divided off by hedges. So Kimchi: The hedges of vineyards and fields were divided off with thorns. See also on Isa. v. 2. On the roads and their division, see p. 664.

units.la: μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας. ἄδικον idem est ac ἄπιστον, & usu Hebræorum falsum significat, ita Hosea 5.11. Divitiæ vocantur falsæ. [illegible, ~8 letters] opponitur τῇ ἀληθινῇ, qui in cœlis est; huius mundi divitiæ enim iniquæ sunt, ideò quòd vocantur divitiæ, cùm tales non nisi nomine sint. Magistri etiam falsas divitias, & ἐσθ τὸ ἀνω- τῷ- τῶτε coniungunt, quando inquiunt, מטון השקר והון העולם בא במחרה וחלף כמהרה falsa divitiæ, & opes mundi, veniunt celeriter, celeriterque transeunt.
units.tr: μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας. ἄδικον means the same as ἄπιστον, and in Hebrew usage it signifies false, as in Hosea 5.11, where riches are called false. [illegible] is opposed to τῇ ἀληθινῇ, which is in heaven. For the riches of this world are unrighteous, because they are called riches when they are such only in name. The masters also couple false riches with [a Greek phrase garbled in the scan] when they say, מטון השקר והון העולם בא במהרה וחלף כמהרה, false riches and the wealth of the world come quickly and pass quickly.

units.la: v.23. εἰς τὸν κόλπον τῆς Ἀβρααμ. Est formula loquendi, quâ felicem statum piorum defunctorum denotant; Kidduschin fol. 72. 2. היום יושב בחיקו של אברהם Hodie sedet in sinu Abrahæ. Gloss. מת mortuus est. Similem loquutionem etiam habemus in Baba Batra fol. 58. 1. Quæsivit R. Banaah, quid fecit Abraham? באני בכנפה דשרה Cubat in ulnis Saræ. Gloss. בין זרועותי Inter brachia eius.
units.tr: v. 23. εἰς τὸν κόλπον τῆς Ἀβραάμ. This is a form of speech by which they denote the happy state of pious departed souls. Kidduschin fol. 72.2: היום יושב בחיקו של אברהם, Today he sits in the bosom of Abraham. Gloss: מת, he has died. We have a similar expression also in Baba Batra fol. 58.1: R. Banaah asked, what did Abraham do? He answers, He lies in the arms of Sarah (Aramaic: ba'ani bekhanfah desharah). Gloss: בין זרועותי, between her arms.
